title: Kelly, Gallego Announce $9.6 Million to Improve Railroad Crossing Safety Across Arizona
text:
Federal funding will support railroad crossing safety projects in Marana, Yuma County, and Phoenix

Today, Arizona Senators Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego announced $9.6 million in federal funding for three projects to improve railroad crossing safety in Marana, Yuma County, and Phoenix. The funding will support planning and design work to address dangerous railroad crossings, reduce traffic delays, and improve the movement of people and goods across Arizona.

The funding was awarded through the Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE) Grant Program, established by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which Kelly helped negotiate and pass.

“Arizonans shouldn’t have to worry about dangerous railroad crossings when they’re driving to work or taking their kids to school,” said Kelly. “This funding to improve our transportation infrastructure will keep families safe.”

“Arizona’s railroads are critical links that keep our state’s economy flowing. This federal funding in railroad crossing safety will further ensure people get where they need to go safely and goods move more efficiently,” said Gallego. “Investing in our infrastructure means creating good-paying jobs, improving safety, and making sure communities across Arizona have access to the public infrastructure they deserve.”

“This $6.4 million federal investment is a major step forward for the Tangerine Road Interchange project and the future of Marana and our region. Once completed, the project will eliminate a major railroad crossing, improve safety and connectivity, and help meet the needs of our growing community. We are grateful to Senator Kelly, Senator Gallego, and Congressman Ciscomani for their support in advancing this project and their continued commitment to our community,” said Jon Post, Mayor of the City of Marana.

“For too long, residents of the Fortuna Foothills have experienced recurring and prolonged closures at the Fortuna Road railroad crossing, disrupting daily travel and raising serious public safety concerns. This $2 million federal investment represents a significant step toward a permanent solution by advancing the project through final design and bringing us closer to construction. We appreciate Senators Kelly and Gallego’s support and the Federal Railroad Administration’s investment in this critical infrastructure project. Yuma County looks forward to continuing our work with our federal and state partners to improve transportation safety, reliability, and emergency access for our residents,” said Martin Porchas, Chairman, Yuma County Board of Supervisors.

title: SENATOR MCCORMICK ANNOUNCES HIS 2026 U.S. SERVICE ACADEMY NOMINATIONSADVISORY BOARD
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Dave McCormick (R-PA) recently announced a distinguished group of veterans, public servants, and community leaders from across the Commonwealth to serve on his Eastern and Western Region Advisory Boards that will help select nominations for U.S. Service Academy appointments.

“I’m deeply grateful to this talented group of veterans and leaders who have volunteered their time for such a vital mission,” said Senator McCormick. “Their service on these advisory boards will help us select the finest young Pennsylvanians to attend our United States Service Academies and lead the next generation of America’s military.”

Candidates applying to the U.S. Coast Guard Academy do not need a Congressional nomination for appointment.

title: Reed Statement on the Passing of Nicolas P. Retsinas
text:
PROVIDENCE, RI – Today, U.S. Senator Jack Reed issued the following statement on the passing of Nicolas P. Retsinas, a lifelong Rhode Islander and leader in local and national housing policy and advocacy, who previously served as Assistant Secretary for the Housing Commissioner at the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD); as Chairman of the Providence Housing Authority; and at Rhode Island Housing:

“I want to express my deep sadness for Nic Retsinas’ death and enduring gratitude for his dedicated, exceptional public service.

“Nic is a giant in the housing world. He was a nationally recognized housing policy expert and a tremendous advocate for people in public housing. He used his considerable skill and passion to advocate for others and connect them to a place to call home. He was a model public servant who treated everyone with decency and respect and prioritized transparency, accountability, and fiscal responsibility in government.

“Nic helped develop good housing policy, built strong affordable housing organizations, and strengthened neighborhoods and communities.

“Our condolences to his beloved wife, Joan, and their children and grandchildren. Nic made Rhode Island and our country a better place. I am grateful to have had the opportunity to work with him and call him a friend.”

title: NEWS: Sens. Schiff, Padilla Announce More Than $116 Million to Improve Railroad Crossing Safety Across California
text:
Washington, D.C. — Earlier this week, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.) announced that six California projects will receive more than $116 million in federal funding through President Biden’s Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), which Padilla and Schiff voted to pass. The funding, awarded through the Federal Railroad Administration’s Railroad Crossing Elimination (RCE) Program, will improve railroad crossing safety, reduce traffic delays, and strengthen rail infrastructure in Burlingame, Sunnyvale, Richmond, Riverside, San Diego, and Suisun City.

“I am proud to help deliver federal funding for critical safety and modernization upgrades for railroad crossings throughout California—made possible by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. All Californians deserve to live in communities with robust transportation infrastructure that helps reduce congestion. These federal investments will help ensure the safety of our pedestrians and drivers,” said Senator Schiff.

“These federal investments will help make California’s railroad crossings safer, reduce traffic delays, and strengthen the transportation infrastructure our communities depend on,” said Senator Padilla. “From eliminating hazardous crossings to planning future safety upgrades, these projects will improve mobility for Californians and support a stronger regional economy thanks to the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. I’ll keep fighting to ensure our communities get these critical investments and the resources they need to grow and thrive.”

The six California projects selected for funding will advance grade separation projects, feasibility studies, and planning efforts to improve safety and mobility for motorists, pedestrians, cyclists, and rail passengers.

Burlingame Broadway Grade Separation Project — $90.42 million: The Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board will eliminate an at-grade crossing by constructing an elevated rail structure and lowering the roadway, improving safety and reducing traffic delays.

Mary Avenue Grade Separation Project, Sunnyvale — $15.50 million: The City of Sunnyvale will advance final design work for a future grade separation along the Caltrain corridor.

Cutting/Carlson At-Grade Crossing Elimination Study, Richmond — $3.36 million: The City of Richmond will plan for a future grade separation at the Cutting Boulevard crossing along the Union Pacific Railroad corridor.

Spruce Street Crossing Closure and Grade Separation Project, Riverside — $2.80 million: The City of Riverside will advance planning and project development for a future grade separation along the BNSF corridor.

San Diego Regionwide At-Grade Crossing Elimination Study — $2.73 million: The San Diego Association of Governments (SANDAG) will plan for safety improvements, separations, or elimination of 39 grade crossings across the regional rail network.

Sunset Avenue Grade Separation Feasibility Study, Suisun City — $2.01 million: The City of Suisun City will evaluate alternatives to separate vehicle, bicycle, and pedestrian traffic from the Union Pacific Railroad corridor.

title: Van Hollen Pushes Trump Administration for Answers Following Death of Marylander in ICE Custody
text:
U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) is pressing the Trump Administration for accountability following the death of Maryland resident Julian Curo-Churata in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody and subsequent apparent retaliation against Mr. Curo-Churata’s wife. In the letter, Senator Van Hollen seeks answers to specific questions around his death from Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin, ICE Acting Director David Venturella, and DHS Inspector General Joseph Cuffari, as well as the release and preservation of all records related to the death of Mr. Curo-Churata and an independent investigation into his death. The Senator also questions the recent launch of deportation proceedings against Mr. Curo-Churata’s wife, in what appears to be a retaliation for her decision to speak out on her husband’s death.

Senator Van Hollen begins, “On September 29, 2026, Maryland resident Julian Curo-Churata died in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody. His death is unacceptable and both his family and the American people deserve answers as to how this could occur on your watch – including a full, independent investigation. To make matters worse, there is now an apparent attempt to retaliate against Mr. Curo-Churata’s wife, Veronica Ramirez, who received a Notice to Appear dated three days after speaking out in the Washington Post about her husband’s death as she sought justice and accountability.”

“Julian Curo-Churata lived with Ms. Ramirez and their two children in Laurel, Maryland. On June 27, less than a week after he had attended a court hearing on his pending immigration case, he was arrested by ICE as he stopped at Home Depot on his way to work. Mr. Curo-Churata was detained at Richwood Correctional Center, an ICE detention facility in Louisiana operated by a private company, until September 28, when he was taken to the hospital after he was found to be in medical distress. The next morning, Mr. Curo-Churata died in the hospital due to cardiac arrest linked to septic shock. He was the 37th person to die in ICE custody in the past year. Johns Hopkins Medicine describes sepsis as a ‘life-threatening emergency that needs to be treated right away’ by medical personnel in a hospital,” he continues.

Senator Van Hollen challenges ICE’s claim that Mr. Curo-Churata received appropriate medical attention while in ICE custody, writing, “In Mr. Curo-Churata’s case, ICE claims that ‘while in custody, Curo received proper medical care.’ However, the facility’s correctional officers reportedly attested that he had been ‘lethargic and unresponsive throughout the day’ on September 28, but he was not transported to the hospital until late that evening. While ICE claimed he was transported to the hospital at 8:14 p.m., hospital records reportedly show he did not arrive until 10:26 p.m., even though the hospital was just a 7-minute drive from the facility. Mr. Curo-Churata passed away at 4:01 a.m. on September 29 from cardiac arrest due to septic shock.”

“Just over a month later, after speaking publicly about the death of her husband, Mr. Curo-Churata’s wife, Veronica Ramirez, received a Notice to Appear from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), indicating the Department’s intent to remove her from the United States. The timing of this notice is highly suspicious, seeming to come in retaliation for her decision to speak out. It was issued just three days after Ms. Ramirez was quoted extensively in the Washington Post about her husband’s death. DHS has already taken one parent away from their children permanently, and now, in their time of grief, threatens to deport the other,” Senator Van Hollen notes.

Among other questions, Senator Van Hollen asks the following:

Please identify every camera that recorded Mr. Curo-Churata between September 27 and September 29, 2026. That includes but is not limited to housing-unit, medical-unit, hallway, sally-port and parking-area surveillance cameras; body-worn cameras worn by escort and transport officers; and any camera inside the transport vehicle. For each, state the normal retention period and whether the footage has been kept. If any footage has been deleted or overwritten, explain when, why, and on whose authority.

When and how did any Richwood staff first receive information that Mr. Curo-Churata was ill or in medical distress on September 28? Please identify every staff member involved and give exact times.

What was the basis for ICE’s statement to the press that facility staff transported Mr. Curo-Churata to Ochsner LSU Health Monroe Medical Center at 8:14 p.m. CDT? Please identify any documents indicating that a transfer to the hospital was ordered, requested, or occurred at or around 8:14 p.m. CDT.

What internal reviews, mortality reviews, or after-action reports has LaSalle Management Company and/or Richwood started or completed regarding Mr. Curo-Churata’s death? Has the facility given records to the DHS Office of Inspector General, the ICE Health Service Corps, or any medical examiner or coroner? Please provide any findings.

When, if ever, has Ms. Veronica Ramirez been issued a Notice to Appear before the one she recently received?

What was the reason that she received the Notice to Appear at this time?

Who made the decision to issue her a Notice to Appear?

“Given these concerns, I’m seeking the release and preservation of all records related to the death of Mr. Curo-Churata, as well as a full, independent investigation into his death,” he concludes.

The full text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Secretary Mullin and Acting Director Venturella and Inspector General Cuffari,

On September 29, 2026, Maryland resident Julian Curo-Churata died in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody. His death is unacceptable and both his family and the American people deserve answers as to how this could occur on your watch – including a full, independent investigation. To make matters worse, there is now an apparent attempt to retaliate against Mr. Curo-Churata’s wife, Veronica Ramirez, who received a Notice to Appear dated three days after speaking out in the Washington Post about her husband’s death as she sought justice and accountability.

Julian Curo-Churata lived with Ms. Ramirez and their two children in Laurel, Maryland. On June 27, less than a week after he had attended a court hearing on his pending immigration case, he was arrested by ICE as he stopped at Home Depot on his way to work. Mr. Curo-Churata was detained at Richwood Correctional Center, an ICE detention facility in Louisiana operated by a private company, until September 28, when he was taken to the hospital after he was found to be in medical distress. The next morning, Mr. Curo-Churata died in the hospital due to cardiac arrest linked to septic shock. He was the 37th person to die in ICE custody in the past year. Johns Hopkins Medicine describes sepsis as a “life-threatening emergency that needs to be treated right away” by medical personnel in a hospital.

In accordance with national detention standards, ICE is required to provide a safe and humane detention environment for its detainees. However, since the beginning of the second Trump Administration, at least 57 people have died in ICE custody. According to a Human Rights Watch report, the mortality rate of deaths in ICE custody is at its highest level in over a decade, including during the COVID-19 pandemic. Public reporting on ICE facilities has consistently revealed inhumane detention conditions and evidence of inadequate and delayed care. It is clear that ICE is not upholding its duty. ICE maintains that it is “committed to ensuring that all those in custody reside in safe, secure and humane environments,” that “comprehensive medical care is provided from the moment individuals arrive and throughout their stay,” and that “at no time during detention is a [detainee] denied emergency care.” The death of Mr. Curo-Churata, as well as the public record on detention conditions during the second Trump Administration, contradict those claims.

In Mr. Curo-Churata’s case, ICE claims that “while in custody, Curo received proper medical care.” However, the facility’s correctional officers reportedly attested that he had been “lethargic and unresponsive throughout the day” on September 28, but he was not transported to the hospital until late that evening. While ICE claimed he was transported to the hospital at 8:14 p.m., hospital records reportedly show he did not arrive until 10:26 p.m., even though the hospital was just a 7-minute drive from the facility. Mr. Curo-Churata passed away at 4:01 a.m. on September 29 from cardiac arrest due to septic shock.

Just over a month later, after speaking publicly about the death of her husband, Mr. Curo-Churata’s wife, Veronica Ramirez, received a Notice to Appear from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), indicating the Department’s intent to remove her from the United States. The timing of this notice is highly suspicious, seeming to come in retaliation for her decision to speak out. It was issued just three days after Ms. Ramirez was quoted extensively in the Washington Post about her husband’s death. DHS has already taken one parent away from their children permanently, and now, in their time of grief, threatens to deport the other.

Given these concerns, I’m seeking the release and preservation of all records related to the death of Mr. Curo-Churata, as well as a full, independent investigation into his death. Additionally, please respond to the following questions no later than November 16, 2026.

title: Whitehouse Announces $430,000 in Federal Funding to Expand Mental Health Services at Children’s Friend
text:
Providence, RI – U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse today joined staff and board members of Children’s Friend in Providence to tour its therapeutic classrooms and announce $430,000 in federal funding for the non-profit.

“Children’s Friend does heroic work to support some of Rhode Island’s most vulnerable children and families,” said Whitehouse. “It is wonderful to see this funding at work ensuring that kids facing mental health challenges can get individualized care that meets their needs.”

Whitehouse secured the earmark in the 2026 minibus, allowing Children’s Friend to expand mental health assessments, clinical capacity, therapeutic classroom visits, and staff training. The funding will allow Children’s Friend to improve individualized mental health and disabilities services for over 800 children enrolled in its early childhood centers and to almost double the organization’s behavioral health staffing.

“The mental health needs of young children are growing and are often overlooked. Yet we know that early intervention can make a profound difference in a child’s life. Thanks to Senator Whitehouse’s leadership and commitment to Rhode Island’s children and families, this $430,000 investment will allow Children’s Friend to expand critical mental health services to our young children. This funding will improve services and support for over 800 children in our early childhood centers. This funding is about giving children the clinical support they need at the earliest possible age, equipping educators with the tools to respond to their needs, and helping families build a stronger foundation for the future,” said David Caprio, President and CEO of Children’s Friend.

Founded in 1834, Children’s Friend is one of the nation’s oldest child-serving organizations and a leading provider of early childhood education and family support services in Rhode Island. Through early childhood education and care sites in Providence, Pawtucket, and Central Falls, Children’s Friend provides comprehensive educational, developmental, and mental health services to young children and families, helping build a strong foundation for lifelong learning and well-being.

title: Rep. Aguilar Announces $5.4 Million to Strengthen Inland Empire Water and Storm Infrastructure
text:
The San Bernardino Valley Water Conservation District will receive $5.4 million in funding from the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation to capture more water and store it underground for future use

SAN BERNARDINO, CA – Today, Rep. Pete Aguilar (CA-33) announced a $5,403,000 million grant for the San Bernardino Valley Water Conservation District’s (SBVWCD) Oak Creek Basins Project. This grant funding will expand SBVWCD’s ability to capture stormwater and store it underground, helping service homes, businesses and farms long after storms have passed.

Captured water will replenish the aquifers our region depends on, so our communities have a reliable water supply even through droughts and dry seasons. The grant award for the Oak Creek Basins Project is the largest award for the Program for Expansion of Recharge Capacity (PERC) to date.

“Access to clean, reliable water is essential for every family and business in the Inland Empire,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar. “I’m proud to announce this funding for the Oak Creek Basins Project, which will help capture stormwater here in the San Bernardino Valley and store it for future use. Investments like this help secure our region’s water supply and ensure that families here can use it for generations to come.”

“Some of the most important investments we make today are the ones our communities will benefit from decades down the road,” said Melody McDonald, Board President, San Bernardino Valley Water Conservation District. “The Program for Expansion of Recharge Capacity (PERC) reflects years of thoughtful planning, strong partnerships, and a shared belief in the future of the San Bernardino Valley. We’re grateful to Congressman Aguilar for recognizing the importance of investing in our local water supplies, and especially proud of the people whose dedication has brought us to this exciting milestone. Their work will make a lasting difference for generations to come.”

“California cannot control when the next storm arrives, but we can be ready to capture the water it brings,” Betsy Miller Vixie, General Manager, San Bernardino Valley Water Conservation District. “The Oak Creek Basins project, part of our broader Program for Expansion of Recharge Capacity (PERC) will expand our ability to put that water underground, where it can support our communities long after the storm has passed. With this federal investment, we are building on more than a century of groundwater recharge experience to make better use of one of our region’s most valuable natural resources.”

This $5.4 million grant award comes from the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation’s Small Storage Program.

title: Bacon, NE Delegation Urge Disaster Declaration for Nebraska Storms
text:
Washington, D.C. – Rep. Don Bacon (NE-02) joined Sens. Deb Fischer (R-NE) and Pete Ricketts (R-NE), and Reps. Mike Flood (NE-01) and Adrian Smith (NE-03) in sending a letter to President Donald Trump supporting Gov. Jim Pillen’s request for a major disaster declaration following severe storms and flooding in Nebraska from Sept. 30 through Oct. 6, 2026.

The requested declaration would apply to Douglas, Fillmore, Lancaster, Saline, Sarpy, Saunders, Seward, and Thayer counties.

Copy of transmitted letter here and text below:

Dear Mr. President:

We write in support of Nebraska Gov. Jim Pillen’s requests for a major disaster declaration and hazard mitigation. These requests follow heavy rain and severe flooding in Douglas, Fillmore, Lancaster, Saline, Sarpy, Saunders, Seward, and Thayer counties, during the period of Sept. 30, 2026, through Oct. 6, 2026.

Severe flash flooding caused widespread damage in Nebraska, and record one-day rainfall was recorded at the Lincoln Airport. These storms also left numerous people displaced after their homes were deemed unlivable. Total damage estimates now exceed $15 million.

We are confident that Nebraskans will once again meet the challenges ahead with strength and determination. We urge the federal government to work alongside the state to help affected communities rebuild and ensure assistance reaches those who need it.

We stand ready and willing to assist in any way possible to ensure prompt evaluation of this request. Please do not hesitate to contact our offices with any questions.

title: Legendary Vietnam Gun Truck to Ride in DC Veterans Parade
text:
A replica of the Vietnam-era gun truck “Brutus” will travel down Constitution Avenue on November 8, 2026, as part of the National Veterans Parade, honoring the soldiers who defended American supply convoys during the Vietnam War.

WHAT: “Brutus” replica participating in the National Veterans Parade

WHEN: Sunday, November 8, 2026; parade begins at noon ET

WHERE: Constitution Ave., Washington, D.C., from the National Archives to the White House

MEDIA OPPORTUNITIES: Photography/videography, Veterans Day-related coverage. Interested media should contact Noah Slayter to coordinate coverage opportunities.

The tribute has personal significance for U.S. Congressman Jim Baird (IN-04). The Congressman served as a convoy commander for the 523rd Transportation Company. The company is known for multiple renowned gun trucks including Ace of Spades, Proud American, King Kong, and Satan’s Lil Angel. As a first lieutenant, Jim Baird led convoys of up to 200 vehicles and often rode aboard the gun trucks that protected them.

“One of the greatest privileges of my time in Congress has been creating opportunities to honor Vietnam veterans,” said Congressman Baird. “Those I served alongside and all who sacrificed for the cause of freedom in that war deserve the recognition too many were denied when they returned home. As we celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, seeing Brutus travel through our nation’s capital will honor their courage and remind Americans of the immense service and sacrifice of Vietnam veterans.”

The original Brutus served with the 359th Transportation Company, defending supply convoys against enemy ambushes. To protect trucks carrying supplies from coastal ports to inland bases, soldiers transformed ordinary Army cargo trucks into “gun trucks,” first adding sandbags, then reinforcing the vehicles with steel armor and mounted machine guns. These improvised defenders helped protect fellow soldiers and keep vital supplies moving.

The National Veterans Parade is a nonpartisan celebration of every veteran, regardless of branch, generation, background, political affiliation, or religious belief.

The 2026 National Veterans Parade is expected to feature more than 150 participating units, including numerous marching bands, active-duty military ceremonial and performing units, historic military vehicles, floats, pageant titleholders, and special tributes to veterans of the past.

title: Castor, Bilirakis, Soto Introduce Bipartisan Locality Pay Adjustment Act to Establish Pay Localities for the Orlando and Tampa Metropolitan Areas
text:
HILLSBOROUGH COUNTY, Fla.—Reps. Kathy Castor (FL-14), Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) and Darren Soto (D-FL-09) introduced H.R.10898, the Locality Pay Adjustment Act—bipartisan legislation to direct the President’s Pay Agent to establish pay localities for the Orlando and Tampa metropolitan areas.

“The cost of living in the Tampa Bay area has escalated rapidly and is pricing out the civilian federal workforce. From our air traffic controllers and TSA agents at Tampa International Airport to our Social Security Administration employees and the more than 8,000 civilians working in critical missions at MacDill Air Force Base, these individuals make an incredible commitment to service every day,” said Rep. Castor. “Tampa’s current lack of a unique locality pay designation—which determines compensation—fails to acknowledge the high cost of living and is harming the ability to hire and retain talent in the public and private sectors. Congress can help fix this, so I am introducing bipartisan legislation with Reps. Soto and Bilirakis to stand up for our hardworking neighbors and proper compensation.”

“Our civilian federal employees serve our Veterans, support our military, and help protect our nation. Yet an outdated pay designation hurts recruitment and retention at MacDill—including SOCOM and CENTCOM—with real consequences for national security. This legislation will ensure relevant factors, including cost of living, traffic, and commute times, are updated to reflect the true cost of living in our region. We must give our federal agencies the tools to attract and retain the skilled workforce our country depends on,” said Rep. Bilirakis.

“In Florida’s Ninth Congressional District, so many of our constituents form part of the civilian federal workforce—whether it be by working at the Space Coast, Orlando International Airport, the Lake Nona and Kissimmee VAs, and so many other critical places that help keep Central Florida moving forward,” said Rep. Soto. “I am proud to introduce this bipartisan bill with Reps. Bilirakis and Castor to support our federal employees as the cost of living continues to increase in the region.”

“The Tampa Bay Chamber strongly supports legislation to establish federal locality pay for the Tampa metropolitan area, ensuring compensation better reflects our region’s competitive labor market. From MacDill Air Force Base to our veterans’ healthcare facilities and other federal agencies, these employees play a vital role in our economy, national security, and quality of life,” said Bob Rohrlack, President & CEO of the Tampa Bay Chamber. "Establishing locality pay is an important step toward strengthening workforce competitiveness, attracting and retaining skilled talent, and supporting the long-term success of our region’s federal institutions.”

“AFGE appreciates the bipartisan bill from Representatives Soto, Castor, and Bilirakis to improve pay for federal employees in Orlando and Tampa. Federal employees all across the country are substantially underpaid relative to their counterparts in the private sector and state and local government,” said Tatishka Thomas, National Vice President of AFGE District 5.

Currently, federal employees in the Tampa Bay and Orlando areas receive “Rest of U.S.” pay, while federal employees in South Florida and the Melbourne/Space Coast areas receive supplemental locality pay, meant to align public sector pay with private sector pay in their respective regions. In the Tampa Bay and Orlando areas, people serving in federal government positions across the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, U.S. Social Security Administration offices, airports, and at MacDill Air Force Base and other military installations do not receive locality pay, even as both the cost of living and private sector pay continue to increase.

title: García, Jackson, Casar Lead Colleagues in Letter to Secretary Rubio Urging Suspension of Military Assistance to Ecuador as President Noboa Escalates Repression
text:
CHICAGO — Representatives Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), and Greg Casar (TX-35), joined by 10 colleagues, sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressing profound concerns regarding surging authoritarianism in Ecuador, a country with which the Trump Administration has deepened military ties despite the rapid erosion of democracy and human rights there. The recent arrest of former presidential candidate Luisa González and crackdown on other opposition officials and parties marks the latest alarming phase in Ecuador’s descent into de facto one-party rule by President Daniel Noboa and his allies.

The letter outlines how under President Daniel Noboa, “Ecuador has seen the repression of opposition actors across the political spectrum, attacks on judicial independence, and restrictions on the freedom of the press.” The members urge Secretary Rubio to “immediately suspend all U.S. security assistance and military cooperation with the Noboa administration until democracy and the rule of law are fully restored, and the persecution of González and other opposition figures and parties cease.”

Other concerns expressed by the Members about the Noboa government include its undermining of the judiciary, a prolonged “state of emergency” under which Noboa has claimed extraordinary powers, restricted civil liberties and abused human rights, and committed other abuses including torture, extrajudicial killings, forced disappearances, arbitrary arrests, and sexual abuse in women’s prisons.

The Members warn Rubio that if the Trump Administration fails to take action to deter the Noboa government’s authoritarian actions, Congress will use the tools at its disposal to compel a change of policy in the United States. The Members conclude, “The United States cannot credibly claim to support democracy and the fight against drug-trafficking and organized crime while at the same time expanding its security relationship with a government that is rapidly tightening its authoritarian grip on power.”

In addition to Representatives García, Jackson, and Casar, the letter was signed by: Representatives Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Summer Lee (PA-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-00), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), and Nydia Velázquez (NY-07).

title: Resources and Updates for Arizonans Impacted by Severe Flooding
text:
Last weekend, historic rainfall caused severe flooding across Arizona. Lives were lost, homes and infrastructure were damaged, and many Arizonans were forced to evacuate. Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) is in frequent contact with federal, state, Tribal, and local officials regarding ongoing recovery efforts and assistance.

Constituents impacted by this disaster are encouraged to visit the Arizona Emergency Information Network’s November 2026 Storms page for official updates and safety guidance. Please see below for county-specific resources:

Apache: Apache County Emergency Management

Coconino: Coconino County Flood Recovery

Gila: Gila County Community Resource Center

Navajo: Northeastern Arizona Public Information System

Yavapai: Yavapai County November Flooding

Since the storms, Rep. Crane and his staff have been on the ground to survey damage and receive the latest information. From Prescott to Kayenta, his team has met with law enforcement, first responders, and community leaders. Rep. Crane is also communicating with Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Administrator Cameron Hamilton, Tribal leadership, and the office of Governor Katie Hobbs.

Federal engagement has already begun with FEMA, the Federal Highway Administration, and land management agencies such as the U.S. Forest Service. Much of FEMA’s disaster assistance requires a major disaster declaration under the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act. Only a Governor or a Tribal Chief Executive can request this declaration, and the President decides whether to grant it. Members of Congress cannot initiate this process. At this stage, damage assessments remain underway, and no request has been submitted. Rep. Crane is coordinating with partners and will use the tools at his disposal to advocate for future requests.

In the meantime, constituents are welcome to reach out to Rep. Crane’s team with questions about the process, where to find current assistance, or anything else related to the flooding. The Prescott District Office can be reached at (928) 286-5338 and the D.C. Office at (202) 225-3361. While staff cannot override an agency’s decision or guarantee a specific outcome, they are available to point residents in the right direction and provide timely updates.

title: Van Hollen, Elfreth Lead Colleagues in Fight to Expand Veterans’ Care at Walter Reed
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) and Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (D-MD-03), a member of the House Armed Services Committee, led their colleagues in urging the Department of Defense and Department of Veterans Affairs to select Walter Reed National Military Medical Center in Bethesda, Maryland, to expand access to care for veterans as part of the implementation of Elfreth’s “Improvement of Availability of Care for Veterans from Facilities and Providers of the Department of Defense” provision of last year’s National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). The Senator and Congresswoman were joined by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD) and John Fetterman (D-PA) and Representatives Steny Hoyer (D-MD-05), Andy Harris (R-MD-01), Jamie Raskin (D-MD-08), Kweisi Mfume (D-MD-07), Glenn Ivey (D-MD-04), Johnny Olszewski (D-MD-02), and April McClain Delaney (D-MD-06) in their advocacy for Walter Reed.

Elfreth worked with Congressman Derek Schmidt (R-KS-02) on this provision to expand access to care for veterans nationwide and is now urging the selection of Walter Reed as a demonstration location to serve veterans in the National Capital Region and Pennsylvania area. The law specifically allows military and VA medical facilities to strengthen resource sharing, increase the utilization of military medical facilities with available capacity, and increase the volume of complex cases available for professional medical education.

“Walter Reed is well positioned to advance these objectives. As the Nation’s flagship joint military medical center, it brings together highly specialized clinical services, medical education, research, rehabilitation, and operational medicine. Its location in the National Capital Region will allow the hospital to serve a large population center of veterans across Maryland, Virginia, West Virginia, Pennsylvania, and the District of Columbia, providing the best site to launch this program and study its success. Walter Reed maintains strong partnerships with leading health and research institutions, including Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, University of Maryland Medical Center, the National Institutes of Health, the VA Maryland Health Care System, the Washington, D.C. VA Medical Center, and the Uniformed Services University of the Health Sciences,” wrote the Maryland delegation members. “Together, its clinical capabilities, regional reach, and institutional partnerships make Walter Reed a strong location to demonstrate how closer coordination between the Departments can improve veterans’ access to care while strengthening military medical readiness, clinical expertise, and professional education.”

“We therefore respectfully request that the Health Executive Committee: Provide the criteria being used to identify participating facilities and the anticipated implementation timeline; Conduct a joint assessment of Walter Reed’s available capacity, clinical capabilities, and suitability for inclusion in an action plan under the FY2026 NDAA provision; Engage Walter Reed leadership and the directors of relevant VA medical centers in developing a facility-level implementation plan; Select Walter Reed as a demonstration location whose practices and lessons could inform future health care sharing agreements nationwide,” the members continued.

Elfreth learned about the ability to expand veterans' access to care on her visit to Walter Reed, which was one stop on her statewide defense tour during her first year on the Armed Services Committee.

The Department of Defense and the Department of Veterans Affairs’ Health Executive Committee are anticipated to make a final decision in the following months and provide a report to Congress a month later on their selection and implementation plan.

title: Finstad Urges Trump Administration to Approve Disaster Declaration in Southeastern Minnesota
text:
ROCHESTER, MN – Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01) joined U.S. Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Tina Smith (D-MN) in urging President Donald Trump and his administration to approve the state of Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance covering Fillmore, Houston, Steele, and Waseca Counties. The letter also calls for President Trump’s support of the Individuals and Households Program, Disaster Unemployment Assistance, and Hazard Mitigation assistance to invest in disaster resiliency efforts.

In September 2026, southeastern Minnesota experienced severe storms and flooding, leading to more than three-quarters of homes, as well as the New Richland Care Center, a skilled nursing care facility, being damaged. Joint federal and state emergency management teams conducted preliminary damage assessments and determined the losses have met the threshold for federal assistance under the Stafford Act through a Major Disaster Declaration.

The letter reads:

Dear Mr. President:

We write to you in strong support of the state of Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance under the Stafford Act to assist our constituents recovering from severe storms and flooding. These natural disasters have caused significant damage, and we ask that you quickly grant approval for federal disaster assistance.

In September 2026, south and southeastern Minnesota experienced severe weather events that caused flooding in the region. A line of thunderstorms formed late September 18 and repeatedly passed over the same communities into early September 19. Approximately 700 square miles across this region received six inches or more of precipitation within 24 hours, according to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources. In the City of New Richland alone, more than three-quarters of homes are damaged and residents of a skilled nursing facility were evacuated and unable to return to the facility. Many homes across the impacted area suffered flooded basements and damaged furnaces and boilers which will need repair or replacement ahead of the Minnesota winter. This storm event has been assessed as at least as destructive as the July 2026 mega-rain that many of these communities experienced and were recovering from just months prior.

Joint federal and state emergency management teams have conducted preliminary damage assessments and have determined that the losses meet the threshold for federal assistance under the Stafford Act through a Major Disaster Declaration. Governor Walz has submitted an official request for disaster assistance for the period of September 18 to September 20, 2026. The request, dated November 2, 2026, covers Fillmore, Houston, Steele, and Waseca Counties.

Time and time again, Minnesotans have stepped up to support their neighbors after natural disasters. When flood waters rise and homes are damaged, volunteers and neighbors are quick to fill sandbags, clean up debris, and lend a hand to those in need. Impacted communities will repair the damage and rebuild following these disasters, but rapid federal assistance will speed up this recovery effort.

We strongly support Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance, including for the Individuals and Households program and Disaster Unemployment Assistance, as well as Hazard Mitigation assistance to invest in disaster resiliency efforts. We ask that you grant its approval without delay.

Sincerely,

Amy Klobuchar, United States Senator

Tina Smith, United States Senator

Brad Finstad, Member of Congress

title: Huffman on Trump Arch Approval: “We’re a Nation of Laws, Not Kings or Kangaroo Commissions”
text:

title: WBUR: $156 million for Mass. solar projects in limbo after courts say EPA illegally withheld funds
text:
Billions of dollars for solar energy projects nationwide remain in limbo more than a month after two federal judges ruled in separate cases that the Environmental Protection Agency illegally canceled the “Solar for All” program.

Massachusetts won $156 million under the competitive Biden-era initiative intended to expand access to solar energy in low-income communities. The EPA shuttered the program in August 2025 and rescinded all grants. Despite the recent court rulings, the fate of that money remains uncertain.

The EPA has until mid-November to appeal the court rulings. A spokesperson for the agency said in an email that “EPA is reviewing the decision and considering options for appeal.”

“This is a program that has the potential to lower people’s energy bills, get inexpensive clean electricity on the grid, and help the communities that the Solar For All program was designed to help,” said James Crowley, a senior attorney at the Conservation Law Foundation, which is representing plaintiffs in one of the court cases.

“We hope that EPA is considering all that — along with Congress’s intent — and they might choose not to appeal,” Crowley said.

Congress funded the $7 billion Solar For All program through the 2022 Inflation Reduction Act. Two years later, Massachusetts won $156 million. The Healey administration said the program could reduce energy costs by 20% for 31,000 low-income and disadvantaged homes, support 2,800 clean energy jobs and dramatically decrease greenhouse gas emissions.

Soon after President Trump’s second term began, his administration froze the Solar for All funds. In July 2025, Congress passed the “One Big Beautiful Bill,” a massive tax and spending law that terminated the program. The bill stipulated that grants already obligated under Solar for All were not affected, but EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin argued that the bill repealed EPA’s authority to administer the program and rescinded the funds.

The EPA then officially canceled the program, calling it a “boondoggle.”

In a statement, Zeldin said the EPA would be “an exceptional steward of taxpayer dollars,” not “a frivolous spender in the name of ‘climate equity.’ ”

A variety of groups that won Solar for All grants sued the EPA, including nonprofits, solar companies and states.

Massachusetts Attorney General Andrea Campbell, a plaintiff in one of the lawsuits, said in a statement that “the Trump Administration’s attempt to illegally gut this program will eliminate good-paying jobs, neglect the dangers of climate change, and raise costs for low-income residents.”

In September, a federal judge in Rhode Island ruled the Trump EPA exceeded its authority when it shut down the program. A few days later, a federal judge in the Washington D.C. ruled in a separate case that the EPA’s termination of the initiative was illegal, arbitrary and capricious.

The EPA has 60 days to appeal the ruling. For now, the Massachusetts Solar for All program remains “on pause,” according to a state spokesperson, as “Massachusetts continues to monitor the status” of the funding.

It’s unclear if the Democrats’ gains in Congress in the midterm elections will affect the EPA’s decision on whether to appeal, or the status of the canceled grants.

Phil Thompson, a professor of urban planning and politics at MIT, said it was possible the incoming Congress could pass legislation to release the funds. With both legislation and the court rulings, he said, “chances are pretty good that the money could be released.”

Even so, he said the delays represent a missed opportunity to address both climate change and rising energy costs.

“People’s utility bills have been going up and up,” he said. “Had we built more alternative sources of energy — whether it’s solar or geothermal or other — it would have stabilized those prices.”

Gretchen Goldman, president and CEO of the Union of Concerned Scientists, said the incoming congressional Democrats will offer climate advocates an opportunity “to make sure that the funds that Congress has obligated get out the door and are used.”

“We’ve seen that be a challenge in the last two years,” she said.

Rep. Katherine Clark, a Massachusetts Democrat, told WBUR after the election that one of her party’s priorities will be to “restore the cuts” made under the One Big Beautiful Bill.

Clark, who is positioned to become House majority leader when the Democrats take control of Congress in January, did not address Solar for All directly, but said bringing down basic living costs would be a priority.

“We’re going to do quick things, small things, and also start to work on big transformative policies,” she said, “but all focused on making sure that we are fighting for those families who feel like they are drowning in this cost of living crisis.”

—

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces the PURGE Act to Target Microplastics in America’s Waters
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C., (Nov. 6, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace (R-SC) introduced the Plastics Understanding and Removal through Government Evaluation (PURGE) Act, legislation directing the Environmental Protection Agency to study and test strategies to remove microplastics from the environment and our water supply and prevent plastics from breaking down into persistent microplastic and nanoplastic particles.

Microplastics are present everywhere in the environment, including our rivers, oceans, and seafood. The PURGE Act demands answers. What works. What it costs. And whether it can be put to use at water treatment and environmental facilities.

The bill focuses on two approaches: removing microplastics already in our environment through filtration and capture, and engineering plastics to break down naturally instead of fragmenting into persistent microplastic and nanoplastic particles.

“Microplastics are in our water and on our dinner plates, and we have yet to know what actually works to stop them,” said Congresswoman Mace. “The PURGE Act puts the EPA to work finding real solutions, tested in the real world and measured by hard science. No more guessing. No gimmicks. Our families deserve a microplastic-free future, and we intend to deliver it.”

The PURGE Act:

Directs the EPA to study anti-microplastic strategies, including their effectiveness, cost, toxic byproducts, and impact on recycling, and report to Congress within 180 days.

Establishes a five-year pilot program testing these strategies in at least three different sites across diverse geographic regions, including riverine, coastal, and municipal wastewater settings to the extent practicable.

Requires the EPA to set measurable success standards before any testing begins.

Prioritizes solutions capable of working with existing water treatment and stormwater infrastructure, without substantial new construction.

Requires biodegradation to be verified through molecular-level testing, not visual inspection or mass-loss measurements alone.

Requires coordination with NOAA, the U.S. Geological Survey, and state environmental agencies.

Requires a final report to Congress on pilot results within one year of the program's conclusion.

title: Wall Street Journal Editorial Board: Mike Johnson’s Good House Service
text:
WASHINGTON — Read today’s editorial from the Wall Street Journal highlighting Speaker Johnson’s record: “Mike Johnson’s Good House Service.”

“The country owes a debt to the Congressman from Louisiana for taking on a nearly impossible job, and the country is the better for his influence,” the Editorial Board wrote.

Read the full WSJ Editorial here or below:

Mike Johnson’s Good House Service

The Editorial Board

Wall Street Journal

November 6, 2026

House Speaker Mike Johnson says he won’t run for Minority Leader after the Republican defeat this week, and Washington would be better if more politicians stepped aside with honor. But the country owes a debt to the Congressman from Louisiana for taking on a nearly impossible job, and the country is the better for his influence.

Mr. Johnson was hardly a household name in 2023 when a faction of House Republicans deposed Speaker Kevin McCarthy with no obvious replacement. The GOP descended into a circular firing squad that lasted weeks. The reserve currency in the panic turned out to be a constitutional lawyer with an aspirational politics and a Ronald Reagan worldview.

Mr. Johnson had to navigate an historically small majority and a President who never tried to persuade the public. He deserves particular credit for renewing the 2017 tax cuts, when failure was possible given divisions over state tax deductions and more. The One Big Beautiful Bill made progress on Medicaid sanity, higher education reform, work requirements and more. Mr. Johnson also helped move through the bipartisan bill on TikTok ownership that perhaps someday a President will follow.

He also deserves credit for his leadership moving military support for Ukraine, Taiwan and Israel, even over heckling from his own party. His speech at the Hudson Institute in the summer of 2024 should be required reading for Republicans trying to pick up the pieces after Mr. Trump.

“Today, we are threatened again by Chinese Communists, by Russian oligarchs, and Islamic terrorists,” he said. “We can choose to ignore them, we can try to appease them. We can listen to the naysayers who say our values aren’t worth defending and that there can be no victory. Or we can choose another course… We can rearm, rebuild, reinvigorate, restore, and reinstate fear in our enemies.”

The GOP Congress wasn’t as productive as we’d hoped, but Mr. Johnson wasn’t the problem. He had to navigate between a President with mercurial and often unrealistic demands and a backbench with too many podcasters and social-media trolls.

The Speaker is taking hits for predicting that Republicans would keep the House, but electoral optimism is a requirement of the job. The defeat wasn’t his fault. He raised record funds for candidates. The Speaker from Louisiana understood, as he likes to say quoting John Quincy Adams, that “duty is ours; results are God’s.”

title: Congressman Griffith’s Weekly E-Newsletter 11.6.26
text:
Veterans Day is an American tradition to honor those who have served in the armed forces of the United States. Their service is rooted in love of country and community.

These values not only shape the brave Americans who enlist in military service, but they also help guide our servicemembers who later become political leaders.

Throughout American history, some who take the oath to enlist in our military later take the presidential oath of office.

America’s first president under the Constitution, General George Washington, led the Continental Army in the fight against the British throne.

Responding to Supreme Court Chief Justice John Marshall’s biography of Washington, Gouverneur Morris, a contemporary of both, wrote to Marshall: “…few men of such steady, persevering industry ever existed, and perhaps no one who so completely commanded himself.”

Another military leader to fight Great Britain before pursuing the presidency was our 7th president and the first from the Democratic Party, Andrew Jackson.

In addition to receiving heavy praise for his role in the Battle of New Orleans, Jackson’s campaign to squash the Seminole created negotiating room for the U.S. to acquire Florida.

While Jackson’s military focus during the War of 1812 was in the South, American forces also had to respond to British attacks in the North.

William Henry Harrison, later America’s 10th president, commanded an army following the British capture of Detroit. Harrison pushed back British and Indian forces in a campaign that led to the recapture of Detroit and even the invasion of Ontario, Canada.

Harrison’s lead in Canada at the Battle of the Thames was considered one of the greatest American victories along with Jackson’s at New Orleans.

Unfortunately, Harrison served as president for just 31 days before his death, becoming the first president to die in office and remaining the shortest-serving president to this day.

The next president to die in office was another Virginia-born military leader, Zachary Taylor.

Taylor’s exceptional command during the Mexican-American War earned him major general honors, three Congressional Gold Medals (the only person in U.S. history) and comparisons to Washington and Jackson.

Serving under Taylor in the war effort was Ulysses S. Grant. The conflict helped shape Grant in his preparation to lead the Union Army during the Civil War.

Grant would later become our country’s first president elected following the Civil War, and the first since Jackson to complete two consecutive terms.

Among others to go from fighting in the Civil War to later living in the White House included the likes of Benjamin Harrison, James Garfield and William McKinley.

As the 25th president, McKinley helped exert American power in the Western Hemisphere, most notably during the Spanish-American War.

American forces showed incredible strength, with leaders like Teddy Roosevelt and his Rough Riders valiantly fighting in Cuba against Spanish armed forces.

Following Roosevelt’s resounding success in the War, he became a rising star in the Republican Party. Accordingly, McKinley tapped Roosevelt as his new vice president. McKinley’s assassination in 1901 meant the Spanish-American War hero would take the reins of the presidency, and in 1904, would be elected in his own right.

Another Republican war hero to become president is General Dwight D. Eisenhower.

Eisenhower, among other campaigns, oversaw the Allied operation in World War II, Operation Overlord, which is one of the most consequential military feats in U.S. military history. The Allied landings at Normandy, the largest seaborne invasion in history, represented the first major breach of Hitler’s “Fortress Europe” and paved the way for America and our Allies to defeat Nazi forces.

Across the world in the Pacific Theater, American forces faced a different threat.

Naval warfare against Japan required courageous aviators to bomb Japanese-held islands. One naval aviator, 19-year-old George Herbert Walker Bush, took on a variety of combat missions.

During one attack, Bush was shot down by enemy fire. He parachuted into the ocean, spending four hours on a life raft before being rescued.

Bush’s military service preceded his rise in public service, where he would become America’s 41st president.

These are just some of the many presidents to have a military service background.

America’s military leaders not only fight on the battlefield, but also on American soil to protect our rights, our way of life and our country.

Obviously, not all veterans can become president. But whether they become president or return to contribute to their communities, every American owes them a debt of gratitude. So, please join me in thanking our veterans for all they do and have done for our country. Happy Veterans Day!

If you have questions, concerns, or comments, feel free to contact my office. You can call my Abingdon office at 276-525-1405 or my Christiansburg office at 540-381-5671. To reach my office via email, please visit my website at https://morgangriffith.house.gov/.

title: Griffith Celebrates Opportunity Zone Designations in Virginia’s Ninth District
text:
The U.S. Department of Treasury approved Virginia’s nomination of 153 new Opportunity Zones (OZs) as proposed by Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger. A map of the new OZs in Virginia, which are set to take effect in January 2027, is available here.

The OZ program is meant to incentivize private investment capital in economically distressed communities. This federal initiative, which was permanently extended through the 2025 reconciliation bill, H.R. 1 - the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, now includes boosted tax incentives for OZs in rural communities. Capital gains placed into rural investments are subject to a discount three times that of non-rural investments. In addition, the investment threshold for improving a facility is reduced. U.S. Congressman Morgan Griffith (R-VA) voiced his support for boosted OZ tax incentives for rural communities as he voted in favor of the Working Families Tax Cuts Act.

In response to this announcement, Congressman Griffith released the following statement:

“As an original supporter of Opportunity Zones, this policy helps attract investments, generate economic growth and create jobs in communities that need it. In 2025, I supported the expansion of this program to allow more rural communities to potentially access private investment.

“Today’s announcement confirms that Virginia’s Ninth District will have more rural Opportunity Zones than any other Congressional District in Virginia.

“I am glad to have secured this outcome for our rural communities by voting for the Working Families Tax Cuts. I will continue to support policies that strengthen economic opportunity in rural America.”

BACKGROUND

According to the Economic Innovation Group, $1.9 billion in OZ investments supported Virginia communities through the end of 2024.

title: SALAZAR, BERA, GIMENEZ INTRODUCE BIPARTISAN BILL TO PROTECT TROPICAL FORESTS AND CORAL REEFS
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representatives María Elvira Salazar (R-FL-27), Ami Bera (D-CA-06), and Carlos Gimenez (R-FL-28) introduced the bipartisan Tropical Forest and Coral Reef Conservation Reauthorization Act of 2026 (H.R. 10505), legislation to continue a longstanding U.S. conservation program that helps protect tropical forests and coral reef ecosystems around the world.

U.S. Senators Chris Coons (D-DE) and John Curtis (R-UT), introduced companion legislation in the Senate.

The legislation would reauthorize the Tropical Forest and Coral Reef Conservation Act of 1998, which allows eligible developing countries to restructure certain debt owed to the United States while directing funds toward the protection and restoration of tropical forests and coral reefs.

Current law authorizes $20 million annually for the program through Fiscal Year 2027. H.R. 10505 would extend that authorization at $20 million per year from Fiscal Year 2028 through Fiscal Year 2032.

"In South Florida and across the globe, ecosystem protection and restoration are central not only to the well-being of wildlife but also play a critical role in boosting local economies," said Rep. Salazar. "By reauthorizing this proven program, we will continue to preserve native wildlife and ecosystems, help grow economies, and strengthen our alliances. I am proud to help lead this bipartisan effort and reinforce America’s leadership in conservation around the world.”

“Protecting tropical forests and coral reefs is essential to preserving biodiversity and protecting our environment for future generations,” said Representative Ami Bera, M.D. “Reauthorizing this funding will ensure we continue to protect and restore critical tropical forest and coral reef ecosystems whose health has far-reaching consequences for communities and economies around the world. I’m proud to join Representative Salazar in supporting this bipartisan effort to continue this vital conservation work.”

"Over the years the Tropical Forest and Coral Reef Conservation Act has helped conserve areas rich with biodiversity," said Catherine Barrett, Legislative Director for The Nature Conservancy. "The law additionally paved the way for innovative conservation funding, leveraging public funding with private and philanthropic investments to benefit nature and people. The Nature Conservancy is grateful to Congresswoman Salazar and Congressman Bera for their bipartisan leadership in introducing this important reauthorization effort."

"Congresswoman Salazar and Congressman Bera are applauded for their leadership in introducing legislation in the House of Representatives to renew the Tropical Forest and Coral Reef Conservation Reauthorization Act," said Kelly Keenan Aylward, Executive Director of Federal Affairs & Policy for the Wildlife Conservation Society. "This innovative policy converts eligible debt into long-term financing for on-the-ground conservation of intact forest, coral reefs, and wildlife while strengthening governance in the natural resource sector."

"The introduction of legislation in the U.S. House to reauthorize the Tropical Forest and Coral Reef Conservation Act is an important step toward unlocking innovative financing for the world’s most vulnerable tropical forests and coral reef ecosystems,” said Kerry Cesareo, senior vice president for forests and freshwater at World Wildlife Fund. “By strengthening this proven approach, we can help nations reduce debt burdens while investing in the natural systems that protect communities, support biodiversity and promote our prosperity. We welcome this bipartisan commitment to solutions that deliver lasting environmental and economic benefits.”

“Thanks to the leadership of then-Representative Rob Portman, and to the support of the International Conservation Caucus Co-Chairs in the Senate & House for the past 20 years, the Tropical Forest Conservation Act (now the Tropical Forest & Coral Conservation Act) is responsible for conserving 126,000,000 acres globally,” said David Barron, ICCF Group Chairman. “Debt-for-nature swaps are the best investment America could make in setting aside land for local people and their economies.”

The bill builds on Rep. Salazar’s record of advancing conservation and resilience efforts important to South Florida. Her bipartisan conservation work includes the REEF Act, which encourages retired Navy ships to be repurposed as artificial reefs, and the Migratory Birds of the Americas Conservation Enhancements Act, both signed into law.

Rep. Salazar has also secured federal investments for coral reef restoration, water quality, flood mitigation, and coastal resilience projects across Florida’s 27th Congressional District.

title: Reps. Vargas, Jacobs, Levin, Peters and Senators Padilla and Schiff Call for Answers and Investigation into Death at Otay Mesa
text:
SAN DIEGO – U.S. Representatives Juan Vargas (CA-52), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), Mike Levin (CA-49), and Scott Peters (CA-50) and U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA)and Adam Schiff (D-CA) called on the Trump Administration for answers following the death of an individual in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody at Otay Mesa Detention Center. Together, the Members are demanding a thorough and transparent investigation into whether all policies, procedures, and standards of care were appropriately followed.

“As Members of the San Diego Congressional Delegation, we write to express our grave concern following the latest death of an individual in ICE custody at Otay Mesa Detention Center in San Diego, California, operated by the for-profit prison corporation CoreCivic,” wrote the lawmakers. “Any death in federal custody is a tragic reminder of the serious responsibility entrusted to DHS, ICE, and their contracted detention facilities, to safeguard the lives of those in their care.”

“A thorough investigation is all the more important in light of previously documented concerns regarding delayed access to medical care, subpar detention conditions, and compliance with public health reporting requirements,” the lawmakers continued. “We further request that the Department regularly update Members of Congress as the investigation progresses. Without complete and accurate information, Congress cannot fully assess whether existing policies, procedures, and safeguards are sufficient to protect individuals in federal custody.”

Read the full letter below:

Dear Secretary Mullin and Acting Director Venturella,

As Members of the San Diego Congressional Delegation, we write to express our grave concern following the latest death of an individual in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody at Otay Mesa Detention Center in San Diego, California, operated by the for-profit prison corporation CoreCivic. This death underscores the importance of ensuring the safety and well-being of detainees in federal custody, particularly given the previously documented concerns about medical care and oversight at the facility.

On Saturday, October 24, a 43-year-old Guatemalan man, subsequently identified by San Diego County officials as Guillermo Pascual Verganza, died while in ICE custody at Otay Mesa Detention Center. ICE initially identified the individual as Roberto Jimenez Gutierrez, raising additional questions regarding the accuracy of the information released following his death. According to CoreCivic, facility staff reported a medical emergency at 11:36 a.m. after discovering Mr. Verganza unresponsive in his assigned living area. Although medical personnel reportedly initiated lifesaving measures and requested emergency medical services, he was pronounced dead before he could be transported from the facility. The cause and circumstances of his death remain under investigation and an autopsy was done on Monday, October 26. While we recognize that the facts and details of this case are still emerging, any death in federal custody warrants a thorough review to ensure that appropriate policies, procedures, and standards of care were followed. This includes examining the medical attention and monitoring provided to Mr. Verganza during his detention, as well as the circumstances of his placement in a safety cell and the facility’s response to the emergency.

Any death in federal custody is a tragic reminder of the serious responsibility entrusted to DHS, ICE, and their contracted detention facilities, to safeguard the lives of those in their care. A thorough investigation is all the more important in light of previously documented concerns regarding delayed access to medical care, subpar detention conditions, and compliance with public health reporting requirements. A California 2026 Department of Justice report identified concerns regarding medical recordkeeping, delays in treatment, and coordination of specialty care referrals and follow-up treatment. The report also documented concerns regarding detention conditions, including overcrowding and insufficient access to toilets in certain housing units.

Separately, a June 2026 San Diego County Health and Environmental Inspection Report, released in August, identified deficiencies in the facility's medical practices, particularly failures to appropriately report and coordinate tuberculosis cases with local public health authorities. County officials found that two tuberculosis cases were not reported by facility medical personnel and instead came to the attention of public health officials through an outside laboratory vendor. Individuals with tuberculosis require reporting within 24 hours and coordinated response as per Health and Safety Code Section 121361. The inspection also identified that no vaccines were stocked at the time of inspection and an individual who had gone 18 months without a replacement for a medically required dental or medical device.

While these findings do not establish that any deficiencies contributed to the recent death, they underscore the importance of a thorough and transparent investigation into the circumstances surrounding it. Given the seriousness of a detainee death, we request that the Department share with Members of Congress any relevant findings and information obtained through its investigation by Friday, November 13. We further request that the Department regularly update Members of Congress as the investigation progresses. Without complete and accurate information, Congress cannot fully assess whether existing policies, procedures, and safeguards are sufficient to protect individuals in federal custody.

title: Baldwin Releases Statement After Video Emerges of Railroad CEO Threatening Retaliation for Opponents of Megamerger
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) released a statement calling out Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena for threatening to raise rates on customers – including Wisconsin farmers, manufacturers, and businesses – who oppose the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern megamerger. In a newly released video, Vena told a room of rail shippers, “I’ll probably increase everybody’s rates that said they didn’t want a seamless railroad by three or four extra percent to teach you a lesson.”

Baldwin has warned for months that this merger will raise costs and worsen already poor rail service for American businesses and consumers. Senator Baldwin’s work to scrutinize this merger – in Senate testimony and public letters – led to federal regulators heeding her calls and ordering the video of Union Pacific’s threats of retaliation be made public. She has called on the Surface Transportation Board to reject the merger.

“For years, I’ve heard from Wisconsin businesses, farmers, and manufacturers about how consolidation in Class I rail has led to unreliable service and high costs that are passed onto Wisconsin families. That’s why I’ve called on the Trump Administration to reject this megamerger and protect American consumers, not the billionaire class and corporations who are just looking to stamp out competition and pad their profits,” said Senator Baldwin. “Today, we can see for ourselves that Union Pacific’s CEO is openly talking about retaliating against shippers who are rightfully concerned that more consolidation in Class I rail will lead to worse service and higher costs for businesses, farmers, and families. That’s no laughing matter to my constituents. I’m calling on the Surface Transportation Board to reject a megamerger that will hurt our Made in Wisconsin economy.”

In March 2026, reports emerged that Union Pacific (UP) CEO Jim Vena threatened retaliation at the Southwestern Association of Rail Shippers annual meeting with rate increases against shippers who oppose the merger. Following these reports, Senator Baldwin questioned Surface Transportation Board (STB) nominee Karen Hedlund about whether federal regulators would take these threats seriously. Hedlund stated that any kind of retaliation against shippers would be “utterly unacceptable.” Senator Baldwin followed up her questioning by calling on the STB to take Union Pacific’s threats seriously. Yesterday, the STB forced Union Pacific to make those remarks public.

Since the 1950s, the rail industry has consolidated from over 100 Class I freight railroads to only six today, leaving U.S. manufacturers, utility companies, agricultural producers, and small businesses paying excessive rates despite poor service and reliability. For months, Senator Baldwin has been urging federal regulators to thoroughly scrutinize this merger’s impact on competition, shipping costs, and service reliability for Made in Wisconsin businesses who rely on freight rail:

July 2025: Baldwin and Republican Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas urged the Surface Transportation Board (STB) to closely examine the proposed merger's impact on competition, costs, and reliability.

November 2025: During a Senate Commerce Committee nomination hearing, Baldwin pressed Surface Transportation Board member nominees Richard Kloster and Michelle Schultz on whether they would act independently of President Trump when making regulatory decisions.

December 2025: Senator Baldwin called on the STB to reject the merger application filed by Union Pacific to acquire Norfolk Southern.

June 2026: During a Senate Commerce Committee nomination hearing, Baldwin questioned STB nominee Karen Hedlund on CEO Jim Vena’s past comments. She also asked for clarification if Union Pacific could disregard its burden to prove the merger satisfies the public interest statute.

July 2026: Baldwin urged the Surface Transportation Board to take Union Pacific’s threat of retaliation against shippers who do not support its merger with Norfolk Southern seriously. Her letter came as Union Pacific’s CEO previously visited President Trump in the Oval Office and committed to helping fund the President’s $400 million White House ballroom.
