title: Warnock Leads Broad Coalition of Senators to Push Senate Leadership to Delay Republican Medicaid Cuts Over Concerns About Coverage Loss
text:
Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock and Luján, along with a broad coalition of Democratic Senators, are calling on Senate leadership to delay new Medicaid cuts enacted in Congressional Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act, warning that the work reporting requirements could cause millions of Americans to lose their health care coverage

Nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts championed by Congressional Republicans and signed into law by President Trump will begin taking effect in January 2027

President Trump and Congressional Republicans have made cuts to Americans’ health care coverage a central part of their legislative agenda; a July report found that two million fewer children were enrolled in Medicaid in April, compared to January 2025 when President Trump took office

Three to seven million Americans are estimated to lose their health care coverage from work reporting requirements alone

Senator Reverend Warnock, Luján: “The midterm results reveal a clear message: the American people are hurting, and we must do what we can to alleviate and prevent further harm”

Washington, D.C. – Today, Senate Finance Members U.S. Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) and Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), along with 14 of their colleagues representing a broad swath of the Democratic coalition, are calling on Senate leadership to delay new Medicaid work reporting requirements enacted in Congressional Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act, warning that the work reporting requirements could cause millions of Americans to lose their health care coverage. Nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts championed by Congressional Republicans and signed into law by President Trump will begin taking effect in January 2027 unless Congress moves to blunt their impact.

“The midterm results reveal a clear message: the American people are hurting, and we must do what we can to alleviate and prevent further harm,” said Senators Warnock and Luján. “While we remain committed to a full repeal of all Medicaid cuts, we urge you to include, in the next legislative vehicle, policies that can mitigate the imminent coverage loss from the work reporting requirements set to take effect on January 1, 2027.”

Medicaid is a cornerstone of the U.S. health care system, providing health insurance coverage to more than one in five Americans. The program covers 40% of U.S. births, provides 20% of all hospital funding, and is the single largest payer of long-term services and supports, including nursing home care. President Trump and Congressional Republicans have made cuts to Americans’ health care coverage a central part of their legislative agenda since President Trump returned to office. A July report found that two million fewer children were enrolled in Medicaid in April, compared to January 2025 when President Trump took office.

Senator Warnock is a leading proponent of Medicaid expansion and has long championed efforts to increase Georgians’ access to affordable health care. Last year, he released a report titled “Healthy People, Healthy Economy,” which found investing in Medicaid stimulates economic growth and promotes access to employment. In June, Senator Warnock forced a vote pushing for the release of data surrounding Medicaid coverage loss nationwide. Senator Warnock’s effort to release the data was blocked by Senate Republicans.

Alongside Senators Warnock and Luján, the letter is cosigned by Senators Michael Bennet (D-CO), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Tina Smith (D-MN), and Tammy Baldwin (D-WI).

A copy of the letter can be found HERE and text is below:

“Dear Chairman Crapo, Ranking Member Wyden, Majority Leader Thune, and Minority Leader Schumer,

“As we approach 2027, we ask that Congressional leaders consider policies that will lessen impending harm to families, communities, and states across the country due to the Medicaid cuts from H.R. 1 in the next moving legislative vehicle. The midterm results reveal a clear message: the American people are hurting and we must do what we can to alleviate and prevent further harm. Absent the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) using its statutory authority and enforcement discretion to protect people from losing their health care due to states clearly not being ready to implement bureaucratic red tape, Congress must step in. While we remain committed to a full repeal of all Medicaid cuts, we urge you to include, in the next legislative vehicle, policies that can mitigate the imminent coverage loss from the work reporting requirements set to take effect on January 1, 2027.

“No state that has attempted work reporting requirements in Medicaid has ever meaningfully increased workforce participation. Instead, every state that has done so has either seen or predicted significant coverage loss for people who continue to be eligible for Medicaid but lose coverage because they can’t navigate all the red tape. That is because affordable and reliable access to health care improves workforce participation, not the other way around: healthy people make a healthy economy.

“Even disregarding the decades of empirical evidence demonstrating that work reporting requirements fail to achieve their intended effects, the reality is that states have had neither the time nor resources to set up complex work reporting systems by 2027. Under H.R. 1, states had fewer than 18 months to make complex eligibility and enrollment systems changes, conduct readiness reviews, train staff, and educate enrollees, during a time when many states are already budget-constrained and experiencing staff shortages at the agencies responsible. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) released its Interim Final Rule (IFR) on the work reporting requirements on June 1, 2026, just six months before states must have their programs up and running, and with less than one month for states to meet the required notification timeframes. The IFR also adds restrictions and requirements beyond the law to the medical frailty definition, adding unexpected complexity.

“According to the non-partisan Congressional Budget Office, more than 5 million Americans are estimated to lose their coverage from the work reporting requirements alone. This represents up to one-third of adults in Medicaid expansion states losing their coverage. Most of the individuals at risk of losing coverage would likely continue to qualify for Medicaid: 92 percent of Medicaid enrollees are already working, caregiving, in school, or have an illness. But they will likely lose coverage nonetheless because of the bureaucratic red tape that Americans will be forced to navigate, a complex system made more chaotic by the rushed timeline that states have been forced to meet.

“In light of these concerns, we urge Senate Leadership to consider a two-year delay in the implementation of the work reporting requirements.

“Sincerely”

###

title: Warnock Presses Trump Ag Trade Nominee on Future of Global Food Assistance Programs
text:
On Tuesday, during a Senate Agriculture Committee hearing, Senator Reverend Warnock pressed President Trump’s nominee for Under Secretary for Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs on his commitment to protecting America’s global food assistance programs

U.S. global food assistance programs have long supported Georgia farmers while providing critical food assistance to vulnerable communities around the world

Senator Reverend Warnock: “When President Trump and Elon Musk shut down [food assistance] programs, they didn’t just hurt starving children and waste taxpayer dollars by letting already purchased food rot in warehouses; they also directly hurt American farmers who supported those contracts”

Washington, D.C. – On Tuesday, during a Senate Agriculture Committee hearing, U.S. Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) pressed Greg Ibach, President Trump’s nominee for Under Secretary for Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs at the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), on his commitment to protecting America’s global food assistance programs. Following the Trump administration’s dismantling of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) in 2025, several of the agency’s global food assistance programs were transferred to USDA, raising questions about how the department will continue supporting American farmers while addressing hunger abroad. U.S. global food assistance programs have long provided a critical market for Georgia farmers while delivering food assistance to vulnerable communities around the world.

“When President Trump and Elon Musk shut down [food assistance] programs, they didn’t just hurt starving children and waste taxpayer dollars by letting already purchased food rot in warehouses,” said Senator Reverend Warnock. “They also directly hurt American farmers who supported those contracts. That includes Georgia peanut farmers who grow the key ingredient for ready to use therapeutic foods which deliver salvation and nutrition to children all over the world.”

Prior to its dismantling, USAID administered the Food for Peace program, a cornerstone of America’s efforts to combat hunger and malnutrition around the world. The program purchased American-grown agricultural commodities to provide emergency food assistance to vulnerable communities facing famine, natural disasters, and conflict. In addition to providing lifesaving humanitarian assistance, the program supported American farmers by creating markets for U.S. agricultural products. In February 2026, USDA announced that it would assume responsibility for administering the program.

Senator Warnock has long championed efforts to combat global hunger while supporting Georgia’s agricultural economy. Following the Trump administration’s cancellation of federal food assistance contracts, Senator Warnock pushed to restore critical funding for organizations working to provide lifesaving nutrition to vulnerable children around the world. As part of these efforts, Senator Warnock worked directly with Secretary of State Marco Rubio to secure the release of millions of dollars in outstanding federal payments owed to MANA Nutrition, helping sustain its operations and support Georgia peanut farmers.

Watch the Senator’s full exchange HERE

See a transcript of the exchange between Senator Warnock and TFAA nominee Ibach below:

Senator Reverend Warnock (SRW): “Thank you, Chair Boozman.”

“Last year, the Trump administration—with the help of Elon Musk—illegally dismantled the USAID, a critical pillar of our national security. USAID administered programs like Food for Peace, which provides food from American farmers to vulnerable people all around the world. It’s part of our diplomatic toolbox. When Trump and Elon Musk shut down this program, they didn’t just hurt starving children and waste taxpayer dollars by letting already purchased food rot in warehouses. They also directly hurt American farmers who supported those contracts. That includes Georgia peanut farmers who grow the key ingredient for ready-to-use therapeutic foods, those RUTF packets, which deliver salvation and nutrition to children all over the world.”

“Mr. Ibach, USDA is now administering Food for Peace, and if confirmed, you would oversee it along with other international food assistance programs. Yes or no? Are you aware—are you aware that the Food for Peace program purchases food from American farmers, including peanut growers, right down in my home state of Georgia?”

TFAA Nominee Greg Ibach (GI): “Yes, sir. I am aware of the fact that we do purchase food from farmers and distribute it around the world. I actually had the opportunity one time traveling with USDA when I was director of agriculture to be in Ghana and witness those packets that you talked about that contained peanut butter being distributed to children in schools there, and the nutrition that it provided was very impressive, and it was very, you know, provided sustainability.”

SRW: “It’s lifesaving. It’s lifesaving.”

“And I’m very proud as a voice for Georgia that the key ingredient comes from Georgia farmers. Do you agree then that these programs can help American farmers who are already suffering from Trump’s tariffs and trade wars?”

GI: “Absolutely. By getting our customers around the world that need food assistance used to the high quality, nutritional content, and the safety of our commodities, hopefully, when they get on their feet and their economies improve, they will become customers of U.S. farmers and ranchers.”

SRW: “Sure. So helpful to families and people who are struggling around the world. Helpful to farmers.”

“The White House has proposed eliminating the Food for Peace program in their 2027 budget request, calling it wasteful. Yes or no? Do you believe that the Food for Peace program should be funded?”

GI: “It would be my obligation to follow the law, whatever the law—”

SRW: “Do you think it should be funded? I’m just asking your opinion. Do you—yes or no? Do you think it should be funded?”

GI: “Food and feeding programs are important part of our humanitarian responsibility as U.S. citizens.”

SRW: “So, that’s a yes?”

GI: “Food and feeding programs are important.”

SRW: “So, the USDA is newly administering food for peace, and it lacks the staff or the expertise of USAID, which has led to significant delays in securing contracts and delivering food. If confirmed, what is your plan to ensure the USDA has the capacity to efficiently and accurately administer food for peace?”

GI: “So, Food for Peace being a new program to USDA, and while I’m familiar with the purchases that we made when I was part of MRP that AMS made, I would look forward to seeking out the expertise to understand the specifics of Food for Peace. I think it’s important that we make sure that we have staffing to not only staff effectively the feeding programs, international feeding programs, but also our trade activities around the world. And so, I would work with the Secretary and the administration to make them aware of any needs we’d have to be effective in our mission.”

SRW: “And did I hear you also say that you would seek out expertise?”

GI: “Seek out expertise, correct.”

SRW: “Does that mean you will also commit to consulting the State Department for technical assistance?”

GI: “Yes, and you know we have two people within the TFAA leadership that come from the State Department, and so hopefully I look forward to using them as advisors as well as seeking out advisors at the State Department or here on Capitol Hill.”

SRW: “Thank you.”

“On numerous occasions, this administration has tried to withhold foreign aid, including life-saving programs like PEPFAR, arguably one of the greatest humanitarian relief programs ever created. And the Trump administration has threatened to withhold that aid, aid like PEPFAR, other aid, unless countries agree to unrelated demands like health data or access to critical minerals. If confirmed, will you commit to deploying food based on need, not to coerce countries into agreeing to other demands?”

GI: “I will follow the law.”

SRW: “When the Trump administration refers to America first, they mean America only. But the American people showed on Tuesday that they do not support that agenda. Food for Peace is a great example. It seems to me of how we do not have to make that false choice. We can support American farmers. We can feed vulnerable families all around the world at the same time. I think that those are related objectives, and there’s nothing stopping the administration from deploying food based on need. You said you would follow the law. I’m glad to hear that. But let me just state for the record: there’s nothing in the law that’s stopping them from deploying food. This is a choice, in my view, an immoral choice that the administration is making. I’m heartened to know that you will seek the expertise of folks who are focused on this, and I hope we can get to better policy somehow in the days ahead.”

“Thank you so very much.”

title: Welch, Crapo, Ruiz, Bilirakis, Tenney Lead Bipartisan, Bicameral Bill to Better Protect Servicemembers from Burn Pits, Improve Care for Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Ahead of Veterans Day, U.S. Senators Peter Welch (D-Vt.) and Mike Crapo (R-Idaho), along with U.S. Representatives Raul Ruiz (D-CA-35), Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12), and Claudia Tenney (R-NY-24), introduced the Waste Incineration Protection, Exposure Oversight, and Updated Tracking of (WIPE OUT) Burn Pits Act. This bipartisan, bicameral legislation would build on the Sergeant First Class Heath Robinson Honoring our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics (PACT) Act by ensuring all instances of toxic exposure from burn pits are accounted for. The legislation would also establish a clear framework for identifying, tracking, and mitigating risks of open‑air burn pits located near U.S. forces and push for replacement with safer alternatives.

The PACT Act, which Senator Welch championed as a member of the House of Representatives, was signed into law by President Biden in 2022, To date, more than 7 million veterans have been screened for toxic exposures because of the PACT Act.

“When we passed the PACT Act four years ago, we took a major step toward ensuring that the cost of war always includes the cost of caring for the warrior. But there’s always more we can do to improve servicemember safety, including finding better ways to track and mitigate the risks of burn pits,” said Senator Welch. “I’m proud to partner with Senator Crapo on this bill which builds on our bipartisan work to expand benefits and open doors to care for veterans exposed to toxic chemicals.”

“While the Pentagon has largely phased out the use of burn pits, many foreign partners and entities continue to operate them near installations where U.S. personnel live and work,” said Senator Crapo. “We must take proactive steps to reduce the risk of toxic exposure by providing safer waste disposal alternatives, working with foreign partners to eliminate hazardous burn pits and ensuring servicemembers’ health records accurately document potential exposure so veterans can access appropriate benefits and care in the future.”

“I’m proud to lead the bipartisan, bicameral WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act to protect servicemembers from the harmful effects of toxic burn pits.” said Rep. Dr. Raul Ruiz. “This bill requires the Department of Defense (DoD) to find, record, and test the air at every burn pit site used by other countries or contractors that are endangering the lives of our troops. The PACT Act gave presumptive benefits and health care to veterans harmed by burn pit exposure. The WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act aims to end the use of toxic burn pits once and for all.”

“Our servicemembers put their lives on the line to defend our nation, and they should never have to face lifelong health consequences because of the toxic exposure they endured while serving. The WIPE Out Burn Pits Act is an important step toward protecting our military personnel, addressing the dangers of burn pit exposure, and ensuring those who serve our country have the support and protections they deserve. We have a responsibility to safeguard the health of our heroes, and I will continue fighting to make that a priority,” said Rep. Bilirakis.

“Our servicemembers should not have to worry that the air they breathe while defending our country could jeopardize their health for years to come,” said Rep. Tenney. “We have seen the devastating consequences of toxic exposure on our veterans and their families, and we must do everything possible to prevent future generations from facing the same challenges. The bipartisan WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act will help identify dangerous exposure risks, improve accountability, and ensure our troops have accurate health records if they need care in the future. Protecting those who serve our nation must remain a top priority, both during their service and long after they return home.”

For decades, the Department of Defense (DoD) relied on open-air burn pits to dispose of waste during overseas contingency operations, exposing U.S. servicemembers to toxins linked to long-term health conditions, including respiratory disease, cancer, and heart issues. The PACT Act took historic steps to expand care and benefits for veterans suffering from toxic exposure.

The WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act builds on that progress by ensuring all instances of toxic exposure from burn pits are recorded in a servicemember’s health records. While DoD has reduced its own use of burn pits, servicemembers are still exposed to active burn pits not controlled by DoD, and safer alternatives exist for instances when DoD does operate burn pits. Specifically, the WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act:

Establishes a clear framework for identifying, tracking, and mitigating the risks of non‑DoD open‑air burn pits located near U.S. forces, and ensure that exposure to toxic substances is incorporated into servicemembers’ health records;

Directs the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to Congress detailing the location and use of all nearby burn pits, including those operated by allies, partners, or local entities;

Requires the deployment of alternative solid waste disposal systems in locations where the DoD operates burn pits; and

Mandates diplomatic engagement, jointly by the Secretaries of Defense and State, with host nations to create a wind down plan the use of burn pits in areas where U.S. personnel could be exposed.

Provisions of the lawmakers’ legislation were included in the Senate’s Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27) National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), including provisions to:

Prioritize the deployment of alternative solid waste disposal systems to contingency locations where DoD identifies that open-air burn pits remain in use;

Update DoD policy to ensure that non-DoD controlled burn pits are recorded in impacted servicemembers’ health records.

The House’s FY27 NDAA report also included provisions from the WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act that would:

Require DoD to brief Members of Congress on servicemember exposure to non-DoD controlled burn pits; and

Study DoD’s current use of alternative waste disposal methods and what is further needed to finally eliminate the DoD’s reliance on burn pits.

This legislation also builds on Senator Welch and Rep. Ruiz’s bipartisan, bicameral Waste and Illegal Property Eradication (WIPE) Act, which supports servicemember health and strengthen national security by improving how the U.S. military eliminates certain materials both at home and overseas. The WIPE Act’s provisions prohibiting the use of open-air burn pits to dispose of contraband or classified materials and authorizing the use of alternative solid waste disposal systems were included in the final National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26).

The WIPE OUT Burns Pit Act is endorsed by Burn Pits 360, the Disabled American Veterans (DAV), FealGood Foundation, Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America (IAVA), Military Officers Association of America (MOAA), and the Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors (TAPS).

Learn more about the WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act.

Read and download the full text of the legislation.

Senator Welch has championed efforts to limit toxic substance exposure among veterans in the Senate, including the bicameral Airborne Hazards and Open Burn Pit Registry 2.0 Act, which passed as part of the FY25 NDAA, and the bipartisan Burn Pit Elimination Act, both bills that would improve protections for veterans under the PACT Act and prevent future toxic exposure cases. A bipartisan amendment led by Sens. Welch, Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), and Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) requiring the VA to conduct a review on mortality and toxic exposure data for veterans who served in Kosovo also passed with bipartisan support in the Senate.

Senator Welch also cosponsored the Burn Pit Registry Enhancement Act, Reducing Exposure to Burn Pits Act, and Toxic Exposure Education for Servicemembers Act, bills that build on the PACT Act to provide increased support for veterans exposed to burn pits, improve data collection on burn pit and toxic substance exposure, and help mitigate future toxic substance exposure for servicemembers.

Senator Welch’s talented team of caseworkers can help Veterans, families, and survivors with casework related to the VA, as well as other federal agencies. Vermont veterans and servicemembers seeking assistance are encouraged to visit welch.senate.gov or call his Burlington office: 802-863-2525.

title: At COP31, Whitehouse to Call for Ending Pollute-for-Free Model Amid Vacuum of American Leadership
text:
Senate climate hawk to rally international climate leaders behind making polluters pay, warn of Great Climate Insurance Collapse and Axis of Climate Evil

Washington, DC – U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, will soon join heads of state, lawmakers, private sector leaders, environmental champions, and civil society leaders from around the world at the United Nations’ 31st session of the Conference of the Parties (COP31)—the largest and most important venue for world governments to gather to solve the global climate crisis. COP31 is taking place in Antalya, Turkey. Whitehouse released the following statement about the meeting:

“Once again, I will be the only Senator going to the COP. There’s a lot to be said and done about climate, but my message in Antalya will focus on the three key essentials for climate safety.

“First is that we will fail on climate, plain and simple, if pollute-for-free persists as fossil fuel’s business model. That industry offloading trillions in harm to humankind is wrong, morally and economically. It’s now also lethal to climate safety.

“The only present global pollution price is the EU CBAM, recently joined by the UK, and we hope soon by Canada and Australia (a waiver from the EU for California would add extra punch). CBAM is our last lifeboat, and we must defend and expand it. No remaining scenario exists for climate safety without a price on fossil fuel emissions.

“Second is that we can already see the leading edge of climate havoc in markets. Whole regions are becoming uninsurable, mortgages are becoming unavailable, and hits to global real estate as big as $25 trillion are predicted. The cascade from insurance collapse to mortgage market failure to property values crash is predicted by top insurers, banks, regulators and investors. Insurance has business and fiduciary reasons to predict our climate future accurately; we should listen. Fossil fuel profits by lying about our climate future; we should beware.

“Crashes by their nature come suddenly, and whether it’s the Great Climate Insurance Collapse or the end of the ‘carbon bubble,’ a sudden economic catastrophe looms. People need to understand the link.

“Third is that the corrupt death grip of fossil fuel influence on our politics must be broken. An Axis of Political Climate Evil is at work, comprised of the fossil fuel industry, its numberless armada of front groups, the corrupt petrostates like Putin’s Russia, and far-right political groups they fund.

“The pollute-for-free subsidy for fossil fuels is measured by the IMF at over $700 billion every year, in the U.S. alone; it’s trillions of dollars every year globally. The Axis has a massive financial incentive to deploy malign political influence. The industry’s climate denial fraud operation and its dark-money corruption operation need to be called out.

“In a nutshell, we’ve passed all the climate exits except pricing carbon pollution; a major economic adjustment looms as markets predict climate reality; and a highly-motivated Axis of Climate Evil is steering us toward that disaster.”

Whitehouse will be the only Senator traveling to COP31 and will be attending the conference with the Global Legislators Organisation for a Balanced Environment as the Trump administration continues to obstruct official participation in the event.

He will participate in discussions on climate risks to the insurance industry, sea-level rise and the health of the Earth’s oceans, the remaining pathways to climate progress, the future of U.S. climate policy, and carbon pricing. The Senator will also participate in meetings with elected officials, international climate leaders, and business leaders throughout the week.

Whitehouse will participate in a Zoom (audio-only) call with media on Wednesday, November 11, at 12:30 PM EST (8:30 PM TRT) to preview the conference. Interested media should RSVP HERE to receive call-in details.

title: Merkley, Wyden Announce $1.8 Million in Federal Funding to Support Public Safety Services in Tribal Communities
text:
Portland, OR – Oregon’s U.S. Senators Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden today announced that four Oregon Tribes have secured a combined $1,804,643 from the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) to develop, expand, and enhance culturally appropriate services for crime victims in Tribal communities.

“We should do all we can to keep our communities safe and support victims of crime,” said Merkley. “This investment from the federal government will allow Tribal communities across Oregon to provide critical services for survivors and their families to begin the process of recovery and healing.”

“Tribal members in Oregon should feel safe in their communities and have appropriate services available if they become victims of crime,” Wyden said. “I’m glad these federal resources are available to achieve those goals, and I’ll keep battling to secure similar funds for tribal communities throughout our state.”

Four of the awards, which come from the DOJ’s Tribal Victim Set-Aside Services and the Services for the Victims of Crime programs, support Tribes implementing trauma-informed, victim-centered services, including direct services like counseling and crisis intervention, culturally specific traditional healing, and infrastructure projects like building shelters or modular homes. Funding also supports Missing or Murdered Indigenous Persons (MMIP) search efforts and family support, alongside strategic planning, community outreach, and provider training.

The four recipients for this latest Tribal Victim Services Set-Aside program funding are as follows:

$494,092 for the Columbia River Inter-Tribal Fish Commission

$284,130 for the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde

$264,918 for the Cow Creek Band of Umpqua Tribe of Indians

$284,130 for the Klamath Tribes

Additionally, the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde received $477,343 from the Services for the Victims of Crime program. With this funding, the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde will expand its Domestic Violence Department by funding one full-time peer support specialist to provide peer support, case management, safety planning, court accompaniment, and victim support group facilitation. The project will also offer contracted civil legal services and support transportation needs of victims. The project addresses critical victim services gaps in this rural area, which is more than 20 miles from courts and social services.

“We thank Senator Merkley and Senator Wyden for standing with the tribal communities of the Columbia River and fighting to secure this funding. Our people have always cared for one another, and this investment strengthens that care. With these resources, we can expand crisis response, legal advocacy, and culturally grounded healing, so that no Native survivor of violence or abuse along the river has to face it alone,” said Aja DeCoteau, Executive Director, Columbia River Inter-Tribal Fish Commission.

“As a tribal people, we carry with us the historical traumas of violence and racism. These fuel the domestic violence cycles that too many of our people experience in their lifetime,” said Grand Ronde Tribal Chairwoman Cheryle A. Kennedy. “Those who suffer at the hands of a loved one are looking for safety. A safe place to live, to rest, and a path to physical and emotional freedom. With these grant dollars the Tribe can further our resources to give them that. Grants like these save lives and we’re grateful that the Department of Justice recognizes that.”

“I extend our appreciation and offer our many thanks to the Oregon Congressional Delegation, Senators Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden and Congressman Cliff Bentz, for much needed U.S. Department of Justice Tribal Victim Services Grant Award,” said Klamath Tribes Tribal Council Chairman William Ray, Jr.

“The Cow Creek Band of Umpqua Tribe of Indians is grateful for this funding and the opportunity it provides to strengthen services for victims of crime in our community,” said Cow Creek Band of Umpqua Tribe of Indians Chair Carla Keene. “Supporting individuals and families who have experienced trauma is an important responsibility, and we are committed to ensuring they have access to the resources, advocacy, and culturally responsive care they need to heal and move forward. This investment will help us continue this important work, not only for our Tribal citizens, but for the broader community we serve. We appreciate the Senators’ support and their recognition of the importance of these services.”

title: Merkley, Wyden, Bentz, Hoyle Push VA to Prioritize Oregon Veterans’ Homes
text:
Washington, D.C. – Marking Veterans Day this week, Oregon’s U.S. Senators Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden, alongside U.S. Representatives Cliff Bentz (OR-02) and Val Hoyle (OR-04), are calling on the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to prioritize funding for the construction of Oregon Department of Veterans’ Affairs’ (ODVA) proposed Roseburg State Veterans’ Home project and renovation of the Edward C. Allworth Veterans’ Home, a 154-bed assisted living facility in Lebanon.

“Continued investment in Oregon’s veterans’ care infrastructure is essential to meet the needs of our state’s geographically diverse veteran population, particularly in rural Oregon,” wrote the bipartisan group of lawmakers to VA Secretary Doug Collins.

Currently, ODVA operates two high-quality, award-winning veterans’ homes. These facilities provide skilled and long-term nursing, memory, and rehabilitative care to veterans, their spouses, and Gold Star parents, which allows veterans to live in a culture of community with fellow veterans and those with shared military experiences. To build on the success of the state’s veterans’ homes, the lawmakers are urging the VA to prioritize fully funding the agency’s Priority 1 State Home Construction List, including the Roseburg Veterans’ Home and Edward C. Allworth Veterans’ Home projects.

“We support efforts to fully fund the Priority 1 list and urge the VA to work quickly in coordination with Congress to make that funding a reality. By working together, the VA, Congress and the State of Oregon can help ensure that veterans and their families have access to the care, dignity and support they have earned,” the lawmakers concluded.

Roseburg has a sizable veteran population, with current estimates suggesting that Douglas County is home to over 10,000 veterans, many of whom served in the Vietnam War era or earlier. A new facility in the community would provide an affordable, high-quality, long-term care option for the estimated 68,000 veterans across the VA Southern Oregon Healthcare System service area, which includes Jackson, Josephine, Klamath, and Lake counties in Oregon as well as Siskiyou and Del Norte counties in California.

Previously, Merkley, Wyden, and Hoyle sent a letter in support of the Roseburg State Veterans' Home project, which remains in the preliminary stages of preconstruction. With Oregon doing its part to make it a reality, the bipartisan group of lawmakers is now urging the VA to work with Congress and fully fund this long-awaited project.

title: Congressman Thompson Congratulates Scott Colom on Historic Victory
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Bennie G. Thompson (MS-02) issued the following statement on Senator-elect Scott Colom’s historic election to the United States Senate:

“I am incredibly proud of Senator-elect Scott Colom and his historic victory. Having known Scott for many years, it has been a pleasure to watch him grow into the leader he is today. His campaign brought together Mississippians from every walk of life—young and old, Black and white, rural and urban—in a way I have never witnessed in more than 50 years of public service. This victory demonstrates the power of grassroots organizing and what can be accomplished when people come together for a common purpose.”

“My relationship with Scott dates back to his participation in the Mississippi Black Leadership Institute, which I helped establish in partnership with the NAACP to develop the next generation of public servants. As one of the program's first graduates, Scott demonstrated the leadership and commitment to public service that would later define his career. Recognizing that potential, I encouraged him to run for District Attorney of Mississippi's 16th Judicial District, where he defeated a 28-year incumbent and went on to serve three terms.

“Having witnessed Scott's leadership firsthand, I had every confidence in his ability to serve as a federal judge when I recommended him to President Joe Biden for nomination in 2022. Former Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith’s decision to block his nomination by withholding her blue slip was disappointing, but it did not lessen my confidence in him or his commitment to serving Mississippi. To see him now elected to the very Senate where his nomination was blocked is especially meaningful and a testament to his perseverance and the trust Mississippians have placed in his leadership.”

“Scott has the experience, character, and determination to be an effective advocate for Mississippi. Throughout my career, I have fought to make sure those at the bottom have an opportunity to move up, and I know he shares that commitment. Having another Mississippi Democrat alongside me in Congress who understands the needs of Mississippians means a great deal. Together, we will fight to improve access to health care, strengthen public education, expand economic opportunities, and ensure our rural and underserved communities are not left behind.

“I look forward to working with Senator-elect Colom and am pleased to welcome him to the Mississippi Congressional Delegation.”

title: $197 Million Awarded for Oregon’s Rural Hospitals in 2027
text:
Washington, D.C. —Congressman Cliff Bentz (R-OR) is pleased to announce that the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has just awarded $197.3 million for fiscal year 2027 to improve and modernize rural health care in Oregon.

This fund is a continuation of the Big Beautiful Bill’s Rural Health Transformation Program, which awarded a similar amount to Oregon for the last year.

So far in 2026, at least $16.4 million is being distributed to 42 “Immediate Impact Award” projects to support initiatives that address urgent and high-priority needs in rural communities. $80.1 million has also been distributed to 103 competitive “Catalyst Award” projects to improve and modernize health care access in areas like maternity care, primary care, senior care, and other critical projects. $21.7 million has also been provided for the nine federally recognized Tribes of Oregon. $35 million has been distributed among each of Oregon’s 35 rural hospitals, and $10 million has been distributed among each of Oregon’s 100 rural health clinics.

With 2027’s awarded funds, the Rural Health Transformation Program will support both the continuation of existing projects and the development of additional initiatives.

Congressman Bentz was the only member of Oregon’s congressional delegation to vote YES to fund improvements to the delivery of health care in rural Oregon.

title: Rep. Bera Celebrates Major Milestone in Implementing His Bipartisan Taiwan Fellowship Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, U.S. Representative Ami Bera, M.D. (CA-06), Co-Chair of the Congressional Taiwan Caucus, joined officials representing the United States and Taiwan to celebrate the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) formally launching the Taiwan Fellowship Program.

The agreement marks a major milestone in implementing Rep. Bera's bipartisan Taiwan Fellowship Act, which was signed into law in December 2022 as part of the FY 2023 National Defense Authorization Act.

Rep. Bera introduced the Taiwan Fellowship Act in 2021 to deepen U.S.-Taiwan relations by creating opportunities for American government officials to live, study, and work in Taiwan. The newly signed agreement between the American Institute in Taiwan (AIT) and the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office (TECRO) puts that legislation into action.

"When I introduced the bipartisan Taiwan Fellowship Act, my goal was to strengthen America's partnership with Taiwan by investing in the next generation of public servants who will help shape our foreign policy," said Representative Bera. "I was proud to see our legislation signed into law in 2022, and this week's agreement represents an important step toward turning that vision into reality.”

"Taiwan is a vital partner in maintaining peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific,” Bera continued. “By giving American officials firsthand experience living and working in Taiwan, we are building the expertise and relationships needed to strengthen this partnership for generations to come. I am grateful to our bipartisan partners in Congress and to AIT and TECRO for helping bring this program to life."

The Taiwan Fellowship Program will equip the next generation of American public servants with a deeper understanding of Taiwan's history, culture, and political landscape. It will also strengthen people-to-people ties and ensure U.S. foreign policy in the Indo-Pacific is informed by firsthand regional experience.

Tuesday's signing represents a significant step forward in implementing legislation championed by Rep. Bera and demonstrates the continued bipartisan commitment to strengthening the U.S.-Taiwan partnership.

title: Bergman, Ruiz Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Preserve Critical Drug Discounts for Safety Net Providers
text:
On October 29, Reps. Jack Bergman and Dr. Raul Ruiz, M.D., introduced the Safety Net Provider Drug Pricing Protection Act (H.R. 10919), bipartisan legislation to preserve critical prescription drug discounts for rural hospitals, community health centers, and other safety-net providers participating in the 340B Drug Pricing Program.

The 340B Program allows eligible hospitals and health centers serving low-income, uninsured, and rural patients to purchase outpatient prescription drugs at discounted prices, enabling them to reinvest those savings into patient care and essential services, including behavioral health, obstetric care, dental care, and other programs that might otherwise be reduced or eliminated. In areas like Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula, where many hospitals and health centers operate on thin – and sometimes negative – financial margins, savings generated through the 340B Program are critical to keeping facilities open and ensuring patients can access the care they need.

In recent years, federal regulators and drug manufacturers have pursued changes to the 340B Program that would replace up-front prescription drug discounts with a rebate-based model, forcing providers to purchase medications at full price and wait for reimbursement. For smaller safety-net providers with limited financial reserves, this shift would create significant financial and administrative burdens, potentially jeopardizing their ability to maintain essential services.

Rep. Bergman has previously worked to block this rebate model through his Community Health Center Drug Pricing Protection Act (H.R. 7391), which seeks to protect Federally Qualified Health Centers from rebate-based pricing models. While implementation of the federal government’s initial rebate model was delayed, regulators have since announced a revised version of the program, scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027.

The Safety Net Provider Drug Pricing Protection Act builds on these efforts by extending protections to a broader range of safety net providers, including Critical Access Hospitals, Federally Qualified Health Centers, Sole Community Hospitals, and other eligible entities. Specifically, the legislation would prohibit arrangements under the 340B Program that require these providers to pay more than the 340B ceiling price at the time of purchase and subsequently recover the difference through a rebate, reimbursement, or other payment. By preserving up-front discounts, the bill would protect financially vulnerable providers from additional costs and administrative burdens while ensuring they can continue directing limited resources toward caring for the patients and communities they serve.

“Rural hospitals and community health centers across Northern Michigan and the Upper Peninsula are already operating on razor-thin margins. The last thing they need is another Washington mandate forcing them to pay more upfront for prescription drugs and then wait to get their money back. The 340B Program is a critical lifeline for these facilities and the patients who depend on them. Our bipartisan legislation puts patients and rural healthcare providers first by protecting the savings they rely on to keep their doors open and deliver quality care close to home. I'll continue fighting to make sure Washington isn't making it harder for our rural communities to access the healthcare they deserve,” said Rep. Jack Bergman.

“Safety net providers are the backbone of healthcare in our communities. These lifelines serving our most vulnerable patients depend on the 340B program to keep their doors open and cannot afford the devastating upfront costs of the new pilot Rebate model. The Safety Net Provider Drug Pricing Protection Act is a critical first step to protect that lifeline, but there is more work to do, and I will keep fighting to make sure our safety nets stay strong,” said Rep. Raul Ruiz, M.D. (CA-25).

“The 340B drug pricing program is a lifeline for sustaining critical access hospitals and the rural communities that depend on them. Aspirus Health strongly supports The Safety Net Provider Drug Pricing Protection Act, which would help ensure continued access to more affordable medications by those who need them most,” said Connie Bradley, Senior Vice President, Acute Care Services, Aspirus Health Care.

“OSF St. Francis Hospital is happy to support the Safety Net Provider Drug Pricing Protection Act. This piece of legislation is a necessary step toward ensuring that critical rural healthcare providers, such as OSF St. Francis Hospital in Escanaba, MI, can continue to utilize the 340B program. OSF St. Francis Hospital is supportive of Congressman Bergman's efforts to champion 340B savings and develop policy solutions that address rural healthcare needs in the Upper Peninsula,” said Kelly Jefferson, President, OSF St. Francis Hospital (Escanaba, MI).

“Programs like 340B are vital to rural hospitals like Schoolcraft Memorial Hospital, helping us stretch limited resources and keep care accessible close to home. Just as important, they directly impact patients—making lifesaving treatments, including oncology therapies, more affordable for individuals who might otherwise go without care. We strongly support the Safety Net Provider Drug Pricing Protection Act to protect this critical lifeline for our community,” said Robert W. Mach, FACHE, CEO, Schoolcraft Memorial Hospital.

"Residents in rural communities throughout our country deserve access to high quality healthcare. The Safety Net Provider Drug Pricing Protection Act sponsored by Congressman Bergman protects rural hospitals by removing the unnecessary administrative and financial burden associated with a 340B drug rebate program. This allows hospitals, like Kalkaska Memorial Health Center, to focus their resources on improving the health and quality of life of the rural communities they serve,” said Jeremy Cannon, MSN, RN, FACHE, Kalkaska Memorial Health Center’s Chief Nursing Officer.

“The Safety Net Provider Drug Pricing Protection Act is an important step in preserving the integrity of the 340B Drug Pricing Program. For Critical Access Hospitals like Munising Memorial Hospital, maintaining the up-front discount structure is essential to ensuring continued access to affordable medications for our rural patients. We appreciate Congressman Bergman’s leadership in protecting rural hospitals and the communities we serve,” said Wendy Frush, CEO, Munising Memorial Hospital.

“Helen Newberry Joy Hospital applauds Congressman Bergman’s efforts to protect some of his most vulnerable constituents. He is assuring access to care by helping make drugs more affordable. Prescription drugs are the fastest growing expense for hospitals, with increases outpacing labor and service costs. Thank you Congressman Bergman for helping to care for your neighbors in small communities across rural Michigan!” said Helen Johnson, RN, FACHE, CEO, Helen Newberry Joy Hospital & Healthcare Center.

The Safety Net Provider Drug Pricing Protection Act is also supported by Mackinac Straits Hospital, the Michigan Center for Rural Health, the NACHC, AHF, ACH, and the NCUIH.

title: Beyer, Huffman, Colleagues Demand Answers on Trump Admin Effort to Gut Endangered Wildlife Protections
text:
Today, Don Beyer (D-Va.), House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), and Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-Mich.), and Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) led 37 other Democratic lawmakers in demanding answers from Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on the Trump administration’s attempts to gut core Endangered Species Act (ESA) protections by reinterpreting what the agencies consider “incidental take” and “harm” in memoranda to federal employees.

The lawmakers warned the reinterpretation would strip protections from wildlife killed or injured by otherwise lawful activities, even when those deaths and injuries could be foreseen. Under the administration’s interpretation, the law’s prohibition on killing or injuring protected wildlife would apply only when someone deliberately targets a protected species. The lawmakers warned this would undermine decades of safeguards that allow economic activity to proceed while requiring commonsense steps to prevent wildlife deaths and injuries.

“For decades, the ESA has provided a framework for allowing economic activity to proceed while requiring reasonable measures to avoid and minimize harm to threatened and endangered species. These memoranda would undermine that framework by removing incentives to prevent foreseeable wildlife deaths and injuries,” the lawmakers wrote.

The letter challenges two identical internal memos issued September 14 by U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Director Brian Nesvik and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration General Counsel John Luce. The memos direct staff to interpret “take” — which includes killing or injuring protected wildlife — as covering only intentional actions targeting those animals. The lawmakers are demanding an explanation of the legal basis for that interpretation and whether activities that could foreseeably kill or injure endangered species still require permits.

The directives came as the Trump administration eliminated the longstanding regulatory definition of “harm,” which covered habitat destruction that kills or injures protected wildlife. Both changes took effect the same day, threatening protections for endangered animals and the places they need to survive.

“Any reinterpretation that could eliminate protections for these species is a serious and troubling departure from that framework and would undermine the law’s implementation,” the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers requested responses by November 30, 2026, including what protections would remain for species threatened by habitat destruction and whether states and Tribes were consulted. They also asked whether Interior would suspend implementation until it publicly explains its legal reasoning and assesses the consequences for endangered wildlife.

“The Services must abandon this approach and preserve the ESA’s longstanding protections for threatened and endangered wildlife and the communities that depend on them,” the lawmakers concluded.

title: Bilirakis, Ruiz, Tenney, Welch and Crapo Lead Bill to Better Protect Servicemembers from Burn Pits and Improve Care for Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Representatives Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12), Raul Ruiz (D-CA-35) and Claudia Tenney (R-NY-24), along with Senators Peter Welch (D-VT) and Mike Crapo (R-ID), introduced the Waste Incineration Protection, Exposure Oversight, and Updated Tracking of (WIPE OUT) Burn Pits Act. This bipartisan, bicameral legislation would build on the Sergeant First Class Heath Robinson Honoring our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics (PACT) Act by ensuring all instances of toxic exposure from burn pits are accounted for and recorded in each servicemember’s health records. The legislation would also establish a clear framework for identifying, tracking, and mitigating risks of open‑air burn pits located near U.S. forces and push for replacement with safer alternatives.

“Our servicemembers put their lives on the line to defend our nation, and they should never have to face lifelong health consequences because of the toxic exposure they endured while serving. The WIPE Out Burn Pits Act is an important step toward protecting our military personnel, addressing the dangers of burn pit exposure, and ensuring those who serve our country have the support and protections they deserve. We have a responsibility to safeguard the health of our heroes, and I will continue fighting to make that a priority," said Rep. Bilirakis.

“I’m proud to lead the bipartisan, bicameral WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act to protect servicemembers from the harmful effects of toxic burn pits.” said Rep. Dr. Raul Ruiz. “This bill requires the Department of Defense (DoD) to find, record, and test the air at every burn pit site used by other countries or contractors that are endangering the lives of our troops. The PACT Act gave presumptive benefits and health care to veterans harmed by burn pit exposure. The WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act aims to end the use of toxic burn pits once and for all.”

“Our servicemembers should not have to worry that the air they breathe while defending our country could jeopardize their health for years to come,” said Rep. Tenney. “We have seen the devastating consequences of toxic exposure on our veterans and their families, and we must do everything possible to prevent future generations from facing the same challenges. The bipartisan WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act will help identify dangerous exposure risks, improve accountability, and ensure our troops have accurate health records if they need care in the future. Protecting those who serve our nation must remain a top priority, both during their service and long after they return home.”

“When we passed the PACT Act four years ago, we took a major step toward ensuring that the cost of war always includes the cost of caring for the warrior. But there’s always more we can do to improve servicemember safety, including finding better ways to track and mitigate the risks of burn pits,” said Senator Welch. “I’m proud to partner with Senator Crapo on this bill which builds on our bipartisan work to expand benefits and open doors to care for veterans exposed to toxic chemicals.”

“While the Pentagon has largely phased out the use of burn pits, many foreign partners and entities continue to operate them near installations where U.S. personnel live and work,”said Senator Crapo. “We must take proactive steps to reduce the risk of toxic exposure by providing safer waste disposal alternatives, working with foreign partners to eliminate hazardous burn pits and ensuring servicemembers’ health records accurately document potential exposure so veterans can access appropriate benefits and care in the future.”

For decades, the Department of Defense (DoD) relied on open-air burn pits to dispose of waste during overseas contingency operations, exposing U.S. servicemembers to toxins linked to long-term health conditions, including respiratory disease, cancer, and heart issues. The PACT Act, signed into law in 2022, took historic steps to expand care and benefits for Veterans suffering from toxic exposure. To date, more than 7 million Veterans have been screened for toxic exposures because of the PACT Act.

While DoD has reduced its own use of burn pits, servicemembers are still exposed to active burn pits not controlled by DoD, and safer alternatives exist for instances when DoD does operate burn pits. Specifically, the WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act:

Establishes a clear framework for identifying, tracking, and mitigating the risks of non‑DoD open‑air burn pits located near U.S. forces, and ensure that exposure to toxic substances is incorporated into servicemembers’ health records;

Directs the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to Congress detailing the location and use of all nearby burn pits, including those operated by allies, partners, or local entities;

Requires the deployment of alternative solid waste disposal systems in locations where the DoD operates burn pits; and

Mandates diplomatic engagement, jointly by the Secretaries of Defense and State, with host nations to create a wind down plan the use of burn pits in areas where U.S. personnel could be exposed.

Provisions of the lawmakers’ legislation were included in the Senate’s Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27) National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), including provisions to:

Prioritize the deployment of alternative solid waste disposal systems to contingency locations where DoD identifies that open-air burn pits remain in use;

Update DoD policy to ensure that non-DoD controlled burn pits are recorded in impacted servicemembers’ health records.

The House’s FY27 NDAA report also included provisions from the WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act that would:

Require DoD to brief Members of Congress on servicemember exposure to non-DoD controlled burn pits; and

Study DoD’s current use of alternative waste disposal methods and what is further needed to finally eliminate the DoD’s reliance on burn pits.

The WIPE OUT Burns Pit Act is endorsed by Burn Pits 360, the Disabled American Veterans (DAV), FealGood Foundation, Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America (IAVA), Military Officers Association of America (MOAA), and the Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors (TAPS).

title: Buchanan Honors America’s Veterans on Veterans Day
text:
Highlights His Support of Legislation to Expand Veterans’ Health Care Access and Protect Their Earned Benefits

Honoring our veterans must go beyond words, it means ensuring they receive the care and benefits they have earned.”

title: Chairwoman Kat Cammack Announces Delegation Leadership for the 120th Congress
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Kat Cammack (FL-03) has been elected Chair of Florida's Republican congressional delegation in the U.S. House of Representatives. She will succeed Congressman Vern Buchanan (FL-16), who has held the post since 2012 and is retiring at the end of this term.

"Florida's Republican delegation is a powerhouse on Capitol Hill," said Congresswoman Cammack. "When we move as a united coalition, we’re able to deliver real results for all Floridians. Whether it’s working across the aisle when disaster strikes – or pushing for commonsense policies to keep Florida free and prosperous – the Chair of the Delegation position is a critical, Florida-first leadership role. I’m grateful to my colleagues for their trust, and I’m looking forward to working with each of them."

"Vern Buchanan has led our delegation for more than a decade and always put Florida first,” Cammack added. “I’m proud to build on his legacy and thank him for his years of faithful service to our great state."

Florida’s House Delegation leadership team for the 120th Congress will be made up of the following members:

Congresswoman Kat Cammack (FL-03), Chair

Congressman Mario Díaz-Balart (FL-26), Dean & Steering Committee Representative

Congressman Scott Franklin (FL-18), Policy Chair

Congressman-elect Ryan Elijah (FL-07), Policy Co-Chair

Congressman Mike Haridopolos (FL-08), Steering Committee Representative

The members released the following statements:

“I can think of no better person to lead the Florida Republican Delegation than my colleague and friend, Congresswoman Kat Cammack,” said Congressman Díaz-Balart, Dean of the Florida delegation. “Kat has brought tremendous energy and passion to Congress, delivering real results and always putting Florida first. She consistently goes above and beyond for our state, and I am confident our delegation will be in excellent hands under her leadership. Congratulations, Kat! I look forward to continuing our work together in the 120th Congress.”

"Leading Florida’s congressional delegation for 14 years has been one of the greatest privileges of my life,” said Congressman Buchanan. “Every day, I’ve worked to put Floridians first and ensure our state has a strong voice in Washington. I’m proud to see Congresswoman Kat Cammack step into this leadership role, and I’m confident the Florida delegation will continue to represent the best state in the nation with strength and conviction."

“Congratulations to Congresswoman Kat Cammack on being elected Chair of Florida’s Republican delegation,” said Congressman Haridopolos. “As a Steering Committee Representative, I look forward to working alongside her and our leadership team to deliver results for Floridians and ensure our state has a strong voice in Washington. I also thank Congressman Vern Buchanan for his years of outstanding leadership and service.”

“Congratulations to Congresswoman Kat Cammack on her election as Chair of Florida’s Republican congressional delegation,” said Congressman-elect Elijah. “I am honored to serve as Policy Co-Chair and look forward to working with her and our delegation to deliver results for Florida.”

Cammack Background:

Cammack steps into the role having already brought Florida members together to take on some of the state’s biggest challenges. She co-led the Freeze Disaster Assistance Act with Congressman Scott Franklin (FL-18), legislation that would send $3.5 billion in emergency aid to Florida growers hit by the January 2026 freeze. Congresswoman Kat Cammack represents Florida’s 3rd Congressional District, covering 12 counties in North Central Florida. Cammack chairs the Republican Women’s Caucus, which she launched with Senator Katie Britt (R-AL) in 2025, and serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

title: Congressman Carson Statement on Veterans Day
text:

Over 1 million veterans lost their VA medical providers since the start of Trump’s second term, barring them from receiving their well-deserved benefits and making wait times too long, especially for mental health services. This afternoon, the House will vote on the Major Richard Star Act, which would let combat-injured veterans receive both the retirement pay and the disability compensation they earned. I urge every one of my colleagues to vote yes with me, and I call on the Senate to send it to the President’s desk without delay.

This year, the House adopted my bipartisan amendment to increase funding for VA Medical and Prosthetic Research to $994 million, supporting research into traumatic brain injury, cancer, and the prosthetics and assistive devices that help injured veterans live full lives. I introduced the Medical Research for Our Troops Act to restore full funding to the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs, which support peer-reviewed research into conditions affecting service members and veterans. I’m proud to have also led the charge to increase funding to combat veteran hunger.

My office has closed over 300 veterans' cases in Indianapolis in 2026 alone, including helping 112 homeless veterans qualify for housing. As we transition into the next Congress, I will continue to fight to expand access to medical, dental, and mental health services for those who put their lives on the line for this country."

title: USCIRF Reauthorization Act of 2026Smith bill promoting international religious freedom becomes law
text:
On the same day that Americans throughout the country headed to the polls, Rep. Chris Smith’s (R-NJ) critical legislation to advance international religious freedom became law in Washington.

The United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) Reauthorization Act of 2026 (HR 1744/PL 119-137), signed into law by President Trump on November 3rd , extends and authorizes annual appropriations for the USCIRF board through fiscal year 2028.

“The U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom is the U.S. government’s most effective, unbiased, and respected voice for victims of religious persecution throughout the globe. I am grateful to President Trump, as well as my colleagues in both chambers of Congress, for recognizing the timeliness and importance of this critical legislation,” said Smith, who has chaired countless congressional hearings on international religious freedom issues.

“Persecuted believers from all faiths have found USCIRF to be one of their most reliable and effective allies. USCIRF is important to millions of our constituents of all faiths,” Smith continued. “Since its founding, USCIRF has issued 27 annual reports and recommended that 26 countries be designated CPCs – 18 of them have ultimately been designated by the State Department.”

Smith noted that the USCIRF board is also a leading force in the global fight against antisemitism: “Since its inception, the Commission has chaired countless hearings and issued numerous reports on the rise of antisemitism throughout the globe.

“USCIRF also provides recommendations to the State Department for how to best confront and combat antisemitism, both at home and abroad, including by briefing and working closely with the U.S. Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism—an ambassador-rank official established by my law, the Special Envoy to Monitor and Combat Antisemitism Act (PL 116-323).”

When Smith’s HR 1744 overwhelmingly passed the House in June, it received broad bipartisan support, with Reps. Brad Sherman (D‑CA), Gus Bilirakis (R‑FL), and Henry Cuellar (D‑TX) signing on as original cosponsors. It was also backed by the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops (USCCB), who wrote a letter in support of USCIRF and urged lawmakers to vote “yes” on the legislation:

“The Catholic Church has long viewed religious freedom as a basic human right since it is rooted in the dignity of the human person and is critical to the health of societies. Over the years, USCCB has advocated strongly for the mission of USCIRF because of its critical role in promoting human rights around the world by monitoring and promoting religious freedom. At a time when international religious freedom is increasingly imperiled, it is vital that USCIRF be reauthorized so that it can continue to highlight the need to protect those who are discriminated against, harassed and even killed for their faith.”

The Commission was initially established by the International Religious Freedom Act (IRFA) of 1998 (PL 105-292), of which Smith was a leading cosponsor. Smith later authored the Frank R. Wolf International Religious Freedom Act of 2016 (PL 114-281), which updated the IRFA to strengthen and expand U.S. efforts to promote religious freedom worldwide.

“History has shown that when the U.S. elevates religious freedom and that priority is conveyed to Countries of Particular Concern, conditions often change for the better, prisoners of conscience gain their freedom, and progress is made toward freer exercise of religious liberty,” said Smith.

Established in 1998, USCIRF is an independent, bipartisan legislative branch agency charged with defending the universal right to freedom of religion or belief abroad. It reviews reports of religious freedom violations and provides policy recommendations to the President, the Secretary of State, and Congress.

title: RELEASE: Congressman Cloud Introduces Bill to Rename Department of Veterans Affairs Clinic in Honor of Master Sergeant Roy P. Benavidez.
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C – Congressman Michael Cloud introduced legislation designating the Department of Veterans Affairs community-based outpatient clinic located in Victoria, Texas, as the “Master Sergeant Roy P. Benavidez Department of Veterans Affairs Clinic”, honoring the Medal of Honor recipient’s exceptional valor and lifetime of service to the United States.

Master Sergeant Roy P. Benavidez was born on August 5, 1935, in Cuero, Texas. On May 2, 1968, near Loc Ninh, South Vietnam, he voluntarily entered a fierce firefight to rescue a 12-man Special Forces team pinned down by enemy fire. Wounded numerous times and refusing to stop, he saved the lives of his fellow soldiers against overwhelming odds. President Ronald Reagan awarded him the Medal of Honor on February 24, 1981.

After a lifetime dedicated to serving the United States of America, he retired to El Campo, Texas, where he devoted the rest of his life to mentoring young Americans until he died in 1998.

“While many people remember my father as a Medal of Honor recipient, I remember him as a man who never forgot the people he served alongside or the community, he came from. Our family is deeply honored that his legacy will continue through a facility dedicated to caring for those who served our nation,” said Noel Benavidez.

“Master Sergeant Roy Benavidez embodied the courage and selflessness that define our nation’s heroes,” said Rep. Cloud. “Renaming this clinic in his honor will be a fitting tribute to his legacy of service as well as that of the veterans who pass through its doors every day,” Rep. Cloud concluded.

The clinic, located at 311 Spring Green Boulevard in Victoria, Texas, serves veterans throughout the surrounding community.

title: Courtney Votes to Advance the Major Richard Star Act to Final Vote
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, on Veterans Day, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02) voted to advance the Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102) to a final vote on the House floor, which is now expected to take place tomorrow.

Courtney and a bipartisan coalition successfully forced tomorrow’s vote on the Major Richard Star Act via a discharge petition, which Courtney signed earlier this year. The Major Richard Star Act would fix an injustice in the law that currently diminishes earned retirement benefits for veteran retirees who also collect service-connected disability benefits.

“As our nation pauses on Veterans Day to recognize the sacrifice and service of veterans, the House has taken a major step to ensure medically retired veterans get the full support and benefits they have earned,” Courtney said. “I implore all of my colleagues to vote ‘yes’ on the Major Richard Star Act when it comes up for a final vote.”

Currently, combat-injured veterans who were forced into medical retirement are only able to receive either U.S. Department of Defense retirement benefits or U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs disability compensation. The Major Richard Star Act would amend the law to allow these medically retired veterans to receive both their full retirement pay and disability compensation.

title: Crow Leads Resolution Recognizing National Veterans Small Business Week
text:
WASHINGTON—Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO) introduced a congressional resolution recognizing November 9-13th as National Veterans Small Business Week in the United States.

Crow’s resolution honors the more than 1.8 million veteran-owned small businesses in the U.S. and their commitment to quality and excellence. These small businesses employ more than 4.5 million American workers and generate more than $1 trillion in economic impact. Colorado alone is home to nearly 50,000 veteran-owned small businesses.

Joining him on the resolution are Congressmen Brad Schneider (D-IL), Brad Finstad (R-MN), and Jake Ellzey (R-TX).

National Veterans Small Business Week coincides with the week of Veterans Day. During this year’s National Veterans Small Business Week, programming for veteran entrepreneurs by the Small Business Administration focuses on Made in America manufacturing and farming; supply chain procurement and contracting; capital access and acquisition financing; and specialized training and resources for veterans.

“Veterans helped defend and build America into the great country that it is. Even after they take off the uniform, veterans are still leaders and entrepreneurs in our communities. National Veterans Small Business Week is just one way we can support veterans, invest in their success, and pay it forward for the service and sacrifice they gave our nation,” said Congressman Crow.

“More than 30,000 veterans call Illinois’ Tenth Congressional District home. This week and every week, we must honor the dedication and commitment of our veterans and ensure they have the tools and support they need to thrive. I am proud to join my colleagues to introduce this bipartisan resolution to honor our veteran entrepreneurs and recognize the rich contributions they make to our communities and nation – even out of uniform,” said Congressman Schneider.

“Representing thousands of veterans in southern Minnesota, I’m honored to join my colleagues in introducing a resolution recognizing National Veterans Small Business Week and emphasizing the importance of supporting veteran-owned small businesses across the country,” said Congressman Finstad. “Not only this week, but every week, we thank the brave men and women who have served our great nation and continue to invest in our communities.”

Crow has long been a champion for Colorado’s small businesses and entrepreneurs to start a business, create jobs, and bolster our economy, including through four years of service on the House Small Business Committee. He recently introduced a bipartisan slate of bills to support small businesses by bolstering resources for innovation, increasing opportunities for apprenticeships and on-the-job training, and supporting their contingency planning. Crow passed his bipartisan SBA Cyber Awareness Act into law to protect small businesses from cyber threats, and he led bipartisan legislation to combat labor shortages and improve businesses’ energy efficiency.

title: On Veterans Day, Democratic Veterans and Newly-Elected Democratic Veterans in Congress Speak in One Voice: End this Iran War and Stand with Veterans
text: “It is no surprise that the American people sent so many Democratic veterans to the Congress last week, and I look forward to serving with them in the 120th Congress” said Congressman Deluzio. “These are leaders who know about courage, public service, and patriotic love of country, and their voices are powerful. title: Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. Introduces Bill to Ban Data Centers on Federal Public Lands
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03) introduced the Protecting Our Public Lands from Data Centers Act to ban the construction of new data centers and related infrastructure on federal public lands managed by the U.S. Forest Service and the Department of the Interior.

“Public lands belong in public hands and Oregonians must have a say before the federal government hands over millions of acres of public land managed by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) for data centers,” said Congresswoman Dexter. “These treasured lands are where people hunt, fish, hike and graze livestock. They are where wildlife habitat and our critical watersheds are protected. My bill keeps these lands safe from data centers now, and for the generations who come after us.”

The Trump administration is opening federal public lands to data center development as demand for computing power grows. Large data centers will put pressure on local water supplies and electric grids. Some proposed campuses include their own gas-fired power plants which can have devastating impacts on air quality, noise pollution can be extreme, and fencing off these sites restricts public access and disrupts wildlife habitat.

“Data centers have no place on public lands,” Randi Spivak, Public Lands Policy Director, Center for Biological Diversity. “They’re water-guzzling, pollution-spewing facilities that turn lands meant for wildlife and recreation into corporate industrial sites. Once a data center goes up, hundreds to thousands of acres of wildlife habitat will be stripped bare and closed to the public for good. We’re deeply grateful to Rep. Dexter for standing up to keep public lands public.”

The Congresswoman’s bill would prohibit the development, sale or transfer of covered federal lands nationwide for new data centers and related infrastructure. It would also require covered lands that are sold or transferred to return to public ownership if used for a data center without congressional approval.

“Our national forests and other public lands should be protected for future generations, not sold off or paved over to make way for massive commercial data centers,” said Athan Manuel, Director of Lands Protection Program, Sierra Club. “Representative Dexter’s legislation draws a clear line by keeping these industrial facilities and their associated infrastructure off lands managed by the Forest Service and Department of the Interior. The Sierra Club applauds Representative Dexter and Senator Wyden for standing up for our public lands and ensuring they remain protected for the people, wildlife, and communities that depend on them.”

“America's public lands are national treasures, and they should be managed as a legacy for future generations, not sacrificed to make way for corporate data centers,” said Steve Pedery, Conservation Director, Oregon Wild. “We strongly support Representative Maxine Dexter's legislation to protect our lands, wildlife, and clean water from data center development.”

“Mt. Hood National Forest supplies drinking and irrigation water to one-third of Oregonians,” said Jordan Latter, Forest Watch Program Manager, Bark. “Its protected headwaters keep our water clean, shelter endangered species, and anchor our shared identity as Oregonians. Data centers have no place here.”

The Center for Biological Diversity, Sierra Club, Earthjustice Action, Save Our Wild Salmon, WaterWatch of Oregon, Bark, Oregon Wild, Columbia Riverkeeper and the Oregon Data Center Defiance Coalition endorse the bill.
