title: TRANSCRIPT: Congresswoman Escobar Speaks on Dignity Act, Future of Immigration Reform
text:
Today, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) joined fellow Democrats, the American Business Immigration Coalition Action (ABIC Action) and the South Texas Builders Association to discuss the future of immigration reform and solutions.

Below is a lightly edited transcript of her remarks. You can find video of her remarks here.

Congresswoman Escobar: Buenos dias! What a beautiful day on Capitol Hill. And we have been blessed with incredible advocates, with an amazing freshman class. We've turned the border blue, and we have a mandate from the American people.

As my colleagues have mentioned, today is Veteran's Day. I would be remiss if I didn't mention that there are hundreds of veterans who have been deported. Not just during this administration, but prior administrations. We need to get them home, and we need to address the broken system that has removed American heroes from American soil. It is incredibly unjust.

As Ashley - one of my personal heroes - has mentioned, I am the co-author of the Dignity Act. My colleague Maria Salazar could not be here with us. She just won her race. And she and I are deeply committed to continuing our effort at bipartisan, comprehensive immigration reform.

When we introduced the Dignity Act in 2023, we were subjected to a lot of criticism about the bipartisan effort that we - the journey - that we began together.

I am a progressive Democrat. I have very aspirational dreams and hopes for immigration reform. But I am also a pragmatist. And as we continue to have Donald Trump in the White House and without a super majority in the Senate, we need Republican support. So any comprehensive immigration reform must be bipartisan.

I am deeply committed to ensuring that the Dignity Act is reintroduced in 2027. To my incoming freshman colleagues: this is the only bipartisan, comprehensive immigration reform bill in the House in over a decade. This last Congress, we had 20 Republicans and 20 Democrats. We want to grow that number and get the bill out of the House, get it to the Senate - where I already have a bipartisan Senate duo very interested in the Dignity Act - and get this bill to the president's desk.

To Republicans and Democrats alike who did not like the Dignity Act because it didn't meet their goals: we are going to reshape it in the coming weeks. If you want to be a part of bipartisan, comprehensive immigration reform compromise so that we can get a bill to the president's desk in 2027, we welcome you with open arms. We welcome your ideas. We welcome your initiative. We want you at the table. And if we can get this passed this upcoming Congress, we can do even more in 2028 to grow and expand what we can do for immigrants, immigrant families, and our economy and our communities.

I know all of us never want to see another family separated ever again. We never want to see private prisons like those run in my district - Camp East Montana, a $1.24 billion facility, a profit-making enterprise that is essentially feeding its profits off of human misery - we need to bring that to an end. We need to bring sanity back to the immigration system. We can do this. We will do this. Thank you all.

title: Congresswoman Escobar Celebrates Veterans Day with Introduction of Senate Companion Bill
text:
This Veterans Day, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) announced that her bipartisan legislation, the VA Home Loan Navigator Act, now has a version in the Senate. S. 5703 was introduced by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD) and Thom Tillis (R-NC) today to help veterans better access and use their VA home loan benefits by providing free, independent guidance and counseling. The House version of the bill was introduced on July 1, 2026, by Congresswoman Escobar and Republican Congressman Jack Bergman (MI-01).

The VA Home Loan Navigator Act would establish a voluntary borrower support program within the Department of Veterans Affairs that connects veterans with free, qualified housing counselors trained to help veterans navigate the benefit. This bill builds on a proven model already used throughout the VA benefits system, extending independent assistance to veterans utilizing one of the most important benefits they have earned through military service. Additionally, the legislation includes strong independence and conflict-of-interest protections and provides VA enforcement authority to ensure compliance.

“Too often, veterans seeking home loans face confusion, misinformation, and predatory scams," said Congresswoman Escobar. "My bipartisan bill extends the same kind of support available for other VA benefits to the home loan program, giving veterans access to free, independent guidance when buying, refinancing, or fighting to stay in their homes. Our veterans and their families have sacrificed so much for our country; ensuring their much deserved benefits are working the way they're intended to is the least we can do. I can see no more fitting day for my Senate colleagues to introduce their version than today."

“We have an obligation to do more than say thank you to those who served our country. Our veterans deserve access to affordable, quality health care, to be able to afford groceries and gas, and be able to buy a home. I am so proud to partner with my colleague Senator Tillis to introduce this critical legislation that will support veterans through the mortgage and loan process and make the American dream of owning a home a reality for those who have served our country,” said Senator Alsobrooks.

“Our veterans have earned the opportunity to achieve the American dream of owning a home and we have a responsibility to ensure they have the resources and support they need to make it happen. The VA Home Loan Navigator Act will provide veterans with free, trusted guidance to help navigate the homebuying and mortgage process, understand their benefits, and address challenges that could put their homes at risk. I’m proud to partner with Senator Alsobrooks on this bipartisan effort to protect our veterans and ensure they receive the benefits they have earned through their service to our nation,” said Senator Tillis.

“Our Veterans earned the VA Home Loan benefit through their service, but too many still face unnecessary confusion when trying to use it,” said Rep. Bergman. “This important legislation helps ensure our Veterans have the same trusted support they've long relied on for other VA benefits, making it easier for them to achieve and protect the American dream of homeownership.”

The VA Home Loan Navigator Act would provide services at no cost to borrowers, including:

Education on VA home loan benefits

Assistance obtaining or resolving issues with certificates of eligibility

Counseling on homebuying, refinancing, and closing

Guidance on appraisal requirements, property standards, and loan documentation

Assistance with loan servicing matters

Counseling on loss mitigation and foreclosure prevention

Coordination between borrowers, mortgage servicers, and the VA, and

Education on housing costs, fees, and financial obligations.

The VA Home Loan Navigator Act is endorsed by the Veterans Housing & Financial Alliance (VHFA) and Vietnam Veterans of America.

title: Figures Marks Veterans Day, Bipartisan Bill to Establish Tuskegee Airmen Memorial in DC Gains Momentum
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, in recognition of Veterans Day, Congressman Shomari C. Figures announced that his bipartisan legislation to establish a monument in Washington, DC, to honor the Tuskegee Airmen has reached 56 cosponsors, including 21 Republicans, and the Chairman and Ranking Member of the House Committee on Armed Services. The memorial will serve as an educational resource, designed to teach future generations about one of the greatest, most well-decorated fighting forces in our nation’s history, and to highlight the important roles that Black military pilots and support personnel played in World War II.

They played a pivotal role in the Allied victory in World War II and paved the way for the desegregation of our military. Their contributions and sacrifice deserve to be memorialized in our nation's capital.”

Congressman Figures’ legislation – the Tuskegee Airmen Memorial Act – would authorize Tuskegee Airmen, Incorporated to establish a memorial on federal land in the District of Columbia. Authorization is an essential, required first step towards making this memorial a reality. Tuskegee Airmen, Incorporated is a national nonprofit founded to preserve the history and achievements of the original Tuskegee Airmen and engage with youth to inspire future careers in aviation.

title: Gallagher Introduces Legislation to Cut Building Costs and Strengthen Disaster Resilience
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (CA-01) introduced the Promoting Resilient Buildings Act, legislation to reduce costly federal red tape and give communities greater flexibility when adopting building codes to protect homes against natural disasters. The bill would help communities strengthen disaster resilience without imposing unnecessary costs on homebuilders and families already struggling with California's housing affordability crisis.

Under current federal law, FEMA's pre-disaster hazard mitigation program recognizes the latest published editions of relevant building codes and standards. Gallagher's legislation would expand that definition to include the two most recently published editions, allowing communities greater flexibility to qualify under the program while maintaining strong building safety standards.

“California is already one of the most expensive places in the country to build a home, and the last thing we need is Washington making it even harder,” said Congressman Gallagher. “We know firsthand in Northern California how devastating wildfires can be. We need homes that can withstand these disasters, but we also need working families to be able to afford them. This bill is a commonsense solution that gives our communities more flexibility without sacrificing safety.”

For communities throughout Northern California still recovering from devastating wildfires, rebuilding homes remains a major challenge. Rising construction costs and regulatory burdens have made it increasingly difficult for families to rebuild and for communities to expand their housing supply.

The Promoting Resilient Buildings Act would allow communities to use either of the two most recent editions of applicable consensus-based building codes and standards for purposes of FEMA's pre-disaster hazard mitigation program. The legislation preserves state and local authority over building code adoption and does not change requirements for other federal disaster assistance programs.

Gallagher's legislation reflects the amended version of the bipartisanSenate bill, S. 388, which advanced through the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee under Chairman Rand Paul (R-KY). The legislation has earned support from the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB), which represents the interests of America's homebuilding industry.

“NAHB commends Rep. Gallagher for introducing this important legislation to strengthen disaster resilience while keeping housing affordable. By recognizing the two most recent editions of relevant codes and standards for FEMA’s pre-disaster hazard mitigation program, this bill encourages communities to adopt updated building codes that improve resilience while considering costs and local needs. This practical approach preserves state and local control over code adoption and helps communities better protect families and their homes,” said Bill Owens, Chairman of the National Association of Home Builders.

“Families in places like Paradise have already paid an enormous price because of devastating wildfires,” Gallagher continued. “We should be making it easier to build safer homes and bring down costs, not forcing communities to choose between affordability and disaster preparedness. That's exactly what this legislation aims to accomplish.”

The Promoting Resilient Buildings Act is part of Gallagher's ongoing efforts to make housing more affordable for California families while supporting disaster preparedness and recovery throughout the North State.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Introduces Legislation to Close Gambling Loophole in Medicaid Work Requirements
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) introduced the No Gambling for Medicaid Act, legislation to close a loophole that allows Medicaid recipients to meet new work requirements through gambling winnings instead of actual employment. Under current rules, someone could report $580 in gambling winnings, even if they lost more than they won, and potentially keep their coverage for another six months without working a single hour.

“If we're going to have Medicaid work requirements, I think it's reasonable to expect people to actually work,” said Congressman Harrigan. “But somehow, under the current rules, you can meet that requirement by winning $580 gambling. You don't have to work a single hour, and it doesn't even matter if you lost more money than you won. Someone could even place bets on both sides of the same game, walk away with almost no losses and still satisfy the requirement. I can't imagine that was what Congress had in mind when we passed these reforms. Medicaid is funded by hardworking taxpayers, and we owe it to them to make sure the rules actually mean something. My bill fixes a loophole that never should have been there in the first place, and frankly, I don't know why this would be controversial.”

“Medicaid’s community engagement requirement can be a powerful tool for helping recipients move toward self-sufficiency. Congressman Harrigan’s No Gambling for Medicaid Act would strengthen the requirement by closing the gambling loophole, preventing abuse of the program and helping more struggling Americans experience the dignity of work,” said Kevin Corinth, Daniel C. Searle Chair and Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute.

"APP is pleased to endorse the No Gambling for Medicaid Act. Gambling addictions have destroyed too many relationships, families, and lives; this bill corrects an oversight that should be common sense. We need to be protecting families from this predatory industry, not giving them twisted incentives to risk money they don't have to qualify for healthcare. We thank Rep. Harrigan for his important work to address this issue,” said Terry Schilling, APP President.

The new Medicaid work requirements, set to take effect January 1, 2027, allow recipients to qualify by earning the equivalent of 80 hours at the federal minimum wage each month. However, the current income calculation counts gambling winnings without deducting losses. The No Gambling for Medicaid Act would exclude those winnings from the calculation, while keeping an exception for people who gamble professionally as a regular business.

The legislation would amend the Social Security Act to address the loophole before the new requirements take effect in 2027. Following its introduction, the bill will be referred to the appropriate House committee for consideration.

title: Huffman, Colleagues Demand Answers on Trump Admin Effort to Gut Endangered Wildlife Protections
text:
Lawmakers warn administration’s changes would leave protected species vulnerable to foreseeable deaths and habitat destruction

Washington, D.C. – Today, House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-Mich.) and Don Beyer (D-Va.), and Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) led 37 other Democratic lawmakers in demanding answers from Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on the Trump administration’s attempts to gut core Endangered Species Act (ESA) protections by reinterpreting what the agencies consider “incidental take” and “harm” in memoranda to federal employees.

The lawmakers warned the reinterpretation would strip protections from wildlife killed or injured by otherwise lawful activities, even when those deaths and injuries could be foreseen. Under the administration’s interpretation, the law’s prohibition on killing or injuring protected wildlife would apply only when someone deliberately targets a protected species. The lawmakers warned this would undermine decades of safeguards that allow economic activity to proceed while requiring commonsense steps to prevent wildlife deaths and injuries.

“For decades, the ESA has provided a framework for allowing economic activity to proceed while requiring reasonable measures to avoid and minimize harm to threatened and endangered species. These memoranda would undermine that framework by removing incentives to prevent foreseeable wildlife deaths and injuries,” the lawmakers wrote.

The letter challenges two identical internal memos issued September 14 by U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Director Brian Nesvik and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration General Counsel John Luce. The memos direct staff to interpret “take” — which includes killing or injuring protected wildlife — as covering only intentional actions targeting those animals. The lawmakers are demanding an explanation of the legal basis for that interpretation and whether activities that could foreseeably kill or injure endangered species still require permits.

The directives came as the Trump administration eliminated the longstanding regulatory definition of “harm,” which covered habitat destruction that kills or injures protected wildlife. Both changes took effect the same day, threatening protections for endangered animals and the places they need to survive.

“Any reinterpretation that could eliminate protections for these species is a serious and troubling departure from that framework and would undermine the law’s implementation,” the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers requested responses by November 30, 2026, including what protections would remain for species threatened by habitat destruction and whether states and Tribes were consulted. They also asked whether Interior would suspend implementation until it publicly explains its legal reasoning and assesses the consequences for endangered wildlife.

“The Services must abandon this approach and preserve the ESA’s longstanding protections for threatened and endangered wildlife and the communities that depend on them,” the lawmakers concluded.

Additional House signers included Representatives Becca Balint (D-Vt.), Suzanne Bonamici (D-Ore.), Julia Brownley (D-Calif.), Ed Case (D-Hawaii), Steve Cohen (D-Tenn.), Jasmine Crockett (D-Texas), Diana DeGette (D-Colo.), Mark DeSaulnier (D-Calif.), Sarah Elfreth (D-Md.), Dwight Evans (D-Pa.), Glenn Ivey (D-Md.), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.), Mike Levin (D-Calif.), Sarah McBride (D-Del.), Dave Min (D-Calif.), Kevin Mullin (D-Calif.), Frank Pallone Jr. (D-N.J.), Scott Peters (D-Calif.), Emily Randall (D-Wash.), Deborah Ross (D-N.C.), Mary Gay Scanlon (D-Pa.), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), Dina Titus (D-Nev.), Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), Jill Tokuda (D-Hawaii), and Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-Fla.).

ERROL LOUIS: I’m Errol Louis, coming to you tonight from Washington, DC. I spent the day on Capitol Hill, where dozens of newly elected Members of Congress are in town for orientation. And earlier today I sat down with Representative Hakeem Jeffries, the Leader of the House Democrats, who is poised to become the next Speaker of the House. Jeffries would be the first Speaker from New York City and the first Black Speaker. We talked about how Democrats won back the House with the largest majority in decades. And how he plans to take on the Trump administration, including a vote on possibly impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

ERROL LOUIS: Let’s talk about the great game. The big news of the day is that one of your Republican colleagues, Thomas Massie of Kentucky, has introduced articles of impeachment against the Secretary of Defense, Pete Hegseth. That’s for unauthorized military actions in Iran, Yemen, Venezuela, extrajudicial military killings, civilian casualties in Iran, et cetera, et cetera, et cetera. Procedurally, what happens now?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, Republicans will likely move to try to either refer the resolution to the Judiciary Committee or table it as a way not to have to vote on the substance. Pete Hegseth has abused his power, undermined America’s national security and gotten us involved in this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran. So I’m a hard Yes on the Hegseth impeachment resolution, and believe that there will be strong Democratic support for that resolution passing.

ERROL LOUIS: Is it the choice of the current Speaker whether or not to table it as opposed to letting it go to the Floor for a vote?

LEADER JEFFRIES: That’s correct. So the majority has the ability to control the Floor in this regard and has the ability to bring a motion to table or a motion to refer, and it’s our understanding that’s what’s going to happen. Now, if Pete Hegseth was an honorable individual, which he’s not, in terms of how he’s conducted himself up until this point, and this is the most unqualified so-called Secretary of Defense in American history, he’s been a disaster. He should have just stepped down, as opposed to putting the country through this type of proceeding when it’s all unnecessary, given the fact that we know at the end of the day Pete Hegseth is not going to be around for much longer.

ERROL LOUIS: What makes you so sure of that?

LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s my view that Donald Trump is, at some point, going to make the decision that Pete Hegseth’s continued presence is a liability as we transition from where we are right now to where we will be in the next Congress, given how decisively MAGA extremism has been eradicated. Along with Stephen Miller, Pete Hegseth is the poster child for MAGA extremism and for the incredible amount of cruel overreach that has taken place over the last two years, and so it doesn’t make a lot of sense to me for Pete Hegseth to be sticking around.

ERROL LOUIS: If it’s tabled and the 119th Congress expires and the new Democratic majority comes into power, would you then, what, just move it to the Floor for a vote?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’ll put that in the hands of the soon-to-be Chair of the Judiciary Committee, Jamie Raskin, as to what the proper procedure will be. But I think you’re going to see over 200 Democrats go on record this week making it clear that Pete Hegseth has got to go.

ERROL LOUIS: Is the idea simply to remove him, or is this leverage to begin winding down the war?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we have to end the reckless and costly war of choice. This is a war that we should have never gotten into. It’s undermined America’s national security. Iran is stronger now than before the war started. There’s no exit strategy. Donald Trump and Republicans promised not to start endless wars, but to stop them, and then turned around and have gotten us involved in an endless war in the Middle East. And we know that the war is directly connected to dramatically increasing the high cost of living, dramatically increasing gas prices and fertilizer prices, food prices and diesel costs.

ERROL LOUIS: The other thing going on right now is there’s a lot of hustle and bustle and new signs going up all around the Capitol. We noticed on your desk—we were poking around before you got here—that you have a copy of the rules of the House, I guess the operational Bible, you have a copy of the Christian Bible, the actual Bible and sort of face book-type pages with the faces of all these brand new Members you’re dealing with. As of today, what is the size of the Democratic majority—

LEADER JEFFRIES: So, right now—

ERROL LOUIS: —of the next Congress?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Right now, we’re looking at 258 seats and counting. There are about four seats right now that we’re tracking. We think it’s more likely than not that we get to at least 260. Right now at 258, it’s the largest majority that either party has had this century and one of the largest incoming classes since 1974, the Watergate class. These are extraordinary Americans. We have pastors and combat veterans, drill instructors, we have police officers, firefighters, smokejumpers, doctors, nurses, union leaders, teachers and even a Tejano music superstar, Bobby Pulido, who’s going to have to briefly leave orientation to go to the Latin Grammy Awards because he’s been nominated.

ERROL LOUIS: How about that? Well, give us a sense of your personal role in the campaign to win this very diverse incoming class in this new majority. I read—it was reported that you visited 50 cities in the last year. Is that right?

LEADER JEFFRIES: That’s probably correct—cities, towns and counties. And I had the opportunity to spend time with and campaign for a lot of our frontline Members who are in battleground districts all across the country. We didn’t lose a single Democratic incumbent. That rarely, if ever, happens, but we were able to pull that off. And I’m so thankful for all of the returning Members of Congress who made the decision, even though more than a dozen of them were drawn into gerrymandered districts designed to stop them from gaining reelection. They didn’t run away from the fight. They ran toward the fight, and every single one prevailed. We also were able to collectively recruit an incredible group of candidates, as I talked about, people with real, authentic life experiences. And that combination of authenticity and the clarity by which they communicated—all of us lifting up the message of the need to aggressively address the affordability crisis and, at the same time, make sure we visit upon those who have unleashed unprecedented corruption on the American people accountability. That clarity of message carried by our candidates and articulated by all of us here in Washington, I think, was very important in setting up the contrast about where we are right now, this national nightmare, and where we need to go, making sure America is the best version of herself.

ERROL LOUIS: Prior to Election Day, when asked, you told reporters to keep an eye on the Sixth District in Kentucky. What was that race about, and what makes it representative of the kind of campaign that you just came out of?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, Zach Dembo’s a great candidate. Andy Beshear, the current Governor of Kentucky, flagged that race for us early. It’s a district that Donald Trump won comfortably all three times by north of 15 points. But the Governor said we could win. The incumbent was running for the Senate. It was an open seat. We had a strong recruit in Zach Dembo, and he was able to pull it off. Now, one of the reasons why I thought it was important to watch Kentucky-6 also is because polls closed in Kentucky at about 6 p.m. So, other than Guam, which is in a different time zone situation. And by the way, we flipped the seat in Guam as well. We found out about that race literally before noon on Election Day. But we knew that, of the races that everyone would be following, that Kentucky-6 was going to be one of the earliest ones. And along with our flip in Indiana—because the polls in Indiana also closed early, around 6—those were sort of the early races to track.

ERROL LOUIS: So you knew at that point it was going to be a wave election and a great night for Democrats?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Once I saw what was happening in Indiana and Kentucky, and before the races were called, but the returns that were coming in—I said, ‘Okay, this is an early foundation for what is emerging into a big night for America and a big night for House Democrats.’ And then when we saw that we were up in all four of the gerrymandered districts in Florida, because the polls also closed early in Florida in most of the state at 7 p.m., it reaffirmed that we were on a very positive trajectory because we knew that there was no path toward Republicans maintaining their narrow majority if they didn’t flip the gerrymandered seats that were redrawn to stop Democrats from being successful. And we had three incumbents in Florida all drawn into incredibly tough districts that Donald Trump won by a significant amount nine, ten points or more—and they’ve all prevailed.

ERROL LOUIS: You personally pressured or recruited someone to try and run in one of those gerrymandered districts, right?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, Pia Dandiya emerged as a great candidate. We got behind her early, even before the primary, which in Florida is late, but we identified her as a great candidate. She’s actually someone who has ties to New York City, started a school as a founding principal in the South Bronx and is raising her family now in South Florida. She went from the South Bronx to South Florida, and now she’s on her way to Congress, so she’s an extraordinary leader.

[…]

ERROL LOUIS: There are these online petitions going around saying that not much more than Jeffries should not be Speaker, call your Member of Congress. They say that. Well, are you hearing from Members? Are they actually jamming the phone lines here? What are you hearing?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Yeah, there’s no indication that Members of Congress have been overwhelmed by any calls. And I think that I’m going to continue to make the case in my conversations with every single member of the Caucus, interested in talking about both the track record that has gotten us here, but more importantly, what we hope to do for the American people in the new Congress and beyond, where we really are going to fight hard to deliver. The American people voted for dramatic change, bold change and transformational change. And we have a responsibility to do everything that we can to improve their high quality of life in all of the areas in ways that they haven’t been experiencing. And it’s unacceptable that you have so many people who are working hard, they’re playing by the rules, they can’t thrive and they can barely survive in New York and all across the country, and we’ve got to turn that around.

ERROL LOUIS: Well, but let’s stick for a minute on the subject of your—the vote for the speakership, which I think is going to happen next week.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Next week.

ERROL LOUIS: Right. Do you have any challengers?

LEADER JEFFRIES: No.

ERROL LOUIS: Okay. And it’s not that you haven’t heard of—there just are none at this point.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Yeah, well, right at this point, someone could always emerge within the next week or so, but right now there are no declared challengers, no indication that anyone may put themselves forward.

ERROL LOUIS: So I mean, an online petition with a million signatures or digital signatures, whatever it may be, does that impact the process at all? What do you make of that?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Yeah, well, actually, I think Members of Congress, at all times, in any of the decisions that they make, are going to really be substantive about, whether it’s the legislative agenda, or the elevation of people to any leadership positions, and think about everything and talk about everything and communicate about everything. And so, I look forward to talking to every single member of the House Democratic Caucus, whether they are a returning Member or incoming Members. And I’ve had the opportunity to talk to a whole bunch about a lot of different things, largely focused on making sure I get to know them, get to know their districts and get to know what they hope to accomplish on behalf of the people that they’re privileged to serve because we want everybody to be successful.

ERROL LOUIS: What’s the etiquette with that? Do they call you, do you call them?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I’ve sat down with a lot of Members to congratulate them, who made their way through the primary process, and then, of course, am working through sitting down and talking to folks who just flipped seats literally a week ago in such an overwhelming number. And now, many of them I spent time getting to know on the campaign trail and campaigned with them, but I haven’t been able to meet everybody on the campaign trail because the numbers now have been so broad and overwhelming. But it’s exciting. I’m looking forward to continuing to talk to them. Everyone is here to serve their communities. The depth and breadth of the victory, and the people who are being sent to Congress, is so extraordinary. We’ve got an awesome responsibility now to deliver.

ERROL LOUIS: So, help me calibrate this. No false modesty, I’ve known you for a long time. But my understanding of a wave election like this, and you said it ranks with the Watergate year in 1974. There’s an argument in 1974 that Richard Nixon helped bring that wave about. It was revulsion at the Watergate scandal and the abuses of that administration. There’s a similar argument now that Donald Trump brought this wave, or at least made it 10 feet higher than it would have been otherwise. There are ultra-progressives and socialists who are saying this was our victory, we brought the message of affordability, we put the boots on the ground, we helped make this happen. And so, as they say, success has a thousand fathers. You’re clearly one of those fathers. But what happened here? Put this in some perspective.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I think, listen, it’s everyone’s victory. Most importantly, it’s a victory for the American people. And never count the American people out when it comes to making sure that when the country is facing significant turbulence, we can turn things around, because everyday Americans are going to stand up and show up and speak up for what they believe to be right, to end this national nightmare that we’ve been in for the last few years and to demand that we have a country that’s the best version of herself. As House Democrats, we knew that we were on the front line of the battle for the heart and soul of this country beginning in January of 2025, particularly when we saw all of the extremism that Donald Trump, through shock and awe, muzzle velocity, flood the zone, that strategy was designed to cause the American people to step back. But collectively, we didn’t step back, we fought back. We battled the Republicans and the Trump administration on every issue—battled them on the One Big Ugly Bill, battled them on the Medicaid cuts, battled them on ICE funding, battled them on the tariffs, battled them on the Affordable Care Act tax credits and their refusal to extend healthcare to tens of millions of Americans, certainly battled them on Epstein transparency, battled them on their gerrymandering scheme and defeated them all across the country.

ERROL LOUIS: So when your critics say that Jeffries is too timid, I don’t know if they think that the job of a Speaker is literally to speak, and that you should be judged based on your TV appearances or your social media feed. But what’s your answer to people who say that this is not the man for the moment?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I think the track record speaks for itself in terms of what we’ve been able to do to get from where we are, where people declared the Democratic Party dead and House Democrats in the wilderness, to where we are today, the most significant majority that either party has had in the 21st Century. And so, we’ve come a long way, but we also recognize that we still have a long way to go. And at the end of the day, criticism comes with the territory, it comes with the job. That’s just the reality of the situation.

ERROL LOUIS: Hey, you sit on the throne, right? This is what happens, right? People will throw rocks at it. Let me, we’re almost out of time, but there are some progressives in the party who are, there seems to be a split within the party, let’s say, around military aid to Israel. Will that get an early vote? What is your thinking about how you plan to steer that question?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Yeah. Well, one of the things that I said in July is that we’ve got to reset the relationship in terms of how assistance is provided moving forward as we navigate the end of the Memorandum of Understanding that was originally entered into in 2016 when Barack Obama was President. And we’re going to do that together as a Caucus and as a Congress. Clearly, dramatic change is necessary, and I’ve repeatedly made that point clear, including in July in a letter to the Caucus. We also foundationally have to make sure that we can continue to uplift two principles: a safe and secure Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, living side by side in peace and prosperity and safety and security with an independent Palestinian state that provides dignity and self-determination to the Palestinian people. And for far too long, I think policymakers have walked away from aggressively leaning in to bringing that two-state solution to life. I think it’s a responsibility of all of us so that we can get to a just and lasting peace, that that’s our North Star as we move forward in the new Congress.

ERROL LOUIS: There’s a new Chief of Staff at the White House. I heard some pretty strong statements from you, but realistically, aren’t you going to have to deal with Stephen Miller?

LEADER JEFFRIES: There’s no circumstances where I’ll deal with Stephen Miller based on his track record. He’s the architect of the violent mass deportation machine that literally has allowed billions of taxpayer dollars to brutalize and kill American citizens—

ERROL LOUIS: But if you call the White House—

LEADER JEFFRIES: —and violently target law-abiding immigrant families.

ERROL LOUIS: If you call the White House and you’ll have reason to, literally, if it’s not him personally, his people are going to answer the phone.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’ll figure that out.

ERROL LOUIS: Have you talked to Donald Trump?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I have not talked to the President or the Vice President. Listen, in the past, either the Chief of Staff or the Vice President—this has happened whether you had Democrats or Republicans in the White House—have been a key point of interacting with the American people’s representatives here in Congress. And so, I don’t have much of a relationship with the Vice President either, but certainly to the extent that we need to deal with the administration, there will be options beyond Stephen Miller.

ERROL LOUIS: Okay, I will leave you to that. The Property Clause of the Constitution, which almost nobody knows about, because we haven’t seen it invoked, but Congress has pretty sweeping, pretty final and clear authority over all public lands and buildings and properties. What will that mean for the various projects that President Trump has going on all around the city, where you can see the Reflecting Pool and the ballroom and these other things?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, it’s a very important provision in the Constitution. And you’re absolutely right, it’s been overlooked by this current Republican-controlled Congress because you’ve got folks who have been behaving like a reckless rubber stamp for Donald Trump’s extreme agenda, as opposed to actually Congress functioning like a separate and co-equal branch of government and a check and balance on an out-of-control executive branch. And so, I think both from an appropriation standpoint, where Congress, of course, pursuant to the Constitution, has the power of the purse and as it relates to the property provision in the Constitution, where authority is clearly delineated to the Congress for the oversight and management of public property and public land, you can expect a very different and aggressive approach that House Democrats will take to make sure that our taxpayer dollars aren’t being spent on vanity projects, but are being spent to make life more affordable for the American people.

ERROL LOUIS: Okay, we’ll let you get to it.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Errol, thank you, man.

ERROL LOUIS: Thanks very much. Good to see you.

title: Kelly votes for sweeping bipartisan veterans' healthcare & benefits legislation
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Today, U.S. Rep. Mike Kelly (R-PA) voted in favor of H.R. 9237, the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act, a comprehensive package of nearly 60 bipartisan bills that make up the largest veterans' healthcare and benefits expansion in decades. Kelly is an original co-sponsor of the bill. The legislation passed by voice vote.

The legislation protects veterans' healthcare access in communities nationwide, cuts red tape in the Department of Veterans Affairs' disability benefits system, and opens the door for more economic opportunities for veterans.

"No veteran should have to cut through red tape to receive basic services. The Take Care of America's Veterans Act puts veterans first, and I'm proud to support it. This sweeping legislation delivers on the promises House Republicans have made to support our entire veteran community," said Rep. Kelly.

Pennsylvania's 16th Congressional District is home to more than 45,000 civilian veterans, according to U.S. Census data.

The Take Care of America's Veterans Act includes:

Major Richard Star Act -- Concurrent VA and Dept. of War benefits receipt issue for medically retired disabled veterans

Veterans’ ACCESS Act -- Rural and urban healthcare access when VA wait times are too high – longstanding GOP and President Trump promise

Briley-Edmundson Benefits Expansion Act -- Benefits increase for severely disabled veterans and Gold Star families

Fox Grants Reauthorization -- Community-based mental health and suicide prevention – longstanding GOP initiative

BEACON Act -- Expand non-pharmacological treatments for veterans with TBI and mental health

VA facility construction reform -- To cut out red tape and ensure VA is delivering for veteran constituents in each member’s congressional district

Improvements to veteran caregiver support, mental health care, VA workforce recruitment and retention, appointment scheduling, rural healthcare access, service dog access, transition assistance to civilian life for servicemembers, and Gold Star survivor benefits.

Organizations supporting the Take Care of America's Veterans Act include:

Americans for Prosperity, Concerned Veterans for America, Veteran Action, The American Legion, Military Officers Association of America (MOAA), Wounded Warrior Project, Elizabeth Dole Foundation, Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors (TAPS), American Veterans (AMVETS), Air Force Sergeants Association, American Optometric Association, Avalon Action Alliance, Commissioned Officers Association of the USPHS (COA), Gold Star Spouses of America, K9s For Warriors, Korean War Veterans Association, Military Chaplains Association, Military Order of the Purple Heart (MOPH), Mission Roll Call, National Defense Committee, National Military Family Association (NMFA), USCG Chief Petty Officers Association (CPOA), Vietnam Veterans of America

title: Rep. Kelly Cosponsors Bipartisan Resolution Honoring America's Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- This week, U.S. Representative Mike Kelly (R-PA) co-sponsored a bipartisan resolution introduced by U.S. Representatives Michael Guest (R-MS) and Susie Lee (D-NV) honoring the service and sacrifice of America's veterans ahead of Veterans Day on November 11, 2026.

The resolution recognizes the heroic actions of American veterans who have defended our nation and protected the freedoms enjoyed by generations of Americans. It also calls on the American people to observe Veterans Day in recognition of the courage, dedication, and sacrifices of those who have served in the United States Armed Forces.

"Veterans Day is an opportunity for all Americans to come together and honor the brave men and women who have answered the call to serve our great nation," said Rep. Kelly. "Generations of American service members have made tremendous sacrifices to defend our freedoms and protect our way of life. I am proud to support this bipartisan resolution recognizing their service, and I remain committed to ensuring our veterans receive the recognition, care, and benefits they have earned."

Originally recognized as Armistice Day to commemorate the end of World War I on November 11, 1918, Veterans Day has since become a national observance honoring all Americans who have served in the United States military.

As the nation celebrates its 250th anniversary, the resolution highlights the generations of Americans who have served with distinction, from the battlefields of World War II, Korea, and Vietnam to the Gulf War and the Global War on Terrorism. It also recognizes the continued sacrifices of service members defending American interests around the world today.

The bipartisan resolution is supported by more than 100 cosponsors in the U.S. House of Representatives.

title: Rep. Latimer Votes to Protect Veterans Benefits
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, the bipartisan Major Richard Star Act passed the House following a discharge petition with more than 218 signatures, forcing it to be brought to the floor for a vote. Congressman George Latimer voted YES to move this important legislation to the Senate.

The Major Richard Star Act would fix the Wounded Warrior Tax, allowing veterans to receive both full military retirement pay and full VA disability compensation concurrently.

On Veterans Day, House Republicans clandestinely fast-tracked the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act for adoption by voice vote, so no members were on the record voting for or against this bill. This bill included the Major Richard Star Act; however, it also included the largest cut to veterans’ benefits in history, with more than $57 million cut in disability compensation for future veterans, elimination of tinnitus as a stand-alone disability, and a decrease in disability compensation for veterans seeking treatment for sleep apnea.

House Democrats delivered for veterans by bringing the Major Richard Star Act to the floor as a standalone bill to ensure veterans receive their earned benefits, without cutting critical programs.

"Veterans Day should be a time to honor those who served, not a time to dismantle their benefits," said Rep. Latimer. "I am proud that the Major Richard Star Act has passed the House as a standalone bill and will ensure our veterans receive the support they need when dealing with combat-related disabilities. I remain committed to delivering for veterans and their families, and I will continue to work to honor those who sacrificed for our country.”

title: REP LIEU COMMEMORATES VETERANS DAY
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Ted W. Lieu (D-Los Angeles County) honors those who have served and sacrificed as members of our nation’s Armed Forces. Last weekend, Congressman Lieu marked Veterans Day with his annual “Conversations with Veterans” where he creates a forum to allow veterans from California’s 36th congressional district to share their stories. Congressman Lieu invited non-veteran members of the community to attend the event to foster understanding and connection among veterans and those for whom they served. This year’s event was held virtually.

“It was an honor to host this annual gathering and hear directly from the veterans in our community about their experiences and sacrifices. I will always fight for them and their families to ensure they receive the care and benefits they earned in service,” said Congressman Lieu. “Every veteran has a story worth hearing. It is important that we take the time to listen. Below are just of few of the many stories shared by our district’s veterans. Happy Veterans Day!”

Michael Acosta, Marine Corps

Early in my training, I depended on the Marines beside me, and in combat we trusted one another with our lives. That responsibility didn’t end when I took the uniform off. Today, that mission looks different, but the commitment remains the same.

Yesenia Rodriguezcarranza, Army

Before I got into the military, I never drank. But in the military, drinking was like a badge of honor ... So, I came home and I continued to abuse alcohol. The bottle was like my shield. I took a long, empty journey. I tried to commit suicide, and I was sent to the hospital. While in the hospital, I had an eye-opening experience that turned the light on in my eyes. And He gave me grace. I went from thinking I was the perfect child – there’s nothing wrong with me, it’s everybody else’s fault – to realizing that I was a hurt child and I needed help. It was a moment of clarity.

Kevin Butler, Coast Guard

My Coast Guard service taught me that serving others isn’t always about being on the front lines. Sometimes it’s being the calm voice on the radio making sure the right information gets to the right people and being ready when the unexpected happens. Nearly two decades after leaving the Coast Guard, those lessons remained at the center of my work. My uniform changed, the mission evolved, but responsibility never left.

Diego Huttepain, Army

During my time in the Army, I was sent to Army Ranger School. And I was able to graduate after spending 120 days there. Basically, it’s a leadership school where they starve, sleep deprive you, stress and push people to their limits. I remember seeing the different ways people reacted and interacted at their lowest points ... The program takes a major toll on your body. It’s hard to graduate, so less than 1 percent of the Army has graduated from Ranger school. But as a result, you learn a lot about yourself. When I made it through, I came to believe I could truly accomplish anything.

title: Rep. Lucas Urges Colleagues to Support 403(b) Legislation
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Representative Frank D. Lucas (OK-03), a member of the House Financial Services Committee and Chairman of the House Financial Services Task Force on Monetary Policy, Treasury Market Resilience, and Economic Prosperity, delivered remarks on the House floor urging his colleagues to support his Retirement Fairness for Charities and Educational Institutions Act, legislation that would allow public servants to have access to the same financial tools as private sector employees when planning for retirement.

Remarks as prepared for delivery:

I rise today in strong support of my bill, H.R. 1013, the Retirement Fairness for Charities and Educational Institutions Act.

This bipartisan legislation will allow our communities’ public servants, such as teachers, nurses, doctors, university professors, and employees of nonprofit organizations, to have the same financial tools available as the private sector when planning for their retirement.

For many of these public servants, their retirement savings are through a 403(b) plan. However, those public servants’ 403(b) plans are unable to invest in the same cost-effective investment products that are available to all other plans, like 401(k) plans.

Under current law, 403(b) plans generally cannot access the same collective investment trusts and insurance company separate accounts available to 401(k) plans.

Collective investment trusts allow retirement plans to pool their investments, providing access to institutional investment strategies at lower costs than many traditional mutual funds.

Similarly, insurance company separate accounts provide another avenue for retirement plans to access professionally managed investments, generally with lower administrative expenses.

The advantage is that these options can be less expensive to operate, leaving more of the investment’s return in the worker’s account.

Over the course of someone’s career, even small reductions in investment fees can translate into thousands of additional dollars in retirement savings.

Consider two Americans saving for retirement. One works for a private company and saves through a 401(k). The other works for a public school or nonprofit and saves through a 403(b).

Both are putting away their hard-earned money for retirement. But because of outdated restrictions, the worker with a 403(b) does not have access to some of the same lower-cost investment options.

This may seem like a small difference, but consider a public servant saving ten thousand dollars a year over a forty-year career.

Assuming a six percent annual return, paying just five basis points more in annual investment fees could cost that worker more than nineteen thousand dollars in retirement savings.

That’s a significant amount of money for someone who has spent their career serving their community.

Our public servants deserve better.

My legislation would give these workers access to the same investment options available to millions of other Americans.

This bill would not only provide a level playing field for workers, regardless of the type of retirement plan their employer sponsors, but would also allow our nonprofit institutions like hospitals, public schools, and charities to compete with the private sector for talent through their retirement plan offerings.

The effort to finally provide parity in retirement options for our public servants is a bipartisan one spanning several Congresses.

I am grateful to my colleagues on both sides of the aisle who have worked hard to ensure that those who serve our communities have equal access to save for retirement.

In the 117th Congress, the Ways and Means Committee unanimously passed this measure under former Chairman Neal’s leadership.

While only the tax code was ultimately fixed for 403(b) plans that year, it was a much-needed first step in correcting this disparity. That vote was nearly unanimous — 414-5.

I introduced this bill in the 118th Congress to finish the work that the Ways and Means Committee began and to correct the underlying securities laws.

In 2023, the Financial Services Committee favorably reported this bill for floor consideration with 35 yeas, and when I offered the measure as an amendment to a broader bill on the floor, it received overwhelming support of over 300 members.

This Congress’s Financial Services Committee again favorably reported this legislation with 43 yeas.

And just last December, the House once again passed this legislation as part of the INVEST Act, which received the support of over 300 members.

For several Congresses, this legislation has received bipartisan support in both committee and on the House floor. It is time we finish the work and ensure that teachers, nonprofit employees, and other public servants have access to the same retirement investment options as private-sector workers.

I urge my colleagues to support this bill so that the Americans who serve our communities can finally have the same retirement investment opportunities as every other worker.

title: Harris Applauds House Passage of Major Veterans’ Benefits Package on Veterans Day
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congressman Mark Harris (NC-08) applauded the House passage of H.R. 9237, the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act, a comprehensive legislative package of more than 60 bipartisan bills to expand veterans’ benefits, improve access to health care, strengthen support for military families, and modernize the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The legislation also includes reforms to reduce government bureaucracy and improve the delivery of services to our nation’s veterans.

“Our veterans have sacrificed so much in service to our country, and we have a responsibility to ensure they receive the care and benefits they have earned,” said Congressman Harris. “There could be no more fitting day than Veterans Day for House Republicans to pass legislation that strengthens health care, expands benefits for wounded veterans, and provides greater support for military families. We owe it to the brave men and women who have worn our nation’s uniform to keep the promises we have made to them.”

The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act includes provisions to:

Expand veterans’ benefits through the Major Richard Star Act, allowing eligible combat-injured, medically retired veterans to receive both their military retirement pay and VA disability benefits.

Improve access to health care by strengthening the Veterans Community Care Program, expanding rural health care services, and improving access to mental health and substance abuse treatment.

Support caregivers and survivors by expanding benefits for catastrophically disabled veterans, their caregivers, and Gold Star families, including protections for surviving spouses who remarry.

Strengthen education and employment opportunities by improving transition assistance, increasing housing allowances for eligible student veterans, and expanding access to career training.

Modernize VA operations by improving disability claims and appeals, strengthening accountability, and reducing unnecessary bureaucracy.

title: Harris Honors Our Nation’s Veterans on House Floor
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congressman Mark Harris (NC-08) delivered remarks on the House floor in recognition of Veterans Day, honoring the more than 38,000 veterans across North Carolina’s Eighth District and the millions of men and women who have served our nation. Harris reflected on the sacrifices made by veterans and their families and emphasized the importance of ensuring those who served receive the respect, care, and benefits they have earned.

Rep. Harris’s remarks as delivered:

“I rise today to honor the more than 38,000 veterans who call North Carolina’s Eighth District home, and the millions of brave men and women across our great nation who have proudly worn the uniform of the United States Armed Forces.

“From the battlefields of the Revolutionary War to the conflicts of today, generations of Americans have answered the call to serve, putting their lives on the line for the freedoms we hold dear.

“As the son of a World War II veteran, I know that the strength of our nation is rooted in the courage and character of those who have defended it.

“Our veterans come from every walk of life. Whether serving on the front lines in times of war or standing ready during times of peace, each shared a commitment to something greater than themselves.

“That commitment has often come at a tremendous personal cost. Some made the ultimate sacrifice and never returned home. Others returned carrying wounds, both seen and unseen. And for countless families, military service meant years apart, missed birthdays and holidays, and precious moments that could never be replaced.

“But their service does not end when they take off the uniform. Our veterans continue making a difference as teachers, first responders, business owners, and community leaders.

“Veterans Day is not simply a day of recognition. It is a reminder that the freedoms we enjoy were not freely given, and that our gratitude must extend far beyond a single day.

“So, to every veteran across North Carolina’s Eighth District and throughout our nation: thank you. Thank you for answering the call, for the sacrifices you have made, and for the example you have set for generations of Americans.

title: McGarvey, Luttrell Introduce Bill to Speed Up Healthcare Innovation for Veterans
text:
INNOVATE Act speeds up VA partnerships with private sector and invests in veteran-owned businesses to develop care by veterans, for veterans

WASHINGTON, D.C. (November 11, 2026) – Today, Congressmen Morgan McGarvey (KY-03) and Morgan Luttrell (TX-08) introduced the Innovation for VA Technology and Entrepreneurship (INNOVATE) Act, a bipartisan bill to strengthen the most innovative offices within the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and cut down on red tape that delays development of the newest treatments and technology for veterans’ healthcare.

As the largest integrated healthcare system in the country, serving more than 9 million veterans, VA is uniquely positioned to develop new treatments through public-private partnerships but struggles to meet the clinical demand of a growing and changing veteran population. Due to outdated bureaucratic hurdles at VA, it currently takes months or even years for the agency to partner with outside innovators.

“Veterans deserve the best and most cutting-edge care in the world,” said Congressman McGarvey. “We must leverage VA’s resources to speed up and encourage that innovation. Like DARPA did for the Defense Department, this bill gives VA the flexibility and agency to discover the newest treatments and keep up with veterans’ changing needs.”

“Innovative treatments shouldn’t be held up by years of red tape before they reach the veterans who need them,” said Congressman Luttrell. “The INNOVATE Act empowers the VA to partner with veteran-owned small businesses to speed up and optimize treatments. I thank Congressman McGarvey for his leadership and urge the passage of this bill.”

The INNOVATE Act would:

Give VA the same fast-track contracting tools and capabilities the Pentagon already uses to quickly collaborate with startups, researchers, and the broader healthcare industry to drive innovation toward veteran-centric solutions;

Prioritize collaboration with veteran-owned small businesses to invest in solutions made by veterans, for veterans, from concept to implementation;

Establish an “Office of Innovation” at the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) to invest in the development of technology the market hasn’t yet developed or optimized for veterans’ healthcare;

Empower the Office of Innovation to quickly and competitively hire the most qualified clinical and technical experts to provide innovative care and build cutting-edge solutions; and

Secure better prices and early access to technology VA helps develop with outside partners.

The INNOVATE Act is endorsed by American Legion, AMVETS (American Veterans), Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America, Veterans of Foreign Wars, Vietnam Veterans of America, and Wounded Warrior Project.

The full text of the bill can be found here.

###

Congressman Morgan McGarvey represents Kentucky’s Third Congressional District, including Louisville and Jefferson County. He serves on the House Veterans Affairs, Small Business, and Budget Committees.

title: McIver’s Bill on Veterans Small Businesses Passes House, On Veterans Day

title: Miller-Meeks Votes to Expand Care for Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks, M.D. (IA-01) voted to pass the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act (H.R. 9237), a sweeping, bipartisan package that expands health care access, strengthens disability and survivor benefits, and improves services for millions of America’s veterans and their families.

“Taking care of the men and women who have served our country is one of our most important responsibilities. Our veterans kept their promise to America, and we must keep our promise to them,” said Rep. Miller-Meeks. “This legislation makes meaningful improvements to the VA, expands access to health care, strengthens support for disabled veterans and their caregivers, and ensures our veterans and their families receive the benefits they have earned. As a 24-year Army veteran, I am proud to support this effort to put veterans first.”

The legislation includes nearly 60 bipartisan bills and represents one of the most significant expansions of veterans’ health care and benefits in decades. It delivers on our nation’s promise to ensure veterans receive the care, benefits, and support they have earned without unnecessary government bureaucracy.

Background

The Major Richard Star Act is included in H.R. 9237 and would allow thousands of combat-injured veterans to receive their full military retirement pay and VA disability compensation without an offset. This change would address a longstanding inequity for veterans who were medically retired before completing 20 years of service.

Congresswoman Miller-Meeks crossed party lines to vote in favor of the Major Richard Star Act as a standalone bill while also supporting a discharge petition to bring the legislation to the House floor for consideration.

title: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Demands RFK Jr. Address Significant Gaps in Coverage for Endometriosis and Pelvic Floor Dysfunction
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) led nine congressional colleagues in a letter to Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., urging the department to address significant gaps in insurance coverage for pelvic floor physical therapy (PFPT) for individuals with endometriosis, chronic pelvic pain, and related pelvic floor dysfunction.

Endometriosis affects an estimated 8.3 million women in the United States and is a leading cause of chronic pelvic pain, infertility, and disability among reproductive-aged women. Chronic pelvic pain affects an estimated 15–26% of U.S. women and is associated with substantial health care utilization, reduced workforce participation, and diminished quality of life.

Despite its prevalence, endometriosis is associated with an average diagnostic delay of approximately 7–10 years. During this period, many patients experience repeated health care visits, multiple diagnostic evaluations, escalating pain, worsening functional impairment, and delayed access to effective treatment.

Improving access to evidence-based conservative and rehabilitative treatments, including pelvic floor physical therapy, may help reduce this downstream burden while improving function and quality of life.

The Members wrote:

“Pelvic floor rehabilitation is commonly recognized as appropriate care for pelvic floor dysfunction associated with pregnancy, childbirth, and certain surgical procedures. Yet patients who experience significant pelvic floor dysfunction related to endometriosis—or following complex endometriosis excision surgery—may encounter visit limits, high cost-sharing, coverage denials, or difficulty locating an in-network pelvic floor physical therapist.”

“The underlying clinical need does not disappear because the cause of pelvic floor dysfunction is different. Federal policy for public insurers, and guidance to private insurers, should reflect functional impairment and medical necessity—not create different standards based primarily on how that impairment developed.”

“We therefore urge HHS to examine whether current coverage policies create an unintended disparity between postpartum pelvic rehabilitation and pelvic rehabilitation required following endometriosis treatment and excision surgery; and to clarify for public and private insurers that there should be parity in coverage for pelvic floor rehabilitation whether a patient is postpartum or impacted by endometriosis.”

This letter was co-signed by Rep. Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Rep. Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Rep. Debbie Dingell (MI-06), Rep. Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Rep. Kelly Morrison (MN-03), Rep. Brittany Pettersen (CO-07), Rep. Lateefah Simon (CA-12), and Rep. Melanie Stansbury (NM-01).

This letter was endorsed by American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, American End of Endo Project, The Center for Endometriosis Care, Endo Black Inc., Endo Excision for All, Endometriosis Foundation of America, Project Endo, The Village Consulting and Media, Women’s Health Advocates Endo & Adeno Coalition

title: House Passes Bipartisan Olszewski, Wied Bill to Help Small Businesses Bring Manufacturing Back to America
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – The U.S. House of Representatives today passed bipartisan legislation sponsored by Maryland Congressman Johnny Olszewski to help small businesses bring manufacturing operations back to the United States. The Reshoring American Manufacturing (RAM) Act passed in a voice vote and will now be considered by the U.S. Senate.

The RAM Act – introduced by Republican Congressman Tony Wied of Wisconsin and co-led by Congressman Olszewski – would create a central database to connect small businesses with information, programs, and verified U.S. manufacturers, producers, and suppliers as they explore opportunities to bring their manufacturing operations home.

“Bringing manufacturing back to America shouldn't be an opportunity only reserved for the biggest corporations,” said Congressman Olszewski, who serves on the House Committee on Small Businesses. “Small businesses are the backbone of our economy, and this bipartisan legislation will help connect them with the American manufacturing partners they need to grow. I'm grateful to Congressman Wied for his partnership and to my House colleagues for advancing this effort.”

While many large corporations have the resources and established networks to identify domestic manufacturing partners, smaller businesses often face greater barriers when exploring opportunities to reshore their operations. The RAM Act would require the Small Business Administration to establish, operate, and maintain a website providing small businesses with information about relevant federal resources, agencies, and potential domestic manufacturing partners.

“Reshoring manufacturing is critical for restoring our nation’s economic independence, maintaining global supply chain control, and supporting American workers,” said Congressman Wied. “This online portal gives small businesses the resources they need to reshore their operations and revitalize Made in America manufacturing. I am proud to see this legislation pass the House, and I urge the Senate to do the same to help bring American jobs back home and strengthen our economy.”

title: On Veterans Day, Olszewski, Bacon, McCollum Lead Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Operation Green Light
text:
(Washington, DC) – Congressman Johnny Olszewski (MD-02) today joined Congressman Don Bacon (NE-02) and Congresswoman Betty McCollum (MN-04) in introducing a bipartisan resolution recognizing Operation Green Light for Veterans, a national campaign that honors veterans and raises awareness of the local resources available to help them transition to civilian life.

Led by the National Association of Counties (NACo) and the National Association of County Veterans Service Officers (NACVSO), Operation Green Light for Veterans encourages counties, cities, businesses, and community members to illuminate buildings and landmarks in green in the days leading up to Veterans Day. The campaign serves as a visible reminder to veterans that their service is recognized, appreciated, and valued by the communities they served.

The resolution recognizes NACo and NACVSO for their leadership in organizing the nationwide campaign and encourages communities across the country to participate by lighting their buildings green from November 4 until November 11. It also calls on Members of Congress and local leaders to help raise awareness of the resources available to veterans and their families, including mental health services, employment and job training programs, housing assistance, and peer support.

“The men and women who have served our country deserve our support, opportunities and resources when they return home,” said Congressman Johnny Olszewski. “Operation Green Light is a visible way to show veterans that they are seen and valued. I'm proud to lead this bipartisan effort and am grateful to NACo and NACVSO for making this campaign a nationwide movement.”

“Our veterans have earned our gratitude and our commitment to ensuring they receive the support they deserve when they return home,” said Representative Bacon. “Operation Green Light is a simple but meaningful way to honor their service while raising awareness of the resources available to veterans and their families as they transition to civilian life. I'm grateful to Reps. Olszewski and McCollum for working with me on this bipartisan effort to recognize those who have served our country.”

“A green light may seem like a small gesture, but to a veteran transitioning into civilian life, it carries a powerful message: you are seen, your service matters, and you are not forgotten,” said Congresswoman Betty McCollum. “I am a cosponsor of the bipartisan resolution recognizing Operation Green Light for Veterans, because it literally shines a light about resources available for veterans. We have a responsibility to ensure our veterans connect with and receive the support they have earned. Just as our military leaves no service member behind on the battlefield, we must never leave our veterans behind when they return home. Honoring those who served requires more than words of gratitude; it requires action. This Veterans Day, let’s turn gratitude into action!”

Operation Green Light for Veterans was started by NACo and NACVSO in 2021 and has grown into a nationwide effort to recognize veterans and connect them with the services they have earned. Through partnerships with local governments and community organizations, the campaign also helps shine a light on the important role counties play in supporting veterans as they navigate the transition to civilian life.

“Every Veterans Day, counties across the country illuminate their buildings in green – the color of hope and renewal – to show our veterans that we see them,” said NACo Executive Director Matthew Chase. “Operation Green Light for Veterans demonstrates the ongoing commitment of America’s county leaders to provide year-round exceptional and accredited support to veterans so that they may access their earned benefits and thrive. Counties thank Representatives Olszewski, Bacon and McCollum for their support of Operation Green Light, and we welcome all public and private sector partners to join us in this endeavor.”

"Operation Green Light is a visual gesture of support for our veterans' service to their country and seeks to raise awareness around the unique challenges they face,” said Michael McLaughlin, 1st Vice President & Legislative Director, NACVSO. “Our goal is to ensure that every veteran knows that they have support and resources right in their local community. Operation Green Light reminds us that veterans' success is not exclusively a national cause; it is and must continue to be a local one too. NACVSO appreciates Representatives Olszewski's, Bacon's and McCollum's efforts to support and elevate Operation Green Light."

title: Congresswoman Pettersen Statement on Vote to Impeach Pete Hegseth
text:

title: In Response to Bombshell NYT Report, Pingree Slams ICE for Sending Agent Into Maine Communities Armed and Unvetted
text:
Congresswoman Chellie Pingree (D-Maine) released the following statement in response to a New York Times investigation revealing that ICE armed and deployed David Brouillette before reviewing his background check findings:

ICE handed David Brouillette a gun and sent him into Maine communities before anyone at the agency had reviewed his background check. The agency restricted his access to certain computer systems because he had not been fully cleared, yet apparently saw no problem trusting him with the power to take someone’s life. That is an unconscionable betrayal of the public’s trust.

Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero should be alive today. He was a young father, building a life for his family in Maine. He was following a lawful immigration process. His family will live with his loss forever. They deserve to know every decision that put Brouillette on the streets with a badge and a gun and deserve accountability for their tragic loss.

Journalists had already uncovered deeply disturbing allegations of violence and abuse against Brouillette. The Times now reveals further warning signs, including vile, racist comments about his own sister’s longtime Colombian partner. His own mother told the Times her son was dangerous and shouldn't have weapons. A thorough review could have brought these serious warning signs to light before ICE sent him out to carry out Stephen Miller’s aggressive immigration crackdown. The danger was foreseeable. Johan Sebastián’s death was preventable.

Who authorized his deployment? What would a thorough review have revealed? An agency whistleblower has already warned the DHS Inspector General of an "unprecedented lowering of standards.” How many other agents are carrying guns in our communities without completed vetting?

I have demanded answers from DHS about training and background checks in the days following Johan Sebastián’s death. This reporting makes a full, independent investigation even more urgent. DHS must release Brouillette’s hiring, vetting, training, and deployment records and cooperate fully with independent investigators.

ICE must be abolished and that is what I will continue to fight for. But perfect can’t get in the way of better. Until we can abolish ICE, this agency needs serious, immediate reforms. I am working on legislation to ensure federal agents are never armed and deployed into our streets without being fully vetted. Our communities’ safety cannot depend on whether this administration finds basic safeguards convenient.

Responsibility reaches beyond the officer who pulled the trigger. It extends to the leadership that armed and deployed him, and to an administration that put its deportation agenda ahead of human life. Every official responsible must be held accountable. Johan Sebastián’s family deserves justice, and I will keep fighting until they get it.
