title: Pressley Welcomes Fletcher as Co-Chair of Reproductive Freedom Caucus, Thanks DeGette For Yearslong Partnership
text:
Pressley & Fletcher to Co-Chair Caucus and Keep Abortion Rights Front and Center for Democrats in 120th Congress

WASHINGTON – Today, the Congressional Reproductive Freedom Caucus (RFC) announced Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07) will succeed retiring Congresswoman and Caucus Co-Chair Diana DeGette (CO-01), joining Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) as Co-Chair for the 120th Congress. Congresswoman Fletcher previously served as the Reproductive Freedom Caucus’s Whip and Vice Chair in the 118th and 119th Congresses, respectively, bringing years of leadership and experience to her new role. She has seen firsthand the devastating impacts of abortion bans on her constituents, and as the women of Texas stand up and demand change, she is ready to turn those demands into action.

As we look ahead to the 120th Congress, we also honor the legacy of Congresswoman Diana DeGette, who has led the Congressional Pro-Choice Caucus, now Reproductive Freedom Caucus, for over 26 years. Throughout her tenure, Congresswoman DeGette has been a steadfast champion for reproductive freedom, helping steer the fight for reproductive rights, justice, and health care access. Her decades of service will continue to shape the Caucus and the broader movement for reproductive freedom, moving us toward a brighter future for people across the country and globe.

The 2026 midterm elections sent a clear message: Americans are demanding reproductive freedom. Voters from Texas to Georgia, the Carolinas to Iowa, suffering under cruel abortion bans, made their voices heard at the ballot box and elected a new congressional majority committed to protecting their rights. These results affirm the continued importance of our fight in communities across the country and provide the first real opportunity since the disastrous Dobbs decision to counter the GOP’s extreme attacks on reproductive health care.

As we begin the 120th Congress, RFC and our Members are clear-eyed about the threats that remain to reproductive freedom, particularly from this administration. Whether from the White House or the Statehouse, we will face continued attacks on patients’ rights and efforts to restrict essential reproductive health care. Our work is far from over. With a new congressional majority, we will meet this moment and fight for the people, working to restore and protect the freedom for every person to make decisions about our bodies, our families, and our futures.

“Democrats have a mandate from the people to fight for our full rights and freedoms, and that includes the fundamental right to reproductive freedom and bodily autonomy,” said Congresswoman Pressley, Co-Chair of the Reproductive Freedom Caucus. “With Trump and Republicans ripping away healthcare and doubling down on their extreme, anti-abortion agenda, I look forward to welcoming Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher as Co-Chair of our Caucus and working with her to protect, restore, and expand abortion rights for everyone who calls America home. It has been an honor to serve alongside Congresswoman Diana DeGette and I am grateful for her yearslong partnership on this critical issue.”

“I am proud join Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley to Co-Chair the Reproductive Freedom Caucus in Congress, and I am grateful to Congresswoman Diana DeGette, who has chaired the caucus since 2000, for her vision and leadership in the fight to ensure access to reproductive healthcare across the country,” said Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher, incoming Co-Chair of the Reproductive Freedom Caucus. “As a Texan, I am proud to be a part of a long tradition of Texas women leading the fight for reproductive freedom and justice for decades. Today, Texans are subject to some of the cruelest and most restrictive abortion laws in the country, and I look forward to working with my colleagues from across our caucus and across the country to protect them and to protect the health, dignity, equality, and freedom of all Americans to make their own reproductive health care decisions.”

“I’ve been honored to lead the Reproductive Freedom Caucus for 25 years, fighting alongside champions, like Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley, Congresswoman Barbara Lee, and others, to vigorously defend Americans’ freedom to make their own health care decisions, including abortion, without interference from politicians,” said Congresswoman Diana DeGette. “Next Congress, this fight continues with a formidable new leader. I am proud to welcome Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher as our next co-chair. She’s been a fierce advocate for women’s reproductive rights for many years and understands the needs of patients living in restrictive states. Together with co-chair Pressley, they will carry on the fight for reproductive freedom that the American people are counting on us to protect. Under their capable leadership, working with our energized coalition partners, I am confident that Congress will restore patients’ access to comprehensive health care, including abortion, and advance reproductive justice for working families across this country.”

We welcome Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher into her new role, and we look forward to building on the legacy of Congresswoman Diana DeGette and continuing the work of the Congressional Reproductive Freedom Caucus. Together, under the leadership of RFC Co-Chairs Congresswomen Ayanna Pressley and Lizzie Fletcher, we will continue fighting until true reproductive freedom is the law of the land.

See and share this news on X here and here; on Bluesky here and here; and on Instagram here.

In her time serving in Congress, Rep. Pressley has fought persistently to protect and advance reproductive justice and ensure fundamental life-saving reproductive health care for all.

title: GOP Lost Because We Failed to Deliver. Why? The Power of Money.
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Republicans lost because we failed to do the one thing voters hired us to do: stop Washington from treating taxpayers like an open ATM.

Some will blame the Iran war. Others will point to the hatred of President Trump or the Democrats’ well-oiled Obama machine. Those factors mattered. But the central failure is simpler and more damning: Americans handed Republicans the House, the Senate, and the White House to lower costs, cut spending, challenge monopolies, and confront corruption. Too many of my colleagues chose instead to protect the same special interests that bankroll both parties’ political machines.

I pressed for a stronger reconciliation package and voted against the weak instructions because I refused to pretend half-measures were victories. I reluctantly supported a revised version only after securing limited reforms to claw back some of the trillions insurers and hospital systems have siphoned off through Medicaid overbilling. It was not enough. Worse, Republicans failed to explain even those modest wins, allowing Democrats to rebrand efforts to stop fraud and overbilling as “cutting benefits.”

Washington runs on legalized corruption. Special interests extract subsidies, regulatory protections, no-bid contracts, and government-protected monopolies. They return a fraction of that money through campaign contributions, PAC donations, and lucrative future K Street jobs. Powerful lobbyists and entrenched D.C. staffers control the agenda, while members either lack the backbone to resist or dream of cashing in themselves. Challenge the machine, and you become the target of fabricated attacks and multimillion-dollar smear campaigns. Play along, and the money and favorable coverage arrive on schedule.

The legislative scorecard tells the story. A reconciliation-compatible SAVE Act died in the Senate. Healthcare price transparency never reached the floor. Medicare PBM transparency and hospital billing reforms were pushed to 2028. Medicare Advantage overbilling was ignored entirely. No serious fiscal commission was created to confront the debt, Social Security, and runaway spending. Housing reforms to help first-time buyers stayed bottled up. Energy, agricultural, and small-business reforms, including incentives for struggling rural communities, were stripped or left out in the Senate. Delphi pension restoration remains stuck in the Senate, leaving retirees waiting.

When lobbyists cannot kill reforms in the House, they run to the Senate, where the swamp runs even deeper.

Meanwhile, Democrats spent years building a permanent grassroots, data, and communications machine designed to exploit frustration and shift blame. Republicans still have nothing comparable. Too many in our own ranks refuse to confront corruption within the party, fight special interests, or support candidates who will actually deliver.

We still have weeks left with a Republican Congress. Leadership should force votes on unfinished business: immediate healthcare transparency, a fiscal commission, Delphi pensions, housing, energy and rural reforms, and a viable path for election integrity. Let voters see who is willing to fight, and who is not.

The same dynamics play out in state and local races, just with smaller checks. The establishment will now use these losses to argue that primary challenges are reckless and that so-called “sensible moderates” must be protected. Yet these are the same politicians whose failure to deliver created the opening for Democrats, and who have repeatedly joined them to protect special interests.

We cannot rebuild the Republican Party by protecting the politicians who helped break it. Unless we confront corruption within our own ranks, 2028 will be even worse.

George Washington lost battles, but he never surrendered the war. Thomas Paine was right: “These are the times that try men’s souls.”

We lost a battle, not the Republic. Americans can still take it back, but only if enough Republicans choose the voters over the money.

title: HOUSE REPUBLICANS PASS MULTIPLE BILLS UNLEASHING NUCLEAR ENERGY ACROSS THE UNITED STATES
text:

Thanks to this legislation, an America that runs on affordable nuclear energy is well within reach during our lifetimes.”

title: Rep. Subramanyam Demands Greater Community Input and Transparency On Proposed Valley North Transmission Line
text:

title: Congresswoman Tenney Leads Bipartisan Effort to Protect Servicemembers from Toxic Burn Pit Exposure
text:
Washington, DC — Congresswoman Claudia Tenney (NY-24) joined Representatives Raul Ruiz (CA-25) and Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) in introducing the bipartisan Waste Incineration Protection, Exposure Oversight, and Updated Tracking of Burn Pits (WIPE OUT Burn Pits) Act to protect American servicemembers from toxic exposure caused by open-air burn pits operated near U.S. military installations overseas. Senator Peter Welch (D-VT) is leading companion legislation in the Senate.

Although the Department of War (DoW) has ended its use of open-air burn pits, servicemembers may still face exposure to toxic smoke from burn pits operated by foreign governments and other entities near U.S. military installations. The WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act would require DoW to identify and report non-DoW controlled burn pits operating within 4,000 meters of military installations or locations where American troops are stationed. The legislation would also require air quality testing, documentation of potential exposure in servicemembers' health records, and a report to Congress on existing burn pits near U.S. personnel. Additionally, the bill would direct DoW to work with host nations to develop plans to eliminate hazardous burn pit operations and implement safer waste disposal alternatives where required.

“Our servicemembers should not have to worry that the air they breathe while defending our country could jeopardize their health for years to come,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “We have seen the devastating consequences of toxic exposure on our veterans and their families, and we must do everything possible to prevent future generations from facing the same challenges. The bipartisan WIPE OUT Burn Pits Act will help identify dangerous exposure risks, improve accountability, and ensure our troops have accurate health records if they need care in the future. Protecting those who serve our nation must remain a top priority, both during their service and long after they return home.”

title: Reps. Tlaib, Dingell introduce bill to secure temporary protected status for Lebanon
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Reps. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) and Debbie Dingell (MI-06) introduced the Lebanon TPS Act, a bill to secure and extend temporary protected status for Lebanon, which is currently set to expire later this month. Those who qualify for TPS are allowed to remain in the U.S. temporarily while conditions in their country of origin remain too dangerous for a safe return.

“We must stand up for our Lebanese neighbors,” said Rep. Tlaib. “The Israeli government continues to illegally occupy and ethnically cleanse entire towns in Lebanon, bulldozing homes that have housed our constituents’ families for generations. Israeli airstrikes continue to kill Lebanese civilians, armed and funded with our tax dollars. To tear Lebanese TPS holders from our communities and send them back to suffer from these war crimes is unacceptable. Our neighbors deserve safety and stability. They belong here, and I will always fight for them.”

“Michigan is home to tens of thousands of Lebanese Americans who have lived here for generations. Today, they live in fear for their families as conditions in Lebanon are too dangerous for them to return. We have a responsibility to provide refuge to those seeking shelter from catastrophe and conflict, and I have long fought for temporary protected status to provide safety and security to those who need it most,” said Rep. Dingell. “We must extend temporary protected status until we can ensure that families can safely return home.”

Conditions in Lebanon have drastically deteriorated since the country was first designated for TPS in November 2024. Over the past 25 months, Israeli military assaults have killed nearly 9,000 Lebanese and injured over 30,000 others. Since March of this year, the people of Lebanon have endured a large-scale Israeli ground invasion and bombing campaign that has killed over 4,380 people and forcibly displaced 1.2 million—over 20% of the entire Lebanese population—from their homes. Those displaced have faced acute shortages of shelter, food, water, healthcare, and education.

Hundreds of thousands remain displaced, significant Lebanese territory remains under illegal military occupation, and entire towns and villages have been systematically demolished, leaving countless Lebanese with no homes to return to at all.

Rather than leave the safety of Lebanese TPS holders up to the whims of the Trump administration, Reps. Tlaib and Dingell’s bill would designate TPS for Lebanon until April 2029.

The Lebanon TPS Act is cosponsored by 18 additional Members of Congress: U.S. Reps. Dwight Evans (PA-03), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Sylvia R. Garcia (TX-29), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Jonathan L. Jackson (IL-01), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Stephen F. Lynch, (MA-08), Kristen McDonald Rivet (MI-08), Gregory Meeks (NY-05), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Hillary Scholten (MI-03), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Nydia M. Velazquez (NY-07), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

title: To Mark Veteran’s Day, Reps. Carter, Luttrell Re-Introduce Bipartisan Warrior Training Advancement Course (WARTAC) Act to Support Veterans Transitioning into Civilian Life
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today on Veteran’s Day, Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. (D-LA) and Congressman Morgan Luttrell (R-TX) announced the reintroduction of the Warrior Training Advancement Course (WARTAC) Act to help raise awareness about and bring improvements to the Warrior Training Advancement Course of the Veterans Benefit Administration (WARTAC). This is a program within the Department of Veteran’s Affairs that helps veterans re-enter the civilian workforce into meaningful roles that also support their fellow veterans.

“Our veterans sacrifice so much to serve our country, and we owe it to them when they transition to civilian life to provide services that help them lead healthy, productive, and meaningful lives,” said Congressman Carter. “This Veterans Day, I’m excited to announce the introduction of Rep. Luttrell’s and my bipartisan Warrior Training Advancement Course Act, which will improve job opportunities and services for veterans re-entering civilian life. By connecting returning service members with critical jobs at the Department of Veterans Affairs, the WARTAC Act can be a win-win for veterans and communities across the country.”

“The WARTAC Act ensures Congress has oversight of the Warrior Training Advancement Course’s effectiveness for our veterans as they begin their transition to civilian life,” said Congressman Luttrell. “I applaud Congressman Troy Carter for his efforts on behalf of the veteran community, and I am proud to join him in leading this bill.”

Background

Every year, over 200,000 brave service members transition out of the Armed Forces and back into civilian life. Due to the unique nature of life in the military, this transition can be daunting and difficult for many.

While the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and its partners have worked to bring the veteran unemployment rate down, there are still a significant number of unemployed veterans nationwide. With the Veteran’s Benefit Administration (VBA) dealing with a severe backlog in cases, it’s in dire need of qualified Veteran Service Representatives and Rating Veteran Service Representatives to process these claims.

This bipartisan legislation would direct the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to report to the bicameral Committees on Veterans Affairs annually on the Warrior Training Advancement Course of the Veterans Benefit Administration, create a structural opportunity to process feedback, and analyze the program for effectiveness and opportunities to grow and improve.

More specifically, the WARTAC Act would:

Include recommendations for best practices and data sets on the number of eligible participants, enrolled participants, participants who successfully complete the program, information on how the Secretary provides the training, and other information deemed relevant.

Require that the Secretary report on hiring information and the cost savings of the program including the determination of the Secretary whether other federal agencies may also save money by establishing a program like WARTAC.

Help veterans receive their benefits more efficiently by increasing the VBA’s hiring capacity.

title: Rep. Van Epps Celebrates the House Passage of the Major Richard Star Act
text:
Washington, D.C.—Rep. Matt Van Epps (TN-07) celebrated the House passage of the Major Richard Star Act, legislation he proudly cosponsored.

“As a servicemember myself, I have seen firsthand the difficulties faced by veterans in my circle who are unable to receive their full retirement pay due to a medical retirement. That’s why I am proud to support this legislation alongside my colleagues,” said Congressman Matt Van Epps. “From the servicemembers stationed at Fort Campbell to the veterans throughout TN-07, I want to ensure our brave warriors are getting the benefits they are owed.”

“No warrior who risked his or her life for this country should be forced to pay a ‘wounded veteran tax.’ It is unconscionable that veterans are financially penalized for injuries or illnesses sustained while honorably serving our nation. Combat-injured veterans deserve the respect and support they were promised,” Rep. Van Epps finished.

Read the Major Richard Star Act here.

Read more about Major Richard Star here.

Background

This legislation would allow veterans medically retired under Chapter 61 with combat-related disabilities to receive both their military retirement pay and VA disability compensation, regardless of years of service. Under current law, retirees with at least 20 years of service and a VA disability rating of 50 percent or higher may receive concurrent receipt through the Concurrent Retirement and Disability Pay (CRDP) program. However, many medically retired combat-injured veterans with fewer than 20 years of service still face a dollar-for-dollar reduction in retired pay due to their receipt of VA disability compensation.

As a voice for veterans and military families, Rep. Van Epps has:

Introduced the HONOR Gold Star Families Act. Learn more here and here.

Heard from veterans at the Hickman County Veterans Lunch here.

Supported the Trump administration's push for full benefits for National Guard Troops here.

Agreed with the VA about stopping the new rule, which lowered disability ratings here.

title: Rep. Van Epps Honors Our Nation’s Veterans, Reflects on Record of Advocacy in Congress
text:

title: Reps. Vargas, Gonzalez, McGovern Reintroduce Bipartisan Legislation to Help Deported Veterans Gain Citizenship
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives Juan Vargas (CA-52), Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34), and James P. McGovern (MA-02) reintroduced the Strengthening Citizenship Services for Veterans Act. Despite enlisting in our military and serving our country, many veterans who were honorably discharged have faced deportation and even been prevented from attending their own naturalization hearings. This legislation would help ensure deported veterans who have successfully completed the preliminary naturalization process can attend their citizenship interview at a port of entry, embassy, or consulate without navigating the complex process of parole.

“Many of the brave men and women who put their lives on the line to defend our nation and our freedoms are immigrants. It's unacceptable that some of these veterans are unable to return to their families and the country they served,” said Rep. Juan Vargas. “It's past time for us to right this wrong. Deported veterans deserve to come home.”

“Just as our service members kept their promise to protect our great nation, we have a sacred duty to keep ours when they return," said Rep. Vicente Gonzalez. “Our bill removes cumbersome bureaucratic hurdles for immigrant veterans and provides a pathway to U.S. citizenship. They have more than earned the right to call America home.”

“It’s shameful that we asked our veterans to put their lives on the line for our country, only to turn around and tell them they don’t belong here,” said Rep. Jim McGovern. “These men and women served our nation with honor, and we have a responsibility to stand by them. Our bill would help deported veterans come home, reunite with their families, and give them a fair path to citizenship without unnecessary barriers or delays.”

This legislation has been endorsed by the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC), Repatriate Our Patriots, and Immigrant Defenders Law Center (ImmDef).

“Veterans who raised their right hand to defend this nation deserve a fair opportunity to become citizens of the country they served. The Strengthening Citizenship Services for Veterans Act would help remove barriers that keep deported veterans from completing the naturalization process. LULAC demands that Congress pass this legislation without delay. Our nation cannot keep asking for sacrifice while leaving those who served stranded abroad. Honor their service. Remove the barriers to citizenship. Bring our veterans home,” said Livier Lázaro, SFC, U.S. Army (Ret.) LULAC National Deported Veterans Subcommittee Chair and San Diego native.

“When we raise our right hand, we make a promise to this country. We kept it. I’m asking our government to keep its promise to the people who serve, to the veterans still waiting to come home, and to the families who have stood beside them all along,” said Danitza G. James, MSW, Repatriate Our Patriots President and CEO.

“It is unconscionable that people who risked their lives in service to this nation are detained, deported, and torn away from the families and communities they call home. These veterans have already given so much to this country, yet the United States government continues to subject them to an inhumane detention framework that disregards their service and the devastating impact of separating them from their loved ones. The Strengthening Citizenship Services for Veterans Act is a critical step toward reuniting deported veterans with their families. Congress must act to ensure those who served this country are not abandoned by the country they once fought to protect,” said Amanda Schuft, ImmDef Legal Services Director.

Vargas and Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) initially introduced this legislation in February of 2020 in the wake of deported U.S. Marine veteran Roman Sabal—who served for six years and received an honorable discharge after attaining the rank of sergeant—being denied reentry into the U.S. near the San Ysidro Port of Entry to attend his own naturalization interview. Only after a pro-bono legal team helped him sue the federal government was he paroled into the U.S. and allowed to complete his naturalization process. While Sabal eventually gained his citizenship in October of 2020, the citizenship interview process remains challenging for deported veterans.

“There is no higher betrayal to our heroes than being deported by the same nation they sacrificed to defend,” said Senator Tammy Duckworth. “As the Trump Administration keeps cruelly targeting Veterans in its extreme deportation campaign, we need to do everything we can to protect our heroes. This common-sense legislation would help ensure these Veterans who served our nation honorably receive a fair chance at gaining citizenship without unnecessary delays that prevent them from reuniting with their families."

In November 2021, the Biden Administration sought to remedy some of these challenges with a new policy allowing deported veterans to conduct their citizenship interviews at ports of entry. The Strengthening Citizenship Services for Veterans Act would codify this policy and expand it to allow deported veterans to also conduct these interviews at consulates and embassies.

This legislation passed the House in the 117th Congress.

The Strengthening Citizenship Services for Veterans Act would:

Direct USCIS to conduct biometric collections, naturalization examinations, and oath of allegiance ceremonies at a port of entry, embassy or consulate for veterans;

Require the Secretaries of Homeland Security and State to issue guidance, facilitate available space, and quality assurance for biometric collections, naturalization examinations, and oath ceremonies for eligible veterans; and

Direct the Secretaries of Homeland Security and State to jointly report to Congress an analysis of the implementation of this policy, the effectiveness of the guidance issued, and update the guidance if any shortcomings are identified.

title: Vasquez, Heinrich, & Luján Call for Independent Review of WIPP Hoist Collapse, Greater DOE Engagement
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02), alongside U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), and U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), sent a letter urging the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to ensure an independent, transparent investigation of an August 19 incident at the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant (WIPP), where an empty lift plunged 1,600 feet to the bottom of the shaft after a cable snapped during safety testing.

“This incident is deeply alarming, and it comes against a backdrop of ongoing, documented concerns about the condition of WIPP's aging hoist infrastructure. The safety of WIPP’s workers must come first. These individuals deserve nothing less than full confidence in the systems and procedures on which their lives depend,” wrote the lawmakers.

“We urge the Department to ensure a thorough, transparent investigation of the August 19 incident and to solicit the full engagement of the Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) as an independent party in that review. Given the nature of the event and the facility's history of hoist-related failures, an independent assessment of these incidents is essential to credibility—both for workers and for the communities that depend on WIPP's continued safe operation,” the lawmakers continued

“This incident also highlights what we understand to be a pattern of unproductive and unsustainable tensions between some WIPP workers and Salado Isolation Mining Contractors, the facility's prime contractor. These dynamics, if unaddressed, present their own risk to the safe and stable operation of the facility. A workforce that does not trust the contractor responsible for their safety is a major operational risk,”the lawmakers continued.

“We want to be clear: the Department of Energy bears ultimate responsibility for the safe, stable, and long-term operation of WIPP...Workers must be kept fully informed of findings and corrective actions, and their safety concerns must be meaningfully addressed, not managed,” the lawmakers concluded.

In September, the lawmakers secured $10 million in federal funding to repair the US 285 Relief Route, a critical road for freight trucks transporting nuclear materials to the WIPP. In 2025, Rep. Vasquez’s proactive and vocal efforts in partnership with local stakeholders prevented the federal government from closing WIPP and leaving New Mexico without a key nuclear waste treatment plant.

title: House Passes Two of Congressman Wied's Bills with Bipartisan Support
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, the U.S. House of Representatives passed two of Congressman Tony Wied’s pro-small business bills with bipartisan support.

The House passed both the Cybersecurity for Small Businesses Act and the Reshoring American Manufacturing Act, which previously advanced through the House Small Business Committee with bipartisan support.

“Whether it’s strengthening cybersecurity for small businesses or helping bring manufacturing back home, I am committed to doing everything I can to put Main Street first and give small businesses the tools they need to continue driving our economy,” said Congressman Wied. “These commonsense pieces of legislation were designed to make life easier for small business owners. I am pleased to see them advance through the House of Representatives and look forward to working with my colleagues in the Senate to get them across the finish line and onto the President’s desk.”

The Cybersecurity for Small Businesses Act:

Requires the Small Business Administration to collaborate with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency and the National Institute of Standards and Technology to provide small businesses with information on cybersecurity best practices.

Requires the Small Business Administration, in coordination with the Secretary of War, to provide specific information related to the levels of cybersecurity requirements for the Department of War’s Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC).

Requires the Administrator to consult the Chief Counsel for Advocacy at the SBA’s Office of Advocacy annually to determine best practices for disseminating information to small businesses.

The Reshoring American Manufacturing Act:

Requires the Small Business Administration to establish, operate, and maintain a webpage that provides a free tool for small businesses seeking information on onshoring their manufacturing capacity to the United States, including a list of resources, relevant organizations, and other information deemed necessary by the SBA.

Requires the SBA’s Office of Manufacturing and Trade to annually consult with the Office of Advocacy to improve and update the webpage’s resources and information.

Congressman Wied was proud to work alongside Congressman Johnny Olszewski (D-MD), who served as the co-lead on the RAM Act.

“Bringing manufacturing back to America shouldn't be an opportunity only reserved for the biggest corporations,” said Congressman Olszewski, who serves on the House Committee on Small Businesses. “Small businesses are the backbone of our economy, and this bipartisan legislation will help connect them with the American manufacturing partners they need to grow. I'm grateful to Congressman Wied for his partnership and to my House colleagues for advancing this effort.”

title: ALSOBROOKS, WYDEN WARN AGAINST PREDICTION MARKETS ALLOWING BETTING ON CLINICAL TRIALS AND DRUG APPROVALS, URGE SECRETARY KENNEDY TO TAKE ACTION
text:
November 11, 2026

WASHINGTON, DC – As reported by CNBC today, Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.) and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) are warning against prediction markets allowing betting on clinical trials and drug approvals and are calling on Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to take immediate action.

“We are concerned about a troubling development that prediction markets are now allowing individuals to bet on clinical trials and drug approvals. Clinical trials and approvals are critical processes that rely on scientific integrity to provide a new avenue of care for patients with targeted conditions and advance medical care for everyone. Allowing individuals to bet on the success of these trials and drugs undermines the scientific process, creates perverse incentives for researchers, harms trial participants, and could lead to dangerous medical outcomes for untold numbers of Americans,” wrote the lawmakers.

“Researchers and medical professionals have expressed concern that offering bets on clinical trials threatens the integrity of the drug development process. Specifically, experts expressed fears that study results may be compromised by participants dropping out of ongoing studies or administrators altering their behavior due to the public prediction market. Troublingly, there are also concerns that this expansion will tempt researchers to place bets on insider knowledge, creating incentives for researchers to tamper with trial data in hopes of a windfall that may have a consequential impact on patient safety and public health,” continued the lawmakers.

Read the full text of the letter here or below:

Secretary Kennedy,

We are concerned about a troubling development that prediction markets are now allowing individuals to bet on clinical trials and drug approvals. Clinical trials and approvals are critical processes that rely on scientific integrity to provide a new avenue of care for patients with targeted conditions and advance medical care for everyone. Allowing individuals to bet on the success of these trials and drugs undermines the scientific process, creates perverse incentives for researchers, harms trial participants, and could lead to dangerous medical outcomes for untold numbers of Americans.

Reports indicate that Kalshi and Polymarket have launched programs allowing users to trade event contracts on drug approvals and clinical trial outcomes. Users have traded on whether the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services’ (HHS or Department) Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will approve experimental medications from weight loss treatments, Alzheimer’s disease, and different cancers, including lung, breast, pancreatic, and blood. Many of the clinical trials implicated by these markets may be funded, in whole or in part, by the National Institutes of Health (NIH), one of the largest sources of clinical research funding in the country. Some trials subject to betting may also be conducted by NIH’s own intramural research program, including at the NIH Clinical Center.

Researchers and medical professionals have expressed concern that offering bets on clinical trials threatens the integrity of the drug development process. Specifically, experts expressed fears that study results may be compromised by participants dropping out of ongoing studies or administrators altering their behavior due to the public prediction market. Troublingly, there are also concerns that this expansion will tempt researchers to place bets on insider knowledge, creating incentives for researchers to tamper with trial data in hopes of a windfall that may have a consequential impact on patient safety and public health. Kalshi has proposed safeguards to limit this concern, however the prediction market platforms do not have access to the long list of people involved in a clinical trial and therefore cannot adequately monitor for misconduct. These concerns are well founded as in the past few years the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has charged multiple people with insider trading connected to clinical trials.

These integrity risks are not merely abstract – they fall most directly on patients, study participants, and volunteers hoping for answers and medical advancement, and whose participation makes these trials possible. Patients must receive informed consent, have their privacy protected, and have provisions put in place for monitoring of the data collected to ensure their safety. Nowhere in the informed consent process, which requires disclosure of reasonably foreseeable risks and inconveniences to study participants, is it contemplated that a treatment outcome could become the subject of public wagering. Allowing individuals to bet on the success of clinical trials allows people to bet on whether another individual is going to receive an available treatment or not. These platforms are allowing bettors to wager on the health, or even life and death, of complete strangers affected by these medical trials. The success of many late-stage cancer trials like those Kalshi is allowing users to trade event contracts is measured by how many participants survive which has raised concerns with patients and clinical trial participants. It is disturbing to encourage a landscape where bettors are “rooting for experimental medicine to fail just to earn a buck.”

These risks to trial integrity and participant welfare fall squarely within your statutory responsibilities. As HHS Secretary, you are responsible for promoting public health through the prompt and efficient review of clinical research. FDA must monitor the progress of clinical trials and ensure the safety of clinical testing and patients in the development of drugs to treat life threatening illnesses, which necessitates frequent oversight to ensure that clinical trial data integrity and patient safety is not compromised due to the trading of event contracts. FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) has also issued guidance directing that trial sponsors – those responsible for initiating, managing, and financing a clinical trial – must: (1) ensure the integrity and confidentiality of data generated and managed to produce reliable results; (2) establish committees whose members have managed conflicts of interest and follow documented decision-making and operating procedures; (3) assess all trial–related decisions for their impact on participant rights; and (4) maintain an appropriate system for managing research quality. NIH imposes parallel obligations on its extramural grantees: investigators receiving NIH funding must disclose significant financial interests related to their research, and their institutions must manage, reduce, or eliminate conflicts that could bias study design, conduct, or reporting. These existing frameworks were not designed with prediction markets in mind, and it is unclear whether they are adequate to address the novel financial incentives these platforms create.

This obligation to safeguard trial integrity extends to your Department’s own workforce. HHS employees cannot have a financial interest in a significantly regulated organization. However, the Department’s ethics policies do not yet include any reference outlining that HHS employees are also barred from trading related event contracts on prediction markets. This gap applies with equal force to NIH’s intramural investigators and staff who serve on Data and Safety Monitoring Boards, both of whom may have access to nonpublic, outcome-relevant trial data. It is essential that the Department take the necessary steps to ensure that employees are not seeking financial gain based on nonpublic information on these markets, and time is of the essence given that prediction markets that focus exclusively on clinical trials have begun to emerge.

Because it is clear that these markets create perverse incentives, undermine public confidence in trial outcomes, and perpetuate the commodification of human suffering, we are requesting that you provide answers to the following questions by December 1, 2026:

Please provide all documents and communications, including but not limited to policies, regulations, guidance, ethics opinions, and internal correspondence, concerning the participation of FDA reviewers, advisory committee members, or contracted personnel in prediction markets or other financial instruments tied to matters pending before the agency. If no such policy currently exists, please provide all documents reflecting any Department consideration of adopting one, including a timeline for doing so.

Please provide all documents and communications between HHS and any of its subcomponents and Kalshi, Polymarket, or any other operator of event-contract markets concerning drug approval or clinical trial outcomes, including but not limited to correspondence regarding data access, market structure, or agency concerns, from January 1, 2026 to the present.

Please provide all documents and communications reflecting FDA policy, guidance, or requirements imposed on clinical trial sponsors, investigators, or contract research organizations regarding the prevention of trading on nonpublic trial data, and all documents reflecting FDA’s assessment of whether such trading violates existing data integrity or good clinical practice requirements.

Please provide all documents, communications, memoranda, or internal analyses reflecting any FDA evaluation of the risk that these markets could incentivize premature unblinding of trial data, participant attrition, or investigator conduct inconsistent with protocol.

Please provide all documents and communications between HHS, FDA, and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission concerning the approval, self-certification, or ongoing oversight of event contracts tied to FDA regulatory actions or clinical trial outcomes.

Please provide all documents and communications reflecting any position taken by you or the Acting Commissioner, internally or externally, on whether these markets are compatible with the Department’s statutory mission and the integrity of the drug approval process.

Please identify any NIH-funded or NIH-conducted clinical trials that are, or have been, the subject of event contracts on prediction markets, and provide all documents and communications between NIH and any such market operator concerning these contracts.

Please provide all documents and communications reflecting whether NIH’s existing financial conflict-of-interest regulations for extramural investigators are understood to apply to, require updating, or are currently being updated in light of, trading on prediction markets tied to the outcome of NIH-funded research.

Please provide all documents reflecting whether NIH intramural investigators, Data and Safety Monitoring Board members, or other NIH staff with access to nonpublic trial data are subject to any policy restricting participation in prediction markets tied to trials in which they are involved.

Clinical trials are essential to the advancement of the medical field and provide hopeful treatment routes for many people struggling with difficult medical conditions. HHS, FDA, and NIH must uphold the integrity of the drug development process and maintain public trust in the public health by putting essential guardrails in place to prevent individuals profiting on the success and approval of drugs that the American people depend on. We look forward to your response.

Sincerely,

Angela D. Alsobrooks

United States Senator

Ron Wyden

United States Senator

title: Making It Easier to Manufacture in America
text:
Making It Easier to Manufacture in America

HOW PERMITTING REFORM CAN STRENGTHEN DOMESTIC MANUFACTURING AND CRITICAL MINERAL SUPPLY CHAINS

American manufacturing depends on more than press releases. It depends on building the energy, infrastructure, and supply chains that make those factories competitive.

THE PROBLEM WITH THE STATUS QUO

America cannot expand manufacturing by permitting factories in isolation. Steel mills, aluminum smelters, and advanced manufacturers depend on reliable power, domestic minerals, and interconnected supply chains. Delays to one project can ripple across entire industries.

The National Association of Manufacturers (NAM) estimates that permitting imposes $12 billion in annual costs, including $7.9 billion in compliance expenses and $4.1 billion from delays and higher energy bills. NAM estimates that fully implementing BAAJA could save manufacturers $4.23 billion annually—roughly 35% of that burden.

And as Peter Cook of the Breakthrough Institute explains, permitting barriers also constrain domestic mining, processing, and recycling, deepening dependence on vulnerable foreign supply chains.

HOW THE BIPARTISAN BILL HELPS

BAAJA would address federal permitting obstacles affecting the infrastructure behind American manufacturing. Enforceable review timelines and more durable approvals could help energy and mineral projects move forward, while focused Clean Water Act certifications and transmission reforms could ease bottlenecks in pipelines, power lines, and other supporting infrastructure.

Industrial projects depend on one another: a smelter needs electricity, a factory needs raw materials, and a mineral-processing facility needs reliable transportation and power. By making federal decisions more predictable across those supporting projects, BAAJA could help companies coordinate investments and bring domestic production capacity online.

WHO SUPPORTS IT — AND WHY

Manufacturers are pressing Congress to address permitting barriers that hold back industrial construction. NAM and 106 manufacturing and business organizations called for passage of BAAJA. NAM amplified its message through an advertising campaign. After the Senate’s November 9 procedural vote, NAM President and CEO Jay Timmons urged Congress to “finish the job.” The New American Industrial Alliance praised the agreement as “government at its finest,” pointing to more durable approvals and limits on litigation delays.

Steel and aluminum producers need reliable energy and infrastructure to expand domestic capacity. The American Iron and Steel Institute (AISI) joined both the November 6 industrial coalition letter and November 9 broader sign-on letter; the November 6 coalition also included the American Institute of Steel Construction, National Steel Bridge Alliance, Steel Manufacturers Association (SMA), and Aluminum Extruders Council. SMA EVP Brandon Farris said the reforms could “unleash investment.” Aluminum Association President and CEO Charles Johnson warned that “America cannot afford to wait” to build the energy and infrastructure supporting domestic aluminum production.

America cannot build infrastructure without the industries supplying its basic materials. The American Chemistry Council welcomed more durable approvals and focused water-quality reviews; American Cement Association President and CEO Diane Tomb said the bill “shortens the path from plan to pour.” The National Ready Mixed Concrete Association also supported the package. Plastics Industry Association President and CEO Matt Seaholm emphasized jobs and competitiveness. National Stone, Sand & Gravel Association President and CEO Michele Stanley warned that “America cannot build what it cannot permit, and it cannot permit what it cannot supply.” The November 6 coalition also included the American Fuel & Petrochemical Manufacturers, Aerospace Industries Association, and The Fertilizer Institute.

Grid construction also depends on American-made electrical equipment. The National Electrical Manufacturers Association highlighted how faster transmission development can support investment in American-made transformers, switchgear, cables, and other grid components.

Other major manufacturers tied their support to the infrastructure that makes industrial expansion possible. A November 9 letter organized by C2ES Action, Ceres, and Third Way included85 organizations, with Nucor, Cummins, Volvo Group North America, and Amrize among the signatories urging Congress to pass BAAJA. Their participation underscores the need to build reliable power and transportation infrastructure alongside new factories.

Domestic manufacturing also begins upstream, with the minerals needed for industrial production. U.S. Chamber of Commerce executive Ruth Demeter Hayes described the jobs, investment, and local revenue lost when mining projects stall. Essential Minerals Association’s Matt Dermody said, “This bill fixes real problems our members face.” The American Exploration & Mining Association separately urged swift passage. National Mining Association President and CEO Rich Nolan called on Congress to ensure that “made in America is also mined in America.”

Building the infrastructure behind American manufacturing is how investment becomes domestic production, stronger supply chains, and American jobs.

title: Bennet Presses Trump Administration on Failure to Stop Megaspeed’s Apparent AI Tech Diversion to China
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a member of the Senate Intelligence Committee, sent a letter to Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, Attorney General Todd Blanche, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton demanding an update on the U.S. government’s investigation into Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm that reportedly acts as a major conduit for transfers of restricted U.S. technology to China, including Nvidia’s advanced AI chips.

The letter also requests U.S. engagement with Southeast Asian governments to address potential violations of U.S. export controls; punitive U.S. action against Megaspeed, such as putting the firm on the Entity List; and far stronger approaches to export controls and enforcement. Additionally, the letter requests an explanation of the Intelligence Community (IC)’s analysis of the threat Megaspeed poses, as well as an explanation of the IC’s sharing of that information with the Departments of Commerce, Justice, State, and the White House. These efforts are crucial given reports that the IC concluded a Megaspeed executive was a Chinese intelligence asset with close ties to Nvidia’s CEO.

“I request an update on the U.S. government’s investigation into the Singapore-based firm Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd. (“Megaspeed”) for potentially circumventing U.S. export controls and exploiting gray areas in the U.S. export control regime to divert advanced American semiconductor capabilities to China, including advanced Nvidia semiconductors. The Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security initially led this investigation but New York Times reporting indicates that the Department of Justice is now leading this effort. Additionally, we request that you engage countries hosting Megaspeed infrastructure – such as Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia – to address potential violations of U.S. export controls. I also request your consideration of specific punitive measures against Megaspeed, as well as stronger approaches to export controls and enforcement,” Bennet wrote.

“This flow of advanced AI chips to China and China’s access to restricted cloud computing capabilities risk enabling Beijing’s development of autonomous weapon systems, advanced cyber-warfare capabilities, and more powerful surveillance tools – which could eventually pose significant challenges to U.S. capabilities. China’s military could one day use these technologies against American servicemembers. Large-scale diversion also creates a gray market that penalizes law-abiding companies and devalues the intellectual property that sustains U.S. global economic leadership,” he continued.

The letter concluded by requesting that Secretary Lutnick, Attorney General Blanche, Secretary Rubio, and Director Clayton provide the following information by November 24, 2026:

An update on the Department of Justice’s continuation of the Department of Commerce investigation into Megaspeed;

A detailed description of any Department of Commerce efforts to prevent Megaspeed, whose top executive is reportedly a Chinese intelligence asset, from purchasing Nvidia chips, such as by sending an “Is Informed” letter to Nvidia blocking certain semiconductor shipments to Megaspeed and potentially placing Megaspeed on the Entity List;

A detailed accounting of:

The Department of Commerce and Department of State’s efforts to coordinate a rigorous response with partners including Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia;

The Department of Commerce’s efforts to close loopholes in U.S. export controls that allow Chinese companies to access restricted U.S. technology, such as semiconductors and cloud computing, through Southeast Asia; and

The Department of Commerce’s efforts to close loopholes in U.S. export controls that allow subsidiaries of China-headquartered firms, including those on whom the United States has already sanctioned, to buy export-controlled AI chips in the United States.

A detailed explanation of the IC’s analysis of Alice Huang’s reported service as a Chinese intelligence asset and the broader threat Megaspeed poses to U.S. national security.

A detailed explanation of the IC’s sharing of such information, on Ms. Huang; and Megaspeed, with the Department of Commerce, the Department of Justice, the Department of State, and the White House.

Bennet has led efforts to ensure U.S. competitiveness and national security by preventing the transfer of advanced U.S. technologies to China. He helped pass legislation to bar American investments in certain advanced technologies with military uses, such as AI and semiconductors, in China and other countries of concern. He secured language in the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence-passed Fiscal Year 2027 Intelligence Authorization Act requiring an intelligence assessment before the U.S. government approves AI technologies for export or signs an AI agreement with a foreign government. That assessment would evaluate the recipient country’s export control regime, its ties to adversaries like China and Russia, the risk of onward proliferation, and the likely end-uses of the technology. Bennet has blasted the Trump administration’s decision to allow the sale of Nvidia H200 AI chips to China and President Trump’s decision to pause U.S. export controls restricting the sale of critical technology to China.

The text of the letter is available HERE and below.

Secretary Lutnick, Attorney General Blanche, Secretary Rubio, and Director Clayton:

I request an update on the U.S. government’s investigation into the Singapore-based firm Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd. (“Megaspeed”) for potentially circumventing U.S. export controls and exploiting gray areas in the U.S. export control regime to divert advanced American semiconductor capabilities to China, including advanced Nvidia semiconductors. The Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) initially led this investigation, but New York Times reporting indicates that the Department of Justice is now leading this effort. Additionally, I request that you engage countries hosting Megaspeed infrastructure – such as Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia – to address potential violations of U.S. export controls. I also request your consideration of specific punitive measures against Megaspeed, as well as stronger approaches to export controls and enforcement.

These efforts are crucial and time-sensitive given New York Times reporting that the U.S. intelligence community found Megaspeed executive Alice Huang to be a Chinese intelligence asset who passed critical information to the Chinese government. Ensuring the integrity of our export controls is central to advancing America’s national security and our long-term economic prosperity, including by preventing China – our only near-peer competitor – from obtaining advanced U.S. technologies with military applications, such as cutting-edge artificial intelligence (AI) chips. Our export control regime must be able to identify and curtail entities actively seeking to evade those controls.

Extensive public reporting suggests that Megaspeed acts as a high-volume conduit for China-bound transfers of advanced American technology through the following activities:

Intelligence Operations: According to The New York Times, U.S. intelligence agencies concluded that a top executive at Megaspeed, Alice Huang (also known as Huang Le), acted as a Chinese intelligence asset to gather information for Beijing. Per this report, electronic surveillance revealed that Ms. Huang cultivated a close relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The report also indicated that Ms. Huang likely funneled information not only about Nvidia to the Chinese government, but also about President Trump’s plans and intentions. The report indicates that Megaspeed continues to trumpet its close connections to Nvidia.

Exploitation of Sanctioned Intermediaries: Reports indicate that Megaspeed operated as a middle man, using Aivres – a U.S.-registered subsidiary of Chinese technology giant Inspur, on which the United States imposed sanctions for supporting China’s military – to source restricted hardware, such as advanced Nvidia AI chips. Aivres was able to purchase this hardware (1) because Aivres was not subject to the sanctions imposed on its parent company Inspur; (2) because the Department of Commerce has rolled back steps that restrict the subsidiaries of Chinese-headquartered firms from buying export-controlled AI chips from U.S. firms; and (3) because the Department of Commerce halted enforcement of licensing requirements for Chinese-headquartered subsidiaries in Malaysia from May 2025, creating more loopholes that have enabled the illicit diversion of sensitive U.S. technology. Aivres thus continued purchasing advanced Nvidia chips, which a Malaysia-based Megaspeed subsidiary then bought. BIS officials who visited Megaspeed’s Malaysia data center suspected that Megaspeed may have sent some of these chips to China. Meanwhile, Aivres currently advertises access to Nvidia’s most advanced and recently released Vera Rubin chips.

Physical Smuggling and Diversion: Reports indicate that since 2023, Megaspeed’s Malaysian and Indonesian subsidiaries have purchased advanced Nvidia chips worth at least $4.6 billion, including the advanced Blackwell processors that the United States has not approved for export to China. A late 2024 BIS inspection of a Megaspeed site in Malaysia discovered advanced hardware in boxes rather than installed and in use, an unusual practice that BIS officials considered a potential indicator of diversion to China.

Backdoor Remote Access: Reports indicate that Megaspeed operates AI data centers in Southeast Asia, potentially with Nvidia Blackwell processors, and may have used them to provide Chinese clients with remote cloud computing power from restricted U.S. hardware. As of October 29, 2026, Nvidia continued to list Megaspeed on its website as a cloud partner. This highlights another gap in current U.S. export control regulations, since the administration has not imposed restrictions to prevent companies headquartered in countries outside of China, like Megaspeed, from providing Chinese clients remote access to export-controlled chips.

Opaque Ownership: Reports indicate that Megaspeed is a spin-off of 7ROAD, a Chinese firm with state-backed ties – raising concerns of corporate restructuring obscuring Beijing’s control in order to evade U.S. oversight. Recent probes underscore the severity of these allegations. The Singapore Police Force has investigated Megaspeed for potential legal violations. Major infrastructure partners like Bridge Data Centres, backed by Bain Capital, have terminated their ties with Megaspeed. That Megaspeed reportedly ceased new orders amid these probes raises serious questions warranting an American response. These facts raise serious concerns about Chinese companies using opaque corporate structures to circumvent U.S. export controls.

This flow of advanced AI chips to China and China’s access to restricted cloud computing capabilities risk enabling Beijing’s development of autonomous weapon systems, advanced cyber-warfare capabilities, and more powerful surveillance tools – which could eventually pose significant challenges to U.S. capabilities. China’s military could one day use these technologies against American servicemembers. Large-scale diversion also creates a gray market that penalizes law-abiding companies and devalues the intellectual property that sustains U.S. global economic leadership.

Accordingly, I respectfully request that you provide the following information to my office in writing by November 24, 2026:

An update on the Department of Justice’s continuation of the Department of Commerce investigation into Megaspeed;

A detailed description of any Department of Commerce efforts to prevent Megaspeed, whose top executive is reportedly a Chinese intelligence asset, from purchasing Nvidia chips, such as by sending an “Is Informed” letter to Nvidia blocking certain semiconductor shipments to Megaspeed and potentially placing Megaspeed on the Entity List;

A detailed accounting of:

The Department of Commerce and Department of State’s efforts to coordinate a rigorous response with partners including Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia;

The Department of Commerce’s efforts to close loopholes in U.S. export controls that allow Chinese companies to access restricted U.S. technology, such as semiconductors and cloud computing, through Southeast Asia; and

The Department of Commerce’s efforts to close loopholes in U.S. export controls that allow subsidiaries of China-headquartered firms, including those on whom the United States has already imposed sanctions, to buy export-controlled AI chips in the United States.

A detailed explanation of the Intelligence Community’s analysis of Alice Huang’s reported service as a Chinese intelligence asset and the broader threat Megaspeed poses to U.S. national security; and

A detailed explanation of the Intelligence Community’s sharing of such information, on Ms. Huang and Megaspeed, with the Department of Commerce, the Department of Justice, the Department of State, and the White House.

Thank you for your attention.

title: Blumenthal Demands Trump U.S. Attorney Preserve Records
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), incoming Chair of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, in response to a baseless threat from the Department of Justice, today demanded the Trump-appointed U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas preserve all records and correspondence, including with the White House or senior Department of Justice officials, related to the Administration’s efforts to protect corporate donors and Administration officials from legitimate oversight.

“I am aware of your letter, posted to X today, which purports to initiate an investigation into me for conducting a congressional inquiry. This is just the latest in a series of unlawful actions on the part of the Trump Administration attempting to intimidate Members of Congress for engaging in constitutionally protected activity. Your implied threat of an investigation is baseless,” wrote Blumenthal.

Blumenthal continued, “The public deserves to know the terms under which dozens of American companies were persuaded to donate millions of dollars to the President’s vanity projects, and whether lawsuits were dismissed, contracts were awarded, or regulations went unenforced in exchange for that money. The public deserves transparency about whether the White House and the corporations it cajoled extracted favors at the expense of American taxpayers. Not only are these appropriate subjects for congressional oversight, but such inquiries are among the constitutional duties that Members of Congress must undertake to become informed about matters on which legislation may be necessary.”

“Since you appear to have evidence of the Trump Administration’s efforts to protect corporate donors and Administration officials from legitimate oversight, I accordingly direct you to preserve all records and correspondence, including all communications with the White House or senior officials at the Department of Justice, related to the decision to draft and post your letter,” Blumenthal concluded.

Blumenthal has led an inquiry into the waste, fraud, and abuse associated with the White House ballroom and other projects throughout the nation’s capital. Blumenthal recently wrote to Big Tech companies and others who may be seeking pay-to-play government favors from their donations to President Trump’s White House ballroom and other projects, reminding recipients of the Subcommittee’s expectation for their prompt cooperation.

The full text of today’s letter is available here and below.

title: Booker, Colleagues Introduce Bipartisan Resolution Honoring Women Veterans Throughout History
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ), Marsha Blackburn (R-TN), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Jeanne Shaheen, (D-NH), Thom Tillis (R-NC), and John Boozman (R-AR) introduced a bipartisan resolution to recognize the service and sacrifice of women veterans throughout American History.

“Women have served our country with courage in every generation often without the recognition they deserve,” said Senator Booker. “This resolution acknowledges all the brave women who have worn our nation’s uniform, and we must do more to provide them with the benefits and support they have earned.”

“From the women who disguised themselves to fight in the American Revolution and Civil War to the Hello Girls of World War I to today’s brave female service members, women have always answered the call to defend our nation,” said Senator Blackburn. “Generations of women have served our country, and this resolution would honor their courage, sacrifice, and vital contributions to our military.”

“Countless women in Nevada and across this country have bravely and selflessly served our nation in uniform, and we owe them a debt of gratitude that can never be repaid,” said Senator Rosen. “I’m proud to help introduce this bipartisan resolution honoring the contributions of women veterans, and I’ll continue working to recognize and support all of Nevada’s veterans.”

“Throughout our nation’s history, women have played a critical role in defending our freedoms and protecting our national security, often overcoming significant barriers to serve our country with courage and distinction,” said Senator Shaheen. “I’m proud to join my colleagues on this bipartisan effort to recognize the invaluable contributions that women veterans have made and ensure that their service and sacrifices are never forgotten.”

“Today, we recognize and honor the women who have worn our nation’s uniform and answered the call to serve with courage and dedication,” said Senator Tillis. “Their sacrifices, strength, and commitment to defending the freedoms we hold dear deserve our utmost gratitude and lasting recognition. We must ensure that every woman who has served our country, across all branches of the Armed Forces, receives the respect, recognition, and support she has rightfully earned.”

“Women veterans have made tremendous sacrifices in service to our nation, and their contributions deserve our gratitude and recognition,” said Senator Boozman. “I am proud to help lead this resolution reaffirming our commitment to honoring women veterans and supporting them and their families. Their service in every branch of our Armed Forces has helped defend our freedoms and strengthen our nation, so this Veterans Day, we recognize that sacrifice and reaffirm that their contributions will never be forgotten.”

The Women Veterans Recognition Resolution would:

Recognize the service and sacrifice of women veterans throughout American history;

Highlight the contributions of women across all branches of the Armed Forces;

Acknowledge the unique challenges women veterans face in accessing healthcare and benefits;

Affirm our support for women veterans and their families

title: On Veterans Day, Booker Releases 2027 Veterans Handbook to Help New Jersey Veterans and Families Access Earned Benefits
text:
NEWARK, N.J. — Today, on Veterans Day, U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-N.J.) released his updated 2027 Veterans Handbook, a guide to the federal and state benefits and services available to New Jersey veterans and their families. For anyone with questions about the benefits they've earned, the programs open to them, or where to turn for help, the handbook offers a clear place to start.’

"This summer, I had the privilege of honoring American patriots in Paramus and hosting a town hall in Holmdel to hear directly from veterans and their families about what's on their minds," said Senator Booker. "Those conversations are a powerful reminder that honoring our veterans means making sure they can get the care, benefits, and support they've earned. Whether you're coming home from military service, looking for your next job, or helping a loved one figure out where to turn for care, finding help shouldn't be hard. That's why my office puts this handbook together. Veterans Day is a time to thank those who served, but our responsibility to them continues every day of the year."

The handbook is designed for veterans at every stage of civilian life, from service members preparing to leave the military to veterans who have been home for years. It brings together information on health care benefits, employment opportunities and workforce centers, federal and state education programs, and crisis support services. Family members can also use it to help a loved one find the right program or office.

title: Budd Joins Cotton, Shaheen in Applauding Senate Passage of Resolution to Establish National Warrior Call Day
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Ted Budd (R-N.C.), a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, joined his colleagues, Senators Tom Cotton (R-Ark.) and Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), in applauding the Senate’s unanimous passage of their resolution designating November 15, 2026, as National Warrior Call Day. The bipartisan resolution emphasizes the need for all Americans to reach out and build meaningful relationships with veterans and those currently serving to help support their mental health and foster community.

“North Carolina is proud to be home to more than 600,000 veterans and one of the nation’s largest military communities. We have a responsibility to ensure that the brave men and women who serve our country have access to the mental health support and resources that they need to thrive both during and after their military service. The overwhelming bipartisan support and passage of this resolution reflects our shared commitment, across party lines, to addressing the mental health challenges facing our service members and veterans. Our nation’s heroes should never have to grapple with those burdens alone,” said Senator Budd.

“Our military members and veterans deserve the support and resources they need to lead active, healthy lives after serving. This bipartisan resolution will raise awareness on the importance of service members’ mental health, and I’m glad to see it pass the Senate unanimously,” said Senator Cotton.

“No veteran should ever feel alone while struggling with their mental health, especially after sacrificing so much to defend our freedoms abroad. Warrior Call Day is one vital way that we can help connect veterans with resources while also reducing the stigma around asking for help and mental health care,” said Senator Shaheen. “I’m proud my Senate colleagues once again recognized the importance of our bipartisan resolution to designate Warrior Call Day because the health and well-being of the men and women in the military shouldn’t be a partisan issue.”

Read the full resolution text HERE.

Senators Budd, Cotton, and Shaheen were joined by Senators John Boozman (R-Ark.), Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska), Tim Sheehy (R-Mont.), Eric Schmitt (R-Mo.), Rick Scott (R-Fla.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.), John Fetterman (D-Penn.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), and Michael Bennet (D-Colo.) in leading the resolution.
