title: Congresswoman Escobar Introduces Legislation to Ban Foie Gras
text:
Today, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) introduced the Ducks and Geese Protection Act. This bill would make it illegal for individuals to knowingly force-feed geese or ducks to produce foie gras.

“Helpless animals like ducks and geese intentionally being force-fed before slaughter — all for our ‘culinary pleasure’ is nothing short of savage. It is also animal cruelty,” said Congresswoman Escobar. “This legislation is common-sense and straightforward. Legislation protecting these innocent, defenseless animals is long overdue.”

“Ducks and geese used for foie gras endure the agony of being force-fed through tubes rammed down their throats, all to produce a food no one needs that is really simply cruelty in a can or torture in a tin,” says PETA Founder Ingrid Newkirk. “PETA thanks Rep. Escobar for her leadership in introducing this compassionate bill, which would help spare sensitive birds from this abominable, indefensible practice.”

“Producing foie gras means forcing tubes down the throats of ducks and geese until their livers become diseased. It is an inhumane practice, and the public has recognized it as such. Voters have overwhelmingly supported local bans on foie gras, and concern about it continues to grow. The Animal Legal Defense Fund commends Representative Escobar for leading the effort to end this needless suffering nationwide,” said Blair Eagleson, Legislative Affairs Fellow at ALDF.

The Ducks and Geese Protection Act would:

Make it illegal for individuals to knowingly force-feed geese or ducks to produce foie gras.

Impose a fine of no more than $14,000 per violation for individuals who violate the Ducks and Geese Protection Act.

title: After winning reelection, Shomari Figures prepares for life in the majority
text:
WASHINGTON — As furniture lines the halls of Capitol Hill with the impending departure and arrival of more than a hundred House members, Rep. Shomari Figures is staying put.

After winning reelection last week in a district redrawn to favor Republicans, the Mobile-turned-Montgomery Democrat is settling in for a second term in Congress, and one in which his party will be in the majority.

Figures won by eight points against Republican State Rep. Rhett Marques in the newly redrawn 2nd Congressional District, which President Donald Trump won by 14 points in 2024.

Every county in the new 2nd District, stretching from the Wiregrass to Montgomery, went more Democratic this year compared to the 2024 presidential election. Figures also flipped rural Barbour County, which went for Trump by 15 points. Figures won it by four.

He said a convergence of factors helped him win this year: backlash to redistricting, economic conditions and anger with the Trump administration.

“I think people were just tired, tired of being lied to by this administration, tired of the theatrics and the antics and the departures from just normal standards of decency and integrity,” Figures told Alabama Daily News in an interview Wednesday in his office.

With Democrats taking control of both chambers, a push and pull is likely to emerge within the party between prioritizing efforts to investigate the Trump administration and legislation to tackle the cost of living.

Figures said affordability should take precedence next year.

“The more pronounced (wrongs), they need to be called out, they need to be investigated, they need to be addressed, and where appropriate, people need to be held accountable,” Figures told ADN.

“But what we cannot do is go into a situation where on day one everybody’s focus is trying to impeach the president. That didn’t work out so well for us last time it happened twice, and so that can’t be the focus.”

Democrats are also eager to work on health care when they take the reins of Congress. Progressives have floated pursuing Medicare for All, a single-payer national health care system, next year while moderates are more focused on incremental reforms rather than sweeping changes.

Figures said it’s important to be realistic about what Democrats can do on health care while President Donald Trump is still in the White House.

“We can drive money to our rural hospitals and our non-rural hospitals to help bolster up the funding,” he said. “We can re-incentivize states to be able to expand Medicaid, which the state of Alabama never did. We can make these changes. These are things that we can do.”

Renewing the Affordable Care Act’s enhanced premium subsidies, which expired last year, is another option, Figures said. He considered those reforms “more palatable than some of the grander objectives.”

Voting rights

After redistricting upended Alabama’s congressional lines and others across the country, the Alabama Democrat said it’s crucial lawmakers “move the ball forward” on voting rights, even if only to prepare for when Trump is no longer in office.

He acknowledged that Trump would most likely not sign sweeping legislation like the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act into law, which would strengthen voting rights protections through federal oversight.

That bill, led by Rep. Terri Sewell, D-Birmingham, would also probably need modifications after the Supreme Court’s Louisiana v. Callais ruling, Figures said.

“There may be some ways that we can get some aspects of voting rights protections across the finish line, but just understanding the realities of this president, probably not necessarily, in terms of getting him to sign something into law,” Figures told ADN.

Committee preferences

In his second term, Figures is eyeing a potential spot on the Appropriations Committee, noting that Alabama’s current appropriators, all Republicans, will be in the minority should they remain on the panel next year.

He said having a Democrat on the coveted committee, which allows lawmakers to send federal dollars home, would benefit the whole state.

“So appropriations around the state is something that we’re going to have to rely on Democrats in the delegation to help with, and so Terri Sewell and myself both stand ready and willing to do that, and so we just want to be helpful as much as we can.”

The congressman is also interested in keeping his spot on the Agriculture Committee, or joining a different committee that touches that industry, such as Energy and Commerce.

Figures also serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, the only Alabama member on that committee during the 119th Congress.

Figures backs Jeffries

In his bid for speaker, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries faces some potential defections from incoming Democrats pushing for change. But Figures is squarely behind Jeffries, who is still expected to ultimately win and lead the chamber next year.

The Democratic leader immediately supported Figures when Alabama’s map changed and backed him throughout his reelection campaign, including visiting the state as his last campaign stop before Election Day.

“He just navigated us through, regardless of where you are on the political spectrum, I think we can all agree this is one of the more tumultuous two-year tenures of any presidential administration in recent memory,” Figures said. “He navigated us through that, raised the most funds that this party has ever raised, and positioned us to be able to deliver the largest majority that either party has had this century…and that is impressive.”

The pair are also members of the Congressional Black Caucus. Should Jeffries win the internal leadership contest next week, he is poised to become the nation’s first Black speaker in January.

title: Bipartisan support grows for Tuskegee Airmen memorial in Washington
text:
U.S. Representative Shomari Figures, D-Alabama, announced Wednesday that his bill to establish a Washington, D.C., monument honoring the Tuskegee Airmen has reached 56 cosponsors.

The legislation, the Tuskegee Airmen Memorial Act, would authorize Tuskegee Airmen Inc. to establish a memorial on federal land in D.C.

Bill cosponsors include 35 House Democrats and 21 Republicans.

Alongside Chairman of the House Committee on Armed Services Representative Mike Rogers, R-Alabama, and Ranking Member Representative Adam Smith, D-Washington, the full Alabama House delegation has co-sponsored the bill.

In a Veterans Day statement, Figures described the legislation as an attempt to honor the Tuskegee Airmen’s service in World War II and their role in desegregating the U.S. military.

“I’m honored to represent the over 40,000 veterans who live in the Second District, and I will continue fighting to ensure that they receive the support and recognition that they deserve,” Figures said.

“Our community has a storied military tradition and is home to the Tuskegee Airmen, who are among the most heroic and impactful service members in our nation’s history,” the congressman continued. “They played a pivotal role in the Allied victory in World War II and paved the way for the desegregation of our military. Their contributions and sacrifice deserve to be memorialized in our nation's capital.”

The Tuskegee Airmen marked the first group of Black military aviators and support personnel to serve in the U.S. Armed Services.

The airmen's achievements in combat and activism challenging segregation in military facilities pressured the federal government to desegregate the Armed Services through a 1948 executive order signed by then-President Harry Truman.

Figures’ office wrote that the proposed memorial seeks to “serve as an educational resource designed to teach future generations about one of the greatest, most well-decorated fighting forces in our nation’s history, and to highlight the important roles that Black military pilots and support personnel played in World War II.”

Tuskegee Airmen Inc. is a national nonprofit dedicated to preserving the legacy of the original Tuskegee Airmen and inspiring youth to pursue future careers in aviation.

Figures staffers described the legislation’s goal of authorizing the nonprofit to establish a memorial in D.C. as “an essential, required first step toward making this memorial a reality.”

title: Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher Appointed Co-Chair of Reproductive Freedom Caucus
text:
Today, the Congressional Reproductive Freedom Caucus announced that Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07) will serve as Co-Chair for the 120th Congress. The Reproductive Freedom Caucus, formerly the Pro-Choice Caucus, is a coalition of members in the U.S. House of Representatives who are working to preserve, protect, and advance policies that ensure reproductive autonomy.

“I am proud join Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley to Co-Chair the Reproductive Freedom Caucus in Congress, and I am grateful to Congresswoman Diana DeGette, who has chaired the caucus since 2000, for her vision and leadership in the fight to ensure access to reproductive healthcare across the country,” said Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher. “As a Texan, I am proud to be a part of a long tradition of Texas women leading the fight for reproductive freedom and justice for decades. Today, Texans are subject to some of the cruelest and most restrictive abortion laws in the country, and I look forward to working with my colleagues from across our caucus and across the country to protect them and to protect the health, dignity, equality, and freedom of all Americans to make their own reproductive health care decisions.”

A long-time advocate for reproductive freedom, Congresswoman Fletcher has led several efforts in Congress to protect access to abortion. She is the lead House sponsor of the bill to protect the right to travel between states to obtain reproductive healthcare, the Ensuring Women’s Right to Reproductive Freedom Act, which passed the House in the 117th Congress. She is also the lead House sponsor of the bill to guarantee access to birth control, the Right to Contraception Act.

Congresswoman Fletcher and Congresswoman Marilyn Strickland (WA-10) introduced the Reproductive Health Travel Fund Act to establish a grant program to help ease the financial burden of women and families being forced to travel, sometimes long distances, to access abortion care. She also introduced the Safeguarding Access to Full-Spectrum Education and (SAFE) Training for OBGYNs Act with Congresswoman Kelly Morrison (MN-03), Congresswoman Kim Schrier (WA-08), and Congressman Ami Bera, M.D. (CA-06), to establish a grant program providing funding for OB/GYN residency programs that train residents residing in states with abortion bans.

Congresswoman Fletcher also introduced the Protecting Reproductive Freedom Act, H.R. 2573, with Congressman Pat Ryan (NY-18) to reaffirm that the abortion pill was appropriately approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Each Congress, Congresswoman Fletcher has been an original cosponsor of the Women’s Health Protection Act, H.R. 12, which establishes a federal right to abortion for all Americans across the United States.

As efforts to undermine reproductive freedom have increased since the Dobbs v. Jackson decision, including the temporary suspension of in vitro fertilization procedures in Alabama, Congresswoman Fletcher has continued advocating for the legalization of abortion in all 50 states.

title: Fong Introduces Bill to Strengthen Workforce Pipelines for American Scientists and Engineers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressmen Vince Fong (CA-20) and Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) introduced the Promoting High-skilled Doctoral Talent (PHD Talent) Act of 2026, bipartisan legislation to build accelerated pathways that take students from a bachelor’s degree to a Ph.D. in critical and emerging technology fields. This legislation will propel more American scientists and engineers into the domestic workforce, ensuring China does not surpass the United States as the global technological leader.

The bill creates a five-year Department of Energy (DOE) pilot program that brings universities, National Laboratories, and private industry together. Students in these programs would get hands-on research experience, mentorship, and workforce training while earning an advanced degree in less time.

“America’s economy and national security depends on us having a deep bench of skilled, capable, and credentialed American workers,” said Congressman Fong. “Whether it’s cybersecurity, advanced manufacturing, defense research, advanced energy systems, medical innovations, or other emerging technologies, we need more homegrown talent. The PHD Talent Act gives students in the Central Valley and across the country a faster, clearer path to the advanced degrees these fields demand.”

"Our country faces a critical shortage of scientists, engineers, and mathematicians,” said Congressman Subramanyam. “This bill shores up and strengthens our pipeline of researchers. This will in turn help the next generation of students make breakthrough discoveries in science, health, and technology, solidifying our country's leadership in these fields."

Specifically, the bill:

Establishes a five-year DOE pilot program, with Ph.D. fellowships, for accelerated bachelor’s-to-Ph.D. pathways in critical and emerging technology fields, including artificial intelligence, quantum science, semiconductors, cybersecurity, and advanced manufacturing, among others.

Supports partnerships among universities, National Laboratories, and industry for accelerated hands-on research and training.

Shortens the time it takes to earn a STEM Ph.D. while maintaining robust academic standards.

Directs funding to fields where DOE identifies a need for more domestic doctoral talent.

Ensures taxpayer-funded student support is reserved for U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, and lawful permanent residents.

Background

The bill builds on the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy’s July 2026 report, Science: A New Golden Age, which calls for investing directly in American researchers and strengthening the domestic pipeline of advanced STEM talent. It was developed in coordination with DOE as part of The Genesis Mission, an initiative to unite industry, academia, and National Labs to harness artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.

Congressman Fong is a Member of the Subcommittee on Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Protection in the House Homeland Security Committee, and the Subcommittee on Research and Technology in the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee. He has made workforce development a priority, including with his NSF AI Education Act, which builds AI and technology pipelines through community colleges and regional universities.

Senators Todd Young (R-IN) and Mark Warner (D-VA) are leading the Senate companion bill of the PHD Talent Act. Text of the legislation can be found here.

title: RELEASE: Congresswoman Friedman Honor’s West Hollywood’s John Heilman in Speech on House Floor
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, November 12, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) delivered remarks on the floor of the U.S. House of Representatives in recognition of John Heilman, one of the founders and current Mayor of West Hollywood, California. Mayor Heilman is retiring this year after more than 40 years of public service.

Watch or download Congresswoman Friedman’s full remarks here.

A full transcript of her floor speech is below:

“Mr. Speaker, I rise today to honor John Heilman, one of the founders and the Mayor of West Hollywood, California who is retiring after nearly forty years on the City Council.

In 1984, John was elected to West Hollywood’s very first City Council. He helped build that city from day one, and he’s one of the longest-serving openly gay elected officials in the United States of America.

In 1985, in the early years of the AIDS crisis, John helped write one of the nation’s first laws banning discrimination against people living with HIV and AIDS. He helped create one of the country’s first domestic partnership registries — extending recognition and benefits to same-sex couples and senior residents. And he co-founded the West Hollywood Community Housing Corporation to build affordable housing.

His colleagues have chosen him to lead as mayor again and again, most recently this past year. Along the way, he’s spent decades teaching law at Whittier, Southwestern, USC, and UCLA, mentoring generations of lawyers. And in his final term, he’s donating his entire council salary to community organizations.

As a former mayor myself, I know how much of this work happens far from the cameras without public accolades. John has done it for four decades, and I want to thank him for all of his work and service.”

###

title: Congressman Maxwell Frost Introduces No Kids as Bait Act to Stop ICE from Using Children to Target Their Families
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Maxwell Alejandro Frost (FL-10) introduced the No Kids as Bait Act, legislation to prohibit U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) from taking children into custody as a way to arrest their parents, relatives, or caregivers. The legislation is cosponsored by 27 House Democrats.

Under the Trump Administration, ICE has used children as bait in its immigration enforcement operations, including attempts to lure parents and other family members out of their homes so agents can arrest them.

In January 2026, ICE agents detained five-year-old Liam Conejo Ramos in Minnesota, using him to lure his mother out of their home before detaining him and his family for nearly two weeks. Other families have reported similar tactics, including an attempt to use a five-year-old girl with autism to pressure her father to surrender.

The No Kids as Bait Act would prohibit the Department of Homeland Security from taking a child into custody for the purpose of apprehending their parent, step-parent, legal guardian, adult relative, or, in the case of an unaccompanied child, their sponsor or a member of the sponsor's household.

“No child should ever be used as bait to arrest their parent. These are children, not tools for ICE to use in its immigration crackdown. Parents should never have to worry that their child could be taken away just because the government wants to get to them. This bill draws a clear line: children deserve to be protected, not used as leverage against their families,” said Congressman Frost.

“Children should never be used as bait in immigration enforcement. Taking a child into custody to lure a parent or sponsor into detention is a cruel and deeply harmful practice that puts children in emotional and physical danger, and undermines the basic trust every family should have in our institutions. The No Kids as Bait Act is an important step toward protecting children from being weaponized by immigration enforcement and affirming that no child should ever be treated as a tool for their parent's arrest. Every child deserves safety, dignity, and the freedom to simply be a child,” said Tessa Petit, Executive Director, Florida Immigration Coalition.

"Children are gifts, not pawns. Toddlers and teens must never be used as bait to lure their families into ICE custody, and such weaponization of a parent’s love is reprehensible. The No Kids as Bait Act is an important step toward preventing abusive tactics from this administration to target families for deportation that undermine a kid's safety and fundamental rights. Congress must make clear that children are not leverage, and that their dignity, family unity, and access to due process must remain paramount,” said Lillie Hinkle, Manager of Federal Policy, Acacia Center for Justice.

"Every child deserves a safe home with family, yet the Trump administration has waged a relentless attack on immigrant children and families. Its enforcement tactics have put kids in harm’s way, torn families apart, and spread fear throughout communities nationwide. In barring the use of sponsor information for civil immigration enforcement, and by prohibiting the apprehension of children as a means of reaching their parents, relatives, or sponsors, the No Kids as Bait Act protects children’s safety and well-being,” said Melissa Adamson, Senior Attorney, National Center for Youth Law.

"Intentionally exposing children to the harm of ICE attacks should fill us with shame. These unethical and inhumane acts will psychologically damage this and future generations if we do not put a stop to it now.” — Nicole Tooker, UPLAN Parent Leader

“There is one question every policy affecting children should have to answer: Is it good for the children? Taking a child into custody to apprehend their mother, father, or sponsor fails that simple test. No child should ever be used as bait, particularly for anti-immigrant enforcement tactics. Those actions are harms and cruelties inflicted on children that have lifelong consequences. First Focus Campaign for Children is proud to endorse Rep. Frost’s No Kids As Bait Act, which puts the safety and well-being of children ahead of an enforcement agenda that treats them as collateral.” — Bruce Lesley, President, First Focus Campaign for Children, President

The No Kids as Bait Act is cosponsored by Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Andre Carson (IN-07), Greg Casar (TX-37), Yvette D. Clarke (NY-09), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Glenn Ivey (MD-04), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Emily Randall (WA-06), Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Adam Smith (WA-09), Mark Takano (CA-39), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Nydia Velázquez (NY-07), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), and Nikema Williams (GA-05).

The No Kids as Bait Act is endorsed by Florida Immigration Coalition (FLIC), Acacia Center for Justice, National Center for Youth Law, National Immigrant Justice Center, First Focus Campaign for Children, Young Center for Immigrant Children’s Rights, United Parent Leaders Action Network, and Center for Law and Social Policy.

___

Background:

The No Kids As Bait Act would also prohibit officers from forcing children to interpret or translate during immigration enforcement interviews, require written documentation of the legal basis for a child's detention within 72 hours, and extend these protections to state and local law enforcement officers operating under 287(g) agreements.

The bill would further prohibit the Department of Health and Human Services from sharing sponsors' immigration status information with DHS for civil immigration enforcement purposes and require regular oversight reports from the Inspectors General of DHS and HHS to ensure compliance.

title: Congressman Fuller Introduces Veterans Claims Timeliness, Accountability, and Care Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.- Today, Congressman Fuller introduced the Veterans Claims Timeliness, Accountability, and Care Act.

These reforms to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) would establish clear legal deadlines to ensure the timely processing of veterans’ disability claims and appeals, hold VA employees accountable for improperly denying claims when those errors are confirmed through quality reviews, and ensure that medical professionals are rewarded based on their productivity and the quality of care they provide. It would also improve the sharing of medical records between the VA’s benefits and healthcare systems and require greater public reporting and transparency.

“Our veterans made sacrifices for this country, and we have a responsibility to keep our promise to them. Veterans should not have to wait months or years for answers regarding the benefits they have rightfully earned through their service and sacrifice to our Nation.This legislation is about honoring our commitment to those who have sacrificed for our freedoms and making sure the VA delivers for them." – Congressman Clay Fuller

title: Rep. Gillen Statement on the Passage of the Major Richard Star Act
text:

“We must keep our sacred promise to care for every veteran and strengthen the benefits they’re owed, including for our wounded warriors. I am proud to be a cosponsor of the Major Richard Star Act and join the bipartisan majority to pass this critical bill. This bill honors our veterans’ sacrifice by providing the full retirement and disability benefits they’ve earned. I will continue standing with our veterans and ensure they have the support they deserve.”

title: Golden pushes for vote to protect Afghan allies in U.S. from deportation
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Jared Golden (ME-02) today joined a bipartisan effort to force a vote in the U.S. House of Representatives on a bill that would provide Temporary Protected Status (TPS) to Afghan citizens residing in the United States, protecting them from deportation.

“When I was deployed to Afghanistan, I met dozens of locals who put their own lives on the line to help keep us safe,” Golden said. “Thousands of Afghans who worked alongside our troops and diplomats now live in the United States, far from the extremists in their own country who would do them harm for the support they provided to America. We owe them the opportunity to build safe, prosperous lives here in the United States.”

Citizens of countries designated for TPS are provided legal residency and work permits in the United States, allowing them to build self-sufficient lives free from the risk of deportation while their immigration cases are processed. Afghanistan’s TPS designation ended in 2025, but conditions in Afghanistan remain dangerous for Afghans who supported the United States.

The Afghanistan TPS Act — bipartisan legislation introduced by Democratic Reps. Jason Crow (CO-06) and Sam Liccardo (CA-16) and GOP Reps. Don Bacon (NE-02) and Maria Elvira Salazar (FL-27) — would restore TPS designation until 2029 for any Afghan citizen already in the United States by July 1, 2029, provided they clear biometric and security screening.

House Republican leadership has thus far refused to bring the bill up for a vote, despite the fact that three in four Americans support letting these vetted allies stay in the United States while their immigration cases are processed.

Rep. Crow introduced a discharge petition for the Afghanistan TPS Act on November 9. If a majority of Members sign the petition, it would require the Speaker of the House to schedule a vote on the bill. Golden signed the petition today, the 109th Member to do so. It takes 218 signatures to force a vote on the bill.

title: House Passes Major Richard Star Act to End the “Wounded Veteran Tax,” Goodlander Calls on Senate to Finish the Job
text:
Goodlander, a Navy Reserve veteran, helped force today’s vote by signing the bipartisan discharge petition and fighting for the bill on the House Armed Services Committee

Washington, D.C. — Today, one day after Veterans Day, the House overwhelmingly passed the Major Richard Star Act, a bipartisan bill that would end the “wounded veteran tax” — a decades-old loophole that forces combat-injured veterans to give up part of their retirement pay if they also receive disability compensation due to the sacrifice they made to our country. Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander, who served 11 years as an intelligence officer in the U.S. Navy Reserve and now serves on the House Armed Services and Veterans’ Affairs Committees, championed the bill as an original cosponsor and helped lead the fight to force today’s vote.

“American heroes like Major Richard Star put their lives on the line for America — the last thing our own government should do is cut the pay and benefits our combat-disabled have earned,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “Right now, our government is taxing tens of thousands of our combat veterans — and it’s dead wrong. No American patriot who gives their health to our country should have to choose between the pay and benefits they earned. The House took a mission-critical step today to correct this grave injustice, and the Senate must act now to make our bipartisan bill law — without delay.”

Under current law, American servicemembers who are medically retired because of combat-related disabilities before reaching 20 years of service see their military retirement pay cut dollar for dollar by their VA disability compensation. The Major Richard Star Act ends that injustice for nearly 60,000 combat-injured veterans, so they receive both benefits in full.

The bipartisan bill is named for Major Richard Star, an Army combat engineer who cleared roadside bombs in Iraq and Afghanistan so his fellow soldiers could make it home safe. In 2018, Major Star was diagnosed with stage 4 lung cancer linked to burn pit exposure and was medically retired before reaching 20 years of service. He spent his final years fighting to change the law that cut his retirement pay. He died in 2021 at age 51. His wife, Tonya, carried on his fight until her death in 2024.

Congresswoman Goodlander has been a leading champion of the Major Richard Star Act. She is an original cosponsor, signed and rallied signatures for the bipartisan discharge petition that forced today’s vote, and championed the Major Richard Star Act as an amendment to the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act.

A Navy Reserve veteran who served 11 years as an intelligence officer and now serves on key House Committees, Congresswoman Goodlander has delivered real results for New Hampshire’s veterans, servicemembers, and military families:

Goodlander helped secure a raise for our troops and lower costs for military families. She helped secure a 3.8% pay raise for our troops in the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act, alongside measures to make child care more affordable, including a pilot program authorizing a 30% increase in the maximum child-care subsidy for children two and younger in high-cost areas. She also fought for a Pentagon PFAS cleanup strategy to protect military families’ drinking water.

Goodlander championed protections for New Hampshire’s Guard and Portsmouth Naval Shipyard. Her bipartisan TRANSFER Act cuts the red tape that keeps the National Guard from holding on to experienced officers. Its provisions and the protections she helped secure against hiring freezes, layoffs, and unjustified hiring delays at public shipyards, including Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, became law in the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act.

Goodlander is fighting to make sure our troops get paid in any government shutdown — and Congress does not. Goodlander helps lead the bipartisan Shutdown Fairness Act to guarantee that servicemembers, reservists, federal employees, and contractors receive their paychecks in full and on time during a government shutdown. She is also championing the bipartisan Withhold Member Pay During Shutdowns Act, which passed the House Administration Committee unanimously and would withhold lawmakers’ pay until the government reopens. She also offered a bipartisan amendment to the FY2027 defense bill to incorporate the Pay Our Troops Act of 2026.

Goodlander is cracking down on “claim sharks.” She joined a bipartisan group of more than 40 members demanding action from the VA, the Federal Trade Commission, and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau against predatory operators illegally charging veterans tens of thousands of dollars for help claiming the disability benefits they have earned. She also cosponsors the bipartisan GUARD VA Benefits Act to restore penalties for charging veterans unauthorized fees.

Goodlander is fighting for the modern VA that New Hampshire has been promised. She helped pass a bipartisan House amendment supporting funding for upgrades at the Manchester VA Medical Center. She will not quit until New Hampshire veterans get every penny they were promised and the health care they have earned, when and where they need it.

Goodlander helped make the ACES Act law. She helped usher the ACES Act of 2025 into law, requiring an independent National Academies study of cancer among military aviators and aircrew to help inform better prevention and care.

Her first bill helps disabled veterans. Goodlander helped lead the bipartisan ASSIST Act, which passed the House by voice vote. It would cut the red tape that keeps disabled veterans from getting the medically necessary vehicle adaptations they need to travel safely.

Goodlander is protecting the care veterans have earned. She cosponsors the bipartisan VET PFAS Act to expand care for veterans and families exposed to PFAS at military installations, and the Molly R. Loomis Research for Descendants of Toxic Exposed Veterans Act of 2025 to strengthen research into the health effects of military toxic exposure on veterans’ descendants. She also helps lead the bipartisan WINGS Act to study military aviators’ long-term brain health. Her work includes strengthening mental-health care and suicide prevention, easing the transition to civilian life, and expanding access to non-opioid pain treatment and dental care.

She is helping veterans turn their service into a degree. Her bipartisan Military Learning for Credit Act would help veterans earn college credit for their military training and experience, reducing duplicative coursework and helping them make the most of their GI Bill benefits.

She is standing up for military kids. Goodlander helped introduce the bipartisan Health Care Fairness for Military Families Act to let military children remain on their parents’ TRICARE coverage until age 26, bringing their coverage in line with private insurance.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer, LaHood Urge DOJ, Intelligence Community to Investigate NVIDIA CEO Relationship
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representatives Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), Ranking Member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence (HPSCI) Subcommittee on the National Security Agency and Cyber, and Darin LaHood (IL-16), Chairman of the Subcommittee, sent a bipartisan letter to the heads of the Department of Justice, the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, the Central Intelligence Agency, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, and the National Security Agency. The letter urges them to investigate the publicly reported relationship between NVIDIA chief executive Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, a former executive of the Singapore-based firm Megaspeed who has reportedly been linked ot the People’s Republic of China (PRC) Intelligence.

In their letter, the members wrote that the relationship “raises significant national security concerns regarding PRC infiltration into one of the world’s most valuable companies and PRC access to restricted high-performance graphics processing units (GPUs) and hardware.” They warned: “In PRC hands, this technology could be used to train military AI systems, accelerate cyber operations against U.S. networks, and expand state surveillance.”

title: House Passes Comprehensive Bill to Support America’s Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Brett Guthrie (KY-02) issued the following statement after yesterday's passage of H.R. 9237, the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act. This legislation, which includes over 60 bipartisan bills, continues to deliver on the House of Representatives’ commitment to provide meaningful support to those who served our nation in uniform.

“As a graduate of West Point and former U.S. Army officer, I was proud to see the passage of the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act to support those who have sacrificed so much for our nation,” said Congressman Guthrie. “From increasing benefits for disabled veterans, to strengthening access to community care, and bolstering grant programs to support mental health care for veterans, this legislation is a win for those who have served our country with distinction. I was glad to support this bill to honor our nation’s heroes in honor of Veterans Day this week.”

title: Congressman Rogers Votes to Advance Major Richard Star Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Rep. Harold “Hal” Rogers (KY-05) voted for the Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102), allowing eligible veterans with a combat-related disability to receive retirement pay without reducing disability compensation. The bill includes veterans with a combat-related disability and fewer than 20 years of creditable service.

The late Army Major Richard Star was forced into early medical retirement before reaching 20 years of service. Star developed lung cancer linked to toxic exposure during deployments to the Middle East. His military retirement pay was reduced dollar for dollar by the amount of VA disability compensation he received. Star lost his battle with cancer in February 2020. The bill named in his memory eliminates that offset for nearly 60,000 veterans.

“Our wounded American heroes deserve their maximum benefits, and they should not be penalized by a reduction in retirement pay. We honor the memory of Major Richard Star by ensuring other wounded warriors must no longer calculate for a loss of benefits when it’s time to retire. This fix has been long overdue, and I was proud to advance the bill out of the House on behalf of our veterans in southern and eastern Kentucky, and across the country," said Congressman Rogers, who is a veteran of the Kentucky National Guard.

The Major Richard Starr Act overwhelmingly passed the House by a vote of 392-18. The bill now moves to the Senate for consideration.

For more information about Congressman Rogers’ work in Washington and at home in Kentucky, visit halrogers.house.gov and follow him on social media.

title: Hoyer Statement on the Passage of the Major Richard Star Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC - Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement regarding passage of H.R. 2102, the Major Richard Star Act:

"I was proud to vote for the Major Richard Star Act, which would finally allow disabled veterans to collect their full military retirement benefits. It is shameful that House Republican leaders blocked the bill from a vote for so long, requiring Democrats and a handful of Republican allies to force it to the Floor with a discharge petition. That it received 392 votes in support demonstrates the foolishness of Republicans leaders’ decision not to allow its consideration.

“Alongside the Major Richard Star Act, the House also considered a Republican alternative - the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act - that would address the same problem but do it in a way that would shortchange other veterans programs. We must not rob Peter to pay Paul, which is why I opposed that bill.

“America must take the best care possible of its wounded warriors. That’s why I’m urging the Senate to take up the Major Richard Star Act without delay - and not the short-sighted Republican alternative. Let’s get this done for our veterans before the end of the 119th Congress.”

title: Merkley, Wyden, Hoyle, Bentz Push VA to Prioritize Oregon Veterans’ Homes
text:
Washington, D.C. – Marking Veterans Day this week, Oregon’s U.S. Senators Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden, alongside Val Hoyle (OR-04) and U.S. Representatives Cliff Bentz (OR-02), are calling on the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to prioritize funding for the construction of Oregon Department of Veterans’ Affairs’ (ODVA) proposed Roseburg State Veterans’ Home project and renovation of the Edward C. Allworth Veterans’ Home, a 154-bed assisted living facility in Lebanon.

“Continued investment in Oregon’s veterans’ care infrastructure is essential to meet the needs of our state’s geographically diverse veteran population, particularly in rural Oregon,” wrote the bipartisan group of lawmakers to VA Secretary Doug Collins.

Currently, ODVA operates two high-quality, award-winning veterans’ homes. These facilities provide skilled and long-term nursing, memory, and rehabilitative care to veterans, their spouses, and Gold Star parents, which allows veterans to live in a culture of community with fellow veterans and those with shared military experiences. To build on the success of the state’s veterans’ homes, the lawmakers are urging the VA to prioritize fully funding the agency’s Priority 1 State Home Construction List, including the Roseburg Veterans’ Home and Edward C. Allworth Veterans’ Home projects.

“We support efforts to fully fund the Priority 1 list and urge the VA to work quickly in coordination with Congress to make that funding a reality. By working together, the VA, Congress and the State of Oregon can help ensure that veterans and their families have access to the care, dignity and support they have earned,” the lawmakers concluded.

Roseburg has a sizable veteran population, with current estimates suggesting that Douglas County is home to over 10,000 veterans, many of whom served in the Vietnam War era or earlier. A new facility in the community would provide an affordable, high-quality, long-term care option for the estimated 68,000 veterans across the VA Southern Oregon Healthcare System service area, which includes Jackson, Josephine, Klamath, and Lake counties in Oregon as well as Siskiyou and Del Norte counties in California.

Previously, Merkley, Wyden, and Hoyle sent a letter in support of the Roseburg State Veterans' Home project, which remains in the preliminary stages of preconstruction. With Oregon doing its part to make it a reality, the bipartisan group of lawmakers is now urging the VA to work with Congress and fully fund this long-awaited project.

Full text of the latest letter can be found HERE.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES: “AMERICA VOTED FOR DRAMATIC CHANGE LAST TUESDAY AND HOUSE DEMOCRATS ARE GOING TO WORK HARD TO DELIVER IT”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries held a press conference, where he emphasized that House Democrats are committed to lowering the high cost of living while holding the crooks who have ripped off the American people accountable.

LEADER JEFFRIES: There’s an ongoing active shooter situation in Washington, D.C. The Capitol complex, as we understand it, is safe. But our prayers and our thoughts certainly go out to anyone who has been victimized or hurt by this tragedy, all of the family members and loved ones, as well as our thanks go out to the Capitol Police, as well as, of course, the Metropolitan D.C. Police Department and all of our law enforcement professionals who continue to work incredibly hard to keep the American people safe. And we’re grateful for their service, their courage, their bravery and their work.

Earlier on the Floor today, House Democrats once again successfully forced a vote on a piece of legislation designed to make life better for the American people. And the American people have had enough—had enough of the corruption, had enough of the extremism, had enough of Republicans in Congress focused on the wealthy, the well-off and the well-connected.

House Democrats are going to focus on making life more affordable for working-class Americans, middle-class Americans, all those who aspire to be part of the middle class and everyday Americans in every part of this great country. We’re going to fight for small-town America. We’re going to fight for rural America. We’re going to fight for urban America. We’re going to fight for the heartland of America. We’re going to fight for Black and brown communities all across America. We’re going to fight to make this country affordable, to drive down the high cost of living and, at the same period of time, make sure that we’re holding the crooks accountable who have visited unprecedented corruption on the American people.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES STATEMENT ON BUILDING COLLAPSE IN FLATBUSH, BROOKLYN
text:
UPDATE: Termination of Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and Syrians

On Tuesday, June 25, 2026, the Supreme Court ruled that the Trump administration could move forward with its plans to rip legal status away from nearly 350,000 current Haitian and Syrian Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders. Following this decision, the Department of Homeland Security announced the termination of TPS for Haitians and Syrians, effective July 27, 2026.

Individuals who have lost TPS may be impacted in different ways, including loss of protection from deportation and loss of work authorization. However, there may be alternative legal pathways to remain and work in the United States. To learn more about what the end of TPS means for you and your family:

All TPS holders regardless of designation should visit the USCIS website for the latest updates on their TPS status.

Visit the NYC Mayor’s Office of Immigration Affairs website to learn more about what the expiration of TPS status means for impacted New Yorkers. Resource documents are available in English, Arabic, French and Haitian Creole.

Contact the Mayor’s Office of Immigrant Affairs (MOIA), whose Legal Support Centers offer free, confidential immigration legal help. Free, safe and confidential immigration legal services are available regardless of your immigration status and in your language by calling the MOIA legal support hotline at 800-354-0365 or visiting nyc.gov/knowyourrights.

title: Congressman Keith Self Introduces Bill to Designate the North American Islamic Trust as Specially Designated Global Terrorist
text:
Today Congressman Keith Self (TX-03) introduced the Designating North American Islamic Trust Act of 2026, or the DesigNAIT Act, which directs the Treasury Department to designate the North American Islamic Trust (NAIT) and its subsidiaries and affiliates as Specially Designated Global Terrorists (SDGTs).

NAIT is an Islamic non-profit which holds the title to mosques, schools, and Islamic centers in 42 states. The organization has faced longstanding scrutiny over its associations with individuals and organizations connected to Hamas and the Muslim Brotherhood. Evidence presented in the federal prosecution of the Holy Land Foundation documents associations between NAIT and Hamas.

Through Sharia finance, NAIT serves as a custodian and real estate trustee to some of the most radical Islamist institutions in North America. This includes mosques that harbored September 11 hijackers, raised money for Palestinian suicide bombers, or operated as “the defacto headquarters of Al Qaeda in North America.” The bill explains how foreign imams and extremists drove out moderate worshippers at local mosques and appointed NAIT as permanent trustee of these properties, perpetuating the hostile takeover of mosques by Islamist hardliners.

“For far too long, Islamist networks have been allowed to build financial and institutional footholds inside the United States while exploiting our laws, our financial system, and our religious institutions,” said Congressman Self. “NAIT's documented associations with Hamas and the Muslim Brotherhood should set off every national security alarm in Washington. Organizations with clear ties to terrorist networks cannot not be allowed to control hundreds of millions of dollars in property and operate without decisive scrutiny. We are done turning a blind eye. The United States will not be a safe haven for terrorists.”

The DesigNAIT Act would:

Require Treasury to designate NAIT, its subsidiaries, affiliates, and successors as Specially Designated Global Terrorists, subjecting their assets to blocking measures and prohibiting unauthorized financial transactions.

Cover NAIT-affiliated investment funds, publications, pooled funds, loan programs, and other entities owned or controlled by NAIT or acting on its behalf.

Establish a process allowing NAIT's interest in covered properties to be transferred to the beneficiary institution itself or an independent successor trustee that is not controlled by or acting on behalf of a designated entity.

The DesigNAIT Act takes a necessary step toward dismantling the financial infrastructure that allows Islamist organizations to maintain influence, move assets, and evade accountability in the United States.

title: Kelly backs funding for Venango County's Two Mile Run Wastewater Facility Project
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Today, U.S. Rep. Mike Kelly (R-PA) applauded $639,280 in federal funding announced by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) for Venango County's Two Mile Run Wastewater Treatment Facility Project. Kelly previously authored a letter of support for the project.

"This funding will be used for critical physical infrastructure projects supporting Venango County residents and patrons of Two Mile Run Park. I believe it's important for everyone to remember: this isn't Washington's money. These are your tax dollars at work in your community," said Rep. Kelly.

The Two Mile Run County Park offers outdoor recreation and is also a venue for family gatherings with its 12 pavilion areas, swimming beach, rental houses, and campgrounds. The current wastewater treatment facility is nearing the end of its life and beginning to fail, threatening county park activities.

title: Rep. Mullin Introduces Bill to Streamline Federal Utility Rate Setting, Lowering Consumer Costs
text:
Washington, D.C. — With electricity demand rising and energy costs putting pressure on consumers, Rep. Kevin Mullin (CA-15) introduced the Reasonable Adjustments To Energy Schedules (RATES) Act to streamline federal utility rate reviews, reduce unnecessary delays, and help keep electricity affordable.

When utilities want to adjust energy rates under federal jurisdiction, they must seek approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). However, under current law, FERC only has the ability to approve or deny utilities’ proposals; it cannot ask for changes that might better protect consumers or reduce costs. This can put pressure on regulators to approve proposals that could otherwise be improved, delaying energy projects and driving up costs.

“Too often, consumers are left paying the price when utility proposals move forward without enough scrutiny,” said Rep. Mullin. “We need to make sure federal regulators have the tools to push back on unreasonable costs and put ratepayers first. Before 2017, the FERC had the flexibility to suggest changes to utility proposals to address concerns and improve them. This bill will restore that authority, giving regulators the tools they need to hold utilities accountable and ensure consumers aren’t left footing the bill.”

“For too long, the way rates are set has been tilted in favor of utility shareholders and against ratepayers,” said Marissa Paslick Gillett, Senior Fellow, American Economic Liberties Project and former chair of the Connecticut Public Utilities Regulatory Authority. “The RATES Act takes an important first step toward leveling the playing field by protecting federal regulators’ ability to do their jobs, and making clear they’re expected to push back when utilities’ requests are unreasonable. The next Congress should build on this legislation and prioritize comprehensive reform of FERC ratemaking as a top-tier affordability solution.”

“Voters sent a clear message that energy affordability is an important issue for consumers, and the RATES Act supports an effective approach to lowering costs,” said Karim D. Marshall, Consumer Federation of America’s Director of Climate and Energy Policy. “This Act will protect consumers by letting jurisdictions expand the power grid while providing affordable and reliable electricity using a commonsense approach.”

The Reasonable Adjustments To Energy Schedules (RATES) Act addresses this by re-establishing a common-sense review process that will allow electric utilities to more efficiently work with FERC. Specifically, the bill would:

Allow FERC to suggest changes to utility rate proposals that are unfair or unreasonable.

Give utilities a clear pathway and timeline to accept the proposed fixes or withdraw the proposal without a penalty.

By helping regulators and utilities work together more efficiently, the RATES Act would help ensure the United States can strengthen its power grid while keeping electricity reliable and affordable.

The bill is endorsed by the Natural Resources Defense Council, Consumer Federation of America, and the American Economic Liberties Project.

title: Kiggans Champions Major Expansion of Veterans’ Benefits with House Passage of the “Take Care of America’s Veterans Act”
text:
Package includes Kiggans legislation to strengthen representation for aging veterans

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02), a member of the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee, joined her colleagues in voting for H.R. 9237, the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act, which passed the House by voice. The bill is a comprehensive legislative package containing more than 60 bills to modernize the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), improve veterans’ access to health care and benefits, and strengthen the support system their caregivers, survivors, and families rely on every day.

Rep. Kiggans is an original co-sponsor of this legislation, and it includes her Representing Our Seniors at the VA Act, which strengthens the VA Geriatrics and Gerontology Advisory Committee by adding representatives from State Veterans Homes and long-term care facilities. The package also includes several provisions supported by Kiggans to expand veterans’ access to health care, improve disability benefits, support family caregivers, strengthen mental health services, and open up employment opportunities for transitioning servicemembers.

Congresswoman Kiggans said, “The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act takes meaningful steps to ensure our veterans receive access to the timely, high-quality benefits they deserve. From expanding access to mental health care services and preventative health evaluations to extending medical coverage for caregivers and benefits for severely disabled veterans, this package delivers for those who answered the call to serve.”

“I’m proud to stand with our servicemen and women, and I urge my colleagues in the Senate to support it,” she concluded.

A few provisions included in the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act would:

End the wounded veteran tax by permitting eligible combat-injured veterans to concurrently receive their full military retirement pay alongside their VA disability compensation benefits through the Major Richard Star Act,

Strengthen support for aging veterans through Kiggans’ Representing Our Seniors at the VA Act, which adds experts from State Veterans Homes and long-term care facilities to the VA Geriatrics and Gerontology Advisory Committee,

Expand access to community care and increase transparency regarding healthcare options through the Veterans’ Access Act,

Increase benefits for catastrophically disabled veterans, survivors, and Gold Star Families while expanding VA home loan eligibility for certain Guard and Reserve members through the Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act,

Broaden access to mental health care and suicide prevention resources by extending funding to the Staff Sergeant Parker Gordon Fox Suicide Prevention Grant Program and community-based mental health initiatives,

Improve research and care for veterans living with traumatic brain injuries by strengthening access to specialized treatment, including hyperbaric oxygen therapy, through the Veterans National Traumatic Brain Injury Treatment Act,

And empower veterans to find employment opportunities in STEM fields by expanding the VET TEC program as outlined in the Improving Emerging Tech Opportunities for Veterans Act.

Read the bill text here.

Read a one-pager here.

The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act now moves to the Senate for consideration.

title: Krishnamoorthi, Landsman Reintroduce Bill to Stop NDAs from Silencing Whistleblowers
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) and Congressman Greg Landsman (D-OH) introduced legislation to prevent federal government employees from being silenced by non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) when reporting government wrongdoing.

The No Disrupting Accountability (NDA) Act would prevent federal funds from being used to mandate government-wide NDAs that violate whistleblower protections and hide waste, fraud, abuse, and corruption from Americans.

Earlier this year, the Trump administration announced its plan to allow federal agencies to require all government employees to sign indefinite, vague NDAs – even if they don’t handle classified information.

In June, Krishnamoorthi and Landsman led a letter to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) demanding answers around the proposal to force all federal employees to sign NDAs.

The No Disrupting Accountability Act is endorsed by the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE), National Treasury Employees Union (NTEU), American Federation of State, County & Municipal Employees (AFSCME), and National Federation of Federal Employees (NFFE).

Congressman Krishnamoorthi:

“Congress has a duty to hold this administration accountable, and that means protecting those who expose wrongdoing. The Trump administration’s new secrecy rule threatens to silence federal workers and conceal waste, fraud, and abuse from the American people. Our legislation would overturn that rule and make clear that no nondisclosure agreement can override federal whistleblower protections. Federal employees must be free to expose wrongdoing without fear of retaliation.”

Congressman Landsman:

“Government employees should never be silenced from exposing waste, fraud, abuse, and corruption – and federal funds should never be used to allow it. Our bill will make sure taxpayer dollars protect the public interest.”

NTEU National President Doreen Greenwald:

“Federal employees have the right to free speech. The administration’s proposed nondisclosure agreement is an attempt to silence the very people who can tell Congress and the American people what’s happening inside their government. NTEU is proud to endorse the No Disrupting Accountability (NDA) Act. We applaud Representatives Krishnamoorthi and Landsman for standing with federal employees and fighting back against this assault on federal worker's rights.”

AFSCME President Patrick Moran:

“Public service workers are meant to be accountable to the public, but they can’t fulfill that responsibility if they’re forced to sign non-disclosure agreements that intimidate them from sharing information that is entirely legal to share. AFSCME applauds Reps. Landsman and Krishnamoorthi for introducing the No Disrupting Accountability Act, which would block federal funds from being used to silence workers. This legislation is urgently needed to protect the public and public service workers from the bullying and fear this administration is imposing on the federal workforce. Public service workers need the freedom to use their voices to expose corruption and ensure accountability in government.”

NFFE National President Randy Erwin:

"Accountability and transparency are critical to our public services, federal workforce, and democracy as a whole. OPM's proposed rule goes against the idea of protecting whistleblowers who report waste, fraud, and abuse. Federal workers and NFFE-IAM members must be free to speak the truth about matters of public concern. NFFE endorses the No Disrupting Accountability (NDA) Act to prevent OPM from issuing this misguided rule. Thank you to Representatives Landsman and Krishnamoorthi for their leadership on this issue."

title: Lawler Introduces New Visa Pathway to Address Healthcare Worker Shortages
text:
Washington, D.C. – 11/12/26… Today, Congressman Mike Lawler introduced the Health and Human Services Workforce Visa Act, legislation that would establish a new temporary visa category for qualified foreign workers in healthcare occupations to help address persistent workforce shortages.

“In the Hudson Valley, we don’t have enough direct support professionals (DSPs), other I/DD direct service workers, nurses, doctors, and the list goes on and on. These shortages limit the amount of care that can be provided and even the quality of care delivered. That’s why I have prioritized improving workforce conditions during my time in Congress, and why I’m introducing this legislation to bolster our numbers. This bill would create a targeted pathway to fill critical positions when qualified American workers are unavailable, while protecting American workers and investing in our domestic workforce, ” said Congressman Lawler.

“The current visa frameworks within DHS are not geared toward healthcare. But at the same time, we have seen the positive impact foreign care workers have had in our communities and on our economic outlook. I was proud to work with Jawonio on this legislation, and look forward to continuing to advance policy that improves the lives of all patients and those in the I/DD community,” concluded Congressman Lawler.

“The shortage of Direct Support Professionals who provide essential services to individuals with disabilities continues to be one of the greatest challenges facing organizations like Jawonio, not just hear but across the country. We are grateful to Congressman Lawler for working collaboratively with us to develop this important legislation. If passed this would offer a promising new pathway to recruit qualified individuals, fill critical vacancies, and ensure the people we support receive the quality care and services they deserve,” said Randi Rios-Castro, CEO, Jawonio, Inc.

Specifically, the Health and Human Services Workforce Visa Act would create a new temporary visa category for qualified foreign workers in eligible health and human services occupations. It prioritizes underserved populations and communities by ensuring allocations go toward employers serving individuals with I/DD, rural and underserved communities, behavioral health populations, FQHC patients, Medicaid enrollees, and people needing long-term services and support.

Congressman Lawler is one of the most bipartisan members of Congress and represents New York's 17th Congressional District, which is just north of New York City and contains all or parts of Rockland, Putnam, Dutchess, and Westchester Counties. He was rated the most effective freshman lawmaker in the 118th Congress, 8th overall, surpassing dozens of committee chairs.

title: Reps. Levin & Crow Introduce New Legislation to Crack Down on Presidential Abuse of the Pardon Power
text:
The Abuse of the Pardon Prevention Act would strengthen oversight, expose conflicts of interest, and prevent corruption in the presidential pardon process.

Washington, D.C.—Today, Rep. Mike Levin (CA-49) and Rep. Jason Crow (CO-06), Co-Chairs of the End Corruption Caucus, introduced the Abuse of the Pardon Prevention Act, legislation to crack down on abuses of the presidential pardon power and establish new safeguards against corruption, bribery, and conflicts of interest in the clemency process.

The legislation comes amid growing scrutiny of President Trump’s misuse of the pardon power to reward individuals with glaring conflicts of interest. The pardon power was intended to be an instrument of justice, not used to reward wealthy donors, political allies, or business associates. The President’s abuses have created a cash-for-clemency economy, fueled by pardon brokers that advertise special access in exchange for lucrative fees. At the same time, President Trump’s pardons have wiped out nearly $120 million in restitution owed to victims – rightful compensation they will now never get back.

"The presidential pardon power was intended to be an instrument of justice and mercy, not a tool for rewarding wealthy donors and political allies,” said Rep. Levin. “But under President Trump, we have seen pardon after pardon involving people with significant financial and personal ties to the President and his family. The abuse of this power has gotten completely out of hand, and it’s clear that we need real reform. No one should ever be able to buy a presidential pardon. That is a fundamental standard we must uphold, regardless of who sits in the oval office and what political party they belong to.”

“No President should be able to abuse the pardon power,” said Rep. Crow. “This bill will reform and provide necessary oversight into presidential pardons. We cannot accept a two-tiered system of justice that treats the wealthy and well connected differently than working people.”

The Abuse of the Pardon Prevention Act would establish critical safeguards to prevent the misuse of the presidential pardon power by:

Requiring independent investigations by the Department of Justice Inspector General into pardons involving potential conflicts of interest, including connections to the President, family members, campaign officials, and political appointees.

Strengthening transparency and congressional oversight by requiring the Justice Department to turn over relevant prosecution and pardon-related materials to Congress within 30 days of covered pardons.

Strengthening federal bribery laws to include the President and Vice President and make it clear that pardons cannot be exchanged for bribes.

Prohibiting presidential self-pardons to prevent presidents from attempting to shield themselves from criminal accountability.

Requiring financial disclosures from pardon recipients who provide certain gifts or contributions to the President, including contributions to presidential campaigns, presidential libraries, or White House construction projects.

The legislation builds on the work of the End Corruption Caucus, founded earlier this year by Reps. Levin, Crow, and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14) to root out corruption, save taxpayer dollars, and restore trust in government. Americans have demanded change, and the End Corruption Caucus will continue working to deliver it by ensuring that government works for the people, not personal pocketbooks.

The Abuse of the Pardon Prevention Act has been endorsed by the Project On Government Oversight (POGO), Public Citizen, and Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW). Companion legislation was introduced in the Senate by Sens. Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) and Adam Schiff (D-CA).

“President Trump’s rampant abuse of the presidential pardon to reward his political allies and business associates is a clear perversion of his executive powers and undermines our democratic system of justice,” said Debra Perlin, Vice President for Policy at Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington. “This legislation addresses the corrupt use of pardons by fostering necessary oversight of the pardon process, prohibiting presidential self-pardons and affirming that bribery laws also apply to pardons. CREW is proud to endorse Representatives Crow and Levin’s ‘Abuse of the Pardon Prevention Act of 2026’ and urges Congress to pass this legislation without delay.”

“The pardon power is intended as a tool to correct injustice,” said David Janovsky, Acting Director of The Constitution Project at POGO. “The American people deserve confidence that this power is being used as designed, not as a pay-to-play tool to enrich presidents and reward their allies. We applaud this effort to bring much-needed transparency to the process.”

“The Constitution created the power to pardon as a means of mercy, but under President Trump it has become a scheme for shakedowns and a license for lawlessness,” said Jon Golinger, Democracy Advocate at Public Citizen. “The growing mountain of outrageously unjust pardons and commutations granted to money launderers, tax cheats, and perpetrators of fraudulent investment schemes is a slap in the face to their victims and to all law-abiding Americans. The Abuse of the Pardon Prevention Act will deter secret sleazy pardon scheming by forcing the disclosure and exposure of all financial gifts by pardon recipients to benefit the president who pardoned them out of the shadows and into the light. It also bolsters independent oversight of questionable pardons and strengthens the bribery laws to make it easier to prosecute anyone who tries to illegally buy pardons. Public Citizen strongly supports this bill and urges Congress to pass it and restore the pardon power to a tool to promote justice, not fraud.”

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces Bill to Close Gaps in Veterans' Cancer Screenings
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (Nov. 12, 2026) – Congresswoman Nancy Mace (SC-01) introduced the Accurate Cancer Screenings for Our Veterans Act of 2026, legislation empowering the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to review its cancer screening practices, address gaps in care, and ensure veterans receive appropriate screenings based on their increased cancer risk.

Veterans who were exposed to burn pits, toxic substances, and other dangerous hazards during military service face an increased risk of developing cancer at younger ages. Yet current VA screening policies largely mirror civilian standards and may not adequately account for those risks.

“Veterans risked their lives serving this country. They should not have to fight the VA to get a cancer screening,” said Congresswoman Mace. “Our duty to them does not end when they come home. The VA must make sure its screening policies reflect the risks they faced in service. Identify the gaps, fix the failures, and make sure every veteran has access to the screenings they need.”

The Accurate Cancer Screenings for Our Veterans Act would:

Review VA Cancer Screening Practices: Require the VA to assess whether its current screening processes provide adequate access and identify cancer in early stages.

Address Staffing Shortages: Examine cancer care coordinator staffing, workloads, and protected time, requiring corrective staffing plans if shortages are identified.

Evaluate Earlier Screening: Review whether veterans with exposure to burn pits, toxic substances, and other military-related hazards should qualify for earlier cancer screenings relative to the civilian population.

Require Accountability: Direct the VA to report its findings to Congress, identify shortcomings in care, and adjust screening policies and eligibility criteria when necessary.

The VA would be required to complete its review within 180 days of enactment and submit a report to Congress within one year. If the review identifies gaps in screening access, the VA must adjust its policies and eligibility criteria within 180 days of submitting the report.

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Statement on House Passage of Major Richard Star Act
