title: Malliotakis-Backed Legislation to Expand Veterans' Healthcare and Benefits Passes House
text:
(WASHINGTON, DC) — On Veterans Day, the House unanimously passed H.R. 9237, the Take Care of America's Veterans Act, a bipartisan legislative package cosponsored by Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis.

"I applaud the House passage of H.R. 9237, the Take Care of America's Veterans Act, a comprehensive package of over 60 bipartisan veterans bills to improve health care, expand mental health services and caregiver support, and strengthen benefits for veterans, surviving spouses, and Gold Star families,” said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis, who cosponsored the legislation.

Today, the House also approved H.R. 2102, the Major Richard Star Act. Congresswoman Malliotakis was an original cosponsor of the legislation, which would eliminate the longstanding “wounded veteran tax” that reduces retirement benefits for certain combat-injured veterans.

“Veterans who were forced into early retirement because of injuries sustained in combat should not be penalized by having their retirement benefits reduced,” said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis. “As an original cosponsor of the Major Richard Star Act, I'm proud to support this bipartisan effort to end the wounded veteran tax and ensure our combat-injured veterans receive the full benefits they have earned through their service and sacrifice.”

Together, these two pieces of legislation include a wide range of reforms to improve care, expand benefits, and strengthen support for veterans and their families, including:

Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102)

Major Richard Star Act: legislation that eliminates the “wounded veteran tax,” allowing eligible combat-injured veterans who were medically retired before completing 20 years of service to receive both their full military retirement pay and VA disability compensation without a reduction in benefits.

Expanding Benefits for Disabled Veterans

Sharri Briley and Eric Edmundson Veterans Benefits Expansion Act: Provides approximately $10,000 annually in additional compensation to certain severely disabled veterans who require daily assistance, while increasing financial support for surviving military families.

VA Disability Rating Reforms: Updates disability rating requirements for future tinnitus and sleep apnea claims, protecting compensation already in effect while using projected savings to fund expanded veterans' benefits.

Improving Veterans' Health Care and Mental Health Services

Veterans' ACCESS Act: Expands access to community-based health care, strengthens mental health and addiction treatment services, and helps veterans receive timely care inside and outside the VA system.

Veterans Infrastructure and Transformation (VITAL) Act: Streamlines VA construction and facility management, helping modernize medical facilities and improve the delivery of veterans' health care services.

Brain Health and Traumatic Brain Injury Research: Strengthens research into brain injuries and repeated blast exposure, expands access to specialized care, and supports improved treatment for veterans living with traumatic brain injuries.

Mental Health and Suicide Prevention: Strengthens mental health treatment, improves access to residential rehabilitation programs, and extends suicide prevention initiatives aimed at helping veterans in crisis.

Women's Health and Prosthetics Modernization: Advances research into menopause and women's health, improves access to prosthetics and adaptive equipment, and expands access to specialized recreational and sports equipment for disabled veterans.

Strengthening Support for Gold Star Families and Caregivers

Love Lives On Act: Eliminates key remarriage penalties that can cause surviving military spouses to lose VA and military survivor benefits, allowing eligible spouses to remarry without sacrificing critical financial and health care support.

Expanded Survivor Benefits: Increases financial support for eligible surviving spouses and families through improvements to Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) and expands access to certain veterans' memorial benefits.

Veteran Caregiver 3R Act: Expands support for family caregivers through continued health care coverage, employment assistance, professional training, and improved retirement planning resources.

Modernizing VA Services and Strengthening Accountability

title: Virginia House Delegation Urges Rejection of NextEra-Dominion Merger
text:
Washington D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) joined Congressmen Don Beyer (VA-08), Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), Eugene Vindman (VA-07) and James Walkinshaw (VA-11), Democrats from Virginia, to urge the Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) to reject the proposed acquisition of Dominion Energy by Florida-based NextEra. In a letter submitted ahead of the SCC’s November 12 public comment deadline, the Members warned that the merger, as currently structured, threatens to increase electricity costs for Virginia families and small businesses for decades to come.

They wrote:

“As proposed, we do not believe the merger is in the public interest. We believe the proposed transaction fails to satisfy the statutory requirements and because the joint petition lacks the structural protections necessary to prevent material harm, the Commission should deny the merger petition in its current form.”

The Members noted that while NextEra stands to benefit from the expanded investment opportunities created by the rapid expansion of data centers across Northern Virginia, residential customers and small businesses could be left footing the bill. The Members also cautioned that the merger could consolidate market power across the regional electricity grid, stifling competition and ultimately increasing electricity costs for Virginia consumers.

They argued that the proposed merger’s temporary incentives fail to offset the merger’s potential long-term costs. They also pointed to the absence of a moratorium on base rate increases, a cap on escalating rate adjustment clauses, and a binding requirement to pass operational savings on to customers.

The letter further raises concerns about NextEra’s corporate governance, including its history of political spending and interference, warning these practices could undermine regulatory oversight, create conflicts with Virginia’s Clean Economy Act requirements, and expose ratepayers to additional financial risks.

Emphasizing the SCC’s statutory responsibility to safeguard consumers and ensure the long-term reliability and affordability of utility service, the Members stated that approving the merger without adequate, enforceable protections would undermine that responsibility.

Full text of the letter follows below, and a signed copy is available here.

***

Dear Commissioners:

We write to express our opposition to the current proposed merger whereby NextEra Energy, Inc. (“NextEra”) would acquire control of Dominion Energy, Inc. (“Dominion”). Under the Utility Transfers Act, the State Corporation Commission (“Commission”) may approve an acquisition of control if it finds that “adequate service to the public at just and reasonable rates will not be impaired or jeopardized. “Applicants must prove that the transaction causes no harm to captive customers. We believe the joint petition fails this statutory test.

We respectfully urge the Commission to reject the proposed NextEra Dominion merger in its current form, as recommended by Commission staff.

Rate Base Inflation and Misaligned Incentives

NextEra’s investor disclosures emphasize that Dominion’s territory offers immense multi-decade capital deployment opportunities, driven in large part by the extraordinary concentration of AI data centers in Northern Virginia and future planned load. Given that this projected future energy demand in the Commonwealth will be reliant on massive bulk transmission lines, which are still socialized across residential rate classes, much of that potential infrastructure will be paid for by ratepayers. And as NextEra’s growth strategy is dependent on maximizing capital deployment, its potential acquisition of Dominion risks creating a sustained, multi-decade upward pressure on ratepayers’ bills. Captive residential and small business ratepayers will be locked into paying decades of capital carrying charges, depreciation, and an authorized Return on Equity (ROE) on this expanded rate base.

We are concerned that much of NextEra’s growth strategy is heavily dependent on data center customers. This increases vulnerabilities that exist due to overbuilding and the ramifications that could materialize for ratepayers if projected revenue from large-load customers fails to cover the full cost of the transmission buildout and necessary upgrades to the grid that increased data center presence would require. While Dominion has started work to hedge against this stranded asset risk, there is insufficient protection in the case for bankruptcy, differing time horizons for service contracts and infrastructure lifespans, as well as the burden of broader grid upgrades required by data centers (rather than just point-to-point infrastructure) where every day ratepayers foot the bill.

There have also been documented concerns about how this merger affects market competition within the broader grid that Dominion is a part of, particularly with respect to transmission and energy generation and how the new merger could create “self-preferencing” or foreclose potential competition, and how those ripple effects could then increase wholesale prices and therefore raise costs for ratepayers in Virginia.

Despite those long-term upward financial pressures, the merger sweeteners of customer bill credits and added funds for the EnergyShare program are both inadequate and only short-term. Once the sweeteners expire, the Virginia-based Dominion workforce would be at risk of significant job cuts, Virginia households and small businesses would be locked into paying those multi-decade elevated rates, with the joint petition providing for no base rate increase moratorium, no cap on escalating rate adjustment clauses (riders), and no binding mechanism to track and pass fuel or operational synergies to captive customers. Additionally, the proposed bill credit for consumers barely covers the impact that increased fuel costs are having on electric bills. Dominion already petitioned the Commission for a $10 per month increase for fuel-related costs this year.

For these reasons, the Independent Market Monitor stated, the “scale, financial strength, and operational breadth all enhance market power and any economic gains are more likely to accrue to investors rather than customers.” Thus, we must look past the near-term sweeteners and toward robust binding, structural protections that prevent long-term negative impacts on Virginia ratepayers.

We believe the primary benefits of the merger should be designed to benefit our constituents, the ratepayers, and we believe the current merger design will raise rates. To that extent, we urge the Commission to, at a bare minimum, require long-term rate protections for consumers as recommended by Commission staff and require substantially larger bill credits as recommended by the Governor’s Office before any potential merger can proceed. As energy prices have considerably increased, and this merger threatens to exacerbate market conditions that could further increase prices for ratepayers it is paramount that the Commission use its authority to protect consumers who are already struggling to afford to keep the lights on.

Corporate Governance Deficits Threaten Rate Case Prudency

A utility’s corporate culture directly governs accounting integrity, affiliate transactions, and ratemaking prudency. The Commission must ensure that any acquiring entity submits to complete regulatory transparency and that captive ratepayers do not cross-subsidize non-utility operations, political spending, or parent-company agendas.

NextEra’s operational history and recent testimony demonstrates documented resistance to transparent regulatory scrutiny. NextEra recently entered into a $150 million settlement to resolve widespread political interference and dark money schemes, which included funding “ghost candidates” against state legislators and covert surveillance of an investigative journalist. This Commission’s Hearing Examiner properly recognized the relevance of these governance practices to regulatory integrity by ordering the production of the internal “Robo memo” into the evidentiary record. We share the position that this memo should be available for review to the Commission and intervenors.

At a time when regulatory scrutiny is at an all-time high, NextEra’s top leadership has aligned itself financially with federal agendas that raise rates and undermine Virginia’s statutory obligations.NextEra’s participation in high-level, opaque federal lobbying networks heightens the risk that Virginia ratepayers could be improperly forced to subsidize national political advocacy that runs counter to their own interests. In this case, aligning with a federal agenda that rolls back renewable energy incentives, curtails offshore wind development, and props up uneconomic generation. Engaging in that advocacy, including through means designed to obscure its involvement, puts NextEra in direct conflict with Virginia’s statutory mandates under the Virginia Clean Economy Act, and introduces an acute risk of asset stranding, resource inadequacy, and costly non-compliance penalties that will inevitably fall upon Virginia consumers.

It is unacceptably risky to transfer Virginia’s premier electric utility to an acquiring entity that displays such a pattern of routine spending, through opaque affiliate channels, to influence regulatory and political outcomes. Such practices, if expanded into Virginia, would directly threaten the Commission’s ability to police affiliate transactions, enforce cross-subsidization prohibitions, and verify the prudency of test-year operating expenses. Captive ratepayers bear the cost when compliance breaks down, transactions lack transparent auditing, or management priorities subordinate the public interest to unregulated political agendas.

Conclusion

The Commission’s statutory mission is to safeguard captive consumers and ensure the long-term reliability and affordability of utility service. As proposed, we do not believe the merger is in the public interest. We believe the proposed transaction fails to satisfy the statutory requirements and because the joint petition lacks the structural protections necessary to prevent material harm, the Commission should deny the merger petition in its current form.

We appreciate the Commission’s careful scrutiny of this proceeding and submit these comments on behalf of our constituents.

Sincerely,

title: House Unanimously Passes First Mejia-Led Bill, Strengthening Disaster Assistance for Small Businesses
text:
For Immediate Release: November 12, 2026

Contact: Beth Wiesinger | NJ11AMPress@Mail.House.Gov

Bipartisan Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act ensures small businesses nationwide receive accurate, consistent information about federal disaster assistance

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, the U.S. House of Representatives unanimously passed the Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act (H.R. 10355), bipartisan legislation introduced by Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) and Congresswoman Kimberlyn King-Hinds (CNMI) to strengthen communications received by small businesses on federal disaster loan assistance. The vote marks a major legislative milestone for Rep. Mejia, as the first bill she has introduced to pass the House since taking office.

The Small Business Administration (SBA) currently distributes different information to small businesses about disaster loan programs depending on their region. As rules and resources change, SBA is responsible for updating all its disaster-specific materials. Without these crucial updates, business owners could miss critical information about the assistance available to help them recover when they need it most.

“My first bill has officially passed the House, marking a victory for small businesses in New Jersey and across the country. When Hurricane Ida devastated North Jersey, small businesses faced damaged storefronts, lost revenue, and an uphill battle to recover. When every dollar and every day counts, business owners should never have to navigate outdated or incomplete information from their own government. That’s why I introduced the bipartisan Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act alongside Representative King-Hinds, to ensure every business owner has accurate, consistent information about the assistance available to help them rebuild. This is a commonsense solution that strengthens government accountability and delivers real results. I’m proud to see it pass the House and urge the Senate to act swiftly,” said Congresswoman Mejia.

“We in the Marianas are no strangers to disasters, having been hit by two Super Typhoons just this year. The SBA’s two disaster loan field operations centers are essential for mobilizing the SBA’s response to natural disasters and for distributing information about the disaster loan program, and this bill would ensure survivors get the timely and accurate information they need,” said Congresswoman King-Hinds.

Background:

The Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act requires the SBA to establish standardized procedures across its field operations centers to ensure disaster assistance materials consistently reflect current loan terms, eligibility requirements, and available resources. The legislation also establishes review and verification processes to prevent outdated or incomplete information from reaching disaster survivors.

With more than one million small businesses in New Jersey and communities increasingly vulnerable to severe storms and flooding, reliable access to disaster assistance is essential to protecting local jobs, livelihoods, and economic recovery.

The legislation previously advanced unanimously out of the House Small Business Committee and now heads to the Senate for consideration.

title: Rep. Menefee Commends the Passage of the Richard Star Act in the House
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) applauded House passage of the Major Richard Star Act, bipartisan legislation that ensures medically retired, combat-injured veterans can receive their full military retirement pay and VA disability compensation without one benefit reducing the other, allowing roughly 59,000 veterans in this country to have more money to spend on gas, groceries, and utilities.

The bill reached the House floor through a bipartisan discharge petition that secured the 218 signatures needed to bypass House leadership and force a vote.

“These veterans didn’t choose to be medically retired. Combat chose that for them. So the least that we can do as a Congress is to make sure that we stop penalizing them,” said Congressman Menefee.

For months, Congressman Menefee has fought to pass the Major Richard Star Act without tying it to legislation that would cut other veterans' benefits. In July, he spoke on the House floor opposing Republican efforts to combine the bill with the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act, which would cut veterans' benefits. Republicans argued that the two bills had to move together, but today's passage of the Major Richard Star Act as a standalone bill proved otherwise.

With more than 250,000 veterans calling the Houston area home, including more than 20,000 in TX-18, for Congressman Menefee, supporting veterans is personal.

“My parents, my sibling, and four of my aunts and uncles have served in the military. When I was in high school, my family used a VA home loan to buy our first home. That benefit made a difference in our lives, and I know it makes a difference for so many other military families, too. Our veterans have earned these benefits. They shouldn't have to fight to receive them,” said Congressman Menefee.

Congressman Menefee will continue pushing for the bill's passage in the Senate and fighting to ensure veterans and their families receive the benefits and support they have earned through their service to our country.

Watch Congressman Menefee’s full remarks from today HERE or by clicking the photo below.

title: Reps. Menefee and Wilson Introduce the SPARKS Act to Combat Youth Suicide Crisis
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) and Congresswoman Frederica Wilson (FL-24) introduced H.R. 10991, the Suicide Prevention for At-Risk K-12 Students (SPARKS) Act, legislation to help public schools implement proven suicide prevention programs tailored to the needs of their students.

Suicide was the second-leading cause of death among Americans ages 10 to 24 in 2023. Suicide rates among Black youth more than doubled between 2010 and 2023, while American Indian and Alaska Native youth continue to face the highest rates. Yet, many schools lack the resources to address this growing crisis. By expanding access to effective, culturally responsive prevention programs, the SPARKS Act would give schools more tools to identify at-risk students, address disparities, and save young lives.

“Our schools are on the front lines of this crisis, and we need to make sure they have the tools to step in before it's too late. What works for kids in one community might not work for kids in another. We ought to be meeting these children where they are, not expecting every child to fit into the same box. That's what the SPARKS Act is about. Giving schools the resources to reach kids who are hurting and, ultimately, save lives,” said Congressman Menefee.

“Our children are hurting, and we cannot afford to look away,” said Congresswoman Wilson. “As a former teacher and principal, I have always believed that protecting our children means seeing the whole child, understanding their struggles, and making sure they know they matter. The SPARKS Act would help schools prevent youth suicide with proven programs that reflect the cultures and experiences of the students they serve. I am proud to co-lead this legislation because every child deserves to be heard, supported, and given a chance to grow up and fulfill their dreams.”

The legislation has earned endorsements from leading suicide prevention organizations, including the American Association of Suicidology (AAS), Suicide Awareness Voices of Education (SAVE), and the American Foundation for Suicide Prevention (AFSP).

“Suicide is the second-leading cause of death among young people ages 10 to 24, with American Indian and Alaska Native youth facing the highest rates while suicide deaths among Black youth climb sharply,” said Jenna Mehnert Baker, DPA, MSW, CEO of the American Association of Suicidology. “The American Association of Suicidology is proud to support the SPARKS Act because closing these disparities requires prevention built for the young people it serves, not a one-size-fits-all approach. Ensuring schools and communities adopt population-specific and research-informed practices is central to AAS’s mission of advancing culturally responsive suicide prevention and intervention.”

“Through SAVE’s Green Bandana Project, we work with students across the country to help them understand what mental health and suicide prevention resources are available and how to reach out for support before or during a crisis. We also work alongside hundreds of organizations throughout the country, including organizations in Texas, to protect children online. Across this work, we see firsthand how barriers to support and treatment affect underserved communities, including young people of color and LGBTQ+ youth. Every young person deserves access to help that respects who they are and understands their experiences. The SPARKS Act would help schools implement evidence-based suicide prevention programs that reflect the needs of the students and communities they serve. SAVE strongly endorses this legislation, and I look forward to working with Representative Menefee and members of both parties to get it passed and signed into law,” said Erich Mische, CEO of SAVE – Suicide Awareness Voices of Education.

The SPARKS Act would direct the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) to:

Identify proven, culturally responsive suicide prevention programs for public K-12 schools.

Fund two-year grants to implement and evaluate these programs.

Support schools with technical assistance to improve prevention efforts.

Report findings to Congress to guide future suicide prevention investments.

Additional co-leads of the legislation include Reps. LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D.C.), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Ritchie Torres (NY-15), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

title: Following Pressure from Menendez, Federal Watchdog Investigates FAA's Handling of Air Tourism Industry
text:
Federal audit comes after Menendez led coalition demanding tighter FAA safety rules, fewer regulatory loopholes, and reduced helicopter noise.

JERSEY CITY, NJ – Following direct pressure led by Congressman Rob Menendez (NJ-08), the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Office of Inspector General (“OIG”) announced it will launch a formal audit into the Federal Aviation Administration’s (“FAA”) safety oversight of the helicopter tourism industry.

The audit comes after Congressman Menendez, alongside Representatives Jerrold Nadler (NY-12), Ed Case (HI-01), Dan Goldman (NY-10), Frank Pallone (NJ-06), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), and Nydia M. Velázquez (NY-07), called on the DOT OIG for an immediate investigation following a series of tragic crashes, including the fatal Hudson River crash in April 2025.

“For too long, non-essential helicopter operators have exploited regulatory loopholes at the expense of public safety and the quality of life of our communities,” said Congressman Rob Menendez. “While this audit is a critical step forward, our work is far from over. We will keep fighting at every level of government until our airspace is safe and our neighborhoods get the relief they deserve.”

“Holding the helicopter tourism industry accountable requires action at every level of government, and I applaud Congressman Menendez for bringing this issue to the attention of the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Inspector General,” said Hudson County Executive Craig Guy. “From supporting federal oversight to working alongside our municipalities to pursue legal action against the heliport operator responsible for these nuisance flights over Hudson County, we remain steadfast in protecting the quality of life and safety Hudson County residents deserve.”

“Every day, hundreds of helicopters fly low over homes, schools and parks across Hudson County. Each one is a risk to the families below, and to the passengers on board,” said Nick Wierda, NJ Board Member for Stop the Chop. “No other densely populated place in America is forced to put up with this, and we shouldn’t have to either. This audit is a first step toward accountability that the federal government owes our communities. We thank Congressman Menendez for forcing the issue, and we hope it leads to serious action that ends these flights outright, before another tragedy happens.”

“For far too long, communities living under or near the flight paths of sightseeing helicopters have had to endure the excessive noise and safety risks of these unnecessary helicopter flights over their homes, schools and businesses,” said Melissa Elstein, Board Chair of the Stop the Chop NY/NJ Advocacy Fund. “In the NY-NJ metro area (the most densely populated in the country), residents continue to suffer from the consequences of Wild West-like conditions in the skies above as endless sightseeing and commuter helicopters criss cross at low altitudes on a daily basis. Major fatal helicopter crashes, such as 2025’s Hudson River and 2018’s East River accidents that killed all tourists on board, have not reigned in this dangerous industry. Whether the flights are the doors off “shoe selfie” tours or are flying with the helicopter doors closed, it is time that these nonessential flights be banned due to their safety hazards for both locals and tourists. We commend Congressmember Rob Menendez and his colleagues for helping lead this important fight. This audit is an excellent next step forward towards safety and common sense.”

The DOT OIG audit will evaluate the FAA’s oversight of commercial helicopter tour operations, specifically examining how operators utilize regulatory exceptions, such as classifying commercial sightseeing flights as “aerial photography” to bypass strict safety requirements. According to federal data, the sightseeing helicopter industry has seen over 170 accidents and more than 30 fatal incidents over the past three decades.

Congressman Rob Menendez has led the fight against non-essential helicopter traffic in the region, repeatedly calling on federal agencies to protect Hudson County and surrounding communities from severe safety risks and constant noise pollution, including leading efforts to pressure the FAA to take action on helicopter safety and calling on the EPA to protect New Jerseyans against helicopter noise pollution. He has also led several bills, including the Improving Helicopter Safety Act, Communities Before Air Tourism Act, and the Protecting Communities from Helicopter Noise Act. Most recently, he co-led the Helicopter Safety and Parity Act, which would elevate helicopters to the highest level of aviation safety standards.

title: ICYMI: Rep. Min on CNN Slams White House Threats Against Congressional Oversight, Vows Accountability for Trump Administration Corruption
text:
Washington, DC – On CNN, Representative Dave Min (CA-47), a member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and Chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus’ Fighting Corruption Task Force, slammed the Trump Administration's attempts to intimidate Congressional Democrats and undermine Congress’ constitutional oversight authority. Rep. Min outlined priorities for the incoming Democratic majority, including investigations of pay-to-play pardons, ICE misconduct, and other abuses of power, while criticizing House Republicans for spending the last two years placating Donald Trump instead of holding this Administration accountable.

WATCH HERE

On White House Threats Against Congressional Oversight

“I read the letter from the White House Counsel. It's embarrassing. It's laughable. And I looked this guy up […] apparently he's a Harvard Law School graduate. And as a fellow Harvard Law alum, I'm embarrassed on behalf of our alma mater because this is not something anyone should put out there. It fails the 1L test, the first year law student test.

It's well established that Congress has broad investigative authorities for oversight purposes and corruption allegations of criminal misconduct by the president and his other people in the White House are clearly subject to our investigative oversight authority.

So this is ridiculous and they're just trying to weaponize the government again to go after members of Congress. But we will not be intimidated.”

On Investigating Trump Administration Corruption

“We should look at all allegations of corruption. Of course, our primary duty should be the executive branch.

And if Donald Trump is worried about corruption, if he's worried about the rule of law, I've got a few other places I might suggest looking, including in his own house, because there have been credible allegations that he is selling pardons to the highest bidder.”

He launched an illegal war against Iran. The tariffs that he has levied are illegal. They're constitutional authority, not the president's. And of course, we have all the allegations of criminal misconduct, including murder and assaults on Americans by members of ICE.

All of this has not been investigated over the last two years and it's about damn time we have some investigations. That’ll all happen starting January 3rd.”

On Affordability and Bipartisan Cooperation

“On affordability, I’m happy to work with anybody and I've got a number of bipartisan bills. I'm happy to work with anyone who will come to the table, including on reversing the Medicaid cuts. That's going to be a huge neutron bomb for millions of households coming up next year.

It's going to basically kick up 10 million or more people off of Medicaid. It's going to raise costs for the rest of us. Renewing the ACA tax credits, I think these are things I hope to work with President Trump and Republicans on.

I also think there's other avenues to lower costs [...] I believe we can sue and we will win on fighting the tariffs and the Iran war and some other illegal things that President Trump has done.

I think if we succeed on the merits, and I believe we have a good chance of doing that, we will be able to lower costs for Americans within 6 to 9 months, but that's up to the courts ultimately.

But this is very clearly illegal stuff that Trump is doing. It's time we had some accountability. It's time that the corruption stops.”

On House Republicans’ Failure to Conduct Oversight

“Republicans in the House have done more hearings on trans athletes in collegiate fencing, and there's one, and it's a co-ed sport, than they have on corruption, on the allegations of pay-to-play pardons, on ICE misconduct, all the things we're hearing about that my constituents are outraged by.

Republicans have done zero hearings on. They're focused on culture wars and kissing up to Donald Trump, and that is about to end.”

title: CONGRESSMAN JOE MORELLE FIGHTS TO KEEP AMERICA'S PROMISE TO AFGHAN ALLIES
text:
(Washington, D.C.)—Today, Congressman Joe Morelle announced he has signed a discharge petition to force a vote on the bipartisan Afghanistan Temporary Protected Status (TPS) Act of 2026, legislation to protect Afghan nationals living in the United States from deportation to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan. The legislation would provide eligible Afghan nationals with Temporary Protected Status through July 1, 2029, helping ensure those who supported American troops and their families are not forced to return to a country where they face the threat of persecution and violence.

“Our Afghan allies put their lives on the line to stand alongside American servicemembers, protect our soldiers, and support our mission overseas. Our country owes them an enormous debt, and we have a moral obligation to keep them safe,” said Congressman Morelle. “President Trump has subjected these brave individuals and their families to the constant threat of detention and deportation, treating their futures like a political game. His administration’s abhorrent immigration policies are putting lives at risk, and the possibility that we could send people who helped our country back into the hands of the very Taliban forces they helped us fight is unacceptable.”

"Afghans who stood shoulder to shoulder with American troops, diplomats, and aid workers are now being detained and deported to the very regime they helped us fight,” said Shawn VanDiver, U.S. Navy veteran and President and Founder of AfghanEvac. “Congressman Morelle has never wavered on this, and his signature on the discharge petition for the Afghanistan TPS Act tells our mission partners in Rochester and across the country that America still keeps its word. Promises aren't temporary. Every member of the House should stand with him."

“Keeping Our Promise thanks Congressman Joe Morelle for recognizing the serious humanitarian concerns facing our Afghan allies and their families by signing the discharge petition concerning Temporary Protected Status (TPS),” said Ellen Smith, Founder and Executive Director, Keeping Our Promise, Inc. “Many of the Afghan families we serve in Monroe County have relatives and friends who legally entered the United States through humanitarian parole or other authorized pathways, including individuals who subsequently applied for asylum. These families fled a country where the Taliban continues to impose extraordinary restrictions on women and girls, including denying girls access to education beyond the sixth grade. The United Nations has documented serious human rights violations against Afghans who have been forcibly returned. The termination of TPS for Afghanistan has created tremendous fear and uncertainty among families who sought safety in the United States. These are people who have followed established immigration procedures, built lives in our communities, and face the possibility of being returned to a country where they would lack fundamental freedoms. We appreciate Congressman Morelle’s attention to the humanitarian consequences of these policies and his recognition of the Afghan families who are now part of our Monroe County community.”

Following the United States' withdrawal from Afghanistan in 2021, thousands of Afghan nationals who had supported American military and diplomatic operations sought safety in the United States. In 2025, the Trump Administration terminated Afghanistan's Temporary Protected Status designation, stripping eligible Afghan nationals of critical protections and exposing them to the threat of deportation. Many of these individuals and their families remain at risk of retaliation and persecution under Taliban rule because of their past assistance to the United States.

title: Griffith Bipartisan Bill to Reform Nuclear Licensing Hearing Process Passes House
text:
The U.S. House of Representatives passed H.R. 5549, the Efficient Nuclear Licensing Hearings Act. This measure, introduced by U.S. Representatives Morgan Griffith (R-VA), Kim Schrier (D-WA) and Marc Veasey (D-TX), seeks to reform federal nuclear licensing processes and improve the overall effectiveness of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC). The bill heads to the U.S. Senate for further consideration.

Following House passage of the bill, Congressman Griffith issued the following statement:

“Federal energy policy must reflect the energy environment of today, not of the 1950s. I am a Republican leader of the Efficient Nuclear Licensing Hearings Act because it will better serve the energy needs of American communities.

“A more efficient process to facilitate new nuclear energy projects will support a reliable and safe source of energy for American homes, businesses, hospitals and more. I will continue to work with my colleagues to meet America’s growing energy demands.”

BACKGROUND

In the 118th Congress, Congressman Griffith introduced H.R. 6464, the Efficient Nuclear Licensing Hearings Act

The bill amends the Atomic Energy Act by dropping the requirement for the NRC to hold a public hearing at the end of the licensing process if the license is not contested by an affected party.

Uncontested licensing hearings result in hours of preparation for the NRC staff, greatly inflate the application fees for the NRC staff’s preparation time and unnecessarily delay the approval of applications.

Senators Tim Scott (R-SC) and Chris Coons (D-DE) carry the Senate companion, S. 1757.

title: Congressman Griffith’s Weekly E-Newsletter 11.12.26
text:
In DC, majority and minority parties impact the art of legislating.

The majority party in office controls the daily legislative agenda, wields greater representation on committees and sets the chamber rules.

As a result, the minority party has less say in contributing to the legislative process.

However, as a matter of governance, there are many opportunities for the majority and minority to engage on policy in a bipartisan manner.

One such opportunity is the Faster Clinical Trials Act. Massachusetts Democratic Congressman Jake Auchincloss came to me shortly after I became Chair of the Health Subcommittee with an idea to modernize clinical trials and reform some aspects related to medication and treatment approval at the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

As Chairman, I asked Auchincloss to work with my health care team to develop actual language to facilitate what I believe to be a great idea. After a year of us working together, we agreed on an expansive bill which not only benefits patients doing clinical trials, but specifically includes opportunities for rural patients to participate in such trials.

I recently co-introduced this bill along with Auchincloss.

Clinical trials serve patients like those with rare diseases. Medical researchers lead the trials to help test potential new treatments and medical breakthroughs for these patients.

While participation in these trials is open to the public, certain patient groups are underrepresented, particularly those in rural communities.

Depending on the type of clinical trial and where you are in Virginia’s Ninth District, the closest clinical trial may be in Charlottesville, Bethesda or Cincinnati.

This places patients in a difficult situation where they question if it is worth the time, the effort and the attention to seek care for their rare illness.

The Faster Clinical Trials Act supports a new and more inclusive landscape where patients can stay closer to home and participate through local health care settings. Our bill creates clinical trial opportunities in community health centers, rural facilities and other underserved settings.

Accordingly, researchers will be able to integrate clinical trials into routine health care delivery.

With this solution, rural communities including those in Virginia will be better represented in our clinical studies!

When it comes to patient and researcher representation, the U.S. needs greater data.

That is why the proposed model in our bill pushes for an increase in U.S. patient representation in clinical trials as well as strengthening oversight of foreign clinical research.

Moreover, the oversight of clinical research moves one step further as the Faster Clinical Trials Act establishes a National Biobank Program.

The National Biobank Program would collect, store and generate molecular data and analyze biological specimens and clinical data. Program participation requires representation from every U.S. State and territory, including urban and rural populations.

By expanding the pool of patient participants, particularly in rural communities, our researchers will be able to more effectively and thoroughly study rare diseases.

As a result, rural patients’ access to care and treatment discovery will improve!

In addition to these provisions, our bill updates cancer drug development. And it authorizes the use of artificial intelligence in lieu of testing on animals.

Taken together, these ideas constitute a substantive proposal that revamps the U.S. clinical trials process, advances American medical research and accelerates the development of new treatments for patients.

The limited calendar for this Congress means that action on the Faster Clinical Trials Act is unlikely by the end of the year. However, Congressman Auchincloss and I remain committed to working with each other in the next Congress to gather widespread support for our bill.

This joint legislative effort proves that it is possible to get things done for the American people.

Notwithstanding the bipartisan collaboration discussed above, there will be areas where working together is not possible.

As someone who previously served in the minority party in both the Virginia House of Delegates and Congress, I recognize there will also be times that require me to stand up and defend the conservative values of Virginia’s Ninth District. That means stopping radical Democratic proposals to take your guns, open our borders and raise your taxes.

Accordingly, I am committed to using whatever resources available to stop radical Democrat ideas.

While governance in the minority for the 120th Congress will look different from the Republican majority in the 119thCongress, I will continue to work with my colleagues on issues that serve the interests of Virginia’s Ninth District.

If you have questions, concerns, or comments, feel free to contact my office. You can call my Abingdon office at 276-525-1405 or my Christiansburg office at 540-381-5671. To reach my office via email, please visit my website at https://morgangriffith.house.gov/. Also on my website is the latest material from my office, including information on votes recently taken on the floor of the House of Representatives.

title: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Continues Leadership to Protect Access to Sexual and Reproductive Health Care
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) led the introduction of a resolution to condemn attempts to criminalize the full range of sexual and reproductive health care including abortion, gender-affirming care, and contraceptive care. The resolution also disapproves of the criminalization of pregnancy outcomes. The resolution is being co-led by Congresswomen Alma S. Adams Ph.D. (NC-12), Veronica Escobar (TX-16), Lois Frankel (FL-22), and Teresa Leger Fernandez (NM-03).

Congresswoman Nikema Williams introduced similar legislation in the 117th & 118th Congress.

In the years since Roe vs. Wade was overturned, states have attempted to impose civil and criminal penalties on people who help others access gender-affirming and reproductive health care. States are also violating the sanctity of the doctor-patient relationship by passing laws threatening provider licensure, certification, or renewal, if even suspected of providing care, regardless of conviction.

The resolution is endorsed by 42 organizations including: Reproductive Freedom for All, National Network of Abortion Funds, Planned Parenthood Federation of America, and Black Mamas Matter Alliance. Click here for the full list of endorsing organizations.

The resolution reads in part:

“Resolved, That the House of Representatives condemns the application or use of criminal laws to punish people for the outcomes of their pregnancies; affirms that people deserve access to high-quality health care without fear of reprisal or punishment; condemns the criminalization of providing or supporting access to essential health care; affirms the ethical obligations of health care providers to safeguard patient privacy and the private medical information integral to the patient-provider relationship; declares a goal for a future in which the ability of patients to access sexual and reproductive health care, including abortion, contraception, and gender-affirming care, is universally free from restrictions, bans, and barriers, and people are able to exercise self-determination in their reproductive and sexual health and manage care on their own terms, free from coercion, discrimination, or punishment; and affirms the commitment of Congress to working toward this goal in partnership with providers, patients, advocates, and their communities.”

Congresswoman Nikema Williams, Vice Chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus and member of the Congressional Pro-Choice Caucus said:

“Since the overturning of Roe v. Wade, states across the country have criminalized care, restricted access to essential services, and threatened health care providers for doing their jobs. These attacks don’t protect people. They put lives at risk. People have died because of abortion bans, and Black women and other marginalized communities are bearing the greatest burden. No one should have to fear criminalization or risk their life to get the health care they need.”

Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03) said:

“No one should face criminal punishment for seeking the care they need, and no provider should be punished for caring for their patients. We must protect access to lifesaving and empowering health care for every American regardless of sexual orientation, or gender. Criminalizing healthcare for any person places our human rights at risk.”

Congresswoman Lois Frankel (FL-22) said:

“In my home state of Florida, we’ve seen firsthand the dangerous consequences of politicians putting themselves in the exam room under the state’s severe anti-abortion policy. Health care should be a fundamental human right and a private matter between patients and their trusted medical providers. Criminalizing medical treatment creates a climate of fear, deepens health care disparities, and puts lives at risk.”

Mini Timmaraju, Reproductive Freedom for All President and CEO, said:

“No one should face arrest or prosecution for accessing essential health care or because of the outcome of a pregnancy. Anti-abortion extremists continue to push policies that undermine our fundamental freedoms and give politicians more control over our bodies and lives. We’re proud to support Rep. Nikema Williams in rejecting the criminalization of abortion, contraception, and other health care, and we’ll keep fighting to restore and expand reproductive freedom.”

MiQuel Davies, Deputy General Counsel (Senior Director of Law & Policy) of National Network of Abortion Funds, said:

“This critical resolution affirms what abortion funds know to be true: that no one should be criminalized for their pregnancy outcomes or for providing, helping someone to get, or receiving essential health care—including abortions. Abortion funds have spent decades adapting to increasingly restrictive legal terrain as they continue to help people get the abortions they want and need. Despite the essential support abortion funds provide in communities across the nation, hostile state and federal lawmakers continue to attempt to criminalize the work of abortion funds and the people they serve. We are grateful for leaders like Congresswoman Williams who fight back alongside abortion funds against surveillance and state violence.”

The resolution is co-signed by: Becca Balint (VT At Large), Joyce Beatty (OH-03), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Julia Brownley (CA26), Salud O. Carbajal (CA-24), Andre Carson (IN-07), Troy A. title: Congressman Patronis Advances Landmark Legislation to Deliver for America's Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, Congressman Jimmy Patronis (FL-01) advanced the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act, a legislative package containing more than 60 bipartisan bills, and the Major Richard Star Act, which he cosponsors. Both measures aim to ensure America’s veterans receive the care and benefits they’ve earned through their service and sacrifice.

“Northwest Florida is home to nearly 100,000 veterans, and I'll be damned if Washington stands between these American heroes and the benefits they've earned,” said Congressman Patronis. “Our veterans fought for this country. They shouldn't have to fight their own government to get the care they deserve. It's only fitting that we advance this legislation during Veterans Day week, when we honor the brave men and women who sacrificed so much for our freedom.”

The Take Care of America’s Veterans Act would:

Expand veterans’ access to healthcare outside the VA and reduce delays in getting treatment.

Increase benefits for disabled veterans and families who have lost a loved one in service.

Speed up VA disability claims and make it easier for veterans to access education benefits.

The Major Richard Star Act would:

Allow eligible combat injured veterans to receive their full military retirement pay and VA disability benefits at the same time.

End penalties that reduce retirement pay when veterans receive disability benefits.

Ensure veterans forced to medically retire before 20 years of service can receive both benefits without losing retirement pay.

title: Job Posting: Legislative Director
text:
LEGISLATIVE DIRECTOR

Office of Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley

Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-7) seeks a Legislative Director based in the Congresswoman’s Washington, DC office. As a senior member of the DC staff, the Legislative Director reports to the Chief of Staff, collaborates directly with the Congresswoman, and leads the office’s legislative team. The Legislative Director advises the Congresswoman on policy and legislative strategy, manages the Legislative Assistants and Legislative Correspondent, and is responsible for carrying out the office’s legislative agenda, including committee work and floor strategy, in close coordination with the Congresswoman and Chief of Staff. The successful candidate will have a demonstrated track record of working with advocates and constituents to build coalitions and advance policy goals. Previous experience in the House, Senate, or Executive Branch is strongly recommended. The successful candidate is committed to progressive values and the congresswoman’s vision of a more just world.

The successful candidate is a skilled manager with a deep understanding of how Congress works, and a demonstrated track record of excellent management and policy/advocacy:

Primary responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Advising the Congresswoman on legislative strategy, policy positions, floor votes, and committee business, and preparing her for hearings, markups, and meetings.

Developing and executing the office’s legislative agenda, including drafting and advancing bills, amendments, and co-sponsorship decisions, and building coalitions with other offices and local and national advocates.

Managing and mentoring the legislative team, including Legislative Assistants, the Legislative Correspondent, and fellows or interns; assigning issue portfolios and ensuring high-quality work.

Handling a portfolio of policy issues, including those tied to the Congresswoman’s committee assignments.

Overseeing appropriations requests, Community Project Funding requests, letters, and other legislative activity.

Reviewing and editing legislative memos, remarks, talking points, and constituent correspondence to ensure accuracy and consistency with the Congresswoman’s positions.

Working with the District Director and district staff to understand and respond to regional policy issues and constituent concerns.

Supporting the legislative team’s hiring process and professional development.

QUALIFICATIONS:

5+ years of Capitol Hill or federal experience in a legislative role; prior supervisory experience strongly preferred.

Strong understanding of the legislative process, including House floor and committee procedures and the federal budget and appropriations process.

Subject-matter expertise in a policy area relevant to the Congresswoman’s committees and priorities (including but not limited to either education, health, civil rights, oversight, or criminal legal reform);

Ties to Massachusetts

Excellent writing, research, and analytical skills.

Strong leadership, organizational, and project management skills with attention to detail.

The ability to multitask, prioritize, and make sound decisions in a fast-paced environment.

A professional, collaborative demeanor when interacting with the Member, colleagues, stakeholders, and constituents alike.

EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE:

Our office prioritizes building a diverse team committed to advocating for the residents of the Massachusetts 7th. As a practice, as an office we do not require any pre-requisite degrees. Please expand on how your unique set of experiences suits you to excel in this role in your cover letter. This is a supervisory position not an entry level position.

The Congresswoman’s office is an equal opportunity employer. The office does not discriminate based on an individual’s race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, genetic information, pregnancy, parenting status, disability, or uniformed service. The office is committed to diversity and inclusion and encourages all individuals from all backgrounds to apply.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

Work is mainly performed in an office environment. Noise levels are usually moderate; current office policy allows remote work on days when Congress is not in session upon request with Chief approval

Ability to work in a small work station without an expectation of privacy; and

This role is based in Washington, D.C.

COMPENSATION:

The salary for the position is $115k, along with a competitive benefits package that includes health insurance, dental, federal student loan payments (terms apply) and 16 weeks of paid caregiver leave following a qualifying event.

title: Rep. Sara Jacobs Stresses Need for Whole-of-Government Strategy for Nigeria
text:
Rep. Sara Jacobs (CA-51), Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Africa, today stressed the importance of the U.S. creating a whole-of-government strategy to address the drivers of conflict and instability in Nigeria and the need for more aggressive oversight of the Trump Administration’s Africa policies.

Watch Rep. Sara Jacobs’ Opening Remarks Here

Rep. Sara Jacobs said:

“Thank you, Chairman Smith, and to Assistant Secretary Frank Garcia and Assistant Secretary Riley Barnes for testifying today. I want to particularly thank Assistant Secretary Garcia for appearing today, as this is the first time our subcommittee has had the pleasure, so we will have plenty of oversight questions for you.

“But let’s first start with looking at Nigeria. We all know here that Nigeria is an incredibly important country as Africa’s largest economy, most populous nation, and a significant actor in the region and on the world stage.

“Meanwhile, Nigeria is facing its own challenges – like rising insecurity, shrinking freedom of expression, and a struggling economy - which are preventing the country from long-term stability and prosperity. So Nigeria’s ability to address these challenges and the United States’ role in supporting them is critical. But these security challenges are complex and vary across the country, affecting both Christians and Muslims.

“In the northeast, Boko Haram and ISIS-WA terrorize both Christian and Muslim communities with Muslims being the majority of victims, preying on grievances from extreme economic inequality between northern and southern regions. In northwest and central Nigeria, armed clashes have occurred both between Christian and Muslim communities and among communities of the same faith.

“The drivers of conflict in Nigeria are diverse, ranging from competition over land and water resources to frustrations over the Nigerian government’s inability to meet the economic and security needs of its citizens. The latter has prompted people to resort to criminality—including banditry and kidnapping for ransom—to meet their basic needs.

“Oversimplification of these conflict dynamics is counterproductive. Insecurity and the failure of governance impacts everyone. And false narratives perpetuate harmful stereotypes and motivate tensions and violence based on religious identity. Distorting what’s happening into solely a religious narrative erases the real drivers of violence and makes it harder to implement effective solutions.

“It’s been one year since the designation of Nigeria as a Country of Particular Concern. So the question is, what has been the result of this designation and the Administration’s engagement with Nigeria? Did the Christmas strike in Sokoto and increased security cooperation get us closer to peace? Has there been real, measurable progress in improving Nigeria’s governance at the federal, subnational, and local level to protect its own citizens from violence and insecurity?

“These issues are complex and require a whole-of-government approach on both the United States’ and Nigerian sides. I have worked on Nigeria policy since I was at the State Department in 2014 so I know firsthand these security challenges are multifaceted and require holistic responses.

“So when the Department of Defense is focused on helping Nigeria target terrorists in the northeast and northwest, the State Department needs to work on the diplomatic and development front to push the Nigerians to address the drivers of violence and insecurity — not just the outcomes of them. And that includes our foreign assistance. Last year, this Administration gutted hundreds of billions of dollars of foreign aid, including hundreds of millions in Nigeria. Sabotaging our response does not demonstrate that the U.S. is serious about helping Nigeria protect its citizens.

“But there are several issues across Africa that our subcommittee has not had the opportunity to dig into in public hearings with senior Administration officials, and it’s long past time that we do so.

“In Sudan, President Trump committed to ending what is currently the largest humanitarian crisis almost exactly a year ago. He calls himself the Peace President. But unfortunately, the Sudanese people are still suffering. This committee doesn’t have clarity on what this Administration’s strategy is in strategic places like Somalia or the Sahel region. We have reports of opaque third-country deportation deals that in some cases included side deals like security assistance to abusive militaries.

“All of these issues deserve more attention in this body and I look forward to discussing some of these important oversight questions with our witnesses today. Thank you.”

title: Rep. Sewell Votes to End the “Wounded Warrior Tax” and Protect Benefits for Combat-Injured Veterans
text:
Washington D.C. — Today, U.S. Rep. Terri Sewell (AL-07) voted in favor of the Major Richard Star Act, bipartisan legislation that would end the so-called “Wounded Warrior Tax” and ensure that veterans who were forced to medically retire due to combat-related injuries receive the full military retirement pay and VA disability compensation they have earned. Today's vote comes after a Democratic-led discharge petition secured the support of 218 House Members, forcing Speaker Mike Johnson to bring the legislation to the House floor.

"When our servicemembers return home with life-altering injuries, they should never have to fight another battle just to receive their benefits," said Rep. Sewell. "I am proud that House Democrats led the effort to force this vote and ensure that this long-overdue legislation finally received consideration on the House floor. It is simply wrong that our combat-injured veterans are forced to choose between the retirement pay they earned through years of service and the disability compensation they deserve for the sacrifices they made. I was proud to vote for the Major Richard Star Act to end this injustice."

The Major Richard Star Act would eliminate longstanding inequities in military retirement benefits by allowing eligible medically retired veterans to receive their full Department of Defense retirement pay and VA disability compensation without an offset. The legislation represents an approximately $12 billion investment in our nation's veterans and is a top legislative priority for Veterans Service Organizations across the country.

For too long, medically retired veterans have faced a dollar-for-dollar reduction in their military retirement pay based on the amount of VA disability compensation they receive. The Major Richard Star Act would end this unfair practice, giving eligible veterans the ability to receive their full retirement pay and disability compensation without penalty.

"Supporting our veterans should never be a partisan issue, and we should never balance our budget on the backs of those who sacrificed so much for our country," continued Sewell. "I am proud to stand with our veterans and the organizations that have fought tirelessly to advance this legislation. We must keep our promise to those who have served and ensure every veteran has the resources they need to live with dignity."

Rep. Sewell remains committed to supporting Alabama's veterans and ensuring that those who have sacrificed in service to our nation receive the care, benefits, and opportunities they deserve.
