title: Blumenthal, Murray, Schumer, Takano Lead More Than 200 Democrats in Fight to Overturn the Trump Admin's Draconian Abortion Ban at VA
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), and House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Mark Takano (D-CA) led more than 200 Senate and House Democrats in filing an amicus brief to Minority Veterans of America v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs, a lawsuit challenging the Trump Administration’s abortion ban at the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

The lawsuit, pending before the US Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, seeks to overturn VA’s ban on abortion care and counseling. In the brief, the lawmakers argue the Trump Administration’s 2025 policy banning abortion counseling and abortion care in almost all cases rests on a flawed legal premise.

“VA’s Final Rule rests on a faulty interpretation of federal law that has significant negative consequences for our nation’s veterans. The issues presented in this case potentially reach roughly 462,000 women veterans of reproductive age who are enrolled in VA health care, along with an estimated 112,000 women of reproductive age enrolled in the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA),” the members wrote.

The members continued, “For them, the Final Rule means a VA physician is prohibited from discussing the full range of a patient’s options during a pregnancy, prohibited from providing the full range of health care available to pregnant women, and is prohibited from intervening when a pregnancy threatens the patient’s health or is the result of rape or incest.”

VA’s abortion ban, implemented by the Trump Administration in 2025, prohibits abortion counseling and care for veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries—even in cases of rape, incest, or if a veteran’s health is endangered. The lawmakers argue in the brief that VA’s erroneous interpretation of federal law means these women now cannot receive abortion care or counseling even in the most harrowing circumstances. They also argue the Veterans’ Health Care Eligibility Reform Act of 1996 allows VA to provide any medical services the Secretary “determines to be needed” and that the Veterans Health Care Act of 1992, which VA used to justify its abortion ban, does not restrict the Secretary’s authority to add abortion care to its medical benefits package.

In the Senate, the amicus brief was signed by all 47 Democratic U.S. Senators. In the House, the brief was signed by 165 Democratic U.S. Representatives.

In March, all present Democratic Senators voted in support of Senator Blumenthal’s Congressional Review Act (CRA) resolution to overturn the Trump Administration’s policy ending abortion counseling entirely and abortion care for veterans in cases of rape, incest, or health endangerment. A CRA resolution is an oversight tool Congress can use to overturn final rules issued by federal agencies with a simple majority vote. The vote failed 48-50 due to lack of adequate Republican support, leaving VA’s abortion ban in place. While the CRA resolution did not receive a vote in the House, it garnered the support of 155 Democratic cosponsors.

In September 2022, VA began to offer abortion counseling to all pregnant veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries, and abortion care in cases of rape, incest, or life or health endangerment of the veteran or CHAMPVA beneficiary. This was in response to the Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization ruling, which created urgent risks to the lives and health of pregnant veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries in states that banned or otherwise severely restricted access to abortion. VA’s dangerous abortion ban means that veterans nationwide now face those same risks.

More than 462,000 veterans of reproductive age are enrolled in VA health care, and more than 112,000 women of reproductive age are enrolled in CHAMPVA. More than half of these women live in states that have enacted abortion bans or restrictions.

The amicus brief can be read in full HERE.

title: NEWS: Senators Blunt Rochester, Fischer Introduce Bill to Improve Truck Driver Bathroom Access
text:
U.S. Senators Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.) and Deb Fischer (R-Neb.), Members of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, today introduced the Trucker Bathroom Access Act, a bipartisan bill that would ensure truck drivers have access to bathroom facilities while they deliver or pick up cargo at establishments across the United States. The House companion to the Trucker Bathroom Access Act is led by Congressman Nehls and Congresswoman Houlahan.

“America’s truck drivers are vital to keep our country moving forward,” said Senator Blunt Rochester. “Increasingly, more women are filling these critical jobs, and they should feel confident their basic needs will be met. I’m proud to partner with Senator Fischer to break down barriers for men and women in the trucking community and continue efforts to sustain and support our economy.”

“This is another way we can help our truckers who put in long hours to keep products moving,” said Senator Fischer. “I thank Senator Blunt Rochester for leading this bill, and I will keep working to take care of truckers across the country.”

The Trucker Bathroom Access Act:

Ensures that truck drivers have access to the restroom while they do their jobs, which is especially important with more female drivers on the road.

Does not require businesses to construct new restroom facilities. It does require that truckers have the same restroom access as a business’s customers or employees.

This bipartisan legislation is supported by the Owner-Operator Independent Drivers Association (OOIDA), the American Trucking Association, the Women in Trucking Association, She Trucking, and Trinity Logistics.

“For truck drivers who spend long hours on the road serving our businesses and communities, access to a restroom shouldn’t be something they have to worry about,” said Sarah Ruffcorn, President of Trinity Logistics. “Showing drivers that we value them starts with how we treat them in everyday moments. I’m thankful to see this important issue receiving attention and we are proud to support efforts that make life a little better for the drivers who do so much for all of us.”

“Truckers are the heartbeat of our economy and critical to supply chain continuity,” said Henry Hanscom, Chief Advocacy & Public Affairs Officer of the American Trucking Associations. “When drivers stop to make pickups or deliveries—which can take hours on end while waiting to be loaded or unloaded—they should be able to use restroom facilities. Access to such basic accommodations is about more than common courtesy; it is about ensuring the dignity of the men and women who do the heavy lifting to provide for everyone in this country. This legislation can also help reduce a major barrier to retaining and recruiting more truck drivers, particularly women. ATA appreciates Senator Blunt Rochester and Senator Fischer’s leadership in addressing this persistent challenge and supporting professional truck drivers.”

“Access to safe, clean and readily available facilities is a basic need for every professional truck driver, yet the lack of reliable restroom access can be an especially significant barrier for women in trucking, said Lana Nichols, Interim President & CEO, Women In Trucking Association, Inc. When drivers cannot access a restroom during their workday, it can affect their safety, health, dignity and overall experience on the job. As the industry works to attract and retain more women, we need infrastructure and facilities that support the workforce. Ensuring drivers have access to these basic necessities is a practical step toward creating a safer, more welcoming and sustainable profession for everyone.”

“Over 70% of America’s freight is exclusively carried by trucks, yet every single day men and women truck drivers are forced to ‘hold it’ because they aren’t allowed access to the restroom when picking up or delivering freight, said Todd Spencer, President of the Owner-Operator Independent Drivers Association. “OOIDA and truckers across America thank Senator Blunt Rochester and Senator Fischer for showing tremendous leadership on this issue and we look forward to working with them and our coalition partners to get this commonsense, bipartisan legislation signed into law.”

title: Booker, Durbin, Hirono Reintroduce Legislation to Improve Maternal Health Care for Incarcerated Moms
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), and Dick Durbin (D-IL) reintroduced the Justice for Incarcerated Moms Act, legislation to improve care for pregnant and postpartum women who are incarcerated. The bill would fund high-quality maternal health care and support programs in prisons and jails, commission research on the maternal health crisis behind bars, and incentivize states and localities to end the shackling of pregnant people.

“Every person, including those who are incarcerated, deserves dignity and support at all stages of motherhood,” said Senator Booker. “A woman’s incarceration does not diminish her humanity or her worth, and it should never mean she is denied the basic care every mother deserves. We have a moral obligation to protect these mothers and their babies.”

“No mother should have to deliver their child while shackled. Our correctional system should have standard practices and programs to ensure that moms who are incarcerated get the care they need to have healthy and safe pregnancies and deliveries,” said Senator Durbin. “I’m proud to join Senators Booker and Hirono to introduce the Justice for Incarcerated Moms Act to improve maternal and child health outcomes for incarcerated individuals.”

“Far too many women in prison and jail are forced to give birth in shackles—a practice that is both cruel and needlessly dangerous to mother and child,” said Senator Hirono. “This commonsense legislation protects maternal health in prisons by banning shackling a woman during childbirth and by funding comprehensive healthcare and wellness support before, during, and after childbirth.”

According to the Prison Policy Initiative, nearly 200,000 women and girls are incarcerated in the United States on any given day. Incarcerated women face a heightened risk of maternal mortality and severe maternal morbidity, and these poor outcomes disproportionately affect Black women, who are imprisoned at 1.6 times the rate of white women.

Specifically, the Justice for Incarcerated Moms Act would:

Incentivize state and local prisons and jails to end the practice of shackling pregnant people.

Provide funding for federal, state, and local prisons and jails to establish programs for pregnant and postpartum people in their facilities, including access to doulas and other perinatal health workers, counseling, reentry assistance, and maternal-infant bonding opportunities, as well as diversion programs that keep pregnant and postpartum people out of incarceration.

Commission a comprehensive study on maternal mortality and severe maternal morbidity among incarcerated people, with a particular focus on racial and ethnic disparities in maternal health outcomes.

The Justice for Incarcerated Moms Act is endorsed by The Sentencing Project; Campaign Legal Center; Chicago Votes; Civil Survival; Community Spring; Dream.Org; Empowering Descendant Communities to Unlock Democracy; Equity and Transformation; EXPO of Wisconsin; FirstFollowers; Gift of Voice; Healing Our Land Inc; Illinois Alliance for Reentry and Justice; Illinois Coalition to End Permanent Punishments; Just Future Project; Live Free Illinois; More Than Our Crimes; National Association of Criminal Defense Attorneys; National Coalition for Prisoner Voting Rights; NCJW Chicago North Shore; Raise The Floor Alliance; SACRED Acts (South Asian American Coalition to Renew Democracy Acts); Unlock Civics Coalition; Unlock Civics NM; Urban Community Unity Solutions LLC; Vermont Citizens and United for the Rehabilitation of Errants.

title: Booker, Husted, Collins Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Give Federal Police Officers the Retirement Benefits They Have Earned
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ), Jon Husted (R-OH), and Susan Collins (R-ME) introduced bipartisan legislation that would give nearly 30,000 federal police officers the same retirement benefits as the other federal law enforcement officers they serve alongside. The Law Enforcement Officers Equity Act would end a long-standing inequity that denies these officers enhanced retirement benefits, even though they perform the same dangerous work. U.S. Representatives Andrew Garbarino (R-NY) and Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA) have introduced companion legislation (H.R. 3226) in the House.

“Federal police officers at VA hospitals, military installations, and federal facilities across the country protect veterans, servicemembers, and federal workers, and face the same dangers as their fellow law enforcement officers,” said Senator Booker. “It is unfair that the federal government denies them the same retirement benefits because of a job classification. This bipartisan bill fixes that language to ensure every federal law enforcement officer who keeps us safe receives the full benefits they have earned through their service and sacrifice.”

“Federal law enforcement officers who put their lives on the line shouldn’t be shortchanged in retirement because of a technicality in the law,” said Senator Husted. “These men and women risk everything for our safety and face the same dangers as the officers next to them. This bill fixes that oversight so every one of them gets the benefits they’ve earned.”

“In Maine, we are fortunate to have so many terrific and professional law enforcement officers devoted to their duty and to doing what is right,” said Senator Collins. “This legislation would expand retirement and pension benefits to thousands of federal law enforcement officers who are currently excluded from them under the outdated federal definition of a law enforcement officer.”

Most federal law enforcement officers receive enhanced retirement benefits that recognize the rigorous training their jobs require and the danger they face. But nearly 30,000 officers classified as GS-0083 police officers are excluded, despite carrying similar responsibilities and facing similar risks. These officers serve at agencies including the Department of Defense, the Department of Veterans Affairs, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the U.S. Postal Service, the U.S. Mint, and the National Institutes of Health.

The Law Enforcement Officers Equity Act would:

Extend enhanced law enforcement retirement benefits, known as "6(c)" coverage, to these officers. That would allow them to retire at age 50 with 20 years of service, or at any age with 25 years of service;

Expand the federal definition of "law enforcement officer" for retirement purposes to cover employees who are authorized to carry a firearm and whose duties include investigating or apprehending suspected criminals, including GS-0083 police officers. The definition would also cover Internal Revenue Service employees whose primary duties are collecting delinquent taxes and securing delinquent returns, U.S. Postal Inspection Service employees, and Department of Veterans Affairs police officers; and

Count current officers' future service as law enforcement service for retirement purposes. Officers could also have their past service credited by submitting a written election to the Office of Personnel Management within five years of the bill's enactment or before leaving federal service, whichever comes first.

“All Federal law enforcement officers put their lives on the line every day, no matter which Federal agency they work for. This bill will ensure that all Federal law enforcement officers receive the same benefits when they retire,” said Yoes, President, National Fraternal Order of Police. “The FOP is grateful to Senators Booker, Husted, and Collins for introducing this legislation, which would expand the definition of ‘law enforcement officer’ for retirement benefits to include all Federal law enforcement officers.”

“Federal law enforcement officers deserve the same recognition, protections, and benefits as their counterparts across the law enforcement community,” said Mathew Silverman, National President, Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association (FLEOA). “The Law Enforcement Officer’s Equity Act is an important step toward ensuring fairness and closing longstanding gaps that disadvantage dedicated federal officers. FLEOA applauds Senators Booker, Husted, and Collins for their leadership and commitment to those who serve and protect our nation.”

title: Booker, Kim Reintroduce Legislation to Stop Employers From Punishing Workers Who Care for Their Families
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Andy Kim (D-NJ) are fighting to make sure no one loses their job for taking care of an aging parent, a sick child, or a loved one with a disability. During National Family Caregivers Month, Booker and Kim reintroduced the Protecting Family Caregivers from Discrimination Act, which would make it illegal for employers to fire, demote, refuse to hire, or otherwise punish workers because of their caregiving responsibilities. The bill would close a gap in federal law that leaves many working caregivers unprotected when they face discrimination on the job.

"No one should have to choose between keeping their job and caring for the people they love," said Senator Booker. "Millions of Americans put in a full day at work and then go home to care for an aging parent, a child with a serious illness, or a family member with a disability. Too many of them are fired, demoted, or passed over simply for being caregivers. That's wrong. Almost every one of us will be a caregiver at some point in our lives, and this bill makes sure that doing right by your family never costs you your livelihood."

Nearly 2 million New Jerseyans, more than one in four adults in the state, are family caregivers, and 75 percent of them work while providing care, according to AARP New Jersey. Nationwide, 63 million Americans are family caregivers, and six in 10 are employed, according to AARP and the National Alliance for Caregiving. Yet federal law does not explicitly protect workers from discrimination based on their caregiving responsibilities.

The Protecting Family Caregivers from Discrimination Act would:

Prohibit employers from firing, demoting, mistreating, refusing to hire, or taking other adverse action against workers because of their family caregiving responsibilities.

Bar retaliation against workers who seek to enforce these protections.

Establish a grant program to help prevent and combat caregiver discrimination.

"We applaud Sen. Booker for his leadership combatting workplace discrimination against caregivers. No one should be punished at work just because they have family caregiving responsibilities at home. Women make up the majority of caregivers in this country and addressing discrimination on the job is a key way to reduce gender inequality. Especially during an affordability crisis, losing a paycheck--or even your job--is devastating for families. We can improve workers' financial security at the same time we drive up our economy by passing this critical legislation" said Elizabeth Gedmark, Vice President at A Better Balance.

"For far too long, working women have carried the impossible burden of balancing family caregiving with their job responsibilities," said Lauren Khouri, Senior Director of Workplace Equality at the National Women’s Law Center. "Even though family caregiving provides an essential benefit to our communities, caregivers—especially women—continue to suffer unfair workplace discrimination. The Protecting Family Caregivers from Discrimination Act is vital legislation that safeguards the employment rights of individuals delivering critical support across America. Protecting caregivers is an indispensable step toward building equitable workplaces that support everyone."

The legislation is endorsed by: The Center for WorkLife Law, National Employment Law Project, The National Alliance for Caregiving, The Caregiver Action Network, The National Women’s Law Center, A Better Balance, National Partnership for Women & Families, The Arc of the United States, California Women’s Law Center, Main Street Alliance, Physicians for Reproductive Health, Center for Law and Social Policy (CLASP), and Legal Momentum.

title: Boozman Announces New Chief of Staff
text:
WASHINGTON—U.S. Senator John Boozman (R-AR) announced Rosie Heiss will become his Chief of Staff upon the departure of his current top aide, Toni-Marie Higgins, at the start of the 120th Congress.

“Rosie first served as a key advisor to me on national security and veterans policy before returning to our team to lead my entire legislative staff, including our Appropriations Committee efforts that deliver critical federal investments to The Natural State. She has admirably dedicated her talents and expertise to public service for much of her career. I am confident that she will continue providing invaluable counsel and strategic initiative as my incoming Chief of Staff to the benefit of all Arkansans,” Boozman said.

Heiss was active-duty U.S. Air Force during the Global War on Terror and deployed in support of operations in Iraq. She also held civilian roles with the U.S. Navy and the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency prior to her time on the Hill. Previously, she served as Boozman’s Senior Defense Advisor and then as a Professional Staff Member on the Senate Appropriations Committee Subcommittee on Defense. She returned to Boozman’s staff in January 2025 as Legislative Director and Deputy Chief of Staff.

Her father is a native of Carlisle, Arkansas, and also served in the Air Force. Heiss’ parents both graduated from the University of Arkansas.

“I am honored to serve in this new capacity for Senator Boozman and the team, as well as incredibly grateful that I get to keep serving Arkansans. The senator always tells us to use the power of the office for good, and that will continue to be my favorite part of this new job,” Heiss said.

Higgins is departing for an opportunity in the private sector, having worked for Boozman since 2007 and serving as Chief of Staff since 2017. Her leadership has been integral to advancing the senator’s policy priorities as well as his celebrated constituent casework and outreach. Higgins was named Senate Republican Chief of Staff of the Year in 2026 by the Congressional Management Foundation, served as a Stennis Center for Public Service Senior Fellow, and was recognized as one of the most influential women on Capitol Hill by Washingtonian Magazine.

title: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Delivers Remarks Ahead of Senate Confirmation of U.S. District Judge for the Northern District of Alabama, Justice Greg Cook
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) celebrated the confirmation of Alabama Supreme Court Justice Greg Cook, President Trump’s nominee to serve as a U.S. District Judge for the Northern District of Alabama. Justice Cook, a resident of Vestavia Hills, Alabama, serves as an associate justice on the Alabama Supreme Court and was confirmed by a vote of 49-27. The Senator delivered remarks on the Senate floor ahead of the vote.

Senator Britt expressed her strong support for Justice Cook’s confirmation:

“I am proud to speak today in support of Justice Greg Cook of the Alabama Supreme Court to serve as a Federal District Judge in the Northern District of Alabama. Justice Cook is beyond qualified to serve in this role. When you look at his resume, starting from growing up in the Shoals, where he was cemented core values of faith, family and freedom, going on into Duke University and then Harvard Law School, and then having a very distinguished career in public service, which includes being a captain of the United States Air Force.

“In everything that Greg has done in life, he’s done it to the best of his ability. He’s given it his whole heart, and he’s made sure to put the needs of the state, the country, first. Since serving in the Air Force, he became a distinguished partner at one of our state’s top law firms, where he was elected after that to be an Associate Justice of the Alabama Supreme Court in 2022, and this is actually when I got to know Greg. We traveled around the state together on the campaign trail. I got to watch him interact with people. I got to know he and his wife, Kimberly, their love for the Lord, their love for their family, and Greg’s love for the law.

“Greg wrote the Alabama Rules of Civil Procedure book, which is quite thick. Greg would take it out around as he talked to, what he would hope to be, the people he was able to serve on the Alabama Supreme Court, the citizens of the great state of Alabama. And he would always tell them the one thing that they could count on from him is not only his tireless hard work, but that he would be ‘boring and predictable.’ And what he meant by that was he was going to follow the law. The words that were in that book, that would be what guided him, the Constitution, and knowing that he was not there to create laws, he was there to interpret them. More important than his many accolades, I am really proud to call him and his wife friends.

“He truly embodies the very best of the great state of Alabama. I have every faith and confidence that he will use everything in his being to make sure that he serves the people of the Northern District and this nation to the very best of his ability. I want to thank President Trump for Justice Cook’s nomination, and I want to urge my colleagues to support him in the upcoming vote. Mr. President, this is the exact kind of person we want to see on the federal bench. This is a good day for the state of Alabama and a great one for our nation. I yield the floor.”

You can watch the Senator’s full remarks here.

title: U.S. Senator Katie Britt’s Bipartisan Water Research Optimization Act Passes Senate Unanimously
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) today celebrated the Senate’s unanimous passage of the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Reauthorization (WEATHER) Act of 2026, which would modernize weather forecasting and research to save lives and mitigate the devastating impacts of natural disasters. It passed the Senate by unanimous consent Tuesday evening and now heads to the U.S. House of Representatives for consideration.

Several bills were included in this legislative package, including Senator Britt’s bipartisan Water Research Optimization Act of 2025. This legislation, which Senator Britt leads with Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), would streamline and enhance hydrological forecasting by codifying the National Water Center, located in Tuscaloosa, Alabama, as the primary hub for coordinating flood forecasting and model development across multiple federal agencies.

“The National Water Center at the University of Alabama is leading the nation in water forecasting, and the work being done in Tuscaloosa helps communities across America prepare for floods, droughts, and severe weather,” said Senator Britt. “I’m grateful to my colleagues for unanimously passing this commonsense, bipartisan legislation and to Senator Welch for his partnership. I urge the House to take up this bill without delay so we can get it signed into law.”

Water-related disasters pose one of the most persistent and costly threats to communities across the United States. Flooding, in particular, causes an average of $8 billion in damage annually and claims more lives than any other weather hazard, underscoring the urgent need to strengthen the nation’s resilience to these threats.

The Water Research Optimization Act of 2025 would place the National Weather Service’s 13 River Forecast Centers under the direct supervision of the Office of Water Prediction and coordinate their operations with the National Water Center. River Forecast Centers use various data to forecast floods, predict water levels, and assist with water resource management efforts across the country.

By integrating each of the centers’ forecasting operations under one hub, rather than 13 separate regional offices, this legislation promotes a unified approach to flood forecasting and mitigates information silos that impede severe weather warning capabilities.

“Investing in hydrology modeling and prediction is crucial to boosting flood resilience across the country, from Vermont to Alabama. That includes supporting important hydrology research and programs at the University of Vermont that improve hydrologic forecasting, such as the Cooperative Institute for Research to Operations in Hydrology,” said Senator Welch. “I’m grateful for the support of our Senate colleagues for advancing our bipartisan bill which will strengthen and align current hydrology research at the National Weather Service with vital research at UVM to foster flood resilience and help communities rebuild better after natural disasters. I urge my colleagues in the House to support this bill and send it to the president’s desk.”

Additionally, the legislation would codify the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) Cooperative Institute for Research in Operations to Hydrology (CIROH), located at the University of Alabama (UA), to provide certainty and allow for long-term planning for its critical research. CIROH is a national consortium of 28 institutions, including UA and the University of Vermont, that leverages expertise from industry, government, and academia to promote operational research in hydrology including hurricane intensity forecasting, drought and wildfire monitoring, and storm surge prediction. This would be the first of NOAA’s 16 Cooperative Institutes to be codified in statute.

“The University of Alabama is proud to be a national epicenter for water research,” said Dr. Bryan Boudouris, Vice President for Research at the University of Alabama. “We look forward to continuing this vital work for years to come and appreciate Senator Britt’s tireless advocacy and support.”

UA has made water research a priority, founding the Alabama Water Institute (AWI) in 2017 and helping establish Tuscaloosa as a national hub for water science. The university is also home to the U.S. Geological Survey’s Hydrologic Instrumentation Facility, which opened in August 2024, and the Global Water Security Center, which conducts and translates leading global water science research into actionable insight for U.S. national security decisionmakers.

Senator Britt has previously touted UA’s water research capabilities, saying, “The hydrological research conducted at the University of Alabama is critical to our country’s national security and future.”

Senators Britt and Welch reintroduced the Water Research Optimization Act of 2025 in April 2025, and the Senate Commerce Committee unanimously advanced the bill in May 2025.

title: Budd Applauds Senate Passage of Weather Act Which Includes Budd-Led Provisions to Strengthen Hurricane Forecasting & Modernize Radar Systems
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Ted Budd (R-N.C.), member of the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, released the following statement after two of his bills, which were included as provisions in the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Reauthorization (Weather) Act of 2026, passed the Senate with wide bipartisan support. Senator Budd’s Hurricane Forecast Improvement Program Enhancement Act and Radar Next Program Act were included in the final Weather Act package, which is now headed to the President’s desk.

“North Carolina knows firsthand the devastating toll natural disasters take on our communities. From Hurricane Helene’s mass destruction in Western North Carolina to the powerful storms that threaten our coast, we have identified the consequences of gaps in our nation’s weather forecasting and warning systems. I am proud that my Hurricane Forecast Improvement Program Enhancement Act and Radar Next Program Act were included in the final bipartisan Weather Act package to modernize our weather systems, improve hurricane forecasting and radar technology, and give Americans ample time to prepare before a severe storm strikes. North Carolinians deserve accurate, timely warnings that help protect lives, safeguard property, and keep our communities safe. I am confident that our widely bipartisan Weather Act, now headed to the President’s desk to be signed into law, has the right tools to improve NOAA’s forecasting programs to better serve the American people in times of crisis,” said Senator Budd.

BACKGROUND

Senator Budd is an original co-sponsor of the Weather Act, which updates the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) research and forecasting programs to ensure the agency remains focused on public safety by modernizing weather systems and upgrading critical safety systems.

Below is a summary of the Budd-led provisions included in the final package of the Weather Act:

Hurricane Forecast Improvement Program Enhancement Act:

Enhances the Hurricane Forecast Improvement Program at NOAA by developing and extending accurate hurricane forecasts, predictions, and warnings to reduce loss of life, injury, and damage to the economy. This legislative provision would:

Improve the prediction of rapid intensification and the track of hurricanes;

Improve the forecast and communication of storm surges from hurricanes;

Incorporate risk communication research to create more effective watch and warning products; and

Evaluate and incorporate innovative observations, including acoustic or infrasonic measurements.

Radar Next Program Act:

Establishes at NOAA the Radar Next Program, which will carry out the planning and deployment of the next-generation weather radar system in the United States. This legislative provision would:

Direct NOAA to develop a plan to replace the aging Doppler radar network and implement the replacement plan by the end of fiscal year 2040;

Require the development of a phased array radar test, which can scan the atmosphere in under a minute, six times faster than current Doppler radars, detecting rapid changes in storms that allow for increased warning lead times and fewer false alarms; and

Give NOAA the authority to contract with third parties to fill data gaps in weather radar coverage by acquiring data, services, and technologies.

title: Cotton to Lutnick: Ban Communist Chinese Memory Chipmaker CXMT from American Market
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact: Tatum Wallace or Hannah McCarthy

November 12, 2026

Cotton to Lutnick: Ban Communist Chinese Memory Chipmaker CXMT from American Market

WASHINGTON—Senator Tom Cotton (R-Arkansas) today sent a letter to Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick requesting the Commerce Department ban ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) products from the American market and deny CXMT access to American technologies. CXMT poses a growing risk to American economic prosperity and military superiority due to its ties to the Chinese Communist Party.

In part, Senator Cotton wrote:

“I respectfully ask the Commerce Department to add CXMT to the Commerce Department’s Entity List to broadly deny the company access to U.S. technologies and technical support, including semiconductor manufacturing equipment and tools for any CXMT fabs. I also encourage you to exercise authorities through your information and communication technology services (ICTS) office to explore a prohibition on sales of CXMT products, especially as American and allied technologies are available.”

Full text of the letter may be found here and below.

November 12, 2026

The Honorable Howard Lutnick

Secretary of Commerce

Department of Commerce

1401 Constitution Avenue, NW

Washington, D.C. 20230

Dear Secretary Lutnick,

I write to you concerning Chinese firms threatening American dominance in the SI race. ChangXin Memory Technologies, Inc. (CXMT), one of Communist China’s national memory chip champions, poses a growing risk to our economic prosperity and military superiority. The U.S. must take action to prevent CXMT from gaining a stronger foothold in the global market.

CXMT is a leading Chinese state-subsidized dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) manufacturer critical to China’s Military-Civil Fusion strategy, meaning CXMT technology could be used against American warfighters. The U.S. government has appropriately taken steps to combat the threat posed by CXMT. The Department of War designated CXMT in its Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies. The Bureau of Industry and Security’s end use controls restrict exporting a variety of advanced technologies to some CXMT fabs. Congress also curbed further government procurement of CXMT products in the FY23 National Defense Authorization Act.

Despite Communist China’s continued efforts to achieve SI self-sufficiency, these actions have had real effects. Recent reporting reveals that CXMT will start producing High Bandwidth Memory 3 Extended (HBM3E). The company’s HBM3E chips perform poorly compared to competitors’ equivalents and their HBM3E manufacturing yields hover at 20 percent. This decision to move forward in less than ideal conditions highlights both Communist China’s desperation for chips and manufacturing struggles without advanced equipment and knowledge.

More can be done to ensure that CXMT is cut off from the financial and technological resources that aid its supply chain and undercut American growth. I respectfully ask the Commerce Department to add CXMT to the Commerce Department’s Entity List to broadly deny the company access to U.S. technologies and technical support, including semiconductor manufacturing equipment and tools for any CXMT fabs. I also encourage you to exercise authorities through your information and communication technology services (ICTS) office to explore a prohibition on sales of CXMT products, especially as American and allied technologies are available.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Tom Cotton

United States Senator

###

title: Crapo Honors 23 Idaho Veterans and Volunteers with Spirit of Freedom Award
text:
Washington, D.C.--U.S. Senator Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) announced 23 Idahoans will be recognized with the 2026 Spirit of Freedom: Idaho Veterans Service Award. Each year, veterans organizations and community members across the state nominate Idaho veterans and volunteers who have demonstrated an exceptional commitment to serving our nation and supporting its veterans and military families.

“Recognizing the remarkable service of Idahoans through the Spirit of Freedom Award has given me an opportunity to spotlight some of the great compassion and heroism demonstrated across our state,” said Crapo. “These honorees have gone above and beyond in service to our nation and in support of our veterans, and their continued commitment to serving others reflects the very best of Idaho.”

Since Crapo created the award in 2002, 447 Spirit of Freedom Awards have been presented. Each recipient will receive a certificate for their service as well as a United States flag that has been flown over the U.S. Capitol building. Nominations for the 2027 Spirit of Freedom Service Award can be submitted by contacting Courtney Lehosit in Crapo’s Boise office.

The following biographies highlight each recipient’s significant contributions to our country and its veterans:

Veterans:

Joseph (Joe) Deacon, Coeur d’Alene: The Kootenai County Veterans Treatment Court nominated Joseph Deacon, who served in the United States Air Force from 1963 to 1967 as a sergeant, earning recognition for his performance as a laser weapon research scientist. He currently serves as Kootenai County Veterans Treatment Court Mentor Coordinator and has provided remarkable support for the Court through recruiting mentors, educating the community, establishing a supporting non-profit and raising resources. For 35 years, Joe was a member of the State Bar of California and the District of Columbia in the aerospace industry and fortune 100 corporate legal and technical fields. Joseph has continued to serve his communities and fellow veterans in numerous ways, including leading veterans organizations and efforts. Joe has two sisters. His two brothers also served during the Vietnam era, and his son served in the U.S. Marine Corps. He also has a daughter and five grandchildren.

Cody De Los Reyes, Pocatello: Bannock County Veterans Services nominated Cody De Los Reyes, who served in the U.S. Air Force for 23 years, earning the rank of senior master sergeant and a long list of military recognitions. They include the Meritorious Service Medal with one Oak Leaf Cluster; Air and Space Commendation Medal; and Air and Space Achievement Medal with three Oak Leaf Clusters. Prior to retiring from the military, Cody served as the Air Transportation Flight Chief for the 67th Aerial Port Squadron at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, among his many other assignments. He was deployed four times, supporting Operation Enduring Freedom in Afghanistan, Operation Iraqi Freedom, Operation Unified Response in Port-au Prince, Haiti, and as part of the International Security Assistance Force. Cody currently works as the U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs-Veteran Outreach Specialist and previously served as Veterans Clinic Supervisor. He and his wife, Alanna, have one daughter and one son.

Russell (Russ) Dodd, Meridian: The Idaho Veterans Assistance League (IVAL) nominated Russell Dodd, who served in the U.S. Navy for four years and has volunteered at the Idaho State Veterans Home-Boise for the past six years. When nominating Russ, Roy Ledesma wrote, “His commitment and reliability have been instrumental to IVAL’s success. Simply put, it is hard to imagine where IVAL would be today without his outstanding service and leadership.” Some of the many ways Russ has supported IVAL, the home and veterans, include serving as IVAL’s secretary, consistently preparing meeting spaces, developing agendas, recording and distributing meeting minutes and communicating with attendees to ensure everyone stays informed. Russ also represents IVAL at community events and donation presentations, serving as a professional ambassador for the organization. Russ is known as “a dedicated problem solver who works tirelessly to address issues until they are fully resolved.”

Todd Hayes, Kuna: The Combat Veterans Motorcycle Association (CVMA) nominated Todd Hayes, who served in the U.S. Air Force for 26 years, earning the rank of Chief Master Sergeant and many awards, including the Bronze Star and multiple Meritorious Service Medals while deployed in support of combat operations and leading personnel. He has since devoted 19 years to volunteering on behalf of veterans throughout Idaho and the region. After joining the CVMA, Todd served in leadership roles, including secretary and chapter commander. He has been instrumental in raising funds for the chapter, making it possible for the chapter to assist veterans throughout the region. Todd, who is married to his spouse of 34 years, Kris, has six children and eight grandchildren. He involves his grandchildren in the many CVMA activities he leads and participates in supporting the veterans community.

Leo L. Hellyer, Boise: The Boise Rescue Mission Ministries nominated Leo Hellyer, who served in the U.S. Air Force for 22 years and earned the rank of master sergeant, before serving at the Rescue Mission for 25 years. Leo is the Veterans Transitional Living Program Director at the Rescue Mission, which provides transitional living and services to homeless veterans. Leo earned many awards and medals for his dedicated military service that include two Air Force Commendation Medals, five awards of the Good Conduct Medal and the Air Force Achievement Medal. When nominating Leo, Reverend Bill Roscoe characterized Leo as “a strong, compassionate leader” and noted that Leo gives his all to caring for veterans in his program and staying at the Mission, as he serves as a liaison to every veterans program in the Valley and beyond. Leo, who was married to his late wife for 53 years, has two daughters and four grandchildren.

Monte Cache Hibbert, Pocatello: Bannock County Veterans Services nominated Monte Hibbert, who served in the U.S. Army and Army National Guard. Monte’s military service included an 18-month deployment in 2004-2005 in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom III as a public affairs officer with the Idaho Army National Guard’s 116th Brigade Combat Team. Monte retired as a major from the Idaho Army National Guard in 2009 and was honored as the Military Person of the Year in 2018. Among his many other recognitions for his military service, Monte was recognized with the Meritorious Service Medal for more than 20 years of dedicated service to the Armed Forces of the United States. Monte works as a federal protective security officer, providing security at federal buildings. He also works as a support broker and community support worker, helping adults with disabilities access services. Additionally, Monte is an Eagle Scout and has received recognition for his service in Scouting America. He also volunteers as a 4-H leader, a Master Gardener and with the Girl Scouts. Monte and his wife, Farhana, have six children and two grandsons.

Dennis Hinrichs, Boise: Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) Post 4000 of Meridian nominated Dennis Hinrichs, who served in the U.S. Air Force for 20 years, including in support of Operation Desert Storm. Dennis earned many recognitions for his military service, including multiple Air Force Commendation Medals. Tammy Clement explained that Dennis was nominated because “he serves from the heart.” Tammy wrote, “Time and again, Dennis gives generously of his time to support Help Us Help Vets, volunteering countless hours and offering his truck and trailer whenever needed. Whether he is transporting supplies, hauling equipment, or simply stepping in wherever help is required, Dennis can always be counted on. His quiet dedication, selflessness, and genuine care for his fellow veterans have touched many lives and strengthened the organization’s mission. Dennis asks for nothing in return; he serves because he believes veterans deserve support, remembrance, and never to be left behind.”

David (Dave) Keaggy, Post Falls: The Idaho State Veterans Home-Post Falls nominated David Keaggy, who served as a U.S. Marine Corps sergeant during the Vietnam War, earning many recognitions, including the Purple Heart. Before joining the Marines, Dave excelled in archery, earning world records and world championships. After his service and while recovering from his injuries in Vietnam, he developed a passion for powerlifting, and he went on to win the powerlifting heavyweight national championships in 1979. Dave also coached the United States Powerlifting: Federation National Team and contributed to the team earning four gold medal titles. Dave took on his now third generation family business, where he spent 30 years in food service design. Dave also has a passion for artwork and spends his days immersed in drawing beautiful artwork. He also enjoys time with family, which includes one son and three grandchildren, exercising and reminiscing.

Rick Manning, Boise: The Idaho State Veterans Home-Boise nominated Rick Manning, who served 15 years in the U.S. Navy and continues to serve the veterans community. Rick earned many medals and awards for his military service, including the Navy Achievement Medal, Good Conduct Award and Southeast Asia Medal. He also served in local and federal law enforcement in California. When nominating Rick, Jo Ann Daron wrote of the numerous ways Rick generously shares his time and talents at the home, including his gift for storytelling: “Drawing from a lifetime of rich experiences, he brings humor and engaging conversation to his volunteer shifts, enriching the lives of everyone he meets!” Rick also brings his dog, Raider, to visit residents, helped build the raised garden boxes used in the residents' horticulture program, and refurbished display boards that showcase resident activities throughout the home. His wife, Carol, son, Cameron and daughter, Courtney, have also generously volunteered their time. Rick and Carol recently welcomed their first grandchild, a grandson, Jaxon, born to Courtney and her husband, Sean. Jo Ann wrote, "We are deeply grateful for Rick and his family. Their generosity and commitment have helped make our community a better place."

David E. McFerrin, Filer: American Legion Post 47 of Filer nominated David McFerrin, who retired from the U.S. Army after 40 years of service. He earned the rank of command sergeant major and numerous medals and awards that include the Legion of Merit, Bronze Star and Meritorious Service Medal. David’s service included deployment to Iraq as the 40th Division Combat Aviation Brigades’ Command Sergeant Major. During his military career, he was employed as a federal technician, helicopter/aircraft technician and flight operations technician. David and his wife of more than 48 years, Beverly, have two sons, both of whom also served in the U.S. Army, and five grandchildren. David has served in various positions within churches and veterans groups, including the American Legion, VFW, Twin Falls Veterans Council and Magic Valley Honor Guard. His leadership roles have included service as commander of both American Legion Post 47 and VFW Post 2136 of Twin Falls.

James (Jim) P. O’Donnell Jr., Twin Falls: The Twin Falls Veterans Council nominated Jim O’Donnell, who began his military service as a Reserve Commissioned Officer of the U.S. Army in 1970 in the Idaho State University Reserve Officers' Training Corps program. Jim graduated flight training and then deployed to Vietnam. He earned an Air Medal for meritorious achievement while participating in aerial flight, a Combat Infantryman Badge, Vietnam Service Medal and other awards for his service. Jim has drawn from his experiences living in various parts of the world and country and his love of history to dedicate much of his adult life to working as a history teacher. He has been an ordained pastor for 50 years and has served as a law enforcement chaplain. Jim also has a deep knowledge and passion for aeronautics and has served as the Director of the Magic Valley Air Show for multiple years, bringing the U.S. Navy Blue Angels to Twin Falls. He also coordinates the Magic Valley’s annual Police Officers Memorial each May, celebrating fallen officers and all law enforcement officers who work tirelessly to keep the Magic Valley safe and providing solace to their families. Jim is a pillar of the community, and as Rondal Lang noted, “Jim O’Donnell’s extensive background in education, leadership, and narrative sharing has helped him create memorable experiences for countless people.”

Kathy Peterson, Twin Falls: American Legion Post 7 of Twin Falls nominated Kathy Peterson, who served our country in the Vietnam War and is actively involved in many veterans associations. They include the American Legion, VFW and Disabled American Veterans. When nominating Kathy, Brian English, Commander of American Legion Post 7 wrote, “She also volunteers to watch over the giant flag in the canyon as needed, she drives a golf cart around to help seniors get to the fair, the 250 Celebration at the Visitors Center, and the 9/11 program that was held there. She is also one of the driving forces to get our van back to the VA so we can transport veterans as needed in our area.”

James (Jim) A. Wolcott, Lewiston: The Idaho State Veterans Home-Lewiston nominated James Wolcott, who served as a first lieutenant in the U.S. Army in the Vietnam War. Jim, who was born and raised in Idaho, served with the 68th Medical Group and the 3rd Surgical Hospital. His service included serving approximately a year in Dong Tam, providing emergency care during a period that included the aftermath of the 1968 Tet Offensive. Jim was awarded the Bronze Star for his work during Dong Tam and his unwavering dedication to those who needed his care. His service decorations also include the National Defense Service Medal, the Vietnam Service Medal and the Republic of Vietnam Campaign Medal with 1960 device. After returning home, Jim earned his Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetist credentials and worked as a nurse anesthetist in Idaho and Washington, before embracing the opportunity to develop the anesthesia department at a hospital in McCall, Idaho, and spending five years in Florida specializing in pain management. Prior to starting his military service, Jim married the love of his life, Marilyn “Petey” Wolcott. Jim and Petey have been married more than 60 years and have raised two sons, Jeff and Wes, both of whom have given their father reasons to be proud.

Volunteers:

Travis Bartschi, Lewiston: The Lewis Clark Valley Veterans Council nominated Dr. Travis Bartschi, a dentist and owner of LC Smiles, for the assistance he provides to community veterans. When nominating Dr. Bartschi, Sheila Kopezynski wrote about the challenges many veterans face in accessing affordable dental care. Dr. Bartschi saw the need in the community and took action, hosting what is now called “Smiles for Freedom.” The one-day event provides veterans and active-duty military members with free dental services, while veterans are also honored, a meal is shared and activities are provided. Sheila noted that Dr. Bartschi and his staff elect to give their time and talent without compensation the day of the event, recognizing that “One day’s pay is significant when you consider that they too have responsibilities and families depending on them.” Sheila also wrote, “I am continuously in awe of his indefatigable energy, his people first leadership style, customer-focused business approach, and most importantly his kind heart.”

Matthew E. Biggs, Kuna: Bobby D. Tettleton of the VFW nominated Matthew Biggs, who served 20 years in the United States Navy rising from enlisted sailor to Chief Warrant Officer 3. Matthew now leads as an Information Technology Area Manager at the Boise U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Medical Center and was elected to serve his community on the Kuna City Council. During Matthew’s military service, he was selected for assignments aboard three carrier/cruiser-class warships and with Fleet Air Reconnaissance Squadron Two. He deployed in support of five named operations and earned numerous recognitions for his distinguished service that include the Defense Meritorious Service Medal, four Navy and Marine Corps Commendation Medals and six Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medals. Bobby Tettleton noted, “Few sailors serve across this many named contingencies; it stands as a direct measure of his readiness, reliability, and the Navy’s confidence in his abilities under pressure.” Matthew is the third generation of his family to serve in the military. He and his wife, Angie, have raised their daughter and son in that same tradition of service.

Chris Donahue, Rathdrum: The Idaho State Veterans Home-Post Falls nominated Chris Donahue citing his great skill in reminiscing with residents by listening, showing he cares and serving. Chris, who spent 22 years serving our country in the U.S. Navy with two deployments followed by serving with the Idaho State Police, employs his years of experience in serving at the home. Chris shared that inspiration for volunteering stems from “how well they took care of my Dad.” When making the nomination, Kady Aamot noted his excellence in encouraging residents to lean into their interests. A standout experience for Chris was when he invited a resident to an art class, and the resident responded, “I can’t paint.” Chris responded, “I can’t paint either.” They ended up going to art class, learning to paint together and have been regular participants since. Kady wrote, “Chris has a life of serving and the impact he has had has made a difference in our community.”

Luke Paul Haywarde, Wilder: Bobby D. Tettleton of the VFW nominated Luke Haywarde, cited his more than 26 years of distinguished military service as both an infantryman and a U.S. Army Green Beret, and his continued dedication to veterans and the community through the VFW. Bobby Tettleton wrote that Luke, “embodies the spirit of service, sacrifice and freedom this award recognizes. His life stands as a testament to the principle that a soldier never truly retires.” Bobby Tettleton further noted, “Over six combat tours in Afghanistan, Luke earned the Combat Infantryman Badge, four Bronze Stars and one Bronze Star with Valor device, in recognition of his exceptional service and courage under fire.” In retirement, Luke continued to train and support National Guard and Reserve units preparing for overseas deployments. Luke also joined the VFW in Wilder, Idaho, where he has served in a progression of leadership roles, including post senior vice commander, post commander, state sergeant-at-arms and currently, aide-de-camp. Among his many examples of service, Luke, alongside his wife of 41 years and fellow post and auxiliary members, organized and delivered supplies to firefighters battling the large grass fire near Jordan Valley, Oregon.

Brenda Coons Houser, Homedale: VFW District 4 Past Commander Matthew Biggs nominated Brenda Coons Houser for her exceptional leadership and her commitment to caring for veterans and her community. He noted she has dedicated more than 25 years to serving veterans and shown supreme dedication to the VFW and VFW Auxiliary values and children’s programs. Brenda serves in a number of VFW Auxiliary leadership roles, including the Department of Idaho VFW Auxiliary Guard. Brenda’s volunteer activities include actively coordinating volunteers, assisting with community fundraisers and evaluating scholarship applications. She also enjoys baking and crafting handmade items to donate for fundraising efforts. Brenda serves in a number of other community efforts that include serving on a dedicated team to host the annual Homedale Lions Club Demolition Derby. She started driving derby cars at age 18, returned to it after taking a break to raise her children and eventually transitioned into serving as a board member for the club. She has also been a volunteer with USA Wrestling, helping run local, regional and national tournaments.

Thomas (Tom) Morrical, Meridian: The Idaho Veterans Assistance League nominated Thomas Morrical, who is a regular volunteer at the Idaho State Veterans Home-Boise. He helps mostly in the canteen, but also with bingo, outings and taking pictures at some of the home’s signature events. The nominators shared, “His enthusiasm and servant-hearted attitude have made an extraordinary difference, and we are truly grateful for all he has contributed.” Tom is considered indispensable at the home, where his reliability and consistency quickly earned trust, and he took on the role of trainer. He has since provided thoughtful and effective training for individual volunteers and small groups. Tom shared, “My father was a vet and has since passed. The VA hospital was wonderful to him in his last 2 years, and I want to help veterans.” He also wrote about how the interaction with the veterans and veterans’ families are what he enjoys most about volunteering: “Each person has a life story and commitment to this country that is exceptional.”

Gregory (Greg) D. Munden, Post Falls: Newby-ginnings of North Idaho, Inc. nominated Gregory Munden for his commitment to honoring the lives of our nation’s heroes. Greg dedicated more than 20 years to military service that included service in the U.S. Navy, U.S. Naval Reserve, Idaho National Guard and Washington Air National Guard. His service included two tours in Vietnam, and he earned many medals and commendations. When nominating Greg, Theresa Hart wrote, “For the past 12 years, he has been an invaluable part of Newby-ginnings of North Idaho, serving as a volunteer, Board Member, and Board President. His dedication extends to the American Legion and VFW Honor Guards, where he ensures that fellow Veterans are honored with dignity and respect. Greg leads by example, with humility, integrity, compassion, and an unwavering commitment to making a difference.” Greg also devoted 33 years to the Idaho Transportation Department, retiring in 2010. Greg and his wife, Kay, have been married for 54 years and are proud parents of two daughters and grandparents to five grandchildren. Their family’s proud tradition of military service continues through one of their grandsons, who currently serves in the U.S. Army.

Barbara J. Ronzzo, Athol: The Idaho Veterans Assistance League (IVAL) nominated Barbara Ronzzo for her volunteer efforts that have spanned 41 years. Barbara has been an active volunteer at the Idaho State Veterans Home-Post Falls, where she assists staff in planning and executing outings, events and celebrations. She also volunteers in the home’s Bistro. When nominating Barbara, Leonard A. Crosby III wrote about Barbara having a true heart for veterans as the spouse of an Air Force veteran and daughter of a World War II veteran. He noted her wonderful interactions with the veteran residents at the home, and that she “goes out of her way to brighten their day, engage them in conversation and make them laugh. Her close relationship with her father, who taught her the importance of service and patriotism, and her respect for those who have served in our country’s armed forces have and continue to inspire her to continue her volunteer efforts.”

London Talbot, Meridian: The Idaho State Veterans Home-Boise nominated London Talbot. He joined the home’s volunteer team a year ago and has generously shared his talents in many ways, often behind the scenes. London, whose grandfather’s service as a U.S. Army medevac pilot during the Vietnam War inspired London to serve veterans, has assisted with updating the home’s volunteer handbook, created unique and engaging invitations to the home’s volunteer events and has served as a photographer for many of the home’s major events. When nominating London, Jo Ann Daron wrote, “His photographs have helped preserve and showcase the experiences of our volunteers and residents alike.” Jo Ann also wrote about how London used a local community network to fill the need for volunteers at the home’s canteen. Jo Ann wrote, “Thanks to this remarkable show of community support, every volunteer shift is now filled, ensuring the canteen remains open seven days a week and continues its important mission of serving the veterans in our home. We are truly grateful for London’s willingness to contribute his time and creativity.”

Debb Yandle, Boise: VFW Post 4000 of Meridian nominated Debb Yandle for her exceptional commitment to veterans, their families and others in need. Debb volunteers with VFW Meridian Post 4000 and Help Us Help Vets. Her service includes distributing Buddy Poppies, assisting at homeless encampments, placing veterans’ wreaths at the Idaho State Veterans Cemetery, wrapping Christmas gifts for veterans’ families and cooking meals four times a week for two veteran widows in the neighborhood. When nominating Debb, Tammy Clement wrote, “Inspired by her genuine desire to help others, she brings kindness, happiness, and meaningful support to her community. Her consistent, compassionate service reflects the award’s true spirit.” Tammy also noted that Debb enjoys the friendships formed through volunteering and the happiness she brings to others: “Making people smile is important to her, and she values every opportunity to help.”

title: Sen. Cruz Introduces Legislation to Honor Medal of Honor Recipient Master Sgt. Benavidez
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) introduced legislation to designate the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) clinic in Victoria, Texas, as the Master Sergeant Roy P. Benavidez Department of Veterans Affairs Clinic. The legislation honors Master Sergeant Roy Perez Benavidez, a South Texas native and Medal of Honor recipient who served in the U.S. Army Special Forces during the Vietnam War.

Sen. Cruz said, “Naming the Victoria VA clinic after Master Sergeant Roy Perez Benavidez honors one of our nation’s most decorated soldiers. Born in Cuero, Texas, he earned the Medal of Honor for his extraordinary heroism during the Vietnam War. His courage, patriotism, and sacrifice exemplify the highest traditions of American military service. Master Sergeant Benavidez’s extraordinary service continues to inspire generations of Texans.”

U.S. Rep. Michael Cloud (R-Texas-27) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

Rep. Cloud said, “Master Sergeant Roy Benavidez embodied the courage and selflessness that define our nation’s heroes. Naming this clinic in his honor will be a fitting tribute to his legacy of service as well as that of the veterans who pass through its doors every day.”

Read the bill text here.

BACKGROUND:

Master Sergeant Roy Perez Benavidez was born in Cuero, Texas. He enlisted in the Texas Army National Guard in 1952 and entered active duty in the United States Army in 1955. He volunteered for the Army Special Forces after completing airborne training, and served with the 5th Special Forces Group (Airborne) during the Vietnam War.

On May 2, 1968, Benavidez volunteered to rescue a 12-man reconnaissance team surrounded by a much larger North Vietnamese force. Armed only with a medical bag and a knife, he spent nearly six hours under intense enemy fire rescuing wounded personnel, organizing the defense, directing air support, recovering classified documents, and evacuating surviving team members. Despite sustaining dozens of gunshot, shrapnel, and bayonet wounds, he refused evacuation until the mission was complete. President Ronald Reagan awarded him the Medal of Honor on February 24, 1981 for his extraordinary heroism during the battle.

After retiring from the Army in 1976, Master Sergeant Benavidez advocated for veterans, mentored young Americans, and traveled throughout the country speaking about military service, patriotism, leadership, and sacrifice.

title: Sens. Cruz, Cantwell, Colleagues Applaud Unanimous Senate Passage of Bipartisan, Bicameral Comprehensive Weather Forecasting Bill
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas), Chairman of the Senate Commerce Committee, Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), Ranking Member of the Senate Commerce Committee, U.S. Rep. Brian Babin (R-Texas-36), Chairman of the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee, and Rep. Zoe Lofgren (D-Calif.-18), Ranking Member of the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee, applauded the Senate's unanimous passage of the bipartisan Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Reauthorization Act of 2026 (Weather Act).

Senate passage reflects a bicameral agreement on this legislation reauthorizing many weather forecasting and hazard communication programs at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). In light of this agreement, it is anticipated that the House of Representatives will take up and send the Weather Act to the President’s desk before the end of the 119th Congress.

Sen. Cruz said, “The Senate took a pivotal step toward ensuring Americans are prepared for severe weather. Texans know all too well the devastation storms can bring. The lives lost in the July 4, 2025, Texas floods are a heartbreaking reminder of what is at stake. The Weather Act brings together over a dozen bipartisan bills to modernize radar systems, deliver more accurate and timely forecasts, and improve warnings so families and first responders have more time to act, no matter where they are and no matter the time of day. These improvements will help protect property and, more importantly, save lives in Texas and across the country.”

Sen. Cantwell said, “Americans are facing increasingly dangerous and costly weather disasters, and better forecasts give communities more time to prepare and get out of harm’s way. The Weather Act will advance next-generation weather radar, modernize lifesaving warning systems, and improve forecasts for atmospheric rivers and wildfires, like the devastating fires that forced thousands to evacuate in Spokane last month. Today’s Senate passage brings us one step closer to giving forecasters, emergency managers, and communities the tools they need to save lives and protect property.”

House Science, Space, and Technology Committee Chairman Brian Babin (R-Texas-36) said, “Reliable weather forecasts and timely warnings are essential to protecting American lives and property. Last year’s devastating floods in Texas served as a tragic reminder of the need to better predict severe weather and communicate critical information to communities in harm’s way. The Weather Act Reauthorization represents an opportunity to modernize our nation’s forecasting capabilities and strengthen emergency preparedness. Building on the legislation the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee advanced last September, the Senate-passed bill reflects a bipartisan, bicameral compromise and a shared commitment to protecting American communities. I thank Chairman Cruz, Ranking Member Lofgren, Rep. Lucas, and our colleagues in both chambers for their hard work in reaching this agreement. I look forward to continuing our efforts to get this legislation across the finish line.

House Science, Space, and Technology Committee Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren (D-Calif.-18) said, “This is a long time coming. The Weather Act Reauthorization will give NOAA the support it needs to carry out its critical mission. I want to thank Chairman Babin, my former Committee partner, Mr. Lucas, and the dedicated staff on both sides of the aisle for getting this to the finish line. The World Meteorological Organization just released its State of the Climate update emphasizing that the supersized El Niño we are experiencing is expected to bring record heat, flooding, and drought conditions for the next year. Now more than ever, more observations and data are needed to bolster our nations forecasting capabilities to protect lives, property, the economy, and national security. We have to ensure that NOAA has the tools, staffing, and infrastructure to help support communities prepare for and respond to disasters. This bill will help us do that.”

In addition to Chairman Cruz and Ranking Member Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), Senate cosponsors include Sens. Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), Jerry Moran (R-Kan.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), Tim Sheehy (R-Mont.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), Ted Budd (R-N.C.), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), John Curtis (R-Utah), and John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.).

Read the bill text here.

BACKGROUND:

More than a dozen bipartisan bills are in the Weather Act, including Chairman Cruz’s NOAA Weather Radio Modernization Act. The Radio Modernization Act upgrades weather radio equipment to make broadcasts of emergency notices during severe weather more reliable and accessible nationwide. This bill, along with numerous other underlying measures in the Weather Act, came about as a response to gaps identified after the deadly July 2025 floods in Texas’ Hill Country.

The legislation would:

Reauthorize multiple weather forecasting programs while advancing next-generation forecasting technologies and improving research-to-operations transition efforts.

Improve forecasting for flooding, hurricanes, tornadoes, droughts, landslides, wildfires, and atmospheric rivers.

Enhance public communication of weather risks — including through NOAA weather radio —to ensure warnings are clear, timely, and actionable.

Modernize NOAA’s aging radar network through planning and deployment of next-generation weather radar and targeted efforts to close radar coverage gaps, including gaps in flash-flood prone and under-observed regions such as the Texas Hill Country.

Improve coastal marine fog forecasting where dense fog can disrupt shipping and maritime commerce.

Advance long-range weather forecasting to support farmers, ranchers, and water managers by improving weather outlooks weeks to months in advance.

title: Duckworth, Bennet, Sanders, Van Hollen Release Joint Statement Opposing Spending Package that Funds Trump’s War on Iran
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Bernie Sanders (I-VT) and Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) today released a joint statement underscoring their opposition to a government funding deal that does not restrict President Trump’s ability to continue his war with Iran:

“The American people have been clear: We must end President Trump’s illegal and disastrous war with Iran. This conflict has driven up the cost of gas, groceries and fertilizer. More than 20 American servicemembers have been killed and hundreds more wounded, while achieving none of President Trump’s stated goals and harming civilians across the region. As we approach the December 11 funding deadline, we should not accept a short-term spending deal that continues to provide billions of additional dollars for President Trump’s war of choice. Any short-term package must include language that restricts the Trump Administration from using appropriated funds to continue his war against Iran.

“We know from Vietnam, Afghanistan and Iraq that these wars can take decades to end—hurting our economy, draining our military resources and making Americans less safe. Meanwhile, Americans all across the country will continue bearing the cost, with higher grocery bills, higher gas prices and a higher toll on our troops. The American people do not want more war in the Middle East—but that is what President Trump has given them. Congress cannot allow Trump to continue his conflict—we must force him to end it. Not doing so will only prolong the American people’s pain and opens the door to further escalation as he has threatened.

“When we vote on appropriations, we intend to fund the government and stop funds for this war. It is what the American people demand, and what they deserve.”

Duckworth has been an outspoken critic of Trump’s illegal, needless war in Iran since it began. She is one of the Senate Six—the original group of Senators who have been forcing votes on War Powers Resolutions that would cease hostilities in Iran, which Republicans have shamefully blocked fourteen times. Duckworth continues to lead her fellow Senate Democrats in calling for public hearings to investigate how this Administration’s failure to end Trump’s war has taken a widespread physical, emotional and mental toll on troops deployed to the region. She has also committed to voting against the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (NDAA) unless her amendment to end President Donald Trump’s illegal war against Iran is included.

title: Duckworth on Her Alive Day: “Not One More Cent Toward Trump’s Illegal War”
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] — Today on her “Alive Day,” the day she almost died in a shootdown that took both of her legs and partial use of her right arm, U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) issued the following statement announcing her opposition to a funding deal that would allow Trump to continue waging his disastrous, illegal and unjustified war in Iran:

“22 years ago today, my life was forever changed when the helicopter I was co-piloting was hit by an RPG. I wouldn’t have lasted the hour if it weren’t for my buddies who thought I was dead but refused to leave my body behind. Waking up in Walter Reed 11 days later, I vowed to find a way to repay them, as well as all those who sacrifice so much for our nation.

“Reflecting on that day now, it sickens me to my core how much this Administration exploits today’s heroes. Our brave troops will always answer the call to serve. Our nation’s leaders owe it to them to ensure the missions we ask them to carry out are justified. The President has still failed to tell our servicemembers why his illegal war is worth their sacrifices, how long they’ll be asked to remain overseas and what his plan is to bring them home safely.

“Enough is enough. As Congress negotiates the next funding package, I refuse to accept a deal that continues to hand Donald Trump billions toward waging his disastrous, illegal and out-of-control war. Congress wields the power of the purse, and we cannot allow one more cent to go toward a war the American people have made clear they do not want and that their elected representatives never voted for.”
