title: Gallego, Kelly Press US Foods Over Alleged Anti-Union Activity in Arizona
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Senators Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) and Mark Kelly (D-AZ) sent a letter to US Foods, Inc. CEO David Flitman and Area President Michelle King raising concerns over allegations of anti-union activity, employee intimidation, and retaliation against Arizona based US Foods workers who are attempting to organize with Teamsters Local Union 104. In the letter, the senators called on US Foods to address the allegations and cooperate with any investigation.

“Many hardworking drivers, warehouse workers, and meat preparation workers are attempting to organize a union to secure higher wages and better working conditions. However, serious allegations have been brought to our attention regarding US Foods’ conduct during this union campaign,” the senators wrote.“ These allegations include management intimidation of workers, anti-union messaging, interference with organizing efforts, and retaliation against employees seeking to join Teamsters Local Union 104.”

“These allegations warrant immediate attention and an appropriate investigation, and they raise significant questions regarding US Foods’ commitment to respecting the federally protected rights of its employees to organize, engage in collective bargaining, and make decisions regarding union representation without coercion, intimidation, or retaliation,” the senators continued.

The senators added that employees have the right to organize, support a labor union, engage in protected concerted activities, and seek collective representation under Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA). Section 8(a)(3) of the law prohibits discrimination regarding employment to encourage or discourage union membership.

title: Gillibrand, Colleagues Introduce Bill To Lower Age Of Medicare Eligibility To 50, Bring Down Healthcare Costs
text:
Medicare At 50 Act Would Give More Than 58 Million Americans Ages 50 To 64 Another Option For Affordable Healthcare

Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) joined nine of her Senate colleagues to introduce the Medicare at 50 Act, legislation to lower the Medicare eligibility age to 50 and allow Americans ages 50 to 64 to buy into Medicare. As Americans list the cost of healthcare as a top concern, the bill would expand access to affordable healthcare and give more than 58 million Americans more coverage options.

“Under President Trump, Americans nearing retirement are being forced to choose between paying for lifesaving care and simply being able to afford a life,” said Senator Gillibrand. “The Medicare at 50 Act would provide the security and support of Medicare years earlier to millions of aging Americans, lowering their healthcare costs and helping them save for retirement. As the top Democrat on the Senate Aging Committee, I am proud to support this important legislation, and I will continue fighting to expand access to quality and affordable care for older Americans.”

More than 60 million Americans are between the ages of 50 and 64, a population that faces significant challenges accessing affordable, comprehensive health insurance. While the Affordable Care Act (ACA) expanded access to coverage, millions of older Americans continue to face high premiums, out-of-pocket costs, and limited coverage options. Today, 11.5% of Americans between the ages of 55 and 64 remain uninsured.

President Trump and Republicans have made matters worse with sweeping healthcare cuts in their Big Ugly Bill and their refusal to extend the ACA’s enhanced premium tax credits, driving up costs for older Americans who purchase insurance through the ACA Marketplace.

The Medicare at 50 Act would help close this gap and give Americans between the ages of 50 and 64 the option to buy into Medicare before reaching the traditional eligibility age of 65. Individuals who choose to enroll would receive the same benefits and protections available under Medicare Parts A, B, and D, including the option to enroll in a Medicare Advantage plan. The legislation would also allow eligible individuals to receive the same premium tax credits and cost-sharing subsidies they would qualify for through the ACA Marketplace, helping make coverage more affordable.

Senator Gillibrand has long fought to lower healthcare costs for older Americans and to protect Medicare access. This year, she introduced the Medicare Cost Cap Act to cap out-of-pocket costs for seniors with Medicare, and she demanded an end to the Trump administration’s WISeR program that allows for AI-driven Medicare denials. Last year, she pressed Republicans to extend the enhanced ACA premium tax credits that helped millions of Americans afford coverage.

In addition to Senator Gillibrand, the bill is co-sponsored by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Jack Reed (D-RI), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Ed Markey (D-MA) and Tammy Baldwin (D-WI).

Full text of the bill is availablehere.

title: ICYMI: City & State Highlights Senator Gillibrand’s Leadership During Historic Midterm Cycle For Democrats
text:
*** Read City & State’s Full Article Here***

In case you missed it, City & State published an article highlighting U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand’s leadership of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee during the 2026 cycle, in which Democrats flipped at least eight seats in last week’s midterms and cemented a Democratic Senate majority.

In the story, Senator Gillibrand credited Democrats’ laser focus on lowering costs for American families as a key to the sweeping Election Day victory, and she said that the new Democratic Congress must continue to focus on affordability and expanding healthcare access if the party is to build on its success in 2028.

Read the full City & State story here or below:

Kirsten Gillibrand’s leadership lessons

After flipping at least seven Senate seats, the DSCC chair wants to stay in Democratic leadership.

John Celock | November 10, 2026

While remaining coy on her exact long term plans, U.S. Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand wants to remain as part of the Democratic leadership team in the Senate, after last week’s “blue tsunami.”

Gillibrand hopes to stay on as the chair of the Democratic Senate Campaign Committee for a second term following an Election Day that exceeded even the Democrats’ most optimistic assumptions. The party picked up at least seven seats in the upper chamber, with two more outstanding but leaning Democratic. It recalls 2006, when U.S. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer led Senate Democrats to a majority, helmed the DSCC for a second term and later became the party’s Senate leader.

“I do. I definitely want to be part of our leadership going forward,” Gillibrand told City & State when asked if she wanted to run for the leadership in the future. “I want to be a voice to get commonsense things done that help the American people. And so I hope that I can keep building my capabilities and building my ability to help people by doing politics well. And hopefully, I can continue to lead through that process.”

Asked specifically about the possibility of following Schumer’s path to the top Democratic job in the Senate, Gillibrand was more coy. “I will look at all opportunities for sure,” she said.

Of course, that would mean holding her seat, when she’s up for reelection in 2030 – far from a sure thing in New York, where an emboldened progressive movement is itching to take her out.

The DSCC chair is appointed by the Democratic leader, not elected by the full Democratic caucus – which means the only one she needs to convince is Schumer (assuming he’s reelected as leader). Gillibrand said one reason she wants to stay on at the DSCC is because the job gives her a seat at the Democratic leadership table, enabling her to help set the party’s agenda and message as they retake the majority for the second half of the current Trump presidency.

Under Gillibrand’s leadership, the DSCC raised $200 million and opened up new Senate opportunities that had not been anticipated – from Kansas to Mississippi.

Gillibrand sees a lot of similarities between the current midterms cycle and the one Schumer led two decades ago. It was then, amid a similar climate of economic distress and overseas wars (then, in Iraq; now, in Iran) that Gillibrand first made it to Congress, flipping a Republican-leaning congressional seat in 2006 before being reelected in2008 and then appointed to the U.S. Senate in 2009.

“I think I’m uniquely positioned to understand what it takes to win red and purple places because of my own experience,” she said. “So I want to continue to do this work. I want to do it for the caucus. I want to do it for the country, and I want to help people.”

Colm O’Comartun, a national political strategist who runs 50 State, described roles like the DSCC chair as high-risk and high-reward for an ambitious politician like Gillibrand – who launched, and soon dropped, a presidential campaign ahead of 2020. She can bask in the glory of a wave election like this year, but will also take the blame if the party does not do as well going forward.

“I think it’s a great sign that she’s somebody who’s really interested in helping her caucus and and helping build a team and a bench and in some ways thankless job, and hopefully she’ll be able to get something miraculous, which is two of these difficult years in a row (because) these these maps aren’t easy for Democrats,” he said.

O’Comartum, a former executive director of the Democratic Governors Association, said two terms at the DSCC could position Gillibrand well for a future leadership bid. He said the 59-year-old Gillibrand could take advantage of the call for generational change in the Democratic ranks and easily build relationships with the younger Senate generation in the party by campaigning with them and positioning them to get to Washington.

“There’s every reason to believe that she’s just at the right age to assume leadership, and will have a better relationship through her campaigning with these new members than maybe some others,” he said.

Last September, Gillibrand predicted to City & State that Mississippi would be a 2026 U.S. Senate battleground – an idea that at the time seemed borderline-delusional. But Gillibrand would prove eerily accurate; in Mississippi, Democratic challenger Scott Colom now narrowly leads Republican U.S. Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in a race that still hasn’t been called.

Gillibrand said that she became intrigued by Colom’s candidacy after meeting him and hearing about how Hyde-Smith blocked his bid to become a federal judge. She said data from previous elections suggested a Black Democrat had the potential to do well in the state. Recalling how Georgia Democrats had flipped two Senate seats in a fellow southern state in 2020 and thinking back to her own 2006 congressional run in a ruby-red district, she could see a pathway in a state that Democrats traditionally wrote off.

“I wasn’t daunted that it was R+23 because, again, my district hadn’t been Democrat since Nixon, and so I thought, this is just like my election, just on a Senate-wide basis in a red state that needs to be organized just like Georgia. And if we start putting the time and effort in (and) have the best kind of candidate possible, everything is in play, and it was,” she said.

Looking ahead to 2028, Gillibrand sees opportunities for Democrats in some of the same states that helped to fuel this year’s blue wave, including North Carolina, South Carolina, Kansas and Iowa (all of which just flipped U.S. Senate seats to the Democrats), along with Wisconsin (where Democrats swept statewide offices and picked up congressional seats), and Alaska (where Democrats lead in still-uncalled Senate and gubernatorial races). She indicated that North Carolina and Wisconsin will be top targets given the Democratic registration numbers.

Gillibrand said the key will be for the new Democratic Congress to focus on the issues that fueled this year’s victories like affordability and healthcare, particularly Medicare. She added that new members in Republican-leaning and swing districts need to better communicate Democratic accomplishments over the next two years. By New York standards,Gillibrand is ideologically a moderate, and although she does not believe Republicans will be able to weaponize the new crop of democratic socialist electeds against the Democratic Party, she does want to caution the party against tacking too far to the left, which she blames for its 2008 losses.

She attributed the victories of leftist leaders Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Michigan U.S. Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed to their focus on affordability over unrealistic and alienating progressive policies. “They ran on costs. They made costs a cool message. They brought in new voters. Young people were excited about their youth, and that’s exciting.” she said. “They were on message. Do not get that confused. They were on message on the economic priorities and concerns of everyday voters across the country.”

title: Grassley Details Legislative Priorities for the Remainder of the 119th Congress
text:
Floor Remarks by Senator Chuck Grassley of Iowa

Senate President Pro Tempore

“119th Congress End-of-Year Priorities”

Thursday, November 12, 2026

VIDEO

With the 2026 midterm elections behind us, Congress must finish its work for this Congress.

On my agenda for Iowans in the coming weeks: first of all, confirming President Trump's remaining judicial nominees to lifetime appointments on the federal branch, and that's a responsibility that falls on my shoulders as chairman of the Judiciary Committee.

And then, obviously, we know it costs money to shut the government down. It costs taxpayer money to open the government up. So, keeping the government open beyond the short-term funding bill that expires on December 11th ought to be high on the agenda.

And then, passing the National Defense Authorization Act, which we have done for 65 years in a row. And that legislation includes stuff out of my Judiciary Committee that protects kids who are in danger of the things that are online.

And then enacting a Farm Bill that contains year-round nationwide E15 ethanol and addresses high input costs that farmers face.

And then passing common sense permitting reform to unlock the American infrastructure and reduce government red tape. And that permitting bill is the subject of debate right now on the floor of the United States Senate.

And then, lastly, something that I've been involved in for decades to emphasize the responsibilities that we have to maintain rural healthcare.

That would include reauthorizing the Medicare-dependent and low-volume hospital programs, the Rural Community Hospital Demonstration program and a Medicare payment floor for rural state doctors and clinics.

As we look to the 120th Congress, I've personally congratulated the new members of the Iowa federal delegation on their elections. I look forward to working with all of those new members on behalf of the people of Iowa.

The next Congress has a lot to accomplish, and I'm ready to work with these new members and the members of both parties to get things done.

Affordability was front and center in this election and must be the bipartisan focus next year. Any serious affordability agenda will need to focus on fiscal sanity and reduce waste, fraud and abuse in federal programs.

Our national debt now stands at levels we've not seen since the end of World War II, while Social Security is projected to become insolvent in just six years, and Medicare shortly thereafter. We must find a bipartisan solution to a very real fiscal crisis that has been staring Congress in the face for too long of a time.

title: Grassley-Durbin Bankruptcy Legislation Becomes Law, Benefiting American Small Businesses and Families
text:
WASHINGTON – Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and Ranking Member Dick Durbin’s (D-Ill.) Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act has become law. The bipartisan legislation supports American small businesses and families by reinstating modern debt limits for Subchapter V and Chapter 13 bankruptcy, restoring access to critical reorganization tools.

“The Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act is now the law of the land, ensuring our nation’s bankruptcy code works for Americans, not against them,” Grassley said. “By restoring modern debt limits and eliminating barriers to reorganization, this bipartisan bill provides American small businesses and families the tools they need to regain their financial footing. I thank Senator Durbin for his partnership in getting our bill across the finish line, as well as my colleagues in the Senate and House of Representatives for their support.”

“Bankruptcy is often a painful last resort for small business owners. This bill restores a quicker and cheaper pathway for entrepreneurs to settle debts, keep the lights on, and keep serving their neighbors. It also expands eligibility for Chapter 13 bankruptcy to help more families manage rising costs, stay in their homes, and get back on their feet. Following unanimous passage in the Senate and House, I’m thrilled the President signed our bipartisan bill into law,” Durbin said.

The bipartisan legislation is cosponsored by Sens. John Cornyn (R-Texas), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.) and Chris Coons (D-Del.).

Bill text can be found HERE.

Background:

The Grassley-Whitehouse Small Business Reorganization Act, signed into law in 2019, established Subchapter V within Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code. The bipartisan legislation streamlined the bankruptcy process, reduced procedural burdens on small business owners and lowered filing costs. Legislation signed into law in 2020 allowed more small businesses to qualify for these procedures by increasing the upper debt limit for Subchapter V to $7.5 million.

In 2022, the Grassley-Whitehouse Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment and Technical Corrections Act was signed into law, extending the $7.5 million debt limit for small businesses filing under Subchapter V and establishing a new debt limit of $2.75 million for individuals and families filing under Chapter 13. However, when the Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment and Technical Corrections Act expired in 2024, the debt thresholds for both programs reverted to lower levels.

The Grassley-Durbin Bankruptcy Threshold Adjustment Act permanently restores the Subchapter V debt limit to $7.5 million and the Chapter 13 debt limit to $2.75 million.

title: Grassley, Johnson Seek Declassification of All Crossfire Hurricane Records to Secure Lasting Transparency
text:
WASHINGTON – Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations Chairman Ron Johnson (R-Wis.) are urging President Donald Trump to declassify all government records related to the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s (FBI) weaponized Crossfire Hurricane investigation.

Trump signed an Executive Order in March 2025 approving the declassification of Crossfire Hurricane materials. Yet, key governments emails, hundreds of transcripts from Department of Justice (DOJ) Office of Inspector General interviews and a 400-page DOJ Inspection Division investigation report remain classified.

“We appreciate your strong efforts to bring transparency and accountability to Crossfire Hurricane and its related investigations. For approximately a decade, we’ve investigated Crossfire Hurricane and have sought possession of a wide array of government records to expose the facts and evidence once hidden from the American public. The more we’ve investigated the matter, the more information has come to light exposing the political rot that infected that operation from the get-go,” the senators wrote.

“Your administration possesses a treasure trove of records that prove out weaponization against Republicans, including you and your family, which we’ve investigated for many years. These records need to see the light of day, consistent with your declassification Executive Order and the overriding public interest,” the senators concluded.

Read the full letter HERE and below.

November 10, 2026

VIA ELECTRONIC TRANSMISSION

The Honorable Donald J. Trump

President of the United States

The White House

Dear President Trump:

We appreciate your strong efforts to bring transparency and accountability to Crossfire Hurricane and its related investigations. For approximately a decade, we’ve investigated Crossfire Hurricane and have sought possession of a wide array of government records to expose the facts and evidence once hidden from the American public. The more we’ve investigated the matter, the more information has come to light exposing the political rot that infected that operation from the get-go. We write today about records that have yet to be declassified that should be based upon your declassification Executive Order and for public transparency.

First, on August 17, 2026, we wrote to the DOJ, FBI, and ODNI concerning a December 2019 email from Tony Riedlinger, then an FBI Section Chief, to FBI Supervisory Special Agent Joe Pientka that contained a description as well as an attached document. The email and attachment, when read together, appear to corroborate existing public evidence that you were the target of a political hit and the basis of evidence that would lead a person to reasonably make that conclusion appears to have been known to the DOJ and FBI for some time. Yet, those agencies proceeded with weaponized investigations again you.

We’ve requested that the DOJ, FBI, and ODNI declassify the email and attachment to the fullest extent possible under the law, but that has yet to be done.

Second, the DOJ has produced an approximately 400-page DOJ Inspection Division investigation report related to Crossfire Hurricane but it too is classified. This report provides additional context separate from the Justice Department’s Inspector General report on Crossfire Hurricane, including additional interviews with personnel involved in Crossfire Hurricane. The report also provides additional context about the questionable beginnings of Crossfire Hurricane that ought to be made known to the American people. Even though the approximately 400-page report was produced to our SCIF in classified form, it still contains redactions. After all these years of weaponization in Crossfire Hurricane, that document should be declassified for the public.

Finally, since 2023, we’ve requested from the Justice Department Inspector General the full set of the transcripts that office created as part of its investigation titled “Review of Four FISA Applications and Other Aspects of the FBI’s Crossfire Hurricane Investigation.” The Inspector General at that time failed to produce those records. On March 17, 2025, we wrote to DOJ and FBI requesting that they work with the DOJ Office of the Inspector General to produce unredacted transcripts of interviews connected to that report. It is our understanding that during its review, the DOJ OIG interviewed more than 170 individuals and of those, 165 interviews were transcribed. To date, we have received 58 transcripts with redactions, two memoranda of investigation summarizing follow-up interactions after initial interviews, and one document labeled a memorandum of record also summarizing an interaction after an initial interview. The rest of the transcripts have yet to be produced with some still classified. We appreciate the new Inspector General and current DOJ and FBI leadership working to produce transcripts that previous leadership failed to produce. However, it’s been years, and these records have taken too long to reach Congress and the public. We urge your administration to produce the rest in short order and without unnecessary redactions.

Your administration possesses a treasure trove of records that prove out weaponization against Republicans, including you and your family, which we’ve investigated for many years. These records need to see the light of day consistent with your declassification Executive Order and the overriding public interest.

Thank you for your attention to this important matter.

title: Grassley Questions Ag, Treasury and Commerce Nominees on Trade Policy, Whistleblowers, National Debt and More
text:
WASHINGTON – Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) submitted questions for the record to President Donald Trump’s nominees who appeared before the Senate Finance and Agriculture Committees this week. Grassley's questions focused on protecting Iowa pork producers amid U.S.-Mexico trade negotiations, expanding opportunities for small and beginning farmers, strengthening the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Whistleblower Program and addressing the nation's rising debt.

Nominees who testified before the Finance Committee on Tuesday were Francis Browne to be an Under Secretary of the Treasury, Christopher Abbott to be an Assistant Secretary of Commerce and Robert Stebbins to be General Counsel for the Department of the Treasury. Nominees who testified before the Agriculture Committee were Gregory Ibach to be Under Secretary of Agriculture for Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs and Carl Bednarski, John Grunewald II and James Russell Middleton to be members of the Farm Credit Administration Board.

In his written questions to nominees from both committees, Grassley cited his letter with the Iowa congressional delegation last month urging the administration to consider the impact of its decision to terminate a trade agreement with Mexico that has threatened Iowa’s pork industry and contributed to higher tomato prices for American consumers.

Grassley underscored to the Farm Credit Administration board nominees the need to support small and beginning farmers.

Finally, in questions to the Finance Committee nominees for the Treasury and Commerce Departments, Grassley stressed the need to address longstanding delays in the IRS Whistleblower Program’s payment process. Grassley authored the 2006 legislation to create the IRS Whistleblower Program, which has brought in over $8 billion to the Treasury. Grassley also questioned the nominees on America’s dire fiscal state and asked what types of policies they would advise the administration to pursue to put budget deficits and the national debt on a sustainable fiscal path.

Senators submit Questions For the Record (QFRs) to hearing witnesses to receive detailed, written responses from witnesses. Grassley expects timely answers from the nominees.

title: Hagerty Introduces President Trump’s Nominee for District Judge for the Eastern District of Tennessee
text:
WASHINGTON—Today, United States Senator Bill Hagerty (R-TN), a member of the Senate Appropriations, Banking, Rules, and Foreign Relations Committees and former U.S. Ambassador to Japan, introduced President Trump’s nominee to serve as District Judge for the Eastern District of Tennessee, Samuel Adkisson, before the Senate Judiciary Committee.

*Click the photo above or click here to watch*

Remarks as prepared for delivery:

“It is my privilege to introduce Samuel Adkisson—President Trump’s nominee to be District Judge for the Eastern District of Tennessee. Hailing from the mountains near Chattanooga, he brings exceptional intellect, broad litigation experience, and the character we expect from our federal judiciary.

Sam is a distinguished graduate of my alma mater, Vanderbilt University. He was an All-American on the mock trial team, graduating summa cum laude. He then attended Yale Law School, where he served on two law journals and received the top prize for excellence in trial presentation. Although Yale doesn’t utilize a standard grading system, ‘Honors’ marks in 21 out of 22 graded courses speaks volumes.

As an advocate, Sam has practiced law at elite firms. He’s played key roles in high-stakes litigation, including billion-dollar bankruptcies and civil liberties cases. Importantly, in his current role as Special Assistant and Associate Counsel to the President, Sam has played a key role supervising the mountain of litigation involving the federal government the last two years.

Sam’s experience isn’t limited to above-the-fold cases. Consider his law review article, titled, ‘System-Level Standards: Driverless Cars and the Future of Regulatory Design.’ We need judges who, like Sam, can adeptly apply our law not only to yesterday’s problems, but also to the problems of tomorrow.

Sam is bright, consistent, and demonstrates a steady hand. His impressive resume shows he’s ready to be a district judge.

But let me put this in a more personal context. You’re about to meet a Vanderbilt and Yale graduate who clerked for the Chief Justice and two outstanding circuit judges, and now is counsel to the President. You’re expecting to meet someone who’s learned, hard-working, and brilliant. Yes, Sam is all of those things—but much more besides. He is honest, quick to laugh, humble, and devout. He is devoted to his wife and their three children.

Public service has placed high demands on their family, and Sam’s gratitude for their unwavering support is apparent. His pastor back home in Tennessee said that ‘Sam is the epitome of a servant-hearted man.’

Sam understands the proper role of a judge: that the Constitution’s original meaning is binding, and that the law must be applied as it is, not how he or anyone else would like it to be. I urge you to quickly advance his nomination. Thank you.”

title: Senator Hassan Honors Veterans Day at Events Across New Hampshire
text:
NEW HAMPSHIRE – U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan, a member of the Senate Veterans Affairs Committee, joined New Hampshire veterans, service members, and their families at the Manchester Veterans Day Parade and at a wreath laying ceremony in Veteran’s Memorial Park yesterday, where she spoke about the importance of honoring veterans’ service.

“Veterans Day is a chance to honor those who served and to recommit ourselves to ensuring that veterans receive the care, benefits, and support that they have earned. The heroes who fought for our freedom abroad should not be left to struggle for their health care or left to sleep on the streets,” said Senator Hassan. “Our veterans put their lives on the line for us, and now it’s our turn to fulfill our promise to them.”

Senator Hassan joins the Manchester Veterans Day Parade

Last week, Senator Hassan visited the New Hampshire State Veterans Cemetery in Boscawen, where she joined other Granite Staters in placing American flags at the gravesites of veterans in honor of their service and sacrifice. Senator Hassan also spoke at the Woodbury School’s Veterans Day Program in Salem.

“Through their courage, veterans have given us the gift of safety and security for our very way of life. We enjoy peace because others are willing for our sakes to endure war; we can sleep at night because some heroes serving on the far side of the world volunteer to stand a post each day,” Senator Hassan said at the Woodbury School. “Simply to be a veteran requires a degree of selflessness that is extraordinary. Veterans understand what matters most in life, because more than anyone they know how precious life truly is. So on this Veterans Day, we should each examine our own lives and resolve to offer America’s veterans not only words of thanks, but also deeds.”

Senator Hassan has worked to support service members, veterans, and their families during her time in the Senate, including by:

Helping develop and pass into law the PACT Act, which fundamentally reforms and improves how veterans exposed to toxic substances receive health care and benefits from the VA.

Supporting provisions in the landmark 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act to help veterans buy homes.

Introducing a bipartisan bill to increase job support for gold star spouses. The bill passed the Senate earlier this year.

Introducing the Military Spouse Hiring Act to help boost hiring of military spouses.

Helping pass into law comprehensive, bipartisan retirement security legislation, including provisions to help military families save for retirement.

Introducing and passing into law the bipartisan Reserve Component Parental Leave Parity Act, which expanded parental leave eligibility for Reserve and National Guard members to cover all new parents.

Working to honor America’s POW/MIA servicemembers, including by backing the Bring Our Heroes Home Act to make it easier for families to access the records they need to help recover their missing or unaccounted for loved ones. She also led the successful bipartisan push to return the POW/MIA flag above the White House.

title: AFL-CIO and Nation’s Largest Building Trades Endorse Heinrich’s Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
text:
Broad coalition of national and local labor organizations representing hundreds of thousands of skilled workers supports legislation projected to create up to 105,600 trades and manufacturing jobs

WASHINGTON — The AFL-CIO has endorsed U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich’s (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), joining a broad coalition of national and local labor organizations representing the skilled workers who build, operate, and maintain America’s energy infrastructure.

The AFL-CIO’s endorsement adds to growing support from across organized labor, including the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers (IBEW), International Association of Iron Workers, International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail, and Transportation Workers (SMART), International Brotherhood of Boilermakers, International Brotherhood of Teamsters,International Union of Operating Engineers (IUOE), Laborers’ International Union of North America (LIUNA), North America’s Building Trades Unions (NABTU), United Association of Plumbers and Pipefitters, Pipeliners Local 798, and the New Mexico Building and Construction Trades Council. These organizations represent the electricians, ironworkers, sheet metal workers, boilermakers, Teamsters, operating engineers, laborers, plumbers, pipefitters, and other skilled tradespeople who will build the next generation of America's energy infrastructure.

The labor support comes as an independent analysis from Employ America estimates that BAAJA will create up to 105,600 trades and manufacturing jobs through 2040 by making it easier to build and maintain new energy infrastructure, including wind, solar, battery storage, and transmission projects.

BAAJA will lower energy costs for working families, provide greater certainty for energy infrastructure projects, and help ensure American workers are on the job building the infrastructure our country needs.

Independent analyses find that BAAJA will:

Create up to 105,600 trades and manufacturing jobs through 2040;

Require data centers to pay for increased grid and energy costs they create, estimated at $55 billion over the next 10 years;

Save $19 billion in residential electricity bills over the next 14 years;

Nearly double the amount of solar and wind that can connect to the grid; and

Avoid 1.5 gigatons of CO2 emissions, the equivalent of taking 39 coal plants offline for a decade.

BAAJA will lower energy costs for working families, provide greater certainty for energy infrastructure projects, and help ensure American workers are on the job building the infrastructure our country needs.

title: Hickenlooper Statement on Knowles Fire Investigation
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper released the following statement on the Department of the Interior (DOI) investigation into the Knowles Fire burnover incident that led to the deaths of four Colorado firefighters – Emily Barker, Nick Hutcherson, Sydney Watson, and Nathan Matthews – and severely injured a fifth firefighter.

“Four firefighters died in the Knowles Fire burnover, and a fifth remains severely injured. Their families have waited to learn why. Our thoughts are with them today.

“We asked one question: why were these firefighters deployed into conditions this extreme? While we appreciate DOI’s work to make these findings public, the report doesn’t give us satisfying answers.

“Faster, hotter wildfires are our new normal. We need to adequately staff our wildfire response teams and question whether DOI’s full suppression strategy is the right policy. Our team will review the report with DOI and push for the answers we need to protect Colorado’s firefighters.”

Hickenlooper led the push for a federal investigation into the Knowles Fire. In July, he took to the Senate floor to call for a comprehensive federal investigation. In August, he sent a letter to the Trump administration pushing for the investigation. In October, he joined Senators Mark Kelly, Ruben Gallego, and Gary Peters to push DOI to examine whether staffing shortages and their “full suppression” strategy put the firefighters at increased risk.

title: Kaine, Colleagues Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve Schools’ Access to Mental Health Grants
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, National School Psychology Week, U.S. Senator Tim Kaine (D-VA), a member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, joined a bipartisan group of his colleagues introducing the Creating Access and Resources in Education (CARE) for Student Mental Health Act to increase the number of school-based mental health services and providers by helping schools apply for federal grants funded in part by the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act.

“We can and must do more to support young people in our communities who are experiencing anxiety, depression, and other mental health challenges, and boosting school-based mental health services is an important way we can do that,” said Senator Kaine. “I’m proud to introduce this bipartisan legislation to help recruit, hire, and retain the professionals we need to provide these critical services.”

One in five children has a diagnosable mental or behavioral health disorder, and approximately 40 percent of students will experience symptoms of depression or anxiety by the seventh grade. Despite this growing crisis, a majority of school districts have limited or no access to school-based mental health providers such as psychologists, counselors, and social workers.

Championed by Senator Kaine, the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act was signed into law in June of 2022, making historic investments in school-based mental health and supportive services, including $1 billion for the Mental Health Service Professional Demonstration Grant Program and School-Based Mental Health Services Program to hire more school psychologists, counselors, social workers, and other mental health services providers. However, less than 3 percent of eligible entities have applied for these grants, oftentimes because they do not have the administrative bandwidth to do so or the awareness that these grants are available.

The CARE for Student Mental Health Act would help bridge the gap between schools in need and available mental health resources by:

Clarifying the distinction, purpose, and allowable activities of each grant to help eligible entities quickly determine which grant best meets their needs;

Requiring the U.S. Department of Education to improve notification and technical assistance for potential grantees to enable more school districts with limited administrative capacity to apply and compete for these federal grants;

Authorizing and streamlining the Strengthening the Pipeline of School-Based Mental Health Services Providers Program, which supports partnerships between colleges, universities, and school districts to increase the number of properly trained school-based mental health service professionals;

And authorizing the School-Based Mental Health Services Program that assists high-need school districts to recruit, hire, and retain school-based mental health personnel for students to remain healthy, engaged, and safe at school.

In addition to Kaine, the legislation was introduced by U.S. Senators John Cornyn (R-TX), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), and Thom Tillis (R-NC), and is endorsed by the National Association of School Psychologists.

title: Kelly, Gallego Press US Foods Over Allegations of Worker Intimidation and Anti-Union Activity in Arizona
text:
Today, Arizona Senators Mark Kelly and Ruben Gallego wrote to US Foods, Inc. CEO David Flitman and Area President Michelle King regarding allegations of anti-union activity, worker intimidation, and retaliation against Arizona employees seeking to organize with Teamsters Local Union 104. In the letter, the senators called on US Foods to address the allegations and cooperate with any investigation.

“Many hardworking drivers, warehouse workers, and meat preparation workers are attempting to organize a union to secure higher wages and better working conditions. However, serious allegations have been brought to our attention regarding US Foods’ conduct during this union campaign,” the senators wrote. “These allegations include management intimidation of workers, anti-union messaging, interference with organizing efforts, and retaliation against employees seeking to join Teamsters Local Union 104.”

“These allegations warrant immediate attention and an appropriate investigation, and they raise significant questions regarding US Foods’ commitment to respecting the federally protected rights of its employees to organize, engage in collective bargaining, and make decisions regarding union representation without coercion, intimidation, or retaliation,” the senators continued.

The senators added that employees have the right to organize, support a labor union, engage in protected concerted activities, and seek collective representation under Section 7 of the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA). Section 8(a)(3) of the law prohibits discrimination regarding employment to encourage or discourage union membership.

“Arizona’s working families deserve employers that respect their dignity, their contributions, and their rights under the law. Companies operating in our state must be investigated when credible allegations of unlawful labor practices arise and held accountable where appropriate,” the senators concluded.

title: Senator Kim Holds Annual Veterans Town Hall in Cape May County
text:
CAPE MAY COURT HOUSE, NJ – Yesterday, Senator Andy Kim (D-NJ) held his annual veteran’s town hall where he was joined by members of the South Jersey and veteran community. A special event that started in 2019, this town hall offers a chance to lift up voices of New Jersey veterans while highlighting the importance of service.

Senator Kim was joined by special guests Army Staff Sergeant Torie Fisher, Marine Sergeant Erin Kirk-Cuomo, Specialist Lucy Del Gaudio, and Petty Officer Jenna Leigh Carlton. Throughout the morning, each guest reflected on their time in uniform and spoke about what public service means to them. They also discussed the importance of prioritizing veteran mental health, the adjustment servicemembers face when returning to civilian life and the support needed for success, and the realities of serving as a woman in uniform.

“Veteran’s Day is a time to put politics aside and honor the sacrifices made every day by our servicemembers to keep us safe, both at-home and around the world,”said Senator Kim. “I’m grateful to the veterans who shared their stories this morning, and for everyone who came out today to participate in a reflective conversation on public service.”

“I’m really proud to be able to sit here with other women that are pushing [veteran mental health] forward, because these are the things that [veterans] don’t like to talk about …there’s a lot of veterans sitting at home, sitting in the dark struggling, and so we continue to advocate and assist veterans in any area that they need, whether it’s housing, financial, mental health – but there is so much work that needs to happen,” said SSG Torie Fisher.

As a member of the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Government Affairs (HSGAC), Senator Kim fights for our service members every day by pushing for better healthcare and access to VA benefits and efforts to make veteran transition easier into civilian life.

title: King, Colleagues Introduce Legislation Extending Toxic Exposure Benefits to Iran Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Angus King (I-ME), a member of the Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee (SVAC), is introducing new legislation to ensure Iran War Veterans who later experience illnesses due to toxic exposures are eligible for the same care and benefits under the PACT Act as servicemembers involved in other conflicts. The New PACT for Iran Veterans Act builds on the landmark protections established by the 2022 legislation, which passed with overwhelming bipartisan support, helping generations of veterans suffering from toxic exposure receive their earned healthcare and benefits.

The PACT Act of 2022, cosponsored by Senator King, empowered the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to establish a list of locations where it is legally assumed troops were exposed to toxic substances, thus expanding VA benefits eligibility to support veterans exposed to toxic hazards like burn pits and Agent Orange. The New PACT for Iran Veterans Act is seeking to extend those same commitments to veterans who served in Iran.

“Our veterans deserve access to prompt, timely healthcare – regardless of the conflict and country where they serve for our country,” said Senator King. “Just as the PACT Act represented a historical milestone for Vietnam, Iraq, and Afghanistan veterans, our New PACT for Iran Veterans Act will ensure that the VA recognizes the unique current toxic exposure risks of our service members sacrifice and guarantee they receive the support they have earned, without delay.”

Specifically, New PACT for Iran Veterans Act would:

Cut Red Tape for Iran War Veterans by statutorily presuming toxic substance exposure for Iran War Veterans, helping streamline their access to health care and benefits at VA. The bill would ensure that federal law protects all Veterans who fought in Iran, including those who operated in Iranian airspace and territorial waters.

Leave No Veteran Behind by requiring for the first time, that the VA’s Military Environmental Exposure Sub-Council (MEESC) conducts studies at least every five years to review all overseas assignments for toxic substance exposures. Additionally, when the military begins a contingency operation, the VA must commence a similar review of the locations from which servicemembers support this operation within 180 days. This would ensure the VA proactively looks into whether servicemembers are being exposed to toxic hazards, for current and future assignments.

Enhance Transparency at the VA by requiring the VA Secretary to publicly explain their justification for any denial of a country that’s recommended for presumed toxic-exposures in these reviews, or any removal of existing presumptions.

King is joined on the legislation by U.S. Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Peter Welch (D-VT), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Patty Murray (D-WA), John Fetterman (D-PA), Ron Wyden (D-OR) and Maria Cantwell (D-WA).

title: Senator Markey Applauds Senate Passage of His Forecasting and Climate-Health Provisions in Weather Act Reauthorization Package
text:
Washington (November 12, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), member of the Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, applauded the Senate’s unanimous passage of the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Reauthorization Act of 2026, which includes provisions from the Senator’s bipartisan Forecasting Optimization for Robust Earth Climate Analysis and Subseasonal-to-Seasonal Tracking (FORECAST) Act in Sec. 501 and his Coordinated Federal Response to Extreme Heat Act in Sec. 207. These provisions will improve long-term weather forecasting efforts and bolster a federal whole-of-government effort to keep Americans informed and prepared during extreme temperature events that will help prevent loss of life, injury, and damage to critical infrastructure.

“Extreme weather events are on the rise and pose an imminent threat to the safety of communities, and climate change poses a growing threat to the ability of farmers and other industries to plan and adapt to changing conditions. More reliable and accessible weather information supports our farmers, mariners, and emergency planners as we work to keep each other safe from devastating climate disasters,” said Senator Markey. “I applaud the Senate’s unanimous passage of legislation to improve this information, including my legislation to bring more reliable long-term weather predictions and more accessible extreme heat information to Americans as they weather increasing threats to their safety in everyday life.”

Senator Markey’s bipartisan FORECAST Act was reintroduced with Senator Roger Wicker (R-Miss.) in April 2025 and would direct the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to improve the reliability of longer-term forecasts—commonly referred to as subseasonal-to-seasonal (S2S) forecasting—by modernizing data modeling and prediction systems used in forecasting.

Senator Markey’s Coordinated Federal Response to Extreme Heat Act codifies NOAA’s National Integrated Heat Health Information System, an interagency effort to increase the accessibility of information about extreme heat and associated health risks and improve research on the dangers of extreme heat on our health and well-being. The program makes available a public online dashboard that provides warnings about extreme heat events and educational materials on heat health and will also establish an interagency committee to coordinate federal activities to reduce health risks from heat and deadly extreme temperatures.

title: Senator Markey Statement Celebrating Launch of Taiwan Fellowship Program
text:
Washington (November 12, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.) released the following statement on the Taiwan Fellowship Program Memorandum of Understanding entering into force. Senator Markey, along with then-Senator Marco Rubio, introduced the Taiwan Fellowship Act, in 2021 and the legislation passed into law in 2022 as part of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). The legislation establishes a fellowship exchange program for U.S. federal government employees to live on the island and work for Taiwan ministries, agencies, or parliamentary offices or other organizations in Taiwan related to their home agency work. Fellows will also learn Mandarin Chinese.

“I am proud that the historic Taiwan Fellowship Program, which was created by legislation that I introduced with Senator Marco Rubio in 2021 and which passed into law in 2022, will now enter into force. The Taiwan Fellowship Program will build essential ties between the United States and Taiwan by establishing a fellowship for U.S. federal government employees to live on the island and work for Taiwan ministries, agencies, or parliamentary offices. Taiwan is a vibrant democracy and a critical U.S. ally that shares our commitment to human rights, the rule of law, and security across the Indo-Pacific region and beyond. I look forward to seeing the first class of U.S. fellows arriving in Taiwan soon to start this important program.”

In May 2024, Senator Markey and then-Senator Rubio, along with a bipartisan group of their Senate colleagues, wrote to then-Secretary of State Antony Blinken, urging the United States Department of State to swiftly finalize an agreement with Taiwan to implement the Taiwan Fellowship program to allow its first fellows to arrive in Taiwan by the end of 2024.

title: SENATOR MCCORMICK CELEBRATES ELI LILLY’S $3.5 BILLION INVESTMENT IN THE LEHIGH VALLEY
text:
FOGELSVILLE, PA — U.S. Senator Dave McCormick (R-PA) today celebrated Eli Lilly and Company’s announcement of a $3.5 billion pharmaceutical manufacturing facility in Fogelsville, Pennsylvania, in the Lehigh Valley. The investment is expected to create 850 high-paying permanent jobs and approximately 2,000 construction jobs, further strengthening Pennsylvania’s position as a national leader in life sciences, innovation, and advanced manufacturing.

“Lilly’s $3.5 billion investment in the Lehigh Valley is another major win for Pennsylvania, bringing 850 high-paying jobs, strengthening American manufacturing, and cementing the Commonwealth’s position as a leader in life sciences,” said Senator McCormick. “When I talk about building a pro-growth environment in Pennsylvania, this is the type of investment I am working to attract.”

Senator McCormick is proud to have worked alongside Eli Lilly Chairman and CEO David A. Ricks and the Governor to help bring this significant investment to the Lehigh Valley. The project represents another major step toward expanding Pennsylvania’s economy, attracting private-sector investment, and creating new opportunities for Pennsylvania workers and families.

The facility will produce next-generation injectable medicines using advanced technologies, including AI and automation. It is expected to be operational by 2031. As part of the investment, Lilly also plans to provide up to $1 million over five years to the Upper Macungie Township Community Fund to support community programs focused on nutrition, healthy living, access to fresh food, and other health resources. The Lehigh Valley facility is part of Lilly’s broader $50 billion commitment to expanding pharmaceutical manufacturing sites the company has announced since 2020.

title: Merkley, Wyden, Bynum Lead Congressional Resolutions Honoring Silver Rail Elementary School and Bend Community
text:
Washington, D.C. – Oregon’s U.S. Senators Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden partnered with U.S. Representative Janelle Bynum (OR-05) to announce the introduction of resolutions in the Senate and House that express the condolences of Congress and honor the memory of the victims of the Silver Rail Elementary School shooting in Bend on October 15, 2026:

title: Senator Moody Calls on President to Approve Florida’s Request for Expedited Emergency Declaration Following Major Flooding Event
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Senator Ashley Moody is calling on President Trump to swiftly approve Florida’s request for an expedited emergency declaration following the major flooding that occurred in large swaths of the state last week. The effort supports Governor DeSantis’s request for federal disaster assistance in nine Florida counties: Brevard, DeSoto, Hardee, Highlands, Indian River, Martin, Okeechobee, Palm Beach, and St. Lucie.

“Following the major rain event we saw last week, many Florida homes were flooded, roads were washed out, and communities are still struggling to recover. We must act quickly to get help to those who need it most. I’m calling on the administration to approve the state’s request for federal disaster assistance, and I will continue working with President Trump and state officials to ensure Florida families have the resources they need to recover and rebuild,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

From November 1 through November 3, a historic rainfall event brought widespread flash flooding to portions of Florida, with some areas of Brevard County receiving an estimated 25 to 30 inches of rain. The severe flooding inundated homes, damaged infrastructure, closed roadways, and prompted emergency rescues. In Brevard County alone, more than 2,000 residents reported flooding impacts to their homes.

Governor DeSantis’s request for expedited emergency declaration seeks individual assistance, federal assistance for debris removal and emergency protective measures, direct federal assistance, and funding through the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program.

Read the Congressional letter here.

The disaster comes as Florida continues recovery efforts following Hurricane Isaias. Following Isaias, Senator Moody was on the ground working with state and federal officials to get aid to those in need as quickly as possible.

This effort is the latest in Senator Moody’s ongoing work to help Floridians recover from disasters. Senator Moody recently announced she has secured more than $2.5 billion in FEMA disaster funds for Florida communities affected by previous disasters.

Senator Moody introduced the TRACK Act (Transparency in Recovery Assistance & Claims Knowledge Act) to bring more transparency to the FEMA disaster aid process, which has now been passed into law.

The TRACK Act mandates a status tracker on the FEMA website, so victims of a disaster have easily available knowledge and insight of their claim’s progress.

If Floridians need help with federal agencies in the aftermath of the recent flooding or Isaias, Senator Moody’s office can assist—visit Moody.Senate.Gov to learn more.

title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Champions Legislation to Bring Greater Transparency and Accountability to Federal Courts
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Senator Ashley Moody is working to bring greater transparency to the judicial system. Senator Moody is championing the Blocking Overt Attempts at Shopping By Enforcing Randomization Guidelines (BOASBERG) Act, which would require cases to be randomly assigned to judges, helping prevent manipulation of the judicial process. Currently, loopholes exist to allow parties to shop around for a favorable judge. The BOASBERG Act will help ensure cases are decided fairly in America’s judicial system.

“As a former judge and prosecutor, I understand the importance of an independent judiciary and upholding the rule of law. That’s why I’m championing legislation to bring greater transparency and accountability to our federal courts. The American people need confidence that justice is administered fairly and impartially—and I’ll keep working to protect the integrity of our courts,” saidSenator Ashley Moody.

BACKGROUND:

The BOASBERG Act would enforce random case assignment, promoting confidence in judicial impartiality and helping prevent erroneous rulings.

The BOASBERG Act requires all district courts to randomly assign civil cases to ensure that no party, attorney, or judge can select or influence the assignment of a case to a particular judge.

The bill also requires Circuit Court of Appeals panels to be assigned at random, stopping improper panel rigging.

The bill requires cases to be reassigned to a new district judge if the Supreme Court overturns the original district judge’s ruling.

The legislation also requires courts to publicly disclose their randomization procedures.

Read bill text here.

Senator Moody recently introduced legislation to clean up two federal courts in Washington, D.C. Senator Moody’s Better Bench Act would allow nominees and active judges on the Court of Federal Claims and the Federal Circuit – both courts with nationwide jurisdiction – to reside anywhere in the United States by doing away with an outdated residency requirement that limits service to those in the D.C. area.

title: PASSED: Senate Unanimously Approves Sen. Moran’s FORECAST Act
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Jerry Moran (R-Kan.) – a member of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation – applauded the Senate’s unanimous passage this week of his legislation, the FORECAST Act, as a part of the Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Reauthorization Act of 2026 (Weather Act), which includes more than 17 bipartisan bills to help address natural disaster preparedness, radar and satellite modernization, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Weather Radio modernization and other programs focused on public safety and strengthening weather forecasting and communication. The Weather Act was approved by the Senate Commerce Committee in March 2026.

“Kansans, particularly farmers and ranchers, rely on access to timely and reliable weather data every day,” said Sen. Moran. “I’m pleased this bill incorporates my legislation, the FORECAST Act, to help make certain National Weather Service offices remain staffed to provide lifesaving 24/7 weather forecasting to their communities. Passage of this legislation is an important step to improve access to timely weather data for Kansans.”

Sen. Moran’s FORECAST Act would exempt certain National Weather Service (NWS) employees from any executive order or memorandum imposing a hiring freeze. Moran secured a national exemption from a federal hiring freeze to enable the NWS to hire meteorologists and weather forecasters, which helped address staffing shortages at the Goodland, Kansas, NWS office by providing a temporary rotation of NWS employees from other offices as they worked to fill vacancies.

title: Murray Joins Colleagues in Introducing Bill to Ensure Iran War Veterans Are Covered Under PACT Act
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), a senior member and former Chair of the Senate Committee on Veterans’ Affairs, joined Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and colleagues in introducing new legislation that would ensure Iran veterans are covered under the PACT Act, cutting unnecessary red tape and making it easier for our servicemembers, who are being exposed to toxic substances, to access the specialized treatment they need when they return home. In 2022, the PACT Act helped generations of veterans, who served in places from Vietnam to Iraq, more easily receive care from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) by establishing a list of locations where it is presumed by law that troops who served there were exposed to toxic hazards. However, Iran is currently not included on this presumptive list, despite troops being exposed to many of the same hazards. The New PACT for Iran Veterans Act would require the VA to add Iran to the list of covered locations and take more proactive action to ensure Iran War veterans—and all veterans who serve in future conflicts—don’t have to jump through bureaucratic hoops in order to access the care they need through their service.

“Donald Trump might not care, but the cost of war includes supporting our veterans when they come back home,” said Murray. “This legislation is a commonsense next step to expand the PACT Act to make sure our servicemembers who served in Iran continue to receive the care they need after their service is over. As I continue fighting to end the war—I want to be crystal clear that I won’t let this President leave American veterans in the dust.”

Specifically, the New PACT for Iran Veterans Act would:

Cut Red Tape for Iran War veterans by statutorily presuming toxic substance exposure for Iran War Veterans, helping streamline their access to health care and benefits at VA. The bill would ensure that federal law protects all veterans who fought in Iran, including those who operated in Iranian airspace and territorial waters.

Leave no veterans behind by requiring, for the first time, that the VA’s Military Environmental Exposure Sub-Council (MEESC) conducts studies at least every five years to review all overseas assignments for toxic substance exposures. Additionally, when the military begins a contingency operation, the VA must commence a similar review of the locations from which servicemembers support this operation within 180 days. This would ensure the VA proactively looks into whether servicemembers are being exposed to toxic hazards, for current and future assignments.

Enhance transparency at the VA by requiring the VA Secretary to publicly explain their justification for any denial of a country that’s recommended for presumed toxic-exposures in these reviews, or any removal of existing presumptions.

In addition to Senators Murray and Duckworth the legislation was also cosponsored by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Angus King (I-ME), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Peter Welch (D-VT), Michael Bennet (D-CO), John Fetterman (D-PA), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Maria Cantwell (D-WA), Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), and Chris Van Hollen (D-MD).

The legislation is endorsed by Disabled American Veterans (DAV), Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America (IAVA), Paralyzed Veterans of America (PVA), VoteVets, Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW) and the American Legion.

Full text of the bill is available HERE.

title: Murray Joins Colleagues in Push for Senate, House Leadership to Strip Provisions in NDAA that Mandate U.S.-Israel Defense, Intelligence Cooperation
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, joined Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD) and colleagues in pressing Senate and House leadership to exclude provisions in the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) that would require the President to expand and enhance defense cooperation and intelligence sharing with the Government of Israel. These provisions would undermine the United States’ ability to act independently and in line with U.S. national security interests at a time when the Government of Israel’s actions are increasingly not aligned with those interests.

The Senators begin, “As you prepare to conference the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), we respectfully urge you to exclude three provisions from the final bill that would further entrench concerning aspects of the U.S.-Israel defense and intelligence relationship at a time when the Israeli government’s actions are increasingly undermining U.S. interests and values. These provisions would constrain the Administration’s ability to independently determine how best to protect U.S. national security and would lock in long-term commitments despite our serious concerns with the Israeli government’s actions in Gaza, the West Bank, and other parts of the region.”

On the threats to U.S. national security, the lawmakers note, “The agreements and projects these provisions envision threaten U.S. national security interests by handing Israel leverage over American weapons systems and military technology. This is not hypothetical. The Netanyahu government has already leveraged its existing coproduction agreement with the United States on missile defense to block American Iron Dome batteries from reaching Ukraine, in direct opposition to U.S. national security interests. Should these provisions be enacted, it would further increase Israel’s leverage over the United States through some of the most sensitive technologies in warfare. That is not in the U.S. interest. If enacted, these agreements would create long-term dependencies by embedding Israeli technology into the U.S. defense industrial base that could make future policy changes costly or difficult to implement. President Trump, at his own discretion, could choose to enter new agreements with Israel under existing law. The executive branch does not need a congressional mandate to more deeply entrench U.S.-Israel defense cooperation.”

“Moreover, we do not share, let alone co-produce, many of these sensitive technologies even with our closest partners, including NATO or other treaty allies. To do so in this instance would be unwise, especially as the Government of Israel continues to pursue policies in Gaza, the West Bank and other parts of the region that are inconsistent with U.S. interests and values,” the lawmakers write.

“Prime Minister Netanyahu has openly stated that such an initiative was his idea. In a letter to Representative Stutzman, who led a resolution calling for an effort similar to these provisions, Prime Minister Netanyahu states, ‘I was glad to receive your proposed Congressional resolution endorsing my plan to shift the framework of the US-Israel defense cooperation from aid to partnership.’ The intention behind this is clear: to move U.S. security assistance governed through more traditional pathways, like Foreign Military Financing and arm sales, to more opaque, less discernible avenues through defense acquisitions and programs of record that reduce transparency, as well as increase Israel’s leverage over the United States and our dependency on Israeli technology. This is particularly problematic after Prime Minister Netanyahu boasted that he has been trying to start a war with Iran for 40 years. That war has proven to be a strategic disaster for the United States and against U.S. interests,” the Senators continue.

“For all these reasons, we should not legally mandate an expansion in defense co-production or a requirement to increase intelligence sharing with the Government of Israel. We therefore urge you to exclude Section 1217, Section 219, and Section 618 from the NDAA final conference report,” they conclude.

In addition to Senators Murray and Van Hollen the letter was cosigned by Senators Ron Wyden (D-OR), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Elizabeth Warren, (D-MA), Ed Markey (D-MA), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Tina Smith (D-MN), Peter Welch (D-VT), and Andy Kim (D-NJ). The letter was sent to Senate Majority Leader John Thune, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, House Speaker Mike Johnson, House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) Chair Roger Wicker, SASC Ranking Member Jack Reed, House Armed Services Committee Chair (HASC) Mike Rogers, and HASC Ranking Member Adam Smith.

The full text of the letter is available HERE and below.

Dear Majority Leader Thune, Minority Leader Schumer, Speaker Johnson, Minority Leader Jeffries, Chairman Wicker, Ranking Member Reed, Chairman Rogers, and Ranking Member Smith:

As you prepare to conference the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), we respectfully urge you to exclude three provisions from the final bill that would further entrench concerning aspects of the U.S.-Israel defense and intelligence relationship at a time when the Israeli government’s actions are increasingly undermining U.S. interests and values. These provisions would constrain the Administration’s ability to independently determine how best to protect U.S. national security and would lock in long-term commitments despite our serious concerns with the Israeli government’s actions in Gaza, the West Bank, and other parts of the region.

Both Section 1217 from the Senate Armed Services Committee-reported bill and Section 219 of the House-passed bill mandate the creation of a “United States-Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative” to expand and accelerate the U.S.-Israel defense relationship, including technology sharing, co-production of weapons systems, and bilateral research and development across multiple domains of warfare such as biotechnology, quantum, autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, cyberwarfare, and others.

The agreements and projects these provisions envision threaten U.S. national security interests by handing Israel leverage over American weapons systems and military technology. This is not hypothetical. The Netanyahu government has already leveraged its existing coproduction agreement with the United States on missile defense to block American Iron Dome batteries from reaching Ukraine, in direct opposition to U.S. national security interests. Should these provisions be enacted, it would further increase Israel’s leverage over the United States through some of the most sensitive technologies in warfare. That is not in the U.S. interest.

If enacted, these agreements would create long-term dependencies by embedding Israeli technology into the U.S. defense industrial base that could make future policy changes costly or difficult to implement. President Trump, at his own discretion, could choose to enter new agreements with Israel under existing law. The executive branch does not need a congressional mandate to more deeply entrench U.S.-Israel defense cooperation.

Moreover, we do not share, let alone co-produce, many of these sensitive technologies even with our closest partners, including NATO or other treaty allies. To do so in this instance would be unwise, especially as the Government of Israel continues to pursue policies in Gaza, the West Bank and other parts of the region that are inconsistent with U.S. interests and values.

Prime Minister Netanyahu has openly stated that such an initiative was his idea. In a letter to Representative Stutzman, who led a resolution calling for an effort similar to these provisions, Prime Minister Netanyahu states, “I was glad to receive your proposed Congressional resolution endorsing my plan to shift the framework of the US-Israel defense cooperation from aid to partnership.” The intention behind this is clear: to move U.S. security assistance governed through more traditional pathways, like Foreign Military Financing and arm sales, to more opaque, less discernible avenues through defense acquisitions and programs of record that reduce transparency, as well as increase Israel’s leverage over the United States and our dependency on Israeli technology. This is particularly problematic after Prime Minister Netanyahu boasted that he has been trying to start a war with Iran for 40 years. That war has proven to be a strategic disaster for the United States and against U.S. interests.

In addition to the provisions discussed above in the Senate and House NDAAs, the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence (SSCI) FY27 Intelligence Authorization Act, which is typically incorporated in the final NDAA, includes a provision (Sec. 618) that mandates the executive branch “expand and enhance intelligence sharing with the Government of Israel,” and also states that intelligence sharing with Israel “shall not be suspended, reduced, or otherwise materially limited.” The provision would tie the President’s hands from limiting intelligence sharing with Israel, even when doing so may be necessary to protect U.S. national security. That would be irresponsible and especially troubling given public reports that the Defense Intelligence Agency recently raised the counterintelligence threat from Israel to its highest level.

For all these reasons, we should not legally mandate an expansion in defense co-production or a requirement to increase intelligence sharing with the Government of Israel. We therefore urge you to exclude Section 1217, Section 219, and Section 618 from the NDAA final conference report.

###

title: Warnock, Ossoff Secure More Than $74 Million in Federal Funding for Railroad Safety, Blocked Crossing Relief Across Georgia
