title: Padilla, Blumenthal, Warren Introduce Transformative Bill to Address Veteran Housing Crisis
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Following Veterans Day, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Veterans’ Affairs, and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, announced the End Veterans Homelessness Act to help address the veteran housing crisis in California and across the country. The legislation would expand veterans’ eligibility for housing vouchers through the Department of Housing and Urban Development-Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing (HUD-VASH) program while reducing casework bottlenecks that prevent veterans from securing housing.

On any given night in America, nearly 32,500 veterans — including over 9,300 Californians — experience homelessness. To address this crisis, Congress created the HUD-VASH program to distribute vouchers to veterans, prioritizing those with chronic mental illnesses or substance use disorders. As of July 2026, Congress has funded nearly 116,000 HUD-VASH vouchers, but about 20,900 of these vouchers are not being utilized in part due to strict statutory requirements.

The End Veterans Homelessness Act would help veterans access these unused vouchers by enhancing the efficiency of the HUD-VASH program, broadening program eligibility, increasing oversight, and reducing bureaucratic red tape.

“Our veterans have made immense sacrifices to defend our nation, and we owe them our unwavering support, including a stable roof over their heads,” said Senator Padilla. “Too many federally funded HUD-VASH vouchers are going unused every year due to red tape and outdated eligibility requirements. The End Veterans Homelessness Act takes a critical step toward expanding access to essential housing support for veterans and honoring their immense service and sacrifice for our country.”

“No veteran should go without food or shelter,” said Senator Blumenthal. “Every year, thousands of HUD-VASH vouchers—one of our most successful tools to help end veterans homelessness—go unused. Our commonsense legislation will help ensure more housing vouchers get used and will put more veterans into stable housing.”

“Veterans who put their lives on the line to serve our country shouldn’t end up sleeping on the streets. This legislation will cut red tape in the VASH Program to ensure veterans have the assistance and support they need when struggling to find stable, affordable housing,” said Senator Warren.

Specifically, the End Veterans Homelessness Act would:

Broaden HUD-VASH eligibility to include veterans and their families who are experiencing or at risk of homelessness and veterans who do not require intensive supportive services (and are currently ineligible for the program), while preserving priority for chronically homeless veterans and veterans with chronic disabilities;

Allow veterans currently receiving housing assistance through other programs to transfer into HUD-VASH, freeing up limited housing subsidies for non-veterans in need;

Adopt effective Emergency Housing Voucher program flexibilities and allow public housing authorities to use administrative fees to streamline the process; and

Increase transparency and oversight by directing HUD to provide Congress with an annual report on voucher utilization and barriers to access, and by requiring a Government Accountability Office review of HUD-VASH and veteran housing stability across federal programs.

California Representatives Mark Takano (D-Calif.-39), Maxine Waters (D-Calif.-43), and Mike Levin (D-Calif.-49) led companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

The bill is endorsed by organizations including National Alliance to End Homelessness, National Low Income Housing Coalition, American Legion, National Federation of Federal Employees, and National Coalition of Homeless Veterans.

“We thank Senator Padilla and Representative Takano for reintroducing the End Veterans Homelessness Act,” said Ann Oliva, CEO of the National Alliance to End Homelessness. “Veteran homelessness shows what happens when the nation commits to permanent housing and the services people need to stay housed: it works. Our new preliminary 2026 point-in-time estimate shows continued progress among veterans. HUD-VASH is a big part of that success. This bill would strengthen and expand the program so more veterans can get housed, and it would bring us closer to the goal of ending veteran homelessness for good.”

“I want to thank Senator Padilla and Representative Takano for their leadership in introducing the End Veterans Homelessness Act, which would improve and expand the HUD-VASH program to allow more veterans experiencing homelessness to access permanent housing and wraparound services,” said NLIHC President and CEO Renee Willis. “The HUD-VASH program has been a critical tool for addressing and ending homelessness for hundreds of thousands of veterans. Expanding and building upon the success of the program will bring the nation closer to the goal of ending veteran homelessness and serve as a roadmap for how we can ensure everyone has a safe, affordable place to call home.”

“All veterans should be able to access the housing supports that are most appropriate for their needs and preferences,” said Kathryn Monet, Chief Executive Officer, National Coalition for Homeless Veterans. “This legislation is necessary to remove barriers to housing for veterans and to allow them to transition between programs when that is the right choice for them.”

Padilla has consistently fought to improve veterans’ access to housing and services. In July, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act became law, which included Padilla’s bipartisan Housing Unhoused Disabled Veterans Act (HUDVA) to ensure that veterans experiencing homelessness and receiving VA disability benefits maintain access to crucial housing support. The HUDVA provision would permanently exclude disability payments received by veterans from annual income for housing assistance eligibility purposes through the HUD-VASH Program. In 2024, Padilla passed a bipartisan amendment into law to increase and streamline veterans’ access to HUD-VASH housing vouchers through the FY24 appropriations package. Last year, Padilla and Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) urged VA Secretary Doug Collins to provide emergency housing and health care for veterans affected by the Los Angeles fires.

In May, Padilla announced more than $110 million in federal funding from the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to support updates at Veterans Home in Yountville – which serves the needs of nearly 1,000 veterans and their families.

Padilla believes everyone deserves access to affordable and safe housing and recognizes the need to drastically increase the affordable housing stock to address the homelessness crisis facing California and the country, including through his Housing for All Act. This legislation would invest in proven solutions to address affordable housing shortages and provide a historic level of federal funding for existing programs to reduce homelessness and for innovative, locally developed solutions to support vulnerable populations experiencing homelessness.

title: ON THE JOB FOR MICHIGAN: Traverse City Veterans Service Officer Highlights Peters’ Efforts to Pass the PACT Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – In a new “On the Job” video from U.S. Senator Gary Peters’ (MI) office, Michael Roof, Director of Grand Traverse County Veterans Affairs, highlights Peters’ efforts to help pass the Sergeant First Class Heath Robinson Honoring our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics (PACT) Act into law. The PACT Act delivered VA health care and benefits to all generations of toxic-exposed veterans, and their survivors, for the first time in our nation’s history. As of March 2026, more than 2.4 million veterans, including nearly 43,000 veterans across Michigan, have received VA health care benefits as a result of this law. The video is part of the On the Job for Michigan series, which highlights Peters’ leadership and advocacy on behalf of Michigan constituents and communities.

“When I started doing this in 2012, you heard a lot of Vietnam Veterans who were exposed to Agent Orange and herbicides. Then comes the current war, they’re suffering with cancers and other toxic related injuries for years,” said Michael Roof, Grand Traverse County Veterans Affairs Director. “Those Veterans that were getting out, it was hard to connect them with benefits. The PACT Act... that opened up a whole new world for Veterans.”

“Now, we have the systemic momentum of the Veterans community,” said Kevin Hensley of the Michigan Burn Pits 360 Chapter. “What it means for Veterans, is they finally get the opportunity to file those claims.”

Watch the “On The Job” video here.

“We have a responsibility to ensure all of our veterans can access the health care, benefits, and support they have earned,” said Peters. “The PACT Act did exactly that. That historic law is delivering long overdue benefits and health care to Michigan veterans who were exposed to toxic substances like Agent Orange and toxic burn pits during their service. I encourage all veterans who are suffering from toxic-exposure to reach out to their local veteran agencies to get a claim filed today.”

During his service in the U.S. Navy Reserve, Peters earned a Seabee Combat Warfare Specialist designation and rose to the rank of Lieutenant Commander. After the September 11th terrorist attacks on our country, Peters volunteered again for drilling status and served overseas as part of his Reserve duty. He later earned a diploma from the College of Naval Command and Staff, U.S. Naval War College.

In the Senate, Peters has remained committed to supporting our nation’s servicemembers and veterans. In 2021, Peters was inducted into the Michigan Military and Veterans Hall of Honor for his efforts to support our nation’s veterans and military. In 2017, Peters was recognized as Legislator of the Year by the Vietnam Veterans of America for authoring the bipartisan Fairness for Veterans Act, which was signed into law as part of the national defense bill. The legislation requires veteran discharge review boards to give liberal consideration to petitions for honorable discharge status if the servicemember has been diagnosed with PTSD, TBI, or other related conditions connected to their military service.

title: Peters Statement Opposing Nomination of Eric Ueland to Be GAO Comptroller General
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Gary Peters, Ranking Member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, issued the following statement opposing the nomination of Office of Management and Budget Deputy Director Eric Ueland to be the Comptroller General of the Government Accountability Office (GAO) for a 15-year term:

“The Comptroller General is a position that serves Congress, and Congress alone, as we work to identify waste, fraud and abuse, and craft critical reforms to improve the daily lives of Americans. President Trump’s appointment of Eric Ueland – and Congressional Republicans’ rubber stamp of this appointment in violation of longstanding bipartisan practice – only provides further power to the Executive Branch at a time when independent oversight from Congress is needed more than ever. I will oppose this nomination, and I urge my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to join me so we can preserve Congress’ independent oversight abilities.”

Last week, Peters issued a statement along with Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, and U.S Representative Robert Garcia, Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, calling out the sham process Republican leaders instituted to pave the way for this nomination. As required by statute, a 10-member bipartisan, bicameral Commission recommends at least three candidates, and the President chooses a nominee from the Commission’s recommendations. The bipartisan Commission is made up of the Speaker of the House of Representatives, the President pro tempore of the Senate, the majority and minority leaders of the House and Senate, the Chair and Ranking Member of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, and the Chair and Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform. All three times the Commission process has occurred in the past, the president has selected a nominee with bipartisan support.

title: Reed Condemns House Republican ‘Sneak Attack’ on Veterans Benefits
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Yesterday, as America celebrated Veterans Day by saluting those who served, House Republicans tried to pull a fast one on veterans across the country by slashing their benefits.

Republican leaders used a “voice vote” – with no roll call indicating who supported or opposed the measure – to try to sneak through Republicans’ so-called Take Care of America's Veterans Act (H.R. 9237). This highly partisan and controversial bill would actually cut $57 billion from the disability benefits of future veterans – the largest veterans’ benefits cut in American history.

U.S. Senator Jack Reed, a member of the Appropriations Committee, who graduated from West Point and served in the U.S. Army, says he will do everything he can to block the bill in the U.S. Senate in order to prevent the drastic cuts to veterans, which would nearly triple the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs’ (VA) streamlined refinancing fee.

“Our veterans fought honorably to serve the entire country and they deserve our best. You don’t expand benefits for a few by taking away benefits from disabled veterans who earned them and depend on them. It is a shame so-called Republican leaders tried to use procedural gimmicks to cloak their action, but Democrats and independent members of the media exposed this attempted betrayal. Our nation’s veterans made incredible sacrifices on our behalf, and we must thank them with more than words, but with deeds. That means keeping the promise to ensure they have access to health care, opportunity, and the benefits they earned,” said Senator Reed.

According to The Hill newspaper, House Republicans departed from standard House procedures to pass the bill, which House Democrats labeled ‘dirty pool’:

“Democrats opposed the GOP’s Take Care of America’s Veterans Act (TCAVA), saying it would expand some veterans’ benefits by slashing others. In her daily whip notice, Rep. Katherine Clark (D-Mass.) urged House Democrats to vote no.

“Yet when Rep. Addison McDowell (N.C.), the Republican lawmaker presiding over the House chamber Wednesday afternoon, brought the bill up for consideration, no one on the Democratic side demanded a recorded vote — a curious silence given that Democrats were whipping against the bill. That allowed McDowell to declare the bill passed instantly, by voice vote.

“Furious Democrats accused Republicans of playing “dirty pool.” They said Republicans pulled Rep. Mark Takano (D-Calif.), the ranking member of the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee, away from the podium, where he was leading the Democratic side of the debate, in order to discuss changes to the bill. It was during that parley — while Takano was away from his microphone — that McDowell fast-tracked the proposal, they said.

“After publicly announcing a recorded vote on the TCAVA legislation, House Republicans asked if RM Takano and Democrats would agree to last minute engrossment corrections,” a Democratic leadership aide said.”

Senator Reed noted that the bill still must pass the U.S. Senate before it can become law and vowed to prevent it from being enacted as is. Reed says while he supports some provisions in the bill that would benefit veterans and caregivers, he strongly opposes the changes to tinnitus and sleep apnea ratings that would reduce compensation for many affected veterans.

“I support balanced, fiscally responsible solutions. Let’s end the war in Iran. That would save billions. But I have little respect for those who repeatedly vote to send troops off to war and then balk at paying to care for our veterans when they return home,” said Senator Reed.

In a scathing rebuke of House Republicans, the VFW issued a press release: VFW Condemns Cowardly and Dishonorable House Passage of Benefit Cuts on Veterans Day noting that “House shirks accountability and quickly claims to pass controversial and unprecedented benefit cuts by voice vote.” The VFW release states: “The VFW has repeatedly raised concerns about Section 108 of the legislation, which would, for the first time ever, write changes to the VA disability rating schedule into law to generate budget savings. Beyond its immediate implications for veterans' disability compensation, the VFW believes this approach creates a roadmap for future Congresses to target veterans’ earned benefits as a budgetary gimmick or to cut benefits out of political convenience.”

Senator Reed stated: “The bottom line is, we should treat all our veterans with respect instead of trying to help one veteran by taking away assistance from others who served our nation in uniform. I hope we can find a principled compromise to uphold our nation’s promise to our veterans. You don’t do that through political tricks and gimmicks; you did it through hard work and by working across the aisle.”

title: Reed Statement on NVIDIA CEO Resignation and Trump’s Failure to Protect America’s National Security
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of NVIDIA, U.S. Senator Jack Reed (D-RI), the Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, issued the following statement:

“Jensen Huang’s resignation does not excuse his recklessness or dispel the alarming questions surrounding NVIDIA and the Trump Administration’s failure to protect American national security from Chinese espionage.

“American semiconductor technology is essential to our military capabilities and our technological advantage over China. Yet the Trump Administration reversed course on critical export restrictions, allowing NVIDIA to sell advanced AI chips to China despite clear national security risks. I am aware of reports that these chips were diverted through intermediaries with ties to Chinese intelligence. This crisis raises alarming questions about the security of our technology and the integrity of our military supply chains under the Trump Administration.

“Indeed, the Commander of U.S. Pacific Command testified to Congress this year that the transfer of advanced semiconductors to China would ‘undoubtedly’ come at the expense of American servicemembers in the event of a conflict.

“Even more disturbing are reports that President Trump was briefed on intelligence linking a suspected Chinese operative to Huang and chose not to act. If true, this represents an extraordinary failure of presidential responsibility. The President’s first obligation is to protect the American people and our servicemembers, not to protect powerful corporate allies or accommodate their commercial interests.

“Millions of Americans also have economic exposure to NVIDIA through their retirement accounts and pension funds. The company has backstopped the AI ecosystem through complex financing transactions. We need full transparency into these deals, an assessment of whether the company is ‘too big to fail,’ and an analysis of how these events may affect the U.S. banking system and credit markets.

“Jensen Huang’s departure does not resolve this matter. We need a full accounting of what the Administration knew, when it knew it, and why it failed to act. Congress must get answers, and those responsible must be held accountable.”

Public reporting revealed that Jensen Huang had an extramarital relationship with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company. The executive is a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Megaspeed has purchased more than $4.8 billion in advanced NVIDIA AI chips since June 2024. The Department of Justice is reportedly investigating Megaspeed for diverting chips to China in violation of export controls. Reporting also suggests that officials at the White House, State Department, and Commerce Department, including President Trump, knew of these concerns, yet continued to approve the sale of advanced semiconductor chips to China.

title: Rosen Bill to Improve Weather Forecasting to Help Nevada Farmers and Ranchers Passes Senate
text:
Senator Rosen’s Legislation Was Included As Part Of The Bipartisan Weather Act

WASHINGTON, DC – This week, U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen’s (D-NV) bill to improve weather forecasting to help Nevada farmers and ranchers passed the Senate as part of the bipartisan Weather Act. Senator Rosen’s Smarter Weather Forecasting for Water Management, Farming, and Ranching Act creates new subseasonal and seasonal forecasting pilot projects under the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to improve advanced forecasts ranging from two weeks to two years, establishing more consistent short-term and long-term weather forecasting. This would help farmers and ranchers be more prepared for potential weather anomalies, such as flash floods or extreme drought. The bill now goes to the House of Representatives, and if passed, would go to the President’s desk.

“The severity of the wildfires and extreme heat in Nevada this past summer reminded us just how important it is that we invest in the latest weather prediction technology and fund critical programs at NOAA,” said Senator Rosen. “I’m glad that my bill, to ensure Nevada’s farmers and ranchers have access to forecasts that will improve their ability to prepare for weather anomalies, is part of the bipartisan Weather Act that has now passed the U.S. Senate. I call on the House of Representatives to pass it soon so we can send it to the President’s desk without delay.”

With extreme weather conditions becoming more common, Senator Rosen has fought to ensure that Nevada has all the federal support it needs to handle even the worst weather anomalies. She recently led Senate colleagues in demanding more assistance from FEMA for wildfire prevention and response. In May, Senator Rosen introduced bipartisan legislation to help protect drinking water infrastructure during extreme heat emergencies. As part of the bipartisan government funding bill for 2026, Senator Rosen secured $4.25 billion to support wildfire suppression across the country, as well as $6.1 million for Regional Climate Centers – one of which is located in Reno.

title: NEWS: Sanders Announces 17th Annual State of the Union Essay Contest
text:
BURLINGTON, Vt., Nov. 12 – Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) has launched his 17th annual State of the Union Essay Contest for Vermont students.

Each year, the president of the United States delivers an address to a joint session of Congress, which outlines priorities for the coming year. Sanders knows that great ideas can come from everyone — not just those in power — which is why he created the State of the Union Essay Contest to encourage young people to engage in the political process. The contest is an opportunity for Vermont high school students to describe a major issue facing our country and propose what they would do to solve it.

“The purpose of this contest is to get young people to start thinking about the many important issues that we deal with every day,” said Sanders. “As proven by the recent midterm elections, all people have the right to express their views and help shape the direction in which our country goes — and that includes young people. I want to see our students be actively engaged, no matter where they stand on the issues.”

The 250-to-500-word essays can be on any issue of national importance. A volunteer panel of Vermont educators will judge the essays on the students’ ability to articulate an issue and propose a solution, without regard to the students’ political views. Following the contest, Sanders will invite the finalists to a roundtable discussion at the Vermont State House and will enter their essays into the Congressional Record — the official archive of the U.S. Congress.

More than 7,000 students from high schools across Vermont have written essays in the past 16 years about critically important issues, including climate change, racial justice, corporate power, immigration reform, artificial intelligence, political polarization and much, much more. Last year, Saralynn Anderson from Essex High School was selected as the winner from 417 submissions for her essay on mental health care for students.

The deadline for student essay submission is January 11, 2027. More information can be found on Sanders’ Senate website HERE or by calling (800) 339-9834.

title: NEWS: Schiff, Huffman, Whitehouse, Dingell, Beyer, and Colleagues Demand Answers on Trump Administration’s Effort to Gut Endangered Wildlife Protections
text:
Lawmakers warn administration’s changes would leave protected species vulnerable to foreseeable deaths and habitat destruction

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), member of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works and Ranking Member of the Fisheries, Water, and Wildlife Subcommittee; U.S. Representatives Jared Huffman (D-Calif.-02), House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member; Debbie Dingell (D-Mich.-06) and Don Beyer (D-Va.-08); and U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Ranking Member on the Senate Committee on Environment & Public Works, led 37 other Democratic lawmakers in demanding answers from Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on the Trump administration’s attempts to gut core Endangered Species Act (ESA) protections by reinterpreting what the agencies consider “incidental take” and “harm” in memoranda to federal employees.

The lawmakers warned the reinterpretation would strip protections from wildlife killed or injured by otherwise lawful activities, even when those deaths and injuries could be foreseen. Under the administration’s interpretation, the law’s prohibition on killing or injuring protected wildlife would apply only when someone deliberately targets a protected species. The lawmakers warned this would undermine decades of safeguards that allow economic activity to proceed while requiring commonsense steps to prevent wildlife deaths and injuries.

“For decades, the ESA has provided a framework for allowing economic activity to proceed while requiring reasonable measures to avoid and minimize harm to threatened and endangered species. These memoranda would undermine that framework by removing incentives to prevent foreseeable wildlife deaths and injuries,” the lawmakers wrote.

The letter challenges two identical internal memos issued September 14 by U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Director Brian Nesvik and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration General Counsel John Luce. The memos direct staff to interpret “take” — which includes killing or injuring protected wildlife — as covering only intentional actions targeting those animals. The lawmakers are demanding an explanation of the legal basis for that interpretation and whether activities that could foreseeably kill or injure endangered species still require permits.

The directives came as the Trump administration eliminated the longstanding regulatory definition of “harm,” which covered habitat destruction that kills or injures protected wildlife. Both changes took effect the same day, threatening protections for endangered animals and the places they need to survive.

“Any reinterpretation that could eliminate protections for these species is a serious and troubling departure from that framework and would undermine the law’s implementation,” the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers requested responses by November 30, 2026, including what protections would remain for species threatened by habitat destruction and whether states and Tribes were consulted. They also asked whether Interior would suspend implementation until it publicly explains its legal reasoning and assesses the consequences for endangered wildlife.

“The Services must abandon this approach and preserve the ESA’s longstanding protections for threatened and endangered wildlife and the communities that depend on them,” the lawmakers concluded.

Additional House signers included Representatives Becca Balint (D-Vt.), Suzanne Bonamici (D-Ore.), Julia Brownley (D-Calif.), Ed Case (D-Hawai’i), Steve Cohen (D-Tenn.), Jasmine Crockett (D-Texas), Diana DeGette (D-Colo.), Mark DeSaulnier (D-Calif.), Sarah Elfreth (D-Md.), Dwight Evans (D-Pa.), Glenn Ivey (D-Md.), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.), Mike Levin (D-Calif.), Sarah McBride (D-Del.), Dave Min (D-Calif.), Kevin Mullin (D-Calif.), Frank Pallone Jr. (D-N.J.), Scott Peters (D-Calif.), Emily Randall (D-Wash.), Deborah Ross (D-N.C.), Mary Gay Scanlon (D-Pa.), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), Dina Titus (D-Nev.), Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), Jill Tokuda (D-Hawai’i), and Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-Fla.).

Additional Senate signers included Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawai’i), Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), and Ron Wyden (D-Ore.).

Background: Recently, Senators Schiff and Whitehouse introduced a privileged resolution to reject the administration’s unprecedented attempt to circumvent Congress’s intent when it passed the Endangered Species Act in 1973 and to stop the reversal of a decades-old provision meant to protect our wildlife. The Senators will force a vote in the coming weeks.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear Secretary Burgum and Secretary Lutnick:

We write in strong opposition to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service’s (FWS’s) and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA’s) – (“the Services”) unlawful reinterpretation of “harm” and “take” in the Endangered Species Act (ESA). In two internal memoranda to staff released on September 14, 2026 – one issued by the FWS Director Brian Nesvik and another from NOAA General Counsel John Luce – the Services reinterpret settled law regarding protections for threatened and endangered wildlife under the ESA. The ESA is one of America’s most successful and widely supported environmental laws.

The memoranda reinterpret unlawful “take” under the ESA to only include intentional actions targeting threatened and endangered species. Under this interpretation, incidental killing, injury, or other forms of take resulting from otherwise lawful activities would fall outside the ESA’s protections. With nearly a third of America’s wildlife at risk of extinction, we should bolster our efforts to protect threatened and endangered species, not weaken them.

This reinterpretation raises concerns about the future of the ESA’s incidental take permitting system. For decades, the ESA has provided a framework for allowing economic activity to proceed while requiring reasonable measures to avoid and minimize harm to threatened and endangered species. These memoranda would undermine that framework by removing incentives to prevent foreseeable wildlife deaths and injuries.

This illegal reinterpretation of take, combined with the Department of the Interior (DOI) and the Department of Commerce (DOC) rule rescinding the regulatory definition of “harm” under the ESA, which went into effect on September 14, 2026, would render Section 9 prohibitions hollow, in essence only preventing purposeful take of an animal. Until September, the Services had long recognized that significant habitat modification or degradation could constitute “harm” because it could have indirect impacts on the survival of an animal. These new memoranda attempt to entirely eliminate any guardrails on incidental take.

We have worked in Congress to safeguard the ESA and ensure federal agencies carry out their duty under the ESA to prevent extinction and recover species. We are alarmed by the enormous consequences the interpretation could have for species across the country. To better understand the Services’ position and assist the oversight of the House Natural Resources Committee and the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, please respond to the following questions by November 30, 2026:

Do the September 14, 2026 memoranda represent the official legal position of DOI and the DOC? If so, when did it take effect, and what legal guidance did DOC and DOI issue to field offices regarding its implementation?

What statutory language and legal precedent support the memoranda’s conclusion that incidental killing or injury of endangered species does not constitute a prohibited “take” unless the activity was specifically intended to target the animal?

How do DOI and DOC reconcile the new interpretation with the Supreme Court’s decision in Babbitt, which upheld the inclusion of habitat modification that kills or injures protected wildlife within the ESA’s definition of “harm”?

Do DOI and DOC continue to require incidental take permits for activities that may foreseeably kill or injure endangered species? If the memorandum changes those requirements, please describe how.

What protections would remain available for endangered species whose threats involve incidental take, including incidental harm and habitat destruction, from otherwise lawful activities?

Did DOI and DOC consult with states, Tribes, or other relevant stakeholders before issuing or distributing the memorandum? If so, please describe the nature and timeline of such consultations.

Will DOI suspend implementation of the memorandum pending a public explanation of its legal basis and an assessment of its implications on the ESA?

The ESA has provided a framework for protecting endangered wildlife while allowing economic activity to continue with appropriate safeguards for over 50 years. Any reinterpretation that could eliminate protections for these species is a serious and troubling departure from that framework and would undermine the law’s implementation. The Services must abandon this approach and preserve the ESA’s longstanding protections for threatened and endangered wildlife and the communities that depend on them.

Please contact the Natural Resources Committee Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife and Fisheries minority staff at (202) 225-6065 with any questions about this request. We look forward to your prompt response to this oversight request.

###

title: NEWS: Schiff, Padilla, San Diego Congressional Delegation Demand Answers After 8-Year-Old is Detained at Immigration Check-In
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) along with Representatives Juan Vargas (D-Calif.-52), Sara Jacobs (D-Calif.-51), Mike Levin (D-Calif.-49), and Scott Peters (D-Calif.-50) demanded answers from the Trump Administration after an eight-year-old Haitian child who lost Temporary Protected Status earlier this year was taken into federal custody after an immigration check-in in San Diego.

“An ICE officer reportedly invoked the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 while taking him into custody, apparently placing the child in restraints and separating him from the person who brought him for his hearing. Video footage appears to show the use of restraints on a child who seemed to pose no threat to those around him, raising serious questions about the handling of this incident,” wrote the lawmakers. “We express concerns about the basis for this action and the harm it may cause a young child who appeared for his required hearing.”

“With this letter, we emphasize that the safety and well-being of children and families in San Diego County must remain the highest priority,” the lawmakers continued. “We also request confirmation on the child’s whereabouts, whether his family is aware of his location, and what steps your agencies are taking to ensure he can be reunited with them.”

Read the full letter here and below.

Dear Secretary Mullin and Secretary Kennedy,

We write to express deep concerns regarding reports that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detained an eight-year-old Haitian child at a scheduled immigration hearing in San Diego, California, on November 5, 2026. An ICE officer reportedly invoked the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 while taking him into custody, apparently placing the child in restraints and separating him from the person who brought him for his hearing. Video footage appears to show the use of restraints on a child who seemed to pose no threat to those around him, raising serious questions about the handling of this incident. We express concerns about the basis for this action and the harm it may cause a young child who appeared for his required hearing before the Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR).

Our September 22, 2026, letter concerning ICE enforcement activity around school and educational institutions addressed the fear and disruption these actions cause in our communities. House Members of the San Diego congressional delegation also wrote to both the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Department of Education on October 14, 2025, highlighting concerns from twenty-five San Diego County school district superintendents. The superintendents requested DHS to adopt clear consistent enforcement policies and coordination between the departments to keep schools safe places to learn. This reported detention underscores those concerns. Following this third-grade student’s detention, San Diego Unified School District reportedly sent crisis counselors to Fay Elementary School to support his classmates, who expressed fear and distress. The effects of this action extend far beyond one child and his family.

With this letter, we emphasize that the safety and well-being of children and families in San Diego County must remain the highest priority. We will continue to monitor this situation closely and expect timely updates on the child’s well-being and your agencies’ response to these concerns. We also request confirmation on the child’s whereabouts, whether his family is aware of his location, and what steps your agencies are taking to ensure he can be reunited with them. We ask that you promptly review this child’s case and give it your full and fair consideration based on its merits, consistent with all applicable laws, rules, and regulations. title: NEWS: Senate Unanimously Passes Sen. Schiff’s Bill to Designate National Scenic Trail in Bay Area
text:
Washington, D.C. – This week, the U.S. Senate unanimously passed U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.)’s legislation to begin the process to designate the Bay Area Ridge Trail as a National Scenic Trail. This designation would enhance the trail’s visibility as a world-class recreation opportunity and attract new visitors, in addition to helping connect the different routes within the trail.

“The Bay Area Ridge Trail gives visitors to the Bay Area and its residents the opportunity to enjoy more than 500 miles of some of California’s most incredible outdoor beauty, including parks and preserves. Providing federal recognition to this ridgeline trail will help preserve it for future generations. I am proud to continue working with federal and local partners to get this across the finish line,” said Senator Schiff.

“The Bay Area Ridge Trail is a crown jewel of our region, providing millions of people with access to some of the most stunning natural landscapes in the country and connecting our communities to the outdoors,” said Representative Huffman. “Designating it as a National Scenic Trail would not only help complete it – it would set it on par with iconic trails like the Appalachian and Pacific Crest and elevate the incredible and diverse Bay Area landscapes. This would be a major boost for the recreation economy, and our bill gets that ball rolling. I’m grateful to my partners in the Senate for moving our bill forward and am excited to get it across the finish line.”

“The Bay Area Ridge Trail is one of Northern California’s many treasures, connecting local communities and visitors to historic and breathtaking landscapes that make our state so special,” said Senator Padilla. “This is an important step toward designating it as a National Scenic Trail in order to safeguard our public lands, strengthen conservation efforts, and bolster our tourism economy. I’m proud to work alongside my colleagues and see our bill pass the Senate, ensuring Californians and visitors alike have access to our extraordinary outdoor recreation opportunities.”

The legislation requires the National Park Service to complete the required feasibility study in consultation with the Bay Area Ridge Trail Council and relevant federal, state, and tribal agencies. The trail meets all the required criteria established in the National Trails System Act of 1968 for National Scenic Trail designation, including:

Extended trail route of more than 100 miles

Provides maximum outdoor recreation potential

Provides for enjoyment of nationally significant scenic, historic, and cultural qualities

Represents desert, marsh, grassland, mountain, canyon, river, and forest

Represents landforms that exhibit significant regional geographic characteristics

Connects with side trails, which provide additional public access

The legislation is led by U.S. Representative Jared Huffman (D-Calif.-02) in the House, and is cosponsored by U.S. Senator Alex Padilla and every member of the Bay Area delegation.

The full text of the legislation is available here.

title: Slotkin Joins Colleagues in Demanding Action After Trump Appointee Interfered in Investigation on Insider Trading in Oil Markets
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), Adam Schiff (D-CA), and Raphael Warnock (D-GA) — fellow members of the Senate Agriculture Committee — pressed the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chairman Selig for answers on reporting that the CFTC sought to retract an investigative referral into potential insider trading in oil markets.

Minutes before President Trump backed away from threats to strike Iranian power plants on March 23, billions of dollars-worth of contracts were placed predicting oil would fall and the S&P would rise, raising concerns about insider trading. According to reporting, CFTC political appointee Arun Mel Gunewardena directed career staff to retract a referral to the Division of Enforcement to examine the suspicious trading activity. He subsequently assembled a separate team to conduct a new analysis of the trading activity, reportedly excluding the CFTC’s career analysts who prepared the original referral.

“Mr. Gunewardena’s reported intervention raises urgent concerns that political leadership may have interfered with career staff’s efforts to investigate potentially unlawful trading, compromising the independence and integrity of the CFTC’s enforcement process. For months, many of us have urged you to investigate a spate of suspicious trades in oil markets, totaling billions of dollars,” the Senators wrote.

“The CFTC has a statutory authority promoting the integrity of America’s commodity futures and derivatives markets and has significant enforcement authorities to punish wrongdoing. Since President Trump’s second inauguration, the CFTC has already seen an exodus of both senior career Division of Enforcement leadership and staff attorneys. Public reporting also indicates that the number of CFTC enforcement actions has declined substantially compared with previous fiscal years,” the Senators continued.

The Senators are requesting the CFTC provide answers on whether the agency was made aware that a referral of suspicious trading had been made, the communications between Mr. Gunewardena and career staff, the CFTC’s procedure to refer, evaluate, and investigate suspected insider trading, what precedent, if any, is there for a political appointee or other senior level CFTC official to direct the retraction of an enforcement referral, and what assurances that enforcement determinations will be made independently by enforcement staff without inappropriate interference from political appointees. They’re also urging the agency to preserve all records and communications relating to the topics addressed.

In addition to Slotkin, Schiff, and Warnock, this letter is signed by Ron Wyden (D-OR), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Jack Reed (D-RI), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Amy Klobuchar (D-MN).

title: Slotkin Statement After Trump Again Called for Her to be Prosecuted Over 90-Second Video
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) released a statement after President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social about her and five of her colleagues, again calling for them to be tried and prosecuted for a 90-second video they recorded last year, restating the law. This also comes after President Trump directed the Department of Justice, and Attorney General Todd Blanche, to investigate Slotkin, just a few days ago.

Slotkin’s statement:

“It’s been almost exactly one year since the six of us made a 90-second video simply restating the law, and the President cannot let it go.

“Based on that video, he ordered his then-Attorney General to ‘investigate, arrest and hang’ us for sedition. Last February, the Attorney General saluted and took us to court, trying to criminally indict us for sedition. A group of jurors, whom I will never meet, unanimously threw it out. The President and the Attorney General came for me again in the last few weeks for yet another freedom of speech issue.

“There is no clearer telltale sign of a disassembling authoritarian leader than when he tries to prosecute those who simply speak up against him. It’s a classic move to try and weaponize the government against your critics — I’ve seen it in places like Eastern Europe and the Middle East, over and over. It’s also a desperate move to distract from the generational loss he’s brought to his party.

“So, I say to President Trump and his Attorney General: Bring it. It would demonstrate to the country just how you’re hitting rock bottom. And if that lets us then begin to recover and repair from your disastrous leadership, please just get on with it.”

title: U.S. Senator Tina Smith Introduces Bipartisan Legislation to Honor Deceased Peace Corps Members
text:
Sen. Smith’s legislation is the result of a Minnesotan who was barred from engraving the Peace Corps symbol into the gravestone of her brother, a longtime Peace Corps member

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Tina Smith (D-MN) introduced a bipartisan bill to allow the official Peace Corps seal, emblem and logo to be used on gravestones, plaques and death announcements for deceased Peace Corps volunteers, officers and staff. Sen. Smith’s bill, the Memorializing Peace Corps Service Act, updates a current law that prohibits the use of the Peace Corps seal, emblem and logo on those commemorative items.

“Volunteering with the Peace Corps is dedicating your life to meaningful service in some of the most difficult corners of our world. It’s an incredibly humbling and inspiring organization to be a part of, and volunteering in the Peace Corps should be honored after someone’s passing,” said Sen. Smith. “We need to change this outdated law so families, like Susan’s, can rightfully honor their loved ones.”

This bill is inspired by the work of Thomas (Tom) W. Stieve, who served in the 1980s as a Peace Corps volunteer in Kiribati (pictured below) and later a Peace Corps–sponsored United Nations volunteer in Vanuatu. During his four years of service, Tom worked on construction projects and built water holding tanks for places that didn’t have clean drinking water.

Tom (pictured below in 2019) developed cancer and passed away in 2023 near his hometown in Michigan at the age of 69. After his passing, Tom’s sister, Susan of St. Paul, MN, wanted to honor her brother’s service by putting the Peace Corps seal on his gravestone. Susan reached out to the Peace Corps to get its blessing for the use of the emblem, but she was told it’s against the law to use that imagery on gravestones or death announcements. Wanting to still honor her brother, Susan reached out to Sen. Smith asking to change the law.

“My brother Tom was diagnosed with incurable cancer in July of 2023. I spent the following months caring for him until he passed away on November 23, 2023. During our last months together, Tom often talked about his Peace Corps service, and we spent time looking at the photos he took in Kiribati and Vanuatu,” said Susan. “Serving in the Peace Corps was the greatest honor of Tom’s life. After he died, I wanted to recognize his service by having the Peace Corp logo inscribed on his gravestone. However, when I reached out to the Peace Corps to seek permission, I learned that memorializing Peace Corps service on a gravestone is prohibited under current law,” Susan continued. “I am deeply grateful to Sen. Smith for introducing legislation that will enable me and other family members of Peace Corps volunteers to honor their legacies of service.”

While Susan was forced to order a gravestone without any commemoration of her brother’s Peace Corps service, she specifically left an open space on his gravestone and written instructions to engrave the Peace Corps logo with Tom’s years of service on the marker, should the law ever change during or after her lifetime.

This bill is co-sponsored by Sen. Mike Rounds (R-SD) and endorsed by the National Peace Corps Association.

“The introduction of Sen. Smith’s Memorializing Peace Corps Service Act is a welcome and timely initiative,” said Carla Brown, President & CEO of the National Peace Corps Association, an alumni organization supporting Returned Peace Corps Volunteers. “The very first Volunteers served in 1961. Volunteers, like Tom Stieve, and the staff who supported them, served our country admirably and are an important part of the American story. We hope this legislation passes with the utmost expediency to give family members, like Susan, a way to honor that service and inspire others to take up the mantle. More than 250,000 Americans have volunteered with the agency during its 65-year history. We look forward to honoring them.”

Photographs of Tom for media use and full text of the bill can be found here.

title: Thune on Congress’ Generational Opportunity to Reform the Permitting Process, Lower Energy Costs
text:
Click here to watch the video.

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) today delivered the following remarks on the Senate floor:

Thune’s remarks below (as delivered):

“Mr. President, in January of 2026, part of a key sewer line serving customers in the Washington, D.C., area collapsed.

“The resulting sewage spill was, the Washington Post reported, and I quote, ‘one of the largest spills of untreated wastewater in U.S. history. Enough raw sewage to fill 364 Olympic-size swimming pools flushed into the Potomac River north of the nation’s capital, exacting an ecological toll that scientists are still trying to calculate.’

“Why do I bring this up, Mr. President?

“Well, I’ll tell you.

“Because D.C. Water had first identified weaknesses in the pipe and proposed repairs a full seven years earlier – seven years earlier – but had been prevented from starting them by a federal permitting process that dragged on. And on. And on. Until the pipe suffered a catastrophic failure.

“It’s an excellent illustration of the need for permitting reform in this country.

“Too often, everything from critical repairs to important new energy projects get bogged down in federal bureaucracy, and are delayed for not months, but years at a time.

“And the Washington, D.C., sewage spill is an outstanding example of the potential consequences.

“Now, Mr. President, it’s important to ensure that serious environmental concerns are addressed before projects are undertaken.

“And it is essential to ensure that the concerns of local stakeholders – in particular local landowners – are listened to and that they have a voice in the approval process.

“But the federal permitting process has gone way beyond that to include years of senseless delays, often caused by endless litigation from environmental groups or from agencies who are set on studying a project literally to death.

“We’ve seen those delays happen to projects for everything from drinking water and irrigation to building affordable energy sources and better roads and bridges.

“And like in the case of the D.C. sewage spill, these delays can even apply to projects where we’re simply replacing something that’s been there for many years.

“These delays all add costs, and those costs are ultimately paid by families through things like higher energy costs, higher gas and diesel prices, and higher taxes.

“The legislation that we are considering today would address that.

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act would streamline and reform the permitting process to ensure that projects are approved or rejected in a timely fashion.

“This is particularly good news on the energy front.

“Needless to say, Americans have been dealing with an elevated cost-of-living since the early days of the Biden administration.

“And when it comes to affordability, energy prices affect pretty much everything. We all know that.

“High energy costs don’t just mean higher gas and electric bills, they mean higher costs for almost everything.

“And one of the best ways to keep prices of all kinds down is to expand domestic energy production – everything from oil and gas to solar and wind to hydropower.

“Too often, however, as I said, new energy projects get bogged down in federal government bureaucracy and end up in limbo for years.

“Streamlining bureaucracy, by contrast, like the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will do, will speed up key projects and bring more jobs and more affordable prices along with it.

“Mr. President, we’ve talked about what this bill would do for energy projects.

“But there’s another kind of project on a lot of Americans’ minds right now – and that is data center construction.

“Communities in my state of South Dakota and around our country are concerned about the movement of data centers into their communities – in particular about what their construction can mean for energy prices.

“And I am pleased to report that the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act would enact new protections for local communities.

“For starters, it would require that data centers shoulder the energy costs associated with their operation and construction – whether that’s day-to-day running costs or the cost of additional infrastructure.

“But Mr. President, the legislation doesn’t stop there.

“It would also provide technical assistance to communities to help them understand and explore the impact a proposed data center would have on their locality – everything from the economic impact to the energy costs and infrastructure requirements that would be associated with the project.

“Mr. President, there are a number of other good elements in this bill.

“I’m always particularly invested in what legislation can do to help farmers and ranchers – which is the livelihood of our economy in South Dakota.

“And I’m very pleased that this bill will extend Clean Water Act permits for farmers from five to 10 years, significantly reducing the frequency with which farmers have to engage with government bureaucracy through that process.

“This legislation will also provide for faster grazing-related reviews, which will make a real difference to ranchers.

“Mr. President, if there’s one thing Americans across our country said in the election last week, it’s that they are hurting economically.

“This bill is one important way that we can help.

“Reforming the permitting process will help advance the kind of projects that will create new jobs, grow our economy, and increase wages.

“And more American energy development means a more reliable and affordable energy supply for American families.

“I want to thank Chairmen … Shelley Moore Capito and Mike Lee for their tremendous work on this legislation.

“This is a bipartisan bill, and President Trump strongly endorsed this legislation on Truth Social earlier this week.

“Mr. President, I look forward to swift Senate passage.

“And I hope the House will follow suit and get this legislation to the president’s desk in the very near future.”

title: Van Hollen, Bennet, Sanders, Duckworth Release Joint Statement Opposing Spending Package that Funds Trump’s War on Iran

title: Warnock, Ossoff Secure More Than $74 Million in Federal Funding for Railroad Safety, Blocked Crossing Relief Across Georgia
text:
Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff secured more than $74.2 million in federal funding to improve safety and help eliminate blocked rail crossings in Georgia

The funding will support railroad crossing improvements in Powder Springs, Fairburn, Waycross, Henry County, and throughout the state

Senator Reverend Warnock: “As Senator for all Georgians, I’ve made strengthening our rail infrastructure and addressing the safety risks posed by stalled trains a priority.”

Washington, D.C.– Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) and Jon Ossoff (D-GA) secured more than $74.2 million in federal funding to reduce blocked crossings, strengthen rail infrastructure, reduce safety risks, and increase connectivity across Georgia.

The funding was provided by the Federal Railroad Administration as part of its Railroad Crossing Elimination/Crossing Safety (RCE) program, which aims to fund highway-rail or pathway-rail grade crossing improvement projects that focus on improving the safety and mobility of people and goods. As a member of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, Senator Warnock championed the creation of the RCE program in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law. Both Senators Warnock and Ossoff have fought to reduce blocked crossing events and train delays that trap communities across Georgia.

“As Senator for all Georgians, I’ve made strengthening our rail infrastructure and addressing the safety risks posed by stalled trains a priority,” said Senator Reverend Warnock. I’m proud to build on those efforts by securing federal investments that will make railroad crossings safer, reduce costly delays, and better connect communities across Georgia.”

“Blockages at rail crossings are not just an inconvenience, but they can be a matter of life and death,” said Senator Ossoff. “Every day, the bipartisan infrastructure law is upgrading transportation, energy, sewer and water, and broadband internet infrastructure across our great state.”

See a full breakdown of the funding below:

Senator Warnock has long championed railroad crossing safety improvements across Georgia. In 2021, Senator Warnock, alongside former Senator Mike Braun (R-IN), introduced the Railway Upgrades for Rural American Lines (RURAL) Act to help states modernize unsafe or functionally outdated railroad warning devices. The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law championed by Senators Warnock and Ossoff, included core components of the RURAL Act.

In 2023, Senator Warnock secured the passage of two critical provisions to address stalled trains trapping Atlanta residents in their neighborhood as part of the Railway Safety Act of 2023. Last month, Senators Warnock and Ossoff secured more than $12 million to improve rail safety across Southwest Georgia, including improving 40 railroad crossings, installing measures to prevent trespassing, and improving safety and reliability.

title: Welch and Britt Celebrate Senate’s Unanimous Passage of Bipartisan Bill to Boost Flood Resiliency and Hydrology Research
text:
Bill would make permanent the hydrology research center at UVM

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Peter Welch (D-Vt.) and Katie Britt (R-Ala.) today celebrated the Senate’s unanimous passage of their bipartisan Water Research Optimization Act, legislation to streamline hydrological forecast modeling within the National Weather Service (NWS). The Senators’ legislation would place America’s 13 River Forecast Centers under the supervision and oversight of the Office of Water Protection and solidify existing hydrology work conducted through the Cooperative Institute for Research to Operations in Hydrology (CIROH), the United States’ first-ever center for water forecast operations.

Water-related disasters pose one of the most persistent and costly threats to communities across the United States. Flooding causes as much as $496 billion in losses each year, underscoring the urgent need to strengthen the nation’s resilience to these threats. Devastating flooding in Vermont in 2023 alone left $2.2 billion in damages. By integrating each of the centers’ forecasting operations under one hub, the Water Research Optimization Act promotes a unified approach to flood forecasting and mitigates information silos that impede severe weather warning capabilities.

The Senators’ legislation advanced out of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation with unanimous support in May 2025. It now heads to the House of Representatives for consideration.

“Investing in hydrology modeling and prediction is crucial to boosting flood resilience across the country, from Vermont to Alabama. That includes supporting important hydrology research and programs at the University of Vermont that improve hydrologic forecasting, such as the Cooperative Institute for Research to Operations in Hydrology,” said Senator Welch. “I’m grateful for the support of our Senate colleagues for advancing our bipartisan bill which will strengthen and align current hydrology research at the National Weather Service with vital research at UVM to foster flood resilience and help communities rebuild better after natural disasters. I urge my colleagues in the House to support this bill and send it to the president’s desk.”

“The National Water Center at the University of Alabama is leading the nation in water forecasting, and the work being done in Tuscaloosa helps communities across America prepare for floods, droughts, and severe weather,” said Senator Britt. “I’m grateful to my colleagues for unanimously passing this commonsense, bipartisan legislation and to Senator Welch for his partnership. I urge the House to take up this bill without delay so we can get it signed into law.”

“We are grateful to Senators Welch and Britt for their leadership in introducing pivotal legislation to support CIROH. Funding for these efforts allows the University of Vermont to continue vital research on water that impacts the quality of life of Vermonters and communities across the country. We are proud to be able to contribute to this work,” said Kirk Dombrowski, Vice President for Research and Economic Development, University of Vermont.

CIROH has evolved into a revolutionary, collaborative hub between the public and private sector for research and development. The Water Research Optimization Act would make CIROH’s research center at the University of Vermont (UVM) permanent and align UVM’s hydrology work with the National Weather Service to boost flood resiliency research.

CIROH’s national coalition of academic, industry, and non-profit partners includes the University of Vermont, which functions closely alongside the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) National Water Center to support stakeholders with hydrological data and important weather-related forecasts and warnings. This legislation would place CIROH Centers under the supervision and oversight of the National Weather Service’s Office of Water Protection and codify the National Water Center’s authority to lead the transition of water resources research.

title: Whitehouse, Wyden, Ossoff Demand Big Health Insurance CEOs Deliver on Promises to Reduce Patient Care Delays
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Ron Wyden (D-OR), and Jon Ossoff (D-GA) sent letters to six major health insurance CEOs demanding evidence that they are following through on their commitments to reduce prior authorization barriers and prevent delays in necessary medical care. The Senators’ action follows an election in which the American people made clear that they want Congress to make health care more affordable and accessible.

Prior authorization is a process by which health insurers require patients and health care providers to obtain approval before certain medical treatments, procedures, tests, or prescription drugs will be covered. These requirements often apply to care recommended by a patient’s own doctor, allowing insurance companies to delay or deny access to medically necessary treatment.

In June 2025, the six insurers joined the Trump administration in announcing a voluntary pledge to reform prior authorizations across commercial, Medicare Advantage, and Medicaid managed care plans. Since then, insurers have touted their progress but provided limited details about the changes they have actually implemented. Their lack of transparency raises serious questions about whether these voluntary commitments are translating into meaningful reforms that reduce barriers and ensure patients receive timely, medically necessary care.

“Patients and physicians share skepticism that insurers participating in this pledge will uphold their promises. Only 39 percent of patients believe insurers will follow through on changes that would make a meaningful difference for them, and just one-third of physicians expressed confidence in the pledge. One year later, we call on you to translate these flashy statistics into meaningful difference that protects patients from abusive delays and denials of care,” wrote the Senators.

The new letters, sent to CEOs of UnitedHealthcare, Aetna, Cigna, Elevance Health, Blue Cross Blue Shield, and Humana, request documentation detailing which services have been removed from prior authorization requirements, how any changes have been communicated to patients and providers, and what plans are in place to implement remaining commitments that are not yet underway. The Senators also requested information on the cost savings insurers expect from these reforms and how those savings will be reflected in patients’ premiums and benefits.

“Aggregate statistics and press releases are not transparency,” the Senators continued. “Patients and providers cannot afford broken promises and inaction.”

Prior authorization remains a crushing administrative burden that delays treatment and drives up overhead costs. Today, 95 percent of physicians report that prior authorization delays necessary medical care, and 92 percent say those delays negatively affect clinical outcomes. On average, physicians and their staff spend 13 hours of physician and staff time each week navigating prior authorization requirements. The consequences extend well beyond the physician’s office: nearly 80 percent of physicians report that patients abandon recommended treatment because of prior authorization barriers.

The Senators requested responses to their inquiries and all relevant documentation from the companies by December 4.

Whitehouse has long championed the fight to end health care bureaucracy and cut red tape to make it faster, easier, and cheaper to deliver high-quality health care. In February, Whitehouse reintroduced his Prior Authorization Relief Act, legislation that would cut the administrative burdens associated with prior authorizations so that patients can get necessary care faster.

title: Merkley, Wyden, Bynum Lead Congressional Resolutions Honoring Silver Rail Elementary School and Bend Community
text:

I’ll never stop working to do that by reducing the risks of similar assaults, supporting investments in youth mental health and passing common-sense gun legislation.”

“It’s been almost a month since we lost our babies in the Silver Rail Elementary School Shooting in Bend. I am with you, and I know we can’t keep saying goodbye to our children like this. I promise to continue fighting to protect all of America’s children.”

title: Ansari and 17 Other U.S. Lawmakers Arrive at COP 31 to Signal America’s Return to Sensible Climate Policy
text:
ANTALYA, TÜRKIYE — Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) and a delegation of 17 other Members of the U.S. House of Representatives led by the Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition Institute (SEEC Institute) has arrived in Antalya for the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31).

“American voters just went to the polls to demand a Congress that helps families get ahead and takes climate change seriously,” said Max Frankel, Executive Director of SEEC Institute. “That’s a mandate, and our Thriving Economy Project offers a blueprint for meeting it. We’re bringing 18 Members of Congress to COP31 ready to get to work, because the challenges we face don’t stop at our borders.”

From November 14–16, the delegation will meet with international policymakers, civil society organizations, advocates and activists, community and business leaders, and experts to strengthen partnerships and explore opportunities for renewed U.S. engagement on climate, energy, and economic policy.

SEEC Institute arrives with a policy blueprint for action at home already in place. Released in September with chapters authored by 9 Members of Congress alongside policy experts, the Thriving Economy Project outlines more than 800 policy recommendations grounded in the belief that a healthy economy and environment go hand in hand. At COP31, Members of Congress will build on that work.

The delegation's programming is organized around eight issue areas:

Food Security, Agricultural Innovation, and Trade

Clean Electrification, Climate Finance, and Private-Sector Competitiveness

Oceans, Science, and Coastal Resilience

Adaptation, Disaster Resilience, and Community Preparedness

Forests, Nature, and Natural-Capital Resilience

Transatlantic Industrial, Trade, and Energy Policy

Climate Equity, Mobility, and Community Leadership

Climate, Energy, and National Security

title: Congressman Bell Issues Statement on Northern Village Tenants Union, Urges In-Person Meeting with Management
text:
Congressman Bell joins the St. Louis County Executive and County Council in urging an in-person meeting with building management

Bell and his office have been closely monitoring the Northern Village situation since tenants first raised concerns about conditions in their units

St. Louis, Missouri – Today, U.S. Congressman Wesley Bell (D-MO-01) issued the following statement on the ongoing health and safety concerns at Northern Village and called for a meeting between tenants and property management.

The Northern Village Tenants Union is the first official tenants union in St. Louis County history. Formed by residents who came together over unsafe and unsatisfactory living conditions, it represents a new way for tenants across the region to make their voices heard.

“Last week, I had the opportunity to meet with the Northern Village Tenants Union. During the meeting, many of the tenants reported unsatisfactory and unsafe conditions in their units. I am deeply troubled by their accounts. The health and safety of the tenants, who are my constituents, is my priority.

During our meeting, the union presented me with a list of urgent requests. First and foremost was a request to meet with property ownership in person.

Today, I am publicly joining the St. Louis County Executive and County Council in urging representatives of this management company to travel to St. Louis to meet with the Northern Village Tenants Union. I am committed to helping mediate an agreement that resolves this ongoing health and safety crisis.

I am proud to stand with the first-ever tenants union in St. Louis County history. Collective bargaining is a foundational pillar of democracy and self-governance, and I applaud my constituents in their fight for change.

In the meantime, my office will continue to work with our community partners and St. Louis County to ensure tenants can secure safe and adequate temporary housing.”

title: Congresswoman Bice Votes for Major Richard Star Act
text:
Washington D.C. – This week, Congresswoman Stephanie Bice voted in support of the Major Richard Star Act, legislation she is an original cosponsor of. This bill allows a veteran with a combat-related disability to receive retirement pay, without reduction, concurrently with their disability compensation.

Congresswoman Bice issued the following statement:

“During the week of Veteran’s Day, I was honored to vote in favor of the Major Richard Star Act. This bill is a matter of fairness, which allows 54,000 veterans access to both their full military retirement pay and compensation for disabilities. Our veterans have sacrificed so much to defend our nation, and we have a responsibility to ensure they receive the care and benefits they have earned.”

title: Congressman Bishop Votes to End Penalty on Combat-Wounded Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON – Yesterday, Congressman Sanford D. Bishop, Jr. (GA-02) voted for the Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102). The bill fixes an unfair rule that cuts the pay of veterans who were wounded in combat. It passed the House, 392 to 18, with strong support from both parties and now goes to the Senate. Congressman Bishop is a senior member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Military Construction and Veterans Affairs.

The problem is simple. Many veterans who serve a full 20-year career receive both their military retirement and their VA disability pay. Receiving both at the same time is known as “concurrent receipt.” But when a servicemember is wounded in combat and forced to medically retire before reaching 20 years, the law cuts their pay. They cannot receive both in full. In effect, they are penalized because they were hurt while serving their country.

The Major Richard Star Act ends that penalty by extending full concurrent receipt to these combat-wounded veterans. They could keep their current arrangement or choose to receive their full retirement pay and their full disability pay, whichever works best for them and their families. About 58,000 veterans would benefit.

“If you were wounded fighting for this country, you should not lose pay because of it,” said Congressman Bishop. “These veterans earned their retirement and they earned their disability compensation. Middle and Southwest Georgia is home to thousands of veterans and military families, and they understand that a promise made should be a promise kept.”

House Republican leaders had kept the bill from getting a vote. Members of both parties, including Congressman Bishop, signed a discharge petition, a rule that lets a majority of the House force a vote, and the House voted on the bill yesterday. Republican leaders had pushed a separate package instead. It included part of the Star Act but paid for it by cutting at least $57 billion in disability compensation for future veterans. Congressman Bishop opposed that approach.

The bill is named for Army Reserve Major Richard Star. He was medically retired after combat service and fought for this change while battling cancer. He died in 2021 at age 51.

title: Budzinski Applauds $63 Million Family Dollar Settlement, Calls for End to Deceptive Pricing Practices
text:
This win follows months of advocacy by Budzinski to demand accountability from the chain

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Nikki Budzinski (IL-13) released the following statement after the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) announced a $63 million settlement with Family Dollar Stores over deceptive pricing practices, marking a significant win for consumers. The settlement follows months of advocacy from Budzinski, who has pressed federal regulators to hold retailers accountable for overcharging customers.

“Today is a win for consumers. When reports surfaced that Family Dollar was misleading customers through deceptive pricing practices, I immediately got to work demanding answers and accountability,” said Budzinski. “I’m pleased to see the FTC take action and secure a $63 million settlement that sends a clear message: retailers cannot mislead customers or charge them more than the prices advertised. But accountability cannot stop here. Family Dollar and other retailers engaging in misconduct must put an end to these practices, and consumers deserve to know they can trust the prices they see on store shelves.”

In December 2025, Budzinski led 29 of her colleagues in a letter to the CEOs of Family Dollar and Dollar General demanding answers about deceptive pricing practices that have misled consumers. Following sustained pressure from Budzinski and other lawmakers, the FTC, alongside 20 states, filed a lawsuit against Dollar General for similar deceptive pricing allegations. Last month, Budzinski also led 33 of her colleagues in a separate letter urging the FTC to investigate reports of widespread overcharging by additional retailers. The letter, which called for greater accountability and price transparency for consumers, was first reported exclusively by The Guardian.
