title: Malliotakis Introduces Legislation to Help American Film & Television Production
text:
(WASHINGTON, DC) — Today, Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) introduced H.R. 11033, the Made in America Film and Television Act, legislation to support film and television production in the United States by expanding a federal tax incentive for domestic production facilities and encouraging greater investment in the American entertainment industry.

The legislation builds on a provision in the One Big Beautiful Bill that allows businesses in industries such as manufacturing, agriculture, and chemical production to immediately deduct the full qualifying cost of certain domestic production facilities. Malliotakis' bill would extend this incentive to qualifying film and television facilities, including soundstages, backlots and production studios, helping reduce investment costs and support American jobs.

“From Ray Donovan and Gotham to Boardwalk Empire, Blue Bloods and Fallout, Staten Island and Brooklyn have served as filming locations for major television productions, creating jobs and generating economic activity for our community,” said Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis. “My legislation would help make it more attractive to invest in American film and television production, support the hardworking people behind the scenes and encourage more productions to take place right here at home.”

Malliotakis also co-leads the bipartisan CREATE Act with Congresswoman Judy Chu (CA-28), which would extend and strengthen Section 181, a federal tax incentive that helps lower the cost of producing movies and television shows in the United States. Together, the two bills seek to encourage domestic investment, support American film and television production, and protect jobs in the entertainment industry.

title: MATSUI, CASTOR, OBERNOLTE INTRODUCE BIPARTISAN BILL TO LOWER ELECTRIC BILLS AND STRENGTHEN GRID RELIABILITY
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representatives Doris Matsui (CA-07), Kathy Castor (FL-14), and Jay Obernolte (CA-23) introduced the Optimizing Networks for Distributed Energy Management and New Demand (ON-DEMAND) Act to help lower electric bills and meet growing energy demand. The legislation supports wider adoption of virtual power plants by directing the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to adopt standards, strengthen consumer protections and provide technical assistance to utilities, regulators and grid operators.

“Families in Sacramento and across the country are paying too much for electricity, and we need to do more to bring those costs down,” said Congresswoman Matsui. “The ON-DEMAND Act will help lower utility bills by making smarter use of the energy resources we already have, including home batteries and smart appliances, to meet growing electricity demand without driving up costs. This is a practical solution that puts money back in Americans’ pockets while building a cleaner, more reliable energy grid.”

“My neighbors need relief from sky-high electric bills, and we should be putting every practical solution to work to lower their costs,” said Congresswoman Castor. “Our ON-DEMAND Act would help communities use rooftop solar, batteries, and smart appliances more safely and effectively, with strong protections for consumers. As demand for electricity grows, we must make our grid more reliable and ensure the benefits of innovation reach the people paying the bills.”

“As electricity demand continues to grow, innovative solutions like virtual power plants can help strengthen our electric grid and lower energy costs for American families,” said Congressman Obernolte. “The ON-DEMAND Act will help remove barriers to the adoption of this technology, allowing consumers to make better use of existing energy resources while improving grid reliability and reducing costs.”

Virtual power plants coordinate devices across homes and businesses, such as batteries, smart thermostats, water heaters and rooftop solar systems, to help balance electricity supply and demand. For example, water heating could be shifted to a less busy time or battery power can be deployed during peak demand.

View the full bill text HERE and section-by-section HERE.

“Amid an unprecedented rise in energy demand, some of the most promising solutions are the distributed resources already in our homes and communities — rooftop solar, smart thermostats, and EV chargers — and the Virtual Power Plants (VPPs) that help them work together. From lowering bills for families to keeping the lights on, VPPs support a more flexible, affordable, and resilient electric grid. Advanced Energy United is proud to support the ON-DEMAND Act. We applaud the work of Representatives Castor, Matsui, and Obernolte to bring this bill to fruition and believe it will help unlock the benefits of VPPs for all Americans." – Dylan Reed, Managing Director at Advanced Energy United.

“Energy security and economic growth depend on a resilient and efficient electric power system. Virtual power plants provide a proven, scalable way to deliver reliable, affordable power amid growing grid constraints,” said NEMA Senior Vice President of Government Affairs, Will Hupman. “By directing the Department of Energy to pursue open, stakeholder-driven processes for VPP standards development and other objectives, the ON-DEMAND Act promises to eliminate hurdles to VPP deployment and scaling, ushering in a new era of grid flexibility.”

“The ON-DEMAND Act represents an important step toward modernizing America's electric grid and ensuring we can meet growing electricity demand affordably and reliably,” said John Pappas, Government Affairs Director for Siemens USA. “By addressing barriers to the deployment of virtual power plants, this legislation will help utilities unlock the full potential of distributed energy resources, improve grid flexibility, and make more efficient use of existing infrastructure. Establishing consistent standards and expanding technical assistance will help accelerate the adoption of innovative grid technologies and build a smarter, more resilient, and more affordable energy system.”

"Leveraging customer-focused energy independent solutions like distributed power plants is essential to creating a more cost-effective, resilient and clean grid for all, particularly amidst the surging demand for electricity. The ON-DEMAND Act will help accelerate the customer-led revolution that's tackling these challenges head-on." – Mary Powell, CEO, Sunrun

"Schneider Electric applauds the introduction of the ON-DEMAND Act and its support for the flexible energy resources needed to build a more resilient, reliable, and affordable grid. As electricity demand grows, flexibility will be essential to balancing supply and demand, improving grid performance, and empowering consumers. Virtual power plants are one important way to unlock that flexibility at scale, and we welcome policies that help accelerate their adoption." – Ruben Llanes, CEO, Digital Grid, Schneider Electric

"Virtual power plants are important tools to add flexibility to the grid at a time of significant load growth," said Arnab Pal, executive director of Deploy Action. “We commend Reps. Castor, Matsui, and Obernolte for their bipartisan leadership to knock down barriers to virtual power plant deployment. This legislation will ensure states and regulators can more readily deploy technologies that we know lower costs for all Americans and contribute to grid flexibility."

Endorsing organizations include Advanced Energy United, Deploy Action, Electricity Consumers Resource Council, Environmental Defense Fund, GridWise Alliance, Information Technology Industry Council, National Association of State Energy Officials, National Electrical Manufacturers Association, Rewiring America, Schneider Electric, Siemens USA, Sierra Club, and Sunrun.

title: Statement from Congresswoman Analilia Mejia on Trump Administration Threats Targeting Congressional Oversight
text:
For Immediate Release: November 13, 2026

Contact: Beth Wiesinger | NJ11AMPress@Mail.House.Gov

The Trump administration has threatened Members of Congress with potential criminal investigations for exercising our constitutional authority to investigate the administration. In a threatening letter sent to Congressional Democrats, the White House singled out members, including myself, for doing our job to hold this administration accountable

Let me be clear: I will not back down. Congressional oversight is not a crime. It is our constitutional duty.

Congress is a coequal branch of government. We did not swear an oath of loyalty to Donald Trump. We swore an oath to uphold and defend the Constitution, and I intend to do so with every lever available.

No president gets to decide which congressional investigations are permitted. The White House cannot use threats of criminal prosecution to obstruct legitimate oversight or intimidate members of Congress into abandoning their responsibilities.

Corruption and government accountability are top priorities for voters, and they are a top priority for me. People deserve to know how their tax dollars are being spent, who is benefiting from decisions made in Washington, and whether those in power are abusing their positions.

I will use every tool at my disposal to investigate abuses of power, examine how taxpayer dollars are spent, and hold this administration accountable.

Being singled out by name will not deter me. I will not be intimidated or discouraged from fulfilling my constitutional responsibilities.

title: Dr. Mike Kennedy Unanimously Elected Co-Chair of GOP Doctors Caucus
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. – Members of the GOP Doctors Caucus elected Dr. Mike Kennedy (UT) to serve as the next co-chair in the 120th Congress, alongside Dr. John Joyce, during its weekly meeting. Dr. Kennedy was elected by unanimous consent.

“First, I’d like to extend my sincere appreciation to my good friend Dr. Greg Murphy for his leadership, dedication, and influence in shaping this caucus’s legacy,” said Congressman John Joyce, M.D. “It has been an absolute honor and privilege to serve as co-chair alongside him for the past two years. In the 120th Congress, I’m pleased to welcome Dr. Mike Kennedy to serve alongside me as the next co-chair. Dr. Kennedy has been a loyal and active member of this caucus, and I have full confidence in his ability to step into this role with fresh insights and new ideas. His background and expertise as a dedicated family doctor will be invaluable as we continue our fight on behalf of America’s patients.”

“I am grateful to my colleagues for unanimously electing me to co-chair the GOP Doctors Caucus,” said Congressman Mike Kennedy, M.D. “Fighting for pro-patient, lower cost, common-sense healthcare policy is a top priority for me, both as a physician and a lawmaker. As co-chair, I will work alongside these seasoned healthcare professionals to elevate the influence of the Doc Caucus and give our members the meaningful voice and seat at the table they deserve in shaping health care policy.”

“I congratulate Congressman Mike Kennedy on his unanimous election as the next co-chair of the GOP Doctors Caucus,” said Congressman Greg Murphy, M.D. “It has been a privilege to serve as co-chair of this influential caucus and work alongside my colleagues to advance patient-centered health care policies. As a fellow physician, I know Mike shares a commitment to putting patients first, lowering health care costs, and ensuring physicians have a meaningful voice in shaping our nation's health care system. I wish him all the best in this new role.”

Background on the GOP Doctors Caucus

Established in 2009, the GOP Doctors Caucus is composed of Republican members of Congress with medical and health care provider backgrounds dedicated to patient-centered health care policy. The caucus serves as a strong voice for patients and physicians and provides meaningful guidance to congressional Republican leadership. It is committed to improving the quality, access and affordability of health care for all Americans.

title: Congresswoman Nikema Williams: I was arrested for speaking up in Georgia. Today, I’m holding my head high.
text:
On November 13, 2018, I was led out of the Georgia Capitol, hands zip tied behind my back for demanding that every vote be counted for my friend and democracy warrior, Stacey Abrams.

I now get to walk back through those doors with my head held high to work with our next governor, Keisha Lance Bottoms. Read more about the journey since that day in my latest op-ed in the AJC.

As published in the Atlanta Journal Constitution:

Eight years ago, I was put in handcuffs and taken out of the Georgia Capitol for standing with my constituents on Nov. 13, 2018.

Before I became the congresswoman for Georgia’s “Fighting Fifth” congressional district, I served as a Georgia state senator representing the 39th District, which included Atlanta, College Park, East Point, South Fulton and Union City.

I showed up that morning to do my job as the “people’s state senator.” The Senate had adjourned, and as I was waiting for the House to convene I noticed a large police presence gathering.

I heard glass break and a commotion on the floor below me in the rotunda, so I went downstairs. I was immediately greeted by people who had been part of the protest. They told me, “They just threw an older lady to the ground, and they’re arresting people.”

The protesters were exercising their First Amendment constitutional rights. Amid mounting concerns of voter suppression, they were demanding that every vote be counted in the still-undecided governor’s race between my friend and colleague Stacey Abrams and then-Secretary of State Brian Kemp.

I went downstairs to make sure my constituents were safe and their voices were heard. I saw one of my constituents standing among the crowd, I stood beside her. I wanted her to know that she was not alone. That she was seen, heard and supported.

Moments later, officers pushed my arm behind my back, placed me in zip-tie restraints and arrested me. Despite knowing I was a state senator there to do the business of the state during the special session, they took me out of the Capitol with my hands zip tied behind my back and transported me to the Fulton County Jail. I was held for hours without even knowing why I was being detained.

While sitting alongside the group with whom I was arrested, we finally learned that everyone there, including me, had received a charge of disrupting the General Assembly. But apparently, I was special, and someone wanted to make a point with me. I received two charges: disrupting the General Assembly and obstruction.

As I was arrested, escorted out of the Capitol, hands behind my back and transported to the Fulton County Jail, I kept thinking about my mentor and friend, the legendary Congressman John Lewis.

He taught us what it meant to make “good trouble, necessary trouble.” I didn’t know it then, but three years later, I would follow in his footsteps and carry his legacy in the very halls of Congress.

That day in the Capitol didn’t end my fight for voting rights. In fact, it strengthened my resolve.

Since my election to Congress, I’ve made protecting the right to vote and ensuring every eligible voter has access to the ballot a priority in my work.

I’ve introduced one of the most comprehensive voting rights legislative packages in congressional history. The package has broad bicameral support, with multiple senators introducing companion bills.

Legislation included in the package would fully fund election administration around the country, reduce long lines that deter people from voting, guarantee workers time off to vote, improve how election mail is delivered and processed, make voting more accessible for people experiencing homelessness, provide election materials in more languages, and help people understand how to register and protect their voting rights when they move.

I’ve also joined another mentor and predecessor in the “Fighting Fifth,” Ambassador Andrew Young, in calling for our state’s district lines not to be redrawn in the aftermath of the U.S. Supreme Court’s Louisiana v. Callais decision.

When President Donald Trump threatened to send U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to the polls, I introduced a congressional resolution to reinforce the ban on federal agents at polling places. And I was at the Fulton County Elections Office after the FBI raided it, demanding answers and accountability.

Over the last two years, I have reminded people, “This is our Civil Rights Movement.” If you’ve ever wondered what you would have done during the Civil Rights Movement, this was your time to find out. If you care about labor rights, climate justice, the economy, immigration or reproductive freedom, you care about voting rights. Our ability to make our voices heard at the ballot box is connected to every issue that affects our lives.

On Nov. 3, Georgia voters showed us exactly what they would have done during the Civil Rights Movement and made their voices heard in a historic way. We elected Keisha Lance Bottoms as the first Black female governor in our nation’s history.

It was the culmination of so much work during our lifetimes — and the lifetimes of those who came before us. I think about Stacey Abrams. I think about the groups that have organized for decades in Georgia. I think about watching former state lawmaker and Atlanta city official Rashad Taylor as a fellow young Democrat, not knowing that one day he’d lead the campaign for the first Black woman governor of our state and country.

When I first ran for the Georgia state Senate, a well-meaning supporter told me to put “Nikke” on my campaign signs. They thought I’d get more votes if people couldn’t tell from my name that I was a Black woman. I ran as Nikema.

Years later, my son, Carter, witnessed Georgia elect Keisha Lance Bottoms, a Black woman who went to Ralph J. Bunche Middle School, the same school he attends. I want Carter and his classmates to know they can put their own names on a campaign sign someday and ask the people of Georgia to trust them to lead. That’s part of what made the words I heard on election night mean so much to me — Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms.

On election night, as I gathered with family, friends and staff, someone in the room exclaimed, “My governor’s name is Keisha, my congresswoman is Nikema and my mayor is Dre!”

Eight years ago, I was led out of the Georgia Capitol, hands zip tied behind my back for demanding that every vote be counted for my friend and democracy warrior, Stacey Abrams. I now get to walk back through those doors with my head held high to work with our next governor, Keisha Lance Bottoms.

I think about the Georgians who stood with me that day and the voters who made this moment possible. I’ll carry them with me every time I walk into the Gold Dome and the U.S. Capitol. I’m ready to work alongside our new governor to protect their right to vote and deliver for the people of Georgia’s “Fighting Fifth.”

title: DEMOCRATIC VETERANS CAUCUS CHAIRS RYAN, DELUZIO, AND LIEU CELEBRATE HOUSE PASSAGE OF THE MAJOR RICHARD STAR ACT
text:
The Major Richard Star Act eliminates the “Wounded Veteran Tax,” under which combat-wounded veterans lose $1 in retirement benefits for every $1 they receive in VA disability benefits

The bill lets combat-wounded, medically retired veterans receive their full military retirement pay and VA disability benefits without one reducing the other

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, the co-chairs of the Democratic Veterans Caucus, Congressmen Pat Ryan (NY, Army), Chris Deluzio (PA, Navy), and Ted Lieu (CA, Air Force), released the following statement celebrating yesterday’s House passage of the Major Richard Star Act:

“When American heroes wounded in service to this country come home, the last thing they should have to worry about is being able to afford their care. That’s why we’ve been fighting tooth and nail for months to advance this legislation, and why we’re so proud to see it pass the House today.

“The Major Richard Star Act is the largest expansion to veterans benefits in years. It rights one of the most egregious wrongs in this country – that retirement pay should be reduced just because a veteran receives disability benefits. It’s straight up un-American. This bill ensures that wounded veterans receive both their full retirement pay and disability benefits – because that’s what they’ve earned. End of story. Especially as the war in Iran rages on – and with 800+ U.S. servicemembers already wounded, some with life-long injuries – it’s more important now than ever that we pass this bill and guarantee to every veteran that we’ve got their back.

“We urge our Senate colleagues – especially our fellow veterans – to move swiftly and Patriotically to immediately pass this lifesaving legislation.”

The Major Richard Star Act would address long standing inequities in military retirement pay for veterans who were forced to medically retire due to combat-related injuries. This bill will:

Ensurethat combat-disabled veterans, and especially those who were catastrophically injured while serving, receive the retirement pay and disability benefits that they deserve;

And invest $12 billion in our nation's veterans to guarantee that they have the resources they need to live with dignity and thrive.

Chaired by Congressman Ryan, an Army veteran; Congressman Chris Deluzio, a Navy veteran; and Congressman Ted Lieu, an Air Force veteran, the Democratic Veterans Caucus is composed of Members from across the country and from all branches of service.

title: AS HUDSON VALLEY FAMILIES FACE HEALTH CARE CUTS AND RISING PRICES, CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN CONTINUES DELIVERING DIRECT ASSISTANCE AND RELIEF WITH NOVEMBER C.A.R.E.S. VAN EVENTS
text:
With the C.A.R.E.S. Van, Ryan and his team deliver one-on-one assistance navigating federal programs and accessing benefits including Social Security, Medicaid, and Medicare directly to constituents in their own community

Ryan’s team has visited every community in NY-18 with the Van and secured over $40 million in casework assistance for NY-18 constituents

KINGSTON, NY – Today, Congressman Pat Ryan announced the schedule of November events for his mobile office, the Constituent Advocacy Resources Empowerment Services (C.A.R.E.S.) Van, across the Hudson Valley. Congressman Ryan’s C.A.R.E.S. Van, staffed by his team of highly-trained caseworkers, will bring direct assistance with federal agencies like the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and IRS to Hudson Valley families right in their own community. Ryan’s C.A.R.E.S. Van team will continue to be all hands on deck to aid constituents hurt by the nonstop cuts to critical federal programs, closures, and uncertainty – in particular regarding health care.

“I’ve heard the heartwrenching stories from countless Hudson Valley families who can no longer afford health care coverage or aren’t sure how they’re going to put food on the table. My team and I are leaving no stone unturned to make sure they get every bit of relief they can,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “Whether you are worried about finding new health care coverage, need help tracking down a long overdue tax return, or have questions about receiving your federal benefits, my team is all-hands-on-deck to help however we can in every corner of the Hudson Valley.”

Congressman Ryan’s C.A.R.E.S. Van assists constituents of NY-18 in accessing earned benefits, such as Veterans’ Affairs benefits and Social Security, federal grant funding, passports and visas, immigration and naturalization services, and resolving issues with federal agencies, such as the Internal Revenue Service.

“For months and months, I heard absolutely nothing back from the VA and was getting so frustrated. When I saw the Congressman's C.A.R.E.S. Van flyer, I was so excited,” said Helen Adams of Wallkill. “Within just a few weeks, I got a letter in the mail back telling me that I was approved for benefits! I can breathe easier now knowing that I will finally be getting the VA benefits I am entitled to. Thank you to Congressman Ryan for caring about seniors like me and having a team who can help us navigate the agencies that we depend on to be able to survive.”

“Congressman Ryan’s team was extremely polite, professional, and emphatic towards my situation as a disabled veteran,” said Middletown veteran Nicholas White. “They contacted me to inform me of everything and what they could do to assist. I was granted 100% P&T disability compensation. My wife and I couldn't be happier. Thank you!”

“We are so grateful for the excellent assistance we received from Congressman Ryan’s office,” said David Friedman of New Paltz. “For two years we have been trying to resolve a problem with the IRS, and because of the intervention of his office, the issue has been properly resolved, and we actually received interest on an amount due from the IRS! It took something special to get this matter looked at and Congressman Ryan’s office provided that!”

“My 2022 tax return was held up by the IRS for nine months,” said Robert Warhola of Kingston. “I had plans for my refund. The case worker assured me this problem could be resolved in two weeks. As promised, I received my refund electronically. It is nice to see our government working efficiently.”

“Thanks to Congressman Ryan’s office, the IRS finally issued refunds this spring for 2 returns I filed back in 2021,” said Stacy Quinn of Rhinebeck. “ After a very frustrating year of follow up – including an appointment at the IRS regional office in Poughkeepsie, multiple IRS assurances that I would hear back but never did, and a request for help from a senator’s office that was ignored – I was about to lose hope. Congressman Ryan’s office responded immediately, however, provided frequent updates, and I received the missing refunds in 6 weeks.”

The C.A.R.E.S. Van’s casework team meets and listens to community members and answers and offers assistance with federal programs and benefits including, but not limited to:

Social Security, Veterans Affairs (VA), Medicare, Medicaid, federal student loans, federal grants for local governments, small businesses and organizations, and households, IRS taxes and tax returns, passports, immigration services, military records and awards, the Office of Personnel for federal workers, connecting with Veterans Service Organizations (VSOs) and the military community in the Hudson Valley, U.S. Service Academy nominations, and more!

In March of 2024, the C.A.R.E.S. Van completed its first district tour, visiting every one of the 82 cities, towns, and villages in NY-18 in under 10 months. During the first district tour, the Van reached over 1,500 constituents and logged 3,341 miles to bring assistance directly to Hudson Valley families where they are at. The Van has been critical in assisting Ryan’s team in securing over $40 million in casework assistance for NY-18 constituents.

The C.A.R.E.S. Van has also been mobilized for specialized events, resource fairs, community events, and to deliver emergency response resources including, but not limited to:

Bringing direct assistance from the Social Security Administration back to Ulster County following closure of the county’s only Social Security Administration office.

Partnering with dozens of community organizations, the Social Security Administration, the Center for Medicare, local governments from across the Hudson Valley for Senior Resource Fairs.

Partnering with Veterans Service Organizations, local governments, and the Hudson Valley military community to deliver Veterans and Military Families Resource Fairs and for Congressman Ryan’s Veterans Week of Action that made stops in every county in NY-18.

Mobilizing a coalition of community partners, emergency response organizations, and local governments to bring direct relief to communities impacted by the catastrophic flooding events of July 2023.

Partnering with the New York State Comptroller’s Office of Unclaimed Funds to connect constituents with money owed to them by the State.

Delivering direct assistance with federal agencies to community events including the Dutchess County Senior Picnics, National Night Out in partnership with local law enforcement agencies, community Trunk-or-Treat Halloween celebrations, community farmers’ markets, Kingston’s Mexican and Central American Independence Celebration, Warwick’s Mental Health Awareness Celebration, the Orange County Veterans’ Picnic, and more!

title: Congresswomen Brittany Pettersen, Joyce Beatty, and Lauren Underwood Introduce Legislation to Protect Women from Criminal Prosecution Following Pregnancy Loss
text:
WASHINGTON – Congresswomen Brittany Pettersen (CO-D), Joyce Beatty (OH-D), and Lauren Underwood (IL-D) introduced the Pregnancy Loss Protection Act, legislation to protect women from criminal prosecution following a miscarriage or stillbirth and ensure that no woman is treated as a criminal for experiencing pregnancy loss.

Since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade in 2022, women across the country have faced growing threats of criminal investigation, arrest, and prosecution related to their pregnancy outcomes. These punitive practices disproportionately impact Black women and women of color, creating fear and uncertainty for those seeking medical care.

“Facing a pregnancy loss is one of the most heartbreaking experiences anyone can endure. The idea that some states or local governments can target, investigate, or criminally prosecute women suffering through a miscarriage or stillbirth is absolutely unconscionable. I am proud to co-lead the Pregnancy Loss Protection Act to ensure every woman going through one of the most painful times is protected and not treated like a criminal,” said Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen.

“Mourning mothers are not criminals,” said Congresswoman Joyce Beatty. “In the wake of the Supreme Court’s Dobbs decision, women are increasingly facing the threat of criminal prosecution for pregnancy loss. We saw this injustice unfold in my home state of Ohio when Brittany Watts was treated like a criminal instead of a woman deserving compassion and care. A miscarriage is not a crime, and grief should never be met with handcuffs. The Pregnancy Loss Protection Act makes one thing clear: women deserve dignity, protection, and care—not jail time.”

“Losing a pregnancy is already a painful and heartbreaking experience, and no woman should have to face the additional trauma of a criminal investigation while she recovers and grieves. Shamefully, after Dobbs, that is the reality for millions of families across our country,” said Congresswoman Lauren Underwood. “The United States has the highest maternal mortality rate of any high-income nation. To save mom’s lives, we must make sure that women can seek quality health care without fear. Our bill will protect women, improve health outcomes, and make sure they can get the care that they need.”

Rep. Pettersen has also consistently supported access to reproductive health care. As states across the country have adopted restrictive measures on abortion, reproductive care, and gender affirming care, Rep. Pettersen joined an amicus brief before the Supreme Court to defend access to mifepristone, an abortion pill that is FDA approved. Rep. Pettersen is also an original cosponsor of the Women’s Health Protection Act, which would establish a federal right to abortion care nationwide. During her tenure at the state level, Rep. Pettersen helped pass the Reproductive Health Equity Act, a law that codified the right to an abortion in the state of Colorado.

Full text of the legislation is available HERE.

title: Pfluger Introduces Legislation to Invest in the Future of America's Military Children
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — This week, Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11) introduced the Trump Accounts for Military Children Act to further invest in the future of America's military children. The legislation would authorize the Secretary of War to pay a bonus of up to $2,500 to a qualifying child's Trump Account, or split it among multiple children, when the child's parent re-enlists or otherwise agrees to extend their service as an officer or enlisted service member.

“Having served in the Air Force for more than twenty-five years, I know firsthand that our military families sacrifice every day so the rest of us can live in freedom. When a service member chooses to reenlist or extend their service, their family is making that commitment too. The Trump Accounts for Military Children Act is a way to say thank you by investing in the next generation of military children and giving them a head start on their financial future,” said Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11).

Congressman Buddy Carter (GA-01) joined Congressman Pfluger in introducing the Trump Accounts for Military Children Act.

“When Republicans passed the Trump Accounts, we kept our promise to invest in the future and success of the next generation. I’m proud to support the Trump Accounts for Military Children Act, which builds on that commitment by creating new opportunities for military families to invest in their child’s financial future,” said Congressman Buddy Carter (GA-01). “The brave men and women of our Armed Forces sacrifice so much to protect our families, and we owe it to them to look out for theirs.”

Background:

Trump Accounts were created through the Working Families Tax Cut Act as a new tax-advantaged savings account for children, designed to support future education, housing, or other major purchases. The accounts officially launched on July 4, 2026, and children born between January 1, 2025, and December 31, 2028, will receive a one-time $1,000 contribution from the U.S. Department of the Treasury.

title: Pou Statement On FAA Nationwide Ground Stop
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today Congresswoman Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09) released the following statement on the nationwide ground stop across all U.S. airports, issued by the Federal Aviation Administration.

“I do not want to speculate the cause of this crisis right now but this is a massive, almost unprecedented disaster impacting tens of millions of Americans. We are nearing the holidays. The Trump administration must be prompt and forthright in providing answers. More generally, I would note this constitutes yet another crisis in the American skies under the Trump administration. Just this week, the GOP majority cancelled a hearing next week with the head of the FAA. Something must change. The American people are owed transparency, and the incoming Congress must seek a full accounting of how air traffic modernization is being implemented and what remains to be done to keep our airspace safe.”

title: Pressley Calls on Democrats to Meet the Moment
text:
Transcript: On House Floor, Pressley Calls on Democrats to Meet the Moment

November 12, 2026

U.S. House of Representatives

Mr. Speaker, I rise today for every person who dreams of a better tomorrow.

For every person who ran, voted, and organized to deliver a mandate for bold, transformative change, from Massachusetts to Texas to Mississippi.

For those who turned hope into action.

Mr. Speaker, it is so important that we fight for a more just America.

It is what we owe to every person who calls this country home.

A more just America where one job is enough and no one goes bankrupt when they get sick.

A more just America where Black men grow old, Black women birth safely, and children live, learn, and play without fear.

A more just America where people don’t have to choose between rent, medical bills, and groceries.

Some say we’re asking for too much, that we should work with the very Republicans who have used their power to exact harm.

But incrementalism is a recipe for failure.

If we moderate our aspirations, we cost people their lives and livelihoods.

Democrats, we must meet the people’s cries with action.

We cannot let money or special interests dictate our fight.

We are accountable to the people who sent us here. Period.

This is the People’s House, and we must advance the people’s agenda.

And with this supermajority on the way, it’s time we move exactly like that. I yield.

title: Brown Votes for Major Richard Star Act, Legislation to End Wounded Veterans Tax
text:
Washington, DC – This week, the House passed The Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102), legislation to end the clawing back retirement pay from combat-injured veterans. Congresswoman Shontel Brown (OH-11)proudly voted for the legislation, cosponsored the bill, and signed the discharge petition led by House Democrats, which forced a vote on the House floor.

The Major Richard Star Act helps veterans who were hurt in combat and had to leave the military early. Currently, these veterans lose one dollar of their military retirement pay for every dollar they get for their injuries. While full-career military retirees are permitted to collect both forms of compensation, this legislation ensures that medically retired veterans receive the same comprehensive financial benefits. The legislation would invest $12 billion in Veteran Affairs services, advance top priorities for veterans, and ensure combat-disabled veterans receive the retirement payment and benefits they deserve.

“I was proud to cosponsor the Major Richard Star Act, fight to bring it to the House floor, and vote to get it across the finish line this week. Our combat-disabled veterans have earned every dollar of their retirement and disability benefits, and they should never have to choose between the two. This is about keeping our promise to those who put their lives on the line for our country. It’s a victory for our veterans, their families, and the values we stand for.” said Congresswoman Shontel Brown

In May of 2026, Congresswoman Shontel Brown joined 213 Democrats and 5 Republicans in signing the discharge petition that allowed the Richard Star Act to come to the House floor.

The bill now heads to the Senate.

title: Congresswoman Lee Votes to Pass Legislation in Support of Combat-Injured Veterans
text:
Image

Link to Video Message

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) voted to pass the Major Richard Star Act, bipartisan legislation to fix the Wounded Warrior Tax, which applies to veterans who were forced to medically retire due to combat-related injuries. These veterans do not currently receive their full military retirement pay or their full disability compensation. Instead, their Department of Defense (DoD) retirement pay is offset – dollar for dollar – by the amount of VA disability pay they receive.

“When veterans pledge their service to the United States, their oath to serve this country doesn’t expire. The promise from the American people to support our veterans shouldn’t either,” said Congresswoman Susie Lee. “This bipartisan bill ensures combat-wounded veterans receive both their disability benefits and full retirement pay. A grateful nation pays its debts to veterans, and I am glad to have voted to pass the Major Richard Star Act to ensure that is the case.”

The House could have already voted on this critically important legislation, but instead of putting it on the floor as a standalone bill, Speaker Mike Johnson combined it into the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act earlier this year, which proposed paying for this legislation by cutting future benefits for other veterans and would have created the largest cut to veterans' benefits in history. Instead, a bipartisan group of members signed a discharge petition to circumvent Republican House leadership and bring this bill to an immediate vote on its own.

What the Major Richard Star Act does:

End the Wounded Warrior Tax, allowing veterans to choose between two paths:

Option 1: They can stay in the Combat-Related Special Compensation (CRSC) program, which provides tax-free payments to retired veterans with service-connected disability caused by combat and disability ratings of at least 30%.

Option 2: They can opt out of the CRSC program to receive their full VA compensation and all their military retirement pay.

This change gives them the autonomy and authority to choose the best path for them.

As southern Nevada’s sole member on the House Appropriations Defense Subcommittee, Congresswoman Lee will continue working to ensure that Nevada’s servicemembers, veterans, and military families receive the benefits, recognition, and support they have earned through their service.

title: Rep. Sykes Announces Federal Grant for Tax Filing Assistance
text:
AKRON, OH – Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS) awarded grants totaling $260,000 to help community members access free tax-filing services. The United Way of Greater Stark County received $160,000 and the United Way of Summit and Medina received $100,000 to run the Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA) and Tax Counseling for the Elderly (TCE) programs.

“Filing taxes can be stressful and expensive, especially for individuals and families already working hard to make ends meet. These grants will help connect more Northeast Ohioans with free, reliable tax preparation services so they can file with confidence. I’m proud to see these investments supporting United Way organizations in our community and helping ensure that cost is not a barrier to accessing important tax services.” said Rep. Sykes.

Nationally, the IRS is awarding 282 VITA grants totaling $46 million and 49 TCE grants totaling $12 million. The VITA program has operated for over 50 years and helps individuals in need file their taxes for free. While the IRS does not set a program-wide income limit, individual VITA sites may establish their own. The program generally focuses on serving individuals who are low income, disabled, or do not speak English.

title: Congressman Taylor Champions Legislation to Codify CDL Fraud Tipline
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Representative Dave Taylor (OH-02) demonstrated his leadership in highway safety through the introduction of his CDL Fraud Tipline Act. This bill would codify the Commercial Driver’s License Fraud Tipline within the Department of Homeland Security. By dialing (866) 347-2423, Americans can report suspected CDL fraud to help prevent unqualified drivers from endangering drivers and causing fatal crashes on the road.

Representatives Harriet Hageman (WY-AL), Jefferson Shreve (IN-06), Mike Bost (IL-12), Pat Harrigan (NC-10), Randy Weber (TX-14), Mary Miller (IL-15), Buddy Carter (GA-01), Beth Van Duyne (TX-24), Eli Crane (AZ-02), and Greg Steube (FL-17) joined Congressman Taylor in introducing this bill.

“American families deserve to know that they’re sharing the road with CDL drivers who are properly trained, vetted, and equipped to operate heavy commercial vehicles in a way that keeps everyone safe,” said Congressman Taylor. “President Trump and the Department of Homeland Security have taken decisive action by launching the CDL Fraud Tipline, and I’m proud to lead the effort to make it permanent to ensure our highways are safe for generations to come.

“Dangerous drivers anywhere threaten families everywhere. While the Trump administration embraces a whole-of-government approach to rid our highways of unqualified drivers, we need all hands on deck to crack down on bad actors. The CDL fraud tipline gives every American an avenue to say something when they see something,” said Congresswoman Hageman.

"Drivers operating with fraudulent CDLs pose a serious threat to public safety, and Republicans recognize that everyday Americans have a critical role in stopping this danger. Congress must make this tipline permanent so citizens can report suspected CDL fraud directly to law enforcement before more innocent lives are lost," said Congresswoman Miller.

"American Truckers United proudly supports Congressman Taylor's bill to codify the Department of Homeland Security's CDL fraud tip line. Fraudulent and unlawfully issued CDLs put unqualified drivers behind the wheel of 80,000-pound trucks and cost American truckers their livelihoods. The drivers and small carriers on the road every day are often the first to see it, and this bill makes sure they always have a permanent place to report it. We thank Congressman Taylor for standing up for American truckers and the motoring public,” said Executive Director Shannon Everett of American Truckers United.

The CDL Fraud Tipline Act would codify the Commercial Driver’s License Fraud Tipline within the Department of Homeland Security. Specifically, this bill would:

Codify the email address, submission form, and any other requirements to submit and maintain the hotline

Require the Department of Homeland Security to submit a report to Congress annually that includes the number of tips the hotline received and the number of fraudulently issued CDLs reported by each state

American Truckers United is a supporting organization of this bill.

The CDL Fraud Tipline Act is available here.

Editor’s note regarding Congressman Taylor:

Congressman Dave Taylor represents Ohio’s Second Congressional District, which includes Clermont, Clinton, Pike, Adams, Brown, Highland, Ross, Scioto, Pickaway, Hocking, Vinton, Jackson, Lawrence, Gallia, and Meigs counties, as well as part of Fayette County. Taylor serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the House Agriculture Committee. Prior to serving in Congress, Taylor worked as an assistant prosecutor for Clermont County before joining his family’s concrete business, where he ultimately served as President. Please visit taylor.house.gov for more information.

title: Rep. Tran Lauds House Passage of Bipartisan Legislation to Expand Benefits for Combat-Injured Veterans
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) celebrated the passage of the Major Richard Star Act, which will allow combat-injured veterans to receive their full retirement pay and disability compensation simultaneously. Representative Tran co-sponsored the bill and signed the discharge petition to bring the bill to the House Floor, where it passed shortly after Veterans Day. Unlike past legislation, this bill also applies to veterans with a combat-related disability who have fewer than 20 years of service, expanding access to VA benefits. Now, the bill awaits Senate consideration.

Under the current policy, service members are required to return home and retire from service upon being injured. During retirement, their earned disability benefits are deducted from their retirement benefits, significantly decreasing their monthly compensation – which covers their food, medicine, and other critical expenses. If passed by the Senate, this legislation would allow all combat-injured veterans who were medically retired, regardless of the length of their service, to accept the full amount of their earned disability and retirement benefits.

“As an Army veteran, my commitment to my brothers and sisters who served is steadfast. Under current policy, combat-injured veterans are forced to forfeit part of their benefits because of injuries beyond their control. It’s just plain wrong: combat-injured veterans must receive their full disability and retirement pay, full stop. I’m proud to have supported this bill to expand benefits for those who sustained lasting injuries in service to our country, and I urge my Senate colleagues to swiftly pass this bipartisan legislation,” said Representative Tran.

H.R. 2102, or the Major Richard Star Act, was introduced by Representative Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12); however, at the time, it was not considered by the House Armed Services Committee. Representative Mark Takano (D-CA-39) brought the bill to the House Floor through a discharge petition, which garnered the required 218 signatures needed to be considered on the House floor. On Thursday, November 12, 2026, the bill passed 392-18. This legislation was named after the late Major Richard Star of the U.S. Army Reserve, a combat-injured veteran and advocate for injured veterans.

As a member of the powerful House Armed Services Committee, Representative Tran is continuously working to expand protections and benefits for veterans:

In July 2025, Representative Tran led a letter with Representative Correa to the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), urging federal support for the construction of the Southern California Veterans Cemetery at Gypsum Canyon.

In September 2026, Representative Tran and colleagues sent a letter to Governor Gavin Newsom to ensure CalVets accepts the funding to build the cemetery.

Rep. Tran’s first piece of legislation, the Protect Veteran Jobs Act, supports the livelihoods of veterans who were wrongfully removed from their civil service positions and allows them to continue serving their country as part of the federal workforce.

Representative Tran introduced the bipartisan Delivering Digitally to Our Veterans Act to allow veterans the option to receive G.I. Bill information and benefits through electronic messages, reducing unnecessary paperwork and increasing accessibility.

Representative Tran also introduced the Carlton H. Ingram Veterans’ Benefits Protection Actto protect veterans’ disability benefits from a change at the Department of Veterans Affairs that would have cut benefits for veterans who rely on medication to manage their disabilities.

title: Congressman Carter Responds to Port of New Orleans Crash
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. issued the following statement following the collision of a tanker with a cruise ship on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans. American Cruise Lines’ riverboat, American Heritage, was docked and preparing to disembark when it was struck by an Atlantic Asphalt tanker, causing it to capsize and sending survivors into the Mississippi River. At the time of the crash, nearly 130 passengers plus crew members were on board.

“I am devastated to hear about the ships crashing near the Port of New Orleans. I am monitoring the situation closely and praying for the swift rescue of survivors and for all emergency crews responding to the situation.

“As we continue to learn more about this tragedy, I commend the swift actions of the NOLA Harbor Police, the New Orleans Fire Department, the New Orleans Police Department, the U.S. Coast Guard, emergency medical personnel including those at the University Medical Center and everyone who responded to the situation.

“I am in communication with the Chairwoman of the National Transportation Safety Board, which is fully engaged and will be en route to New Orleans as soon as the nationwide flight grounding is lifted. We hope to further work with local, state, and federal leadership to address this emergency now and prevent similar situations in the future.

“Tragedies like these remind us why the security of our maritime sector is so important. The Jones Act requires that goods shipped between U.S. ports be transported on vessels that are American-built, American-owned, and American-crewed, ensuring a strong, safe domestic merchant marine fleet. In March, following the dramatic hike in global oil prices from the Administration's reckless war in Iran, the Trump administration waived the Jones Act, letting foreign-flag tankers carry cargo between U.S. ports, in a futile attempt to keep energy prices down. I opposed that waiver, as it unnecessarily increased foreign-flag ships in our busiest waterways without the crew screening, accountability, and transparency required of U.S. vessels.

“The administration issued a sweeping waiver for energy products, including crude oil. The foreign-flagged vessels used for these products are typically large ocean-going tankers with enormous momentum, and one mistake in a busy port can cost lives.

“Today in New Orleans, a foreign-flag asphalt tanker struck a docked river cruise ship carrying 129 passengers, and now a search and rescue mission is underway for missing passengers. We don’t yet know the cause, or whether this ship was operating under the waiver. But if it was, this is exactly why we shouldn’t waive the Jones Act: a huge tanker, a crowded stretch of the Mississippi, and the public bearing the risk.

“The current waiver has resulted in the loss of millions of dollars to our domestic maritime industry and now, endangered American lives. It is set to run through November 15, and the administration should let it end there.

“My heart is with the survivors, their families, and everyone who witnessed this horrific accident.”

###

title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Champions Major Richard Star Act, Passing it Out of the House to Provide Fair Compensation for Combat-Injured Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On November 12, 2026, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) supported the House’s passage of the Major Richard Star Act, legislation Vasquez has championed since its introduction which would allow combat-injured veterans to receive both their full military retirement pay and Veterans Affairs (VA) disability compensation.

Under current law, most military retirees who have completed 20 years of service are eligible to receive their earned retirement and VA disability benefits concurrently. However, servicemembers who are forced into early retirement due to unforeseen combat-related medical injuries are denied that same benefit. This means combat-injured veterans must forfeit their hard-earned military retirement pay to receive VA disability compensation.

The Major Richard Star Act addresses this inequity by allowing combat-injured veterans who were medically retired before reaching 20 years of service to receive both their full military retirement pay and full VA disability compensation. Today, the bill passed in the House with strong bipartisan support with 210 Democrats and 181 Republicans voting in favor. It now heads to the Senate.

Rep. Vasquez has been advocating for this bill’s passage for months.

“Veterans who raised their right hand to commit to faithfully serving our country and whose service was unfortunately cut short due to a medical retirement deserve full and fair compensation,” said Vasquez. “I’m proud to finally put an end to the wounded veterans tax and ensure no combat-injured hero is forced to forgo their military retirement pay. I’ll keep working to pass landmark legislation like this that cuts red tape and ensures veterans get the support and benefits they’ve earned.”

Rep. Vasquez has worked tirelessly to deliver for New Mexico’s veterans:

Introducing the Feed Our Veterans Actto combat food insecurity among veterans and reverse the new burdensome SNAP work requirements introduced under the Republican tax law last summer.

Introducing the Socorro Vet Center Act, which would direct the VA to open a new veteran center in Socorro, providing free, confidential social and psychological support to veterans, service members and their families in southern New Mexico.

Leading theNew Mexico Rural Veteran Health Care Access Act, a bill to ensure that veterans in Otero and Eddy county can more easily access care at other facilities far closer to them.

Introducing the Veteran Education Assistance Adjustment Act, bipartisan legislation to increase the yearly book and supply stipend for student veterans which hasn’t been updated since 2008. If passed, it would increase the stipend from $1,000 to $1,400 and adjust for inflation.

title: Reps. Marc Veasey (TX-33), August Pfluger (TX-11), Nellie Pou (NJ-9), and Zach Nunn (IA-3) Re- Introduce Bipartisan Cybersecurity Clinics Grant Program Act
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. - Representatives Veasey (TX-33), Pfluger (TX-11), Pou (NJ-9) and Nunn (IA-3) recently introduced the Cybersecurity Clinics Grant Program Act. This bill would require the Department of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), to establish a grant program to fund higher education-based cybersecurity clinics at community colleges and minority-serving institutions (MSIs).

“I am proud to work alongside Representatives Pfluger, Pou, and Nunn to help grow and diversify the next generation of young Americans in the cybersecurity workforce,” said Congressman Veasey (TX-33). “The Cybersecurity Clinics Grant Program Act will help do that by ensuring that institutions of higher education, including community colleges and colleges minority-serving institutions, can have the proper tools they need to educate their students in this growing field.”

“Developing a robust cyber workforce is critical to our national and economic security. AI has become an incredible tool for identifying vulnerabilities, but it is also making attacks faster and harder to detect. We cannot defend the homeland without talented professionals who have the skills and know-how to recognize, understand, and stop these threats. Angelo State University, now an NSA National Center of Academic Excellence in Cyber Defense, is training students who protect West Texas cities, schools, and hospitals in real time through its Regional Security Operations Center. I’m proud to co-lead this bipartisan bill to expand on this model and build the cyber workforce that our national and economic security depend on,” said Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11).

“Cybersecurity threats are growing more sophisticated every day. We need to make sure our communities have the tools and trained professionals to meet them,” said Congresswoman Pou. “I am proud to colead the Cybersecurity Clinics Grant Program Act which will help give the next generation of diverse graduates at community colleges, Hispanic-serving institutions, and other minority-serving colleges hands-on experience while strengthening our nation’s cyber defenses through these new cybersecurity clinics. This legislation represents a smart investment in our national security and in the next generation of cybersecurity professionals.”

“Cyberattacks are an increasingly serious threat to our national security, economy, and the small businesses that power communities across Iowa,” said Rep. Nunn. “As a former White House Cybersecurity Director, I know we need to train the next generation of cyber professionals today to stay ahead of tomorrow’s threats. Our bipartisan bill will help community colleges establish cybersecurity clinics that give students hands-on training and real-world experience while equipping small businesses and local governments with the tools to defend against cybercriminals. We’re strengthening America’s cyber workforce and putting those skills to work protecting the communities that need them most.”

This bipartisan legislation will help create the framework for a robust and strategic model that can help the U.S. shore up national security defenses domestically and globally. As the agency with industry leading expertise in cyber policy, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) is in a unique position to help create a vigorous curriculum that community colleges and minority-serving institutions can offer to students interested in breaking into the cyber workforce.

title: Vindman Joins Virginia House Delegation in Urging Rejection of NextEra-Dominion Merger
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives and Virginia Democrats Eugene Vindman, Don Beyer, Jennifer McClellan, Suhas Subramanyam, and James Walkinshaw urged the Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) to reject the proposed acquisition of Dominion Energy by Florida-based NextEra.

In a letter submitted ahead of the SCC’s November 12 public comment deadline, the Members warned that the merger, as currently structured, threatens to increase electricity costs for Virginia families and small businesses for decades to come.

In the letter, Vindman and his colleagues wrote, “As proposed, we do not believe the merger is in the public interest. We believe the proposed transaction fails to satisfy the statutory requirements and because the joint petition lacks the structural protections necessary to prevent material harm, the Commission should deny the merger petition in its current form.”

The Members noted that while NextEra stands to benefit from the expanded investment opportunities created by the rapid expansion of data centers across Northern Virginia, residential customers and small businesses could be left footing the bill. The Members also cautioned that the merger could consolidate market power across the regional electricity grid, stifling competition and ultimately increasing electricity costs for Virginia consumers.

They argued that the proposed merger’s temporary incentives fail to offset the merger’s potential long-term costs. They also pointed to the absence of a moratorium on base rate increases, a cap on escalating rate adjustment clauses, and a binding requirement to pass operational savings on to customers.

The letter further raises concerns about NextEra’s corporate governance, including its history of political spending and interference, warning these practices could undermine regulatory oversight, create conflicts with Virginia’s Clean Economy Act requirements, and expose ratepayers to additional financial risks.

Emphasizing the SCC’s statutory responsibility to safeguard consumers and ensure the long-term reliability and affordability of utility service, the Members stated that approving the merger without adequate, enforceable protections would undermine that responsibility.

Full text of the letter can be found here.

–

Dear Commissioners:

We write to express our opposition to the current proposed merger whereby NextEra Energy, Inc. (“NextEra”) would acquire control of Dominion Energy, Inc. (“Dominion”). Under the Utility Transfers Act, the State Corporation Commission (“Commission”) may approve an acquisition of control if it finds that “adequate service to the public at just and reasonable rates will not be impaired or jeopardized. “Applicants must prove that the transaction causes no harm to captive customers. We believe the joint petition fails this statutory test.

We respectfully urge the Commission to reject the proposed NextEra Dominion merger in its current form, as recommended by Commission staff.

Rate Base Inflation and Misaligned Incentives

NextEra’s investor disclosures emphasize that Dominion’s territory offers immense multi-decade capital deployment opportunities, driven in large part by the extraordinary concentration of AI data centers in Northern Virginia and future planned load. Given that this projected future energy demand in the Commonwealth will be reliant on massive bulk transmission lines, which are still socialized across residential rate classes, much of that potential infrastructure will be paid for by ratepayers. And as NextEra’s growth strategy is dependent on maximizing capital deployment, its potential acquisition of Dominion risks creating a sustained, multi-decade upward pressure on ratepayers’ bills. Captive residential and small business ratepayers will be locked into paying decades of capital carrying charges, depreciation, and an authorized Return on Equity (ROE) on this expanded rate base.

We are concerned that much of NextEra’s growth strategy is heavily dependent on data center customers. This increases vulnerabilities that exist due to overbuilding and the ramifications that could materialize for ratepayers if projected revenue from large-load customers fails to cover the full cost of the transmission buildout and necessary upgrades to the grid that increased data center presence would require. While Dominion has started work to hedge against this stranded asset risk, there is insufficient protection in the case for bankruptcy, differing time horizons for service contracts and infrastructure lifespans, as well as the burden of broader grid upgrades required by data centers (rather than just point-to-point infrastructure) where every day ratepayers foot the bill.

There have also been documented concerns about how this merger affects market competition within the broader grid that Dominion is a part of, particularly with respect to transmission and energy generation and how the new merger could create “self-preferencing” or foreclose potential competition, and how those ripple effects could then increase wholesale prices and therefore raise costs for ratepayers in Virginia.

Despite those long-term upward financial pressures, the merger sweeteners of customer bill credits and added funds for the EnergyShare program are both inadequate and only short-term. Once the sweeteners expire, the Virginia-based Dominion workforce would be at risk of significant job cuts, Virginia households and small businesses would be locked into paying those multi-decade elevated rates, with the joint petition providing for no base rate increase moratorium, no cap on escalating rate adjustment clauses (riders), and no binding mechanism to track and pass fuel or operational synergies to captive customers. Additionally, the proposed bill credit for consumers barely covers the impact that increased fuel costs are having on electric bills. Dominion already petitioned the Commission for a $10 per month increase for fuel-related costs this year.

For these reasons, the Independent Market Monitor stated, the “scale, financial strength, and operational breadth all enhance market power and any economic gains are more likely to accrue to investors rather than customers.” Thus, we must look past the near-term sweeteners and toward robust binding, structural protections that prevent long-term negative impacts on Virginia ratepayers.

We believe the primary benefits of the merger should be designed to benefit our constituents, the ratepayers, and we believe the current merger design will raise rates. To that extent, we urge the Commission to, at a bare minimum, require long-term rate protections for consumers as recommended by Commission staff and require substantially larger bill credits as recommended by the Governor’s Office before any potential merger can proceed. As energy prices have considerably increased, and this merger threatens to exacerbate market conditions that could further increase prices for ratepayers it is paramount that the Commission use its authority to protect consumers who are already struggling to afford to keep the lights on.

Corporate Governance Deficits Threaten Rate Case Prudency

A utility’s corporate culture directly governs accounting integrity, affiliate transactions, and ratemaking prudency. The Commission must ensure that any acquiring entity submits to complete regulatory transparency and that captive ratepayers do not cross-subsidize non-utility operations, political spending, or parent-company agendas.

NextEra’s operational history and recent testimony demonstrates documented resistance to transparent regulatory scrutiny. NextEra recently entered into a $150 million settlement to resolve widespread political interference and dark money schemes, which included funding “ghost candidates” against state legislators and covert surveillance of an investigative journalist. This Commission’s Hearing Examiner properly recognized the relevance of these governance practices to regulatory integrity by ordering the production of the internal “Robo memo” into the evidentiary record. We share the position that this memo should be available for review to the Commission and intervenors.

At a time when regulatory scrutiny is at an all-time high, NextEra’s top leadership has aligned itself financially with federal agendas that raise rates and undermine Virginia’s statutory obligations. NextEra’s participation in high-level, opaque federal lobbying networks heightens the risk that Virginia ratepayers could be improperly forced to subsidize national political advocacy that runs counter to their own interests. In this case, aligning with a federal agenda that rolls back renewable energy incentives, curtails offshore wind development, and props up uneconomic generation. Engaging in that advocacy, including through means designed to obscure its involvement, puts NextEra in direct conflict with Virginia’s statutory mandates under the Virginia Clean Economy Act, and introduces an acute risk of asset stranding, resource inadequacy, and costly non-compliance penalties that will inevitably fall upon Virginia consumers.

It is unacceptably risky to transfer Virginia’s premier electric utility to an acquiring entity that displays such a pattern of routine spending, through opaque affiliate channels, to influence regulatory and political outcomes. Such practices, if expanded into Virginia, would directly threaten the Commission’s ability to police affiliate transactions, enforce cross-subsidization prohibitions, and verify the prudency of test-year operating expenses. Captive ratepayers bear the cost when compliance breaks down, transactions lack transparent auditing, or management priorities subordinate the public interest to unregulated political agendas.

Conclusion

The Commission’s statutory mission is to safeguard captive consumers and ensure the long-term reliability and affordability of utility service. As proposed, we do not believe the merger is in the public interest. We believe the proposed transaction fails to satisfy the statutory requirements and because the joint petition lacks the structural protections necessary to prevent material harm, the Commission should deny the merger petition in its current form.

We appreciate the Commission’s careful scrutiny of this proceeding and submit these comments on behalf of our constituents.

BACKGROUND

Vindman was the first member of Virginia’s congressional delegation to publicly oppose the proposed merger between NextEra and Dominion Energy, raising concerns about its potential impact on electricity rates and Virginia consumers.

Most recently, he delivered remarks at a Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) public hearing on the proposed merger, urging regulators to reject the proposal and put the interests of ratepayers ahead of corporate profits.

title: Walkinshaw Introduces Bill to Keep  Tech Workers in Public Service
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. –Today, Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), founder and co-chair of the Federal Workforce Caucus, introduced the Keep Federal Tech Talent Act, legislation that would let technologists and scientists in temporary federal roles, such as fellowships, move into permanent government careers. As agencies struggle to recruit and keep technical talent, the bill gives these public servants a clear pathway and real incentives to stay and keep serving their country.

Over the past two years, the Trump administration’s DOGE policies have forced out experienced federal employees and created a culture of fear inside federal agencies. This has exacerbated the long-term challenge that federal agencies have faced in recruiting and retaining the next generation of technical talent.

The administration launched the U.S. Tech Force, which places early-career technologists in federal agencies for two-year terms. The government needs this kind of talent, but two years is rarely long enough for a new hire to gain the experience needed to modernize complex federal systems or improve the services Americans depend on. And as the program stands, fellows who want to keep serving their country have no clear pathway or incentive to do so.

“Americans who want to serve their country deserve every opportunity to do so,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “These professionals are writing code that delivers services to Americans, securing networks that keep our data safe, and supporting research that saves lives. If they want to keep serving, we should open the door to a long-term career in federal service.”

“For the federal government to deliver essential public services to the American people, we must hire and retain qualified personnel, including technology experts with specialized skill sets,” said NFFE National President Randy Erwin. “NFFE endorses the Keep Federal Tech Talent Act, which would help temporary federal workers in the tech sector build permanent careers in the civil service while expanding access to training and student loan assistance. These investments are critical to ensuring the government can recruit and retain the skilled personnel it needs. Thank you to Representative Walkinshaw for leading on this issue and his unwavering commitment to the federal workforce.”

“At a time when the federal workforce has just endured a massive loss of personnel and expertise in STEM and highly skilled roles, we look to Congress to find urgent solutions that strengthen the federal talent pipeline,” said Matt Biggs, International Federation of Professional and Technical Engineers (IFPTE) President. “That’s why IFPTE supports the Keep Federal Tech Talent Act, legislation that seeks to ensure that temporary federal employees are given opportunities to continue their careers in the civil service. We thank Rep. Walkinshaw for introducing this necessary bill that will bolster the federal government’s research and technology workforce and provide federal agencies with talented and dedicated innovators who serve the American public."

The Keep Federal Tech Talent Act would:

Create a pathway for federal agencies to hire limited term employees in specialized technology and science roles, including software engineering, cybersecurity, AI, data science, and scientific research, into permanent federal careers when they meet the qualifications for an open role.

Require agencies to help those who stay with student loan repayment or additional skills training.

Require agencies to report each year to the Office of Personnel Management on how many workers convert and which positions they fill.

As Walkinshaw fights to recruit technical talent into the federal workforce, he also continues to fight President Trump’s proposed federal pay freeze. “A pay freeze is a pay cut, and it’s one more barrier to attracting top talent,” said Walkinshaw. “We can’t ask these professionals to consider a career in government and then tell them their work isn’t worth fair pay.”

The full text of the Keep Federal Tech Talent Act is available here.
