title: NEWS: Senator Blunt Rochester Receives Response from NFL on Blood Clot Protocol, Pushes for Continued Transparency
text:
U.S. Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), a member of the Senate Committees on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions and Commerce, Science, and Transportation, received a response to her inquiry into the National Football League’s (NFL) deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE) treatment protocols. Last month, the Senator sent a letter to NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell following a medical incident involving Philadelphia Eagles Quarterback Jalen Hurts, who was diagnosed with DVT and bilateral PE.

The NFL’s response provided updates on the NFL and NFL Players Association’s joint review of Jalen Hurts’ injuries and outlined ongoing efforts to track clotting disorders in the NFL.

“The League’s highest priority is the health and safety of players… With respect to the circumstances of Mr. Hurts’ diagnosis, as you may know, the NFL and the NFL Players Association have agreed to conduct a joint review of the circumstances related to his injury. As outlined by the league and NFLPA’s Collective Bargaining Agreement, mutually agreed-upon independent medical experts will review the matter and share their conclusions and recommendations with both parties,” said Jeff Miller, Executive Vice President, Communications, Public Affairs, and Health Policy, NFL.

“The League and Players Association also have several medical committees that review and monitor player injury data closely. For at least the past decade, the NFL has tracked clotting disorders among players every season through a subcommittee of its General Medical Committee, and this information is shared with the NFLPA,” Miller continued. “Following the ongoing joint review, the League and NFLPA will consider appropriate next steps, including whether this case points to a need for additional league-wide guidance.”

Miller concluded, “We welcome the opportunity to provide additional information, and find ways to support your efforts around raising awareness and improving outcomes related to blood clot disorders.”

On the NFL’s response, Senator Blunt Rochester said, “I’m grateful for an update on the NFL’s review of Mr. Hurts’ diagnosis and for information on the League’s efforts to track clotting disorders in its athletes. While I appreciate the NFL’s transparency, I encourage its leadership to use this moment to increase awareness of DVT and PE to better protect its players and support public health. Every year, over 100,000 Americans are affected by blood clots, but with the NFL’s reach and influence, we can increase education and help save lives. I’m hopeful that this unfortunate incident can become a force for good, leading to lasting change within the league and our healthcare system at large. I will continue following up with the NFL to ensure this situation is treated with the diligence and care it deserves.”

title: NEWS: Senator Blunt Rochester Urges NTIA to Fully Restore Digital Equity Act Grants
text:
Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), a member of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, today sent a letter to Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information Arielle Roth urging the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) to implement the Digital Equity Act grant programs.

Congress passed the Digital Equity Act as part of the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act to complement historic federal investments in broadband infrastructure by addressing barriers to broadband adoption and use. However, in May 2025, President Trump announced his intention to terminate the Digital Equity Act grant programs, including the Competitive Grant Program.

“I write regarding the National Telecommunications and Information Administration’s (NTIA) implementation of the Digital Equity Act grant programs. I appreciate NTIA’s commitment to reinstating the Digital Equity Competitive Grant Program (“the Competitive Grant Program”) and its stated intention to issue a new Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) next month. As the agency moves forward with the Competitive Grant Program, I urge NTIA to preserve the substantial work applicants have already undertaken, minimize unnecessary delays and administrative burdens, and make congressionally appropriated funding available as quickly as possible,” said Senator Blunt Rochester.

“These programs are particularly important to Delaware, which is working to become the first state to achieve universal high-speed broadband access. As Delaware builds broadband infrastructure statewide, complementary investments in digital literacy training, device access, and technical assistance will help ensure every Delawarean can fully benefit from internet connectivity,” the Senator continued. “NTIA subsequently awarded Delaware approximately $4.8 million to implement initiatives supporting digital literacy, workforce development, broadband affordability, and device access. However, since the Trump administration’s termination of the program in May 2025, Delaware has been left without a clear path to accessing these funds or implementing its approved plan.”

Blunt Rochester concluded, “Congress established and funded the Digital Equity Act programs on a bipartisan basis because deploying broadband infrastructure alone does not guarantee that Americans can fully benefit from it. Promptly moving forward with the Competitive and Capacity Grant Programs would carry out Congress’s direction, provide certainty to applicants and states, and help ensure that federal investments in broadband infrastructure translate into meaningful connectivity for communities across the country.”

The full text of the letter can be found HERE, and below.

Dear Assistant Secretary Roth:

I write regarding the National Telecommunications and Information Administration’s (NTIA) implementation of the Digital Equity Act grant programs. I appreciate NTIA’s commitment to reinstating the Digital Equity Competitive Grant Program (“the Competitive Grant Program”) and its stated intention to issue a new Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) next month.1 As the agency moves forward with the Competitive Grant Program, I urge NTIA to preserve the substantial work applicants have already undertaken, minimize unnecessary delays and administrative burdens, and make congressionally appropriated funding available as quickly as possible. I also urge NTIA to provide a clear path forward for the State Digital Equity Capacity Grant Program, including previously approved state plans and awarded funding.

These programs are particularly important to Delaware, which is working to become the first state to achieve universal high-speed broadband access. As Delaware builds broadband infrastructure statewide, complementary investments in digital literacy training, device access, and technical assistance will help ensure every Delawarean can fully benefit from internet connectivity. Furthermore, as artificial intelligence increasingly shapes how Americans work, learn, and access essential services, equipping Delawareans with digital skills is more important than ever.

Congress passed the Digital Equity Act as part of the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) to complement historic federal investments in broadband infrastructure by addressing barriers to broadband adoption and use. Through the IIJA, Congress appropriated $1.25 billion for the Competitive Grant Program—$250 million for each fiscal year from 2022 through 2026—to support efforts that help Americans gain the skills, devices, and resources needed to benefit from broadband connectivity.2

Demand for these resources has been substantial. Following NTIA’s 2024 Notice of Funding Opportunity, more than 700 applicants requested over $6.5 billion in funding.3 Local governments, libraries, educational institutions, workforce organizations, nonprofits, and other eligible entities invested significant time and resources to identify community needs, develop programs, and build partnerships in anticipation of these awards.

On May 8, 2025, President Trump on Truth Social announced his intention to immediately terminate the Digital Equity Act grant programs, including the Competitive Grant Program, asserting that the program was “racist” and “illegal” because it included racial and ethnic minorities as part of its targeted covered populations.4,5 On July 15, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia held in National Digital Inclusion Alliance v. Trump that the provision identifying members of racial or ethnic minority groups as a covered population was unconstitutional, but also held that the provision was severable from the remainder of the statute.6 The decision therefore provides a path for the Competitive Grant Program to move forward consistent with the remaining statutory requirements.

On October 23, 2026, NTIA filed an update in National Digital Inclusion Alliance v. Trump stating that NTIA is on track to publish the NOFO and application for the Competitive Grant Program in December 2026.7 As NTIA develops this NOFO, I urge the agency to minimize disruption to applicants by preserving the substantial work already undertaken to develop proposals and establish community partnerships. NTIA should allow applicants to update existing proposals to meet any revised program requirements, rather than requiring them to restart the application process, and provide clear guidance to facilitate a timely transition.

I also urge NTIA to provide a clear path forward for the State Digital Equity Capacity Grant Program. Delaware was the second state in the country to receive federal approval of its State Digital Equity Plan in 2024 and was expected to become the first state to achieve 100% access to high-speed broadband.8 NTIA subsequently awarded Delaware approximately $4.8 million to implement initiatives supporting digital literacy, workforce development, broadband affordability, and device access.9 However, since the Trump administration’s termination of the program in May 2025, Delaware has been left without a clear path to accessing these funds or implementing its approved plan. Because the Capacity Grant Program was not at issue in National Digital Inclusion Alliance v. Trump, its status remains unresolved. I urge NTIA to clarify how it intends to move forward with the program and make congressionally appropriated Capacity Grant funding available as quickly as possible.

Congress established and funded the Digital Equity Act programs on a bipartisan basis because deploying broadband infrastructure alone does not guarantee that Americans can fully benefit from it. Promptly moving forward with the Competitive and Capacity Grant Programs would carry out Congress’s direction, provide certainty to applicants and states, and help ensure that federal investments in broadband infrastructure translate into meaningful connectivity for communities across the country.

Thank you for your attention to this important matter, and I look forward to working with you to ensure these programs are implemented promptly, effectively, and in a manner that is consistent with the law.

###

title: NEWS: Senators Blunt Rochester, Curtis Demand Trump Administration Strengthen AI Chip Export Controls
text:
U.S. Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), a member of the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, and John Curtis (R-Utah), a member of the Committee on Foreign Relations, sent a letter to Department of Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick urging the Trump administration to address loopholes in export controls for advanced artificial intelligence (AI) semiconductors, otherwise known as “chips.” The letter outlines how closing these gaps will maintain our competitive edge over Chinese technologies while buying time to focus on promoting responsible domestic AI policy. This letter follows reports that former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang was involved in a honeypot scheme with a Chinese spy.

“We are deeply concerned by reports that the recently departed CEO of the nation’s top semiconductor company, NVIDIA, was caught in a honeypot scheme with a Chinese spy and executive at Megaspeed, a Singaporean firm known to help Chinese companies circumvent export controls,” said the Senators. “Our concerns about insufficient export controls on these technologies are magnified by numerous rogue artificial intelligence incidents, including autonomous hacking incidents, unauthorized agent access to the internet, and attacks on real-world targets. Whistleblowers from the nation’s leading AI companies have warned that technology is accelerating without sufficient guardrails, further compounding our concerns.”

“Collectively, these incidents show the urgent need for the Trump administration to act and protect the safety and security of Americans. Responsible U.S. domestic AI policy must promote our competitive edge in artificial intelligence through reasonable innovation and regulation. It should not enable our strategic adversaries to embrace risky behaviors with these technologies or to acquire them through nefarious means,” the Senators continued. “China’s frontier artificial intelligence capabilities are rapidly approaching those of the United States, with some experts estimating China’s frontier to be just six to nine months behind the United States…To maintain its competitive edge while promoting responsible domestic AI policy, the United States must ensure Chinese AI labs cannot easily procure the compute required to develop, test, and train advanced artificial intelligence models.”

“We urge you to condition licenses for the export of advanced AI chips on an agreement that recipients will not provide Chinese companies with remote access unless granted a separate and additional license to do so. These policies should not be geographically limited in scope. If they are, China will simply rent access to chips elsewhere, creating a whack-a-mole scenario.” The Senators concluded, “During your confirmation hearing, you called for stronger export controls, saying, ‘If they are going to compete with us, let them compete, but stop using our tools to compete with us.’ Today, the stakes are clear, and our adversaries are not playing by the rules. We must close these loopholes if the United States is to maintain its competitive edge in artificial intelligence.”

The full response letter can be found HERE and below.

Secretary Lutnick:

We write to urge you to take immediate steps to close loopholes in the export regime for advanced AI chips.

We are deeply concerned by reports that the recently departed CEO of the nation’s top semiconductor company, NVIDIA, was caught in a honeypot scheme with a Chinese spy and executive at Megaspeed, a Singaporean firm known to help Chinese companies circumvent export controls.1 Despite the intelligence community raising concerns that Mr. Huang had been compromised, the Department has taken no action to tighten export controls on Megaspeed and other high-risk companies in Southeast Asia2. These concerns are only exacerbated by reports that Under Secretary Kessler discussed ongoing investigations into Megaspeed with NVIDIA’s General Counsel.3 This scenario raises numerous alarms about how you and the Trump Administration are safeguarding highly sensitive technologies.

Our concerns about insufficient export controls on these technologies are magnified by numerous rogue artificial intelligence incidents, including autonomous hacking incidents, unauthorized agent access to the internet, and attacks on real-world targets. Whistleblowers from the nation’s leading AI companies have warned that technology is accelerating without sufficient guardrails, further compounding our concerns.

Collectively, these incidents show the urgent need for the Trump administration to act and protect the safety and security of Americans. Responsible U.S. domestic AI policy must promote our competitive edge in artificial intelligence through reasonable innovation and regulation. It should not enable our strategic adversaries to embrace risky behaviors with these technologies or to acquire them through nefarious means.

China’s frontier artificial intelligence capabilities are rapidly approaching those of the United States, with some experts estimating China’s frontier to be just six to nine months behind the United States.4 Gaining a competitive advantage is a significant motivating factor behind its development of artificial intelligence. China also seeks to leverage the technology to enhance its national security, including by bolstering military capabilities, surveilling adversaries, and tightening its control over information. This is well demonstrated by Anthropic’s recent report Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026, in which Anthropic’s Threat Intelligence team details incidents in which China-based entities and Chinese government affiliates used artificial intelligence for cyber operations, surveillance, scams and fraud, conventional weapons, and distillation.5 If China develops superior artificial intelligence capabilities, it would only increase the threat to the United States and its interests around the globe.

Fortunately, the United States and its allies remain ahead in the key technologies necessary to develop and operate the most advanced frontier models: advanced chips and the equipment necessary to manufacture them. To maintain its competitive edge while promoting responsible domestic AI policy, the United States must ensure Chinese AI labs cannot easily procure the compute required to develop, test, and train advanced artificial intelligence models. To overcome this severe disadvantage, China has developed illicit or subversive means to access advanced chips through remote access, smuggling, and U.S. based subsidiaries of Chinese companies.

As you know, Chinese companies are restricted from purchasing advanced chips, yet they can easily rent access to them through U.S. subsidiaries, overseas shell companies, and other companies like Megaspeed.6 The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace has documented at least eleven state-linked Chinese entities seeking access to chips through cloud services. While Congress is considering legislation to address the Department’s authorities over remote access to chips, we appreciate that you are reportedly making efforts to close this loophole.7 However, the details of the policy changes will be critical. We urge you to condition licenses for the export of advanced AI chips on an agreement that recipients will not provide Chinese companies with remote access unless granted a separate and additional license to do so. These policies should not be geographically limited in scope. If they are, China will simply rent access to chips elsewhere, creating a whack-a-mole scenario.

Furthermore, we are concerned by the access afforded to Chinese companies with subsidiaries located in the United States and urge you to restrict the sale of export-controlled chips to these subsidiaries. This risk is most recently exemplified by the Inspur Group and its U.S. subsidiary, Aivres. The Inspur Group has long been listed on the Department of Commerce’s Entity List, restricting its capacity to do business with the United States due to security concerns.8 However, Aivres exported at least $5.6 billion of advanced technology from the United States to Southeast Asia over a two year period, including more than $3 billion of computers containing the advanced Blackwell chips.9 This technology was then deployed in data centers and technology firms in Southeast Asia, where it serves Chinese tech firms like Alibaba and ByteDance.10 Unfortunately, this is just one subsidiary. To maintain our competitive edge in artificial intelligence, we must close this loophole expeditiously.

Finally, we urge you to restrict the sale of export-controlled chips to non-trusted companies in countries with a high risk of smuggling, including those in Southeast Asia. Some estimate that smugglers have diverted or resold several hundred thousand chips to China, providing up to 40 percent of its training capacity.11 However, smuggling operations will likely adapt to geographic restrictions. To preempt this risk, we urge you to impose a license requirement on exports of large quantities of chips to non-trusted companies in a broader set of countries.

During your confirmation hearing, you called for stronger export controls, saying, “If they are going to compete with us, let them compete, but stop using our tools to compete with us.”12 Today, the stakes are clear, and our adversaries are not playing by the rules. We must close these loopholes if the United States is to maintain its competitive edge in artificial intelligence.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

###

title: Boozman, Padilla Lead Bill to Strengthen National Wildlife Refuge Management
text:
U.S. Senators John Boozman (R-AR) and Alex Padilla (D-CA) introduced bipartisan legislation to strengthen habitat management efforts across the National Wildlife Refuge System by giving the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) explicit authority to partner with state, tribal and non-governmental organizations. The National Wildlife Refuge Habitat Partnership Act would expand opportunities to leverage outside expertise, personnel and equipment to maintain healthy habitats and support the fish, waterfowl, wildlife and plant species that depend on these lands.

The National Wildlife Refuge System, administered by FWS manages hundreds of wildlife refuges across the country. Unlike lands that can largely be left in their natural state, these refuge habitats require regular, active management to maintain healthy conditions for fish, waterfowl, wildlife and plants. This bill would give FWS the authority to enter into contracts or agreements with these nonfederal partners to perform habitat management on National Wildlife Refuge System lands, similar to authorities already provided to the U.S. Forest Service, Bureau of Land Management and National Park Service.

“National wildlife refuges are vital to conserve distinct natural resources by providing unique and essential habitat. Effective management of these sites requires the right resources and collaboration. There are 10 national wildlife refuges in Arkansas and this legislation will give the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service greater flexibility to work with state, tribal and non-government partners to maintain these lands and address management needs. By making better use of available resources and expertise, we can strengthen conservation efforts and ensure these habitats remain healthy for future generations,” said Boozman.

“Our public lands are some of our nation’s greatest treasures. Healthy, well-maintained national wildlife refuges are critical to improving fish and wildlife habitat, reducing the impact of natural disasters, and improving access to recreation. This bill will leverage public, private, and non-profit resources to improve habitat conservation and ensure our public lands are supported and protected,” said Padilla.

The National Wildlife Refuge Habitat Partnership Act is supported by Ducks Unlimited, the Congressional Sportsmen’s Foundation and Delta Waterfowl.

“National wildlife refuges are essential to the future of wetlands and waterfowl conservation. The National Wildlife Refuge Habitat Partnership Act would help refuges expand their capacity to achieve conservation outcomes and provide more places for waterfowl and other wildlife to thrive. It recognizes the expertise of refuge professionals and ensures they retain the ability to make management decisions based on the needs of the resources they protect. Thank you to Sens. Boozman and Padilla for leading this effort to strengthen our nation’s refuges and expand their impact on wildlife habitat,” said Ducks Unlimited COO Karen Waldrop.

"Healthy habitat is the foundation of successful fish and wildlife conservation and quality hunting and fishing opportunities. The National Wildlife Refuge Habitat Partnership Act would strengthen the ability of refuge managers to work with conservation partners on habitat projects that advance each refuge’s purposes. The Congressional Sportsmen’s Foundation (CSF) thanks Congressional Sportsmen’s Caucus (CSC) Co-Chair Sen. Boozman and CSC Member Sen. Padilla for their bipartisan leadership on this practical approach to improving habitat across the National Wildlife Refuge System,” said Senior Vice President & Chief Operating Officer Congressional Sportsmen’s Foundation Taylor Schmitz.

“We sincerely appreciate the leadership of Sen. Boozman and Sen. Padilla to take this practical approach to enhancing habitat on our National Wildlife Refuges. Leveraging the diversity of private sector expertise and capacity, guided by USFWS staff and policy can result in significant improvements on our refuges which are much needed for ducks and duck hunters,” said Delta Waterfowl Chief Policy Officer John Devney.

title: Cantwell Joins More Than 200 Democrats in Fight to Overturn the Trump Admin’s Draconian Abortion Ban at VA
text:
Cantwell Joins More Than 200 Democrats in Fight to Overturn the Trump Admin’s Draconian Abortion Ban at VA

More than 200 Senate and House Democrats filed an amicus brief challenging the Trump VA’s ban on abortion care for veterans in cases of rape, incest, or health endangerment

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA), ranking member of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation and senior member of the Senate Finance Committee, joined more than 200 Senate and House Democrats in filing an amicus brief to Minority Veterans of America v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs, a lawsuit challenging the Trump Administration’s abortion ban at the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA).

The lawsuit, pending before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit, seeks to overturn VA’s ban on abortion care and counseling. In the brief, the lawmakers argue the Trump Administration’s 2025 policy banning abortion counseling and abortion care in almost all cases rests on a flawed legal premise.

“VA’s Final Rule rests on a faulty interpretation of federal law that has significant negative consequences for our nation’s veterans. The issues presented in this case potentially reach roughly 462,000 women veterans of reproductive age who are enrolled in VA health care, along with an estimated 112,000 women of reproductive age enrolled in the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA),” the members wrote.

The members continued, “For them, the Final Rule means a VA physician is prohibited from discussing the full range of a patient’s options during a pregnancy, prohibited from providing the full range of health care available to pregnant women, and is prohibited from intervening when a pregnancy threatens the patient’s health or is the result of rape or incest.”

VA’s abortion ban, implemented by the Trump Administration in 2025, prohibits abortion counseling and care for veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries—even in cases of rape, incest, or if a veteran’s health is endangered. The lawmakers argue in the brief that VA’s erroneous interpretation of federal law means these women now cannot receive abortion care or counseling even in the most harrowing circumstances. They also argue the Veterans’ Health Care Eligibility Reform Act of 1996 allows VA to provide any medical services the Secretary “determines to be needed” and that the Veterans Health Care Act of 1992, which VA used to justify its abortion ban, does not restrict the Secretary’s authority to add abortion care to its medical benefits package.

In the Senate, the amicus brief was signed by all 47 Democratic U.S. Senators. In the House, the brief was signed by 165 Democratic U.S. Representatives.

In March, Sen. Cantwell and all present Democratic Senators voted in support of Senator Richard Blumenthal’s (D-CT) Congressional Review Act (CRA) joint resolution to overturn the Trump Administration’s policy ending abortion counseling entirely and abortion care for veterans in cases of rape, incest, or health endangerment. Sen. Cantwell cosponsored the joint resolution. The CRA is an oversight tool Congress can use to overturn final rules issued by federal agencies with a simple majority vote. The vote failed 48-50 due to lack of adequate Republican support, leaving VA’s abortion ban in place. While the measure did not receive a vote in the House, a corresponding House version garnered the support of 155 Democratic cosponsors.

In September 2022, VA began to offer abortion counseling to all pregnant veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries, and abortion care in cases of rape, incest, or life or health endangerment of the veteran or CHAMPVA beneficiary. This was in response to the Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization ruling, which created urgent risks to the lives and health of pregnant veterans and CHAMPVA beneficiaries in states that banned or otherwise severely restricted access to abortion. VA’s dangerous abortion ban means that veterans nationwide now face those same risks.

More than 462,000 veterans of reproductive age are enrolled in VA health care, and more than 112,000 women of reproductive age are enrolled in CHAMPVA. More than half of these women live in states that have enacted abortion bans or restrictions.

The amicus brief can be read in full HERE.

Sen. Cantwell is a longtime defender of reproductive rights, including for veterans and active service members. In September 2025, Sen. Cantwell joined 232 of her colleagues in sending a letter to VA Acting Under Secretary for Health Steven Lieberman to comment on the VA’s then-proposed near-total ban on abortion and abortion counseling.

In 2023, she spoke at a press conference with her Democratic Senate colleagues, veterans, and reproductive rights groups to oppose Republicans’ attempt to strip reproductive care from veterans and their families. The following month, she joined her colleagues in urging then-Secretary of Defense Lloyd Austin to prioritize reproductive health care for military members.

Strict abortion bans enacted after the Dobbs decision overturned Roe v. Wade in 2022 have created confusion around the treatment medical professionals can provide, even when a pregnant patient’s life or health is in danger. Providers fear they could be sued or prosecuted for providing abortion care, or even miscarriage treatment.

title: Cassidy on Senate Floor: Protecting Social Security Means Protecting America’s Fiscal Future
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA) took to the U.S. Senate floor to urge congressional action before the end of the year to rescue Social Security, warning that a failure to address the program’s insolvency could result in a 28.5% cut to benefits in less than six years. Cassidy called on Congress to move beyond bipartisan disagreements and consider proposals already on the table, specifically urging Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-OR) to allow the committee to take up the issue.

“Social Security is so important. But at this point, the needs for the individual, which is to have a secure Social Security program, is the same as the need for our nation to have a sound fiscal house,” said Dr. Cassidy.

“Now is the time to fix it. Everybody always says it’s the third rail of politics. You can’t touch Social or else you’re going to lose. No, we’re talking about rescuing Social Security…And we can get it done before the next Congress and we can do it now,” continued Dr. Cassidy.

“Let’s do right for the American people. If there’s anything we learned from last Tuesday’s election, if people make promises and don’t keep them, the voters will punish them. Congress has made a promise to take care of the American people’s fiscal house that’s represented by Social Security. Let’s keep that promise,” concluded Dr. Cassidy.

Background

Cassidy has spent over six years working on bipartisan solutions to rescue Social Security from insolvency, including his own proposal to establish an investment fund separate from the Social Security Trust Fund. He has repeatedly called on Congress to act now to address the issue before it is too late and written extensively on his proposal in the Washington Post, the Wall Street Journal, State Affairs, and the Washington Examiner.

title: Duckworth, Durbin Introduce Bill to Make City of Murphysboro the Official Headquarters of Woman’s Relief Corps
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and Dick Durbin (D-IL) introduced legislation to officially update the federal charter of the Woman’s Relief Corps (WRC) so that it reflects the relocation of its national headquarters from Springfield to Murphysboro, Illinois. The WRC, which has served as the women’s auxiliary to the Grand Army of the Republic (GAR) since 1883, moved its headquarters and museum to the General John A. Logan Museum in Murphysboro after its delegates voted unanimously for the relocation in 2023. However, federal law still lists Springfield as the organization’s principal office and the District of Columbia as its legal home. The Senate bill is identical to the House companion introduced by U.S. Representative Mike Bost (R-IL-12), which passed the House of Representatives on February 2, 2026.

“For more than 140 years, the Woman’s Relief Corps has cared for Veterans and ensured that all Americans continue to remember the legacy of the brave Union Soldiers who sacrificed to keep our country together when the Confederacy sought to tear her apart,” said Duckworth. “This relocation is fitting since this city was where General John A. Logan was born, and it was his order that gave us Memorial Day. Southern Illinois is the natural home for this organization, and this bipartisan, bicameral bill will update the law to properly reflect the Corps’ new headquarters in Murphysboro.”

“I am proud to support the Woman’s Relief Corps and its efforts to officially recognize Murphysboro, Illinois, as its national headquarters, honoring the organization’s longstanding legacy of service to our nation’s veterans,” said Durbin.

General John A. Logan was born in 1826 in what became Murphysboro, Illinois, and went on to serve as a Union general in the Civil War and to represent Illinois in both the U.S. House and the U.S. Senate. In 1868, as Commander-in-Chief of the GAR, he issued General Order No. 11, designating May 30 as a day for decorating the graves of Soldiers who died in the war. The observance became Memorial Day.

The WRC was founded in 1883 at the request of the GAR, the Civil War Union Veterans’ organization, and received its federal charter in 1962. The charter calls on the Corps to preserve the GAR’s memory and records and to honor those who have served in any war. Members also take part in Memorial Day observances nationwide.

A copy of the bill text is available on Senator Duckworth’s website.

title: Durbin, Chicago Hospital Leaders Convene Meeting On Eight-Year Progress Of Chicago Heal Initiative
text:
In 2018, Durbin partnered with 10 Chicago-area hospitals to establish the Chicago HEAL Initiative to address the root causes of gun violence

CHICAGO – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) today convened a meeting at Northwestern Medicine Bronzeville Outpatient Center with the hospital CEOs that partnered with him on his Chicago HEAL Initiative to discuss the progress made thanks to the Initiative over the past eight years. Established by Durbin in 2018, the Chicago HEAL Initiative is a partnership between 10 of the largest hospitals serving Chicago with the aim to address the root causes of gun violence through economic, health, and community projects in 18 of Chicago’s neighborhoods with the highest rates of violence and poverty.

Thanks to the Chicago HEAL Initiative, over the past eight years there has been a 69 percent increase in employment in the 18 HEAL neighborhoods—a total of 32,000 people hired, more than 15,000 Chicago Public School students in career pipeline programs, and more than 18,000 patients in trauma recovery programs.

During today’s meeting, each hospital CEO provided an update about their hospital’s efforts within the HEAL Initiative. Leaders from Rush BMO Institute for Health Equity, John H. Stroger Jr. Hospital, and University of Chicago Medicine also delivered a presentation on the Violent Crime Data Sharing Initiative, a partnership between the Chicago Department of Public Health, regional trauma centers, and Chicago-area hospitals to build, develop, and maintain a violent crime injury registry.

Durbin also offered his own reflections on establishing the Chicago HEAL Initiative and thanked each of the partners who worked alongside him to address gun violence in Chicago.

“It is hard to believe that it has been almost a decade since we came up with the Chicago HEAL Initiative. It arose from a common cause among all of you—a desire to treat and help victims of gun violence and trauma outside the operating room,” Durbin said. “Since 2018, you have invested in your surrounding neighborhoods and brought thousands of jobs to communities facing the highest levels of violence. This is why the Chicago HEAL Initiative has become a national model for hospitals to engage the communities that surround them. Through your commitment to our city and this partnership, we have saved and impacted countless lives.”

“The Chicago HEAL Initiative shows the power of collaboration and the vital role hospitals play in strengthening communities beyond the care they provide,” said A.J. Wilhelmi, President and CEO of the Illinois Health and Hospital Association. “Eight years later, our shared commitment has produced meaningful action and measurable impact, expanding economic opportunities, addressing health disparities and helping prevent violence. We commend Senator Durbin for his vision and leadership, and we remain focused on building on this progress to improve lives.”

“Eight years ago, when Chicago was facing rising health disparities, Senator Durbin brought hospitals together in an unprecedented collaboration aimed at collective healing for our most distressed communities. Our shared efforts have contributed to historic community investments and a six-decade low in homicide rates. His efforts have also led to unprecedented hospital and community partnerships and continue to set a national example for how hospitals can not only treat the consequences of violence but also use their position as economic anchors to address its underlying causes. Senator Durbin’s vision and legacy will be measured in the countless lives that have been saved in Chicago,” said David Ansell, MD, senior vice president for community health equity at Rush University Medical Center.

“Senator Durbin has demonstrated an unwavering commitment to improving the health and well-being of patients and communities across Chicagoland,” said Howard Chrisman, MD, President and Chief Executive Officer, Northwestern Medicine. “Through the Chicago HEAL Initiative, he challenged health care organizations to come together, look beyond the walls of our hospitals and invest in the communities we serve. Eight years later, that vision continues to translate into greater access to care, new economic and career opportunities, and meaningful efforts to build healthier, safer communities. Northwestern Medicine is proud to stand with Senator Durbin and our fellow health systems in advancing this important work.”

“Advocate Health Care has been a committed partner in the Chicago HEAL Initiative since its inception. We recognize that addressing the factors that contribute to violence requires a sustained commitment beyond the walls of our hospitals. It means listening to the communities most affected, supporting organizations already doing important work and investing in opportunities that can make a lasting difference. The progress of Chicago HEAL shows what is possible when hospitals and community organizations work together. We are proud of our role in this effort and remain committed to building on that progress,” said Matthew Primack, president of Advocate Illinois Masonic Medical Center.

Photos from today’s meeting are available here.

Over the last five years, Durbin has secured nearly $27 million in federal funding for the Chicago HEAL Initiative, including funding to provide supportive housing to participants of local hospital-based violence recovery programs; to establish a trauma recover center at Sinai Health System for victims of violence; and to support the expansion of Lurie Children’s Hospital’s new hospital-based violence recovery program, serving pediatric victims of violence with trauma-informed mental health and recovery services.

Additionally, because of the Chicago HEAL Initiative, there has been a 69 percent increase in annual new hires from target zip codes and more than 3,700 people have been served by case management through trauma and violence recovery programs.

Health systems involved in the Chicago HEAL Initiative include Advocate Health Care; Ann and Robert H. Lurie Children’s Hospital of Chicago; Ascension; Cook County Health; Loyola Medicine; Northwestern Medicine; Rush University Medical Cetner; Sinai Chicago; UChicago Medicine; and UI Health.

Read more about Durbin’s Chicago HEAL Initiative here.

title: ICYMI: “Grassley Targeted the Kratom Killing our Kids”
text:
Grassley targeted the kratom killing our kids

By Wendy Chamberlain

November 9, 2026

The Cedar Rapids Gazette

‘Kratom is killing our kids."

Sen. Chuck Grassley posted those words in October, and then did something about it. He led a letter, joined by Sens. Mike Lee and Susan Collins, urging the DEA and FDA to finish the emergency scheduling of a kratom compound called 7-OH and to begin permanently scheduling the whole kratom plant. He gave the agencies a deadline to answer in writing.

Those are the words every parent who has buried a child to kratom has been hoping to hear from Washington.

My son Joe was 38 when he sat down in his recliner to watch TV, drifted off to sleep and never woke up. He was my only child and a father to three boys. His toxicology report listed one cause of death: mitragynine toxicity. Mitragynine is the main drug in kratom. It was the only substance in his body.

Joe started taking kratom because he was told it was a natural, healthy pick-me-up. It hooked him the way opioids hook people. Kratom works on the same receptors in the brain as heroin and morphine. People who try to quit go through withdrawal. Some never wake up.

Grassley's letter says what families like mine have been saying at city halls and statehouses for years. He and his colleagues wrote they "worry the availability of these products is providing consumers with a false sense of security because they are readily available and marketed as 'natural.'"

The senators put numbers on the record. Poison control centers received 3,434 kratom exposure reports in 2025, roughly 1,200 percent more than a decade ago. Emergency crews logged 3,672 suspected nonfatal kratom overdoses across 38 states in just over three years. The FDA has told consumers not to use kratom at all. And the DEA has found that some semi-synthetic compounds sold in kratom-labeled products are more potent than morphine.

Iowa has confirmed 45 kratom-associated deaths since 2024, across 23 counties, with 16 of them in the first seven months of this year. Iowa Poison Control calls about kratom are up 467 percent in two years. A ban passed the Iowa House.

The industry behind kratom runs a powerful lobbying operation that fights hard against anyone who opposes it. Grassley has spent his career taking on people who thought they were too big to be questioned on behalf of families who have no lobbyist at all.

For a mother who lost her only child to a product sold next to the gum, that means more than I can say. When the chairman of the Senate Judiciary Committee puts his name on a letter like this, every grieving parent in the country knows we are not making this up, and every agency knows someone with real authority is watching.

Iowans should keep an eye on what the DEA and FDA do next. The agencies still have to act.

I can't bring Joe back. His boys are growing up without him. But for the first time in a long time, someone in Washington said out loud what killed my son. Thank you, Sen. Grassley.

Wendy Chamberlain is the founder of Kratom Danger Awareness. Her son, Joe, died of mitragynine toxicity in 2020.

title: Q&A: Rural Health on the Front Burner
text:
Q: What rural health policy are you pushing to get to the president’s desk yet this year?

A: As Iowa’s U.S. Senator, I’ve leveraged my committee assignments to help keep healthcare close to home for rural communities across our state. As then-chairman of the Senate Finance Committee, I led efforts more than two decades ago to create a federal program to boost financial viability of rural hospitals that I referred to as “tweeners.” These hospitals fell through the cracks of Medicare’s payment system and they didn’t benefit from patient volume in larger urban systems or regional referral hospitals. And yet, these “tweener” hospitals provide primary and emergency healthcare services across rural economic corridors impacting thousands of residents, workers, farmers and families in their respective regions. With passage of the Rural Community Hospital Demonstration program in 2003, my advocacy secured fairness from Medicare’s payment formula and recognized the contribution these hospitals have in our healthcare delivery system, in addition to their influence as major employers and social fabric of their respective communities. The program has been reauthorized three times. By all accounts, it’s provided a financial lifeline to rural hospitals across the country. Currently, four Iowa hospitals participate, including in Fort Dodge, Grinnell, Newton and Spirit Lake. These rural hospitals serve more than their rural communities. In Iowa, these communities are summer vacation destinations, home to county fairs and a NASCAR race and the site of a nationally recognized college.

Up to 30 hospitals may qualify for this federal program and I led the charge to make sure the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services didn’t leave eligible hospitals behind. At my urging, the Trump administration filled 10 available spaces in this program. Most recently, I’m leading a bipartisan coalition in the U.S. Senate to enact the Rural Community Hospital Demonstration Reauthorization Act that would extend the program for another five years. For participating hospitals, the innovative Medicare payment model has a proven track record of provider recruitment and retention, facility and technology upgrades and keeping healthcare services close to home. The Senate unanimously passed my bill in May and I’m pushing to get it to the president’s desk this year.

title: Amid Corruption Allegations, Senator Hassan Opens Investigation Into Purchase of ICE Detention Facility For $420 Million Above Previous Asking Price
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan (D-NH), who is expected to Chair the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee in the new Congress, opened an investigation into allegations of corruption related to the Department of Homeland Security’s (DHS) purchase of a detention facility in Appleton, Minnesota.

In 2025, DHS reportedly purchased the Prairie Correctional Facility from CoreCivic, a major immigration detention contractor, for $495 million — shortly after Minnesota declined to purchase the same facility for $75 million. After paying more than six times the price offered to the state, DHS awarded CoreCivic a contract to operate the facility. Senator Hassan requested that DHS and CoreCivic preserve all records related to the sale.

This push comes just days after CoreCivic’s CEO urged ICE to “move quickly” on these transactions following the recent election, and amid broader allegations of corruption involving DHS contracting. CoreCivic’s main competitor is GEO Group, which allegedly declined to engage in pay-to-play arrangements with Corey Lewandowski, a senior adviser to former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem. Senator Hassan previously opened an investigation into Mr. Lewandowski’s alleged corruption and abuse of taxpayer dollars during his time at the department.

“The Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee is investigating whether federal spending by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) was subject to improper influence, corruption, or other violations of federal law,” Senator Hassan wrote in letters to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and CoreCivic President and CEO Lucibeth Mayberry asking them to preserve records related to the deal.“The transaction raises additional concerns about DHS stewardship of taxpayer dollars, particularly in light of recent findings by the Government Accountability Office that DHS has wasted millions of dollars on failed detention initiatives. It also follows allegations that Corey Lewandowski, a senior adviser to former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem, sought improper payments in connection with the business interests of GEO Group, Inc., another private detention contractor.”

Read Senator Hassan’s letter to CoreCivic hereor see below, and letter to Secretary Mullin here:

Dear Ms. Mayberry:

I write to request that CoreCivic, Inc. (CoreCivic) preserve all records and communications related to Prairie Correctional Facility in Appleton, Minnesota, from January 1, 2025, to date and on an ongoing basis moving forward.

The Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee is investigating whether federal spending by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) was subject to improper influence, corruption, or other violations of federal law. New reporting states that last year DHS bought the Prairie Correctional Facility from CoreCivic for $495 million, even though CoreCivic had previously attempted to sell the facility to the State of Minnesota for only $75 million. The transaction raises additional concerns about DHS stewardship of taxpayer dollars, particularly in light of recent findings by the Government Accountability Office that DHS has wasted millions of dollars on failed detention initiatives. It also follows allegations that Corey Lewandowski, a senior adviser to former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem, sought improper payments in connection with the business interests of GEO Group, Inc., another private detention contractor. Recent reporting also indicates that the Department of Justice is conducting a criminal probe of Mr. Lewandowski related to DHS contracting.

This preservation request encompasses all records concerning the facility’s acquisition, valuation, financing, operation, and any proposed or completed sale, including appraisals, offers, negotiations, contracts, due diligence, financial analyses, internal deliberations, and communications concerning the transaction. It applies to your personal records, corporate records, and all communications with DHS, any person representing or purporting to be acting on behalf of DHS, or any consulting firms associated with DHS or its employees. It also includes any communications with White House and other Executive Office of the President personnel, including White House Border Czar Thomas Homan and Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, special government employees, and other presidential appointees or advisers concerning the facility or its acquisition.

This request applies to all potentially relevant information, regardless of format, location, or medium, including corporate and personal email accounts; electronic files and associated metadata; mobile devices; text messages; encrypted or disappearing messaging applications; social media; calendar entries; meeting notes; voicemail; and other electronic or physical records. CoreCivic should immediately suspend any automatic deletion, overwriting, or other routine destruction of potentially relevant information, including information maintained by third-party service providers, and instruct all relevant personnel to preserve responsive records. This request includes records in the possession, custody, or control of CoreCivic and its personnel, whether maintained on corporate or personal accounts or devices.

Please confirm in writing by November 30, 2026 that CoreCivic has implemented this preservation request, notified all relevant custodians, and taken appropriate steps to suspend routine deletion or destruction of potentially responsive records.

title: Hawley Bill to Designate Missouri Churchill Museum as a National Historic Landmark Signed into Law
text:
WASHINGTON — Senator Josh Hawley’s (R-Mo.) legislation to designate America’s National Churchill Museum in Fulton, Missouri, as a National Historic Landmark was signed into law by President Donald Trump.

The museum is located on the Westminster College campus in Fulton, Missouri. On March 5, 1946, Winston Churchill joined President Harry S. Truman to speak at the Missouri college. It was at this site that Churchill famously described the state of foreign affairs in Europe by saying, “From Stettin in the Baltic, to Trieste in the Adriatic, an iron curtain has descended across the continent.” In the 1960s to honor the 20th anniversary of Churchill’s visit, Westminster College imported a 17th-century church from London to Fulton. The church of St. Mary Aldermanbury was moved stone-by-stone to Westminster’s campus. Reconstruction was completed in 1969 and is today’s location of the museum.

As Senator Hawley said in a floor speech during passage, “But I would suggest even something more: as a commemoration and mark of what we hold dearest together, what we most cherish as Americans, because that church symbolizes, really, the cradle of our civilization; the values that underlie who we are as a people; the sanctity of the individual; the rights of individual conscience; the right to worship; the liberties that flow to us not from a government, not from a bureaucrat, but from almighty God…This church will stand on the campus of Westminster in Fulton, MO, blessed as a National Historic Landmark, to speak to the principles that are at the heart of the American experiment and which we reaffirm in this 250th year and which continue to shine brightly in the State of Missouri.”

title: King Bill Codifies and Prevents Conflicts of Interest on Key Health Prevention Board
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — U.S. Senator Angus King (I-ME) is introducing legislation to codify standards and norms for candidates nominated to the United States Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF). The Protect USPSTF Integrity Act would restore membership qualifications to historic standards, requiring qualified candidates be free of any outside financial – or other – conflict of interest. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) joins Senator King as an original cosponsor of this legislation.

The legislation comes on the heels of new revelations that half of the eight recent appointees for this important panel have needed waivers for financial conflicts. Last month, Senator King led his colleagues in a letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. asking him to explain his abrupt overhaul of the USPSTF, appointing eight new members whose qualifications fall short of the traditional standards of training in prevention and primary care medicine.

“The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force has been effective for over forty years because it has let science and data lead our nation’s decisions and guidance when it comes to prevention medicine,” said Senator King. “While there is certainly much to be gained from subject matter experts and professionals closely tied to the private sector, those voices should be invited to the panel’s work in limited cases where their biases or motivations wouldn’t overshadow the nation’s healthcare work. This bill gets the USPSTF back on track doing the people’s work without fear or favor.”

"With all the concern on high health care costs, insured people particularly prize that preventive care is covered without cost sharing, but that needs to be protected from attack from this administration," said Anthony Wright, executive director of Families USA. "The recent upheaval to the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force threatens the guarantee that covers such care. We support legislation and oversight to ensure an independent Task Force, which is crucial for a strong health system of primary and preventive care. When HHS can rewrite recommendations to fit its political priorities, families pay the price with medical debt and worse health outcomes. Senator King’s bill protects the Task Force’s legacy of independence and expertise, and with it, the processes that guarantee preventive care is covered without cost-sharing."

“Americans make real decisions about their health based on Task Force recommendations, from cancer screenings to blood pressure checks,” said AcademyHealth President and CEO Aaron Carroll, M.D., M.S. “Those recommendations earn their weight because they rest on transparent, rigorous, independent review of the science. We commend Senator King’s leadership in putting durable and nonpartisan safeguards around that process.”

More specifically, the Protect USPSTF Integrity Act would:

Revert to historic membership qualifications prioritizing membership expertise in preventive and primary care medicine;

Codify standards for meeting frequency in line with previous standards;

Create standards for conflicts of interest and requiring relevant recusal;

Codify the historic standards and procedures manual (published April 2023), and requiring public input for any relevant Task Force changes; and

Prevent the Secretary from changing Task Force recommendations on the basis that it no longer effectuates Departmental standards;

Created in 1984, the USPSTF has been solely comprised of primary care providers and experts in broad, general prevention medicine. Specialists have been brought in when needed on Task Force recommendations but have never been selected as USPSTF members in part to prevent conflicts of interest.

Long known as the ‘Prevention Senator,’ King has worked on policy solutions that keep Maine people healthy and lower the costs for patients and providers alike. Last year, he introduced the Preventive Health Savings Act which would instruct the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) to fully study the costs and benefits that could be seen with proposed preventive health care legislation. He has previously introduced legislation requiring private insurance plans to cover three annual primary care visits and three annual outpatient mental health or outpatient substance use disorder treatment visits, without charging a copayment, coinsurance, or deductible-related fee. In doing so, this legislation also would catch smaller, or early health symptoms before they become larger threats requiring more extensive and expensive treatments.

Senator King also introduced the ‘Stand Strong’ legislative package, which included the Stand Strong Falls Prevention Act that would require the development of a National Falls Prevention Plan, the Preventive Home Visits Act, which would provide Medicare coverage for qualified care providers to assess the safety of seniors’ homes, and the Wellness and Education for Longer Lives (WELL) for Seniors Act, which would improve Medicare’s Annual Wellness Visit to encourage seniors and their physicians to work together and confront health issues before they become more serious.

title: Klobuchar Provision Passes Senate to Help Local Communities Prepare for Snowmelt and Protect Against Flooding
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) released the following statement after the Senate passed her bipartisan provision with Sen. Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) to maintain the Aerial Snow Survey Program, which collects critical snowpack data to help local communities forecast snowmelt and protect against flooding. The provision was included in the bipartisan Weather Research and Forecasting Innovation Reauthorization Act of 2026 (Weather Act).

“This past year, communities across Minnesota faced severe weather that affected local businesses, agriculture, infrastructure, and safety. Minnesota is particularly vulnerable to flooding from snowmelt because much of our state drains into large, slow-moving rivers, including the Mississippi and the Red River of the North,” said Klobuchar. “My bipartisan provision to protect the Aerial Snow Survey Program is crucial because it ensures our local communities have the data they need to monitor snowpack, forecast snowmelt, and prepare for potential flooding.”

The Weather Act would strengthen weather forecasting and research by establishing an atmospheric river forecast improvement program, strengthening landslide preparedness, creating an official Fire Weather Services Program, and deploying new technologies to forecast droughts and harmful heat waves.

title: Markey, Wyden, Senate Democrats Demand Answers on Oz Actions to Dismantle Medicaid Fraud Prevention
text:
Senators Seek Information About CMS Compliance with Federal Fraud Prevention Laws

Text of the Letter (PDF)

Washington (November 13, 2026) – Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), member of the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, alongside Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) and four Senate Democrats, launched an inquiry into the Trump administration’s politically motivated campaign against state Medicaid programs, after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) withheld billions of dollars from Democratic-led states while dismantling the federal infrastructure designed to detect and prevent fraud.

“The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services is running the most aggressive public enforcement campaign against state Medicaid programs in the agency’s history, while accelerating the systematic dismantling of the federal infrastructure Congress funded to prevent Medicaid fraud in the first place,” the senators wrote. “That is not program integrity. That is political theater layered over a decade of neglect, with states across the country, and in particular, an overwhelming number of Democratic-led states that have become the Trump administration’s targets, left to answer for both.”

The letter, sent to CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz, comes as the Trump administration has threatened state health programs with severe funding cuts based on flawed data. CMS recently moved to withhold over billions in funding from California and Minnesota without providing any evidence of wrongdoing to the states. At the same time, the Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS OIG) decertified state Medicaid Fraud Control Units (MFCUs) in Hawaii and New York. Public reporting, including an investigation by the Associated Press, revealed that the administration’s fraud claims against New York relied on a basic math error, while other withholding actions have sparked lawsuits from states like Minnesota.

Rather than working with states to fix issues, CMS has replaced on-site reviews and dedicated oversight staff with a public relations “War Room” and unproven artificial intelligence pilots. The letter points out that the administration is violating federal law by failing to maintain the minimum required funding and staffing levels for the Medicaid Integrity Program, which was created by Congress to help states fight fraud.

Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), and Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.) also signed the letter.

title: Sen. Markey Slams Trump Administration Decision to Gut Federal Oversight of School Desegregation
text:
Letter Text (PDF)

Washington (November 13, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), member of the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee, sent a letter to Department of Justice (DOJ) then Acting Assistant Attorney General Jesus Osete to demand answers from the DOJ after its Civil Rights Division moved to dismiss more than 50 school desegregation cases. In the letter, Senator Markey urged the DOJ to explain the drastic deviation from its mandate of protecting students’ civil rights and questioned the agency’s decision to end its involvement in the cases.

In the letter, Senator Markey wrote, “In several recent cases, courts have continued to find intentional discrimination and segregated school environments. In some instances, reporting shows that racial segregation has worsened over time in school districts where DOJ has abandoned its watchdog role. And in other cases, DOJ has appeared to water down the evidentiary standards and scrutiny it applies in evaluating cases for dismissal…It appears that the Trump administration is seeking to curtail federal civil rights enforcement in education rather than using available tools to create fairer learning environments for children. In a period of rising school segregation, we should be conducting more oversight and enforcement of civil rights, not less.”

Senator Markey continued, “As we reflect on the 250th anniversary of our nation’s founding, we must strive to fulfill America’s promise that all are created equal. Since the landmark Supreme Court decision in Brown v. Board of Education and the enactment of Title IV of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the United States has made progress towards that goal. I urge the Department of Justice to ensure we remain on the path to fully achieving it, so that all our nation’s students can learn free from discrimination and in environments that allow them to achieve their full potential.”

Senator Markey requested answers by December 1 to questions including:

In how many school desegregation cases has DOJ sought or supported dismissal, termination of a desegregation order, or withdrawal of DOJ's participation since January 20, 2025?

Has DOJ changed its policies, practices, procedures, or the legal standards it applies for determining whether a school district has satisfied its desegregation obligations since January 20, 2025?

For each covered case, what evidence did DOJ review before deciding to seek or support dismissal or termination of federal oversight?

Since January 20, 2025, what steps did DOJ take to independently verify each school district’s compliance with its desegregation obligations before seeking or supporting dismissal?

In any covered case, did DOJ identify evidence of continuing segregation, racial disparities, or noncompliance with a desegregation order?

What notice and opportunity for input did DOJ provide to private plaintiffs, students, parents, and affected communities before seeking or supporting dismissal in each case?

Who participated in reviewing and approving DOJ’s decision to seek or support dismissal in each covered case?

How have staffing reductions or changes in enforcement priorities within DOJ’s Civil Rights Division affected its review and monitoring of school desegregation cases since January 20, 2025?

Senator Markey is fighting back against the Trump administration’s efforts to dismantle civil rights protections for students. In August, Senator Markey wrote to Linda McMahon, Secretary of the U.S. Department of Education, condemning the agency’s efforts to gut the Equity Assistance Centers (EACs), which provide free technical assistance to school districts, states, and communities to prepare, adopt, and implement plans to desegregate public schools in compliance with federal civil rights law.

title: NEW REPORT: Merkley Unveils Child Care Investigation Exposing Safety Lapses, Drain of Public Resources in Private Equity-Backed Centers
text:
Report Identifies Four Key Findings that Validate Public Concern Over Private Equity’s Increased Role in Child Care Industry

WASHINGTON, D.C. – As the cost of child care continues to skyrocket, U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Ranking Member of the Senate Budget Committee, released a first of its kind investigation on the effect that private equity involvement in the U.S. child care industry has on child safety. The investigation analyzed publicly available information and licensing data from three states—California, Texas, and Virginia—and focused on the two largest for-profit child care companies by capacity: KinderCare Learning Companies (KinderCare) and Learning Care Group (LCG), and their private equity backers, Partners Group and American Securities, respectively. Collectively, KinderCare and LCG have a combined licensed capacity to enroll over 375,000 children throughout the U.S.

Merkley asked both companies, and their private equity backers, to provide information and documents, such as financial records, ownership structure, tuition and cost trends, safety standards, and employment practices,to better understand the effects of private equity investment in the child care industry. All four companies responded with brief narratives and no underlying records.

“From housing to health care and now child care, private equity firms are taking control of American industries that working families rely on and running them into the ground. Wall Street’s profits-over-people playbook fails families every time, and now we have evidence that private equity is raking in bundles of cash while making child care less safe,” said Ranking Member Jeff Merkley.

“These private equity-backed child care centers refused to provide records while publicly available data from their centers show clear evidence of more complaint-triggered inspections and more serious safety violations than centers not backed by private equity; all while collecting millions of taxpayer dollars. It’s outrageous.

“Families deserve affordable, high-quality care without compromising their children’s safety. Congress must act now to curb predatory private equity practices and ensure all children have the resources they need to thrive,” Merkley concluded.

The report established four major findings, a link to the full report is available at the end of this release:

KinderCare and Learning Care Group rely heavily on public funding.

Approximately one-third of KinderCare’s and LCG’s total revenue is from public funding programs, including subsidies. KinderCare collected roughly $1 billion in subsidy-supported tuition in fiscal year 2025.

KinderCare’s and Learning Care Group’s private equity backers and owners, including Partners Group and American Securities, respectively, extracted over $1.25 billion in dividends, leaving the child care companies with substantial debt.

KinderCare and LCG have borrowed more than $1.25 billion to pay dividends to their owners: $620 million at KinderCare and at least $636 million at LCG. These obligations reduce financial flexibility and make it more important to know how the companies balance debt service and investor payments against child safety, staffing, and affordability—information the companies did not provide as requested.

Across three states, KinderCare and Learning Care Group have more frequent, more serious, and more persistent safety problems than centers not backed by private equity.

Based on Democratic staff analysis of child care licensing and violation records in California, Texas, and Virginia, KinderCare and LCG centers were cited more often, more seriously, and more repeatedly than for-profit chains with no private equity backer (“non-PE chains”) and all other centers.

The two companies drew complaint-triggered inspections at roughly twice the non-PE chain rate and up to four times the rate of all other centers and accumulated high-risk violations at up to three times the non-PE chain rate.

All four companies refused to provide key records.

Despite repeated requests, KinderCare, LCG, Partners Group, and American Securities did not provide the documents and data needed to determine how public subsidies and tuition revenues are allocated among safety, operating costs, workforce investments, debt payments, and returns to investors.

Merkley has been calling attention to the poisonous role of private equity in American life, from housing to youth sports. Merkley led the charge to kick hedge funds out of the housing market as large institutional investors gobble up homes in communities across the United States, driving up both purchase prices and rents for single-family homes. His initiative to limit institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes was included in the 21st Century Road to Housing Act, which became law this year. Also this year, he cosponsored the Let Kids Play Act, legislation to stop Wall Street from pricing kids out of sports. The proposed legislation from Sen. Chris Murphy (D-CT) bans private equity firms from taking over youth sports, shutting down the vulture practices they use to jack up costs, and getting money back to the families who have been ripped off. Merkley also previously cosponsored the Corporate Crimes Against Health Care Act, the Take Back Our Hospitals Act, and the Stop Corporate Takeovers of Physicians Act to fight back against private equity abuses in health care.

The full report, titled Who Profits from Child Care?, is HERE.
