title: DeLauro Issues Statement on U.S. Losing Measles-Elimination Status
text:
Today, U.S. Representative Rosa DeLauro (CT-03) issued the following statement on the U.S. losing its measles-elimination status:

“For 26 years, the U.S. has proudly maintained its measles elimination status, thanks to thorough immunization programs and trust in government guidance. But now, progress is unraveling. According to an NBC News investigation, across 31 states, about 70% of counties and jurisdictions fell below the target vaccination rate needed for community protection. That is unacceptable.

“President Trump and RFK Jr.’s reckless rhetoric is fueling preventable outbreaks, draining medical resources and putting our communities in danger. RFK Jr.’s misinformation campaign against vaccine-preventable diseases, like the measles, is irresponsible and should not go unchecked. He must resign so we can begin to build back the progress from the last three decades and keep our citizens safe.”

title: Congressman Deluzio Announces $70,400 for Railroad Crossing Safety Improvements in Glen Osborne
text:
CARNEGIE, PA – Today, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) announced that the Borough of Glen Osborne has received $70,400 in federal funding for a planning grant to improve safety at an at-grade railroad crossing. The crossing is at the intersection of River Road, Route 65, and Beaver Street in Glen Osborne, PA. This restructuring will improve pedestrian and vehicular safety and increase commercial mobility along the Norfolk Southern Fort Wayne Line that is owned by Norfolk Southern and used by Amtrak.

“Rail safety has been one of my top priorities since my first term in Congress,” said Congressman Deluzio. “Ninety-five percent of people in my district lives within five miles of the tracks. They cross them all the time. We need to have strong infrastructure to keep our communities safe, avoid disruptive blocked crossings, and to make sure trains get where they need to go, quickly and without incident. This funding is a huge win for the people of Glen Osborne, and I’m excited to celebrate alongside them.”

“For decades, this crossing has been a safety and noise concern and, because it’s regularly blocked by trains, an unreliable only way in and out for 46 homes and businesses in Glen Osborne and Haysville,” said Jennifer Coyne, Glen Osborne Borough Council Member. “Glen Osborne Council is grateful to the Federal Railroad Administration for funding the planning to finally eliminate the at-grade crossing, improving safety for the more than 20,000 vehicles that travel Route 65 every day and quality of life for our residents."

This funding is appropriated by Congress and granted by the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) through the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA). Further information on funding opportunities through the FRA are available here.

Congressman Deluzio has successfully pushed railroad corporations to improve and upgrade the infrastructure they own in communities across Pennsylvania’s 17th Congressional District. He did so in Midland, PA to allow for municipal stormwater pipe repairs, in Tarentum, PA to fix a deteriorating road, and in Indiana, PA to get the railroad to shore up a crumbling tunnel.

Congressman Deluzio is leading the fight to pass rail safety legislation in the House of Representatives. His efforts first started after the fiery, Norfolk Southern train derailment in East Palestine, OH happened on February 3, 2023, less than two miles from Beaver County, PA.

Congressman Deluzio’s efforts pushing for rail safety legislation include:

February 16 and 21, 2023: Visiting the East Palestine derailment site

February 21, 2023: Pushing for Norfolk Southern to cover all costs of the cleanup and the response to the derailment.

March 5, 2023: Meeting with impacted constituents in Darlington Township, PA

March 21, 2023: Introducing the bipartisan Railway Safety Act of 2023 on March 21, 2023. This is the original version of the bill that was passed via amendment today.

March 28, 2023: Hosting NTSB Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy in Beaver County and setting up meetings between her and local officials and a rail worker.

April 2023: Signing onto a full PA delegation letter to Norfolk Southern's CEO calling on their company to improve communication with local first responders in April 2023.

May 17, 2023: Meeting with former Norfolk Southern CEO Alan Shaw to push him to support the Railway Safety Act and to make Pennsylvania residents harmed by his company’s derailment whole.

August 3, 2023: Writing an op-ed in the Pittsburgh Tribune Review pushing for accountability and rail safety legislation

September 9, 2023: Visiting a Darlington Township farm and holding a press conference six months after the derailment highlighting that the Railway Safety Act had enough Republican cosponsors to pass the House with all Democrats in support.

February 2, 2024: Gave a House Floor Speech and wrote a letter to Speaker Mike Johnson pushing for passage of the Railway Safety Act.

February 16, 2024: Hosting President Joe Biden in Beaver County, PA to visit with local leaders and first responders and talk about the derailment.

February 22, 2024: Releasing a report from the Congressional Research Service on the proximity of his Western Pennsylvania constituents to freight rail tracks.

March 6, 2024: Inviting Darlington Supervisor Mike Carreon as his guest for the 2024 State of the Union.

June 6, 2024: Joining the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee with a goal of fighting for rail safety legislation.

July 3, 2024: Calling for a DOJ investigation into Norfolk Southern Railroad for their actions following the East Palestine derailment.

January 29, 2025: Calling on Vice President Vance to help pass their shared legislation, the Railway Safety Act at a press conference in Western PA.

February 3, 2025: Introduced the bipartisan Railway Safety Act of 2025.

July 22, 2025: Hosting a bipartisan roundtable with rail workers alongside East Palestine’s congressman Mike Rulli.

February 2026: Released a video pushing for action on rail safety legislation ahead of the three-year anniversary of the derailment.

February 3, 2026: Holding a bipartisan press conference on the three-year anniversary of the derailment with union leaders calling for Congress to pass the Railway Safety Act.

March 2, 2026: Reintroducing an updated version of the Railway Safety Act for 2026.

May 21, 2026: Celebrating advance of his ‘Railway Safety Act’ Through Must-Pass Transportation Bill

The Trump Administration’s efforts to freeze funding and pause federal grants has created significant uncertainty for grantees, varying by agency and program. As of now, courts have paused many of these freezes. However, Congressman Deluzio’s office will continue to monitor these developments. Please share any grant-related questions or concerns with Congressman Deluzio’s office at PA17Grants@mail.house.gov.

title: DESJARLAIS GIVES THANKS
text:
Friends,

For 16 years, I have had the distinct honor and pleasure of campaigning in 4 different versions of Tennessee’s Fourth Congressional District that have, at some point, roughly comprised over a third of the Great State of Tennessee. As the final votes have now been tabulated in this new and completely restructured district, it appears that we have a result showing my campaign has come just a few hundred votes short out of just under 200,000 votes cast.

I want everyone to know that I have very much appreciated your support from those earliest days since I ran for Congress for the first time in 2010. I would not trade this experience for anything in the world, and I could not begin to list all of the people I need to thank. I look forward to speaking with as many of you as I can soon to offer my sincerest gratitude. To Amy, Maggie, Ryan, Tatiana, Tyler, Hannah, and our extended and soon to be growing family, thank you for being with me every step of the way. To my staff, both past and present, thank you for your tireless work in helping me serve the best people in the world. And to the people of the Fourth District, thank you for giving me the trust and confidence of your votes for all these years.

I have personally reached out to Ms. Broderick to offer my congratulations and my support on this new undertaking. I am proud of the standard our office has set in terms of representing the values, interests, and needs of our district. We all leave here with our heads held high, and we hope the Fourth District continues to receive the attention and care it so richly deserves. All of us hope that the new Member of Congress feels the same level of awe and gratitude for this tremendous undertaking that I felt every day I had the privilege of serving.

To everything, there is a season, and I will leave here with great love and affection for my time in the Congress, thankful for all of the friends made, and very much looking forward to the next chapter of my life.

title: Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. Introduces Bill that Codifies and Prevents Conflicts of Interest on Key Health Prevention Board
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03) introduced Protect USPSTF Integrity Act codify standards and norms for candidates nominated to the United States Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF). The measure would restore membership qualifications to historic standards, requiring qualified candidates to be free of any outside financial or other – conflict of interest. U.S. Representatives Kelly Morrison (D-MN) and Herbert Conaway (D-NJ) are original cosponsors. U.S. Senators Angus King (I-ME) and Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) introduced the bill in the Senate.

The legislation comes on the heels of new revelations that half of the eight recent appointees for this important panel have needed waivers for financial conflicts. Last month, Senator King led his colleagues in a letter to HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. asking him to explain his abrupt overhaul of the USPSTF, appointing eight new members whose qualifications fall short of the traditional standards of training in prevention and primary care medicine.

“We must not allow undermining the health of the American people to become a path to corrupt self-enrichment,” said Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. “The United States Preventive Services Task Force should be solely focused on ensuring preventive care is grounded in science—not enriching task force members and their affiliates. I am proud to put forth legislation that will protect the integrity of this task force, to make sure no conflicts of interest influence how this group operates or makes decisions."

“The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force has been effective for over forty years because it has let science and data lead our nation’s decisions and guidance when it comes to prevention medicine,” said Senator King. “While there is certainly much to be gained from subject matter experts and professionals closely tied to the private sector, those voices should be invited to the panel’s work in limited cases where their biases or motivations wouldn’t overshadow the nation’s healthcare work. This bill gets the USPSTF back on track doing the people’s work without fear or favor.”

"With all the concern on high health care costs, insured people particularly prize that preventive care is covered without cost sharing, but that needs to be protected from attack from this administration," said Anthony Wright, executive director of Families USA. "The recent upheaval to the U.S. Preventive Services Task Force threatens the guarantee that covers such care. We support legislation and oversight to ensure an independent Task Force, which is crucial for a strong health system of primary and preventive care. When HHS can rewrite recommendations to fit its political priorities, families pay the price with medical debt and worse health outcomes. Senator King’s bill protects the Task Force’s legacy of independence and expertise, and with it, the processes that guarantee preventive care is covered without cost-sharing."

“Americans make real decisions about their health based on Task Force recommendations, from cancer screenings to blood pressure checks,” said AcademyHealth President and CEO Aaron Carroll, M.D., M.S. “Those recommendations earn their weight because they rest on transparent, rigorous, independent review of the science. We commend Senator King’s leadership in putting durable and nonpartisan safeguards around that process.”

More specifically, the Protect USPSTF Integrity Act would:

Revert to historic membership qualifications prioritizing membership expertise in preventive and primary care medicine;

Codify standards for meeting frequency in line with previous standards;

Create standards for conflicts of interest and requiring relevant recusal;

Codify the historic standards and procedures manual (published April 2023), and requiring public input for any relevant Task Force changes; and

Prevent the Secretary from changing Task Force recommendations on the basis that it no longer effectuates Departmental standards;

Created in 1984, the USPSTF has been solely comprised of primary care providers and experts in broad, general prevention medicine. Specialists have been brought in when needed on Task Force recommendations but have never been selected as USPSTF members in part to prevent conflicts of interest.

title: Congresswoman Escobar Leads Over 20 Democrats in Urging DHS Inspector General to Investigate Big Bend Border Wall Contracts
text:
Today, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) led a group of 22 other Democrats in a letter to U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of Inspector General (OIG) Joseph Cuffari urging him to investigate the nearly $7.5 billion in taxpayer funds for border infrastructure projects in the Big Bend Border Patrol Sector.

Joining Congresswoman Escobar (in alphabetical order) are Representatives Greg Casar (TX-35), Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Lloyd Doggett (TX-37), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-7), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Dan Goldman (NY-10), Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34), Al Green (TX-9), Jared Huffman (CA-2), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-8), Stephen Lynch (MA-8), Seth Magaziner (RI-2), Christian Menefee (TX-18), Dave Min (CA-47), Brittany Petterson (CO-7), Emily Randall (WA-6), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Paul Tonko (NY-20), Gabe Vazquez (NM-2), and Nydia Velazquez (NY-7).

The full letter can be found here or below:

Inspector General Cuffari:

We write to urgently request that the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Office of Inspector General (OIG) investigate the contracting process, potential political influence, and award of $7.5 billion in taxpayer funds for massive border infrastructure projects in and around the Big Bend Border Patrol Sector in Texas, including Big Bend National Park.

On October 15, 2025, former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem waived virtually every provision of federal law “with respect to all contracting actions necessary for the construction of physical barriers and roads” in the Big Bend Sector of Texas. This was followed by additional waivers of environmental, historic preservation, and other laws that would ordinarily provide independent review of federal actions affecting more than 500 miles of borderlands. In addition to Big Bend National Park, one of the nation’s most treasured landscapes, these waivers also impact Big Bend Ranch State Park, Texas’ largest state park, and hundreds of miles of privately owned land.

Publicly available information raises serious questions about how these contracts were awarded, whether political relationships played any role in contractor selection, whether the circumvention of normal contracting and oversight safeguards was in the public interest, and whether the enormous expenditures are justified by an operational need.

The Big Bend Sector, and especially Big Bend National Park, encompasses some of the most remote, rugged, and waterless terrain along the southern border. Local law enforcement officials and elected leaders from across the political spectrum, as well as former National Park Service officials, have questioned the need for extensive physical barriers or other major border security infrastructure in this region.

The available data further raises questions about the justification for the waivers or these massive contracts. The Big Bend Sector includes 26% of the southern border, but CBP’s published data shows that in the 5 years that DHS used to justify these actions, it accounted for less than 1% of the apprehensions of migrants across that same border. The national park accounted for only 0.016% of apprehensions in the same period despite spanning 6% of the southern border. DHS’ own press releases cites that apprehensions in the sector have fallen sharply in recent years.

Nevertheless, DHS designated the region an "area of high illegal entry" with an "acute and immediate need" for border infrastructure. “High illegal entry” is a legal necessity established by the Congress under Section 102(a) of the Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act (IIRIRA) to allow the Department to waive legal requirements and expedite construction.

We believe the DHS Office of the Inspector General has a responsibility to scrutinize how the Department has made the decisions, and the impact of those decisions, regarding whether the area in question is truly an area of high illegal entry, whether the subsequently awarded contracts were properly issued (even in light of the waivers), and whether the resulting expenditures are in the public interest. The scale of the expenditures is enormous. Five contracts, totaling $7.5 billion, have been awarded in the Sector.

These contracts include:

$1.0 billion to Barnard Construction (BB1 Project)

$1.2 billion to Fisher Sand & Gravel (BB2 Project)

$960.4 million to Barnard Construction (BB3 Project)

$1.7 billion to Southwest Valley Constructors for work associated with Big Bend National Park. (BB4 project)

$2.6 billion to Fisher Sand & Gravel for work in the Lower Canyons region downstream of the national park (BB5 project)

These expenditures warrant scrutiny because of the contracting practices and political relationships surrounding some of the companies receiving them. Public reporting has documented substantial political connections involving contractors that have received significant border construction awards.

Barnard Construction Chairman Tim Barnard and his wife donated approximately $1 million to a Trump campaign fundraising committee during the 2024 election cycle. Barnard Construction has subsequently received billions of dollars in border construction contracts, including a $1.6 billion contract for approximately 112 miles of border wall in New Mexico that was awarded without competitive bidding based on an asserted need for urgency.

Fisher Sand & Gravel has also been the subject of previous scrutiny over political influence in federal contracting. During President Trump's first term, the company received a $400 million border wall contract after President Trump personally and repeatedly urged federal officials to consider Fisher for the work. Those circumstances prompted a Department of Defense Inspector General review. Public reporting has also connected Fisher to a consulting firm formerly associated with White House Border Czar Tom Homan. Fisher reportedly paid Homan's consulting firm as much as $186,000 while seeking border wall work. The administration has stated that Mr. Homan does not participate in the actual awarding of contracts.

These facts do not by themselves establish that contracts were improperly awarded. They do, however, create a strong public interest in an independent review of whether political relationships, communications, or influence played any role in DHS contracting decisions.

The processes CBP used to award these contracts lacked any transparency, and there has been no opportunity for public oversight of the contracts, or even for the public to understand the scope of the contracts.

A lawsuit brought by a competing contractor – that was subsequently withdrawn -

- alleged that solicitations for broader Texas border work were not genuine competitive opportunities and that winningbidders were subsequently required to perform work outside the scope originally advertised. When discovery was sought in that litigation, DHS moved to seal materials including depositions and affidavits.

At the same time, DHS and CBP have repeatedly changed their public descriptions of what is being built in the Big Bend Sector.

CBP materials initially showed a border wall through the region. The wall later disappeared from public maps, then reappeared. In May, CBP publicly stated that there would be no wall in Big Bend National Park. Approximately one week later, DHS awarded a $1.7 billion contract whose contracting records described work associated with a border wall in the national park. More recently, CBP has described construction inside the park as involving roads, technology, and vehicle barriers.

Taken together, these circumstances warrant an independent investigation. We therefore request that the DHS Office of Inspector General examine:

Whether political relationships, communications, campaign contributions, or other political considerations played any role in the selection of contractors or award of contracts for border infrastructure in the Big Bend Sector;

Whether contracts awarded for work in the Big Bend Sector were awarded through full and open competition and, where they were not, whether DHS properly justified the use of noncompetitive or expedited procurement procedures;

Whether DHS adequately evaluated the operational need, cost effectiveness, and alternatives before committing billions of taxpayer dollars to border infrastructure in a region with comparatively low and declining levels of unlawful crossings;

Whether the scope of work ultimately assigned to contractors materially differed from the work described during the solicitation and bidding process, and whether any such changes disadvantaged competing bidders or increased costs to taxpayers;

Whether any current or former administration officials participated in, attempted to influence, or communicated with DHS or CBP officials concerning the selection of particular contractors;

Whether DHS's waiver of environmental and other statutory requirements, together with limitations on public access to contracting information, diminished safeguards against waste, fraud, abuse, or mismanagement; and

Whether the contracts and expenditures associated with these projects comply with applicable ethics, appropriations, and other federal requirements.

Big Bend National Park is an irreplaceable public resource. Taxpayers deserve confidence that decisions affecting it and the surrounding region— and billions of dollars in federal spending — are based on legitimate public needs rather than political influence or private advantage.

We expect a written response to this letter with an associated timeline for an OIG investigation no later than November 27, 2026. We further expect that the findings of such an investigation be made public.

title: Fedorchak nominates three North Dakota students to U.S. Service Academies
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Julie Fedorchak (R-ND) today nominated three North Dakota high school students, Samuel Chase, Marcus Johnson, and Tyler Warren, to U.S. service academies. The students, from Fargo and Minot, have demonstrated outstanding academic achievement, leadership, and a strong commitment to serving their country.

“North Dakota has a proud tradition of military service, and these three young men are ready to carry that legacy forward,” Fedorchak said. “Nominating outstanding young North Dakotans to our nation’s service academies is a great honor and responsibility. These students have distinguished themselves through their academic achievements, athletics, leadership, and service. I look forward to seeing all they accomplish at their academies, throughout their military careers, and beyond. Wherever life takes them, I believe they will make North Dakota proud.”

A congressional nomination is an important step toward attending one of our nation’s service academies. While a nomination does not guarantee admission, it allows these students to move forward in a competitive selection process. Fedorchak congratulates these outstanding North Dakotans on reaching this stage and wishes them continued success as they pursue their goals of serving our country.

Samuel Chase – Fargo North High School, U.S. Naval Academy

Inspired by his family's military service, Samuel hopes to attend the U.S. Naval Academy and become a commissioned Navy officer. His grandfather, Ralph Chase, served aboard the USS Maryland during World War II, while his other grandfather, Bernard Hoefgen, served in the National Guard. A visit to the Naval Academy further strengthened his desire to serve and pursue the leadership opportunities and challenges of a Navy career.

Samuel has earned a 4.0 unweighted GPA while excelling in athletics as a varsity basketball and baseball player. As basketball team captain, he has set school records for three-point baskets in both a single game and a season.

Marcus Johnson – Fargo North High School, U.S. Merchant Marine Academy

With both grandfathers having served in Vietnam, Marcus has a strong family connection to military service. His interest in service and opportunities on the water led him to pursue the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy. title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Announces Completion of the New Portal North Bridge
text:
Above: Gottheimer Announces Completion of New Portal North Bridge.

KEARNY, NJ — Today, Monday, November 16, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) announced the completion of track cutover work to the new Portal North Bridge, which operates over the Hackensack River. This completion marks another step toward finishing the Gateway Project that Gottheimer funded through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law that he helped write, negotiate, and sign into law.

Watch Gottheimer’s remarks here.

“For too long, we kicked the can down the road while our nation’s bridges, roads, and tunnels continued to crumble. Today, we retire a 116-year-old bridge,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “The Gateway Project will create more than 95,000 good-paying jobs, many of them union jobs, and support many more through new businesses and investment in Jersey and New York.”

Congressman Gottheimer helped secure critical federal funding in 2021 and 2026 for the Gateway Project by helping write, negotiate, and pass the Bipartisan Infrastructure Bill, which invests in the Gateway Train Tunnel Project, the Portal North Bridge, and additional major improvements to New Jersey’s rail infrastructure. More than 200,000 NJ TRANSIT and Amtrak riders rely on this critical stretch of track each day to see loved ones, attend doctors’ appointments, or commute to work.

The Portal North Bridge is a critical component of the Gateway Program, which will eventually double rail capacity between Newark and New York. Both tracks of the new Portal North Bridge are now in service, which officially retires the 116-year-old swing bridge that has been a chronic source of delays on the Northeast Corridor — securing the 20 percent of our nation’s GDP that depends on its reliability.

Gottheimer was joined at the celebration by New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, Congressman Rob Menendez, Congresswoman LaMonica McIver, Congresswoman Analilia Mejia, Assemblyman Craig J. Coughlin, Deputy FRA Administrator Drew Feeley, Regional Administrator Michael Culotta, NJDOT Commissioner Priya Jain, NJ TRANSIT President & CEO Kris Kolluri, Amtrak Interim President Byl Herrmann, Council President Hudson City Building and Construction Trades Pat Kelleher, Dockbuilders Local 1556, Carpenters Local 253, Ironworkers Local 11, Laborers Local 471, IUOE Local 825, Teamsters Local 560, and IBEW Local 164.

title: Dr. Joyce’s Mobility Legislation Signed into Law
text:
November 16, 2026

Congressman Visits Cambria County Business to Highlight Expanded Access

Washington, D.C.– Last week, Congressman John Joyce’s legislation, the Choices for Increased Mobility Act of 2025, was signed into law. Today, Dr. Joyce visited Laurel Medical Solutions in Ebensburg to celebrate the new law and meet with constituents.

H.R. 1703, the Choices for Increased Mobility Act of 2025, is commonsense legislation that gives Medicare beneficiaries greater access to titanium and carbon fiber wheelchairs, which are significantly lighter and easier for them and their families to lift and carry.

"The enactment of this legislation will positively impact the lives of countless individuals and caregivers by supporting their purchase or rental of an ultralightweight manual wheelchair,"said Congressman John Joyce, M.D."Without the burden of cost, persons with disabilities should have access to devices of their choice that facilitate mobility and free them from the physical discomforts that can be associated with the movement and storage of a traditional wheelchair. The clarification of payment rules for manual wheelchairs under part B of the Medicare program is a triumph for all who seek to continue or expand participation in activities outside the home with ease and comfort."

Prior to enactment of the law, Medicare beneficiaries who chose an ultralightweight wheelchair were required to pay the full purchase price upfront and then seek reimbursement from Medicare for only the amount Medicare would have covered for a standard aluminum wheelchair.

Under the new law, Medicare will pay suppliers directly for qualifying titanium or carbon fiber wheelchairs for eligible beneficiaries. Beneficiaries are responsible only for any additional costs associated with optional upgrades that exceed Medicare's covered amount, eliminating the need for substantial upfront out-of-pocket payments.

title: SHNS: Clark: Dems prioritizing reversal of Medicaid, Medicare cuts
text:
Reversing healthcare funding cuts that are set to take effect over the next few months is top of mind for U.S. Rep. Katherine Clark as she and fellow House Democrats eye affordability moves that would help those receiving Medicaid and Medicare public health insurance benefits.

“I think one of the first things that we are going to do is to make sure that we are putting back the cuts, especially to healthcare, that we are going to see take impact in the next few months. The administration and Republicans in Congress designed these cuts so that the full harm of them would not kick in until after the midterm elections,” Clark said Monday while visiting Tufts University for a ribbon cutting and tour of the school’s Innovation Hub for Food and Materials located on Boston Avenue.

Clark, who is seeking to become House majority leader in January, and other House Democrats seeking leadership positions have said their agenda for the next session will focus on lowering costs.

“So, restoring those cuts to Medicare, to Medicaid, to the [Affordable Care Act] to veterans’ benefits and food programs, addressing tariffs, making sure that we are also cleaning up corruption in government and making our campaign financing reforms. Those are going to be top priorities as we move forward,” Clark said.

Reversing the healthcare policy changes and funding cuts Republicans have approved could be costly and would largely affect low- and middle-income adults as well as seniors, those with disabilities, immigrants and rural healthcare centers.

Clark, currently the House minority whip, said the move would help families manage their premium costs as well as stabilize community health centers and major hospitals.

“All of this is how we have to look at stabilizing and changing our healthcare system. It’s the first step to making it patient focused and not insurance focused,” she said.

House and Senate Democrats who are teed up to control Congress in January must still work with President Donald Trump over the next two years. Asked about her outlook on passing policies with Trump still in office, Clark said House Democrats plan to get bills on his desk and what he does with them is up to him.

“We’re going to keep putting forward the policies that will lower costs, expand access to healthcare and hold people who cheat Americans accountable,” she said. “We’re going to put it before the House for votes and if he doesn’t want to go along, we will be very clear about who’s standing between families being able to get a foothold in this economy and progress that we want to make.”

Less than two weeks after the election where Democrats saw historic wins over Republicans, there is already tension brewing between the Trump administration and House Democrats. The latest flashpoint surrounds a rare nationwide ground stop the Federal Aviation Administration implemented for several hours on Friday.

U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who Trump appointed in 2024, leaned on the issue to call for tens of billions in additional funding from Congress to upgrade the country’s aging air traffic control system. Democrats have reportedly criticized the request, saying Congress has approved $12.5 billion for upgrades and the administration has spent only $1 billion. Earlier today, Trump blamed old technology and Democrats, including former President Joe Biden, for the ground stop, according to The Associated Press.

“We all want safe airspace. We want people to be able to rely on secure air travel. But what we have here is mismanagement. We have Secretary Duffy coming out before he even knows what went wrong, demanding more funding. Well, where’s the accountability for the billions of dollars already under his control that he has not spent?” Clark said on Monday.

“I can tell you that Democrats, as we come into the majority, we want to invest in the technology to keep our skies safe and to be able to have travel and tourism be conducted with people being able to rely on schedules and to know that their family and loved ones will arrive safely,” she continued. “This is the work that we are going to challenge this administration to do, instead of playing a blame game. Get to work, manage this correctly, and deliver for the American people.”

Clark spoke with reporters after touring Tufts University’s recently launched research and development center that’s meant to help connect researchers and entrepreneurs in the food and materials innovation sector with industry partners. The hub is funded with $4.6 million from the university and $2.1 million from the Massachusetts Technology Collaborative along with philanthropic donations. The center has space for 10 to 15 startups and has four operating in the space, said Matt McNulty, associate director of Tufts University’s Center for Cellular Agriculture.

“Massachusetts has always been a leader not just in our country but globally, in innovation and taking things out of the academic lab into the marketplace and everything at this hub is playing on those strengths,” Clark said. “But there have been real challenges as this administration and Republicans in Congress have made huge cuts to basic research, to the funding that people are depending on. Whether it’s creating new sources for food, or whether it is that breakthrough in cancer treatment. And so our goal is to help not only support this hub, but bring back those research dollars that Americans deserve.”

title: Tufts Now: Innovation Hub for Food and Materials Accelerates Entrepreneurship and Product Development
text:
University, industry, and government leaders gathered on November 16 to celebrate the grand opening of Tufts’ Innovation Hub for Food and Materials at 200 Boston Avenue in Medford.

The ribbon-cutting ceremony, led by Tufts Vice President for Research and Innovation Bernard Arulanandam, included remarks from Tufts President Sunil Kumar, U.S representative Katherine Clark, Medford Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn, and BioLabs Chief Operating Officer Steven Palmer. Massachusetts Senator Edward Markey delivered a video message. The speaking program was followed by a tour of the cutting-edge 17,000-square-foot facility and featured demonstrations of the technology that innovators can use to develop and test new products.

“The Innovation Hub applies Tufts’ interdisciplinary strengths across engineering, nutrition, and biomedical sciences and engineering, to accelerate the work of research and industry partners,” Kumar said in advance of the event. “This work will highlight the real-world impact we can have when we collaborate with public and private partners beyond the academy.”

The facility includes 46 lab benches; specialized equipment for biotech materials processing, food formulation and sensory testing, and pilot-scale production of future foods and other materials. An on-site test kitchen gives developing food companies a fully equipped space for functional testing and for community and established businesses to refine their products; researchers can use it to prepare foods for studies, from consumer insights to nutrition testing.

Clients will also have access to experts from the School of Engineering and the Gerald J. and Dorothy R. Friedman School of Nutrition Science and Policy, including those affiliated with the Tufts University Center for Cellular Agriculture, the Food and Nutrition Innovation Institute, and the Tufts Gordon Institute Auster Center for Applied Innovation and Research.

“This is how we support small businesses. It’s how we empower researchers to discovery and empower entrepreneurs to bring those discoveries to life through the market,” Clark said in her remarks. “This new innovation hub will give them the tools that they need… That’s how America remains the envy of the world and Massachusetts remains the envy of America.”

As the Tufts Innovation Hub ribbon was being cut, three incubator tenants were already working on the future of food. EntoCellular uses insect cell cultures to produce sustainable pet foods; Galy has developed more efficient ways of growing products, like cocoa and cotton, which have historically been resource-intensive to produce; and Deco Labs develops animal-free ingredients for cell culture that can support production of sustainable food and pharmaceuticals.

In his video remarks, Markey emphasized the potential for this unique facility. “The Innovation Hub for Food and Materials will be the first of its kind—and the first small business incubator here in Medford. This will be the Kendall Square for food science and biomaterials, right here on Boston Ave.,” he said. “It takes an incredible partnership of academia and community to get done, and I’m grateful for leaders in Tufts and in Medford for making it happen.”

“I’m proud to see this kind of innovation taking place at Tufts. This is a great opportunity for Tufts students to expand their learning by engaging in hands-on research and exploring new possibilities in science and technology,” Lungo-Koehn said. “I look forward to seeing the discoveries and opportunities that come from this new center, and I wish the entire Tufts community success as they begin this exciting new chapter.”

At the core of the partnership are the university, philanthropic, and governmental organizations that contributed to building and launching the hub. Tufts has made a $4.6 million investment. Bobby Kishore has agreed to provide $1 million to support innovation and start-ups in the future food domain to catalyze growth in new ventures through augmentation with technology to enhance impact. And the state-sponsored Massachusetts Technology Collaborative (MassTech) has awarded the project a $2.1 million grant.

“The Massachusetts Manufacturing Innovation Initiative helps businesses and academic institutions invest in new equipment to scale their production capabilities, forge new partnerships and bring products to market,” said Lily Fitzgerald, director of the Center for Advanced Manufacturing, a division of MassTech. “With the support of state dollars, the Tufts University Innovation Hub for Food and Materials will help Massachusetts lead in food innovation and create new jobs in this growing industry.”

title: Continuing Discussions with DHS on EVS-TAP
text: Following the Department of Homeland Security's suspension of EVS-TAP, I have remained in regular communication with DHS leadership to better understand the concerns behind the decision and make clear the serious consequences it could have for the CNMI economy. Good public policy requires a full understanding of the interests being pursued and the consequences, both intended and unintended, of the decisions being made. That is especially important when those decisions affect an economy already facing tremendous challenges. Continuing these conversations, last week I met with U.S. Customs and Border Protection Commissioner Rodney Scott and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services Deputy Director James Kernochan to discuss the concerns that led to the suspension and what steps the federal government and the CNMI government can take to address them and restore visitor arrivals to our islands. Thank you, Commissioner Scott, for continuing this important conversation. I look forward to our continued work together toward getting visitors back to the CNMI.

title: Disaster Loan Consistency Act Passes House
text: The House passed H.R. 10355, the Disaster Loan Outreach Consistency Act, a bill I co-led with Congresswoman Analila Mejia of New Jersey, to help ensure small businesses and disaster survivors receive accurate, consistent, and up-to-date information about federal disaster loan assistance. The legislation would require the Small Business Administration to establish standardized procedures for disaster loan outreach materials, including press releases and fact sheets issued by its disaster field operations centers. A May 2026 Government Accountability Office report found inconsistencies in SBA’s disaster loan outreach materials across its two field operations centers. We in the Marianas know just how important timely, accurate disaster assistance information is, and this bill will help ensure no survivor receives different answers simply because their disaster is handled by a different SBA field office. I look forward to working with my bipartisan colleagues to secure its passage through the Senate into law.

title: Legislation to Support Marianas Veterans Passes House
text: On Veterans Day, the House of Representatives passed H.R. 9237, the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act. This major bipartisan package combines roughly 60 veterans bills to expand benefits, health care access, caregiver support, and VA services including two of my priorities: the TRAVEL Act (H.R. 3400) and the U.S. Vets of the FAS Act (H.R. 6652). The TRAVEL Act authorizes VA to send traveling physicians to serve up to one year in the Northern Mariana Islands and other U.S. territories, closing critical gaps. The U.S. Vets of the FAS Act requires the VA to formalize agreements with the Freely Associated States (Palau, Federated States of Micronesia, and Marshall Islands) to deliver telehealth and mail-order pharmacy services to eligible veterans. H.R. 9237 now goes to the Senate for consideration.

title: Rep. Laurel Lee’s Bipartisan Safe Cloud Storage Act Passes Congress, Heads to President’s Desk
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, the U.S. Senate passed Congresswoman Laurel Lee’s (R-FL) bipartisan Safe Cloud Storage Act, sending the legislation to the President’s desk to be signed into law. The bill, which previously passed the U.S. House of Representatives, will modernize how law enforcement securely stores and processes digital evidence in child sexual exploitation investigations, helping investigators identify victims and bring offenders to justice.

Rep. Lee introduced the House legislation alongside bipartisan co-leads Representatives Steve Cohen (D-TN), Madeleine Dean (D-PA), and Brad Knott (R-NC). Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) and Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) championed the legislation in the Senate.

The legislation addresses a growing challenge facing law enforcement as the volume of digital evidence in child sexual exploitation investigations continues to increase. Many agencies still rely on physical storage systems such as thumb drives, external hard drives, and local servers to manage highly sensitive evidence. The Safe Cloud Storage Act removes a legal barrier that has limited law enforcement's ability to work with trusted cloud service providers while maintaining strict security and accountability requirements.

“Every minute matters when law enforcement is working to identify a child being exploited and bring the predator responsible to justice,”said Rep. Laurel Lee.“Our investigators should have access to modern, secure technology that allows them to work as quickly and effectively as possible. The Safe Cloud Storage Act removes an unnecessary legal barrier that has prevented law enforcement from fully utilizing trusted cloud technology while maintaining strong safeguards for this incredibly sensitive evidence. With this bipartisan legislation now headed to the President's desk, we are one step closer to giving law enforcement the tools they need to protect vulnerable children, identify victims, and hold predators accountable. I am proud to have led this effort in the House and look forward to seeing it signed into law.”

"We must do everything in our power to protect children from abuse and prosecute those who commit such despicable crimes — that requires modernizing how law enforcement stores sensitive information so that they can bring more abusers to justice,” Rep. Dean said. “Many police departments still rely on older technology like thumb drives to store materials for child sexual abuse material (CSAM) investigations, which slows down investigations and lets criminals stay one or two steps ahead. Our bipartisan bill is a commonsense measure enabling law enforcement to use secure cloud-based storage, helping them to track, stop, and prosecute more of these heinous crimes. I am thrilled that the Safe Cloud Storage Act will become law, and I’m grateful to my colleagues in the House and Senate for their efforts in its passage.”

"I am thrilled that the SAFE Cloud Storage Act passed through Congress tonight. It was an honor to work with Congresswoman Lee on this critical legislation, and it is now to the President’s desk,” said Congressman Brad Knott. "When I prosecuted cases dealing with sensitive evidence, I saw first hand how essential it is to both modernize evidence handling and its production in these cases. This bill will enable more thorough investigations and efficient convictions. In so doing, it will help ensure that serious criminals are more readily stopped and punished while protecting victims from pervasive uncertainties. I look forward to it becoming law and urge its quick signing.”

“We should do everything we can to protect children from abuse and prosecute those who commit these despicable crimes,” said Rep. Steve Cohen. “That requires modernizing how law enforcement stores sensitive information and indemnifying third parties who store it so that prosecutors can bring more abusers to justice, The Safe Cloud Storage Act will do that.”

The Safe Cloud Storage Act provides limited civil and criminal liability protections to approved cloud service providers contracted by federal, state, and local law enforcement or prosecutorial agencies to securely store and process digital evidence related to child sexual exploitation investigations. The legislation requires covered providers to comply with cybersecurity requirements and establishes exceptions to its liability protections for certain misconduct.

The legislation builds on the framework established by the bipartisan REPORT Act, which was signed into law in 2024 and provided limited liability protections for vendors contracted by the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) to store and transfer child sexual abuse material for investigative purposes.

The Safe Cloud Storage Act is supported by law enforcement, child protection, and victim advocacy organizations, including the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, the Fraternal Order of Police, Thorn, Raven, the Child Rescue Coalition, the National District Attorneys Association, the National Center on Sexual Exploitation, the Association of State Criminal Investigative Agencies, and International Justice Mission.

Key Provisions of the Safe Cloud Storage Act:

Modernizes Evidence Storage: Enables law enforcement-approved cloud service providers to securely store and process digital evidence used in child sexual exploitation investigations.

Provides Limited Liability Protections: Protects approved vendors from certain civil and criminal liability when handling qualifying evidence on behalf of law enforcement.

Maintains Accountability: Preserves liability in circumstances excluded by the legislation and ensures protections are limited to qualifying vendors acting within the scope of their work with law enforcement.

Strengthens Cybersecurity: Requires approved vendors to comply with stringent cybersecurity requirements to protect highly sensitive evidence.

With its passage in both chambers of Congress, the Safe Cloud Storage Act now heads to the President's desk for his signature. Once signed into law, the legislation will help law enforcement more efficiently manage growing volumes of digital evidence, strengthen investigations, and support efforts to identify victims and hold child predators accountable.

title: MATSUI AND COLLEAGUES CALL ON FCC TO ABANDON AGENDA TO DISCONTINUE LANDLINE SERVICES FOR CALIFORNIANS
text:
Washington, D.C. – As the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) moves to clear the way for AT&T to discontinue landline services essential to Californians, Representatives Doris Matsui (D-Calif.-07), Jimmy Panetta (D-Calif.-19) Mike Thompson (D-Calif.-04), and Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) are pushing the FCC to drop this effort that will prevent California from ensuring vulnerable and rural communities have reliable landline phone service.

This new inquiry follows a July 2026 letter the lawmakers sent to the FCC Chairman Brendan Carr urging him to stop AT&T from shutting down landline services; however, rather than address the lawmakers’ concerns, the FCC approved AT&T’s application to decommission approximately 360 wire centers in California. On October 30, the FCC issued a draft order to preempt California’s carrier of last resort (COLR) rules – the exact issue the lawmakers warned about.

If the FCC adopts this order, it will eliminate California’s ability to require proof that wireless or fiber replacements actually work before copper wires are discontinued. It will also allow AT&T to discontinue landline service at several hundred wire centers in the state – affecting roughly 184,000 residential customers and 15,000 business customers in rural areas in California.

“These rules require telecommunications companies to provide basic phone service to anyone within their service area who requests it, ensuring that no Californian is left without access to essential communications services, including 911,” the lawmakers wrote.

While the transition from copper to fiber optic systems and other technologies will modernize communications systems, the lawmakers emphasize the need to ensure service reliability and accessibility for communities.

“We urge you to provide the public with sufficient time and a fair opportunity to review and weigh in on the full text of the order, rather than rush through a final decision that undermines public trust…We share the Commission’s goal in modernizing our nation’s communications networks and expanding fiber-optic infrastructure to underserved communities. However, these efforts must be executed carefully, in a manner that protects vulnerable communities during emergencies and outages and preserves universal telephone service for all Americans,” the lawmakers concluded.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear Chairman Carr:

We write again to raise concern over the Federal Communications Commission’s (FCC) efforts to eliminate California’s legal authority to require carriers to verify that wireless or fiber replacements function properly before retiring copper telephone networks. The draft order you circulated to the Commission on October 30, 2026, purports to preempt the California Public Utilities Commission’s (CPUC) Carrier of Last Resort (COLR) rules. These rules require telecommunications companies to provide basic phone service to anyone within their service area who requests it, ensuring that no Californian is left without access to essential communications services, including 911.

On July 22, 2026, twenty-eight members of the California Congressional delegation asked the Commission to deny AT&T’s petitions, and that request still stands. Following that letter, the Commission approved AT&T’s application to decommission approximately 360 wire centers in California covering about 184,000 residential locations in California.

If the FCC issues this purported blanket preemption, it will take away any oversight ability of California and other states to make sure sufficient alternative service exists without putting any system in place at the federal level to make that determination. In March, the Commission replaced its adequate replacement test with a carrier certification that a replacement service is available. The FCC relies on coverage reported by carriers and does not independently verify that there is alternative functioning service in the areas where copper will be retired. Without verification or oversight, California residents, including those in High Fire Threat Districts, will continue to lose basic service without access to an adequate replacement.

It should be noted that California’s rules do not stand in the way of modernization and are not meant to relegate Californians to outdated technology. The CPUC has told the FCC that its rules require reliable minimum service but do not require that service to be delivered over copper. If carriers can provide a replacement that meets California’s reliability standards, nothing prevents them from retiring copper systems. Congress preserved this protection in Section 253(b) of the Communications Act to allow states to create any necessary requirements to protect public safety, safeguard consumers’ rights, and ensure the continued quality of telecommunications services.

This month, the Commission is allowing copper retirement to begin in eighteen states – Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, and Wisconsin. Those customers’ experiences over time may be helpful in determining the adequacy of wireless replacements. However, there is no dedicated mechanism for consumers to report problems with replacement service after discontinuance. These problems could range from thousands of blocked calls to 911 to problems with TTY devices, medical alert systems, or home alarms. Rural communities and elderly populations will be most at risk.

We urge you to provide the public with sufficient time and a fair opportunity to review and weigh in on the full text of the order, rather than rush through a final decision that undermines public trust. As carriers migrate their networks from copper to fiber optic systems and other technologies, this transition brings new opportunities to modernize our communications systems. At the same time, it raises serious questions about service reliability and accessibility, especially in areas prone to natural disasters, which increasingly extends well beyond California. The Commission recognized these concerns in September when it pulled another discontinuance application from automatic approval for further review, and it should apply the same level of scrutiny in this circumstance. At the very least, any order should carve out areas at high risk for fires and other natural disasters and areas without verified indoor cellular coverage.

We also request that you respond in writing to the following questions by December 15, 2026, and before any vote on the draft order:

Should a carrier have to show, with independently verified data, that its replacement service provides reliable indoor coverage before retiring copper in high-fire-threat areas? If not, what showing should be required?

Of the more than 184,000 California locations approved for discontinuance, how many are in High Fire Threat Districts, and how many lack indoor wireless coverage?

Do you agree that demonstrating wireless coverage under normal operating conditions does not necessarily establish that a network will remain reliable during a wildfire, extended power outage, or other natural disaster?

If testing identifies locations where the replacement service is unreliable or unavailable, will the FCC require the carrier to maintain existing service until an adequate alternative is available?

Many wireless services stop working when the power goes out. Will the FCC require backup power for replacement services in disaster-prone areas so customers can still call 911 during outages?

For customers in states approved for copper retirement, what mechanisms will be available to those individuals to report service failures, and how will the FCC use those reports?

Should a state be permitted to require a carrier to demonstrate that its replacement service is reliable before landline service is discontinued? Should a federal discontinuance authorization automatically override state public safety requirements that address risks the FCC did not evaluate rigorously?

Why should the Commission act before the courts rule on the challenges to the Network Modernization Order?

Will the FCC share outage reporting data with state commissions, local governments, and first responders, with any necessary confidentiality safeguards applied to the data?

We share the Commission’s goal in modernizing our nation’s communications networks and expanding fiber-optic infrastructure to underserved communities. However, these efforts must be executed carefully, in a manner that protects vulnerable communities during emergencies and outages and preserves universal telephone service for all Americans.

title: Representatives April McClain Delaney & Carol Miller Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect Rural Communities from Flooding
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman April McClain Delaney (D-MD) and Congresswoman Carol Miller (R-WV) introduced the bipartisan AGRI-FLOOD Resilience and Infrastructure Act, legislation to help rural communities prepare for severe flooding, protect farmland, and reduce taxpayer costs of disaster recovery.

The bill would establish a new U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) program to modernize aging dams and flood control systems, restore floodplains and wetlands, and improve flood risk information and emergency preparedness. Rather than reinforcing costly disaster recovery programs, this bill prioritizes prevention measures that reduce damage to rural lands and infrastructure while protecting our country’s food security and supply chains.

“Last year’s flooding in Westernport devastated families and underscored the need to better prepare our rural communities,” said Congresswoman McClain Delaney. “Our neighbors deserve to feel safe in their homes and have the tools to prepare for the next flood. That’s why I’m introducing the bipartisan AGRI-FLOOD Act to help rural communities upgrade aging flood infrastructure, restore watersheds, and strengthen early warning and real-time response systems. Investing in prevention now can save lives and spare families the heartbreak and expense of rebuilding. ”

“In West Virginia, aging dams and outdated infrastructure leave many of our communities vulnerable to devastating floods. Our rural communities deserve reliable water systems and the peace of mind that comes with knowing their homes and businesses are safe. This vital legislation will strengthen USDA watershed programs, which support a variety of resilience activities including dam repairs, road upgrades, and rural water infrastructure while cutting unnecessary government red tape that slows down critical projects. Flooding threatens lives and devastates communities. We must do everything we can to prepare for disasters before they strike and ensure West Virginia has the most up to date infrastructure,” said Congresswoman Miller.

The AGRI-FLOOD Resilience and Infrastructure Act directs USDA to establish a Floodplains and Watershed Resilience Program that would provide:

Infrastructure assistance. Financial and technical support to modernize aging dams and flood control infrastructure in rural communities.

Watershed restoration. Projects to restore floodplains, wetlands, and degraded watersheds to reduce future flood risks.

Better flood risk information. National flood risk assessments and publicly accessible flood maps to support local planning and preparedness.

Read the bill HERE

Endorsees Quotes:

“We thank Representatives April McClain Delaney and Carol Miller for introducing the AGRI-FLOOD Act and recognizing the value of protecting both people and rivers through smart conservation investments,” said Tom Kiernan, President, American Rivers Action Fund . “Floodplain restoration and easements are a proven land-management strategy that supports landowners while conserving flood-prone land. These USDA programs provide multiple benefits — from storing floodwaters and improving water quality to creating critical wildlife habitat and helping rivers reconnect with their natural floodplains. Healthy rivers and floodplains make communities more resilient to increasingly severe floods and storms.”

“ASFPM supports the overall goals of the AGRI-FLOOD Resilience and Infrastructure Act because the legislation advances proactive flood risk reduction, watershed resilience, nature-based solutions (including restoration of wetlands), and modernization of aging flood infrastructure,” states Chad Berginnis, Executive Director of the Association of State Floodplain Managers. “We note that NRCS assisted in designing, planning, and constructing nearly 12,000 watershed dams to control flooding and prevent damage to communities since the 1950s. As these dams have aged, surrounding areas have developed, and rainfall patterns have changed, flooding has increased. Rural communities in particular, need assistance to better identify, assess, and mitigate flood risk. ASFPM looks forward to working with Congress and NRCS on this bill as it moves through the legislative process.”

“We thank Representatives April McClain Delaney and Carol Miller for introducing this important legislation to strengthen the nation’s watershed infrastructure,” said Gene Stauborn, Executive Director, National Watershed Coalition. “This bill will help prioritize rehabilitation of high hazard dams that are critical to protecting rural communities, while also generating jobs, supporting agricultural economies, and ensuring these aging structures continue to provide flood protection, water management, and public safety benefits for future generations. By reducing barriers and increasing federal support, this legislation will help local sponsors move urgently needed projects forward without delay.”

“Counties play a critical role in building flood-resilient infrastructure across our nation's rural communities,” said Matthew Chase, Executive Director of the National Association of Counties. “The AGRI-FLOOD Resilience and Infrastructure Act provides targeted technical assistance and financial support for watershed resilience and flood protection efforts, helping rural county leaders better protect our communities. Counties urge Congress to swiftly pass this bipartisan legislation.”

“ASCE strongly supports a watershed management approach that considers all residents within a watershed basin. Rural communities are adversely affected by lack of resources to reduce flood risk, implement plans to mitigate the effects of natural disasters, and ensure that water resources infrastructure is able to withstand increasingly severe weather events. The AGRI-FLOOD Resilience and Infrastructure Act will provide needed assistance to rural communities by providing financial and technical assistance for pre-disaster flood risk reduction, prioritizing projects to improve resilience of high-hazard dams that could otherwise result in loss of life in the event of dam failure, and ensure that accurate and up to date data are available to stakeholders to help improve safety preparation and response capability. ASCE is proud to support this critical bipartisan legislation.” - Marsha Anderson Bomar, President, American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE)

“Rural communities, farmers, and local businesses are facing growing risks from flooding and aging water infrastructure. The Agri-Flood Act is a strong bipartisan step toward strengthening resilience, modernizing critical watershed infrastructure, and supporting economic opportunity in rural communities. American Sustainable Business Network supports policies that invest in resilient infrastructure solutions that are good for businesses, farmers, and communities alike.”

— Liza LaManna, Manager of Agriculture and Water Policy, American Sustainable Business Network

"As the U.S. faces increasing climate risks, we must also acknowledge that extreme precipitation events are becoming more frequent, making the prevalence of high-hazard dams unacceptable. That is why we strongly support the Agri-Flood Resilience and Infrastructure Act as a means of providing States, local governments, Tribal Nations, and territories with the resources they need to improve resilience against flooding in their communities on an expedited timeline." – Jeff Diamond, Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy

title: Menendez, Mejia Lead NJ Democrats to Block Russian Diesel Imports, Warn Port Operators of Legal Liability
text:
Backing Governor Sherrill’s efforts, lawmakers warn the Trump Administration and NJ port operators that offloading Russian fuel breaks federal law and betrays Ukraine

JERSEY CITY, NJ – Today, Representatives Rob Menendez (NJ-08) and Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) led the New Jersey Democratic Delegation to demand immediate action to keep Russian diesel tankers out of state ports. In dual letters to the Trump Administration and New Jersey terminal operators, the lawmakers underscored Governor Mikie Sherrill’s recent warning that accepting Russian diesel still breaks federal law.

In the letter to President Trump and U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent, the lawmakers wrote: “Your administration failed to comply with these statutory requirements when it issued General License No. 135 and subsequently announced a deal to purchase diesel from Russia on October 9, 2026 – all while Russia continued military aggression against Ukraine. As such, any importation of Russian-origin diesel fuel violates federal law and exposes receiving entities in New Jersey and elsewhere to significant legal risk, including criminal and civil liability.”

In the letter to New Jersey refineries and terminals, the lawmakers continued: “We also know that any revenue from energy exports will bolster Russia’s capacity to continue waging war against Ukraine and endanger U.S. security interests abroad. Importing Russian fuel betrays our ally – a betrayal that carries particular significance for New Jersey’s substantial Ukrainian American community. For many members of our communities, Russia’s war against Ukraine is not an abstract foreign policy challenge, but a direct threat to relatives, friends, cultural institutions, and a country to which they remain deeply connected.”

The letters were cosigned by Representatives Frank Pallone (NJ-06), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05), LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), Herbert Conaway (NJ-03), Donald Norcross (NJ-01), and Nellie Pou (NJ-09).

A copy of the letter to the Trump Administration can be found here.

A copy of the letter to New Jersey Refineries and Terminals can be found here.

Congressman Rob Menendez is a member of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus and has consistently advocated for fierce support for Ukraine’s sovereignty, strict enforcement of Russian sanctions, and the protection of New Jersey’s Ukrainian American community.

title: Speaker Johnson: Don’t Give Up on America
text:
WASHINGTON — This weekend, Speaker Johnson joined Saturday in America on Fox News with Kayleigh McEnany for a post-election sit-down interview.

Watch the full interview here.

On the election results:

We worked around the clock and left it all on the field to win. We had to defy history. As you and I both know, it's only happened twice in 90 years that a sitting president has picked up seats for his party in the midterm. But we did everything we could to make that happen. I've been speaker for three years; I've logged enough campaign miles to circle the globe 14 times. I led almost 750 campaign events around the country in almost all 50 states, and I raised almost $900 million for House Republicans for the cause.

But, you know, this was a year where history was not defied. We don't like the results. But, you know, real leadership, I've always believed, you lead from the front and leaders have to take responsibility when things go wrong, whether it’s deserved or not, that's part of it. And so that's why I felt like I'm going to remain in this fight, but I'll do it from a role different than as minority leader in the next Congress. So, after prayer and reflection and we had to make a decision pretty quick.

On looking back at his time as Speaker:

Well, you know, did the speakership for three years, and when you and I did that initial interview, they didn't know if I'd last three weeks or three months. So, there's been a lot of prayer and patience that's gone into this to deliver all these wins and do it in defiance of the odds. We had intercessors, prayer intercessors, literally hundreds of people every day of the week, every week of this speakership who prayed for the Congress, prayed for the leaders, everyone, to ensure that we could do the right thing for the right reasons for the people. And it's been an incredible run. You know, not anything I ever expected but we're grateful. That's the word, gratitude. That's what I have in my heart. It's been the honor of my life to serve as the 56th Speaker of the House.

I'm grateful for the team I work with. I'm encouraged going forward, and I do believe that this Republican team can win back the majority in 2028. I think the contrast is going be so stark for the people that there will be a big desire for that. So, we're going to work every day to make that happen.

On the path forward:

Well, we have a lot more left to do. Kelly and I prayed about this. I don't believe that God's releasing me from that responsibility. John Quincy Adams said, “Duty is ours, results are God’s.” So we're going to do our duty every day and I’m going to do everything I can to ensure that our team prevails. Our timeless principles, the Republican principles, the founding principles of America endure. And whatever role that is, God has for us in the future, we're going to be involved in that directly and heavily. So, don't give up on America. I mean, election cycles come and go. There are epics in history, but we stick to our principles and that's what's going to save this great country.

###

title: Members of IN Delegation Send Letter to NOAA Requesting NERR in Northwest Indiana
text:
Washington, DC – Today, members of the Indiana Congressional delegation, including Rep. Frank J. Mrvan, Rep. Jim Baird, Senator Todd Young, and Senator Jim Banks, sent a letter to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) in support of the State of Indiana’s request to establish a National Estuarine Research Reserve (NERR) in Northwest Indiana.

Congressman Frank J. Mrvan stated, “Northwest Indiana is home to such incredible environmental wonders on our Lake Michigan shoreline, and I applaud the initiative of the State of Indiana and its partnership with Purdue University to continue to enhance conservation and research opportunities in this area. I look forward to continuing to partner with all of my fellow members of the Indiana Congressional delegation and federal officials to advance this worthwhile proposal.”

Congressman Jim Baird stated, "Lake Michigan is an ecological marvel with a rich natural history. Glaciers and shifting sands shaped this Great Lake thousands of years ago. Today, Lake Michigan remains a beautiful and crucial natural resource for the Hoosier State. Designating the coastal region bordering Lake Michigan as a National Estuarine Research Reserve brings valuable support and recognition to ongoing conservation efforts. My alma mater, Purdue University, has been a leader in these efforts, and this designation will provide support to help protect this magnificent ecosystem and the economic opportunities it provides, for future generations."

Senator Todd Young stated, “Lake Michigan is a vital part of Northwest Indiana’s economy and one of our state’s most important natural resources. A National Estuarine Research Reserve could build on the work already underway to protect Lake Michigan by expanding research and conservation efforts, with Purdue University bringing valuable expertise to the table. Taking a closer look at what a reserve could offer The Region is a sensible next step.”

Senator Jim Banks stated, “Lake Michigan is one of Indiana’s greatest natural resources and is an important part of Northwest Indiana’s economy. Establishing a National Estuarine Research Reserve would strengthen conservation efforts, expand research opportunities, and help protect our shoreline for generations. I am proud to support this effort and urge the NOAA to move Indiana’s request forward.”

The text of the letter is below and a pdf is available here.

“Dear Dr. Jacobs,

“We write in support of the State of Indiana’s request to establish a National Estuarine Research Reserve (NERR) in Northwest Indiana, along the coastal region bordering Lake Michigan. In November 2024, then-Governor Eric Holcomb submitted a formal request for a designation, and, in July 2026, Governor Mike Braun sent a letter reaffirming interest in this initiative. As members of the Indiana Congressional delegation, we urge NOAA to advance the State’s request through the appropriate designation process and provide an update on its status.

“Northwest Indiana’s Lake Michigan coastal region is a key environmental resource that provides unique economic, recreational, and educational opportunities in our state. We are committed to preserving and strengthening this region and believe that a NERR designation would support its long-term vitality, restoration, and resilience.

“Since 2001, Indiana has partnered with NOAA in coastal management through the Indiana Lake Michigan Coastal Program, which has supported public access improvements, educational opportunities, habitat preservation and restoration, and technical assistance for local coastal communities. Establishing a NERR in Northwest Indiana would build upon these efforts and provide meaningful benefits to the state and the broader Great Lakes bioregion.

“Currently, Indiana does not have a NERR, and only two reserves are designated in the Great Lakes region, neither of which is located along the southern shore of Lake Michigan. This region includes unique freshwater estuarine habitats that warrant sustained research, monitoring, and education. Establishing a NERR in Northwest Indiana would provide distinct value to the overall Reserve system by addressing research gaps, advancing scientific understanding of the region’s unique ecological processes, and enhancing management and restoration efforts for similar systems across the Great Lakes.

“Additionally, Purdue University’s College of Agriculture is strongly positioned to serve as the lead organization for this initiative. As a nationally recognized land grant institution, Purdue has a proven record of partnering with state and federal agencies, including the Indiana Department of Natural Resources, to advance research, education, and outreach efforts. Purdue is also home to several NOAA-funded programs, such as the Illinois-Indiana Sea Grant College Program and the Midwestern Regional Climate Center. This demonstrated expertise in coastal management prepares the university to support the long-term success of a NERR in Indiana.

“The Lake Michigan coastal region is essential to Indiana’s identity, economy, and environment. By expanding opportunities for research, education, and community engagement, establishing a NERR in Northwest Indiana would safeguard this vital environmental resource for generations to come. We appreciate NOAA’s consideration of this request and look forward to continuing to work together to strengthen the Great Lakes region.”

Sincerely,

Congressman Frank J. Mrvan (IN-01)

Congressman Jim Baird (IN-04)

U.S. Senator Todd Young (IN)

U.S. Senator Jim Banks (IN)

###

title: Norton Announces Deadlines for Constituent Services Ahead of Retirement
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC) today announced upcoming deadlines for constituent services as her office prepares for the conclusion of her congressional service at the end of the 119th Congress.

Norton's office will stop accepting new constituent casework at the close of business on Friday, November 20th.
