title: Murray, Shaheen, Baldwin Call for Inspector General Investigation into How Trump and RFK Jr. Worsened the Cyclospora Outbreak
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee; Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies; and Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Ranking Member of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, sent a letter to Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Inspector General Thomas March Bell, asking him to open an investigation into how the Trump administration’s personnel and policy changes at the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) contributed to this summer’s extensive Cyclosporiasis (Cyclospora) outbreak.

“We write to request that you open an investigation into how personnel and policy changes at the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) contributed to this summer’s Cyclosporiasis (Cyclospora) outbreak, which was an unusually large, multistate outbreak that resulted in more than twelve thousand confirmed cases and two deaths,” the lawmakers wrote. “It is clear that the FDA and CDC failed to adequately prevent and respond to this outbreak, and we believe that is, in no small part, due to this Administration’s illegal staffing cuts over the last 18 months. Additionally, we are concerned that political interference resulted in delayed recalls and inspections of facilities linked to this outbreak.”

Noting that the Trump administration pushed out over 4,600 FDA staff since taking over, the lawmakers state that: “The FDA failed to quickly inspect the suspected source of the outbreak. It took the FDA over a month to access the Taylor Farms facility and farms that have now been linked to this Cyclospora outbreak. It is also important to note that the facility’s most recent inspection took place in 2019, meaning that the FDA has not had eyes on the conditions of this facility for at least seven years.”

The lawmakers also addressed the failure to respond to the outbreak from the CDC: “It is clear it was not just the FDA that failed to quickly and effectively respond under this administration. Similar personnel, funding, and policy decisions at CDC call into question how the agency responded to this outbreak—and its ability to effectively address others. The Trump administration has pushed out approximately 3,000 CDC staff members since January 2025, greatly diminishing the agency’s ability to respond to public health emergencies. Due to attrition and probationary staff firings, the CDC lab that responds to outbreaks of cyclospora was downsized from eleven people to just three last year.”

They also write that the Trump administration’s decision to remove mandatory reporting of cyclospora by the Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network (FoodNet) and its failure to fully staff and operate the White House Office of Pandemic Preparedness and Response (OPPR) have contributed to the administration’s failure to respond to the outbreak.

The full letter is available HERE and below:

Dear Inspector General Bell,

We write to request that you open an investigation into how personnel and policy changes at the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) contributed to this summer’s Cyclosporiasis (Cyclospora) outbreak, which was an unusually large, multistate outbreak that resulted in more than twelve thousand confirmed cases and two deaths. It is clear that the FDA and CDC failed to adequately prevent and respond to this outbreak, and we believe that is, in no small part, due to this Administration’s illegal staffing cuts over the last 18 months. Additionally, we are concerned that political interference resulted in delayed recalls and inspections of facilities linked to this outbreak.

According to data from the Office of Personnel Management (OPM), the Trump administration has pushed out over 4,600 FDA staff since January 2025. Through a series of mass reductions in force (RIFs), the Trump administration has fired key staff working in policy, human resources, IT, procurement, and communications, as well as staff who worked to write guidance documents, regulations, and issue press releases about the FDA’s activities such as recalls. These policy and communications staff are not dispensable; they play a key role in ensuring the American people have information about disease outbreaks that could jeopardize their health. Having staff working to disseminate this information is especially important during recalls, like during the cyclospora outbreak, in order to quickly share information to keep people safe. The absence of clear, consistent communication from the FDA was evident during this outbreak, led to unnecessary confusion, delayed responses, and likely led to more people getting sick. Furthermore, Secretary Kennedy’s comments that the cyclospora outbreak was “under control” only led to more confusion for the public as the FDA continued to expand the outbreak to more and more states.

Last year, the Trump administration pushed out support staff who worked directly with inspectors to ensure they can seamlessly visit FDA-regulated facilities. This has left inspectors responsible for coordinating their own travel, scheduling their inspections, communicating with FDA-regulated facilities, and filling out paperwork for which they used to have additional support—all of which simply meant that they were able to conduct fewer inspections and keep our food supply safe. The FDA reports that outside of the years of COVID-19, 2025’s inspection count was the lowest since 2011, and based on available data, inspections for 2026 will be at a similarly low rate. The FDA has struggled to retain inspectors for many years, and instead of working to hire and retain more and ensure they have the support they need to effectively do their jobs, the Trump administration destroyed their support base. The U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) made three recommendations about ways to improve retention of inspectors to better protect the U.S. food supply in January of 2025, and as of June 2026, the FDA had concurred with the recommendations but has failed to respond to several of the key recommendations, including defining the appropriate size and workload for its foreign investigators to meet the FDA’s foreign inspection needs to protect the American food supply and developing performance management processes to improve inspection goals.

The FDA failed to quickly inspect the suspected source of the outbreak. It took the FDA over a month to access the Taylor Farms facility and farms that have now been linked to this Cyclospora outbreak. It is also important to note that the facility’s most recent inspection took place in 2019, meaning that the FDA has not had eyes on the conditions of this facility for at least seven years. It is also troubling that Taylor Farms appears to have interfered in the FDA and CDC’s ongoing investigation of this cyclospora outbreak, including by potentially delaying access to their facility directly linked to this outbreak in Mexico. Of similar concern is the fact that Taylor Farms reportedly met with the White House and made contributions to Republican Political Action Committees in order to change the course of the investigation. We request an investigation into whether political interference from Taylor Farms put the American people at further risk by delaying the time it took to remove their products from the market, thus increasing the number of cyclospora cases this summer.

It is clear it was not just the FDA that failed to quickly and effectively respond under this administration. Similar personnel, funding, and policy decisions at CDC call into question how the agency responded to this outbreak—and its ability to effectively address others. The Trump administration has pushed out approximately 3,000 CDC staff members since January 2025, greatly diminishing the agency’s ability to respond to public health emergencies. Due to attrition and probationary staff firings, the CDC lab that responds to outbreaks of cyclospora was downsized from eleven people to just three last year. CDC staff are already stretched thin responding to other outbreaks, including a rapidly worsening Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Further impacting CDC’s ability to respond to the cyclospora outbreak is the loss of $40 million in funding from the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) after the Trump administration illegally dismantled it in 2025. While CDC hopes to recover some of that funding, it will only be a fraction of what it used to receive from USAID. The reduction in funding has resulted in the loss of staff who would often be called upon to assist in an emergency response situation. Fewer staff and experts make it impossible to respond quickly to an outbreak, where timely response is vital.

The Trump administration’s decision to remove mandatory reporting of cyclospora by the Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network, (FoodNet) is also confounding—and has put our food supply at risk. While FoodNet is not used to track outbreaks in real time, the removal of cyclospora mandatory reporting risks negatively affected the ability for the program to understand this outbreak and provide an analysis on trends of cyclospora outbreaks over time, which in turn could help reduce the risk of future wide-spread outbreaks.

Lastly, the Office of Pandemic Preparedness and Response (OPPR) was created by Congress to coordinate the federal government’s response to public health crises like this outbreak. This administration has utterly failed to ensure it is fully staffed and operational to protect Americans from disease outbreaks and ensure coordination across government. For over a year, OPPR did not so much as have a director or even any staff. It has been widely reported that the administration appointed Dr. Sara Brenner, a former FDA official, to lead OPPR in July of this year. But it’s not clear how long she will remain in the position, or if a single additional person is serving on staff.

For all these reasons, we request that you open an investigation that evaluates the following questions:

Have RIFs of support staff for inspectors affected inspectors’ ability to meet demand for inspections?

Has the loss of support staff taken inspectors away from the critical parts of their jobs?

Will the FDA meet inspection targets for the Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) in 2026 and if not, what is needed to meet those targets in future years?

Why hasn’t the FDA implemented all of the GAO’s recommendations for retaining inspectors?

Are there additional challenges that are affecting the inspectorate at the FDA that are not outlined in the GAO report?

Does HHS OIG have additional recommendations to improve recruitment and retention for inspectors?

How will the July 2028 implementation of the FDA’s Food Traceability Rule impact any corrective actions that should be taken in the wake of future foodborne illness outbreaks?

Should the FDA implement inspection targets for international food facilities like those of domestic facilities to have better oversight of all the food entering the U.S. market?

Why did it take over a month for the FDA to access the Taylor Farms facility in Mexico that has now been linked to this outbreak?

In areas where the U.S. government may have security concerns internationally, what contingencies has the FDA put into place to ensure that the FDA’s inspectors are able to access facilities to ensure the safety of the FDA-regulated products?

If there are not contingencies in place, should the U.S. government consider preventing imports from areas with international security concerns to protect the FDA’s inspectors and the American public until contingencies are created?

Prior to accessing the Taylor Farms facility in Mexico in July, why hadn’t the facility been inspection since 2019?

Did meetings or communications with the White House or donations to Trump-associated Political Action Committees delay the FDA’s response to this outbreak and identifying Taylor Farms as the culprit?

We appreciate your work on this important inquiry.

###

title: Murray Slams Trump Administration’s New Rule that Shortchanges Head Start Teachers and Families
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), a senior member and former Chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee and former pre-school teacher issued the following statement slamming the Trump administration for a new final rule unveiled on Friday that would roll back wage and benefit requirements for Head Start educators.

“Moms and dads in every corner of the country count on Head Start teachers to help their kids learn, grow, and thrive—they play a vital role in communities all over this country,” said Senator Murray. “Everyone knows that these educators are overworked and underpaid, creating retention challenges that limit options for families. This is a real problem that Donald Trump and RFK Jr. want to make worse. Donald Trump wants Head Start teachers to get paid less and take away health insurance and paid leave to boot—how many of these teachers will just leave for a better paying job? I’ve taught preschool and I’ll tell you what: you can’t help more kids with fewer teachers. I’ll be fighting to stop this policy dead in its tracks every way I can—just like I’ll keep pushing back on Trump’s attempts to gut Head Start’s health and safety standards. And you can bet I’ll be fighting to invest in Head Start and setting our kids up for success instead of Trump’s illegal wars overseas.”

Head Start currently serves over 750,000 kids nationwide, and the program has served more than 40 million children and their families nationwide since its inception in 1965. There are over 17,000 Head Start centers nationwide and these centers are particularly important in serving rural communities with fewer options for care.

Throughout his second term, President Trump has gutted the offices that keep Head Start centers and child care programs across the country running. Since taking office, the Trump administration has fired 40 to 50% of the staff at the Department of Health and Human Services’ (HHS) Office of Head Start and Office of Child Care. In April of 2025, Trump continued to hollow out HHS, by shuttering five of the 10 regional offices for both Office of Child Care and Office of Head Start, which served 22 states and five territories. President Trump also illegally impounded funding provided by Congress for Head Start programs across America, in violation of the Impoundment Control Act (ICA). In response, Senator Murray raised alarm bells and she led her colleagues in demanding that the funds get moving.

Notably, a leaked memo indicated that the Trump administration—in keeping with Project 2025—would push to completely eliminate Head Start as a part of its FY26 budget request. Ultimately, strong public outcry and backlash prevented the Trump administration from including the elimination of Head Start in its budget request.

Also last year, HHS took steps to attack immigrant children and their families by issuing a notice reinterpreting longstanding guidance under the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act (PRWORA) to reinterpret Head Start as a federal public benefit subject to immigration restrictions. The guidance, currently tied up in litigation and stalled from being enforced, threw programs and families into chaos, sparking confusion and driving many families to keep their kids at home out of fear of discrimination or immigration enforcement.

In the face of Trump’s calls to cut investments in state early childhood education programs and repeated attacks on the program, Democrats have consistently defended resources for child care and early childhood education. In March of this year, Senator Murray led her colleagues and established a new working group as the latest major push in Democrats’ fight to lower costs and deliver child care for every American family. The Child Care for America working group will bring Democratic members of Congress together to coordinate broad support for landmark child care legislation.

In April, President Trump said “Don’t send any money for day care, because the United States can’t take care of day care… We’re fighting wars. We can’t take care of day care… It’s not possible for us to take care of day care, Medicaid, Medicare, all these individual things.”

In August, Senator Murray slammed the HHS proposed rule changes that would gut Head Start by shredding basic standards that keep kids safe and advance their education. The proposed rule would remove most of Head Start’s 133 pages of requirements for math and literacy curriculums, class sizes, medical screenings, home visits, and more.

title: Senator Murray Slams Loss of Measles Elimination Status Under Trump & RFK Jr.’s Failed Leadership
text:
Senator Murray recently announced the launch of the Public Health for America Working Group: an initiative to develop the ideas, safeguards, and legislation needed to build and improve the nation’s public health system after nearly two years of attacks on the agencies, scientists, and institutions that save lives and keep Americans safe and healthy

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), a senior member and former Chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee, released the following statement after the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) determined that the United States lost its measles elimination status:

“For 26 years, measles was eliminated in the United States—until Trump and RFK Jr. turned back the clock and brought a deadly, preventable disease roaring back. This is outrageous. Measles cases are at record highs, ten people have died from measles this year, including infants. Instead of doing everything in his power to stop this, RFK Jr. has accused state health officials of exaggerating the outbreak, suggested the deaths may have been ‘fabricated,’ and changed how the CDC counts measles deaths—Americans deserve real leadership, not a coverup,” said Senator Murray. “Trump has given RFK Jr. free rein to spread conspiracy theories and this is the result. Vaccines are safe and effective—full stop. If we had an HHS Secretary willing to say that plainly, we would not be watching children die of a disease this country beat a generation ago. A Democratic majority will hold RFK Jr. accountable for tearing apart our public health system, we are going to protect science, and we are going to rebuild the trust they’ve shattered—because no family should bury a child over a disease we already know how to prevent.”

Last week, PAHO held its annual meeting of the Regional Verification Commission for the Elimination of Measles, Rubella, and Congenital Rubella Syndrome (RVC). The Commission reviews all countries in the Americas annually. The United States has held a measles elimination status since 2000, but last year PAHO classified the United States’ measles status as “sustained with major concerns.” According to PAHO, a country loses measles elimination status if transmission is re-established and continues uninterrupted for at least 12 months. The decision comes after the United States recorded over 5,400 measles cases so far this year, including ten deaths from measles.

Senator Murray forcefully opposed notorious anti-vaccine activist Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s nomination to lead HHS and has been one of the leading voices in Congress holding him accountable ever since. She has fought back against his purge of the CDC’s vaccine advisory committee, his mass firings of career scientists and public health experts, his cancellation of lifesaving research, and his sidelining of independent expert panels that Americans rely on for sound, evidence-based guidance. She has confronted Kennedy directly in multiple Senate HELP and Appropriations Committee hearings, led her colleagues in demanding he reverse actions that have left the nation less prepared for emerging outbreaks, and called for his firing multiple times after he ousted the CDC Director and drove the agency’s senior leadership to resign—a call she continues to reiterate loudly and consistently.

As a longtime appropriator and former Chair of the Senate HELP Committee, Senator Murray has worked successfully for decades to fund and authorize key public health programs with her colleagues on both sides of the aisle. In October, Senator Murray announced the launch of the Public Health for America Working Group:an initiative to develop the ideas, safeguards, and legislation needed to build and improve the nation’s public health system after nearly two years of attacks on the agencies, scientists, and institutions that save lives and keep Americans safe and healthy. Senator Murray formed the working group in response to this administration’s unprecedented steps to politicize public health agencies, overrule experts, promote misinformation, and undermine trust in the nation’s public health infrastructure.

title: Trump Nominating Vought Acolyte to Lead Congress’ Nonpartisan Watchdog
text:
President Trump nominates OMB Deputy Director Eric Ueland to serve as GAO Comptroller General

Washington, D.C. – Today, Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, issued the following statement on President Trump’s nomination of Eric Ueland to serve a 15-year term as Comptroller General of the nonpartisan Government Accountability Office (GAO).

Ueland is currently serving as the Deputy Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB), and he has served recently as both the Acting Administrator of the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) and the Acting Director of the United States Office of Government Ethics (OGE).

“It would be lunacy for the Senate to hand a 15-year term leading Congress’ nonpartisan watchdog to a Russ Vought acolyte who spends his days plotting new ways for this administration to defy Congress. Ueland orchestrated the president’s destructive mass firing campaign, is presiding over the razing of USAID, and is the last person who should be leading GAO.

“GAO has a long, proud tradition of providing unbiased, expert analysis under the leadership of comptrollers general supported by members on both sides of the aisle.

“It’s bad enough that Senate Republicans confirmed Russ Vought to lead OMB; it would be a tremendous betrayal to now give his deputy—who is actively working to steal Congress’ power of the purse—a set of keys to the building for the next 15 years.

“Every Republican who cares about protecting their own power should work with us to reject this outrageous nomination, modernize the appointment process for GAO, and ensure this critical resource for Congress continues to be led in a nonpartisan, professional way.”

While GAO is a legislative branch agency tasked with providing expert, nonpartisan research to Congress and with protecting Congress’ constitutional powers, under current law, the president is empowered to nominate the Comptroller General, subject to confirmation by the Senate. Senator Murray has pushed to modernize the appointment process for GAO to ensure that the heads of legislative branch agencies are chosen by the legislative branch.

title: Sen. Ossoff Working to Make College More Affordable for Georgia Students
text:

title: ICYMI: Rosen’s Carson City Lands Bill Passes Senate
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen’s (D-NV) Carson City Public Land Correction Act passed the Senate last week with bipartisan support. This bill would help improve public lands management, support flood mitigation and outdoor recreation, and expand economic development opportunities in Carson City, Nevada, all while ensuring environmentally sensitive areas remain protected. As the state with the highest percentage of public land in the nation, Nevada relies on federal legislation to make land available for development and other public purposes. The bill now heads to the House of Representatives, and if passed, would go to the President’s desk.

KOLO Reno: Rosen’s Carson City Lands Bill Clears Senate

Nevada Senator Jacky Rosen’s lands bill has cleared the Senate. The Carson City Public Land Correction Act will now head to the House.

The bill would transfer nearly 1,300 acres of BLM land to Carson City for flood mitigation, recreation, water improvements and a rifle range and more.

“As communities across Nevada continue to grow, we need to make sure that federal lands are being used in a way that best fits local needs. I’ve been proud to work with Mayor Bagwell to put together a bill that will ensure land is available for Carson City, spurring economic development, supporting infrastructure improvements, expanding access to outdoor recreation, and more,” said Senator Rosen. “I’m excited to announce that my bill has passed the U.S. Senate and is closer to becoming law. I urge the U.S. House of Representatives to pass it and ensure that the bill reaches the President’s desk as soon as possible.”

“I want to sincerely thank Senator Jacky Rosen for her leadership and tireless efforts in helping pass the Carson City Lands Bill,” said Mayor Lori Bagwell, Mayor of Carson City. “This important legislation will create new opportunities for economic development, responsible growth, and preservation of our treasured open spaces. Senator Rosen’s commitment to Carson City will have a lasting impact on our community for generations to come.”

Carson Now: Rosen’s Carson City lands bill would transfer 1,270 BLM acres to city, open 380 for private develop

Carson City could receive over 1,200 acres of federal land for recreation, flood mitigation and other public uses under legislation passed Thursday by the U.S. Senate. If passed, the Carson City Public Land Correct Act would also open roughly 380 acres for private sale, and adjust rules relating to land management.

If approved, the federal government would transfer the 1,270 acres to Carson City at the city’s request without charging a purchase price. The land would remain restricted to authorized public uses, and the federal government could reclaim parcels that no longer meet those requirements. The city would pay associated survey, administrative and applicable environmental costs.

The proposal updates provisions of the 2009 law governing federal land transfers and management in Carson City. Rosen introduced it in December 2025 after discussions with city officials about growth, infrastructure and conservation according to a press release following the passage.

Nevada Appeal: U.S. Senate approves Carson City public lands bill

Thursday, the U.S. Senate by unanimous consent approved the Carson City Public Land Correction Act.

…the bill would help improve public lands management, support flood mitigation and outdoor recreation, and expand economic development opportunities in Carson City, all while ensuring environmentally sensitive areas remain protected.

The House passed Amodei’s bill on Sept. 14, according to his chief of staff, Ken Brooke. “We are working with Senators Cortez Masto and Rosen to get that bill back out of the Senate and signed into law by the end of the year,” he said Friday.

Rosen also introduced the Truckee Meadows Public Lands Management Act, also known as the Washoe County Lands Bill, to expand economic development opportunities and make more land available for housing in Washoe County, support local tribal communities, increase access to outdoor recreation and protect public lands.

title: NEWS: Amid FCC’s Moves to Discontinue Landline Service for Hundreds of Thousands of Californians, Schiff, Matsui, Panetta, and Thompson Call on FCC to Abandon Proposed Order
text:
Washington, D.C. – As the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) moves to clear the way for AT&T to discontinue landline services essential to Californians, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and U.S. Representatives Doris Matsui (D-Calif.-07), Jimmy Panetta (D-Calif.-19) and Mike Thompson (D-Calif.-04) are pushing the FCC to drop this effort that will prevent California from ensuring vulnerable and rural communities have reliable landline phone service.

This new inquiry follows a July 2026 letter the lawmakers sent to the FCC Chairman Brendan Carr urging him to stop AT&T from shutting down landline services; however, rather than address the lawmakers’ concerns, the FCC approved AT&T’s application to decommission approximately 360 wire centers in California. On October 30, the FCC issued a draft order to preempt California’s carrier of last resort (COLR) rules – the exact issue the lawmakers warned about.

If the FCC adopts this order, it will eliminate California’s ability to require proof that wireless or fiber replacements actually work before copper wires are discontinued. It will also allow AT&T to discontinue landline service at several hundred wire centers in the state – affecting roughly 184,000 residential customers and 15,000 business customers in rural areas in California.

“These rules require telecommunications companies to provide basic phone service to anyone within their service area who requests it, ensuring that no Californian is left without access to essential communications services, including 911,” the lawmakers wrote.

While the transition from copper to fiber optic systems and other technologies will modernize communications systems, the lawmakers emphasize the need to ensure service reliability and accessibility for communities.

“We urge you to provide the public with sufficient time and a fair opportunity to review and weigh in on the full text of the order, rather than rush through a final decision that undermines public trust…We share the Commission’s goal in modernizing our nation’s communications networks and expanding fiber-optic infrastructure to underserved communities. However, these efforts must be executed carefully, in a manner that protects vulnerable communities during emergencies and outages and preserves universal telephone service for all Americans,” the lawmakers concluded.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear Chairman Carr:

We write again to raise concern over the Federal Communications Commission’s (FCC) efforts to eliminate California’s legal authority to require carriers to verify that wireless or fiber replacements function properly before retiring copper telephone networks. The draft order you circulated to the Commission on October 30, 2026, purports to preempt the California Public Utilities Commission’s (CPUC) Carrier of Last Resort (COLR) rules. These rules require telecommunications companies to provide basic phone service to anyone within their service area who requests it, ensuring that no Californian is left without access to essential communications services, including 911.

On July 22, 2026, twenty-eight members of the California Congressional delegation asked the Commission to deny AT&T’s petitions, and that request still stands. Following that letter, the Commission approved AT&T’s application to decommission approximately 360 wire centers in California covering about 184,000 residential locations in California.

If the FCC issues this purported blanket preemption, it will take away any oversight ability of California and other states to make sure sufficient alternative service exists without putting any system in place at the federal level to make that determination. In March, the Commission replaced its adequate replacement test with a carrier certification that a replacement service is available. The FCC relies on coverage reported by carriers and does not independently verify that there is alternative functioning service in the areas where copper will be retired. Without verification or oversight, California residents, including those in High Fire Threat Districts, will continue to lose basic service without access to an adequate replacement.

It should be noted that California’s rules do not stand in the way of modernization and are not meant to relegate Californians to outdated technology. The CPUC has told the FCC that its rules require reliable minimum service but do not require that service to be delivered over copper. If carriers can provide a replacement that meets California’s reliability standards, nothing prevents them from retiring copper systems. Congress preserved this protection in Section 253(b) of the Communications Act to allow states to create any necessary requirements to protect public safety, safeguard consumers’ rights, and ensure the continued quality of telecommunications services.

This month, the Commission is allowing copper retirement to begin in eighteen states – Alabama, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Michigan, Mississippi, Missouri, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, and Wisconsin. Those customers’ experiences over time may be helpful in determining the adequacy of wireless replacements. However, there is no dedicated mechanism for consumers to report problems with replacement service after discontinuance. These problems could range from thousands of blocked calls to 911 to problems with TTY devices, medical alert systems, or home alarms. Rural communities and elderly populations will be most at risk.

We urge you to provide the public with sufficient time and a fair opportunity to review and weigh in on the full text of the order, rather than rush through a final decision that undermines public trust. As carriers migrate their networks from copper to fiber optic systems and other technologies, this transition brings new opportunities to modernize our communications systems. At the same time, it raises serious questions about service reliability and accessibility, especially in areas prone to natural disasters, which increasingly extends well beyond California. The Commission recognized these concerns in September when it pulled another discontinuance application from automatic approval for further review, and it should apply the same level of scrutiny in this circumstance. At the very least, any order should carve out areas at high risk for fires and other natural disasters and areas without verified indoor cellular coverage.

We also request that you respond in writing to the following questions by December 15, 2026, and before any vote on the draft order:

Should a carrier have to show, with independently verified data, that its replacement service provides reliable indoor coverage before retiring copper in high-fire-threat areas? If not, what showing should be required?

Of the more than 184,000 California locations approved for discontinuance, how many are in High Fire Threat Districts, and how many lack indoor wireless coverage?

Do you agree that demonstrating wireless coverage under normal operating conditions does not necessarily establish that a network will remain reliable during a wildfire, extended power outage, or other natural disaster?

If testing identifies locations where the replacement service is unreliable or unavailable, will the FCC require the carrier to maintain existing service until an adequate alternative is available?

Many wireless services stop working when the power goes out. Will the FCC require backup power for replacement services in disaster-prone areas so customers can still call 911 during outages?

For customers in states approved for copper retirement, what mechanisms will be available to those individuals to report service failures, and how will the FCC use those reports?

Should a state be permitted to require a carrier to demonstrate that its replacement service is reliable before landline service is discontinued? Should a federal discontinuance authorization automatically override state public safety requirements that address risks the FCC did not evaluate rigorously?

Why should the Commission act before the courts rule on the challenges to the Network Modernization Order?

Will the FCC share outage reporting data with state commissions, local governments, and first responders, with any necessary confidentiality safeguards applied to the data?

We share the Commission’s goal in modernizing our nation’s communications networks and expanding fiber-optic infrastructure to underserved communities. However, these efforts must be executed carefully, in a manner that protects vulnerable communities during emergencies and outages and preserves universal telephone service for all Americans.

###

title: NEWS: Sen. Schiff, Senators Push CTFC To Reverse Ban on Geofencing by Prediction Markets
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), a member of the Senate Agriculture Committee, and other Senate Democrats are calling out Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chair Michael Selig for the agency’s decision to prohibit prediction markets from geofencing, effectively requiring prediction markets to offer contracts in all 50 states and Tribal lands. The Senators note Selig’s action directly conflicts with active court orders in California, Michigan, Nevada and Washington – and demand that he reverse it.

“Numerous courts have held that sports-related event contracts are not swaps and instead are indistinguishable from sports bets subject to state and tribal gaming laws…. The courts have ordered platforms to cease offering various prediction contracts in Michigan, Nevada, and Washington, and on the land of two California tribes, and imposed geofencing requirements. The Commission now appears to be encouraging prediction markets to offer prohibited contracts in contempt of these court orders during active litigation,” the Senators wrote.

“We are particularly troubled that this action came just hours after the Northern District of California issued its latest court order in Blue Lake Rancheria v. Kalshi requiring Kalshi to geofence around the plaintiff’s tribal lands. This interpretation raises concerns that the Commission may be coordinating with platforms currently engaged in litigation and encouraging them to violate state and tribal gaming laws… The Commission must withdraw the interpretation or freeze all efforts to implement until litigation is resolved.” the Senators continued.

Joining Schiff are all Senators representing California, Michigan, Nevada and Washington, Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), Gary Peters (D-Mich.) and Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), as well as the Ranking Member of the Senate Agriculture Committee Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.).

The full text of the letter can be found here and below:

Dear Chairman Selig:

We write to express our opposition to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s November 5 interpretation ordering Designated Contract Markets (DCMs) to end access criteria that restrict access to certain event contract markets based on prospective traders’ location or residence (e.g., geofencing) within 30 days. Your unilateral decision directly conflicts with active court orders, undermines state and tribal law, and must be reversed.

Numerous courts have held that sports-related event contracts are not swaps and instead are indistinguishable from sports bets subject to state and tribal gaming laws. Your novel interpretation of the impartial access requirements effectively requires DCMs to offer improperly regulated gambling products in all fifty states without regard to state and tribal gaming laws and these state and federal court decisions. There is no basis or precedent under 17 CFR 38.151(b)’s impartial access requirements for this interpretation and indeed this argument has been made in several of the active cases—and rejected.

The Sixth and Ninth Circuits have ruled that states retain the authority to apply state gaming laws to prediction markets. The Ninth Circuit has also ruled that sports event contracts on Tribal lands constitute unauthorized Class III gaming under the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act in the preliminary-injunction context. The courts have ordered platforms to cease offering various prediction contracts in Michigan, Nevada, and Washington, and on the land of two California tribes, and imposed geofencing requirements. The Commission now appears to be encouraging prediction markets to offer prohibited contracts in contempt of these court orders during active litigation.

We are particularly troubled that this action came just hours after the Northern District of California issued its latest court order in Blue Lake Rancheria v. Kalshi requiring Kalshi to geofence around the plaintiff’s tribal lands. This interpretation raises concerns that the Commission may be coordinating with platforms currently engaged in litigation and encouraging them to violate state and tribal gaming laws.

The Commission must withdraw the interpretation or freeze all efforts to implement until litigation is resolved. At minimum, the Commission must expressly state that the following do not violate Regulation 38.151(b): geographic restrictions imposed by court order, those adopted to comply with the Indian Gaming Regulatory Act or tribal-state compacts, and those an exchange adopts voluntarily.

We further request that the Commission preserve all records and communications relating to the topics addressed in this letter, from January 1, 2025, to the present and continue preserving existing and future materials on an ongoing basis. This preservation hold applies to all relevant records within the Commission’s possession and any person or entity representing or purporting to be acting on its behalf. This includes, but is not limited to, records and communications via email, whether official or personal; mobile devices; encrypted or disappearing messaging applications; social media; calendar entries; meeting notes; and voicemail and text messages. To the extent that the Commission uses any auto-delete functions, it should immediately suspend auto-delete functions and notify persons with control over potentially relevant records of similar preservation obligations.

Thank you for your attention to this matter. We look forward to your prompt response by November 23, 2026, including a written confirmation that the Commission is preserving all records related to this Congressional inquiry.

###

title: Shaheen Joins Colleagues in Fight to Overturn the Trump Administration’s Abortion Ban at VA
text:
(Washington, DC) – U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), a senior member of the U.S. Senate Armed Services Committee, joined more than 200 of her Senate and House Democratic colleagues in filing an amicus brief to Minority Veterans of America v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs, a lawsuit challenging the Trump Administration’s ban on abortion care and counseling at the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), including in cases of rape, incest or when a veteran’s health is endangered.

The members of Congress wrote, in part: “VA’s Final Rule rests on a faulty interpretation of federal law that has significant negative consequences for our nation’s veterans. The issues presented in this case potentially reach roughly 462,000 women veterans of reproductive age who are enrolled in VA health care, along with an estimated 112,000 women of reproductive age enrolled in the Civilian Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veterans Affairs (CHAMPVA).”

They continued: “For them, the Final Rule means a VA physician is prohibited from discussing the full range of a patient’s options during a pregnancy, prohibited from providing the full range of health care available to pregnant women, and is prohibited from intervening when a pregnancy threatens the patient’s health or is the result of rape or incest.”

The full text of the amicus brief can be read HERE.

The amicus brief, led by Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Mark Takano (CA-39), was signed by all 47 Democratic U.S. Senators and by 165 Democratic U.S. Representatives.

Senator Shaheen has long worked to expand access to quality health care for veterans and protect the reproductive freedoms of women service members and military families. In March 2026, Shaheen spoke on the Senate floor in support of Blumenthal’s Congressional Review Act (CRA) to overturn the Trump Administration’s restrictions on abortion care and counseling for veterans. Shaheen also secured provisions in the Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Military Construction, Veterans Affairs and Related Agencies (MilCon-VA) Appropriations bill to improve veterans’ access to substance use disorder treatment and strengthen efforts to prevent and respond to intimate partner violence. Shaheen secured provisions in the final FY2025 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) to expand access to contraception for women service members and military dependents. In 2024, Shaheen introduced bipartisan legislation to provide mental health support to women service members before and after giving birth. Shaheen has also led efforts to protect access to reproductive health care, including abortion services, for service members and their families regardless of where they are stationed.

title: Thune: Republicans Continue Aggressive Pace of Confirming President Trump’s Nominees
text:
Click here to watch the video.

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) today delivered the following remarks on the Senate floor:

Thune’s remarks below (as delivered):

“Madam President, on Thursday the Senate confirmed Gregory Cook to be U.S. district court judge for the Northern District of Alabama.

“Judge Cook is the 57th federal judge confirmed during this Congress.

“Later today, we’ll confirm our 58th.

“And there will be more to come.

“Thanks to the diligent work of Chairman Grassley and the Judiciary Committee, we have a number of additional judges to confirm before the year is out.

“And we’ve already locked in floor votes for every available judicial nominee.

“In fact … Madam President … if you look at this chart and the number that have been confirmed, the noms that are teed-up, which we will process here shortly, there are zero remaining on the calendar.

“In other words, that have been recommended by the administration and gone through the process at the Senate Judiciary Committee where they’ve been reported out to the floor for consideration.

“So, 57 confirmed already, six that are teed-up that we will be confirming here shortly, and then hopefully, Madam President, we will have more that we will be able to put on the calendar soon … as the administration makes recommendations and the Judiciary Committee is able to process that.

“So, we’ve locked votes in for every available judicial nominee.

“Every available judicial nominee has been locked in right now on the floor to be voted on.

“So, Madam President, we will also confirm more than one hundred additional presidential nominees before the end of the year.

“And once again, our committees have done excellent work processing these nominations.

“Madam President, since this majority took over last January … we’ve confirmed 606 civilian nominees.

“And that includes getting the president’s Cabinet in place at the fastest pace in over 20 years – in half the time – half the time – it took to fill the Obama and first Trump Cabinets.

“We’ve consistently cleared the calendar of available nominees throughout our majority.

“As I said, we’ll confirm our 58th judicial nominee today.

“And I’ll note that when it comes to judges, we’re turning nominations into confirmations at the fastest pace since the Reagan administration.

“Madam President, when this majority took over nearly two years ago, building this kind of record on nominations didn’t look very likely.

“It was clear from the outset that Democrats were intent on a historic level of obstruction.

“And they dragged out the process for virtually every nominee to come before this body.

“It took a year and a half before Democrats finally let a few nominees go by voice vote – something no other president has had to deal with.

“In fact, if you look at recent history, presidents have had the vast majority of their nominees approved by voice vote or unanimous consent – because, historically, this institution has cooperated to try and make sure that an administration has their people in place.

“If you look throughout history, Madam President, 98 percent for Presidents George H.W. Bush and Clinton.

“98 percent of the nominees that they made for positions in the executive branch of our government were confirmed either by voice vote or unanimous consent here on the floor of the Senate.

“98 percent.

“90 percent for Presidents George W. Bush and Barack Obama.

“Well, then came President Trump’s first administration, when Democrats introduced an unprecedented level of partisanship to the confirmation process, forcing time-consuming votes on nominees who would normally have gone by unanimous consent or voice.

“But even with this new level of partisanship, President Trump in his first term and President Biden each had more than half of their nominees approved by unanimous consent or voice vote here in the United States Senate.

“Well, then President Trump started his second term – and Democrats took it up a notch.

“Quite a few notches, actually.

“Madam President, as I said, until earlier this year, Democrats had not allowed a single – single – nominee to be confirmed by voice or unanimous consent.

“They also dragged out the process on nominees who went on to get bipartisan support in their confirmation votes – sometimes by large margins here on the floor.

“So let’s not mistake Democrats’ obstruction for some sort of principled stand.

“This was partisan politics.

“But Republicans were determined to overcome Democrats’ obstruction and ensure that the president got his nominees in place.

“That included taking action to restore the Senate’s practice of confirming noncontroversial nominees in batches – the way things have traditionally been done around here.

“That’s allowed us to clear the nominations calendar on several occasions.

“Most of all, Madam President, we’ve just done a lot of work.

“To begin with, we had the longest continuous session in 15 years, which allowed us to confirm the Cabinet, as I said earlier, at a historically quick pace.

“And when we turned to lower-level nominees, we continued to put in the work in committees and on the floor.

“We showed up for the votes.

“Lots and lots of votes.

“In fact, last year, Madam President, 2025, the first year, as a lot of these nominees were coming to … the Senate for consideration – we cast more votes in 2025 than any Senate in history with one exception, going back 80 years.

“Lots and lots of votes.

“And we did the same when it came to confirming judges to the federal bench.

“The results speak for themselves.

“Madam President, we are going to continue our aggressive pace for the remainder of this year.

“Because when Democrats take control of the Senate next year, our job is going to get a lot harder.

“But there’s time left on the clock for this Republican majority.

“And we intend to use it.”

title: Warner, Kaine, Van Hollen, Alsobrooks Meet with WMATA GM to Discuss Funding, Modernization Priorities Ahead of Major Transportation Bill
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) and Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks (both D-MD) met with Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (WMATA) General Manager and CEO Randy Clarke to discuss the future of Metro, the importance of sustained federal investment in public transportation, and opportunities to modernize and improve transit service across the National Capital Region.

The meeting comes as Congress prepares to consider the next surface transportation reauthorization bill, which will determine federal funding levels and priorities for public transportation systems across the country.

“Metro is the backbone of our region’s transportation network, connecting millions of residents and visitors to jobs, schools, businesses, and essential services. A safe, reliable, and affordable transit system is critical to our region’s economy and residents’ quality of life. We’ve made significant progress in improving Metro’s safety and reliability, but there’s still more work to do. As Congress prepares to take up the next transportation bill, we’re committed to protecting critical federal investments and making sure Metro has the resources it needs to serve our region for decades to come,” said the senators.

During the meeting, the senators and WMATA leadership discussed the importance of maintaining federal transit funding at levels established under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, including funding for critical maintenance and state-of-good-repair projects. They also discussed the federal Capital Investment Grants program, which supports major transit improvements and modernization projects including the Richmond Highway BRT project in Fairfax and the Veirs Mill Road BRT project in Montgomery County, Maryland.

These investments are particularly important as Metro works to modernize aging infrastructure, improve reliability, and reduce its maintenance backlog. Since 2016, Metro has reduced its backlog of state-of-good-repair projects from approximately $7 billion to $4 billion, progress that could be jeopardized by reductions in federal funding.

The discussion also included major regional transit priorities, including Metro’s proposed Red Line Modernization Project, which would upgrade aging signaling technology and improve operations across the system.

The region’s senators have long advocated for robust federal support for public transportation.

title: After Warnock Calls for Delay, Trump Administration Announces Six-Month Pause on New Medicaid Requirements
text:
Days after Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock called for a delay of Medicaid cuts, the Trump administration announced it would give states who opt-in an additional six months to prepare for the new requirements

Nearly $1 trillion in Medicaid cuts championed by Congressional Republicans and signed into law by President Trump will begin taking effect in January 2027

The move allows states to delay ending Medicaid coverage due to the new requirements until July 2027

Three to seven million Americans are estimated to lose their health care coverage from work reporting requirements alone

Senator Reverend Warnock: “I’m glad the administration is finally acknowledging what we’ve been saying all along: this is a bad law, and millions of Americans are at risk of losing their health care because of it”

Washington, D.C. – Days after U.S. Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) and Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), both members of the Senate Finance Committee, led a coalition of Democratic Senators in calling for a delay of new Medicaid cuts enacted in Congressional Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act, the Trump administration announced it would give states that opt-in an additional six months to prepare for the new requirements. The move will allow states to delay denying or terminating Medicaid coverage for individuals who do not meet work reporting requirements until July 2027.

President Trump and Congressional Republicans made Medicaid cuts a central part of their massive tax and spending bill, which overwhelmingly benefited wealthy Americans while weakening the social safety net for working families. Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, an estimated three to seven million Americans risk losing their health care coverage because of work reporting requirements.

“I’m glad the administration is finally acknowledging what we’ve been saying all along: this is a bad law, and millions of Americans are at risk of losing their health care because of it,” said Senator Warnock. “This delay is a step in the right direction, but six months isn’t enough. That’s why I’ll keep fighting for a full repeal of these disastrous cuts.”

Medicaid is a cornerstone of the U.S. health care system, providing health insurance coverage to more than one in five Americans. The program covers 40% of U.S. births, provides 20% of all hospital funding, and is the single largest payer of long-term services and supports, including nursing home care. President Trump and Congressional Republicans have made cuts to Americans’ health care coverage a central part of their legislative agenda since President Trump returned to office. A July report found that two million fewer children were enrolled in Medicaid in April, compared to January 2025 when President Trump took office.

Senator Warnock is a leading proponent of Medicaid expansion and has long championed efforts to increase Georgians’ access to affordable health care. Last year, he released a report titled “Healthy People, Healthy Economy,” which found investing in Medicaid stimulates economic growth and promotes access to employment. In June, Senator Warnock forced a vote pushing for the release of data surrounding Medicaid coverage loss nationwide. Senator Warnock’s effort to release the data was blocked by Senate Republicans.

title: Welch Joins Senate Agriculture Democrats in Demanding USDA Reverse Course on Proposed Rule Restricting Food Assistance
text:
Proposed rule could threaten SNAP for an estimated 6.3 million Americans, including more than 10,000 Vermonters

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Agriculture Subcommittee on Rural Development, Energy, and Credit, joined every Senate Agriculture Committee Democrat in urging the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to withdraw a newly proposed rule to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) that will severely narrow eligibility requirements for the nation’s largest anti-hunger program.

In their letter to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins, the Senators warn that the department’s proposed rule to restrict SNAP’s Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE)—which helps food-insecure Americans access food while supporting work and financial stability—could threaten access to SNAP for an estimated 6.3 million Americans, including more than 10,000 Vermonters. The Senators emphasize that USDA should not make changes to SNAP that leave families with fewer resources to meet their basic needs at a time when everyday Americans are already struggling to afford groceries.

The Senators write: “Children should not go hungry, seniors should not have to spend down their savings to afford groceries, and working families should not lose assistance while they are still struggling to make ends meet. USDA’s proposal would put these families at greater risk while adding costs and complications for states. We urge USDA to withdraw the proposed rule in its entirety.”

The Senators highlight the dangers of USDA’s proposed changes to SNAP’s BBCE requirement, which helps working families and seniors on fixed incomes access food: “Without it, a working family could lose SNAP benefits entirely after a modest raise, even when the additional earnings are not enough to replace the assistance it loses. BBCE allows states to prevent this abrupt cutoff so that families can continue receiving assistance as their earnings increase and their SNAP benefits gradually decline. It also allows low-income families and seniors to maintain modest emergency savings without losing assistance. These protections help people meet their basic needs while building assets and working toward greater financial security and economic mobility. This flexibility has been embraced by leaders of both parties and is now used in 43 states, the District of Columbia, Guam, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.”

The Senators underscore how, beyond directly harming families, the proposal would make SNAP more difficult and expensive for states to administer: “Most states use BBCE to raise or eliminate SNAP’s restrictive and complex federal asset test, reducing paperwork and the potential for payment errors. Reinstating these tests would require households to provide additional financial verification and place significant new demands on state workers. According to an analysis by the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, asset-related errors added approximately one percentage point, on average, to SNAP payment error rates in states that retained asset tests in fiscal year 2023. Under H.R. 1, which ties states’ share of SNAP benefit costs to their payment error rates, even a small increase could push states into higher cost-sharing tiers. With states already absorbing a larger share of SNAP administrative expenses, this proposal would impose new burdens while leaving them with fewer resources to manage those demands.”

“The effects would also reach well beyond SNAP. Children in households that lose SNAP eligibility would lose their SNAP-based automatic certification for free school meals, requiring families without another automatic eligibility pathway to submit additional applications and schools to verify eligibility. This would add unnecessary red tape for families and schools and increase the risk that eligible children miss out on meals. Fewer children directly certified through SNAP would also put federal school meal reimbursements at risk, particularly for schools participating in the Community Eligibility Provision,” the Senators continue. “The proposal would also complicate access to the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), requiring some families to provide additional income documentation and leaving others ineligible for assistance altogether.

The Senators highlight how USDA’s repeated claims that the proposed rule aligns SNAP rules with congressional intent, the legislative history clearly demonstrates otherwise: “Congress established categorical eligibility to simplify access to food assistance and preserved this framework when it created Temporary Assistance for Needy Families in 1996. States have relied on this flexibility for decades to serve low-income households and administer SNAP more efficiently. Congress subsequently considered proposals to eliminate or restrict BBCE during the 2005 reconciliation debate and the 2014 and 2018 Farm Bill negotiations, but these restrictions were ultimately rejected on a bipartisan basis and excluded from the final legislation. While maintaining SNAP eligibility for 6.3 million Americans who need it should be reason enough, the fact that this proposed rule is contrary to congressional intent and the law is another reason it should be withdrawn.”

Read and download the Senators’ full letter to USDA Secretary Rollins.

Senator Welch has been a leading advocate for protecting and expanding access to nutrition programs in the Senate. The Senator has led bipartisan and bicameral legislation to help more Americans access SNAP and improve child nutrition, including the Senior Hunger Prevention Act, COLAs Don’t Count Act, Farm to School Act, Keep SNAP Funded Act, Local School Foods Expansion Act, Improving Access to Nutrition Act of 2025, Student Loan Deduction Act, Whole Milk for Healthy Kids Act, and the School Lunch Debt Cancellation Act.

title: Chairman Wicker Delivers Speech on Putin’s Military Failures
text:
WASHINGTON- U.S. Senator Roger Wicker, R-Miss., Chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, today delivered a speech on the floor of the U.S. Senate outlining Vladimir Putin’s military failures and Russia’s deteriorating situation.

Watch Video Here

Read Chairman Wicker’s Speech as delivered.

Madame President, I now want to discuss with my colleagues the situation going on in Ukraine, and, specifically, Vladimir Putin’s illegal war on Ukraine and the Ukrainian people. I am wearing on my lapel, as I do most days, the United States flag and the Ukrainian flag to demonstrate my support and to emphasize to people who see me my view that it’s in the best interest of America and of the American people for the United States and for this Senate and this Congress to support the effort in Ukraine to defend themselves and their people against Russia’s aggression.

Listen to these words, and I quote:

“After getting to know and fully understand the Ukraine/Russia Military and Economic situation and, after seeing the Economic trouble it is causing Russia, I think Ukraine, with the support of the European Union, is in a position to fight and WIN all of Ukraine back in its original form.

Madame President, those are not my words. Those are the words of Donald J. Trump, made a little over a year ago, precisely on September 23, 2025. These are the words of our commander-in-chief just a year ago or so. And so let me read them again, along with all of President Trump’s full statement.

I begin again:

“After getting to know and fully understand the Ukraine/Russia Military and Economic situation and, after seeing the Economic trouble it is causing Russia, I think Ukraine, with the support of the European Union, is in a position to fight and WIN all of Ukraine back in its original form.

I applaud the president in that remark. Continuing to quote from our commander-in-chief, Donald J. Trump:

With time, patience, and the financial support of Europe and, in particular, NATO, the original Borders from where this War started, is very much an option.

Why not? Russia has been fighting aimlessly for three and a half years a War that should have taken a Real Military Power less than a week to win.

These are the words of our commander-in-chief. I continue to quote him:

This is not distinguishing Russia. In fact, it is very much making them look like “a paper tiger.”

When the people living in Moscow, and all of the Great Cities, Towns, and Districts all throughout Russia, find out what is really going on with this War, the fact that it’s almost impossible for them to get Gasoline through the long lines that are being formed, and all of the other things that are taking place in their War Economy, where most of their money is being spent on fighting Ukraine, which has Great Spirit, and only getting better, Ukraine would be able to take back their Country in its original form and, who knows, maybe even go further than that!

Our president said, a year ago. Continuing on with quoting from our president:

Putin and Russia are in BIG Economic trouble, and this is the time for Ukraine to act.

Further to quote our president:

In any event, [he says] I wish both Countries well. We will continue to supply weapons to NATO for NATO to do what they want with them. Good luck to all!

Well, let me say this, Madame President, I do wish the people of those countries well. I wish—I have nothing but admiration for the Ukrainian people. And after having visited them, as many senators have over time, my admiration for them and what they’re going through and the resolve that they’re showing, is a matter of, something to admire. And I have nothing but heartache and affection for the people of Russia. They are suffering under a war criminal, under a dictator, who should not be entertained and feted in the palaces of this world and of democratic countries but should be in jail as a war criminal. But I do have affection for the Russian people. They deserve better than what they’re getting from their president.

Russia’s position has continued to deteriorate in the year since President Trump made these remarks. The statement that our commander-in-chief made thirteen months, fourteen months ago is even truer today. Putin’s continued losses vindicate President Trump’s words: Russia has not distinguished itself. On the contrary, it’s shamed its leadership. Putin is likely the most inept military leader of our century. Vladimir Putin is perhaps the most inept military leader of our century.

Consider Russia’s dismal rate of territorial gains, with all their power.

Last year, Russia gained 1,874 square miles of territory—or about 0.8 percent of Ukraine’s territory.

That’s not impressive, but it gets worse for Vladimir Putin, the war criminal and dictator.

This year, Russia has managed a mere 46 square miles of territory gained in Ukraine. That is 0.02 percent of Ukrainian territory. What an accomplishment for this vast military power. It’s less than half the land area of my state’s capital city, Jackson.

This summer, Ukraine’s heroic Vivaldi counteroffensive blocked Russia’s attempt to breach the Fortress Belt. This is the line of cities in Donetsk that are key to the defense of eastern Ukraine, and it was a key target of Vladimir Putin’s war aims.

As the president said, a real military power should have succeeded in this campaign—should have succeeded easily in this campaign. Instead, Putin managed only 46 square miles since the start of this year.

And the trend is getting even worse.

In September and October, Russia actually lost ground. The tide is turning, with a net loss of 31 square miles in September and a net loss of 10 square miles in October. The Ukrainians are pushing the Russians back.

Both these gradual battlefield losses and meager battlefield gains have come at a terrible, tragic, growing cost for Russia’s frontline troops. And the tragedy is for average Russian families, for young Russian men and women who have suffered at the lust for power and territory of their dictator.

In October of 2026, Russian forces experienced their highest monthly casualties of the entire war. It was the fourth month in a row that Russia exceeded 40,000 casualties in one month, Madam President. Now a casualty is more than an injury. A casualty is either a fatality or a war wound that takes the troop out of action. Those are casualties. There have been more injuries. 40,000 in one month.

In the past year, Vladimir Putin passed a grim milestone. Now this is the truth. One point five million casualties in his war. A tragedy for Russian moms and dads. An incredible, tragic, needless number. To put this in context: Russia’s population is less than half ours—340 million for the United States, 143 million only for Russia. That’s like having more than 3 million American casualties. That’s the rate.

Can you imagine what a democratic, representative republic would do to a president who had resulted, gratuitously, in that level of casualties? At some points this year, Russia’s casualty rate exceeded the recruitment rate. They’re losing more boys and girls than they’re actually able to bring into the military. It is a shame on the leadership, the dictatorship of Russia. It’s no wonder he’s had to turn to bribing and tricking foreigners to replenish the ranks of his army.

But Putin’s troubles have been further complicated by Ukraine’s own long-range missile campaign. Consider Ukraine’s effective strikes on Putin’s energy supplies. I’m glad they finally started. Yes ma’am, I’m glad they finally started. Russian energy sales fund Putin’s war machine. It’s Russia’s energy sales that fund the death of Ukrainian boys and girls and 1.5 million casualties on Russia itself. Putin’s energy supplies. Russian energy sales fund Putin’s war machines, but Ukraine has managed to put 30 percent of Russia’s oil refining capacity offline—good for them. I hope Ukraine puts more of Russia’s oil refining capacity offline.

For years, Putin’s terror campaign has felt distant to residents of Russia’s major cities—St. Petersburg, Moscow. Ukraine’s effective counter has made the war real even to them, to the sophisticated people of Western Russia. They see the smoke plumes. They see the way Putin has to ration oil. They certainly do not appreciate sitting in long lines to fill up their vehicles.

Russia’s situation continues to deteriorate. Putin has reinforced the truth of President Trump’s words, which I have just quoted, verbatim, from the president, “Putin and Russia are in BIG Economic trouble.” And I say bravo to that.

I agreed with the president in September of last year, and I still agree with those words.

President Trump said that with time, patience, and assistance, Ukraine can win. I believe that.

We and our European partners can give Ukraine all three.

We will soon see the end of five years of this war. Incredible. Within that time, Ukraine has proven steadfast, and Russia has proven weak and unable to achieve its battlefield goals.

Putin has made it clear that he, not Ukraine, is the obstacle to peace. For years, President Zelensky has agreed to ceasefires. He would agree to a ceasefire in place today, I firmly believe, Madam President. Putin doesn’t want peace. Putin wants the Donbas. Putin wants Crimea. But he can’t have it. He’s not entitled to it under international law, and he can’t even get the Donbas after four, almost five years of war.

Instead of rushing into a bad deal, our president and Ukraine have been patient. And Ukraine’s stewarded its patience well. They have capitalized on Putin’s incompetence by taking the war to the Kremlin. And bravo for them.

And, finally, with assistance, Ukraine has been wearing Russia down. After nearly five years of war, it’s clear that the only thing that will change Putin’s calculations is strength.

President Trump asked in his statement, which I quoted, “Why not?” Why can’t Ukraine win back its territory? It’s a good question. It is a result devoutly to be wished. And it’s a prospect that stirs the heart of anyone who loves freedom and hates tyranny.

Russia continues to send missiles that reign death on Ukrainian women and children. We ought to help Ukraine defend against those missiles.

We and our European allies should increase sanctions on Russian energy and crack down on its shadow fleet, continuing to do that.

And we should do what we can to expedite Ukraine’s growing defense industry.

And our European allies must continue doing so as well. And I applaud the president for making that a key part of his program, his success, in this regard. Yes, our European allies are doing more, as they should. Together, we can increase the pressure on Putin and bring a faster, more just end to this war.

The president wants peace. I want peace. And no one wants peace more than the Ukrainian people. Putin, the war criminal, wants territory. He wants conquest. As the president said, let’s put Ukraine, “in a position to fight and WIN all of Ukraine back in its original form.”

And so I come back to how I started, Madam President. President Trump’s words last year are true. They are still absolutely true. The world will be safer—and Americans will be safer—if we help Ukraine do just that—win their victory.

Thank you, Madame President. And I yield the floor.

###

title: Senator Wicker’s International Political Prisoners Resolution Approved by the Senate
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Roger Wicker, R-Miss., welcomed the Senate’s unanimous approval of his “International Day of Political Prisoners” resolution. This measure supports designating each October 30 as a day to honor political dissidents around the world who have been unjustly detained.

Senator Wicker’s resolution formally conveys the Senate’s condemnation of all forms of political repression and expresses the institution’s solidarity with those who are imprisoned for peacefully expressing their political or religious beliefs. Further, the resolution applauds efforts by the U.S. government to secure the release of political prisoners and urges further action to hold regimes accountable for political persecution.

In addition to Senator Wicker, Senators Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., and Jeanne Shaheen, D-N.H., co-sponsored the resolution.

“In many parts of the world, ordinary individuals are punished and imprisoned for speaking their minds or criticizing their leaders – freedoms that Americans often take for granted,” said Senator Wicker. “Many of these prisoners are the ones taking a stand against brutal regimes that threaten our national security. We owe it to these courageous men and women to stand in solidarity with them.”

Background on Senator Wicker’s Resolution:

On October 30, 1974, Soviet prisoners of conscience held in gulags launched a hunger strike to raise awareness of their plight and other individuals held under similar charges. In the years that followed, October 30 became a yearly day of remembrance and activism for political prisoners not only in the then-Soviet Union but around the world.

Currently, there are an estimated 1 million individuals across the globe who are detained or imprisoned for voicing disagreement with their government. These include journalists, activists, government critics, and opposition leaders, among others.

Senator Wicker has long been a voice for political activists wrongfully imprisoned by authoritarian regimes. In 2023, Senator Wicker spoke out on behalf of Vladimir Kara-Murza, an outspoken critic of Russia’s aggression, who was persecuted by Putin’s regime. When Mr. Kara-Murza was released the next year, Senator Wicker reunited with him at the U.S. Capitol.

The full text of the resolution is available here.
