title: Wicker, Colleagues Introduce Legislation to Support Families Facing Rare Childhood Diseases
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Roger Wicker, R-Miss., Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn., Eric Schmitt, R-Mo., and Chris Coons, D-Del., today introduced the Genomic Answers for Children’s Health Act of 2026. This legislation would clarify that Medicaid must cover genomic sequencing for children with suspected rare diseases or genetic disorders who are enrolled in the program.

“Parents of children with rare diseases often spend years waiting for a diagnosis. Even when test results arrive, the answers can be frustratingly inconclusive,” said Senator Wicker. “Genomic sequencing offers families faster and more reliable results. Through early detection, more patients will be able to get the care they need without endless delays and extensive testing, saving families and providers money in the long run.”

“For parents, few things are harder than knowing your child needs help and not having answers or knowing what options are available to help them. By expanding access to genomic sequencing for children with suspected rare diseases and genetic disorders, we can help parents get answers faster, doctors make more accurate diagnoses, and ensure families can get the care their children need,” said Klobuchar. “This bipartisan bill is an important step toward improving health outcomes and saving children’s lives.”

“As the father of a child with a rare medical condition, I understand firsthand the challenges Missouri families like mine face. Worrying about the cost of care should be the last thing on a parent’s mind. By ensuring Medicaid covers genomic sequencing for children with rare diseases, Missouri families will be able to better access the answers and care their children need,” said Senator Schmitt.

“When your child is sick, there’s nothing you wouldn’t give to make them better,” said Senator Coons. “For millions of families across the nation whose children have a rare disease, they are left waiting and waiting for the answers and treatments they need. This bill brings an end to the waiting, giving families access to the keys that could unlock their children’s futures.”

Background on the Genomic Answers for Children’s Health Act of 2026:

Approximately 30 million Americans suffer from rare diseases, and half of these patients are children. For many, the diagnosing process can take between four to eight years, and it can still yield inaccurate results and amount to thousands of dollars in medical costs. Genomic sequencing—a type of testing that examines an individual’s entire DNA sequence—is a more efficient and accurate alternative.

If signed into law, Senator Wicker’s bill would:

Require Medicaid to cover whole genome sequencing and whole exome sequencing as mandatory benefits for enrollees under the age of 21

Direct states to expand access to genomic testing in hospital settings

Instruct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to raise awareness about genomic sequencing

As Chairman of the Senate’s Rare Disease Caucus, Senator Wicker has been a leader in strengthening medical research and expanding access to care for individuals suffering from extraordinary health conditions. When he served as a member of the House of Representatives, Wicker authored the MD CARE Act, which allocated extensive funding for research dedicated to Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD). Last year, Senator Wicker introduced the Scientific EXPERT Act, which would allow the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to use findings and insights from medical experts in its work to improve outcomes for patients battling rare diseases.

The full text of the bill is available here.

title: Wyden, Merkley, Bonamici Announce $440,000 to Support Coastal Victims of Trafficking
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, along with U.S. Representative Suzanne Bonamici, today announced $440,000 in federal awards to support victims of trafficking in Clatsop County.

“Survivors of human trafficking carry unimaginable trauma, and they deserve strong, coordinated support systems rooted in their own communities,” Wyden said. “I’m glad to see these federal dollars heading to Astoria so The Harbor can broaden its outreach, strengthen local emergency response networks and ensure no victim in Clatsop County has to navigate recovery alone.”

“We must continue to do everything in our power to protect people from the horrors of human trafficking and support its survivors,” Merkley said. “This essential funding will help The Harbor continue its critical work of raising awareness, supporting victims, and providing hope to survivors in Clatsop County.”

“We must empower and support survivors of the despicable crime of human trafficking. The Harbor in Clatsop County has been doing this important work and has earned the community's trust and support,” Bonamici said. “This grant will help to deliver more services and outreach where they are needed throughout Clatsop County, increase awareness of trafficking, and help develop a coordinated response. I’m grateful to my colleagues in the Senate for helping secure this funding and to The Harbor’s staff for their important work.”

The $440,000 in federal awards from the Department of Justice’s Office of Justice Program will be distributed to The Harbor in Astoria. The Harbor is a nonprofit that provides advocacy, prevention and support for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault and stalking in Clatsop County. The federal award will be used to expand services to victims including crisis intervention, case management, safety planning, shelter, emergency financial assistance and referrals. The Harbor will also conduct outreach to increase awareness of trafficking and available services for victims, and will develop partnerships with local agencies and organizations to develop a coordinated human trafficking response.

title: Wyden, Merkley, Colleagues Push for Senate, House Leadership to Strip Provisions in Defense Bill that Mandate Concerning U.S.-Israel Defense, Intelligence Cooperation
text:
Washington D.C.—U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley said today they have joined Senate colleagues in pressing congressional leadership to exclude provisions in the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act that would require the president to expand and enhance concerning aspects of defense cooperation and intelligence sharing with the Israeli government.

The provisions would undermine the United States’ ability to act independently and in line with U.S. national security interests at a time when the government of Israel’s actions are increasingly not aligned with those interests, the Oregon senators said.

“These provisions would constrain the Administration’s ability to independently determine how best to protect U.S. national security and would lock in long-term commitments despite our serious concerns with the Israeli government’s actions in Gaza, the West Bank, and other parts of the region,” the lawmakers wrote to Senate and House leadership.

“The agreements and projects these provisions envision threaten U.S. national security interests by handing Israel leverage over American weapons systems and military technology. This is not hypothetical. The Netanyahu government has already leveraged its existing coproduction agreement with the United States on missile defense to block American Iron Dome batteries from reaching Ukraine, in direct opposition to U.S. national security interests,” the lawmakers continued. “Should these provisions be enacted, it would further increase Israel’s leverage over the United States through some of the most sensitive technologies in warfare. That is not in the U.S. interest. If enacted, these agreements would create long-term dependencies by embedding Israeli technology into the U.S. defense industrial base that could make future policy changes costly or difficult to implement. President Trump, at his own discretion, could choose to enter new agreements with Israel under existing law. The executive branch does not need a congressional mandate to more deeply entrench U.S.-Israel defense cooperation.”

“Moreover, we do not share, let alone co-produce, many of these sensitive technologies even with our closest partners, including NATO or other treaty allies. To do so in this instance would be unwise, especially as the Government of Israel continues to pursue policies in Gaza, the West Bank and other parts of the region that are inconsistent with U.S. interests and values,” the lawmakers wrote.

“Prime Minister Netanyahu has openly stated that such an initiative was his idea. In a letter to Representative Stutzman, who led a resolution calling for an effort similar to these provisions, Prime Minister Netanyahu states, ‘I was glad to receive your proposed Congressional resolution endorsing my plan to shift the framework of the US-Israel defense cooperation from aid to partnership.’ The intention behind this is clear: to move U.S. security assistance governed through more traditional pathways, like Foreign Military Financing and arm sales, to more opaque, less discernible avenues through defense acquisitions and programs of record that reduce transparency, as well as increase Israel’s leverage over the United States and our dependency on Israeli technology. This is particularly problematic after Prime Minister Netanyahu boasted that he has been trying to start a war with Iran for 40 years. That war has proven to be a strategic disaster for the United States and against U.S. interests,” the senators wrote.

The letter was led by U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen, D-Md. In addition to Wyden and Merkley, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Patty Murray, D-Wash., Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., Brian Schatz, D-Hawaii, Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., Edward J. Markey, D-Mass., Tammy Duckworth, D-Ill., Tina Smith, D-Minn., Peter Welch, D-Vt., and Andy Kim, D-N.J. The letter was sent to Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., House Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) Chair Roger Wicker, R-Miss., Ranking Member Jack Reed, D-R.I., House Armed Services Committee Chair Mike Rogers, R-Ala., and Ranking Member Adam Smith, D-Wash.

title: Young, Indiana Delegation Support Efforts to Explore Establishing National Estuarine Research Reserve in Northwest Indiana
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator Todd Young (R-Ind.) joined Senator Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Representatives Frank J. Mvran (D-IN-01) and Jim Baird (R-IN-04) in sending a letter urging the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to consider the State of Indiana’s request to establish a National Estuarine Research Reserve (NERR) along Lake Michigan in Northwest Indiana.

“Lake Michigan is a vital part of Northwest Indiana’s economy and one of our state’s most important natural resources,” said Senator Young. “A National Estuarine Research Reserve could build on the work already underway to protect Lake Michigan by expanding research and conservation efforts, with Purdue University bringing valuable expertise to the table. Taking a closer look at what a reserve could offer The Region is a sensible next step.”

“Lake Michigan is one of Indiana’s greatest natural resources and is an important part of Northwest Indiana’s economy,” said Senator Banks. “Establishing a National Estuarine Research Reserve would strengthen conservation efforts, expand research opportunities, and help protect our shoreline for generations. I am proud to support this effort and urge the NOAA to move Indiana’s request forward.”

“Northwest Indiana is home to such incredible environmental wonders on our Lake Michigan shoreline, and I applaud the initiative of the State of Indiana and its partnership with Purdue University to continue to enhance conservation and research opportunities in this area,” said Representative Mrvan. “I look forward to continuing to partner with all of my fellow members of the Indiana Congressional delegation and federal officials to advance this worthwhile proposal.”

“Lake Michigan is an ecological marvel with a rich natural history. Glaciers and shifting sands shaped this Great Lake thousands of years ago,” said Representative Baird. “Today, Lake Michigan remains a beautiful and crucial natural resource for the Hoosier State. Designating the coastal region bordering Lake Michigan as a National Estuarine Research Reserve brings valuable support and recognition to ongoing conservation efforts. My alma mater, Purdue University, has been a leader in these efforts, and this designation will provide support to help protect this magnificent ecosystem and the economic opportunities it provides, for future generations.”

The text of the letter is available below and HERE.

“Dear Dr. Jacobs,

“We write in support of the State of Indiana’s request to establish a National Estuarine Research Reserve (NERR) in Northwest Indiana, along the coastal region bordering Lake Michigan. In November 2024, then-Governor Eric Holcomb submitted a formal request for a designation, and, in July 2026, Governor Mike Braun sent a letter reaffirming interest in this initiative. As members of the Indiana Congressional delegation, we urge NOAA to advance the State’s request through the appropriate designation process and provide an update on its status.

“Northwest Indiana’s Lake Michigan coastal region is a key environmental resource that provides unique economic, recreational, and educational opportunities in our state. We are committed to preserving and strengthening this region and believe that a NERR designation would support its long-term vitality, restoration, and resilience.

“Since 2001, Indiana has partnered with NOAA in coastal management through the Indiana Lake Michigan Coastal Program, which has supported public access improvements, educational opportunities, habitat preservation and restoration, and technical assistance for local coastal communities. Establishing a NERR in Northwest Indiana would build upon these efforts and provide meaningful benefits to the state and the broader Great Lakes bioregion.

“Currently, Indiana does not have a NERR, and only two reserves are designated in the Great Lakes region, neither of which is located along the southern shore of Lake Michigan. This region includes unique freshwater estuarine habitats that warrant sustained research, monitoring, and education. Establishing a NERR in Northwest Indiana would provide distinct value to the overall Reserve system by addressing research gaps, advancing scientific understanding of the region’s unique ecological processes, and enhancing management and restoration efforts for similar systems across the Great Lakes.

“Additionally, Purdue University’s College of Agriculture is strongly positioned to serve as the lead organization for this initiative. As a nationally recognized land grant institution, Purdue has a proven record of partnering with state and federal agencies, including the Indiana Department of Natural Resources, to advance research, education, and outreach efforts. Purdue is also home to several NOAA-funded programs, such as the Illinois-Indiana Sea Grant College Program and the Midwestern Regional Climate Center. This demonstrated expertise in coastal management prepares the university to support the long-term success of a NERR in Indiana.

“The Lake Michigan coastal region is essential to Indiana’s identity, economy, and environment. By expanding opportunities for research, education, and community engagement, establishing a NERR in Northwest Indiana would safeguard this vital environmental resource for generations to come. We appreciate NOAA’s consideration of this request and look forward to continuing to work together to strengthen the Great Lakes region.”

Sincerely,

Congressman Frank J. Mrvan (IN-01)

Congressman Jim Baird (IN-04)

U.S. Senator Todd Young (IN)

U.S. Senator Jim Banks (IN)

title: Whitehouse, Reed, and Amo Announce $532,000 in Federal Funding for Safer Roads in Smithfield
text:
Smithfield, RI – TODAY, U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), U.S. Senator Jack Reed (D-RI), and Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) announced $532,450 in federal funding for safety improvements along the Pleasant View Avenue corridor in Smithfield.

“Schools, small businesses, and homes line the busy Pleasant View Avenue corridor. This federal funding will help town leaders develop a plan to make the street safer for drivers and pedestrians,” said Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI). “Our Bipartisan Infrastructure Law continues to improve travel in the Ocean State.”

“I was pleased to work with then-Senator Tom Carper (D-DE) and others to help create this program back in 2021 and glad to see Smithfield earn this competitive grant to make needed road improvements and safety upgrades along Pleasant View Avenue,” said Senator Jack Reed (D-RI).

“Whether walking or driving, Rhode Islanders must be able to navigate the Pleasant View Avenue corridor safely,” said Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI). “These federal resources will help Smithfield develop a comprehensive plan to protect everyone who uses the street. I will keep working alongside our Senators to deliver federal funding that makes our communities better and safer for Rhode Islanders.”

“The Town of Smithfield community is very pleased with the award of Federal funds to improve the safety for traffic utilizing the Pleasant View Avenue corridor which is a heavily traveled roadway that cuts through the center of town. The safety improvements will benefit automobiles, motorcycles, bicycles and pedestrian traffic. We are grateful for the efforts of Senator Reed, Senator Whitehouse and Representative Amo for securing the funding. All three are great supporters of our town. Without this funding the town would not be able to support this level of safety improvements. This roadway sees many accidents annually. The federal funding will allow us to be proactive in reducing these accidents,” said Smithfield Town Manager Robert Seltzer.

Background

The competitive grant, funded through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law’s Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) program, was awarded to the Town of Smithfield to update its Comprehensive Safety Action Plan and conduct supplemental safety planning along the 2.7-mile Pleasant View Avenue corridor. Planned work includes updating the Action Plan with the most recent crash data, completing corridor and school safety studies, and testing temporary quick-build countermeasures. Findings of these studies will be used to develop projects to improve the roadway.

title: Congressman Bell to Host Health and Wellness Fair November 21
text:
Free screenings and medical services from mobile health units

Residents can connect with local health care providers and learn about resources

St. Louis, Missouri – Today, Congressman Wesley Bell (D-MO-01) announced he will host a Health and Wellness Fair on Saturday, November 21, from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. CT at Delmar Divine, in partnership with the Community Wellness Project.

The event will connect constituents with health care resources and on-site health screenings.

"Staying healthy takes more than a doctor’s visit. It takes access, information, and support. That is why I’m proud to partner with the Community Wellness Project to bring screenings, mobile health services, and local resources to Delmar Divine, and I hope neighbors will come out, get checked, and connect with the care they need,” said Congressman Bell.

"Better health starts with knowing where you stand. As part of Cigna Healthcare's commitment to improving the health and vitality of those we serve, the Wellness in Motion Tour brings convenient health screenings, personalized education, and expert guidance directly to the community. Visit the Wellness in Motion van at this weekend's Health and Wellness Fair for complimentary biometric screenings, including blood pressure, cholesterol, blood sugar, body mass index (BMI), and skin cancer screenings. In less than 15 minutes, you'll receive valuable insights into your health and meet one-on-one with a health coach who can help you understand your results and identify next steps toward better health. No appointment is needed, and you do not have to be a Cigna Healthcare® customer to participate. WHAT: Congressman Bell’s Health and Wellness Fair

WHERE: Delmar Divine, 5501 Delmar Blvd., St. Louis, MO (entrances on Belt Ave. and Enright Ave.)

WHEN: Saturday, November 21, 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. CT

title: Bilirakis Applauds Action to Protect Veterans from Fraud
text:
Washington, DC: Earlier today, Congressman Gus Bilirakis released the following statement:

“I applaud the Department of Justice, the Department of Veterans Affairs, and the VA Office of Inspector General for today's announcement of coordinated enforcement actions targeting fraud against veterans' benefits programs," said Congressman Gus Bilirakis. "The men and women who served our nation earned these benefits through their sacrifice, dedication, and commitment to protecting our freedoms. Those benefits should be used to support Veterans and their families, not exploited by individuals seeking to profit at their expense. Fraud targeting Veterans is particularly reprehensible because it undermines programs designed to serve those who have already given so much to our country. I commend the federal investigators, prosecutors, and law enforcement partners involved in this nationwide effort. Our Veterans deserve nothing less than a system that protects their benefits, honors their service, and ensures that those who seek to exploit them are held accountable."

title: Buchanan Celebrates Son James Buchanan’s Swearing-In as State Senator
text:
Applauds His Son’s Eight Years of Service in the Florida House as He Begins His Term in the State Senate

“As a Parent, You Measure Your Own Success by What Your Children Choose to Do with Their Lives.”

TALLAHASSEE, Fla. — Congressman Vern Buchanan today celebrated the swearing-in of his son, James Buchanan, as the new state senator for Florida Senate District 22, which covers Sarasota County and part of Manatee County. James took the oath of office during the Florida Legislature’s organization session in Tallahassee after eight years of service in the Florida House of Representatives.

“As a parent, you measure your own success by what your children choose to do with their lives,” said Buchanan. “I could not be more grateful that James chose public service. During his eight years in the Florida House, he put Floridians first, working to keep our state affordable and the best place in the country to raise a family. He earned the trust of the people of Sarasota and Manatee counties, and today he carries that trust into the Senate.”

James was first elected to the Florida House in 2018 and served four terms representing House District 74 in Sarasota County. During his time in the House, he built a reputation as a consistent, strong voice for Floridians. He was a lead advocate for limited government, lower taxes and policies that keep Florida affordable for working families.

Earlier this month, voters in state Senate District 22 elected James to succeed Sen. Joe Gruters, after he won the Republican primary in August with nearly 78 percent of the vote.

title: Buchanan, Joyce Bill to Expand Wheelchair Access for Seniors Signed into Law
text:
Choices for Increased Mobility Act Gives Medicare Beneficiaries an Affordable Path to Lighter and Stronger Wheelchairs

WASHINGTON – Congressman Vern Buchanan, Vice Chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee and Chairman of the Health Subcommittee, announced that the bipartisan Choices for Increased Mobility Act (H.R. 1703), has been signed into law by President Donald Trump. Buchanan co-led it with Rep. John Joyce (R-Pa), a physician.

“No senior should have to choose between their savings and their independence,” said Buchanan. “For too long, Medicare rules forced wheelchair users to pay thousands of dollars up front to get a lighter, stronger and safer wheelchair that fits their needs. The Choices for Increased Mobility law fixes that by letting patients pay only for the upgrade. I came to Congress to solve problems, and nothing has been more rewarding than the work we’ve done for seniors and families in Florida. As I close out 20 years in the House, this is the kind of result I’ll be proudest of. A bipartisan fix that hands people back their independence and asks nothing of the taxpayer.”

“This law will make a real difference for patients and caregivers by improving access to lightweight wheelchairs that can make daily life easier,” said Congressman John Joyce, M.D. “Medicare beneficiaries should have the freedom to choose mobility equipment that best meets their needs and helps them stay active and independent.”

For a manual wheelchair user, weight is not a luxury feature. A lighter chair is easier to self-propel, easier to lift into a car and gentler on shoulders doing the work of legs. Until now, Medicare’s rules put those chairs out of reach for the people who need them most: a beneficiary who wanted titanium or carbon fiber had to buy the chair outright, then wait for Medicare to reimburse only what it would have paid toward a heavier standard model. The difference ran into the thousands, enough to stop most seniors and Americans with disabilities before they started.

The Choices for Increased Mobility Act requires Medicare to create separate billing codes for ultralightweight manual wheelchairs, including one for chairs built with titanium or carbon fiber. Beneficiaries can now upgrade within their coverage and pay only the difference in cost. The legislation is designed to be budget neutral and does not increase Medicare spending or payment amounts.

The bill passed the House Energy and Commerce Committee 45-0 in May. It then passed the full House by voice vote in July and the Senate by unanimous consent in September. Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) and Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.) led the Senate companion bill, S. 247.

The new law adds to a two-decade record that has placed Buchanan among the most effective members of Congress. As Chairman of the Health Subcommittee, he has authored bipartisan legislation to protect Medicare, expand access to care for seniors and veterans and lower prescription drug costs. Buchanan, the longest-serving Republican to represent Southwest Florida in the U.S. House, will retire at the conclusion of his current term.

title: Congresswoman Kat Cammack, Paris Hilton Rally Bipartisan Women's Caucuses to Pass the DEFIANCE Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Kat Cammack (FL-03), Chairwoman of the Republican Women’s Caucus, hosted child safety advocate Paris Hilton and members of the Republican and Democratic Women’s Caucuses today at the U.S. Capitol to push for House passage of the DEFIANCE Act. The bipartisan bill would give survivors of nonconsensual, sexually explicit deepfakes a federal right to sue the people who create and spread them.

After the conversation, Cammack, Hilton and House members from both parties walked down the Capitol steps together and held a press conference at the House Triangle.

“Anyone can become a target. It takes one ordinary photo to make a fake, explicit image that spreads faster than it can be taken down,” said Congresswoman Cammack. “The DEFIANCE Act lets survivors take the people who did it to court. The Senate passed it without a single objection, and it’s sitting at the House desk right now. Let’s get it done before this Congress ends.”

The DEFIANCE Act (H.R. 3562) is led in the House by Reps. Laurel Lee (FL-13) and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-13), with more than 50 cosponsors from both parties, including Congresswoman Cammack. Sen. Dick Durbin (D-IL) and the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-SC) introduced the Senate companion, S. 1837, which passed by unanimous consent on January 13, 2026.

Cammack voted for the TAKE IT DOWN Act, which passed the House 409-2 and became law in May 2025. That law makes it a federal crime to publish nonconsensual intimate images, including AI-generated ones, and requires platforms to remove them within 48 hours of a victim’s request. The DEFIANCE Act would add a civil path for survivors to sue for damages in federal court.

Hilton helped drive passage of the Stop Institutional Child Abuse Act, which cleared the Senate unanimously and the House 373-33 before it was signed into law in December 2024. In January, she joined Reps. Lee and Ocasio-Cortez at the Capitol to call for House action on the DEFIANCE Act.

“Paris has spent years fighting for survivors, and she’s brought that same heart to this bill,” Cammack added. “We’re grateful to have her with us, and we’ll keep showing up alongside her until the DEFIANCE Act becomes law.”

“When I make a promise to survivors, I keep it,” said Hilton. “So I will come back to these halls as many times as it takes until the DEFIANCE Act is signed. Because the abuse hasn’t stopped, and neither will I.”

“The images may be fake, but the victims are real,” said Rep. Lee. “Their suffering is real, and their right to seek justice should be real, too.”

“To Representatives Sykes and Cammack and the Democratic and Republican Women’s Caucuses, thank you both so much for working together to ensure that Congress does not overlook an issue so personal to so many women and girls across the country,” said Rep. Ocasio-Cortez.

What the DEFIANCE Act does:

Lets survivors sue anyone who knowingly makes or shares a nonconsensual, sexually explicit deepfake, solicits and receives one, or holds one intending to share it.

Sets liquidated damages at $150,000, or $250,000 when the deepfake is tied to actual or attempted sexual assault, stalking or harassment, so survivors don’t have to prove a dollar loss. Survivors can instead seek actual damages, including the defendant’s profits.

Allows courts to order the images deleted or destroyed and to block further spread. Survivors who win recover attorney’s fees and costs.

Protects survivors’ privacy in court, including the option to file under a pseudonym.

Gives survivors 10 years to sue, counted from when they discover the violation or turn 18, whichever is later.

Works alongside existing state and tribal laws.

title: Carbajal Meets with Family of Central Coast Resident Held in Russian Prison; Presses State Department for Expedited Action to Free Him
text:
U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24) met with the family of Aleksandr Antonov, a 66-year-old Santa Barbara resident who has been wrongfully detained in Russia for over 600 days. On November 12, 2026, Carbajal met with Natalya Antonov, Aleksandr’s wife; and their two children, Anastasia and Andrey. The group discussed Aleksandr’s case and a joint letter Carbajal co-led with Rep. George Latimer (D-NY-16) urging the State Department to use every diplomatic, economic, and strategic tool available to secure the release of five U.S. nationals detained in Russia — including Aleksandr.

“Aleksandr Antonov is a Central Coast resident who has been detained by Russian authorities for over 600 days. I recently met with Aleksandr’s family, who told me that he has been subject to brutal treatment — including being beaten for being American, resulting in a traumatic brain injury that has so far gone untreated,” said Rep. Carbajal. “Like so many on the Central Coast, I am outraged by Aleksandr’s imprisonment. I stand with him, his loved ones, and the other Americans who are wrongfully imprisoned in Russia. I joined Congressman Latimer in demanding the State Department use every tool available to secure their release, including expediting the ‘wrongful detainment’ designation. I will continue to fight for Aleksandr’s release so he can finally come home to the Central Coast.”

“My family and I are so grateful to Rep. Carbajal for his proactive leadership in advocating for my father's freedom. He is an innocent American citizen who has been unjustly detained in Russia for over 600 days, very sick, and needs to come home to his family," said Anastasia Antonova, daughter of Aleksandr Antonov.

“The recent releases of Stephen Hubbard and Robert Gilman on ‘humanitarian grounds’ by the Russian Federation reinforces for me the continued suffering of Olga Jezler and other Americans detained for years in horrible conditions on trumped up charges. We are asking Secretary Rubio to use the power of the State Department to create the right conditions to bring our people safely home,” said Rep. Latimer.

Background:

Aleksandr Antonov is a 66-year-old husband and father. In the 1990s, Aleksandr and his wife, Natalya, left the former Soviet Union and settled in Santa Barbara, where the entire family became naturalized U.S. citizens.

Mr. Antonov frequently traveled to Ukraine and Crimea for business and often stayed for months at a time to care for relatives still living in Dnipro, Ukraine. On March 5, 2025, while attempting to cross the border from Russia’s western Pskov region into Estonia en route back to Santa Barbara, he was arrested by Russian authorities for having pro-Ukrainian messages on his cellphone. He was ultimately charged with inciting terrorism and extremism and sentenced to six years in prison.

Since his arrest, the Antonov family has been in contact with the American Citizen Services unit at the U.S. Embassy in Moscow to push for his release, and they have sent a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio requesting his assistance.

In late October, the family also reached out to Rep. Carbajal’s office for help, resulting in Rep. Carbajal signing onto Rep. Latimer’s letter shortly thereafter. Following that letter, CBS White House correspondent Jennifer Jacobs questioned President Trump on October 30 (video here) regarding the situation, prompting the President to note that his administration is working on eight cases involving Americans still detained in Russia.

The family has since followed up with the State Department’s Office of the Special Presidential Envoy for Hostage Affairs (SPEHA) to confirm whether Aleksandr is among the eight cases President Trump referenced, and they are awaiting a response. Rep. Carbajal met with the family on November 12, 2026, and continues to work closely with them to secure Aleksandr’s release.

The full letter to the State Department is available HERE and below.

Dear Secretary Rubio,

We write to express our grave concern for the U.S. nationals detained by the Russian Federation under circumstances that raise serious questions about their safety and wellbeing, due process, and violations to international norms. In particular, we write with concern for U.S. nationals who have been detained for extended periods and are recognized by the Department of State as “cases of concern” but who have not yet been designated as wrongfully detained under the Robert Levinson Hostage Recovery and Hostage-Taking Accountability Act ("Levinson Act") by the Department, a reality which deeply undermines the negotiating position of the United States in securing their safe and rightful return home, perpetuating their suffering under an unjust regime.

We are grateful that Stephen Hubbard was released from Russian custody after more than 1,663 days in prison. Mr. Hubbard was the only American in Russia designated wrongfully detained under the Levinson Act prior to his release. We also recognize and appreciate the continued efforts by the Office of the Special Presidential Envoy for Hostage Affairs (SPEHA), the U.S. Embassy in Moscow, and others in the administration who continuously engage on these critical cases and with the families of those wrongfully held by the Russian government, as well as the efforts of the Department of State to engage with Congress on constituent cases. In addition to Stephen Hubbard, we join the Gilman family in their relief following the August 2026 release of Robert Gilman after 1,666 days wrongfully detained in Russia and after horrific reports on his health and the conditions of his imprisonment.

Notably, when Robert was released near death, the Russian government commented about not having prioritized him because he had not been designated as unlawfully detained by the U.S.

Today, at least five U.S. nationals remain in these same conditions without designation. The continued detention of Americans in Russia underscores the need for sustained engagement and a renewed urgency to obtain their release, including in independent and direct negotiations with the Russian government separate from broader, ongoing negotiations on Russia’s war against Ukraine. Given the stalled status of negotiations between Russia and Ukraine, we are deeply concerned that tying the fate of these Americans and their families to broader issues in the U.S.-Russia relationship and deferring their designation as wrongful detainees undoubtedly prolongs their hardship.

Families of detainees endure significant emotional and financial hardship while awaiting progress on the release of their loved ones. Several of our offices have received troubling reports from family and community members regarding the conditions of detention of their loved ones and the perpetual nature of their detention. Many detainees have remained in Russian custody for years with no clear pathway for their release or return to the United States. As time passes, the physical, emotional, and psychological toll on both the detainees and their families continues to mount. The cases of detained U.S. nationals in Russia, include, but are not limited to, many of our constituents. As of October 21, 2026, these individuals have been held in Russian custody for the following days:

Andre Khachatoorian - 1,758 days

David Barnes - 1,742 days

Olga Jezler - 1,577 days

Alexsandr Antonov - 594 days

Chuck Zimmerman - 490 days

All of these individuals have deteriorating medical situations that are exacerbated, or are not being addressed, by the Russian prison system. Chuck Zimmerman is a U.S. Navy veteran kidnapped from international waters. He is in critical condition, literally starving to death due to an untreated critical gastrointestinal issue. Aleksandr Anotonov was beaten in a Russian prison for being American. He is now barely surviving with an untreated traumatic brain injury. Olga Jezler is a vibrant 36-year-old woman, languishing from a treatable medical condition that could put her at risk of losing her ability to have children, or worse. Andre Khachatoorian is fighting a worsening autoimmune disease with no access to proper medication. David Barnes is suffering debilitating dental issues, losing six teeth and has needed, and been denied, critical surgery while in prison.

Post-release reports that Robert Gilman’s medical situation was within 1-2 days of causing his death underscore our concern that action is warranted before a situation becomes potentially irreversible.

We are united in the belief that the safe return of U.S. nationals detained abroad must remain a priority of the United States government. We are deeply concerned that the authorities outlined in the Levinson Act to designate these U.S. nationals detained by the Russian Federation as wrongful detainees are not being fully leveraged. Using this invaluable legislation to its fullest extent, as Congress intended, would maximize U.S. government coordination and advance negotiations to ensure their swift release. The designation is also key for providing needed resources to the families as they advocate for their loved ones, while also ensuring full support to released detainees upon their return to the U.S.

We urge the administration to continue employing all diplomatic, economic, and strategic tools available to secure the release of these detained U.S. nationals, steadfastly support their families throughout this process, and conduct these negotiations regardless of a Russia-Ukraine peace process or other issues of bilateral concern. Specifically, we ask that this include:

1. Continuing to demand and ensure adequate consular access to all U.S. nationals held in Russian detention.

2. Expediting the consideration and employment of the "wrongful detention" designation as intended under the Levinson Act and subsequent legislation that has expanded the Levinson Act, including continued communication with Congress on the criteria and deliberations of such designations.

3. A plan and path forward to secure the release of U.S. nationals currently detained in the Russian Federation outside of negotiations related to Russia' s invasion of Ukraine or broader issues in the U.S.-Russia bilateral relationship.

4. Consideration of the use of the State Sponsor of Wrongful Detention designation that has already been used on other repeat offender nations, including Iran and Afghanistan.

title: Ciscomani Secures $3.1 Million Federal Investment for Southern Arizona Veterans’ Memorial Cemetery
text:
Sierra Vista, AZ - In a major win for Southern Arizona’s veterans, Representative Juan Ciscomani announced that the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs has awarded over $3.1 million to expand the Southern Arizona Veterans’ Memorial Cemetery. This transformative investment honors those who have bravely served our nation and ensures they may be laid to rest with dignity, close to the families and communities they love.

"This is a crucial investment in our veterans and their families, who have given so much for our country," said Rep. Juan Ciscomani. "Our heroes deserve to be honored with the utmost dignity and respect. With this funding, we can ensure veterans are laid to rest near their loved ones and the communities they served. This is a lasting tribute to the brave men and women whose sacrifices safeguard the freedoms we enjoy today."

For veterans and their families across Southern Arizona, a local veterans’ cemetery is more than a final resting place. It is a lasting symbol of honor and remembrance that connects generations and communities. As the veteran population grows, this expansion ensures their legacies will be preserved for years to come.

"The Southern Arizona Veterans’ Memorial Cemetery stands as a testament to our community’s gratitude for those who served," said Sierra Vista Mayor McMcaa. "This $3.1 million investment will guarantee that veterans and their families have a dignified, local place to remember their loved ones. We thank Representative Ciscomani for his unwavering commitment to our veterans and for his leadership in securing this vital funding."

The Southern Arizona Veterans’ Memorial Cemetery is one of 21 veterans’ cemeteries nationwide selected to receive a Fiscal Year 2026 grant through the VA’s Veterans Cemetery Grants Program. The program provides federal funding to establish, expand, and improve state and tribal veterans’ cemeteries, helping ensure veterans and eligible family members have access to dignified burial options.

The funding builds on federal investments secured through the appropriations process, including legislation to reopen the government that provided funding for veterans’ cemeteries. Representative Ciscomani has consistently opposed government shutdowns and supported legislation to keep the government open while ensuring critical services and investments for veterans continued.

Eligibility extends to veterans discharged under conditions other than dishonorable, as well as members of the Armed Forces, including the National Guard and Reserve, who meet service requirements. Spouses and dependent children are also eligible, with spouses able to be laid to rest even if they predecease the veteran.

As the representative of a district home to nearly 80,000 veterans, Representative Ciscomani has made recognizing and supporting those who served a priority. From fighting to expand access to veterans’ benefits to securing federal investments for Southern Arizona communities, he has worked to ensure those who served our nation receive the support and recognition they have earned.

title: Rep. Cisneros Introduces Bill to Expand Opportunities for Service-Disabled Veteran, Women-Owned, and Certified HUBZone Small Businesses
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31) introduced the Cutting Red Tape for Small Businesses Act to reduce the administrative bureaucracy slowing down federal contracting opportunities for Women-Owned Small Businesses (WOSBs), Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSBs), and certified HUBZone businesses. If passed, the legislation would streamline the process for sole source awards and give SDVOSB, WOSB, and HUBZone businesses a competitive edge in the federal contracting marketplace.

“Federal agencies should not have to jump through administrative hoops to provide contracting opportunities for women-owned or service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses, or businesses in historically underutilized business zones,” said Rep. Gil Cisneros. “It’s time we level the playing field and make it easier and faster for federal agencies to award contracts to eligible businesses, and encourage greater utilization of programs designed to help them succeed.”

“The National Veteran Small Business Coalition (NVSBC) strongly supports the Cutting Red Tape for Small Businesses Act, which would eliminate the requirement for written Justification and Approval (J&A) for eligible sole-source contracts,” said Scott Jensen, CEO of the National Veteran Small Business Coalition/National Veteran Small Business Coalition Education Foundation. “This legislation would reduce administrative burdens and help contracting officers use their sole-source authorities more effectively. By streamlining the award process, it would expand opportunities for Veteran entrepreneurs and other eligible small businesses, strengthening their capacity to meet federal needs, and bolster our industrial base.”

“We applaud Representative Cisneros for his leadership in streamlining sole-source contracting for women-owned small businesses,” said the Women’s Procurement Circle. “These contracts help federal agencies access the innovation and expertise small businesses bring to the marketplace. Reducing burdensome approval requirements helps women-owned businesses win federal opportunities and allows agencies to meet their needs more efficiently.”

“This bill takes a practical step toward making federal contracting more accessible to service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses,” said Rebecca Aguilera-Gardiner, CEO of the Veterans in Business (VIB) Network. “Our members bring expertise across industries and across the country, but navigating unnecessary paperwork takes time and resources away from serving their federal customers. We thank Representative Cisneros for his leadership in reducing those barriers.”

Full text of the bill can be found here.

Rep. Cisneros is a member of the House Committee on Small Business, the Ranking Member on the Subcommittee on Contracting and Infrastructure, and on the Subcommittee on Oversight, Investigations, and Regulations. He is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and serves on its leadership team as the Freshman Representative.

title: CORREA INTRODUCES RESOLUTION HONORING FOOD BANKS AS SNAP CUTS DRIVE RECORD DEMAND
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Ahead of Thanksgiving, Congressman Lou Correa (CA-46) introduced a resolution honoring food banks, food pantries, and community organizations in Orange County and nationwide as they struggle to meet surging demand after the Trump Administration’s cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).

More than 4 million Americans, including children, seniors, and veterans, are expected to face serious hardship following passage of H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cut federal funding for SNAP and other food programs. In California alone, 333,062 people have lost SNAP coverage.

“As we come together with friends and family this holiday season to give thanks, enjoy good conversation and a warm meal, we remember how fortunate we truly are. But that is not true for everyone in America. Food insecurity is a significant problem here in Orange County and across this country, and the Trump Administration's SNAP cuts are making it worse," said Correa. "Each year, I volunteer at a local food bank and pack and hand out nutritious food boxes and other supplies to families in need. I see first-hand the impact these organizations have every day, especially now, as they work to fill the gap left by cuts to SNAP. Every one of them deserves our thanks and federal recognition for the crucial work they do to better the lives of those who call our community home."

The need is severe:

48 million Americans, including over 7 million children, lived in food-insecure households in 2024.

One in five military and veteran households is food insecure.

Food insecurity costs the U.S. economy over $160 billion a year in health costs.

In 2023, food banks and their 60,000 partners served more than 5 billion meals to over 50 million people.

“On behalf of Second Harvest Food Bank of Orange County, I want to thank Congressman Correa for introducing the Food Bank Resolution of 2026. Every day, food banks across our country work to make sure no family has to choose between putting food on the table and paying rent, filling a prescription, or keeping the lights on. That work depends on dedicated staff, generous volunteers, and partners who understand what’s at stake. Representative Correa has been one of those partners, standing with both of Orange County’s food banks and championing the work we do together. This resolution recognizes the people behind that work, and it reminds all of us that ending hunger is a shared responsibility. We’re grateful for his leadership and look forward to continuing to work alongside him,” said Claudia Bonilla Keller, CEO, Second Harvest Food Bank of Orange County.

Specifically, this resolution acknowledges that food banks, food pantries, and other community-based organizations provide essential food assistance and other services to countless individuals across Orange County and throughout the United States. Led by Correa, it has also been co-sponsored by Reps. Nanette Barragan, Shontel Brown, Nikki Budzinski, Troy Carter, Ed Case, Judy Chu, Bonnie Coleman, Jim Costa, John Garamendi, Jesus “Chuy” Garcia, Sylvia Garcia, Eleanor Holmes-Norton, Jonathon Jackson, Hank Johnson, Mike Levin, Zoe Lofgren, Dave Min, Seth Moulton, Richard Neal, Brittany Pettersen, Mark Pocan, Deborah Ross, Linda Sanchez, Brad Schneider, Mark Takano, Shri Thanedar, Dina Titus, Lateefah Simon, Juan Vargas, Gabe Vasquez, and George Whitesides.

This resolution has also been endorsed by Alameda County Community Food Bank, California Food Banks, Community Action Partnership of Orange County, Feeding Colorado, Feeding Texas, Food Bank of Contra Costa and Solano, Los Angeles Regional Food Bank, San Diego Hunger Coalition, San Francisco-Marin Food Bank, Second Harvest Food Bank of Orange County, Second Harvest Food Bank of Santa Cruz County, and Second Harvest Food Bank of Silicon Valley.

You can read the full text of the resolution HERE.

title: Crow Calls for Action to Ban Stock Trading by Members of Congress
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), Co-Chair of the End Corruption Caucus, is calling for action to ban stock trading by members of Congress in the new Democratic majority.

Joining Crow at his press conference were Representatives Adelita Grijalva, Chris Deluzio, and Pramila Jayapal, and Representatives-elect Matt Little, Zach Dembo, Jake Johnson, Sam Forstag, Dan Koh, Cyril Jefferson, Mitchell Berman, Paige Cognetti, Luke Bronin, Lindsay James, Brad Lander, Manny Rutinel, Katy Padilla Stout, and Will Lawrence.

“Americans, right, left, and center, are fed up with a system that’s captured by corporate lobbyists, with a system that’s captured by super PACs, with a system that over and over again, shows that it can’t do the big things that Americans overwhelmingly support because of the chokehold of corporate money and lobbyist money on this town,” Congressman Crow said.

“There are many things that members of Congress can just do today to show they will walk the talk,” Crow said. “That’s why 57 incoming members and I have taken the Political Integrity Pledge to refuse corporate PAC money, to push for a ban on stock trading by Members of Congress, to ban lobbying by former Members of Congress for at least five years, and to support the overturning of Citizens United… We can do those things when we start the 120th Congress. We are dedicated and committed to pushing leadership, to pushing our colleagues, and to making sure communities back home know that we represent them and not the special interests.

“We will not accept no for an answer on this,” Crow concluded.

Watch Crow’s full press conference HERE.

Crow does not own or trade stocks and has never taken a dime of corporate PAC money. He is the only sitting member of Colorado’s Congressional delegation to take the Political Integrity Pledge to refuse corporate PAC money and support efforts to ban stock trading by members of Congress, institute a five-year lobbying ban on former members of Congress, and push for the overturning of Citizens United. He is the only sitting member of Colorado’s Congressional delegation to take the Unrig Washington pledge to refuse corporate PAC money and support efforts to crack down on dark money and ban stock trading by members of Congress.

Crow is an original cosponsor of the TRUST in Congress Act to ban members of Congress and their families from owning or trading stocks. He has led outreach to House leadership urging them to ban stock trading for high-ranking government officials and ban members of Congress and their staff from insider trading on prediction markets. He is leading the fight to root out corruption in our elections, including through his End Dark Money Act to crack down on dark money’s influence on U.S. elections and his SHINE Act to limit the creation of shady pop-up PACs just before an election.

title: Dingell, Sewell Introduce Legislation to Cap Out-of-Pocket Medicare Costs, Lower Healthcare Costs for Seniors
text:
U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and Terri Sewell (D-AL-07) introduced the Medicare Cost Cap Act, legislation to establish an annual $5,000 out-of-pocket cap for services covered under traditional Medicare and expand programs that help low-income seniors and people with disabilities afford their healthcare.

“People work their entire lives and pay into Medicare expecting it will be there when they need it. But a serious illness can still leave them facing medical bills they cannot afford,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “I hear from seniors who are stretching every dollar and worrying about whether getting the care they need will cost them their savings. This legislation would put a limit on what people pay out of pocket for care under traditional Medicare and help more people with limited incomes get financial assistance. No one should have to put off seeing a doctor or getting the care or medicine they need because they are afraid of the bill.”

"In Alabama and across the country, Medicare beneficiaries who have worked hard their entire lives are still vulnerable to overwhelming out-of-pocket costs when they get sick. While Medicare Advantage plans already provide an annual limit on out-of-pocket spending, traditional Medicare offers no such protection, leaving millions of seniors exposed to potentially devastating medical bills. By establishing a $5,000 annual cap on out-of-pocket costs in traditional Medicare, this bill will provide meaningful relief and greater financial certainty for seniors and their families. At a time when too many Americans are struggling with the rising cost of health care and everyday necessities, this legislation represents a commonsense step toward making health care more affordable and strengthening the Medicare program for generations to come," said Congresswoman Sewell.

The Medicare Cost Cap Act would:

Establish a $5,000 annual out-of-pocket cap for deductibles, copayments, coinsurance, and other cost-sharing for services covered under traditional Medicare Parts A and B. Once beneficiaries reach the limit, they would owe no additional cost-sharing for covered services for the remainder of the year. The cap would be adjusted annually based on growth in Medicare spending.

Expand financial assistance to more low-income beneficiaries by raising the income eligibility thresholds for the Qualified Medicare Beneficiary program and the Medicare Part D Low-Income Subsidy, also known as Extra Help, to 200 percent of the federal poverty level beginning in 2028.

Eliminate asset tests for these assistance programs, allowing otherwise eligible beneficiaries to qualify without being disqualified because of their savings.

Simplify access to assistance by aligning eligibility rules and requiring qualifying Extra Help recipients to be treated as Qualified Medicare Beneficiaries, helping people receive assistance with both medical and prescription drug costs.

title: Dexter, Bonamici Introduce Bill to Help College Students Without Stable Housing Stay in School
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswomen Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03) and Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01) introduced the Postsecondary Attainment Through Housing Supports Demonstration Act to help students experiencing homelessness or at imminent risk of losing their housing stay enrolled and earn a degree. The bill would create a federal pilot program that pairs stable housing with support such as tutoring, childcare and transportation.

“Students are struggling far too much to earn a degree while facing unaffordable costs of living,” Congresswoman Dexter said. “As a first-gen college grad who had access to an affordable education and housing, I’m determined to help unlock the American Dream for more students. A college degree is one of the surest paths to economic success. This legislation brings colleges and nonprofit housing providers together so we can help students maintain the stability they need to complete their education.”

“Students struggle to learn if they're worrying about where to sleep at night,” Congresswoman Bonamici said. “I'm co-leading the PATHS Act to support sustainable housing options and wraparound support services for students to increase their chances of completion and success in higher education.”

Roughly one in seven college students nationwide experienced homelessness between 2023 and 2024, and nearly half experienced housing insecurity. The legislation builds on community programs that pair housing with services that help students stay in school.

“Students experiencing homelessness are working hard to stay in school, with most holding down jobs and many raising children,” said Barbara Duffield Executive Director of SchoolHouse Connection. “For too many, housing is the missing piece between enrolling and earning the degree or credential that leads to a stable job and a life free from homelessness. The PATHS Act builds on innovative local partnerships that pair housing with support services, and we’re deeply grateful to Rep. Dexter for her leadership in championing these students and their futures.”

The bill would direct the U.S. Department of Education, in consultation with the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, to award competitive grants of up to $2 million over five years to nonprofit housing providers that partner with colleges, including community colleges. The grants would supplement existing housing and education funding.

“With more than 55 years of experience owning and operating affordable student housing, we have seen firsthand how access to affordable housing and supportive services can change the trajectory of a student’s life,” said Pam Blumenthal, Chief Impact Officer, College Housing Northwest. “In 2020, recognizing the growing need, we launched the Affordable Rents for College Students (ARCS) Program. Since then, we have provided housing to more than 230 housing-insecure and homeless students, who have collectively earned more than 82 college degrees and credentials. These outcomes demonstrate what is possible when students have a stable place to call home and the support they need to succeed. This legislation recognizes the critical connection between housing stability and educational success and will help bring greater attention, resources, and opportunities to expand this work and support similar programs across the country.”

Grantees could use the funds to acquire, rehabilitate or repurpose existing housing and connect students with case management, tutoring, mental and behavioral health care, childcare, transportation and career services. The program would prioritize former foster youth, transition-aged youth and students who are parents.

The bill is endorsed by SchoolHouse Connection, Center for Higher Education Policy and Practice at SNHU, Corporation for Supportive Housing, Fostering Academic Achievement Nationwide, The Hope Center for Student Basic Needs, Just Strategy, National Network for Youth, New America Higher Education Policy Program, Today’s Students Coalition, Trellis Strategies, Youth Villages, Achieve Atlanta, College Housing Northwest, Communities for Our Colleges (WA), CUNY Rising Alliance, Detroit College Access Network, Educate Tomorrow (Florida), New Mexico Basic Needs Consortium and Washington Postsecondary Basic Needs Coalition.

title: Congresswoman Escobar, House Democrats Urge DHS to Release El Paso Family from Dilley Detention Center
text:
Today, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) led a group of Democrats in a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Acting Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Director David Venturella urging them to release the Guerrero-Germán family from the Dilley Detention Center.

Joining Congresswoman Escobar (in alphabetical order) are Representatives Greg Casar (TX-35), Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Lloyd Doggett (TX-37), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-7), Jesus “Chuy” Garcia (IL-4), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Al Green (TX-9), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Summer Lee (PA-12), Stephen Lynch (MA-8), Christian Menefee (TX-18), Emily Randall (WA-6), Linda Sanchez (CA-39), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Juan Vargas (CA-52), and Representatives-Elect Leticia Gutierrez (TX-9) and Katy Padilla-Stout (TX-23).

The full letter can be found here or below:

Secretary Mullin and Acting Director Venturella:

I am writing with an urgent plea regarding Michell Germán and her family, who are currently being held at the South Texas Family Residential Center, also known as Dilley Detention Center (Dilley), in Dilley, Texas.

The Guerrero-Germán family, originally from Venezuela, have been residents of El Paso, Texas for several years after being paroled into the United States and pursuing an asylum determination. Parents Pablo Jose Guerrero-Pimentel and Dolores Emilia Zarraga-Colina, along with daughters Michell Germán and her 11-year-old sister were detained on October 22, 2026 in El Paso. The family was apprehended by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) during what ICE referred to as “targeted enforcement arrests” in a statement to local news outlet KVIA. In that same statement, ICE claims that neither parent has “documentation to remain in the U.S. legally”.

However, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, a lawyer for the family, shared in a statement to El Paso Matters that the family is in “valid immigration proceedings, has a lawyer and work permits, and no criminal record”. The detention has impacted the entire family and “traumatized” the two girls.

Michell is a star student at El Paso High School, where she’s enrolled in the school’s Center for Career and Technology Education Program studying cosmetology. Social and outgoing, Michell is a member of the Tigerettes, the school’s dance team, has a part-time job, and volunteers with seniors in the El Paso community. Earlier in the schoolyear, Michell was part of the school’s Homecoming Parade and crowned Lady-in-Waiting.

During her time at El Paso High School, Michell has created a close-knit community of friends who clearly value her and her family. Classmates share that Michell is reliable and trustworthy, and that shows up for her friends. In an interview with El Paso Matters, a friend describes Michell and her family as “incredible people” with good hearts.

When Michell was unable to join her classmates in being honored at Senior Night as a result of being detained by ICE. When her name was called to step out onto the football field at the school stadium, her friends carried a poster of her onto the field to cheers and applause from classmates and families in the stands. Michell should have been on the field among her friends, but was instead sitting over 500 miles away, in detention at Dilley.

Dilley Detention Center was closed in 2024, but reopened in 2025 by the second Trump administration as they began detaining families as part of the President’s mass deportation campaign. In a ProPublica article titled “The Children of Dilley” and published on February 9, 2026, mothers and children detained at Dilley shared several concerns about the conditions at the facility. Parents and children shared instances of mold and worms in food, and drinking water that made people feel ill. Mothers shared that conditions at the facility are so dire, that some children developed suicidal ideation and attempted self-harm. Parents and children alike described insufficient medical care at Dilley, including children with medical complaints frequently experiencing delays, dismissals, or lack of follow-up from on-site medical staff.

I urge you to release Michell German and her family from Dilley Detention Center. They should be allowed to continue pursuing their asylum case at home in El Paso, where they will be able to better communicate with their legal team and prepare for any upcoming court dates or hearings pertinent to their case.

title: Reps. Foushee, Ross, Adams Demand Answers from DHS Secretary Mullin Regarding the Imminent Reopening of the Rivers Correctional Institution in Winton, North Carolina
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (November 17, 2026) — Today, Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04), Congresswoman Deborah Ross (NC-02), and Congresswoman Alma Adams (NC-12) sent a letter to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin demanding answers regarding the imminent reopening of the Rivers Correctional Institution (RCI) in Winton, North Carolina in partnership with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

On July 29th, The GEO Group, Inc. announced that it had entered into a five-year contract with ICE to operate a federal immigration processing center at the GEO-owned Rivers Correctional Institution.

“The facility would open during the deadliest period for people in ICE custody in more than two decades, at a site with a documented history of violence and medical neglect, run by a contractor whose facilities are currently under state investigation,” the lawmakers wrote.

“At a time when North Carolina families are struggling with the rising cost of housing, health care, and groceries, private prison companies are receiving billions of dollars in federal funds. North Carolinians deserve robust investment in needed infrastructure and economic opportunities, not federal subsidization of a new detention facility,” the lawmakers continued.

"At least 10 people died in GEO-operated facilities in 2025, and deaths have continued in 2026. At Delaney Hall in Newark, New Jersey, Jovanny Lopez Cornejo died in August. His mother said he was not receiving his daily medication for diabetes and high blood pressure and had complained of numbness in his face and hand. When New Jersey health inspectors arrived at Delaney Hall in May, they were barred from the medical unit,” the lawmakers concluded. “A company that blocks state health inspectors from auditing their facilities should not be entrusted with more lives in North Carolina.”

The letter includes the following questions for U.S. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Mullin relating to facility operations, legal access and immigration court, medical and mental healthcare, and community impacts:

What is the current status of ICE's contract with GEO Group for the Winton facility, and when will it begin receiving detainees?

Will the facility open at full capacity or phase in its detained population? If phased, what is the anticipated timeline for reaching full operational capacity?

Please provide a copy of the contract, including its term, per-diem rate, and any guaranteed minimum occupancy provision.

How many full-time and part-time correctional staff will be employed at Rivers?

What population will Rivers house (men, women, children)?

Are there any categories of detained individuals that Rivers will not be equipped or authorized to house? (ex. Pregnant people, people living with disabilities, unaccompanied minors, people with certain security-classifications, etc.)

What ICE AOR (Area of Responsibility) and ERO (Enforcement Removal Operations) field office will be in control of this facility?

Does ICE anticipate that Rivers will operate as a regional facility? If so, serving which state populations?

Which detention standards (NDS 2025, PBNDS 2011, or other) will govern the facility, and will ICE or an independent body complete a pre-occupancy inspection? If such an inspection was already completed, please provide the results.

How many private attorney-client visitation rooms will be available?

Will Rivers participate in ICE’s Virtual Attorney Visitation program? If so, how many confidential video stations will be available?

In what immigration court will cases for individuals detained in this facility take place?

Will immigration hearings for individuals detained at Rivers occur in person, by video teleconference, or both?

Will legal organizations be permitted to conduct Know Your Rights presentations?

What medical staffing levels are required under the contract, including physicians, nurses, and mental health professionals?

Will Rivers be contracting with an outside provider for medical or mental health services? If so, who?

Will medical personnel be physically present on-site 24/7 for medical emergencies?

What are the nearest hospitals capable of emergency and specialty care, what are the transport times, and what protocols govern emergency transfers?

How many mental health beds will be available?

How many restrictive-housing or solitary confinement beds will be available?

Did ICE evaluate the 2016 DOJ findings and the 2007 medical care litigation at Rivers when deciding to contract for this site?

What, if any, corrective measures has GEO Group committed to?

What steps has ICE taken to review GEO Group's medical care practices in light of deaths at Delaney Hall and Adelanto?

Given the state of New Jersey's litigation over access to Delaney Hall, will ICE require GEO Group to permit unannounced inspections by state and local health authorities at Winton?

Will any inspections as to facility fitness/safety be conducted prior to opening?

Have any evaluations been made regarding the impact that the re-opening of Rivers will have on the infrastructure of Winton and the surrounding area (e.g. traffic, emergency services, hospital capacity)?

What agreement, if any, has ICE or GEO reached with local entities regarding services associated with Rivers? (ex. EMS providers, local law enforcement, hospitals, local government)

Will local government or service providers receive federal reimbursement for costs associated with Rivers?

title: Rep. Gillen Urges Secretary Duffy to Testify Before Congress on National Ground Stop, $50 Billion Funding Request
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) urged U.S. Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy to testify before the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee to provide answers on the November 13th national ground stop, the billions of dollars Congress has already provided for air traffic control modernization and the Secretary’s request for $50 billion in additional funding for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

“The impact of the events of November 13, 2026, cannot be overstated. You will recall that following reports of radar and communications issues at several air route traffic control centers (ARTCCs) and terminal radar approach control (TRACON) facilities, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered the extraordinarily rare, hours-long, nationwide ground stop,” wrote Rep. Gillen to Secretary Duffy. “12,000 flights were canceled, thousands more were delayed on Friday alone and airlines are still recovering. Thankfully, no lives were lost during this event. However, the American people deserve answers about what transpired and what steps the FAA is taking to ensure that it does not happen again.”

In her letter, Rep. Gillen highlighted the more than $14 billion Congress has provided to the Department of Transportation for air traffic control system upgrades since 2025. She also addressed the Secretary’s lack of response following his commitment in 2025 to visit TRACON N90 in Westbury, which manages the busiest airspace in the country.

“I do not believe it is productive to engage in finger pointing at this critical juncture. I am ready to work with you and my colleagues in Congress to modernize our skies and ensure that the public travels safely and efficiently. In order to move forward, you should provide Congress with a clear plan to safeguard our airspace and a full accounting of how the Department has spent billions of dollars Congress has already appropriated for air traffic control modernization,” continued Rep. Gillen.

In July 2025, Congress provided $12.5 billion to modernize the FAA's air traffic system in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. In February 2026, Congress provided an additional $1.9 billion through the FY26 Transportation, Housing and Urban Development and Related Agencies (THUD) Appropriations Act, for a total of $14.4 billion.

As a member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Subcommittee on Aviation, Rep. Gillen has led bipartisan efforts to advance nationwide air traffic control modernization. She has also championed legislation to support, recruit and retain air traffic controllers. In 2025, Rep. Gillen introduced the bipartisan Military Air Traffic Control Transition Act to address the nationwide air traffic controller shortage by streamlining military controllers into civilian roles. In 2026, she also introduced the bipartisan Air Traffic Situational Awareness Enhancement Act to equip air traffic controllers with modern tools and training to strengthen aviation safety. Rep. Gillen is a cosponsor of the Aviation Funding Solvency Act to protect FAA operations and air traffic controller pay during government shutdowns.

During a May 2025 House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee hearing, Rep. Gillendemanded answers from the FAA about relocating 12 air traffic controllers from the TRACON N90 facility in Westbury on Long Island to Philadelphia to manage Newark airspace, citing severe staffing shortages, burnout, outdated technology and communication blackouts. Following her pressure, the U.S. Department of Transportation (USDOT) Inspector General opened an audit into the relocations and communication issues. In August 2025, Gillenvisited the Westbury facility to praise the USDOT's investigation and continue her calls to modernize air traffic control and return controllers to Long Island.

The full letter can be found HERE and below:

Dear Secretary Duffy:

As a member of the Subcommittee on Aviation, I am keenly focused on and concerned about the safety of our airspace. The nationwide ground stop that occurred on November 13, 2026, has only amplified my concerns and demonstrated the need for an immediate action plan to secure our skies. It is imperative that you appear before Congress to: 1) brief Members on the ground stop, 2) account for the billions of dollars Congress has already provided for modernization upgrades; and 3) explain your request for billions in new funding and articulate your specific plans to accomplish our shared goals of protecting the flying public and preventing future emergencies.

The impact of the events of November 13, 2026, cannot be overstated. You will recall that following reports of radar and communications issues at several air route traffic control centers (ARTCCs) and terminal radar approach control (TRACON) facilities, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered the extraordinarily rare, hours-long, nationwide ground stop. 12,000 flights were canceled, thousands more were delayed on Friday alone and airlines are still recovering. Thankfully, no lives were lost during this event. However, the American people deserve answers about what transpired and what steps the FAA is taking to ensure that it does not happen again.

Over the past two years, Congress has significantly increased funding for improving and modernizing our airspace. Last year, Congress provided $12.5 billion for the Department of Transportation to make critical safety upgrades. In February of this year, Congress provided another $1.9 billion, bringing the total to $14.4 billion appropriated this Congress alone. However, the Administration has only obligated $4.3 billion of that funding and has spent just $1 billion on modernization so far.

When you appeared before the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure on July 16, 2025, I expressed my willingness to work with you to help modernize our air traffic control and safeguard our airspace. During that hearing, you gave me your commitment on the record that you would join me for a visit to TRACON N90, which plays a critical role in managing the most complex and congested airspace in the country, including LaGuardia and JFK. I have followed up with you on this request multiple times over the past year, and am still waiting for you to confirm your visit.

I do not believe it is productive to engage in finger pointing at this critical juncture. I am ready to work with you and my colleagues in Congress to modernize our skies and ensure that the public travels safely and efficiently. In order to move forward, you should provide Congress with a clear plan to safeguard our airspace and a full accounting of how the Department has spent billions of dollars Congress has already appropriated for air traffic control modernization. That is why I urge you to appear before the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee as soon as possible to answer questions about the ground stop and the Administration’s request for an additional $50.1 billion in funding.

I agree with you that our outdated air traffic control system has been long-neglected and should be a bipartisan priority. I look forward to seeing you before the Committee and to working with you and my colleagues in Congress to get this done. Thank you and I look forward to your response.

In this hate incident, they were promoting the so-called “replacement” theory, a false claim that non-white and non-Christian people are brought in to replace white Christian Americans.
