“When the Department of Homeland Security publishes a graphic mocking a Sikh man with the message, ‘Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive Mr. Singh,’ it should come as no surprise that Mr. Lang and Mr. Allen were emboldened to disrupt a cultural celebration and boast a racist sign demanding that Indian Americans be deported,” continued the Members.

title: Boston Globe: Tufts debuts new Innovation Hub for Food and Materials in Medford
text:
Insect-based pet foods, and lab-grown fabric and chocolate. Those are some of the ideas that startups located at Tufts University’s new Innovation Hub for Food and Materials are cooking up.

The 17,000-square-foot incubator located on Boston Avenue seeks to fill a gap in the innovation market for food and materials as well as expand the state’s biotechnology industry. The hub helps connect researchers and entrepreneurs in the food and material innovation sector with industry partners to help bring ideas to market.

“Boston has long been really, really good for health innovation in general, but these types of companies almost take a backseat to that because they didn’t get the financing, they didn’t have the type of space,” said Adam Jenkins, regional director for BioLabs, the firm managing the facility. “A lot of them would go out to the West Coast. So, having a space on the East Coast in Boston will hopefully really spark that infrastructure ecosystem.”

The 46-lab-bench hub can house 10 to 15 startups and currently has four operating there. Among them are EntoCellular, which uses insect cell cultures to make pet foods, and GALY, which produces plant-based products like chocolate and cotton from cells instead of farming them on land.

“This will be the Kendall Square for food science and biomaterials right here on Boston Avenue,” US Senator Ed Markey said in a video message presented during a ribbon cutting ceremony for the hub Monday.

Jenkins said the lab is expected to be full by October 2027. The goal is for startups to outgrow the hub and relocate within two to four years to make room for more companies to come through.

“This is meant for a space for them to come, learn, grow, prove that their product is going to be made and then graduate out hopefully into their own space as they become a commercial entity,” Jenkins said. “The turnover is also vital to this space. As you bring in more ideas, you bring in more products, more founders, more ideas. The community grows, the network grows, the science continues to grow.”

Before then, startups rent lab space and offices at the hub for about $2,000 to $3,000 per month, Jenkins said.

Included within the space is the university’s open cell bank where researchers can access cultured cells — a resource that can save biotech entrepreneurs millions of dollars and in some cases, years at a time needed to get cell lines, said Matt McNulty, associate director of Tufts University’s Center for Cellular Agriculture.

“Here, we provide open access licensing cells so that innovators can come and take cells and everyone can have a shared starting point that’s further up the mountain so to speak, together,” McNulty said. “So, it’s almost as if you can start at a base camp versus starting at the bottom of the mountain.”

The space also includes a test kitchen, shared offices, bioreactors to grow cells in controlled conditions, an electronic nose used to test a product’s smell as well as other equipment like 3D printers and cell analyzers that research companies will need to show that their products are viable.

The hub is funded with $4.6 million from Tufts University, $2.1 million from the Massachusetts Technology Collaborative, and support from philanthropic donations.

The hub’s launch comes as MassBio recently found the state’s life sciences sector reported job losses last year for the first time in more than two decades. The trade group’s report found that Massachusetts reported the steepest drop in research and development jobs among major hubs nationwide and argued that it’s crucial to support startups.

US Representative Katherine Clark said that the House will be a partner to the hub “every step of the way.”

“This is a model of the kind of progress we want to see in the rest of the country, this is how we support small businesses. It’s how we empower researchers to discovery and empower entrepreneurs to bring those discoveries to life through the market,” she said. “This new innovation hub will give them the tools that they need from the very beginning. That’s how we stay out front. That’s how we create good-paying jobs that are family-sustaining. That’s how America remains the envy of the world, and Massachusetts remains the envy of America.”

—

title: Kennedy Leads Legislation to Expand Animal Adoptions and Help Address Shelter Overcrowding Through New Federal Tax Credit
text:
The HEART Act Would Give Families a Refundable Credit for 50% of Adoption Fees, Removing a Barrier for Adoption

BUFFALO, N.Y. - Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) stood at the City of Buffalo Animal Shelter to announce the introduction of the Helping Encourage Animal Rescue through Tax Credits (HEART) Act, bipartisan legislation he is leading. The bill would create a refundable federal tax credit covering 50% of adoption fees paid to nonprofit animal rescues and government-run shelters, up to $500 per animal, to encourage more families to adopt and to ease overcrowding at shelters across the country.

“Every animal deserves a loving home, and too many of them are waiting longer than ever to find one,” said Congressman Kennedy. “Adoption fees can add up to hundreds of dollars per animal, and for a working family, that cost can be the difference between bringing a rescue home and walking away. The HEART Act puts money back in families’ pockets when they choose to adopt, and it takes pressure off shelters like Buffalo’s. This is the City of Good Neighbors, and that includes our four-legged neighbors. I’m proud to lead the introduction of this commonsense, bipartisan legislation, and I urge my colleagues to join us.”

“Many animal shelters across the country are at capacity. Choosing adoption helps the animal you take home while also freeing up space and resources so that shelters can help other animals in need,” said Maggie Garrett, Vice President of Federal Affairs for the ASPCA. “The ASPCA applauds Representatives Kennedy and Fitzpatrick for introducing legislation that encourages and incentivizes adoption from a shelter or rescue for those seeking to add a pet to their family.”

“Every animal deserves the chance to find a loving family, and shelters and rescues play a vital role in making those connections possible,” said Sara Amundson, President of Humane World Action Fund. “By offering tax incentives to adopt shelter animals, the HEART Act will help secure loving homes for more animals. We thank Congressman Kennedy for his leadership to make adoption more affordable which will support shelters, animals, and communities.”

“The data shows that animals are staying in shelters longer, rising household costs are contributing to more animal surrenders, and many of these facilities are way over capacity,” said Blair Eagleson, Legislative Affairs Fellow at the Animal Legal Defense Fund. “Congressman Kennedy’s HEART Act is a great idea as it will get more animals out of the shelters and into loving homes. A refundable tax credit for animal adoption fees makes adoption more affordable, eases the burden on shelters, and rewards Americans who choose to adopt, rather than shop.”

“We are grateful for Rep. Kennedy’s dedication to getting more shelter animals into their forever homes by providing a tax incentive to adopt,” said Nancy Blaney, Director of Government Affairs at the Animal Welfare Institute.

“Our Buffalo Animal Shelter staff and volunteers work hard every day to care for animals and help them find loving homes,” said Buffalo Mayor Sean Ryan. “This summer, more animals were coming through the shelter’s doors than were being adopted, putting real pressure on our limited space and resources. The HEART Act would help ease the cost of adoption for families and make room for more animals in need of care. I thank Congressman Kennedy for advancing this legislation, and I urge Congress to pass it.”

“The HEART Act recognizes that the decision to adopt a shelter animal is not only an act of compassion, but a meaningful investment in the well-being of animals and our communities,” said Cait Daly, President and CEO of the SPCA Serving Erie County. “At the SPCA Serving Erie County, we see every day how adoption gives animals a second chance while creating the opportunity for people and pets to build lifelong bonds. A refundable tax credit for eligible adoption fees can help make adoption more accessible to families while encouraging more people to choose shelter animals. We are proud to endorse the HEART Act and support Congressman Kennedy’s efforts to strengthen and expand opportunities for animals in need to find loving homes.”

According to the ASPCA, animals, especially dogs, are staying in shelters longer than they were five years ago. In 2025 alone, 5.8 million dogs and cats entered U.S. shelters and rescues, and nearly 600,000 animals were euthanized in shelters, often because of overcrowding. In Buffalo, the City of Buffalo Animal Shelter reached capacity in June, housing new arrivals in overflow crates and calling on the community for adoptive and foster homes.

There are currently no federal tax benefits for adopting an animal. Because the HEART Act’s credit is refundable, families can receive the full benefit regardless of how much they owe in taxes, so the help reaches the working families who need it the most.

The HEART Act would create a refundable tax credit for 50% of eligible animal adoption fees, capped at $500 per animal and apply to adoptions from nonprofit 501(c)(3) animal rescues and government-run shelters. The HEART Act is endorsed by the ASPCA, Humane World for Animals, the Animal Welfare Institute, the Animal Legal Defense Fund, Best Friends Animal Society, the Erie County SPCA, and the City of Buffalo.

title: Krishnamoorthi, Jayapal, Meng Demand Investigation of Hateful Conduct at Seattle Diwali Celebration
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Representatives Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Pramila Jayapal (WA-07), and Grace Meng (NY-06), Chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus (CAPAC), are demanding an investigation into the disruption of a Diwali celebration in Seattle, WA, where Jake Lang and Thomas Allen entered the venue with signs containing racial slurs and hateful language.

“It is vital that those of us entrusted with public offices confront hate wherever it appears. No family should have to wonder whether it is safe to light a lamp, perform a dance, or bring their children to a festival in their own city,” wrote the Members. “The events in Seattle follow a troubling series of threats against South Asian communities across the country.”

Allen and Lang have both faced criminal charges, including charges against Lang for allegedly assaulting police officers during the January 6 insurrection, after which he received a pardon from President Trump. In this hate incident, they were promoting the so-called “replacement” theory, a false claim that non-white and non-Christian people are brought in to replace white Christian Americans. This incident comes on the heels of rising anti-South Asian hate, which has been stoked by the Trump Administration.

“When the Department of Homeland Security publishes a graphic mocking a Sikh man with the message, ‘Get off our roads, you don’t know how to drive Mr. Singh,’ it should come as no surprise that Mr. Lang and Mr. Allen were emboldened to disrupt a cultural celebration and boast a racist sign demanding that Indian Americans be deported,” continued the Members.

The letter urges the Department of Justice to investigate whether Lang and Allen’s actions violated federal civil rights statutes, including:

18 U.S.C. § 245, which prohibits intimidation or interference by force or threat of force based on race, color, religion, or national origin in connection with federally protected activities, including access to public accommodations;

18 U.S.C. § 241, which prohibits conspiracies to injure, oppress, threaten, or intimidate people in the exercise of rights secured by the Constitution or federal law;

18 U.S.C. § 247, which prohibits intentional obstruction, by force or threat of force, of a person’s free exercise of religious beliefs.

The letter also calls on the Department of Justice to re-prioritize hate crime investigations and re-invest in its Community Relations Service, the agency that was established by the Civil Rights Act to help communities resolve conflict and that has been decimated by the Trump Administration. The Members also requested a briefing by December 4 on the incident and efforts to prevent further acts of hate against Indian American and South Asian American communities.

The full text of the letter can be read HERE.

The letter was also signed by Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Ami Bera, M.D. (CA-06), Judy Chu (CA-28), Suzan K. DelBene (WA-01), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Emily Randall (WA-06), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Adam Smith (WA-09), Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), and Shri Thanedar (MI-13).

title: ICYMI: Harris Chairs House Education and Workforce Committee Field Hearing in Charlotte on Protecting Workers’ Rights
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — On Friday, Congressman Mark Harris (NC-08) chaired a House Committee on Education and Workforce field hearing in Charlotte, North Carolina, focused on protecting workers’ rights and holding union leadership accountable.

The hearing, titled “Workers in Charge: Restoring Choice and Accountability in the Workplace,” examined whether federal labor laws give workers a meaningful say in decisions made by the unions that represent them. Under current law, unions are not required to allow members to vote on major decisions, including whether to approve contracts or authorize strikes, even though those decisions can directly affect their paychecks, benefits, and job security.

“During the hearing, we heard from witnesses representing workers, businesses, and labor organizations about the need for policies that protect workers, provide stability for businesses, and encourage job creation,” said Congressman Harris. “For too long, Democrats have prioritized the interests of powerful union leaders over the hardworking men and women those unions are supposed to represent. It is time to put American workers first, not union bosses.”

Harris has introduced two bills aimed at giving union members a stronger voice and greater protections. His Ask the Union Members Act would require secret-ballot votes before unions approve contracts or authorize strikes, while his Fair Access to Justice for Union Members Act would remove unnecessary barriers that prevent union members from taking legal action to protect their rights.

title: Rep. McBride Leads Colleagues in Urging Congress to Block Development of New Nuclear Weapons Systems
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representative Sarah McBride (D-Del.), member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, led a group of lawmakers in urging House and Senate Armed Services Committee leaders to remove Section 1521(a) from the final Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), a provision that would authorize the development of two new nuclear weapon systems.

In the letter, the lawmakers warned that approving the proposed weapons could jeopardize public safety by increasing the risk of nuclear escalation and weakening Congressional oversight of the executive branch.

“Section 1521(a) would authorize the Secretaries of Defense and Energy to initiate research, development, and production programs for two new theater-range nuclear weapons and their respective delivery systems, including a surface-launched system and an air-launched system. We are deeply concerned that these additional nuclear capabilities are unnecessary, increase the likelihood of nuclear conflict, and risk undermining existing nuclear modernization efforts,” wrote the lawmakers.

While the Trump administration has argued that these additional nuclear capabilities would benefit the country in the event of a regional conflict with foreign adversaries, Rep. McBride and her colleagues warned that the United States already maintains nuclear capabilities sufficient for deterrence and that adding more nuclear weapons could lower the threshold for their use without guaranteeing that a conflict remains contained to specific a region.

“In today’s nuclear landscape, there is no guarantee of a rational or limited nuclear exchange,” the lawmakers continued. “Once a nuclear weapon is used, the risk of broader escalation cannot be credibly contained. The United States already maintains several theater nuclear capabilities sufficient for deterrence. The development of additional weapons is redundant and risks lowering the threshold for their use, increasing the danger of catastrophe in an era of increasing proliferation.”

The lawmakers also warned that launching two additional nuclear weapons programs could divert attention and resources away from ongoing efforts to maintain and modernize the nation’s nuclear arsenal. The National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) is already managing several major weapons and infrastructure projects. Adding two more programs, the lawmakers argue, could strain the resources needed to complete existing priorities.

“NNSA is already pursuing five simultaneous nuclear warhead programs, modernizing pit production, and exploring the development of two additional systems. There is bipartisan concern that these commitments have already placed significant strain on NNSA’s resources,” wrote the lawmakers. “Congress has [also] already mandated the limited deployment of the nuclear-capable sea-launched cruise missile (SLCM-N) by 2032. The authorization of additional nuclear weapons programs, absent congressional debate on the underlying policy implications, risks undermining NNSA’s modernization efforts and existing congressional mandates.”

Rep. McBride and her colleagues also questioned why Congress would authorize two new nuclear weapons systems before the administration has demonstrated that either is necessary. They argued that Congress has a responsibility to demand concrete explanations before committing taxpayer dollars to major new weapons programs. Particularly when the stakes involve the nation’s nuclear arsenal, responsible stewardship requires a clear demonstration that an investment is strategically necessary and will strengthen national security.

“We are also concerned by the absence of a budgetary or strategic justification for these new weapons systems…Authorizing two additional nuclear weapons programs without formal requests or adequate documentation undermines established budgetary procedure and congressional oversight of the executive branch,” wrote the lawmakers.

The lawmakers reiterated the need for a disciplined approach to nuclear deterrence. Maintaining a credible deterrent, they argued, does not require continually expanding the number of nuclear weapons available to the United States; it requires making deliberate choices about which capabilities are necessary to keep the country secure while reducing the risk of nuclear conflict.

“We recognize the critical importance of maintaining robust nuclear deterrence. However, expanding our nuclear arsenal at the expense of existing defense priorities would not strengthen our national security…We stand ready to work with you to ensure that U.S. nuclear policy remains grounded in strategic necessity, congressional oversight, responsible stewardship of taxpayer resources, and the prevention of nuclear conflict,” the lawmakers concluded.

title: McClellan and Kelly Introduce Resolution to Designate November as Prematurity Awareness Month
text:
Washington, D.C. –​​ On Prematurity Awareness Day, Congresswomen Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) and Robin Kelly (IL-02) introduced H.Res. 1664, a resolution to federally recognize November as Prematurity Awareness Month.

Preterm birth remains a serious threat to the health and lives of mothers and their children. Prematurity is a leading cause of infant death, can result in lifelong health complications and is often preventable. Yet preterm birth rates remain stubbornly high amid persistent racial disparities and gaps in access to maternity care, earning the United States a D+ preterm birth grade in the 2026 March of Dimes Report Card. For the fourth year in a row, the United States had a preterm birthrate of 10.4%, with nearly 380,000 babies born prematurely in 2025, and babies born to Black, American Indian and Alaska Native mothers experience preterm birth rates significantly higher than those born to white mothers. Thousands of families face the devastating consequences of preterm birth, underscoring the urgent need to raise awareness, expand resources and strengthen prevention efforts.

“My daughter and I both nearly died when my placenta ruptured nine weeks before her due date. Her six weeks in the NICU were the most stressful of my life,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “While preterm birth can affect any family, communities of color bear a disproportionate burden in tackling this public health crisis. Behind every statistic lies a family whose life has been changed because of a premature birth. We cannot begin to address our maternal and infant health crisis without first raising awareness and ensuring families have access to the resources and support they need. During my tenure in the Virginia legislature, I fought to designate November as Prematurity Awareness Month. Now, I’m committed to carrying on these efforts at the federal level.”

“Too many families have to face the life-threatening impacts of preterm birth. A healthy start to life begins with a healthy mom, and every mother deserves adequate care before, during, and after delivery,” said Congresswoman Robin Kelly, Chair of the Congressional Black Caucus Health Braintrust. “In particular, Black and Indigenous moms continue to face disproportionate barriers to maternal care, resulting in significantly higher rates of preterm birth and maternal mortality rates. I’ve sounded the alarm on maternal mortality since I first came to Congress, and I am committed to continuing the fight for the wellbeing of moms and infants.”

“For the fifth consecutive year, the U.S. has received a preterm birth grade of D+, meaning nearly 380,000 babies were born too soon last year,” said Stacey Brayboy, Senior Vice President of Public Policy and Government Affairs at March of Dimes. “Persistent racial inequities also remain with Black babies facing a higher preterm birth rate than white and Asian babies. We must keep working together to raise awareness, advance policies that support healthier pregnancies and births, and address the systemic barriers that put too many families at risk. March of Dimes is grateful for the leadership of Representatives Jennifer McClellan and Robin Kelly in recognizing Prematurity Awareness Month and remains committed to fighting for the health of all moms and babies, so that every family has the best possible start.”

The resolution is cosponsored by Reps. Eleanor Homes Norton (DC), Nikema Williams (GA-05), Nanette Barragan (CA-44), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), Debbie Dingell (MI-06) and Morgan McGarvey (KY-03).

title: McClellan Announces 2026 Veteran of the Year Recipient at Veterans Appreciation Lunch
text:
Richmond, Va. – Yesterday, Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) celebrated Veterans Appreciation Month with a Veterans Appreciation Lunch at the Virginia War Memorial. At the lunch, Congresswoman McClellan recognized Sergeant First Class Norma Jean Newman as the 2026 Veteran of the Year recipient.

“Each year, my office celebrates veterans and their loved ones in Virginia’s Fourth District by honoring not only their military service, but also their continued service to their communities in retirement,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “This year, I announced Sergeant First Class Norma Jean Newman as our 2026 Veteran of the Year. Dr. Newman represents the very best of our service community, through nearly a quarter-century of honorable military service and decades of unwavering commitment to fellow veterans to ensure that those who served our military receive the care, benefits and dignity they have earned.”

Dr. Newman served in the United States Army from 1984 to 2008, retiring with the rank of Sergeant First Class after 24 years of honorable service. A Gulf War veteran, she deployed in support of Operations Desert Shield and Desert Storm and was injured while conducting air-quality testing related to chemical exposure. During her military career, she earned numerous awards and decorations, including the Army Meritorious Service Medal, Army Commendation Medal, Army Achievement Medals, National Defense Service Medal and additional awards recognizing her exemplary leadership and service to our nation.

Drawing upon her expertise in Veterans Affairs disability claims documentation and medical board proceedings, Dr. Newman has since dedicated herself to helping veterans navigate complex benefits systems and access the support they earned through their military service. For nearly three decades, she has trained veteran service officers and provided hands-on assistance to thousands of veterans at no cost. Through her work with The American Legion, Disabled American Veterans, AMVETS and numerous other organizations, she has become a highly respected and effective advocate for veterans in the Commonwealth. She is an active member of the National Buffalo Soldiers Association’s Mark Matthews Chapter in Petersburg, serves as Chair of Trustees at First Baptist Church West Petersburg, and has also served on both the Washington, D.C., and Roanoke Veterans Appeals Boards, where she fought tirelessly on behalf of veterans seeking fair consideration of their VA benefits claims.

At the Veterans Appreciation Lunch, McClellan provided reflections on Veterans Day and Veterans Appreciation Month, honored Dr. Newman, provided an update on her work addressing veterans’ issues in the 119th Congress and took questions from the audience.

title: Reps. McGarvey and Pettersen Introduce Bill to Extend FMLA for NICU Parents
text:
Associated Press: Bipartisan bill targets a painful gap: 12 more weeks of unpaid leave for US parents with NICU babies

WASHINGTON, D.C. (November 17, 2026) – ICYMI: Congressman Morgan McGarvey (KY-03) co-lead introduction of the Stand By NICU Babies and Families Act with Reps. Brittany Pettersen (CO-07), Ryan Mackenzie (PA-07), and Mike Lawler (NY-17). The bill would allow NICU parents to take up to 12 additional weeks of Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) leave to be with their newborn.

NICU care is essential for infants born preterm and at a low birth weight – a leading cause of infant mortality - or other serious health conditions. NICU parents can quickly exhaust most or all of their FMLA leave during their infant's hospitalization, leaving little or no time to recover and bond with their infant when the baby returns home.

“When your baby’s in the NICU, all you can focus on is getting them home,” said Congressman McGarvey. "My wife and I waited 99 days to bring our twins home. During those difficult days, no parent should be worried about their parental leave running out. I’m grateful for Rep. Pettersen’s leadership, and I’m proud to co-lead this bill to give NICU parents the same precious days at home with their newborns as every other parent.”

As a NICU parent himself, McGarvey has long championed legislation to support premature babies and their families, including a bill requiring insurance to cover specialized nutrition support for premature babies, which McGarvey passed into law as a Kentucky state Senate more than a decade ago.

Specifically, the Stand By NICU Babies and Families Act would:

Provide eligible employees with up to 12 additional workweeks of FMLA leave while their child is admitted to the NICU;

Ensure NICU leave does not count against the existing 12 weeks of FMLA leave available to eligible employees; and

Allow parents to take NICU leave flexibly, as needed, for the first year of their child’s life.

The full text of the bill can be found here.

###

Congressman Morgan McGarvey represents Kentucky’s Third Congressional District, including Louisville and Jefferson County. He serves on the House Veterans' Affairs, Small Business, and Budget Committees.

title: Menendez, McIver, Pou Demand Polluter Accountability for Full Cleanup of Passaic River Superfund Site
text:
“It is essential that the consent decree does not prejudice DOJ’s ability to recover the full funding necessary to remediate and restore the river.”

WASHINGTON, D.C. - Representatives Rob Menendez (NJ-08), LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), and Nellie Pou (NJ-09) are seeking answers on the proposed $125 million Passaic River settlement, pushing for the next stage of cleanup at the Diamond Alkali Superfund site while warning that the final deal must not limit future funding to restore the river.

“The proposed Passaic River cleanup agreement is a promising step forward for families in Newark and neighboring communities who have borne the brunt of toxic pollution for far too long,” said Congressman Rob Menendez. “But polluters must remain accountable for completing this essential work. We are conducting oversight to ensure that this deal protects taxpayers, supports future efforts to fully restore the river, and advances environmental justice for the communities that we serve.”

"New Jersey families have suffered the consequences of delayed cleanups and lack of accountability from polluters for too long. This agreement is an important step toward delivering the relief our communities deserve,” said Congresswoman LaMonica McIver. “But our work does not end here. We must ensure that environmental justice and restoration projects remain long-term priorities so that our residents are protected and our districts can thrive.”

“Our communities along the Passaic River have lived with the consequences of toxic pollution for far too long,” said Congresswoman Nellie Pou. “The companies responsible must be held accountable for the full cost of cleaning up what is one of the largest and most complicated Superfund sites in the nation. This $125 million agreement can be a critical step forward, but we need assurances that corporate restructuring and legal scheming will not leave taxpayers on the hook for billions of dollars in any remaining cleanup costs.”

The submission follows a joint effort led by Congressman Menendez alongside Congresswomen McIver and Pou urging the Environmental Protection Agency (“EPA”) and the Department of Justice (“DOJ”) to hold polluters accountable and accelerate site remediation.

The Diamond Alkali site remains severely contaminated by industrial waste, including dioxins from Vietnam War-era production of herbicides used in Agent Orange. Decades of delays have left local waterways poisoned by toxic pollution and threatened the health and safety of generations of residents. The lawmakers are pushing federal agencies to build cleanup sites onshore and hold polluters accountable.

In their comment, the lawmakers requested explicit answers from the DOJ and EPA to five key questions:

What is the rationale for entering into the consent decree now and as structured, particularly the decision to enter into the agreement solely with ERH?

Why is OxyChem TX not a party to the consent decree?

What financial assurances have DOJ and EPA received from ERH? Please share all documents received regarding the assets and liabilities of ERH and OxyChem TX.

Can ERH fulfill the full remaining cleanup obligations beyond the scope of this consent decree?

In your view, could this consent decree prejudice future liability claims against other potentially responsible parties, such as OxyChem TX?

The full public comment is available here.

Congressman Rob Menendez has represented New Jersey’s Eighth Congressional District since 2023. He serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including the Subcommittees on Environment, Energy, and Communications and Technology. Menendez remains committed to advancing environmental justice and ensuring working-class communities across New Jersey are protected from toxic pollution.

title: Nadler: Stolen (Not Super) Intelligence: Why Congress Must Stop Big AI From Ripping Off Creators
text:
Washington, D.C. –Congressman Jerrold Nadler, Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on the Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust, argued the need to regulate artificial intelligence (AI) to protect authors, artists, and creators from intellectual property (IP) theft in his latest op-ed published by Billboard.

Earlier this month, Congressmen Jerrold Nadler, Jamie Raskin, and Hank Johnson submitted an amicus brief opposing the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) dangerous argument in favor of allowing AI companies to train their models on copyrighted work, including New York Times journalism, without compensation. The brief, filed in the Southern District of New York in In re OpenAI, Inc. Copyright Infringement Litigation, reminds the court that the arguments in DOJ’s brief violate the plain text of the Copyright Act, which does not contain any national security exception to allow private companies free and unfettered use of copyrighted materials.

Read Congressman Nadler's op-ed here and below:

Stolen (Not Super) Intelligence: Why Congress Must Stop Big AI From Ripping Off Creators

For over 30 years, I’ve had the privilege of sitting on the House Judiciary Committee, and one of my priorities has been to ensure that the most powerful companies are held to account for ripping off Americans. As we grapple with fast-moving technological change, lawmakers must be vigilant that new technologies do not create new socio-economic harms. Sadly, some of the largest and wealthiest AI companies are running roughshod over intellectual property (IP) rights. Far from being “super intelligence” — as President Trump calls it — when you look at how these models are trained, they can more fittingly be described as “stolen intelligence.”

There are currently dozens of lawsuits in the U.S. and around the world alleging that AI companies have violated copyright by training their models on millions of articles, songs, books, voice recordings, videos and other creative content without permission and without payment.

The outcome of these lawsuits will have far-reaching ramifications. Worryingly, Trump’s Department of Justice is trying to put its finger on the scale, siding with billionaires in Silicon Valley against the creative and cultural beating heart of America, made up of thousands of journalists, authors, artists, actors, songwriters and musicians.

Last month, the DOJ filed a brief in the New York Times v. Microsoft and OpenAI in support of Microsoft and OpenAI. The Times alleges that Microsoft and OpenAI copied millions of its articles to train ChatGPT. Recently unsealed court filings show that a senior Microsoft scientist privately described the practice as “an astonishing theft of unprecedented proportions,” yet Donald Trump and his hand-picked lawyers argue that the clear evidence of market harm isn’t theft, but “fair use.”

While just one filing, AI developers everywhere may try to use the Trump Administration’s argument to defend the practice of mass intellectual property theft.

It’s not just the free press that’s under attack. Just look at the music industry. Suno, the most widely used AI music generator, is being sued by major record labels for training its model on their recordings without permission. Like OpenAI, Suno claims this is “fair use,” despite admitting in court that it trained on essentially all music files of reasonable quality accessible on the open internet. If the DOJ’s argument takes hold, Suno will have every reason to keep doing it.

We’re already seeing widespread market harm from Stolen Intelligence across the creative sector. Anyone streaming music has almost certainly listened to an AI-generated track without even knowing it. Most platforms are drowning in AI-generated slop, and AI makes it easier than ever for bad actors to perpetrate streaming fraud — which costs artists and rightsholders hundreds of millions, or even billions, each year, according to experts.

This causes real and disproportionate harm to artists and consumers. Every listen on an AI-generated track dilutes the share of streaming proceeds that go to human artists, from global artists to independent musicians hoping a viral song will turn a passion into a career.

Consumers are served an imitation without even knowing it, with one label, Sony Music, recently stating they have requested over 260,000 takedown requests of AI deepfakes of their artists and the epidemic becoming “an uphill struggle.”

Unless Congress draws a line in the sand, more and more companies like OpenAI and Suno will determine that they can rip off the artists, authors and creators that they rely on to train their models. We cannot let the Trump Administration give permission for mass IP theft by the back door. America can lead the world in artificial intelligence without building it on theft.

Stolen Intelligence is not an achievement; it is a liability, and Congress should treat it as one.

title: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Introduces the Know Your Body Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) introduced the Know Your Body Act that would direct the Department of Health and Human Services to create educational materials for elementary and secondary school-aged children on uterine, ovarian, and related hormonal and menstrual disorders, such as endometriosis, uterine fibroids, and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.

Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) said:

“I’ve lived with endometriosis and its debilitating pain since I was 14. When I was younger, my doctor dismissed my symptoms and told me I was exaggerating. I had to do research on my own body and find a doctor who would finally listen before I could get a diagnosis. Back then, information about endometriosis was hard to find, and far too little has changed. No one should have to fight for basic information about their own health. The Know Your Body Act will help young people get the information they need to make informed decisions about their health and take control of their futures.”

“These mandated educational materials would also provide information on treatment options, follow-up care, and strategies to help young people advocate for themselves in health care settings. Under the legislation, HHS would be required to develop these resources within one year of enactment and update them at least every five years to reflect current medical evidence.”

The legislation is co-sponsored by: Rep. Deborah K. Ross (NC-02), Rep. Lois Frankel (FL-22), Nanette Barragán (CA-44), Rep. Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Rep. Shri Thanedar (MI-13)

title: Olszewski, Morelle Introduce Legislation to Create National Public Campaign Financing Program
text:
(Washington, DC) — U.S. Congressman Johnny Olszewski (MD-02) today introduced the Government by the People Act to establish a national small-dollar public campaign financing program for candidates running for the U.S. House of Representatives. The legislation would reduce candidates' reliance on wealthy donors and special interests while giving everyday Americans a greater shot at running for office. New York Congressman Joe Morelle, who is the Ranking Member of the Committee on House Administration, joined Olszewski as a co-lead of the legislation.

The 2026 midterm elections were the most expensive midterm cycle in American history, with total spending reaching nearly $12 billion. The rising cost of campaigns creates barriers for candidates without personal wealth or established fundraising networks, mutes the influence of grassroots supporters, and forces candidates to spend more time raising money and less time engaging with their communities.

“We should do everything we can to make it easier for everyday Americans to participate in our democracy,” said Congressman Johnny Olszewski. “Our elections should be about earning the support of the people we represent, and public service should be focused squarely on delivering for those people. The Government by the People Act would help break down the financial barriers that keep qualified people from running for office, give everyday Americans a greater voice in our elections, and allow candidates to spend less time chasing big checks and more time listening to the communities they hope to serve. That's how we build a government that is accountable to the people — not the powerful.”

“Americans deserve to know they have an equal voice in our government. We cannot allow wealthy interests to drown out their voices. It’s time to empower everyday Americans, break down the financial barriers that keep good people from running for public office, and ensure our elected officials answer to their communities—not wealthy donors. I’m grateful to Congressman Olszewski for leading this important effort,” said Ranking Member Joe Morelle.

Specifically, the Government by the People Act would:

Establish a new fund for U.S. House candidates that matches individual contributions of $200 or less. The fund would be financed through increased fines for corporate campaign finance violations.

Create a state-based voucher program through which participating states could provide additional matching funds for small-dollar donations to U.S. House candidates.

Together, these programs would help level the playing field for candidates while encouraging them to build broad coalitions of grassroots supporters. By making small-dollar contributions more meaningful, the legislation would give everyday Americans a greater stake in elections and help ensure candidates hear from a wider cross-section of their communities.

The legislation builds on Congressman Olszewski's work as Baltimore County Executive, when he helped establish the County's small-dollar public campaign financing program for local candidates. Under his leadership, the County began matching small-dollar contributions, setting individual contribution limits, and requiring candidates to demonstrate a threshold of grassroots support. The program created a pathway for candidates without extensive fundraising networks or personal wealth to compete for public office.

The Government by the People Act also builds on the legacy of former Maryland Congressman John Sarbanes, a longtime champion of good-government and democracy reforms. Sarbanes' landmark For the People Act — twice designated as H.R. 1 in the House of Representatives — included a similar small-dollar public campaign financing system as part of a broader effort to strengthen voting rights, reform redistricting, and improve government ethics.

title: Rep. Onder Introduces the Allergy & Asthma Patient Protection Act
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

November 17, 2026

Contact: Brooke Morgan

(Washington, D.C.) – Today, U.S. Congressman Bob Onder, M.D. (R-MO), an allergist, introduced theAllergy & Asthma Patient Protection Act, which would amend the Public Health Service Act to require group health plans and health insurance issuers offering group or individual coverage to cover allergy and asthma diagnostic testing and to ensure that plans covering allergy shots pay for every medically necessary phase of treatment, consistent with recognized clinical standards. Rep. Onder and patient and physician groups released the following statements:

“Patients shouldn’t have to fight their insurance company to get medically necessary allergy and asthma care. As an allergist, I’ve witnessed insurers deny the buildup phase of allergy shots, cap the number of allergens that can be tested, and impose paperwork that has nothing to do with good medicine. My bill protects access to diagnostic testing and ensures patients covered for allergy shots receive every medically necessary phase of treatment. Coverage decisions should follow the clinical standards physicians use, not arbitrary rules set by insurance companies,” said Congressman Bob Onder.

“For families dealing with allergies and asthma, timely testing and effective treatment can make a tremendous difference in their quality of life,”said Rep. Bacon. “Unfortunately, unnecessary insurance restrictions can delay care, increase costs and make it harder for patients to receive the treatment they need. Our bipartisan legislation addresses these barriers and protects access to care based on established medical standards. I'm glad to work with Rep. Onder on this commonsense legislation that puts patients and their doctors first.”

“The American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology strongly endorses the Allergy and Asthma Patient Protection Act. Commercial insurers are increasingly restricting access to essential allergy and asthma treatments, including allergy immunotherapy, a safe and effective treatment that benefits more than 2.6 million patients annually. We thank Representative Onder, the only allergist in Congress, for introducing this important legislation to protect patient access to care and help allergists deliver the treatments their patients need,”said ACAAI President Dr. Cherie Zachary president and ACAAI President Elect Dr. David Stukus.

"Millions of Americans who rely on essential asthma testing and allergy immunotherapy face unfair insurance hurdles, arbitrary coverage limits, and out-of-pocket delays just to get the care their doctors prescribe. The Allergy & Asthma Patient Protection Act guarantees that private health plans cover medically necessary diagnostic testing and every stage of immunotherapy treatment. This bill ensures that care is dictated by clinical science, not administrative interference. It would protect patient access to proven treatments that can help manage disease, so children can stay in school, parents can go to work, and families can stay healthy." - Lynda Mitchell, CEO, Allergy & Asthma Network.

“For more than a century, allergy shots have helped patients take control of their allergic disease. Insurers shouldn't be allowed to undercut that care with arbitrary restrictions that ignore clinical standards and physician decision making. The Allergy & Asthma Patient Protection Act ensures that care decisions related to testing and treatment stay between patients and their physician,” said Casey McPherson Executive Director for Patient Access.

"Every patient deserves a treatment plan tailored by their clinician, not dictated by an insurer parsing their coverage arbitrarily. When insurers step outside their role as a payer to restrict testing or underfund essential treatments, patients are the ones who suffer. Decisions around testing and immunotherapy must remain between a patient and their clinician, free from arbitrary coverage denials and payment cuts. By passing the Allergy & Asthma Patient Protection Act, Congress can restore common sense to patient care and ensure insurers fulfill their fundamental role of covering the medical services patients rely on." – Sung Poblete, PhD, RN, CEO of FARE (Food Allergy Research & Education)

“The allergy season is longer and more intense, and for people with allergic asthma, allergies can trigger asthma attacks. Between 9-11 Americans die from asthma every day. Rep. Onder's bill protects access to the testing and allergy shots that help patients control their allergies. This means fewer hospitalizations, fewer missed days of work and school, and fewer lives lost. We are happy to support this bill and grateful to Rep. Onder for his leadership,” said Kenneth Mendez President and CEO of the Asthma and Allergy foundation of America.

“The Oregon Society of Allergy, Asthma, and Immunology strongly supports the Allergy & Asthma Patient Protection Act. Allergy shots and testing are proven, cost-effective care, yet restrictive insurer policies make them harder to provide and harder to access. By aligning coverage with clinical standards and ensuring fair reimbursement, this bill will help our members keep serving patients and keep care within reach for our communities.” — Executive Board, Oregon Society of Allergy, Asthma, and Immunology (OSAAI)

“No Nut Traveler supports the Allergy & Asthma Patient Protection Act because it would put clinical standards at the center of coverage decisions, from the tests that help diagnose allergies and asthma to the care patients need once they have answers. Families deserve to spend less time sorting out coverage and more time getting the care that helps them sleep, learn, work, and enjoy their lives.” — Lianne Mandelbaum, MS, PT, Founder and President, No Nut Traveler, Inc.

“Patients living with allergies and asthma deserve access to timely, accurate testing and medically necessary treatment without unnecessary barriers imposed by insurance companies. The Allergy & Asthma Patient Protection Act addresses these challenges by protecting access to essential diagnostic testing and allergen immunotherapy. Families should never have to choose between their financial well-being and receiving appropriate medical care. As an advocate for allergy and asthma patient safety, I strongly support this legislation and its commitment to ensuring that treatment decisions are guided by established clinical standards, not arbitrary insurance restrictions. Access to care should be a right, not a barrier patients must fight to overcome.” -Thomas SIlvera, MSHS-PH, Vice President Elijah-Alavi Foundation

"Ignoring a health issue is the best way to ensure poor outcomes and maximum cost to treat that very issue. The Allergy & Asthma Patient Protection Act embraces the power of diagnostics and preventative care for those who need it most. The Foundation for AAIR fully supports this logical measure to keep patients on the path to the best treatment and lasting health, all while saving long term costs for all of us" — Chris Martinez President and CEO of The Foundation for Asthma and Allergy impact and Rescue (AAIR)

"Effective and appropriate treatment begins with accurate diagnosis. Diagnostic decisions made between a doctor and their patients are critical decision points, ensuring neither patients nor the healthcare system is burdened by overdiagnosis, underdiagnosis, or misdiagnosis. Limits to effective diagnosis and appropriate treatment result in physical, financial, psychological strain for patients, as well as additional health risks that can complicate and compound future health decisions. Support for the Allergy & Asthma Patient Protection Act aligns coverage with clinical practice, improving the lives of patients and their families while employing a forward-thinking strategy for insurers and the healthcare system as a whole." — Erin Malawer, Executive Director of AllergyStrong

Background Information

Allergen immunotherapy (allergy shots) has been used successfully for more than 110 years to treat patients with environmental allergies. Patients receive gradually increasing doses of allergen by injection, starting with a buildup phase and eventually reaching a maintenance dose. It is a cost-effective, disease-modifying treatment that changes the course of allergic disease rather than managing symptoms. Yet a growing number of insurers are adopting billing and coverage policies that make it harder for patients to access this important treatment.

Some insurers are:

● Refusing to cover the buildup phase of immunotherapy (the period when a patient's dose is gradually increased)

● Imposing arbitrary unit and volume limits on allergy shots that fall well below clinical standards

● Capping the number of allergens that can be tested, or denying testing done on the same day as an office visit

● Reducing payment for extracts that contain diluent, a standard part of preparing nearly every allergy shot

● Denying claims when a patient's extract must be split into multiple vials for safety or potency

These policies have no clinical justification and contradict the practice standards established by medical specialty societies that treat allergic conditions. They are administrative barriers that shift costs onto patients and the physicians who treat them.

WHAT THE ALLERGY & ASTHMA PATIENT PROTECTION ACT DOES:

● Requires coverage of allergy and asthma diagnostic testing in private health insurance, without arbitrary limits that conflict with clinical standards

● Protects allergy shot coverage by requiring plans that cover immunotherapy to pay for extract preparation and every medically necessary phase of treatment

● Ties coverage to the clinical standards physicians already follow, the practice parameters published by the national allergy and immunology specialty societies and CPT code descriptions

title: Rep. Panetta Introduces Legislation to  Foster Wildfire Risk Reduction and Preparedness
text:
Washington, D.C. – United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) authored and introduced the Wildfire Emergency Act to reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires in the American West through forest restoration, energy resilience, investments in critical infrastructure and home hardening, and firefighter training. Senator Alex Padilla (D-CA) has introduced companion legislation in the U.S. Senate.

Since 2020, major wildfires along California’s Central Coast have burned more than half a million acres combined. This wildfire season, the Timber and Plaskett fires broke out in Monterey County’s Big Sur region and burned more than 55,000 acres combined. Statewide, CAL FIRE recorded 8,232 wildfires last year that burned 507,817 acres and destroyed 16,627 structures, with a preliminary death toll of 31. The change in our climate contributes to longer, more active fire seasons across the western United States as hotter, drier conditions leave vegetation more likely to ignite and fires more likely to spread.

“From the hills of South San Jose up into the mountains of Santa Cruz County and down the Monterey County coastline to northern San Luis Obispo County, we’ve seen wildfires put our communities at risk,” said Rep. Panetta. “Of course, we are so thankful for the amazing and dedicated work of our firefighters and first responders to suppress wildfires, but the federal government must step up when it comes to preventing these types of fires. The Wildfire Emergency Act would help communities across our 19th Congressional District invest in ways to restore forests, harden homes, keep critical facilities powered, and provide vulnerable communities the training and resources necessary to help prevent these types of fires and protect lives, land, and livelihoods.”

Key provisions of the Wildfire Emergency Act include allowing the U.S. Forest Service to leverage private financing to accelerate forest restoration projects, creating a program to ensure power at critical facilities during wildfire disruptions, expanding a weatherization grant program to help low-income households harden their homes against wildfires, and establishing one or more centers for prescribed fire training for the western United States.

Specifically, the Wildfire Emergency Act would:

Provide the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) with a pilot authority to bring together local stakeholders, conservationists, and private financing groups to leverage additional funds to increase the pace and scale of forest restoration projects. The USFS would be able to enter into up to 20 conservation finance agreements using this pilot authority. Federal obligations would be capped at $250 million over 10 years and $50 million per agreement. The pilot would give priority to larger landscapes, particularly those of at least 100,000 acres. The bill also requires a report to Congress on the impact of this pilot authority and any barriers to its broader use.

Establish an energy resilience program at the Department of Energy (DOE) to ensure that critical facilities can keep operating during wildfire disruptions. The bill would authorize $100 million for the program. On-site backup power would use renewable resources, low-carbon liquid fuels, and energy storage.

Expand an existing DOE weatherization grant program for low-income households to support wildfire-hardening retrofits, such as ember-resistant roofs or gutters. The bill raises the average weatherization cost limit to $13,000 per home, adjusted annually for inflation.

Expedite the placement of wildfire detection equipment on the ground, such as sensors or cameras, and expand the use of space-based observation to identify new fires faster and help firefighters respond more effectively.

Authorize grants to professional organizations, state agencies, and academic institutions to expand the forest conservation and wildland firefighting workforce. These grants would increase outreach to interested students and support training and internships for the next generation of foresters and firefighters.

Establish one or more prescribed fire-training centers in the West.

Authorize a total of $50 million for fiscal years 2027 through 2031 to support community grants of up to $50,000 per year for locally focused land stewardship and conservation.

Full text of the bill is available here.

title: Pingree Demands Full Accounting of NEH’s Taxpayer-Funded Rome Conference
text:
Congresswoman Chellie Pingree (D-Maine), the top Democrat on the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies, is demanding answers from National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH) Chairman Michael McDonald about a recent NEH-sponsored conference in Rome, Italy.

The two-day, taxpayer-funded event at a Roman palazzo—which featured several controversial right-wing academics, including one with close ties to former Hungarian dictator Viktor Orbán—was not publicized by NEH in advance and recordings of the panels were only available on an Italian government website.

“The fact that NEH has not highlighted this conference itself raises even more questions about whether you would prefer this event was kept under the radar,” Pingree wrote. “But such a seemingly exorbitant trip requires transparency and accountability to the American taxpayer and justification for its purpose.”

Pingree, who is set to take the gavel of the powerful Appropriations Subcommittee that oversees the NEH, also criticized the agency’s decision to dismantle longstanding programs that served veterans, educators, and communities across the country, while funneling tens of millions of dollars to President Trump’s pet projects.

“I find it inexplicable that you would convene a conference—which has resulted in no specific policy or program—in a Roman palazzo while simultaneously eroding the reach and capacity of the Endowment to support everyday Americans,” Pingree said.

Pingree requested additional information about the two-day conference—as well as NEH’s travel budget and expenses—including documentation relating to travel costs and accommodations, the source of the funding within NEH’s budget for such a trip, a list of attendees, and a breakdown of NEH’s travel budget for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.

The full letter is available here and is copied below.

Last year, Pingree sounded the alarm over the Trump Administration’s unprecedented and legally dubious grantmaking practices, and called the integrity of the NEH into question.

+++

Dear Chairman McDonald:

I am writing to seek information regarding the concerning use of taxpayer funds for a National Endowment for the Humanities (NEH)-sponsored junket called “Classical Foundations and Moral Authority" at the Palazzo San Macuto in Rome, Italy.

According to The New York Times, the two-day conference featured nearly a dozen Anglophone academics, most of them conservative critics of universities, modern secular liberal democracy, or both. Speakers also included the president of a Budapest think tank closely aligned with former Hungarian President Viktor Orbán. Recordings of the panels were posted on an Italian government website, yet NEH chose not to publicize the conference in advance or while it was happening.

The fact that NEH has not highlighted this conference itself raises even more questions about whether you would prefer this event was kept under the radar. But such a seemingly exorbitant trip requires transparency and accountability to the American taxpayer and justification for its purpose.

Historically, NEH funding has reached thousands of towns and communities, supporting local organizations and providing access to humanities for all Americans. During your tenure, NEH has gutted funding for public programming in favor of large dollar sole-source grants. You have also canceled or significantly rolled back all programming for veterans, Humanities Perspectives on Artificial Intelligence, and educator professional development, among other topics.

Even more disturbingly, you are siphoning off tens of millions of dollars towards President Trump’s vanity projects, including his proposed Triumphal Arch, the Garden of Heroes, and other so-called beautification efforts in the District of Columbia.

Under your leadership, NEH has laid off more than 100 employees and unlawfully terminated more than 1,400 grants to support scholars, research institutions, and humanities organizations. I find it inexplicable that you would convene a conference—which has resulted in no specific policy or program—in a Roman palazzo while simultaneously eroding the reach and capacity of the Endowment to support everyday Americans.

Please provide a response to these questions and the requested information by December 17, 2026.

Provide all documentation related to this conference, including the purpose and a breakdown of costs, including airfare, lodging, per diems, honoraria, etc.

Provide the source of the funding within NEH’s budget that was used to support these expenses.

In your opening remarks at the conference, you express “profound gratitude” to the Wilson Center and its President, Natasha Jacome. Specifically, what support did the Wilson Center provide? Was it financial, and if so, provide a complete accounting of the funds.

Provide a list of attendees of the conference and the justification for each person whose attendance was covered by NEH or Wilson Center funding.

Provide a breakdown of the NEH’s travel budget for fiscal years 2026 and 2027.

Do you intend for this conference to be a one-time event, or recurring?

Sincerely,

###

title: Reps. Pou, Veasey, Pfluger and Nunn Re- Introduce Bipartisan Cybersecurity Clinics Grant Program Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Representatives Nellie Pou (D-NJ-09), Marc Veasey (D-TX-33), August Pfluger (R-TX-11) and Zach Nunn (R-IA-3) introduced the Cybersecurity Clinics Grant Program Act. This bill would require the Department of Homeland Security, through the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, to establish a grant program to fund higher education-based cybersecurity clinics at community colleges and minority-serving institutions.

“Cybersecurity threats are growing more sophisticated every day. We need to make sure our communities have the tools and trained professionals to meet them,” said Congresswoman Pou. “I am proud to co-lead the Cybersecurity Clinics Grant Program Act which will help give the next generation of diverse graduates at community colleges, Hispanic-serving institutions, and other minority-serving colleges hands-on experience while strengthening our nation’s cyber defenses through these new cybersecurity clinics. This legislation represents a smart investment in our national security and in the next generation of cybersecurity professionals.”

“I am proud to work alongside Representatives Pfluger, Pou, and Nunn to help grow and diversify the next generation of young Americans in the cybersecurity workforce,” said Congressman Veasey. “The Cybersecurity Clinics Grant Program Act will help do that by ensuring that institutions of higher education, including community colleges and colleges minority-serving institutions, can have the proper tools they need to educate their students in this growing field.”

“Developing a robust cyber workforce is critical to our national and economic security. AI has become an incredible tool for identifying vulnerabilities, but it is also making attacks faster and harder to detect. We cannot defend the homeland without talented professionals who have the skills and know-how to recognize, understand, and stop these threats. Angelo State University, now an NSA National Center of Academic Excellence in Cyber Defense, is training students who protect West Texas cities, schools, and hospitals in real time through its Regional Security Operations Center. I’m proud to co-lead this bipartisan bill to expand on this model and build the cyber workforce that our national and economic security depend on,” said Congressman Pfluger.

“Cyberattacks are an increasingly serious threat to our national security, economy, and the small businesses that power communities across Iowa,” said Congressman Nunn. “As a former White House Cybersecurity Director, I know we need to train the next generation of cyber professionals today to stay ahead of tomorrow’s threats. Our bipartisan bill will help community colleges establish cybersecurity clinics that give students hands-on training and real-world experience while equipping small businesses and local governments with the tools to defend against cybercriminals. We’re strengthening America’s cyber workforce and putting those skills to work protecting the communities that need them most.”

This bipartisan legislation will help create the framework for a robust and strategic model that can help the U.S. shore up national security defenses domestically and globally.

###

title: Pressley, Duckworth Renew Push to Ensure Paid Leave Benefits for Families Experiencing Pregnancy Loss, Invest in Research to Improve Care
text:
As Trump attacks workplace protections for pregnant women, bicameral bill would shine light on pregnancy loss, increase access to resources, workforce support and patient-centered care

Bill Text (PDF)

WASHINGTON – Today, as the Trump Administration works to scale back workplace protections for women experiencing pregnancy- and reproductive health-related complications, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) and Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) are reintroducing legislation to support those navigating pregnancy loss by establishing new paid leave benefits for workers across the nation who are experiencing painful, traumatic challenges while seeking to start or grow their family. The bicameral Support Through Loss Act would increase access to resources and patient-centered care while providing 7 days of paid leave for all American workers after they experience some of the many challenges that hopeful parents face on the road to parenthood, including a pregnancy loss, an intrauterine insemination or an assisted reproductive technology procedure that did not result in a live birth, a stillbirth, a failed adoption arrangement or surrogacy arrangement, a diagnosis or event that impacts pregnancy or fertility.

“The journey of expanding a family can be a beautiful process, but it can also be a path marked by hardship and grief. Miscarriage, stillbirth, unsuccessful IVF cycles, and other forms of pregnancy loss can be devastating, especially when families are left without support,” said Rep. Pressley. “Nothing can take away the pain of a loss, but passing this bill would help provide impacted families with workforce support, essential health care, and resources as they navigate the healing process. I am grateful to Sen. Duckworth for her leadership and partnership and to every family and advocate that has trusted us with their stories.”

“We should be doing everything we can to support hopeful parents, not leaving them behind when they’re experiencing devastating setbacks and disappointments on the road to parenthood,” said Sen. Duckworth. “My family faced our own heartbreaks and challenges when growing our family, and I wouldn’t have my two girls today if it weren’t for the miracle of IVF. The Support Through Loss Act would provide so many hopeful parents with the time they need to grieve and heal when living through difficult losses. Let’s get it passed so we can better support the thousands of families struggling through these all-too-common experiences.”

At least 10-20% of known pregnancies end in miscarriage, but too often this common occurrence of pregnancy loss among families is underreported. The Support Through Loss Act would also direct the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to develop and disseminate public information regarding pregnancy loss and invest in long-overdue research with the National Institutes of Health.

Specifically, the Support Through Loss Act would:

Ensure employers provide at least seven days of paid leave for workers to process and address health—including mental health—needs following a pregnancy loss an intrauterine insemination or an assisted reproductive technology procedure that did not result in a live birth, a stillbirth, a failed adoption arrangement, a failed surrogacy arrangement, a diagnosis or event that impacts pregnancy or fertility;

Direct the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to develop and disseminate educational resources for the public regarding pregnancy loss and the range of treatment options for pregnancy loss, including recurrent pregnancy loss; and

Provide $45 million in annual funding for the National Institutes of Health to expand, intensify and coordinate federal research and programs with respect to pregnancy loss to help develop a better understanding of the problem and potentially suggest best practices to reduce pregnancy loss.

A copy of the full bill text can be found here.

Along with Congresswoman Pressley, the Support Through Loss Act is cosponsored in the House by U.S. Representatives Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ-03), Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), Judy Chu (D-CA-28), Yvette Clarke (D-NY-09), Glenn Ivey (D-MD-04), Timothy Kennedy (D-NY-26), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC-At Large), Chellie Pingree (D-ME-01), Ritchie Torres (D-NY-15), Bonnie Watson Coleman (D-NJ-12), Nikema Williams (D-GA-05) and Frederica Wilson (D-FL-24).

In August 2023, Rep. Pressley issued a statement on the Fifth Circuit Court decision in Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine v. FDA.

In July 2023, Rep. Pressley, alongside Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Rep. Cori Bush (MO-01), and Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), reintroduced the Reproductive Health Care Accessibility Act, legislation to help people with disabilities—who face discrimination and extra barriers when seeking care—get better access to reproductive health care and the informed care they need to control their own reproductive lives.

In July 2023, Rep. Pressley applauded the Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) approval of over-the-counter birth control.

In May 2023, Rep. Pressley applauded the FDA Advisory Committee’s unanimous, 17-0 vote to recommend the approval of the first-ever application for over-the-counter birth control. In May 2023, Rep. Pressley, along with Representatives Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14) and Ami Bera, MD (CA-06) and Senators Mazie Hirono (D-HI) and Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), reintroduced their bicameral Affordability is Access Act to ensure that once the FDA determines an over-the-counter birth control option to be safe, insurers fully cover over-the-counter birth control without any fees or out-of-pocket costs.

In April 2023, Rep. Pressley issued a statement condemning the Texas court ruling on mifepristone, and discussed the Texas case in a recent floor speech in which she affirmed medication abortion as routine medical care and access to mifepristone as essential. She later joined Governor Maura Healey, Senator Elizabth Warren (D-MA), and local leaders in announcing action to protect Mifepristone in Massachusetts.

In March 2023, Rep. Pressley, along with Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Reps. Schakowsky, Lee, DeGette, Torres and Strickland, reintroduced the Abortion is Healthcare Everywhere Act harmful and discriminatory Helms Amendment and expand abortion access globally.

In March 2023, Rep. Pressley and Senator Hirono led their colleagues in reintroducing a bicameral congressional resolution honoring abortion providers and clinic staff.

In March 2023, Rep. Pressley delivered a speech in which she discussed the pending court case in Texas, which aims to restrict access to medication abortion across the entire nation. In her remarks, Rep. Pressley affirmed medication abortion as routine medical care, and accessibility to the abortion pill mifepristone as essential.

In September 2021, Rep. Pressley issued a statement condemning the Supreme Court’s inaction on SB-8, Texas’ restrictive abortion law. Later that month, she participated in a House Oversight Committee hearing to examine the threat posed by abortion bans and underscored the urgency of the Senate passing the Women’s Health Protection Act.

In April 2021, Rep. Pressley, along with Congresswomen Barbara Lee (CA-13), Diana DeGette (CO-01) and Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), led a group of 131 Democratic members in reintroducing the Equal Access to Abortion Coverage in Health Insurance Act or the EACH Act, which would repeal the Hyde Amendment and ensure that all people, regardless of income, insurance or zip code, can make personal reproductive health care decisions without interference from politicians. She re-Introduced the legislation In January 2023.

Rep. Pressley has led calls in Congress for the FDA to remove medically unnecessary restrictions on the medication abortion drug mifepristone, and applauded the FDA’s action in January 2023 to allow retail pharmacies to dispense abortion medication pills.

As Chair of the Pro-Choice Caucus’s Abortion Rights and Access Task Force, Congresswoman Pressley led the fight to repeal the Hyde Amendments from annual Labor, Health and Human Services, Education and Related Agencies appropriations bills and in July 2020 published a Medium post on the importance of doing so. She applauded the removal of the Hyde Amendment in President Biden’s FY2022 budget.

In May 2020, she led more than 155 Members of Congress in calling on House Democratic leadership to ensure that any future COVID-19 relief packages rejected Republican efforts to use the public health crisis to diminish abortion access.

In August 2021, Rep. Pressley, Oversight Chairwoman Carolyn Maloney, and Pro-Choice Caucus Co-Chairs Reps. Diana DeGette and Barbara Lee led more than 70 of their House Democratic colleagues in introducing a resolution in support of equitable, science-based policies governing access to medication abortion care.

In January 2023, Rep. Pressley introduced a resolution to condemn all forms of political violence in the U.S., regardless of its target or intent. That same day, she delivered a powerful speech on the House floor slamming Republicans’ harmful, misleading anti-abortion resolution.

In September 2022, Rep. Pressley hosted U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra at the Codman Square Health Center in Dorchester for a convening on their work to address the Black maternal health crisis and the criminalization of abortion care in states across the nation following the harmful U.S. Supreme Court decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health.

In May 2019, she led more than 100 colleagues in introducing H.Con.Res.40, a resolution reaffirming the House of Representative’s support for Roe v. Wade.

In June 2019, Rep. Pressley introduced H.R. 3296, the Affordability is Access Act, to make oral contraception available without a prescription.

In September 2016, as a member of the Boston City Council, Pressley championed a resolution calling on Congress and President Obama to repeal the Hyde Amendment and reinstate insurance coverage for abortion services.
