title: Cantwell Joins Tribal, Business, & Conservation Leaders to Sound the Alarm on Permitting Reform Proposal
text:
Cantwell Joins Tribal, Business, & Conservation Leaders to Sound the Alarm on Permitting Reform Proposal

Senate to vote this week on legislation that would weaken Clean Water Act protections & limit tribal input on projects that impact their historic sites & natural resources

WASHINGTON, D.C. –Today, U.S. Senator Maria Cantwell (D-WA), a senior member of the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources, joined tribal, outdoor recreation, and conservation leaders for a virtual press conference to push back on a permitting reform proposal that would undermine tribal nations and weaken protections for our waters, land, and wildlife.

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA, is being voted on by the Senate this week. If the Senate passes the bill, it may be taken up by the House of Representatives before the end of the year.

“Don't sacrifice the Clean Water Act, or hunting or fishing grounds, historic or sacred sites, or protections of tribal sovereignty,” said Sen. Cantwell. “We all need new sources of energy and power. I've been committed to that my whole time in the United States Senate. But this bill, as it's currently drafted, is not the answer.”

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is the single greatest threat to our ability to protect our sacred spaces, our ancestors, traditional ceremonies, and our culture in decades,” said Oneida Vice Chair Jameson Wilson (WI). “Any effort to accelerate development must strengthen, not diminish and erode tribal sovereignty and meaningful consultation. If we and other tribes across the country had been consulted by the authors of this bill or been able to submit feedback through the regular legislative process, we could have helped draft a bill that gives developers the certainty they need to build on federal and tribal land, while still ensuring we are able to protect our sacred spaces. However, this bill was drafted in secret by four senators without any tribal input, not a single congressional hearing or vote, and now it is being fast tracked for passage.”

“One of BAAJA’s most insidious and hidden attacks on clean water is through codifying changes to the Clean Water Act with regard to the protection of wetlands,” said Brian Chaffin, owner of the Sundog River Guide Company (AK) and Executive Director of the Clark Fork Coalition in Montana. “The act would remove the requirement for Section 404 permits to consider the loss of wildlife habitat and flood control structures, particularly in headwater states like Montana. This has a compounding effect. When we fill wetlands without assessment and mitigation, the impacts of increasing size and intensity of floods will be felt far downstream from Montana to New Orleans. Removing this protection will lead to an increase in flood-related disasters, property damage, loss of life, and the need for emergency federal assistance.”

“The purpose of environmental laws is not simply to provide remedies after harm occurs; it is to help us make sound decisions before that harm becomes irreversible,” said Yakama Tribal Councilmember John Washines (WA). “You cannot bring back an extinct salmon run with an after-the-fact apology. My people have already paid far too much for this country's energy development. We should not be asked to sacrifice our salmon and our treaty rights yet again.”

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act jeopardizes land, water, and access critical to the $1.2 trillion outdoor industry economy,” said Corley Kenna, head of communications and policy for Patagonia Outdoor Clothing & Gear. “This bill will weaken bedrock environmental laws, undermine tribal nation sovereignty, and make it harder for state governments and the public to challenge harmful extractive projects if the bill is passed in its current form. Provisions could lock in drilling, mining, logging, and other development on public lands with little to no opportunity to undo those actions -- threatening wildlife, clean water, and culturally significant areas.”

“The Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation supports responsible economic development and permitting reform,” said Prairie Band Potawatomi Nation Chairman Joseph “Zeke” Rupnick (KS). “However, reform cannot come at the expense of tribal sovereignty, sacred places, natural resources, or the federal government's legal obligations to tribal nations. We call upon Congress to halt advancements of BAAJA until meaningful government-to-government consultation occurs.”

“The BAAJA drafting process has been rushed and it's deeply flawed. The project certainty provision within it weakens states' rights, and we -- business owners, and all citizens -- lose local control and our own voices,” said Grant Bixby, realtor and volunteer leader of the Business Alliance for Protecting the Pacific Coast (CA). “We can't afford BAAJA. It risks harming our waters and lands upon which our businesses depend. In California, offshore mineral resources makes up 1% of our marine economy employment, should we put the other 99% of our employment at risk of closure and devastation? I think not.”

BAAJA would:

Limit public input: Impose new deadlines and restrictions on lawsuits challenging federal environmental decisions, while limiting courts' ability to halt certain projects even when violations are identified.

Undermine tribal sovereignty and protections for sacred sites: Rewrite federal historic preservation requirements, impose new deadlines on tribal consultation, and limit certain legal challenges—weakening Tribal Nations’ ability to influence federal decisions affecting their ancestral lands, sacred sites, and cultural resources.

Reduce environmental review: Expand circumstances in which projects can proceed without a full federal environmental review and narrow the alternatives considered.

Change clean water and wetlands protections: Revise state water-quality certification, wetlands permitting, and judicial review procedures.

Alter endangered species protections: Change federal consultation and review requirements affecting salmon, steelhead, and other protected species.

Restrict agency flexibility after project approval: Establish new limitations on modifying or revoking certain federal permits.

Sen. Cantwell is one of the Senate’s staunchest protectors of our public lands. She led the 12-year-long battle to stop the Pebble Mine in Bristol Bay, Alaska, which would have devastated one of the world’s largest salmon runs. Last year she led the fight against GOP proposals to sell public lands to the highest bidder.

title:
VIDEO: Capito Honors the Life and Legacy of
Former Senator Jay Rockefeller
text:
Click here or on the image above to watch Senator Capito’s floor speech.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.) today delivered a floor speech honoring the life of former U.S. Senator Jay Rockefeller (D-W.Va.) and his service to West Virginia. Senator Rockefeller dedicated nearly five decades to West Virginia, serving as a VISTA worker, a delegate in the West Virginia Legislature, Secretary of State, Governor, and a U.S Senator.

Following her speech, a resolution honoring the life of Senator Rockefeller, led by Senators Capito and Jim Justice (R-W.Va.), passed by unanimous consent. Click here to read the full resolution.

Below is a transcript of Senator Capito’s full speech, as prepared for delivery:

“Mr. President –

“Today, I rise to honor the life and legacy of a remarkable West Virginian, former Governor and U.S. Senator, Jay Rockefeller.

“Jay was many things: a dedicated public servant, a passionate advocate for West Virginia, and a respected leader in this very chamber.

“But, to me, he was a mentor, a dear friend, and a true gentleman.

“I’d also like to take a moment to recognize his beloved wife, Sharon, and daughter, Valerie, who are here with us to honor his life and legacy.

“Thank you both for being here.

“Anyone who knew Jay knew how deeply he loved West Virginia and the people he represented. But above all else, Jay loved his family.

“And at the center of that love was always Sharon.

“Their partnership was a special one, and I know how much his children and grandchildren meant to him as well.

“My personal relationship with Jay began under difficult circumstances.

“My father, Arch Moore was a political rival of Jay’s, and putting it politely, I would say they were not the best of friends.

“Apparently, my father, when he was Governor, would throw some critical comments about Jay out into the public and I believe Jay would return the fire.

“So, when I was elected to the House of Representatives from West Virginia in 2000, I was not sure what to expect.

“But what I got was a warm friendship from a man who expressed to me that his relationship with my Dad was immaterial to how our relationship could progress.

“That showed me that not only was Jay a man of integrity, but he was kind, and thoughtful throughout our years of service together.

“Jay and I came from different political parties, and we certainly didn’t always agree.

“But those differences never stood in the way of our friendship.

“Jay understood that working together for the good of the people we represent always comes first.

“And I think that is something we could all be reminded of from time to time.

“Jay was born into a famous family of tremendous wealth.

“He could have lived anywhere, done anything, and enjoyed a life of privilege.

“But he was called to serve, and extraordinarily found a place where he belonged, and that place was West Virginia.

“The song Country Roads talks about the feeling that I should have been home yesterday.

“A feeling that I think Jay felt when he came to Emmons, West Virginia.

“He uprooted his entire life in New York to come be a VISTA Worker in our state to try and make a difference.

“And what began as an opportunity to serve grew into a lifetime of public service.

“He went on to serve as a Delegate in the West Virginia Legislature, Secretary of State, Governor, and then onto D.C. where he served in the Senate for 30 years.

“He devoted his life to a state he chose to call home, and in doing so, helped shape its future for generations to come.

“But there was so much more to Jay than his impressive record of public service.

“Jay was a man of many wonders, with a particular love for baseball, Asian art, and, interestingly, Baroque music.

“He studied Japanese at the International Christian University in Tokyo and Asian history at Yale, and he received a degree in Far Eastern languages and history from Harvard.

“Jay’s experiences enabled him to view life from all different points of view.

‘And his depth of knowledge and understanding for others is what, I think, made him fit for his many roles, and what made his work so special.

“Jay was a problem solver and brought thoughtful solutions to the needs of West Virginians with unrelenting passion.

“He approached the challenges facing West Virginians with an unwavering commitment to improving their lives.

“Few areas demonstrate that commitment more clearly than his work on health care.

“Jay played a monumental role in advancing the Children’s Health Insurance Program, better known as CHIP.

“Because of his leadership, hundreds of thousands of West Virginia children have benefited from that vision.

“Following his mother’s diagnosis with Alzheimer’s disease, Jay became a strong advocate for neurological research and treatment, helping lay the groundwork for what is now the Rockefeller Neuroscience Institute at West Virginia University.

“As someone whose own parents battled Alzheimer’s, this part of Jay’s legacy is particularly meaningful to me.

“I know firsthand the devastating toll this disease takes on individuals and their loved ones.

“And I am proud to continue building on the work Jay championed, and the hope he helped provide to so many families.

“Jay was also a fierce advocate for the men and women who power our country.

“After the Sago Mine tragedy, Jay spent much of his time working with our coal miners to learn how we can better advocate for their health and safety.

“He authored the Rockefeller Coal Act to protect lifetime healthcare and retirement benefits for retired miners and the widows of those who have passed.

“As well as the MINER Act to improve underground mine safety, emergency response, and rescue protocols.

“One of his most enduring accomplishments was helping bring Toyota to West Virginia.

“Now, Toyota has over 2,100 employees creating cutting-edge automobiles in West Virginia.

“I am proud to have worked with Jay over the years to foster our relationship with Toyota and help them continue to grow and expand in our state, and I will continue to build that legacy with his words of encouragement in mind.

“During his time in the Senate, Jay served in some of this chamber’s most consequential leadership roles, including as chairman of the Intelligence and Commerce Committees.

“He took those responsibilities seriously and delivered meaningfully for West Virginia.

“Jay epitomized West Virginians’ warmth and friendliness, and I am forever grateful for his leadership and guidance.

“His willingness to work with others and ability to put differences aside for the good of West Virginia and our country is commendable.

“I am honored to have succeeded him in the Senate and am indebted to the advice and support he offered to me early on and throughout my career.

“Jay fought hard for West Virginia, he treated everyone with love and always found a way to move our country forward, together.

“He served with integrity and was a true gentleman.

“And in this day and age, I think those are extremely great traits for a public servant and man.

“West Virginia is a better place because of Jay Rockefeller, and I am a better public servant for having known him.

“He will be deeply missed, but his legacy will endure for generations to come.”

# # #

title: Senator Collins’ Bipartisan Bill to Expand Federal Worker Access to Health Care Passes Senate Unanimously
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Susan Collins announced that the bipartisan Improving Access to Workers’ Compensation for Injured Federal Workers Act that she introduced with Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) passed the Senate last night by voice vote. The bill now heads to the House of Representatives for consideration.

Currently, federal employees—including the more than 12,000 working in Maine—can select a Physician Assistant (PA) or a Nurse Practitioner (NP) as their primary health care provider within the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program. However, the Federal Employees Compensation Act (FECA) permits only a physician to make diagnoses, certify injuries and the extent of a disability, and oversee a federal employee’s treatment and care when they are injured on the job.

The Improving Access to Workers’ Compensation for Injured Federal Workers Act would amend FECA to allow PAs and NPs to certify injuries and oversee treatment for federal workers with injuries or illnesses that occurred on the job, when doing so is consistent with the scope of their practice under state law.

“In a large, rural state like Maine, finding access to health care close to home can be a challenge. Nurse practitioners and physician assistants help to fill in this gap by providing quality medical services to local communities,” said Senator Collins. “By allowing injured federal workers to be treated by these professionals, our bipartisan bill would help prevent the need for long and difficult travel, reduce wait times for care, and improve employees’ overall health and wellbeing. The Senate’s unanimous approval of the bill reflects broad bipartisan agreement that this unnecessary barrier to care should be removed.”

The bill has been endorsed by dozens of organizations, including the American Association of Nurse Practitioners (AANP), the American Academy of Physician Associates, the American Academy of Nursing, the PA Education Association, the American Association of Colleges of Nursing, the American Federation of Government Employees, and the National Federation of Federal Employees.

“The American Association of Nurse Practitioners (AANP), on behalf of the over 461,000 nurse practitioners (NPs) nationwide, commends Senators Collins and Blumenthal for their leadership on passing S. 3296, the Improvising Access to Workers' Compensation for Injured Federal Workers Act, in the US Senate”said AANP President, Valerie J. Fuller, PhD, DNP. “As a dual board-certified nurse practitioner in Portland, Maine, I know the importance of this legislation to federal employees. Authorizing NPs to certify federal workplace injuries and oversee the patient's treatment and care will ensure injured federal employees receive the care they need from their chosen and trusted health care providers to get them back to work sooner. We look forward to advancing this bill through the House and securing the President’s signature this year.”

“AFGE strongly commends Senators Collins and Blumenthal for securing Senate passage of the Improving Access to Workers’ Compensation for Injured Federal Workers Act. By allowing nurse practitioners and physician assistants to diagnose injuries and provide care, this bill will significantly help federal workers hurt on the job. Federal workers are regularly called to work in remote and rural locations where health care is limited and physicians are scarce. This much-needed reform will directly benefit the public servants who protect and serve the American public every day. AFGE calls on the House to pass this bill immediately under suspension of the rules and send it to the president’s desk,” said Dr. Everett B. Kelley, National President, American Federation of Government Employees, AFL-CIO (AFGE).

“The American Academy of Physician Associates (AAPA) applauds Senators Collins and Blumenthal for championing this commonsense legislation. Too many federal workers still face outdated barriers that delay or deny the care they need when they are injured on the job,” said AAPA President and Chair of the Board of Directors David J. Bunnell, PhD, PA-C, DFAAPA. “With more than 200,000 PAs nationwide delivering high-quality care across every specialty, passing this bill is essential for modernizing our system and ensuring federal employees can get timely, expert care without unnecessary roadblocks.”

The complete text of the bill can be read here.

title: Cortez Masto, Curtis Introduce Legislation to Improve Grid Reliability and Affordability
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) and John Curtis (R-Utah) introduced the High-Capacity Grid Act to modernize America’s transmission system by requiring the use of best-available transmission conductors for new interstate transmission lines and rebuilds.

The rising cost of energy transmission is one of the biggest drivers of high utility costs, and lines are more prone to failure, fires, and line losses – all of which increase costs for Americans. This legislation would help modernize transmission conductors to lower costs.

“This commonsense, bipartisan bill will require that new transmission projects and rebuilds use high-performance, efficient conductors,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “American families are paying too much for their utility bills, and improving the conductors we use for transmission lines is a way to lower costs and make our infrastructure work better for everyone.”

“Utah needs an electric grid that can keep pace with rising demand without passing unnecessary costs on to families and businesses,” said Senator Curtis. “Our bipartisan bill would invest in more efficient transmission technology—utilizing infrastructure we already have, strengthening American energy security, and helping keep electricity affordable for Utahns.”

The High-Capacity Grid Act directs the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to establish a best-available transmission conductor standard, requiring utilities to use the highest-capacity and highest-efficiency commercially available conductors for interstate transmission. It also expands the number of projects that must use these state-of-the-art conductors to improve grid reliability at the lowest possible cost for consumers. Companion legislation is led by Representative Fedorchak (R-N.D.-At Large) in the House of Representatives.

“NEMA applauds the introduction of the High-Capacity Grid Act and its focus on advancing transmission technologies that strengthen grid reliability, improve efficiency and help keep electricity affordable. America’s electrical manufacturers are delivering the innovative and proven solutions needed to quickly and affordably expand grid capacity and meet growing energy demand. We commend Senators Catherine Cortez Masto and John Curtis for their leadership in advancing a stronger, more resilient electric grid,” said Will Hupman, Senior Vice President of Government Affairs for the National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA).

Senator Cortez Masto has led efforts in Congress to ensure the electric grid can handle growing demand. She has led bipartisan legislation to encourage the production of electric distribution transformers, devices that are critical to the energy grid and secure America’s energy supply chain. This year, she introduced the Securing Community Upgrades for a Resilient Grid Act (SECURE Grid Act), bipartisan legislation to empower states to fully assess the risks to their electric grids, from extreme weather to cyber threats and other vulnerabilities.

###

title: Cortez Masto, Rosen, Schiff, Senate Democratic Colleagues Push CFTC to Reverse Ban on Geofencing by Prediction Markets
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) and Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.) joined Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif) in calling out Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chair Michael Selig for the agency’s decision to prohibit prediction markets from geofencing, allowing prediction markets to continue operating in all 50 states and on Tribal lands.

This CFTC decision undermines Nevada’s state gaming laws applicable to sports event contracts listed on prediction markets, which were upheld by the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in August, and similar state and Tribal restrictions in Michigan, California, and Washington. Both Senators from each of these states joined the letter.

“Numerous courts have held that sports-related event contracts are not swaps and instead are indistinguishable from sports bets subject to state and tribal gaming laws…. The courts have ordered platforms to cease offering various prediction contracts in Michigan, Nevada, and Washington, and on the land of two California tribes, and imposed geofencing requirements. The Commission now appears to be encouraging prediction markets to offer prohibited contracts in contempt of these court orders during active litigation,” wrote the Senators.

“We are particularly troubled that this action came just hours after the Northern District of California issued its latest court order in Blue Lake Rancheria v. Kalshi requiring Kalshi to geofence around the plaintiff’s tribal lands. This interpretation raises concerns that the Commission may be coordinating with platforms currently engaged in litigation and encouraging them to violate state and tribal gaming laws… The Commission must withdraw the interpretation or freeze all efforts to implement until litigation is resolved,” they continued.

Senators Cortez Masto, Schiff, and Rosen were joined by Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.), Gary Peters (D-Mich.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), and Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.).

The full text of the letter can be found here.

Senators Cortez Masto and Rosen have repeatedly called for more stringent oversight of prediction markets. The Senators have previously called on the CFTC to prohibit prediction markets incentivizing physical injury, death, or war; raised the alarm about offshore prediction markets allowing people to bet on wildfires; and pushed the CFTC to do more to combat insider trading in prediction markets. They have also urged Selig to abstain from intervening in pending litigation involving prediction markets. Cortez Masto is a co-sponsor of the Prediction Markets Are Gambling Act, which would prohibit CFTC-registered entities – like Polymarket and Kalshi – from listing any prediction contracts that resemble a sports bet or casino-style game.

title: Cotton to Bessent: Investigate Chinese-Controlled Delivery Network for National Security
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact: Tatum Wallace or Hannah McCarthy

November 17, 2026

Cotton to Bessent: Investigate Chinese-Controlled Delivery Network for National Security

WASHINGTON—Senator Tom Cotton (R-Arkansas) today sent a letter to Secretary of Treasury Scott Bessent encouraging the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) to review Chinese-controlled parcel carrier J&T Express’s investment in American carriers. Chinese carriers act as surveillance networks mapping military bases, power plants, and other critical infrastructure for the Communist Chinese government.

In part, Senator Cotton wrote:

“I write to urge the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) to review J&T Express’s stake in SwiftX, an American parcel carrier that delivers to homes in 12 states. J&T started in Indonesia and is incorporated in the Cayman Islands, but it is a Chinese company, founded by Chinese nationals and headquartered in Shanghai. China produces two of every three parcels it carries. Pinduoduo, the sister company of Temu, once supplied 90 percent of its Chinese orders. Tencent, which the Department of War lists as a Chinese military company, was its largest outside investor when it listed in Hong Kong.”

Full text of the letter may be found here and below.

November 17, 2026

The Honorable Scott Bessent

Secretary of the Treasury

U.S. Department of the Treasury

1500 Pennsylvania Avenue NW

Washington, D.C. 20220

Dear Secretary Bessent,

I write to urge the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) to review J&T Express’s stake in SwiftX, an American parcel carrier that delivers to homes in 12 states. J&T started in Indonesia and is incorporated in the Cayman Islands, but it is a Chinese company, founded by Chinese nationals and headquartered in Shanghai. China produces two of every three parcels it carries. Pinduoduo, the sister company of Temu, once supplied 90 percent of its Chinese orders. Tencent, which the Department of War lists as a Chinese military company, was its largest outside investor when it listed in Hong Kong.

In May, Chinese business press reported that J&T completed a strategic investment for a 40 percent stake in SwiftX and sent its own operations team to rebuild SwiftX’s delivery stations. SwiftX is not J&T’s first American carrier, J&T has also reportedly invested in SpeedX. This spring, SpeedX left more than 840 million files open on the internet, including customers’ names and home addresses, photos of their homes, and images of drivers’ licenses. SwiftX delivers for Temu, TikTok, and AliExpress. SpeedX delivers for Shein and Temu and says it handles more than one million packages a day. In March, SpeedX joined ProShip, which processes a massive volume of packages daily for large American retailers, including 30% of the National Retail Federation’s Top 100 Shippers.

A delivery network is a surveillance network. Every package tells the carrier who lives at an address, what they bought, and when they are home. Every route logs the roads around military bases, power plants, and ports. J&T handles 100 million parcels a day worldwide and has the money to take SwiftX to every doorstep in America. Chinese law requires every Chinese company and citizen to “support, assist, and cooperate with national intelligence efforts.”

Treasury’s own rules place geolocation data among the sensitive personal data that gives CFIUS jurisdiction over foreign investment in an American business. I urge CFIUS to open a review of J&T’s stake in SwiftX and to examine any other J&T investment in American carriers, including SpeedX. The government should require J&T to sell its stakes, as it did with StayNTouch and PatientsLikeMe. At a minimum, CFIUS should bar all access from China to SwiftX’s delivery data and require outside audits.

Chinese-controlled carriers are expanding inside the United States. CFIUS should act before J&T expands further.

Sincerely,

Tom Cotton

United States Senator

title: Sen. Cruz Applauds Senate Passage of Bipartisan Bill to Designate Route 66 a National Historic Trail
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) released the following statement applauding the Senate passage of his bipartisan Route 66 National Historic Trail Designation Act. This bill designates approximately 2,400 miles of historic U.S. Route 66, from Chicago, Illinois, to Santa Monica, California, as a National Historic Trail under the National Trails System Act. This bill will also help preserve the history of Route 66 while ensuring that new and existing energy and infrastructure projects along the route are not impeded.

Sen. Cruz said, “For 100 years, Route 66 has been an iconic part of American history, connecting communities and facilitating commerce across eight states from the Midwest to the West Coast. In Texas, Route 66 helped transform the Panhandle, supporting small businesses like family-owned restaurants and gas stations that served travelers along the route. Designating Route 66 as a National Historic Trail will help recognize its legacy while supporting tourism and economic opportunities in communities along the historic route. I’m grateful to my colleagues in the Senate for passing my legislation, and I urge my colleagues in the House to advance it to President Trump’s desk.”

U.S. Sens. Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Eric Schmitt (R-Mo.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), and Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) are cosponsors of this legislation.

Click here to read more about the bill.

BACKGROUND:

Established in 1926, Route 66 was part of the first federal highway system and played a critical role in 20th-century American history, including during the Dust Bowl migration and World War II. It remains an enduring symbol of American automobile travel. This year marks Route 66’s centennial. The bill amends the National Trails System Act to designate Route 66 as a National Historic Trail. Route 66 runs through Illinois, Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, New Mexico, Arizona, and California.

Designating Route 66 as a National Historic Trail will help preserve its history, increase public interest in the highway, and encourage restoration projects. The bill includes protections for landowners, energy production, and infrastructure projects.

title: Daines Previews Historic Trump-Xi-Putin Meeting on America Reports: “These Relationships Are Too Big To Fail”
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Steve Daines today joined John Roberts on America Reports to discuss President Trump’s historic visit to Asia ahead of his meetings with global leaders.

Watch the full exchange HERE.

Daines on Trump-Xi-Putin meeting:

First, it’s a great first stop for the president. This is over 60 percent of the world’s economy is going to be involved in these meetings he’ll be having over the course of the next couple of days. Pulled allies in closer, a great first step. But this next set of meetings he’s going to go to, this trilateral meeting, it’s going to be with Putin, with Xi, President Trump. It’s the first time that’s ever happened in American history. These relationships are too big to fail, particularly starting with China. It’s 42% of the world’s economy between the United States and China. This relationship is too big to fail from an economic viewpoint, but second from a national security viewpoint. These are two countries now that are nuclear superpowers. Bring in Russia to this with those three countries. 92% of the world’s nuclear weapons are controlled by those three leaders in that room.

Daines on Iran:

I’ll tell you what, what the President said there, I hope that wasn’t missed, this is why Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon. If they’re planning to put a dirty bomb here in our capital city, imagine what they do with ballistic missiles with nuclear warheads that we saw when they [aimed] that ballistic missile that got all the way to Diego Garcia. That proved the Iranians could hit any capital. Or at least it was aiming at Diego Garcia. It didn’t quite get there. But that means they could hit any European capital with a nuclear bomb if they had that capability. This is why the President’s spot on to make sure we deter Iran from ever having a nuclear weapon.

Daines on denuclearization:

We’re not hearing much about that from Xi and Putin. I think the expectation should be low in terms of outcome, but the beginning of that dialogue is very important. So the fact the President is talking about it, I think there’s other things we could do is make sure we strengthen our mill -to-mill crisis communication lines to make sure we’ve got somebody in the Chinese military, there’s direct contact with some of the U.S. military. If two subs bumped in the night in the Taiwan Strait, we want to de-escalate, de-conflict that as quickly as possible. There’s certainly a lot more Chinese vessels out there than there ever has been in the past.

Daines on FAA system:

Before we jump to throwing more federal money at a problem, let’s understand exactly what happened. Just as if there was an airline that crashed, what would we do? We have the NTSB investigate it, find out the cause of the crash, and make sure it never happens again. Similarly, let’s first understand exactly at a technical level what caused that ground stoppage in the United States, [first time] since 9-11. So you want to get certainty on what caused it, and then you want to see a line-item listing. It’s like do something, even if it’s wrong, just have a knee-jerk reaction. This is time for thoughtful understanding of what happened, understand the problem, the root cause, then put a solution in place.

title: Duckworth, Pressley Renew Push to Ensure Paid Leave Benefits for Families Experiencing Pregnancy Loss, Invest in Research to Improve Care
text:
As Trump attacks workplace protections for pregnant women, Bicameral bill would shine light on pregnancy loss, increase access to resources, workforce support and patient-centered care

[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – As the Trump Administration works to scale back workplace protections for women experiencing pregnancy- and reproductive health-related complications, U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and U.S. Representative Ayanna Pressley (D-MA-07) are reintroducing legislation to support those navigating pregnancy loss by establishing new paid leave benefits for workers across the nation who are experiencing painful, traumatic challenges while seeking to start or grow their family. The bicameral Support Through Loss Act would increase access to resources and patient-centered care while providing 7 days of paid leave for all American workers after they experience some of the many challenges that hopeful parents face on the road to parenthood, including a pregnancy loss, an intrauterine insemination or an assisted reproductive technology procedure that did not result in a live birth, a stillbirth, a failed adoption arrangement or surrogacy arrangement, a diagnosis or event that impacts pregnancy or fertility.

“We should be doing everything we can to support hopeful parents, not leaving them behind when they’re experiencing devastating setbacks and disappointments on the road to parenthood,” said Duckworth. “My family faced our own heartbreaks and challenges when growing our family, and I wouldn’t have my two girls today if it weren’t for the miracle of IVF. The Support Through Loss Act would provide so many hopeful parents with the time they need to grieve and heal when living through difficult losses. Let’s get it passed so we can better support the thousands of families struggling through these all-too-common experiences.”

“The journey of expanding a family can be a beautiful process, but it can also be a path marked by hardship and grief. Miscarriage, stillbirth, unsuccessful IVF cycles, and other forms of pregnancy loss can be devastating, especially when families are left without support,” said Pressley. “Nothing can take away the pain of a loss, but passing this bill would help provide impacted families with workforce support, essential health care, and resources as they navigate the healing process. I am grateful to Sen. Duckworth for her leadership and partnership and to every family and advocate that has trusted us with their stories.”

At least 10-20% of known pregnancies end in miscarriage, but too often this common occurrence of pregnancy loss among families is underreported. The Support Through Loss Act would also direct the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to develop and disseminate public information regarding pregnancy loss and invest in long-overdue research with the National Institutes of Health.

Specifically, the Support Through Loss Act would:

Ensure employers provide at least seven days of paid leave for workers to process and address health—including mental health—needs following a pregnancy loss an intrauterine insemination or an assisted reproductive technology procedure that did not result in a live birth, a stillbirth, a failed adoption arrangement, a failed surrogacy arrangement, a diagnosis or event that impacts pregnancy or fertility;

Direct the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to develop and disseminate educational resources for the public regarding pregnancy loss and the range of treatment options for pregnancy loss, including recurrent pregnancy loss; and

Provide $45 million in annual funding for the National Institutes of Health to expand, intensify and coordinate federal research and programs with respect to pregnancy loss to help develop a better understanding of the problem and potentially suggest best practices to reduce pregnancy loss.

A copy of the full bill text can be found using the link on Senator Duckworth's website.

Along with Duckworth, the Support Through Loss Act is cosponsored in the Senate by U.S. Senators Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Tina Smith (D-MN), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Adam Schiff (D-CA) and John Fetterman (D-PA).

Along with Pressley, the Support Through Loss Act is cosponsored in the House by U.S. Representatives Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ-03), Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), Judy Chu (D-CA-28), Yvette Clarke (D-NY-09), Glenn Ivey (D-MD-04), Timothy Kennedy (D-NY-26), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC-At Large), Chellie Pingree (D-ME-01), Ritchie Torres (D-NY-15), Bonnie Watson Coleman (D-NJ-12), Nikema Williams (D-GA-05) and Frederica Wilson (D-FL-24).

“Losing a pregnancy can be devastating, traumatic, and heartbreaking, but what it should never be is shameful,” said Laura Narefsky, Senior Counsel at the National Women's Law Center Action Fund. “The Support Through Loss Act is commonsense legislation that would provide the care, support, and space that grieving families need to heal and move forward. We are grateful to Senator Duckworth and Representative Pressley for working to expand support for families experiencing pregnancy loss, and we urge Congress to ensure that all people can access paid leave without barriers.”

“The incidence of pregnancy loss is all too frequent. Sadly, families often grieve in silence, and workers return to their jobs without time off to heal and process. The National Partnership for Women & Families is proud to endorse the Support Through Loss Act because no one should have to fear risking wages or job stability while navigating such a traumatic event. This bill also calls for desperately needed research and outreach and education programs so that we can eliminate stigma and support those going through pregnancy loss more effectively. We are grateful for the leadership of Senator Duckworth and Congresswoman Pressley in crafting legislation that is committed to providing meaningful support for American families,” said Jocelyn Frye, President of National Partnership for Women & Families.

This legislation is supported by American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists; Bobbie; Building Military Families Network; Catholics for Choice; Center for Reproductive Rights; In Our Own Voice: National Black Women’s Reproductive Justice Agenda; MANA: A National Latina Organization; March of Dimes; MomsRising; National Partnership for Women & Families; National Women’s Law Center; Physicians for Reproductive Health; Planned Parenthood Federation of America; Poppy Seed Health; Recurrent Pregnancy Loss Association; Reproductive Freedom for All; RESOLVE: The National Infertility Association; What to Expect Project; the American Society for Reproductive Medicine; U.S. Women’s Health Alliance; Unified Women’s Healthcare; Women Employed; and Workplace Fairness.

title: Duckworth, Families of Flight 5342 Renew Call for Congress to Pass Strongest Aviation Safety Bill Possible to Keep the Flying Public Safe
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) joined the Families of Flight 5342, U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy, Federal Aviation Administration Administrator (FAA) Bryan Bedford, her fellow Congressional colleagues and aviation safety advocates to renew their call for Congress to finalize and pass the strongest aviation safety legislation possible in order to keep the flying public safe. At a press conference marking nearly two years since the horrific DCA midair collision on January 29, 2025, that stole 67 lives, Duckworth underscored the importance of ensuring an aviation safety package that passes both chambers, setting the highest possible standards for aviation safety mandates. She also recommitted to using every tool at her disposal to make our skies safe for the traveling public, including using her role on the Aviation Subcommittee and the Armed Services Committee to push for aviation safety and continue asking the hard questions. For years, Duckworth has been sounding the alarm that we must make critical aviation safety investments to prevent all-too-often near-misses from becoming catastrophic tragedies. Duckworth’s full remarks can be found on the Senator's YouTube.

Key Quotes:

Duckworth on the need for an aviation safety law: “Let me make it clear. The NTSB told us exactly what went wrong. They gave us fifty recommendations — thirty-three to the FAA, eight to the Army. The NTSB sent those recommendations to those agencies because those agencies have the power to carry them out. They didn’t need laws to carry them out, they could have carried them out. Nothing stops them from meeting every one of those NTSB recommendations — and going further to keep the American flying public safe. But they have not. Even after two years of too many near-misses and even additional collisions, the FAA and the Army have not implemented the vast majority of the NTSB’s recommendations. So here we are. This is why we need a law. Not because these agencies lack authority — but because they have shown us, they will not use that authority unless it is in law.”

Duckworth calling on Congress to pass a law that sets highest possible standards: “We passed the ROTOR Act in the Senate unanimously eleven months ago. The House passed the ALERT Act back in April. We must ensure that this final aviation safety package sets the highest possible standards for aviation safety by mandating ADS-B In — a fix the NTSB has recommended more than a dozen times—and yet, still has not been implemented. Along with ensuring military aircraft operate with ADS-B Out turned ON, unless there is an actual national security reason and not because it was standard practice.”

Duckworth on using every tool at her disposal to make the skies safe for travelers: “I’m going to make sure that I use every tool I have to make our skies safe for the traveling public. I’ve pressed the FAA and the Army on every one of the NTSB’s recommendations every opportunity I’ve had. And I’m going to continue to use my role on both the Aviation Subcommittee and on the Armed Services Committee to push for aviation safety and to keep asking the hard questions. It is the very least that I could do. Because, you see, I know as a pilot myself what we ask of these pilots and controllers. They deserve a resilient system that is based on redundancy. And to the Families of Flight 5342, you deserve the strongest aviation safety law possible—nothing less.”

Duckworth’s remarks as delivered can be found below:

Thank you for letting me join you here today.

We should not have to be standing here almost two years later fighting for justice, accountability and safer skies. I thank the Families of Flight 5342 for the battle that you’ve waged. But you are here. And I am with you.

Let me make it clear. The NTSB told us exactly what went wrong. They gave us fifty recommendations — thirty-three to the FAA, eight to the Army.

The NTSB sent those recommendations to these agencies because these agencies have the power to carry them out. They didn’t need laws to carry them out, they could have carried them out.

Nothing stops them from meeting every one of those NTSB recommendations — and going further to keep the American flying public safe.

But they have not. Even after two years of too many near-misses and even additional collisions, the FAA and the Army have not implemented the vast majority of the NTSB’s recommendations.

So here we are. This is why we need a law. Not because these agencies lack authority — but because they have shown us, they will not use that authority unless it is in law.

We passed the ROTOR Act in the Senate unanimously eleven months ago. The House passed the ALERT Act back in April.

We must ensure that this final aviation safety package sets the highest possible standards for aviation safety by mandating ADS-B In — a fix the NTSB has recommended more than a dozen times— and yet, still has not been implemented. Along with ensuring military aircraft operate with ADS-B Out turned ON, unless there is an actual national security reason and not because it was standard practice.

I’m going make sure that I use every tool I have to make our skies safe for the traveling public.

I’ve pressed the FAA and the Army on every single one of the NTSB’s recommendations every opportunity I’ve had.

And I’m going to continue to use my role on both the Aviation Subcommittee and on the Armed Services Committee to push for aviation safety and to keep asking the hard questions.

It is the very least that I could do. Because, you see, I know as a pilot myself what we’re asking of pilots and controllers. They deserve a resilient system that is based on redundancy.

And to the Families of Flight 5342, you deserve the strongest aviation safety law possible—nothing less. Thank you for being here, the fight’s not over, we’re going to pass this law but we need to make sure that these recommendations are implemented. And I’m not going to stop until they are. Thank you.

title: Durbin Calls For Passage Of Stop CSAM Act & Better Protections For Kids Online During Opening Statement At Senate Judiciary Subcommittee Hearing On Dangers Of Roblox
text:
Today’s Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism hearing explored the dangers posed to children on Roblox, as well as the platform’s efforts to prevent victims of abuse from seeking justice in court

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, delivered an opening statement during today’s Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism hearing entitled “Roblox and Online Gaming: Digital Playgrounds Endangering America’s Children.” Today’s hearing explored the dangers posed to children on Roblox and the gaming platform’s efforts to prevent victims of online grooming or abuse while on the site from receiving justice.

Following their joint investigation into Roblox earlier this year, Durbin and U.S. Senator Josh Hawley (R-MO) this week introduced new bipartisan legislation to empower families of children harmed by tech products and by child sexual exploitation online. The No Forced Arbitration for Child Sexual Exploitation and Cyber Injuries Act would allow the families of minor children who are harmed to take their claims to court, even if a company’s terms of service require private arbitration. Notably, Roblox requires users to give up their constitutional right to a trial when creating a user account on their platform.

In his opening remarks, Durbin commended the bipartisan work done by the Senate Judiciary Committee to protect children online, and he called for final passage of his bipartisan STOP CSAM Act to hold Big Tech accountable for abuses occurring on their platforms.

Key Quotes:

“Two years ago, I was Chair of this Committee, honored to be, and we started working on legislation to protect children. We found out very quickly it was a bipartisan cause. I remember the day that I was going to bring my STOP CSAM bill to the floor and I didn’t have a Republican sponsor. Then there was a tap on my shoulder, and the Senator from Missouri was standing there and said, ‘I’d like to cosponsor the bill.’ It was Senator Hawley.”

“This has been a bipartisan effort from the start, and it should be. It has nothing to do with whether the families are Democrat, Republican, [or] independent. It’s about their kids, innocent kids who are being lured into this terrible situation.”

“What is the STOP CSAM Act? It’s pretty basic. Before I came to Congress, I was a trial lawyer. Want to get someone’s attention? Serve them with a complaint. Let them know they’re going to have to answer in court, under oath, as to what they’ve done… That’s what we’re facing here.”

“We will examine today at this hearing how predators have used the online gaming platform Roblox to exploit kids; how Roblox has responded to these tragedies; and what more needs to be done.”

“Roblox is a massively popular online gaming platform with 138 million daily active users. By its own estimates, 75 percent of kids ages 9 to 12 play Roblox games regularly, and the company markets itself to kids as young as five years old. Not surprisingly, child predators have recognized Roblox as a good hunting ground.”

“Roblox has long been aware of platform features—like its virtual Robux currency—that have been used by predators to facilitate sexual exploitation. There have been too many stories of predators using Roblox to trade child sexual abuse material, participate with kids in sexually explicit and violent games, bribe and extort kids, and connect with kids they later lured into in-person meetings.”

“Let me tell you a tragic story about a nine-year-old boy in Cook County, Illinois. He was groomed by an adult male predator posing as a child on the platform. The adult cultivated the child’s trust and then manipulated him into sharing explicit photographs.”

“In 2025, Roblox submitted 65,381 reports of suspected child exploitation to NCMEC, the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children. Each of these reports represents an individual, a family, forever impacted by this experience.”

“And when lawsuits have been filed against the company, the response has been to attempt to silence victims by arguing that these minor users agreed to arbitrate all disputes. A five-year-old making a legal agreement? Get real.”

“Let me put that differently. According to Roblox’s arguments, a kid as young as five could agree to give up their constitutional rights to a trial simply by going to Roblox, creating a username, and entering a birth date. That’s it. That’s wrong.”

“While Roblox recently has taken steps [to address the risks on their platform], they haven’t done enough. The fact that they aren’t here today says that they’re ashamed of what they’re doing, but they’re still raking in the money.”

“This Committee has a long history of working on a bipartisan basis. We want this to be bipartisan.”

“We have pending legislation [the STOP CSAM Act] in the National Defense Authorization Act, which is pending on the floor, which we can pass in the closing days before the end of December. Protecting children is an important part of it. Let’s make it real. Let’s make it the law of the land. Let’s tell parents across the country that we got the message, and we did something on a bipartisan basis.”

title: Durbin Continues To Call Out Judiciary Committee Republicans For Violating Committee Norms To Fast-Track Judicial Nominations
text:
Durbin: “Senate Republicans turned obstruction of judicial nominees into an art form under President Obama. So, forgive me if I shed no tears when Republicans complain about Democrats refusing to rubberstamp unqualified MAGA nominees once we take the majority in January.”

WASHINGTON – During his opening statement at today’s Senate Judiciary Committee executive business meeting, U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, slammed Committee Republicans for continuing to violate numerous longstanding Committee norms to fast-track unqualified MAGA nominees, all without the consent of the minority. These actions include holding nominations hearings less than two weeks apart on November 10 and 18; slating nominees for the November 18 hearing despite receiving Senate Judiciary Questionnaires (SJQ) less than 28 days in advance; slating nominees for hearings even if their FBI background investigations have not been cleared by staff in advance; and slating as many as eight nominees for a single hearing.

Key Quotes:

“Observers of the Senate Judiciary Committee know we typically meet on Thursday mornings at 10:00 a.m., as specified in our rules. Yet here we are, second week in a row, meeting on Tuesday at 9:00 a.m., prior to a previously-scheduled hearing on a different topic. What’s going on? Republicans are in a mad scramble to confirm as many judicial nominees as possible before the Democrats take majority control of the Senate in January.”

“My Republican colleagues argue this is business as usual. In fact, the majority is violating longstanding bipartisan Committee norms to jam through nominees in the Senate in this lame-duck session.”

“Republicans claim they aren’t acting any differently than Democrats did when we were in the majority. That simply is not true. The reality is these practices have been followed for years by Republicans and Democrats to ensure both sides have adequate time to review prospective lifetime nominees to the federal bench and to fulfill our advice and consent responsibility under the Constitution.”

“On the rare occasions that we’ve deviated from these rules it has only been with the consent of the minority. There is no consent with what we are doing now.”

“The Chairman is within his rights to schedule any nominee he would like for a hearing. But I want to warn my Republican colleagues: you will regret changing the 28-day rule to the 7-day rule… Remember this day when a future Democratic Chair moves judicial nominees through the Committee with one week for you to review their background and qualifications for a lifetime appointment.”

“Why are [Republicans] doing this? Simple: under the 28-day rule, nominees put forward after the election can’t be confirmed before the end of the Congress. So, Republicans decided change the rule, in fact break the rule, and the hell with the minority’s consent.”

“Senate Republicans turned obstruction of judicial nominees into an art form under President Obama. So, forgive me if I shed no tears when Republicans complain about Democrats refusing to rubberstamp unqualified MAGA nominees once we take the majority in January.”

Video of Durbin’s opening statement is available here.

Audio of Durbin’s opening statement is available here.

Durbin then spoke against the nominations of Jesus Osete, to be a U.S. District Court Judge for the Western District of Missouri, and Chris Inabinett, to be U.S. Marshal for the Middle District of Alabama.

Key Quotes:

“Mr. Osete graduated from law school in 2016… Even among the unqualified and inexperienced nominees put forward by the President, Mr. Osete stands out.”

“Over the course of his career, he has attacked voting rights, reproductive rights, LGBTQ rights. Since last year, he has served as a senior political appointee in the Civil Rights Division of the Justice Department, known as the crown jewel of the Justice Department. During Mr. Osete’s tenure, the Trump Administration has decimated this Division.”

“Mr. Osete has a history of moving in whichever way he thinks the political wind is blowing. In 2016, he rightly criticized the Supreme Court’s decision in Shelby County[ v. Holder] that struck a major blow to the Voting Rights Act. But over the past two years, he joined the Trump Administration’s efforts to attack voting rights and undermine confidence in elections.”

“Similarly, in 2020, he posted on social media several times in support of efforts to increase diversity in the legal profession. At one point he wrote, ‘We need more diversity in these institutions.’ But while working for the Trump Justice Department, he got religion. He has frequently attacked diversity initiatives and stated, ‘DEI will either die on its own or we will kill it.’”

“Considering his record, I have my doubts as to whether Mr. Osete is able to be a neutral arbiter on the federal court. He’s going to have a lifetime to prove me wrong [with] this Republican majority.”

Video of Durbin’s remarks about Jesus Osete is available here.

Audio of Durbin’s remarks about Jesus Osete is available here.

Footage of Durbin’s remarks about Jesus Osete is available here for TV Stations.

Key Quotes:

“I am deeply troubled by Mr. Inabinett’s law enforcement career. During his time as Director of Alabama’s State Bureau of Investigations, he repeatedly denied requests to release body-worn camera footage from police shootings.”

“In 2023, a police officer claimed he shot and killed a Black Alabaman named Steve Perkins because Mr. Perkins aimed a weapon at him. Almost immediately, Mr. Inabinett’s agency issued a press release in support of the officer’s statement.”

“Yet, when the Perkins family asked to view the officer’s body-worn camera footage, Mr. Inabinett denied the request, claiming that disclosing the recording would affect an ongoing investigation. Months later, the officer who killed Mr. Perkins was charged with murder and other officers on the scene were later fired.”

“In 2025, police officers shot an Alabama man in the back, killing him. When the man’s family requested a private, supervised viewing of the footage, Mr. Inabinett and his agency refused to let them see the video footage.”

“This Committee has held hearings on body-worn cameras, and there is bipartisan agreement that these cameras can enhance public trust in police. But how can body-worn cameras be effective when people like Mr. Inabinett block that footage from seeing the light of day?”

“Mr. Inabinett’s record is so troubling the National Urban League and the Urban League of Alabama issued a letter opposing his nomination… Listen to what they said: ‘Mr. Inabinett has a troubling record of excusing violence and suppressing information related to officer-involved shootings…that make him fundamentally unfit to handle the awesome responsibilities of this role.’”

title: Durbin, Hawley Introduce Bill Empowering Survivors Of Online Exploitation Ahead Of Major Hearing On Roblox
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, and U.S. Senator Josh Hawley (R-MO) introduced new bipartisan legislation to empower families of children harmed by tech products and by child sexual exploitation online. This bill allows the families of minor children who are harmed to take their claims to court, even if a company’s terms of service require private arbitration.

“In the digital age, predators can target our kids from anywhere—including online gaming platforms like Roblox. And sadly, the numbers show that they have. Therefore, an ‘agreement’ buried in the terms of service shouldn’t limit a child’s or family’s rights to bring their claim before a judge or jury. I’m proud to partner with Senator Hawley on this bipartisan issue, and I won’t stop until this bill—and other key measures to protect children online—are signed into law,” Durbin said.

“I am investigating allegations that Roblox, a popular online gaming platform for kids, has become a breeding ground for sexual predators,” said Hawley. “This week, as my Subcommittee holds the first-ever congressional hearing on Roblox’s practices, Senator Durbin and I will introduce new bipartisan legislation to give survivors justice. We must hold these platforms accountable and ensure no child is left vulnerable to exploitation online.”

In August, Durbin and Hawley launched a joint investigation into Roblox in the Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism. And today, Durbin and Hawley will convene the first-ever hearing into this massive gaming platform entitled: “Roblox and Online Gaming: Digital Playgrounds Endangering America’s Children.” The hearing will occur at 2:30 PM ET in Dirksen Senate Office Building Room G50. Watch the hearing LIVE here.

The No Forced Arbitration for Child Sexual Exploitation and Cyber Injuries Act would:

Open courthouse doors to families of children harmed by tech products or sexual exploitation, allowing them to file lawsuits even if a company’s terms of service require private arbitration.

Close loopholes to ensure that a click-through agreement can’t limit a child’s rights, and ensure that a judge, rather than an arbitrator, decides whether the law applies to a child’s claim.

Allow lawsuits to proceed either individually or collectively in class or collective actions.

Preserve choice for survivors and their families, allowing them to choose whether to bring their claim in public court or confidential arbitration.

Read the full bill text here.

Durbin has used his role on the Senate Judiciary Committee to prioritize child safety online through hearings, legislation, and oversight efforts.

On January 31, 2024, while Durbin was serving as Chair, the Committee held a hearing featuring testimony from the CEOs of social media companies Discord, Meta, Snap, TikTok, and X (formerly known as Twitter). This hearing highlighted the ongoing risk to children and the immediate need for Congress to act on the bipartisan bills reported by the Committee.

Last year, Durbin and Hawley joined forces to reintroduce the bipartisan STOP CSAM Act, which would combat online child sexual abuse material. The bill passed the Judiciary Committee unanimously and awaits action on the Senate floor.

In addition, Durbin’s bipartisan Disrupt Explicit Forged Images and Non-Consensual Edits Act of 2024 (DEFIANCE Act) passed the Senate unanimously in July 2024 and again in January 2026. The legislation would hold accountable those responsible for the proliferation of nonconsensual, sexually-explicit “deepfake” images and videos. The bill awaits consideration by the House.

Durbin also introduced the Sunset Section 230 Act with the late U.S. Senator Lindsey Graham (R-SC), which would repeal Section 230 two years after the date of enactment so that those harmed online can bring legal action against the companies that caused the harm. The bill awaits consideration by the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee.

title: Durbin Pushes For Medicare To Have More Authority To Negotiate Prescription Drug Costs During Senate Judiciary Committee Hearing
text:
Durbin also railed against congressional Republicans’ cuts to Medicaid, saying “How could this be good for the country, for more and more people to be uninsured?”

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, today questioned witnesses during the Senate Judiciary Committee hearing entitled “Prescribing Sunshine: How Competition & Transparency Lowers Prescription Drug Costs.” During the hearing, Durbin spoke about the benefits of providing the federal government with more authority to negotiate the cost of prescription drug prices as the provisions in the Inflation Reduction Act have allowed Medicare to negotiate directly with Big Pharma, yielding enormous savings for taxpayers while allowing Americans to receive their medications at a lower cost.

Durbin began his questioning by emphasizing that research done at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), a taxpayer-funded medical research center, lays the foundation for nearly all new prescription drugs that enter the market.

“Is it true or not true that 95 percent of the new drugs that are available in America started with federal research at the National Institutes of Health?” Durbin asked, to which the witnesses agreed. “The starting point is: the American people are already paying for the basic research that leads to the drugs which they need to stay healthy, true?”

The witnesses affirmed Durbin’s analysis.

Durbin then spoke in favor of the Inflation Reduction Act’s provision that allowed Medicare to negotiate the price of 10 of the most commonly used prescription drugs.

“Let’s talk about the call that many politicians are making for Medicare for All. Let’s take a look at Eliquis under Medicare… Eliquis fell into these Part D drugs, the 10 that were reduced in cost through Medicare [under the authority granted by the Inflation Reduction Act]. Eliquis was originally $521 for a 30-day supply. It’s now $231 for a 30-day supply. A pretty dramatic [decrease in] cost because the government said to the maker of Eliquis, ‘You’re entitled to a profit, but you’re charging too much. We won’t pay it under Medicare,’” Durbin said.

“Out of the 70 million people who are under Medicare, which some politicians brand as socialism, four million take Eliquis. What has happened to the cost to the federal government of this Part D mandate by the government to reduce the 30-day cost of Eliquis from $521 to $231? The federal taxpayers have saved $10 billion for this blood thinner. That’s pretty amazing,” Durbin continued.

“So the question in my mind is, why don’t we just go ahead and go all the way? Why don’t we put everyone under Medicare?” Durbin said.

Durbin posed a question to Mr. Alex Oshmyansky, CEO and co-founder of Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company, about how his company is able to pay less for prescription drugs than the federal government.

“Mr. Oshmyansky, I listened to you explain how Mr. Cuban has been able to give people discounts on drugs just by paying what the drug companies are charging, but the federal government is paying more. Why?” Durbin asked.

Mr. Oshmyansky replied that intermediaries mark up the cost of these medications. He explained that cutting out the middleman and allowing the federal government to negotiate directly with pharmaceutical companies will reduce the cost of these medications.

Durbin then asked the witnesses about their stance on Medicare for All.

“Anybody here opposed to Medicare for All?” Durbin asked the panel at large.

While Professor Neeraj Sood of the USC Schaeffer Institute for Public Policy and Government Service expressed some hesitation, Ms. Merith Basey, CEO of Patients for Affordable Drugs Now, spoke about the necessity of tackling the list price of prescription drugs to achieve Medicare for All.

Durbin then spoke out against pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), which have grown into powerful intermediaries that have contributed to the rise of prescription drug costs by steering patients toward their affiliated pharmacies and marking up the costs.

“If you read a PBM defense what they’re doing, it sounds perfectly reasonable. [They say,] ‘We’re bringing competition and rebates and cuts and discounts,’ and yet, when it’s all over, Americans pay four times as much as other people around the world for the same [brand-name] drugs. So the system with PBMs is hardly working to the benefit of the consumers,” Durbin said.

Turning to Dr. Karriem Watson, CEO of UI Health Mile Square Health Center in Chicago, Durbin asked about the anticipated impact of congressional Republicans’ so-called One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cuts nearly $1 trillion to Medicaid and threatens the ability for hospitals to provide care to uninsured patients.

“Dr. Watson, I’ve been to Mile Square [Health Center]. The people who come in there, some of them are covered by Medicaid, and now there’s talk about taking $1 trillion out of Medicaid. What is that going to do?” Durbin asked.

Mr. Watson explained that he anticipates a drastic impact on his patient population. According to Mr. Watsom, more than 60 percent of their adult patients are covered by Medicaid, and if those patients become uninsured under the Republicans’ Medicaid cuts, the cost of health care would go up as these uninsured patients would be more likely to seek treatment in emergency rooms only after their medical condition has worsened.

Durbin concluded by underscoring that eliminating health care coverage for millions of Americans leads to a sicker population and severe harms to hospitals’ ability to provide care to patients. Durbin invoked his personal experience as an uninsured father desperate to find treatment for his newborn daughter with a serious heart condition.

“How could this be good for the country, for more and more people to be uninsured? Have you ever been uninsured with a sick baby? Yes [Durbin raises his own hand]. You will never forget it as long as you live. And we’re going to do this to millions of people now?” Durbin concluded his questioning.

title: Durbin Raises Alarm About Abuses Occurring On Roblox, Discord During Senate Judiciary Subcommittee Hearing
text:
Durbin called for the passage of his bipartisan STOP CSAM Act to protect children from abuses perpetrated on platforms like Roblox and Discord

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, today questioned witnesses during the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism hearing entitled “Roblox and Online Gaming: Digital Playgrounds Endangering America’s Children.” During his questioning, Durbin underscored that social media and gaming platforms, including Roblox, must take accountability for the abuse they have allowed to occur on their platform and do more protect their users.

Durbin began by asking Myriam Gilles, Professor of Law at Northwestern Pritzker School of Law, about how Roblox approaches legal disputes brought against them by families of children abused on the platform.

“Is it my understanding that they’re arguing that the user, the child in this case, can consent to forced arbitration?” Durbin asked Professor Gilles.

Professor Gilles confirmed that Roblox does ask all users, regardless of age, to consent to forced arbitration.

“I’m trying to remember that contracts course I took a long time ago. If I do remember it properly, if a child showed up at an auto dealership and signed up to buy a car for $25,000, that would be a voidable contract, wouldn’t it? Why?” Durbin asked.

Professor Gilles explained that, under common law, children cannot consent to those types of purchases.

“Why is this an exception? That a child can consent under Roblox[’s terms of use] to activity which is potentially so dangerous?” Durbin followed up. “This is hard to imagine that any court, any judge, can see a nine- or ten-year-old and say they have the capacity to consent to conduct and activity that is potentially so dangerous.”

Professor Gilles explained that both Roblox and the platform Discord claim that under their user agreements, only an arbitrator can decide whether a child validly “opt-ed out” of a mandatory arbitration provision. In other words, a child’s family would have to go to arbitration and ask an arbitrator to decide whether they have a right to go to court in a process kept secret from the public. Professor Gilles pointed out that in two recent cases, courts have upheld the argument that young children have the ability and did consent to arbitration. She went on to note that the Supreme Court’s interpretation of the Federal Arbitration Act has resulted in arbitration provisions being treated differently than other contracts.

“They’re basically setting up a scenario where they always win it. As long as they can keep it secret, you don’t know what’s happening. As long as the courts give a nod of approval, this will continue,” Durbin said.

Durbin then asked Michael Schlep and Woody Doe, both online safety advocates and survivors of abuse themselves, about what dangers exist on Discord.

Mr. Schlep spoke about the cases of child exploitation on Discord, noting that there have been accounts flagged for child safety violations, yet those accounts are allowed to remain active on the platform.

“Mr. Doe, your story is nothing short of amazing,” Durbin said of Mr. Doe’s background as a Marine Corps veteran and an engineer. As a child, Mr. Doe experienced sexual abuse on Roblox, and his abuser later lured him to his home to continue the abuse. In 2025, Mr. Doe sued Roblox, alleging design defect, negligence, and misrepresentation claims, and he continues to speak out against predators who use Robux—the currency on Roblox—to manipulate children.

“What you’ve been through, your life’s journey with the Marine Corp and your own family, you had courage to come here today,” Durbin told Mr. Doe. “You really are saving lives by this testimony. I believe that some people watching this are going to change their attitude towards this dangerous situation.”

Durbin then asked Khari James, Senior Legal Counsel at the National Center on Sexual Exploitation (NCOSE), about the volume of complaints filed at the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC).

“Ms. James, you must see this in the organization you work for coming at you on a regular basis, thousands of complaints…What are we talking about in terms of volume of victims across the United States?” Durbin asked.

Ms. James noted that NCMEC received more than 65,000 reports related to Roblox in 2025, more than double the reports received from Roblox in 2024.

Durbin concluded his questioning by reflecting on the harms done to children on these platforms, and he called on his colleagues to hold Big Tech accountable by passing the STOP CSAM Act.

“First, this isn’t just a child signing a contract for a car. It’s signing a contract for a car with no brakes. That to me, ought to be taken into consideration as well when you consider the danger,” Durbin said.

“The second thing I observed is—what in the hell are we thinking as a nation? We let our kids and grandkids be lured into this kind of a horrible situation and dream up legal theories to justify it. What is wrong with us? The answer is nothing is wrong with us, and the richest people in the world who are exploiting these kids need to be held accountable. It’s up to us, put the party aside, to do the right thing for the people and families of this country,” Durbin said.

“Senator Hawley, he and I are as different as night and day on some issues, we really see this the same way. I hope we can get something done before the end of the year. There is no excuse for why another child is exploited while we twiddle our thumbs and think of some reason why we can’t get around to it. We have a bill before us on the floor, the STOP CSAM Act. It’s in the defense authorization bill, and it’s time to pass it,” Durbin concluded his remarks.
