title: Hirono Presses Cao on Illegal War in Iran, Readiness Concerns, Threats in Indo-Pacific
text:
~ Watch Senator Hirono’s Questions Here ~

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI), a senior member of the Senate Committee on Armed Services, questioned Secretary of the Navy nominee Hung Cao on how the ongoing illegal war in Iran is impacting overall Navy readiness. During his nomination hearing, Senator Hirono raised alarm over how critical munitions shortages, extended deployments, and deferred ship maintenance are exacerbating long-term readiness risks in the Indo-Pacific theater. During her question line, Senator Hirono pressed Acting Secretary Cao on whether he has honestly conveyed the negative impacts of the war on the Navy to U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and President Trump.

“We have gone through tens of billions of dollars burning through critical munitions, diverting ships from the Indo-Pacific, delaying critical maintenance, and forcing our Sailors and their families to endure extended deployments,” said Senator Hirono. “I am wondering whether you have the ability to tell the President that this war is draining our resources. Have you had that conversation with the President or with Secretary Hegseth that you have concerns about what this war is doing to our readiness?”

While Acting Secretary Cao confirmed that the war in Iran has stressed naval resources, he then claimed that the war was “setting China back on their heels,” which Senator Hirono quickly refuted.

“As we are turning our attention to the Middle East, China is quite active in the Indo-Pacific. I don’t think you can sit there and tell me we are setting China back on its heels. They have more planes, more ships, more of all the resources that we need more of,” said Senator Hirono.

During her line of questioning, Senator Hirono also highlighted how the lack of carrier strike groups positioned in the Indo-Pacific is especially concerning given the threats posed by China and North Korea. Acting Secretary Cao dismissed those warnings by stating that China “does not have our enlisted community.”

Senator Hirono concluded her questioning by reiterating that the war in Iran is draining critical military resources, jeopardizing servicemembers’ safety, and threatening global security. She pressed Acting Secretary Cao on whether he had conveyed the full scope of those strains to the President. In response, Cao claimed to have briefed the President and Secretary Hegseth on the state of the Navy, as well as “mitigation and fallback plans.”

“And yet there is no end in sight to this war,” Senator Hirono said.

title: Husted, Ossoff lead bipartisan bill to expand affordable housing access for military families
text:
“Our servicemembers and their families sacrifice enough without having to worry about finding an affordable place to live near where they’re stationed.”

WASHINGTON – Sens. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) and Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) today introduced the Military Families Affordable Homes Act, a bill that would expand when military housing allowances can be excluded from income calculations for affordable, tax-exempt rental housing eligibility.

“Our servicemembers and their families sacrifice so much for our nation, and this bill would help them afford homes near installations like Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, without spending a single new taxpayer dollar. I’m glad to work with Senator Ossoff on this commonsense, bipartisan solution for military families in Ohio and across the country,” said Husted.

“Military families make immense sacrifices in our national defense, and they continue to struggle affording housing. I am introducing this bipartisan bill with Sen. Husted to help military families afford housing,” said Ossoff.

Affordable housing developers may use tax-exempt exempt-facility bonds to finance certain residential rental projects. To qualify, those projects generally must reserve a share of their units for households at or below a set percentage of area median gross income. The Basic Allowance for Housing (BAH), tax-free housing compensation paid to eligible service members, may currently be excluded from household income when determining eligibility for these units, but only in counties associated with a qualifying military installation.

Under the bill, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base would meet the updated definition for eligible military installations. Wright-Patterson does not currently meet the requirements under existing law.

title: Senator Justice Delivers Floor Speech Memorializing Senator Jay Rockefeller
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Senator Jim Justice joined Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV) in introducing a resolution commemorating Senator Jay Rockefeller’s decades of public service and lasting contributions to the people of West Virginia:

“Today, I honor a man who gave more than 50 years of his life to the people of West Virginia — our former Governor and United States Senator, Jay Rockefeller. Jay came to our state as a young man in 1964, a VISTA volunteer in a small coalfield community. He could have gone back to everything his name offered him, instead, he chose West Virginia. His work will live on in the coalfields, our hospitals, our schools, our veterans, the jobs he helped bring to our communities, and the lives of generations of West Virginians,” said Senator Jim Justice.

title: Kelly, Kennedy Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Stop Insurance Companies from Reversing Coverage of Completed Medical Care
text:
Today, Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and John Kennedy (R-LA) introduced the bipartisan Protecting Approved Care Act to prevent Medicare Advantage insurance plans from reversing coverage decisions or reducing payments after patients have already received approved medical care.

Currently, Medicare Advantage plans often require approval for medical treatment before it takes place, known as prior authorization. Insurers are increasingly approving these prior authorizations, only to reverse that decision, deny coverage or demand repayment from doctors and hospitals after patients receive care. These practices create financial uncertainty for health care providers and increase administrative burden, while putting patient finances at risk and potentially limiting networks of care.

“Arizonans should be able to get the medical care they need without worrying about insurance companies changing the rules after the fact,” said Kelly. “If people are told that their insurance plan will cover a treatment, that should be the end of it. Reversing coverage hurts patients and creates unnecessary red tape for providers.”

“Insurance companies cannot have it both ways. They shouldn’t be able to approve a patient’s medical care and then refuse to pay for it after doctors have done the work. Patients and doctors deserve better, and our bill would put an end to this unfair practice,” said Kennedy.

Representatives Bob Onder (R-MO-03) and Greg Landsman (D-OH-01) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives.

“Even as health care costs rise, these insurance companies continue to take advantage of Americans by putting their business over patients. These predatory practices have to end. If coverage is approved, they need to keep their word,” said Landsman.

“The American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA) commends Senators Kennedy and Kelly for their bipartisan leadership on the Protecting Approved Care Act. Podiatric physicians deserve the reassurance that medically necessary care, once approved, will remain covered. This legislation would establish comprehensive guardrails that prevent retroactive denials, reduce administrative burden, and support long-term financial stability for podiatric practices,” said Patrick A. DeHeer, DPM, APMA President.

“Prior authorization, denials, and downcoding by Medicare Advantage organizations represent three of the top administrative burdens for medical groups. These excessive utilization tactics delay care, undermine appropriate physician payment, and force practices to divert resources from patient care into unnecessary administrative tasks. The Protecting Approved Care Act helps ensure medical groups are not denied payment for services approved by Medicare Advantage plans by preventing plans from later denying coverage, reopening a determination of coverage, or changing the code assigned to a claim. MGMA applauds Sens. John Kennedy (R-LA) and Mark Kelly (D-AZ) for introducing this legislation, which would give medical groups the certainty that an approval means payment and let focus on what matters most: caring for patients,” said Anders Gilberg, Senior Vice President, Government Affairs, Medical Group Management Association.

“The Healthcare Business Management Association (HBMA) thanks Senator Kennedy for his leadership on the Protecting Approved Care Act. HBMA members see firsthand how unexpected payment denials create unnecessary administrative work, delay reimbursement, and threaten patients’ access to care. This legislation would help hold Medicare Advantage plans accountable for honoring their prior authorization decisions, ensuring providers are reimbursed for the care they deliver,” said Landon Tooke, HBMA President and Holly Louie, HBMA Government Relations Chair.

“The American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology and its Advocacy Council strongly support the Protecting Approved Care Act. Burdensome insurance practices restrict access to essential treatments, including allergy immunotherapy, which benefits more than 2.6 million patients annually. By preventing Medicare Advantage plans from denying previously approved care, this legislation would help protect patients’ access to timely, potentially lifesaving treatments and help allergists deliver the treatments their patients need,” said Dr. David Stukus, American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology (ACAAI) President.

Background:

The Protecting Approved Care Act would:

Prevent coverage reversals by prohibiting Medicare Advantage plans from denying previously approved care based on medical necessity.

Protect doctors and hospitals by preventing insurers from reopening coverage or payment decisions without good cause or reliable evidence of fraud.

Stop unfair payment reductions by prohibiting insurers from changing billing codes to reduce payments without good cause or reliable evidence of fraud.

Extend protections to medical services that do not require prior authorization.

title: Kelly Unveils Framework to Protect Americans from Most Advanced AI Models
text:
“We should hold AI to the same standard we have held other dangerous technologies: the more dangerous it is, the tighter the controls.”

Today, Arizona Senator Mark Kelly unveiled A Safety and Security Framework for Frontier AI, a plan to protect Americans from risks posed by the most advanced AI models. The framework draws on decades of experience and isbased on how America already treats risks like nuclear materials and weapons systems. It would establish clear safety standards for powerful AI models, deploy independent examiners to assess national security risks and evaluate companies’ safeguards as models are developed, and require rigorous testing and accountability for AI used in military operations.

“I’ve spent my career around powerful technology: fighter jets, spacecraft, weapons systems. The rule has always been simple: the more dangerous it is, the more carefully you check it. AI should be no different. This framework makes sure the companies building the most powerful AI systems are held to the same standards we expect everywhere else when national security is on the line,” saidKelly.

Kelly’s framework comes as whistleblowers from top frontier AI companies warn of the risks of unchecked acceleration of AI technology and following the Hugging Face attack where a powerful OpenAI model broke out of its controlled environment, exploited security vulnerabilities, and hacked into a separate AI company without being instructed to do so. He warns of the risks of advanced AI models being misused for cyberattacks or the development of weapons, all of which could harm Americans.

The framework points to three problems: there is no common measuring stick for when a model becomes dangerous, companies oversee themselves with outside review only after the fact, and AI models used by the military lack standardized acquisition and deployment requirements.

In the framework, Kelly lays out why the governmenthas tostep in: “The same advanced AI models that could help cure deadly diseases can also help someone develop biological weapons or launch devastating cyberattacks. Yet today, companies are deciding for themselves which models are dangerous and how much protection is enough. Too often companies act in the best interest of their bottom line, not the safety of the American people […] We can’t wait until Americans are harmed to act.”

The framework answers with three pieces that build on each other: a rulebook, a referee, and accountability. Standards define the safeguards needed to address AI risks, independent examiners identify national security threats as models are developed, and new defense acquisition rules require rigorous safety testing and hold contractors accountable for hiding or neglecting known risks.

Kelly also pushes back on the idea that the federal governmentshouldn’tstep in to protect Americans: “Some will believe that the federal government can’t — or shouldn’t — take on this problem. They seem to have lost faith that we can do hard things. Looking at how we have handled other dangerous, rapid innovations in the past, one thing is clear: It’s not a question of if we have the power to do big, hard things and protect the American people — it’s if we have the courage.”

Kelly’s framework draws on his experience as a Navy pilot and astronaut, and his national security oversight on the Senate Armed Services and Select Intelligence Committees. It also builds on Kelly’s leadership in AI.

Last year, Kelly released AI for America, a roadmap outlining principles to make AI work for all Americans—not just large companies. In September, Kelly introduced the Make AI Work for Americans Act to require the companies benefitingmost from AI to pay into a federal fund that invests in American workers. Kelly has also introduced bills to improve research on how AI is changing the workforce, secure America’s AI systems from foreign adversaries, preserve human judgment and accountability as the military integrates AI with two bills included in this year’s Senate NDAA, study how AI affects older Americans, and protect seniors from deceptive AI chatbots.

title: WATCH: Kelly Presses Acting Navy Secretary on Suicide Attempts, Hunger among Sailors During Extended Deployments
text:
“We also have a responsibility to give our servicemembers the support and resources they need to carry out their mission.”

Today, during a Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) confirmation hearing, Arizona Senator and Navy combat veteran Mark Kelly (D-AZ) pressed Secretary of the Navy nominee Hung Cao on reports of sailors going without adequate food and mental health support during multiple extended combat deployments in the Middle East, including eight reported suicide attempts aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln.

Kelly, a formernaval aviator, laid out what he was hearing from families: “One parent told us that their kid lost more than 45 pounds in six months because of a lack of food, but also lacked basic hygiene supplies. Another reported significant weight loss among Marines, some visibly malnourished. Families report that servicemembers are not getting adequate nutrition and are relying on care packages.”

When Cao suggested sailors were simply being picky about food,comparing it to kids“opening up the refrigerator door and saying, ‘there’s nothing to eat in here,’”Kelly pushed back directly: “Mr. Secretary, somebody doesn’t lose 45 pounds just because they don’t like the options. I don’t think that’s a fair assessment.”

Kelly also pressed Cao on the eight suicide attempts aboard the Lincoln during its 321-day deployment, rejecting Cao’s framing of them as successful mitigations: “We shouldn’t have conditions where sailors are wanting to end their lives because of the deteriorating conditions aboard the ship.”

Kelly closed with a warning: “If this isn’t corrected, these issues are going to continue, and we’re going to continue to come back at you.”

This hearing follows Kelly’s push for accountability on conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln when he demanded answers from Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth after reports of suicide attempts, mental health crises, food and water shortages, broken plumbing, and other deteriorating conditions aboard the carrier during its record-setting deployment.

Sen. Kelly questions Secretary Cao during a SASC hearing.

Click here to download a video of Kelly’s remarks. See the transcript below:

Senator Kelly:

Thank you, Mr. Chairman. Secretary Cao. I want to discuss the well-being of our sailors that are deployed in support of operations in the Middle East. As a guy who spent a lot of time underway on an aircraft carrier, particularly during combat operations, I know the challenges. Not only the challenges for the sailors, but also the challenges for the Navy, I get it. But we also have a responsibility to give our servicemembers the support and resources they need to carry out their mission. And it’s clear to me that was not the case. Earlier this year, we saw reports about unacceptable conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln. That was during an extended 321-day deployment. But the reports included inadequate supplies, deteriorating mental health, and sailors attempting suicide. You subsequently confirmed that eight sailors across the Lincoln carrier strike group had attempted to take their own lives during the deployment. I’m also hearing concerns about conditions aboard the USS George Washington (Bush) and the Boxer Amphibious Ready Group, including reports of not enough food and inadequate basic necessities.

One parent told us that there’s their kid lost more than 45 pounds in six months because of a lack of food, but also lacked basic hygiene supplies. Another reported significant weight loss among Marines, some visibly malnourished. Families report that servicemembers are not getting adequate nutrition and are relying on care packages, so their families are having to ship them food to supplement the inadequate supply aboard the ship. These are servicemembers deployed in support of combat operations, and they’re not even being given the basic things to stay healthy and carry out their missions. This is completely unacceptable. What I find even more troubling is that when this was brought up to the Secretary of Defense, he dismissed it. Says ‘We do everything and they have everything they need.’ Not the case. What’s even more concerning is that we’re hearing these same problems after everything that happened aboard Lincoln. So, it continues. The Navy was already on notice about the toll that these deployments were taking on our sailors. We shouldn’t be waiting for another crisis before addressing these very basic needs that our sailors and Marines have.

So let me ask you this. What is the Navy doing to ensure that sailors deployed in the region have adequate food, adequate mental care, mental health resources, and other essential supplies, particularly for the extended deployments as the up-tempo increases? And please be specific.

Secretary Hung Cao:

Senator, I share your concern with about the well-being of our sailors and Marines deployed. Every day I walked down to our watch floor when I get a brief on current conditions on board their ships, and I look at the number of days of rations they still have left. Right now, the one that worries me most of us is Gonzalez, a destroyer, they have about a week left. Usually, I don’t like them to go below two weeks of supplies —

Kelly:

Do you know if those supplies that they have are actually adequate to their needs?

Cao:

Yes, they are adequate. It might not be all the—

Kelly:

How often does one of those ships get to zero? You say there’s a week. Does it ever get down to zero?

Cao:

It has never gone to zero. Senator.

Kelly:

Not once?

Cao:

No, Senator.

Kelly:

So are you saying then, that these reports of somebody losing 45 pounds are not true?

Cao:

Well, Senator, it’s just not what they want. It’s like my kids opening up the refrigerator door and saying there’s nothing to eat in here.

Kelly:

No, I don’t think that—Mr. Secretary, somebody doesn’t lose 45 pounds just because they don’t like the options. I don’t think that’s a fair assessment. Have you done, speaking of assessments, have you done a fleet wide assessment of the living conditions, supply shortfalls, mental health resources?

Cao:

We have Senator. Again, this is why we have five—well, every small boy, all these all the destroyers will have a one chaplain aboard. All the carriers have five chaplains as well as mental resiliency counselors, as well as the mental health specialists as well. So that’s why you see eight suicide attempts I see is eight suicide mitigations that we’re able to keep these young men and women.

Kelly:

Okay. Well, it’s actually both there were eight individuals that tried to take their own lives and it was mitigated. I’ll give you that.

Cao:

Yes, Senator.

Kelly:

But we shouldn’t have conditions where sailors are wanting to end their lives because of the deteriorating conditions aboard the ship. Hey, these are demanding deployments. I get it. There should be adequate food on board. There isn’t. If this isn’t corrected, these issues are going to continue, and we’re going to continue to come back at you. So, I suggest you do everything you possibly can to make sure they have adequate food, adequate mental health counseling aboard the ship, adequate hygiene supplies, because otherwise this is going to continue to be a problem.

Cao:

Senator, if I’m confirmed, I will work with you to make sure that we take care of our sailors and Marines.

Kelly:

Thank you.

Cao:

Yes, sir.

title: Kennedy explains how permitting reform will help bring down the cost of living: “This bill is a start”
text:
Watch Kennedy’s comments here.

WASHINGTON – Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.) explained how the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, a permitting reform bill, will help bring down energy costs for Americans in a speech on the U.S. Senate floor.

Key excerpts of the speech are below:

“The federal rules and regulations with which Americans have to comply cost $3 trillion a year. Not millions, not billions, $3 trillion a year. That’s the cost of all of the federal government rules and regulations.

“Now, the businesses that have to comply with those rules and regulations pay those costs. . . . In most instances, businesses pass those costs on to the American people, to the consumers. That’s not the only reason we’re having inflation. But that’s a big part of it.

“I’m not saying get rid of every federal rule and regulation. I’m just saying be reasonable and understand there’s no free lunch, and you don’t get one now. Anything free, somebody had to work for. It’s not free. So, what we’re trying to do with this bill—and it has bipartisan support, Democrats and Republicans—is to make it faster and cheaper and easier to build infrastructure projects, particularly energy projects.”

. . .

“If we do this right and if we pass this bill, then it will result in lower electricity prices for Americans. Because in the last six years, the average electricity bill in America has gone up between 30% and 40%. Mine has. Yours has. And we need to start talking about how to make it cheaper. This bill is a start.”

title: U.S. Senate confirms Kennedy-backed nominee Anna St. John to the U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals
text:
WASHINGTON – Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.), a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, today voted to confirm Anna St. John, President Donald Trump’s nominee to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit. The full U.S. Senate confirmed her nomination by a vote of 52-46.

“Anna St. John knows the Constitution like the back of her hand. She has the smarts, experience and judgment to be a great, fair judge. I was proud to support her confirmation to the federal bench earlier this year and I’m pleased my colleagues have once again recognized her qualifications. I know Anna will serve the people of Louisiana and our country well on the Fifth Circuit,” said Kennedy.

Sen. Bill Cassidy (R-La.) also voted to confirm St. John.

“We need people like Anna St. John who will stand up for Americans in court and put the Constitution first. Anna is eminently qualified for the job. I am glad to have supported her nomination and am pleased to have another judge on the Fifth Circuit from Louisiana,” said Cassidy.

The U.S. Senate previously confirmed St. John by a vote of 51-45 in March 2026 to serve as a U.S. district court judge for the Eastern District of Louisiana, with Kennedy’s strong support.

Before joining the federal bench, St. John worked as a litigation attorney and as President and General Counsel of the Hamilton Lincoln Law Institute. She argued cases before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Second, Seventh, Ninth and D.C. Circuits, two state appellate courts and multiple federal district courts.

St. John earned a Bachelor of Arts (BA) from Louisiana State University and her Master of Arts (MA) and Juris Doctor (JD) from Columbia University’s Graduate School of Arts and Sciences and Columbia Law School, respectively.

title: King: Navy Budget “Not Supportive” of Shipbuilding Priorities
text:
The full hearing exchange can be viewed or downloaded here

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Angus King (I-ME) pressed a Pentagon nominee on the administration’s current proposed budget for the Navy and how it is inconsistent with the administration’s stated priority of rebuilding the shipbuilding industrial base. In a hearing of the Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC), King questioned Navy Secretary nominee, and current Acting Secretary, Hung Cao on the discrepancies between the Navy’s presented budgets and stated priorities.

Early in the conversation between the two, Senator King cited an old New England saying that “what you’re doing speaks so loudly I can’t hear what you’re saying” before pressing Cao on the substance of the Navy’s plan.

Acting Secretary Cao began, “Sir, going back to Bath built, and you know Bath built is best built. We’ve talked about this, Chuck up there has done such amazing work, and that’s why we added another destroyer into the budget this year, Senator.”

“There was only one [destroyer] that was in the budget,” Senator King responded. “There was only one, one has been added by the committee, and I understand that has been accepted in the House and is in the recently put forth mark of the Appropriation committee. But you started with just one, and that’s not enough to keep the flow going at Bath and at Ingalls.”

Acting Secretary Cao replied, “Senator, I understand, again we have to get back to moving faster. Again, when Arleigh Burke was actually first built, it took two years between when we laid the keel and when we commissioned the ship. Right now, it is taking six to eight years to build it. And so, I’ve worked with the shipyards in order to diminish what the Navy has done. We accelerated by seven months by taking out a lot of the redundant inspections and everything else, and the shipyards are now owing me another year so we can get down to five years. Senator, I would put 100 destroyers up there if I could, if I knew they could build it. That’s why we were very –“

“Let the record show the secretary just said he wanted 100 new destroyers,” Senator King joked. “Well, you understand budgets are policy and the budget should reflect the policy, and the policy right now is not supportive of what I believe the priorities for shipbuilding should be.”

As a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC), Senator King has long championed funding for Bath Iron Works (BIW) and criticized the administration’s approach to foreign ship building, lack of prioritization for destroyers and the decision to abandon the DDX. Most recently, however, Senator King helped secure an Arleigh Burke-class destroyer Bath Iron Works (BIW) can compete to build in the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) which passed out of committee. He also advocated for maintaining America’s domestic shipbuilding industry and resisted any efforts to build vessels outside of the country – calling potential offshoring shipbuilding efforts the “worst decision since the Red Sox traded Babe Ruth”. In prior years, Senator King worked to include authorization for funding of destroyers, modernization projects, and employee improvements that benefited the scope of work and workplace experience at Bath Iron Works.

title: Klobuchar, Sheehy Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Address Federal Hemp Ban, Protect Consumers
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Tim Sheehy (R-MT) introduced the bipartisan Hemp Guardrails Act. This legislation would establish a comprehensive federal regulatory framework for hemp-derived consumer products.

“Minnesota is a national leader in hemp, and our state has shown that we can protect kids and support responsible hemp businesses. But a looming federal ban on hemp products is threatening farmers, brewers, small businesses, and consumers across Minnesota and the country,” said Klobuchar. “This new bill with Senator Sheehy would keep safe hemp products on store shelves, protect consumers from dangerous products, and ensure that farmers and small businesses can continue to operate, grow, and create jobs.”

“We’re taking a commonsense approach to this issue. Our bill will put every bad actor in the hemp space out of business and keep intoxicating products out of the hands of children. It will also stop Congress from turning the farmers, veterans, and cancer patients who rely on these products into criminals overnight,” said Sheehy.

The bipartisan Hemp Guardrails Act creates a responsible federal framework that protects children, strengthens consumer safety, and keeps safe hemp products on the market.

What the bill does:

Protects children: Prohibits the sale, possession, and consumption of consumable hemp products by individuals under 21, and directs FDA to establish strict child-resistant packaging, labeling, manufacturing, and testing requirements for hemp products.

Bans “gas station weed”: Prohibits raw floral hemp material, smokable hemp flower, and hemp pre-rolls intended for inhalation.

Prohibits copycat marketing: Prohibits misleading packaging, imitation branding, and advertising targeting children, while requiring appropriate health warnings.

Bans dangerous cannabinoids: Bans delta-8, delta-10, and THC-O products and restricts their production outside of the hemp plant.

Bans synthetics: Doubles down on the ban on synthetic cannabinoids that was included in the most recent government funding law.

Strengthens enforcement: Authorizes FDA to inspect facilities, seize adulterated or misbranded products, and enforce federal requirements for consumable hemp products entering interstate commerce.

Establishes federal oversight: Creates categories for hemp-derived cannabinoid products and dietary supplements under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

Protects American farmers: Requires hemp products to be cultivated, processed, finished, and packaged in the United States, and offers farmers more flexibility on testing when growing a hemp crop.

Preserves access to CBD: Protects access to qualifying hemp-derived CBD products.

Respects states' rights: Preserves states' authority to enact stricter hemp regulations.

title: ICYMI: Sen. Markey on Senate Floor on Energy Permitting Deal: Americans Deserve Better

text:

Washington (November 17) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), a member of the Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, Ranking Member Senator Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), and all Democratic members of the committee wrote to Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz (R-Texas) calling on him to remove Danielle Thumann Severs from the markup scheduled for November 18, 2026. Ms. Thumann Severs is a Republican nominated to serve as a Commissioner on the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), and Democrats are united that Ms. Thumann Severs should only advance if joined by the renomination of current Democratic Commissioner Anna Gomez and the nomination of another Democrat.

title: Senators Markey, Warren, Massachusetts Delegation Urge Trump Administration to Ensure Benefits for Salvadoran TPS Holders
text:
Letter Text (PDF)

Washington (November 17, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.) led Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and the entire Massachusetts delegation—Representatives Richard Neal (MA-01), Jim McGovern (MA-02), Lori Trahan (MA-03), Jake Auchincloss (MA-04), Katherine Clark (MA-05), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), and Bill Keating (MA-09)—in sending a letter to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) Director Joseph Edlow urging the Trump administration to ensure that essential benefits for Salvadoran Temporary Protected Status (TPS) holders remain available, and to restore any benefits wrongfully terminated.

Reports indicate that, after the Trump administration failed to publish a formal notice of the extension of TPS benefits, Salvadorans have been unable to access Social Security Administration (SSA) benefits, renew drivers’ licenses, and verify employment authorization, owing in part to the failure of USCIS’s Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) and E-Verify programs to recognize their status as TPS holders. In the letter, Senator Markey demands that the Administration uphold the lawful immigration status of Salvadoran TPS holders.

In the letter, the lawmakers wrote, “The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) formally announces TPS decisions in the Federal Register, the government’s official publication for agency actions. These notices explain who is covered, how long protections last, and how employers and agencies should recognize extended work permits. Yet the Trump administration let September 9, 2026, pass without publishing a new notice for El Salvador. U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) has nevertheless announced that Salvadoran TPS holders retain their protections, including work authorization, pending a further announcement. But a website assurance is no substitute for clear instructions and systems that recognize those protections.”

The lawmakers continued, “One Massachusetts resident received an October 2, 2026, Social Security Administration (SSA) notice stating: ‘We cannot pay you benefits because you are not lawfully present in the U.S.’ SSA said benefits were no longer payable beginning in September, demanded repayment of more than $1,200 within 30 days, and gave the recipient just 10 days to submit proof of lawful presence to prevent an interruption. That is not an abstract paperwork problem. It is a sudden loss of income, a bill for more than $1,200, and a scramble to prove eligibility.”

The lawmakers requested answers by Friday, November 27, 2026, to questions including:

What information are SAVE and E-Verify returning for Salvadoran TPS holders whose documents show expired dates?

When did DHS and USCIS first learn of these verification problems, and what caused them?

How many Salvadoran TPS holders have been affected since September 9, 2026?

What is DHS doing with SSA to determine why Salvadoran TPS holders have been found not lawfully present?

What written guidance have you provided to employers and benefit and licensing agencies to prevent further harm?

How will you prevent these failures from recurring?

Senator Markey has consistently worked to protect TPS holders from Trump administration attacks. In September, Senator Markey called for the passage of the SECURE Act to provide a permanent pathway to citizenship for TPS holders after the Trump administration temporarily kept in place TPS designation for El Salvador. Senator Markey is a co-sponsor of the legislation. In August, Senator Markey called on Senate leadership to schedule a vote to extend TPS protections for Haiti after the Supreme Court cleared the way for the Trump administration’s termination of Haiti’s TPS status. Senator Markey has been fighting to preserve protections for the more than 300,000 Haitian TPS holders in the United States and has championed the legislation to protect Haiti’s TPS status in the Senate alongside Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.).

title: SENATOR MCCORMICK CELEBRATES RETURN OF ARMY-NAVY GAME TO PHILADELPHIA
text:
PHILADELPHIA —U.S. Senator Dave McCormick (R-PA), a West Point graduate and Army veteran, today celebrated the announcement that Philadelphia will host the Army-Navy Game in 2028, 2030, 2032, and 2034, securing four future matchups of one of America’s most cherished sporting traditions in the Commonwealth.

“The Army-Navy Game belongs in Philadelphia,” said Senator McCormick. “As a West Point graduate and Army veteran, I know this historic rivalry represents so much more than football. Bringing America’s Game back to Pennsylvania has been a priority of mine since the day I was sworn into the Senate, and I’m proud to have played a role in making it happen.”

First played in 1890, the Army-Navy Game is one of the oldest and most celebrated rivalries in American sports. Philadelphia has hosted the matchup more than any other city, establishing a special connection between the annual contest and the birthplace of the United States Army and Navy in 1775.

Bringing the Army-Navy Game back to Philadelphia has been a top priority for Senator McCormick. He has been attending and storming the field at Army-Navy games in Philadelphia for the past 50 years. Senator McCormick has worked closely with Philadelphia Mayor Cherelle Parker, Comcast, and Army leadership to support efforts to bring the historic rivalry back to Pennsylvania. Senator McCormick also thanked the many state, local, and organizational leaders who helped make this effort possible, including Michael Kelly, Director of Naval Academy Athletics; Tom Theodorakis, Director of Army Athletics; Governor Josh Shapiro; Rick Siger, Secretary of the Pennsylvania Department of Community & Economic Development (DCED); Anne Ryan, Deputy Director of Tourism for the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania; Don Smolenski, President of the Philadelphia Eagles; Frank Gumienny, Chief Operating Officer of the Philadelphia Eagles; Gregg Caren, President of the Philadelphia Convention and Visitors Bureau (PHLCVB); Maria Grasso, Chief Sales Officer of PHLCVB; and John McNichol, President of the Pennsylvania Convention Center.

Philadelphia is already scheduled to host the 2027 Army-Navy Game at Lincoln Financial Field. With the addition of the 2028, 2030, 2032, and 2034 matchups, the city will continue its proud tradition as a home for America’s Game for years to come. The city will also have the chance to compete for hosting rights in the three remaining years of the seven-year agreement.

title: GILLIBRAND, MERKLEY INTRODUCE LEGISLATION TO ADDRESS REPUBLICAN CUTS AND HELP STUDENTS ACCESS ESSENTIAL GRADUATE DEGREES
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Jeff Merkley (D-OR) introduced the Professional Student Degree Act to ensure financial stability for students and strengthen essential workforce pipelines. The bill would reverse harmful Republican cuts to federal student loan programs by expanding the definition of a “professional degree” to include certain critical graduate programs currently excluded by the U.S. Department of Education (ED), such as those in nursing, education, and public health.

Currently, ED’s implementation of federal student loan provisions enacted by President Trump and congressional Republicans under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act creates an immediate “loan cliff” for certain graduate degrees. By narrowing the definition of a “professional degree” to just 11 eligible programs, the current framework severely limits financial access to graduate programs in essential fields already facing critical labor shortages.

Students in these newly designated “non-professional” programs face annual student loan caps that are almost $30,000 lower, and aggregate limits $100,000 lower, than students in designated professional tracks. This limits students’ ability to secure the federal loans needed to complete their education and threatens to worsen nationwide workforce shortages, particularly in healthcare.

The Professional Student Degree Act would correct this by adding several key graduate programs to the federal list of professional degrees eligible for higher borrowing limits.

“Students who want to pursue critical fields like social work, public health, nursing, and education should not have to break the bank to serve their communities,” said Senator Gillibrand. “This bill would expand the definition of what constitutes a professional degree, giving students in high-need fields access to the financial resources they need to complete their education and serve others. This bill would help our students, our universities, and our communities, and I’m determined to get it passed.”

“Nurses, teachers, and social workers are dedicated public servants, and Congress must do everything it can to help recruit the next generation of these heroes,” said Senator Merkley. “We’re already facing a shortage of these critical workers, and new limits on federal student loans for these professions and others threaten to further jeopardize the future of our workforce. Financial freedom and flexibility are essential to aspiring students, and I’m leading the charge with my colleagues to oppose these dangerous changes and stand up for affordable student loans so folks can continue to achieve their dreams and serve the public.”

The Professional Student Degree Act would impact the following degree programs:

Maintains Professional Status for: Pharmacy, Dentistry, Veterinary Medicine, Chiropractic, Law, Medicine, Optometry, Osteopathic Medicine, Podiatric Medicine, Theology, Clinical Psychology

Restores and Codifies Professional Status for: Social Work, Audiology, Physician Assistant, Occupational Therapy, Physical Therapy, Nursing, Public Health, Business Administration and Management, Accounting, Architecture, Education, and Special Education

Flexibility to Expand: The Secretary of Education may add any other programs that meet “professional degree” requirements.

Without a statutory or legislative fix, students entering these costly but essential degree programs will be priced out of the workforce, further destabilizing already high-need professions.

The bill has been endorsed by the American Academy of Audiology, American Academy of Physician Associate, American Association of State Colleges and Universities, American Council on Education, American Institute of Architects, American Institute of Architecture Students, American Physical Therapy Association, Association of Collegiate Schools of Architecture, Association of Public and Land-grant Universities, Columbia University, Commission on Independent Colleges & Universities, Dominican University New York, National Architectural Accrediting Board, National Council of Architectural Registration Boards, National Organization of Minority Architects, New York Medical College, Oncology Nursing Society (ONS), Physician Assistant Education Association, Yale University, Binghamton University, and the University at Buffalo.

The full text of the Professional Student Degree Act can be found here.

title: Murray Says Anti-Abortion Extremist Heidi Overton’s Nomination Will Go Nowhere
text:
***WATCH: Senator Murray’s full remarks***

ICYMI: Murray Presses FDA Nominee Heidi Overton on Her Anti-Abortion Extremism and FDA’s Failures to Keep Food Safe

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), a senior member and former Chair of the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee delivered the following remarks with reproductive rights leaders at a virtual press conference denouncing Dr. Heidi Overton’s nomination to be Commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) ahead of the HELP markup to advance her nomination.

“We have decades of proof that medication abortion is safe and effective. Millions upon millions of women have used this medication. But in our hearing, Dr. Overton would not say what the science has said for years now: that the abortion pill is safe and effective. At the same time, she also tried to avoid acknowledging her past claims that the abortion pill was ‘dangerous’—perhaps because she knows they are embarrassingly wrong,” said Senator Murray. “I am going to be doing everything I can to make sure Dr. Overton’s nomination goes nowhere.”

In September, at Dr. Heidi Overton’s nomination hearing, Senator Murray grilled Overton on the FDA approval of mifepristone and the safety of medication abortion, the mass foodborne illness outbreaks over the summer, and extreme claims that birth control is abortion. Overton refused to acknowledge that mifepristone is safe and tried to downplay her previous published comments, describing medication abortion as “dangerous to women.” Overton also refused to admit that birth control, specifically in the form of an IUD, is not an “abortifacient.”

Senator Murray’s remarks, as delivered, are below:

“FDA Commissioner is a serious role. They make life and death decisions. The public has to trust their judgement. People have to believe FDA is following the science—not politics, not conspiracies, and not whatever scheme Trump and RFK Jr. cook up. It takes a stiff spine, and someone who will stick to the facts—even when it’s not easy or popular.

“Heidi Overton could not be farther from that person. Especially when it comes to women’s reproductive rights.

“I asked her some of the most basic, barebones questions at our hearing. Is medication abortion safe? Is an IUD abortion? Honestly, those should be softballs!

“We have decades of proof that medication abortion is safe and effective. Millions upon millions of women have used this medication. But in our hearing, Dr. Overton would not say what the science has said for years now: that the abortion pill is safe and effective. At the same time, she also tried to avoid acknowledging her past claims that the abortion pill was ‘dangerous’—perhaps because she knows they are embarrassingly wrong.

“And really, that’s a failure on two counts. She can’t be honest about the science, and she can’t be upfront about her own record! How is someone like that supposed to stand up for science when RFK Jr. launches another attack on vaccines? How are they supposed to stand up to Trump and Stephen Miller when they demand new restrictions on medication abortion?

“I thought it couldn’t get worse to be honest, but then I asked about birth control. Everyone knows birth control does not cause abortion. That is science—and really just basic common sense.

“The only people who can’t admit that basic fact—are far right extremists who want to rip birth control away, or people who just cave to far right extremists. Now, I don’t know which of those two Dr. Overton is, but I do know, either way—she is someone who has no business anywhere near FDA leadership!

“Public health in this country is at a crisis point. Measles is surging, trust is plummeting. We have to start turning the ship around at FDA before it’s too late. But you can’t do that with a Captain who won’t even admit which way is up. Or in this case a doctor who can’t even admit birth control is not abortion.

“So you better believe, I am going to be raising a ruckus with my colleagues across the aisle—and making clear we cannot confirm this person. No way, no how.

“There are Republicans who talk a big game about public health, and even about reproductive rights. I’m putting them on notice. Talk is cheap. And if you put this person, who is dangerously unqualified, in charge of FDA—we will not let anyone forget it.

“Your leverage is your vote—not some promise about what they might do once they’re in office. I am going to be doing everything I can to make sure Dr. Overton’s nomination goes nowhere.”

title: Watchdog Concludes Trump & Vought Broke Law When Cherry Picking What Emergency Funds to Spend
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, issued the following statement responding to the Government Accountability Office’s (GAO) determination that the Trump administration broke the law when refusing to spend some, but not all, of the emergency funding provided in the fiscal year 2025 continuing resolution.

“Once again, GAO has made clear what’s been obvious from the start: Russ Vought brazenly broke the law when refusing to spend billions of dollars in emergency funding Congress provided on a bipartisan basis. The law does not allow the White House to cherry pick what emergency funds to spend. Congress, not Russ Vought and not Donald Trump, controls the power of the purse, and Democrats are going to ensure this tactic is never on the table for this administration again.”

In March 2025, at Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Director Russ Vought’s recommendation, President Trump refused to spend some emergency funding provided by Congress, while spending other funds—expressly violating the text of the law, which made clear all or none of the funds must be designated by the president as emergency funds and made available to spend. Vice Chair Murray immediately called out the illegal maneuver and sent a bipartisan letter to Director Vought calling on him to reverse it.

title: Reed: Measles Resurgence in U.S. Under Trump Admin is a Costly, Inexcusable Public Health Failure
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – After decades of progress, the United States has officially lost its hard-fought measles elimination status according to the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), which is the regional office of the World Health Organization. More accurately, according to U.S. Senator Jack Reed (D-RI): the Trump Administration has lost control of measles.

The designation was officially revoked today after a nearly two-year concerted effort by the Trump Administration to slash federal public health agencies and a rash of anti-vaccine propaganda spread by White House officials, including U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr – who Senator Reed believes to be a vocal anti-vaccine conspiracy theorist who advocates for unscientific policies at HHS that undermine vaccine access, including to the measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine (MMR).

Measles is a highly contagious airborne disease caused by a virus that destroys immune cells and can lead to severe complications like loss of hearing, blindness, cognitive decline, and death. The disease was deemed to be officially ‘eliminated’ in the U.S. – defined as the absence of endemic measles virus transmission for more than 12 months – back in 2000.

The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) reports over 5,400 cases and 10 deaths this year, which is double last year's count and the highest number since 1991.

Rhode Island has reported two confirmed cases of measles this year, both of which were unrelated and connected to international travel, according to the Rhode Island Department of Health.

Reed, a leading member of the Appropriations Committee who opposed the Trump Administration’s unscientific efforts to disrupt and dismantle the nation’s public health safeguards and infrastructure, called for a renewed push to stop transmission of the measles virus and spread awareness about safe and effective vaccines.

“This was entirely preventable and it’s a national disgrace by the Trump Administration that will take years to clean up. When the White House stokes unfounded fears about vaccines and slashes proven programs that strengthen public health and improve care, people needlessly get sick. Measles is a dangerous virus. And I believe we had it beat until the Trump Administration helped to erode herd immunity and make America contagious again,” said Reed. “Congress must play a leading role in restoring our nation’s leadership in public health because viruses don’t stop at borders. The longer we wait, the more people will get sick with preventable diseases around the globe. While this is a shameful moment in our nation’s history, it must also motivate all of us to do better, follow the science, and follow the advice of doctors and health care professionals.”

The successful U.S.-led fight to effectively eradicate measles at home and abroad spared countless children from suffering, long-term health damage, and death. However, vaccine skepticism in the U.S. and around the world is growing.

The Trump Administration has routinely tried to downplay the threat of measles.

According to the Rhode Island Department of Health, about 97 percent of students entering kindergarten in Rhode Island have received their measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shot. Due to the state’s high vaccination rate and herd immunity, a serious measles outbreak is less likely to spread widely in Rhode Island than in a place like Texas that has lower rates of childhood vaccination uptake.

Doctors say the most effective way to combat the measles is to get vaccinated: MMR is 97 percent effective in preventing illness. Health officials suggest individuals born between 1963 and 1967 should check with their physician to see if they need to be immunized again.

title: Rosen Convenes Meeting with U.S. Navy Leadership, Churchill County, Fallon Ranchers, to Discuss Fallon Range Modernization Disputes
text:
FALLON, NV – U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV), a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, recently convened a meeting between Brendan Rogers, Assistant Secretary of the U.S. Navy for Energy, Installations, and Environment, Churchill County commissioners, and Fallon ranchers to discuss problems with implementation of the Navy’s Fallon Range Training Complex modernization and expansion. The Fiscal Year 2023 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) outlined a process for the Navy to follow as they expand the ranges, which included guidelines regarding access to local roads and compensation for holders of grazing allotments for the permanent, lifetime loss of their impacted permit. As modernization has progressed, it has become evident that greater specificity is needed to mitigate the impact on Churchill County and to fairly compensate ranchers for their lifetime loss, as was the Congressional intent when the law was passed.

“It’s extremely important for our national security that the Navy can modernize the Fallon Range Training Complex. From the beginning, my goal has been to ensure that our pilots, SEALs, and Marines are able to receive realistic training while the needs of the local community are met and fair outcomes are achieved for all parties involved,” said Senator Rosen. “I am glad I was able to bring Navy leadership from Washington, DC, Churchill County, and fifth-generation Nevada ranchers, Justin and Adrienne Snow, together so that Navy leadership could hear directly from impacted stakeholders. We had a productive meeting, and while there is still work ahead of us to justly compensate ranchers for their losses and mitigate the impact on the County, I appreciate the Navy’s willingness to engage with the local community. I will continue working to facilitate a solution that’s fair to Nevada’s ranchers and Churchill County.”

Senator Rosen helped secure the compromise proposal for Fallon modernization in the FY23 NDAA, which protected over half a million acres of public land, mitigated environmental concerns, and laid the groundwork for ranchers to receive fair compensation for the loss of grazing operations. As challenges have arisen, Senator Rosen has routinely pressed Navy leadership in hearings and private meetings, including earlier this year during a hearing with Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao, where she pushed for fair compensation for Fallon ranchers.

title: Rosen, Cortez Masto, Senate Democratic Colleagues Push CFTC to Reverse Ban on Geofencing by Prediction Markets
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) joined Senator Adam Schiff (D-CA) in calling out Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chair Michael Selig for the agency’s order to prohibit prediction markets from geofencing, allowing prediction markets to operate in all 50 states and on Tribal lands. Before this action from the CFTC, Nevada’s Attorney General had secured a court order blocking Kalshi and other prediction markets from operating in the state, as these entities failed to follow state gaming laws.

This CFTC decision undermines Nevada’s state gaming laws, which were upheld by the 9th U.S. Circuit of Appeals in August, and similar state and Tribal restrictions in Michigan, California, and Washington. All Senators from each of these states joined the letter.

“Numerous courts have held that sports-related event contracts are not swaps and instead are indistinguishable from sports bets subject to state and tribal gaming laws…. The courts have ordered platforms to cease offering various prediction contracts in Michigan, Nevada, and Washington, and on the land of two California tribes, and imposed geofencing requirements. The Commission now appears to be encouraging prediction markets to offer prohibited contracts in contempt of these court orders during active litigation,” wrote the Senators.

“We are particularly troubled that this action came just hours after the Northern District of California issued its latest court order in Blue Lake Rancheria v. Kalshi requiring Kalshi to geofence around the plaintiff’s tribal lands. This interpretation raises concerns that the Commission may be coordinating with platforms currently engaged in litigation and encouraging them to violate state and tribal gaming laws… The Commission must withdraw the interpretation or freeze all efforts to implement until litigation is resolved,” they continued.

You can find the full letter HERE.

Senator Rosen has expressed the need for more regulation surrounding online prediction markets at the federal level. Earlier this year, she joined Senator Cortez Masto in raising concerns about prediction markets allowing bets on wildfires. They have also urged CFTC Chair Michael Selig to abstain from intervening in pending litigation involving prediction markets. Senator Rosen also joined Senate colleagues in a letter urging the appropriators to protect states’ and Tribal nations’ rights to regulate prediction markets.

title: NEWS: Schiff, Padilla, Wyden, Senate Colleagues Demand Answers on Oz Actions to Dismantle Medicaid Fraud Prevention
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senators Adam Schiff, Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.), Ron Wyden, Jeff Merkley (both D-Ore.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), and Ed Markey (D-Mass.) launched an inquiry into the Trump Administration’s politically motivated campaign against state Medicaid programs, after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) withheld billions of dollars from Democratic-led states while dismantling the federal infrastructure designed to detect and prevent fraud.

In their letter to CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz, the Senators explained that CMS attacks on state Medicaid programs have undermined fraud-prevention infrastructure within the federal government and targeted Democratic-led states.

“The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services is running the most aggressive public enforcement campaign against state Medicaid programs in the agency’s history, while accelerating the systematic dismantling of the federal infrastructure Congress funded to prevent Medicaid fraud in the first place,” the lawmakers wrote. “That is not program integrity. That is political theater layered over a decade of neglect, with states across the country, and in particular, an overwhelming number of Democratic-led states that have become the Trump administration’s targets, left to answer for both.”

The letter comes as the Trump Administration has threatened state health programs with severe funding cuts based on flawed data. CMS recently moved to withhold billions in funding from California and Minnesota without providing any evidence of wrongdoing to the states. At the same time, the Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS OIG) decertified state Medicaid Fraud Control Units (MFCUs) in Hawaii and New York. Public reporting, including an investigation by the Associated Press, revealed that the Administration’s fraud claims against New York relied on a basic math error, while other withholding actions have sparked lawsuits from states like Minnesota.

Rather than working with states to fix issues, CMS has replaced on-site reviews and dedicated oversight staff with a public relations “War Room” and artificial intelligence pilots. The letter points out that the Administration is violating federal law by failing to maintain the minimum required funding and staffing levels for the Medicaid Integrity Program, which was created by Congress to help states fight fraud.

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

Administrator Oz:

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) is running the most aggressive public enforcement campaign against state Medicaid programs in the agency’s history, while accelerating the systematic dismantling of the federal infrastructure Congress funded to prevent Medicaid fraud in the first place. That is not program integrity. That is political theater layered over a decade of neglect, with states across the country, and in particular, an overwhelming number of Democratic-led states that have become the Trump administration’s targets, left to answer for both.

Since you were confirmed as Administrator, you sent all 50 governors letters demanding provider revalidation on a ten-business-day clock. You moved to withhold more than $2 billion annually in federal Medicaid funds from Minnesota without providing the State any details on its alleged noncompliance, and then issued successive deferral actions in February, April, and July 2026 totaling more than $500 million in additional federal Medicaid funds. In successive deferral actions in May, July, and October 2026, you also withheld more than $3.4 billion in federal Medicaid funds tied to California’s In-Home Supportive Services program and personal care services, citing nothing more than California’s growth rate relative to other states, with no specific evidence of wrongdoing.

The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services Office of Inspector General (HHS OIG) has decertified Hawaii and New York’s Medicaid Fraud Control Units and placed all 53 Medicaid Fraud Control Units (MFCUs) under review. Though most MFCUs are housed within state Attorneys General offices, all serve as the primary mechanism for prosecuting Medicaid provider fraud; consequently, decertifying them in the name of fighting fraud is self-defeating. Moreover, while statutory oversight of MFCUs rests with HHS OIG, the CMS Center for Program Integrity (CPI), whose statutory role is to serve as the federal bridge to state MFCUs so that state Medicaid program integrity units work in partnership with and refer cases to their respective MFCUs, has provided no visible support to states navigating this review. During New York’s decertification, it appears that CPI provided no technical assistance or support to the program integrity unit, leaving state investigators without a functioning federal pathway. Instead, you have launched a Medicaid Fraud “War Room” that your Deputy Administrator publicly calls “what modern program integrity looks like.” Modern program integrity should start with meeting the mandates Congress already wrote into law.

Medicaid program integrity has been under-resourced across administrations. That is precisely why Congress established the Medicaid Integrity Program (MIP) in the Deficit Reduction Act of 2005 and imposed a statutory floor of no less than $75 million and no fewer than 100 full-time employees (FTEs) dedicated annually to working collaboratively with states to fight Medicaid provider fraud and abuse. At the same time, Congress enacted mandatory federal technical assistance, on-site state reviews, and analytical support to states. Those obligations are not discretionary, and CMS cannot treat dedicated funding as optional funding or repurpose it at will.

The Trump administration and CMS under your leadership are not meeting these binding statutory obligations. Instead, you are hollowing out MIP under the guise of enforcement and compounding institutional failures:

The Division of Fraud Research and Detection, the only CMS division dedicated exclusively to Medicaid analytics, which maintained direct data feeds from approximately sixteen states’ Medicaid Management Information Systems (MMIS), was eliminated in the 2015 CPI reorganization. The defining failure of the current era is that these vital tools were never rebuilt, allowing what was once a temporary reorganization to harden into a permanent blind spot.

Comprehensive on-site State Program Integrity Reviews have been replaced with remote “Focused Reviews” issuing non-binding “Observations.” CMS no longer tells states what to fix; it tells states what to consider. Until this administration, even as the MIP infrastructure weakened, CMS and states maintained a working collaborative relationship on program integrity – sharing data, issuing joint fraud alerts with HHS OIG, and working through disallowances backed by evidence. That collaborative posture has been replaced by performative enforcement.

The Medicaid Integrity Institute’s residential training at the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) Ernest F. Hollings National Advocacy Center (NAC), CMS’s flagship in-person training for state program integrity staff, has been eliminated in favor of an all-virtual calendar. State program integrity directors have asked, in every available forum, for the in-person peer-led instruction to return, and CMS has refused. Public reporting and CMS’s own training calendars indicate the Institute has been reduced to a handful of virtual webinars per year and a few regional in-person listening sessions with State Medicaid Agencies and MFCUs between July and November 2026.

Publicly reported accounts indicate the federal workforce dedicated exclusively to Medicaid program integrity has fallen dramatically below the 100-FTE floor Congress set.

CMS state liaisons, fraud alerts issued jointly with HHS OIG, State Medicaid Director letters on program integrity, and the Annual Summary Report of Program Integrity Reviews have all been eliminated or discontinued.

An enforcement campaign built on gutted infrastructure produces shoddy results. On April 10, 2026, news reports revealed that CMS acknowledged its fraud probe of New York Medicaid rested on a figure that was off by a factor of ten – a basic mathematical error in calculating annual unique beneficiaries that independent analysts traced to a fundamental misunderstanding of how Medicaid data is counted. The administration publicly shared whatever figures served its political purposes, and the resulting mistake was then used to threaten a state. California has faced a separate but equally troubling pattern: CMS has imposed federal payment deferrals that have now accumulated to more than $3.4 billion, with California’s Medicaid director publicly rejecting the validity of CMS’s claims and stating that CMS has provided no evidence supporting the deferrals. Minnesota has gone further and filed suit against CMS, HHS, you, and Secretary Kennedy over the attempted withholding of $243 million in Medicaid payments, alleging that CMS imposed the withholding, without informing the state, despite it asking repeatedly, how it was noncompliant or what corrective steps were required.

CMS is putting on theatrics about going after states to “crush fraud” without any legitimate data to back up their claims, all the while starving the federal office Congress created to help states prevent those failures. A fake war room is not a substitute for a Medicaid integrity program that meets its statutory obligations. Contracting Medicaid analytics out to General Dynamics Information Technology (GDIT), the current Trusted Third Party for the Healthcare Fraud Prevention Partnership (HFPP), a multi-payer public-private partnership, is also not incompliance with a statute that requires Medicaid-dedicated federal capacity.

On October 15, 2026, your Deputy Administrator announced at an industry conference that CMS is piloting artificial intelligence to flag suspicious Medicaid billing patterns “in near real-time before Medicaid payments are made,” with the stated goal of scaling the pilots into a “national, standardized, continuously improving platform.” CMS does not, however, operate the claims systems that generate the underlying data. In fee-for-service Medicaid, state agencies adjudicateclaims; in managed care, Medicaid Managed Care Organizations do. CMS receives Medicaid claims and encounter data on a lag, and the federal pre-payment analytical capacity that could plausibly support such a platform is precisely the capacity CMS dismantled. Congress is entitled to understand what data CMS actually has, how it is obtaining it, and under what legal authority, before any such platform is scaled nationally.

Therefore, to assess CPI’s current compliance with Section 1936 of the Social Security Act (the Act) and the fiscal accounting of the MIP appropriation, I request the following documents and information by November 27, 2026:

For each fiscal year from FY 2015 through the present, please provide the number of filled federal FTE coded exclusively to the MIP appropriation, reconciled to the 100-FTE statutory floor under Section 1936 of the Act. To the extent the workforce has fallen below the statutory floor in any fiscal year, please provide CMS’s legal justification for its noncompliance.

Please provide SF-133 quarterly budget execution reports for the MIP Treasury Account Symbol for FY 2020 through FY 2025, including unobligated balances brought forward each fiscal year.

Please identify any MIP-appropriated funds obligated since FY 2015 for Medicare activities, shared CMS overhead, non-Medicaid purposes, or Medicaid beneficiary eligibility verification (as distinct from the statutorily specified provider fraud and abuse purpose), together with CMS’s legal justification for those obligations under the Purpose Statute, the Anti-Deficiency Act, and the Miscellaneous Receipts Act, given that MIP is a mandatory appropriation with a specific statutory purpose.

Please provide the methodology for, and actual allocation of, Unified Program Integrity Contractor costs between the MIP appropriation and Medicare appropriations from FY 2020 through the present, with Medicaid-specific deliverables identified for each fiscal year.

Please provide, for each fiscal year from FY 2015 through the present, (a) MIP funds obligated to the Medicaid Integrity Institute residential training program housed at the DOJ NAC, including all deobligations and modifications of the CMS-DOJ interagency agreement, (b) actual institute expenditures by fiscal year, with a breakdown of in-person training expenditures, virtual training expenditures, and non-training expenditures (including per-class costs and number of classes offered) and (c) documentation of how funds no longer obligated for in-person training have been reallocated.

Please identify any current, planned, or forecasted contract action, modification, or statement of work moving Medicaid Integrity Institute functions, including training logistics, curriculum development, state travel administration, or data analytics, to a contractor, including but not limited to GDIT. For any such action, please provide (a) the proposed and executed contract value compared to historical institute operating costs under the DOJ interagency agreement; (b) the methodology for allocating contractor labor hours and overhead between MIP-funded Medicaid-exclusive activities and HFPP funded multi-payer activities; (c) CMS’s legal analysis under the Purpose Statute, the Anti-Deficiency Act, and the Miscellaneous Receipts Act of using MIP’s Medicaid restricted mandatory appropriation to fund any multi-payer or non-Medicaid-exclusive activity; and (d) the current status of the CY 2027 MII training calendar, including whether its publication is dependent on the execution of any HFPP-related contract action.

Please identify the appropriation account, funding source, staffing plan, contractor support, and Medicaid-specific deliverables of the Medicaid Fraud War Room. Please state whether any Fraud War Room resources, including, but not limited to, personnel, contract, or overhead, are drawn from the MIP appropriation, and provide the legal basis for any such allocation. Please also provide the underlying data documentation for the $203 million and 50-provider figures announced on July 28, 2026, and a breakdown of amounts actually recovered versus payments flagged, together with the underlying data documentation for the updated $342 million and 124 notices-of-intent-to-exclude figures referenced in your Deputy Administrator’s October 15, 2026 ADAPT conference presentation, and an explanation reconciling the two sets of public figures.

Please describe the artificial intelligence and machine learning pilots referenced by your Deputy Administrator at the ADAPT conference on October 15, 2026, including: (a) the data sources, data flows, and legal authorities under which CMS is obtaining Medicaid claims or encounter data on a pre-payment basis in fee-for-service and managed care Medicaid; (b) the states participating in each pilot and the terms of their participation, including the Indiana-Oracle pilot and the five additional state pilots referenced; (c) the contractor(s) supporting each pilot and the acquisition vehicle(s) under which they were engaged; (d) the appropriation account(s) funding each pilot, including whether any MIP appropriated funds are being used; (e) the privacy, data security, and HIPAA frameworks governing CMS’s collection and use of pre-payment Medicaid claims and encounter data; and (f) the relationship, if any, between the pilots’ data architecture and the direct state MMIS data feeds maintained by the Division of Fraud Research and Detection prior to its elimination.

Please explain how the President’s FY 2027 Budget submission treats the MIP appropriation, the Medicaid Integrity Institute, and the Section 1936 workforce, training, and technical assistance mandates, and state CMS’s position on statutory compliance in the current and coming fiscal years.

Please provide all internal analyses, contractor deliverables, and data sources supporting (a) the 5 million people with personal care services figure cited in your April 2026 letter to New York Governor Kathy Hochul, (b) the alleged noncompliance related to the withholding action against Minnesota including the analytical and evidentiary basis, (c) all federal payment deferrals imposed against Minnesota, including the analytical and evidentiary basis for each deferral, (d) all federal payment deferrals imposed against California, including the analytical and evidentiary basis for each deferral, and (e) CPI’s role, if any, in supporting the HHS OIG process leading to the decertification of Hawaii and New York’s respective MFCUs.

I also request a staff-level briefing within two weeks on CPI’s current compliance with Section 1936 of the Act and the operational and fiscal relationship among the MIP, the Medicaid Fraud War Room, and the Healthcare Fraud Prevention Partnership.

Medicaid serves more than 73 million Americans. Program integrity in a program of that scale demands sustained investment, deep expertise, and genuine partnership with states. Congress created and funded the infrastructure to do this work, and the administration and CMS are required by law to carry out those mandates. CMS is not free to redirect the funding, redefine the mission, or replace true program integrity with a flashy, politicized rebrand.
