title: Senator Schmitt Celebrates Senate Passage of His Bipartisan Gateway Partnership Act
text:
Bill Creates More Opportunities for Gateway Arch National Park to Benefit St. Louis Communities

U.S. SENATE — Today, U.S. Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) celebrated Senate passage of his bipartisan Gateway Partnership Act following the Senator’s unanimous consent request on the Senate floor. Senator Schmitt’s bill would authorize the Gateway Arch National Park to enter into an agreement with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation allowing the Foundation to manage, market, and execute private events on the Park’s property. Current projections show that private events at the Park could generate up to $780,000 in additional annual revenue, creating a direct stream of investment in the Park’s maintenance, staffing, and visitor services.

Watch the senator’s full speech HERE.

“As a St. Louis native, I am proud to see the Senate pass my Gateway Partnership Act and take another step toward unlocking the full potential of this beloved landmark. Gateway Arch National Park is unique as the smallest National Park in the U.S., and as such, its management should be unique too. The Gateway Partnership Act does exactly that—giving the Gateway Arch Park Foundation the ability to formally manage, market, and execute private events at the park,” said Senator Schmitt. “This legislation was drafted with one goal in mind: creating more opportunities to bring people together and drive economic growth in the St. Louis region. The Gateway Arch belongs to the people of St. Louis and to all Americans, and I’m glad to see this bipartisan effort move one step closer to becoming law.”

In 2024, Senator Schmitt originally introduced the Gateway Partnership Act to the 118th Congress alongside a companion bill introduced in the House of Representatives by Rep. Ann Wagner (R-MO); in 2025, Senator Schmitt re-introduced the Gateway Partnership Act in the 119th Congress alongside a companion bill introduced in the House of Representatives by Rep. Wesley Bell (D-MO) and Rep. Ann Wagner (R-MO).

Senator Schmitt previously announced the bill’s passage through the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. Read that announcement HERE.

Background:

The Gateway Arch National Park is Missouri’s most visited landmark, drawing more than two million visitors annually and acting as an economic engine for the City of St. Louis.

This legislation will authorize the National Park Service (NPS) to enter into a 5-year contract with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation to enter into a formal agreement allowing the Foundation to formally manage, market, and execute private events at Gateway Arch National Park grounds (including the Arch Visitor Center, Old Courthouse, and any other building administered by the NPS).

Since 2009, Gateway Arch Park Foundation has been a staple in transforming visitor services at Gateway Arch National Park. Particularly, through the Foundation’s leadership of the CityArchRiver Project—the largest private investment in a National Park project in U.S. history—which was shown to generate more than $570 million in economic impact throughout the St. Louis region in 2024.

As the only National Park located inside a major city, Gateway Arch National Park is uniquely positioned as a prime location for private events in St. Louis. Projections show a potential annual revenue of $780,000 generated from private events under this proposed partnership, all of which will be reinvested into the park.

title: Senator Schmitt Takes to Senate Floor to Urge Congress to Modernize America’s Aviation Infrastructure
text:
Schmitt Calls for Passage of His Modern Skies Act to Invest $30 Billion in Air Traffic Control Technology, Airport Infrastructure, and Aging Control Towers

U.S. SENATE — Today, U.S. Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) took to the Senate floor to urge Congress to pass his “Modern Skies Act,” legislation that would invest $30 billion to modernize America’s air traffic control system and airport infrastructure. Following last week’s nationwide ground stop, Schmitt emphasized the urgent need to replace aging technology, strengthen the nation’s aviation communications network, and ensure America’s air traffic control system can meet the demands of future air travel.

Watch the senator’s full speech HERE.

Excerpts from Schmitt’s remarks as prepared for delivery:

“On Friday, our nationwide ground stop was a stark reminder that we cannot remain the world’s aviation leader while relying on technology from a bygone era. For hours and hours, air travel came to a total standstill…

“Americans were afraid…

“Americans were stranded…

“Separated from their families…

“And left wondering when or if they would make it home.”

…

“Our air traffic control system depends on aging infrastructure, antiquated equipment, and communications technology designed for decades past.

“Keeping aging systems running gets harder and more expensive the longer we put off replacing them.

“When those systems fail, the consequences can reach far beyond one airport: ground stops, missed connections, and families stranded far from home.

“We Americans rely on these systems every time we fly.

“Millions of us do, each and every day.

“Yet those systems are dated, lagging behind, and deteriorating right before our eyes. We cannot accept their continued deterioration.

…

“That’s why I introduced the Modern Skies Act.

“My legislation will modernize the digital backbone of air traffic control, address infrastructure needs, and replace deteriorating control towers. All while investing seriously in the future of American aviation.”

“The Modern Skies Act would invest $30 billion to finish that work, building on the $12.5 billion down payment already made through the Working Families Tax Cut.”

…

“This shouldn’t be partisan. This is an American problem. It’s time to invest in the safety of American families and the reliability of our transportation systems. It’s time to restore what we’ve lost over the past several decades:”

“The ambition to build great things again.”

“Our ancestors built the modern age of aviation.”

“Now, it’s our turn to build the next one.”

title: ICYMI: Following Clear Affordability Message from Voters, the INSULIN Act is Again Offered as an Immediate Solution
text:
(Washington, DC) – In case you missed it: Several of the nation’s largest health care advocacy organizations recently sent letters to President Donald Trump, Speaker of the House Mike Johnson (LA-04), House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (NY-08), Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD) and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) urging the group to support and immediately pass Senator Shaheen’s bipartisan INSULIN Act to cap the cost of insulin at $35 a month during the lame duck session. The letters highlight the excessively high cost of the life-saving medication and come after historic midterm elections where the American public made it overwhelmingly clear that they want to see real solutions to the affordability crisis. Both letters continue a trend of growing support for the INSULIN Act, where in September senators on both sides of the aisle increasingly pointed to the legislation as an immediate step Congress can take to lower health care costs.

The letters were signed by the American Association of Clinical Endocrinology, American Diabetes Association, Association of Diabetes Care & Education Specialists, Beyond Type 1, Blue Circle Health, Breakthrough T1D, Children with Diabetes, Diabetes Leadership Council, Diabetes Patient Advocacy Coalition, Endocrine Society, National Black Nurses Association, National Kidney Foundation, Prevent Blindness, T1D Exchange, The Diabetes Link and The diaTribe Foundation.

The letter to President Trump can be found HERE and the letter to Congressional leadership HERE.

“Voters sent a clear message this election that Congress needs to take urgent action to lower costs for American families,” said Senator Shaheen. “With my INSULIN Act, we have a bipartisan opportunity right in front of us to deliver meaningful relief by capping monthly insulin costs at just $35. The bill has strong support from Republicans and Democrats in both the House and Senate—getting it across the finish line is a top priority of mine before year's end.”

Shaheen’s bipartisan Improving Needed Safeguards for Users of Lifesaving Insulin Now (INSULIN) Act would cap monthly out-of-pocket insulin costs at $35 for Americans with insurance, expanding the effective price cap for Americans on Medicare. Shaheen has championed efforts to lower insulin costs throughout her time in office, and the bill is closer than ever before to passing out of the U.S. Senate. In July, the INSULIN Act advanced out of the U.S. Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, and in September companion legislation was introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives.

Senator Shaheen has worked tirelessly to lower health care costs for Granite Staters and Americans. As co-chair of the U.S. Senate Diabetes Caucus, Senator Shaheen has consistently pressed to hold insulin manufacturers, insurers and pharmacy benefit managers accountable for the skyrocketing cost of life-saving insulin and otherwise support patients and families facing diabetes. Polling released from the American Diabetes Association this summer found that 40% of respondents who rely on insulin report paying more than $150 per month for insulin, and 76% of respondents across political parties support a $35 limit on cost sharing for insulin.

title: Sheehy, Klobuchar Introduce Bipartisan Hemp Guardrails Act
text:
U.S. SENATE – Senators Tim Sheehy and Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.) today introduced the Hemp Guardrails Act to establish a comprehensive federal regulatory framework for hemp-derived consumer products.

This legislation puts strict federal guardrails on the hemp industry and seeks to address every issue that was raised during the government funding battle. It also protects American farmers, consumers, and those with chronic illness who rely on lawful hemp products.

“We’re taking a commonsense approach to this issue. Our bill will put every bad actor in the hemp space out of business and keep intoxicating products out of the hands of children. It will also stop Congress from turning the farmers, veterans, and cancer patients who rely on these products into criminals overnight,” said Senator Sheehy.

“Minnesota is a national leader in hemp, and our state has shown that we can protect kids and support responsible hemp businesses. But a looming federal ban on hemp products is threatening farmers, brewers, small businesses, and consumers across Minnesota and the country. This new bill with Senator Sheehy would keep safe hemp products on store shelves, protect consumers from dangerous products, and ensure that farmers and small businesses can continue to operate, grow, and create jobs,” said Senator Klobuchar.

Background:

Many Americans, including veterans and seniors, rely on consumer hemp products for their health and wellness. One in five adults used these products in the last year, and many say they improve chronic pain tremendously.

The bipartisan Hemp Guardrails Act ensures these Americans, along with the farmers and businesses who serve them, are not suddenly criminalized overnight. Instead, it creates a responsible framework that protects children, strengthens consumer safety, and fully preserves states’ authority to set even stricter rules for hemp-derived products.

What the bill does:

Protects children: Prohibits the sale, possession, and consumption of consumable hemp products by individuals under 21. Directs FDA to establish strict child-resistant packaging, labeling, manufacturing, and testing requirements for hemp products.

Bans “gas station weed:” Prohibits raw floral hemp material, smokable hemp flower, and hemp pre-rolls intended for inhalation.

Prohibits copycat marketing: Prohibits misleading packaging, imitation branding, and advertising targeting children, while requiring appropriate health warnings.

Bans dangerous cannabinoids: Bans delta-8, delta-10, and THC-O products and restricts their production outside of the hemp plant.

Bans synthetics: Prohibits synthetic cannabinoids which often originate in China.

Strengthens enforcement: Authorizes FDA to inspect facilities, seize adulterated or misbranded products, and enforce federal requirements for consumable hemp products entering interstate commerce.

Establishes federal oversight: Creates categories for hemp-derived cannabinoid products and dietary supplements under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

Protects American farmers: Requires consumable hemp products to be cultivated, processed, finished, and packaged in the United States. Sets allowable THC threshold for hemp cultivation at 1% total THC on a dry-weight basis to avoid unintentionally criminalizing farm operations.

Protects American jobs: Prevents the destruction of a $30 billion American industry that supports 350,000 jobs.

Preserves access to CBD: Protects access to qualifying hemp-derived CBD products through the Trump Administration’s CMS initiatives.

Respects states’ rights: Preserves states’ authority to enact stricter hemp regulations.

title: Slotkin Joins Colleagues Demanding USDA Withdraw Rule Restricting Food Assistance for Michiganders
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -— U.S. Senator Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), a member of the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry, along with fellow committee Democrats, urged the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to withdraw its proposed rule restricting Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) that will severely narrow eligibility requirements for the nation’s largest anti-hunger program.

This rule could potentially lead to the loss of SNAP benefits for tens of thousands of Michiganders. Over 150,000 Michiganders, including an estimated 54,000 children, have already lost access to SNAP benefits as a result of the cuts included in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

“We write to strongly urge the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to withdraw its proposed rule restricting Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE) under the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). Should this rule take effect, an estimated 6.3 million Americans, including many seniors and nearly 1.8 million children, would lose SNAP benefits according to the USDA’s own analysis. At a time when everyday Americans are already struggling to afford groceries, USDA should not be making changes to SNAP that leave families with fewer resources to meet their basic needs,” said the senators.

Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility helps working families and seniors afford groceries at a time when the rising costs of housing, child-care, health care, and other necessities are stretching household budgets. It gives states flexibility to help low-income households access food assistance while supporting work and financial stability.

Without BBCE, families could lose SNAP benefits even when they are still struggling to make ends meet. It also allows families and seniors to build and maintain modest savings without jeopardizing their access to food assistance.

This proposed rule would also make SNAP more challenging and costly for states to administer, increasing paperwork, the risk of payment errors, and demands on state workers.

Children in households that lose SNAP eligibility could also lose automatic certification for free school meals, requiring families to submit additional applications to establish eligibility and creating more administrative work for schools.

This added red tape could prevent eligible children from receiving meals and reduce federal reimbursements for schools, threatening efforts to provide free school meals to all students. The proposal could also create additional red tape for families seeking assistance through the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), potentially leaving some families unable to access benefits and others ineligible for assistance altogether.

The text of the letter is available here.

title: Thune: Permitting Reform Will Help Lower Costs, Get America Building Again
text:
Click here to watch the video.

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) today delivered the following remarks on the Senate floor:

Thune’s remarks below (as delivered):

“Mr. President, one of our priorities this Congress has been finding ways to make life easier for hardworking Americans.

“And one of the ways we’ve gone about that is by eliminating some of the red tape that drives up prices and causes headaches for consumers, businessowners, and builders.

“We’ve rescinded costly regulations through the Congressional Review Act that would have driven up prices for a host of items.

“In fact, we have voted [on] 25 different CRA – Congressional Review Act – resolutions of disapproval to undo burdensome Biden-era … regulations.

“Twenty-five times here, the Senate has voted on those, Mr. President, in an attempt to try and lessen the cost and the red tape of doing business and creating jobs in this country, and ultimately of driving up costs for consumers, which is what all that red tape, in the end, does.

“We passed the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which cuts some of the red tape that has driven up the price of housing by making it difficult to build new homes.

“And we’re continuing those efforts this week with the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act – a major permitting reform bill to help America build again.

“Mr. President, the federal permitting process is broken.

“Too often, projects are bogged down in bureaucratic delays for months, and often years, at a time.

“Delays cause project budgets to balloon, which then leads to higher costs for American consumers.

“And it’s not just the dollars-and-cents cost, Mr. President.

“Project delays have serious opportunity costs as well:

“Jobs put on hold because a new factory won’t open on time.

“Communities without internet access because broadband infrastructure is delayed.

“And Americans driving on bad roads and rickety bridges while plans for improvements are stuck in an office in Washington.

“Mr. President, it’s not that construction projects shouldn’t undergo a thorough review of their impacts on communities and the environment.

“Input from the local community, from state and local governments, and from other stakeholders is a critical part of determining whether and how to execute a project.

“But the federal permitting process has unfortunately gone far beyond these reasonable expectations.

“And that’s due in large part to senseless delays caused by cascading litigation from environmental groups and by agencies determined to study a project to death.

“We’ve seen those delays happen to everything from water projects to broadband deployment to affordable energy and improving roads and bridges.

“Mr. President, last week I mentioned the Potomac Interceptor, which burst earlier this year and sent nearly 250 million gallons of raw sewage spewing into the Potomac River.

“The local water company identified vulnerabilities in this 60-year-old sewer pipe a full seven years before it burst.

“But proposed repairs languished in the federal permitting process year after year after year.

“And the project was still undergoing an environmental review when the pipe burst and caused an environmental disaster.

“And that was just to replace something that had been there for decades.

“Mr. President, for Americans wondering why important projects aren’t making progress, the answer is too often federal permitting delays.

“It takes four and a half years on average for federal agencies to approve an environmental impact statement.

“Add another 15 months to that for a new bridge.

“And if a NEPA lawsuit is filed over a proposed project, it takes almost two years to resolve it.

“Mr. President, if we want better roads and bridges, if we want to strengthen American manufacturing, if we want to be energy independent, we need permitting reform.

“And I’m grateful to Chairs Shelley Moore Capito and Mike Lee for working with their Democrat counterparts to put forward a bipartisan permitting reform bill that I hope we will complete this week.

“This bill would streamline the review process, putting federal bureaucrats on the clock to give a yes or no answer to a project.

“This would make a huge difference on energy projects.

“As I said, projects are often stuck in limbo for years as they work their way through government approvals.

“That adds costs to the project, delays construction, and ultimately leaves American families paying higher utility bills.

“But by streamlining those processes, the Council of Economic Advisers estimates that provisions in this bill could save a typical household hundreds of dollars on energy bills and other expenses every single year.

“Importantly, this bill also provides much-needed certainty and clarity to a variety of stakeholders, including farmers and ranchers.

“For one, it extends Clean Water Act permits from five to 10 years, giving farmers more time to complete projects before having to renew their permits.

“It shortens reviews under the Endangered Species Act, allowing grazing-related projects – like a new fence on a ranch – to move along faster.

“And it ensures that local governments and landowners will continue to have a say in projects that affect them.

“Mr. President, for a lot of Americans, the type of project that most concerns them these days is a data center coming to their community.

“And I’m pleased to report that the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act would enact new protections for local communities when it comes to data centers.

“That starts with requiring – requiring – data centers to shoulder their own energy costs – whether that’s their operating and construction costs or the cost of grid improvements needed to accommodate them.

“This legislation ensures those costs don’t show up on household utility bills.

“It would also provide assistance to communities to help them understand and explore the impact a proposed data center would have on their locality – everything from the economic impact to the energy costs and infrastructure requirements that would be associated with the project.

“Mr. President, well-intentioned rules and regulations can quickly turn into death by a thousand cuts.

“Or, as is too often the case, death by delay.

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act restores the balanced approach to permitting that’s needed.

“It ensures local stakeholders have a say in projects in their community.

“And it provides accountability to ensure that bureaucrats in Washington don’t prevent needed projects from moving forward.

“A closed bridge.

“A burst sewer pipe.

“A factory built overseas.

“Bureaucratic delays, Mr. President, have real consequences.

“We need to get permitting reform done to get things built in this country and to make life more affordable for American families.”

title: Thune: Senate Republicans Will Run Through the Tape on the 119th Congress
text:
Click here to watch the video.

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) today spoke at a press conference with Senate Republican leadership:

Thune’s remarks below (as delivered):

“Our Republican conference is moving aggressively, running through the tape, and ensuring that we get as much done as we can.

“And we have a generational opportunity to cut red tape, thanks to the good work that Senator Capito and others have done on permitting reform.

“That’s a piece of legislation which, if passed, will dramatically reduce the cost of energy in this country, make it more affordable for American families, as well as allow us to produce a more reliable supply of energy in this country.

“It’s a decades-long effort to try and do something in a meaningful way that will cut the bureaucracy and red tape and regulations associated with trying to build any project in this country, energy projects or otherwise.

“So this is a really important piece of legislation.

“It’s been very bipartisan throughout the entire process.

“And I hope that we can conclude it this week in a way that will enable the legislation to get put on the president’s desk, the House pick it up hopefully and pass it, and let’s do something that’s really, really critical and important for the builders in this country, the job creators in this country, and something that’s an affordability issue for the American people.

“Of course, then also we’re going to continue to work on judges and, as you know, I think, we’ve got a number of them already teed up to vote on.

“There will be more being reported out of the Senate Judiciary Committee here in the next few days, and when they are, we will get those scheduled on the floor as well.

“But I think it’s an important point to make that President Trump has more active judges on the appellate and district benches in this country than any other president.

“And that doesn’t happen by chance or happen by accident; it happens because we have been committed here in the United States Senate to ensuring that his judges move across the finish line at a fast pace.

“In fact, outstripped any president going back to the Reagan administration in terms of the pace of getting these judges done once they are submitted and nominated and through the process.

“The final … point I’ll make, and that has to do with funding the government: … there’s been talk, reporting, and I’m increasingly concerned that the Democrats may try to initiate another, a third – third – government shutdown this year.

“And that would be a terrible outcome for the American people, and something I hope that they will think better of …

“We’ve already had two long, extended government shutdowns.

“We saw the impact that has on the American people.

“The American people don’t need another government shutdown.

“And we need to make sure that people are getting paid, we’re keeping this government open and operating, and we’re going to do everything to ensure that that happens and work with our Democrat colleagues to ensure that there is not a government shutdown.

“But I think that would be a colossal mistake and a real disservice to the people of this country.

“And I hope, again, that they will think better of it.”

title: Tuberville Speaks with Secretary of the Navy Nominee
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator Tommy Tuberville (R-AL) spoke with the Honorable Hung Cao, President Trump’s nominee to be Secretary of the Navy during a Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) hearing. Sen. Tuberville emphasized the need to modernize shipbuilding in America and highlighted Alabama’s important role in the Navy defense industry.

Read Sen. Tuberville’s remarks below or watch on YouTube or Rumble.

TUBERVILLE: “Mr. Secretary, thank you for being here. And your passion for your job because we need that. We need that in all areas. And, you know, I grew up [in] a military family and, you know, I know that all these people on these ships were tired and hungry and all that. My dad was over a year and a half sleeping underneath the tank after he landed at Normandy. And they never complained [that] they had to save this world. And that’s what military is supposed to do. So, thank you for your work.

But one thing that you brought up earlier in your opening statement is very concerning. [I’m] getting ready to be the new Governor of Alabama. I’m dealing with a lot of things right now with change orders. It costs a fortune when you change order something. Can you expound on that who is changing the […] the design? I mean, can we not come up with a design of a ship that we’re gonna use and make 15 or 20 of them and build these damn things instead of worrying about changing things? Go ahead.”

CAO: “Senator, I share the same concern you do. When I found out I was flabbergasted and I put out an order that all changes from this point on, when we’re building ships, has to come to the Assistant Secretary of the Navy for Research, Development, and Acquisitions and then approved by myself as well because we just can’t keep changing. I mean, it’s unattainable. And this is exactly why we’re delayed. That’s why it takes six to eight years to build a Destroyer now when it used to take two years.”

TUBERVILLE: “Who makes those change orders? Who gives that order to put a bathroom on the front or the back or whatever? Who makes that decision?”

CAO: “A lot of times, Senator, the tech warrant holders come in last minute, and this is why we build these portfolio acquisitions executives because […] in the past, you’d have four or five people that tells you know, but now we’re aligning everybody underneath that PAE in order to have including the tech warrant holders so that you have to go through that one single source to say yes or no. And then again, for the issuing change proposals would have to go up to ASN RDA and then myself as well.”

TUBERVILLE: “Who underneath you makes that decision? Because you can’t keep, I mean, who does that? Who keeps an eye on the, you know, the architecture, the designers, or the planners to keep their feet to the fire saying, ‘No. Hell no. We’re not gonna do it this way. We’re gonna build these ships and get them done. We need them.’ Who does that?”

CAO: “Sir, that’s our PA Maritime. So, again, I just promoted Rear Admiral Rucker and I hope that this Committee will accept our request to promote him to Vice Admiral because John Rucker is really a change agent. He’s right now works under Vice Admiral Rob Gaucher, who is the DRPM submarines, and they’ve been able to accelerate submarine building. So, I’m stealing him over to put him into the maritime, to a submarine, or to build ships for us because he’s his right type of person make this happen.”

TUBERVILLE: “Yeah. Well, thank you.

Also as being a new governor, we build ships. We build submarines in the state of Alabama.”

CAO: “And I heard this is really nice there in wintertime too.”

TUBERVILLE: “Yeah. It’s very nice. A lot better in Mississippi. But the thing also is we also-“

WICKER: “Time has expired.”

TUBERVILLE: “Here’s one other problem we’re running into. We have a lot of defense contractors in my state. We build Tomahawks. We build Patriots. All over our state. We have a huge shortage of steel in this country. And the steel is going to a lot of our manufacturers because President Trump’s got manufacturing coming back galore into our country. Thank God. We got jobs for our kids, but we’ve gotta start pushing to make more steel.

American steel, to build ships, to build missiles, and do those things. And I’ve just heard from our defense contractors here lately, and they can’t get steel to upgrade and build more Patriots and Tomahawks. I mean, we’re between a rock and hard place, but that’s for something else.

But recently, Admiral Sief, noted that we just released 10 submarines. I think they were returned to service. Is that correct?”

CAO: “Yes, Sir.”

TUBERVILLE: “Yeah. What class were those?”

CAO: “It was a Los Angeles class submarine. So, again, they’re still good. Again, if you look at the Charlotte, she’s a 32-year-old submarine that did some very exquisite things out there against very new platforms, but also, they were the first submarine to launch a torpedo and sinker ship since World War II.”

TUBERVILLE: “Yeah. The thing that we’re gonna do in our state is we’re gonna [do] workforce development. We’re gonna have a thousand electricians., plumbers,[…] welders, […] kids that can use their hands and make a heck of a better living than getting a social justice degree to some of these universities. So, we’re committed to that. So, Mr. Secretary, thank you for what you’re doing, and keep pushing hard. We need more ships. We need to protect the greatest country ever in that United States of America. Thank you, God bless you.”

CAO: “Thank you, Governor-elect.”

Senator Tommy Tuberville represents Alabama in the United States Senate and is a member of the Senate Armed Services, Agriculture, Veterans’ Affairs, HELP and Aging Committees.

title: Senate Intel Vice Chair Warner Statement on Network Outages
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Sen. Mark R. Warner (D-VA), Vice Chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence and co-chair of the Senate Cybersecurity Caucus, released the following statement:

“I understand why Americans are concerned about the widespread outages we’ve seen in recent days, affecting everything from banks and major technology companies to critical government systems. At this point, there is no indication that these incidents are the result of a cyberattack, foreign interference, or some coordinated effort. What appears to be happening instead is a consequence of how quickly artificial intelligence is changing the cybersecurity landscape. AI is making it possible to identify vulnerabilities across enormous numbers of systems at unprecedented speed, creating enormous pressure on companies and government agencies to patch those vulnerabilities immediately, often all at once, putting tremendous strain on systems that weren’t built to handle that pace of change. While we still need to get to the bottom of these incidents, the evidence so far points toward legitimate efforts to secure our systems, not malicious activity.

“Still, these disruptions should serve as a wake-up call. It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences. This is exactly why I’ve been pushing for commonsense guardrails on AI and stronger cybersecurity protections. Unfortunately, President Trump has shown little interest in confronting these challenges, his administration has repeatedly undermined its own credibility, and its cuts to CISA have weakened the very expertise we need to navigate moments like this. Americans deserve clear, reliable information and a government that is prepared to respond. I’m going to keep digging into these incidents, pressing for answers, and making sure we’re doing everything possible to protect our critical systems. But based on what we know today, there is good reason to believe these disruptions are the unintended consequences of efforts to make our systems safer, not evidence of a broader attack.”

Sen. Warner has been a leading voice in Congress on the national security, economic, and societal implications of artificial intelligence. Earlier this year, he unveiled A Framework for America’s AI Future, a comprehensive legislative agenda focused on AI safety and competition, national security, workforce disruption, and the infrastructure needed to power the technology. Most recently, Warner introduced the Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 with Sens. Brian Schatz (D-HI) and Andy Kim (D-NJ), legislation that would establish enforceable safety and security standards for the most advanced AI systems, including pre-deployment testing, stronger cybersecurity requirements, and mandatory reporting of serious AI safety and security incidents. Warner and his colleagues took to the Senate floor this week to seek unanimous consent to pass the legislation.

title: Warner, Walkinshaw Introduce Bill to Staff Federal IT Contracting to Match Real Workloads
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Sen. Mark R. Warner (D-VA) and U.S. Rep. James R. Walkinshaw (D-VA-11) introduced the IT Acquisition Readiness Act. The bill would require the largest federal agencies to find gaps in their IT contracting workforce and fix them with hiring, training, and retention plans built on real workload data.

A 2025 Government Accountability Office (GAO) report found that the Social Security Administration (SSA) lacked reliable workload data to determine its IT contracting staff needs, and did not have a training plan that would adequately close known skills gaps within that workforce. The same problem plagues other federal agencies, especially as the federal workforce has lost experienced federal IT acquisition staff in the aftermath of massive cuts to the federal workforce.

“Federal employees are responsible for managing increasingly complex IT contracts, but too often agencies lack the data and planning needed to ensure that they are appropriately investing in and supporting this professional acquisition workforce,” said Sen. Warner. “When agencies don’t adequately plan for their workforce needs, critical projects get delayed, costs go up, and taxpayers pay the price. This legislation would require agencies to identify IT contracting skills and staffing gaps and develop plans to recruit, train, and retain workers, all while delivering better results for the people they serve.”

“Buying laptops and replacing a legacy system an agency relies on every day can each count as one contract, but they can require very different amounts of time and expertise,” said Rep. Walkinshaw. “Our bill requires agencies to account for the volume and complexity of that work when planning how to hire, train, and retain staff.”

“A modern federal government requires a skilled acquisition workforce equipped to manage increasingly complex technology procurements. The IT Acquisition Readiness Act takes an important step toward that goal by identifying workforce gaps, strengthening recruitment and training, and leveraging technology to reduce administrative burdens on contracting professionals. The Center for Procurement Advocacy applauds Representative Walkinshaw and Senator Warner for their leadership in ensuring federal agencies have the acquisition expertise and resources necessary to deliver better outcomes for taxpayers,” said Tim Brennan, president of the Center for Procurement Advocacy (CPA).

“A skilled, well-staffed acquisition workforce is the foundation of smart IT buying. The IT Acquisition Readiness Act gives agencies a clear picture of the contracting workforce they have and the one they need to deliver modern capabilities to the mission. PSC is proud to support Rep. Walkinshaw’s and Sen. Warner’s commitment to a stronger, better-equipped federal workforce,” said Jim Carroll, PSC CEO.

The IT Acquisition Readiness Act would:

Require agencies to assess staffing and skills gaps among federal IT acquisition professionals

Require agencies to build recruitment, training, and retention plans from those assessments and from data on the quantity and complexity of employees’ workloads

Require plans to include strategies that incorporate the use of modern tools to help reduce administrative burden

Require OPM and OMB, respectively, to support related workforce development activities and implementation of the bill’s requirements across federal agencies

Require OMB to submit to congress a report on agency plans and the progress of their implementation

title: Welch Pushes Bipartisan Bill to Lower Cost of Prescription Drugs, Streamline Drug Patent Litigation
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — In a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing this week, U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.) encouraged support for the advancement of his bipartisan bill, the Eliminating Thickets to Improve Competition (ETHIC) Act. The ETHIC Act, which he co-leads with Judiciary Committee colleagues Sens. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) and Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), aims to streamline drug patent litigation, encourage fair market competition, and lower prescription drug prices by making it easier for generic and biosimilar companies to enter the market.

“My hope is that we’re going to be able to do some bipartisan legislation that focuses on competition; that takes away the manipulation of the patent system. Senator Hawley and I have the ETHIC Act which would essentially get rid of patent thickets,” said Senator Welch. “We’ve got a reset opportunity here. This is not at all a Republican-Democratic deal. I mean, we’ve got people who’ve been working on this forever. They’re very practical. Nobody who is on this panel is anything but supportive of the benefits of good medication. They’re all in favor of making that accessible and essentially, not by taking away the incentive, but by taking away the ripoff. So, my hope is that we could work together to incorporate the ideas that have been presented here by this panel to benefit all the people we represent, including in your wonderful state of Iowa, and my state of Vermont.”

Watch the Senator’s full remarks below:

Read key excerpts from Senator Welch’s exchange with Merith Basey, CEO of Patients For Affordable Drugs Now:

Sen. Welch: I’ll just ask a little bit about the patent thickets, because I am working on that with Senator Hawley. Ms. Basey, could you talk a little bit about that? You know, you have a patent system—I support a patent system, it gives exclusivity and rewards innovation. But the thicket system means that the patent system is just rampantly abused for self-gain and beyond what the purpose of what the patent system is. Could you talk a little bit about that?

Ms. Basey: So, the patent system was designed to incentivize genuine innovation—novel treatments that save lives. Right now, the patent system isn’t just incentivizing innovation, it’s incentivizing manipulation. That is the subject of these bills. What patent thickets are: a drug company can file multiple duplicative non-obvious, non-innovative patents on a single drug. Even if they expire at the same time, they create a thicket which makes it much harder for a generic or biosimilar competitor to enter the market.

Sen. Welch: As a matter of principle, if you have one invention, does it make sense to have one patent?

Ms. Basey: The simple answer’s yes, but I think on the key elements that are truly innovative, the system should reward those. But there’s an example with a drug called SYMBRAVO, and there’s two patents in particular of the 90-something that it has: one of them is for pain relief, and one is for pain freedom. Now, that is not the type of innovation that patients in our community are seeking.

Sen. Welch: That’s a verbal manipulation.

Ms. Basey: Yeah, and it’s mocking.

The U.S. Patent system was designed to promote innovation and foster competition. However, pharmaceutical companies are exceedingly abusing the patent system through patent extension strategies such as “patent thicketing,” a strategy in which pharmaceutical companies develop a “web” of patents around their most profitable drugs. These patent thickets deter generic and biosimilar drugs from entering the market, due to the high cost of legally challenging each patent in a thicket.

The ETHIC Act codifies the practice that many federal district courts across the country already apply by limiting the number of patents or patent claims a company can assert in litigation. Specifically, this bipartisan bill:

Streamlines patent litigation by limiting the number of patents per thicket a pharmaceutical company can assert in litigation to one.

Prohibits a patent owner from asserting multiple patents from the same thicket in separate actions against the same alleged infringer to circumvent the intent of the law.

Safeguards quality patents that improve existing drugs, benefiting patients.

The ETHIC Act is endorsed by the Association for Accessible Medicines and Generation Patient. U.S. Representatives Jodey Arrington (R-TX-19), Lloyd Doggett (D-TX-37), Issa Darrell (R-CA-48), August Pfluger (R-TX-11), Pramila Jayapal (D-WA-07), Diana Harshbarger (D-TN-01), Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Rashida Tlaib (D-MI-12), Jesús García (D-IL-04), and Angie Craig (D-MN-02) introduced companion bipartisan legislation in the House.

Learn more about the ETHIC Act and read and download the full text of the bill.

title: Whitehouse, Reed, & Amo Announce $532,000 in Federal Funding for Safer Roads in Smithfield
text:
Grant from Bipartisan Infrastructure Law will improve safety measures for in Smithfield school zone

Smithfield, RI – U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse, the top Democrat on the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, joined U.S. Senator Jack Reed and U.S. Representative Gabe Amo to announce $532,450 in federal funding for safety improvements along the Pleasant View Avenue corridor in Smithfield.

“Schools, small businesses, and homes line the busy Pleasant View Avenue corridor. This federal funding will help town leaders develop a plan to make the street safer for drivers and pedestrians,” said Senator Whitehouse. “Our Bipartisan Infrastructure Law continues to improve travel in the Ocean State.”

“I was pleased to work with then-Senator Tom Carper (D-DE) and others to help create this program back in 2021 and glad to see Smithfield earn this competitive grant to make needed road improvements and safety upgrades along Pleasant View Avenue,” said Senator Reed.

“Whether walking or driving, Rhode Islanders must be able to navigate the Pleasant View Avenue corridor safely,” said Congressman Amo. “These federal resources will help Smithfield develop a comprehensive plan to protect everyone who uses the street. I will keep working alongside our Senators to deliver federal funding that makes our communities better and safer for Rhode Islanders.”

The competitive grant, funded through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law’s Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) program, was awarded to the Town of Smithfield to update its Comprehensive Safety Action Plan and conduct supplemental safety planning along the 2.7-mile Pleasant View Avenue corridor. Planned work includes updating the Action Plan with the most recent crash data, completing corridor and school safety studies, and testing temporary quick-build countermeasures. Findings of these studies will be used to develop projects to improve the roadway.

“The Town of Smithfield community is very pleased with the award of Federal funds to improve the safety for traffic utilizing the Pleasant View Avenue corridor which is a heavily traveled roadway that cuts through the center of town. The safety improvements will benefit automobiles, motorcycles, bicycles and pedestrian traffic. We are grateful for the efforts of Senator Reed, Senator Whitehouse and Representative Amo for securing the funding. All three are great supporters of our town. Without this funding the town would not be able to support this level of safety improvements. This roadway sees many accidents annually. The federal funding will allow us to be proactive in reducing these accidents,” said Smithfield Town Manager Robert Seltzer.

Whitehouse and Reed helped create the U.S. Department of Transportation’s SS4A program through passage of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, with $5 billion in SS4A funding available over five years.

title: Senator Wicker Honors Emmett Till’s Story at Tallahatchie County Courthouse’s Grand Opening
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Roger Wicker, R-Miss., this weekend attended the grand opening of the new Tallahatchie County Courthouse in Sumner, Mississippi. The new facility will replace the current courthouse, which was the location of the infamous 1955 trial for Emmett Till’s murder. The existing courthouse will now transition to a fully historic site.

Senator Wicker has worked extensively to preserve the legacy of Emmett Till. In 2014, Senator Wicker joined Senate colleagues in dedicating a memorial tree on the U.S. Capitol grounds to honor Emmett Till. In 2017, Senator Wicker and then-Senator Thad Cochran worked to secure a $500,000 grant from the National Parks Service to support the Tallahatchie County Courthouse restoration project. In 2021, Senators Wicker and Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., along with Senator Tammy Duckworth, D-Ill., introduced legislation to mark Chicago’s Roberts Temple Church of God in Christ, the location of Emmett Till’s funeral, as a national historic site.

“This weekend, we cut the ribbon on the new Tallahatchie County Courthouse. At the ceremony, we remembered Emmett Till, whose name means ‘truth’ in Hebrew. We shined a bit more light on the truth of his tragic story,” said Senator Wicker. “Mississippi has resolved not to forget stories like his. We are the only state to fund our own civil rights museum, and we have marked key sites with monuments and memorials. I have urged my colleagues in Washington and my friends from around the country to visit Mississippi and remember these pivotal moments in the history of our country.”

title: Young Applauds 126 New Opportunity Zone Designations Across Indiana
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator Todd Young (R-Ind.) applauded the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s announcement of 126 new Opportunity Zone designations across Indiana.

Opportunity Zones, made permanent through the Work Families Tax Cuts supported by Senator Young, provide tax incentives to encourage private investment in designated communities. The law also provides enhanced incentives for investments in eligible rural areas, helping attract capital to communities that have historically struggled to secure investment.

“Opportunity Zones are an important tool for attracting private investment and creating economic opportunity in communities across Indiana,” said Senator Young. “By making this program permanent and strengthening incentives for rural communities, we are helping bring new investment to areas that need it most. These designations will support job creation and long-term economic growth for Hoosiers.”

Of Indiana’s 126 new Opportunity Zones, 42 qualify for enhanced ruralinvestment incentives under the Working Families Tax Cuts. The designations span 47 counties across Indiana and take effect January 1, 2027.

title: Aderholt, Moolenaar, Smith, and House VAT Members Urge President Trump to Raise Political Prisoners with Xi Jinping at the APEC Summit
text:
Image

November 18, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Robert B. Aderholt, Chairman of the House Values Action Team, joined by VAT Members, including Executive Committee Member, Congressman John Moolenaar, Chairman of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, and Congressman Chris Smith, Co-Chairman of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China, today called on President Trump to reiterate to Xi Jinping that the United States remembers the wrongfully detained Americans and other political prisoners held unjustly by the Chinese Communist Party when the two leaders meet Thursday at the APEC Summit.

Members co-signing the statement include: House VAT Co-Chairs Rep. Josh Brecheen (OK-02) and Rep. Mary Miller (IL-15); VAT Executive Committee Members, Rep. Riley Moore (WV-02); Rep. Gary Palmer (AL-06) and Rep. Marlin Stutzman (IN-03); Rep. Sheri Biggs (SC-03); Rep. Vince Fong (CA-20); Rep. Russ Fulcher (ID-01); Rep. Glenn Grothman (WI-06); Rep. Andy Harris (MD-01); Rep. Mark Harris (NC-08); Rep. Mark Messmer (IN-08); Rep. Barry Moore (AL-01) Senator-elect; Rep. John Rutherford (FL-05); Rep. Glenn “GT” Thompson (PA-15); Rep. Randy Weber (TX-14); and Rep. Joe Wilson (SC-02).

The lawmakers pointed to the release of Pastor Ezra Jin in July as an example of productive diplomatic engagement from the Trump administration, while encouraging recognition that other prisoners still remain. They made this statement:

"The fundamental freedoms of religion, of speech and of free association are endowed by our Creator on every human being, but the CCP continues to strip them from innocent people. Pastor Ezra Jin spent nearly nine months in prison for leading a church. Jimmy Lai is 78 years old and was handed a 20-year sentence for running a newspaper. A sentence that long for a man his age is a death sentence. title: Smith, Colleagues Introduce Bill to Increase Housing Opportunities
text:
Today, U.S. Representatives Adrian Smith (R-NE), Claudia Tenney (R-NY), and Nathaniel Moran (R-TX), members of the House Ways and Means Committee, introduced the More Homes for Americans Act to help increase the supply of housing and expand opportunities for hardworking Americans. The bill would encourage new housing investment by allowing developers to immediately deduct 100 percent of eligible construction costs associated with building new residential rental properties.

“Renting is often an important first step toward homeownership, giving individuals and families the flexibility they need to build financial stability before purchasing a home. Yet our tax code puts the construction of rental housing at a disadvantage compared to homes built for sale. I introduced the More Homes for Americans Act to level the playing field, encourage new investment, and expand affordable housing opportunities for hardworking Americans,”said Smith.

“Across New York, families are struggling with rising rents and a shortage of affordable housing options. The answer to our housing shortage is simple: we need to build more homes. High construction costs and outdated tax policies make it harder to get new projects off the ground. Our More Homes for Americans Act encourages private investment, expands the supply of rental housing, and helps bring down costs for hardworking families. This is a practical, market-driven solution that addresses the housing shortage without growing government bureaucracy,”said Tenney.

"To build more homes, we need to remove the barriers holding back investment in new construction. Under current law, builders of new apartments, multifamily complexes, and single-family build-to-rent homes have to spread out their costs a little at a time, over decades. That leaves less money to start the next project. This legislation lets builders deduct the full cost of building new rental housing up front, so they can put that money back to work right away. This is a pro-growth solution to get more rental homes built for families who need them,”said Moran.

BACKGROUND:

Under current law, construction costs for homes built for sale can generally be recovered immediately as inventory, while costs associated with newly constructed residential rental properties must be depreciated over 27.5 years.

The More Homes for Americans Act would create parity by allowing developers to immediately deduct 100 percent of eligible construction costs for newly built apartment buildings, multifamily housing, and single-family build-to-rent properties.

By improving the economics of new rental construction, Smith’s bill would encourage developers to build more housing to meet market demand, expand the overall housing supply, and ease pressure on rents and home prices.

The More Homes for Americans Act applies only to newly constructed residential rental properties and excludes land costs, existing properties, and conversions of existing properties. Properties used for short-term vacation rentals would be subject to recapture of a proportionate amount of the deduction.

title: Smith, Moran Introduce Bill to Restore Flexibility in the Housing Market
text:
Today, U.S. Representatives Adrian Smith (R-NE) and Nathaniel Moran (R-TX), members of the House Ways and Means Committee, introduced the Unlocking Homes for Families Act to eliminate the tax disparity facing single and widowed homeowners and help bring more homes onto the market.

Under current law, individuals can exclude up to $250,000 in capital gains when selling their primary residence, while married couples filing jointly can exclude up to $500,000. The Unlocking Homes for Families Act would double the exclusion for individual filers to $500,000, giving single and widowed homeowners greater flexibility to make their next move while helping bring more homes onto the market for the next generation of buyers.

“Your home's value doesn't depend on your marital status, and neither should the tax treatment when you sell it. Single homeowners shouldn't face a higher tax burden simply because they are not married. My Unlocking Homes for Families Act will eliminate this disparity, give homeowners greater flexibility to make their next move, and help put more homes on the market for young families and first-time homebuyers,”said Smith.

“The amount a single homeowner can keep tax-free when they sell their homes has stayed at $250,000 which was set nearly 30 years ago. The Unlocking Homes for Families Act raises the limit to $500,000 and keeps it current, so more homeowners can sell without a penalty, and more homes open up for the next family to buy. I appreciate Rep. Adrian Smith’s leadership, and it’s a privilege to co-lead this bill with him. Americans work hard for their homes. They should keep more of what they earn,”said Moran.

BACKGROUND:

Smith’s Unlocking Homes for Families Act would expand the Section 121 capital gains tax exemption for primary residences by doubling the exclusion limit for individual filers from $250,000 to $500,000. This would bring the individual exclusion in line with the current limit for married couples filing jointly. The legislation would also index the exclusion amounts to inflation.

title: Reps. Aguilar, Obernolte Introduce Bipartisan Resolution Designating November 18 as National Geographic Information System Day
text:
Dozens of industries use GIS technology to respond to emergencies, study environmental changes, maintain our infrastructure and more

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Reps. Pete Aguilar (CA-33) and Jay Obernolte (CA-23) introduced a bipartisan resolution designating November 18, 2026, as National Geographic Information System (GIS) Day. The resolution recognizes GIS as an essential, rapidly growing technology and encourages students, educators and professionals across the country to use it to learn, solve problems and grow the economy.

GIS collects, analyzes and maps location data so users can better visualize and make sense of geospatial information, patterns and the relationships of our world. Government agencies, businesses, nonprofits, schools and the public use it for things like urban planning, emergency response and disaster management, supply chain logistics, farming, utilities and infrastructure and scientific research.

“From wildfire preparedness to neighborhood zoning, GIS shapes our lives in countless ways most people never see,” said Rep. Pete Aguilar. “GIS users in the Inland Empire and across the world are innovators who drive economic growth and keep our communities safe and well-connected. I’m proud to recognize their work and the importance of this technology with a bipartisan resolution designating National GIS Day.”

“Geographic Information Systems have become indispensable to everything from emergency preparedness and infrastructure development to economic growth,” said Rep. Jay Obernolte. “Here in California’s 23rd District, Esri continues to demonstrate how American innovation can address real-world challenges while supporting high-quality jobs and technological advancement. I’m pleased to recognize National GIS Day and the dedicated professionals, educators, and students who continue to advance this important technology.”

“I want to commend Representatives Aguilar and Obernolte for their bipartisan collaboration in introducing the House resolution honoring GIS Day 2026,” said Jack Dangermond, President, Esri. “This annual event celebrates geographic information systems and the dedicated GIS technologists who are having an ever-increasing impact on all sectors. These tools play a crucial role in operations at every level of government and help nonprofits, educational institutions, and the private sector with geospatial analysis of a wide range of questions and issues. GIS systems are driving significant economic growth and are integrating with AI-enabled tools to better help us solve problems. Happy GIS Day to all!”

“On behalf of the National Society of Professional Surveyors (NSPS), I thank Representatives Aguilar and Obernolte for once again recognizing National GIS Day,” said Tim Murphy, PLS, NSPS President. “Every map, model, and spatial analysis depends on knowing precisely where things are. Land surveyors and GIS professionals share responsibility for that foundation. As advances in high-accuracy positioning and the modernization of the National Spatial Reference System change how we measure our nation, the partnership between surveying and GIS has never been more important. GIS Day is an opportunity to honor the work of the geospatial community and to inspire the next generation to join it.”

“On behalf of the Subsurface Utility Engineering Association (SUEA), we commend the bipartisan leadership of Representatives Pete Aguilar and Jay Obernolte for sponsoring the GIS Day resolution,” said Nicholas Zembillas, SUEA President. “The value and practice of subsurface utility engineering is enhanced by leveraging GIS technology to help identify, designate, and locate underground utilities using records research, geophysical methods, and non-destructive excavation to reduce project risk. When used accurately and combined with the best practices and standards in SUE, GIS technology enables SUE professionals and professional firms conducting SUE to best serve their clients and help protect the public.”

“New and exciting applications of geospatial data, services, and technology portrayed, visualized, and accessed in Geographic Information Systems (GIS) are brought to the market for the benefit of individual citizens, government at all levels, and private enterprise every day,” said John “JB” Byrd, Policy Coordinator, U.S. Geospatial Executives Organization (U.S. GEO). “And Congress is increasingly recognizing the value of ‘where’ in legislation. GIS Day is a time to recognize how billions of dollars in business activity, the creation and support of tens of thousands of jobs, economic growth and development, protection of the environment, and many other important activities are supported by GIS. U.S. GEO commends Representatives Aguilar and Obernolte for introducing the GIS Day resolution in the U.S. House of Representatives.”

title: Representatives Bell, Keating, & McBride Introduce Bill to Track Covert Russian Attacks on NATO Allies
text:
The WATCH Russia Act requires quarterly reports on Russian gray zone activities against NATO allies

Reports would cover cyberattacks, sabotage, disinformation, and other Russian tactics considered below the level of open war

In September, Congressman Bell went on a bipartisan Congressional delegation trip to Ukraine to underscore the importance of our support of allies in the region

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representatives Wesley Bell (D-MO-01), Bill Keating (D-MA-09), and Sarah McBride (D-DE-AL) introduced the Warning Allies and Tracking Covert Hostilities by Russia (WATCH Russia) Act.

The bill requires the Secretary of State to notify Congress of covert and coercive activities the Russian Federation carries out or directs against NATO allies. Congressman Bell serves on the House Armed Services and Foreign Affairs Committees. Congressman Keating is the Ranking Member for the Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on Europe.

“Russia’s attacks on our allies don’t always look like traditional warfare. Putin is using cyberattacks, sabotage, and election interference to stoke fear and wreak havoc across Europe, threatening our democratic allies. The more we allow Putin to operate unchecked in Ukraine and across Europe, the more we are allowing the erosion of NATO and our other alliances without triggering a response. The WATCH Russia Act makes sure Congress sees those tactics for what they are and can respond effectively,” said Rep. Bell.

What the WATCH Russia Act would:

Require the Secretary of State to report to Congress within 90 days of enactment, and quarterly thereafter, on Russia’s “gray zone” activities against NATO allies.

Each report must describe the activity, who is responsible, its goals and effects, and any U.S., NATO, or allied response.

Covers cyberattacks, disinformation, sabotage of critical infrastructure, election interference, and airspace or territorial incursions, among other tactics.

Reports must be unclassified, with the option of a classified annex.

“Russian hybrid warfare has threatened American, European, and transatlantic security, and we must ensure Congress is informed of Russian gray zone activities whenever they occur,” said Rep. Keating. “I thank Congressman Bell for his leadership on this important legislation and look forward to continuing to address these threats to NATO in the upcoming Congress.”

“The United States has a responsibility to stand with our NATO allies, and this legislation will help us better identify and respond to Russia’s evolving covert operations. I am proud to join Reps. Bell and Keating in introducing this bill to strengthen congressional oversight, hold Putin accountable, and protect our national security,” said Rep. McBride.

“Russian gray-zone activities have become increasingly frequent and brazen, threatening the security of our NATO allies. These activities include airspace violations by Russian drones and threats to critical infrastructure and industrial facilities. The Joint Baltic American National Committee (JBANC) supports the WATCH RUSSIA Act, which would help ensure that Congress has the assessments necessary to understand and counter Russian gray-zone activities and strengthen our own preparedness,” said the Joint Baltic American National Committee (JBANC) leadership.

“Razom for Ukraine strongly supports the WATCH Russia Act. This bill will help bring Russia’s hostile activities targeting our NATO partners out of the shadows. Ukraine’s security services have fended off Russia’s covert operations, sabotage attempts, and cyberattacks for years,” said Razom leadership. Razom for Ukraine is a U.S. based non-profit dedicated to building a secure, prosperous, and democratic Ukraine.

Congressman Bell is a member of the Congressional Ukraine Caucus. In September, he traveled to Kyiv as part of a bipartisan congressional delegation. He has also worked on bipartisan legislation to support Ukraine and strengthen the U.S. response to Russian aggression, including the Frontline Innovation Act and the Baltic Security Assessment Act.

title: Rep. Bera Signs Discharge Petition to Force Vote on Bipartisan Afghanistan TPS Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, U.S. Representative Ami Bera, M.D. (CA-06) signed a discharge petition to force a House vote on the bipartisan Afghanistan Temporary Protected Status (TPS) Act of 2026.

Cosponsored by Rep. Bera, the legislation would protect eligible Afghan nationals living in the United States from deportation to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan.

“Sacramento County is the proud home to one of the largest Afghan communities in America,” said Congressman Bera. “Many stood side by side with our troops in Afghanistan. We have a responsibility to honor our commitment to them and protect them from threats of persecution by the Taliban.

“That’s why I signed the discharge petition to bring the Afghanistan TPS Act to a vote and protect eligible Afghans from deportation. We cannot turn our backs on those who stood with us when we needed them most,” Bera continued.

Last year, the Trump administration terminated Afghanistan’s TPS designation which ended TPS protections for thousands of Afghan nationals. The decision, coupled with the administration’s intensified immigration enforcement efforts, has raised concerns about the potential deportation of Afghans to a country where they face threats of persecution and retaliation under Taliban rule.

The Afghanistan TPS Act of 2026 would restore TPS eligibility for qualifying Afghan nationals who have been continuously present in the United States since the legislation’s enactment. The bill would provide temporary protection from deportation and eligibility for employment authorization through July 1, 2029. Applicants would be required to undergo criminal background checks and national security screenings.

The discharge petition would allow the legislation to advance to the House floor for a vote if it receives the required 218 signatures.

title: SEEC Members Renew U.S. Climate Leadership at COP31
text:
Washington, D.C. – This week, 18 members of the House of Representatives, including House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition (SEEC) Vice Chairs Reps. Don Beyer (VA-08), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Sean Casten (IL-06), and Mike Levin (CA-49), as well as Reps. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Ami Bera (CA-06), Kathy Castor (FL-14), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Jared Huffman (CA-02), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Lucy McBath (GA-06), Dave Min (CA-47), Emily Randall (WA-06), Raul Ruiz (CA-25), and Nikema Williams (GA-05), joined the international climate community at the 31st Conference of Parties (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye to renew and strengthen U.S. engagement on climate leadership on the global stage. The member delegation reaffirmed partnerships and highlighted shared challenges, including topics ranging from energy affordability and clean electrification to food security and disaster resilience. Members returned to Congress with new relationships and new ideas to build a more affordable, clean, and healthy future for our nation and the world.

SEEC members participated in events across 8 themes.

Forests, Nature, and Natural-Capital Resilience

SEEC members highlighted how protecting and restoring ecosystems can preserve nature’s capacity to absorb and sequester carbon, while bolstering climate resilience for our planet.

“For millions of people around the world, forests sustain their livelihoods, provide clean water, and store the carbon we desperately need to keep out of the atmosphere,” said House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (CA-02). “As climate change fuels more destructive wildfires and floods, protecting the forests we still have and restoring those we’ve lost is essential to protecting communities, supporting local economies, and giving people a say in the future of the lands they depend on. We’ll fight to keep public lands in public hands, restore the lands and waters our communities depend on, and cut the pollution that’s making these disasters worse.”

Adaptation, Disaster Resilience, & Community Preparedness

SEEC members joined panels and discussions on adaptation, disaster resilience, and community preparedness to highlight how adaptation must be a central pillar of climate action.

“Extreme weather threatens our critical infrastructure and makes life more expensive – something my neighbors in Tampa Bay know too well,” said Congresswoman Kathy Castor (FL-14). “At COP, we showed up to work with and learn from our international partners to address these shared challenges together. We’re ready to put SEEC Institute’s Thriving Economy Project into action – our blueprint to lower costs, strengthen American leadership, and make our communities safer.”

Clean Electrification, Climate Finance, and Private-Sector Competitiveness

SEEC Members engaged with experts in the clean electrification and climate finance space, and engaged with private sector voices from around the world.

“Anyone who can access electricity, heat, and transportation without burning fossil fuels not only lowers their costs, but also cuts down on pollution and helps provide a livable planet to our children and grandchildren,” said Congressman Sean Casten (IL-06). “Clean electrification is the moral and economically smart path forward for anyone interested in helping both their pocketbooks and our future. It's an imperative next step in addressing both the cost-of-living crisis and climate crisis."

Ocean, Science, & Coastal Resilience

SEEC Members participated in events related to ocean, science, and coastal resilience to highlight how the climate crisis is transforming marine ecosystems and coastal livelihoods.

“The ocean has given us time we did not earn,” said Congresswoman Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01). “It has absorbed our emissions, buffered our climate, and fed our communities. The challenge now is whether we will answer that generosity with responsibility. If we get the science right, and we get the trust right, ocean carbon removal will have a fair chance to prove itself and we will have the evidence to decide wisely. The ocean, and the communities that depend on it, deserve our best evidence and our full partnership.”

Transatlantic Industrial, Trade, and Energy Policy

SEEC Members highlighted how the U.S. and Europe must work together to transition away from fossil fuel dependence.

“The United States and Europe have a shared responsibility to lead the global transition away from fossil fuels,” said Congressman Mike Levin (CA-49). “That means working together to accelerate clean energy deployment, strengthen our economies, and reduce our dependence on fossil fuel markets. Our transatlantic partnership is essential to building a cleaner, more secure, and more affordable energy future.”

Climate Equity, Mobility, and Community Leadership

SEEC Members highlighted how the climate challenge exacerbates existing social inequities and climate solutions must expand economic opportunity, while giving communities agency in shaping their futures.

“The families with the least wealth, insurance, and political voice are hit first and recover last, from Chicago to the Horn of Africa to the Caribbean. Congress’ job is to help people stay home safely where they can, and move with dignity when they can’t,” said Congressman Jonathan Jackson (IL-01). “I am proud to lead the Congressional Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Caucus in the House of Representatives. Equity should not be a controversial topic, and I am proud to be here with you today to discuss how we can work together on equitable solutions to the climate crisis.”

Climate, Energy, and National Security

SEEC Members joined discussions on how climate resilience, clean energy deployment, and international cooperation are essential to our collective security.

“Now more than ever – it’s important to show the world that Democrats in Congress are committed to engaging with the global community to ensure that we are living up to our obligations to protect our planet and our future,” said Congresswoman Emily Randall (WA-06). “I’m grateful to bring the stories and experiences of my neighbors in Washington’s 6th district who face climate threats like coastal erosion and wildfires, and hear from other leaders and organizations that are both domestically and globally situated to help our communities achieve a climate-secure future.”

Food Security, Agricultural Innovation, and Trade

SEEC Members participated in events related to food security, agricultural innovation, and trade that spoke to solutions to help farmers adapt to the climate crisis, build more resilient food systems on a global level, and ensure that feeding the world and protecting the planet go hand in hand.

title: Boyle Announces Safe Skies Over Luxury Jets Act Following Nationwide FAA Outage
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Following last week's nationwide FAA outage that grounded flights and stranded travelers across the country, Congressman Brendan F. Boyle (PA-02), Ranking Member of the House Budget Committee and senior member of the Ways and Means Committee, today announced plans to introduce the Safe Skies Over Luxury Jets Act, legislation that would impose a federal tax on private jet purchases exceeding $1 million and use the revenue to modernize aging air traffic control technology and hire more air traffic controllers.

"Last week's nationwide FAA shutdown showed just how badly we need to modernize our aviation system," said Congressman Boyle. "If you can afford to spend millions on a luxury private jet, you can afford to pay a little more to keep our skies safe. It's time to put the safety of everyday Americans ahead of tax breaks and luxuries for billionaires.”

On November 13, a failure involving outdated FAA communications infrastructure triggered a nationwide ground stop, disrupting thousands of flights and exposing serious vulnerabilities in America's air traffic control system.

Boyle's proposed legislation would dedicate revenue from the new tax to upgrading FAA technology, modernizing air traffic control infrastructure, and recruiting and training additional air traffic controllers.

title: Boyle Introduces Ahmad Butler Pediatric Cancer Hope for a Cure Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Brendan F. Boyle (PA-02) introduced the Ahmad Butler Pediatric Cancer Hope for a Cure Act, named for Ahmad Butler, who passed away from brain cancer at 6 years old. Boyle stood alongside his constituent Latanya Morrison, Ahmad’s grandmother and founder of the Ahmad Butler Foundation, to announce the legislation.

“When I heard Latanya Morrison tell Ahmad’s story at the end of her march to Washington, I immediately told her I would introduce legislation to help children like Ahmad in the fight against childhood cancer,” said Congressman Boyle. “Congress must do more to deliver a cure for this heartbreaking disease. I hope this legislation will help ensure no one has to go through what Latanya and her family have endured.”

The Ahmad Butler Pediatric Cancer Hope for a Cure Act expands federal investment in pediatric cancer research by $2 billion over ten years, improves access to clinical trials, supports holistic and innovative therapies, and reduces the financial burden on families. Boyle first met with Latanya Morrison after her 179-mile march from Philadelphia to Washington, DC, in memory of Ahmad. Congressman Boyle has also shared Ahmad’s story with Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and urged him to declare childhood cancer a national emergency.

Boyle recently introduced a bipartisan resolution recognizing November as Lung Cancer Awareness Month and leads the bipartisan Women and Lung Cancer Research and Preventive Services Act, which would take action to study and prevent lung cancer among women. He serves on the powerful Ways and Means Committee’s Subcommittee on Health.
