title: Budzinski Statement on Future for Gateway Regional Hospital
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Nikki Budzinski (IL-13) released the following statement regarding the ongoing financial crisis at Gateway Regional Hospital, following the state’s decision to deny a bailout of the hospital’s financial mismanagement.

“The state is right to deny this proposal that fails to deliver a credible path towards stabilizing Gateway and removing it from the control of American Healthcare Systems (AHS). Illinois taxpayers should not be forced to shoulder the burden of this company’s repeated failures. The people of the Metro East deserve better.

“After the first reports of Gateway’s financial troubles and their failure to provide robust patient care, I have repeatedly pressed hospital leadership for answers, including during my visit on September 8th where leadership assured me that conditions were improving and they would pay off outstanding debts. Since that meeting, we have been met with missed deadlines, requests for extensions, and continued uncertainty. Our office operated in good faith, but time and time again, AHS has failed to provide the answers our community deserves. Most recently, employees have once again been left without their paychecks. This pattern cannot continue.

“I have fought to keep Gateway’s doors open because I know how much this hospital means to Granite City and the surrounding communities. When a hospital is at risk of closing its doors, the consequences extend far beyond the facility itself — threatening access to care, jeopardizing jobs, and leaving families uncertain about where to turn when they need help most. But unfortunately, we’ve reached a point of no return.

“It is long past time for Mike Sarian and AHS to take responsibility for the damage they have caused. To the healthcare professionals who have continued providing crucial services to our communities – despite delayed paychecks or uncertainty around your benefits – thank you. My office will continue working with state and local partners to ensure our community will have care options and not be left behind.”

title: Burlison Names UAP Whistleblower Jake Barber Senior Adviser
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Eric Burlison (MO-07) announced today that U.S. Air Force Veteran and UAP whistleblower Jake Barber has joined his office as a senior adviser on unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP).

Barber brings experience in military aviation, special operations, and defense contracting. In January 2025, he came forward publicly with firsthand accounts of UAP-recovery operations.

“Jake brings firsthand experience and an investigative background that will strengthen our efforts to get answers,” said Congressman Burlison. “President Trump has opened the door to greater transparency, and Congress needs to keep pushing. We have an opportunity to follow the evidence and uncover information the American people deserve to see.”

Barber will assist with congressional investigations, witness engagement, and efforts to independently verify UAP-related evidence.

“Testimony is evidence. It helps us understand where to look and what questions to ask,” said Barber. “But our goal is to build on that testimony with technical measurements, multiple independent observations, and reliable documentation. We're interested in evidence that can stand on its own.”

His appointment comes amid President Trump's ongoing disclosure efforts through the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters (PURSUE), which has resulted in the release of hundreds of government records.

Burlison is also working to advance his UAP Disclosure Act, which passed the House as part of the fiscal year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. The legislation would establish an independent review board to oversee the preservation and release of government UAP records.

title: Carbajal, Garamendi Announce DHS Will Not Use Cal Poly Maritime Academy Ship for Mass Deportations
text:
This week, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) confirmed to U.S. Representative Salud Carbajal (D-CA-24), top Democrat of the House Subcommittee on Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation, and U.S. Representative John Garamendi (D-CA-08) that it will not use ships, including training vessels or private foreign ships, for deportations.

This confirmation comes after Carbajal and Garamendi sent a letter demanding the agency abandon its proposal to use maritime vessels for mass deportations. The Congressmen sent the letter following New York Times reporting that revealed DHS considered using ships for mass deportations and identified Cal Poly Maritime Academy’s training ship, the Golden Bear, as a possible deportation vessel.

“While this commitment from DHS is a major victory for the Central Coast and congressional oversight, our work is not done. We must continue to hold the Trump Administration accountable for its extreme immigration enforcement and mass deportation agenda,” said Rep. Carbajal, the top Democrat on the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee and a Senior Member of the Armed Services Committee. “When Congressman Garamendi and I spoke out against the Trump administration’s plan to use maritime vessels—including the Cal Poly Maritime Academy’s Golden Bear—for deportations, they had no choice but to back down. This is a major win for accountability, but we cannot let up. I will continue pressing DHS for answers, closely monitoring its actions, and pushing back against policies that undermine due process and put people’s safety and rights at risk.”

“When Congressman Carbajal and I said that Donald Trump, Markwayne Mullin, and ICE will never use the Golden Bear or any ship for their mass deportation agenda, we meant it,” said Rep. Garamendi. “Today, I’m proud to announce the Department of Homeland Security has confirmed that it will not use any ship, including training vessels or private or foreign ships, for deportations. This isn’t the final step; we will continue to use our oversight powers to make sure Trump’s DHS keeps its word. I’m glad to stand with Congressman Carbajal on this issue, and I will continue to stand with him and every member of Congress to hold the Trump Administration to account.”

The Department of Homeland Security’s response can be found HERE.

Carbajal and Garamendi’s original letter can be found HERE.

Background

Carbajal is a leader in fighting the Trump administration’s extreme immigration policies.

In October 2026, Carbajal visited the Santa Maria ICE facility — marking his third visit since 2025 — as part of his ongoing investigation into the recent surge in ICE activity on the Central Coast. In the same month, the Congressman demanded a full investigation into the October 21 detention and injury of 20-year-old Erik Zepeda, a U.S. citizen and Santa Maria High School student with disabilities who was tackled, restrained, and questioned by ICE agents while walking to school. Zepeda was hospitalized and underwent surgery for wrist injuries sustained during the wrongful detainment.

Carbajal visited the Adelanto ICE processing facility in May 2026 to meet with detainees, three of whom are Central Coast constituents. The Congressman also assessed conditions in the facility and inquired about the reported deaths of detainees.

Carbajal is a co-sponsor of the No Secret Police Act, which would require law enforcement officers and agents of DHS engaged in border security and civil immigration enforcement to clearly display identification and insignia when detaining or arresting individuals and to ban them from using home-made, non-tactical masks.

title: Select Committee Democrats Call on Trump to Uphold U.S. Interests and Values in Meeting with Xi and Putin
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Ranking Member Ro Khanna (CA-17) of the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (CCP), alongside Committee Democratic Members Representatives Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Shontel Brown (OH-11), André Carson (IN-07), Kathy Castor (FL-14), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Greg Stanton (AZ-04) Tom Suozzi (NY-03), and Ritchie Torres (NY-15) issued the following statement ahead of President Trump’s Thursday meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China:

“As Members of the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, we strongly urge President Trump to stand up for American interests and democratic values in Thursday’s meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

President Trump must make clear that American workers, manufacturers, and security will not be sacrificed to advance the interests of Beijing or Moscow. Concerning AI, it is vitally important that the U.S. leads the conversation on an AI treaty that establishes clear guardrails to reduce the risk of conflict, prevent the misuse of advanced AI systems, and promote transparency while preserving American technological leadership.

President Trump should use this opportunity to directly address China’s enabling of Russia’s illegal war in Ukraine and demand the two leaders cease their military, economic, and gray-zone coercion of U.S. allies and partners in the Indo-Pacific and Europe. The security of Taiwan’s people must under no circumstance be a bargaining chip. Similarly, the future of Ukraine must not be discussed without Ukrainians at the table.

Meanwhile, we urge President Trump to call for the release of Americans unjustly imprisoned in both countries and for the humane treatment of political prisoners. Xi must immediately end the CCP’s ongoing genocide against the Uyghur people and reverse its inhumane policies.”

title: Castro Pushes For Release Of El Paso Family From Dilley Trailer Prison
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) released the following statement:

“Last night, Michell Germán’s classmates rallied at El Paso High for her and her family's release from the Dilley Trailer Prison.

“Michell and her 11-year-old sister, Paola, are beloved and bright young girls who belong in school with their friends, not locked away.

“They are asylum seekers who have done nothing wrong. I joined Rep. Veronica Escobar’s in demanding ICE release the family and bring them home to El Paso.”

Background:

Congressman Castro joined Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) and other house Democrats in a letter to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Director David Venturella urging them to release the Guerrero-Germán family from the Dilley Trailer Prison. Read the full letter here.

The Guerrero-Germán family came to the United States from Venezuela in 2022 as asylum seekers and settled in El Paso, Texas. Both parents hold work permits and have an affirmative asylum case. Michell and her 11-year-old sister, Paola, were detained on their way to school with their father, Pablo Jose Guerrero-Pimentel on October 22, 2026. Their mother, Dolores Emilia Zarraga Colina, is also detained at the Dilley Trailer Prison.

Read previous statements from Castro here and here. Castro met with the family at the Dilley Trailer Prison on October 30, 2026.

title: Opening statement of Co-Chairman Smith at hearing on Christian persecutionWorldwide Persecution of Christians: Responding to New Challenges
text:
The following are excerpts of Co-Chairman Chris Smith’s (R-NJ) opening statement at the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission’s November 18th hearing, entitled “Worldwide Persecution of Christians: Responding to New Challenges”:

This hearing—“Worldwide Persecution of Christians: Responding to New Challenges”—will come to order.

In February of 1996, I chaired a hearing—the first of many—called “The Persecution of Christians Worldwide,” and our witnesses, then, as now, focused on pervasive discrimination, torture and death to believers.

The cruelty and hate must be rigorously exposed, confronted and combatted.

So, I want to thank our distinguished witnesses for their extraordinary commitment to protecting Christians—and other people of faith—from abuse.

We can—and must—do more.

In the United States, religious freedom is often called our first freedom. The First Amendment protects the free exercise of religion, and the Declaration of Independence reminds us that all human beings are endowed by their Creator with certain unalienable rights.

Religious freedom is a universal human right. It belongs to every person, everywhere, regardless of faith or belief. But, there are good reasons to examine the persecution of Christians separately and in some depth. Last year, we held a hearing examining the “Worldwide Persecution of Jews”—because antisemitism is a unique spiritual disease.

One of the things most immediately striking about the persecution of Christians is the geographical scope and scale of persecution. Christians are among the most widely dispersed religious communities in the world. They are also among the most widely persecuted. They face severe persecution in a very large number of countries, and on every continent.

The perpetrators and sources of this persecution are extraordinarily diverse: adherents of other religions, often mobilized by extremist or majoritarian movements; authoritarian and totalitarian states seeking to subordinate religious institutions and independent belief to political power; hostile societies that marginalize, intimidate, or attack Christian minorities as “outsiders” to a national community, which the persecutors demand must be religiously homogeneous; and non-state actors, including terrorist organizations, militias, and criminal networks.

Nor are the threats confined to places traditionally associated with religious extremism or authoritarian rule. Increasingly, Christians also encounter restrictions in ostensibly neutral, liberal states, where laws and regulations ostensibly designed to serve other purposes can be used to restrict religious expression, worship, and the exercise of conscience.

These different forms of persecution should not be trivialized or ignored. The murder of Christians by armed militants, the imprisonment of pastors by an authoritarian government, the forced displacement of ancient Christian communities, and the prosecution or censorship of peaceful religious expression in a liberal democracy are not the same phenomenon. But each presents a serious challenge to the freedom of Christians to live and practice their faith.

The numbers alone convey something of the magnitude. According to Open Doors’ 2026 World Watch List, more than 388 million Christians worldwide face high levels of persecution and discrimination because of their faith— that’s more than one in seven of the world’s Christians. And this horrific problem is not confined to a handful of countries or a single region. It is a global challenge, and one that demands a response informed by an understanding of its different causes and manifestations.

Last week, on November 12, I chaired a hearing examining Nigeria's egregiously flawed and inadequate efforts to protect Christians and secure the Middle Belt, where Christian communities continue to suffer killings, kidnappings, attacks on churches, and forced displacement.

On September 22, I chaired a hearing of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China (CECC) examining the Chinese Communist Party’s repression of prisoners, families, and religious communities, including Christians.

These hearings addressed particular situations. Today’s hearing looks at the situation from a global perspective and asks our witnesses to discern new threats to Christians—and which responses or tools are working or should be tried to defend Christians.

There are several developments that merit particular attention. In parts of Africa, radical Islamist organizations and armed militias continue to attack Christian communities, while weak governance and the failure of authorities to provide effective protection leave vulnerable populations exposed.

In the Middle East, political upheaval and the expansion of regional powers have placed historic Christian communities under renewed pressure. In the Caucasus, the survival and independence of Christian institutions have become entangled in broader geopolitical struggles. And in Europe and elsewhere, new regulatory and censorship regimes raise questions about the future of religious expression and the ability of Christians to live according to their convictions.

These developments also remind us that persecution does not always take the form of overt violence. Sometimes it proceeds through the gradual erosion of a community’s ability to sustain its religious institutions, educate its children, worship freely, and maintain its presence in the places where its members have lived for generations.

A community can be driven out not only by bullets and bombs, but also by intimidation, discrimination, coercion, and the cumulative effects of official restrictions.

This is why the focus of today’s hearing emphasizes responding to new challenges. We need to understand not only where persecution is occurring, but how it is changing.

Are new actors becoming involved? Are established forms of repression being supplemented by new methods of surveillance, censorship, and social control? How are geopolitical rivalries and regional ambitions affecting the security of Christian communities? And what can churches, humanitarian organizations, civil society, foreign governments, and the United States do to respond effectively?

The United States has a range of tools at its disposal: diplomacy, international religious freedom reporting and designations, humanitarian assistance, support for displaced communities, engagement with governments and religious leaders, and, where appropriate, legislation and other measures. But these tools must be adapted to the circumstances. What works in one setting may be ineffective in another.

We should be prepared to learn from organizations working directly with persecuted communities, from those documenting developments on the ground, and from those examining the legal and political dimensions of these challenges.

Our witnesses are an extraordinarily distinguished group, who have worked for many years to defend people persecuted for their faith. I have known some of them for decades, and my own legislative work has drawn on their courage and tenacity in visiting the imprisoned and threatened, searching for the missing, and ransoming the enslaved. Their courage is extraordinary, and their determination to preserve their faith and communities deserves our attention and support.

Forty-six years ago, during my first term in the Congress, I read a book entitled “Tortured for Christ” by the Reverend Richard Wurmbrand, a Romanian evangelical minister. In it, he detailed the horrific, agonizing 14-year ordeal that he endured for his faith in Christ during Ceausescu’s brutal dictatorship in Romania.

He said, and I quote, “the underground church is a poor and a suffering church, but it has no lukewarm members.” I have found, and I know members of our panel have found, that throughout the world, there are no lukewarm members when it comes to the underground churches. Wurmbrand said, “The message I bring out of the Underground Church is: ‘Don’t abandon us! Don’t forget us! Don’t write us off!’”

title: Reps. Chu, Scott Reintroduce POWER Act to Protect Workers’ Rights
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Reps. Judy Chu (CA-28) and Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03) reintroduced the Protecting Our Workers from Exploitation and Retaliation (POWER) Act. The bill would take critical steps toward creating a safe and just workplace for all workers in America by providing temporary protection against deportation for immigrant workers who exercise their rights under existing labor and employment laws.

These protections are needed now more than ever. Earlier this year, the Department of Labor confirmed that its memorandum of understanding with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), in place since 2011 to generally keep immigration enforcement out of workplaces under active labor investigation, is no longer in effect. This follows the Trump administration’s 2025 termination of Deferred Action for Labor Enforcement, a 2023 program that offered temporary protection from deportation to workers who reported abuses and cooperated with investigations. Without these safeguards, workers who report abuse or unsafe conditions are vulnerable to immigration-related employer retaliation.

“Immigrant workers are essential to our economy, yet some employers still use the threat of deportation to silence them when they try to report wage theft, unsafe conditions, harassment, or other illegal employment practices,” said Rep. Chu. “The Trump administration recently terminated a longstanding program that had protected workers who spoke up, leaving them with nowhere to turn. Allowing abusive employers to evade accountability undermines working conditions for all workers in this country. That is why I am proud to reintroduce the POWER Act with Ranking Member Scott. No one worker should have to choose between standing up for their rights and risking deportation. When immigrant workers can report abuse without fear of retaliation, we make workplaces safer and fairer for everyone.”

"The POWER Act will strengthen protections for workers and ensure that corrupt employers are brought to justice for labor violations,” said Rep. Scott. “This bill is an important step forward in making sure that workers can fully realize their rights on the job and do not have to live in fear while trying to make a living. Employers should never be able to use the threat of deportation to retaliate against, intimidate, or punish employees for exercising their rights."

"The AFL-CIO has long supported the POWER Act to provide explicit protections to workers who help lift standards for all of us by taking action to defend our labor laws. This bill takes on new urgency in the context of the mass deportation agenda, which has created an environment of impunity for abusive employers," said Shannon Lederer, director of Immigration Policy for AFL-CIO. "Working people are ready to stand up and fight back against wage theft, discrimination, union busting, unsafe workplaces, and other egregious labor violations. The POWER Act will help us do that, together, and it needs to be a part of any sensible reform package."

“Immigrant workers too often risk retaliation when they assert their rights on the job or organize for better working conditions alongside their colleagues – especially now, as this administration wages a vicious campaign of fear and cruelty against immigrant communities. The POWER Act would help create safer workplaces and help all workers hold abusive employers accountable. We thank Representatives Chu and Scott for their leadership in introducing the POWER Act, and we urge Congress to swiftly pass this crucial bill,” said Kica Matos, president of the National Immigration Law Center.

"No worker should have to choose between speaking out against workplace abuse and risking immigration enforcement,” said Rebecca Dixon, president and CEO of the National Employment Law Project. “The POWER Act would protect immigrant workers from retaliation and strengthen enforcement of workplace laws for everyone."

“The only way to truly protect all workers from wage theft, unsafe workplaces and other abuses is to allow all workers to freely exercise their democratic rights in the workplace, which is the core purpose of the POWER Act,” said Erica Smiley, executive director of Jobs with Justice.

The POWER Act would:

Expand U-Visa Eligibility for Workers Who Experience Serious Labor Violations. The POWER Act would expand U-visa eligibility for workers who come forward to report or assist in investigating serious workplace violations and who have suffered substantial abuse or harm related to the workplace claim or would face extreme hardship upon removal.

Provide Temporary Protection and Work Authorization for Workers Who Come Forward. The bill would allow federal, state, or local law enforcement officials, labor officials, and worker protection agencies to ask the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to provide temporary lawful status with employment authorization to workers who have filed a workplace claim or are material witnesses in any pending or anticipated workplace claim.

Strengthen Labor Agencies’ Investigative Powers. When DHS conducts a worksite enforcement action where (1) a workplace claim has been filed or (2) the action resulted from information provided to DHS in retaliation against workers exercising their labor rights, the bill would require DHS to notify the appropriate labor agency and give it an opportunity to interview workers who are victims of or material witnesses to workplace violations before those workers can be removed.

Hold Employers Responsible for Labor Law Violations. The bill would provide workers in removal proceedings with a stay of removal and employment authorization if they have filed a workplace claim, are a material witness in certain workplace or civil claims, or have applied for U-visa relief. These protections would remain in place until the workplace claim is resolved or U-visa relief is finally denied, whichever is later.

Remove the Caps on U visas. There is a backlog of almost 240,000 U-visa applicants because only 10,000 visas are available annually. This bill would remove this limitation and expand the time frame for stays of removal while the U-visa petition is pending. It also waives the expensive fees for U-visa applicants.

The bill is cosponsored by Reps. Becca Balint (VT-AL), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Danny Davis (IL-07), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Dina Titus (NV-01), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Juan Vargas (CA-52), and Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25).

The bill is endorsed by AFL-CIO, National Immigration Law Center (NILC), National Employment Law Project (NELP), and Service Employees International Union (SEIU), and Jobs With Justice (JWJ).

title: Higgins Leads Oversight Hearing Exposing Unconstitutional ATF Gun Registry
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Clay Higgins (R-LA), Chairman of the Federal Law Enforcement Subcommittee of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, led a hearing today titled “Oversight of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives’ Out-of-Business Records Retention Practices.” The hearing examined how the ATF stores and uses sales records turned over by legal firearms dealers, and whether these records have become an unconstitutional and illegal gun registry.

In his opening remarks, Subcommittee Chairman Higgins said: “Searching by name is a function that ATF has simply turned off from its tech to remain compliant with federal law. Could just as easily be turned on. Think about that impact. The difference between this database and an illegal national gun registry may come down to a software setting that the ATF itself controls.”

Watch his full opening remarks here.

During questioning, Subcommittee Chairman Higgins pressed witnesses on whether ATF digital records could be configured to be searchable by name. After witnesses answered in the affirmative, Subcommittee Chairman Higgins mentioned that the list is “precariously close to being an illegal federal registry.”

Watch his full questioning here.

In his closing remarks, Subcommittee Chairman Higgins said: “The Second Amendment is an inalienable right, and the federal law, long-standing, prohibits the establishment of a registry of legally owned firearms. This is fact. It’s also fact that the seizure of weapons and the components of light weaponry was the decisive catalyst that led to the armed conflict of the American Revolution. It was asked earlier, who are we protecting? We are protecting the entire Republic, the very foundation upon which our Republic stands when we defend individual rights, liberties, and freedoms, and Constitutional protections, and to guard against those individual rights, liberties, and Constitutional protections, we must explore whether federal government is encroaching upon the Citizenry’s daily life, and we must identify a potential threat, especially in a massive form.”

title: Quindaro Townsite National Historic Landmark Act Passes out of Natural Resources Committee
text:
(Washington, D.C.) – Today, the Quindaro Townsite National Historic Landmark Act, introduced by U.S. Representatives Emanuel Cleaver, II (D-MO), Sharice Davids (D-KS), and Derek Schmidt (R-KS), was passed out of the House Committee on Natural Resources. The bipartisan legislation would designate the Quindaro Townsite in Kansas City, Kansas, as a National Historic Landmark. The site served as a critical entry point for anti-slavery settlers and a sanctuary for those escaping bondage via the Underground Railroad prior to and during the U.S. Civil War.

“Today, we took another step forward in our effort to preserve the Quindaro Townsite and the important history that deserves to be shared with the generations of Americans still to come,” said Congressman Cleaver. “I’m thankful to my colleagues on the Natural Resources Committee for moving this bipartisan bill forward in the legislative process, and I look forward to the legislation receiving a vote in the full House of Representatives.”

“Quindaro is an important part of Kansas history and our nation’s story,” said Congressman Schmidt. “Its legacy of courage, freedom, and determination deserves to be recognized and preserved for future generations. The National Historic Landmarks Committee has already unanimously recommended this designation, and I’m pleased our legislation has passed through committee and I look forward to it getting a House vote soon.”

“Granting Quindaro national landmark status is well past due. From helping freedom seekers on the Underground Railroad to its historic connection with the Wyandot Nation, Quindaro is central to who we are in Kansas City. Today’s hearing moves our legislation forward so we can cut through bureaucratic delays and safeguard this history for our children and grandchildren,” said Rep. Sharice Davids.

National Historic Landmarks are designated through the National Park Service System Advisory Board or an official act of Congress. Last May, the National Historic Landmarks Committee unanimously recommended Quindaro Townsite for designation as a National Historic Landmark, however the administrative process has since stalled. This bill would bypass the administrative process and designate the site by congressional action.

Representatives Cleaver and Davids submitted a letter to the House Committee on Natural Resources in support of the bipartisan legislation. The official letter is available here.

Official text of the Quindaro Townsite National Historic Landmark Act is available here.

Emanuel Cleaver, II is the U.S. Representative for Missouri's Fifth Congressional District, which includes Kansas City, Independence, Lee's Summit, Raytown, Grandview, Sugar Creek, Greenwood, Blue Springs, North Kansas City, Gladstone, and Claycomo. He is a member of the exclusive House Financial Services Committee and Ranking Member of the House Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance.

title: Cline Elected Chairman of the Republican Study Committee
text:

Cline previously served as the Chairman of the RSC Budget Taskforce in the 118th and as the Vice Chair of the Caucus in the 119th Congress.

I do not take this responsibility lightly, and I remain committed to advancing the principles that make our Nation strong and preserve the American Dream for generations to come. The RSC has been shaped by the dedication and leadership of those who came before, and I am proud to build upon that legacy. I want to thank Chairman Pfluger for his outstanding leadership over the past two years and for the lasting impact he has made on this Caucus and our Nation.

title: Ark Valley Voice: Crow Calls for Action to Ban Stock Trading by Members of Congress
text:
Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), Co-Chair of the End Corruption Caucus, is calling for action to ban stock trading by members of Congress in the new Democratic majority.

“Americans, right, left, and center, are fed up with a system that’s captured by corporate lobbyists, with a system that’s captured by super PACs, with a system that over and over again, shows that it can’t do the big things that Americans overwhelmingly support because of the chokehold of corporate money and lobbyist money on this town,” said Congressman Crow.

He added:

“There are many things that members of Congress can just do today to show they will walk the talk,” Crow said. “That’s why 57 incoming members and I have taken the Political Integrity Pledge to refuse corporate PAC money, to push for a ban on stock trading by Members of Congress, to ban lobbying by former Members of Congress for at least five years, and to support the overturning of Citizens United… We can do those things when we start the 120th Congress. We are dedicated and committed to pushing leadership, to pushing our colleagues, and to making sure communities back home know that we represent them and not the special interests.

“We will not accept no for an answer on this.”

Crow does not own or trade stocks and has never taken a dime of corporate PAC money. He is the only sitting member of Colorado’s Congressional delegation to take the Political Integrity Pledge to refuse corporate PAC money and support efforts to ban stock trading by members of Congress, institute a five-year lobbying ban on former members of Congress, and push for the overturning of Citizens United.

He is also the only sitting member of Colorado’s Congressional delegation to take the Unrig Washington pledge to refuse corporate PAC money and support efforts to crack down on dark money and ban stock trading by members of Congress.

Crow is an original cosponsor of the TRUST in Congress Act to ban members of Congress and their families from owning or trading stocks. He has led outreach to House leadership urging them to ban stock trading for high-ranking government officials and ban members of Congress and their staff from insider trading on prediction markets.

Crow is leading the fight to root out corruption in our elections, including through his End Dark Money Act to crack down on dark money’s influence on U.S. elections and his SHINE Act to limit the creation of shady pop-up PACs just before an election.

title: Davids Joins Flight 5342 Victims’ Families at Capitol to Demand Passage of Bipartisan Aviation Safety Bill
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, Representative Sharice Davids (KS-03) joined more than 20 family members of the victims of Flight 5342, safety professionals, and a bipartisan coalition of lawmakers — including Senator Jerry Moran (R-KS) and U.S. Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy — to urge immediate action on aviation safety legislation. The event marked more than 22 months since the tragic midair collision involving Flight 5342, which claimed 67 lives, including Kansans.

“Flight 5342 was carrying neighbors, friends, and loved ones from Kansas to Washington — 67 lives that should still be here today. For nearly two years, you all have turned unimaginable grief into a mission to make sure no other family ever has to endure this kind of loss,” Davids said during today’s press conference. “I am glad to join Secretary Duffy here today because aviation safety isn’t a Democratic issue or a Republican issue — it’s a human issue. The House and the Senate have both passed strong safety measures, and there is no excuse for letting the clock run out on this year without finishing the job. We need to come together, take the very best parts of both bills, and get this legislation across the finish line immediately. These families cannot wait another year, and they shouldn't have to repeatedly ask for Congress to protect the flying public.”

WATCH: Davids speaks during yesterday’s press conference

On January 29, 2025, Flight 5342 departed Wichita, KS (ICT), bound for Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA). As the flight approached its destination, it collided midair with a military training helicopter, tragically killing the two pilots, two flight attendants, and 60 passengers on the airplane, along with all three crew members aboard the helicopter.

During yesterday’s gathering, families and supporters formed a human airplane around 67 empty chairs on the Capitol lawn to call on House and Senate leaders to reconcile and pass comprehensive aviation safety reforms before the current Congress adjourns.

Earlier this year, the U.S. House passed Davids’ ALERT Act, bipartisan legislation she introduced to reduce the risk of future tragedies. The bill, which is supported by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), would upgrade aircraft collision warning systems, strengthen air traffic controller training, improve airspace communication, review airspace congestion and airport capacity, and enhance military aviation safety.

Davids also voted to support the Rotorcraft Operations Transparency and Oversight Reform (ROTOR) Act – a bipartisan bill aimed at improving aviation safety standards. Although it failed to pass the U.S. House, it is supported by the victims’ families and safety professionals. Davids is working to bring the strongest provisions of both bills together and get commonsense aviation safety reforms signed into law.

WATCH: Davids speaks on the U.S. House Floor about the impact of her ALERT Act

Following the tragic collision, Davids has taken several additional steps to improve aviation safety and honor the lives lost:

Met with the victims’ families in Wichita and pledged to be a voice for transparency and reform in the investigation.

Pressed FAA and NTSB experts in a U.S. Transportation and Infrastructure Committee hearing on air traffic controller shortages and safety protocols.

Toured the Olathe Air Traffic Control Center to highlight critical staffing needs and renew her call for increased investments in aviation safety infrastructure.

Responded to initial NTSB recommendations with a commitment to act on any legislative fixes needed to keep passengers and crew safe.

Pledged to act on recommendations from an initial NTSB investigative hearing on the tragic midair collision.

Honored the one-year anniversary by submitting a statement into the Congressional Record pledging continued action to prevent future tragedies.

title: Deluzio Celebrates Launch of Second Daily Amtrak Service, Better Connecting Pittsburgh to the Commonwealth and Beyond
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17) celebrated the launch of Amtrak’s new, second daily train on the Pennsylvanian route, which connects Pittsburgh to New York City via stops in places across Pennsylvania to Philadelphia. The second Pennsylvanian train begins service on November 18th, 2026.

“Three years ago, I was thrilled to announce this more than $143 million federal investment in Pennsylvania’s long-neglected passenger rail service,” said Congressman Deluzio. “Today, I am proud to celebrate the start of this long-awaited second daily train connecting Pittsburgh and Philadelphia—and the Pennsylvania communities in between. This is a big win, but the fight is not over. I want world-leading high-speed trains across our Commonwealth and across America.”

“Today marks an exciting milestone for passenger rail in Pennsylvania,” said Rob Gleason, Amtrak Board Member and Chair of the System Growth Committee. “The second daily Pennsylvanian gives our customers more choices and greater flexibility while strengthening connections between communities across the Commonwealth. We’re proud of what Amtrak, PennDOT, and our partners have accomplished together to make this expanded service a reality.”

Back in December 2023, Congressman Deluzio helped announce a $143,629,028 federal grant from the Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) to the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation (PennDOT) to expand Amtrak passenger rail service on the Keystone West Corridor—specifically for a second daily round-trip between Pittsburgh and Harrisburg. This funding was from the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act of 2021.

title: House Passes Johnson’s Rural Water Bills
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, the House unanimously passed U.S. Representative Dusty Johnson’s (R-S.D.) legislation that moves forward three South Dakota rural water projects. The South Dakota Water Feasibility Studies Act directs the Department of the Interior to conduct a feasibility study for each of the Lewis and Clark, Dakota Mainstem, and Western Dakota regional water systems.

“Water is an essential resource, and as South Dakota continues to grow, we will need more of it,” said Johnson. “I’m proud to support the Lewis and Clark, Dakota Mainstem, and Western Dakota projects which are working hard to ensure there will be ample water to for our future communities, businesses, and families. I hope the Senate passes this important legislation soon.”

“Reliable water supplies are essential to families, farms and growing communities throughout South Dakota,” said House Committee on Natural Resources Chairman Bruce Westerman. “H.R. 9785 directs the Department of the Interior to evaluate three proposed projects that could deliver municipal, rural and industrial water across the region. I commend Rep. Johnson for giving local leaders the information they need to make responsible decisions and plan for South Dakota’s long-term water needs.”

The Lewis and Clark Regional Water System Expansion Feasibility Study Act authorizes the Bureau of Reclamation to carry out a feasibility study for a proposed drinking water project drawing from the Missouri River. This project would support Lewis and Clark Regional Water System’s efforts to supply drinking water to 350,000 people in southeast South Dakota, northwest Iowa, and southwest Minnesota. Click here for bill text. Click here for Johnson’s remarks.

The Dakota Mainstem Water Supply Project Feasibility Study Act authorizes the Bureau of Reclamation to carry out a feasibility study for a proposed water project drawing from the Missouri River to supplement local supplies and address long-term water scarcity and quality challenges. This project will help Dakota Mainstem support more than 50 water providers in South Dakota, Iowa, Minnesota, and Nebraska. Click here for bill text. Click here for Johnson’s remarks.

title: Congresswoman Escobar Announces Over 50 Supporters in Congress for the Dignity Act
text:
Today, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) announced that her bipartisan, comprehensive immigration reform bill, the Dignity Act, now had over 50 supporters in the United States House of Representatives.

“The Dignity Act of 2025 now has bipartisan support from over 50 members of Congress from every faction of the two major political parties,” said Congresswoman Escobar. “I’m grateful for the growing support for common sense solutions among my colleagues. Bipartisan immigration reform has been my top priority - and will remain so until Congress finally modernizes this very broken, outdated system.”

Last week, Congresswoman Escobar announced her intention to reintroduce the Dignity Act next Congress with changes to reflect the incoming Democratic majorities in the House of Representatives and the Senate.

title: CONGRESSMAN CLEO FIELDS CELEBRATES HISTORIC NOMINATION OF DEMOCRATIC LEADER HAKEEM JEFFRIES FOR SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Congressman Cleo Fields (LA-06) released the following statement today following the House Democratic Caucus’ historic nomination of Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries to serve as the next Speaker of the United States House of Representatives. “I am elated that the House Democratic Caucus has nominated my good friend and colleague, Hakeem Jeffries, to serve as the next Speaker of the United States House of Representatives. This is a historic occasion for the entire nation. In the nearly 250-year history of this country, not one, single African American has ever served as Speaker of the House. We now stand at the threshold of changing that.

I’ve had the privilege of serving alongside Leader Jeffries in this 119th Congress. I have tremendous respect for his leadership, his judgment, and his commitment to the American people. He has earned the confidence of his colleagues, and I believe, without a shadow of a doubt, he is well prepared to lead the United States House of Representatives at this important time in our nation’s history.

The significance of this moment should not be lost on any of us. It speaks to the progress we have made as a nation, and this is indeed a great day in America.

I proudly congratulate Leader Jeffries on this historic nomination to become Speaker of the 120th Congress of the United States House of Representatives.”

title: Rep. Fitzgerald’s Bill Authorizing Wisconsin Memorials at National Battlefields Passes House Natural Resources Committee
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Scott Fitzgerald’s (WI-05) legislation authorizing memorials at Antietam National Battlefield and Manassas National Battlefield Park to recognize the service and sacrifice of the Second, Third, Fifth, Sixth, and Seventh Wisconsin Infantry Regiments during the Civil War passed the House Natural Resources Committee today.

“Wisconsin soldiers fought with extraordinary courage and made tremendous sacrifices in some of the bloodiest battles of the Civil War. Their service deserves to be remembered and honored for generations to come,” said Congressman Scott Fitzgerald. “The House Natural Resources Committee’s passage of this legislation brings us one step closer to fulfilling work that began more than a century ago to establish these memorials and ensure their legacy is never forgotten. I thank Chairman Westerman for bringing this bill before the Natural Resources Committee and my colleagues for their support.”

“Wisconsin infantry officers and enlisted men fought bravely at the Battles of Antietam and the Second Bull Run,” said Chairman Bruce Westerman. “I applaud Rep. Fitzgerald for leading H.R. 7495 to honor these soldiers so their service and sacrifice during the Civil War will be remembered throughout history.”

BACKGROUND: In August 1862, General Stonewall Jackson and Confederate forces surrounded Union General John Pope and his men on their return to Washington. Among the Union units were the Second, Sixth, and Seventh Wisconsin Infantry Regiments. As the Union troops advanced toward Gainesville, Wisconsin’s Second Regiment was brought under fire by an enemy artillery battery. Despite being severely outnumbered, the Second regiment charged the Confederate troops before later being supported by the Seventh and Sixth regiments. After hours of fighting and standing firm, Union leaders ordered the men back. Devastatingly, 515 men from Wisconsin who entered the fight had been killed, wounded, or remained missing.

Later, on September 17, 1862, the Battle of Antietam stopped the Confederate Army’s first invasion of the North and helped give President Lincoln confidence to issue the Emancipation Proclamation mere days after the battle. Among the brave soldiers who fought in the deadliest one-day battle in American military history were officers and enlisted men from the Second, Third, Fifth, Sixth, and Seventh Wisconsin Infantry Regiments. Four of these regiments fought in the cornfield at Antietam, while the Fifth regiment was held in reserve to support artillery efforts. Together, men from these regiments paid the ultimate price and suffered great loss, with over 500 killed, wounded, or missing after the battle.

To honor the bravery and sacrifice of these men, the Wisconsin Legislature authorized a monument commission in 1913 to explore constructing a monument at the Antietam and Manassas Battlefields. Unfortunately, this effort never came to fruition. Over a century after the effort began to honor these men, it’s time to make this unkept promise a reality.

COSPONSORS: Congressman Bryan Steil (WI-01), Congressman Derrick Van Orden (WI-03), Congressman Glenn Grothman (WI-06), Congressman Tom Tiffany (WI-07), Congressman Tony Wied (WI-08), Congressman Mark Pocan (WI-02), and Congresswoman Gwen Moore (WI-04).

title: Fong, Gottheimer Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen U.S. Cybersecurity
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressmen Vince Fong (CA-20) and Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05) introduced H.R. 11055, the Bridging Resources for Innovative Defense and Government Expertise in Artificial Intelligence (BRIDGE AI) Act. This bipartisan legislation would authorize the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to collaborate with experienced private-sector artificial intelligence (AI) professionals to better defend U.S. critical infrastructure.

“Communities and critical industries across the country are trying to keep up with the surge in AI-driven cyberattacks that steal sensitive data and disrupt operations,” said Congressman Fong. “In the Central Valley, cyberattacks have increasingly targeted schools, hospitals, and water systems, threatening the critical services our communities depend on. These attacks are becoming more frequent and sophisticated. These threats are real, and they aren’t waiting for the government to catch up. By bringing in AI and emerging technology specialists from the private sector, the BRIDGE AI Act ensures our nation’s cybersecurity experts receive the additional tools and expertise needed to modernize our systems, address vulnerabilities, and protect the essential services Americans rely on.”

“Our adversaries are using AI to attack our networks faster than ever, and CISA, the agency on the front lines of defending them, doesn’t have enough capacity to keep pace,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “The BRIDGE AI Act is a commonsense, bipartisan fix that gives CISA a fast way to bring in the best AI and tech minds to hunt down intruders, patch vulnerabilities, and stress-test AI tools before they are exploited. Protecting our families, our water systems, and our national security shouldn’t be a partisan issue, and I’m proud to partner with Congressman Fong to get this done.”

Specifically, the bill:

Creates a mission-focused pilot program for 75 - 125 private-sector professionals to serve within CISA.

Supports structured knowledge transfer so that career CISA employees gain advanced AI expertise.

Ensures rigorous ethics and conflict of interest safeguards.

Requires a semiannual report to Congress on program status, participation, and recommendations for improvement.

Background

CISA leads national efforts to defend against emerging cyber threats by working with federal agencies, state, local, tribal, and territorial governments, and private-sector partners to protect America’s 16 critical infrastructure sectors.

In April, Congressman Fong hosted a cybersecurity roundtable with Homeland Security Committee Chairman Andrew Garbarino, CISA, regional military installations, local officials, and infrastructure sectors. The discussion focused on current, existing, and future cybersecurity challenges facing the Central Valley, developing a local workforce ready to combat cybersecurity threats, and protecting utility providers, local governments, and their infrastructure from cyberattacks. You can learn more about the roundtable here.

Recent examples highlighting how the cyber threat environment is escalating include:

February 2026: A ransomware attack on the University of Mississippi Medical Center (UMMC) forced the closure of all 35 clinic locations statewide and the cancellation of scheduled appointments and elective surgeries. The attack took down UMMC's IT network, including its EPIC electronic medical records system.

May 2026: Instructure, the provider of the popular Canvas education system, suffered a massive data breach orchestrated by the ShinyHunters cybercriminal group. The historic breach exposed student names, IDs, and private communications, ultimately forcing Instructure to pay a ransom to prevent a catastrophic data leak.

July 2026: A suspected Iran-linked cyber group, CyberAv3ngers, executed a wave of cyberattacks that disrupted municipal water operations across at least 12 states, targeting more than 30 municipal water systems in Minnesota alone.

October 2026: a cyberattack on the University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center forced New Mexico’s only Level I trauma center to divert ambulances and halted outpatient surgeries and appointments, disrupting access to emergency care.

Just this week, a cyberattack compromised 178 of the world’s most visited websites, including those belonging to Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, CNN, Salesforce, and IKEA, in an effort to steal cryptocurrency and infect iPhones.

AI is fundamentally reshaping the cyber battlefield, identifying weaknesses, analyzing systems, and accelerating cyber operations at a speed that was unimaginable just a few years ago. As our adversaries gain access to these capabilities, we must ensure federal agencies like CISA have the most advanced tools available to protect our critical infrastructure. By partnering our nation’s cyber defense agency with AI experts from the private sector, CISA can help communities strengthen their defenses, stay ahead of emerging risks, and keep our critical infrastructure secure and resilient.

Today, Rep. Fong and Rep. Gottheimer hosted a press conference to announce the introduction of the legislation. Click here to watch.

title: Gallagher, Padilla Advance Bipartisan Legislation to Return Ancestral Land to Pit River Tribe
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman James Gallagher (R-CA-01) and U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-CA) are working together to advance the bipartisan Pit River Land Transfer Act, legislation originally championed in the House by the late Congressman Doug LaMalfa. The measure would transfer 557 acres of federal land in Shasta County into trust for the Pit River Tribe, bringing the Tribe closer to reclaiming ancestral land it has sought to acquire for more than a decade. Following its passage in the House by unanimous consent, the legislation now heads to the President's desk to be signed into law.

Known as the Four Corners property, the land holds deep cultural and historical significance to the Pit River Tribe. Despite years of efforts to acquire the property through federal processes, the Tribe has faced repeated delays in securing the land.

“Doug LaMalfa was a tireless advocate for the North State, and returning this land to the Pit River Tribe was a cause he believed in,” said Congressman Gallagher. “I'm honored to carry his work forward and grateful to Senator Padilla for his partnership in moving this legislation through the Senate. The Tribe has waited more than a decade for this, and it's encouraging to see Republicans and Democrats working together to get it across the finish line.”

“For too long, California’s Pit River Tribe has been denied the right to manage and preserve their ancestral lands. The historic passage of our bill represents a key step toward righting our historical wrongs,” said Senator Padilla. “Restoring tribal land to its original owners preserves traditions, strengthens communities, and protects local environments across California. I am proud to support the Pit River Tribe and grateful for the bipartisan, bicameral support that made this land transfer possible.”

The Pit River Land Transfer Act would direct the transfer of 557 acres currently administered by the U.S. Forest Service to the Department of the Interior, where the property would be held in trust for the Pit River Tribe.

The legislation was originally introduced in the House by Congressman LaMalfa, while Senators Padilla and Adam Schiff introduced companion legislation in the Senate. Following Senate action on an amended version of the bill, Gallagher and Padilla have continued working across chambers to advance the measure.

The Pit River Tribe consists of 11 autonomous bands with ancestral ties to the Pit River region. The Four Corners property has long served as an important cultural site for the Tribe, which has sought its return through federal channels for more than a decade.

The bipartisan effort reflects a shared commitment to honoring the Tribe's longstanding connection to the land and completing work championed by Congressman LaMalfa.

title: Garamendi, Carbajal: DHS Will Not Use “Golden Bear” Training Ship for Deportations
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the Department of Homeland Security confirmed to Congressmen John Garamendi (CA-08) and Salud Carbajal (CA-24), two senior members of the House Armed Services Committee and the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, that it will not use ships, including training vessels or private foreign ships, for deportations.

The confirmation follows a letter the two sent to the agency demanding as much. Their demands came after The New York Times reported that DHS was considering using ships for mass deportations and identified Cal Poly Maritime Academy’s training ship, the Golden Bear, as a possible vessel.

“When Congressman Carbajal and I said that Donald Trump, Markwayne Mullin, and ICE will never use the Golden Bear or any ship for their mass deportation agenda, we meant it,” said Congressman Garamendi. “Today, I’m proud to announce the Department of Homeland Security has confirmed that it will not use any ship, including training vessels or private or foreign ships, for deportations. This isn’t the final step; we will continue to use our oversight powers to make sure Trump’s DHS keeps its word. I’m glad to stand with Congressman Carbajal on this issue, and I will continue to stand with him and every member of Congress to hold the Trump Administration to account.”

“While this commitment from DHS is a major victory for the Central Coast and congressional oversight, our work is not done. We must continue to hold the Trump Administration accountable for its extreme immigration enforcement and mass deportation agenda,” said Rep. Carbajal, the top Democrat on the Coast Guard and Maritime Transportation Subcommittee and a Senior Member of the Armed Services Committee. “When Congressman Garamendi and I spoke out against the Trump administration’s plan to use maritime vessels—including the Cal Poly Maritime Academy’s Golden Bear—for deportations, they had no choice but to back down. This is a major win for accountability, but we cannot let up. I will continue pressing DHS for answers, closely monitoring its actions, and pushing back against policies that undermine due process and put people’s safety and rights at risk.”

Garamendi and Carbajal’s initial letter is the latest oversight action addressing President Donald Trump’s misuse of the military for his mass deportation agenda.

In December 2025, Congressman John Garamendi (D-CA-08) and U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) released a report detailing the Trump administration’s diversion of funds and resources from the Department of Defense (DoD) to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for immigration enforcement.

In January 2025, after discovering that military planes from Travis Air Force Base were used to deport undocumented immigrants, Congressman Garamendi demanded answers from the DoD. After Garamendi pushed back, DHS and the DoD later moved away from using military aircraft for deportations.

In February 2025, Garamendi demanded answers about the Trump administration’s attempt to divert much-needed medical personnel to the Guantanamo Bay detention facility. After the letter was sent, the military canceled its orders.

In May 2025, after plans were floated to turn Travis into a mass migrant detention center, Garamendi and Representative Mike Thompson (D-CA-04) pushed back. DHS later dropped its plan to turn the military base into a detention center.

title: Congressman Gonzalez’s Hands Off Our Boca Chica Beach Act Advances Out of Natural Resources Committee
text:
Contact: Alexis Torres

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) advanced H.R. 9779, the Hands Off Our Boca Chica Beach Act, through the House Committee on Natural Resources, marking a pivotal step toward it becoming law. The bill would protect the historic Boca Chica Beach name, which was targeted earlier this year by an out-of-state attempt to rename the site, “Cyber Beach.”

“Boca Chica Beach is, and always will be, part of South Texas,” said Congressman Gonzalez. “By codifying its name into law, we will cement a legacy that has defined our region’s vibrant history and protect a trusted landmark for future generations. We are now one step closer to making this a reality, and I look forward to working with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to get this legislation across the finish line.”

The House Committee on Natural Resources met today for a full committee markup to debate, amend, and vote on various pieces of legislation, including the Hands Off Our Boca Chica Beach Act. During the markup, the Committee adopted an amendment that removed the requirement for the Domestic Name Committees—a key federal division of the U.S. Board of Geographic Names (BGN)—to notify the respective Member of Congress of any proposed name change affecting their district. The amended bill fully protects the Boca Chica Beach name by codifying it in federal law, and Congressman Gonzalez will continue working directly with the Administration to advocate for greater transparency in BGN’s federal renaming process and policies.

title: RELEASE: On the Heels of Weekend Attacks, Gottheimer, Fong Announce Bipartisan Legislation to Strengthen Government Cyber Defenses
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Wednesday, November 18, 2026, on the heels of last week’s attacks, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) and Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20) announced the bipartisan BRIDGE AI Act, new federal legislation to help the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) bring in additional AI expertise to secure American critical infrastructure.

Watch Gottheimer’s remarks here.

“Our adversaries are using AI to attack our networks faster than ever, and CISA, the agency on the front lines of defending them, doesn’t have enough capacity to keep pace,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “The BRIDGE AI Act is a commonsense, bipartisan fix that gives CISA a fast way to bring in the best AI and tech minds to hunt down intruders, patch vulnerabilities, and stress-test AI tools before they are exploited. Protecting our families, our water systems, and our national security shouldn’t be a partisan issue, and I’m proud to partner with Congressman Fong to get this done.”

“Communities and critical industries across the country are trying to keep up with the surge in AI-driven cyberattacks that steal sensitive data and disrupt operations,” said Congressman Fong (CA-20). “In the Central Valley, cyberattacks have increasingly targeted schools, hospitals, and water systems, threatening the critical services our communities depend on. These attacks are becoming more frequent and sophisticated. These threats are real, and they aren’t waiting for the government to catch up. By bringing in AI and emerging technology specialists from the private sector, the BRIDGE AI Act ensures our nation’s cybersecurity experts receive the additional tools and expertise needed to modernize our systems, address vulnerabilities, and protect the essential services Americans rely on.”

Investing in the people securing our critical infrastructure will directly protect American families and our national security. Foreign adversaries, including China, Iran, and Russia, are using AI to find and exploit weaknesses in U.S. networks faster than ever. CISA is the agency responsible for defending federal networks and helping protect critical infrastructure, but it doesn’t have enough in-house AI expertise to keep up, and the Trump administration has repeatedly slashed the agency to the bone. Recent software outages of critical services, including the government’s classified systems, paired with this summer’s cyber attacks on municipal water systems in at least a dozen states underscore this urgent need.

The BRIDGE AI Act creates a pilot program that lets experienced tech professionals serve inside CISA and speeds up onboarding, so experts can start helping bolster U.S. cybersecurity sooner. These new hires would work on specific projects with clear goals, including:

Hunting for intruders in federal networks;

Fixing known vulnerabilities faster;

Testing AI tools for security flaws.

The BRIDGE AI Act builds on Congressman Gottheimer’s role as Co-Chair of the House AI Commission, where he has worked to develop policies that protect American systems and critical infrastructure from the growing cybersecurity threat AI poses:

The bipartisan AI Cyber Defense Act gives America’s critical infrastructure operators free access to the most powerful, cyber-capable AI models.

The bipartisan Securing Our Critical Infrastructure Act creates a dedicated rapid-response and threat notification service at CISA, built specifically for small and medium water and electric utilities.

title: ICYMI: Rep. Grijalva Joins Colleagues in Calling for Day-One Ban on Congressional Stock Trading, Other Measures to Restore Trust in Government
text:
Washington, D.C. — Yesterday, November 17, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva joined Representative Jason Crow and more than a dozen incoming members of Congress at a press conference calling on the 120th Congress to make banning congressional stock trading a day-one priority.

Organized by the Political Integrity Project, the press conference highlighted growing bipartisan support for ending congressional stock trading and restoring public trust in government. She called for a comprehensive ban without loopholes or carve-outs, extending to the President, Vice President, and Supreme Court.

Grijalva also called for broader accountability in government, including banning Super PACs and overturning Citizens United.

Watch the full press conference here. A full copy of her remarks is below:

“Thank you to the Political Integrity Project and Nico for organizing this press conference.

Thank you to my colleagues for your leadership on this issue, and the incoming freshman class who will help us finally get this done.

To me, this is such a commonsense issue: Members of Congress should not be allowed to enrich themselves by trading stocks.

As a part of our jobs, many of us have access to information the rest of the world does not.

Using that information to make a profit is called insider trading – and for any other person, it would be illegal.

Members of Congress should not get to play by different rules.

This is also about conflicts of interest.

When a member's personal financial interests conflict with the interests of their constituents, who are they really representing?

If you want to make a living trading stocks – I won’t judge you. Go to Wall Street. Make a killing.

But those of us here in Washington D.C – who have the privilege of representing our communities back home – were elected to serve the people, not our stock portfolios.

It’s time to enact a ban on Congressional stock trading – and yes, this should extend to the President, the Vice President, and Supreme Court as well.

We need to pass a real ban, not one with carve outs and exceptions as the Republicans did earlier this year.

And while we’re at it, let’s ban Super PACs and overturn Citizens United.

In the midterms, Democrats ran on accountability.

But we cannot begin to hold the Trump administration accountable, if we can’t hold ourselves accountable.

No more congressional stock trading. Let’s get it done.”

###

title: Grothman Introduces Bipartisan Resolution Recognizing Hmong New Year
text:
Congressman Glenn Grothman (R-WI) has reintroduced a bipartisan resolution recognizing the cultural and historical significance of the Hmong New Year and honoring the contributions of Hmong Americans to communities across the country.

Grothman is joined by Representatives Tony Wied (R-WI), Gwen Moore (D-WI), Mark Takano (D-CA), Judy Chu (D-CA), Zoe Lofgren (D-CA), Mark Pocan (D-WI), and Kelly Morrison (D-MN) in recognizing the importance of this annual celebration and the Hmong community's rich cultural heritage.

“Wisconsin is home to the third-largest Hmong population in the country, and I am fortunate to represent one of the state's largest Hmong communities,” said Grothman. “Each year, I look forward to attending Hmong New Year celebrations throughout my district, including in communities like Oshkosh and Sheboygan. The Hmong people played an important role alongside the United States in fighting communism during the Vietnam War. That’s why I am proud to lead on this bipartisan resolution recognizing the Hmong community's contributions to our country and the important role Hmong Americans continue to play in our communities.”

“I’m proud that California is home to one of the largest Hmong American populations in the country, including a thriving community in Fresno County,” said Rep. Lofgren. “Hmong New Year is a cherished tradition to celebrate the end of harvest season, and I extend my warmest wishes to those celebrating around the world."

"The Hmong New Year is a joyous celebration of family, ancestors, and the harvest, a time for families and communities to come together and give thanks," said Rep. Chu."As Chair Emerita of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus, I am proud to join this bipartisan resolution to recognize and honor the Hmong community's history, resilience, and contributions to our nation.”

"I join my colleagues in celebrating the Hmong New Year," said Rep. Takano. "I wish good health and bright futures to all who are celebrating with friends and family. I am proud to join this bipartisan effort to recognize the vibrancy and contributions of the Hmong community in our nation.”

“Milwaukee is home to a vibrant, thriving Hmong community, which I am so proud to represent. I join my constituents in celebrating the Hmong New Year and wish them prosperity in the upcoming year,” said Rep. Moore.

“Hmong New Year is a time to celebrate family, community, and the rich cultural traditions that have been passed down through generations,” said Rep. Morrison. “Minnesota is home to one of the largest Hmong communities in the country, and Hmong Minnesotans have made extraordinary contributions to our state’s culture, history, and communities. I’m proud to join my colleagues in recognizing this important holiday and wish everyone celebrating a happy and prosperous New Year.”

Background Information

The Hmong New Year is traditionally celebrated at the end of the rice harvest season in Laos and Southeast Asia in late November and early December. The celebration provides an opportunity for the Hmong community to honor ancestors, give thanks for the harvest, celebrate cultural traditions, and welcome the year ahead. In the United States, Hmong New Year celebrations take place throughout the fall and early winter, bringing together families and communities to preserve and share their heritage.

Wisconsin is home to approximately 62,000 Hmong Americans, making it the third-largest Hmong population in the nation. Hmong Americans have made lasting contributions to Wisconsin and communities throughout the country through their service, hard work, and commitment to their families and communities.

title: Harshbarger Elected to House GOP Steering Committee for 120th Congress
text:
“I am deeply honored to be elected to the House Republican Steering Committee and represent Tennessee and Kentucky. As we head into a new Congress, House Republicans must put our strongest team forward, with leaders in place who will hold the Democrats accountable and keep fighting for the conservative agenda. The decisions this committee makes will shape how our conference leads over the next two years. I’m committed to helping build a team that is united, prepared, and ready to earn back the trust of the American people. There’s plenty of work ahead, and I’m ready to get to it,” said Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger.

The House Republican Steering Committee sets committee assignments for Republican members of the House.
