title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces Bill to Stop Taxpayer-Funded Animal Abuse
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (Nov. 18, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace (R-SC-01) introduced the Painful Research and Investigations on Monkeys Abused in Taxpayer-funded Experiments Stops Act of 2026, or the PRIMATES Act, to stop the National Institutes of Health (NIH) from using taxpayer dollars to fund experiments causing significant pain and distress to nonhuman primates.

“Your tax dollars should not be paying for monkeys to suffer in a lab. Period,” said Congresswoman Mace. “There is no excuse for a federal agency to put animals through pain and distress, especially on the American people’s dime. The NIH should never have been allowed to get away with this in the first place. Our bill puts an end to it. The abuse stops now.”

The issue hits close to home in South Carolina. Alpha Genesis, a primate breeding and research facility in Yemassee, has faced serious scrutiny over animal welfare and facility oversight. In November 2024, 43 monkeys escaped from the facility, and there have been numerous instances where primates have died due to cruel and inhumane conditions and negligence. They also manage the NIH’s controversial monkey colony on Morgan Island. They have received over $110 million in federal contracts since 2008, including from the NIH. What happened at Alpha Genesis is exactly why we need stronger protections.

The PRIMATES Act amends the Public Health Service Act and draws a clear line: the NIH cannot conduct these experiments, cannot use taxpayer dollars to fund them, and cannot simply transfer its animals to another laboratory to continue the same painful research.

The PRIMATES Act would:

Prohibit taxpayer-funded experiments causing significant pain or distress: Prevent the NIH from conducting or providing financial support for research causing significant pain or distress to nonhuman primates.

Stop the transfer of monkeys to other laboratories for painful experiments: Prohibit the NIH from transferring any nonhuman primate it owns to an intramural or extramural laboratory for research causing significant pain or distress.

Establish clear standards for covered research: Include studies classified as Category D or Category E by the U.S. Department of Agriculture.

Set a clear implementation timeline: Make the restrictions effective 90 days after the legislation is enacted.

title: Rep. Mejia Demands Answers as DHS Secretary Mullin Dodges Questions on Roxbury ICE Detention Plans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) confronted DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin during a House Homeland Security Committee hearing over plans to convert a Roxbury warehouse into an ICE detention facility, despite strong local opposition and a federal court order restricting conversion work.

Mullin claimed the project was still in the bidding process, despite public records showing DHS had already awarded a $31.8 million contract to Tennessee-based company SK2 LLC on November 5th. Mullin evaded all demands for transparency. He could not confirm whether an environmental review had been completed, provide an opening timeline, or account for detainee activity. Throughout the exchange, Mullin evaded accountability and refused to provide meaningful transparency about the administration's plans to spend millions in taxpayer dollars on a detention facility the people of Roxbury have already rejected.

For a transcript of the remarks, see below.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Mr. Secretary, while DHS initially abandoned plans to convert a Roxbury warehouse into a detention camp in Roxbury, New Jersey, it has since reversed course. Can you please share a timeline for this conversion and a timeline for its anticipated opening?

Secretary Mullin: We were wanting to not have to do that. We're trying to work with your governor.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Timeline only, sir. I’m short on time.

Secretary Mullin: But I'm just saying, we were trying not to have to do that because of the circumstances working with the governor, it forced us to. We're still putting it out for bid. Once we get the bid complete, we'll let you have a timeframe.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Got it. So you don't have a timeline. Has any conversion work begun at the facility?

Secretary Mullin: Right now, we're still looking out and trying to figure out what the best approach forward is.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: So should I take that as a no?

Secretary Mullin: We haven't started full construction, no. We're looking at what we need to do.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: So full construction means partial construction has begun?

Secretary Mullin: No, full construction means that all we're doing is putting it out for bid right now.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Let me ask this again very clearly: has any work to convert Roxbury, the Roxbury warehouse, into a detention camp? Has any work begun?

Secretary Mullin: Ma'am, don't call it a detention camp. Those are ridiculous words that you're using.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Okay. Reclaiming my time. According to a court order, any conversion work is restricted pending an environmental review. Has that review been conducted?

Secretary Mullin: I've said this is part of the bid process. So we're still looking into it.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: So that's a no.

Secretary Mullin: Ma'am. I said we're putting it up for bid. And that's part of it.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: It’s such a clear question. Has there been an environmental review conducted, yes or no?

Secretary Mullin: We're still going through all the requirements right now.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Okay. So that's a no.

Secretary Mullin: I don't know if it's been completed or not.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Okay, that's an “I don't know." That's a fair answer. Okay. So let me ask, ICE had admitted that they had detained 14 individuals at Roxbury on September 4th and September 8th for processing. Can you share, have any detainees ever been brought inside of the warehouse?

Secretary Mullin: Ma'am, I'm not familiar with it. If they have, I don't know.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Okay. So you don't know. Do you know if your officers, ICE agents, anyone under your jurisdiction, are they informed about any court decisions about a facility like Roxbury? I.e. would they know that there is a court order saying this facility is not to be used?

Secretary Mullin: That communication would be with the Acting Director, and I don't know if he's informed his employees.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Okay. May I ask, since September 8th, have any detainees been brought to the site, either inside or outside, during any moment of your tenure?

Secretary Mullin: Ma'am, if you'd like, I can take that and get it back to you.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: I would love that. I would love that, actually. May I make a request? Will you commit to submitting to this committee, to my office, and to the state of New Jersey your timeline for the conversion, your timeline for the environmental review, and your anticipated timeline for an opening of this facility?

Secretary Mullin: What is statutorily required of us, we will do.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Okay. You just said that you would share information, and now I'm asking for three pieces of information. You just said that you would share the information about the environmental review.

Secretary Mullin: You asked me questions about operations. I said that I'll take that and get back to you. The questions you're asking me now, I said that I will take those that are statutorily required of me to report those to you, I will.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Okay, so what I have, what I am requesting for this committee, the state of New Jersey, and my office is for you to inform us on when that environmental review will take place. Are you able to share that information, yes or no, at this point or at a future date?

Secretary Mullin: Let me get back to you on that.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Okay. Let me now shift a little bit. You said that you do not cherry-pick laws. May I ask, do you believe that citizens and non-citizens alike have due process and equal protection rights according to our Constitution?

Secretary Mullin: Ma'am, our immigration policy is policy that Congress set, and I follow that policy.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: That's not what I'm asking. I'm trying to understand your understanding of our Constitution.

Secretary Mullin: They are not one and the same.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: Are you aware, do you believe that citizens and non-citizens alike have due process and equal protection laws afforded to them according to the 14th Amendment of our Constitution? Yes or no?

Secretary Mullin: American citizens have unique rights that are given to them.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: That's not what I'm asking. But it's okay if you don't understand that; if you do not have awareness of our Constitution, that's totally okay. It's shocking, but I'll let that pass. Let me ask. New Jersey passed a law barring ICE agents from using masks when they're carrying out operations. And yet officers, agents, persist. Is that cherry-picking laws? Adherence to laws?

Secretary Mullin: I’ll enforce our immigration policy that Congress sets. If you want to change your policies, you want to change your laws.

Rep. Analilia Mejia: So you ignore state law.

Secretary Mullin: Ma'am, I enforce the immigration policy.

Chairman: The Gentlelady's time is now expired.

###

title: Congressional Jewish Caucus Urges Congressional Armed Services Leadership to Protect Religious Freedom in the National Defense Authorization Act
text:
Washington, D.C. –Today, Congressmen Jerrold Nadler (NY-12) and Brad Schneider (IL-10) led the Congressional Jewish Caucus in sending a letter to Congressional Armed Services leadership to urge them to reject portions of the Military Chaplains Modernization Act from the final version of the FY 2027 National Defense Authorization Act that could result in unwanted proselytization and infringe upon service members’ religious freedom. The letter follows receipt of concerns from former military chaplains, community faith leaders, veterans' groups, and civil rights organizations regarding these provisions.

“Military chaplains provide essential pastoral care and counseling to service members of many faiths and traditions, as well as those who do not practice any specific religion,” the lawmakers wrote. “Because chaplains serve a richly diverse military community, they must be required to protect the religious freedom of all those they serve. The language in these provisions would undermine that fundamental principle by broadly protecting chaplains who engage in unwelcome proselytization, violating service members' freedom of religion.”

“This is especially important for members of minority faiths, including Jewish service members who may serve where a Jewish chaplain is unavailable,” the lawmakers continued.

“They, and all service members, should be able to seek religious support with confidence that their beliefs will be respected. Failure to protect these service members from such proselytization undermines readiness and combat effectiveness, weakening our Armed Forces. We insist that the Department of Defense should uphold a clear and consistent approach to religious liberty across the Armed Forces, ensuring that service members are protected from unwanted religious advocacy and can access the pastoral care they seek,” the lawmakers concluded.

Read the full letter here and below.

Dear Chairmen Rogers and Wicker, Ranking Members Smith and Reed,

As members of the Congressional Jewish Caucus, we write to urge the House and Senate Armed Services Committees not to include provisions of the Military Chaplains Modernization Act of 2026 that could result in unwanted proselytization and infringe upon service members’ religious freedom in the final Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. We share concerns of many former military chaplains, community faith leaders, veterans' groups, and civil rights organizations regarding these provisions.

Military chaplains provide essential pastoral care and counseling to service members of many faiths and traditions, as well as those who do not practice any specific religion. Because chaplains serve a richly diverse military community, they must be required to protect the religious freedom of all those they serve. The language in these provisions would undermine that fundamental principle by broadly protecting chaplains who engage in unwelcome proselytization, violating service members' freedom of religion.

This freedom is grounded in the First Amendment, which protects the free exercise of religion while prohibiting the government from establishing or favoring a religion. Service members should be able to freely seek spiritual support without concern that they will be subjected to unwanted religious advocacy or pressure. This is especially important for members of minority faiths, including Jewish service members who may serve where a Jewish chaplain is unavailable. They, and all service members, should be able to seek religious support with confidence that their beliefs will be respected. Failure to protect these service members from such proselytization undermines readiness and combat effectiveness, weakening our Armed Forces.

title: Joe Neguse Elected Assistant Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives
text:

The millennial Congressman, 42, will serve as both the youngest and only non-coastal member of senior House Democratic leadership.

As the fourth-highest ranking member of the Chamber, Neguse will become the highest-ranking Colorado lawmaker in modern history. I’m deeply grateful to my colleagues for electing me to serve in this role, and I look forward to the critical work ahead that we must do to end corruption in Washington D.C. and expand opportunity for every single Coloradan in our great state,” said Neguse.

The Colorado Congressman joins House Democrats’ top leadership team, alongside Speaker of the House designate Hakeem Jeffries of New York, Majority Leader-elect Katherine Clark of Massachusetts, and Majority Whip-elect Pete Aguilar of California.

The last lawmaker to hold the title of Assistant Speaker was Clark back in 2021. She was preceded by now-Senator Ben Ray Luján.

Neguse has been widely described as a rising star in the Democratic Party since first being elected to represent Colorado’s 2nd District in 2018. He has held numerous leadership positions, including his current roles as Assistant Democratic Leader and Chair of the House Democrats’ Litigation Task Force. He previously served as Chair of the Democratic Policy and Communications Committee (DPCC) and as an impeachment manager during President Trump’s second impeachment trial. He has also received national recognition for his legislative effectiveness, efforts to restore faith in democratic institutions, and commitment to modeling servant leadership.

title: Pfluger's Big Bend National Park Boundary Adjustment Act Passes House Natural Resources Committee
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, the House Committee on Natural Resources passed Congressman August Pfluger's (TX-11) Big Bend Boundary Adjustment Act. The legislation would expand Big Bend National Park by more than 6,000 acres via private donation or exchange, fulfilling the Fulcher Family's wish and advancing the goals of several conservation groups working to preserve the park.

The expansion honors the wishes of the Fulcher Family, a West Texas ranching family that has longed to see its land donated to Big Bend National Park. The land would be donated at no cost to the federal government and includes existing housing structures that park staff and law enforcement can use while patrolling the area. Developed in coordination with local landowners, this legislation ensures that any land added to Big Bend National Park is acquired voluntarily, without the use of eminent domain.

"The Fulcher Family has been part of West Texas for generations, and their decision to donate this land to Big Bend National Park is a generous act of stewardship. I'm proud to carry this bill forward to honor their wish and protect one of the most breathtaking landscapes in our state for future generations. I thank the Big Bend Conservancy for helping get this bill through the House Committee on Natural Resources, and I'll keep working to get it signed into law," said Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11).

“Expanding a national park should never come at the expense of private property rights. H.R. 2323 authorizes the Secretary of the Interior to acquire approximately 6,100 acres along Terlingua Creek only through voluntary donation or exchange, expressly barring eminent domain and condemnation. I commend Rep. Pfluger for working with local landowners to strengthen this iconic Texas landscape while ensuring Washington cannot force anyone off their land," said House Committee on Natural Resources Chairman Bruce Westerman (AR-04).

Background:

The Fulcher Family has lived in West Texas for generations and owned land along Terlingua Creek, just west of Big Bend National Park. The Big Bend Conservancy, the park’s nonprofit partner, acquired the land from the family and plans to donate it to the park at no cost to taxpayers. Because only Congress can expand a national park’s boundary, this legislation is needed to allow the park to accept the donation.

title: CONGRESSWOMAN PLASKETT CELEBRATES HOUSE DEMOCRATIC CAUCUS’ HISTORIC NOMINATION OF HAKEEM JEFFRIES TO BE THE FIRST BLACK SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE IN THE 120TH CONGRESS
text:
For Immediate Release Contact: Tionee Scotland

November 18, 2026 202-808-6129

PRESS RELEASE

CONGRESSWOMAN PLASKETT CELEBRATES HOUSE DEMOCRATIC CAUCUS’ HISTORIC NOMINATION OF HAKEEM JEFFRIES TO BE THE FIRST BLACK SPEAKER OF THE HOUSE IN THE 120TH CONGRESS

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Stacey E. Plaskett (D-VI) released the following statement after the House Democratic Caucus nominated Leader Hakeem Jeffries to serve as Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives for the 120th Congress. The House of Representatives will formally elect the Speaker by roll call vote when the 120th Congress convenes on January 3, 2027.

“Today, House Democrats made history. In nominating Hakeem Jeffries as our choice for Speaker for the 120th Congress, House Democrats have placed one of the most consequential offices in our government on the path to being held, for the first time, by a Black American. It is a fitting honor for a man who has earned it through steadiness, discipline, and an unshakable faith in what this institution can be.

“I have served alongside Leader Jeffries for years, and I have watched him lead with conviction and grace through some of the most difficult moments our country has faced. He has kept our caucus united when it would have been easy to fracture, met hostility with resolve, and never lost sight of the working families we were sent here to serve. He is a lawyer’s lawyer, a son of Brooklyn, and a leader who listens.

“This moment belongs to generations of Americans who were told this chamber was not meant for them. Leader Jeffries stands on the shoulders of Shirley Chisholm, John Lewis, and so many others who fought to open these doors. He is the realization of the aspirations and dreams of mothers and fathers who sacrifice to educate and create possibilities for sons and daughters. His intention has always been to hold those doors open for whoever comes next.

“For the people of the Virgin Islands and the U.S. territories, Leader Jeffries has been a true partner who understands that the Americans who live in the territories deserve full dignity, fair treatment, and a real voice in this government.

“As I complete my final term in Congress, few things give me greater hope for this institution’s future than knowing it will be led by Hakeem Jeffries. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to him, his wife and my Caribbean sister Kennisandra, and their family on this historic day, and I look forward to celebrating again with them on January 3, 2027.”

###

title: VIDEO: Pressley’s Statement Following Democratic Leadership Vote
text:
Pressley Explained Her Strategy to Advance the “People’s Agenda” in a New Video Released Today

Pressley Has Consistently Called on Democrats to Meet the Moment by Delivering Bold, Transformative Policy in 120th Congress

Video (YouTube)

WASHINGTON – Today, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) issued the following statement and released a new video on the Democratic Leadership nominations and negotiations with Leader Hakeem Jeffries.

Congresswoman Pressley has consistently called on Democrats to meet the moment and use their new majority to pursue bold, transformative policies and aggressively pursue accountability for the corruption, cruelty, and harm inflicted by the Trump administration over the past two years.

“The people delivered a mandate for bold, transformative change, and Democrats have a responsibility to honor that mandate by pursuing an affirmative agenda that goes as far and deep as the hurt our communities are facing. What happened on Election Night was a condemnation and a rejection of Donald Trump and Republicans’ anti-freedom agenda—but it was not an affirmation of the Democratic Party. We cannot default to an unjust status quo.

“I have been head-down in ongoing, late night, and early morning negotiations in recent days. I am so grateful for every constituent that has had my back and helped press for and advance the critical commitments we seek—from those who co-crafted priorities at our latest town hall, to the thousands who have called our office. Our people, our neighbors, have always been and continue to be my focus. Families are at a breaking point choosing between rent and groceries, denied medical care, torn away from their loved ones by rogue ICE agents, and desperately praying for an end to wars and genocide. I am clear and undeterred: we must use this majority to advance Medicare for All, restore reproductive freedom, deliver reparations, abolish ICE, end the wars, and so much more. This is about keeping the people’s trust and advancing the people’s agenda, and how we do so is so much bigger than any one person. I do not seek positional authority—I seek impact.

“I have been in close conversation with Leader Jeffries about how Democrats can meet the moment in the 120th Congress, and while our negotiations are far from over, he has committed to working with me to deliver. He has made commitments to me about urgent legislation to advance reproductive freedom, a reparative agenda for Black America, Medicare for All, and protecting our immigrant neighbors. Today, I supported his nomination in caucus to be our next Speaker as our negotiations continue, and I will continue working to ensure Democrats deliver and that our shared agenda is responsive and urgent. I will have much more to say on this in the coming weeks and will continue to enlist the public and our constituents to advance this agenda and hold everyone in Washington accountable.”

At a town hall in East Boston this week, Congresswoman Pressley laid out her vision and priorities for the Democratic majority in the 120th Congress and solicited feedback from constituents about what policies she should fight for in a “People’s Agenda.” In her remarks at the town hall, the Congresswoman outlined several policy fights Democrats should take on in the 120th Congress, including but not limited to: Medicare for All and healthcare justice; housing affordability; abolishing ICE and immigrant justice; reproductive freedom; racial and economic justice; affordability and lowering costs; peace and human rights; AI regulation and stopping data centers; rooting out corruption and pursuing accountability; and more.

title: Ramirez to Mullin: “Get comfortable. I have a lot of unanswered questions.”
text:
November 18, 2026

Congresswoman Ramirez is pursuing the chair of the Oversight Subcommittee of the Homeland Security Committee, where she plans to lead investigations into the department, the secretary, and directors of agencies.

Washington, DC—Today, Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03) confronted Markwayne Mullin about the impunity of DHS agents who have been identified by the Illinois Accountability Commission for their criminal use of force against Chicagoans. Ramirez used her time to demand the agents be held accountable and entered their names into the hearing record. According to ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations numbers as of July 2026, only ONE agent has been placed on a temporary suspension as a result of internal investigations.

During her time, Ramirez also outlined the oversight investigations she plans to continue through the Oversight Subcommittee, including investigating the corrupt use of DHS funding to reward campaign donors, deaths and medical neglect at detention centers, use of force violations, the erosion of FEMA, CISA, Coast Guard, TSA’s mission, and DHS’s failures to address the recent cybersecurity concerns.

“Last time I told Mullin not to get too comfortable in that seat because he will be held accountable. Well, I take it back: he should get comfortable. Because I have a lot of unanswered questions and, next Congress, I hope to chair the oversight subcommittee. And when I do, he will spend a lot of time in that seat,” says Ramirez. “We will uncover this administration’s corruption, rein in the abuses of power, and hold all those who have profited from our pain accountable. I’ll see him again in the Homeland Security Committee room real soon.”

For the full video of the Congresswoman’s remarks, CLICK HERE.

Full remarks as prepared for delivery:

Secretary Markwayne Mullin, yes or no, are you comfortable in that seat?

Secretary Mullin, I have sent 10 separate oversight inquiries to the Department of Homeland Security that have gone unanswered.

Five of them during your tenure, about conditions at the Campbell County and El Valle detention facilities, data-sharing agreements within TSA, and your department’s use of shock gloves and “less lethal” weaponry.

Even though your Department seems unable to promptly and thoroughly respond to oversight from members of this committee, you have no problem talking to me on X.

Your most recent post suggested that DHS and its agents are keeping Americans safe.

So, when Martin Lagunas pointed his firearm in Carolina Molina’s face - a licensed mental health professional and U.S. citizen - was he keeping Americans safe?

When Charles Exum crashed into the vehicle of Marimar Martinez, a U.S. citizen and teaching assistant, and shot her five times, was he keeping Americans safe?

When Border Patrol Agents Matthew Sulek, Michael Turner, Oscar Meza, Andrew Torabpour, Joseph Brennan, Martin Davalos, and Alexander Mills crashed into the vehicle of Dayanne Figueroa, a U.S. citizen and paralegal, pointed weapons at her, pulled her out of her vehicle by her feet, pinned her face down, and utilized excessive force as they detained her, were they keeping Americans safe?

When Border Patrol Agents Enrique Camacho, Angel Nieves, and Ricardo Moreno deployed tear gas on a public road, near an elementary school while children played nearby, were they keeping Americans safe?

You know, there are a lot of examples of “threats” coming from the government right now.

And many of those threats are among your ranks.

They don’t respect the civil rights of our neighbors or the rule of law; they terrorize our communities; they act with impunity.

According to ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations own number to this committee in July, while they have opened 53 internal investigations, only ONE agent has been held “accountable”... a temporary suspension.

Do you have an update on that, Secretary Mullin? Since the last report, have YOU held any of the agents who violated the rights of or harmed our neighbors accountable?

Last time I told you not to get too comfortable in that seat because you will be held accountable.

Well, I take it back: do get comfortable. Because I have a lot of unanswered questions and, next Congress, I plan to chair the oversight subcommittee.

And when I do, you will spend a lot of time in that seat.

I will be bringing you and your staff in to answer:

The use of federal funding to reward campaign donors, like GEO Group and CoreCivic, and grant contracts to friends and family members.

The illegal and unconstitutional surveillance of the American people by DHS and its contractors.

The medical neglect, miscarriages, and abuse in detention centers.

Stephen Miller's calls to ignore habeas corpus.

DHS agents’ due-process violations with impunity.

The rapid spread of 287(g) agreements threatening the safety and stability of our communities.

The defunding of FEMA, CISA, Coast Guard, and TSA to support the Trump Administration's mass deportation campaign.

The politicization of FEMA’s mission.

The incompetence of you and your department to protect us from cyber attacks.

AND SO MUCH MORE.

We will uncover this administration’s corruption, rein in the abuses of power, and hold all those who have profited from our pain accountable.

We know the world we are building: we will abolish ICE, end detention, dismantle DHS, and reimagine safety.

I’ll see you again in this room real soon.

title: Representatives Ross, Joyce Reintroduce Bipartisan Bill to Bolster Support for Police, First Responders Struggling with PTSD
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Deborah Ross (NC-02) and Congressman Dave Joyce (OH-14) introduced the Fighting Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder Act. This bipartisan, bicameral legislation addresses the high rates of Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) among first responders by expanding access to specialized treatment for public safety officers. The Senate has recently passed companion legislation led by Senators Chuck Grassley (R-IA) and Chris Coons (D-DE).

PTSD disproportionately affects first responders. According to the Institutes of Health, one in three first responders will develop PTSD compared to one in five Americans in the general population.

This legislation directs the Office of Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) within the Department of Justice (DOJ) to develop a program to expand access to specialized treatment and preventative care. The bill focuses on public safety officers and telecommunicators such as police officers, firefighters, emergency medical technicians, and 911 dispatchers dealing with job-related PTSD or acute stress disorder.

“The first responders and law enforcement officers who put their lives on the line to protect our communities experience a tremendous mental toll that often goes unseen,” said Congresswoman Ross. “Their work to keep us safe puts them at higher risk of post-traumatic stress disorder and related mental illnesses. It’s time Congress acts to ensure these brave individuals can access the care they deserve while serving communities in North Carolina and across the country.”

title: Rep. Derek Schmidt’s Quindaro Landmark Bill Advances Out of House Natural Resources Committee
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Legislation led by Congressman Derek Schmidt (KS-02) to designate the historic Quindaro Townsite in Kansas City, Kansas, as a National Historic Landmark has passed the House Committee on Natural Resources, marking an important step forward in efforts to preserve and recognize one of the region’s most significant historic sites.

The Quindaro Townsite National Historic Landmark Act, introduced by Congressman Schmidt alongside Congresswoman Sharice Davids (KS-03) and Congressman Emanuel Cleaver (MO-5), would designate the site as a National Historic Landmark through an act of Congress. Quindaro served as a critical entry point for anti-slavery settlers and a sanctuary for people escaping bondage via the Underground Railroad before and during the Civil War.

“Quindaro is an important part of Kansas history and our nation’s story,” Congressman Schmidt said. “Its legacy of courage, freedom, and determination deserves to be recognized and preserved for future generations. The National Historic Landmarks Committee has already unanimously recommended this designation, and I’m pleased our legislation has passed through committee and I look forward to it getting a House vote soon.”

“Granting Quindaro national landmark status is well past due,” Congresswoman Davids said. “From helping freedom seekers on the Underground Railroad to its historic connection with the Wyandot Nation, Quindaro is central to who we are in Kansas City. Today’s hearing moves our legislation forward so we can cut through bureaucratic delays and safeguard this history for our children and grandchildren.”

“Today, we took another step forward in our effort to preserve the Quindaro Townsite and the important history that deserves to be shared with the generations of Americans still to come,” Congressman Cleaver said. “I’m thankful to my colleagues on the Natural Resources Committee for moving this bipartisan bill forward in the legislative process, and I look forward to the legislation receiving a vote in the full House of Representatives.”

“The Quindaro Townsite was a critical free-state port of entry for the Underground Railroad," Chairman Bruce Westerman said. "I applaud Rep. Schmidt for leading H.R. 8276 to classify this important site as a National Historic Landmark so future generations of Americans can visit and learn about the town’s historic role in both the fight against slavery and the education of newly freed African Americans.”

Westerman chairs the House Committee on Natural Resources.

National Historic Landmarks are designated through the National Park Service System Advisory Board or by an act of Congress. The National Historic Landmarks Committee unanimously recommended Quindaro Townsite for designation in May 2025, but the administrative process has since stalled. The legislation would bypass that process and secure the designation through congressional action.

Passage out of the House Natural Resources Committee moves the bipartisan legislation one step closer to consideration by the full House of Representatives.

BACKGROUND

Founded in 1857, Quindaro emerged as a beacon for Free-State advocates during the turbulent “Bleeding Kansas” era. Strategically located along the Missouri River, it served as a critical entry point for anti-slavery settlers and a sanctuary for those escaping bondage via the Underground Railroad. The town’s establishment was a collaborative effort among the Wyandot Nation, New England abolitionists, and African American settlers, exemplifying a remarkable multicultural alliance during a period marked by division and conflict.

Beyond its pivotal role in the anti-slavery movement, Quindaro became a center for African American advancement following the Civil War. The establishment of the Quindaro Freedman’s School, later known as Western University, marked a significant milestone in education for African Americans west of the Mississippi River. Institutions such as Douglass Hospital further demonstrated the community’s commitment to education and healthcare.

Archaeological excavations have uncovered artifacts that offer valuable insights into the daily lives of Quindaro’s diverse inhabitants. The site’s preserved foundations and structures provide a tangible connection to this important history. Quindaro has been listed on the National Register of Historic Places since 2002 and was designated a National Commemorative Site in 2019.

title: CONGRESSIONAL JEWISH CAUCUS URGES CONGRESSIONAL ARMED SERVICES LEADERSHIP TO PROTECT RELIGIOUS FREEDOM IN THE NATIONAL DEFENSE AUTHORIZATION ACT
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, the Congressional Jewish Caucus sent a letter to Congressional Armed Services leadership to urge them to reject portions of the Military Chaplains Modernization Act from the final version of the FY 2027 National Defense Authorization Act that could result in unwanted proselytization and infringe upon service members’ religious freedom. The letter follows receipt of concerns from former military chaplains, community faith leaders, veterans' groups, and civil rights organizations regarding these provisions.

“Military chaplains provide essential pastoral care and counseling to service members of many faiths and traditions, as well as those who do not practice any specific religion,” the lawmakers wrote. “Because chaplains serve a richly diverse military community, they must be required to protect the religious freedom of all those they serve. The language in these provisions would undermine that fundamental principle by broadly protecting chaplains who engage in unwelcome proselytization, violating service members freedom of religion.”

“This is especially important for members of minority faiths, including Jewish service members who may serve where a Jewish chaplain is unavailable,” the lawmakers continued. “They, and all service members, should be able to seek religious support with confidence that their beliefs will be respected. Failure to protect these service members from such proselytization undermines readiness and combat effectiveness, weakening our Armed Forces.”

“We insist that the Department of Defense should uphold a clear and consistent approach to religious liberty across the Armed Forces, ensuring that service members are protected from unwanted religious advocacy and can access the pastoral care they seek,” the lawmakers concluded.

Read the full letter here and below.

Dear Chairmen Rogers and Wicker, Ranking Members Smith and Reed,

As members of the Congressional Jewish Caucus, we write to urge the House and Senate Armed Services Committees not to include provisions of the Military Chaplains Modernization Act of 2026 that could result in unwanted proselytization and infringe upon service members’ religious freedom in the final Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. We share concerns of many former military chaplains, community faith leaders, veterans' groups, and civil rights organizations regarding these provisions.

Military chaplains provide essential pastoral care and counseling to service members of many faiths and traditions, as well as those who do not practice any specific religion. Because chaplains serve a richly diverse military community, they must be required to protect the religious freedom of all those they serve. The language in these provisions would undermine that fundamental principle by broadly protecting chaplains who engage in unwelcome proselytization, violating service members freedom of religion.

This freedom is grounded in the First Amendment, which protects the free exercise of religion while prohibiting the government from establishing or favoring a religion. Service members should be able to freely seek spiritual support without concern that they will be subjected to unwanted religious advocacy or pressure. This is especially important for members of minority faiths, including Jewish service members who may serve where a Jewish chaplain is unavailable. They, and all service members, should be able to seek religious support with confidence that their beliefs will be respected. Failure to protect these service members from such proselytization undermines readiness and combat effectiveness, weakening our Armed Forces.

We ask you to omit the provisions of the Military Chaplains Modernization Act of 2026 that risk enabling unwanted proselytization and undermining service members’ religious freedom from the final Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act. We insist that the Department of Defense should uphold a clear and consistent approach to religious liberty across the Armed Forces, ensuring that service members are protected from unwanted religious advocacy and can access the pastoral care they seek.

title: Congresswoman Scholten Announces $440,000 to Expand Supportive Services for Human Trafficking Survivors in West Michigan
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, U.S. Congresswoman Hillary Scholten (D-MI-03) announced she secured $440,000 in federal funding for Puertas Abiertas in Grand Rapids through the U.S. Department of Justice's (DOJ) Office for Victims of Crime. The funding will help expand supportive services for survivors of human trafficking throughout West Michigan, including case management, basic needs assistance, housing, employment services, and mental health support.

“We must work together to ensure every survivor of human trafficking has access to the support and resources they need to rebuild their lives. Puertas Abiertas is doing incredibly important work to make those services more accessible to people across West Michigan,” said Congresswoman Scholten. “I'm so proud to have helped secure this federal funding and bring resources back to our district that support survivors and strengthen our communities.”

Through this funding, Puertas Abiertas will expand its existing services and adapt its current treatment model to include a human trafficking screening tool. Staff will also receive specialized training to work with survivors and the organization will develop a referral network and conduct outreach and awareness training for local law enforcement and first responders.

title: After Devastating Wildfire Season, Congresswoman Schrier Introduces Bill to Improve Forest Management, Support Rural Communities, Lower Housing Costs
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) and House Agriculture Committee Chairman GT Thompson (PA-05) introduced the bipartisan Forest Bioeconomy Act to expand the use of low-value timber to decrease wildfire risk, support sustainable local timber production, and support affordable housing. The bill would incentivize industries to use low-value timber for wood products central to local economies across the country – lowering the cost of building materials and housing. Companion legislation was introduced in the Senate by Sens. Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Steve Daines (R-MT), Raphael Warnock (D-GA), and Jim Justice (R-WV).

Congresswoman Schrier’s bill responds to a letter from Chelan County leaders earlier this fall asking for improved national forest management policy, including incentivized use of low-value wood material thinned from forests in fire-prone areas.

“Communities across Washington state are still reeling from the damage of last summer’s devastating wildfires,” said Congresswoman Schrier. “Our families also face skyrocketing prices across the board, and need relief now. I am proud that this bill works to support our local economies, lower housing costs, and reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires by creating new demand for low-value timber. I will continue my work to ensure our communities and local leaders have the tools they need to keep Washingtonians safe and protect our cherished environments.”

“Forestry has sustained Pennsylvania’s rural communities for generations, which is why I am pleased to introduce the bipartisan Forest Bioeconomy Act. This bill will modernize the Forest Service’s public-private research partnerships so that innovations developed in federal laboratories reach the mills, manufacturers, and landowners who can put them to work. These commonsense provisions will keep Pennsylvania's forestry industry going for years to come, and ensure businesses have the tools necessary to meet increasing demand," Congressman GT Thompson said.

BACKGROUND: Forests across the country are currently overstocked, mostly with small-diameter, sick, lowstrength, or otherwise un-merchantable fiber. This overstocking increases wildfire risk and prevents healthy forest ecosystems from forming. The Forest Bioeconomy Act aims to support aging local markets and timber communities that sell this lower-value wood, creating high-demand products and ultimately lowering housing and building costs.

Currently, mass timber remains an early but promising application of low value timber. The durable material can reduce construction and transportation schedules while emitting less carbon in its lifecycle compared to other components. However, high costs and unfamiliarity in the industry remain large barriers for widespread adoption.

The Forest Bioeconomy Act would expand research and help build new innovative markets for forest products, especially including mass timber used for building materials. This research would bolster industry collaboration efforts similar to the success found at the Department of Energy. DOE has more than 40,000 patents and 1,400 active licenses, while the Forest Service has 42 patents and eight active licenses.

A closer connection between Forest Service research and the wood products industry would promote the use of low-value timber to lower costs and support local economies, while also reducing the risk of catastrophic wildfires.

“Washington State has long been a leader in sustainable forestry and innovative wood utilization,” said George Geissler, Washington State Forester. “I applaud Representatives Schrier and Thompson for introducing the Forest Bioeconomy Act. This legislation bridges a vital gap between federal research, local mills, and rural communities, turning low-value woody materials into viable products that grow our economy and protect our forests from climate change and catastrophic wildfire.”

“Forest-dependent communities have long called for investments that connect healthy forests with strong local economies,” said Cole Jenson, Acting Coalition Director of Rural Voices for Conservation Coalition. “The Forest Bioeconomy Act responds to that need by helping turn publicly funded research on underused wood into valuable products and new opportunities for rural businesses and workers. We applaud this effort to connect innovation with the practical needs of communities working to restore and steward our forests.

“We applaud Rep. Schrier and Chairman Thompson for their leadership introducing the House companion to the Forest Bioeconomy Act. Healthy forests depend on healthy markets, and right now, the wood products industry is facing real challenges,” Jackson Morrill, President and CEO of the American Wood Council, said. “Homebuilder sentiment is at its lowest level in over a decade, and we are grappling with a changing residuals market. The Forest Bioeconomy Act will spur much needed development in emerging markets like mass timber and will encourage critical technology transfer between the Forest Service and industry. We encourage Congress to work quickly to advance this bipartisan measure and look forward to working with both sponsors to secure passage.”

“In Washington state, we know how closely our communities’ safety and livelihoods are tied to the health of our forests,” said Annie Schmidt of the Alliance for Wildfire Resilience. “The Forest Bioeconomy Act would help communities across the country turn small trees and woody material removed to reduce wildfire risk into desirable products such as mass timber. That means making forest restoration more affordable, supporting rural jobs, and helping protect more homes and lives. We’re grateful to Congresswoman Schrier for advancing a practical solution to a national challenge.”

Endorsers: Rural Voices for Conservation Coalition, American Wood Council, National Association of Forest Owners, Alliance for Wildfire Resilience, and National Association of State Foresters.

Read more about the bill HERE.

title: Over 5,000 Join Congressman Brad Sherman's Town Hall on Priorities for the New Congress
text:
SHERMAN OAKS, CA — On Tuesday, November 17, Congressman Brad Sherman (CA-32) hosted a Telephone Town Hall -- his eighth district-wide Town Hall of the year -- bringing together over 5,000 residents for a wide-ranging discussion on the recent midterm elections, priorities for the incoming Congress, and pressing issues facing the country and local communities.

“The American people have made their voices heard loud and clear at the ballot box, and now it’s time for Washington to listen,” said Congressman Sherman. “As we prepare for a new Congress, I’m grateful for the opportunity to hear directly from my constituents about their priorities, and I look forward to continuing the fight for our interests, holding the administration accountable, and delivering results for the people I’m honored to represent.”

In his opening remarks, Congressman Sherman discussed the results of the November midterm elections and the priorities facing the incoming Congress, including congressional oversight of the Trump Administration, protecting vital federal programs, addressing economic challenges facing American families, and ensuring Congress fulfills its constitutional responsibilities. Sherman also addressed the upcoming transition in House leadership and the importance of delivering results for constituents in the new Congress.

Turning to local issues, Sherman highlighted his continued efforts to secure federal disaster assistance for communities devastated by the Los Angeles wildfires, including his participation in discussions with Governor Gavin Newsom and other California leaders at the U.S. Capitol earlier that day. Sherman reiterated his commitment to securing the additional federal resources needed to help families rebuild, restore damaged infrastructure, and support the region's long-term recovery.

The Telephone Town Hall featured special guest Councilmember-elect Barri Worth Girvan who discussed her plans and priorities for the West San Fernando Valley. Sherman welcomed the opportunity to work together on issues affecting their shared constituents, including public safety, infrastructure, housing affordability, and neighborhood quality of life.

Participants also had the opportunity to respond to interactive survey questions, providing Sherman with direct feedback on their priorities and expectations for the incoming Congress.

The results of the survey questions are as follows:

Should Rep. Hakeem Jeffries be elected Speaker of the House of Representatives?

Yes, vote for Hakeem Jeffries – 61%

No, vote for Jim Jordan – 4%

Vote for someone else, even if they are not running – 25%

Unsure – 10%

What should Congress do?

title: Over 50 Ohio Organizations Join Growing List  Supporting Brown for House Ag Chair
text:
Washington, DC – A coalition of over 50 Ohio agriculture, food, and conservation organizations have endorsed Vice Ranking Member Shontel Brown (OH-11) as the next Chair of the House Committee on Agriculture.

In a letter sent to Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, the Ohio Association of Foodbanks, Appalachian Center for Economic Networks, Children's Hunger Alliance, Ohio Ecological Food and Farm Association, Ohio Produce Growers and Marketers Association, Ohio Forestry Association, the BIPOC Food and Farming Networkand other signers wrote, “throughout Representative Brown’s time in Congress, she has been a steadfast champion for farmers, families, and food security, including strong support for SNAP and the critical role it plays in helping families put food on the table. She has demonstrated an ability to bring diverse voices together, build coalitions, and work toward meaningful results. Her leadership reflects an understanding that the interests of farmers, food producers, consumers, and the communities they serve are deeply connected.”

For a full list of signers and to read the letter, click here.

The Ohio coalition letter is the fourth major letter of endorsement in support for Vice Ranking Member Brown.

On November 10, the Ohio Farm Bureau Federation and Eight Statewide Ohio Commodity Organizations endorsed Vice Ranking Member Brown, writing: “We believe the committee needs a leader who listens to agricultural stakeholders, understands the challenges facing producers, and can build consensus around practical solutions. Representative Brown would bring these qualities to this important role.”

On November 12, the Midwest Council on Agriculture endorsed Vice Ranking Member Brown, writing: “The Agriculture Committee has long been one of the places in Congress where members have found common ground in service to farmers, ranchers, rural communities, and consumers. We believe she is well positioned to continue that tradition and to lead the committee in a way that reflects its longstanding bipartisan character.”

On November 13, the Ohio Farmers Union endorsed Vice Ranking Member Brown, writing: “She is a strong advocate of the three critical constituencies necessary to pass a farm bill; farm programs, conservation, and nutrition. She understands the need for a durable and effective farm safety net, the critical need for well-designed conservation programs and the growing demand for nutrition programs serving increasing numbers of primarily hungry seniors, single mothers and children.”

What They’re Saying:

“At the Ohio Association of Foodbanks, we believe that we can build stronger communities and better outcomes across Ohio through reliable access to healthy food. Our network has a decades-long track record of partnering with Ohio’s food and agriculture industry toward common ground solutions and strong food systems. Representative Brown is well-positioned to serve as U.S. House Agriculture Committee Chair because she will bring this same collaborative approach to the role. She has been a champion for Ohio’s foodbanks and the families that count on us to put food on the table, and she understands that issues around food and nutrition security, like SNAP, are deeply interconnected with issues impacting agriculture and the broad food supply chain. title: Congresswoman Tenney’s Fort Ontario Holocaust Refugee Shelter National Historical Park Act Advances Out of House Natural Resources
text:
Washington, DC — Congresswoman Claudia Tenney (NY-24) today announced that her Fort Ontario Holocaust Refugee Shelter National Historical Park Establishment Act (H.R. 1031) advanced out of the House Natural Resources Committee, advancing legislation to preserve Fort Ontario's historic legacy and recognize its unique role in providing refuge to Holocaust survivors during World War II.

Located in Oswego, New York, Fort Ontario served as "Safe Haven" from 1944 to 1946, the only refugee shelter established in the United States for victims fleeing the Holocaust. The shelter provided safety to 982 predominantly Jewish refugees escaping Nazi persecution. Tenney's legislation would establish portions of Fort Ontario as part of the National Park System, providing greater national recognition and long-term preservation of this important piece of American history. The legislation would maintain the existing State Historic Site under state management while ensuring the City of Oswego, Oswego County, and local organizations continue playing a central role in preserving and sharing Fort Ontario's history. Following its advancement through the House Natural Resources Committee, the legislation is now eligible for consideration by the full House of Representatives.

"The story of Fort Ontario is a powerful reminder of America's role as a refuge for those fleeing persecution and the importance of standing against hatred and antisemitism," said Congresswoman Tenney. "During one of the darkest chapters in human history, 982 refugees found safety and a new beginning in our community of Oswego. Their stories are an important part of our nation's history and must never be forgotten. Advancing this legislation through the Natural Resources Committee brings us one step closer to securing the national recognition Fort Ontario deserves. I look forward to working with my colleagues to move this bill through the House and ensure future generations understand the significance of this extraordinary place."

“The story of America’s only shelter for Jewish refugees fleeing the Holocaust deserves a permanent place in our national memory," said Chairman Bruce Westerman. “H.R. 1031 paves the way for Fort Ontario, where 982 refugees found safety during World War II and many later became American citizens, to become a unit of the National Park System. I commend Rep. Tenney for honoring their courage and ensuring future generations understand this powerful chapter of American history.”

title: Rep. Tlaib introduces bill to ban non-disclosure agreements between government agencies and corporations
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Rep. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) introduced the No Secret Deals Act, which would prohibit government agencies and public officials from entering into private non-disclosure agreements with corporations. NDAs have been increasingly used to accelerate contracts and projects like AI data centers and water utility privatization, hiding potential environmental and public health harms, details of tax break packages, and shielding government from accountability to the people.

In Michigan, NDAs have been abused by state and local governments to hide key details of tax giveaways to corporations. A 2023 report found that 1 in 5 Michigan lawmakers had signed an NDA with a state agency to shield business incentive details from the public. As the Detroit City Council debates a $548 million tax incentive package for billionaire Dan Gilbert’s Renaissance Center redevelopment, key details of the project are hidden by an NDA.

“Our government is making secret deals with greedy corporations that we know don’t have our best interests in mind. They know these projects like AI data centers are unpopular, so they’d rather make these business arrangements in the dark and cut out public opinion entirely,” said Rep. Tlaib. “My bill stops the secret deals and brings them into the light so people can see how their tax dollars are being spent. We deserve to have a say in projects that use our tax dollars and public land, that affect our health and environment.”

Even after data centers are built, NDAs help hide and obscure their energy effects. A research team from Harvard University relied on satellite imagery and carbon footprints to determine that 403 data centers in the US used more electricity than both New York City and Los Angeles combined and emitted 25.7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide. Data centers are also not required to publicly disclose their electricity use and emissions.

The No Secret Deals Act would unveil critical details of agreements and business dealings between government agencies and corporations, protecting the public’s right to be informed. Read the full bill text here.

The bill is cosponsored by U.S. Reps. Maxwell Frost (FL-10) and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07).

“No private company should be allowed to enter into an NDA with public officials – whether a data center, meat packers, a private water utility or any other profit-driven company. NDAs seek to keep critical information from voters and impacted communities. They are used to subvert democracy,” said Mitch Jones, Managing Director of Policy and Litigation at Food & Water Watch. “We thank Reps. Tlaib, Frost and Grijalva for introducing the No Secret Deals Act of 2026. By banning these NDAs, communities will at least have a clear picture of what these aggressive corporations are angling for, and where their local leaders stand.”

“For generations, communities of color and low-income have been excluded from critical permitting decisions that have adverse consequences for their health, local economies, and overall quality of life,” said Yosef Robele Federal Policy Manager at WE ACT for Environmental Justice. “Communities have a right to know what potentially harmful projects are being built in their backyards. The industry practice of using NDAs allows polluting projects such as data centers, warehouses, and other facilities to be built with little transparency and accountability. We need legislation like the No Secret Deals Act to stop this antidemocratic practice and protect the rights of environmental justice communities.”

“The No Secret Deals Act is exactly the kind of sound legislation we need to reign in an out of control tech industry that puts billionaires over people and the planet. The data center buildout has been opaque from the start, with corporations hiding environmental and public health impacts of their facilities while making us subsidize the harms and costs,” said Mar Zepeda Salazar, legislative director at Climate Justice Alliance. “Banning nondisclosure agreements imposed by corporations on local governments is a great first step to ensure communities have all the information they need to make informed decisions about what is built in their backyards. We applaud the members of Congress who are spearheading this direly needed legislation.”

It is also endorsed by 114 organizations: 198 methods, 350 Bay Area Action, 350 Conejo / San Fernando Valley, 350 Triangle, 350Hawaii, Americans for Financial Reform, ANHE-Alliance of Nurses for Healthy Environments, Animal Alliance Network, Animals Are Sentient Beings, Inc., Between the Waters, Bucks Environmental Action, Center for Organizing, Center for Progressive Reform, Change Begins With ME Indivisible, Cherokee Concerned Citizens, Church Women United in New York State, Clean Air Council, Clean, Healthy, Educated, Safe & Sustainable Community, Climate Defenders, Climate Families NYC, Climate Justice Alliance, Climate Reality Project – NJ, Climate Revolution Action Network, Coalition to Protect New York, Community Water Justice, Concern Citizens of Northampton County, Court Nativity of Our Lady #931 CDA, Dominican Sisters of Sparkill, Don’t Gas The Meadowlands Coalition, Don’t Waste Michigan, EarthCare Animal Ministry at Unity of Buffalo, Environmental Advocates Mississippi, Flint Rising, Flow Water Advocates, FoCo Trash Mob, a Beyond Plastics Affiliate, Food & Water Watch, Fossil Free Tompkins, FreshWater Accountability Project, Friends of Bell Smith Springs, Friends of the Earth US, GELF (Green Education and Legal Fund), Great Egg Harbor Watershed Association, GreenFaith, GreenLatinos, Greenpeace USA, Greenvest, Habitable, Holy Spirit Missionary Sisters, USA-JPIC, Honor the Earth, Income Movement, Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy, John Muir Project, Little Lakes Sustainability Network, Long Beach Alliance for Clean Energy, Maine Unitarian Universalist State Advocacy Network, Maryknoll Sisters, Merchantville (NJ) Democratic Committee, Milwaukee Riverkeeper, MLK Coalition of Greater Los Angeles; Topanga Peace Alliance, Move Past Plastic (MPP), MoveOn.org HobokenRESIST!, National Coalition Against Cryptomining, NC Climate Justice Collective, NC WARN, New Jersey Poor People’s Campaign, New York Progressive Action Network, Northjersey Pipeline Walkers, Nuclear Information and Resource Service, Ohio Nuclear Free Network, Oil and Gas Action Network, Oil Change International, PAUSE (People of Albany United for Safe Energy) / 350Albany, People Power United, Physicians for Social Responsibility, Progressive Democrats of America, Progressives for Climate, Protect PT, Salvation and Social Justice, San Francisco Bay Physicians for Social Responsibility, SaveOldYork.org, Seneca Lake Guardian, Sisters of Charity of New York, Sisters of St. Dominic of Blauvelt, NY, South Jersey Progressive Democrats, STG Ministries of North America Southwest Pennsylvania, Stop the Algonquin Pipeline Expansion, Sustainable Medina County, Teaneck Peace and Justice, Terra Advocati, The Clean Air Coalition of Western New York, The Grape Belt Community Group, Therapists for Peace & Justice, Third Act, Third Act Colorado, Third Act Georgia, Third Act Maryland, Third Act New Jersey, Third Act Union, Third Act Upstate NY, Tucker United, Turtle Island Restoration Network, Unitarian Universalist Action New Hampshire, Unitarian Universalists for Social Justice, United Native Americans, UpstreamPgh, UU FaithAction NJ, UUCOV Social Justice Committee, Vessel Project of Louisiana, Virginia Citizens Consumer Council, Water You Fighting For, Waterspirit, WE ACT for Environmental Justice, WESPAC Foundation, Inc., and Westchester for Change.

title: Rep. Derek Tran Statement on Hakeem Jeffries’ Historic Election as Democratic Nominee for Speaker of the House
text:

With an overwhelming majority, Hakeem Jeffries was voted to be the Democratic nominee for the Speaker of the House of Representatives for the 120th Congress:

As a proud veteran, I often return to my military training as a beacon of light. In the United States Army, there is a foundational truth taught to every soldier from day one: you do not choose the terrain you fight on, and you do not win a campaign with a divided platoon. You win through discipline, unity of command, and a leader who never leaves a soldier behind.

From the streets of Crown Heights to the floor of the House, Jeffries has stood shoulder-to-shoulder with every wing of our Caucus— Members in purple districts, staunch progressives, members of the Congressional Asian and Pacific American Caucus, Black Caucus, Hispanic Caucus, and Equality Caucus, veterans, and newcomers alike. He has fearlessly led our party through the dark days of the Trump administration, advocated on behalf of American families, and will chart a new path forward for Democrats to deliver prosperity to the American people.

He came to Congress as a freshman Member from Brooklyn, rose to leadership and became the first African American to serve as a party leader in Congress, and now Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries will make history as the first Black Speaker of the House of Representatives. title: Representative Tran Urges Trump Administration  to Release $15.3 Billion in Taiwan Defense Funding
text:
Washington, D.C. – This week, ahead of President Trump and President Xi Jinping’s meeting in China, U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) led a letter to President Trump demanding the release of $15.3 billion in security assistance for Taiwan. This critical funding will shore up Taiwan’s defense capabilities and aid the United States in continuing our longstanding diplomatic partnership with Taiwan.

“Our commitment to supporting Taiwan’s security helps to promote the political, security, and economic interests of the United States. The continued delay of funding and defense packages to Taiwan jeopardizes these interests. As such, we urge you to maintain our commitment to Taiwan during conversations with President Xi, obligate the funds approved by Congress for Foreign Military Financing and the Taiwan Security Cooperation Initiative, and submit the $14 billion package of Foreign Military Sales for formal Congressional approval as soon as possible,” Representative Tran and his colleagues wrote in the letter.

The United States’ relationship with Taiwan has long been based on the Taiwan Relations Act and the Six Assurances to Taiwan, a foundation that guides U.S. commitment to regional peace and shapes our security relationship with Taiwan. This relationship includes providing defensive arms to strengthen Taiwan's self-defense. In accordance with this policy, Congress appropriated $1.3 billion in security assistance for Taiwan last year; however, the Trump Administration has yet to release the funds. This $1.3 billion is in addition to a $14 billion package that the Administration signaled to Congress in January but has failed to move forward.

Alongside Rep. Tran, the letter was also signed by Representatives Wesley Bell (MO-01), Joe Courtney (CT-02), Dave Min (CA-47), Pat Ryan (NY-18), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), Jill Tokuda (HI-2), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Tom Suozzi (NY-03), Jim Costa (CA-21), André Carson (IN-07), Ted Lieu (CA-36), and Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06).

As a member of the powerful House Armed Services Committee and the Congressional Taiwan Caucus, Representative Tran is committed to upholding peace and security in the Pacific and strengthening the U.S. partnership with Taiwan:

Rep. Tran cosponsored the Taiwan Representative Office Act, which renames the “Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office” to the “Taiwan Representative Office,” reaffirming U.S. support for Taiwan.

Rep. Tran also cosponsored the Taiwan and American Space Assistance Act, which expands the authority of NASA and NOAA to cooperate directly with the Taiwan Space Agency for civilian space activities.

title: Vindman Introduces Legislative Package to Lower Electricity Costs and Hold Utility Companies Accountable
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) introduced a package of four bills aimed at lowering electricity costs, strengthening oversight of utility companies, and protecting Virginia families and small businesses from bearing the costs of unnecessary utility company projects.

As electricity demand continues to grow and utility companies invest billions in expanding and modernizing the electric grid, consumers must not be forced to shoulder costs that could be avoided or fairly assigned back to utility companies.

“Virginians are already struggling with rising electricity bills, and they shouldn’t have to pay even more for utility companies’ poor investments and lack of accountability,” said Vindman. “As energy demand grows, we need to modernize our grid, make sure large energy users like data centers pay their fair share, and protect families and small businesses from being saddled with unnecessary costs. The bottom line is simple: hardworking Virginians shouldn’t be footing the bill for utility companies and massive corporations to protect their bottom lines.”

As we face the rapid expansion of energy-intensive data centers, outdated transmission infrastructure, and unnecessary utility spending, Virginians deserve a grid that is reliable, affordable, and built with ratepayers in mind. This package would promote smarter investments, reduce unnecessary costs, and hold utility companies accountable for putting consumers first.

The following bills are included in this package:

The Make Data Centers Pay Act would protect Virginians from rising utility bills by requiring medium and large data centers to pay the full cost of the power generation, transmission lines, and grid upgrades needed to serve them.

The Lower Electricity Bills Act wouldforce utilities to use low-cost modern technologies whenever they build or upgrade transmission lines, and to deploy them wherever the benefits outweigh the costs. Companies that fail to make these improvements will face penalties from federal regulators.

The Smart Transmission Line Placement Act would cut unnecessary red tape by exempting transmission line upgrades within existing right-of-way corridors from lengthy federal reviews. This policy improvement would make it easier for utility companies to boost grid capacity by modernizing infrastructure already in place rather than building new projects.

The Local Transmission Accountability Act would strengthen oversight of utility companies’ local transmission projects to help prevent unnecessary infrastructure spending from driving up electricity bills for consumers. Utility companies that start projects that harm local ratepayers will face steep fines.

BACKGROUND

Vindman has long been a champion for holding data centers and electric utilities accountable.

He introduced the Make Data Centers Pay Act to protect hardworking Virginia families and small businesses from being forced to shoulder the rising electricity costs associated with the growing electricity demands of data centers.

He also introduced the Smart Data Center Policy Act to prevent data center development near neighborhoods, schools, and parks.

Vindman introduced the Home Energy Affordability Act to limit how often utilities can change residential utility rates and change prices for everyday Virginians, as well as the Utility Hikes Transparency Act, which would create the first comprehensive, machine-readable federal database of retail utility rate changes in the United States.

He has also fought against corruption in the energy sector by championing the Energy Utility Lobbying Ban Act, which would bar former government officials from lobbying on behalf of the companies they used to regulate.

What’s more, Vindman was the first member of Virginia’s congressional delegation to publicly oppose the proposed merger between NextEra and Dominion Energy, raising concerns about its potential impact on electricity rates and Virginia consumers.

He delivered remarks at a Virginia State Corporation Commission (SCC) public hearing on the proposed merger, urging regulators to reject the proposal and put the interests of ratepayers ahead of corporate profits. Vindman submitted official public comments to the SCC urging them to block the NextEra-Dominion merger.
