title: Wittman, Dingell’s Earth Mapping Resources Initiative Reauthorization Act Passes House
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Rob Wittman (VA-01) and Congresswoman Debbie Dingell’s (MI-06) bipartisan Earth Mapping Resources Initiative (MRI) Reauthorization Act of 2026 passed the House unanimously. This legislation will reauthorize the Earth MRI program that identifies, maps, and studies domestic minerals.

“Before we can begin to develop our domestic resources, we must first identify, map, and study our mineral supply — which is why I’m supportive of Earth MRI and the ongoing domestic mapping efforts at the Department of Interior,” said Rep. Wittman. “Geological mapping produces economic returns many times greater than its cost, increases exploration activities, and strengthens domestic critical mineral supply chains, strengthening our economy and making the U.S. less dependent on foreign adversaries. I am proud to have introduced this legislation with Congresswoman Dingell.”

“This is a huge step forward in strengthening our critical mineral supply chains. I am proud to have worked alongside Congressman Wittman to pass this legislation, which will provide us with the data to better understand our nation’s mineral resources. By strengthening our critical mineral supply chains, we are strengthening American manufacturing and decreasing our reliance on critical minerals from adversaries like China. This bipartisan bill will help build a stronger economy, create good-paying jobs, and support American workers.” - Rep. Dingell

“America cannot secure its mineral future without knowing what resources lie beneath our feet. H.R. 9640 reauthorizes the Earth Mapping Resources Initiative through 2031 and incorporates modern sensing technologies to improve our understanding of our nation’s mineral wealth. I commend Representative Wittman for being a champion of this program that strengthens the data available to support domestic resource development and build more secure American mineral supply chains.” - Chairman Westerman

Background:

Established in 2019, Earth MRI focuses on enhancing our understanding of the geologic features of the United States. The initiative seeks to complete comprehensive mapping of domestic minerals by 2031. As Congress and this administration work to strengthen domestic supply chains for critical minerals, reduce dependence on foreign adversaries, and support American manufacturing, Congressman Wittman recognizes that responsible resource development begins with reliable data. Senator Murkowski has introduced companion legislation in the Senate.

title: Baldwin, Marshall Lead Bipartisan Group Calling on Regulators to Reject Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern Rail Mega-Merger
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) and Roger Marshall (R-KS) led Senators Martin Heinrich (D-NM), John Hoeven (R-ND), Steve Daines (R-MT), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Tim Sheehy (R-MT), and Chuck Schumer (D-NY) in calling on federal regulators to reject a mega-merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern. The Senators argue that the merger would drastically reduce competition in freight rail, raising costs on consumers and worsening already poor service for American farmers, manufacturers, and businesses that rely on freight rail to get their goods to market.

“If approved, this transaction would represent the most significant consolidation in the freight rail industry in decades and would reshape the U.S. freight rail network and supply chain. Specifically, we are concerned that a merger of this magnitude could increase costs, reduce transportation options for shippers, undermine reliable service, and further diminish competition in an already highly consolidated industry,” wrote the Senators in a letter to the Surface Transportation Board (STB), which is currently reviewing the merger. “Given these significant risks to rail shippers, consumers, and the broader U.S. economy, we urge the Board to reject the proposed merger.”

Since the 1950s, the rail industry has consolidated from more than 100 Class I freight railroads to only six today. This consolidation has left many manufacturers, utility companies, agricultural producers, and small businesses with limited competitive options for moving their goods. In recent years, shippers across the country have raised concerns about rail service, reliability, and rates, particularly where they are served by only one carrier. Further consolidation threatens to exacerbate existing service challenges and further entrench the lack of competition that has left shippers with little leverage to negotiate fair rates or secure reliable service.

The Senators also raised concerns about threats Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena made earlier this year against shippers – including Wisconsin farmers, businesses, and manufacturers – who speak out against the merger. In a video Senator Baldwin helped make public, Vena told a room of rail shippers that he’ll probably raise rates on anyone who opposes the merger to “teach [them] a lesson.” The Senators urged the Surface Transportation Board to take Vena’s words seriously and consider whether such threats prevent shippers from raising legitimate concerns about this merger’s impact on already high costs and poor service.

“Given the extraordinary scale and potential consequences of this transaction, the applicants must demonstrate that the merger will enhance competition and deliver meaningful benefits to shippers and consumers—rather than simply promise greater efficiencies. We do not believe that the railroads have met that standard, and we believe further consolidation of the freight rail industry is not in the public interest. We urge the Board to reject the proposed UP-NS merger,” concluded the Senators.

For months, Senator Baldwin has been urging federal regulators to thoroughly scrutinize this merger’s impact on competition, shipping costs, and service reliability for Made in Wisconsin businesses who rely on freight rail:

July 2025: Senators Baldwin and Marshall urged the Surface Transportation Board (STB) to closely examine the proposed merger's impact on competition, costs, and reliability.

November 2025: During a Senate Commerce Committee nomination hearing, Baldwin pressed STB member nominees Richard Kloster and Michelle Schultz on whether they would act independently of President Trump when making regulatory decisions.

December 2025: Senator Baldwin called on the STB to reject the merger application filed by Union Pacific to acquire Norfolk Southern.

June 2026: During a Senate Commerce Committee nomination hearing, Baldwin questioned STB nominee Karen Hedlund on CEO Jim Vena’s past comments threatening retaliation. She also asked for clarification if Union Pacific could disregard its burden to prove the merger satisfies the public interest statute.

July 2026: Baldwin urged the Surface Transportation Board to take Union Pacific’s threat of retaliation against shippers who do not support its merger with Norfolk Southern seriously.

November 2026: A video Senator Baldwin helped make public showed Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena threatening to raise rates on customers – including Wisconsin farmers, manufacturers, and businesses – who oppose the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern megamerger, saying he’ll probably raise rates on shippers who oppose the merger to “teach [them] a lesson.”

A full version of this letter is available here and below.

Dear Chair Fuchs, Vice Chair Schultz, Member Hedlund, and Member Kloster,

We write today with serious concerns regarding the proposed merger of Union Pacific (UP) and Norfolk Southern (NS). If approved, this transaction would represent the most significant consolidation in the freight rail industry in decades and would reshape the U.S. freight rail network and supply chain. Specifically, we are concerned that a merger of this magnitude could increase costs, reduce transportation options for shippers, undermine reliable service, and further diminish competition in an already highly consolidated industry. Given these significant risks to rail shippers, consumers, and the broader U.S. economy, we urge the Board to reject the proposed merger.

Since the 1950s, the rail industry has consolidated from more than 100 Class I freight railroads to only six today. This consolidation has left many manufacturers, utility companies, agricultural producers, and small businesses with limited competitive options for moving their goods. In recent years, shippers across the country have raised concerns about rail service, reliability, and rates, particularly where they are served by only one carrier. Further consolidation threatens to exacerbate existing service challenges and further entrench the lack of competition that has left shippers with little leverage to negotiate fair rates or secure reliable service.

We are also deeply concerned by the recently released video of UP CEO Jim Vena's remarks at the Southwest Association of Rail Shippers annual conference in March 2026. Mr. Vena suggested raising rates by an additional three to four percent on customers who opposed the merger to "teach [them] a lesson." While UP has characterized these remarks as a joke, the company resisted public disclosure of the footage, including by appealing an administrative law judge's order, prompting the Board to deny its appeal on November 4, 2026. The video is now public, and the Board should take Vena at his word that he plans to retaliate against shippers and consider whether shippers can meaningfully participate in the Board's review process without fear of retaliation. The Board must be able to hear candidly from shippers to fully evaluate the potential impacts of this merger, particularly in an industry where many customers have limited competitive alternatives.

A merger of this magnitude could also trigger consolidation among the remaining Class I railroads. The Board recognized this concern when it adopted its major rail merger rules in 2001, establishing a heightened standard for major transactions and requiring applicants to demonstrate that a proposed transaction is consistent with the public interest and adequately addresses competitive harms. Those rules also require consideration of the potential downstream effects of further consolidation. We strongly urge the Board to apply these standards rigorously in its review of the proposed UP-NS merger.

The proposed UP-NS merger would further concentrate market power in an already consolidated industry, threatening to increase costs, undermine reliable service, and leave shippers with even fewer options. The recent concerns surrounding potential retaliation against shippers only underscore the risks associated with increased consolidation. Given the extraordinary scale and potential consequences of this transaction, the applicants must demonstrate that the merger will enhance competition and deliver meaningful benefits to shippers and consumers—rather than simply promise greater efficiencies. We do not believe that the railroads have met that standard, and we believe further consolidation of the freight rail industry is not in the public interest. We urge the Board to reject the proposed UP-NS merger.

###

title: EXCLUSIVE: Senate Republicans Advance Trump’s Effort to Abolish Dept of Education
text:
The legislation would codify President Donald Trump and Linda McMahon’s executive actions to wind down the agency

FIRST ON FOX: Senate Republicans are advancing a major legislative push to dismantle the Department of Education, introducing a 10-bill package aimed at permanently transferring the agency’s core programs to other federal departments.

Sen. Jim Banks, R-Ind., introduced the Senate companion to the Less Bureaucracy, Better Education legislative package on Wednesday, which would codify President Donald Trump and Education Secretary Linda McMahon’s executive actions to wind down the department. Sens. Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., and Ashley Moody, R-Fla., are co-sponsoring the Senate effort.

“The federal education bureaucracy has failed students and families for decades. President Trump and Secretary McMahon are finally putting parents first and returning power where it belongs. Our bills will make their reforms permanent, eliminate layers of Washington bureaucracy, and ensure taxpayers are no longer forced to prop up a failed department,” Banks told Fox News Digital.

DEPT OF ED PUSHES AHEAD WITH EFFORTS TO DISMANTLE FEDERAL BUREAUCRACY AFTER BLUE WAVE

Throughout his 2024 presidential campaign, Trump promised to eliminate the Department of Education, later signing a March 2025 executive order directing McMahon to begin dismantling the 45-year-old agency. While fully abolishing a Cabinet-level department requires congressional approval—and 60 votes to overcome a Senate filibuster—Republicans are moving to lock in the administration’s restructuring piece by piece.

McMahon told Fox News Digital that the department acts primarily as a pass-through entity for federal dollars and contends that its day-to-day operations are nonessential.

“For too long, an overgrown Washington bureaucracy has funneled trillions of taxpayer dollars into top-down mandates and administrative red tape. Exactly one year after we announced six critical partnerships to begin reversing that trend, Senators Banks, Tuberville, Moody, and Lee are introducing the ‘Less Bureaucracy, Better Education’ package to permanently codify the Trump Administration’s historic reforms,” she said.

She went on to say, “This vital legislation will make permanent the work we have done to align programs with the agencies best suited to support them and return education authority to those closest to the child. I commend their leadership in launching this important effort, and I look forward to working together to improve education for our students and families.”

The Senate introduction follows 10 interagency agreements signed between May 2025 and March 2026 across five federal departments — Labor, Treasury, Health and Human Services, State and Interior — as the Education Department seeks to shrink its footprint.

TRUMP’S FIRST-YEAR GOVERNMENT OVERHAUL DELIVERS CHANGE WASHINGTON HASN’T SEEN SINCE THE 1960S

For example, the Department of Labor took on a major role in the day-to-day administration of adult education, family literacy and career and technical education programs under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act and the Perkins Act. While Labor manages operational duties, the Department of Education retains statutory oversight as services shift to states and grant recipients.

In another major move, the agency partnered with the Department of the Treasury to assume operational responsibility for managing the federal student loan portfolio and collecting on defaulted student debt.

MCMAHON CALLS FOR ‘RESET’ OF EDUCATION AFTER US SPENT $3 TRILLION AND STILL SAW READING SCORES DECLINE

According to Department of Education officials, the goal of the partnerships is to demonstrate a “proof of concept” to Congress that essential federal education functions and funding flows can be reallocated across executive branch agencies without disruption. An agency official previously told Fox News Digital that staffers are effectively working to put themselves out of a job under Trump’s orders because the department is unnecessary.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS ‘HARD RESET’ FOR AMERICAN SCHOOLS, VOWS TO PUT PARENTS ‘BACK IN CHARGE’

The House Education and Workforce Committee, led by Chairman Tim Walberg, R-Mich., already advanced its version of the 10-bill package along party lines in July.

“Every student deserves an education that works for them, yet the status quo is failing our children. Republicans believe in a new vision that puts students, families, and educators in the driver’s seat. I am glad to see my colleagues in the Senate take action to end the bureaucracy and deliver on that vision for the American people,” Walberg told Fox News Digital.

CHARTER SCHOOL FOUNDER BACKS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PUSH TO DECENTRALIZE K-12 EDUCATION

Sen. Mike Lee, R-Utah, echoed that sentiment, arguing that Washington has sidelined local communities for too long.

“For too long, the centralized bureaucracy of the Department of Education has overridden state and local control of schooling while failing America’s families. As President Trump returns education to the people, our legislation returns the remaining worthwhile function of the Department to other appropriate federal agencies,” Lee told Fox News Digital.

ED announced earlier this year it moved to a smaller building to reduce the agency’s footprint as part of its broader effort to dismantle itself.

Department staff will move out of the Lyndon B. Johnson headquarters building, so the Department of Energy can eventually move in by August.

“Our schools are supposed to be preparing the next generation of Americans for LIFE—not pushing some woke ideology. I’m proud to introduce this bill with Sen. Banks to codify one of President Trump’s biggest promises—dismantling the [ED]. Let’s put our students first and get it done,” Sen. Tuberville told Fox News Digital.

title: Sen. Banks and Colleagues Introduce Package to Dismantle Department of Education Bureaucracy
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and three Senate colleagues introduced the Less Bureaucracy, Better Education legislative package, a set of 10 bills that would codify President Donald Trump and Secretary of Education Linda McMahon’s work to dismantle the federal education bureaucracy and ensure students, families, and taxpayers come first.

In March of 2025, President Trump signed an executive order directing the Secretary of Education to take all lawful steps to facilitate the closure of the Department of Education, return authority over education to states and local communities, and maintain the delivery of services, programs, and benefits on which Americans rely. The Department has since entered into interagency agreements to co-administer federal education functions to agencies better equipped to administer them. These 10 bills would codify those agreements and make the administration’s reforms permanent.

Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.): “The federal education bureaucracy has failed students and families for decades. President Trump and Secretary McMahon are finally putting parents first and returning power where it belongs. Our bills will make their reforms permanent, eliminate layers of Washington bureaucracy, and ensure taxpayers are no longer forced to prop up a failed department.”

U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon: “For too long, an overgrown Washington bureaucracy has funneled trillions of taxpayer dollars into top-down mandates and administrative red tape. Exactly one year after we announced six critical partnerships to begin reversing that trend, Senator Banks, Tuberville, Moody and Lee are introducing ‘Less Bureaucracy, Better Education’ package to permanently codify the Trump Administration’s historic reforms. This vital legislation will make permanent the work we have done to align programs with the agencies best suited to support and return education authority to those closest to the child. I commend their leadership in launching this important effort, and I look forward to working together to improve education for our students and families.”

Sen. Tommy Tuberville (R-Ala.): “Our schools are supposed to be preparing the next generation of Americans for life­—not pushing some woke ideology. I’m proud to introduce this bill with Sen. Banks to codify one of President Trump’s biggest promises—dismantling the DOE. Let’s put our students first and get it done.”

Sen. Mike Lee (R-Utah): “For too long, the centralized bureaucracy of the Department of Education has overridden state and local control of schooling while failing America’s families. As President Trump returns education to the people, our legislation returns the remaining worthwhile function of the Department to other appropriate federal agencies.”

House Education and Workforce Committee Chairman Tim Walberg (R-Mich.): “Every student deserves an education that works for them, yet the status quo is failing our children. Republicans believe in a new vision that puts students, families, and educators in the driver’s seat. I am glad to see my colleagues in the Seante take action to end the bureaucracy and deliver on that vision for the American people.”

Read the Fox Exclusive here:

The Less Bureaucracy, Better Education Legislative Package:

Less Bureaucracy, Better Workforce Development Act, sponsored by Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.):

Transfers the Department of Education’s career, technical, and adult education functions–including Perkins Career and Technical Education programs and WIOA Title II adult education programs–to the Department of Labor.

Less Bureaucracy, Better Foreign Gift Transparency Act, sponsored by Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.):

Transfers enforcement of foreign gift and contract disclosure requirements for colleges and Universities from the Department of Education to the Department of State.

Less Bureaucracy, Better K-12 Education Act, sponsored by Sen. Tommy Tuberville (R-Ala.):

Transfers most functions of the Office of Elementary and Secondary Education, including Title I, charter schools, rural education, impact aid, and education for homeless children and youth to the Department of Labor.

Less Bureaucracy, Better Higher Education, sponsored by Sen. Tommy Tuberville (R-Ala.):

Transfers numerous postsecondary education programs, including TRIO, GEAR UP, HBCU and other minority-serving institution programs, veteran student support, and disability-related higher education programs, to the Department of Labor.

Less Bureaucracy, Better Student Aid Act, sponsored by Sen. Ashley Moody (R-Fla.):

Transfers administration of federal student aid, including Pell Grants, federal student loans, Federal Work-Study, and loan servicing and collection, from the Department of Education to the Department of the Treasury.

Less Bureaucracy, Better Foreign Medical Accreditation Act, sponsored by Sen. Mike Lee (R-Utah):

Transfers foreign medical accreditation functions from the Department of Education to the Department of Health and Human Services.

Less Bureaucracy, Better Tribal Education Act, sponsored by Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.):

Transfers 22 tribal and Native education, career and technical education, and job-training programs from the Department of Education to the Department of the Interior.

Less Bureaucracy, Better Child Care for Student Parents Act, sponsored by Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.):

Transfers the Child Care Access Means Parents in School program from the Department of Education to the Department of Health and Human Services.

Less Bureaucracy, Better International Education Oversight Act, sponsored by Sen. Mike Lee (R-Utah):

Transfers Title VI international education and foreign language programs and the Fulbright-Hays program from the Department of Education to the Department of State.

Less Bureaucracy, Better Family Engagement Act, sponsored by Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.):

Transfers several K-12 family, community engagement, and school support programs from the Department of Education to the Department of Health and Human Services.

The House Education and Workforce Committee advanced legislation in July.

title: Sen. Banks Applauds Senate Approval for New VA Clinic in Fishers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the Senate Committee on Veterans’ Affairs approved the major lease authorization for a new VA outpatient clinic in Fishers. This constitutes final approval by the Senate. Now, the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs must approve the lease to allow the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to move forward with the project. The Fishers clinic will complement the replacement Roudebush VA Medical Center in downtown Indianapolis.

Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.): “Veterans north of Indianapolis deserve VA health care in a modern facility closer to home. This clinic will be a one-stop-shop for outpatient care and the 37th VA facility in Indiana. Senate approval is a major step forward, and I will keep working to get the project done.”

Background:

The new VA outpatient clinic will be located in Fishers, serving veterans in Hamilton County and the area between Lafayette, Peru, Marion, and Muncie. It will be one of VA’s largest outpatient clinics, nearly 190,000 square feet, and include the full range of primary and specialty outpatient care. The Fishers clinic is intended as a more convenient destination for veterans living north of Indianapolis to get routine care, while the Roudebush VA Medical Center and its eventual replacement will continue to provide inpatient and complex care in Indianapolis. VA plans to award a 20-year lease to a developer to construct the Fishers clinic according to VA requirements and specifications.

title: Sen. Banks Secures $20 Million for New Harmony Bridge in Senate Appropriations Proposal
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Senator Jim Banks (R-Ind.) secured the inclusion of $20 million to rehabilitate the Harmony Way Bridge in the Senate Appropriations Committee’s proposed fiscal year 2027 Transportation, Housing, and Urban Development (THUD) appropriations bill. If enacted, the funding, along with state or local matching dollars, would enable an estimated $25 million project to restore and reopen the bridge, which has been closed to vehicles and pedestrians since 2012.

Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.): “The New Harmony Bridge was an important link between Southwest Indiana and Illinois that residents, workers, farmers, shoppers, first responders, and patients long relied on to cross the Wabash River quickly and safely. The bridge was also the gateway to New Harmony, one of Indiana’s cultural treasures. It has been closed for far too long. I have been working closely with local leaders, citizen groups, and Senator Durbin to reopen it, and my $20 million funding request is a major step forward. I’ll keep pushing to get this funding enacted and restore the New Harmony Bridge.”

The prospective $20 million of federal funding would cover 80% of the project’s cost, with the remaining $5 million of state or local matching dollars covering the other 20% to be split between Indiana and Illinois. Posey County, the town of New Harmony, and a citizen benefactor have already pledged significant contributions to help Indiana meet its matching commitment.

The Senate Appropriations Committee’s fiscal year 2027 THUD bill is not final, and it will need to be enacted in order to appropriate the $20 million. Since mid-2025, Banks has worked with the New Harmony and Wabash River Bridge Authority and leaders in Posey and Vanderburgh counties, Mount Vernon, New Harmony, Evansville, and the surrounding region to pursue options for rehabilitating the bridge. Sen. Banks also collaborated closely with Sen. Durbin (D-Ill.) to secure the funding. Durbin submitted a similar funding request and has facilitated conversations with the Illinois Department of Transportation.

The Posey County Council, Posey County Commissioners, Posey County EMS, Posey County Trail Coalition, Town of New Harmony, New Harmony Business Association, One New Harmony, City of Evansville, Evansville Trail Coalition, Evansville Regional Economic Partnership, and Vanderburgh County Commissioners have all submitted letters supporting the project and Sen. Banks’ funding request.

title: Permitting Reform Means More Energy, Built Faster, and Lower Costs for Families
text:
“It is time for Congress to pass historic permitting reform. America wants to build. America is ready to build. We have the resources, the tools, and the talent to build. Now, Washington D.C. needs to get out of the way and let Americans get to work.”

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso (R-Wyo.) today touted the broad support for the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026.

Senator Barrasso called for the swift passage of the legislation because it will streamline environmental reviews, rein in out-of-control judicial reviews and abusive lawsuits, and lower the cost of energy for American families.

Click HERE to watch Senator Barrasso’s remarks.

Sen. Barrasso’s remarks as prepared:

“It is time for Congress to pass historic permitting reform. America wants to build. America is ready to build. We have the resources, the tools, and the talent to build. Now, Washington D.C. needs to get out of the way and let Americans get to work. If we want life to be more affordable in America, we need to make it more affordable to build in America.

“On Monday, 70 Senators came to this Floor and voted in support of our Senate permitting reform bill. A strong, bipartisan majority voted yes to cut through red tape – red tape that slows down our progress.

“The support reaches far beyond this chamber. Organizations who support job creators and labor unions alike support this bill. Many energy producers and utility companies support this bill. Manufacturers who are ready to invest

and workers who are ready to build are calling on Congress to act. Even some liberal climate groups are urging swift passage.

“Support for permitting reform is especially strong in my home state of Wyoming. The Petroleum Association of Wyoming supports it. The Wyoming Mining Association supports it. The Wyoming Energy Authority supports it. This bill is good for Wyoming and good for America.

“The Editorial pages of major newspapers are calling for swift passage. The Washington Post endorsed this legislation. The Wall Street Journal endorsed it. Bloomberg endorsed it. Even the liberal New York Times endorsed it.

“Some Democrats in the House seem to oppose it. Let me remind these Democrats what the liberal writer Ezra Klein wrote just this week in The New York Times. Klein wrote, ‘Leaving the system unchanged is a guarantee of calamity.’ He goes on to say, ‘The status quo has left us completely unable to build the energy system we need.’ Even the New York Times admits what we are doing here is important and necessary for the country. “Surviving the review process is only half the battle. Trial lawyers and environmental activists have used the courts to bury necessary projects in further delays. Each case is filed to prevent a project from moving ahead. This drives up costs and creates uncertainty.

“The Senate bill fixes that. First, it streamlines environmental reviews. Next, it reins in out-of-control judicial review and abusive lawsuits. These reforms are common sense. title: Bennet and Schmitt Lead Letter to Air Force Secretary Calling for Greater U.S.-New Zealand Space Cooperation
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a member of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, and Senator Eric Schmitt (R-Mo.), a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, led seven bipartisan colleagues on a letter to Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink calling for additional steps to strengthen space cooperation with New Zealand, writing that doing so would create opportunities for mutual partnership and innovation that advance U.S. national security.

Senators Bennet and Schmitt were joined on this letter by Senators Kevin Cramer (R-N.D.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Deb Fischer (R-Ne.), Pete Ricketts (R-Ne.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Mike Lee (R-Utah), and Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.).

“We write to express our continued support for the U.S. Space Force and U.S. Space Command’s efforts to collaborate with allies and partners across the Indo-Pacific and to request your consideration of additional steps to improve such efforts with New Zealand, a key Five Eyes partner, where doing so advances U.S. national security interests and strengthens collective capability. We believe these efforts would complement existing U.S. exchange and interoperability arrangements with Australia and other Five Eyes members to enhance regional deterrence and space-related collaboration,” wrote the senators.

They noted that the Royal New Zealand Air Force’s No. 62 Squadron plays a crucial role as the Pacific Cell Lead of U.S. Space Command’s Commercial Operations (JCO) Unit, training partner nations and helping enhance shared space domain awareness. Additionally, the senators noted that the further maturation of New Zealand’s space program, coupled with the country’s strategic geography and smaller bureaucracy, would advance U.S. national security objectives – helping ensure allied and partner space superiority by providing opportunities for additional satellite tracking, space surveillance, missile coverage, and communications redundancies – while offering considerable avenues for mutual partnership and opportunities to innovate.

“As Senators representing states with U.S. Space Force missions or other space-related equities, we share a deep appreciation of the extent and complexity of securing the space domain. For this reason, we believe in the necessity of having ready and capable allies and partners. Increased interactions, particularly through U.S. New Zealand exchanges, present an opportunity to enhance both countries’ capabilities in space. Where such arrangements address identified operational needs and provide reciprocal benefits, expanding space-related exchanges between the NZDF and our Joint Force could strengthen interoperability and enhance collective deterrence across the Indo-Pacific,” continued the senators.

Bennet leads several efforts to enhance U.S. and allied space superiority, and bolster cooperation with Indo-Pacific allies to enhance regional deterrence.

Bennet secured language in the Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27) Senate Intelligence Authorization Act requiring the Intelligence Community to strengthen intelligence cooperation with U.S. allies and partners in the Indo-Pacific, including New Zealand. Bennet, Schmitt, and Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.) also lead legislation, included in the FY27 NASA reauthorization bill, to enhance U.S.-Taiwan space collaboration. Last year, Bennet secured passage of his legislation requiring the Secretary of Defense to strengthen U.S.-led multilateral efforts – with allies including Australia, Japan, South Korea, and the Philippines – to deter China’s aggression in the Indo-Pacific.

The text of the letter is available HERE and below.

Dear Secretary Meink,

We write to express our continued support for the U.S. Space Force and U.S. Space Command’s efforts to collaborate with allies and partners across the Indo-Pacific and to request your consideration of additional steps to improve such efforts with New Zealand, a key Five Eyes partner, where doing so advances U.S. national security interests and strengthens collective capability. We believe these efforts would complement existing U.S. exchange and interoperability arrangements with Australia and other Five Eyes members to enhance regional deterrence and space-related collaboration.

During retired Chief of Space Operations General Chance B. Saltzman’s May 2026 visit to New Zealand, he met with officials from the Ministry of Defence and the Royal New Zealand Air Force’s No. 62 Squadron, New Zealand’s only dedicated space unit. The No. 62 Squadron plays a crucial role in the U.S. Space Command’s Joint Commercial Operations (JCO) cells, serving as the Pacific Cell Lead and supporting partner nation training around the world. The Squadron’s participation in the JCO enables New Zealand to build its own space domain awareness capabilities, particularly with regard to satellite tracking.

Additionally, the New Zealand Defence Force (NZDF) works through the U.S.-led Combined Space Operations initiative to protect shared space interests from disruption, denial, or destruction, and promote responsible behavior in the domain. The NZDF has also launched experimental payloads into orbit on U.S. satellites, while Prime Minister Christopher Luxon established a dedicated ministerial position for space in 2023.

These efforts demonstrate the seriousness with which New Zealand’s government and the NZDF approach space. Further maturation of New Zealand’s space program and additional investment in capabilities that complement U.S. and allied efforts would advance U.S. national security objectives, helping ensure allied and partner space superiority by providing opportunities for additional satellite tracking, space surveillance, missile coverage, and communications redundancies. Moreover, the relatively small scale of New Zealand’s military space bureaucracy– coupled with the country’s geographically advantageous launch and operational environments and growing commercial space sector – offers considerable avenues for mutual partnership and opportunities to innovate.

As Senators representing states with U.S. Space Force missions or other space-related equities, we share a deep appreciation of the extent and complexity of securing the space domain. For this reason, we believe in the necessity of having ready and capable allies and partners. Increased interactions, particularly through U.S.-New Zealand exchanges, present an opportunity to enhance both countries’ capabilities in space. Where such arrangements address identified operational needs and provide reciprocal benefits, expanding space-related exchanges between the NZDF and our Joint Force could strengthen interoperability and enhance collective deterrence across the Indo-Pacific.

We stand ready to support efforts, as appropriate, that strengthen U.S. capabilities and enable greater contributions from Indo-Pacific allies and partners. We look forward to engaging further.

Thank you for your attention.

###

title: CONNECTICUT CONGRESSIONAL DELEGATION BLASTS FEDERAL BUREAU OF PRISONS’ ATTEMPTS TO DISMANTLE UNION WORKERS’ RIGHTS AND PROTECTIONS
text:
[WASHINGTON, DC] – Today, U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and Chris Murphy (D-CT) and U.S. Representatives John Larson (D-CT), Joe Courtney (D-CT), Rosa DeLauro (D-CT), Jim Himes (D-CT), and Jahana Hayes (D-CT) wrote Director of the Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) William K. Marshall III voicing strong opposition to the Bureau’s attempts to terminate its legally negotiated Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) with the American Federation of Government Employees’ National Council of Prison Locals 33 (CPL-33).

CPL-33 represents more than 30,000 public servants in critical jobs within the federal penitentiary system, including employees at the Federal Correctional Institution in Danbury. The Collective Bargaining Agreement addresses how and where staff are assigned to work, their schedule including breaks and time off, and when workers receive overtime. Furthermore, the CBA provides a framework for negotiations with wardens and institutional managers.

In September 2025, the Bureau of Prisons (BOP) initially terminated its Collective Bargaining Agreement with CPL-33, blaming President Trump’s Executive Order 14251, before later changing its tune and calling the union “an obstacle to progress.” Since then, the Bureau has stopped at nothing to strip away workplace protections, even going so far as to circumvent a preliminary injunction earlier this year that required the Bureau to operate under the Collective Bargaining Agreement.

“The BOP’s efforts to end the CBA with CPL-33 are one more example in a litany of actions the Trump Administration is taking to dismantle workers’ rights and protections. Since President Trump took office, his administration has eliminated the collective bargaining rights of more than one million federal workers. These efforts attack not only unions but also individual civil servants across our country,” the Delegation members wrote.

The full text of the Delegation’s letter is available here and copied below.

Dear Director Marshall III,

We write with concern regarding the Federal Bureau of Prisons’ (BOP) attempts to terminate its legally negotiated Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) with the American Federation of Government Employees’ National Council of Prison Locals 33 (CPL-33). Union members, including the 30,000 civil servants represented by CPL-33, are the backbone of the federal penitentiary system, serving in critical jobs that protect our nation.[1] We are aghast at BOP’s unceasing, politically motivated efforts to strip away its employees’ rights, and the blatant disregard BOP has shown for the welfare of its employees over the past two years.

In September 2025, the BOP terminated its CBA with CPL-33. Although the BOP claimed President Trump’s Executive Order 14251 as the basis for its decision, you admitted to the real reason: posting a message to the BOP website on the same day BOP terminated the contract, claiming that the “whole purpose of ending this contract” was because the “union [was] an obstacle to progress” and “the current contract has too often slowed or prevented changes.”[2] However, the CBA played a vital role in protecting BOP employees, who serve in some of the nation’s most dangerous environments and maintain and uphold our public safety. The CBA established nationwide workplace protections and provided a framework for local unions to negotiate arrangements with wardens and other institutional managers. For example, the CBA addressed how and where staff are assigned to work, their work schedule, including lunch breaks and time off, when workers receive overtime, steps BOP must take to ensure the health and safety of its employees, and the right to union representation.[3]

Following the decision to terminate the contract, the BOP wasted no time in stripping its workers of their rights and due process protections against arbitrary management decisions. The BOP quickly dismantled its labor relations apparatus, changed more than 70 labor-related policies, and rushed to resolve pending disciplinary actions, which now lacked the procedural safeguards of the original CBA, including union representation of the employee accused of wrongdoing by management.[4] These changes had immediate, real-life consequences. In two egregious instances, BOP sent a sick-leave abuse letter to an employee who was in the hospital for kidney surgery and placed a different employee who was recovering from surgery on Absent Without Leave (AWOL) status, erroneously and unconscionably threatening them with termination if they did not return to work. Without the CBA, these employees had to face disciplinary proceedings without due process or union support.[5] These unwarranted, arbitrary actions are precisely why the CBA provides for a fair review process of management accusations.

Despite the preliminary injunction issued earlier this year, BOP continues to pursue avenues to avoid operating under the CBA[6]. In October 2026, BOP attempted to circumvent the injunction by rescinding its original termination that had been enjoined, and then immediately re-terminating the contract.[7] Although the court voided this naked power play to evade the court’s order and BOP eventually filed a Notice of Compliance with the Judge’s orders on October 28, 2026, we are concerned that the BOP will continue to undermine the CBA as the Bureau’s actions impact its employees across the country.[8] In fact, staff have reported that the BOP’s attempts to terminate the contract are leading to low staff morale.[9] A union representative at the Federal Correctional Institution in Mendota, California, described the efforts as “nothing more than…giving the rule of law the middle finger.”[10] He also voiced his concerns that the BOP is still not honoring certain workplace agreements, including providing essential safety equipment such as footwear.[11] We find it unacceptable for the BOP to subvert the CBA and leave workers who are upholding our public safety system without critical protections.

The BOP’s efforts to end the CBA with CPL-33 are one more example in a litany of actions the Trump Administration is taking to dismantle workers’ rights and protections. Since President Trump took office, his administration has eliminated the collective bargaining rights of more than one million federal workers.[12] These efforts attack not only unions but also individual civil servants across our country. We strongly oppose BOP’s efforts to undermine CPL-33, and we urge BOP to end its misguided effort to terminate the Collective Bargaining Agreements immediately.

title: Booker, Gottheimer Reintroduce Bill to Put Federal Dollars Behind Life-Saving Fentanyl and Xylazine Test Strips
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) reintroduced the Preventing Overdoses with Test Strips Act, legislation that would help prevent overdoses by expanding access to drug test strips. Drug test strips are a low-cost tool that can show whether a drug contains harmful substances such as fentanyl or xylazine, reducing overdose risk. But confusion over whether federal funds can pay for them has kept many programs from buying them, even as overdoses claim more than 180 American lives every day. Booker's bill would end that confusion. U.S. Representative Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

"We are losing people every day to fentanyl and xylazine, and test strips are one of the simplest, most affordable tools we have to keep people alive," said Senator Booker. "This bill cuts through the confusion and makes clear that federal grant dollars can pay for these life-saving tools, so communities across New Jersey and the country can meet people where they are and connect them to care."

“Too many families in Jersey and across our country have lost someone they love to fentanyl. There’s no single solution to end addiction, but when Democrats and Republicans work together, we can save lives. That’s why I’m proud to help lead the Preventing Overdoses with Test Strips Act in the House to provide more of these life-saving test strips. It’s a commonsense, proven step we can take to protect our loved ones,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5).

An estimated 66,478 Americans died of drug overdoses in the 12-month period ending in May 2026, according to provisional CDC data. At the same time, the drug supply keeps changing as xylazine and other dangerous adulterants spread.

Test strips are a proven, easy-to-use tool for keeping up with that changing supply. The Preventing Overdoses with Test Strips Act would explicitly allow federal substance use and mental health grant funding to be used to purchase and distribute test strips and other devices that detect fentanyl, xylazine, and other deadly adulterants.

Booker first announced this legislation in August 2023 in Paramus, New Jersey, alongside U.S. Representative Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5), after touring the Substance Use Disorder Treatment Program at Bergen New Bridge Medical Center. It builds on his Expanding Nationwide Access to Test Strips Act, which would decriminalize drug test strips nationwide, and on his broader work to treat addiction as a public health issue.

title: Boozman Introduces Cody Hiland to Judiciary Committee
text:
U.S. Senator John Boozman (R-AR) introduced Arkansas Supreme Court Justice Cody Hiland at a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing to consider his nomination to serve as a United States Circuit Judge for the Eighth Circuit.

Boozman praised Hiland’s extensive legal experience and voiced confidence that he would be a valuable addition to the federal judiciary.

“Cody Hiland has all the qualities we want in a federal judge,” said Boozman. “Extensive legal experience, sound judgement and a commitment to upholding the law rather than legislating from the bench. I strongly support his nomination and urge my colleagues to do the same.”

A native of Conway, Hiland is a graduate of the University of Central Arkansas and University of Arkansas-Little Rock’s Bowen Law School. He previously served as a prosecuting attorney in Arkansas’s 20th Judicial District and later as the U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas.

Below are Boozman’s remarks as delivered:

It is an honor to be with you today with my friend and fellow Senator Tom Cotton to introduce Justice Cody Hiland, President Trump’s outstanding nominee to serve as United States Circuit Judge for the Eighth Circuit.

Cody is a native of Arkansas. He earned his undergraduate degree from the University of Central Arkansas before completing his legal studies at the University of Arkansas-Little Rock’s Bowen Law School.

He has experience in private practice in addition to providing legal counsel to the Arkansas Public Service Commission and Department of Public Safety.

He was also a Legislative Liaison and Aide to our dear friend Governor Mike Huckabee.

Cody’s service in those roles, as well as his exemplary performance as prosecuting attorney in Arkansas’s 20th Judicial District, made him a top candidate to serve as the U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas during the first Trump administration.

Senator Cotton and I were pleased to recommend him for that role, and will both attest to the tremendous job he did improving public safety and holding criminals accountable.

In fact, at the time he was sworn in, his jurisdiction included four communities with some of the highest crime rates – violent crime rates – in the United States per capita.

But Cody worked incredibly hard to turn the tide, especially by targeting gun crimes and gang activity, eagerly partnering with local, state and federal agencies to protect communities and stand with law enforcement to make everyone safe.

That body of work culminated in his appointment to the Arkansas Supreme Court by Governor Sarah Huckabee Sanders, where he has honorably served since 2023 and was subsequently elected to a full term.

Cody has all the qualities we want in a federal judge: extensive real-world and courtroom experience, sound judgement, and a deep commitment to upholding the law rather than legislating from the bench.

I am confident that his integrity and temperament will be assets to the Eighth Circuit.

I strongly urge my colleagues to join me in supporting his nomination.

title: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Introduces Legislation to Strengthen National Scam and Fraud Prevention
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.), a member of the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, today introduced the National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention Act, legislation to improve the nation’s response to scams and fraud targeting American families, seniors, and small businesses.

The legislation would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention within the Executive Office of the President to develop a comprehensive national strategy and strengthen coordination among federal agencies, law enforcement, financial institutions, telecommunications providers, technology companies, and other stakeholders.

“Hardworking Americans should not have to worry that one fraudulent call, text, or online message could cost them their life savings,” said Senator Britt. “From seniors to small business owners, fraudsters are targeting people across Alabama and throughout our country. Banks, law enforcement, telecommunications providers, and technology companies all have an important role to play, but we cannot expect any one of them to solve this problem alone. We need a coordinated approach that helps stop scams before families lose their hard-earned money.”

Scams increasingly cross industries and jurisdictions, often beginning with a fraudulent text message, phone call, social media post, or online advertisement before reaching the financial system. While individual companies and agencies work to protect consumers, criminals can exploit gaps in information sharing and response efforts across the broader fraud ecosystem.

Under the bill, the Office would promote timely intelligence sharing across the public and private sectors, coordinate consumer education efforts, support cooperation with state and local authorities and international partners, and help improve assistance for victims.

“This effort is about bringing everyone to the table and making sure our response keeps pace with the criminals who are exploiting new technologies and gaps between sectors,” continued Senator Britt. “When we work together to identify threats earlier and share information more effectively, we can better protect American families and businesses.”

The Office would review federal spending related to scam and fraud prevention and provide annual reports to Congress on fraud trends, prevention initiatives, coordination challenges, and potential improvements to the national response.

Several quotes of support for Senator Britt’s legislation from the American Bankers Association (ABA), the Independent Community Bankers of America (ICBA), Financial Services Forum (FSF), America’s Credit Unions, the Alabama Credit Union Association (ACUA), and the Consumer Bankers Association (CBA) can be found below.

“Scams and fraud are a growing threat to consumers, businesses and our national security,” said ABA President and CEO Rob Nichols. “Senator Britt’s National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention Act would strengthen the federal government’s ability to coordinate the fight against fraud while supporting a whole-of-ecosystem response to bring government, financial institutions, telecommunications companies and online platforms together to combat these crimes. ABA strongly supports this bill and applauds her leadership on this critical issue.”

“Community bankers see the toll scams can take on their customers every day, from seniors who lose their retirement savings to small businesses whose payments get diverted. They often serve as the last line of defense, but the fight against fraud can’t fall on banks alone,” said ICBA President and CEO Rebeca Romero Rainey. “Scammers reach consumers long before a transaction ever hits a bank, through a phone call, a text, or a social media message. Senator Britt’s bill recognizes that every link in the chain has a role to play, and better information sharing will help community banks protect the customers and communities they serve. ICBA thanks Senator Britt for taking on this important fight.”

“It takes partners across every sector to protect Americans from scams and fraud,” said FSF President and CEO Amanda Eversole. “The Forum applauds Senator Britt’s leadership and legislation to align government, financial institutions, telecommunications providers, and technology companies behind a national strategy to stop fraudsters.”

“America’s Credit Unions supports efforts to coordinate a comprehensive, cross-sector response to fraud and scams. The proposed bill would advance that objective by establishing the strategic infrastructure and leadership needed to address scams earlier in their lifecycle. We appreciate Senator Britt’s leadership in introducing the National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention Act and look forward to working with her to pass the bill,” said Kathleen Coulombe, Chief Advocacy Officer of America’s Credit Unions.

“Credit unions are member-owned cooperatives, so when scammers strike, they’re stealing from neighbors, retirees and working families who trust us with their savings. We applaud Senator Britt for taking a whole-of-ecosystem approach that brings the financial sector, government, telecom and tech partners together to stop scams before they reach our members,” said Ibby Dickson, Manager of Federal Advocacy, ACUA.

“As the FTC and others have repeatedly documented, Americans lost tens of billions of dollars from scams last year alone. At a time when Americans are increasingly focused on affordability and their financial well-being, protecting consumers from fraud and scams is more important than ever. Unfortunately today, fraudsters and scammers are exploiting gaps between telecommunications companies, digital platforms, and financial institutions. Senator Katie Britt’s National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention Act directly addresses those vulnerabilities by promoting real time intelligence sharing across both public and private sectors. We strongly support this comprehensive effort to bring all stakeholders to the table and ensure a unified defense against fraud,” said Lindsey Johnson, President and CEO, Consumer Bankers Association.

title: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Urges Congress to Protect Children Against Big Tech Forced Arbitration Agreements
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) yesterday attended a Senate Judiciary Crime and Counterterrorism Subcommittee hearing on how the online gaming platform, Roblox, is endangering America’s children.

This week, Senators Britt and Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) introduced the Ending Forced Arbitration of Children Online Act. During the hearing, Senator Britt used her time to question witnesses about Roblox’s attempt to use forced arbitration as a shield against accountability in cases of child exploitation and grooming. Witnesses included Michael Schlep and Woody Doe, both survivor and online safety advocates; Khari James, Senior Legal Counsel at the National Center on Sexual Exploitation; and Professor Myriam Gilles of the Northwestern Pritzker School of Law.

Senator Britt began by thanking witnesses for telling their story and calling for commonsense protections: “Thank you for telling your story … The things we’re talking about today are absolutely commonsense, right? There is no way an eight-year-old … could read those terms and then sign away their right to a moment in court, effectively silencing themselves, dealing with the trauma that they endured online and then the trauma of not being able to use their voice and tell their story. And as a result of that, more and more children become victims. And at what point is this body not going to stand up and do the right thing?”

Senator Britt highlighted several of her legislative priorities to protect children from Big Tech companies: “I am hopeful that we will all stand with Senator Blumenthal and Senator Blackburn and get the Kids Online Safety Act, get that passed before the end of this Congress. We cannot allow Big Tech to continue to put their profits ahead of people, ahead of precious children, stealing innocence and in the most just damning circumstances, stealing lives … I was so honored to stand next to Senator Blumenthal and introduce yesterday the Ending Forced Arbitration of Children Online Act. The time to pass this is now. This bill would invalidate the pre-dispute arbitration agreements in cases in which a minor has suffered harm on a platform, including physical injury, mental or psychological harm, a violation of privacy or a misuse of personal data. Platforms covered by this bill of Senator Blumenthal’s and mine include social media platforms and gaming platforms like Roblox. I believe arbitration does have a place in our judicial system, but I do not believe that platforms like Roblox should be able to use arbitration as a shield against accountability for the harms they have caused to minors allowing them to become repeat offenders over and over and over again.”

Professor Gilles explained what parents should know about Roblox: “Well, first of all, they are completely aware that the design choices they’ve made are basically delivering these children to predators, and they’re doing nothing about it. And when families and victims sue them, trying to get change, trying to get some reform, they force those cases into secret arbitration. Let’s be clear, arbitration has a place in the system … If a family or a victim would like to go into arbitration, we should let them do that … But forcing a child as a precondition to playing a game, which we’ve heard is a game that they want to play, forcing them to sign away rights they don’t even understand, that’s not fair. That’s not that’s not real … Now, this is all happening in secret, and I think children are going to continue to be abused and harmed unless this body does something.”

Senator Britt asked Mr. Schlep to detail Roblox’s conscious decision to deemphasize moderators on the platform: “In fact, Roblox bragged to investors in a shareholder announcement that they were decreasing their spending on moderation while their player base was exploding. What context does that even make sense for Roblox to decrease their moderation while their users are going up? Hindenburg found that Roblox has one of the lowest moderator-to-user ratios than any other social media website … [T]he current leadership at the company has truly shown that they are putting profits ahead of safety. And that’s not me giving my opinion, that is their own employees saying that.”

Senator Britt continued, asking the witnesses, “What is the one thing you feel like this body needs to know or could do that would make a difference in what we’re seeing on kids’ online safety in general? I think it is absolutely reprehensible and feckless that Congress has done nothing. The most vulnerable and our most precious asset is the next generation, and we continue to kick the can down the road instead of do the right thing.”

Professor Gilles responded, highlighting Senator Britt’s legislation, “As we’re looking at what we do towards the end of the year, there are some wonderful bills. You and Senator Blumenthal have a bill, Senators Hawley and Durbin have a bill. Pass one of these bills and just get rid of forced arbitration. You will be amazed by how quickly the company will change its behavior once it is sued in public court.”

Ms. James agreed that online gaming platforms like Roblox need to be held liable in order to enact change: “I agree with my colleague here that there needs to be a consequence, and the consequence is being held liable, and how we can make that happen is through passing legislation, whether it’s Stop CSAM, KOSA, the Forced Arbitration Act, something has to be done.”

Mr. Doe noted, “They’re protecting themselves from their investors through this forced arbitration. All their dirty laundry is hidden. The minute that goes out the window, they’re really going to feel the repercussions of their actions. All I can ask is please get on those bills.”

Finally, Mr. Schlep called for better moderation from Roblox: “I fundamentally believe that Roblox needs better moderation … And some of the stuff that they’ve released, like age estimation and all this other stuff, is clearly not working. And at the end of the day, their overreliance on stuff like AI moderation, when they should be doing stuff in-house here in the United States, is something that I really think Roblox needs to do more of.”

title: Budd Introduces Bill to Elevate Special Operations Leadership within the Department of War
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Ted Budd (R-N.C.), a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, introduced the Office of Strategic Services Act of 2026 yesterday, which would expand the role of special operations within the Department of War. The bill would grant the Pentagon’s senior special operations official the same level of authority as a military service and rename the position to Under Secretary of War for Strategic Services, which will oversee the new Office of Strategic Services (OSS). Additionally, the bill would require senior Pentagon officials to incorporate special operations into strategic planning, authorize increased funding for the new OSS, and add 200 positions to support its expanded operations within the Department of War.

“North Carolina is proud to be the home of U.S. special operations. Elite forces from across the Army, Marine Corps, Air Force, Navy, and Joint units carry out some of our nation’s most complex and demanding military missions around the globe to advance U.S. national security interests. Given the high operational tempo and the unique demands placed on our Special Operations Forces (SOF) operators, the SOF community has long deserved elevated authority within the Department of War. By elevating special operations leadership to the same level as a military service, my legislation would finally give operators a direct voice in advocating for operational needs and essential manpower funding to ensure they are ready to respond to national security threats at the highest level,” said Senator Budd.

Read the full bill text HERE.

BACKGROUND

Senator Budd’s Office of Strategic Services Act would codify the Secretary of War’s intent, as specified in a memorandum to senior Pentagon leadership earlier this month, to elevate the authority of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict (ASD(SO/LIC)) and strengthen departmental support of the Special Operations enterprise. This legislation builds upon previous National Defense Authorization Acts (NDAA) that created and expanded the role of ASD(SO/LIC) to better resource and supervise special operations and irregular warfare activities.

FY1987 NDAA (Nunn-Cohen Amendment): Established U.S. Special Operations Command (USSOCOM) and ASD(SO/LIC) to provide civilian oversight, policy direction, and a “service-like” advocacy role for special operations.

FY2017 NDAA (Section 922): Placed ASD(SO/LIC) over USSOCOM in its administrative chain of command, enhancing oversight of SOF organization, training, equipping, and resources.

FY2025 NDAA (Section 907): Directed the Department of Defense to update internal guidelines to solidify the Service Secretary-like authorities of ASD(SO/LIC).
