title: Gallego, Colleagues Introduce Bill to Increase Access to Financial Aid for Graduate Degrees in Essential Fields
text:
WASHINGTON — Yesterday, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) joined Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Jeff Merkley (D-OR) in introducing the Professional Student Degree Act, which would ensure financial stability for students and strengthen essential workforce pipelines. The bill would also reverse harmful cuts to federal student loan programs by expanding the definition of a “professional degree” to include certain critical graduate programs currently excluded by the U.S. Department of Education (ED), such as those in nursing, education, and public health.

“America is facing a teacher, nurse, and public servant shortage and students wanting to work these essential jobs shouldn’t go broke trying to get their degree.” said Senator Gallego. “We shouldn’t be discouraging people from pursuing these careers. Let’s reverse the administration’s decision to cap financial aid to certain graduate programs and get more people in these critical roles serving their communities.”

Currently, ED’s implementation of federal student loan provisions enacted by President Trump and congressional Republicans under the One Big Beautiful Bill Actcreates an immediate “loan cliff” for certain graduate degrees. By narrowing the definition of a “professional degree” to just 11 eligible programs, the current framework severely limits financial access to graduate programs in essential fields already facing critical labor shortages.

Students in these newly designated “non-professional” programs face annual student loan caps that are almost $30,000 lower, and aggregate limits $100,000 lower, than students in designated professional tracks. This limits students’ ability to secure the federal loans needed to complete their education and exacerbates nationwide workforce shortages, particularly in healthcare.

The Professional Student Degree Act would correct this by reinstating several key graduate programs to the federal list of professional degrees eligible for higher borrowing limits.

The Professional Student Degree Act would impact the following degree programs:

Maintains Professional Status for: Pharmacy, Dentistry, Veterinary Medicine, Chiropractic, Law, Medicine, Optometry, Osteopathic Medicine, Podiatric Medicine, Theology, Clinical Psychology

Restores and Codifies Professional Status for: Social Work, Audiology, Physician Assistant, Occupational Therapy, Physical Therapy, Nursing, Public Health, Business Administration and Management, Accounting, Architecture, Education, and Special Education

Flexibility to Expand: The Secretary of Education may add any other programs that meet “professional degree” requirements.

title: WATCH: At Hearing, Gallego Grills Interior Department Inspector General Nominee on his Commitment to Protect Arizona Public Lands
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, during a hearing of the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources (ENR), Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) grilled Dennis Kirk, nominee to be Inspector General (IG) at the Department of Interior, on the Trump administration’s lack of effort to protect Arizona’s public lands.

At the hearing, Senator Gallego questioned Kirk’s commitment to upholding the 2012 Grand Canyon Watershed Mining Withdrawal and asked if the Interior Department will commit to restoring lands around the Grand Canyon burned in the Dragon Bravo Fire.

Watch Senator Gallego’s questioning HERE and read excerpts below:

Senator Gallego began by raising concerns about the department’s willingness to protect Arizona’s public lands — lands that federally recognized tribes considered sacred.

“In 2012, the department withdrew more than one million acres of federal land from new mining claims for a 20-year period to protect the region. When you talk about mining, we’re also talking about uranium mining which is very important because we have a lot of water systems that can potentially be damaged. So, I am concerned that this administration has taken unprecedented steps to violate the government commitment to public lands,” said Senator Gallego.

He continued: “If confirmed, will you ensure that the Department honors the 2012 mining withdrawal through its full term?”

Department of the Interior Inspector General nominee Dennis Kirk responded:“I am not sure if the IG has that authority, Senator. If brought up to staff, yes, I will have an opinion on it. We will, of course, report to Congress.”

Senator Gallego pressed him, saying that he hopes he “understand[s] why this [is] very important for me and very important for my state: to make sure we have some understanding of where you stand on this, what your opinion would be on this. Because it does affect not just potentially millions of people, but also billions of dollars’ worth of tourism as well as the sovereignty of tribal nations.”

He continued, then asked: “I am concerned about the administration’s ability and willingness to support recovery from this fire. Because we’ve already seen some indications of corruption and simplification of the disaster [recovery] that goes into that area.

“Can you commit to ensuring contracts are awarded through fair and competitive prices, free of conflict of interest or political favoritism, and more importantly, quickly?”

title: WATCH: Gallego Joins Tim Snyder, Slams Jensen Huang for Compromising U.S. National Security; Calls for Investigations into Trump Family’s Corruption
text:
WASHINGTON — This week, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) joined Tim Snyder on his Substack, “Thinking about…,” to discuss congressional Democrats’ plans to investigate Nvidia and its former CEO, Jensen Huang, for threatening U.S. national security by allowing advanced AI chips on export control lists to fall into Chinese hands. The senator also called for a major overhaul of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to keep communities safe and highlighted the need for campaign finance reform.

WATCH: Timothy Snyder’s Substack, “Thinking about…”

On Nvidia selling chips to adversaries:

“They don’t care. I mean, they are literally selling us out just to make sure that dividends are high and corporate shareholders are happy. And look, we all have different pensions. We all have 401ks. Obviously, we all like to make sure that they stay healthy. But what’s important is the national security of this country.

“At the end of the day, we ended up being compromised. Our national security got compromised. Obviously, our allies are getting compromised.

“And then when you have the combination of NVIDIA chips plus Starshield going down, it’s a pretty bleak environment that we’re putting a lot of our allies in.”

On what Democrats need to do to hold corrupt politicians accountable:

“A stock trade ban and a crypto ban are the first things that we [Democrats] should be doing. And that includes members of the House and the Senate, because there’s been a lot of members… that have been trading.

“And then we still try to pass a national law that would try to rein in this president. I actually tried working on this for quite a while — especially when it came to crypto — to make sure that a lot of the crypto dealings that this president and people within his administration would be cut off.

“And they were so hesitant about it. And it was very apparent that they just want to continue to do the rug pulls that they’re doing.

“As well as, of course, now going into the amount of stocks trading that this [president] has been involved in. It’s clear that he’s using both compromised information or information that he is using that only he has access to actually get some trade, and likely also altering certain situations in order for him to have a favorable trade or portfolio.

“And, so, we need to try to pass legislation. Now, he may veto it because he is that shameless, but that does not mean that us as Democrats shouldn’t impose our own stock trade [and] crypto trade ban when it comes to our rules.

“Number two, we have to investigate, too. There’s been so many different contracts, insider deals that have been put out by friends and family of Donald Trump, you see it all the time.”

On the need to reform ICE:

“Well, look, you always have to have immigration enforcement. We’re always going to have a deportation force… every country does. The priorities of the country, though, need to be reflected in that force. And clearly the priorities of this country are not for mass deportation.

“So, when we say ‘you don’t need ICE,’ it means you don’t need ICE at the level and scale and the power it has right now. And partly the way that we do that is to make sure that we downsize and right-size ICE or any type of enforcement, it doesn’t have to be ICE.

“ICE and its detention force has a bigger budget than the United States Marine Corps.

“So, with Homeland Security, what I want to do is obviously have oversight. But at any time and point, try to reduce that budget as much as possible.

“That is why it’s causing two things. Number one: the grift you see. But number two: these mass deportations. Because you put that much money into the system, you are going to require something to come out of it.”

title: Major AI Platforms Generated Terrorist Attack Plans During Independent Government Audit
text:
WASHINGTON — A new official Government Accountability Office investigation requested by U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan (D-NH), incoming Chair of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, found that four of the most-used AI platforms — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Grok — all provided terrorist attack plans in a real-world test to determine AI safety risks. The results raise serious alarm bells about the need for Congress to take up and pass safety legislation, which incoming Chair Hassan announced today will be an early priority of the Committee.

“A terrorist can log onto an AI platform and in less than 12 hours walk away with a concrete playbook for how to carry out a deadly attack. Today’s new report makes it clear that the AI public safety threat is no longer theoretical. If Congress does not act, it is a question of when – not if – a bad actor will use AI to plan and carry out a major attack,” said incoming Chair of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, Senator Maggie Hassan. “Congress must quickly take up and pass legislation to address AI safety threats. To that end, in the new Congress, one of the first hearings of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee will focus on the risk that AI poses to our homeland security and critical infrastructure, and our committee will prioritize developing legislation to address these threats.”

During an independent government audit, AI platforms were asked to provide plans to conduct either a mass casualty event by developing an improvised explosive device (IED) or to maximize economic harm through an attack on electrical infrastructure in major cities. All four AI platforms provided terrorist attack plans in less than 12 hours, including dates, times, guides to maximize damage, maps, diagrams, and more depending on the platform. While the platforms initially avoided providing the requested information or deleted information after it was provided, all of these safeguards were easily bypassed. Independent experts also confirmed that the details provided by the platforms would, in fact, have detonated explosives or caused harm. For safety reasons, the report withholds the exact prompts used to bypass the safeguards and which platform provided what level of information.

In response to the findings, incoming Chair Hassan announced that she will work to address the threat that AI platforms can pose to public safety and our critical infrastructure, and that one of the Committee’s first hearings in the new year will focus on AI safety. Incoming Chair Hassan is exploring various solutions to address this safety threat, including requiring more rigorous safety testing before AI platforms publicly release models.

title: Hawley Applauds $1 Billion in RECA Claims Paid Nationwide
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Senator Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) announced the Department of Justice (DOJ) has paid out $1 billion in claims to radiation survivors, including downwinders, uranium minors, and those affected by uranium processing facilities under Hawley’s expansion of the Radiation Exposure Compensation Act (RECA). Fully 28 percent of that total, or $282 million, has been paid out to residents of Missouri alone, which surpasses any other state.

As of today, nearly 6,500 Missourians have received compensation under the law. Many more claims remain pending.

In 2025, Senator Hawley fought for and successfully secured enactment of legislation to reauthorize and expand the RECA to residents of Missouri. For decades, Missourians who lived near Coldwater Creek and similar properties that were exposed to radioactive waste from a former uranium processing site in St. Louis were unable to receive compensation under the law.

The Senator’s expansion provision revived RECA for survivors, allowed tens of thousands of new claimants to receive life-saving assistance—including those across Missouri—and protected the program for years to come. For two years, Senator Hawley led the fight to secure funding for survivors of nuclear contamination across the country, passing a reauthorization bill through the Senate in July 2023 and March 2024.

Missourians can apply for relief through DOJ’s online portal here.

title: Hawley Chairs First Congressional Hearing on Roblox, Demands Accountability for Child Exploitation and Forced Arbitration
text:
WASHINGTON — Yesterday, U.S. Senator Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) chaired a Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism hearing to expose child sexual abuse connected to the kid’s gaming platform Roblox, as well as Roblox’s practice of trying to force victims into arbitration.

The hearing was an extension of Senators Hawley and Dick Durbin (D-Ill.)’sinvestigation into Roblox, calling attention to the explicit content and child sexual exploitation connected to the platform. Just this week, the bipartisan pair introduced legislation to end forced arbitration for victims of online exploitation and to empower survivors from platforms like Roblox.

Survivors offered powerful testimony at the hearing. Roblox CEO David Baszucki declined Senator Hawley’s invitation to testify at the hearing.

Senator Hawley began, “We’re here today to discuss a question that I know from personal experience weighs on the mind of every parent in America, which is, ‘Are my children safe online?’ And the answer is, if your children are on Roblox, and millions of American children are every single day, they are not safe at all. Roblox is one of the most popular gaming platforms in the world, and if your children are on Roblox, they are being exposed, in all likelihood, to sexual predators, to sexually obscene materials, to sexually exploitative content, left, right, and center.”

He continued, “The company is worth 33 billion dollars. The company’s CEO is worth 3.3 billion dollars on his own. And the sad fact of the matter is, is that much of that money and many of those profits have come from exposing children, and I do mean children, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 years old, to sexually obscene material. And the worst part of it is, is that after Roblox does this, and they know what’s going on on their platform, after they do it, they force these same child victims into arbitration, which is a fancy way of saying they slam the courthouse door shut in their faces. We’re talking about children now. Child victims of sexual exploitation online are denied their day in court by the very company that has exposed them to the content to begin with. Why? For money. It’s always the same answer. It’s for money.”

Hawley then took a moment to recognize the parents of victims and survivors who were present in the room. “I want to say thank you for being willing to come and take a stand. Thank you for risking the pain that comes with reliving what your children went through … Thank you for being willing to come and to risk your own sense of well-being to be here and to speak out about what happened to you. Thank you for being advocates for the truth.”

“Nearly 75% of all American children between the ages of nine and 12 play Roblox regularly,” Senator Hawley stated. ” … Predators pose as minors on Roblox to gain the trust of children. They also extort children with Roblox’s digital currency called Robux. As a result, countless criminal cases have come out of Roblox. It’s absolutely sickening.”

He asked Woody Doe, survivor and online safety advocate, “Thanks for your service to our country, and thank you for the service to your family that you’re now entering as a husband and father. Let me just ask you: You were 11 years old. You said when you first started playing on Roblox, and when you were exploited. Is that right?”

Mr. Doe responded, “Yes, Mr. Senator.”

“When you got onto Roblox, did you think it was a safe platform, and did you have any reason to think it wouldn’t be?” Hawley questioned.

“There were no indications that this would have been something dangerous for a young man to get onto … It seemed just like a virtual playground, like it was to … code, to come up with my own little worlds, and so I was so involved in it,” Doe answered.

The Senator queried, “If you’re willing to say something more about it, how did the abuse that you experienced as a very young boy affect you years down the line?”

He stated, “It came in multiple ways, if I’m being honest. There was years of feeling inadequacy … I felt vulnerable. I felt abused, and so with that, that stemmed all the way up into my military career, where I missed out on my second daughter’s actual birthday because I’d been volunteering, deployment, attachment, everything I could possibly embellish myself into to distract myself from the damages that had happened to me as a child, the long-lasting effects.”

“I just got to pause there and say to the CEO of Roblox who isn’t with us today: Is it really worth it? I mean, is the money really worth that? What you did to this man and this incredible guy who’s in front of us now, who’s turned his life around and is an incredible advocate, father, husband? But no amount of money justifies what you went through, Mr. Doe. No amount of profit can justify that, and no amount of profit can justify closing the courtroom door on you or hundreds, thousands. Who knows how many of other victims who deserve their day in court who are getting exactly the same treatment you’re getting right now from this company,” Senator Hawley asserted. “What’s your view of Roblox now?”

“I see them as lazy. Being honest, they have so much money to dump into their safety programs and protecting children, and they just refuse. The fact that this thing has happened to me over 15 years ago, and I’m still hearing the cases happening very similar to myself. It just goes to show that they haven’t put really any effort into keeping our kids safe,” Doe said.

Senator Hawley then addressed Michael Schlep, survivor and online safety advocate, “Based on your experience catching predators on Roblox, does Roblox ensure that predators can’t contact children on their platform?”

Schlep answered, “It was unbelievably easy for child predators to reach out. You know, I was able to find games where child predators would message me on Roblox within seconds. They allowed games based off of the now defunct platform Omegle, which was sued out of existence for child exploitation, to rack up tens of millions of visits on the platform, and Roblox’s chief safety officer Matt Kaufman actually played these games according to his Roblox profile, and these games weren’t removed until a major public outcry happened. And it goes to show that Roblox is very aware of some of these hubs and hotspots on the platform, but weren’t taking action. So this goes far beyond just you know allowing them to exist.”

“When you started exposing just how common predation is on the Roblox platform and how common contact with predators is with children, how did Roblox respond again? Did they thank you? Did they say thank you for bringing this to our attention? Did they work with you? And what was their response?” Hawley questioned.

“Roblox’s response was to send me a legal threat,” Schlep responded. “Roblox, they said that I was causing more of a danger to their users than the predators that I caught, which are now convicted. One was just recently sentenced to five years in prison, and you know the the thing is too. After all that came out, Roblox actually went as far as to compare me to child predators for running decoy accounts on their platform.”

Hawley declared, “The CEO of Roblox said, … ‘If you’re not comfortable, then don’t let your kids be on Roblox.’ And you know, maybe that is actually a really good piece of advice … Roblox lies to parents all the time about how their how their their platform is safe. They tell parents it’s safe. They tell parents that there’s these safety features, and then when there’s a problem with kids … they turn around and they blame you. They say, well, ‘It’s your fault. You should have done it. You should have known. You should have been there. We’re doing our part, and it’s really your fault.’ When the truth is just the reverse. You’re doing your part, and they’re making the money. You’re doing your part, and they’re exploiting your kids, and it’s time to put a stop to it here.”

He continued, “When Roblox says that they’ve implemented these safety features, they’re lying to you. Essentially, it’s all smoke and mirrors, it’s games, it’s window dressing, because they want their revenue stream to continue, and their revenue stream depends on kids who are my children’s age … Their whole business model depends on those kind of kids being on that platform all the time, which means it depends on lying to us parents about it and making sure we really can’t control anything that goes on the platform.”

Senator Hawley then turned to Myriam Gilles, a law professor at Northwestern Pritzker School of Law, “Could you just underscore again why it’s so important that these cases happen in public, that they go into a real courtroom that that where there’s a jury right that that jury right is accessible. Tell us again why this is so viable.”

“The short answer, Senator, is that courts produce a public record, and arbitration is designed to do the exact opposite. Right? It’s designed, as you’ve said, to muzzle, to to make everything as secret as possible, and public accountability produces reform,” Professor Gilles answered.

“One of the terms and conditions is this: it’s a limitation of liability, and it says when you click that little box, you agree to that forced arbitration, no matter what your age is, and you also agree that any suit, any claim, any damages against Roblox or its affiliated parties for all claims will be limited to $1,000 total,” Hawley asserted. “They are currently worth $33 billion. The founder and CEO alone is worth $3.3 billion. Is 1000 bucks going to change anybody’s behavior?”

Gilles said, “Absolutely not.”

“What they’re really trying to do is they’re trying to avoid the moral responsibility for what they’re doing on their platform, and they don’t want any moral limits enforced on them. They want to say, ‘We’ll exploit your kids and take everything we can from them … there won’t be a thing you can do about it.’ And you know what? What we’ve said as a country over and over and over again is, we believe in markets and we believe in competition, but there are moral limits that we as a country impose on businesses and everybody else, and one of them is that you can’t exploit children,”he expressed. “… And the idea that we would allow this company to sexually exploit children or expose them to such in order to make money is just fundamentally un-American. It’s not who we are, and they know that, and they’re trying to get around our system of justice. And what I’m saying today is, what I hear everybody on this dais saying is, ‘It’s time to put a stop to that. It’s time to get back to some basic principles of right and wrong, and make the company follow up like everybody else in America does.'”

Senator Hawley concluded, “I want to say to Roblox: You chose not to come here today, but you know what you’re doing is wrong, and we call on you today to admit your wrongdoing and to stop it. You can change your behavior, and you should. You should implement real safety regulations and restrictions like we talked about today. But you should also voluntarily end forced arbitration. I just say to CEO of Roblox, if you truly believe that your platform is the safest place on the internet for anybody. Prove it. End forced arbitration. You can announce it right now. Do it today. Today, announce that you will allow any victim who has been harmed on your platform to have their day in court because you have nothing to hide. I challenge you to do it. And in the meantime, I will not rest until this body marks up and passes a bill ending forced arbitration for victims of sexual exploitation and other exploitation online.”

Watch the full hearing here.

title: Hirono Presses Interior Inspector General Nominee Kirk on Commitment to Independent Investigations
text:
~ Watch Senator Hirono’s Questions Here ~

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI), a senior member of the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources, pressed U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) Inspector General (IG) nominee Dennis Kirk on his commitment to independent oversight. During his nomination hearing, Senator Hirono questioned Mr. Kirk on his loyalty to the president, outlining President Trump’s track record of firing inspectors general who attempt to hold the president accountable through independent oversight.

“Whether or not you are confirmed, your main job is to do [independent] investigations. […] You are the co-author of a chapter in Project 2025, […] and you are very much in line with what the president wants to do. Do you want to reassure us again you will do your job without fear or favor?,” said Senator Hirono.

Mr. Kirk has served at DOI since July 2026, after holding multiple positions in both Trump Administrations. Mr. Kirk also served as an Associate Director for Personnel Policy at the Heritage Foundation, where he co-authored a chapter in Project 2025 focusing on reshaping the federal civil service, and making it easier for the president to fire tens of thousands of civil service workers.

“It is clear you are working for a president that expects loyalty, do you agree?” asked Senator Hirono.

Mr. Kirk did not directly answer her question.

“You are working for a president who does not believe that the rule of law applies to him. That is one of the reasons why he fired 17 IGs. He does not want people or entities—and he certainly won’t nominate people— who will question what he does,” said Senator Hirono.

During the hearing, Senator Hirono also questioned Assistant Secretary of Energy nominee Toby Deen on the United States’ involvement in Venezuela, particularly as it pertained to President Trump’s assertions that the United States took control of Venezuelan oil reserves.

title: Husted delivers farewell speech on the Senate floor
text:
“I leave our nation’s capital with gratitude in my heart and enduring hope that my state and my country’s best days still lie ahead.”

View Husted’s remarks here.

WASHINGTON – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) today delivered a farewell speech on the Senate floor, reflecting on his time serving Ohioans throughout his more than 25 years of public service and the accomplishments he delivered on their behalf.

Husted got four bills signed into law, returned millions of dollars to Ohioans through constituent casework and local infrastructure projects and advanced policies to make life more affordable for Ohio families and help the workforce and economy grow through his time in the Senate.

Husted also reflected on the importance of building on that progress and continuing to keep Ohio and America moving forward.

Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) and Sens. Roger Wicker (R-Miss.) and Bill Cassidy (R-La.) also spoke on the Senate floor to honor Husted’s service to Ohioans.

Thune remarks

Wicker remarks

Cassidy remarks

Key excerpts include:

“Since 2001, I have had the honor of serving in the Ohio State House as Speaker of the House, as Secretary of State, Lieutenant Governor, and now serving Ohio as its U.S. Senator.”

. . .

“I remember having two main goals.

“It was education and jobs.”

. . .

“In 2010, Ohio had a 9% unemployment rate and $0.89 left in our rainy-day fund.

“We were broke, and CNBC had ranked Ohio the 34th worst state in the country to do business.”

. . .

“16 years later, it is a new day with the rising sun.

“As of this year, in 2026, Ohio hit the lowest unemployment rate in our state’s history at 3.3%.

“It had the most jobs in our state’s history and has over $4 billion in the state’s rainy-day fund.

“And CNBC ranked Ohio the number-one state in the country to do business.”

. . .

“I’m not going to go through all of what it takes to do this, but you don’t go from 34th to 1st by accident.

“I know what it takes.

“I was part of most of it, and I led much of it.”

“I often say you can’t do Made-in-America without Made-in-Ohio because from the food you eat, to the cars you drive, to the trucks that deliver, to the airplanes that fly, to the steel, to the energy, to space exploration.

“And yes, even your AI and online life depends on the Ohio supply chain.

“We make things and we’re really good at it.”

. . .

“I’ve always believed that at a public officials most important contribution is to help people get a good education and to create good jobs for them.”

. . .

“This is what makes public service worth the sacrifice.

“When you go get to meet people who you’ve actually done something to change their future, it makes it all worth it.”

. . .

“I hope you will see that in all these things that I am most proud of, they had nothing to do with politics, political ideology, or labels.

“They’re just about solving people’s problems and making their lives better.

“That’s been my passion.”

. . .

“If you step into the Capitol Rotunda and you look up the stories painted on the dome, you’re reminded of an enduring pattern.

“Americans built our nation through personal sacrifice, often at a steep human cost.”

. . .

“A nation that once rallied around sacrifice, in war, in rebuilding, in laying foundations for the future, however, has seemingly given away to a new cultural mood.”

. . .

“In 1967, the year I was born, the national debt stood at $330 billion.

“Today, it’s over $40 trillion.

“And a child born today inherits $121,000 as their share of that burden.”

. . .

“We only sacrifice for the things we love.

“If we truly love our country and our children and our grandchildren, we should stop taking from them and make sacrifices for them.”

. . .

“We need to prove that we love our children by ending the generational theft that has occurred over the past 50 years.

“And I know that’s tough. So tough.

“I’m not preaching here, I’m praying.

“I’m not trying to tell people I know the right way, because I know you all know the right way.

“But it’s hard, it’s hard to overcome the politics of our time.”

. . .

“But I’ll still pray that you find a way.”

. . .

“Serving Ohioans from the state house to the upper chamber of the people’s house been a great honor and a privilege.

“It really is one for which I will always be grateful.”

. . .

“To the people of the great state of Ohio.

“Whether you voted for me or you’ve never voted for me, thank you for the honor of representing and serving you.”

. . .

“Public service has given me a daily purpose in life.

“I’m grateful for it and I’m sure I’ll miss it.

“I leave our nation’s capital with gratitude in my heart and enduring hope that my state and my country’s best days still lie ahead.

“Mr. President and colleagues, may God bless and guide you in your service, and may God bless the United States of America.”

title: Kelly, Capito Introduce Bipartisan, Bicameral Legislation to Help Women Detect Breast Cancer Early
text:
Free risk assessment tools are available to help women understand their breast cancer risk and improve early detection, but too many women don’t know these tools exist or aren’t offered them by their doctors

Actress and breast cancer survivor Olivia Munn worked with Sen. Kelly to develop the legislation

Read in PEOPLE Magazine: Olivia Munn Says She’s Found ‘My Mission’ After Facing Breast Cancer: ‘This is What I Can Do in the World’ (Exclusive)

Today, Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV) introduced the Know Your Risk Act, bipartisan, bicameral legislation to make breast cancer risk assessment tools a routine part of health care. The bill would increase clinical use of these tools that can catch cancer earlier, giving women the highest chance of survival.

Representatives Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA-01) and Kim Schrier (D-WA-08) are introducing companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

The Know Your Risk Act was developed with the support of actress and breast cancer survivor Olivia Munn, who was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2023 after her doctor recommended the Tyrer-Cuzick Risk Assessment tool. Even after receiving a clear mammogram, a clear ultrasound, and negative genetic testing, the assessment helped lead to her cancer being detected early and potentially lifesaving care.

Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers affecting women in the United States. When caught early, the five-year relative survival rate is nearly 99 percent. Tools like the Tryer-Cuzick Risk Calculator and Breast Cancer Risk Assessment Tool (BCRAT) already exist to help doctors identify higher-risk patients, but despite decades of scientific validation, it’s been found that just 50 percent of physicians use them.

Sen. Kelly and Olivia Munn on Capitol Hill.

(Official U.S. Senate photo by Jill Craig)

“My mom and grandmother both had breast cancer, when I think about this disease I think about them and my daughters and granddaughters. My friend Olivia Munn was able to catch her breast cancer early thanks to a risk assessment test. We know early detection saves lives. That’s why we’re teaming up on this bipartisan bill to make sure more women understand their risk, know what screening options are available to them, and have doctors who are using these tools to help them get the care they deserve,” said Kelly.

“One of the things I find so encouraging about working with Senator Mark Kelly is that this is an issue where we have the opportunity to put politics aside and do something meaningful for women. Breast cancer doesn’t distinguish between political parties, and neither should our commitment to finding better ways to prevent it and detect it earlier. What we’re asking for is a relatively small, achievable change in how we approach women’s healthcare, but one that could have an extraordinary impact. We have an opportunity to shift some of the responsibility away from women having to know every question to ask, every risk factor to research, and every step to advocate for themselves, and put more of that responsibility where it belongs: with the medical professionals caring for them. The Lifetime Risk Assessment test is a tool that can help doctors identify risk earlier; making it a part of standard care is a light lift for policymakers that could make an enormous difference in women’s lives,” said Olivia Munn, actress and breast cancer survivor. “I know firsthand how powerful this tool can be because it led me to my breast cancer diagnosis when other standard tools missed it which ultimately helped save my life. Had it not been for that assessment, my breast cancer may not have been identified when it was. That experience is exactly why it’s important other women have access to the same opportunity. Sometimes the most consequential changes don’t require reinventing the system; they require the people with the power to make a difference to recognize an opportunity and act on it. That’s what makes this legislation so important, and why I’m proud to be working alongside Senator Kelly to move it forward.”

“Roughly 1 in 8 women will develop breast cancer at some point in their lifetime, and risk assessment tools have proven to detect early on and save lives,” Sen.Capito said. “Strengthening these critical tools will expand the opportunity for women—including many West Virginians—to determine their own risk.”

“Every woman deserves to have the information and resources needed to understand her breast cancer risk and make informed decisions about her health. By expanding access to evidence-based risk assessment tools, improving their accuracy, and raising awareness, we can help women identify potential breast cancer risks earlier and connect them with the appropriate screening, preventive care, and treatment they need,” said Dr. Miller-Meeks. “Early detection saves lives, and this legislation is an important step toward improving early identification, expanding access to care, and delivering better outcomes for all women.”

“Some women, because of increased risk factors, need more extensive breast cancer screening than a yearly mammogram,” said Rep. Schrier, M.D. “This bill will ensure that women are evaluated for risk, get screened appropriately, and have breast cancer detected and treated early. This bill will help save lives.”

TheKnowYourRiskActis supported by Susan G. Komen, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), Breast Cancer Research Foundation, The Estée Lauder Companies, National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN), Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center, Anne Klein, Brem Foundation to Defeat Breast Cancer, My Density Matters, FORCE: Facing Our Risk of Cancer Empowered, the Prevent CancerFoundation, Breast Cancer Early Detection Coalition (BCEDC), Women’s Health Advocates, Alliance for Women’s Health and Prevention, Check for a Lump, Families Fighting Hereditary Cancer, HealthyWomen, Living Beyond Breast Cancer, Lynch Syndrome Awareness and Education, Men Supporting Women with Cancer, SHARE Cancer Support, Sharsheret | The Jewish Breast & Ovarian Cancer Community, Society of Breast Cancer Imaging, The Latino Cancer Institute, Tigerlily Foundation, TOUCH, The Black Breast Cancer Alliance, Unite for HER, and the Young Survival Coalition.

See what advocates are saying about the Know Your Risk Act:

“Too many people are being diagnosed with breast cancer before anyone ever told them they were at risk, sometimes before they are even old enough for a first mammogram,” said Amber Guild, President & CEO, Susan G. Komen. “That is a failure we can fix. When people understand their risk early, they can begin screening sooner, advocate for the care they need, and catch this disease when it is most survivable. The Know Your Risk Actputs that power where it belongs, in people’s own hands, and it moves us toward the goal at the heart of our mission: finding breast cancer earlier, for everyone. We thank Senator Kelly for his leadership, and we will not rest until no one dies from breast cancer.”

“Breast cancer risk assessment is complex but very important in identifying who may benefit from increased screening, ultimately decreasing the cancer burden and most importantly saving lives. ACOG is grateful to Senator Mark Kelly for leading this bill to support ongoing research related to breast cancer risk assessment tools, determine evidence-based strategies to implement these tools, and educate the public about their breast cancer risk,” said Camille A. Clare, MD, MPH, CPE, President of the American College ofObstetricians and Gynecologists(ACOG).

“As the world’s largest private funder of breast cancer research, the Breast Cancer Research Foundation is proud to support the Know Your Risk Act. Since our founding more than 30 years ago, BCRF-funded scientists have been behind every major breakthrough in breast cancer research, transforming our understanding of breast cancer risk, prevention, treatment, survivorship, and metastasis. By advancing evidence-based, personalized risk assessment, this legislation builds on that progress and brings us closer to a future where more women, particularly younger women who may not yet receive routine mammograms, can take proactive steps to protect their health,” saidDonna McKay, President and CEO,the Breast Cancer Research Foundation.

“The Estée Lauder Companies believes a world without breast cancer is possible. For nearly 35 years, we have funded global research, education, and access to care in pursuit of that goal. As the founding partner and largest corporate donor of the Breast Cancer Research Foundation, the world’s largest private funder of breast cancer research, we support the science that deepens our understanding of breast cancer. We are proud to support the Know Your Risk Act and its focus on making evidence-based risk assessment a routine part of health care, a critical step toward prevention and early detection that will help save lives,”said Stéphane deLaFaverie, President and CEO, The Estée Lauder Companies.

“NCCN thanks the bipartisan sponsors of this critical legislation. The Know Your Risk Act will increase public awareness of individual breast cancer risk while also investing in research to further improve and understand the role of breast cancer risk assessment in managing cancer risk. Breast cancer screening saves lives. It makes it possible to treat cancer early, when we have the most options and the highest chance for a positive outcome. Evidence-based guidelines have different screening and follow-up recommendations depending on cancer risk levels. The Know Your Risk Act is an important step to make sure everyone has access to the best screening schedule for them. We applaud the bill’s sponsors for taking significant action in the fight against breast cancer,” said Crystal S. Denlinger, MD, Chief Executive Officer, National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN).

“Advances in cancer prevention, diagnosis, and early intervention are now not only available, but can significantly improve health and well-being. Knowing one’s risk to be able to choose the right next steps is therefore critical. An informed and engaged public is an important part of this advance, so this and all efforts to achieve that goal are commendable,” saidDr. Larry Norton, Medical Director,Evelyn H. Lauder Breast Center,Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center.

“Knowledge is power in early detection and personalized screening is key. With breast cancer incidence on the rise for younger women – combined with what we already know about the unacceptably high mortality rates for Black women – it is critical for women to understand their individual risk factors for breast cancer, so they can be their own best breast health advocates. I applaud Senator Kelly for introducing the Know Your Risk Act, which will empower women, increase survival rates and reduce intensity of care,” said Dr. Rachel Brem, MD, FACR, FSBI,Chief Medical Officer, Brem Foundation to Defeat Breast Cancer.

“Two months after I received an ‘all clear’ mammogram, I was diagnosed with Stage 4 breast cancer. I didn’t know my tumor was hidden by my dense breast tissue, or that my breast density put me at higher risk. I founded My Density Matters because I don’t want my story to become anyone else’s story. Every woman deserves to know her risk. I’m deeply grateful to Senator Kelly for introducing this legislation, and I urge Congress to pass it swiftly,” said Leslie Ferris Yerger, CEO and Founder,My Density Matters.

“Cancer risk is not one-size-fits-all. For many people, waiting until age 40 to begin mammograms or other breast cancer screening may be too late. For instance, women with certain genetic mutations should start breast imaging at age 25. Assessing risk factors—including family history, genetics, breast density, weight, etc.—by ages 25 to 30 can help guide tailored prevention, screening, and early detection strategies. The Know Your Risk Act is a critical step toward expanding the use of evidence-based tools to identify individuals who may be at increased risk of breast cancer. Earlier identification of those at elevated risk, coupled with access to appropriate preventive and screening interventions, has the potential to save lives and improve outcomes,”said Lisa Schlager, Vice President, Public Policy,FORCE:Facing Our Risk of Cancer Empowered.

“Understanding individual breast cancer risk is an important part of informed decision-making around prevention and early detection. Evidence-based risk assessment tools—when paired with routine screening—can help patients and providers make more informed decisions about their health. The Prevent Cancer Foundation supports the bipartisan Know Your Risk Act as it aims to improve access to these tools and help people better understand their breast health,” said Jody Hoyos, CEO, Prevent Cancer Foundation.

“Early detection saves lives and knowledge of and access to breast cancer risk assessment tools play a vital role in making sure this happens for all women and men facing this disease, and that’s what the Know Your Risk Act would enable and why it has the full support of our advocates in all 50 states,” said Liz Powell, Esq., MPH, Founder,the Breast Cancer Early Detection Coalition (BCEDC) and Women’s Health Advocates. “Our advocates will be educating lawmakers on just how important this bill is and why we need to pass it as soon as possible.”

Background:

The Know Your Risk Act would:

Establish a task force of experts to recommend strategies to expand access to and evaluation of evidence-based risk assessment tools, as well as ways to improve access to medically needed care after utilizing such a tool.

Direct the National Cancer Institute to update and expand publicly available educational materials about risk assessment tools for patients and providers.

Direct HHS and NIH to study and continually improve the accuracy of risk assessment tools.

title: Klobuchar, Blackburn Bill to Allow Law Enforcement to Better Investigate Child Exploitation Passes Senate
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) passed their bipartisan Safe Cloud Storage Act unanimously out of the Senate.

This legislation will ensure law enforcement can use modern technologies like cloud computing to assist in investigations of child sexual abuse material and child sexual exploitation. The bill now heads to the President to be signed into law.

“We must do everything we can to protect our children from online exploitation and abuse,” said Klobuchar. “This commonsense, bipartisan bill would improve investigations and prosecutions by allowing law enforcement to safely store, transmit, and evaluate evidence using cloud systems – saving time and resources. I encourage President Trump to swiftly sign it into law.”

“Those helping law enforcement in the fight against child sexual exploitation must be able to securely store evidence of these horrific crimes,” said Blackburn. “Our bipartisan Safe Cloud Storage Act would ensure investigators can securely handle and store CSAM evidence in the cloud by providing limited liability protections, and I’m pleased it is heading to President Trump’s desk.”

The legislation is supported by Minnesota local law enforcement, including Rochester Police Department Chief Jim Franklin:

"Today’s child sexual abuse crimes generate vast amounts of digital evidence, and our laws must match this reality. Law enforcement must have secure, modern tools to store and analyze that information quickly and responsibly. This bill positions the Rochester Police Department to develop a partnership that will modernize our investigative capabilities — enabling faster evidence processing, quicker arrests, stronger court cases, and the potential to rescue more victims sooner, ultimately strengthening the pursuit of justice for our most vulnerable," said Rochester Police Department Chief Jim Franklin.

The Safe Cloud Storage Act is also co-sponsored by Senators John Cornyn (R-TX), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Katie Britt (R-AL), Chris Coons (D-DE), Mike Lee (R-UT), Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Ashley Moody (R-FL), and Ron Wyden (D-OR).

The Safe Cloud Storage Act ensures that law enforcement-approved vendors who assist in investigations of child exploitation are permitted to securely store this evidence that is critical to holding these criminals accountable. Specifically, this bipartisan bill would permit law enforcement-approved vendors to provide secure, cloud-based storage of CSAM evidence without facing a civil claim or criminal charge—giving law enforcement the flexibility they need as they work to investigate and target these horrific criminals. This legislation would require vendors to adhere to strict cybersecurity standards to ensure that this material is securely stored. Importantly, these law enforcement-approved vendors will not be shielded from civil or criminal claims under this bill’s limited liability protections if they engage in intentional misconduct, negligent conduct, or if they act with malice.

This legislation is endorsed by prominent national organizations including Raven, National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC), Thorn, International Justice Mission, Fraternal Order of Police, Child Rescue Coalition, National District Attorneys Association, Association of State Criminal Investigative Agencies, and National Center on Sexual Exploitation.

“Congress’s passage of the Safe Cloud Storage Act marks a significant step toward modernizing how law enforcement investigates child sexual exploitation. By authorizing secure, cloud-based storage for CSAM evidence, the legislation will equip investigators with modern tools to move cases faster, identify victims sooner, and hold offenders accountable, while maintaining strong cybersecurity protections. Raven is proud to have worked alongside congressional offices, law enforcement, and business stakeholders to help bring this legislation across the finish line and to ensure it reflects the practical realities investigators face in the field. We are grateful for the bipartisan leadership that made this possible and look forward to seeing this important legislation signed into law,” said Jennifer Dunton, Executive Director of Raven.

title: Luján: Republicans Give FCC Nominee a Free Pass for False Statements to Congress
text:
POLITICO, Bloomberg, Newsweek, Los Angeles Times, Broadband Breakfast on Luján’s Push to Demand Accountability over Danielle Thumann’s False Statements to Congress

Thumann: “…I have not worked with the Chairman on any media-related issues…”

Trove of Emails Directly Contradict Thumann’s Own Testimony; Republicans Rushed Through Her Nomination Despite This Evidence

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the Senate Commerce Subcommittee on Telecommunications and Media, issued the following statement after Commerce Committee Republicans advanced the nomination of Danielle Thumann to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) despite evidence of false statements in her oral and written testimony before Congress:

“Lying to Congress is a crime, and when a nominee comes before this Committee and fails to tell the truth, we must hold them accountable. Ms. Thumann looked me in the eye and said she had not worked on media-related issues. Her own emails prove otherwise. Rather than delaying today’s vote to seek the truth, Republicans rushed through her nomination without even acknowledging her false statements.

“That is why I refused to participate in today’s markup. I will not be part of a process that turns a blind eye to false statements made before Congress. When Democrats retake the majority in January, we will exercise our oversight authority, demand answers, and pursue accountability. Ms. Thumann and her boss, Chairman Carr, will find themselves before this Committee again.

“This will not be the last time that Ms. Thumann and Chairman Carr hear from me.”

Senator Luján called on Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz (R-Texas) calling on him to remove the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) following revelations that appear to contradict her testimony during her nomination hearing.

During Ms. Thumann’s November 10th confirmation hearing, she testified in response to questioning from Senator Luján that she had not worked with FCC Chairman Brendan Carr on any media-related issues. However, documents obtained by Senator Luján reveal that Ms. Thumann worked on several media-related matters, including helping draft commitments made by Skydance that facilitated the FCC’s approval of its merger with Paramount.

The documents reveal that Ms. Thumann reviewed and edited a draft letter that Skydance later submitted to the FCC outlining its commitments to eliminate diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives at Paramount. The documents also reveal Ms. Thumann’s involvement in media issues related to CBS’ 60 Minutes and Jimmy Kimmel, directly contradicting her testimony before the Commerce Committee.

“While I find it hard to believe that Ms. Thumann simply misspoke or misunderstood the question, I hope that her inability to answer was not indicative of willful deception. Either way, if her testimony departed this far from the record on what we can see, the Committee has every reason to ask her what else she has hidden. Before moving forward with her nomination, this Committee must conduct another hearing to fully explore this new information and allow Ms. Thumann to correct the record,” Senator Luján wrote in his letter to Chairman Cruz.

title: Lummis, Gillibrand, Colleagues Urge Treasury to Give State Stablecoin Issuers Equal Footing with Federal Issuers
text:
Washington, D.C. — Senate Banking Committee Digital Assets Subcommittee Chair Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) and Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) led their colleagues Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Kevin Cramer (R-ND), Pete Ricketts (R-NE), and Mark Warner (D-VA) in sending a letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urging the Treasury Department to give state stablecoin issuers equal footing with federal charters as section 3 of the GENIUS Act comes into effect.

The letter urges Treasury to grant a safe harbor from compliance with section 3 to states which have certified their regulatory regimes as “substantially similar” to federal law while the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee reviews these certifications in 2027. Issuers supervised by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) were granted a similar safe harbor in Treasury’s proposed rulemaking. Parity with the OCC is essential to preserve the dual banking system. Congress explicitly envisioned states including Wyoming, New York, and Nebraska would be “substantially similar” to federal law from the start because it granted those states an expedited certification process under GENIUS section 4(c)(7).

“For Treasury to finalize this proposal in a way that reflects Congressional intent, it must allow issuers to choose from state or federal charters, as contemplated by the GENIUS Act, without the risk of business disruption or uncertainty,” the Senators wrote.

BACKGROUND:

Congress wrote the GENIUS Act to give stablecoin issuers a real choice between a federal and state charter. The law allows issuers with $10 billion or less in outstanding stablecoins to operate under a state regulatory regime, as long as that regime is “substantially similar” to the federal framework. Moreover, issuers in certain states, including Wyoming, with existing digital asset regulatory regimes are not required to submit to federal supervision when they reach $10 billion.

Nearly a decade ago, Wyoming established itself as a leader in digital asset regulation, creating its Special Purpose Depository charter in 2019 and giving digital asset companies a fully reserved, state-regulated home long before Congress acted. Senator Lummis helped write the GENIUS Act to ensure states like Wyoming remained meaningful partners in stablecoin regulation.

title: Ranking Member Shaheen, Senate Foreign Relations Democrats Statement Ahead of President Trump’s Meetings with Xi and Putin
text:
President Trump must use this summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin to defend American interests and values and confront the growing threats posed by Beijing and Moscow—not simply look out for his own bottom line.

“This meeting must not be yet another convergence of would-be-strongmen, carving up the world into spheres of influence, but an American president fighting for American values, including the rule of law. He must stand up to President Xi and make clear that the United States will strictly enforce export controls to prevent Beijing from exploiting American technology to erode our economic and national security advantages. He must confront China’s military intimidation of Taiwan and reaffirm our commitments under the Taiwan Relations Act and the Six Assurances by following the law and sending $14 billion in previously approved arms sales to Taiwan. He must also demand the release of Jimmy Lai, Min Zin and all other Americans wrongfully detained in China.

“China and Russia are cooperating in unprecedented and dangerous ways to undermine American security and prosperity. Xi and Putin cannot be allowed to use this meeting as a forum to advance their interests at the expense of the United States. The President should not let China’s indispensable support for Russia’s brutal war against Ukraine continue; he must crack down on Chinese suppliers and financial institutions facilitating Putin’s war machine that murders Ukrainian civilians with every passing day. This can only be achieved by standing up to Xi and Putin, rather than accommodating their imperial impulses. President Trump must be prepared to tell Putin unequivocally that European security is non-negotiable and that there will be no talks about Ukraine without Ukraine.

“American security cannot be traded away for photo opportunities or personal aggrandizement. President Trump must demonstrate that he is prepared to impose real costs on Putin for his aggression, rather than reward him with concessions that undermine Ukraine, our NATO Allies and U.S. national security. It is clear that the American people want lower prices, not more pageantry. We urge President Trump to use this summit to make Americans safer, strengthen our alliances and counter the destructive actions of our adversaries.”

title: VIDEO: Sen. Moran Joins the Families of Flight 5342 in Calling for Passage of Aviation Safety Legislation
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Jerry Moran (R-Kan.) – chairman of the Senate Commerce Subcommittee on Aviation, Space and Innovation – this week joined the Families of Flight 5342 at the Safer Skies for All Memorial outside the U.S. Capitol to call for the passage of comprehensive aviation safety legislation that can be signed into law by the President before the end of the year and to honor those lost in the January 29, 2025, midair collision near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport.

“There can be no excuse,” said Sen. Moran. “No excuse whatsoever for the failure of Congress to pass this legislation and for the President to sign it into law between now and the end of the year.”

“There can be no excuse. None. No excuse whatsoever for the failure of Congress to pass this legislation and for the President to sign it into law between now and the end of the year. None. No family member deserves anything other than an outcome that puts ADS-B In on aircraft across the country, and no excuse, no department, no agency, should stand in the way to this success.

“It’s an honor to stand here with you. While I say this is personal, it’s not personal in any way close to those who lost loved ones. You have done something that takes tragedy that turns it into value, as long as Congress and the administration get their jobs done. Thank you, and God bless you.”

title: At SVAC Hearing, Senator Murray Presses VA, Oracle on Flawed Electronic Health Record Modernization Program
text:
***WATCH: Senator Murray’s full questioning***

Washington, D.C. — Today, at a Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee (SVAC) hearing, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA)—a former chair and senior member of SVAC—questioned Dr. Neil Evans, Program Executive Director (PED) of VA’s Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) Integration Office, and Mike Sicilia, Co-CEO of Oracle Health, on the serious issues and system defects that remain unaddressed with the EHR program.

Senator Murray has been conducting oversight of the flawed EHR system rollout in Washington state since the Trump administration first negotiated the contract with Cerner (later acquired by Oracle), and at every point in the process since then. Murray has consistently pushed VA on its failed implementation of EHR—conducting oversight, holding the administration accountable, and, in 2022, calling on VA to halt the deployment of EHR in Washington state until it was fixed. In March 2023, Murray introduced comprehensive legislation that would require VA to implement a series of EHR reforms to better serve veterans, medical personnel, and taxpayers. In the Fiscal Year 2024 funding bills that Senator Murray negotiated and passed as then-Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Murray secured key provisions to better hold VA and Cerner accountable for the rollout of the EHR system. In May 2024, she sent a letter urging VA to consider feedback on the system from providers and veterans in Spokane and Walla Walla and reiterating that VA must not move forward on the rollout of EHR until the myriad issues that have plagued the system are fixed.

Last year, Senator Murray grilled Secretary Collins during his confirmation hearing on how he would prioritize fixing the issues with the EHR system before deploying it to more sites, and she has continued to press Secretary Collins to fix unresolved issues with the EHR system. As Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, Senator Murray fought to secure provisions in the Senate Military Construction, Veterans Affairs, and Related Agencies (MilCon-VA) appropriations bill for Fiscal Year 2026 that improve oversight and accountability of EHR. The legislation provides $3.4 billion to improve the EHR modernization effort and makes 30 percent of funds contingent upon the VA Secretary providing to Congress detailed information on EHR.

[WA EHR DEPLOYMENTS]

Senator Murray began by asking Dr. Evans if EHR will work with research partners to avoid disruptions to patient care, noting how the previous attempt at implementation at the Mann-Grandstaff VA Medical Center in Spokane, Washington put the lives of veteran patients at risk.

MURRAY: It has been over six years since the VA launched its first EHR deployment at the Mann-Grandstaff VA in my home state of Washington. It was a complete disaster. It literally put veterans’ lives in danger. So, it won’t surprise you to hear that I’m very skeptical about deploying the system to other VAs in my state.

Dr. Evans, Puget Sound is the largest VA in Washington and the specialty care hub for Alaska, Idaho, and Montana. VA is scheduled to roll out EHR there next year. Ahead of this next Washington deployment, have you spoken directly with providers at Mann-Grandstaff about the lessons learned?

EVANS: Yes.

MURRAY: Do you want to tell us what they told you?

EVANS: Sure. First of all, I’ve spoken, I’ve been to Man-Grandstaff several times in person. In fact, when we started, it was frankly in partnership with you and the prior hearing. Which is a hearing when I had been on the job for a month, where you encouraged us to.

MURRAY: I just want to know what they told you.

EVANS: They shared with us some of the challenges, but they also, I will argue, have been incredibly helpful in providing feedback that has led to some of the 13,000 changes that we have made to the system. In part, because we have learned from what they shared. So I would argue that the staff at Mann-Grandstaff and the staff in Walla Walla, and frankly all of our original sites in the Pacific Northwest, are staff that we have a significant debt of gratitude to for their—

MURRAY: I appreciate that, but I think you know there are still concerns, and I’m hoping you’re talking to them before you roll this out.

Let me just say that one of the failures in the past EHR rollouts was that the VA systems couldn’t work with research universities and partners. The Puget Sound VA works with outside partners, including the University of Washington, to [research] groundbreaking new treatments for veterans. Can you assure me today that VA has resolved those issues coordinating with its research partners, so this EHR rollout won’t mean disruptions in clinical research and in patient care?

EVANS: Yes, absolutely. You may recall that one of the reasons why we were on track to go live in Ann Arbor, numerous years ago, and we stopped that go live because of concerns about our ability to adequately support the research mission in Ann Arbor. Ann Arbor has partnerships with the University of Michigan and other.

MURRAY: Have those been resolved?

EVANS: And those have all been resolved. So we’ve gone live in Ann Arbor. We went live with over 100 clinical trials in Ann Arbor and have been very successful at doing so.

MURRAY: So you can assure me today that there won’t be any disruptions when you go live with any of their partners, including, as I said, research and patient care.

EVANS: That’s correct.

MURRAY: There will not be, none. You’re testifying to that today?

EVANS: We work closely with Oracle. We actually send a team, there actually is a dedicated team from Oracle that supports working with our principal investigators to make sure that we are getting the build right for each of the clinical research trials. This has been a proven model over all of the medical centers over this past year where we do support research, and we will of course be doing the same when we go to Seattle.

MURRAY: Well let me just say that after the missteps we have seen, I want to put you on notice today that I am watching like a hawk to make sure quality service and veteran safety are being prioritized every step of the way.

[COST OF EHRM TRIPLES]

Senator Murray continued by asking Dr. Evans and Mr. Sicilia about miscalculations and incorrect estimates made on EHR records, users, and time frame.

MURRAY: Oracle told my staff that its EHR contract increased a whopping $17 billion because there were changes in the scope of the project. Between 2018 and 2026, the number of veteran records increased from eight million to over 26 million. Apparently, VA got this estimate dead wrong under the first Trump administration.

Dr. Evans, when did VA realize the project was more than three times larger than originally negotiated?

EVANS: So I’ll first say there, we shared that a year ago, as I’ve mentioned the cost estimate. So we have certainly been aware of what the costs are going to be, in part because of the realization that the estimate, so I’ll just take us back to 2017 and 2018. That estimate of $9.996 billion, that was the original ceiling estimate, was an estimate based on an assumption of what it would take to successfully deploy the federal EHR. We together have learned a lot. We have increased, for example, you heard mentioned of learning labs. We added learning labs. That was not—

MURRAY: Okay. My question was, and I will run out of time here, and I have more questions because the estimate was way off. Oracle also said that, in addition to record increases, there was a 129 percent increase in end users. How do you explain that? I’m really confused about how this number is increasing when the Trump administration is simultaneously putting a hiring freeze on VA clinical staff. These miscalculations are a big red flag to all of us, and we need more information on how VA comes up with these estimates that apparently were really wrong. That’s what I’m very concerned about.

Mr. Sicilia, in July 2022, you told this committee that Oracle would provide VA with an EHR system that exceeds expectations without exceeding the contracted cost. Was that a promise that you kept: yes or no?

SICILIA: I believe that what was contemplated at that time is very different than what’s been delivered today, and I believe that we have delivered on after the reset on the redesigned program.

MURRAY: Well, let me just say that more than tripling the cost of the project kind of feels like a no to me.

And you’ve also said the number of interfaces Oracle has to build to connect to other systems has also increased by 187 percent since 2018. So let me just ask you, does the new contract account for future work to connect to those other systems?

SICILIA: The new contract, the contemplated IDIQ, takes into account all of the scope changes that we made. All of the additional interfaces, and they continue to roll out to complete the VAMC rollout. That is all in the new IDIQ. The question is about value versus cost. I want to go back to what I said about a sincere commitment. If Congress believes that the system doesn’t have value, that is something that only Congress and the VA can ultimately decide. We made every effort to deploy this system as efficiently and as cost-effectively as we can. If Congress believes that the cost is simply too high, but the value is still there, I would encourage you to challenge us.

MURRAY: Look, what I’m just saying is, you told this committee that the system would exceed expectations without exceeding the contracted cost. We are here not much later, and it’s done that considerably. So, Mr. Chairman, let me just say I want to make sure that you are not going to walk away after the end of this contract and leave veterans with a system that still doesn’t work. We all know veterans deserve access to the best health care technology, and you are responsible for upholding that promise to them.

title: Padilla, Schiff Tribal Land Transfer Bills to be Signed into Law
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.) announced that their bicameral and bipartisan bills to promote Tribal management of over 800 acres of land in California passed in the Senate and House of Representatives. The Pit River Land Transfer Act and Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians Land Transfer Act now head to President Trump’s desk to be signed into law.

“For too long, California’s Tribal nations have been denied the right to manage and preserve their ancestral lands. The historic passage of these two bills represents a key step toward righting our historical wrongs,” said Senator Padilla. “Restoring tribal land to its original owners preserves traditions, strengthens communities, and supports ecological health across California. I am proud to support the Pit River Tribe and the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians and I am grateful for the bipartisan, bicameral support that made these land transfers possible.”

“For generations, California’s tribes have fought to rightfully restore their ancestral homelands and preserve the culture of their ancestors,” said Senator Schiff. “I am proud Congress has passed our legislation to help the Pit River Tribe and Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians reclaim their cultural lands and promote tribal sovereignty.”

Pit River Land Transfer Act

This bill would transfer 557 acres of federal land administered by the United States Forest Service to the Department of the Interior to be held in trust for the Pit River Tribe. The Tribe has been actively trying to acquire this land through various governmental processes for over a decade. However, they have experienced a series of delays that have added years to the process. The late Representative Doug LaMalfa (R-Calif.-01) led companion legislation in the House of Representatives, which is now led by Representative James Gallagher (R-Calif.-01).

“Doug LaMalfa was a tireless advocate for the North State, and returning this land to the Pit River Tribe was a cause he believed in,” said Representative Gallagher. “I’m honored to carry his work forward and grateful to Senator Padilla for his partnership in moving this legislation through the Senate. The Tribe has waited more than a decade for this, and it’s encouraging to see Republicans and Democrats working together to get it across the finish line.”

“For the Pit River Tribe, Four Corners is more than a parcel of land. It is a place that connects our ancestors, our history, and our future,” said Pit River Tribe Chairman Yatch Bamford. “Passage of this legislation brings us closer to caring for this land as its Stewards, preserving a site central to our people’s struggle for justice, and creating a place where future generations can learn our history. We thank Senator Padilla for his leadership and tireless work in securing passage of this bill, and Senator Schiff for his support. We are also deeply grateful to the late Congressman Doug LaMalfa for his leadership and work to advance this legislation. Their commitments to our Tribe made this milestone possible, as we work toward a future rooted in our culture and shaped by our people.”

The Pit River Tribe consist of 11 autonomous bands traditionally inhabiting the area surrounding the Pit River and its tributaries. They are known for their deep spiritual connection to the land, with a rich cultural heritage centered around fishing, hunting, and seasonal gatherings.

The proposed land to be transferred is known as the Four Corners Property, located in Shasta County. The Tribe has strong cultural and historical connections to the Four Corners, and they view it as a central landmark of their ancestral lands. In October 1970, members of the Tribe erected a Quonset hut on the Four Corners, staking a peaceful, yet firm claim. That month, over 100 sheriff’s deputies, federal marshals, and forest rangers ordered the occupants to evacuate the property, which eventually resulted in violence and the hospitalization of several Tribal members.

Full text of the Pit River Land Transfer Act is available here.

Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians Land Transfer Act

This bill would place approximately 80 acres of land currently managed by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) into trust for the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians, a federally recognized Tribe whose reservation is located near Placerville in the western Sierra Nevada foothills. The bill would also place into trust 185 acres of fee land already owned by the Tribe. Representative Tom McClintock (R-Calif.-05) is leading companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

“The Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians survived near annihilation during the Spanish and Gold Rush eras to become a prosperous and integral part of El Dorado County. I am honored to carry this legislation that will continue their progress and contributions to their posterity and to our community into the years ahead,” said Representative McClintock.

“This legislation is about our homeland and the future we are building for our children and grandchildren,” said Chairwoman Regina Cuellar. “Its passage brings us closer to securing these lands for our people and strengthening our ability to care for them for generations to come. We thank Senators Padilla and Schiff and Congressman McClintock for their leadership and work to secure passage of this legislation. We are deeply grateful for their commitment to our Tribe and support for our future.”

The Tribe’s current trust land base is just 317 acres and their reservation access was significantly disrupted decades ago when Highway 50 was constructed across their only entrance. While the Tribe has since invested in an off-ramp to restore access, their existing land remains insufficient to meet the needs of their citizens.

This bill would place BLM land into trust for the Tribe to maintain it for open space and fire risk management. By enabling the Tribe to place their existing fee land into trust, the bill would help the Tribe build much-needed housing.

Full text of the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians Land Transfer Act is available here.

Padilla is a strong advocate for restoring Tribal ownership of ancestral lands. Last week, Padilla and Schiff introduced legislation to transfer over 800 acres of federal land into trust for the Barona Band of Mission Indians. In July, Padilla testified at a Senate Committee on Indian Affairs hearing to advocate for critical water investments for California Tribes. In March, Padilla and Schiff introduced legislation to transfer 860 acres of land from the BLM into trust for the Pechanga Band of Indians.
