title: WATCH: Padilla Condemns Republican Attacks on Social Security
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today during a Senate Budget Committee hearing, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) condemned the Trump Administration’s relentless attacks on the Social Security system and failure to address the unaffordability crisis created by the President’s disastrous economic policies. He also blasted Republicans’ unserious attempts to address Social Security insolvency.

Ahead of the hearing, Senator Ron Johnson (R-Wis.), Chair of the Senate Committee on the Budget, went on Fox News and said to “shut it down,” referring to Social Security. He also repeatedly referred to Social Security as a “Ponzi scheme” and suggested that the program was unfixable. Padilla joined several Democratic colleagues in condemning Johnson’s alarming comments and noted that Republican policies have been the biggest contributors to mounting deficits and wasteful government spending.

Padilla also highlighted the Trump Administration’s cruel mass deportation agenda, which has further weakened the Social Security system and the long-term health of the nation’s economy. He noted that immigrants pay into the Social Security system regardless of legal status, which benefits the system’s bottom line.

Key Excerpts:

On Trump’s reckless attacks on Social Security

PADILLA: For the last two years the president and the Republican majority have been doing only taking actions only making economic anxiety worse. Want to talk about how, you know, why the deficit situation has gotten worse? We can point to the tariff policies. We can point to the Iran war, which is unauthorized and unpopular. We can talk about the cuts to healthcare overall. But no, they don’t want to talk about that. They want to shift the blame here, all of the sudden, to Social Security. So, let’s call out the facts for what they are: when you cut taxes for the ultra-wealthy and the largest corporations, and you cut healthcare access. That’s where we ought to be looking, because when the president wants it, there seems to be money for a war that Congress has not authorized, but there’s not money to address Social Security. There’s money for a war and tax breaks for the most wealthy, but there’s not money for healthcare for working families in America, or to buttress Social Security. That’s the contrast. That’s the contrast, and that’s the frame for this conversation

On Trump’s So-Called One Big Beautiful Bill

PADILLA: The Administration has claimed a big win: no taxes on Social Security, they say. Through the “Anything But Beautiful Bill Act.” But the truth is that the substantial majority of low and middle-income seniors will not benefit from this new tax deduction, nor will Social Security beneficiaries younger than 65, including people with disabilities and those on survivor benefits. And of course, the deduction fails to compensate for the drastic cuts to healthcare and food assistance in the Anything But Beautiful Bill that have left millions of lower-income seniors worse off.

On the Essential Role of Immigrants in Social Security Contributions

PADILLA: So many workers in the United States who are not citizens, different immigration status, who pay into Social Security but cannot benefit from Social Security. This administration, the Republican majority, has been hell bent on trying to crack down and deport so many immigrant workers, whether they’re undocumented, many with work permits, many legal permanent residents. Is that helping address the solvency concern for Social Security? Yes, no, and how so?

EDWARDS: Immigrants, whether they are unauthorized or authorized, pay into Social Security are an unequivocal windfall for its bottom line.

In March, Padilla highlighted the critical role of immigrant contributions in funding Social Security and supporting the workforce and economy. In the same hearing, he warned of the dangers posed by the Administration’s abuse of sensitive Social Security data. Last year, Padilla condemned the Trump Administration’s weaponization of the Social Security Administration (SSA) against immigrants through its decision to classify certain immigrants as “dead” in master files. Padilla also demanded the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) stop its attacks on Social Security, including staffing cuts, plans for indiscriminate closures of field offices across the country, and limits to phone services.

title: WATCH: Padilla Slams Project 2025 DOI Nominee Over Staffing Cuts and Proposed Yosemite Land Transfer
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), a member of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, pressed Department of the Interior (DOI) Inspector General nominee Dennis Kirk and Assistant Secretary of Energy nominee Toby Deen about the Trump Administration’s proposed Yosemite land transfer, DOI staffing cuts, and geothermal technologies.

In his questioning, Padilla raised serious concerns about land in Yosemite being given away and demanded answers about political and personal interests influencing the proposed land transfer. Kirk declined to commit to investigate the proposed land transfer. Kirk also admitted to co-authoring Project 2025 and refused to answer Padilla’s questions about Kirk’s support for DOI staffing reductions since Trump took office.

Padilla also questioned Deen about the potential and growth of geothermal technologies in California and secured a commitment from Deen that, if confirmed, he would work with Padilla on a plan to maximize the geothermal and critical mineral potential of the Salton Sea region.

Key Excerpts:

On Trump’s Proposed Yosemite Land Transfer

PADILLA: Will you commit to investigating the circumstances surrounding this proposed land exchange, including whether or not political connections or personal financial interests influence the department’s consideration of the proposal?

KIRK: Thank you for the question, Senator Padilla, but I have not been briefed on that transfer or that sale. However, I will say that these areas are where independent examinations may have value if it’s responsive to the things that work themselves up through the agency, or I trust my staff explicitly.

On Kirk’s involvement in Project 2025

PADILLA: How do you expect to do the job when you’re relying on the staff, when the staff themselves – and I hear from a lot of employees in California saying they’re now having a tough time filling their statutory obligations because of all these reductions.

KIRK: Well, I’ve been privileged to talk to our Sacramento offices out there, and they’re doing a great job. And I trust that they’re—

PADILLA: They’re doing a great job to the best of their ability, given the minimum support they’ve received from the top down because of the cuts to budgets and personnel that you advocated for.

KIRK: I was not part of DOGE. And when I’ve come in,

PADILLA: I didn’t say you were. I said you were part of Project 2025.

KIRK: Oh yeah.

PADILLA: Are you going to tell me on the record under oath that you weren’t?

KIRK: In fact, I was the, um—

PADILLA: Were you or were you not? Yes or no?

KIRK: I was about to say I was a co-author with a, a brilliant doctor, Dan Devine, and Paul Dans of Chapter Three, and in fact…

PADILLA: And that tells me all I need to know about how you’re going to approach this position.

On Geothermal Technologies in California

PADILLA: California probably has more geothermal than all other states combined. The generating capacity that is, and I’m pleased to see recent expansion of geothermal leasing. We can achieve great things not just with geothermal as we know today, but with evolving geothermal technologies.

On leveraging the Salton Sea

PADILLA: Would you work with my office to develop that specific plan and approach to maximize the benefit of the Salton Sea?

DEEN: Yes, Senator. If confirmed, I look forward to collaborating with your office.

Senator Padilla has been a longtime advocate of protecting Yosemite and national parks across the nation. In September, Padilla led his colleagues in urging the DOI abandon their proposed transfer of federally managed public land within Yosemite National Park. In July, Padilla slammed the Trump Administration for eliminating the Yosemite reservation system, pressing DOI officials on their plans to ensure Yosemite’s ability to manage wildfire risk, enhance visitor safety, and conserve natural resources. In 2025, Padilla introduced the Review and Evaluation of Strategies for Equal Reservations for Visitor Experiences (RESERVE) Federal Land Act to expand access to public lands, improve visitor experience, and enhance transparency of how fees are collected for federal lands and national parks.

Video of Padilla’s questioning is available here.

title: ON THE JOB FOR MICHIGAN: West Michigan Veterans Service Officer Applauds Peters’ Bill Inspired by Grand Rapids Veteran
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – In a new “On the Job” video from U.S. Senator Gary Peters’ (MI) office, Thornell Billingslea, Vice President of the West Michigan Veterans Assistance Program, highlights Peters’ efforts to pass the Fairness for Veterans Act into law. In the video, Billingslea shares the story of Patrick, a West Michigan Veteran who was suffering from a Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) related to his service. Since Patrick was erroneously given a less-than honorable discharge at the conclusion of his service, he was deemed ineligible for certain VA benefits that would have provided much-needed assistance during his transition to civilian life.

“Because of his eyesight, because of his limp, because of TBI, he had some serious issues,” said Billingslea. “He was not in a position to work, so how is he going to have a life that would be suitable for him and productive for him? The only way for him to do that is to have his discharge reversed.”

Watch the “On The Job” video here.

Billingslea brought this story to Senator Peters, which inspired him to introduce and pass the Fairness for Veterans Act into law. The legislation requires veteran discharge review boards to give liberal consideration to petitions for honorable discharge status if the servicemember has been diagnosed with PTSD, TBI, or other related conditions connected to their military service. Since being passed in 2016, the Fairness for Veterans Act has helped more than 21,000 veterans across America access earned veteran benefits.

“All Americans share a sacred obligation to stand behind our veterans and ensure they have access to the benefits they earned and certainly deserve,” said Senator Peters. “Patrick’s story has helped thousands of veterans get the care they need, and none of it would have been possible without Thornell’s tireless advocacy.”

The video is part of the On the Job for Michigan series, which highlights Peters’ leadership and advocacy on behalf of Michigan constituents and communities.

ICYMI: WXMI Fox 17 Grand Rapids: How a law that's helped more than 20,000 veterans get healthcare got its start in Grand Rapids

“An honorable discharge from the U.S. military gives veterans full access to various benefits provided by the Department of Veterans Affairs, including healthcare.

“But for almost all of our country's history, veterans who received a less than honorable discharge due to bad behavior have been unable to access the full scope of these benefits, even if their behavior was caused by a mental health condition.

“Ten years ago, this all changed with the Fairness for Veterans Act, a law written by Michigan Sen. Gary Peters that was inspired by a Grand Rapids veteran.

“‘We have an obligation as a country to stand behind those who've stood on the front line for us,’ Sen. Peters said to FOX 17 News. ‘We should do everything we can to make sure they can transition into civilian life, and live a comfortable life that can take care of their families and provide for their future.’

“After a Marine who served in Afghanistan received a less than honorable discharge — a designation that came by way of bad behavior brought on by a pair of traumatic brain injuries — he was unable to receive the medical and mental health treatment he needed and fell on misfortune.

“Patrick was his name. He was homeless, living on the streets of Grand Rapids, and went to the West Michigan Veterans Assistance Program to find a place to stay.

“‘He had issues,’ said Thornell Billingslea, vice president with the WMVAP. ‘There's a lot of them like Patrick. They don't know what to do. They wait years and years and years (for assistance).’

“Billingslea took Patrick's story to Peters, and one man's life led to legislation.

“The Fairness for Veterans Act directs the Department of Defense to ‘give liberal consideration to petitions for changes in discharge status to honorable if the servicemember has been diagnosed with PTSD, TBI or related conditions in connection with their military service,’ according to Peters' office.

“By way of this law, the office says 21,000 veterans across the country have earned access to veteran benefits for the first time.

“Patrick was one of those people. According to Billingslea, he's now living in Louisiana and is ‘doing well.’

“‘People need to make sure that their voices are heard,’ Peters said. ‘When they are heard, that can lead to substantial change.’”

During his service in the U.S. Navy Reserve, Peters earned a Seabee Combat Warfare Specialist designation and rose to the rank of Lieutenant Commander. After the September 11th terrorist attacks on our country, Peters volunteered again for drilling status and served overseas as part of his Reserve duty. He later earned a diploma from the College of Naval Command and Staff, U.S. Naval War College.

In the Senate, Peters has remained committed to supporting our nation’s servicemembers and veterans. In 2017, Peters was recognized as Legislator of the Year by the Vietnam Veterans of America for authoring his Fairness for Veterans Act. In 2021, Peters was inducted into the Michigan Military and Veterans Hall of Honor for his efforts to support our nation’s veterans and military. In 2022, Peters helped enact the Sergeant First Class Heath Robinson Honoring our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics (PACT) Act – which delivered VA health care and benefits to all generations of toxic-exposed veterans and their survivors for the first time in our nation’s history.

title: Ricketts Introduces Bill to Enhance Retirement Opportunities for Seniors
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NE) introduced the Enhancing Choice and Protections for our Seniors Act. The legislation would allow trusted financial professionals to advise on Home Equity Conversion Mortgages (HECMs). This would expand financial options for seniors preparing for retirement.

“Nebraska’s senior citizens deserve to retire with dignity,” said Ricketts. “Trusted financial advisors provide much-needed guidance when planning for the future. Allowing them to consult on mortgages can help seniors understand their financial options and protect them from fraud. I will always fight to protect the Good Life for our seniors and all Nebraskans.”

Currently, one in five adults over 50 has no retirement savings. Nearly 61 percent worry about being financially prepared for the future. HECMs can provide seniors with the certainty and capital to prepare for retirement.

“This legislation removes a barrier to comprehensive retirement planning for consumers while ensuring appropriate consumer protections. Modernizing the law so seniors can receive holistic retirement planning from their trusted advisors that includes Home Equity Conversion Mortgages helps improve informed decision-making,” said Alex Pistone, President at Mutual of Omaha Mortgage. “We appreciate Senator Ricketts leadership and work on this important issue.”

The Enhancing Choice and Protections for our Seniors Act would:

Permit qualified financial professionals to consult on and originate HECMs under standards from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.

Enhance consumer protections by increasing transparency between financial advisors and lenders.

Protect seniors by prohibiting mandatory purchases of additional products as a condition for origination.

title: Ricketts Introduces Eric Hamilton for U.S. District Court of Nebraska
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Ricketts introduced Eric Hamilton to the Senate Judiciary Committee. Hamilton is nominated to serve on the U.S. District Court of Nebraska.

“Senator Fischer and I recommended Eric Hamilton to the President because of his dedication to public service and his commitment to the rule of law,” Ricketts said. “If confirmed, Eric will continue to represent and protect the Good Life.”

Watch the Senator’s full remarks here.

TRANSCRIPT

“Thank you, Mr. Chairman, thank you Ranking Member for holding this important hearing.

“I very much appreciate it.

“My senior senator has done a fine job of talking about Eric Hamilton, but I will add my voice as well.

“It’s a privilege to be able to introduce and support an exceptionally qualified Nebraskan for this important role.

“Eric Hamilton is President Trump’s nominee for the U.S. District Court in Nebraska.

“Now, I have known Eric since he was 18 years old.

“About 20 years ago when we were both getting involved in politics is when I had the opportunity to meet him.

“And I will tell you back then he had hair; I did not.

“But you’ll notice, he has adopted the very sleek look that I sport here in the U.S. Senate.

“Senator Fischer and I recommended Eric Hamilton to the President because of his dedication to public service and his commitment to the rule of law.

“His career and record highlight this.

“Eric has served our country with distinction, serving now in two presidential administrations.

“In these roles, he has defended and protected American values and freedom. He carried on this service back in Nebraska as our Solicitor General.

“In Nebraska, he defended the bills passed by the state legislature, including Nebraska’s law to protect preborn babies after 12 weeks.

“In his current role, he continues to defend both Congress’s statutes and the executive branch’s actions.

“As Deputy Assistant Attorney General, Eric took the historic enforcement action against China-based Suirui Group.

“This was the first time that the U.S. government forced a Chinese company to divest after review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States, otherwise known as CFIUS.

“Eric served our state with integrity.

“He fought for Nebraskans and our way of life.

“He is a sixth-generation Nebraskan, raised in Omaha.

“He graduated from Millard West High School, received his bachelor’s degree from the University of Nebraska—Lincoln, and as my senior senator mentioned, graduated from Stanford Law.

“In Nebraska, our motto is “The Good Life.”

“If confirmed, Eric will continue to represent and protect the Good Life in my state.

“Mr. Chairman, thank you for the opportunity to introduce Eric Hamilton.

“I encourage this Committee to support his nomination.

“I recommend him most highly.

“Thank you very much for your time this morning.”

title: Rosen, Commerce Committee Colleagues Demand Answers from Transportation Department, FAA on Cause of Recent Nationwide Ground Stop
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) joined her Democratic colleagues on the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation in sending a letter demanding clear, fact-based answers from Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Administrator Bryan Bedford about the root cause of last Friday’s nationwide ground stop. The letter comes as Secretary Duffy and Administrator Bedford are demanding $50 billion in funding for air traffic control modernization, up from a request for $30 billion just last week. There have been various prior outages earlier this year, impacting Philadelphia Terminal Radar Approach Control and Minneapolis Air Route Traffic Control Center.

“The Department of Transportation (DOT) and FAA must explain how this failure occurred and identify the corrective actions and oversight needed to prevent a recurrence,” the Senators wrote. “Identifying the device that failed does not establish why it failed. FAA must investigate further to determine the root cause and report to Congress on how it intends to prevent future issues.”

“DOT, FAA and OMB must provide Congress with a complete account of what happened and how additional funding would address the vulnerabilities presented on November 13,” the Senators wrote. “Congress deserves clear answers on how the FAA is ensuring the safety of the aviation system for the traveling public while these new systems are being deployed.”

“Modernization cannot come at the expense of operational safety,” they concluded.

You can find the full letter HERE.

Senator Rosen has been a champion for Nevada’s travel and tourism industry, ensuring that Nevada’s airways and ports of entry are safe and efficient. In July, she announced nearly $30 million in federal funding for improvements and renovations to airports across Nevada. Senator Rosen recently introduced a bill that would restrict ICE operations at airports, protecting travelers and airport employees and reining in ICE conduct. Senator Rosen has also urged the administration to support the tourism industry, including pushing for the reconvening of an essential travel and tourism board that the Trump administration has neglected.

###

title: Rosen, Padilla Introduce Bill to Limit ICE Operations at Airports
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, U.S. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and Alex Padilla (D-CA) introduced the Travel Without Fear Act, a bill to limit the ability of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) to conduct civil immigration operations at or near airports without a judicial warrant related to a felony criminal conviction. The bill would also ban information sharing between ICE and TSA for civil immigration enforcement actions that do not have a judicial warrant for a specific target. The legislation would further require ICE agents to ensure that targets for arrest or detention are not within a period of authorized stay, prohibit ICE from accessing passenger data without a warrant, require ICE to notify airports and airlines in advance of any enforcement action, and codify the online database that tracks detainee locations for their families and attorneys, while mandating that it be updated within six hours of a detainee’s change in custody.

Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) also signed on to the legislation.

In the last year, there has been an increase in violent ICE civil enforcement operations at airports across America. This includes an incident at Harry Reid International Airport where masked and plain-clothed ICE agents attempted to violently arrest an elderly man without a judicial warrant. According to their own reports, ICE recorded the highest number of administrative arrests in ICE’s history.

“ICE should not be allowed to operate recklessly and aggressively in our communities – putting lives and livelihoods at risk. We’ve even seen ICE operating with impunity inside airports, sowing chaos and fear, and further disrupting Nevada’s tourism economy,” said Senator Rosen. “That’s why I’m introducing this bill to prohibit ICE from conducting civil enforcement operations at airports without a judicial warrant, and to set clear guidelines for their conduct when they have one.”

“ICE is out of control, and these are bare minimum standards for reining it in: officers who are visibly identifiable, as my VISIBLE Act requires, protections for travelers’ personal information, and a check for pending applications before arrests,” said Senator Padilla. “These safeguards protect everyone involved – travelers, officers, and the public. It’s commonsense and responsible.”

Senator Rosen has been one of the main proponents in the Senate for stricter guardrails and more accountability for ICE agents. She led Senate colleagues in a letter demanding answers from the Trump administration over TSA cooperation with ICE at airports. Senator Rosen also joined a push against the rollout of electric shock gloves for use by ICE agents. In June, Senator Rosen voted against the ultra-partisan Republican budget, which gave ICE more funding without any guardrails or accountability mechanisms.

###

The Tribe has waited more than a decade for this, and it’s encouraging to see Republicans and Democrats working together to get it across the finish line.”

“For the Pit River Tribe, Four Corners is more than a parcel of land. It is a place that connects our ancestors, our history, and our future,” said Pit River Tribe Chairman Yatch Bamford. “Passage of this legislation brings us closer to caring for this land as its Stewards, preserving a site central to our people’s struggle for justice, and creating a place where future generations can learn our history. We thank Senator Padilla for his leadership and tireless work in securing passage of this bill, and Senator Schiff for his support. We are also deeply grateful to the late Congressman Doug LaMalfa for his leadership and work to advance this legislation. Their commitments to our Tribe made this milestone possible, as we work toward a future rooted in our culture and shaped by our people.”

The Pit River Tribe consist of 11 autonomous bands traditionally inhabiting the area surrounding the Pit River and its tributaries. They are known for their deep spiritual connection to the land, with a rich cultural heritage centered around fishing, hunting, and seasonal gatherings.

The proposed land to be transferred is known as the Four Corners Property, located in Shasta County. The Tribe has strong cultural and historical connections to the Four Corners, and they view it as a central landmark of their ancestral lands. In October 1970, members of the Tribe erected a Quonset hut on the Four Corners, staking a peaceful, yet firm claim. That month, over 100 sheriff’s deputies, federal marshals, and forest rangers ordered the occupants to evacuate the property, which eventually resulted in violence and the hospitalization of several Tribal members.

Full text of the Pit River Land Transfer Act is available here.

Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians Land Transfer Act

This bill would place approximately 80 acres of land currently managed by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) into trust for the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians, a federally recognized Tribe whose reservation is located near Placerville in the western Sierra Nevada foothills. The bill would also place into trust 185 acres of fee land already owned by the Tribe. Representative Tom McClintock (R-Calif.-05) is leading companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

“The Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians survived near annihilation during the Spanish and Gold Rush eras to become a prosperous and integral part of El Dorado County. I am honored to carry this legislation that will continue their progress and contributions to their posterity and to our community into the years ahead,” said Representative McClintock.

“This legislation is about our homeland and the future we are building for our children and grandchildren,” said Chairwoman Regina Cuellar. “Its passage brings us closer to securing these lands for our people and strengthening our ability to care for them for generations to come. We thank Senators Padilla and Schiff and Congressman McClintock for their leadership and work to secure passage of this legislation. We are deeply grateful for their commitment to our Tribe and support for our future.”

The Tribe’s current trust land base is just 317 acres and their reservation access was significantly disrupted decades ago when Highway 50 was constructed across their only entrance. While the Tribe has since invested in an off-ramp to restore access, their existing land remains insufficient to meet the needs of their citizens.

This bill would place BLM land into trust for the Tribe to maintain it for open space and fire risk management. By enabling the Tribe to place their existing fee land into trust, the bill would help the Tribe build much-needed housing.

Full text of the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians Land Transfer Act is available here.

title: WATCH: Sen. Schiff Says Chairman Selig “Blatantly Deceived” Committee on Prediction Markets at CFTC Nomination Hearing
text:
Washington, D.C. – During a Senate Agriculture Committee hearing today considering nominations to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) called out CFTC Chairman Michael Selig for misleading the Committee while under oath on his stance on prediction markets.

Schiff highlighted that despite Selig previously telling the Committee that he would “follow what the courts say,” under his unilateral leadership, the CFTC has intervened in prediction market litigation and sued 12 states for attempting to enforce their own gambling laws.

“Over the last two years, the rapid growth of prediction markets has allowed users to gamble on just about anything…These markets are operating in a Wild West, desperately in need of regulation and guardrails,” Senator Schiff said during the exchange.

“During his confirmation hearing, I asked Chairman Selig a simple question of whether a prediction contract on who wins or loses a football game is sports betting. He told me that he would be a blank slate on whether prediction markets were gambling and that he would defer to the courts… But he has been anything but a blank slate. He has not looked to the courts. He’s filed briefs to tell the courts what to do, and when the courts have ruled in a way that doesn’t favor the prediction markets, he has basically told companies to ignore the courts, ignore court orders, don’t geofence, don’t respect state or Tribal laws. Anything but a blank slate. I don’t know that I’ve ever been so blatantly deceived by a nominee before” Senator Schiff said.

Schiff also pressed Nathan Amonick, nominee to be Commissioner of the CFTC, on whether he would defer to the courts and respect state and Tribal laws on prediction market regulation. Since his confirmation, Chairman Selig has yet to appear before the Senate Agriculture Committee.

Watch the full clip here

Read the full transcript below:

Schiff: Thank you, Mr. Chairman. Mr. Anonick, and Mr. Rowland, congratulations on your nominations. Thank you for your service to the Committee and to the Senate.

Currently, we have only one Senate-confirmed Commissioner, and I’m glad that the Committee is considering a bipartisan pair of Commissioner nominees today, it is long overdue.

Over the last two years, the rapid growth of prediction markets has allowed users to gamble on just about anything. In many cases, these contracts are offered in direct contravention of state and tribal law. They create rampant opportunities for insider trading. Too often, they are offered with no regard for national security or even basic morality. The rapid growth of these prediction markets has been fueled by billions of dollars in sports betting, illegally offered on prediction market platforms in all 50 states and on tribal lands. These markets are operating in a wild west, desperately in need of regulation and guardrails.

During his confirmation hearing, I asked Chairman Selig a simple question of whether a prediction contract on who wins or loses a football game is sports betting. He told me that he would be a blank slate on whether prediction markets were gambling and that he would defer to the courts. In fact, I can’t tell you how many times he told me exactly that, “Mr. Senator,” he said. “It would be irresponsible for me to prejudge that issue. I will look to the courts.” In answer to another question, “Senator, I, again, would look to the courts on these questions of facts and interpretation of the law. It’s a complex issue. I will follow what the courts say.” And again, “Senator, on this issue, I would look to the courts. So, I would look to what the courts say about the issue.” And I asked him if I’m betting on a Bills game, or what would you say about that? “Well, there are many lengthy opinions have been written on one word in statute, and I want the benefit of understanding what the judges think about the issue,” and again, “I think it would be irresponsible for me to prejudge that issue.” And so, I would come to the issue, into the issue at the commission, have confirmed with a blank slate, and look to the courts, because I asked him whether he had a preconceived idea, whether he was a tabula rasa, he said he was a blank slate. Well, I don’t know whether he was just lying to us, or once he was confirmed, he had some kind of an epiphany. But he has been anything but a blank slate. He has not looked to the courts. He’s filed briefs to tell the courts what to do, and when the courts have ruled in a way that doesn’t favor the prediction markets, he has basically told companies to ignore the courts, ignore court orders, don’t geofence, don’t respect state or tribal laws. Anything but a blank slate. I don’t know that I’ve ever been so blatantly deceived by a nominee before. This is certainly not the kind of leadership that we need at CFTC. So, Mr. Anonick, let me ask you really the same question I asked him: If I bet using a prediction market on who will win this Thursday’s NFL game between the Colts and the Texans, is that a sports bet?

Nathan Anonick: Senator, thank you for that question, and I can only speak for myself, not anyone else. I do think that question, from a legal perspective, is complex, and that federal courts have disagreed on that.

Schiff: Okay, but is it really complex? I mean, if we’re betting on who wins a football game on Thursday night, it kind of sounds like a sports bet, right?

Anonick: I certainly appreciate the practical argument. I just say it’s legally complex.

Schiff: If betting on who wins a football game is not a sports bet, can you tell me what a sports bet is?

Anonick: I agree, Senator, that the fact that there’s been different federal courts’ opinions makes that question confusing. But it is an issue that the federal courts have disagreed with. Again, I can only speak for myself, Senator.

Schiff: Well, let me ask you: Are you a tabula rasa? Are you a blank slate? Are you going to defer to the courts, or are you going to act like our current Chairman and tell the courts what to do?

Anonick: Senator, if confirmed, the Supreme Court reaches a decision on this. I would fully support that the CFTC needs to follow that decision, regardless of the decision.

Schiff: And are you going to take a position in that litigation and tell the Supreme Court that you think that states and Tribes should not have a say; that companies should ignore court orders if they don’t defer to the CFTC and its jurisdiction. Is that the position you’re going to take, the same as the Chair?

Anonick: Senator, I’m not trying to be evasive. I don’t know a position I would take on anything. If I was confirmed and there was a matter before me, and I would take the role as Commissioner seriously. I think that means a robust, thorough fact-finding process. That means talking to Office of General Counsel. That means talking to outside counsel, that means talking to the Tribes and the states and all of the stakeholders. And anything before me would be my own decision, and I would own that. But out of respect for the seriousness that I think being a commissioner requires, and going through that robust process, I don’t have a preconceived position because it would be irresponsible of me to make that position until I’ve gone through that process.

Schiff: I just hope that I don’t have another confirmation hearing for another proposed nominee and have to read your testimony back. I hope you’ll be true to what you’ve just said, and approach this with an open mind, and hear the stakeholders, including the states and the Tribes, and their perspective before you make a judgment.

I thank you, Mr. Chairman. I yield back.

title: Schmitt Celebrates Committee Passage of His COLLUDE Act
text:
Schmitt Continues Fight to Protect Americans’ First Amendment Rights from Big Tech Censorship

U.S. SENATE — Today, U.S. Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) celebrated the passage of his bill, the COLLUDE Act, out of the Senate Commerce Committee. The bill gives the American people the ability to sue Big Tech companies if the companies infringe on their First Amendment rights by censoring their online speech at the behest of the federal government. Thislegislation marks the latest step in Senator Schmitt’s ongoing fight to protect free speech and combat Big Tech censorship. As Missouri’s Attorney General, Senator Schmitt led the charge against government collusion with social media companies to censor Americans by filing Missouri v. Biden.

Download Senator Schmitt’s remarks HERE.

“America’s Founders understood the principle on which self-government depends: a free people must be able to criticize those in power. They wrote the First Amendment into our Constitution to protect the freedom of speech from government suppression. My COLLUDE Act gives ordinary Americans a direct way to fight back against social media platforms censoring them at the behest of the federal government,” said Senator Schmitt.

Background:

In 2022, Senator Schmitt filed Missouri v. Biden to expose federal officials’ role in suppressing Americans’ speech online. Earlier this year, the landmark case was settled, marking a massive win for Americans’ First Amendment rights.

As amended, the COLLUDE Act prohibits social media platforms from censoring, restricting, or altering expression protected by the First Amendment in response to a federal agency, officer, or employee taking or threatening to take adverse action against the platform to induce such censorship, restriction, or alteration.

As amended, the COLLUDE Act provides a private right of action for Americans whose expression was censored, altered, or restricted to sue the social media platform for statutory damages, punitive damages, compensatory damages, and reasonable litigation costs, as well as injunctive relief.

As amended, the COLLUDE Act prevents defendant social media platforms from asserting Section 230 immunity as a defense to lawsuits brought under the COLLUDE Act.

Building on Senator Schmitt’s litigation strategy in Missouri v. Biden, the COLLUDE Act provides plaintiffs with a motion for pre-motion to dismiss discovery for up to 30 days and a possible additional 30-day extension for good cause.

title: Shaheen Highlights Outdoor Recreation's $1.3 Trillion Economic Contribution Following Release of Annual Impact Report
text:
**The economic impact report is a result of a bipartisan Shaheen-led bill that was signed into law in 2016**

(Washington, DC) – Today, U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) applauded the release of an annual report by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) showing the continued significant role of outdoor recreation in bolstering New Hampshire and the entire country’s economy. According to the report, the outdoor recreation sector contributed $1.3 trillion to the U.S. economy in 2025, including adding $4.3 billion to New Hampshire’s economy. In New Hampshire, outdoor recreation accounted for 3.4% of the state’s GDP and supported 34,017 jobs. The industry has experienced significant long-term growth, with economic contribution increasing by about $1 billion since 2022. The Outdoor Recreation Satellite Account estimate, provided by the BEA through the U.S. Department of Commerce, is a result of Shaheen’s bipartisan Outdoor Recreation Jobs and Economic Impact Act that was signed into law in 2016.

“From hiking in our mountains to kayaking on the lakes, New Hampshire’s outdoor spaces play a vital role in supporting local economies, small businesses and communities across our state,” said Senator Shaheen. “Today’s report shows that outdoor recreation continues to be a major economic driver for New Hampshire, supporting thousands of good-paying jobs and contributing billions of dollars to our state’s economy. I’m proud to have led the legislation that makes this annual report possible and to have championed investments throughout my career that will protect our treasured outdoor spaces for generations to come.”

Before 2017, the federal government did not formally track the economic contributions of outdoor recreation, relying instead on independent analyses, including reports from the Outdoor Industry Association (OIA). Shaheen's Outdoor Recreation Jobs and Economic Impact Act established federal reporting on the industry's economic impact, providing policymakers and business leaders with valuable information on job creation and consumer spending associated with outdoor recreation. The legislation also directs the Department of Commerce to provide Congress with a comprehensive assessment of the industry's contributions to the national economy.

Senator Shaheen has consistently worked to strengthen New Hampshire's outdoor recreation economy and preserve access to the state's natural resources. As part of the Fiscal Year 2026 Interior, Environment and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, Shaheen helped secure Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF) funding to support parks, forests and outdoor recreation projects across New Hampshire. In 2025, Shaheen introduced the bipartisan Snow Survey Northeast Expansion Act to improve snowpack monitoring and provide critical information to communities and small businesses that depend on winter recreation. She also supported the bipartisan Ski Hill Resources for Economic Development (SHRED) Act to increase investments in outdoor recreation infrastructure in mountain communities. In 2020, Shaheen helped pass the Great American Outdoors Act, which permanently provided full funding for the LWCF and dedicated funding to address deferred maintenance on public lands. Shaheen also joined her colleagues in introducing the bipartisan America the Beautiful Act to further address deferred maintenance needs across national parks, forests, and other public lands.

title: Thune Delivers Farewell Remarks for Senator Husted
text:
Click here to watch the video.

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) today delivered the following remarks on the Senate floor:

Thune’s remarks below (as delivered):

“Mr. President, later this morning Ohio Senator Jon Husted will make his farewell speech here on the floor.

“He was appointed to the Senate just two years ago, so his tenure has been short.

“But his impact has been substantial.

“As a lifelong public servant – state representative, speaker of the state House, state senator, secretary of state for Ohio, and lieutenant governor for Ohio – there was never any question that Jon Husted was going to do anything but hit the ground running here in the Senate.

“And he did.

“A longtime advocate for, as he says, making it ‘easy to vote and hard to cheat,’ Jon was a leading voice in the Senate for commonsense voter ID requirements during the SAVE Act debate.

“And the permitting legislation that we will hopefully pass this week – the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act – builds on the work of his Ratepayer Protection Act.

“Mr. President, it’s been a true pleasure to serve with Jon.

“He’s someone who through faith and hard work found a real calling to public service, and who cares very deeply about our country and the men and women that he represents.

“I’m profoundly sorry to see him depart the Senate.

“But I’m excited to see what way he serves next.

“And in the meantime, I hope he gets some well-deserved rest and some time to spend with his wife Tina and the rest of his family.”

title: Thune Joins America Reports on Fox News
text:
Click here to watch.

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) today joined America Reports on Fox News:

On government funding:

“We have to fund the government and that discussion will get underway. The continuing resolution that funds the government expires on December the 11th … the Democrats aren’t engaging with us yet. In fact, they’re not talking at all.”

…

“[Democrats have] shut the government down twice on our watch already … One of them was the longest total government shutdown in history. The other one was 75 days, and that was shutting down ICE and CBP, which we had to use extraordinary measures to get those agencies funded through the end of President Trump’s term.

“We’re prepared to do whatever it takes to ensure that the government is funded and, most importantly, that our national security imperatives are met, and that we’ve got sufficient funding in place for defense. Now, the Democrats, if they want to shut the government down for yet a third time, obviously, that’s their prerogative. But I think that backfires on them … I don’t think that anybody in this country wants to see the government shut down because the Democrats don’t want to fund the military.

“I think most people recognize that national security is the number one priority of any government. And I’ve always said, if you don’t get national security right, the rest is conversation. So we’re going to be pushing hard to ensure that the government is funded, and we will see if the Democrats want to play ball or not. But if they don’t, they’re going to own it.”

On the historic nominations pace:

“We’re going to get as many of these [nominations] done as we can and then a big bloc of about 120 executive branch nominations that we we’ll move en bloc before the end of the year as well … We’ll be very, very busy from now until the time that the Democrats take power in January.”

On confirming judges:

“You want to make the most of every day that we have available to us until January, when the Democrats take control of the Senate. So that means getting through a lot of the judges that are stacked up … As soon as the administration nominates them, we’re getting them ready for floor consideration. And we’ve been able to do that at a much faster rate, about three times faster, than during the first Trump administration. But we have a total of 23 – four circuits and nineteen district – judges that we need to get confirmed by the Senate. That’s, under the Constitution, a responsibility the Senate has and those are lifetime appointments. So that’s our highest priority.”

On air traffic control modernization:

“We had Secretary Duffy up here yesterday and talked to … Republican senators … There was a big chunk of money, $12.5 billion … in the Working Families Tax Cuts legislation that we allocated to Air Traffic Control to do some of the modernization and the upgrades and things that they were talking about. So, the question Republican senators had is, ‘Okay, how has that money been used? … You’re asking for this now big additional block of money. How is that going to be used?’ And I think that those are fair questions to ask. We’ll see where that lands.

“That ought to be a bipartisan priority. That ought to be something you can do through the normal appropriations process. But we continue to have that discussion.”

title: Thune: Senate Republicans Continue Building on Strong Record of Judicial Confirmations
text:
Click here to watch the video.

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) today delivered the following remarks on the Senate floor:

Thune’s remarks below (as delivered):

“Mr. President, yesterday the Senate confirmed its 59th Article III judge of this Congress.

“We have floor votes locked in for four more.

“And we continue to move forward on a robust year-end package to confirm around a hundred more of the president’s nominees.

“Mr. President, confirming lower-level presidential nominees would once not have warranted much in the way of floor remarks.

“And that’s because expeditiously confirming presidential nominees used to be a standard practice.

“Whether you’d voted for a president or not, the assumption was that presidents should be able to staff their administrations.

“And so no one was lining up scores of nominees for time-consuming floor votes.

“Most nominees were confirmed by voice vote or unanimous consent – a way of expediting their consideration here on the Senate floor.

“All of that changed, however, during President Trump’s first administration.

“Democrats introduced an unprecedented level of partisanship into the confirmation process, dragging out nominations that would once have been speedily approved by voice vote or unanimous consent.

“President Obama had had 90 percent of his nominations confirmed by voice vote or unanimous consent.

“President Trump in his first term had 65 percent.

“But at least a decent number were still going by voice vote.

“Now fast forward to the current Trump administration.

“Beginning immediately after President Trump’s election, Democrats introduced a no-holds-barred level of partisanship on nominations.

“For the first year and a half of his administration, Democrats dragged out the process on every single one of his nominees.

“And that applied not just to nominees they voted against, but to nominees they eventually ended up voting for!

“As of today, President Trump has 2.5 percent – 2.5 percent – of his nominees confirmed by voice vote.

“2.5 percent, Mr. President.

“Or a tiny, tiny, tiny fraction of the rates enjoyed by Presidents Obama and Biden.

“And so what would once have been taken for granted – the swift confirmation of a majority of a president’s nominees – has become something of note, thanks to Democrats’ unprecedented level of partisanship and obstruction.

“Mr. President, I’m proud of the work we’ve done, in the face of historic opposition, to ensure the president gets his team in place.

“We’ve spent many, many, many hours in session this Congress – nearly twice the time in session spent by the House of Representatives – and we’ve taken a lot of votes.

“We also implemented reforms to restore the Senate’s tradition of en bloc confirmations of largely uncontroversial nominees.

“And thanks to those reforms, both Democrat and Republican presidents will see some protection against Democrat-type partisanship in the future.

“Mr. President, Senate confirmation of nominees is important.

“There is no substitute for Senate confirmation, especially when it comes to judges.

“We’ve given the president the assurance of individuals who can serve throughout his administration – or, in the cases of the judges, for life.

“Mr. President, unfortunately I am very much afraid that the president will have a hard time getting any nominees through in the next Congress – not because of any deficiency in the nominees, but because Democrats would stand in the way of George Washington himself if President Trump nominated him to serve in his administration.

“And it is that which lends a particular urgency to confirmations here in the lame-duck session.

“Presidents should be able to get their teams in place.

“And the American people deserve – deserve, Mr. President – to have fully staffed administrations.

“And so for the remainder of this Congress Senate Republicans will double down on what we’ve been doing this entire Congress, and that is putting in the work to get as many nominees confirmed as possible.”

title: Tuberville, Banks Introduce Legislative Package to Dismantle DOE
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator Tommy Tuberville (R-AL) joined U.S. Senator Jim Banks (R-IN) in introducing the Less Bureaucracy, Better Education legislative package, a set of 10 bills that would codify President Trump’s work to dismantle the federal education bureaucracy and ensure students, families, and taxpayers come first. Fox Digital first reported the introduction.

In March of 2025, President Trump signed an executive order directing the Secretary of Education to take all lawful steps to facilitate the closure of the Department of Education, return authority over education to states and local communities, and maintain the delivery of services, programs, and benefits on which Americans rely. The Department has since entered into interagency agreements to co-administer federal education functions to agencies better equipped to administer them. These 10 bills would codify those agreements and make the administration’s reforms permanent.

“Our schools are supposed to be preparing the next generation of Americans for life­—not pushing some woke ideology,” said Sen. Tuberville. “I’m proud to introduce this bill with Sen. Banks to codify one of President Trump’s biggest promises—dismantling the DOE. Let’s put our students first and get it done.”

“The federal education bureaucracy has failed students and families for decades,” said Sen. Banks. “President Trump and Secretary McMahon are finally putting parents first and returning power where it belongs. Our bills will make their reforms permanent, eliminate layers of Washington bureaucracy, and ensure taxpayers are no longer forced to prop up a failed department.”

“For too long, an overgrown Washington bureaucracy has funneled trillions of taxpayer dollars into top-down mandates and administrative red tape,” said U.S. Secretary of Education McMahon. “Exactly one year after we announced six critical partnerships to begin reversing that trend, Senator Banks, Tuberville, Moody and Lee are introducing ‘Less Bureaucracy, Better Education’ package to permanently codify the Trump Administration’s historic reforms. This vital legislation will make permanent the work we have done to align programs with the agencies best suited to support and return education authority to those closest to the child. I commend their leadership in launching this important effort, and I look forward to working together to improve education for our students and families.”

U.S. Sens. Tuberville and Banks were joined by U.S. Sens. Mike Lee (R-UT) and Ashley Moody (R-FL) in introducing the package. Tim Walberg (R-MI-08) led the effort in the House of Representatives.

BACKGROUND:

Sen. Tuberville is sponsoring two bills as a part of the Less Bureaucracy, Better Education legislative package.

Less Bureaucracy, Better K-12 Education Act:

Transfers most functions of the Office of Elementary and Secondary Education, including Title I, charter schools, rural education, impact aid, and education for homeless children and youth to the Department of Labor.

Less Bureaucracy, Better Higher Education:

Transfers numerous postsecondary education programs, including TRIO, GEAR UP, HBCU and other minority-serving institution programs, veteran student support, and disability-related higher education programs, to the Department of Labor.

Senator Tommy Tuberville represents Alabama in the United States Senate and is a member of the Senate Armed Services, Agriculture, Veterans’ Affairs, HELP and Aging Committees.

title: Warnock Questions Trump CFTC Nominees on Commitment to Fighting President’s Corruption
text:
On Tuesday, during a Senate Agriculture Committee hearing, Senator Reverend Warnock questioned President Trump’s nominees to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on their commitment to protecting the agency from conflicts of interest and political interference by the Trump administration

Recent reporting details how political appointees at the CFTC have used the agency to benefit companies with close financial ties to President Trump and his family

In fiscal year 2025, the CFTC took just 13 enforcement actions, down from 58 in 2024 and 96 in 2023

The CFTC is responsible for overseeing U.S. derivatives markets and protecting against fraud, manipulation, and other market abuses

Senator Reverend Warnock: “I am deeply concerned about President Trump’s unceasing efforts to enrich himself at the expense of the American people. Under its current chair, the CFTC has repeatedly sued states to block regulation of companies that the president’s own son invested in and advised”

Washington, D.C. – On Tuesday, during a Senate Agriculture Committee hearing, U.S. Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) questioned President Trump’s nominees to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), Nathan Anonick and Matthew Roland, on their commitment to protecting the agency from conflicts of interest and political interference by the Trump administration. Recent reporting has raised questions about how political appointees at the CFTC have used the agency to benefit companies with close financial ties to President Trump and his family. In May, the New York Times reported several instances in which career employees were sidelined, disciplined, or fired for questioning the activities of cryptocurrency and prediction market firms with ties to President Donald Trump and his son Donald Trump, Jr.

Political pressure from the administration also appears to have halted an investigation into nearly $600 million of suspicious oil futures trades mere minutes before President Trump announced a pause of attacks on Iranian infrastructure in March of this year. The CFTC is responsible for overseeing U.S. derivatives markets and protecting against fraud, manipulation, and other market abuses.

“I am deeply concerned about President Trump’s unceasing efforts to enrich himself at the expense of the American people,” said Senator Reverend Warnock. “Under its current chair, the CFTC has repeatedly sued states to block regulation of companies that the president’s own son invested in and advised. The CFTC’s political leadership has stopped senior career officials from looking into firms that has business dealings with the Trump family…Mr. Anonick, do you think it is appropriate for political leadership at the CFTC to discipline or cire career staff or question a company because it is closely tied to the President?”

In May, Senator Warnock and several of his Senate Agriculture Committee colleagues sent a letter to the CFTC calling for the agency to provide a public update and report to Congress regarding a series of suspicious trades in the oil futures market. Public reporting at the time revealed at least three instances in which traders have timed the oil markets curiously well since the start of President Trump’s War in Iran. The trades on oil futures have raised concerns that material nonpublic information is being used to facilitate trades and game the system.

Senator Warnock has consistently pushed for greater transparency and accountability across the federal government, including stronger oversight of the Trump administration. Earlier this year, he launched in inquiry into reports of political interference at the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and urged the White House to preserve bipartisan leadership at federal financial regulatory agencies. Senator Warnock continues to push for meaningful oversight to ensure federal agencies serve the interests of the American people, not the political interests of those in power.

Watch the Senator’s full exchange HERE

See a transcript of the exchange between Senator Warnock and the CFTC nominees below:

Senator Reverend Warnock (SRW): “Thank you, Chair Boozman.”

“Congratulations to both of you on your nominations, and we welcome your families here today. I’m sure they’re very, very proud.”

“Congress created the CFTC with a five-member bipartisan commission to help ensure stability and balance. But under the Trump administration, the CFTC has suffered from instability, including massive attrition of its career staff, and for over a year it has been led by a single Republican commissioner. I’m glad that President Trump finally found the time to nominate additional commissioners, but we are not there yet. I want to ask each of you: Do you agree that a full CFTC commission with a diverse membership, including at least two members of each party, is essential to the agency’s effectiveness? Mr. Anonick—yes or no? Just yes or no?”

CFTC Nominee Nathan Anonick (NA): “Yes, sir.”

SRW: “Mr. Roland?”

CFTC Nominee Matthew Roland (MR): “Yes, Senator.”

SRW: “Will you join me in emphasizing—thank you so much for those answers—will you join me in emphasizing to the White House that the president must nominate additional members of both parties to the CFTC, Mr. Anonick?”

NA: “Senator, I would certainly share my view that I think a full commission is the best—I’ll share my view with anybody who asks—that I think a full commission is the best approach to sound, durable policy.”

SRW: “I appreciate that.”

MR: “Yes, Senator, I will. And I just want to add that I am hopefully that if confirmed, Mr. Anonick and I can demonstrate through our service the benefits of a bipartisan commission.”

SRW: “Very good.”

“I’m also deeply concerned about President Trump’s unceasing efforts to enrich himself at the expense of the American people. Under its current chair, the CFTC has repeatedly sued states to block regulation of companies that the president’s own son invested in and advised. The CFTC’s political leadership has stopped senior career officials from looking into firms that had business dealings with the Trump family. In one case, two career officials tried to look into the anti-fraud controls of a company that Donald Trump Jr. invested in. In response, the CFTC’s political leadership placed one career official under investigation, investigating the investigator, and showed the other the door.”

“Mr. Anonick, do you think it is appropriate for political leadership at the CFTC to discipline or fire career staff or questioning a company because it is closely tied to the president?”

NA: “Senator—thank you for that. I’ve seen the articles. I don’t know more information beyond that, but if confirmed, I would look to learn more information and certainly—”

SRW: “Well, answer generally. Do you think it’s appropriate for the CFTC to discipline or fire career staff for questioning a company because it is closely tied to the president? Theoretically, even if you don’t want to opine on this particular case, in principle is what I’m asking you?”

NA: “Senator, in principle, I think the commission should follow all employment laws, and any decision shouldn’t be made off anything other than what the law says on that.”

SRW: “I want to ask you both: should a company’s ties with the president or his family ever affect how the CFTC treats it, Mr. Rowland?

MR: “Thank you, Senator. I think that the law needs to be enforced fairly without fear or favor, and so the answer is no.”

SRW: “The answer is no. Would you agree with that, Mr. Anonick?”

NA: “Senator, I’d agree that I think the law should apply equally and fairly to everyone. It should not matter who is involved.”

SRW: “Yeah. Does it give you heartburn if you have a sense that people are concerned about investigating because a company is tied to the president’s family? Would that give you heartburn? Would that raise concerns for you?”

NA: “Senator, if I thought the law wasn’t being applied equally and fairly to everyone, regardless of the situation, it would give me concern.”

SRW: “Last month, just minutes before President Trump announced a pause on infrastructure attacks in his war with Iran, commodity traders bet nearly $600 million that the price of oil futures would drop, those traders made millions off of what looks a lot like inside information about what the president would do. My colleagues and I sent the CFTC a letter urging the agency to open an investigation and asking for any update on its findings in May. We never got a response. Last month, Bloomberg reported that the CFTC had opened an investigation, but that a political appointee in the agency had ordered career staff to “retract it”. My colleagues and I wrote the CFTC another letter, and we haven’t heard back on that one either.”

“Mr. Anonick, do you agree that political appointees should not interfere with ongoing investigations by career CFTC staff?”

NA: “Senator—again, I know the article. I don’t know any more information. It is something that, if confirmed—”

SRW: “Do you agree that they shouldn’t interfere?”

NA: “Broadly speaking, yes, Senator.”

SRW: “If confirmed, would you commit to investigating this matter and sending me a response within 30 days?”

NA: “If confirmed, Senator, I commit to you that I will look into this and send you responses as quickly as humanly possible.”

SRW: “Okay, I know I’m running out of time, Mr. Chair. Very quickly, if you would indulge me, Mr. Anonick—more broadly, do you agree with the decision to cut the CFTC’s enforcement actions by nearly 80% during the first year of the Trump administration?”

NA: “Senator, I would want to have access to all the information before I could give you a conclusive statement. But as a general principle, I think it’s very important that the CFTC police markets for violation of the law, and that is something, if confirmed, that I would stress.”

SRW: “I agree that it’s critical, and the CFTC has a difficult job maintaining the integrity of our nation’s derivative markets. But from personal corruption to political interference, the Trump administration has undermined the CFTC’s integrity at every turn. And if confirmed, you must do everything you can to restore it.”

“Thank you so very much for your service, and welcome again to your families.”

title: Senators Wicker and Luján Introduce Legislation to Block Exploitative Bots & Protect Intellectual Property
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Roger Wicker, R-Miss., and Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., today introduced the Stealth Bot Prohibition Act to confront the illegal and deceptive use of internet bots that threaten Americans’ intellectual property.

In light of the rise of artificial intelligence (AI), automated web crawlers are now roaming across the internet. While many have legitimate uses, bad actors have exploited the technology to wreak havoc on online producers, including local newspapers and journalists. Many of these advanced bots evade paywalls, scrape information, and overwhelm websites. “Stealth bots” are a particular class of disguised web crawlers that America’s adversaries deploy to steal protected online content and use it to train their own AI models.

The Stealth Bot Prohibition Act would enact transparency standards to combat these unauthorized practices. If passed, this legislation would provide a new tool for publishers to combat deceptive operators by requiring the disclosure of identities and purposes of bots when accessing websites without banning legitimate research and other beneficial automated material.

The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) would be in charge of the enforcement of the bill’s provisions and would empower state attorneys general to take legal action to protect residents from violators.

“The Chinese Communist Party is notorious for stealing Americans’ intellectual property by any means possible. Now, it is weaponizing artificial intelligence and deploying droves of malicious bots against online publishers,” said Senator Wicker. “Our legislation recognizes these threats and offers a solution to insulate digital producers from bad actors.”

“AI is advancing rapidly, creating new challenges and threats for the American people. Congress must act immediately to ensure transparency and accountability for those who misuse this technology,” said Senator Luján. “That’s why I’m joining my colleagues in introducing the Stealth Bot Prohibition Act to crack down on bad actors and protect creatives, small businesses, and local news. No one should profit by stealing others’ hard work, ideas, or livelihoods.”

“News publishers of all sizes are drowning in bot traffic, hurting their ability to provide high-quality content to the American public. The Stealth Bot Prohibition Act is a common-sense, bipartisan solution to the problem of bad bots. It offers straightforward transparency requirements and enforcement mechanisms that uncover bad actors while leaving responsible uses of bots unaffected. The News/Media Alliance thanks Senators Wicker and Luján for their leadership on this issue, and their commitment to protecting American content creators, websites, and consumers, from a flood of bad bots. We look forward to working with them and their colleagues in Congress to pass this critical piece of legislation and offer American businesses and the American people the relief they deserve,” said Danielle Coffey, President and CEO of the News/Media Alliance.

“As AI bots continue to pose an increasing threat across the creative landscape, the Stealth Bot Prohibition Act will be a critical tool in ensuring that the constitutional copyright protections of creators can continue to be upheld and respected, especially across online platforms. AAP thanks Senators Roger Wicker and Ben Ray Lujan and Representatives Laurel Lee, Valerie Foushee, and Gus Bilirakis for introducing this important legislation to help defend the integrity of human innovation,” said Maria A. Pallante, President and CEO, Association of American Publishers (AAP).

To read the full text of the bill, click here.

title: Wyden, Markey, Lujan Question Tech Companies Over Proliferation of ‘Nudify’ Apps, in App Stores, Digital Ads
text:
Senators Write Meta, Google and Apple Following Reports That Nonconsensual Image Generating Apps Are Evading Bans by App Stores and Meta Ads

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden, D-Ore., Edward J. Markey, D-Mass., and Ben Ray Lujan, D-N.M., today questioned Big Tech companies over the widespread availability of so-called ‘nudify’ apps in app stores, nearly a year after the senators raised concerns about X and Grok remaining available despite enabling mass-generation of nonconsensual sexual images of women and children.

Although Apple and Google ban nudify apps in their terms of service, researchers recently revealed that apps marketed on Meta ads as nonconsensual sexual image generators are widely available in app stores, and generated over $100 million in revenue. One common tactic is for apps to be updated after passing review to add nudification tools.

“These findings raise questions not only about individual failures of app review, but also about [Google and Apple’s] ability to identify repeat offenders, disrupt coordinated networks, and monitor apps after approval,” the senators wrote.

The senators also questioned Meta over its continued role in advertising apps marketed as generating nonconsensual intimate images of women and children.

“Despite Meta’s stated prohibition on these ads, independent investigations have documented extensive ad campaigns on Facebook and Instagram directing customers to apps capable of digitally undressing people in photographs or placing their likeness into sexually explicit content without their consent,” the senators wrote.

AI tools have supercharged the spread of nonconsensual sexual imagery online, creating real harm to women and children in particular. A 2024 survey by the Center for Democracy & Technology found that 15% of U.S. public high school students knew of AI-generated nonconsensual intimate imagery (NCII) depicting someone at their school. A separate 2025 Thorn survey found that 6% of young people reported having been targeted by AI-generated NCII.

NCII is frequently weaponized against female journalists, human rights defenders, politicians, and other prominent women - not simply to humiliate them, but to discredit, intimidate, and silence their work and advocacy. Research by the American Sunlight Project revealed that one in six female Members of Congress were targeted by sexually explicit deepfakes and a 2025 New America investigation documented 100 cases involving public officials across 14 countries, 97 of them involving women.
