title: Young Introduces Northern District of Indiana Judicial Nominee Joe Falvey
text:
**Click here or above to watch Senator Young’s introduction**

WASHINGTON – Today, Senator Todd Young (R-Ind.) introduced Joe Falvey, President Trump’s nominee to serve as U.S. District Judge for the Northern District of Indiana, at a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing.

During his remarks, Young highlighted Falvey’s distinguished record of military and public service and expressed his strong support for the nomination.

Senator Young’s full remarks, as prepared for delivery:

Thank you Chairman Cruz, Ranking Member Durbin, and members of the committee.

It is an honor to introduce Joe Falvey – a fellow Hoosier and Marine – as the nominee to serve as a district judge in the Northern District of Indiana.

Joe embodies the Marine Corps mantra “honor – courage – and commitment.”

Joe has dedicated his entire life in service to our great nation.

If confirmed – the Northern District of Indiana will gain a judge that exhibits integrity – collegiality – and an unparalleled work ethic.

Joe hails from South Bend, Indiana, home of course of the Fighting Irish.

Joe graduated magna cum laude from Notre Dame, where he participated in the ROTC Program.

The Falvey family has a long history of military service, and Joe proudly followed in their footsteps.

He received his commission as a Marine Corps officer in 2009 where he pursed the hardest path and became an infantry officer.

Joe went on to serve with distinction in two of the fiercest combat zones of our lifetimes – Marjah and Sangin in the dreaded Helmand Province of Afghanistan.

Joe saw significant combat and was awarded the Navy and Marine Corps Achievement medal with “valor device” for his heroism under fire.

In one incident, his unit became pinned down under heavy Taliban machine gun fire.

Joe left the safety of their defense and ran under fire to their mortar position.

He personally readjusted their mortar fire onto the enemy, and forced the Taliban attackers to retreat.

I always have a special level of respect for our judicial nominees who served in uniform, but it is extremely rare to see one with a combat record like this.

After his tour on active duty, Joe graduated from Yale Law School, where he was a notes editor on the Yale Law Journal.

Along with law review, Joe served as President of the Catholic Law School Association and Vice President of Yale Law’s Federalist Society chapter.

It remains unclear to me when he slept.

Following law school, Joe clerked for three renowned jurists here in DC:

Dabney Friedrich on the district court, Thomas Griffith on the DC circuit, and Chief Justice John Roberts.

Joe has a distinguished record of service in both the civil and criminal realms.

In four years at Jones Day, Joe helped litigate some of our judiciary’s most complex civil matters.

But, his commitment to public service called him back home to South Bend, where he joined the Northern District as a federal prosecutor.

After less than two years as a line prosecutor, he was elevated to Acting Chief of the Criminal Division for the Northern District – a true testament to his competence, work ethic, and dedication to justice.

In February of this year, he was made Chief of the Appellate Division.

Those who have worked with him repeatedly extol his brilliance, his work ethic, and his collegiality.

I have had the pleasure to get to know Joe through this process.

The thing that stands out about Joe is that despite his sterling credentials and achievements, he is as humble and down-to-earth as can be.

Joe’s humility and thoughtfulness will serve him well on the bench.

And if anyone has any questions about his dedication to the Constitution, Joe demonstrated he was willing to risk his life defending it on the battlefield.

Joe, you make me proud to be a Hoosier.

Joe’s proudest achievement, though, is marrying Catherine, who is with us here today.

Catherine was also a Marine Officer and like myself, an intelligence officer.

To use Marine Corps terminology for a second, Joe and Catherine have two fireteams of children – that is, eight children.

Catherine, thank you for being here and for your support and partnership with Joe over the years.

I also want to recognize Joe’s father, Judge Joseph Falvey Jr., who is here with us today and serves on the U.S. Court of Appeals for Veterans Claims.

Thank you for your own service to our nation.

I’m grateful to President Trump for making this exceptional nomination and to this committee for your consideration.

I am confident you will walk away just as impressed by Joe as I am.

Thank you.

title: Young: Stop Insider Trading Act Must Pass Before Year’s End
text:
**Click here or above to watch Senator Young’s floor speech**

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Todd Young (R-Ind.) spoke on the Senate floor and called on the Senate to pass the Stop Insider Trading Act before year’s end. This legislation would prohibit members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from purchasing individual publicly traded stocks.

In his remarks, Young said the midterm elections made it clear that the American people want Congress to focus on eliminating corruption.

“Roughly 200 members of Congress own shares in publicly traded companies,” said Senator Young. “They sit on committees that craft policy for and conduct oversight on the very industries in which they invest. Most are good, ethical people. They came to Washington for the right reasons. But representative government runs on public confidence. Even the slightest opportunity for lawmakers to profit from their office, or the perception that the system allows it, erodes that trust and alienates the public.”

To watch Young’s full speech, click here.

Excerpts from Senator Young’s remarks are below:

… The midterm elections made it perfectly clear:

When it comes to potential self-enrichment, Americans, regardless of their party, have little faith in government officials abiding by an honor system.

A broad majority of voters from both parties voted against perceived government corruption earlier this month.

According to one poll 90 percent of Americans said that corruption was a motivating factor for how they cast their ballot.

If there is even a perception that officials are double dealing, already declining levels of trust in government will continue to sink.

The project of restoring confidence in Washington is a long-term endeavor, I know.

But there is a small step we can take to begin the work:

Pass the Stop Insider Trading Act.

… Today Congress wields regulatory power over the world’s largest economy.

Lawmakers write and pass bills that significantly impact the market.

We sit on committees of jurisdiction that oversee entire sectors of America’s economy.

We regularly have access to briefings and updates that provide nonpublic market information.

There is little to prohibit members of Congress from using such privileged information to guide their personal selection of stocks.

In fact, in the last two decades, members have made trades conspicuously timed around market-moving events—events shaped by information they had access to or legislation they helped advance.

Roughly 200 members of Congress own shares in publicly traded companies.

They sit on committees that craft policy for and conduct oversight on the very industries in which they invest.

Most are good, ethical people. They came to Washington for the right reasons.

But Representative government runs on public confidence.

Even the slightest opportunity for lawmakers to profit from their office, or the perception that the system allows it, erodes that trust and alienates the public.

… Over two centuries ago, Hamilton, Madison and their founding colleagues recognized that corruption was among the greatest dangers to republican government.

They designed a government that drew a line between personal gain and public office.

And they charged future generations with the task of ensuring that it remained in place.

Let us honor their wisdom, keep their charge, and answer the demands of the voters and pass the Stop Insider Trading Act.

It is important first step we can take to restoring trust in this institution.

title: Rep. Adams Opposes USDA Proposal to Remove 6 Million Americans from Food Assistance
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Alma S. Adams, Ph.D. (NC-12), joined Agriculture Committee Ranking Member Angie Craig and 212 Democrats on a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins opposing a new proposed rule that would kick an estimated 6.3 million Americans – primarily older or disabled beneficiaries and families with children – off the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).

“Hunger is not a political issue. It is a human issue. And this proposed USDA rule does nothing but punish people for being poor,” said Congresswoman Adams. “The Trump administration is threatening food assistance for 6.3 million Americans, including children and seniors who depend on these programs. More than 1.7 million children could lose automatic access to school meals, tens of thousands could lose free meals altogether, and hardworking families would face even more bureaucratic barriers to receiving the assistance they already qualify for.”

“No child should go hungry, no senior should have to choose between food and medicine, and no family should have to fight through mountains of paperwork just to put food on the table,” the Congresswoman continued. “We should be working to end hunger in America, not making it harder for Americans to eat. I urge my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to stand up for our most vulnerable neighbors and reject this harmful rule.”

5.5 million Americans have already been kicked off SNAP, including nearly 2 million children, since President Trump’s Big Ugly Bill passed last July. According to the trump administration’s own regulatory impact analysis, the proposed rule will cause 3.2 million households will lose their SNAP benefits entirely.

title: Smith, Colleagues Introduce Bill to Build a Stronger Financial Future for Every Child
text:
Today, U.S. Representatives Adrian Smith (R-NE), Blake Moore (R-UT), and Brian Jack (R-GA) introduced the Investing in America’s Children Act to expand access to Trump Accounts and give families more flexibility to build long-term savings for their children.

“Trump Accounts created an unprecedented opportunity for families to invest in their children’s futures starting on day one. This is why we must ensure that every eligible child has the opportunity to benefit. I introduced the Investing in America’s Children Act to expand access for children in foster care, give employers greater flexibility to contribute, and allow families to put unused education savings to work,” said Smith.

“Trump Accounts are revolutionizing economic opportunity for each and every American child. This bill takes important steps to build on the successes of this program by expanding and enhancing eligibilities and contribution limits so even more children can benefit from Trump Accounts. I am honored to be part of this effort and will continue to look for opportunities to ensure these accounts reach their full potential,”said Moore.

BACKGROUND:

Smith’s Investing in America’s Children Act would make several improvements to Trump Accounts to ensure that more children can benefit from these savings opportunities.

Specifically, the bill would:

Guarantee access through automatic enrollment: Codify Treasury’s automatic enrollment mechanism so every eligible American child, including those in foster care, can receive an account and begin receiving contributions without unnecessary delays.

Strengthen support for children in foster care: Codify efforts under First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future initiative by allowing states to claim and maintain accounts for eligible foster youth. States could also elect to claim the federal $1,000 seed contribution on behalf of eligible children.

Expand employer contribution flexibility: Apply the $2,500 annual employer contribution limit on a per-child, rather than per-employee, basis, allowing employers to contribute more when employees have multiple children.

Put unused education savings to work: Allow families to roll over unused funds from 529 and Coverdell education savings accounts into Trump Accounts, giving excess education savings another opportunity to grow.

title: Smith in Washington Times: Expanding Choices for America’s Seniors
text:
Today, Congressman Adrian Smith (NE-03), a senior member of the House Ways and Means Subcommittee on Health, penned an op-ed in the Washington Times urging his colleagues in Congress to help put patients back in the driver’s seat of their own healthcare by passing his Bringing Rehabilitation, Integrated Delivery, and Greater Extended (BRIDGE) Care at Home Act.

Click here to read the full op-ed or read an excerpt below:

Just as every American has different needs, priorities and circumstances, so does every patient. What works for someone in an urban community may not be practical for someone living in a rural area like many people across Nebraska’s Third District. The right care setting for one patient may not be the best option for another, which is why our healthcare system must provide the flexibility to meet different needs and circumstances.

As a senior member of the House Ways and Means Subcommittee on Health, I am working to challenge this status quo and put patients back in the driver’s seat of their own healthcare. That means expanding access for patients, empowering providers and ensuring Americans have meaningful choices when deciding how and where they receive care.

Last week, I introduced my bipartisan Bringing Rehabilitation, Integrated Delivery, and Greater Extended (BRIDGE) Care at Home Act to address this need for our seniors.

Consider a senior who just had a hospital stay and needs skilled nursing care as they continue their recovery. They may feel more comfortable continuing their recovery at home, surrounded by family and in a familiar environment. Yet, under current Medicare policy, qualifying skilled nursing care is only covered in a facility without a comparable payment model for delivering those same services at home. That means patients can be left without a choice, even when receiving care at home may better suit their needs and preferences.

When it comes to delivery of care for our seniors and rural patients, we must think outside the box. Too often, Medicare has failed to do so.

My BRIDGE Care at Home Act would establish a five-year Medicare Skilled Nursing Facility-at-Home (SNF-at-Home) pilot program. Similar to how Hospital-at-Home allows patients to receive inpatient-level care at their residence, SNF-at-Home would allow eligible Medicare beneficiaries to receive qualifying skilled nursing services in the comfort of their own homes rather than being limited to a traditional facility-based setting. This would give patients and their families a greater say in how and where they recover while allowing providers to develop care models that better reflect individual needs.

title: Alford Introduces PATHS Act to Support Students in Military Families
text:
Congressman Mark Alford (MO-04) today introduced the Pathways to Academic Triumph for Homefront Students (PATHS) Act. This legislation would direct the Department of War (DoW) to establish a three-year pilot program providing academic support to military-connected K-12 students whose education has been disrupted by military service.

“Missouri is proud to be home to Fort Leonard Wood and Whiteman Air Force Base, and the families who serve there and across the country deserve our full support. This commonsense legislation gives these kids extra academic help when they need it, so a move or a deployment doesn’t mean starting over in the classroom,” said Congressman Alford.

The PATHS Act is supported by Folds of Honor.

"For nearly two decades, Folds of Honor has worked alongside military families to make sure their children's education doesn't become another casualty of service. A child falling behind in school after a parent's deployment, injury, or death is a burden no military family should carry alone. The PATHS Act builds on what's already working. It pairs Department of Defense resources with the experience of organizations that know these families and the providers who serve them. Congressman Alford's PATHS Act tackles that challenge head-on and he has put forward a practical, results-driven approach. It is good for kids, good for families, and good for readiness, and Folds of Honor is honored to stand with him," said Lt. Col. Dan Rooney, Founder and CEO, Folds of Honor.

Read the full text of the legislation here.

Background

Military-connected students often change schools several times before graduation, and existing DoW transition programs don’t consistently offer tutoring, credit recovery, or other hands-on academic help, especially for students in schools that aren’t run by DoW.

The PATHS Act:

Supports students whose schooling has been disrupted by a permanent change of station, a parent's deployment, a parent's serious service-connected injury, illness, or death, or a move to or from a DoW school.

Covers dependents of active-duty servicemembers, activated Guard and Reserve members, and servicemembers or veterans who are recovering from a serious service-connected injury or illness or who died as a result of their service.

Offered services include evidence-based tutoring, academic assessments, transition support, credit recovery, academic case management, and college and career counseling.

title: Following Oversight Visit by Ansari, Grijalva, and Dexter Pregnant Woman Maria Brinez Released from Eloy Detention Center
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Representatives Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), and Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03) announced the release of Maria Alejandra Valero Brinez, a high-risk pregnant woman detained at the Eloy Detention Center, following their October 21 oversight visit alongside Reproductive Freedom for All President Mini Timmaraju.

“I am incredibly relieved that Maria is free. No pregnant woman should have to throw herself on the ground and beg for medical care, fear for her wellbeing and that of her pregnancy, or go without adequate food while in ICE custody,” said Rep. Ansari. “As soon as January, with a Democratic majority, we will use our oversight authority to investigate these abuses, demand answers, and hold this Administration accountable for their profound lack of human dignity.”

“I am grateful that Maria was released and will be able to continue her pregnancy outside the walls of an immigration detention facility,” said Rep. Grijalva. “No pregnant person should have to fight for medical attention or worry about the safety of their baby while in government custody. While Maria’s release is welcome news, it comes after the courts forced ICE’s hand, and it does not undo the harm she has already endured. Pregnant people do not belong in immigration detention.”

“Maria is finally free! Her and her baby’s health and safety were recklessly put at grave risk by the Trump administration, and it should never have taken a court to force ICE to release her” Rep. Dexter said. “As a critical care physician, I’ve cared for countless patients whose lives depended on getting treatment in time, and keeping a high-risk pregnant woman behind bars, unable to get the care she needs, is not just cruel, it is malpractice. Maria’s release does not erase the harm she endured. I will do all I can in the months to come to ensure the imprisonment of innocent pregnant women and children is outlawed.”

“Maria faced unconscionable treatment inside Eloy, and we worked with Reps. Grijalva, Ansari, and Dexter to make sure the country heard what ICE does to pregnant women held in detention centers,” said Reproductive Freedom for All President and CEO Mini Timmaraju. “Today we celebrate her freedom, and we urge the new Congress to act immediately to end ICE’s cruelty and abuses of power.”

Reps. Ansari, Grijalva, Dexter on October 21, for oversight visit of the Eloy Detention Center

BACKGROUND

During the visit, the lawmakers met directly with women detained at Eloy to hear about their experiences accessing reproductive health care, medical treatment, and basic necessities while in immigration detention. The visit focused on concerns about the treatment of pregnant women and the urgent need to protect reproductive health and ensure access to adequate medical care.

Maria, a 24-year-old Venezuelan woman and mother of a 6-year-old son, was approximately five months pregnant at the time of the visit. She had been detained since August and was living in Mesa, Arizona, before her detention. Maria has valid employment authorization through 2029, a pending asylum petition, and no criminal convictions.

During the meeting, Maria described serious concerns about her pregnancy and the lack of adequate medical care. She had experienced spotting and reported having to throw herself on the ground and plead for medical attention. When she was finally able to receive care, doctors informed her that she had a low-lying placenta—the same condition that led to a stillbirth three years earlier.

Despite her high-risk pregnancy, Maria said she had not been provided ultrasound images or adequate information about her and her pregnancy. She feared for their safety and well-being. She also expressed fear about showing emotional distress, given the possibility of being placed in solitary confinement.

Maria also raised concerns about access to drinking water and adequate food. Despite doctors recommending double food portions, she said a guard routinely dismissed the recommendation and provided only a standard portion. She also reported not receiving antibiotics following a dental abscess that resulted in a tooth extraction.

title: Beyer, Jacobs, Maloy Release Outline For Sweeping, Bipartisan AI Safety Legislation
text:
Today U.S. Representatives Don Beyer (D-VA), Sara Jacobs (D-CA), and Celeste Maloy (R-UT) released an outline containing details of the Safe and Accountable Federal Evaluations of Artificial Intelligence (SAFE AI) Act, forthcoming bipartisan legislation that would create federal safety requirements for frontier artificial intelligence.

The broad, ambitious legislation would mandate safety frameworks, incident reporting, and increased transparency from frontier labs with strong government oversight and due process. The outline is available here.

“This outline is a roadmap towards a safer AI future for the country and the world.” said Rep. Don Beyer. “Recent AI incidents and the growing chorus of warnings from experts underscore the urgency of the task before us. It is vitally important that Congress tackle AI safety swiftly, and that we get it right. At this moment we are continuing to seek input on our forthcoming legislative text from experts and safety leaders, in coordination with committees of jurisdiction. We are sharing this blueprint today to show the direction our work is taking and to encourage further constructive feedback and discussion on what we believe should be a priority for Congress. I thank Reps. Jacobs and Maloy for the leadership and partnership on this bill, which I hope will move the ball forward on AI safety so we can usher in an age of responsible AI innovation."

“No industry gets to police itself, and AI shouldn’t be the exception,” said Rep. Sara Jacobs. “Right now, the companies write their own rules while their own models break out of test environments and hack other companies’ systems. Americans are rightly concerned about unchecked AI threatening public safety, critical infrastructure, national security, and the systems we all depend on. That’s why the bipartisan SAFE AI Act puts real guardrails on frontier models, with civil penalties for violations and targeted emergency authority to stop dangerous models when they pose a serious and immediate danger. Our proposal is a floor – not a ceiling, empowering states to adopt stronger protections for their communities. And it is built to adapt as the technology changes, so Americans’ safety never depends on a company’s promise.”

"The companies building the most powerful AI systems ought to be able to show they’ve done their homework before those systems go into wide use,” said Rep. Celeste Maloy. “This bill gives them clear rules, brings in an outside set of eyes to check their work, and leaves room for Utah and other states to set safeguards of their own."

Rep. Don Beyer (D-VA) serves as co-Chair of the Congressional Artificial Intelligence Caucus, and previously served on the bipartisan Task Force On Artificial Intelligence, convened by Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries and Speaker Mike Johnson. He is the author of the AI Foundation Model Transparency Act and a lead cosponsor of the CREATE AI Act, the Federal Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Act, and the Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act. Beyer is currently attending George Mason University as a part time student pursuing a master’s degree in machine learning, to help inform his work on AI in Congress.

title: Reps. Beyer, Whitesides, and Moran Launch First Congressional Caucus Focused on AI Safety and Innovation
text:
Today, Reps. Don Beyer (D-VA), George Whitesides (D-CA), and Nathaniel Moran (R-TX), announced the launch of the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, the first congressional caucus focused specifically on addressing AI safety and security risks posed by increasingly advanced AI systems while ensuring the United States remains a global leader in innovative AI technologies.

As AI capabilities accelerate, so do the potential consequences of catastrophic misuse, loss of control over advanced systems, and threats to national security. In July, an experimental OpenAI agent escaped its testing environment and breached the external platform Hugging Face to cheat on an evaluation, without any human directing it to. Anthropic also disclosed three separate incidents in which its AI models escaped testing environments and gained unauthorized access to external organizations during cybersecurity evaluations. These recent security incidents have underscored the need for Congress to better understand these risks and develop policy solutions to prevent these incidents before emerging threats become larger problems. By addressing these challenges proactively, Congress can help create the conditions for continued American innovation and ensure the public can confidently benefit from advances in AI.

“AI has immense potential to improve our lives and strengthen American innovation, but that progress can’t come at the expense of our national security or public safety,” said Rep. Don Beyer. “Recent cyberattacks involving AI agents and growing warnings from leaders and researchers at the companies developing these technologies make clear that the risks are real and growing. We can’t afford to wait for a major catastrophe before putting meaningful safeguards in place. I’m proud to join the AI Safety Caucus and work with my colleagues to advance responsible legislation that strengthens oversight, security, and transparency while ensuring AI is developed and deployed safely and responsibly.”

“AI is advancing faster than ever before, and Congress needs to move just as quickly,” said Rep. George Whitesides. “Now is the time to build bipartisan consensus and advance commonsense guardrails we know will reduce the most serious risks. Americans are rightly concerned about where this technology is heading, but too often the debate in Washington is framed as a choice between doing nothing and banning AI altogether. That’s a false choice. We have an opportunity to pursue smart, targeted solutions that protect the public while allowing American innovation to thrive. I co-founded this caucus with Reps. Moran and Beyer to fight for that balance, because safe, secure, and controllable AI is the only path to unlocking its full promise for humanity.”

“We don’t have to choose between innovation and safety,” said Rep. Nathaniel Moran. “We can, and we should, do both. Artificial intelligence affects every American, and it should not be a partisan issue. This caucus gives us a place to find the areas of consensus, set partisanship aside, and put smart, targeted policies in place so we can innovate while we keep people safe. Congress needs to be prepared, and I’m proud to be one of the co-chairs leading that work.”

Specifically, the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus will:

Champion AI safety legislation: Develop legislative proposals and endorse existing bipartisan bills that establish thoughtful, targeted guardrails against the most serious AI risks while supporting continued innovation and American technological leadership.

Rapidly respond to AI incidents: Convene AI developers, technical experts, and government officials to brief Members and staff when significant AI safety incidents or developments occur and identify potential policy responses.

Equip congressional offices: Keep Members and staff informed about emerging AI developments, connect them with outside experts, and provide resources to navigate complex AI policy decisions.

Elevate AI safety publicly: Raise public awareness and make AI safety a national priority through public statements, op-eds, and press events.

Shape Congress’ AI agenda: Help develop federal AI safety policy and provide Members outside the committees of jurisdiction with an avenue to contribute to the conversation and legislative process.

By quickly addressing emerging threats, the AI Safety and Innovation caucus will ensure AI can continue to make key improvements in the fields of American science, medicine, productivity, and national security. This new bipartisan caucus will advance thoughtful, targeted guardrails, engaging technical experts and industry leaders, and equip Congress to respond quickly to emerging risks and significant AI incidents while ensuring America continues to lead in AI innovation.

The House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus launched with Reps. George Whitesides (D-CA), Nathaniel Moran (R-TX), and Don Beyer (D-VA) serving as co-chairs. Founding members include Reps. Greg Casar (D-TX); Yvette Clarke (D-NY); Ben Cline (R-VA); Mike Flood (R-NE); Bill Foster (D-IL); Valerie Foushee (D-NC); Pat Harrigan (R-NC); Jim Himes (D-CT); Sara Jacobs (D-CA); Mike Kennedy (R-UT); Ro Khanna (D-CA); Sam Liccardo (D-CA); Ted Lieu (D-CA); Zoe Lofgren (D-CA); Doris Matsui (D-CA); April McClain Delaney (D-MD); Blake Moore (R-UT); Jay Obernolte (R-CA); Scott Peters (D-CA); Brad Sherman (D-CA); Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA); Ritchie Torres (D-NY); Lori Trahan (D-MA).

title: Representatives Moore, Smith, Jack Introduce Legislation to Build a Stronger Financial Future for Every Child
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Representatives Blake Moore (R-UT), Adrian Smith (R-NE), and Brian Jack (R-GA) introduced the Investing in America’s Children Act to expand access to Trump Accounts and give families more flexibility to build long-term savings for their children.

“Trump Accounts are revolutionizing economic opportunity for each and every American child," Rep. Moore said. "This bill takes important steps to build on the successes of this program by expanding and enhancing eligibilities and contribution limits so even more children can benefit from Trump Accounts. I am honored to be part of this effort and will continue to look for opportunities to ensure these accounts reach their full potential.”

“Trump Accounts created an unprecedented opportunity for families to invest in their children’s futures starting on day one. This is why we must ensure that every eligible child has the opportunity to benefit. I introduced the Investing in America’s Children Act to expand access for children in foster care, give employers greater flexibility to contribute, and allow families to put unused education savings to work,” Rep. Smith said.

BACKGROUND:

The Investing in America’s Children Act would make several improvements to Trump Accounts to ensure that more children can benefit from these savings opportunities.

Specifically, the bill would:

Guarantee access through automatic enrollment: Codify Treasury’s automatic enrollment mechanism so every eligible American child, including those in foster care, can receive an account and begin receiving contributions without unnecessary delays.

Strengthen support for children in foster care: Codify efforts under First Lady Melania Trump’s Fostering the Future initiative by allowing states to claim and maintain accounts for eligible foster youth. States could also elect to claim the federal $1,000 seed contribution on behalf of eligible children.

Expand employer contribution flexibility: Apply the $2,500 annual employer contribution limit on a per-child, rather than per-employee, basis, allowing employers to contribute more when employees have multiple children.

Put unused education savings to work: Allow families to roll over unused funds from 529 and Coverdell education savings accounts into Trump Accounts, giving excess education savings another opportunity to grow.

title: Bonamici Introduces Bill to Help SNAP Benefits Reach People Experiencing Homelessness
text:
WASHINGTON, DC [11/19/26] – Today Congresswoman Suzanne Bonamici (D-OR) introduced legislation to increase access to SNAP benefits for people experiencing homelessness.

The Securing Unhoused People's Program for Outreach Resources and Transportation (SUPPORT) for SNAP Act would provide funding to establish outreach programs and train staff who work with people experiencing homelessness on SNAP applications. Approximately 5.5 million people, including many people who are unhoused, lost SNAP following major changes to the program after the Republicans passed the Big Ugly Bill in July 2025.

“SNAP is the most effective program we have to end hunger, but because of bureaucratic red tape it remains out of reach for many of the people who need it most,” said Congresswoman Suzanne Bonamici. “I’m introducing the SUPPORT for SNAP Act so people experiencing homelessness have the practical help they need to get SNAP benefits.”

The legislation is endorsed by the Alliance to End Hunger, Food Research & Action Center, National Alliance to End Homelessness, National Community Action Foundation, and National Health Care for the Homeless Council.

“People experiencing homelessness frequently face hunger as well,” said Eric P. Mitchell, President of the Alliance to End Hunger. “We commend Rep. Bonamici and her colleagues for supporting the SUPPORT for SNAP Act, which will help connect individuals in need with food assistance and other essential services.”

“FRAC commends Rep. Suzanne Bonamici for introducing the SUPPORT for SNAP Act, which would equip frontline organizations and local and state agencies with the resources to help individuals and families experiencing homelessness access food assistance. At a time when far too many people are forced to choose between keeping a roof over their head and putting food on the table, this bill would help address the significant barriers to enrollment people experiencing homelessness often face by funding things like outreach and enrollment assistance, ensuring more people can access the nutrition they need to stay healthy and food-secure,” said Crystal FitzSimons, President of the Food Research & Action Center (FRAC).

"National Health Care for the Homeless Council applauds Congresswoman Bonamici for introducing the SUPPORT for SNAP Act, which recognizes that access to SNAP requires more than just making benefits available,” said Bobby Watts, CEO of the National Health Care for the Homeless Council. “For people experiencing homelessness, navigating the application process can be especially difficult, resulting in missed food assistance for those who need it most. By supporting community organizations and outreach, this legislation will help connect people experiencing homelessness with the assistance they need to access healthy food."

The SUPPORT for SNAP Act includes:

Application assistance for people who are experiencing homelessness and seeking SNAP benefits;

Street outreach activities to connect caseworkers with individuals about their new potential eligibility as well as exemptions from work requirements and time limits, if applicable;

Engagement with Continuums of Care, Community Action Agencies, and other organizations with experience supporting very low-income families or people experiencing homelessness on SNAP applications;

Allowing funding to provide transportation to SNAP offices for people who need to apply in-person because of technology access;

Funding for training on SNAP benefits, including the shelter deduction and homeless household deductions that can improve benefit values for vulnerable SNAP recipients; and,

Translating materials and improving screening processes to better support everyone accessing the benefits they are eligible for.

The full text of the legislation can be found here.

It is sponsored by Representatives Barragan, Brown, Carson, Chu, Cohen, Garcia (IL), Jackson, Krishnamoorthi, Meng, Nadler, Norton, Omar, Pingree, Ramirez, Salinas, Sanchez, Scanlon, Torres (NY), and Watson Coleman.

title: Chairman Calvert Statement on Reconciliation and FY2027 Defense Appropriations: “Managed Decline is a Choice”
text:
“The American people sent us here to make the hard choices – both Democrats and Republicans. The recent election was certainly a message on the issues that are impacting Americans the most – inflation, affordability, and the price of gas. Republicans did not deliver on those issues, and I respect the choice of the electorate. However, the election was not a permission slip for the abdication of our duties when it comes to the defense of our country and our national security interests.

We need to be clear-eyed about what another Continuing Resolution would mean for our military:

Munitions and magazine depth collapse

Ongoing operations and prior support to partners have burned through stocks of precision munitions, interceptors, and long-range fires. Multi-year procurement contracts and industrial-base ramp-ups are among the items most dependent on stable or supplemental funding. Prolonged CRs block or delay these, leaving the U.S. and allies short for a high-intensity fight.

Readiness and force-generation erosion

CRs restrict new starts, limit production-rate increases, and force deferral of maintenance, training, and exercises. Navy ship maintenance availabilities are particularly vulnerable; deferred work compounds into longer future yard periods and lower availability. Flying hours, live-fire training, and large-scale exercises (critical for Indo-Pacific deterrence) suffer. GAO and service leaders have documented schedule delays, higher costs, and reduced readiness from repeated CRs. Extended deployments already strain the fleet; funding uncertainty accelerates the problem.

Delayed modernization against the China pacing threat

China’s rapid nuclear expansion (projected toward 1,000+ warheads by 2030), conventional buildup, space/counterspace systems, and gray-zone activities in the Indo-Pacific require sustained investment in missile defense, autonomous systems, undersea warfare, long-range fires, and resilient C4ISR/space architectures. CRs prohibit most “new starts” create stop-start uncertainty that raises costs and slows fielding. This directly weakens deterrence and warfighting capacity in the primary theater.⁠

Industrial base and long-term capacity atrophy

Unpredictable demand signals deter private investment, slow production lines, raise unit costs, and risk loss of skilled labor and suppliers. Once lost, capacity is expensive and time-consuming to rebuild—exactly when surge production would be needed most. Fragile supply chains are further strained, resulting in a loss of providers further destabilizing the defense industrial base. New companies that are investing in R&D, facilitation, equipment and technology will fail as DOW is prevented from putting new activities on contract.

This town is full of excuses for why we cannot pass the funding bills and reconciliation before us. Budget hawks will argue that we cannot add to the debt. I would respond that we must address the true drivers of that debt—and national security spending is not one of them. In fact, defense spending as a share of GDP is near a historic low, exceeded only by the post-Cold War lows of the 1990s.

To the Democrats who want more domestic spending to match defense spending, almost 72% of all outlays are on domestic programs, only 13% are for the national defense. The remaining 15% is servicing our debt.

We are at an inflection point, do we continue to be the lone world superpower, the reserve currency of the world, or do we choose to accelerate a decline that began in 1990s at the infamous 'Last Supper' event that launched a dire period of drastic industry consolidation? Passing these bills is hard, and it will require negotiation, compromise, and determination. That is what the American people expect of us. It is unconscionable that as we have U.S. servicemembers deployed around the world, Representatives and Senators are all too eager to leave town. Let’s stop making excuses and get to work.”

title: Cammack Commends New Ethics Rules as Sexual Misconduct Reform Package Nears the Finish Line
text:
November 19, 2026

New rules put public disclosure of Member misconduct findings in writing and speed up investigations, while protecting victims’ identities

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Kat Cammack (FL-03) today commended the House Ethics Committee for adopting new rules to speed up investigations and increase transparency in sexual misconduct cases involving Members, as the broader reform package her bipartisan task force is building nears completion.

A spike in House Ethics Committee investigations involving sexual misconduct this year led House leadership to designate Rep. Cammack in May to co-lead a bipartisan effort to combat sexual misconduct in Congress. In July, she co-hosted a packed meeting with House staff, and her task force is now building a broader package of reforms to make Capitol Hill a safer workplace.

“Since this spring, I’ve heard from former staffers about what they went through,” said Congresswoman Cammack. “The entire system on Capitol Hill has been designed to create a chilling effect for victims. That is untenable for an institution that asks the American people for their trust. The Ethics Committee’s new rules are a serious response. Putting public disclosure of misconduct findings in writing, while protecting every victim’s identity, gives staffers a commitment they can count on. Faster investigations mean they get answers in time to matter. This is exactly the kind of change our bipartisan task force has been pushing for.Accountability built on due process is accountability that lasts.”

The Ethics Committee has long made substantiated findings of sexual misconduct public as a matter of policy. Today’s vote writes that commitment into the Committee’s rules.

Rep. Cammack will keep working with colleagues on both sides of the aisle to pass the task force’s full set of reforms before the end of the year.

What the Ethics Committee’s new rules do:

Write into the Committee’s rules its policy of publicly disclosing any finding that a Member engaged in sexual harassment or other sexual misconduct, while explicitly prohibiting publication of any victim’s identity.

Allow the Chairman and Ranking Member to issue subpoenas jointly, without a vote of the full Committee.

End an investigative subcommittee’s role once it adopts findings, so the Committee can move to resolve a matter sooner.

Consolidate the deadlines for a Member to respond to findings, preserving a reasonable window while limiting delay tactics.

Clarify that a matter can be resolved on the existing record instead of a burdensome hearing.

Make fines and denial of privileges available as sanctions for any abuse of position.

title: Cammack’s Crackdown on Prison Cellphones Crosses the Finish Line at FCC
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Kat Cammack (FL-03) today celebrated a major win in her push to shut down contraband cellphones behind bars, as the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) voted to grant state and local prisons and jails first-ever authority to jam contraband phones.

Rep. Cammack has driven the issue on multiple fronts. She has worked directly with FCC Chairman Brendan Carr and held several meetings with Florida Department of Corrections leaders to work toward a solution. She also joined colleagues in a September 2025 letter supporting the rule-making the Commission adopted today.

“Every call an inmate can’t make on a smuggled phone is a crime that doesn’t happen,” said Congresswoman Cammack. “Criminals have used these phones to order hits and run drug operations from their cells, and some have even used them to target children. Our district is home to 15 state prisons and correctional institutions, and the officers who work inside them deserve every tool we can give them. We worked this directly with Chairman Carr and Florida’s corrections leaders, and I’m grateful the Commission got it done. Now Congress needs to finish the fight and make this authority permanent.”

“The illegal use of contraband cellphones is a growing crisis that demands immediate attention if we intend to keep our facilities, staff, and communities safe,” said Florida Department of Corrections Secretary Richard Comerford. “Today’s vote to allow prisons to jam contraband cellphones is a monumental step forward in our fight to stop this dangerous criminal enterprise. On behalf of FDC, we thank Congresswoman Kat Cammack, FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, and our law enforcement partners across the country for recognizing this security threat and taking bold action to counteract this growing crisis.”

According to the FCC, inmates have used contraband cellphones to call in hits, coordinate violent gang activity and run criminal enterprises from behind bars. Getting the phones inside is often a criminal operation of its own. In March 2026, a Florida jury convicted Mario Crawford, a Jacksonville man with 49 prior convictions, for using drones to drop cellphones, SIM cards, drugs and razor blades into three Florida prisons. He was sentenced to 81 years in prison, according to the Florida Attorney General’s Office.

The problem is widespread. A 2024 study found that prison authorities nationwide recovered more than 25,000 cellphones in a single year. In Florida alone, 8,376 cellphones have been recovered so far in 2026 from facilities operated by the Florida Department of Corrections and its private partners, according to FDC. Before today’s vote, the FCC had authorized other technologies to combat contraband phones but had never allowed jamming.

Rep. Cammack will keep working with her colleagues to make this authority permanent through legislation such as the Cellphone Jamming Reform Act, introduced by Senator Tom Cotton (R-AR) and Rep. David Kustoff (R-TN).

What the FCC’s action does:

Allows, but does not require, state and local prisons and jails to use jamming technology against contraband cellphones.

Requires jamming systems to pass testing showing they cause no harmful interference outside the facility.

Limits jamming to Commission-authorized areas where wireless device use is already prohibited.

Gives wireless carriers, FirstNet, public safety coordinators and 911 authorities advance notice of on-site testing, and notifies nearby communities before deployment.

Seeks public comment on closing loopholes that let contraband phones operate on other frequencies and services, and on further protections for public safety communications.

Read the letter Rep. Cammack joined here. Read the FCC announcement here.

title: Casten, Fry Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Include Fire Investigators in Federal First Responders’ Benefit Program
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Representative Sean Casten (D-IL-06) and Russell Fry (R-SC-07) introduced the bipartisan Fire Investigators Recognition Act, legislation to include fire investigators in the Public Safety Officers’ Benefit Program.

“Fire investigators are exposed to dangerous environments when they respond to the aftermath of catastrophic fires and explosions,” said Rep. Casten. “It’s time to close the gap in our benefit programs and ensure fire investigators receive the support they deserve for putting their lives on the line to keep us all safe.”

“Long after flames are extinguished and smoke is cleared, fire inspectors and investigators willingly step into hazardous scenes to uncover the truth behind fires and explosions,” said Rep. Fry. “These brave men and women face many of the same risks as other first responders, and their families deserve the same protections if tragedy strikes. Our bill closes a gap in federal law by ensuring qualifying fire investigators are recognized under the Public Safety Officers’ Benefits program, providing critical financial support to their loved ones in the event of a line-of-duty death. Their service and sacrifice should never go unrecognized.”

“Public service fire investigators perform essential public safety work,” said Devin J. Palmer, president of the International Association of Arson Investigators. “They deserve the same line-of-duty injury, death, and survivor benefits already afforded to law enforcement officers and firefighters. The Fire Investigators Recognition Act provides that recognition and support.”

Fire investigators, also known as fire inspectors or arson investigators, determine the causes of fires and explosions and help inform prevention strategies. Like all fire service professionals, fire investigators are exposed to hazards involved in fire response, such as structural instabilities, carcinogens, and other toxic materials in post-fire and post-explosion environments, often for extended periods of time.

The Public Safety Officers’ Benefit Program (PSOB) provides benefits to first responders who have been catastrophically injured in the line of duty. The program also includes death and education benefits to survivors of fallen law enforcement officers, firefighters, and other first responders.

Despite fire investigators’ key role in fire response, many fire investigators and their surviving family members are not eligible to receive benefits because the job is not explicitly listed under the PSOB's definition of a qualifying first responder. The Fire Investigators Recognition Act fixes this gap in the law by officially naming fire investigators as an occupation that is eligible to receive federal first responder benefits.

Text of the legislation can be found here.

The legislation is endorsed by the International Association of Arson Investigators. A statement of support from IAAI can be found here.

title: Smith hearing examines global persecution of Christians
text:
At yesterday’s Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission (TLHRC) hearing chaired by Co-Chairman Chris Smith (R-NJ), expert witnesses from across civil society testified about the ongoing persecution of and threats against Christians communities in different parts of the world.

The hearing, entitled “Worldwide Persecution of Christians: Responding to New Challenges,” examined the evolving trends and patterns of Christian persecution throughout the globe. Witnesses assessed the factors influencing where and why Christian persecution is increasing; how churches, civil society organizations, and foreign governments are responding to the uptick in religious violence; and how the U.S. government can further defend the rights of the faithful.

During his opening statement, Smith said, “Religious freedom is a universal human right. It belongs to every person, everywhere, regardless of faith or belief. But, there are good reasons to examine the persecution of Christians separately and in some depth.

“One of the things most immediately striking about the persecution of Christians is the geographical scope and scale of persecution. Christians are among the most widely dispersed religious communities in the world. They are also among the most widely persecuted. They face severe persecution in a very large number of countries, and on every continent,” continued Smith, a leading lawmaker on international religious freedom issues.

Smith highlighted the findings of Open Doors’ 2026 World Watch List, which reported that more than 388 million Christians worldwide suffer high levels of persecution and discrimination for their faith. “That’s more than one in seven of the world’s Christians,” noted Smith.

“And this horrific problem is not confined to a handful of countries or a single region. It is a global challenge, and one that demands a response informed by an understanding of its different causes and manifestations.”

The hearing’s witnesses included David K. Trimble, the President of the Religious Freedom Institute; John Eibner, the International President of Christian Solidarity International; Timothy Shah, a Distinguished Research Scholar in Politics at the University of Dallas and the Secretary of the Board at the G20 Religion Forum; Jeremy Tedesco, Senior Counsel and the Senior Vice President of Global Free Speech at the Alliance Defending Freedom; and Matthew Soerens, the Vice President of Advocacy and Policy at World Relief.

During his testimony, Trimble specifically detailed the dire threats facing Christians in Nigeria and Syria. “Modern day Nigeria is one of the deadliest countries in the world to be a Christian,” Trimble said. “Open Doors Int’l reports an estimated 3,490 Christians have been killed in 2026. Approximately 12 Christians per day are killed in Nigeria because they are Christian.”

Trimble further noted that “Nigerian authorities have deliberately ignored or been complicit in the violence. They have failed to hold violent perpetrators systematically accountable. They have downplayed the violence and reporting, failed to govern with accountability, and left Christian communities especially vulnerable.”

Regarding Syria, Trimble explained that “despite promises by the transitional government to provide protections for religious communities, Christians (sometimes as part of broader sectarian violence toward all religious minorities) continue to face violence, intimidation, discrimination, and daily uncertainties regarding their religious freedom.”

Christian Solidarity International President John Eibner described the persecution of Christians in Turkey under Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan as relentless:

“When it comes to Turkey’s multi-denominational Christian community, persecution today comes mainly in the form of harassment, restrictive administrative measures, interference with church leadership, deportation of non-Turkish church workers and semi-official media campaigns portraying Christians as aliens in society. These day-to-day forms of repression are interspersed with occasional murders intended to intimidate vulnerable communities.”

He also detailed how the influence of Turkey and Azerbaijan on the Armenian government have contributed to the persecution of the Armenian Apostolic Church:

“I speak of the effort by the current Armenian government to overthrow the head of the global Armenian Apostolic Church, Catholicos Karekin II, and impose state control over this historic bulwark of Christian Armenia… In fact, this persecution is intrinsically connected with Turkey and Azerbaijan’s efforts to jointly extend their strategic depth. So tight are the bonds between these two Turkic states that Erdogan and his Azerbaijani counterpart, Ilham Aliyev, routinely speak of the two countries as a ‘one nation, two states’ condominium. When it comes to asserting supremacy over Armenia’s Christians, Turkey and Azerbaijan work as a unit. The persecution, though handled by the Armenian government led by Nikol Pashinyan, is driven by these two Turkic Muslim powers.”

Eibner urged the United States to reassess its alliance with Turkey, “[re-energize] its support for religious freedom in Turkey’s sphere of influence, and [prioritize] the survival of beleaguered Christians and religious minorities in its policymaking.”

In a similar vein, witness Jeremey Tedesco of the Alliance Defending Freedom described the specific threats to practicing Christians in Europe—namely, in Finland, the United Kingdom, Ireland, Germany, France, Spain, and Malta. Tedesco provided numerous examples of lawfare against and censorship of practicing Christians in Europe, asserting that “what EU officials classify as ‘hate speech’ can be as innocent as a citing a Bible verse, making a social media post, or distributing a church pamphlet.”

Tedesco connected the “the insidious interplay between online censorship and Christian persecution” to the EU’s Digital Services Act (DSA) and the UK’s Online Safety Act (OSA), which, he noted, “give European officials the machinery to export European speech restrictions worldwide, often targeting Christians and their most fundamental practices and beliefs… This means churches, ministries, and speakers feel the effects of European censorship far beyond Europe’s borders, including here in the United States.”

To combat the censorship and targeting of Christians and Europe, Tedesco urged Congress to use diplomatic tools and “have candid, in-person conversations with foreign officials to raise concerns about the DSA’s impact on these rights both at home and abroad.” He also urged the United States’ governing body to “support the calls, by the President and 25 federal lawmakers, to have the U.S. Trade Representative investigate the EU’s overregulation and excessive fines on American corporations that do not submit to the EU’s censorship regime.”

Timothy Shah, an expert on international religious freedom issues, provided insights into the global scope and primary drivers and causes of Christian persecution. Offering a snapshot of the current state of global Christian persecution, Shah cited a recent Pew Research Center study on religious freedom, which found that “‘Christians were harassed by government officials or nongovernmental actors in 165 countries in 2023… In other words, Pew’s data suggest an increase of more than 50% in the number of countries where Christians are experiencing some level of persecution between 2007 and 2023.’”

Regarding the primary causes of Christian persecution, Shah noted that the three main drivers of are “authoritarianism, in secular, Islamist, and religious-nationalist forms; violence and armed conflict; and radical non-state actors.”

Matthew Soerens, Vice President of Advocacy and Policy at World Relief—who previously served as a Department of Justice-accredited immigration legal counselor for World Relief’s local office in suburban Chicago—detailed the immigration trends of Christians fleeing persecution: “When persecution becomes sufficiently acute, some are forced to flee. In their most recent report, Open Doors reported that 224,129 Christians had to leave their homes to escape persecution just in the prior year.”

###

title: EWTN News article on Smith's Christian persecution hearing'Christians are world's "most persecuted religious community," expert says at congressional hearing'
text:
By Amira Abuzeid

Published November 19, 2026 at 6:17 PM ET

Lawmakers on Capitol Hill this week examined the continued persecution of Christians around the world, focusing on emerging threats and what can be done to protect vulnerable communities.

At the Nov. 18 Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission hearing on the worldwide persecution of Christians, co-chaired by Rep. Chris Smith, R-New Jersey, and Rep. James P. McGovern, D-Massachusetts, lawmakers and experts examined how areas with political and social unrest are seeing increases in religious-freedom violations, including rising persecution and violence against Christians.

The commission cited the Open Doors’ World Watch List, which estimates that in the 50 countries on its list, more than 388 million Christians live with high levels of discrimination and persecution.

Violations take many forms, according to a memo released by the commission, and can range from a denial of rights, repression, and discrimination by the state itself to attacks by armed groups and international criminal networks. The growth of such groups as well as oppressive political regimes has made the problem worse, the commission said.

The witness panel at the Nov. 18, 2026, Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission hearing on the worldwide persecution of Christians includes (left to right) David Trimble, John Eibner, Timothy Shah, and Jeremy Tedesco. | Credit: House Creative Services

Nigeria ‘deadliest country’ in the world to be a Christian’

David Trimble, president of the Religious Freedom Institute, told the commission that “nowhere in the world today do Christians face a more severe threat of persecution than in Nigeria.”

Trimble said the number of violent extremists in Nigeria is growing, and each group is affiliated either with Al-Qaeda or the broader Islamic State, such as Boko Haram, who, along with other bands of militants and criminal bandits, are the biggest perpetrators of violence against Christians in the country. He said the groups act with impunity and often with the government’s assistance.

Christians make up nearly half of Nigeria’s population, according to the U.S. State Department. Despite this, according to Open Doors International, more than 3,100 Christians were killed in 2025, and so far in 2026, nearly 3,500 Christians have been killed, making the country “one of the deadliest countries in the world to be a Christian,” Trimble said. In addition, almost 2,300 Christians have been kidnapped so far this year.

Among several recommendations, Trimble called for prioritizing religious freedom education in offending countries, calling education “a deterrent to violence and a significant factor in preventing genocide.”

Situation in Syria

After the fall of the Bashar Al-Assad regime in Syria, Trimble said, Christians and other religious minorities continue to face violence and other religious freedom violations, including the threat of genocide.

He also called for an Atrocity Prevention Commission with statutory authority made up of “experts who oversee analysis of geopolitical contexts of persecution and recommend methods of crisis response to avoid escalating violence and genocide.”

John Eibner, president of Christian Solidarity International, said that Christians are “the most persecuted religious community in the world.” He cited Vatican estimates that state that in 2025, 5,000 people were killed for their Christian faith and 400 million faced violence or persecution.

He said there are a variety of emerging challenges regarding Christian persecution but focused on the influence of Turkey.

Eibner pointed to the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom’s finding that “Turkey’s religious freedom violations remain systematic and ongoing,” arguing that as Turkey’s geopolitical influence continues to rise, Christians in Azerbaijan, Armenia, Syria, and surrounding countries will continue to suffer.

As Eibner sees it, the U.S. and other Western nations have essentially turned a “blind eye” to the plight of Christians in the region, calling on U.S. policymakers to prioritize “the survival of beleaguered Christians and religious minorities.”

“If present trends and policies remain in place, even more Christian communities in the immense Turkish-Azerbaijani sphere of influence will be destroyed or wither away,” he said. “Needless to say, this outcome would be a world-historical tragedy for Christianity and for international religious freedom.”

title: Rep. Chu, Sen. Booker Reintroduce DIPLOMA Act to Strengthen School and Community Partnerships, Support Students
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) and Sen. Cory Booker (NJ) reintroduced the Developing Innovative Partnerships and Learning Opportunities that Motivate Achievement (DIPLOMA) Act, legislation that would provide federal grants to states to encourage and support community schools, which are collaborations between schools and community partners to address students’ holistic needs through evidence-based practices. The bill would also provide planning grants to help states design their strategies, ensuring thoughtful and effective implementation.

Grants awarded under the DIPLOMA Act would enable schools to integrate services addressing academic, health, and social challenges. Schools could use these funds to expand early childhood programs, provide academic enrichment opportunities like tutoring and summer learning, and develop alternative pathways to graduation, such as dual enrollment and dropout recovery programs. The legislation also stresses the importance of youth development through mentoring, leadership training, and career counseling, while expanding access to critical health services, including primary care, mental health, and nutrition programs. In addition to directly supporting students, the bill aims to strengthen family engagement in their students’ education and to support teacher recruitment and retention efforts.

“As a former educator, I know that students are much more likely to struggle in the classroom when their basic needs aren’t being met,” said Rep. Chu. “Schools and teachers shouldn’t have to solve these challenges alone. The DIPLOMA Act would bring more comprehensive services like health care, tutoring, and family support into our schools, helping them become full-service community hubs that set students and families up for success in and out of the classroom. I’m proud to reintroduce this bill with Senator Booker so that every child has the resources to succeed.”

"Growing up and serving the people of Newark, I have seen firsthand how strong communities can open doors for young people and how inequities can hold them back,” said Senator Booker. “The DIPLOMA Act will help bring schools, families, and community partners together to ensure every child has access to the resources, support, and opportunities they need to succeed.”

The DIPLOMA ACT would provide state-led grants to support local partnerships between public schools and at least one community partner such as a local government, institution of higher education, nonprofit, business, or foundation. These partnerships could use funds to:

Integrate services: Build a continuum of academic and social support by coordinating public and private services in a collaborative framework.

Enhance early childhood and family programs: Support early reading initiatives, child care, home visitation, and parental education programs.

Provide academic enrichment and remediation: Offer tutoring, afterschool programs, and summer learning to close achievement gaps and reduce absenteeism.

Expand pathways to graduation: Establish programs such as dual enrollment, early college high schools, and dropout recovery initiatives.

Promote youth development: Facilitate mentoring, leadership training, civic engagement, and career counseling opportunities.

Improve health services: Provide primary care, mental health, dental care, and nutrition services to address students’ physical and emotional well-being.

Strengthen teacher support: Invest in professional development and training for educators and staff to enhance recruitment and retention.

Engage families and communities: Develop programs to educate families, encourage parental involvement, and foster strong community connections.

"The DIPLOMA Act will equip states with the resources needed to implement and scale the Community Schools we know they want, as well as strengthen school-community partnerships around comprehensive, evidence-based goals for continuous improvement. At IEL, we know that in order to build resiliency in our education system, we need innovation and robust public policy that is informed by the needs and interests of those most affected by policy decisions: youth, families, and communities. We believe this bill provides just that and are excited to see the continued expansion of Community Schools through this state-level support,” said Kwesi Rollins, interim president, Institute for Educational Leadership (the home of the Coalition for Community Schools).

The DIPLOMA Act is endorsed by the Institute for Educational Leadership (IEL), the Coalition for Community Schools, and the American Federation of Teachers (AFT).

title: Rep. Chu, Sen. Wyden Reintroduce PROGRESS Act to Increase Capital for Women- and Minority-Owned Businesses
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Judy Chu (CA-28) and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (OR) reintroduced the bicameral Providing Real Opportunities for Growth to Rising Entrepreneurs for Sustained Success (PROGRESS) Act to strengthen access to capital for small businesses owned by women and people of color.

“Small businesses are the backbone of our communities, but too many entrepreneurs, especially women and people of color who lack longstanding relationships with financial institutions, still struggle to access the capital they need to grow,” said Rep. Chu, who serves on the House Ways and Means Committee. “That is a missed opportunity for all of us. Senator Wyden and I are reintroducing the PROGRESS Act to establish tax credits for first employees and investors, so that these promising businesses aren’t held back simply because they lack the right connections. When we level the playing field for women-owned and minority-owned businesses, we create jobs, strengthen our local economies, and unlock their full potential.”

“Capital in America has a blind spot when it comes to people of color and women business owners, and as a consequence that’s holding back a lot of hardworking entrepreneurs and big economic potential,” Senator Wyden said. “This bill gives us an opportunity to drive more dollars toward a lot of dedicated entrepreneurs who are eager to grow successful businesses and create jobs.”

On average, white business owners start with nearly three times the working capital of black-owned businesses. Male entrepreneurs, on average, start with nearly twice as much capital as female entrepreneurs. The numbers are even worse when considering only third-party capital. In 2025, only 1 percent of venture capital funding went to companies founded solely by women. This disparity is acutely felt by women of color who now account for 47 percent of all women-owned firms, yet received less than 1% of venture capital funding over the past decade.

Because of their size, their industry, or the way they are organized, many women-owned businesses can’t take advantage of tax benefits designed for small businesses. Simply put, minority and female entrepreneurs are underrepresented, underestimated, and undercapitalized. This lack of capital has limited the ability of these entrepreneurs to grow their businesses.

The PROGRESS Act establishes two new tax incentives to unlock the resources these businesses need to grow and reach their full potential:

First Employee Credit:

A new first employee credit will stimulate business growth and job creation.

A credit equal to 25 percent of reported W-2 wages can be claimed annually, up to $10,000 in a single tax year, with a lifetime limit of $40,000.

Because many businesses do not turn a profit in their early years, the first employee credit can be claimed against the business’ payroll tax liability.

Certain businesses that have not reported full-time equivalent W-2 wages in a previous year are eligible for the credit.

Eligible businesses must be majority-owned by U.S. individuals who each earn $100,000 or less per year ($200,000 in the case of joint filers).

Investor Credit:

A new investment credit will encourage third-party capital investment and help small businesses grow and thrive.

A credit of up to 50 percent of a qualified debt or equity investment can be claimed, up to $10,000 in a single tax year, with a lifetime limit of $50,000.

Investors who fund eligible businesses can use the credit to boost their rate of return.

Eligible businesses must have at least one full-time equivalent employee and be majority-owned by U.S. individuals who each earn $100,000 or less per year ($200,000 in the case of joint filers).

“We support the creation of tax incentives designed to boost the potential of all small businesses, but we're particularly encouraged to see legislation that would help support historically underserved businesses—those owned by women and minorities,” said Alexis D'Amato Falvey, Senior Director of Federal Government Affairs for Small Business Majority. “Many types of small businesses struggle to access the capital they need to grow, but small firms owned by women and minorities are more likely to experience funding challenges. Meanwhile, our research found that the current tax code falls short for these businesses, with existing deductions instead disproportionately benefiting the largest firms. Policies like the tax credits proposed by Sen. Wyden and Rep. Chu would help address the capital gap and are critical to ensuring a level playing field that provides more entrepreneurs with a chance to succeed.”

“Small businesses are the backbone of our economy, and ensuring that women and people of color owned businesses have the resources and opportunities to grow is essential to building a stronger, more inclusive small business landscape. The reintroduction of the PROGRESS Act by Rep. Chu and Sen. Wyden represents an important step toward addressing persistent barriers to entrepreneurship by creating targeted tax credits that help small business owners navigate real economic challenges, invest in their businesses, and sustain long-term growth. At Main Street Alliance, we know that expanding access to meaningful financial support is critical not only to helping small businesses start and grow, but also to ensuring they can remain resilient, retain employees, and continue contributing to thriving local economies,” said Lauren Bealore, National Director of Policy & Programs of Main Street Alliance.

“Access to capital remains one of the greatest hurdles for Asian American and Pacific Islander (AAPI) entrepreneurs striving to launch and scale their businesses,” said Chiling Tong, President and CEO of the National Asian Pacific Islander American Chamber of Commerce (National ACE). “The reintroduction of the PROGRESS Act is vital to breaking down systemic barriers as it leverages tax credits to increase private investment for start-ups. This legislation directly empowers our small business owners to innovate, expand, and drive job creation across the country. We deeply appreciate Congresswoman Chu and Senator Wyden for their continued leadership and commitment to championing all small businesses.”

“Angel investing, venture capital (VC), and other forms of investment can and should be viable options for women in the early stages of their businesses. Yet in 2022, women-founded startups received less than 2% of all venture capital dollars. Women, especially women of color, remain underrepresented and undercapitalized in angel investing and VC. WIPP’s Access to Capital Framework calls on congressional leaders to create tax incentives for angel investors, including incentives to invest in women- and minority-owned businesses. We are pleased to see Congresswoman Judy Chu take meaningful steps toward that goal with the PROGRESS Act,” said Angela Dingle, President and CEO of Women Impacting Public Policy. “By creating two tax credits, one for first-time employees and another for investors, the bill would pave the way for women business owners to access capital without turning to loans or dipping into their personal savings.”

“Small businesses are the backbone of our economy, yet too many entrepreneurs, particularly women and people of color, continue to face significant barriers to accessing the capital and resources they need to succeed,” said Anne Zimmerman, Co-Chair of Small Business for America’s Future. “The PROGRESS Act takes an important step toward leveling the playing field by providing targeted tax incentives that help small business owners invest in their businesses, create jobs, and build long-term economic stability. At a time when rising costs and economic uncertainty are putting increasing pressure on Main Street, we need commonsense solutions that give entrepreneurs the tools to grow and thrive. Small Business for America’s Future is proud to support this legislation and its commitment to expanding economic opportunity for small business owners across the country.”

The bill is cosponsored by Reps. Ilhan Omar (MN-05) and Lateefah Simon (CA-12).

title: García, Casar Lead Colleagues in Reintroducing  Legislation to Promote Youth Employment
text:
Washington, D.C. 一 Today, Representatives Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04) and Greg Casar (TX-35) led their colleagues Representatives Judy Chu (CA-28), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Elenor Holmes Norton (DC-00), Mark Pocan (WI-02), and Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) in reintroducing the Connecting Youth to Jobs Act, which would mandate Congress to enact a national subsidized jobs program that creates living-wage employment opportunities for young people facing barriers to employment and historically disadvantaged youth.

“I’ve been involved in community development for almost five decades, fighting to end decades of disinvestment from our neighborhoods and create opportunities for our youth. The Connecting Youth to Jobs Act, would create good paying job opportunities for young people in Chicago and across the country. This bill would also offer them wraparound services that would allow them to stay employed, like child care and transportation,” Rep. García. “At a time when there are almost 32 million people between 18 and 24 years old in the United States, we must act and invest in supporting and training our workforce of today and tomorrow.”

The bill sets a minimum wage of at least $17 for all program participants and protects their right to join in union activity when applicable. The bill also ensures that income received under the program does not affect participants’ eligibility for SNAP or other benefits under any federal program or under any state or local program financed by federal funds.

The Connecting Youth to Jobs Act would:

Guarantee federally subsidized employment opportunities by providing States and local areas with funds for employment programs that lead to unsubsidized, full time employment or provide the necessary skills for at least one postsecondary credential.

Establish a $10 billion competitive grant for providing wraparound services to youth employment program participants and work-based learning opportunities for youth.

Direct the Department of Labor (DOL) to collect youth employment program performance data and submit a report to Congress.
