title: CORREA DEMANDS TRANSPARENCY ON FORCED VOLUNTARY DEPARTURES AT SANTA ANA ICE FIELD OFFICE
text:
SANTA ANA, Calif. – Congressman Lou Correa (CA-46), a senior member of the House Homeland Security and Judiciary Committees, today sent a letter to Marcos Charles, Executive Associate Director of Enforcement and Removal Operations at U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The letter demands transparency regarding reports that ICE field offices are pressuring people into voluntary departures, including at the Santa Ana office, which is overseen by the Los Angeles office.

“I am writing to express concern and demand transparency regarding reports of forced voluntary departures at U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) field offices, including in Santa Ana, California. I have received reports of detainees being unlawfully forced to sign deportation documents, and in some instances ICE agents using physical force to compel detainees to sign the documents. Under no circumstance should individuals be coerced to sacrifice their constitutional rights,” Correa writes.

“In order to provide transparency and accountability, I respectfully request the number of voluntary departure forms signed at the Los Angeles ICE field office, listed per month and divided by each subfield office location, from January 2025 through November 2026. I also request a briefing on the agency’s process for voluntary departures, including what safeguards are in place to ensure transparency and understanding by those signing these documents,” Correa concludes.

title: Correa Opposes USDA Effort to Kick 6 Million Americans Off Food Assistance
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Lou Correa (CA-46) sent a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins opposing a new proposed rule that would kick an estimated 6.3 million Americans – primarily older or disabled beneficiaries and families with children – off the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).

title: Rep. Crane Urges Swift Approval of Navajo Nation’s Disaster Declaration Request After Severe Floods
text:
Today, Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) sent a letter to President Donald J. Trump and Robert J. Fenton, Regional Administrator of Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Region IX. He wrote in support of the Navajo Nation’s request for a major disaster declaration following extreme weather in Arizona and New Mexico.

In September, intense monsoon storms brought heavy rainfall and flash flooding to communities across both states. Tragically, three Navajo Nation citizens lost their lives as a result. Washed-out roads and disrupted utilities have since limited access to essential services, and bridges and other key systems also sustained damage. Older adults and other vulnerable residents now face significant hardship.

FEMA’s Individual Assistance assessment has identified 86 impacted homes. The Nation and its chapters have committed substantial resources to the initial response, ranging from rescuing people left stranded to making repairs and delivering supplies. However, the scale of the losses exceeds what local and Tribal budgets can cover.

Navajo leaders filed for the declaration on November 17, 2026, under Section 401 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act. Rep. Crane stands firmly behind this effort, and he is hopeful the White House will promptly approve the application and authorize both Individual Assistance and Public Assistance. That aid would benefit eligible households. It would also allow the Nation to meet urgent needs and restore critical infrastructure.

title: Crow Speaks on 1-Year Anniversary of “Don’t Give Up the Ship” Video
text:
WASHINGTON—Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a former paratrooper and Army Ranger who serves on the House Armed Services Committee and House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, spoke on the one-year anniversary since he and his colleagues filmed a video reminding servicemembers of their oaths to the Constitution and to not follow illegal orders.

Crow taped the “Don’t Give Up the Ship” video alongside fellow veterans of the military and intelligence community Sens. Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) and Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and Representatives Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA), Chris Deluzio (D-PA), and Maggie Goodlander (D-NH).

“All six of us, years ago, took our first oath to the Constitution,” Crow said at a press conference with his colleagues. “We have taken many oaths since, but that first one was a lifetime oath—to defend the Constitution, to uphold the rule of law, and to fight back against enemies foreign and domestic. That oath never expires.”

A three-time combat veteran, Crow made clear that, as they said in their video, they stand with the brave servicemembers who are working to uphold their oaths to the Constitution. “I have a deep love for our brothers and sisters in the military, who right now are being asked to do difficult things and being put into positions by this President that they should not be put into,” Crow said. “Our message is simple: We stand with you. We stand with our brothers and sisters in the military who are working hard to uphold their oaths, to stand by the Constitution, to defend this country. America stands with you.”

“Donald Trump doesn’t actually understand what we talked about,” Crow continued. “He doesn’t understand service. He doesn’t understand commitment to something bigger than himself. He certainly doesn’t understand the Uniform Code of Military Justice. [His threats] were about trying to send a message to Americans that if you step out of line, you dare speak up and question his power, he will use the force of government to crush you. That is a message we are never going to allow him to send.”

Crow concluded that while fear is contagious, so is courage–especially the courage shown by Americans everywhere: “Donald Trump is trying to spread fear throughout the nation… We’ve seen CEOs bend the knee, companies capitulate, universities and law firms cow and bow down to go along and get along. But the story of this moment is not their story. This is about the tens of millions of Americans who have stood up, organized, mobilized, taken to the streets, held the line in their communities to protect their friends and neighbors. It’s their story, and I will draw courage from them and never back down.”

Watch the full press conference with Crow, Slotkin, Kelly, Houlahan, and Goodlander HERE.

In the year since Crow and his colleagues posted their “Don’t Give Up the Ship” video, President Trump has repeatedly said he wants the lawmakers arrested and put on trial. Trump called them traitors engaged in seditious behavior punishable by death and said they should be in jail, investigated, arrested, and hanged for sedition. He directed his Administration to move on those threats, but a D.C. grand jury refused in February to indict Crow and the other veteran and national security lawmakers. A year later, the President continues to threaten the six lawmakers, as he weaponizes the federal government and the Department of Justice against those who speak out against him.

title: ICYMI: After Kansas Family Shares Healthcare Struggle, Davids Speaks on Her Bill to Expand Medicare Access for Early-Onset Alzheimer’s Patients
text:
In case you missed it, Representative Sharice Davids (D-KS-03) published an op-ed in the Washington Times today detailing how a conversation with Overland Park constituent Nina Westvold inspired her to introduce the Early-Onset Alzheimer’s Coverage Act — common-sense legislation to close a Medicare coverage gap affecting younger Americans diagnosed with terminal Alzheimer’s disease.

"When a constituent brings a broken system to my attention, I don't just sympathize with them. I take action to fix it... No spouse should have to choose between financial ruin and caring for a dying partner. No parent who stayed home to raise the next generation should be denied healthcare access when a fatal disease strikes," wrote Davids.

In the piece, Davids shares the story of Nina Westvold and her husband of 35 years, Kent, who was diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer’s at age 61. Under current law, Americans under 65 with terminal illnesses can only access Medicare early if they qualify for Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) — which requires a specific number of years in the workforce. Because Kent spent more than a decade as a stay-at-home dad raising their son, he did not meet SSDI work requirements, leaving the couple under 65, ineligible for Medicare, and facing astronomical out-of-pocket private insurance costs while Nina retired early to become his full-time caregiver.

After hearing directly from Nina, Davids took action in Washington by introducing the Early-Onset Alzheimer’s Coverage Act. The legislation removes the arbitrary SSDI prerequisite and creates a direct pathway for individuals under 65 diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer’s to buy into Medicare Parts A, B, and D. It also establishes a dedicated three-month enrollment window following diagnosis and ensures access to Medigap supplemental plans to keep out-of-pocket medical bills manageable.

Read the full op-ed HERE or below:

A Lifeline for Families Facing Early-Onset Alzheimer’s

By Representative Sharice Davids (KS-03)

When people think about a Member of Congress’ day-to-day work, they often imagine big speeches on the House floor or heated debates during late-night hearings. But the most important work I do doesn’t happen in Washington — it happens at home in Kansas, sitting around the table listening to the priorities of my constituents.

During a town hall last year, I heard from Nina Westvold, a resident of Overland Park, KS. Her story broke my heart, but it also exposed a glaring defect in our nation’s healthcare system.

So, I got to work.

Nina’s husband of 35 years, Kent — whom she calls the “love of my life” — was diagnosed with early-onset Alzheimer’s at just 61 years old. A diagnosis like that turns a family's world upside down. Alzheimer's is a fatal disease, and managing it requires extensive medical care and constant support.

Hoping to navigate this devastating news, Nina looked into healthcare coverage options. Medicare, our national healthcare program for seniors, typically starts at age 65. However, federal law allows some younger Americans diagnosed with terminal illnesses to access Medicare early if they have been on Social Security Disability Insurance.

That is where Nina and Kent ran into a brick wall.

To qualify for Social Security disability, a person must have worked and paid into Social Security for a certain number of years. But years ago, Kent stepped back from the workforce to stay home full-time, keep their son focused on school, and manage their household while Nina worked. It was a choice that paid off for their family — their son grew up, graduated college, bought a home, and started a successful career.

Yet, because Kent was a stay-at-home dad for over a decade, he lacked the qualifications needed for Social Security disability, and therefore, could not get access to early Medicare coverage.

Nina had to retire early to become Kent’s full-time caregiver. With both of them under 65 and unable to access Medicare, they were forced to pay astronomical costs out of their own pockets for private medical insurance while facing a terminally ill diagnosis.

As Nina put it to me, finding out her husband couldn’t get Medicare simply because he chose to raise their child felt like “a punch in the gut.” Parents sacrifice so much for their families; they should never be punished by the healthcare system when tragedy strikes.

When a constituent brings a broken system to my attention, I don't just sympathize with them. I take action to fix it.

That is why I introduced the Early-Onset Alzheimer’s Coverage Act, which Nina described as “a true lifeline.”

The fix is straightforward and practical. My bill creates a direct pathway for people like Kent to buy into Medicare coverage.

It removes the arbitrary requirement that forces terminal patients to go through the disability system first just to get health coverage. Families like Nina and Kent would also have a designated Medicare enrollment window, as well as access to supplemental plans to keep medical bills manageable.

This policy isn't about partisan debates; it's about basic fairness and common sense. No spouse should have to choose between financial ruin and caring for a dying partner. No parent who stayed home to raise the next generation should be denied healthcare access when a fatal disease strikes.

Nina said, “I am so grateful to Representative Davids for standing up for families like mine, listening to our pain, and taking real action to fix this broken system.”

But the work is not over. We must reach across the aisle to pass the Early-Onset Alzheimer’s Coverage Act to fix this gap, support our caregivers, and offer a real lifeline to families facing one of the hardest challenges life can bring.

title: Dingell Re-Elected to House Democratic Leadership, Will Return as Chair of House Democrats’ Communications Committee
PASSED: Dingell’s Bipartisan Bill to Uncover America’s Critical Minerals Passes House
text:
U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and Rob Wittman (R-VA-01) successfully passed their bipartisan Earth Mapping Resources Initiative (MRI) Reauthorization Act through the House of Representatives. This legislation will reauthorize the Earth MRI program that identifies, maps, and studies domestic minerals.

“This is a huge step forward in strengthening our critical mineral supply chains. I am proud to have worked alongside Congressman Wittman to pass this legislation, which will provide us with the data to better understand our nation’s mineral resources. By strengthening our critical mineral supply chains, we are strengthening American manufacturing and decreasing our reliance on critical minerals from adversaries like China. This bipartisan bill will help build a stronger economy, create good-paying jobs, and support American workers.” said Congresswoman Dingell.

“Before we can begin to develop our domestic resources, we must first identify, map, and study our mineral supply — which is why I’m supportive of Earth MRI and the ongoing domestic mapping efforts at the Department of Interior,” said Congressman Wittman. “Geological mapping produces economic returns many times greater than its cost, increases exploration activities, and strengthens domestic critical mineral supply chains, strengthening our economy and making the U.S. less dependent on foreign adversaries. I am proud to have introduced this legislation with Congresswoman Dingell.”

Established in 2019, Earth MRI focuses on enhancing our understanding of the geologic features of the United States. The initiative seeks to complete comprehensive mapping of domestic minerals by 2031. As Congress works to strengthen domestic supply chains for critical minerals, reduce dependence on foreign adversaries, and support American manufacturing, Congresswoman Dingell recognizes that responsible resource development begins with reliable data. Senators Hickenlooper and Murkowski have introduced companion legislation in the Senate.

title: Following Oversight Visit by Dexter, Ansari, Grijalva Pregnant Woman Maria Brinez Released from Eloy Detention Center
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representatives Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03), Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), announced the release of Maria Alejandra Valero Brinez, a high-risk pregnant woman detained at the Eloy Detention Center, following their October 22 oversight visit alongside Reproductive Freedom for All President Mini Timmaraju.

“Maria is finally free! Her and her baby’s health and safety were recklessly put at grave risk by the Trump administration, and it should never have taken a court to force ICE to release her,” Rep. Dexter said. “As a critical care physician, I’ve cared for countless patients whose lives depended on getting treatment in time, and keeping a high-risk pregnant woman behind bars, unable to get the care she needs, is not just cruel, it is malpractice. Maria’s release does not erase the harm she endured. I will do all I can in the months to come to ensure the imprisonment of innocent pregnant women and children is outlawed.”

“I am incredibly relieved that Maria is free. No pregnant woman should have to throw herself on the ground and beg for medical care, fear for her wellbeing and that of her pregnancy, or go without adequate food while in ICE custody,” Rep. Ansari said. “As soon as January, with a Democratic majority, we will use our oversight authority to investigate these abuses, demand answers, and hold this Administration accountable for their profound failure of human dignity.”

“I am grateful that Maria was released and will be able to continue her pregnancy outside the walls of an immigration detention facility,” Rep. Grijalva said. “No pregnant person should have to fight for medical attention or worry about the safety of their baby while in government custody. While Maria’s release is welcome news, it comes after the courts forced ICE’s hand, and it does not undo the harm she has already endured. Pregnant people do not belong in immigration detention.”

“Maria faced unconscionable treatment inside Eloy, and we worked with Reps. Grijalva, Ansari, and Dexter to make sure the country heard what ICE does to pregnant women held in detention centers,” said Reproductive Freedom for All President and CEO Mini Timmaraju. “Today we celebrate her freedom, and we urge the new Congress to act immediately to end ICE’s cruelty and abuses of power.”

BACKGROUND

During the visit, the lawmakers met directly with women detained at Eloy to hear about their experiences accessing reproductive health care, medical treatment, and basic necessities while in immigration detention. The visit focused on concerns about the treatment of pregnant women and the urgent need to protect reproductive health and ensure access to adequate medical care.

Maria, a 24-year-old Venezuelan woman and mother of a 6-year-old son, was approximately five months pregnant at the time of the visit. She had been detained since August and was living in Mesa, Arizona, before her detention. Maria has valid employment authorization through 2029, a pending asylum petition, and no criminal convictions.

During the meeting, Maria described serious concerns about her pregnancy and the lack of adequate medical care. She had experienced spotting and reported having to throw herself on the ground and plead for medical attention. When she was finally able to receive care, doctors informed her that she had a low-lying placenta—the same condition that led to a stillbirth three years earlier.

Despite her high-risk pregnancy, Maria said she had not been provided ultrasound images or adequate information about her and her pregnancy. She feared for their safety and well-being. She also expressed fear about showing emotional distress, given the possibility of being placed in solitary confinement.

Maria also raised concerns about access to drinking water and adequate food. Despite doctors recommending double food portions, she said a guard routinely dismissed the recommendation and provided only a standard portion. She also reported not receiving antibiotics following a dental abscess that resulted in a tooth extraction.

title: Fitzgerald Leads WI House Delegation in Honoring Victims Ahead of Fifth Anniversary of Waukesha Christmas Parade Attack
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Scott Fitzgerald (WI-05) led the entire Wisconsin House delegation in introducing a bipartisan House Resolution honoring the victims of the devastating 2021 Waukesha Christmas Parade attack ahead of the tragedy’s fifth anniversary.

“Nearly five years have passed since a horrific act of violence shattered what should have been a joyous celebration and claimed the lives of six innocent people: Wilhelm Hospel, Virginia Sorenson, LeAnna Owen, Tamara Durand, Jane Kulich, and Jackson Sparks,” said Congressman Scott Fitzgerald. “For the families who lost loved ones and a community forever changed, the passage of time does not diminish the weight of the loss. In the years since, Waukesha has demonstrated extraordinary strength and compassion, coming together to support one another and honor those taken far too soon. As we approach this solemn fifth anniversary, I am proud to stand alongside Wisconsin’s House delegation to ensure the names and stories of the six lives lost are never forgotten. May their memory endure for generations to come, forever held in the hearts and minds of all who call Waukesha home.”

title: Ranking Member Foushee's Opening Statement at Space Weather Hearing
text:
WASHINGTON, DC (November 19, 2026) — Today, the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology is holding a Space Subcommittee hearing titled, “Weathering the Solar Storm: Advancing America’s Space Weather Capabilities".

Space and Aeronautics Subcommittee Ranking Member Valerie Foushee (D-NC)'s opening statement is below as prepared for the record:

Good morning. Thank you, Chairman Babin, for hosting this committee hearing to review our national efforts to research, forecast, and mitigate the effects of space weather. I thank our two witnesses, from NASA and NOAA, for attending today as well.

We live in an increasingly technologically dependent society. If we did not realize this already, I think that all of us who had our e-mail communications disrupted, planes grounded and delayed, and bank accounts made inaccessible just in the last week have been reminded of it. And through my work on advancing responsible AI policy, I have emphasized the importance of ensuring that emerging technologies and the critical infrastructure we increasingly depend on are safe, secure, and reliable for the American public.

None of those disruptions were due to space weather phenomena, of course. But, as it turns out, they are all examples of the kinds of disruptions that can occur if a severe space storm hit Earth; such an event could degrade our power grid, aircraft radio communications, GPS satellites, and other critical infrastructure, with implications across our society. It has become important for operators across sectors as diverse as finance, transportation, agriculture, defense, cybersecurity, and communications to monitor space weather forecasts and know how to respond when an extreme event is predicted, just as they do for potential extreme terrestrial weather events, such as those we have experienced in my district and across North Carolina. And although they share the term “weather,” terrestrial and space weather are fundamentally different, and each requires specialized observations, models, and advanced forecasting capabilities to provide accurate predictions and protect lives, property, and critical infrastructure.

NASA and NOAA, who we will hear from today, as well as NSF, lead and support essential components of a robust space weather ecosystem, including the scientific foundation, observation systems, and the development of operational forecasts and predictions. These essential efforts require a considerable amount of coordination and collaboration across the federal government beyond these core agencies, as well as the necessary funding to sustain these critical activities.

The Science Committee—which many of us often fondly refer to as the Committee of the Future—has been on the case. In 2020, after many years of effort, Congress passed the Science Committee’s Promoting Research and Observations of Space Weather to Improve the Forecasting of Tomorrow Act, or the PROSWIFT Act, which codified the roles and responsibilities of many of the key agencies involved. The law also directed new activities to improve coordination across the federal government, the research community, and the end user community, while ensuring the advancement of basic research and the continuity of critical space weather observing systems.

This hearing provides an opportunity to assess progress in implementing PROSWIFT, and to identify any remaining challenges and potential opportunities moving forward.

I am concerned that much of the momentum for federal space weather activities that had been maintained under multiple Administrations and supported by Congress on a bipartisan basis may be stalled, as activity seems to have slowed, or even halted altogether, under the second Trump Administration.

I think we all know that we simply cannot afford to slow down here. Again, I thank our witnesses for appearing today, and I look forward to their testimony.

With that, I thank you, Mr. Chairman, and I yield back.

title: RELEASE: Momentum Continues Growing to Enact Federal Film Tax Credit with New Support Amongst House, Senate, and Key Stakeholders
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Momentum continues to grow for the bipartisan and bicameral Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, legislation to create a federal film tax incentive, with the addition of 60+ new cosponsors in the House, new bipartisan support in the Senate, and new key stakeholders. The legislation was introduced in September in the U.S. House of Representatives by Representatives Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas-1), Linda Sánchez (D-Calif.-38), Brian Jack (R-Ga.-3), and Laura Friedman (D-Calif.-30) and in the Senate by U.S. Senators Tim Scott (R-S.C.) and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.).

The new Senate cosponsors include: Senators Chris Coons (D-Del.), Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), Katie Britt (R-Ala.) and Dick Durbin (D-Ill.). The legislation is also cosponsored by Senators John Cornyn (R-Texas), Steve Daines (R-Mont.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Tim Sheehy (R-Mont.), Mark Warner (D-Va.), and Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.).

New organizations endorsing include: The American Federation of Labor and Congress of Industrial Organizations (AFL-CIO), American Hotel and Lodging Association (AHLA), the American Entertainment Alliance (AEA), The Internet and Television Association (NCTA), and the Laborers’ International Union of North America (LIUNA).

The introduction of the bill follows years of advocacy to create a nationwide tax credit for film and television production, a push recently echoed by President Donald Trump.

“Republicans and Democrats from every corner of the country keep signing on, because this is a national jobs issue with a commonsense fix. Crews in California, Georgia, Texas, New York, New Jersey, and beyond all want the same thing: to keep this industry in America instead of watching the work move overseas. I’m grateful to every partner who has joined this fight, and I’m ready to get a national film tax credit across the finish line,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman.

“The bipartisan coalition for our bill continues to grow, and I’m proud of the support we have gained from members of Congress representing different states across the country. This bill will create new jobs, boost our local economies, and stop the offshoring of film and TV production from leaving the United States, and it’s time we make this much-needed incentive a reality. Given the support from Republicans and Democrats in both chambers and the president, we can get this legislation across the finish line,” said Senator Schiff.

“Film and television production supports good-paying jobs and drives investment in communities far beyond Hollywood, including in states like Alabama,” said Senator Britt. “But for too long, countries have used aggressive incentives to lure American production companies, and the jobs that come with them, overseas. This bipartisan legislation would level the playing field and reward companies for bringing production back home. I’m proud to join my colleagues in this effort.”

“American film and television are some of our most successful cultural exports and engines of our economy,” said Senator Coons. “It’s worth investing in that power and creativity. I’m glad so many others from Democrats to Republicans to stakeholders agree, and we should keep working to move this bill forward.”

“American film and television productions support good-paying jobs, creative talent, and economic growth in communities across the country. We should be doing everything we can to ensure that these productions stay in the United States rather than move overseas to take advantage of more competitive incentives,” said Senator Durbin. “This legislation will help support American workers, strengthen our economy, and keep these jobs here at home.”

“North Carolina has a rich history in film and television production, and we should be doing everything we can to ensure that legacy continues,” said Senator Tillis. “This bipartisan legislation will help incentivize production companies to bring their projects and investments back to the United States, while supporting hardworking industry professionals and creating economic opportunities for North Carolina workers and businesses.”

“The bipartisan support behind this bill is there for a reason. The need is real. Members of both parties have watched jobs in their districts move overseas. Momentum is on our side, and we need to strike while the iron is hot by passing this bill before the end of the year,” said Congresswoman Linda Sánchez.

Organizations announced in September include the American Federation of Musicians; American Society of Composers, Authors, and Publishers (ASCAP); CreativeFuture; Coalition for American Production (CAP); Directors Guild of America (DGA); FilmUSA; Independent Film and Television Alliance (IFTA); International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees (IATSE); Laborers’ International Union of North America (LIUNA); Motion Picture Association (MPA); NCTA – The Internet & Television Association; Producers Guild of America (PGA); Screen Actors Guild – American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA); Teamsters; Television Academy; U.S. Film and Television Production Coalition; Writers Guild of America East (WGAE); and Writers Guild of America West (WGAW).

AFL-CIO also sent a letter urging Congress to support this legislation.

title: GARAMENDI AND SIMON INTRODUCE LEGISLATION TO PROTECT OUR LONG-TERM IMMIGRANT NEIGHBORS
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman John Garamendi (CA-08), Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren (CA-18) and Congressman Juan Vargas (CA-52) today announced the introduction of the Protect Our Neighbors Act, bicameral legislation to protect long-term immigrant residents who have lived and contributed to their communities for over 10 years.

This legislation was inspired by the story of Congressman Garamendi’s and Congresswoman Simon’s constituent, Harjit Kaur, a 73-year-old grandmother who, despite living in the United States for over thirty years, was cruelly detained and later deported by ICE.

“President Trump promised to go after the ‘worst of the worst’ in his immigration policy. Yet his administration has repeatedly decided to cruelly deport residents who have been working, paying taxes, and raising families in their communities for decades,” said Rep. Garamendi (CA-08). This is exactly what happened to one of our constituents. Nearly one year ago, ICE cruelly detained and deported Harjit Kuar, a 73-year-old grandmother with no criminal record — who faithfully reported to ICE every six months for more than 13 years. Her cruel and unreasonable detention and deportation is just one more example of the thousands of individuals across the country whose lives and families have been upended by Trump’s ICE. Unfortunately, this has become far too common under Donald Trump’s mass deportation agenda, which is exactly why I’m proud to introduce this commonsense and humane fix to our immigration system with Representatives Simon, Lofgren and Vargas.”

“No one should have to live in constant fear of being torn away from their family and community after spending years building a life in this country. I am sick of the Trump Administration targeting our neighbors and threatening the lives they have worked so hard to build. These are people who have spent years contributing to our communities, working hard, and putting down roots,” said Congresswoman Simon (CA-12). “The Protect Our Neighbors Act would provide people, like Ms. Kaur who worked in my district for decades, with a fair opportunity to move beyond a final order of removal and continue building futures here in the U.S where they have made their homes and families. I am incredibly grateful to Congressmembers Garamendi, Lofgren, and Vargas for standing with me and partnering on this important legislation.”

“We need a sensible immigration policy for those who have resided peacefully for a long time in America and have been upstanding members of their communities,” said Congresswoman Lofgren (CA-18), a senior member of the House Judiciary Committee and a former immigration lawyer. “Detaining and deporting folks with no criminal record is not what Donald Trump campaigned on, and it’s not what the American people want. The Protect Our Communities Act provides long-term residents who have built their lives here with a fair opportunity to resolve outdated removal orders and earn lawful permanent status.”

“The Trump Administration’s anti-immigrant agenda is destroying lives. Trump isn’t going after the ‘worst of the worst,’” said Congressman Vargas (CA-52). “He’s terrorizing our communities and ripping families apart. I’m proud to introduce this legislation alongside Representatives Garamendi, Simon, and Lofgren to bring a commonsense fix to our immigration system. We need comprehensive immigration reform and an end to Trump’s mass deportation agenda.”

“We are still traumatized and horrified by the cruel treatment of our grandmother one year ago,” said Harjit Kaur’s family. “Harjit was a pillar to our family and our community. She spent over thirty years in the United States, raising her children and later her grandchildren, and became a grandmother figure to our whole community. What was worse about her treatment was how unnecessary it was. We tried to work with ICE to bring her back to India, but at every turn the agency chose the more violent and cruel path — denying her food, moving her in the middle of the night without letting us know, and sending her back without letting us say goodbye. The pain that we still feel today remains with the knowledge that Harjit is one of thousands who’ve experienced the same situation. We thank Congressman Garamendi, Senator Schiff, and Congresswoman Simon for their continued advocacy, and we hope that some good could come from Harjit’s story with this bill and others like it.”

BACKGROUND:

A final order of removal is a formal legal order requiring a noncitizen to leave the U.S., but it doesn’t always mean immediate removal. Removal can be delayed through deferred action, a stay, ongoing litigation, or other circumstances.

According to the American Immigration Council, roughly 1.19 million people with removal orders remain in the U.S., many having spent years building lives, raising families, and working here. Under President Trump, DHS and ICE have aggressively pursued individuals with final removal orders, regardless of how long the case had been deferred, putting long-term residents who have routinely complied with check-ins at renewed risk of detention and deportation.

The Protect Our Communities Act aims to protect these long-standing immigrants by:

Establishing a 10-year expiration on final orders of removal for individuals who have been continuously present in the U.S. and have not been convicted of a crime.

Amending the Immigration and Nationality Act to create a pathway to lawful permanent residency (green card) for individuals with expired orders of removal. This pathway includes an application fee and requirement to confirm an individual’s taxpaying status.

HARJIT KAUR BACKGROUND

Harjit Kaur, 73, had lived in the U.S. since the early 1990s and was a constituent of Congressman John Garamendi. After her asylum case was denied in 2012, she complied with ICE check-ins every six months for over 13 years.

On September 8, 2025, she was detained during a routine check-in and held at an ICE facility in Bakersfield. At around 2:00 am on September 19, she was transported in handcuffs to Los Angeles, flown to Georgia without notice to her family or attorney, and then placed on a charter flight to India — deported before her family, who had arranged to travel with her, could say goodbye.

Kaur had sought travel documents from the Indian Consulate but was reportedly turned away multiple times; she had not refused to return but couldn’t depart without valid documents. During her detention, she was held without a bed, forced to sleep on the floor, shackled during transfers, denied vegetarian meals for her religious beliefs, and denied adequate food, water, and medication.

Since her return to India, she has remained in contact with family but continues to face health issues without relatives nearby to help her.

title: Rep. Gillen Slams FAA After Audit Confirms Failures in Relocation of Long Island Air Traffic Controllers
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) slammed the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) following the release of an audit by the Department of Transportation’s (DOT) Office of Inspector General (OIG) confirming significant failures in the agency’s decision to relocate 12 air traffic controllers and transfer responsibilities from New York control center TRACON N90 to Philadelphia.

The audit was announced in 2025 after Rep. Gillen pressured FAA leadership for answers on the relocation and urged U.S. Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy to visit N90 following multiple outages. The audit found that the FAA failed to develop a comprehensive plan to address potential safety risks before transferring operations.

“As I said from the start, relocating air traffic controllers from Long Island to Philadelphia was a deeply misguided decision that put the safety of our airspace at risk,” said Rep. Gillen. “I demanded answers from the FAA and Secretary Duffy about this, and the audit that followed confirms exactly what I feared. The FAA failed to adequately assess the risks and put one of the busiest air traffic control hubs in the country in a dangerous position. The FAA must take responsibility for these failures, act on this report and ensure TRACON N90 has the staffing and resources needed to keep the public safe.”

During the summer of 2024, the FAA relocated 12 air traffic controllers responsible for overseeing Newark Liberty International Airport from N90 on Long Island to the Philadelphia Air Traffic Control Tower (PHL) and transferred responsibilities for the airspace. After this relocation, the radar and communications systems that help controllers direct planes in and out of Newark failed repeatedly, leaving controllers unable to see or talk to planes in the area.

The OIG audit found that the FAA failed to develop a comprehensive staffing plan or properly assess the risks before transferring Newark-area airspace operations to Philadelphia. The agency also failed to account for outdated documentation in its risk assessments. The report includes three recommendations to improve the FAA's planning, risk assessment and response to operational challenges. This includes creating a comprehensive framework for future relocations, updating operating procedures for both N90 and PHL and ensuring that the Newark feed for PHL is fully functional.

As a member of the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, Rep. Gillen has been a leading advocate for Long Island's air traffic controllers and aviation safety. She previously met with New York members of the National Air Traffic Controllers Association (NATCA) to discuss supporting the air traffic controller workforce and modernizing aviation technology. Rep. Gillen also met with air traffic controllers and FAA officials at N90 in Westbury to discuss staffing shortages and working conditions. After the FAA announced its audit, Rep. Gillen visited TRACON N90 and applauded the decision.

In 2025, Rep. Gillen introduced the bipartisan Military Air Traffic Control Transition Act to address the nationwide air traffic controller shortage by streamlining military controllers into civilian roles. In 2026, she also introduced the bipartisan Air Traffic Situational Awareness Enhancement Act to equip air traffic controllers with modern tools and training to strengthen aviation safety. Rep. Gillen is a cosponsor of the Aviation Funding Solvency Act to protect FAA operations and air traffic controller pay during government shutdowns.

Earlier this week, Rep. Gillen urged Secretary Duffy to testify before the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee to provide answers on the November 13th national ground stop, the billions of dollars Congress has already provided for air traffic control modernization and the Secretary’s request for $50 billion in additional funding for the FAA.

title: Golden introduces bipartisan bill to stop feds from charging children for erroneous Social Security payments to their parents
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Jared Golden (ME-02) and Don Bacon (NE-02) today introduced the bipartisan Children Are Relieved of Overpayments Act, which stops the Social Security Administration (SSA) from charging children for overpayments made to their parents after those parents have died.

“Losing a parent at any age is already one of the most difficult things you can go through, and the last thing anyone needs when dealing with that kind of grief is to be left holding the bag for the government’s mistakes,” Golden said. “Many of these children have reached out to our office, desperate for relief from a debt they did not incur and often never knew existed. Any self-respecting society would see the problem for what it is and put an end to this cruel practice.”

“Children should not be forced to pay for mistakes they did not make, and the federal government should be held accountable when it makes those mistakes,” Bacon said. “I'm joining Rep. Golden to introduce the Children Are Relieved of Overpayments Act to protect children from unfair Social Security repayment demands and ensure Americans are notified of overpayments in a timely manner. No family should be blindsided by a government repayment demand decades later.”

Overpayments occur when SSA overpays beneficiaries by mistake. Current law allows SSA to claw back those overpayments from the recipient’s dependents, including children. The SSA also has no fixed deadline to notify someone of an overpayment before recovering it, meaning an individual can be hit with collection demands for mistakes made decades earlier, resulting in a loss in benefits or unexpected debt.

As a result, it’s possible for overpayments to occur and for SSA to not notice the mistake until after the recipient has passed away.

The Children Are Relieved of Overpayments Act implements the following:

Bars SSA from recovering an overpayment from a child beneficiary when it was made to a parent receiving Social Security disability benefits while the child in their care received dependent benefits.

Creates a six-year deadline for SSA to act on overpayments in both Social Security and SSI, so that SSA cannot adjust future payments or recover an overpayment from anyone unless it notifies them within six years of the date the overpayment was made. This rule also would apply to overpayments outstanding and not yet collected at enactment.

Full text of the bill can be found here.

title: Goodlander, Flood Continue Bipartisan Push to Cut Federal Delays Holding Up Affordable Homes
text:
Lawmakers urge HUD and the Made in America Office to streamline Buy America waivers, building on their bipartisan Build Housing Affordably Act

Washington, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) and Congressman Mike Flood (NE-01) led a bipartisan letter urging the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and the Made in America Office to cut unnecessary bureaucratic delays that are driving up housing costs and holding back affordable housing developments across the country.

Requirements under the Build America, Buy America (BABA) Act have devastated affordable housing projects across New Hampshire and New England, where builders are prevented from acquiring necessary materials due to strict sourcing requirements. Impacted projects have included a 126-unit affordable housing project in Manchester; an expansion of the New Hampshire Veterans Home in Tilton; a rooftop solar installation in Conway; and a housing project in Whitefield, among others.

Goodlander and Flood’s letter calls on HUD and MIAO to improve implementation of BABA by establishing targeted waivers for construction products facing persistent domestic shortages and streamlining waiver review.

“Granite Staters are being priced out of the communities they love, and the last thing they need is Washington making it harder and more expensive to build homes,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “We can support American workers, strengthen American manufacturing, and build more affordable housing. These goals should go hand in hand. I’m proud to be working on a bipartisan basis with Congressman Flood to press HUD to cut through unnecessary red tape, lower construction costs, and make sure federal bureaucracy isn’t standing in the way of homes that Granite States desperately need.”

“New housing shouldn’t have to wait months for federal paperwork to be approved, driving up compliance costs and putting additional pressure on budgets,” said Congressman Flood. “We need to modernize and streamline the current BABA waiver process to reduce hurdles for builders and communities working to address housing shortages across the country. I’m glad to join Congresswoman Goodlander and my colleagues in calling on HUD and MIAO to make commonsense changes that will help get more housing on the market while also continuing to support domestic manufacturing.”

“We share the goal of building everything we need right here in America but the reality is, those markets don’t exist. Electric transformers sit on overseas docks in Poland waiting to come to America – but federal red tape prohibits this vital piece of equipment from powering our homes,” said Matt Mayberry, CEO, New Hampshire Home Builders Association. “We need an aggressive approach to granting waivers. We applaud the efforts of Representatives Goodlander and Flood and stand behind them. We want to build homes for the American workforce. We want it done safely, effectively and efficiently. Until the United States develops manufacturing plants for every single item needed to build homes, release the bureaucratic shackles and let us do our jobs.”

“The affordable housing crisis in New Hampshire is solvable,” said Nick Taylor, Executive Director of Housing Action NH. “But we need to make it easier, faster, and less expensive to build the homes our communities desperately need. That includes ensuring federal requirements like BAB don’t unnecessarily delay projects or drive up costs when materials aren’t available. Targeted waivers and a faster, more predictable review process would help housing providers spend less time navigating red tape and more time building homes. We thank Congresswoman Goodlander and Congressman Flood for their continued bipartisan leadership in making federal housing dollars go further.”

Build America, Buy America establishes domestic sourcing requirements for iron, steel, manufactured products, and construction materials used in federally assisted infrastructure projects. As HUD has implemented those requirements across housing programs, affordable housing providers have raised concerns about difficulty finding compliant products, documenting complex supply chains, and securing timely waiver decisions, which in some cases have taken more than a year. The lawmakers’ push addresses this problem, which has resulted in increased financing and construction costs, missed deadlines, and less home production.

Affordable housing developments often combine federal, state, local, and private financing. Uncertainty over one federal requirement can disrupt an entire financing package and construction schedule. Targeted waivers for products that remain difficult to source domestically, together with more efficient agency review, would help housing providers plan projects and put housing dollars to work.

In their letter, Goodlander and Flood urge HUD and MIAO to take two immediate steps to address these challenges:

Establish targeted waivers for products facing persistent domestic supply shortages.Rather than requiring individual housing developments to repeatedly request waivers for the same hard-to-source materials, HUD and MIAO should establish product-specific or category-based waivers where domestic supply is insufficient. These waivers could be time-limited to allow American manufacturers to expand production while keeping affordable housing projects moving.

Streamline the federal waiver review process. HUD and MIAO should eliminate duplicative reviews, improve coordination between agencies, and establish more predictable timelines for waiver decisions. These changes would reduce unnecessary administrative burdens, provide greater certainty for housing developers, and help prevent costly construction delays.

The letter builds on HUD’s recent efforts to identify products facing persistent domestic supply challenges and urges the agencies to use that information to implement practical reforms that preserve BABA’s goals while making the process more efficient.

ADDITIONAL BACKGROUND

In September, Goodlander led the New Hampshire congressional delegation in a letter urging the VA and the Made in America Office to expedite review of a narrow BABA waiver for the New Hampshire Veterans Home’s 20-room expansion project in Tilton. Goodlander pressed for a timely decision to prevent construction delays, contractor disruption, and added taxpayer costs over products representing less than one percent of the project’s cost.

Goodlander and Flood have worked together to address federal barriers to affordable housing development, including through their bipartisan Build Housing Affordably Act, which they introduced in June. The bill would:

Require HUD to measure BABA’s impact on affordable housing. Their bill directs HUD to study material costs, administrative and compliance expenses, waiver-related costs, construction delays, incomplete projects, and homes not built because of compliance burdens. It also requires a review of the BABA waiver process after numerous reports of delays.

Provide a temporary pause for covered housing projects. Their bill would pause implementation of BABA requirements for covered projects until 60 days after HUD delivers its report to Congress.

Put a deadline on waiver decisions. Their bill requires HUD to decide covered waiver requests within 90 days of receiving them. If HUD misses that deadline, the waiver would be deemed granted, final, and irrevocable.

When they introduced the bill, Goodlander and Flood drew support from more than 30 national housing organizations, including Habitat for Humanity International, the National Association of Home Builders, the National Council of State Housing Agencies, and the National Low Income Housing Coalition. New Hampshire Housing, Housing Action NH, and the New Hampshire Home Builders Association also welcomed their effort to streamline the process and help build more affordable homes.

title: PHOTO RELEASE: Gottheimer Keeps Hangar Tenants in Place After Working with Governor Sherrill, NJDEP, and Local Electeds to Pause Evictions at Andover-Aeroflex
text:
Above: Gottheimer tours Andover Aeroflex with NJDEP Commissioner.

ANDOVER, NJ — Following weeks of pressure, conversations, and meetings from Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5), the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) has paused the eviction notices it sent to tenants at Andover-Aeroflex Airport in Sussex County. The pause keeps woman-owned Andover Flight Academy, the airport’s aircraft maintenance shop, and several other aircraft owners from their hangars. Gottheimer worked with the NJDEP, the Governor’s office, the airport’s tenants, the mayor, and other local elected officials to get there.

On October 16, Gottheimer toured the airport with NJDEP Commissioner Ed Potosnak, Andover Mayor Tom Walsh, and state officials. He brought two engineering and demolition experts to review the condition of the hangars first-hand.

“The Andover-Aeroflex Airport is a Sussex County treasure, and the flight school, the mechanics, and the pilots who rely on it deserve straight answers and a real plan, not an eviction notice,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “I’m glad the NJDEP heard us and hit pause, and I thank Commissioner Potosnak, the Governor Sherrill, Mayor Walsh, and the tenants who stood up for this airport. This is a big step toward keeping it permanently open, and I will keep fighting until these tenants are in place for good and the necessary changes are made to keep this airport strong.”

“I would like to take a moment to personally thank Rep. Gottheimer for the work he and his team have done on our behalf. When things were looking decidedly bleak, he picked up the mantle and worked on our behalf far above anything I expected or could have hoped for. I’m generally not a political person and had no idea what to expect. What I found was a dedicated representative who truly has the interests of his constituents at heart, and frankly that is refreshing. Regardless of your politics, I truly believe he cares about the people in our district. There’s still a lot of work left, and with Josh at the helm, I feel heartened about the future and preservation of Aeroflex,” said Damian Delgaizo of Andover Flight.

“We are very relieved and grateful to have reached this positive outcome regarding the hangar situation at Andover airport. We are deeply grateful to everyone in the community who stood behind us throughout this process. The support and encouragement shown by so many people have meant more than words can express. We want to extend a special thank you to the US Representative Josh Gottheimer whose efforts were instrumental in helping us reach this outcome and we truly appreciate his willingness to step up and help when it mattered most. He showed us the kind of dedication, commitment to the community, and leadership that makes a real difference. With his support, we are confident we can achieve a lasting solution for the airport and preserve it as an asset to our community,” said Justine Pasniewski, a co-owner and full-time flight instructor (CFI) at Andover Flight Academy.

“The Aircraft Owners & Pilots Association greatly appreciates Representative Gottheimer, as well as the state and local officials, who have rallied support for Aeroflex-Andover Airport. This airport is an irreplaceable general aviation facility and an important asset to New Jersey. With the Congressman’s help, AOPA and the general aviation community look forward to a long-term solution that will preserve it for future generations,” said Leon Jackler, J.D. CFI-I, Vice President of Airports and State Advocacy, Aircraft Owners & Pilots Association.

“I would like to thank Congressman Gotheimer for his efforts in stalling the demolition of the Aeroflex-Andover airport hangars. We at Andover Township look forward to working with the Congressman, as well as LD-24, in seeking a permanent resolution. The Congressman has always been a good friend to our Township,” said Thomas Walsh, Mayor of Andover Township.

The pause follows a sustained push by Gottheimer. On October 1, the NJDEP issued eviction notices to the tenants, and the State planned to demolish the airport’s hangars. On October 2, Gottheimer held a press conference at the airport asking the NJDEP to rescind the notices. On October 5, he sent a letter to Governor Mikie Sherrill and Commissioner Potosnak making the same request and asking the Commissioner to tour the facility. The Commissioner toured the site on October 16.

The stakes were high for local businesses. The Andover Flight Academy has taught New Jersey residents to fly for 40 years and is nationally known for tailwheel and bush-flying instruction. People and the U.S. military travel across the country and the world to be trained at the flight school, including Harrison Ford. The maintenance shop is the only one in the area, and it keeps the airport’s planes airworthy. Many of those aircraft are fabric-covered vintage airplanes and cannot safely be kept on outdoor tie-downs. Additionally, there is a shortage of hangar spaces across Jersey, and many airplane owners are on years-long waitlists to get a hangar. Local pilots and advocates warned that demolishing the income-producing hangars would remove the airport’s revenue base and its tenants, putting the field on a path toward eventual closure.

The pause on evictions and extensions offered by the NJDEP is a step in the right direction. Gottheimer will continue to work with the State to find a permanent solution that supports the small businesses, tenants, and Forest Fire Service that call the Andover-Aeroflex home.

title: Memorial Tree Dedicated to Congressman Raúl M. Grijalva During Ceremony in Front of the United States Capitol
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, the Architect of the Capitol dedicated a memorial tree during a ceremony in front of the U.S. Capitol honoring the life and legacy of Congressman Raúl M. Grijalva. The bur oak tree was dedicated in Rep. Grijalva’s honor with the support of Congressional Hispanic Caucus Chairman Adriano Espaillat. Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva released the below statement following the event:

“My dad, Congressman Raúl M. Grijalva, dedicated his life to fighting for our most vulnerable communities, championing justice and equity for all, and believing in our shared responsibility to leave behind a better world for future generations. Like the values he championed, this oak tree will stand strong and continue to grow long after we are gone. It is only fitting that Congressman Grijalva’s legacy takes root in the heart of our nation’s capital, where his service and commitment to the people will never be forgotten. Grijalva's lifetime of integrity, resilience, and principled leadership. title: Grothman Announces 2026 Congressional App Challenge Winner for Wisconsin’s Sixth Congressional District
text:
Congressman Glenn Grothman (R-WI) announced that Anderson Kirby, a student at Cedarburg High School, has won the 2026 Congressional App Challenge for Wisconsin’s Sixth Congressional District.

Anderson developed Focus, a task management application designed to help students organize their schoolwork by tracking assignments, notes, and calendars all in one place.

The app integrates with Canvas, a learning management platform used by thousands of schools and universities nationwide, and Google Calendar to automatically import assignments and other tasks. Users can also create their own tasks and notes, making the app useful for both academic and everyday organization.

“I want to congratulate Anderson on winning this year’s Congressional App Challenge,” said Grothman. “It’s encouraging to see students in Wisconsin’s Sixth District using their creativity and technical skills to solve everyday problems. Anderson recognized a challenge that many students face and took the initiative to develop a practical solution. I commend him for his hard work and look forward to seeing how he continues to develop his talents.”

“One thing that stood out this year was how often students started with a problem they knew firsthand,” said Joseph Alessi, Program Director of the Congressional App Challenge. “They saw a need at school, at home, or in their community and got to work figuring out what an app could do about it.”

Focus’s mobile version is currently undergoing private beta testing, while the web version is publicly available.

To learn more about Anderson’s application and watch his demonstration video, click here.

Background Information

The Congressional App Challenge is an official initiative of the U.S. House of Representatives and the nation’s largest student coding competition. Since 2015, participating Members of Congress have hosted local competitions for middle and high school students to build original apps and develop their computer science skills. The Internet Education Foundation administers the program on behalf of the House.

17,211 students across the country registered to participate in this year’s Challenge, which was hosted by 387 Members of Congress.

Challenge winners will have their names displayed in the US Capitol Building and featured on House.gov for one year. Winners will also receive an invitation to attend #HouseofCode at the U.S. Capitol in April 2027 and have their submission’s copyright registration fees waived.

title: Guthrie, National Institutes of Health Director Bhattacharya Tour University of Louisville Research Facilities
text:
LOUISVILLE, KY – On Monday, Congressman Brett Guthrie (KY-02), Chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, and Dr. Jay Bhattacharya, Director of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), visited the University of Louisville to meet with researchers and see the transformative work being done on campus to improve the health of Americans.

“I am grateful to the entire University of Louisville community for giving a warm welcome to Director of the National Institutes of Health Dr. Jay Bhattacharya and me this week,” said Chairman Guthrie. “I enjoyed seeing the important research being done on campus to improve health outcomes for patients battling diseases like cancer, keep Americans safe from newly emerging infectious diseases, and develop comprehensive strategies to prevent ailments in patients before they arise. I appreciate Director Bhattacharya making the trip to Kentucky to see the impacts of NIH research grants at institutions in our Commonwealth.

“Visiting the University of Louisville with Chairman Guthrie was a great opportunity to see how NIH investments translate into real progress for patients,” said Director Bhattacharya. “The scientists and students I met are tackling some of our toughest health challenges, and I came away encouraged by their talent and commitment. NIH is proud to support this work in Kentucky."

"The University of Louisville has a national reputation as a research powerhouse. This week, we were proud to welcome National Institutes of Health Director Dr. Jay Bhattacharya and U.S. Rep. Brett Guthrie to see firsthand the work taking place at our university and hear from the people behind it, said University of Louisville President Dr. Gerry Bradley. "I especially enjoyed the conversations with our students and researchers, who are doing exciting work to improve lives here in Kentucky and far beyond. UofL has a great deal to contribute to the future of health and discovery, and I’m proud to share that work with our visitors."

During their visit, Chairman Guthrie and Director Bhattacharya visited several research laboratories including: the Center for Cancer Immunology and Immunotherapy, Nutrition and Metabolic Health Center, Center for Predictive Medicine for Biodefense and Emerging Infectious Diseases, and the Louisville Clinical and Translational Research Center. The pair also joined student researchers for lunch on campus, met with senior leadership at the university, and participated in a campus-wide fireside chat with UofL students.

Pictures from this week’s visit can be found HERE.

Background:

Early this year, Congress appropriated $48.7 billion for Fiscal Year 2026 for the NIH as part of H.R. 7148, the Consolidated Appropriations Act,2026. This topline funding is an increase of $415 million compared to Fiscal Year 2025.

In total, for Fiscal Year 2025, the University of Louisville was awarded $220 million in research expenditures and $170.2 million in competitive awards to support 857 grants and projects, and 263 clinical trials. Today, the University of Louisville ranks 71st in NIH funding among U.S. medical schools, up from 75th the year prior.

title: Houchin Introduces Bill to Increase Parental Control Over Screen-Based Instruction
text:
WASHINGTON—Congresswoman Erin Houchin (IN-09) introduced H.R. 11058, Families’ Option to Choose Unplugged Schooling (FOCUS) Act. Companion legislation has been introduced in the U.S. Senate by Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV).

Concern about classroom screen time has grown rapidly, and at least four states have enacted laws in 2026 to limit or regulate classroom screen time. The FOCUS Act would ensure Federal Communications Commission E-Rate support goes to schools that give parents a meaningful ability to opt their children out of screen-based instruction. The FOCUS Act does not mandate anything of states or schools. It attaches conditions to a voluntary federal subsidy and does not change E-Rate's funding baseline.

“Parents know their kids best, and they should have a real say in how much of the school day their children spend staring at a screen,” said Congresswoman Houchin. “Research increasingly shows that excessive classroom screen time can undermine learning, and families deserve a choice. The FOCUS in the Classroom Act is a commonsense step that attaches one simple condition to federal dollars: if a school takes E-Rate funding, it must give parents an option for unplugged instruction. I’m proud to lead this effort with Senator Capito to put parents back in the driver’s seat.”

“West Virginia parents deserve to have a say in how their children learn. Unfortunately, studies continue to show that increased screen time negatively affects the way our youth are learning. It is critical to ensure our children’s academic success, which is why I’m proud to introduce the FOCUS Act because our children deserve an education that balances technology with traditional learning,” Senator Capito said.

“Federal broadband policy should put student outcomes first, follow the evidence, and respect parents’ role in decisions about their children’s technology use,” said Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Communications and Information and NTIA Administrator Arielle Roth. “As NTIA Administrator, I have made it a priority to bring parents, students, teachers, and child development experts to the table because those closest to what is happening in classrooms deserve a say in the programs that affect them. I thank Senator Capito for her leadership and partnership in this effort to give parents greater control over their children’s education and ensure federal funding serves the interests of students and families.”

“Every-day American parents deserve the right to enroll their children in screenless education, without having to pay tens of thousands of dollars per year for a specialized school. Senator Capito and Congresswoman Houchin’s FOCUS Act allows for just that, without taking the screens away from other children in the classroom,” said Janet Kelly, CEO, Alliance for a Better Future.

Specifically, the FOCUS in the Classroom Act:

Directs the FCC, within one year, to amend its E-Rate rules so that, as a condition of funding, covered schools give parents an option for non-screen-based instruction.

Prohibits schools from penalizing students who opt out and requires that opted-out students cover the same material through other means.

Requires schools to file annual compliance certifications with the FCC, which the FCC posts in a public, searchable database.

Protects schools from penalties when they act in good faith and promptly fix any known violation, and gives schools up to two years after enactment to comply.

Clarifies that schools are not required to monitor incidental device use by opted-out students.

Background:

Congresswoman Erin Houchin serves on the House Energy & Commerce Committee, which has jurisdiction over E-Rate. She has led multiple efforts to ensure parents have the choice and ability to protect their children online, including H.R. 10337, 16 & Up Social Media Act.

The FOCUS Act is endorsed by Do No Harm and the Alliance for a Better Future.

title: Jayapal Introduces Legislation to Create Jobs, Address Climate Crisis
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) is introducing the Climate Workforce Resilience Act, legislation to make bold investments in building a skilled workforce that is capable of preparing for and responding to the climate crisis while creating millions of jobs and centering communities that are disproportionately affected by the harms of climate change.

“Wildfires, floods, droughts — across the board, climate disasters are getting worse and more destructive,” said Jayapal. “These disasters cause billions of dollars in damages every year, affecting millions of Americans. My Climate Workforce Resilience Act will invest in a skilled workforce capable of responding on the scale necessary to rebuild homes and communities, as well as prepare more susceptible communities before disaster strikes.”

In 2025, 23 individual weather and climate disasters caused at least $1 billion in damages. The total direct cost in 2025 was approximately $115 billion.

The Climate Resilience Workforce Act would:

Create millions of climate resilience jobs through grants to states, counties, cities, tribal governments, labor organizations, and community-based nonprofit organizations.

Remove barriers to employment in climate resilience jobs based on immigration status by providing a roadmap to citizenship for workers employed in climate resilience sectors or in workforce training programs.

Remove barriers to employment based on prior involvement with the criminal justice system by prohibiting employers from inquiring about criminal history before an offer has been made and providing protections against offer revocation.

Create new and fund existing workforce development programs through grants that train workers for employment within climate resilience sectors, with a priority for pre-apprenticeship and apprenticeship programs.

Fund the development of regional, state, local, and community-based climate resilience action plans that center frontline communities and identify effective strategies to achieve climate resilience.

Create an Office of Climate Resilience within the White House that would focus on planning, worker protection, and equity.

The legislation is co-sponsored by Representatives André Carson (IN-07), Adelita S. Grijalva (AZ-07), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), and Rashida Tlaib (MI-12).

title: Kaptur Celebrates $6.7 Million US Dept of Health and Human Services Investment in Toledo Head Start
text:
Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, announced that the Toledo Public Schools Head Start program will receive $6,735,6888 to serve Toledo-area preschoolers and families. The award is administered through the US Department of Health and Human Services’ (HHS) Administration for Children and Families.

“All Northwest Ohio children deserve an opportunity to learn and grow in a supportive and caring environment,” said Congresswoman Kaptur (OH-09). “Toledo’s Head Start programs provide just that, giving opportunity to countless children in our communities year after year. I am honored to have secured this significant investment in our very local Head Start programs that will empower them to continue investing in our children who are the future of our City and our region.”

“Toledo Public Schools extends its sincere thanks to Congresswoman Kaptur for her continued advocacy and support of our students and families,” said Dr. Romules Durant, Superintendent of Toledo Public Schools. “This $6,735,686 installment of our $13,471,372 Head Start grant directly strengthens our early childhood programming, allowing us to move forward without interruption to provide high-quality learning environments, nutrition, and wrap-around family services that set our youngest learners on a path to lifelong success.”

Head Start, along with its companion program Early Head Start, helps children under the age of 5 and their families prepare for school. Through learning experiences, health assessments, family support, and early intervention, Head Start serves more than 25,000 young children throughout Ohio.

title: NPR: Incoming House majority leader Katherine Clark stresses Democratic unity
text:
House Democrats needed a bigger room Wednesday to accommodate their newly expanded caucus, according to Rep. Katherine Clark of Massachusetts.

Nominated to become the first woman to serve as House majority leader next year, Clark reflected on the moment in an interview with Morning Edition on Thursday.

“It was really looking at the diversity of that caucus, people who have been sent to Congress from all walks of life, that gives me the optimism and the energy that we can really deliver for the American people,” she said.

Clark, who is currently the House minority whip, was nominated for House majority leader by a unanimous voice vote. Democrats also nominated Hakeem Jeffries for speaker and Pete Aguilar for majority whip.

The incoming leadership faces the challenge of lowering living costs while investigating alleged corruption in the Trump administration.

“Of course we can,” she said when asked whether Democrats could accomplish both. “That’s our responsibility.”

She also called President Trump’s description of himself as “Mr. Veto” a “stunning statement,” expressing hope for bipartisan cooperation on healthcare.

But Democrats face divisions within their own ranks.

Jeffries won his nomination 251-11. Opposition came from incoming progressives including Darializa Avila Chevalier of New York and Adam Hamawy of New Jersey. They have pressed for Medicare for All, immigration enforcement reforms and an end to the war in Gaza.

The two leaders have differed over U.S. aid to Israel. In July, Clark voted for a Republican amendment that would have cut aid to Israel, while Jeffries opposed it.

Despite that disagreement and concerns among other Democrats about Jeffries’ leadership, she emphasized party unity when asked whether the 11 votes against him could complicate Democrats’ agenda.

“We are having conversations with every part of our new caucus, and they are united behind making life better for working people,” she said.

—
