title: Reps. Laurel Lee and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez Host Paris Hilton to Urge Passage of the DEFIANCE Act
text:
Washington, D.C. – This week, Congresswomen Laurel Lee (FL-15) and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14) joined Paris Hilton, fellow House members, and advocates at the U.S. Capitol for a press conference urging the passage of the Disrupt Explicit Forged Images and Non-Consensual Edits Act (DEFIANCE Act), bipartisan legislation that would grant survivors the right to take civil action against individuals who knowingly produce, distribute, solicit, receive, or possess with the intent to distribute nonconsensual sexually explicit digital forgeries.

Congresswoman Lee, Congresswoman Ocasio-Cortez, Paris Hilton, and advocates previously gathered in January to urge the passage of the DEFIANCE Act. The renewed bipartisan effort today emphasizes the importance of strengthening protections for women and children targeted by sexually explicit deepfakes and ensure victims have the legal recourse they deserve.

“The images may be fake, but the victims are real, their suffering is real, and their right to seek justice should be real, too,”said Congresswoman Laurel Lee.“As artificial intelligence continues to advance, we must ensure our laws keep pace with emerging threats and protect women and children from online sexual exploitation. The bipartisan DEFIANCE Act gives victims meaningful legal tools to seek justice and hold perpetrators accountable. I am pleased to work alongside Congresswoman Ocasio-Cortez, Paris Hilton, and the courageous survivors and advocates who have brought national attention to this issue. Protecting victims and holding perpetrators accountable should never be a partisan issue, and I urge my colleagues to come together and support this critical legislation.”

“Every single day that the DEFIANCE Act does not pass is a day that more children, women, and people are victimized with no recourse and that there is no accountability for abusers and predators. And so what it means is that thousands of people in this country, if not tens of thousands and eventually millions, could be subject to sexual abuse on our watch just due to complacency.”said Representative Ocasio-Cortez.“I am grateful for the support of my co-lead Representative Laurel Lee, Paris Hilton and the Democratic and Republican Women’s Caucuses in pushing this critical legislation across the finish line.”

“The Defiance Act would give survivors a civil path to hold people accountable for creating and distributing non-consensual, sexually explicit deep fakes. The Senate understood the urgency and passed this legislation unanimously in January. Now the House must act too,”said Paris Hilton.“Why wait another day? If they don't pass this bill before the end of the year, all of our progress will be lost and we will have to start all over again.”

Stefan Turkheimer, RAINN VP of Public Policy: "RAINN is grateful to Congresswomen Ocasio-Cortez and Lee for their bipartisan leadership in fighting for the DEFIANCE Act. Deepfake sexual abuse causes real harm, and survivors deserve a path to justice. The Senate has acted. Now it’s the House’s turn to stand for survivors and give them their day in court."

The DEFIANCE Act would establish a federal civil right of action for victims of nonconsensual sexually explicit digital forgeries, allowing survivors to seek damages and hold perpetrators accountable. The legislation builds on progress made through the TAKE IT DOWN Act, signed into law in May 2025, by providing victims with a legal avenue to seek justice for the damage caused by exploitation.

In January 2026, the Senate passed the DEFIANCE Act by unanimous consent, demonstrating broad bipartisan support for addressing digital sexual exploitation. Congresswoman Lee, Congresswoman Ocasio-Cortez, and advocates are continuing their efforts to secure passage in the House and send the legislation to the President’s desk.

title: Congresswoman Simon Introduces New Immigration Bill to Protect Community Members from Deportation and Create Pathway to Status
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Congressman John Garamendi (CA-08), and Congressman Juan Vargas (CA-52) introduced new legislation called the Protect Our Neighbors Act, which would provide relief to individuals with final orders of removal and create a pathway for them to obtain legal permanent residency.

There are approximately 1.19 million individuals in the United States living with final orders of removal.[1] However, a final order of removal does not mean someone will necessarily be deported. For many, removal may be delayed or suspended for years, including through deferred action or other circumstances. During that time, they build lives and become valued members of their community. These individuals raise families, work essential jobs, pay taxes, and put down meaningful roots in the only home they may have known for decades. Yet, despite the lives they have built, these individuals live with the uncertainty of being separated from their families and communities at any moment. For 73-year-old East Bay resident and Sikh community member, Ms. Harjit Kaur, that uncertainty became reality as a result of Trump’s cruel mass deportation agenda. Last year, Ms. Kaur was abruptly arrested during a routine immigration check-in despite having worked and lived in California for over thirty years.

The Protect Our Neighbors Act would give people a fair chance to move forward and past their final orders of removal. It would establish a 10-year expiration on final orders of removal for individuals who have been continuously present in the country and not convicted of a crime. It would also create a pathway for these individuals to apply for legal permanent resident status.

“We need a sensible immigration policy for those who have resided peacefully for a long time in America and have been upstanding members of their communities," said Rep. Lofgren, a senior member of the House Judiciary Committee and a former immigration lawyer. “Detaining and deporting folks with no criminal record is not what Donald Trump campaigned on, and it’s not what the American people want. The Protect Our Communities Act provides long-term residents who have built their lives here with a fair opportunity to resolve outdated removal orders and earn lawful permanent status."

“No one should have to live in constant fear of being torn away from their family and community after spending years building a life in this country. I am sick of the Trump Administration targeting our neighbors and threatening the lives they have worked so hard to build. These are people who have spent years contributing to our communities, working hard, and putting down roots,” said Congresswoman Simon. “The Protect Our Neighbors Act would provide people, like Ms. Kaur who worked in my district for decades, with a fair opportunity to move beyond a final order of removal and continue building futures here in the U.S where they have made their homes and families. I am incredibly grateful to Congressmembers Garamendi, Lofgren, and Vargas for standing with me and partnering on this important legislation.”

“We are still traumatized and horrified by the cruel treatment of our grandmother one year ago,” said Harjit Kaur’s family. “Harjit was a pillar to our family and our community. She spent over thirty years in the United States, raising her children and later her grandchildren, and became a grandmother figure to our whole community. What was worse about her treatment was how unnecessary it was. We tried to work with ICE to bring her back to India, but at every turn the agency chose the more violent and cruel path — denying her food, moving her in the middle of the night without letting us know, and sending her back without letting us say goodbye. The pain that we still feel today remains with the knowledge that Harjit is one of thousands who’ve experienced the same situation. We thank the Members of Congress for their continued advocacy, and we hope that some good could come from Harjit’s story with this bill and others like it.”

"President Trump promised to go after the 'worst of the worst' in his immigration policy. Yet his administration has repeatedly decided to cruelly deport residents who have been working, paying taxes, and raising families in their communities for decades,” said Rep. Garamendi. This is exactly what happened to one of our constituents. Nearly one year ago, ICE cruelly detained and deported Harjit Kuar, a 73-year-old grandmother with no criminal record — who faithfully reported to ICE every six months for more than 13 years. Her cruel and unreasonable detention and deportation is just one more example of the thousands of individuals across the country whose lives and families have been upended by Trump's ICE. Unfortunately, this has become far too common under Donald Trump's mass deportation agenda, which is exactly why I'm proud to introduce this commonsense and humane fix to our immigration system with Representatives Simon, Lofgren and Vargas."

“The Trump Administration’s anti-immigrant agenda is destroying lives. Trump isn’t going after the ‘worst of the worst.’ He’s terrorizing our communities and ripping families apart. I’m proud to introduce this legislation alongside Representatives Garamendi, Simon, and Lofgren to bring a commonsense fix to our immigration system. We need comprehensive immigration reform and an end to Trump’s mass deportation agenda,” said Rep. Vargas.

Full bill text can be found HERE.

Community members in Alameda County who witness ICE actions or know someone who has been detained by ICE can utilize the Alameda County Immigration Legal Education Partnership (ACILEP) immigration rapid response network.

title: Representative Mannion Seeks Protection of U.S. Candle Industry and Syracuse Jobs From Predatory Practices by Foreign Manufacturers
text:
SYRACUSE, NY — Representative John W. Mannion (NY-22) today led a bipartisan letter to ChairmanBrett Doyle of the U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) to protect the U.S. candle industry and jobs in Syracuse from predatory pricing practices by foreign, Chinese candle manufacturers.

The finest liturgical candles in the world are made in Syracuse at Cathedral Candle Company, a 5th generation family-owned business that began production in 1897.

Cathedral Candle Company President Mark Steigerwald said, “Cathedral Candle Company has manufactured candles in Syracuse, New York for nearly 130 years. This anti-dumping duty has been critical to ensuring that our family business can compete with a level playing field and continue manufacturing in Syracuse with our over 90 union employees for many years to come.”

The bipartisan letter outlines the risk of sunsetting the antidumping duty order on petroleum wax candles from China. Without the order, U.S. candle companies report that they face material harm, market loss, and an undermining of manufacturers and their workers. The letter urges the ITC to conclude its review in a way that ensures that American producers can compete on a level playing field. Representative Mannion was joined on the bipartisan letter by Representatives Lloyd Smucker (PA-11), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Dave Min (CA-37), Thomas Kean Jr (NJ-07), Jefferson Shreve (IN-06), Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), and Bryan Steil (WI-01).

The full text of the letter is below, and a formatted version can be found here:

The Honorable Brett Doyle

Chairman

U.S. International Trade Commission

500 E Street, SW

Washington, DC 20436

Dear Chairman Doyle,

We write in support of submissions before the U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC) to protect the domestic petroleum wax candle industry from predatory pricing practices by foreign, Chinese candle manufacturers. The Commission recently initiated its sixth sunset review of the antidumping duty order on petroleum wax candles from China. On behalf of candle manufacturers and workers in our districts and across the country, we urge the ITC to expeditiously conclude its review in a manner that ensures that American producers can compete on a level playing field.

Antidumping measures against petroleum wax candles from China have been in place for 40 years, beginning in 1986. Since then, Commerce and the ITC have reaffirmed the need for this trade remedy through five consecutive sunset reviews. Moreover, the antidumping margin has increased over time, reflecting an escalation of unfair trade practices and an ongoing threat to our domestic industry.

U.S. candle companies report that, without the continuation of this antidumping order against cheap imports from China, they face a real and immediate threat of material harm and market share loss. Foreign businesses must be prevented from engaging in unfair, predatory price manipulation. U.S. trade remedy laws were explicitly designed to combat this type of anticompetitive conduct, which undermines U.S. manufacturers and their workers.

The U.S. candle making industry represents hundreds of U.S. companies, many of them family-owned businesses that have endured for generations and are deeply rooted in their communities. Together, they create thousands of jobs and contribute significantly to local economies. This order also deeply impacts U.S. supplier jobs for paraffin and soy wax producers, fragrance suppliers, and hardware.

The ITC should continue to rigorously enforce U.S. trade remedy laws to eliminate distortions in the U.S.market and maintain a level playing field for our domestic manufacturers. We also respectfully urge the ITC to conduct an expedited review of the order given the domestic industry’s complete and timely response to the notice of institution and complete lack of participation by any foreign producer in these proceedings. In fact, no foreign producer has even entered an appearance, demonstrating there is no expectation that anyforeign producer intends on cooperating with the ITC’s review.

We thank the Commission for its consideration of this matter and look forward to your response.

title: McClellan, Davis, Grijalva Introduce ACCELERATE Act to Invest in STEM Educators and Better Prepare STEM Students for Success
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) and Congresswoman Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07) introduced the Advancing Credentialing and Career Empowerment for Leadership in Education, Recognition, and Teacher Excellence (ACCELERATE) Act to invest in science, technology, math and engineering (STEM) educators while improving STEM education and career advancement for students.

H.R. 11081, or the ACCELERATE Act, would establish a grant program to expand the recognition and use of STEM micro-credentials for educators. Micro-credentials allow learners to upskill and demonstrate mastery of STEM skills while providing them the flexibility needed for professional growth and closing gaps for Title I schools and rural communities. This program would better align STEM educators with the evolving demands of the job market, strengthen classroom instruction and keep our nation competitive on the global stage.

“STEM education remains a top priority for any country that hopes to stay on the cutting edge of technological advancement. And above all else, our children deserve only the best from our teachers as they prepare to become the workforce of tomorrow,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “The ACCELERATE Act empowers our educators to earn skill-based credentials that they can then apply to the classroom to better teach their students. As our job market increasingly values these technical skillsets, we must continue to provide opportunities that challenge our teachers to constantly be learning and improving — so that they can bring the best versions of themselves into the classroom to work with the next generation of researchers, builders and thinkers.”

“In eastern North Carolina, we want our young people to have every opportunity to pursue good-paying STEM careers. The ACCELERATE Act would give educators more opportunities to strengthen their skills, grow professionally, and bring what they learn back into the classroom,”said Congressman Don Davis. “When we invest in our teachers, we invest in our students and the future of communities across America.”

“Our students deserve an education that prepares them for the opportunities of the future, and that starts with investing in our educators,” said Congresswoman Grijalva. “The ACCELERATE Act will help teachers build the skills they need to deliver high-quality STEM education and ensure that all students, regardless of zip code, have access to these opportunities. I’m proud to support this effort to empower our educators and expand access to STEM for our students.”

The ACCELERATE Act is endorsed by digiLEARN, Digital Promise, New America, National Council of Teacher Mathematics (NCTM), STEM Education Coalition, and the American Association of Colleges for Teacher Education (AACTE).

“High-quality STEM education is vital to U.S. competitiveness and to preparing students, particularly those in rural and hard-to-serve areas, for a STEM-driven economy. Representative McClellan’s proposed Accelerate Act for Teacher Advancement would fund state grants to develop rigorous, competency-based STEM credentials that support teacher development and career advancement and help teachers inspire students’ interest in STEM,” said Bev Perdue, Chair of digiLEARN and former North Carolina Governor. “The bill also promotes regional and community business–education partnerships aligned with local workforce needs and includes research accountability to assess effects on student outcomes and economic development.”

“Digital Promise is proud to endorse the ACCELERATE Act, which aligns with our longstanding commitment to expanding high-quality, competency-based credentials for educators,” said Jean-Claude Brizard, President and CEO of Digital Promise. “By validating real-world STEM skills and linking them to career pathways, this bill lays the groundwork for powerful learning—engaging, relevant experiences that foster student agency, curiosity, and purpose; support well-being; and drive lifelong economic mobility. Ultimately, the ACCELERATE Act ensures that every learner is guided by highly skilled educators who can equip them to thrive in a rapidly changing world.”

“By supporting state efforts to enhance and verify STEM teachers’ skills through high-quality, evidence-based micro-credentials, the ACCELERATE Act strives to strengthen student learning in subject areas that are critical to our nation’s economic success,” said Melissa Tooley, Director of Educator Quality for New America’s PreK-12 Education Initiative.

“Every student deserves to learn mathematics and STEM subjects from a teacher who has the knowledge, skills, and confidence to help them succeed. High-quality, sustained professional learning is essential to ensuring that teachers can continually strengthen their practice, respond to evolving instructional needs, and inspire the next generation of problem-solvers,” said Dewey Gottlieb, President of the National Council of Teachers of Mathematics. “The ACCELERATE Act recognizes that investing in teachers is one of the most effective ways to support student achievement. By expanding access to rigorous, competency-based professional learning and creating meaningful opportunities for teachers to demonstrate their expertise and advance professionally, this legislation will help strengthen the teaching profession and improve STEM learning opportunities for students nationwide.”

“Students get more out of STEM when their teachers have the time and support to bring hands-on, real-world learning into the classroom,” said James Brown, Executive Director of the STEM Education Coalition. “The ACCELERATE Act would help states and Tribal education agencies develop systems to recognize high-quality micro-credentials that give teachers a way to build those skills, use them in their classrooms, and earn recognition for what they’ve learned. We appreciate Congresswoman McClellan’s focus on reaching educators in high-poverty and rural communities, and we’re pleased to support the bill.”

The ACCELERATE Act amends the Elementary and Secondary Education Act to establish a STEM Micro-Credential Grant Program to support state and tribal educational agencies in developing, implementing, and improving standards, guidelines, and processes for the recognition of STEM micro-credentials. More specifically, this bill supports states with:

establishing and implementing quality-assurance standards for the recognition of STEM micro-credentials, including through the development and use of rigorous micro-credential design rubrics; evidence-based professional learning resources; and valid and reliable scoring criteria;

conducting outreach to familiarize educators with STEM micro-credentials and the potential benefits they offer to educators and their students;

developing and communicating opportunities for educators to use STEM micro-credentials to satisfy initial and ongoing licensure requirements;

collaborating with local educational agencies, institutions of higher education, STEM industry partners, and non-profit organizations to implement research-backed STEM micro-credential standards, guidelines, and processes;

incentivizing educators to earn STEM micro-credentials through the provision of stipends and other benefits, including opportunities for career advancement;

coordinating, as appropriate, with federally supported STEM education research and evaluation activities, including those of the National Science Foundation Directorate for STEM Education; and

evaluating the overall impact of STEM micro-credentials on educator professional development and student outcomes.

The bill authorizes $50 million annually and caps each grantee at $500,000 over three years to build, evaluate, and sustain micro-credential recognition systems that improve educator development and student outcomes.

title: McIver Speaks on Major Third Circuit Decision to Allow Case to Proceed
text:
“While I am the first lawmaker they have tried to jail, I will surely not be the last.”

NEWARK, NJ – Today, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit declined en banc hearing of pre-trial motions to dismiss U.S. v. McIver, the landmark government oversight case brought by the Trump Department of Justice (DOJ) against Congresswoman LaMonica McIver (NJ-10).

The court’s denial is a hit to the protection of oversight. The major constitutional questions McIver’s case presents have come under sharper focus since November’s midterm elections, after which the Trump administration has immediately ramped up targeting of Democratic members of Congress for performing their oversight duties.

At present, however, McIver remains the only member of Congress facing criminal penalties for oversight. She faces 17 years in federal prison if convicted at trial.

“Donald Trump continues to send warning shots to Democrats in Congress and in all levels of power—but their case against me right now, in broad daylight, goes well beyond a warning. Because of a weaponized Department of Justice and because I dared to do my job and conduct oversight of ICE, I am facing 17 years in prison. Now, due to the disappointing decision by the Third Circuit, we are all one step closer to a world in which the president of the United States can try to imprison people simply because he does not like what they stand for,” said Rep. LaMonica McIver. “This result is frustrating, but my lawyers and I are looking at every possible option for what comes next. This month, the American people clearly told us that they are against the president putting his own interests over the country’s, that they are against ICE’s reign of terror, and that they want action to stop this abuse. I hope that everyone who feels that way will stand with me in my fight against these unjust charges because, while I am the first lawmaker they have tried to jail, I will surely not be the last.”

The case is not over. McIver’s pre-trial appeal sought to have the charges brought by the Trump DOJ dismissed wholesale. McIver now faces the prospect of trial for doing her job. The move for hearing en banc came after a divided panel of three Third Circuit judges refused to dismiss the case against McIver in August, and a district court’s denial to dismiss her case in January, 2026.

The charges against McIver stem from an oversight visit she conducted at Delaney Hall, a controversial ICE detention center in her district, in May, 2025.

title: Legislation by Reps. Mfume, Palmer to Increase Transparency in Federal Agency Settlement Agreements Unanimously Passes House of Representatives
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Yesterday, the United States House of Representatives unanimously passed H.R. 7934, the Settlement Agreement Information Database (SAID) Act of 2026. The bipartisan legislation introduced by Congressman Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), along with Representative Gary Palmer (AL-06), will provide overdue transparency and accountability standards for federal settlement agreements.

The SAID Act will promote greater transparency in the federal government by bringing long-needed visibility to federal settlement agreements and consent decrees. The legislation would require federal agencies to submit information about these agreements to a publicly accessible electronic database.

“The American people deserve to know how their tax dollars are spent,” said Congressman Kweisi Mfume. “With yesterday's vote, the House has said once again that federal agencies cannot cut deals in the dark on the taxpayers’ dime. Under the SAID Act, no agency will be able to hide the terms of a settlement or consent decree just by calling them confidential. If an agency wants to keep that information from the public, it will have to tell Congress and explain to the American people why. I am proud to have led this bipartisan bill with my colleague Congressman Gary Palmer, and to carry on the work of the late Democratic Oversight Committee Leader Gerry Connolly. The House has now passed this bill in five straight Congresses. It is time for the Senate to finish the job. I urge my friends in the Senate to take it up before the end of this Congress and send it to the President’s desk. The American people cannot give informed consent without transparency.”

“For too long, the American people have been kept in the dark about legally binding agreements made by federal agencies on their behalf. Such settlements must be transparent and accessible to the public. With no database or recordkeeping standard, this information is released by agency discretion, often in the form of a press release,” said Rep. Palmer. “This bipartisan bill will substantially increase government transparency by making these records publicly accessible in a centralized, searchable database. By shining a light on these deals, Congress and the American people will be able to better understand how federal agencies are exercising their authority and hold them accountable when those actions impose burdens outside the normal legislative or regulatory process. I was honored to introduce this bipartisan legislation alongside Rep. Mfume, and I encourage the Senate to act swiftly.”

Click HERE to read the bill's full text.

The Settlement Agreement Information Database (SAID) Act would:

Improve transparency by requiring federal agencies to report information on settlement agreements and consent decrees to a centralized, searchable public database;

Strengthen oversight by having the database administered under the guidance of the Office of Management and Budget and ensuring that the information disclosed includes key details such as agreement dates, payment amounts, attorney fee awards, and the state and local governments affected;

Enhance accountability by requiring the agency head to notify Congress if they determine that certain information must remain confidential and provide a public explanation of why that information cannot be disclosed.

title: Rep. Mike Kennedy, U.S. Chamber and Point of the Mountain Chamber host Transportation Roundtable
text:
LEHI, UT – The U.S. Chamber of Commerce, in partnership with Point of the Mountain Chamber of Commerce, recently convened a roundtable discussion with Rep. Mike Kennedy and local business leaders in Lehi, Utah.

The event, part of the U.S. Chamber’s Keep America Moving national infrastructure tour, is helping build momentum for Congress to enact a new, long-term surface transportation bill. The discussions covered how the federal government can best support Utah's growing transportation needs, particularly as the state prepares to host the Winter Olympic Games in 2034.

Congressman Kennedy and the civic and business leaders in the room agreed that Congress should pass the bipartisan BUILD America 250 Act and continue to prioritize strong, long-term certainty and policies that reduce general fund costs, such as modernizing the Highway Trust Fund and streamlining permitting processes to ensure faster project delivery.

“Robust and reliable federal investment in our nation’s transportation infrastructure is essential for economic growth,” said Jennings Imel, Vice President at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. “The conversation with Congressman Kennedy and business and community leaders in fast-growing Utah County underscored how investments in roads, transit, and highways strengthen economic competitiveness and improve quality of life. We commend Congressman Kennedy for his leadership and support of bipartisan transportation legislation that provides long-term funding and streamlines permitting processes that will help expedite the delivery of critical projects in Utah.”

“Utah is growing fast, and our infrastructure needs to keep pace,” said Congressman Mike Kennedy. “We need long-term certainty in our transportation infrastructure to keep our economy moving and competitive. I’m grateful to the state and federal leaders who came together to discuss what the future of Utah’s transportation looks like.”

“Utah’s continued growth and economic success depend on a transportation system that keeps people and goods moving. We appreciate Congressman Kennedy’s leadership on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and his commitment to advancing Utah’s priorities in the next surface transportation reauthorization. Utah has taken a thoughtful, collaborative approach to planning for its transportation future, with Utah's Unified Transportation Plan serving as a national model for how local, regional, state, and federal partners can work together to identify priorities and make strategic investments. The roundtable was a valuable opportunity to continue that collaboration and discuss how we can advance these shared priorities to support Utah’s quality of life," said Andrew Gruber, Executive Director of the Wasatch Front Regional Council.

“Northern Utah County is one of the best places to live, work, and start a business, but we can only continue to thrive if we have strong and reliable investments in our transportation system,” said Marcee Gundry, President & CEO of the Point of the Mountain Chamber. “We are grateful that Congressman Mike Kennedy understands our region’s needs and supports bipartisan bills that invest in our community, such as the BUILD America 250 Act, and we appreciate him taking the time to meet with our businesses and community leaders.”

title: Miller, Delaney Introduce AGRI-FLOOD Resilience and Infrastructure Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, Representative Carol Miller (R-WV) joined Representative April McClain Delaney (D-MD) in introducing the AGRI-FLOOD Resilience and Infrastructure Act. This bipartisan legislation strengthens rural water infrastructure by restoring degraded watersheds and modernizing flood prevention systems to better protect communities from devastating floods and other water-related disasters.

“In West Virginia, aging dams and outdated infrastructure leave many of our communities vulnerable to devastating floods. Our rural communities deserve reliable water systems and the peace of mind that comes with knowing their homes and businesses are safe. This vital legislation will strengthen USDA watershed programs, which support a variety of resilience activities including dam repairs, road upgrades, and rural water infrastructure while cutting unnecessary government red tape that slows down critical projects. Flooding threatens lives and devastates communities. We must do everything we can to prepare for disasters before they strike and ensure West Virginia has the most up to date infrastructure,” said Congresswoman Miller.

“Last year’s flooding in Westernport devastated families and underscored the need to better prepare our rural communities. Our neighbors deserve to feel safe in their homes and have the tools to prepare for the next flood. That’s why I’m introducing the bipartisan AGRI-FLOOD Act to help rural communities upgrade aging flood infrastructure, restore watersheds, and strengthen early warning and real-time response systems. Investing in prevention now can save lives and spare families the heartbreak and expense of rebuilding," said Congresswoman McClain Delaney.

The AGRI-FLOOD Resilience and Infrastructure Act directs USDA to establish a Floodplains and Watershed Resilience Program that would provide:

Infrastructure assistance: Financial and technical support to modernize aging dams and flood control infrastructure in rural communities.

Watershed restoration: Projects to restore floodplains, wetlands, and degraded watersheds to reduce future flood risks.

Better flood risk information: National flood risk assessments and publicly accessible flood maps to support local planning and preparedness.

Endorsees Quotes:

“We thank Representatives April McClain Delaney and Carol Miller for introducing the AGRI-FLOOD Act and recognizing the value of protecting both people and rivers through smart conservation investments. Floodplain restoration and easements are a proven land-management strategy that supports landowners while conserving flood-prone land. These USDA programs provide multiple benefits — from storing floodwaters and improving water quality to creating critical wildlife habitat and helping rivers reconnect with their natural floodplains. Healthy rivers and floodplains make communities more resilient to increasingly severe floods and storms,” said Tom Kiernan, President, American Rivers Action Fund.

“ASFPM supports the overall goals of the AGRI-FLOOD Resilience and Infrastructure Act because the legislation advances proactive flood risk reduction, watershed resilience, nature-based solutions (including restoration of wetlands), and modernization of aging flood infrastructure. We note that NRCS assisted in designing, planning, and constructing nearly 12,000 watershed dams to control flooding and prevent damage to communities since the 1950s. As these dams have aged, surrounding areas have developed, and rainfall patterns have changed, flooding has increased. Rural communities in particular, need assistance to better identify, assess, and mitigate flood risk. ASFPM looks forward to working with Congress and NRCS on this bill as it moves through the legislative process,” said Chad Berginnis, Executive Director of the Association of State Floodplain Managers.

“We thank Representatives April McClain Delaney and Carol Miller for introducing this important legislation to strengthen the nation’s watershed infrastructure. This bill will help prioritize rehabilitation of high hazard dams that are critical to protecting rural communities, while also generating jobs, supporting agricultural economies, and ensuring these aging structures continue to provide flood protection, water management, and public safety benefits for future generations. By reducing barriers and increasing federal support, this legislation will help local sponsors move urgently needed projects forward without delay,” said Gene Stauborn, Executive Director, National Watershed Coalition.

“Counties play a critical role in building flood-resilient infrastructure across our nation's rural communities. The AGRI-FLOOD Resilience and Infrastructure Act provides targeted technical assistance and financial support for watershed resilience and flood protection efforts, helping rural county leaders better protect our communities. Counties urge Congress to swiftly pass this bipartisan legislation,” said Matthew Chase, Executive Director of the National Association of Counties.

“ASCE strongly supports a watershed management approach that considers all residents within a watershed basin. Rural communities are adversely affected by lack of resources to reduce flood risk, implement plans to mitigate the effects of natural disasters, and ensure that water resources infrastructure is able to withstand increasingly severe weather events. The AGRI-FLOOD Resilience and Infrastructure Act will provide needed assistance to rural communities by providing financial and technical assistance for pre-disaster flood risk reduction, prioritizing projects to improve resilience of high-hazard dams that could otherwise result in loss of life in the event of dam failure, and ensure that accurate and up to date data are available to stakeholders to help improve safety preparation and response capability. ASCE is proud to support this critical bipartisan legislation,” said Marsha Anderson Bomar, President, American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE).

“Rural communities, farmers, and local businesses are facing growing risks from flooding and aging water infrastructure. The Agri-Flood Act is a strong bipartisan step toward strengthening resilience, modernizing critical watershed infrastructure, and supporting economic opportunity in rural communities. American Sustainable Business Network supports policies that invest in resilient infrastructure solutions that are good for businesses, farmers, and communities alike,” said Liza LaManna, Manager of Agriculture and Water Policy, American Sustainable Business Network.

"As the U.S. faces increasing climate risks, we must also acknowledge that extreme precipitation events are becoming more frequent, making the prevalence of high-hazard dams unacceptable. That is why we strongly support the Agri-Flood Resilience and Infrastructure Act as a means of providing States, local governments, Tribal Nations, and territories with the resources they need to improve resilience against flooding in their communities on an expedited timeline,” said Jeff Diamond, Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy.

This bill is endorsed by: Institute of Agriculture & Trade Policy, Farm Aid, Family Farm Defenders, Women, Food, and Agriculture Network, Wild Farm Alliance, River Partners, Association of Floodplain State Managers, American Sustainable Business Council, Responsible Alpha, ACRES Land Trust, Alabama Rivers Alliance, Alliance for the Great Lakes, American Rivers, American Sustainable Business Network, Appalachian Citizens' Law Center, Appalachian Voices, Association of State Floodplain Managers, Belmar Farm (Kentucky), Bozeman Birders, Californians for Western Wilderness, Chesapeake Conservancy, Chicago Sierra Club, Civilized Humanity, Clean Energy Action, Climate Reality Chicago Metro, Climate Reality Project Regenerative Agriculture Coalition, Climate Systems Solutions, CO - Energy & Environment Initiative, Cojujo Farm (Vermont), Contra Costa Resource Conservation District, Creation Justice Ministries, Empower our Future, Endangered Habitats League, Environmental Working Group, Family Farm Defenders, Farm Aid, Farmers Solidarity for Agricultural and Social Development (SOPADAS), Friends of the Big Sioux River, Friends of the Chemung River Watershed, Friends of the Mississippi River, Healthy Ocean Coalition, Hispanic Federation, Hoosier Environmental Council, Indiana Conservation Voters, Inland Ocean Coalition, Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy, Iowa Citizens for Community Improvement, Iowa Environmental Council, Iowa Prairie Network, Kansas City Zoo, Kentucky Waterways Alliance, Lake Pepin Legacy Alliance, Micah Six Eight Mission, Missouri Confluence Waterkeeper, National Association of Counties, National Mississippi River Museum & Aquarium, Natural Heritage Institute, New Mexico Wild, New Mexico Wildlife Federation, Northern Prairies Land Trust, NTS Group, Ohio River Foundation, Pasa Sustainable Agriculture, PennFuture, Project Eleven Hundred, Protect Our Commonwealth, Responsible Alpha, Rio Grande Headwaters Land Trust - del Norte, CO, Rio Grande International Study Center, River Network, River Partners, Sana Global, Shedd Aquarium, Sierra Club, SoCal 350 Climate Action, The Barn Group, The Black Appalachian Coalition, The Ocean Project, The Wei LLC, Vets United, Virginia Conservation Network, Water Environment Federation, Waterkeepers Chesapeake - Fair Farms Initiative, Web of Life Products, Wellsave / Food System CARE, Western Nebraska Resources Council, Western Slope Conservation Center, Whatcom Ag Water Board, Wild Farm Alliance, Winyah Rivers Alliance, Women, Food and Agriculture Network (WFAN)

Background

West Virginia is among the most flood-prone states in the nation due to its mountainous terrain and extensive network of rivers and streams. Every county in the state has experienced a federally declared flood disaster since 1967. In June 2016, catastrophic flooding claimed 23 lives and caused approximately $1.3 billion in damage.

More than 12,000 USDA-assisted dams were built in the mid-20th century, and many are now deteriorating or no longer meet modern safety standards, creating significant hazards for rural communities.

Rural and agricultural communities are especially vulnerable due to outdated infrastructure and limited access to federal support programs.

This legislation promotes a modern, integrated approach to flood resilience by combining natural infrastructure solutions (such as wetlands and floodplain restoration) with smart water management technologies.

title: Bloomberg Tax: Republican Proposes Tax Relief for IP Repatriated Back to the US
text:
A House GOP tax writer is introducing a bill that would allow American companies to return their intellectual property to the United States without triggering an anti-abuse tax.

Rep. Nathaniel Moran‘s (R-Texas) “Investing in American Innovation Act,” would allow US companies to transfer their IP — formulas, patents, and copyrights — from their foreign subsidiaries back home without exposure to the so-called base erosion and anti-abuse tax, known as BEAT.

“American ideas should be owned in America,” said Moran in a press release. “We need IP here in the United States to boost manufacturing which creates jobs. Right now, U.S. multinational companies could face unintended tax consequences for bringing their own innovations home, so too much of that value stays parked overseas.

The BEAT provision, under Section 59A, seeks to limit companies from making payments from the US to low-tax jurisdictions. Companies are subject to a BEAT rate of 10.5% if they have a three-year average of $500 million in gross receipts and deductible payments to foreign-owned affiliates totaling 3% of their overall deductions.

These payments include those that are made by the US company to a controlled foreign corporation, or CFC, for intellectual property. A CFC is a foreign subsidiary that’s more than 50% owned by a US shareholder.

Moran’s bill would remove tax under BEAT for “qualified IP repatriations” — transactions in which the US shareholder pays a foreign subsidiary for its IP. In addition, the US parent company wouldn’t recognize an income gain from the foreign subsidiary’s sale of the IP back to the US, and therefore wouldn’t be subject to tax under Subpart F and the net CFC tested income (NCTI) regime.

Companies with passive income from foreign subsidiaries are subject to a 21% tax rate under Subpart F of the tax code. The NCTI regime imposes a 12.6% effective tax rate on a US company’s active profits from a CFC.

title: Congressman Moran Co-Launches First Congressional Caucus Focused on AI Safety and Innovation
text:
Today, Congressman Nathaniel Moran (R-TX) joined Reps. George Whitesides (D-CA) and Don Beyer (D-VA) in announcing the launch of the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, the first congressional caucus focused specifically on addressing AI safety and security risks posed by increasingly advanced AI systems while ensuring the United States remains a global leader in innovative AI technologies.

As AI capabilities accelerate, so do the potential consequences of catastrophic misuse, loss of control over advanced systems, and threats to national security. In July, an experimental OpenAI agent escaped its testing environment and breached the external platform Hugging Face to cheat on an evaluation, without any human directing it to. Anthropic also disclosed three separate incidents in which its AI models escaped testing environments and gained unauthorized access to external organizations during cybersecurity evaluations. These recent security incidents have underscored the need for Congress to better understand these risks and develop policy solutions to prevent these incidents before emerging threats become larger problems. By addressing these challenges proactively, Congress can help create the conditions for continued American innovation and ensure the public can confidently benefit from advances in AI.

“We don’t have to choose between innovation and safety. We can, and we should, do both. Artificial intelligence affects every American, and it should not be a partisan issue. This caucus gives us a place to find the areas of consensus, set partisanship aside, and put smart, targeted policies in place so we can innovate while we keep people safe. Congress needs to be prepared, and I’m proud to be one of the co-chairs leading that work,” said Congressman Nathaniel Moran.

“AI is advancing faster than ever before, and Congress needs to move just as quickly,” said Rep. George Whitesides. “Now is the time to build bipartisan consensus and advance commonsense guardrails we know will reduce the most serious risks. Americans are rightly concerned about where this technology is heading, but too often the debate in Washington is framed as a choice between doing nothing and banning AI altogether. That’s a false choice. We have an opportunity to pursue smart, targeted solutions that protect the public while allowing American innovation to thrive. I co-founded this caucus with Reps. Moran and Beyer to fight for that balance, because safe, secure, and controllable AI is the only path to unlocking its full promise for humanity.”

“AI has immense potential to improve our lives and strengthen American innovation, but that progress can’t come at the expense of our national security or public safety,” said Rep. Beyer. “Recent cyberattacks involving AI agents and growing warnings from leaders and researchers at the companies developing these technologies make clear that the risks are real and growing. We can’t afford to wait for a major catastrophe before putting meaningful safeguards in place. I’m proud to join the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus. and work with my colleagues to advance responsible legislation that strengthens oversight, security, and transparency while ensuring AI is developed and deployed safely and responsibly.”

Specifically, the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus will:

Champion AI safety legislation: Develop legislative proposals and endorse existing bipartisan bills that establish thoughtful, targeted guardrails against the most serious AI risks while supporting continued innovation and American technological leadership.

Rapidly respond to AI incidents: Convene AI developers, technical experts, and government officials to brief Members and staff when significant AI safety incidents or developments occur and identify potential policy responses.

Equip congressional offices: Keep Members and staff informed about emerging AI developments, connect them with outside experts, and provide resources to navigate complex AI policy decisions.

Elevate AI safety publicly: Raise public awareness and make AI safety a national priority through public statements, op-eds, and press events.

Shape Congress’ AI agenda: Help develop federal AI safety policy and provide Members outside the committees of jurisdiction with an avenue to contribute to the conversation and legislative process.

By quickly addressing emerging threats, the AI Safety and Innovation Caucus will ensure AI can continue to make key improvements in the fields of American science, medicine, productivity, and national security. This new bipartisan caucus will advance thoughtful, targeted guardrails, engage technical experts and industry leaders, and equip Congress to respond quickly to emerging risks and significant AI incidents while ensuring America continues to lead in AI innovation.

The House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus launched with Reps. George Whitesides (D-CA), Nathaniel Moran (TX-01), and Don Beyer (D-VA) serving as co-chairs. Founding members include Reps. Ted Lieu, Jay Obernolte, Doris Matsui, Sara Jacobs, Pat Harrigan, Greg Casar, Scott Peters, April McClain Delaney, Sam Liccardo, Lori Trahan, Ritchie Torres, Bill Foster, Blake Moore, Mike Kennedy, Mike Flood, Zoe Lofgren, Ben Cline, Brad Sherman, Yvette Clarke, Valerie Foushee, Ro Khanna, Suhas Subramanyam, and Jim Himes.

title: Moran Introduces Legislation to Bring American Inventions Home from Overseas
text:
U.S. Representative Nathaniel Moran (TX-01) introduced the Investing in American Innovation Act. The bill removes tax code barriers that discourage American companies from bringing intellectual property (IP) held by their foreign subsidiaries back to the United States.

“American ideas should be owned in America,” said Rep. Moran. “We need IP here in the United States to boost manufacturing which creates jobs. Right now, U.S. multinational companies could face unintended tax consequences for bringing their own innovations home, so too much of that value stays parked overseas. This legislation removes those tax penalties while keeping strong guardrails in place. When intellectual property comes home, the research, the investment, and the jobs that come with it are more likely to follow.”

This legislation:

Removes the Base Erosion and Anti-Abuse Tax (BEAT) when bringing intellectual property home. When a foreign subsidiary transfers patents, copyrights, formulas, processes, designs, or similar property to its U.S. parent, the U.S. company’s payment for the repatriated property will not count as a base erosion payment.

Supports research that creates U.S.-owned IP. When a U.S. company pays a foreign affiliate to do research that creates intellectual property that the U.S. company will wholly own, those costs do not count toward the BEAT.

Prevents double taxation. The U.S. parent company can claim a credit against foreign taxes paid on the transfer of the intellectual property.

Implements anti-abuse rules. U.S. parent companies cannot exclude the subsidiaries’ gain from U.S. tax while simultaneously increasing the property’s basis, they cannot generate multiple tax credits through repatriation, and they cannot apply these favorable treatments to other unrelated repatriations.

Background:

When a U.S. company transfers intellectual property from a foreign subsidiary to its American parent, under current tax law, that transfer could face the Base Erosion and Anti-Abuse Tax (BEAT), which the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act created to prevent abusive tax practices. These tax penalties give companies a reason to leave valuable intellectual property, and the income it could earn, overseas.

title: CONGRESSMAN JOE MORELLE, SENATOR LISA BLUNT ROCHESTER INTRODUCE LEGISLATION TO PREVENT GUN THEFT AND KEEP ILLEGAL FIREARMS OFF OUR STREETS
text:
(Washington, D.C.)—Today, Congressman Joe Morelle (D, NY-25) and Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D, DE) announced the introduction of the Gun Theft Prevention Act, legislation to prevent firearms from being stolen from gun dealers and entering the illegal gun market. The bill would establish stronger security standards for federally licensed firearms dealers, increase inspections by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), and provide law enforcement with additional tools to combat gun theft and trafficking.

“Stolen firearms too often end up in the wrong hands, putting families and communities at risk,” said Congressman Joe Morelle. “We need to stop these weapons from reaching our streets in the first place. The Gun Theft Prevention Act strengthens security at gun dealers and gives law enforcement the tools to prevent theft before it happens.”

“Gun violence in America is a public health crisis, and Congress has every responsibility to intervene. Communities across the country are facing increased rates of firearm theft, and reining in this issue is a key step in tackling the gun violence epidemic,” said Senator Blunt Rochester. “ I’m proud to introduce the Gun Theft Prevention Act alongside Congressman Morelle to strengthen security standards for gun dealers and provide law enforcement with the right tools to stop gun theft and trafficking. We must make every effort to end gun violence and make our country a safer place.”

“Theft of firearms from gun dealers, manufacturers, and importers is a public safety threat that affects us all. Too often, these stolen guns are illegally trafficked and diverted into other criminal activity that endangers our communities. The Gun Theft Prevention Act will strengthen gun industry security measures and provide them with tools to prevent gun theft and trafficking. Brady is grateful to Congressman Morelle and Senator Blunt Rochester for introducing this important legislation and for their continued commitment to preventing the illegal trade of firearms,” said Mark Collins, Director of Federal Policy, Brady.

Specifically, the Gun Theft Prevention Act would:

Require federally licensed firearms dealers, manufacturers, and importers to implement security measures, including locked storage, alarm systems, video surveillance, reinforced locks, and additional physical barriers where necessary.

Require ATF to inspect federally licensed firearms dealers at least once every three years to help ensure compliance with federal law and applicable security requirements.

Require additional security inspections following reported thefts from firearms dealers to identify vulnerabilities and recommend corrective measures.

Establish additional background check requirements for employees of federally licensed firearms dealers.

Support increased ATF staffing and oversight capacity to help enforce federal firearms laws and prevent gun theft.

For more information on the Gun Theft Prevention Act, including the full legislative text, click here.

title: Congressman Griffith’s Weekly E-Newsletter 11.19.26
text:
Families across Central, Southside and Southwest Virginia continue to make purchases for a delicious Thanksgiving dinner.

With all the grocery shopping taking place ahead of Thanksgiving, local grocery stores will surely be busy.

While the avalanche of customers hitting grocery stores paints a rosy picture of holiday cheer, it is important to remember not all people get to share the cheer.

In many communities, there are folks who struggle to make ends meet. Being able to afford basic food items can be a tricky financial task. Providing a Thanksgiving meal for an entire family creates an even higher expense.

The United Way of Southwest Virginia is one local organization that tries to address hunger in our region. Every Thanksgiving, United Way partners with Food City to hold its annual “Celebrity Bagging” event.

The event aims to raise funds and awareness for various initiatives that serve the needy. Numerous community leaders and Food City locations participate.

Accordingly, I help in a small way by volunteering at a Food City store to bag groceries in order to raise awareness of the United Way food security program.

The United Way of Southwest Virginia also partners with other groups to address hunger challenges. One such group they work with is Feeding Southwest Virginia.

Feeding Southwest Virginia serves 26 counties and 9 cities, most of which are in Virginia’s Ninth Congressional District.

This past September, for Hunger Action Month, I joined elected officials in Abingdon at the Feeding Southwest Virginia Distribution Center.

This effort was part of the nearly 20 million pounds of food that Feeding Southwest Virginia annually distributes across the region.

We all volunteered to pack bags of potatoes, express our support for the charitable program and encourage others to get involved.

Pamela Irvine, Founder and CEO of Feeding Southwest Virginia, has worked diligently through her 45 years of service to get people involved.

Thanks to her leadership, Feeding Southwest Virginia collects thousands of volunteers to help at its facilities in Abingdon, Roanoke and Salem.

Irvine is stepping down from her position this December.

During an October celebration of her service, I delivered remarks that highlighted how much our communities appreciated Irvine and her service to our region.

Not only do people find her inspiring for her hard work to feed people, but her advocacy brought people from all political persuasions together. Democrats, Republicans and independents all love working with Irvine.

I enjoyed a productive and outstanding relationship with Irvine over the years. I have met with her in the district and in DC when she came to advocate for various anti-hunger programs and initiatives. I am glad to call her a friend.

While Irvine will be greatly missed by many, she plans to continue supporting local food banks, helping feed families and advocating for our region.

Even though Irvine is retiring, I plan to continue working on policies that help anti-hunger groups like Feeding Southwest Virginia deliver food access for families. And I am sure that somewhere along the way, Irvine will let me know her thoughts on federal policies impacting food insecurity.

This April, I voted for H.R. 7567 - the Farm, Food, and National Security Act, or more commonly known as the Farm Bill.

This bill provides funding for The Emergency Food Assistance Program (TEFAP) and other food programs.

These programs support food banks in caring for the hungry.

In addition, the Farm Bill that the House passed included new cooperative agreements for food banks to buy fresh, local food.

As a result, underserved and food insecure communities will access food pantries that provide healthy and nutritious food options.

As a leader on the Health Subcommittee, I remain committed to encouraging healthy eating habits for happier and healthier lifestyles.

This Thanksgiving, I join our communities to offer our profound thanks for the gifts that Irvine, the United Way and others provide to our neighbors in need.

While there will always be plenty of work to do to fight hunger, community networks and food pantries are critical resources for our society.

Moreover, I look forward to participating in the 20th edition of the United Way-Food City Celebrity Bagging event. As I engage with shoppers, I will be sure to wish them and their families a happy Thanksgiving!

Last but not least, I give thanks for numerous blessings that God has bestowed upon me. After all, giving thanks is the purpose of this holiday.

If you have questions, concerns, or comments, feel free to contact my office. You can call my Abingdon office at 276-525-1405 or my Christiansburg office at 540-381-5671. To reach my office via email, please visit my website at https://morgangriffith.house.gov/.

title: Rep. Obernolte's Bipartisan Preventive Health Savings Act Passes House
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Jay Obernolte (CA-23) announced today that his bipartisan Preventive Health Savings Act (H.R. 4464), legislation to modernize how Congress evaluates the long-term fiscal impact of preventive health care policies, has passed the U.S. House of Representatives.

Led by Rep. Obernolte and Rep. Diana DeGette (CO-01), the Preventive Health Savings Act will allow the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) to evaluate the potential long-term savings of preventive health care legislation over a 30-year period. Currently, CBO primarily evaluates legislation within a 10-year budget window, which can overlook savings from policies that prevent chronic diseases, reduce the need for costly medical treatments, or improve long-term health outcomes.

“Preventive health care has the potential to improve patient outcomes while reducing long-term health care costs, and our budget process should reflect those impacts,” said Congressman Jay Obernolte (CA-23). “The Preventive Health Savings Act will help Congress make more informed decisions by accounting for potential savings that extend beyond the traditional budget window. I'm pleased to see this bipartisan legislation pass the House and move us one step closer to a more accurate and responsible approach to evaluating federal health care investments.”

“I am proud to have worked on The Preventive Health Savings Act for over a decade," said Congresswoman Diana DeGette (CO-01). "This bill will revolutionize and modernize how Congress assesses health initiatives by accurately gauging the long-term savings from preventive health programs. Passage of this bill is a huge win for our country's fiscal health and a big step towards a healthier, more affordable future for all Americans. Now, the Senate must act quickly to pass this bill so that it can be signed into law.”

By providing Congress with a more complete understanding of the potential long-term savings associated with preventive care, the legislation aims to support evidence-based health care policies that improve patient outcomes while reducing future federal health care expenditures.

The Preventive Health Savings Act previously passed the House Budget Committee unanimously by a vote of 29-0 in September. Following House passage, the legislation now heads to the U.S. Senate for consideration.

title: ICYMI: Ocasio-Cortez, Lee, Paris Hilton Call for Immediate House Passage of DEFIANCE Act in the Lame-Duck Session
text:
WATCH HERE

Washington, D.C. - This week, Congresswomen Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (NY-14) and Laurel Lee (FL-15) and Ms. Paris Hilton were joined by impacted individuals for a press conference to push for passage of the Disrupt Explicit Forged Images and Non-Consensual Edits (DEFIANCE) Act during the lame-duck session. This bipartisan legislation would grant survivors the right to take civil action against individuals who knowingly produce, distribute, solicit, receive, or possess, with the intent to distribute, nonconsensual sexually explicit digital forgeries.

“Every single day that the DEFIANCE Act does not pass is a day that more children, women, and people are victimized with no recourse and that there is no accountability for abusers and predators. And so what it means is that thousands of people in this country, if not tens of thousands and eventually millions, could be subject to sexual abuse on our watch just due to complacency.” said Representative Ocasio-Cortez. “I am grateful for the support of my co-lead Representative Laurel Lee, Paris Hilton and the Democratic and Republican Women’s Caucuses in pushing this critical legislation across the finish line.”

“Deepfakes are not harmless, and they are not victimless. They are deliberate digital forgeries—often sexual in nature—created to exploit, harass, and humiliate. While the images and videos may be fake, the harm is very real. For too long, our laws have lagged behind this technology, leaving victims without clear legal tools when their likeness is stolen and weaponized,” said Representative Laurel Lee. “The DEFIANCE Act closes that gap. It is about restoring dignity, restoring accountability, and restoring justice. I am committed to working with my colleagues to see this legislation enacted, so perpetrators face consequences for their actions and victims across this country finally have the protections they deserve.”

“The Defiance Act would give survivors a civil path to hold people accountable for creating and distributing non-consensual, sexually explicit deep fakes. The Senate understood the urgency and passed this legislation unanimously in January. Now the House must act too,” said Paris Hilton. “Why wait another day? If they don't pass this bill before the end of the year, all of our progress will be lost and we will have to start all over again.”

Stefan Turkheimer, RAINN VP of Public Policy: "RAINN is grateful to Congresswomen Ocasio-Cortez and Lee for their bipartisan leadership in fighting for the DEFIANCE Act. Deepfake sexual abuse causes real harm, and survivors deserve a path to justice. The Senate has acted. Now it’s the House’s turn to stand for survivors and give them their day in court."

This push comes after the legislation has been stalled in the House for 10 months, following its unanimous passage in the Senate. The legislation has broad bipartisan support, with 74 cosponsors: 38 Democrats and 36 Republicans.

Earlier in the day, the representatives and Paris Hilton spoke about the need to pass the legislation on FOX News.

title: Olszewski, Quigley Introduce COUNT Act to Better Measure Community College Success
text:
Community colleges serve students whose educational journeys often look different from the traditional four-year college experience. Many, for example, attend part-time while working, return to school as adults, pursue workforce training, apprenticeship or non-credit programs, or transfer to four-year institutions.

Yet federal measures of student success have historically focused on full-time, first-time students pursuing degrees or certificates, often using completion timelines that fail to capture the broader community college experience. The COUNT Act would address these gaps by expanding the information collected through the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), the federal government's annual higher education data collection process.

“Community colleges help people build careers and create better lives for themselves and their families,” said Congressman Johnny Olszewski. “When federal data only recognizes traditional four-year college experience, we miss a huge part of that story. The COUNT Act is a common-sense way to give policymakers a more complete understanding of community college outcomes and to ensure that federal policies and investments reflect the students and communities these institutions serve.”

“Our community colleges in Chicago offer affordable, flexible opportunities for anyone wanting to further their education,” said Congressman Mike Quigley. “I’m leading the COUNT Act with Rep. Olszewski because we need to keep investing in our community colleges, and we can only do that if we modernize the federal research process to adequately represent these institutions. Our community colleges deserve respect, recognition, and the funding they need to succeed.”

With better data, the COUNT Act would give policymakers a stronger foundation for making federal funding decisions, helping ensure that community colleges are appropriately recognized for the students they serve, the credentials they award, and the workforce pathways they support.

For example, the Community College of Baltimore County (CCBC) in Congressman Olszewski’s district enrolled 55,000 students last year. Under current IPEDS measurement, it graduated 871 students. Under the COUNT Act – which would account for all degrees, transfers, certificates and workplace certifications – the graduation rate soars to 14,051.

“The power of America’s community colleges has been vastly underreported for decades because of the narrow success parameters defined by IPEDS,” said Dr. Sandra Kurtnitis, President of CCBC. “The Federal Reserve Bank model has opened the door to include success metrics of all community college students, whether completing an associate degree or a short-term credential. It is time that the full breadth of community college competition metrics are valued and measured appropriately and not skewed to the negative by outdated metrics never designed for our institutions.”

The legislation is endorsed by the Maryland Association of Community Colleges (MACC).

“Community colleges serve working adults, part-time learners, transfer students, apprentices, dual-enrollment students, and those pursuing noncredit workforce training,” said Dr. Brad Phillips, Executive Director, MACC. “Yet federal data measures still leave too many of these students invisible. The COUNT Act would modernize IPEDS reporting to better reflect the students we serve, the pathways they follow, and the credentials and skills they attain. More complete data will lead to better policy and more equitable investment in institutions that drive workforce development and economic mobility.”

title: Omar and Mfume Raise Concerns Over Access to Postal Employee Retirement and Health Benefits
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Representatives Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) and Kweisi Mfume (D-Md.), Ranking Member of the House Oversight and Government Reform Subcommittee on Government Operations, led 10 colleagues in asking the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) to verify the availability of alternative benefit access pathways for USPS employees.

Currently, USPS employees use Login.gov to access the Postal Service Health Benefits Program. But technical errors can leave them locked out with no other way to view their retirement and benefit information.

“Constituents in our districts are facing prohibitive barriers caused by simple technical errors, such as a failure to match phone numbers during identity verification. That means USPS employees are only one error message away from losing access to critical information regarding their retirement and benefit plans,” the lawmakers wrote.

According to requirements outlined by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and the General Services Administration (GSA), agencies are required to provide an alternative method of accessing agency services to support users who cannot access Login.gov services.

The lawmakers request that USPS verify whether it offers alternative access methods for viewing services when Login.gov fails, and provide information on how many employees have been affected by identify verification issues. The letter also asks the agency to outline steps it is taking to be consistent with OPM and GSA policies.

The letter was also signed by the U.S. Reps. James Walkinshaw (D-Va.), Chair of the Postal Service Caucus Nikki Budzinski (D-Ill.), Wesley Bell (D-Mo.), Stephen Lynch (D-Mass.), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), Angie Craig (D-Minn.), Maxwell Frost (D-Fla.), Rashida Tlaib (D-Mich.), Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.), and Greg Casar (D-TX).

You can read the full letter here and below:

Dear Postmaster General Steiner,

We write to convey concerns we have heard from constituents regarding the accessibility of the U.S. Postal Service’s (USPS) Login.gov website. Specifically, we are concerned about the lack of an alternative access capability, which is critical to employee benefit and retirement information.

The Office of Management and Budget (OMB) recently published a memorandum enforcing the use of the universal single sign-on platform. According to OMB Memorandum M-26-18, government agencies are expected to transition to Login.gov, a service operated by General Services Administration (GSA)’s Technology Transformation Services2 with the goal of using a digital design that lowers technology costs, cuts duplicative security measures, and provides ease for users of government agency websites.

In 2024, USPS expanded its use of Login.gov by requiring employees to make an account to access the Postal Service Health Benefits Program. While this transition was intended to simplify access for employees, constituents in our districts are facing prohibitive barriers caused by simple technical errors, such as a failure to match phone numbers during identity verification. That means USPS employees are only one error message away from losing access to critical information regarding their retirement and benefit plans.

GSA’s Login.gov website states that “applications using Login.gov’s identity verification services are required to provide an alternative method of accessing agency services to support users who are unable to complete Login.gov’s identity verification process. This requirement is based on OMB Memorandum M-23-22, which states that agencies “must always maintain an accessible method (i.e., physical availability) for completing a digital service through in-person, paper-based, or other means, so customers without the ability to use a digital service are not deprived of or impeded in their ability to access it.

While Login.gov offers in-person identity verification for some services, this method also requires phone number authentication prior to obtaining materials to complete in-person processes, creating an additional barrier for individuals who are already unable to authenticate by phone. As employees are planning for retirement, seeking health care, or making important financial decisions, they should not lose access to essential information because an online identity-verification system fails. USPS employees deserve a reliable way to access the benefits they have earned.

Given these concerns, we are requesting answers to the following questions:

Please verify whether USPS currently does or does not provide alternative access pathways for employees to view retirement information or benefits when Login.gov is inaccessible.

Does USPS track instances in which employees are unable to access benefits or retirement information because of Login.gov errors?

If so, how many USPS employees have been unable to access their benefits or retirement information because of Login.govissues since the system was implemented?

What are the most common causes of Login.gov authentication failures reported by USPS employees?

How many individuals were prevented from logging into their accounts due to phone number verification issues?

How many of those cases remain unresolved?

What steps has USPS taken to assess whether its current use of Login.gov’s requirement that agencies using its identity verification services provide an alternative method of access, as well as the alternative access standard in OMB Memorandum M-23-22?

What is USPS’s timeline for establishing an alternative access pathway for employees who cannot use Login.gov?

How does USPS coordinate with the Office of Personnel Management when an employee cannot access benefit information, so that employees are not referred back and forth between agencies without a resolution?
