title: Owens Introduces MUSTER Act to Streamline Service Members’ Transition to Civilian Life
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Burgess Owens (UT-04) introduced the Military Units for Separation, Transition, Employment, and Readiness (MUSTER) Act, legislation that directs the Department of War to evaluate dedicated separation battalions to guide servicemembers through their final 90 days of service and send them into civilian life with verified records of the skills they earned.

“I know what it is like to walk away from a career that shaped who you are. When I left the NFL, I had to figure out what the next chapter of my life looked like, and that transition is not always easy. Our servicemembers face the same transition, but with higher stakes. The MUSTER Act seeks to help our men and women in uniform accurately take the skills and abilities they’ve acquired through their service and translate them into opportunities by opening doors to high-demand, high-wage careers, in a way that is transparent and portable across states, industries, and employers,” said Rep. Burgess Owens (UT-04).

What the MUSTER Act Does

The MUSTER Act directs the Secretary of War to submit a written report to the congressional defense committees within 180 days of enactment on the feasibility and advisability of establishing dedicated separation battalions, or equivalent commands, to:

Streamline the final 90 days of active-duty service for members separating from the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, or Space Force.

Issue verified and interoperable Learning and Employment Records to these servicemembers.

The report must also include the operational impacts of establishing these units, their estimated costs, and the Secretary’s recommendations regarding pilot programs and partnerships with state entities.

Why it Matters

Leaving the military is one of the most consequential transitions a servicemember will ever make. The MUSTER Act ensures that the critical skills they’ve acquired throughout their military service don’t get lost or squandered because of bureaucratic hurdles.

Pairing that transition with verified, interoperable Learning and Employment Records means veterans would enter civilian life with a trusted, portable record of their skills that employers and schools can recognize immediately. The MUSTER Act builds on Rep. Owens’ leadership on Learning and Employment Records, skills-based hiring, and the commitment to ensuring America’s duty to its servicemembers does not end when they return home.

Full Bill Text.

title: Owens Introduces SERVICE Act to Turn Military Skills into Civilian Careers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Rep. Burgess Owens (UT-04) introduced the Servicemember Experience Recognition and Validation for Industry Credentials and Employment (SERVICE) Act, legislation that requires the Department of War to deliver Congress a plan to ensure the training, education, and experience servicemembers earn in uniform translate directly to civilian employment.

“No American who has worn the uniform of our Armed Services should have to start life from scratch when they take that uniform off. Our servicemembers are the best-trained fighting and logistics force in the world. Those skills shouldn’t be undervalued and unrecognized due to a mismatch on bureaucratic records. Service members who have spent years maintaining aircraft, driving vehicles, treating the wounded, or leading teams under more pressure than any boardroom can match have the skills employers need. The SERVICE Act makes sure we’re removing the barriers that often get in the way of that transition and translation between military and civilian life,” said Rep. Burgess Owens (UT-04).

What the SERVICE Act Does

The SERVICE Act directs the Secretary of War, in consultation with the nation’s governors and the Secretaries of Education, Labor, and Veterans Affairs, to submit a written report to Congress within 180 days of enactment containing a plan to ensure military training and experience translate to civilian employment. The report must include:

A list of military occupational specialties in the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Space Force, along with their civilian equivalents.

A list of the training and education provided to service members and their civilian equivalents, including postsecondary education, certifications, and apprenticeships.

A plan to make Department of War transcripts and records digitally portable.

Recommendations for statutory or regulatory changes to make military experience, credentials, and training more transferable to civilian employment.

The report will be delivered to the House and Senate Armed Services and Appropriations Committees, the House Committee on Education and the Workforce, and the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

Why it Matters

Every year, service members leave the military with world-class training and hands-on experience in fields like aviation maintenance, logistics, cybersecurity, and emergency medicine. Yet many still find that their skills do not carry over cleanly to the civilian job market, forcing them to repeat training or earn credentials for work they have already mastered. Employers miss out on proven talent, and veterans lose valuable time getting their careers started.

The SERVICE Act builds on Rep. Owens’ work to modernize America’s workforce system through portable Learning and Employment Records and skills-based hiring. By requiring the Department of War to deliver a report to Congress on their plan to connect military competencies to civilian skills and make those records digitally portable, the bill lays the groundwork for a system where service to country opens doors to opportunity, not paperwork.

title: Palmer Bill Creating Transparency Within Federal Agencies Passes House
text:
For Immediate Release

Media Contact: Hope Martin (202) 225-4921

WASHINGTON, D.C. – The Settlement Agreement Information Database Act (SAID Act), H.R. 7934, introduced by Representative Gary Palmer (AL-06) and Representative Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), passed the House of Representatives on November 18, 2026, by unanimous vote.

Following the passage of his bill, Rep. Palmer released the following statement:

“For too long, the American people have been kept in the dark about legally binding agreements made by federal agencies on their behalf. Such settlements must be transparent and accessible to the public. With no database or recordkeeping standard, this information is released by agency discretion, often in the form of a press release,” said Rep. Palmer. “This bipartisan bill will substantially increase government transparency by making these records publicly accessible in a centralized, searchable database. By shining a light on these deals, Congress and the American people will be able to better understand how federal agencies are exercising their authority and hold them accountable when those actions impose burdens outside the normal legislative or regulatory process. I was honored to introduce this bipartisan legislation alongside Rep. Mfume, and I encourage the Senate to act swiftly.”

“The American people deserve to know how their tax dollars are spent,” said Congressman Kweisi Mfume. “With yesterday's vote, the House has said once again that federal agencies cannot cut deals in the dark on the taxpayers’ dime. Under the SAID Act, no agency will be able to hide the terms of a settlement or consent decree just by calling them confidential. If an agency wants to keep that information from the public, it will have to tell Congress and explain to the American people why. I am proud to have led this bipartisan bill with my friend Congressman Gary Palmer, and to carry on the work of the late Democratic Oversight Committee Leader Gerry Connolly. The House has now passed this bill in five straight Congresses. It is time for the Senate to finish the job. I urge my friends in the Senate to take it up before the end of this Congress and send it to the President’s desk. The American people cannot give informed consent without transparency.”

A similar version of this bipartisan legislation passed the House in the 118th Congress on January 24, 2023, as H.R. 300.

title: FOLLOWING LOCAL REPORTS OF PRACTICE CLOSURES, CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN URGES HUDSON VALLEY PATIENTS TO FILL OUT COMMUNITY INQUIRY ON OPTUM’S PRACTICES
text:
Ryan first launched his Community Inquiry into Optum in April 2025 and received thousands of community responses detailing the avalanche of dysfunction at Optum-owned medical practices in the Hudson Valley

Chief among the concerns raised by the community were a declining quality of care, an increase in fees and incorrect billing, and issues with customer service and accessibility negatively impacting people’s ability to get health care

Now, amid local reporting and outreach from constituents, Ryan is raising the alarm on Optum’s plans to shutter certain Hudson Valley medical practices – including pediatric care in Rhinebeck – Ryan is encouraging Hudson Valley residents to fill out his community inquiry

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressman Pat Ryan is encouraging Hudson Valley community members to fill out his community inquiry into Optum – a subsidiary of UnitedHealth – following reports that Optum is shuttering certain Hudson Valley medical practices, including pediatric care in Rhinebeck.

Ryan first launched the inquiry in April 2025, and received thousands of community responses detailing the avalanche of dysfunction at Optum-owned medical practices in the Hudson Valley.

“The way that Optum has taken over our Hudson Valley healthcare ecosystem has been devastating for our community. They now control every part of the system – they own the insurance company, they own your doctor, they own the pharmacy and they own the software that processes all of your information – and they use it all to keep prices high and drive quality down. Now, patients have been calling my office, worried that their Optum pediatric practices may be closing entirely,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “Ripping away care from our community without explanation or satisfactory alternatives is completely unacceptable. Throughout the fight to hold Optum and United accountable, input from our community has been absolutely vital. That’s why I am asking you to make your voice heard. We’ve reached out to UnitedHealth for more information, and we’re prepared to fight like hell to protect our community’s care – but I need to hear from YOU. Please fill out my community inquiry, and I’ll keep fighting to elevate our community’s stories, and break up this greedy, exploitative monopoly once and for all.”

Community members are encouraged to fill out Ryan’s Community Inquiry into Optum.

Across the country, Optum has purchased doctor’s offices at an aggressive pace. It has become the largest employer of doctors, with one in ten physicians nationwide now under its control. Optum’s parent company, UnitedHealth Group, also owns the largest insurance company, one of the three largest Pharmacy Benefit Managers, and the largest medical claims manager. United has used this vast power to rip off patients and enrich its shareholders, with profits of $14 billion in 2024.

Nationwide, Optum has spent $31 billion on acquisitions over a two-year period, and has purchased everything from physician practices to ambulatory surgical centers. These acquisitions threaten equitable access to care, raise costs, and reduce physicians’ clinical autonomy. It is also a conflict of interest – insurance companies like United can steer patients to their own providers and subsidiaries, potentially to increase profits, rather than focusing on medical necessity.

In 2022, Optum purchased CareMount Medical, a medical group with over 2,100 providers and 1.6 million patients in the tri-state area. In 2023, Optum further consolidated the market for physician services in the Hudson Valley with its acquisition of Crystal Run Healthcare, with about 400 providers. Patients across the Hudson Valley have reported that the shift to Optum has worsened the quality of their care and reduced access to medical providers in our area. This includes difficulty scheduling doctor’s appointments, inaccurate billing, unexplained fees, long wait times, and poor customer service. In addition, Optum employees have reported layoffs and chaotic, overburdened work schedules, leading to staff burnout.

Following the initial responses, Ryan introduced his Patients Over Profits Act to break up UnitedHealth and undo the harms inflicted by their mass acquisition of Hudson Valley medical practices and to lower care prices across the region.

title: Pelosi Pays Tribute to Gloria Steinem on House Floor: “She Was a Star.”
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi delivered remarks on the House Floor honoring the life and legacy of Gloria Steinem, a champion for equality, following Steinem’s memorial service yesterday.

In her remarks, Pelosi credited Steinem with inspiring generations of women to run for office and called on the House to honor her legacy by passing the Equal Rights Amendment early in the next Congress.

Watch Pelosi’s Floor remarks here.

Read Speaker Emerita Pelosi's remarks below:

Thank you, Mr. Speaker.

Mr. Speaker, I rise today to honor Gloria Steinem, a champion for equality and a dear friend to so many of us here.

She championed the Equal Rights Amendment and helped found the National Women's Political Caucus to get more women elected.

It's a joy to me to say, when I came to Congress, there were twelve Democratic women, and now there are nearly 120. Ten times as many.

So many people are responsible for that. While I take some credit myself, Gloria Steinem gave women confidence to run, to lead, to do the job.

Her memorial service was a celebration of life. Where else would you see a service where three first ladies are on the stage dancing to the music of Gloria Steinem?

Michelle Obama, Jill Biden, and, of course, Hillary Clinton—candidate for president herself.

When we would have our circle of women at our home, this was the tradition of Gloria Steinem, so many people would come. It would overflow into the streets. Not once, not twice, but many times.

She was a star. Again, she championed the Equal Rights Amendment.

I hope we will make it the business of this caucus in a new term to, very early on, pass the Equal Rights Amendment—a tribute to all women, but led by Gloria Steinem.

I yield back the balance of my time.

title: Pfluger, Ernst, and Dingell Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Improve Broadband Deployment, Transparency, and Access
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman August Pfluger (R-TX), Senator Joni Ernst (R-IA), and Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (D-MI) introduced the bipartisan PROTOCOL Act, which would create a single, searchable database of federal broadband investments. The bill aligns the FCC’s Broadband Deployment Locations Map with NTIA’s Broadband Infrastructure Funding Database, strengthening oversight and helping ensure funding reaches truly unserved communities.

In 2023, the Government Accountability Office (GAO) identified 133 federal programs that support broadband, including 13 with overlapping efforts. Now, states are receiving their shares of the $42.5 billion Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment (BEAD) Program on top of that existing funding. Without better coordination, taxpayer dollars can be duplicated while underserved communities wait for access.

"Billions of taxpayer dollars are flowing into broadband programs, but there is no single avenue to see where those funds are going. The PROTOCOL Act gives Congress, agencies, and the public one searchable database of federal broadband investments, increasing much-needed transparency. Communities across the country are waiting on broadband access, and this legislation brings us one step closer to reality," said Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11).

“There are more than 100 federal broadband programs, but no single source showing where all that money goes,” said Senator Joni Ernst (R-IA). “The PROTOCOL Act ends the hide-and-seek game for providers, government entities, and consumers. This transparency-forward bill will prioritize underserved areas and eliminate duplicative projects for already well-connected areas.”

“Reliable broadband internet access is critical to every community, and we must ensure no one is left behind,” said Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (MI-06). “The PROTOCOL Act will ensure people across the country, regardless of ZIP code, have access to the opportunities broadband provides by improving the mapping process for broadband funding and better coordinating how funding is awarded.”

"USTelecom – The Broadband Association supports the bipartisan PROTOCOL Act, introduced by Senator Ernst and Reps. Pfluger and Dingell. Using the FCC’s broadband maps to guide federal funding will help agencies better work together, avoid spending taxpayer dollars twice, and get funding to communities that still lack reliable broadband. We urge Congress to pass the PROTOCOL Act," said Brandon Heiner, Senior Vice President of Government Affairs at USTelecom – The Broadband Association.

title: Pingree, 200+ House Democrats Fight to Stop USDA’s Plan to Kick 6.3 Million More Americans off SNAP
text:
Congresswoman Chellie Pingree (D-Maine), a member of the House Agriculture Committee, sent a letter to U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins opposing a new proposed rule that would kick an estimated 6.3 million Americans – primarily older or disabled beneficiaries and families with children – off the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).

"As the cost of groceries and other basic needs continue to rise, the Trump administration has made life less affordable for everyday Americans. Since passage of the 'One Big Beautiful Bill,' SNAP participation nationwide has plummeted by more than 5.5 million people, including approximately 2 million children,” the Members wrote. "Implementing this rule and cutting millions more people off from vital food assistance in the middle of an affordability crisis is both illegal and cruel.”

The letter was signed by 214 House Democrats. Read the letter here.

"SNAP is a critical tool in preventing hunger and helping families make ends meet. Taking food assistance away will only deepen food insecurity and place greater pressure on Maine’s food security network that is already under mounting pressure to meet a sustained high demand for assistance,” said Heather Paquette, President of Good Shepherd Food Bank. "We applaud Congresswoman Pingree and her colleagues for standing up for access to food and opposing policies that will make it harder for people to put food on the table."

"This is another attempt by the federal administration to make it harder for struggling Mainers to get and keep food assistance. Not only will eliminating Broad-based Categorical Eligibility increase bureaucratic paperwork and administrative costs - it will also hurt household budgets, school budgets and our state budgets,” said Anna Korsen, Co-Executive Director of Full Plates Full Potential. "Ultimately, more Maine kids will go hungry because of this decision, and I don't believe anyone in Maine wants that.”

"Just before winter and the holidays, when over 24,000 Mainers have already lost SNAP, the Trump Administration proposes to cut food assistance for thousands more in Maine, including for our kids,” said Alex Carter, Senior Policy Advocate at Maine Equal Justice. "Why is this administration intent on taking food off the plates of low-income Mainers, who are already on the front lines of the affordability crisis?"

According to the Trump administration’s regulatory impact analysis of the proposed rule:

6.3 million individuals in 3.2 million households will lose their SNAP benefits entirely.

The 3.2 million families impacted make up 17 percent of SNAP households.

SNAP benefits will be cut by $50.82 billion.

Federal spending on benefits will be cut by $44.65 billion over 5 years (FY2027-FY2031), and state spending on benefits will be cut by $6.17 billion.

SNAP administrative expenses will increase by $1.24 billion.

Federal spending on administrative expenses will increase by $309.5 million over five years.

State spending on administrative costs will increase by $928.5 million.

Increased burden on participants is estimated to be approximately $71.7 million over five years.

Because SNAP participation is often used to streamline eligibility for basic needs programs, the proposed rule's effects reach beyond the program.

1.78 million children would no longer be categorically eligible for school meals. Of those children:

97 percent would likely remain eligible but need to go through an onerous paperwork process to maintain eligibility.

93,000 children would be shifted from free to reduced-price school meals.

28,000 children would lose free school meals entirely and have to pay full price.

42,000 children will no longer receive Summer EBT (“Sun Bucks”) beginning in the summer of 2029.

An estimated 13,000 of these children would lose benefits they qualify for due to administrative burden (i.e., not applying for SEBT, even though they remain eligible).

5,500 women, infants and children would be kicked off the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC).

The number of states opting in to broad-based categorical eligibility has increased steadily each year because of its positive impacts on participants and program administration. Currently, 46 states, Republican and Democratic alike, opt to use BBCE.

Under President Trump and Secretary Rollins, food insecurity in America has increased, according to independent analysis. Food inflation accelerated in October. Thanksgiving staples are up 11 percent year-over-year, outpacing inflation.

title: Pingree, Balint, Ross Probe Possible DOJ Bias in Landmark OpenAI Copyright Fight
text:
Congresswoman Chellie Pingree (D-Maine), co-chair of the Congressional Arts Caucus, along with Congresswomen Becca Balint (D-Vt.) and Deborah Ross (D-N.C.), are demanding answers from Attorney General Todd Blanche about the Justice Department’s decision to intervene in a major copyright case involving OpenAI and Microsoft. The case could shape whether AI companies must seek permission to use copyrighted work to train their models, with consequences for artists and creators who rely on licensing income, among other sources, to make a living.

In their letter to Blanche, the lawmakers ask why DOJ reportedly bypassed the U.S. Copyright Office and the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office before filing its September 1 statement of interest—and whether any outside companies or organizations helped influence the filing.

The case, brought by The New York Times and other plaintiffs, could have ramifications well beyond newsrooms. Musicians, photographers, illustrators, and authors can earn income by licensing their work. A ruling on whether AI training qualifies as fair use could affect their ability to negotiate how their work is used and whether they’re paid for that use. Those decisions are especially important to independent creators and small publishers, whose work can help train tools that produce content competing with their own.

“In re: OpenAI, Inc. Copyright Infringement Litigation will likely be one of the most consequential intellectual property cases of the decade. The ruling will undoubtedly have ripple effects through the creative sector, which was estimated to contribute over $2 trillion or 7.66% to U.S. GDP,” Pingree and the lawmakers wrote. “There are nearly 150 copyright lawsuits involving an AI system, model, training pipeline, or output currently pending that hinge on the resolution of many of the legal questions this case raises.”

DOJ argued that restricting the use of copyrighted material to train generative AI could harm U.S. national security. The lawmakers questioned how broadly DOJ applied that argument to AI tools with widely different uses. They also asked how the filing squares with the Trump Administration’s stated support for letting courts resolve whether AI training on copyrighted material constitutes fair use.

“The DOJ’s apparent decision to forego consultation with USCO and USPTO and its efforts to justify intervening in this case altogether raise serious questions about potential bias,” the lawmakers wrote. “This SOI stands to undermine public trust in the impartiality of the DOJ and its ability to represent the best interests of the nation.”

The lawmakers are asking DOJ to provide the following by November 30:

Its procedures for reviewing and approving statements of interest in intellectual property cases, including who approved the September 1 filing.

Confirmation of whether DOJ consulted either federal office and an explanation for any decision to proceed without its input.

All internal drafts and supporting documents used to develop the filing, along with the names of any outside companies or organizations that provided legal analysis, briefing materials, or other communications related to it.

Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (D-Ore.), Greg Casar (D-Texas), Judy Chu (D-Calif.), Valerie Foushee (D-N.C.), Maxwell Frost (D-Fla.), Jared Huffman (D-Calif.), Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-Calif.), Ro Khanna (D-Calif.), and Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.) joined Pingree, Balint, and Ross in signing the letter.

The letter is available here.

title: Pou, Menendez, McIver Demand Polluter Accountability for Full Cleanup of Passaic River Superfund Site
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Representatives Nellie Pou (NJ-09), Rob Menendez (NJ-08), and LaMonica McIver (NJ-10) are seeking answers on the proposed Environmental Protection Agency (“EPA”) and the Department of Justice (“DOJ”) $125 million Passaic River settlement, pushing for the next stage of cleanup at the Diamond Alkali Superfund site while warning that the final deal must not limit future funding to restore the river.

“Our communities along the Passaic River have lived with the consequences of toxic pollution for far too long,” said Congresswoman Nellie Pou. “The companies responsible must be held accountable for the full cost of cleaning up what is one of the largest and most complicated Superfund sites in the nation. This $125 million agreement can be a critical step forward, but we need assurances that corporate restructuring and legal scheming will not leave taxpayers on the hook for billions of dollars in any remaining cleanup costs.”

“The proposed Passaic River cleanup agreement is a promising step forward for families in Newark and neighboring communities who have borne the brunt of toxic pollution for far too long,” said Congressman Rob Menendez. “But polluters must remain accountable for completing this essential work. We are conducting oversight to ensure that this deal protects taxpayers, supports future efforts to fully restore the river, and advances environmental justice for the communities that we serve.”

"New Jersey families have suffered the consequences of delayed cleanups and lack of accountability from polluters for too long. This agreement is an important step toward delivering the relief our communities deserve,” said Congresswoman LaMonica McIver. “But our work does not end here. We must ensure that environmental justice and restoration projects remain long-term priorities so that our residents are protected and our districts can thrive.”

The submission follows a joint effort led by Representatives Pou, Menendez, and McIver urging the EPA and DOJ to hold polluters accountable and accelerate site remediation.

The Diamond Alkali site remains severely contaminated by industrial waste, including dioxins from Vietnam War-era production of herbicides used in Agent Orange. Decades of delays have left local waterways poisoned by toxic pollution and threatened the health and safety of generations of residents. The lawmakers are pushing federal agencies to build cleanup sites onshore and hold polluters accountable.

In their comment, the lawmakers requested explicit answers from the DOJ and EPA to five key questions:

What is the rationale for entering into the consent decree now and as structured, particularly the decision to enter into the agreement solely with ERH?

Why is OxyChem TX not a party to the consent decree?

What financial assurances have DOJ and EPA received from ERH? Please share all documents received regarding the assets and liabilities of ERH and OxyChem TX.

Can ERH fulfill the full remaining cleanup obligations beyond the scope of this consent decree?

In your view, could this consent decree prejudice future liability claims against other potentially responsible parties, such as OxyChem TX?

The full public comment is available here.

The Passaic River runs through North Jersey’s Ninth Congressional District, impacting nearly thirty cities and towns across Bergen, Passaic, and Hudson counties. The river is also home to the Great Falls National Historical Park in Paterson. The cleanup of the Diamond Alkali Superfund Site is a project that Representative Pou has pushed for since 2025, among other environmental initiatives meant to restore, revitalize, and re-invest in the Passaic River. The EPA has previously estimated that it will take $1.38 billion to clean up the river.

title: WATCH: Pressley Honors Life and Legacy of Constituent & Safe Streets Advocate Louisa Gag
text:
Heartfelt Floor Speech Comes on the Heels of World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims

Video (YouTube)

WASHINGTON – Today, during a speech on the House floor, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Chair of the Future of Transportation Caucus, honored the life and legacy of Louisa Gag, a lifelong Boston resident, dedicated safe streets advocate, and city transportation planner whose life was stolen in a truck collision earlier this year. In her remarks, Rep. Pressley spoke of her experience working with Louisa to pass essential pedestrian and cyclist protections in Boston and uplifted Louisa’s family’s continued advocacy to create safer streets and more livable, enjoyable communities.

A full transcript of the Congresswoman’s speech is available below and the video is available here.

Transcript: Pressley Honors Life and Legacy of Constituent & Safe Streets Advocate Louisa Gag

November 19, 2026

U.S. House of Representatives

Mr. Speaker, I rise today in commemoration of World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims to honor the life and legacy of Louisa Gag.

Born and raised in Boston, Louisa dedicated her life to the city she loved as a transportation planner, street safety advocate, and biking enthusiast.

During my tenure on the Boston City Council, I worked with Louisa to pass the nation’s first truck side-guard ordinance to protect pedestrians and cyclists from collisions.

Our city has been made better because of her.

This July, we tragically lost Louisa to a truck collision while riding her bicycle, doing what she loved most.

My husband Conan and I extend our deepest sympathies to Louisa’s parents, Laura and Steve, and her sister, Emily.

While grieving this unimaginable loss, they have dedicated themselves to finishing the work Louisa started.

By raising awareness, fundraising, and working to pass critical legislation—Louisa’s Law—Louisa’s family is asking us to put our prayers into action and save lives.

In her memory, and as she surely would have wanted, let us commit ourselves to safer streets and more livable communities.

I yield.

—–

In October 2019, Rep. Pressley founded and currently co-chairs the Future of Transportation Caucus, a Congressional caucus focused on centering equity, access, and sustainability in our transportation systems.

In September 2026, Congresswoman Pressley convened a roundtable with transit safety advocates to discuss their priorities to create safer communities and more accessible transit options for pedestrians, cyclist, & commuters across the Massachusetts 7th Congressional District.

In 2014, as a Boston City Councilor, Congresswoman Pressley partnered with then Mayor Marty Walsh, the Boston Cyclists Union, and the LivableStreets Alliance to pass the nation’s first municipal truck side-guard ordinance, creating safety standards for city-owned vehicles and advancing the prevention of fatal collisions.

In July 2025, Congresswoman Pressley and Senator Markey re-introduced the Freedom to Move Act, their legislation to support state and local efforts to establish public transportation as a public good through fare-free services. In August 2025, Rep. Pressley, Sen. Markey, and Mayor Wu announced their continued efforts to implement fare-free public transportation in Boston and across the Commonwealth. Rep. Pressley and Sen. Markey originally introduced the Freedom to Move Act in June 2020. Following the bill’s introduction, Senator Markey, Congresswoman Pressley, and then-Councilor Michelle Wu published an op-ed that discussed the bill and the need to fund public transportation as a public good. In July 2020, the House of Representatives passed the Moving Forward Act that included a fare-free pilot program modeled after the two lawmakers Freedom to Move Act. In August 2026, Rep. Pressley and Sen. Markey released a new report, Making Transit Free, Frequent, and Reliable: Massachusetts shows the need for federal investment in fare-free transit, detailing the need for increased federal investments in fare-free transit.

In September 2026, Rep. Pressley and Mayor Michelle Wu announced that the City of Boston is filing a lawsuit challenging the Trump Administration’s unlawful withdrawal of a $20 million federal grant for critical street infrastructure improvements along three major corridors in Roxbury. In 2022, Rep. Pressley helped deliver these investments which would fund safety, transit, accessibility, and traffic flow improvements to essential roadways in Roxbury. Rep. Pressley has been advocating for federal funding to support the Roxbury Resiliency Corridors Project and submitted a letter of support for the project to DOT in April 2022. In September 2025, Rep. Pressley vehemently condemned the Trump administration’s cancellation of this essential federal grant.

In December 2025, Rep. Pressley led 14 colleagues in sending a letter to House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Chair Sam Graves and Ranking Member Rick Larsen urging they prioritize affordability, accessibility, and sustainability in crafting the Surface Transportation Reauthorization bill—including by investing in fare-free transit. These priorities reflect the mission of the Future of Transportation Caucus, which reimagines America’s transportation systems to center equity, access, and sustainability.

In August 2022, Rep. Pressley and Senator Markey called on the MBTA to make the entire T fare-free for the duration of the Orange Line’s shutdown.

title: Quigley, Olszewski Introduce COUNT Act to Better Measure Community College Success
text:
U.S. Representatives Mike Quigley (IL-05) and Johnny Olszewski (MD-02) today introduced the Community College COUNT (Capturing Outcomes and Understanding Nontraditional Trajectories) Act to modernize federal higher education data collection to ensure community colleges receive appropriate recognition – and federal investment.

Community colleges serve students whose educational journeys often look different from the traditional four-year college experience. Many, for example, attend part-time while working, return to school as adults, pursue workforce training, apprenticeship or non-credit programs, or transfer to four-year institutions.

Yet federal measures of student success have historically focused on full-time, first-time students pursuing degrees or certificates, often using completion timelines that fail to capture the broader community college experience. The COUNT Act would address these gaps by expanding the information collected through the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), the federal government's annual higher education data collection process.

“Community colleges help people build careers and create better lives for themselves and their families,” said Congressman Johnny Olszewski. “When federal data only recognizes traditional four-year college experience, we miss a huge part of that story. The COUNT Act is a common-sense way to give policymakers a more complete understanding of community college outcomes and to ensure that federal policies and investments reflect the students and communities these institutions serve.”

“Our community colleges in Chicago offer affordable, flexible opportunities for anyone wanting to further their education,” said Congressman Mike Quigley. “I’m leading the COUNT Act with Rep. Olszewski because we need to keep investing in our community colleges, and we can only do that if we modernize the federal research process to adequately represent these institutions. Our community colleges deserve respect, recognition, and the funding they need to succeed.”

With better data, the COUNT Act would give policymakers a stronger foundation for making federal funding decisions, helping ensure that community colleges are appropriately recognized for the students they serve, the credentials they award, and the workforce pathways they support.

For example, the Community College of Baltimore County (CCBC) in Congressman Olszewski’s district enrolled 55,000 students last year. Under current IPEDS measurement, it graduated 871 students. Under the COUNT Act – which would account for all degrees, transfers, certificates and workplace certifications – the graduation rate soars to 14,051.

“The power of America’s community colleges has been vastly underreported for decades because of the narrow success parameters defined by IPEDS,” said Dr. Sandra Kurtnitis, President of CCBC. “The Federal Reserve Bank model has opened the door to include success metrics of all community college students, whether completing an associate degree or a short-term credential. It is time that the full breadth of community college competition metrics are valued and measured appropriately and not skewed to the negative by outdated metrics never designed for our institutions.”

The legislation is endorsed by the Maryland Association of Community Colleges (MACC).

“Community colleges serve working adults, part-time learners, transfer students, apprentices, dual-enrollment students, and those pursuing noncredit workforce training,” said Dr. Brad Phillips, Executive Director, MACC. “Yet federal data measures still leave too many of these students invisible. The COUNT Act would modernize IPEDS reporting to better reflect the students we serve, the pathways they follow, and the credentials and skills they attain. More complete data will lead to better policy and more equitable investment in institutions that drive workforce development and economic mobility.”

title: After Confronting Mullin, Ramirez Grills FEMA Administrator Over Politicized Response to Illinois’ Disaster Declaration
text:
November 19, 2026

FEMA Administrator Cameron Hamilton confirmed it was Trump’s decision to deny Illinois' FEMA disaster declaration

Washington, DC—Today, Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03) questioned the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Administrator Cameron Hamilton about the agency's politicized response to Illinois’ request for emergency funding. During the committee hearing, the FEMA Administrator failed to provide concrete criteria for denying Illinois’ request three times and instead pointed to the agency following Trump’s discretion.

Image

[CLICK HERE FOR FULL EXCHANGE]

“While thousands of families across Illinois needed assistance, Trump and Mullin turned their backs on our communities in political retribution,” said Congresswoman Ramirez. “Not liking a governor is not enough for FEMA to deny assistance to a state that needs it.”

The exchange came the day after Congresswoman Ramirez confronted Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and told him she would lead investigations into the politicization of FEMA.

For the full video of the Congresswoman’s remarks, CLICK HERE.

BACKGROUND:

Illinois’ request came after the August 2026 severe storms, which brought 60-70 miles-per-hour winds, 8 inches of rain, flooded homes, and damaged infrastructure across Boone, Cook, Kane, McHenry, and Will counties. In September, Illinois declared a disaster and requested federal assistance. According to Illinois State documents, Governor Pritzker’s presidential request totals $27.6 million, exceeding the threshold for statewide disaster assistance by almost $3 million. FEMA’s standard for Illinois is $24.9 million.

Full remarks as prepared for delivery:

Thank you, Chair and Ranking Member, for holding today’s hearing, and to Administrator Hamilton for joining us.

Just yesterday, I told Markwayne Mullin that the politicization of FEMA would be one of my oversight investigations next Congress. So, I am glad we are here today.

You see, States with Republican governors are more likely to have their disaster declarations approved than Democratic governors - 80% to less than 60%, respectively.

You know how I know? Because I have personal experience with that disparity.

When my state asked for federal assistance from FEMA after terrible summer storms, we were denied not ONCE, but THREE TIMES.

In August 2026, severe storms led to 60-70 mile an hour winds, 8 inches of rain, flooded homes, and impacted infrastructure across Boone, Cook, Kane, McHenry, and Will counties.

There were 4,519 residential structures damaged throughout the state, including 46 that were completely destroyed.

Most of the destroyed homes were in Cook County, which also accounted for half of the state’s damaged homes. Nearly half of Cook County residents suffered flood damage that was not covered by insurance.

In September, Illinois declared a disaster and requested federal assistance.

And yet, we were denied, denied, denied: Trump’s administration said that supplemental federal assistance under the Stafford Act is not warranted for this incident. When we appealed, we were denied AGAIN.

According to Illinois State documents, Governor Pritzker’s presidential request that was denied by FEMA exceeded the threshold for statewide disaster assistance by almost $3 million – the damage totaled $27.6 million, while FEMA’s standard for Illinois is $24.9 million.

Administrator Hamilton, can you state for the record why Illinois’ request was denied?

Given Indiana suffered damage from the same storms Illinois faced and Indiana DID receive FEMA approval for disaster assistance for those same storms, can you state for the record which statutory criterion Indiana met that Illinois failed to meet?

Is having a Republican governor now a statutory requirement for getting FEMA assistance?

While thousands of families across Illinois needed assistance, Trump and Mullin turned their backs on our communities in political retribution.

Unfortunately, this Administration’s cruelty comes as no surprise. Trump doesn’t want to care for Americans facing emergencies - he wants to use assistance to curry favor, to reward loyalists, and to privatize services so his cronies profit from our pain.

The Trump administration has been clear that their priority is to enrich their corporate bosses, not to protect our rights, our safety, and our well-being.

So we must be clear that the only way our families will be safe is by returning CISA, FEMA, and the Coast Guard to their mission. Together, we must pass my Reimagining Safety Act to dismantle DHS, abolish ICE, and strengthen the agencies that keep us safe!

And with that, I yield back.

title: HOUSE PASSES RILEY-BACKED BILL TO TAKE DOWN FOREIGN CRIME NETWORKS TARGETING UPSTATE NEW YORKERS
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — The U.S. House of Representatives has passed the Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act (H.R. 5490) – legislation cosponsored by Representative Josh Riley (NY-19) to protect Upstate New Yorkers from online scams. This bipartisan bill creates a first-of-its-kind interagency task force to shut down the foreign criminal networks behind mass online scams targeting Americans.

As AI and other technological developments have fueled a wave of increasingly sophisticated online scams, New Yorkers are among the hardest hit. The Consumer Federation of America estimates that New Yorkers lose $8.7 billion a year to online scams and fraud. In 2025, 45,255 New Yorkers reported cybercrimes to the FBI – one of the highest rates in the country.

“Folks shouldn’t have to wonder whether that call, text, or email from their grandchild or friend is real or a con,” said Riley. “Scammers go after seniors on fixed incomes and working families who’ve spent their whole lives saving, and they hide overseas, thinking nobody will come after them – but we are. This bill shuts down their operations, sanctions the corrupt officials who protect them, and makes clear that if you rob Americans, you’re going to pay for it.”

Since 2021, Chinese criminal organizations active in Southeast Asia have increasingly targeted Americans with elaborate investment schemes. Run by so-called “scam centers,” they often operate as joint ventures between the Chinese criminal groups and autocratic governments in Burma, Laos, and Cambodia. They have robbed thousands of people of their life savings while making transnational criminal syndicates and corrupt leaders richer and more entrenched.

In addition to creating a task force to take on these scam centers, the Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act authorizes sanctions on corrupt officials who enable and profit from these networks. It will also strengthen international law enforcement by helping trusted foreign partners investigate financial crimes, shut down scam compounds, combat money laundering, and protect trafficking victims.

You can read the text of the Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act HERE.

title: Rep. Roy Introduces Bill to Defeat Costly E15 Mandate Expansion
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressman Chip Roy (R-TX) introduced legislation to wind down the costly Renewable Fuels Standard (RFS), bolster domestic refining, give consumers more choice, and help Americans save more at the pump.

The Fuel Freedom Act winds down the burdensome Renewable Volume Obligations (RVOs), which the EPA has set higher every year since the program was first initiated. The RFS has slowly strangled our nation’s domestic refining capacity and compliance with the program adds roughly 30 cents per gallon of gas. The bill also allows gasoline blends of E15 and higher to be sold year-round giving consumers their choice of fuel blend by repealing the patchwork bureaucratic process dictating when and where these blends can be sold.

“The Fuel Freedom Act puts consumers, farmers, and American energy independence first. By eliminating costly government mandates and removing barriers to E15 and higher ethanol blends, we’re empowering the free market, expanding consumer choice, and strengthening America’s domestic energy sector,” said Rep. Roy.

title: Jacobs, Maloy, Beyer Release Outline For Sweeping, Bipartisan AI Safety Legislation
text:
Today U.S. Representatives Sara Jacobs (D-CA), Celeste Maloy (R-UT), and Don Beyer (D-VA) released an outline containing details of the Safe and Accountable Federal Evaluations of Artificial Intelligence (SAFE AI) Act, forthcoming bipartisan legislation that would create federal safety requirements for frontier artificial intelligence.

The broad, ambitious legislation would mandate safety frameworks, incident reporting, and increased transparency from frontier labs with strong government oversight and due process. The outline is available here.

“No industry gets to police itself, and AI shouldn’t be the exception,” said Rep. Sara Jacobs. “Right now, the companies write their own rules while their own models break out of test environments and hack other companies’ systems. Americans are rightly concerned about unchecked AI threatening public safety, critical infrastructure, national security, and the systems we all depend on. That’s why the bipartisan SAFE AI Act puts real guardrails on frontier models, with civil penalties for violations and targeted emergency authority to stop dangerous models when they pose a serious and immediate danger. Our proposal is a floor – not a ceiling, empowering states to adopt stronger protections for their communities. And it is built to adapt as the technology changes, so Americans’ safety never depends on a company’s promise.”

“The companies building the most powerful AI systems ought to be able to show they’ve done their homework before those systems go into wide use,” said Rep. Celeste Maloy. “This bill gives them clear rules, brings in an outside set of eyes to check their work, and leaves room for Utah and other states to set safeguards of their own.”

“This outline is a roadmap towards a safer AI future for the country and the world,” said Rep. Don Beyer. “Recent AI incidents and the growing chorus of warnings from experts underscore the urgency of the task before us. It is vitally important that Congress tackle AI safety swiftly, and that we get it right. At this moment we are continuing to seek input on our forthcoming legislative text from experts and safety leaders, in coordination with committees of jurisdiction. We are sharing this blueprint today to show the direction our work is taking and to encourage further constructive feedback and discussion on what we believe should be a priority for Congress. I thank Reps. Jacobs and Maloy for the leadership and partnership on this bill, which I hope will move the ball forward on AI safety so we can usher in an age of responsible AI innovation.”

title: Peters Statement on Senate Passage of the Largest Energy and Infrastructure Bill in History
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) released the following statement after the Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). Central components of the package draw on Rep. Peters’ priorities to unleash clean energy, fast-track transmission, and lower utility costs.

“BAAJA lowers costs and lowers emissions. It’s that simple. It’s unimaginable that after this month’s election, when the entire country demanded lower costs, we would whiff on the opportunity right in front of us.

“Senate Democrats and Republicans just came together to pass the largest permitting reform package in history. Unfortunately two Senators, at the last minute, opposed bipartisan amendments to make a good bill better for tribal partners. We should make sure this bill gets across the finish line to lower costs and emissions and then continue our work to make the progress they opposed, and more.

“An environmental movement in 2026 that doesn’t prioritize greenhouse gas emissions doesn’t make any sense. Climate change is the biggest threat to our environment and underserved communities. We call it a crisis for a reason. But we will never mitigate this challenge unless we build things quickly and resolve challenges fairly and faster. We must transition to renewable energy at scale, and reduce emissions, now. BAAJA’s transmission and process reforms are our only chance to do that. All reputable analyses agree it would reduce our carbon footprint.

“There will be no better deal on the table. With Donald Trump in the White House and 60 required votes in the Senate, bipartisanship is unavoidable, whether it’s this Congress or next.

“The status quo isn’t working. House leadership should bring this package to the floor as soon as possible so we can get it to the President’s desk and signed into law before this Congress ends.”

Background:

Since coming to Congress, Rep. Peters has been an outspoken advocate for faster energy and permitting reform. As a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, he has long argued that excessive process requirements slow the clean energy buildout and has pushed for transmission to be included in any permitting reform legislation.

Rep. Peters has authored major bipartisan bills including the SPEED and Reliability Act to streamline the buildout of electric transmission lines to lower costs for consumers, the CERTAIN Act to accelerate energy and infrastructure projects by enforcing strict application timelines and stop administrations from canceling permits that were already legally approved, the CLEAR Act to give developers and local stakeholders the certainty to plan and build large energy infrastructure and transmission projects, the BIG WIRES Act to direct FERC to better coordinate construction of an interregional transmission system, and the ePermit Act to digitize the U.S. permitting process.

These bills are all included in BAAJA, and most of the package is built on bipartisan legislation from Rep. Peters' colleagues on the Energy and Commerce committee.

After BAAJA was unveiled in the Senate, he highlighted BAAJA’s inclusion of several bills he’s championed over multiple sessions of Congress and encouraged further discussions and input on the bill. He also hosted a press conference in San Diego with leaders from the renewable energy and labor sectors to discuss local and federal efforts to hold data centers accountable, increase clean energy production, lower costs, and create jobs.

See a full breakdown by Rep. Peters on the need to pass BAAJA here.

title: Rep. Sewell Hosts World Pancreatic Cancer Day Roundtable Highlighting Landmark Advances in Detection and Treatment
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Rep. Terri Sewell (AL-07) convened lawmakers, researchers, advocates, industry experts, and a pancreatic cancer survivor for a roundtable discussion on Capitol Hill marking World Pancreatic Cancer Day and highlighting groundbreaking advances in pancreatic cancer detection and treatment. The discussion focused on the historic progress made in 2026, the importance of sustained federal investment in cancer research, and the work still needed to improve outcomes for patients and families.

Additional photos are available here.

“2026 has shown us what is possible when we invest in groundbreaking research, embrace medical innovation, and work together to put patients first,” said Rep. Sewell. “From the FDA's approval of a promising new targeted treatment to the enactment of our Nancy Gardner Sewell MCED Act, we are making meaningful progress in the fight against cancer. But we cannot afford to let up now. I will continue fighting to increase federal investments in pancreatic cancer research and ensure that patients and families have access to the breakthroughs that can save lives. Our goal must be to make early detection more accessible, expand treatment options, and turn today's progress into tomorrow's cures.”

The roundtable featured Julie Fleshman, JD, MBA, President and CEO of the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network (PanCAN); Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Harvard Medical School; Don Frost, PharmD, MBA, Senior Director of Payer and Health Systems Liaison at Revolution Medicines; and Joe Damore, a pancreatic cancer survivor.

This year has marked a landmark moment in the fight against pancreatic cancer. In August, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved RASONQUE (daraxonrasib), the first broad RAS-targeted treatment for metastatic pancreatic cancer. The groundbreaking therapy represents a major step forward for patients with advanced disease, offering a new treatment option against a cancer that has historically been extremely difficult to treat.

The year also brought a historic victory for early cancer detection with the enactment of the Nancy Gardner Sewell Medicare Multi-Cancer Early Detection (MCED) Screening Coverage Act, bipartisan legislation led by Rep. Sewell and signed into law in February. The law establishes a pathway for Medicare coverage of qualifying multi-cancer early detection tests once FDA approved, helping ensure that seniors can benefit from emerging technologies capable of detecting multiple cancers through a single screening test.

“On World Pancreatic Cancer Day, we celebrate an extraordinary year of progress for pancreatic cancer patients with breakthroughs in research that were once thought impossible, but we know more work is needed,” said Julie Fleshman, JD, MBA, President and CEO of PanCAN. “Thanks to the leadership of Representative Sewell and the continued federal investment in pancreatic cancer research, advances are bringing new hope to patients and families. We must build on this momentum by continuing to increase the federal investment in cancer research to ensure the next generation of breakthroughs reaches patients who need them and survival becomes the expectation, not the exception.”

Rep. Sewell has also made increasing federal investment in pancreatic cancer research a priority. Earlier this year, she successfully led the effort to restore and increase appropriations for pancreatic cancer research through in the Congressionally Directed Medical Research Program (CDMRP) in the FY26 defense bill after funding for the program was completely eliminated in FY25 under Republicans' continuing resolution. Sewell secured a historic $20 million for the program, a $5 million increase from FY24 funding levels. Building on that achievement, she secured an additional $25 million in the House-passed FY2027 defense appropriations bill.

Pancreatic cancer remains among the deadliest forms of cancer, in large part because it is often diagnosed at an advanced stage when treatment options are limited. Today's roundtable underscored the importance of continued collaboration among researchers, medical professionals, advocates, industry leaders, policymakers, and survivors to accelerate scientific discovery and ensure that promising advances reach the patients who need them most.

title: Congresswoman Simon Introduces New Immigration Bill to Protect Community Members from Deportation and Create Pathway to Status
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Congressman John Garamendi (CA-08), Congresswoman Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), and Congressman Juan Vargas (CA-52) introduced new legislation called the Protect Our Neighbors Act, which would provide relief to individuals with final orders of removal and create a pathway for them to obtain legal permanent residency.

There are approximately 1.19 million individuals in the United States living with final orders of removal. However, a final order of removal does not mean someone will necessarily be deported. For many, removal may be delayed or suspended for years, including through deferred action or other circumstances. During that time, they build lives and become valued members of their community. These individuals raise families, work essential jobs, pay taxes, and put down meaningful roots in the only home they may have known for decades. Yet, despite the lives they have built, these individuals live with the uncertainty of being separated from their families and communities at any moment. For 73-year-old East Bay resident and Sikh community member, Ms. Harjit Kaur, that uncertainty became reality as a result of Trump’s cruel mass deportation agenda. Last year, Ms. Kaur was abruptly arrested during a routine immigration check-in despite having worked and lived in California for over thirty years.

The Protect Our Neighbors Act would give people a fair chance to move forward and past their final orders of removal. It would establish a 10-year expiration on final orders of removal for individuals who have been continuously present in the country and not convicted of a crime. It would also create a pathway for these individuals to apply for legal permanent resident status.

“No one should have to live in constant fear of being torn away from their family and community after spending years building a life in this country. I am sick of the Trump Administration targeting our neighbors and threatening the lives they have worked so hard to build. These are people who have spent years contributing to our communities, working hard, and putting down roots,” said Congresswoman Simon. “The Protect Our Neighbors Act would provide people, like Ms. Kaur who worked in my district for decades, with a fair opportunity to move beyond a final order of removal and continue building futures here in the U.S where they have made their homes and families. I am incredibly grateful to Congressmembers Garamendi, Lofgren, and Vargas for standing with me and partnering on this important legislation.”

“We are still traumatized and horrified by the cruel treatment of our grandmother one year ago,” said Harjit Kaur’s family. “Harjit was a pillar to our family and our community. She spent over thirty years in the United States, raising her children and later her grandchildren, and became a grandmother figure to our whole community. What was worse about her treatment was how unnecessary it was. We tried to work with ICE to bring her back to India, but at every turn the agency chose the more violent and cruel path — denying her food, moving her in the middle of the night without letting us know, and sending her back without letting us say goodbye. The pain that we still feel today remains with the knowledge that Harjit is one of thousands who’ve experienced the same situation. We thank the Members of Congress for their continued advocacy, and we hope that some good could come from Harjit’s story with this bill and others like it.”

"President Trump promised to go after the 'worst of the worst' in his immigration policy. Yet his administration has repeatedly decided to cruelly deport residents who have been working, paying taxes, and raising families in their communities for decades,” said Rep. Garamendi. This is exactly what happened to one of our constituents. Nearly one year ago, ICE cruelly detained and deported Harjit Kuar, a 73-year-old grandmother with no criminal record — who faithfully reported to ICE every six months for more than 13 years. Her cruel and unreasonable detention and deportation is just one more example of the thousands of individuals across the country whose lives and families have been upended by Trump's ICE. Unfortunately, this has become far too common under Donald Trump's mass deportation agenda, which is exactly why I'm proud to introduce this commonsense and humane fix to our immigration system with Representatives Simon, Lofgren and Vargas."

“We need a sensible immigration policy for those who have resided peacefully for a long time in America and have been upstanding members of their communities," said Rep. Lofgren, a senior member of the House Judiciary Committee and a former immigration lawyer. “Detaining and deporting folks with no criminal record is not what Donald Trump campaigned on, and it’s not what the American people want. The Protect Our Communities Act provides long-term residents who have built their lives here with a fair opportunity to resolve outdated removal orders and earn lawful permanent status."

“The Trump Administration’s anti-immigrant agenda is destroying lives. Trump isn’t going after the ‘worst of the worst.’ He’s terrorizing our communities and ripping families apart. I’m proud to introduce this legislation alongside Representatives Garamendi, Simon, and Lofgren to bring a commonsense fix to our immigration system. We need comprehensive immigration reform and an end to Trump’s mass deportation agenda,” said Rep. Vargas.

title: Strong Highlights Redstone Arsenal's Central Role in Homeland Security During Worldwide Threats Hearing
text:
WASHINGTON – Representative Dale Strong (AL-05), a member of the Committee on Homeland Security, highlighted North Alabama’s critical role in protecting the nation and pressed senior federal officials on opportunities to strengthen national security capabilities at Redstone Arsenal during the Committee’s annual “Worldwide Threats to the Homeland: 25 Years After 9/11” hearing.

“North Alabama is home to some of the most advanced national security capabilities in the country, and Redstone Arsenal continues to play a critical role in protecting the American people,” said Rep. Dale Strong. “The FBI's counter-drone training mission at Redstone is a prime example of how the expertise concentrated in our region is strengthening our nation's security. Much of the technology used to counter drone threats comes from our district, and I will continue advocating for these capabilities to protect large gatherings across America. Whether it's the Olympics or a college football stadium packed on a Saturday, we must make sure law enforcement has the tools and training needed to stay ahead of these threats and keep Americans safe.”

The hearing examined the evolving threats facing the United States in the 25 years since September 11 and the efforts of federal agencies to address these challenges. Strong questioned FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia about Redstone Arsenal's importance to the Bureau's mission and opportunities for continued growth and collaboration in Huntsville. He also questioned Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on the importance of collaboration with North Alabama's national security community in identifying and addressing emerging threats.

EXCERPTS FROM THE HEARING TRANSCRIBED BELOW:

During his exchange with FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia, Strong highlighted the growing national security capabilities at Redstone Arsenal.

STRONG: “Deputy Director Raia, can you speak to the importance of Redstone Arsenal and the broader Huntsville community to the FBI's mission, and the opportunities you see for continued growth and collaboration there?”

RAIA: “I think one of the biggest strides that we’ve made in the last 21 months, not only with the FBI but with the Department of Homeland Security and our federal partners, is in that fight against counter-UAS. [...] In the last 21 months, based on a multitude of things, to include the standing up of [the] National Counter-UAS Training Center, [...] we are much better postured against that threat than we were 21 months ago. And I appreciate your support, and I appreciate everything you’ve done to help us in that effort.”

Strong also addressed the importance of interagency collaboration with Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin.

STRONG: “Secretary Mullin, from DHS's perspective, how important is collaboration with the national security community in North Alabama to identifying and addressing emerging threats to the homeland?”

MULLIN: “We couldn’t do it without the cooperation. It is vital for state, local, [and] federal cooperation. It’s the only way we’re going to effectively combat it.”

title: Thompson, Schrier Introduce Legislation to Improve Forest Management, Support Rural Communities, Lower Housing Costs
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, U.S. Representatives Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-Pa.) and Kim Schrier (D-Wash.) introduced the bipartisan Forest Bioeconomy Act. This legislation will expand the commercial uses of low-value timber to decrease wildfire risk, support sustainable local timber production, and provide affordable housing. This will incentivize industries to use low-value timber for wood products.

United States Senators Steve Daines (R-Mont.), Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.), Jim Justice (R-W. Va.), and Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) introduced the Senate companion legislation.

“Forestry has sustained Pennsylvania’s rural communities for generations, which is why I am pleased to introduce the bipartisan Forest Bioeconomy Act. This bill will modernize the Forest Service’s public-private research partnerships so that innovations developed in federal laboratories reach the mills, manufacturers, and landowners who can put them to work. These commonsense provisions will keep Pennsylvania's forestry industry going for years to come, and ensure businesses have the tools necessary to meet increasing demand," Rep. Thompson said.

“Communities across Washington state are still reeling from the damage of last summer’s devastating wildfires,” Rep. Schrier said. “Our families also face skyrocketing prices across the board, and need relief now. I am proud that this bill works to support our local economies, lower housing costs, and reduce the risk of catastrophic wildfires by creating new demand for low-value timber. I will continue my work to ensure our communities and local leaders have the tools they need to keep Washingtonians safe and protect our cherished environments.”

“We applaud Rep. Schrier and Chairman Thompson for their leadership introducing the House companion to the Forest Bioeconomy Act. Healthy forests depend on healthy markets, and right now, the wood products industry is facing real challenges,” said Jackson Morrill, President and CEO of the American Wood Council. “Homebuilder sentiment is at its lowest level in over a decade, and we are grappling with a changing residuals market. The Forest Bioeconomy Act will spur much needed development in emerging markets like mass timber and will encourage critical technology transfer between the Forest Service and industry. We encourage Congress to work quickly to advance this bipartisan measure and look forward to working with both sponsors to secure passage.”

“Forest-dependent communities have long called for investments that connect healthy forests with strong local economies,” said Cole Jenson, Acting Coalition Director of Rural Voices for Conservation Coalition. “The Forest Bioeconomy Act responds to that need by helping turn publicly funded research on underused wood into valuable products and new opportunities for rural businesses and workers. We applaud this effort to connect innovation with the practical needs of communities working to restore and steward our forests."

This legislation is also endorsed by the National Association of Forest Owners, Alliance for Wildfire Resilience, and National Association of State Foresters.

Background: Forests across the country are currently overstocked, mostly with small-diameter, sick, low strength, or otherwise low-value fiber. This overstocking increases wildfire risk and prevents healthy forest ecosystems from forming. The Forest Bioeconomy Act will support aging local markets and timber communities that sell this lower-value wood, creating high-demand products and ultimately lowering housing and building costs.

The Forest Bioeconomy Act will expand the U.S. Forest Service's public-private research partnerships and help build new innovative markets for forest products, including mass timber used for building materials. This research will enhance industry collaboration efforts similar to the success found at the Department of Energy (DOE). DOE has more than 40,000 patents and 1,400 active licenses, while the Forest Service has 42 patents and eight active licenses.

title: Trahan, Bennet, Grassley, Miller-Meeks Press Trump Administration to Accelerate Implementation of Law to Improve Kids’ Access to Life-Saving Care
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (D-MA-03), a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee’s Health Subcommittee, joined Senators Michael Bennet (D-CO) and Chuck Grassley (R-IA) and Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-IA-01) in urging timely implementation of the Accelerating Kids’ Access to Care Act. Trahan championed the bipartisan legislation, which was signed into law in February to improve access to life-saving care for children with complex medical conditions.

“We appreciate the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) work to implement the Accelerating Kids’ Access to Care Act (Section 6101 of Public Law 119-75). Our most vulnerable kids and their families deserve a health care system that coordinates care and produces healthier outcomes, rather than one that requires them to navigate excessive bureaucracy and red tape. Our law will improve health care access for children with complex medical conditions by simplifying out-of-state Medicaid screening and enrollment processes for pediatric care providers, all while retaining key safeguards to preserve the integrity of the program. We request that CMS expeditiously initiate the rulemaking ahead of the three-year implementation deadline and issue guidance to State Medicaid Agencies (SMAs) advising them on current law and regulations in the interim,” the lawmakers wrote.

Being a parent of children with complex medical needs can be extremely challenging. On average, these children see five to six specialists and up to as many as 20 to 30 health professionals, leaving parents to navigate numerous providers, countless appointments, and complex insurance coverage. Additionally, this kind of timely specialty care requires coordination between out-of-state and in-state providers, along with State Medicaid officials, which often leads to delays in getting medically necessary specialty care. With all of this in mind, helping these families remove bureaucratic barriers is essential, especially with advancements in care.

“Our law established a streamlined pathway for eligible providers caring for children with complex medical needs to enroll in out-of-state Medicaid programs without facing duplicative processes. Eligibility is limited only to providers who are enrolled in good standing in Medicare or their home state Medicaid program, and who have not been prohibited from participating in any federal health care programs. This law passed Congress with tremendous bipartisan support and the backing of hundreds of health care providers and provider organizations, patient advocacy groups, and other entities. Once implemented, it will remove impediments that delay access to time-sensitive care and reduce unnecessary administrative costs and burdens for children with complex medical needs and their families,” the lawmakers continued.

“We are grateful that the Accelerating Kids’ Access to Care Act is now law. We urge CMS to move forward expeditiously with the necessary rulemaking and implementation work, so that its benefits can be felt by children with complex medical needs and their families. We look forward to working with you on this important matter,” the lawmakers concluded.

First introduced by Trahan in 2023, the Accelerating Kids’ Access to Care Act addresses harmful delays caused by insurance prior authorization requirements for children with complex and chronic conditions. The law streamlines approval processes for pediatric specialists and treatments, helping ensure that children battling rare diseases can receive timely, often lifesaving care without families facing repeated denials or dangerous treatment delays.

title: Trahan Releases Updated FRONTIER Act Section-by-Section
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), a member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, released a section-by-section summary of her updated Frontier Risk Oversight, National Transparency, Independent Evaluation, and Reporting (FRONTIER) Act. Full bill text will follow in the coming weeks.

“The American people are fed up with the biggest AI companies writing their own rules and grading their own homework. That approach failed on social media, and we can’t let it happen again with an even more powerful technology,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “We can’t wait until January to start building strong, durable guardrails that can pass both chambers of Congress and be signed into law. Building the coalition to get there starts now.”

Trahan is working to update the legislation to reflect months of feedback from a broad coalition of stakeholders. Key changes include:

Floor preemption: State laws more protective than the legislation are preserved. States with weaker or no standards are preempted to create a federal floor.

Embedded, independent verification. Prescriptive language to guarantee embedded access for independent verification organizations (IVOs) and mechanisms for government assignment of IVOs to avoid a race-to-the-bottom.

Addressing recursive self-improvement. Automated AI research and development, including recursive self improvement, is its own category of catastrophic risk. Each of the bill’s obligations apply to it, including frameworks, reporting, and IVO assessments.

Enforceable corrective orders. When frontier developers fail to adequately mitigate risk, the federal government can require specific corrective action, backed by civil penalties and injunctive relief. IVOs have a duty to recommend corrective actions to developers.

Penalties and reporting requirements for near misses. Penalizes frontier developers for near misses to incentivize precautions before a catastrophe materializes. Also mandates that developers report these incidents to the government.

Office of AI Security. Formally establishes a new office within the U.S. Department of Commerce to administer the regulatory regime, led by a Senate-confirmed Assistant Secretary for AI Security. The bill authorizes significant appropriations for this office and grants it special hiring authorities.

Broader incident reporting. Reportable incidents now include near misses, models deceiving their developers, and incidents affecting critical infrastructure. Also includes a broader knowledge standard, requiring developers who “should have known” about an incident to report it.

Outcome-based standard. Frontier developers’ published safety frameworks must be reasonably designed to adequately mitigate catastrophic risk. Commerce must publish guidance for companies on best practices, standards, and methods to meet the standard.
