title: AI, Drones, and Nihilistic Violent Extremism: Rep. Van Epps Questions Top Security Officials at Worldwide Threats Hearing
text:
Today, the House Homeland Security Committee held a hearing titled “Worldwide Threats to the Homeland: 25 Years After 9/11.” Witnesses included Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin; Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton; and Deputy Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation Christopher Raia.

Click here to watch Rep. Van Epps’ Remarks and Questions

Rep. Van Epps gave the following opening statement:

“Thank you, Chairman Garbarino, for continuing to hold these hearings, and thank you, Secretary Mullin, Deputy Director Raia, and Director Clayton, for joining us today. I am deeply grateful for the services you provide to this country.

It is an honor to serve on this committee dedicated to stewarding this country's security. We know that the threats facing us today are more varied and complex than ever before [as] the cyber domain grows increasingly competitive and difficult to defend; our critical infrastructure is vulnerable to attacks from the other side of the planet; our young people are being radicalized online, [and] biological, technological, and ideological threats evolve faster every day.

During last year’s Worldwide Threats hearing, I discussed emerging AI threats. Today, that threat is still a priority. Foreign cyber actors continue to use AI tools to threaten our cyber infrastructure. Part of our responsibility is to ensure the federal government safeguards our critical systems from these threats while also clearly delineating how AI can be used across our systems to make them stronger and more efficient.”

Rep. Van Epps was also able to ask the following questions:

Rep. Van Epps asked:

“Director Clayton, leading American AI developers have activated heightened safeguards on their most capable models because they cannot rule out that those models could meaningfully help a novice build a biological weapon. In September, Anthropic disclosed five cases since December in which users tried to get around its safeguards on dual-use biology, involving highly pathogenic avian influenza, orthopoxviruses, and toxins. Open-weight models offer no such protections once downloaded. Does ODNI assess [that] terrorist groups or other non-traditional actors are actively seeking to use AI to acquire chemical or biological weapons capabilities, and how has the intelligence community adjusted its collection to detect it?”

Director Clayton responded:

“Thank you, and I commend you for the context in which you placed that question. American frontier model developers are at the forefront; that capability is very important to national security for many of the reasons that you just mentioned. That is not isolated work. They are ahead; they are working with us, seeking to develop this capability in what I would say is a responsible and controlled environment. That does not mean people around the world are following those same rules. It is one of those reasons why we need to be out in front… of those who would seek to develop similar technology, seek to have similar compute, and not use it for good. The United States has demonstrated through every technological development that our leadership is good for the world. We need to keep doing that.”

Rep. Van Epps then asked:

“Deputy Director Raia, the terror threat landscape in the U.S. is increasingly shaped by emerging Nihilistic Violent Extremism, or NVE. These decentralized online groups are primarily run by minors who promote cycles of victimization and coercion, including self-harm, extortion, and mass attacks. I am very concerned about what this is doing to our youth. At the federal level, how has the FBI approached investigations and prosecutions tied to NVE groups since most are minors with prosecutorial limitations?”

Deputy Director Raia responded:

“Thank you for that question, Congressman. I, as yourself, [am] very concerned about that threat, and the FBI is concerned about that threat. That is a threat that we have pushed a lot of resources into. It encompasses, obviously, for us, it is considered a domestic terrorism threat. Groups like 764, the Com, which I know you are familiar with. But it also has a crimes against children aspect to it. Because it is targeting one of our most vulnerable populations, our children. So what we have done at the FBI is create the NVE fusion cell, and we have taken experts from our domestic terrorism folks and experts from our crimes against children folks, and we put them in one room in order to create that synergy to investigate those cases. So we have seen a lot of wins in that space recently. But as you have said, a lot of these are minors, and as you know, the federal system is not set up for minors, so we rely a lot on our state and local partners in not only disrupting those individuals but also in getting some type of jail time in making sure they are held accountable. In extreme circumstances, with some of our older children, we can go to the Attorney General and prosecute on a federal law. But that is something that does not happen that often. That is something we continue to work on, we’re going to continue to push a lot of energy into, and we’re going to continue to keep our children safe because that is a priority of this administration and of our director.”

Congressman Van Epps asked if Deputy Director Raia had any additional comments on UAS systems.

Deputy Director Raia responded:

"We have made a lot of space in [the] last 21 months, and we are much better postured now combating as a country, state, local, and federal… combating that threat than we were just 21 months ago."

Watch Rep. Van Epps talk about the hearing on Washington Watch here.

title: Ahead of Holiday Travel Season, Vindman Introduces Bill to Require Airlines to Seat Families Together at No Extra Cost
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Ahead of the busy holiday travel season, Congressman Eugene Vindman (Va.-07) today introduced legislation to ensure families with young children can sit together on commercial flights without being forced to pay additional seat-selection fees.

The Families Fly Together Act would require all commercial airlines operating in the United States to seat children under the age of 13 with their accompanying family members at no additional cost, establishing a uniform national standard to protect families from unnecessary fees and ensure children can travel safely alongside their parents or guardians.

“As a dad, I know that traveling with children can be stressful enough without having to worry about paying extra just to sit together as a family,” said Vindman. “With the holiday travel season right around the corner, families across Virginia and the country are already facing rising costs. The last thing they need is another unnecessary airline fee just to sit next to their kids. Parents should never have to pay a premium to keep their children by their side. This legislation will help put an end to these unfair practices, keep families together, and make air travel more affordable for hardworking Americans.”

Specifically, the legislation would:

Require airlines to provide adjacent seating for children under 13 and an accompanying parent or legal guardian without charging additional fees.

Prohibit airlines from separating eligible families solely because they did not purchase premium seat assignments.

Require airlines to make family seating accommodations during booking process.

Direct the U.S. Department of Transportation to enforce compliance and establish penalties for airlines that repeatedly violate the requirement.

title: Vindman Joins Colleagues in Urging $11 Million in Additional Funding for Mental Health Support at Cyber Command Following Suicides
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Eugene Vindman (D-Va.-07) joined Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (D-Md.-03) and a bipartisan group of their colleagues on the House Armed Services Committee’s Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation (CITI) Subcommittee in requesting an additional $11 million in funding for mental health support at U.S. Cyber Command, following reports of multiple suicides earlier this year.

Vindman and Elfreth were joined by Representatives Don Bacon (R-Neb.-02), Ro Khanna (D-Calif.-17), Rich McCormick (R-Ga.-07), Chrissy Houlahan (D-Pa.-06), Herbert Conaway (D-N.J.-03), and Pat Ryan (D-N.Y.-18).

“We respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high-performance team training… Headquartered at Fort George G. Meade, U.S. Cyber Command is central to Maryland’s national security community and relies on service members, civilian employees, and families throughout our state to conduct some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent missions,” wrote the CITI members.

“One loss of life is one too many,” they continued. “We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at NSA and Cyber Command has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again.”

The full letter can be found here and below.

—

Dear Chairman Cole, Ranking Member DeLauro, Chair Collins, and Vice Chair Murray:

As Congress completes the Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act, we respectfully urge you to retain the $11 million program increase for U.S. Cyber Command high performance team training included under H.R.9495, Budget Activity 12D, Cyberspace Operations. This targeted investment would help Cyber Command build durable mental health and resilience support for the service members, civilian employees, and teams conducting some of the Nation’s most demanding and persistent military operations. Recent public reporting has described several deaths by suicide among personnel in cyber operations and the Fort Meade community over a short period. Each death is layered with unique personal and professional challenges that no single program can specifically address, however there are areas where prevention efforts have been proven effective. Nevertheless, the concentration of these tragedies within a small, highly specialized workforce demands sustained attention and an institutional response proportionate to the operational strain these personnel bear.

During the Cyber, Information Technologies, and Innovation subcommittee’s recent visit, we saw firsthand that the Cyber personnel operate in a uniquely stressful environment. Many of whom are effectively “deployed in place” for two- or three-year assignments, conducting real-world operations against capable adversaries without the clear start and end points, protected recovery periods, or unitlevel reconstitution cycles associated with conventional deployments.

Because much of their work is classified, personnel may be unable to discuss the source of their stress with family members or with medical professionals who lack the clearances or facility access. These conditions can isolate personnel, limit timely access to appropriate care, and ultimately weaken readiness, retention, and operational effectiveness. Congress and the Department have already recognized this gap. Congress previously directed a review of the psychological and occupation specific demands placed on cyber operators, and the Department subsequently acknowledged that existing resources did not fully meet the needs of the U.S. Cyber Command. The Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) also expanded mental health services intended to address the Cyber Command’s unique requirements by integrating behavioral health professionals with security clearances within cyber units.

Nevertheless, the force has not yet fully implemented recommended dedicated support teams and embedded care consistently across the force. The requested $11 million would allow Cyber Command to begin closing that gap by funding the FY26 NDAA provision. Embedded support would give providers a better understanding of the mission and its operational tempo, improve access to care for service members inside secure facilities, identify problems earlier, and help commanders build sustainable training, recovery, and resilience practices.

Successful models in other high-demand communities, including special operations and remotely piloted unmanned aircraft units and dedicated intelligence commands, demonstrate the value of treating human performance and psychological health as a readiness requirement. Cyber Command noted that this funding could meaningfully reduce burnout and force degradation. This is a modest investment compared with Cyber Command’s broader annual budget and the strategic value of its highly trained workforce. Recruiting, clearing, and developing cyber operators takes years; losing experienced personnel harms families, disrupts teams, increases replacement and training costs, and reduces the Nation’s capacity to defend critical systems and conduct military cyber operations. Including this funding will also help ensure that the Department’s response is not limited to short-term crisis intervention after a tragedy, but instead establishes accountable, enduring prevention and care. One loss of life is one too many.

We must do everything we can to make sure our servicemembers and everyone at NSA and Cyber Command has the full mental health support and resources they need, so that a tragedy like this does not occur again. Accordingly, we respectfully request that the final Fiscal Year 2027 Department of Defense Appropriations Act retain the following program increase: 12D CYBERSPACE OPERATIONS High Performance Team Training: $11,000,000.

Providing this funding will signal that Congress values the health and readiness of cyber personnel as much as the technologies and capabilities they operate. We appreciate your continued leadership and your consideration of this urgent request.

BACKGROUND

Vindman is a 25-year Army veteran and member of the Democratic Veterans Caucus. He also sits on the House Armed Services Committee.

title: Reps. Whitesides, Moran, and Beyer Launch First Congressional Caucus Focused on AI Safety and Innovation
text:
Bipartisan congressional caucus will champion AI safety legislation, address emerging security threats, and help Congress respond more quickly to AI safety incidents

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Reps. George Whitesides (D-CA), Nathaniel Moran (R-TX), and Don Beyer (D-VA), announced the launch of the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, the first congressional caucus focused specifically on addressing AI safety and security risks posed by increasingly advanced AI systems while ensuring the United States remains a global leader in innovative AI technologies.

As AI capabilities accelerate, so do the potential consequences of catastrophic misuse, loss of control over advanced systems, and threats to national security. In July, an experimental OpenAI agent escaped its testing environment and breached the external platform Hugging Face to cheat on an evaluation, without any human directing it to. Anthropic also disclosed three separate incidents in which its AI models escaped testing environments and gained unauthorized access to external organizations during cybersecurity evaluations. These recent security incidents have underscored the need for Congress to better understand these risks and develop policy solutions to prevent these incidents before emerging threats become larger problems. By addressing these challenges proactively, Congress can help create the conditions for continued American innovation and ensure the public can confidently benefit from advances in AI.

“AI is advancing faster than ever before, and Congress needs to move just as quickly,” said Rep. George Whitesides. “Now is the time to build bipartisan consensus and advance commonsense guardrails we know will reduce the most serious risks. Americans are rightly concerned about where this technology is heading, but too often the debate in Washington is framed as a choice between doing nothing and banning AI altogether. That’s a false choice. We have an opportunity to pursue smart, targeted solutions that protect the public while allowing American innovation to thrive. I co-founded this caucus with Reps. Moran and Beyer to fight for that balance, because safe, secure, and controllable AI is the only path to unlocking its full promise for humanity.”

“We don’t have to choose between innovation and safety,” said Rep. Nathaniel Moran. “We can, and we should, do both. Artificial intelligence affects every American, and it should not be a partisan issue. This caucus gives us a place to find the areas of consensus, set partisanship aside, and put smart, targeted policies in place so we can innovate while we keep people safe. Congress needs to be prepared, and I’m proud to be one of the co-chairs leading that work.”

“AI has immense potential to improve our lives and strengthen American innovation, but that progress can’t come at the expense of our national security or public safety,” said Rep. Don Beyer. “Recent cyberattacks involving AI agents and growing warnings from leaders and researchers at the companies developing these technologies make clear that the risks are real and growing. We can’t afford to wait for a major catastrophe before putting meaningful safeguards in place. I’m proud to join the AI Safety Caucus and work with my colleagues to advance responsible legislation that strengthens oversight, security, and transparency while ensuring AI is developed and deployed safely and responsibly.”

Specifically, the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus will:

Champion AI safety legislation: Develop legislative proposals and endorse existing bipartisan bills that establish thoughtful, targeted guardrails against the most serious AI risks while supporting continued innovation and American technological leadership.

Rapidly respond to AI incidents: Convene AI developers, technical experts, and government officials to brief Members and staff when significant AI safety incidents or developments occur and identify potential policy responses.

Equip congressional offices: Keep Members and staff informed about emerging AI developments, connect them with outside experts, and provide resources to navigate complex AI policy decisions.

Elevate AI safety publicly: Raise public awareness and make AI safety a national priority through public statements, op-eds, and press events.

Shape Congress’ AI agenda: Help develop federal AI safety policy and provide Members outside the committees of jurisdiction with an avenue to contribute to the conversation and legislative process.

By quickly addressing emerging threats, the AI Safety and Innovation caucus will ensure AI can continue to make key improvements in the fields of American science, medicine, productivity, and national security. This new bipartisan caucus will advance thoughtful, targeted guardrails, engaging technical experts and industry leaders, and equip Congress to respond quickly to emerging risks and significant AI incidents while ensuring America continues to lead in AI innovation.

The House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus launched with Reps. George Whitesides (D-CA), Nathaniel Moran (R-TX), and Don Beyer (D-VA) serving as co-chairs. Founding members include Reps. Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ); Greg Casar (D-TX); Yvette Clarke (D-NY); Ben Cline (R-VA); Mike Flood (R-NE); Bill Foster (D-IL); Valerie Foushee (D-NC); Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ); Pat Harrigan (R-NC); Jim Himes (D-CT); Sara Jacobs (D-CA); Mike Kennedy (R-UT); Ro Khanna (D-CA); Sam Liccardo (D-CA); Ted Lieu (D-CA); Zoe Lofgren (D-CA); Celeste Maloy (R-UT); Doris Matsui (D-CA); April McClain Delaney (D-MD); Blake Moore (R-UT); Jay Obernolte (R-CA); Scott Peters (D-CA); Brad Sherman (D-CA); Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA); Ritchie Torres (D-NY); Lori Trahan (D-MA).

title: Baldwin Introduces New Bill to Expand Paid Leave for Parents Who Lose a Child Under the Age of 26
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) introduced the Parental Bereavement Leave Expansion Act, a new bill to expand access to paid leave for federal employees who lose a child. Under current law, federal employees are only eligible for paid leave when a child dies if they are 17 years old or younger. Baldwin’s bill would extend eligibility for paid leave for these Americans who lose a child under the age of 26, ensuring more grieving parents have time to mourn and be with their families without worrying about missing a paycheck.

“Losing a child is every parent’s worst nightmare, and no family should have to worry about missing a paycheck or rushing back to work while grieving such a tragic loss,” said Senator Tammy Baldwin. “After hearing from a Wisconsin mother who was denied paid leave following the heartbreaking loss of her son, I knew we needed to do more. My bill will close this gap and ensure more grieving parents have the time they need to be with their families.”

Under current law, qualifying federal employees are entitled to two administrative weeks of paid parental bereavement leave following the death of a child 17 years old or younger. Baldwin’s bill extends that age limit to 26, extending the benefit to parents who lose a child in their late teens or early adulthood. Baldwin also wrote the law that gives people ages 26 or younger the ability to be on their parents’ health insurance plan, a provision she included in the Affordable Care Act.

The legislation comes after a Wisconsin mother lost her 18-year-old son to suicide in 2023 but was denied paid parental bereavement leave because her son was too old to qualify for leave under current law.

The legislation is supported by American Federation of Government Employees and National Partnership for Women and Families.

Full text of the legislation is available here. A one-pager on the legislation is available here.

title: Senator Banks Helps Secure Indiana Priorities in Draft Republican Defense Appropriations Bill
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Senator Jim Banks (R-Ind.) highlighted funding increases and other provisions in the Senate Appropriations Committee’s proposed defense appropriations bill that benefit Indiana. The proposal supports Hoosier workers and manufacturers, strengthens national defense, and advances research vital to national security.

Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.): “Indiana plays a critical role in America’s national defense, from producing essential equipment to developing technologies our military needs. I am pleased to see these Indiana priorities reflected in the Republican defense appropriations bill, including investments tied to our defense workforce, military installations, and research institutions. I’ll keep fighting for these priorities as the appropriations office moves forward.”

The proposed bill includes:

Sonobuoys: $350 million increase for Navy Sonobuoys, which are made in Columbia City.

Nuclear Sea-Launched Cruise Missile (SLCM-N): $250 million increase for the program, which is tested and developed at Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane.

HMMWV Mobile Maintenance Equipment: $40 million increase for mobile maintenance equipment systems for the High Mobility Multipurpose Wheeled Vehicle. The equipment is made in Mishawaka.

Department of War Language Programs: $20 million increase for language flagship programs, including Indiana University.

Munitions Demilitarization: $5 million increase for demilitarization processes for white phosphorus ammunition items with work tied to Crane Army Ammunition Activity.

Air National Guard Facilities: $5 million increase for F-16 squadron operations center repairs, including repairs at 122nd Fighter Wing in Fort Wayne.

Trusted and Assured Microelectronics: $210 million for secure Department of War microelectronics, work tied to Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane.

Next-Generation Jamming Technologies: $50 million for next-generation jammers, with work tied to Naval Surface Warfare Center Crane.

MV-75 Cheyenne: $2.1 billion for the MV-75 Cheyenne, whose engines are made in Indianapolis.

Meals Ready-to-Eat: Language recommending full funding to Meals Ready-to-Eat, which are manufactured and packaged in Evansville.

The proposed bill must continue through the appropriations process, including a vote on the Senate floor, before funding is final.

title: Senator Banks Introduces Bill to Honor Fallen Delaware County Deputy
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Todd Young (R-Ind.) introduced legislation to rename the Muncie Post Office at 501 West Memorial Drive the “Officer Blake A. Reynolds Post Office Building,” honoring the Delaware County Sheriff’s Corporal who was killed in the line of duty last November.

The Senate bill is a companion to legislation introduced by Rep. Victoria Spartz (R-IN-05) and supported by members of the Indiana House delegation.

Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.): “Corporal Blake Reynolds gave his life serving the people of Delaware County. He was a dedicated deputy, a member of the Indiana Army National Guard, and a proud son of the Muncie Community. Naming this post office in his honor would recognize his sacrifice and ensure his service is remembered for generations.”

Background:

Blake Adair Reynolds was born in Muncie, Indiana, and graduated from Delta High School in 2013. He earned a bachelor’s degree in criminal justice from Ball State University, where he worked with the Youth Opportunity Center and the Delaware County Probation Department. Reynolds joined the Delaware County Sheriff’s Office in 2022 and rose to the rank of corporal. He also served in the Indiana National Guard.

On November 12, 2025, Reynolds was killed while assisting a motorist along Interstate 69. His death was the first line-of-duty death in the history of the Delaware County Sheriff’s Department. Approximately 600 people attended his funeral at Delta High School, including law enforcement and officers from across Indiana.

title: Barrasso Celebrates National Rural Health Day
text:
“I will continue to fight for rural hospitals. I will continue to fight to protect rural communities. As a doctor, I will continue to fight so that patients, regardless of where they live, can get the care they need from a doctor they choose at lower costs.”

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso (R-Wyo.) today celebrated National Rural Health Day. Senator Barrasso spoke about how Republicans created the Rural Health Transformation Fund, which is already improving access to healthcare in rural and frontier communities in Wyoming as well as across the country.

Click HERE to watch Senator Barrasso’s remarks.

Sen. Barrasso’s remarks as prepared:

“I rise to speak about life in rural America – specifically about healthcare in rural America.

“I am a doctor. I practiced medicine for 24 years in my hometown of Casper, Wyoming. I know what patients want: care that is available, affordable, and reliable. I also know the challenges they face. In some places, it’s not just rural medicine. It’s frontier medicine. There are unique challenges. There are vast distances and long drives. There is severe weather. There are low patient volumes at our rural hospitals. That makes it hard to cover fixed operating costs.

“Across the country, rural hospitals are stretched, strained, and struggling. More than 100 rural hospitals have closed their doors since Obamacare became law 16 years ago. So, the question is, how can we strengthen rural hospitals and rural providers? How can we make rural delivery networks stronger for the patients who need them?

“Republicans are leading the way. Last year, we delivered $50 billion for rural healthcare. We did it through a program called the Rural Health Transformation Fund. It is part of the Working Families Tax Cuts law. This is the largest investment in rural healthcare in American history.

“This was not a one-size-fits-all government takeover. Each state sets their own priorities. Each state is in the driver’s seat. The money gives them freedom and flexibility. It empowers states to improve prevention to strengthen chronic disease management and to invest in modern technology.

“Every state in America receives money this year. They will continue to receive money over the next five years. The states receiving the most money are the rural states – the states with long distances and small populations.

“In Wyoming, we are putting these resources to work. Last month, I joined Governor Mark Gordon to announce how Wyoming is using its first $205 million. Now, an additional $207 million is coming to Wyoming for next year. We are building on our progress. The benefits are immediate and immense.

“Funding is going straight to our critical access hospitals and emergency medical services. It is going to produce more family medicine physicians at Rural Training sites. One is located in Thermopolis, Wyoming. This is the hometown of the Wyoming Physician of the Year. He was the first to introduce Advanced Trauma Life Support into Wyoming.

“Funding is also going to our schools for workforce training programs. They are focused on training and retaining nurses, lab technicians, and other healthcare workers. It is going to clinics and health centers in vulnerable rural communities. This is going to help treat patients closer to their homes.

“Wyoming has proven it will use these dollars wisely. We will strengthen and expand access to medical care in every corner of our state.

“Democrats in the Senate continually try to destroy this program. Democrats have voted repeatedly to strip away all this money from rural hospitals. Democrats continue to vote to starve rural hospitals and health clinics across the country. To make matters worse, Democrats are now pushing a radical plan to kick millions of Americans off the insurance they like and want to keep. That is the health insurance they get from work.

“One of the radical incoming Democrat Senators declared, ‘Medicare for All guarantees you a public healthcare plan and eliminates your private one.’ Let me repeat that. This new Democrat Senator wants to take away your private health insurance that you get from your work. He wants you to be completely dependent on the government for your healthcare.

“This is a far cry from President Obama’s statement: ‘If you like your doctor, you can keep your doctor.’ That’s the statement that one of the national newspapers called the ‘Lie of the Year.’ Now, radical Democrats in the Senate are promising, ‘If you like your healthcare plan, we are going to take it away from you.’

“Under the radical Democrat plan, families would pay more to wait longer for worse care. Rural communities would be especially vulnerable. Rural hospitals need to be able to keep their doors open. Americans know one-size-fits-all, government-run healthcare is not the answer. The American people deserve better.

“I will continue to fight for rural hospitals. I will continue to fight to protect rural communities. As a doctor, I will continue to fight so that patients, regardless of where they live, can get the care they need from a doctor they choose at lower costs.”

title: Senate Passes Bipartisan Permitting Reform Bill
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator John Barrasso (R-Wyo.) released the following statement after the U.S. Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026:

“Today, the Senate passed bipartisan permitting reform legislation that will unleash Wyoming energy, lower energy costs, and create jobs across our state. It’s a win for Wyoming and for America.

“Right now, critical infrastructure projects spend years trapped in the regulatory penalty box. Energy projects in Wyoming bear the brunt of this dysfunction. Wyoming is America’s energy breadbasket. We have world-class coal, oil, natural gas, and uranium. Wyoming energy workers are ready to produce the energy America needs. The broken federal permitting process is standing in our way. That’s why I worked with Senator Joe Manchin last Congress to produce the bipartisan Energy Permitting Reform Act. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 builds on our work.

“This critical legislation cuts Washington red tape, streamlines environmental reviews, and reins in never-ending, abusive legal challenges. It will help us build better, faster, cheaper, and smarter, and lower energy costs for American families. I urge the House to act quickly so we can send this bill to President Trump’s desk and experience the benefit as soon as possible.”

Background:

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 enacts commonsense permitting and power transmission reforms. It will allow for responsible energy production while preserving our nation’s natural resources and federal lands.

The bill implements changes across several permitting and infrastructure review processes, including environmental regulations, electric grid planning, the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), and other processes. These changes would establish a clear and accountable federal environmental review process so that all infrastructure projects can move forward with predictable milestones and enforceable deadlines.

It provides certainty in the federal permitting process by ensuring previously issued permits cannot be rescinded without a justification based on significant new problems or violations of federal law; and requires delays past new statutory deadlines to be justified only in certain reasonable circumstances.

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 includes several reforms that were part of Senator Barrasso’s Energy Permitting Reform Act. It would make it significantly easier to issue oil and gas permits on split-estate basins. It fixes the Rosemontdecision prohibiting ancillary mining activities on mining leases. It also reduces the ability of bad actors to file frivolous lawsuits meant to put good, responsible energy and infrastructure projects out of business.

title: Bennet, Grassley, Trahan, Miller-Meeks Call for Accelerated Implementation of Law to Improve Kids’ Access to Life-Saving Care
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet led U.S. Senator Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) as well as U.S. Representatives Lori Trahan (D-Mass.) and Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-Iowa) in urging timely implementation of the Accelerating Kids’ Access to Care Act. The lawmakers championed this legislation, which was signed into law in February to improve access to life-saving care for children with complex medical conditions.

“We appreciate the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) work to implement the Accelerating Kids’ Access to Care Act (Section 6101 of Public Law 119-75). Our most vulnerable kids and their families deserve a health care system that coordinates care and produces healthier outcomes, rather than one that requires them to navigate excessive bureaucracy and red tape. Our law will improve health care access for children with complex medical conditions by simplifying out-of-state Medicaid screening and enrollment processes for pediatric care providers, all while retaining key safeguards to preserve the integrity of the program. We request that CMS expeditiously initiate the rulemaking ahead of the three-year implementation deadline and issue guidance to State Medicaid Agencies (SMAs) advising them on current law and regulations in the interim,” began the lawmakers.

Being a parent of children with complex medical needs can be extremely challenging. On average, these children see five to six specialists and up to as many as 20 to 30 health professionals, leaving parents to navigate numerous providers, countless appointments, and complex insurance coverage. Additionally, this kind of timely specialty care requires coordination between out-of-state and in-state providers, along with State Medicaid officials, which often leads to delays in getting medically necessary specialty care. With all of this in mind, helping these families remove bureaucratic barriers is essential, especially with advancements in care.

“Our law established a streamlined pathway for eligible providers caring for children with complex medical needs to enroll in out-of-state Medicaid programs without facing duplicative processes. Eligibility is limited only to providers who are enrolled in good standing in Medicare or their home state Medicaid program, and who have not been prohibited from participating in any federal health care programs. This law passed Congress with tremendous bipartisan support and the backing of hundreds of health care providers and provider organizations, patient advocacy groups, and other entities. Once implemented, it will remove impediments that delay access to time-sensitive care and reduce unnecessary administrative costs and burdens for children with complex medical needs and their families,” continued the lawmakers.

“We are grateful that the Accelerating Kids’ Access to Care Act is now law. We urge CMS to move forward expeditiously with the necessary rulemaking and implementation work, so that its benefits can be felt by children with complex medical needs and their families. We look forward to working with you on this important matter,” concluded the lawmakers.

The text of the letter is available HERE and below.

Dear Administrator Oz,

We appreciate the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) work to implement the Accelerating Kids’ Access to Care Act (Section 6101 of Public Law 119-75). Our most vulnerable kids and their families deserve a health care system that coordinates care and produces healthier outcomes, rather than one that requires them to navigate excessive bureaucracy and red tape. Our law will improve health care access for children with complex medical conditions by simplifying out-of-state Medicaid screening and enrollment processes for pediatric care providers, all while retaining key safeguards to preserve the integrity of the program. We request that CMS expeditiously initiate the rulemaking ahead of the three-year implementation deadline and issue guidance to State Medicaid Agencies (SMAs) advising them on current law and regulations in the interim.

On average, children with complex medical needs see five to six specialists and up to as many as 20 to 30 health professionals. Children and families often experience delays getting medically necessary specialty care outside their home states. Timely specialty care requires coordination between out-of-state and in-state providers, along with Medicaid officials. Parents are often overwhelmed by caring for their children’s complex health care needs, including navigating providers, appointments, and insurance coverage. Helping these families remove bureaucratic barriers is critical, especially with advancements in care, including cell and gene therapies that can only be administered at a limited number of specialized sites.

Our law established a streamlined pathway for eligible providers caring for children with complex medical needs to enroll in out-of-state Medicaid programs without facing duplicative processes. Eligibility is limited only to providers who are enrolled in good standing in Medicare or their home state Medicaid program, and who have not been prohibited from participating in any federal health care programs. This law passed Congress with tremendous bipartisan support and the backing of hundreds of health care providers and provider organizations, patient advocacy groups, and other entities. Once implemented, it will remove impediments that delay access to time-sensitive care and reduce unnecessary administrative costs and burdens for children with complex medical needs and their families.

To ensure timely implementation, we request that CMS issue guidance urging SMAs to prepare for upcoming rulemaking and encourage them to take early state-level action to prepare for its implementation. Any guidance should remind states of current laws, regulations, and guidance that allow and encourage them to avoid duplicative screens. We request that CMS concurrently begin work on rulemaking to implement the provisions of the law. We request CMS transmit a proposed timeline for the planned implementation actions, including any guidance, rulemaking, or other formal communications to SMAs.

In addition to advancing the rulemaking, we recommend you consider the following to ensure implementation results in streamlined and timely specialized care for children with complex medical needs:

Establish best practices for facility-level screening, enrollment, and payment: When a child travels out-of-state for complex medical care, they often see multiple specialists – many of whom cannot be identified until the patient arrives. Requiring every individual clinician at the same facility to independently navigate an out-of-state Medicaid agency’s screening, enrollment, and billing process creates administrative bottlenecks that delay care. To streamline this process, CMS should allow pediatric specialty providers at the same facility to enroll and enter into agreements as a single facility-level entity on behalf of their eligible providers, or another alternative approach that reduces administrative burden. Under this model, the facility would manage the administrative requirements, receive out-of-state Medicaid reimbursement, and distribute funds – ensuring children receive immediate care without administrative delays, while maintaining robust program integrity. We encourage CMS to enable this as an option for providers.

Allow State Medicaid Agencies to issue letters of good standing or similar certifications to help verify a provider’s eligibility status: This would enable an out-of-state provider’s home Medicaid agency to help verify that a provider is in good standing in their state. CMS could specify the data elements needed for these letters or certifications and produce a recommended template to ensure a standardized approach. This recommendation should not stand in the way of a state’s additional program integrity safeguards.

Establish minimum necessary data elements: CMS could also issue “the minimum necessary (data) for such State to provide payment to an eligible out-of-State provider” along with a standardized format as outlined in our law. Taking this approach would enable states to seamlessly transmit the data necessary to support out-of-state provider enrollment between one another.

In addition, we request that CMS provide a work plan and milestones to Congress about its ongoing Provider Enrollment, Chain and Ownership System (PECOS) modernization work. In CMS’s fiscal year 2026 budget justification document, the agency said it planned to resume modernization of PECOS, which has been paused to give CMS time to evaluate and implement the best technical approach moving forward. In addition, in CMS’ fiscal year 2027 budget justification document, the agency said it would use discretionary and mandatory funding to continue modernization of PECOS, including improving the provider enrollment experience, transitioning to a cloud-based platform, and improving provider enrollment processing. We understand the PECOS modernization work has the opportunity to enhance Accelerating Kids’ Access to Care Act efforts.

We are grateful that the Accelerating Kids’ Access to Care Act is now law. We urge CMS to move forward expeditiously with the necessary rulemaking and implementation work, so that its benefits can be felt by children with complex medical needs and their families. We look forward to working with you on this important matter.

title: Bennet Releases Amendment to Restrict Funding for Trump’s Disastrous Iran War
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a member of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, released a proposed amendment to restrict the Trump administration from using any funds for his reckless Iran war. This includes all funding in a short-term spending package or funds provided by previous legislation, such as the 2025 Republican reconciliation bill. Bennet modeled his amendment on the 1973 Case-Church Amendment when Congress on a bipartisan basis forced President Richard Nixon to end his bombing of Cambodia.

“The American people were clear. We must end President Trump’s disastrous Iran war, which has inflicted economic pain across our country and made the United States weaker. After nine months of conflict, he has not achieved any coherent goals. He has no strategy to win, let alone end the war on American terms,” said Bennet. “That is why I am proposing this amendment, modeled on the precedent Congress set in 1973. When we vote on short-term spending in the near future, we can fund the government and end this war. It is what the American people demand, and what they deserve.”

Specifically, Bennet’s amendment does the following:

Prohibits the Trump administration from using any included funds in a forthcoming spending package or previous legislation, such as the Department of Defense “slush fund” created by the 2025 Republican reconciliation bill, for combat activities in or over Iran, or in Iranian territorial waters; and

Maintains this prohibition until Congress authorizes such use of military force against Iran.

Bennet’s amendment allows the United States to continue:

Defending itself against potential Iranian armed attacks;

Collecting, analyzing, or sharing intelligence and counterintelligence information to defend against such attacks and help other nations do the same;

Assisting other nations in defensive measures, but specifically excluding U.S. participation in or support for other countries’ or entities’ military, paramilitary, or intelligence activities in Iran; and

Escorting commercial vessels through the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waters to alleviate the war’s costs for the American people.

Last week, Bennet led a joint statement with Senators Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), and Tammy Duckworth (D-IlI.) underscoring their opposition to any year-end funding package that does not restrict President Trump’s ability to continue his war on Iran. Earlier, Bennet sent a letter to his Senate colleagues urging them to draw a hard line on Iran war funding and refuse to advance any funding package that includes further appropriations for President Trump’s Iran war.

Bennet has demanded a full accounting of the costs of Trump’s war, introduced legislation to prevent the administration from obscuring those costs, called on Trump to lower energy prices, and warned that the war could strengthen Iran’s hardline regime and nuclear ambitions.

title: BLUMENTHAL & SCHIFF DEMAND ANSWERS FROM LOBBYISTS FUNNELING CORPORATE DONATIONS TO TRUMP BALLROOM
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – Today, U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), the incoming Chair of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, and U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-CA) demanded answers from lobbyists who played an instrumental role in funneling corporate donations into Donald Trump’s ballroom project.

In letters sent to Brian Ballard, President of Ballard Partners, and Reince Priebus, Chairman of the Board of Advisors of Michael Best Strategies, the Senators called on the lobbyists to produce all documents, records, and communications related to contributions to the ballroom and their efforts to solicit donations from Big Tech companies and other major companies with interests before the Trump Administration who may be seeking favors from their donations to the President’s favorite vanity project.

“This pipeline of corporation donations raises concerns of widespread corruption at the White House, with quid pro quo transactions potentially tainting official government action. Many questions remain about how funds are being raised for this project, including how donors are being identified and solicited, what promises have been made in exchange for these substantial contributions, and the extent of any solicitations or pledges that have not yet been disclosed. This information will prove instructive as the incoming Congress considers the efficacy of federal ethics and anti-corruption laws pertaining to the executive branch,” the Senators wrote.

Blumenthal and Schiff previously wrote to Ballard, Priebus, and others seeking information about their role in soliciting donations for the ballroom. After Ballard and Priebus failed to respond, the Senators are reiterating their request, writing, “Please also note that failure to voluntarily produce the requested records and information by January 4, 2027, will leave the Subcommittee with no choice but to consider alternative measures to obtain compliance.”

Blumenthal has been leading an inquiry into waste, fraud, and abuse associated with the ballroom project and Trump’s other vanity projects throughout the nation’s capital, including potential pay-to-play schemes and the ballooning costs to taxpayers. The full text of today’s letter to Ballard is available here and below. Today’s letter to Priebus is available here.

Dear Mr. Ballard:

Since July 2025, President Trump has solicited more than $300 million in private donations to build what has been presented to donors and the public as “the President Donald J. Trump Ballroom” (“Trump Ballroom”).[1] To raise such a large sum of money in little more than a year required coordination and expertise, with lobbyists such as yourself playing an instrumental role in funneling corporate donations into President Trump’s favorite vanity project.[2] This pipeline of corporation donations raises concerns of widespread corruption at the White House, with quid pro quo transactions potentially tainting official government action. Many questions remain about how funds are being raised for this project, including how donors are being identified and solicited, what promises have been made in exchange for these substantial contributions, and the extent of any solicitations or pledges that have not yet been disclosed.[3] This information will prove instructive as the incoming Congress considers the efficacy of federal ethics and anti-corruption laws pertaining to the executive branch.

For well over a year, the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (“the Subcommittee”) minority has been conducting an inquiry into President Trump’s solicitation of these donations from corporate America.[4] The Subcommittee previously wrote, along with Senators Elizabeth Warren and Adam Schiff, requesting documents and information regarding your fundraising efforts for the President’s ballroom, however, you have failed to respond. Given this failure, I am writing to renew my previous request for records and information and to reiterate my expectation that you promptly comply.

To assist our offices in our inquiry into the financing of the demolition of the East Wing and construction of the Trump Ballroom, please produce all documents, records,[5] and communications[6] related to contributions to the Trump Ballroom and your efforts to solicit such donations, and provide the following information:

A comprehensive description of your role in the effort to raise funds for the Trump Ballroom, including but not limited to:

When were you first asked to assist with efforts to raise funds for the Trump Ballroom?

Who requested your participation in this effort? Please identify everyone you spoke with about the project, including but not limited to all White House personnel or members of the Trump family.

What was the target amount of funds that you were originally asked to raise?

Has the target fundraising goal changed at any point in time? If so, to what amount and why?

What guidance or instructions were provided to you regarding which donors or type of donors to solicit funds from?

Were you told not to solicit funds from any individual donors or type of donor (e.g., foreign countries or entities)?

What were you told to offer donors in exchange for a contribution to the Trump Ballroom? Did this vary based on the identity of the donor or the amount of the contribution? If so, how?

Were donors offered the opportunity to be named in an acknowledgement wall or other similar fashion within the Trump Ballroom?

Please produce all materials that you were provided or otherwise used to solicit donations for the Trump Ballroom.

How are you and/or your organization being compensated for your role in the Trump Ballroom fundraising project?

Will you receive a fixed fee or are you receiving a percentage of funds raised?

Are you eligible for incentive payments for achieving target fundraising goals?

What is the total amount of compensation you expect to receive for raising funds for the White House Ballrooms?

Please produce any and all agreements you have entered into reflecting the scope of your fundraising efforts and/or any compensation you or your company will receive in exchange.

Please provide a complete list of individuals or entities that you have solicited for donations or pledges to fund construction of the Trump Ballroom, as well as the following information about each solicited pledge or contribution

The total amount of each donation or pledge solicited;

The date of each solicitation;

Whether the donation or pledge was made and, if so, in what amount;

The date the donation or pledge was made or offered;

Whether the donation or pledge was intended to be anonymous;

Was anything offered in exchange for the donation or pledge, including but not limited to access to government officials, attendance at White House or other events, public or private recognition of the donation, or anything else, regardless of inherent monetary value?

Will the donation be made to the Trust for the National Mall or to another entity (including the name of any other entity receiving the donation)?

The Subcommittee expects you to carefully review and follow the enclosed production instructions to ensure that all records produced can be accessed and reviewed in a timely manner. Please begin producing responsive records by no later than December 18, 2026, with additional records to follow on a schedule agreed upon in advance by Subcommittee staff. Any questions about the scope of the enclosed requests should be relayed to Subcommittee staff well in advance of the deadline. Please also note that failure to voluntarily produce the requested records and information by January 4, 2027, will leave the Subcommittee with no choice but to consider alternative measures to obtain compliance.

Please contact Subcommittee staff by November 23, 2026, to confirm receipt of this letter.

Sincerely,

title: NEWS: Senator Blunt Rochester, Congressman Joe Morelle Introduce Legislation to Prevent Gun Theft and Keep Illegal Firearms Off Our Streets
text:
Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.) and Congressman Joe Morelle (D-N.Y.-25) introduced the Gun Theft Prevention Act, legislation to prevent firearms from being stolen from gun dealers and entering the illegal gun market. The bill would establish stronger security standards for federally licensed firearms dealers, increase inspections by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), and provide law enforcement with additional tools to combat gun theft and trafficking.

“Gun violence in America is a public health crisis, and Congress has every responsibility to intervene. Communities across the country are facing increased rates of firearm theft, and reining in this issue is a key step in tackling the gun violence epidemic,” said Senator Blunt Rochester. “I’m proud to introduce the Gun Theft Prevention Act alongside Congressman Morelle to strengthen security standards for gun dealers and provide law enforcement with the right tools to stop gun theft and trafficking. We must make every effort to end gun violence and make our country a safer place”

“Stolen firearms too often end up in the wrong hands, putting families and communities at risk,” said Congressman Joe Morelle. “We need to stop these weapons from reaching our streets in the first place. The Gun Theft Prevention Act strengthens security at gun dealers and gives law enforcement the tools to prevent theft before it happens.”

“Theft of firearms from gun dealers, manufacturers, and importers is a public safety threat that affects us all. Too often, these stolen guns are illegally trafficked and diverted into other criminal activity that endangers our communities. The Gun Theft Prevention Act will strengthen gun industry security measures and provide them with tools to prevent gun theft and trafficking. Brady is grateful to Congressman Morelle and Senator Blunt Rochester for introducing this important legislation and for their continued commitment to preventing the illegal trade of firearms,” said Mark Collins, Director of Federal Policy, Brady.

Specifically, the Gun Theft Prevention Act would:

Require federally licensed firearms dealers, manufacturers, and importers to implement security measures, including locked storage, alarm systems, video surveillance, reinforced locks, and additional physical barriers where necessary.

Require ATF to inspect federally licensed firearms dealers at least once every three years to help ensure compliance with federal law and applicable security requirements.

Require additional security inspections following reported thefts from firearms dealers to identify vulnerabilities and recommend corrective measures.

Establish additional background check requirements for employees of federally licensed firearms dealers.

Support increased ATF staffing and oversight capacity to help enforce federal firearms laws and prevent gun theft.

title: Booker Introduces Legislation to Address Critical Gaps in Education Benefits for Veterans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) is fighting to make sure veterans receive the benefits they need to finish their degrees and have equal opportunity to pass those hard-earned benefits to their dependents by reintroducing the Veteran Education and Transfer (VET) Extension Act.

"When our veterans signed up to serve, this country made them a promise: to provide them with the benefits and resources they earned and deserve," said Senator Booker. "Too many veterans are watching that promise come up short. By improving education benefits for veterans, including increasing eligibility for remedial courses and expanding transferability, the VET Extension Act creates more opportunities for veterans and takes an important step toward fulfilling our promise."

Most student veterans receive education benefits through the Post-9/11 GI Bill, which grants up to 36 months of educational entitlement to veterans after they separate from the military. However, those 36 months do not include the time needed for service members to take remedial courses, which are often required for students who are out of school for a period of time.

Current transferability rules create a second gap. If a service member separates from the military and does not have a child or spouse to sign their education benefits over to, they lose the ability to transfer those benefits. This places veterans who become parents after separating from service at an unjust disadvantage compared with veterans who had dependents while still serving.

The VET Extension Act would address these issues by:

Providing up to 15 additional months of Post-9/11 GI Bill educational assistance so veterans can finish their degrees.

Allowing service members without dependents during their service to transfer their entitlement to dependents they identify later.

Booker first introduced the VET Extension Act in 2018 after hearing from student veterans at Rutgers University. Matthew Kelly, a Rutgers–New Brunswick student veteran who joined Booker for the bill's launch, needed a year and a half of remedial classes before he could start his computer science major. He took 40 credits in a single year to stretch his benefits, and he still expected them to run out before his final semester.

title: Booker Pushes For Emergency Relief for NJ Farmers Impacted by April Freeze
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ), a member of the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry, Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks, along with five of their colleagues, pushed for emergency agricultural disaster funding to support farmers in New Jersey and across the country who were impacted by the catastrophic April 2026 freeze. In a letter to the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies, Booker stressed the need for relief for farmers facing losses from the freeze event that destroyed crops across the region.

On the devastating impact of the freeze, the Senators wrote, “In the early morning hours of April 21, 2026, the Mid-Atlantic region of the United States experienced a severe temperature drop, resulting in a freeze that devastated specialty crops across seven states including Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Delaware, New York, New Jersey, and West Virginia. This region, which is among the top areas of the country for specialty crop production, experienced devastating, and historic losses, including hundreds of millions of dollars in damage with some farmers and companies experiencing complete loss of their crop. In addition to crop loss, some growers are facing permanent damage to their trees and grapevines compounded by ongoing drought conditions throughout the region which will have lasting implications beyond this season.”

The senators continued, “In New Jersey, preliminary estimates point to at least $135–$170 million in damage from the freeze, with significant additional losses expected to be reported in the coming months... Producers across the Mid-Atlantic continue to face the challenges of labor and maintenance for their farms, despite the absence of a harvestable crop to offset the costs. This has resulted in significant economic hardship for the industry.”

“Congress has consistently demonstrated support of specialty crop growers through policy and appropriations. While this freeze event has informed meaningful conversations on improving existing emergency relief programs long-term, the urgency of the immediate need for relief for specialty crop producers in the Mid-Atlantic cannot wait. We appreciate your support for specialty crops in the Mid-Atlantic and look forward to your partnership in providing critical relief for producers,” the senators concluded.

The letter builds on the successful effort to secure USDA approval of New Jersey’s request for an agricultural disaster declaration following the April freeze, making emergency financial assistance available to impacted farmers as quickly as possible.

In August, Senator Booker visited a vineyard in Cumberland County where he saw firsthand the crop damage caused by the unprecedented freeze and spoke with farmers who experienced significant crop losses and were facing devastating financial strain.

“The April 2026 freeze damage has hurt the livelihood of many of New Jersey’s family farms,” said New Jersey Secretary of Agriculture Ed Wengryn. “New Jersey is a national leader in blueberry and peach production, with growing direct-to-consumer markets for apples, cherries, and pears. Emergency grants are critical to helping these specialty crop producers recover.”

Senator Booker was joined in sending the letter by Senators Andy Kim (D-NJ), Mark Warner (D-Va.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Tim Kaine (D-VA), John Fetterman (D-PA), , Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), and Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD).

SEE ALSO:

Booker Helps Secure USDA Disaster Designation, Unlocking Federal Relief for New Jersey Farmers Impacted by April Freeze

title: Booker, Warnock Reintroduce RESTORE Act to End Lifetime SNAP Ban for People with Certain Drug Offenses
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Raphael Warnock (D-GA) both members of the Senate Agriculture Committee, reintroduced the Restoring Essential Support to Overcome Re-entry and Ensure Access to SNAP (RESTORE) Act, legislation to end the lifetime ban on Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits for people with drug felony convictions.

"Denying people food assistance because of a past drug conviction serves no public safety purpose. It only makes it harder for people to get back on their feet," said Senator Booker. "Someone who has repaid their debt to society should not have hunger as an additional barrier to restarting a productive life. The RESTORE Act ends this outdated policy, which will reduce recidivism and make our communities safer."

Congress enacted the lifetime ban on SNAP for drug felony convictions in 1996 as part of a "war on drugs"-era welfare reform law. The ban cuts off food assistance for people who have already served their sentences. While most states have opted out of the ban, 22 states continue to place SNAP eligibility restrictions on people with drug convictions.

Research shows that people denied SNAP are more likely to be rearrested, and food assistance also supports people in recovery from addiction.

Specifically, the RESTORE Act would:

Repeal the lifetime SNAP ban for people with drug felony convictions;

Allow people scheduled for release within 30 days to apply for SNAP, so they can prepare for successful reentry.

This legislation is cosponsored by Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Peter Welch (D-VT), John Fetterman (D-PA), Tina Smith (D-MN), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Adam Schiff (D-CA), and Dick Durbin (D-IL).

This legislation builds on Senator Booker's longstanding work to reform the criminal justice system and support people in productively reentering their communities. Booker helped author and pass the bipartisan First Step Act, which reformed federal sentencing, and authored the Fair Chance Act, which "bans the box" on federal hiring applications so people with records get a fair shot at employment. He has also introduced the Next Step Act, the Dignity for Incarcerated Women Act, and the Making Essentials Available and Lawful (MEAL) Act, an earlier bill to repeal the lifetime ban on SNAP and Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) benefits for people with felony drug convictions.

title: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Votes to Pass Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) celebrated passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA), legislation that overhauls the federal permitting process to speed the construction of energy and infrastructure projects and lower costs for American families. The Senate passed the bill by a vote of 62-33.

“Alabama families and small businesses are paying too much to keep the lights on, and Washington’s broken permitting system is one of the primary culprits,” said Senator Britt. “Projects that would create good-paying jobs and deliver affordable, reliable energy have been stuck behind red tape for years and are often suffocated by endless litigation. This bill sets firm deadlines on process reviews and puts an end to frivolous lawfare. These provisions, among others in the bill, still retain crucial environmental and preservation standards while accelerating the approval of critical infrastructure projects. Under Republican leadership, the Senate worked across the aisle and with President Trump to get done what Washington has talked about for decades. Lowering costs is the top priority for Alabamians, and the House should send this bill to the President’s desk without delay.”

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 codifies the Ratepayer Protection Act, of which Senator Britt is a proud cosponsor. Senator Britt has long called to codify President Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Pledge to lower energy prices for Alabamians and ensure families and small businesses aren’t left paying for the energy infrastructure needed to support new data centers.

Federal agencies take an average of 4.5 years to complete an environmental impact statement, according to a White House Council on Environmental Quality analysis of reviews from 2013 to 2018. Three-quarters of U.S. adults say their home energy costs have gone up in recent years, according to a Pew Research Center survey released in May of 2026.

Data from the National Association of Manufacturers shows that permitting delays are costing America’s manufacturers $12.1 billion every year, including $363 million in additional costs in Alabama alone. According to data from McKinsey, $1.8 trillion of investments are locked up in the federal permitting system right now, including $20.6 billion of sidelined investments in Alabama.

Senator Britt has been a consistent champion for meaningful permitting reform. In August, she joined Senator Alan Armstrong (R-OK) in introducing the American Energy and Mineral Infrastructure Act. Many of the provisions within are included in the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, including Clean Water Act reforms that foster consistent, science-based environmental decision-making, and EPA permitting reforms that broaden certainty for both general and nationwide permits.

title: Budd Introduces Bill to Promote Fairness Across Consumer Financial Protection Laws
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Ted Budd (R-N.C.) introduced the FCRA Liability Harmonization Act yesterday to place a reasonable cap on total statutory damages for class action lawsuits and align the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) with other consumer financial protection laws. The legislation ultimately aims to promote fairness while still allowing for class action litigation in the event of authentic FCRA violations.

“Every day consumers rely on credit reports to confirm their ability to purchase a home or a car, but when damages are left uncapped, the door is left wide open for a predatory trial bar to drive up the costs of obtaining consumer credit information. To date, FCRA is the only consumer financial services law on the books that fails to impose a reasonable cap on total statutory damages for class action lawsuits, and it is long overdue for that to change. My legislation responsibly levels the playing field across consumer financial protection laws by implementing a reasonable cap on total statutory damages, promoting greater fairness,” said Senator Budd.

The FCRA Liability Harmonization Act is supported by Consumer Data Industry Association (CDIA), American Bankers Association (ABA), U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Consumer Bankers Association (CBA), Electronic Transaction Association (ETA), Online Lenders Alliance, American Fintech Council, Professional Background Screening Association, America’s Credit Unions, National Independent Automobile Dealers Association, National Automobile Dealers Association, National Association Mutual Insurance Companies (NAMIC), Innovative Lending Platform Association, ACA International, and American Property Casualty Insurance Association (APCIA).

“Consumers are best served by an FCRA that is fair, predictable, and consistent with other federal consumer protection laws. Today, however, the FCRA enables abusive litigation tactics that ultimately harm consumers, with trial lawyers often collecting the bulk of the payout. These commonsense reforms would bring the FCRA in line with those laws, ensuring that consumers are appropriately compensated while placing reasonable and consistent standards on class action lawsuits. CDIA has led the fight for litigation reform, and we will continue to advocate for these changes,” said Dan Smith, President and CEO, Consumer Data Industry Association.

Read the full bill text HERE.

BACKGROUND

FCRA is a comprehensive federal law that regulates the collection, use, and dissemination of consumer credit information by credit reporting agencies and other entities that compile consumer reports. The law also regulates who can access credit reports, restricting access to legitimate business purposes such as lending decisions, employment, insurance, and other authorized uses.

Currently, class action lawsuits are being filed for small, technical FCRA violations involving thousands of members, many of whom have no idea they are part of the lawsuit. If the claims the maximum statutory damages award of $1,000, these lawsuits potentially cost millions of dollars each.

The FCRA Liability Harmonization Act would cap class action lawsuit awards at $500,000 or 1% of the defendant’s net worth, whichever is less. Placing a reasonable cap on total statutory damages for class action lawsuits harmonizes FCRA with other consumer financial protection laws. The bill promotes fairness by aligning FCRA with the caps on punitive damages for individual suits as established in the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, Electronic Fund Transfer Act, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, and Truth in Lending Act.

title: Budd Releases Statement After EDA Announces $33+ Million Grant to Rebuild Western NC’s Economy & Advance the Biotech Workforce
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Ted Budd (R-N.C.) released the following statement after the Economic Development Administration (EDA) announced a $33.2 million Disaster Supplemental Grant for the Research Triangle Institute to strengthen Western North Carolina’s economic development across the region’s life sciences and biotechnology sector after Hurricane Helene. title: Cortez Masto Statement on Senate Passage of Permitting Reform Bill
text:
Senator Cortez Masto voted against final passage of the bill because it contains provisions harmful to Tribal sovereignty

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) released the following statement after the Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). Cortez Masto voted against final passage of this bill because it contains harmful changes to the National Historic Preservation Act that undermine Tribal sovereignty and fail to protect government-to-government Tribal consultation.

“This country needs permitting reform. I support efforts to lower energy costs and have championed proposals to make it easier to build clean energy projects, upgrade our electrical grid, and grow our critical mineral supply chain in the U.S. In fact, I fought to ensure this bill includes my Mining Regulatory Clarity Act and High-Capacity Grid Act, language I drafted to support geothermal development, and provisions from my FREEDOM Act to streamline NEPA reviews and deliver project certainty to clean energy projects. But there is no reason to threaten Tribal sovereignty to accomplish these goals.

“The version of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act that passed the Senate today ignores Tribal input and makes changes to the National Historic Preservation Act that Tribes across the country do not support. I’m disappointed that Republicans wouldn’t allow this section to be struck from the bill.”

title: PASSED: Cortez Masto, Budd Legislation to Protect Veterans from Fraud
text:
Washington, D.C. – The U.S. Senate passed legislation by Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) and Ted Budd (R-N.C.) to go after fraudsters who target veterans. The Veterans Protection from Fraud Act would create a sentencing enhancement of up to ten years in prison for scammers who specifically target veterans. It now heads to the House of Representatives for consideration.

“Every year, thousands of veterans who spent years protecting our homeland and defending our freedoms are targeted by scammers because of their service. By not taking these crimes seriously, we have been failing those who risked their lives for our country,” said Senator Cortez Masto. “The Senate just sent a clear message to scammers: fraud against veterans will not be tolerated.”

“Scammers who prey on our nation’s veterans deserve to face severe consequences. Yesterday, the Senate took a strong bipartisan stand to increase penalties for these criminals. I urge my colleagues in the House to stand with us and swiftly pass this legislation to protect the men and women who served our nation and fought to defend our freedoms,” said Senator Budd.

Fraud cost veterans, service members, and their families $477 million in 2023. Federal law already includes a sentencing enhancement for fraud crimes targeting seniors, but no similar enhancement exists for fraudsters who target veterans. The Veterans Protection from Fraud Act would establish a sentencing enhancement of up to ten years in prison for someone convicted of committing or conspiracy to commit fraud that purposefully targeted a veteran.

The full text of the legislation can be found here.

Senator Cortez Masto is a consistent champion for Nevada’s service members and veterans. She is leading related bipartisan legislation to create a new criminal offense for fraudulent schemes targeting veterans’ benefits. Cortez Masto recently introduced sweeping legislation to improve health care for veterans. She helped pass the 2026 National Defense Authorization Act, which included a 3.8 percent pay raise for veterans. She has worked to support veterans exposed to toxins while serving at the Nevada Test and Training Range. Cortez Masto was instrumental in the approval of the Elko Veterans Cemetery, working with Presidents Trump and Biden to ensure Nevada veterans finally got the local cemetery they’d waited decades for.
