title: Cotton Leads Arkansas Delegation in Calling on FDA to Ban Contaminated Unwashed Poppy Seeds
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact: Tatum Wallace or Hannah McCarthy

November 19, 2026

Cotton Leads Arkansas Delegation in Calling on FDA to Ban Contaminated Unwashed Poppy Seeds

WASHINGTON—Senator Tom Cotton (R-Arkansas), along with Senator John Boozman (R-Arkansas) and Representatives Rick Crawford (Arkansas-01), French Hill (Arkansas-02), Steve Womack (Arkansas-03), and Bruce Westerman (Arkansas-04), today sent a letter to Acting U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Commissioner Kyle Diamantas encouraging the FDA to finalize guidance that would protect Americans from contaminated, unwashed poppy seeds.

In April 2025, Senator Cotton introduced the Stephen Hacala Poppy Seed Safety Act to prohibit the sale of poppy seeds containing harmful levels of opiates. The bill’s namesake, Stephen Hacala Jr. of Fayetteville, Arkansas, died from morphine-laced poppy seeds purchased from Amazon.

In part, the lawmakers wrote:

“It is imperative that FDA finalizes official guidance that establishes action levels for opiate alkaloids on poppy seeds as soon as possible to prevent harm and further deaths. We look forward to working with you on this important matter.”

Full text of the letter may be found here and below.

November 19, 2026

Kyle Diamantas

Acting Commissioner

U.S. Food and Drug Administration

10903 New Hampshire Avenue

Silver Spring, MD 20993

Dear Acting Commissioner Diamantas:

We write urging the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to finalize guidance regarding opiate alkaloid contamination on poppy seeds.

Unwashed poppy seeds remain a significant threat to the American public. They are often contaminated with illicit substances including morphine and codeine. At least 19 Americans are confirmed to have died from morphine overdoses, and an additional 20 Americans experienced non-fatal overdoses after consuming contaminated poppy seeds.

We commend FDA’s recent actions to protect the American public from dangerous unwashed poppy seeds. On April 21, 2026, FDA launched a webpage that describes federal research and monitoring of opiate alkaloids on poppy seeds, adverse health effects, and additional key consumer information. On June 29, 2026, FDA’s Human Foods Program announced that it intends to develop guidance that would establish action levels for opiate alkaloids on poppy seeds.

It is imperative that FDA finalizes official guidance that establishes action levels for opiate alkaloids on poppy seeds as soon as possible to prevent harm and further deaths. We look forward to working with you on this important matter.

Sincerely,

Tom Cotton

United States Senator

title: Senate Passes Permitting Reform to Unleash North Dakota Energy, Infrastructure Development
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Coal miners, homebuilders, oil and gas producers, manufacturers, labor workers, and construction firms applauded the passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act in the U.S. Senate. The legislation delivers lower energy prices, upgraded infrastructure, and economic growth to the American people.

The legislation, passed today by a bipartisan vote of 62 to 33, accelerates project approvals, limits frivolous litigation, and provides businesses with greater investment certainty. Endorsed by President Donald Trump, the bill now heads to the House of Representatives for consideration.

U.S. Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND), chair of the Senate Environment and Public Works Subcommittee on Transportation and Infrastructure, has spent much of the last year building bipartisan support for the legislation and applauded its passage.

In recognition of the bill’s passage, Cramer delivered a speech on the Senate floor, saying, “For decades, the process of approving the building of the infrastructure necessary to meet the demands of a growing and dynamic economy have been mired in partisan politics, and an out-of-control bureaucracy, which limits our nation's potential, our prosperity, and stifles our global competitiveness. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is an opportunity for us to turn that corner. […] Whether it's transmission lines to load centers, or pipelines to refineries, steel mills, or drone factories, or family housing, we must secure durable changes to the federal permitting reform process or continue to fall behind our global competitors.”

For energy-producing states like North Dakota, timely federal permitting is essential to responsibly developing natural resources. Pipelines, electric transmission lines, processing facilities, roads, and other infrastructure often depend on federal permits. Delays mean deferred investment, which leads to inefficient supply chains, cost increases, and fewer opportunities for workers.

“It took uncommon leadership, and I'm grateful for my colleagues who worked tirelessly, mostly cheerfully, for the last year to get us to this point,” said Cramer in his floor speech. “Most importantly, I thank you, Environment and Public Works Chair Shelley Moore Capito and Ranking Member Sheldon Whitehouse. […] And thank you, Energy and Natural Resources Chair Mike Lee and Ranking Member Martin Heinrich, for hanging in there. […] The work of these four leaders and a host of others is what results in the law that is as durable as it is balanced. A special thank you also goes to the president's team at the White House. […] Now, let’s get the job done. […] Because today, our country depends on us.”

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is historic permitting reform legislation which updates key federal laws to grow the economy, reduce costs, strengthen national security, and improve quality of life—all while maintaining the nation’s worldwide standard of environmental protection.

The bill incorporates U.S. Senator John Hoeven (R-ND) and Cramer’s BLM Mineral Spacing Act to eliminate certain federal oil and gas drilling permit requirements on nonfederal lands where the federal government owns less than 50% of the mineral estate. It also reforms the laws governing federal environmental reviews and permitting, including the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), Clean Water Act, Endangered Species Act, National Historic Preservation Act, and federal land management authorities to establish clearer timelines, improve project certainty, and limit judicial review.

Judicial Reforms

The legislation streamlines judicial review of federal permitting decisions by setting tighter deadlines for lawsuits, limiting who can sue, and giving federal agencies greater deference. These changes are intended to prevent prolonged litigation from delaying linear infrastructure projects and allow them to continue while agencies and developers correct potential legal deficiencies instead of courts halting construction.

NEPA: Lawsuits challenging NEPA reviews must be filed within 150 days—down from six years—by individuals who participated in the public comment process and can demonstrate direct harm. Cases would go directly to federal courts of appeals rather than district courts. The only remedy courts could impose would be a procedure known as remand without vacatur or an injunction, during which time agencies and developers would have 180 days to make necessary corrections.

Clean Water Act: Challenges to Section 404 permits, state-assumed programs, and general-permit verifications must be filed within 150 days. Only parties that participated in the public comment period to raise their relevant legal concerns can challenge. Courts cannot vacate or enjoin permits unless there is an “imminent and substantial danger,” and remands are limited to 180 days.

Modernizing NEPA

The bill represents the most significant NEPA reforms in decades. The reforms reinforce the Supreme Court’s Seven Counties decision which limited the scope of NEPA to the immediate impacts of a project and clarify NEPA establishes a procedural framework rather than mandating a particular project outcome. It exempts projects from NEPA review when the federal government’s only involvement consists of a loan or loan guarantee. The bill narrows the definition of major federal actions by excluding transmission and pipeline repairs, retrofits, upgrades, and modifications within existing rights-of-way which do not increase capacity by more than 20%.

The bill empowers states and tribes to satisfy NEPA requirements through their own environmental review processes when those processes serve a similar function. It also requires the lead agency to issue a record of decision within 45 days of a published review and outstanding federal authorization within 90 days for agencies participating in the review and 120 days for those that didn’t.

Clean Water Act Reforms

This provision maintains the ability of states to enforce Section 401 water quality certifications and compliance while limiting states’ ability to use the process to simply block or delay projects. States may deny certification only when they present clear and convincing evidence no reasonable conditions could address their concerns and must act within one year. For gas pipelines and transmission lines, the reforms limit reviews to direct point-source discharges and impose a nine-month deadline.

The legislation extends key Clean Water Act permit terms from five to ten years, including Section 402 National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System permits and Section 404 nationwide permits. It also bars the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency from retroactively vetoing Section 404 permits.

Transmission Provisions

The legislation reforms the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (FERC) federal backstop transmission siting authority and eliminates the existing U.S. Department of Energy’s National Interest Electric Transmission Corridor framework. FERC may site interstate transmission lines of 230 kV or greater when a state lacks siting authority, fails to act within one year of an application, or denies a certificate. It requires transmission costs to align roughly with the benefits received, while exempting public power entities and electric cooperatives.

The bill strengthens ratepayer protections against data center-related costs. It prohibits grid operators from shifting incremental costs associated with data centers to other customers, regardless of the facility’s size. Separately, it creates a new oversight mechanism allowing state public utility commissions to refer local transmission projects they believe conflict with local transmission needs to FERC’s Office of Enforcement.

Project Certainty

The bill prohibits federal agencies from rescinding or suspending a permit, halting construction, or stopping the operation of a project unless a court has ordered the action, the permit was violated, the permittee committed fraud, or to prevent immediate harm to life, property, or national security. The bill allows permit holders to seek an expedited court review if they believe the federal actions to cancel or suspend a permit were not justified and entitles them topursue attorneys’ fees, costs related to the delay, and economic damages.

It establishes a one-year deadline for authorizations which do not go through NEPA and allows applicants to seek injunctive orders to force agency action within 60 days and requires the court to act within 120 days.

title: Duckworth Announces She Will Vote Against Any Government Funding Package That Doesn’t Defund Trump’s Illegal War
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) announced she will vote against any government funding deal that does not cut off funding from President Donald Trump’s illegal, disastrous and pointless war. Last week, Duckworth unveiled an amendment alongside U.S. Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) and Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD) that would defund the war until this conflict is authorized by Congress, as the Constitution requires. The group issued a statement making it clear they would immediately offer the amendment to any proposed government funding deal that is struck. In addition to blocking any funding toward this conflict, the Senators’ amendment would require the Secretary of Defense to produce a report on the impact this illegal war has had on military readiness and our nation’s servicemembers. Duckworth’s full remarks can be found on the Senator's YouTube. Photos from the press conference can be found on the Senator’s website.

Key Quotes:

“Two weeks ago, the American people made their voices heard in historic fashion. And the takeaway couldn’t be clearer: Americans hate Donald Trump’s illegal, disastrous and pointless war. A war that is driving up costs, killing our troops and making us all less safe.”

“We are demanding that any government funding bill include our amendment, which would make sure that not one more cent goes toward funding this conflict that we never should’ve started in the first place. Congress must heed Americans’ call and use our power of the purse to force the President to end this war. And if a government funding bill does not cut off spending on this illegal war, I will vote no.”

“This is about ending a war that the American people hate and that Congress never authorized. We’ve already tried tool after tool to get the President to rein in this conflict. Nine months in, defunding the war is the only way to force Trump to end it.”

Duckworth’s remarks as delivered can be found below:

Hello everyone.

Two weeks ago, the American people made their voices heard in historic fashion.

And the takeaway couldn’t be clearer:

Americans hate Donald Trump’s illegal, disastrous and pointless war…

A war that is driving up costs, killing our troops and making us all less safe.

They made that clear in states both red and blue. In areas both urban and rural. In zip codes both wealthy and underserved.

They made it clear that this war has to end.

So as Senators, it is our job to listen.

That’s why we are demanding that any government funding bill include our amendment, which would make sure that not one more cent goes toward funding this conflict that we never should’ve started in the first place.

Congress must heed Americans’ call and use our power of the purse to force the President to end this war.

And if a government funding bill does not cut off spending on this illegal war, I will vote no.

Look, I’m here today not only as a Senator, but also as a former Soldier, who served in uniform the last time a president rashly sent our troops into an unjustified war in the Middle East.

And, you know, I’m proud of every mission I completed in Iraq.

But I would never wish another needless, endless, unjustified war like the one I served in on anybody else.

I wouldn’t wish it on the heroes who’ve packed up their rucks, knowing they may never touch American soil again.

I wouldn’t wish it on their families, who are being forced to spend their days anxiously waiting for news from across the world.

And I wouldn’t wish it on the American people, who want their president to focus on bringing down costs here at home, not starting new, expensive, taxpayer-funded wars thousands of miles away.

Listen, our troops will always do the best job possible.

They will always execute their orders to the maximum capability of their professionalism.

And they’re proud to do it. No matter the risk. No matter the sacrifice.

That isn’t the problem.

The problem is that the person who’s supposed to be leading them spends more time talking about decorating his Marie Antoinette ballroom than he does sitting in the Situation Room trying to get us out of this war.

The problem is that the man in charge of nuclear codes has gone increasingly nuclear and grows more delusional by the day.

Every hour that Trump leaves our heroes mired in the muck of his war with Iran, he is showing that he cares more about saving face than saving lives…

That he cares more about his arch of dishonor going up than gas prices going up.

Well, screw that.

That’s why we’re here today.

This is about ending a war that the American people hate and that Congress never authorized.

We’ve already tried tool after tool to get the President to rein in this conflict.

Nine months in, defunding the war is the only way to force Trump to end it.

At least 23 of our heroes are dead. Hundreds more are wounded.

Only someone as inept and unfit as Trump would see this as “winning.”

Only a draft-dodging coward would think that this is the right way to treat our warfighters.

Only a failed businessman who has a history of going bankrupt and ripping off American workers would think this is the right use of folks’ money.

Only a 14-time convicted felon would think he can just keep on ignoring the law as he continues to wage an illegal, unconstitutional war.

At this point we all know that Donald J. Trump will always be more interested in looking out for his own self-interest rather than serving our national interest.

Forcing this amendment onto his desk is how we tell him: “enough.”

Thank you.

-30-

title: Duckworth, Durbin Lead Illinois, Iowa Bipartisan Lawmakers in Calling on Army, EPA to Consider Delaying Planned Detonation of Lead Azide, Request Detailed Plans
text:
In their letter, lawmakers express concern about public health and lack of adequate communication from the Army and EPA with local officials and communities

[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL); U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL); U.S. Representatives Darin LaHood (R-IL-16), Mary Miller (R-IL-15), and Eric Sorensen (D-IL-17); Illinois Governor JB Pritzker; and Senators-elect Julianna Stratton (D-IL) and Josh Turek (D-IA) today sent a letter to Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin expressing the lawmakers’ grave concerns with Friday’s planned detonation of 9,700 pounds of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa, and called on the Army and EPA to consider delaying this detonation until there is an opportunity to explore safer alternatives. Lead dust is particularly harmful to children and pregnant women, and it can contaminate soil and critical farmland indefinitely. Further, communities across both Iowa and Illinois were informed of the planned detonation only this week.

“While we understand the urgent need to address these volatile materials, their detonation has the potential to spread lead contamination in and around the region. We call on you to consider delaying this detonation until there is an opportunity to explore safer alternatives,” the lawmakers wrote.

At a minimum, the lawmakers—recognizing the risks associated with transporting lead azide—requested an immediate update before the Army proceeds on the detailed detonation plans; mitigation efforts; likely range and location of the possible toxic plume, including as modeled for weather conditions; pre- and post-detonation monitoring and sampling; possibilities of alternative disposal procedures; and plan to remain in timely communication with state and local officials and communities both before and after the detonation.

“We encourage you to remain in timely communication with state and local officials and communities across both Iowa and Illinois, which were informed of the planned detonation only this week,” the lawmakers wrote. “Our offices have received reports of poor communication from the Army and EPA about the detonation plans and anticipated monitoring after the detonation. In addition, there are significant concerns about appropriate Army and EPA oversight of this contractor-operated facility, the site of which remains on the Superfund list. We urge you to examine the contractor’s handling of this and other hazardous material to prevent any future issues.”

The lawmakers’ letter concludes, “Given the urgency of this scheduled detonation, we request an immediate reply to this letter before any planned detonation and look forward to working with you to ensure that the health and safety of families across Iowa and Illinois remains the highest priority.”

Full text of the letter is available on Senator Duckworth’s website and below:

November 19, 2026

Dear Acting Secretary Telle and Administrator Zeldin:

We write to express our grave concerns with this Friday’s planned detonation of 9,700 pounds of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa. While we understand the urgent need to address these volatile materials, their detonation has the potential to spread lead contamination in and around the region. We call on you to consider delaying this detonation until there is an opportunity to explore safer alternatives. At a minimum, we request an immediate update before the Army proceeds on the detailed detonation plans; mitigation efforts; likely range and location of the possible toxic plume, including as modeled for weather conditions; pre- and post-detonation monitoring and sampling; possibilities of alternative disposal procedures; and plan to remain in timely communication with state and local officials and communities both before and after the detonation.

We appreciate that the Army and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) have studied the need to address the degraded lead azide at the IAAAP, including the risks associated with transporting the material. However, Iowa and Illinois residents understandably are concerned about the potential health impacts of the scheduled detonation. Lead dust is particularly harmful to children and pregnant women. It can contaminate soil and critical farmland indefinitely.

We encourage you to remain in timely communication with state and local officials and communities across both Iowa and Illinois, which were informed of the planned detonation only this week. Our offices have received reports of poor communication from the Army and EPA about the detonation plans and anticipated monitoring after the detonation. In addition, there are significant concerns about appropriate Army and EPA oversight of this contractor-operated facility, the site of which remains on the Superfund list. We urge you to examine the contractor’s handling of this and other hazardous material to prevent any future issues.

Given the urgency of this scheduled detonation, we request an immediate reply to this letter before any planned detonation and look forward to working with you to ensure that the health and safety of families across Iowa and Illinois remains the highest priority.

Sincerely,

-30-

title: Duckworth Introduces Slate of Bills to Take Care of Military Families
text:
As Trump Administration leaves military families in limbo, Duckworth’s bills would make housing, child care and health care more affordable and accessible for them

[WASHINGTON, D.C.] — Combat Veteran and U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) today introduced a slate of bills that would better support our military families as the Trump Administration continues stretching them past their limits. Between unpredictable extended deployments for Trump’s illegal war and the skyrocketing cost of living as a direct result of this President’s failed agenda, our heroes’ families need relief now. While the Trump Administration makes the lives of our military families infinitely harder, the Senator’s five bills would help increase their access to quality health care, make it easier for them to find a home and decrease their child care costs.

“Military families already sacrifice so much for our country. But for nine months, Trump’s illegal war has forced them to sacrifice even more than they should with no end in sight,” said Duckworth. “While indefinite extended deployments to the Middle East are leaving so many military families in limbo, they’re also facing sky-high costs for basic needs. These families deserve our support urgently—not just because their sacrifices should be honored, but to ensure these problems don’t impact our military readiness and retention efforts in the long run. These bills would help make basic needs more affordable for military families, filling in support gaps as Donald Trump keeps failing them at every turn.”

Duckworth’s slate of bills, which is being introduced during Military Family Appreciation Month, would address the housing, health care, child care and affordability issues that are challenging military families:

The Continuity of Care During Military Moves Act, bipartisan legislation cosponsored by U.S. Senator Mike Rounds (R-SD) which would ensure servicemembers and their families experience no gap in specialty health care when relocating by requiring timely referral decisions and transfer of patient medical records to ensure a seamless handoff between providers at the departing and arrival locations.

The Military Housing Optimization Mapping for Efficiency (Military HOME) Act, which would improve military family relocation and make finding on-base housing easier by expanding an existing online real-estate inventory tool across multiple installations to help identify available on-base housing as well as unused space that can be used to construct new facilities to support families.

The Military Family Diaper Assistance Act, which would provide increased child care support for military families by establishing a pilot program that connects community diaper banks with military installations to distribute diapers and diapering supplies to families in need.

The Military Family Limb Loss Support Act, which would improve care for military families experiencing limb loss and limb difference by implementing a program to connect eligible beneficiaries with peer mentorship, family navigation, educational resources and non-clinical support services.

The Preeclampsia Prevention for Military Moms Act, which would help expectant and new moms detect preeclampsia earlier, reduce avoidable medical expenses and strengthen military family resilience by creating a pilot program to remotely monitor blood pressure.

Last week, Duckworth led several colleagues in announcing their intent to offer an amendment to any government funding deal that would defund Trump’s disastrous war until it’s authorized by Congress, as required by the Constitution. The Senator’s forthcoming amendment mirrors her amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (NDAA), which Republicans shamefully blocked.

Duckworth has long been a fierce leader and advocate for our nation’s military families and Veterans. She has repeatedly pushed to expand IVF access for military families through her Right to IVF Act and her IVF for Military Families Act, which respectively would codify a nationwide right to access IVF treatment and require TRICARE coverage of fertility services—including IVF—to ensure servicemembers and their families have access to the same level of IVF coverage that Members of Congress and other federal workers already receive.

Some of her efforts also include:

On August 10, 2026, Duckworth and several of her colleagues led an extensive group of Senate and House Democratic lawmakers in pressing the Trump Administration on its efforts to coordinate to arrest, detain and deport hundreds of Veterans and military families.

On May 15, 2026, Duckworth announced the release of military spouse Deisy Rivera Ortega from ICE detention after the Senator personally called U.S. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin advocating on Ms. Rivera Ortega’s behalf. Ms. Rivera Ortega—wife of active-duty U.S. Army Sgt. 1st Class Jose Serrano—was arrested and detained by ICE during a routine immigration check-in appointment.

On April 30, 2026, Duckworth helped introduce the Servicemember Civilian Transition Support Act to better support servicemembers as they transition back to civilian life.

On April 3, 2026, Duckworth introduced the bipartisan Copay Fairness for Veterans Act to eliminate unfair out-of-pocket health care costs for Veterans. Earlier this year, she helped lead a bipartisan push to make it easier for Veterans to use their GI Bill benefits in apprenticeship programs.

On March 27, 2026, Duckworth helped introduce the bipartisan Veterans Health Administration Novel Therapeutics Preparedness Act to increase Veterans’ access to innovative health care and ensure the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is prepared to better care for Veterans with emerging mental health therapies.

On February 18, 2026, Duckworth demanded that the VA rescind a rule change that put millions of Veterans’ disability ratings and care at risk. The VA then paused and later rescinded enforcement of the rule.

On May 7, 2025, Duckworth introduced the Protecting Veterans in Crisis Act to help safeguard the Veterans Crisis Line (VCL) for the brave Veterans who depend on it by increasing transparency and strengthening Congress’s oversight of it. On the same day, Duckworth also introduced the VA Employee Fairness Act to empower VA health care professionals with the protections needed to speak out about disruptions and advocate for the Veterans they serve as Donald Trump and Elon Musk’s VA cuts continued to jeopardize care.

On March 10, 2025, Duckworth introduced the Protect Veteran Jobs Act to reinstate Veterans who were fired from their jobs as part of Donald Trump and Elon Musk’s indiscriminate purge of federal employees.

On January 3, 2019, Duckworth’s bipartisan Veterans Small Business Enhancement Act was signed into law, allowing Veteran small business owners to acquire surplus federal equipment and personal property by adding Veterans to the list of eligible recipients, which already includes women and minority small business owners.

title: Durbin Calls Out Senate Republicans For Jamming Through Extreme And Unqualified Judicial Nominees
text:
Durbin: “Believe me when I tell you that in the past two years, my colleagues on the other side of the aisle have largely disregarded their advice and consent duty to confirm some of the most extreme nominees in our nation’s history.”

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, today delivered a speech on the Senate floor calling out Senate Republicans for jamming through the Trump Administration’s extreme and unqualified judicial nominees during the lame-duck session. In his remarks, Durbin slammed Senate Republicans for violating longstanding bipartisan Senate Judiciary Committee norms to fast-track judicial nominees because Democrats are poised to lead the Senate come January. Further, Durbin pointed to the judicial misconduct allegations against Daniel Ballou, who has been nominated to be a district court judge in the Eastern District of Kentucky and who Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD) has filed cloture on, as a dangerous example of Senate Republicans’ ploy to cram the bench with extreme judges with a history of behavior unbecoming of a lifetime appointment.

“I have been a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee for nearly 30 years and I chaired the Committee for a four year period of time. I have closely evaluated the credentials and records of more than a thousand judicial nominees appointed by Presidents of both parties. So believe me when I tell you that in the past two years, my colleagues on the other side of the aisle have largely disregarded their advice and consent duty to confirm some of the most extreme nominees in our nation’s history,” Durbin began.

“In the aftermath of this month’s Democratic landslide election, they [Senate Republicans] are shattering a number of Committee norms to jam through more inexperienced nominees before Democrats are in control of the Senate on January 3,” Durbin said.

Since the election, Senate Republicans have tried to fast-track nominees by holding nominations hearings eight days apart despite norms dictating that these hearings should be scheduled at least two weeks apart; slating nominees for hearings sooner than the standard 28 days after receiving their Senate Judiciary Questionnaires; and calling nominees for hearings even if their FBI background investigations have not yet been cleared by staff.

“What these decisions mean is that Senators of both parties will have less time to carefully consider these lifetime appointees…Republicans are setting new precedents to rush through unqualified MAGA nominees,” Durbin said. “Mark my words: Democrats will be well within our rights to rely on these precedents in the future to confirm nominees. As I have said many times, there cannot be one set of rules for Republicans and another for Democrats.”

“For as long as I can remember, every judicial nominee has been closely vetted by the Federal Bureau of Investigation and Committee staff have reviewed these investigations to determine, before a nominee’s confirmation hearing, that there are no concerning aspects of their record,” Durbin said. “As a threshold matter, Senators should feel confident that judicial nominees don’t have a criminal record, that they are not financially insolvent, and that they are well-regarded by judges and others in the legal community. This week, the Judiciary Committee will do something unprecedented: it will slate nominees for these lifetime appointments to the federal bench even if their background investigations haven’t been completed and reviewed by the Committee.”

Further, Senate Republicans have allowed blatantly unqualified nominees to seek lifetime appointments to the federal bench.

“If there is a theme among Trump nominees, it is the vast majority are blatantly inexperienced. As an example, at last week’s nominations hearing, we heard from two nominees who have been out of law school for just eight years. One of them has practiced law for just seven years. The other has only practiced for five years. That is less experience than any Biden nominee or any prior Trump nominee,” Durbin said. “Two of the nominees at last week’s hearing have never tried a case.”

Durbin then called out Majority Leader Thune for filing cloture on Daniel Ballou, nominated to be a district court judge in the Eastern District of Kentucky, despite being the subject of an outstanding judicial misconduct allegation.

“This is not the first time that Judge Ballou has been investigated while on the bench. In 2011, he was publicly reprimanded by Kentucky’s nonpartisan Judicial Conduct Commission for using his position as a judge to campaign for a political candidate. And just days ago, the same commission filed three new misconduct charges against Judge Ballou for repeatedly belittling an attorney for posting a video on social media that Judge Ballou didn’t personally like,” Durbin said.

“These allegations reveal a troubling pattern of poor judgment, which is going to be rewarded with a lifetime appointment to the federal bench by this Republican majority in the Senate. My Republican colleagues seem intent on advancing Judge Ballou regardless of his conduct. What a shame. In my time in the Senate, I cannot recall another instance where we confirmed a judge who was the subject of a pending judicial misconduct complaint,” Durbin continued.

Durbin concluded his remarks by calling on Senate Republicans to abandon their plans to jam through unqualified judicial nominees and instead honor their constitutional advice and consent responsibility.

“It is clear that to this President, experience and sound judgment do not matter when it comes to judges…His sole consideration is loyalty,” Durbin said.

“My colleagues on the other side of the aisle are opening Pandora’s box—their flouting of longstanding norms will reshape the way that we approach judicial confirmations for years to come. It is not too late to reverse course. It is not too late to honor our responsibility under the Constitution to provide advice and consent,” Durbin concluded his remarks.

title: Durbin Introduces Legislation To Repeal MLB’s 100-Year-Old Antitrust Exemption
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, introduced the Competition in Professional Baseball Act to repeal Major League Baseball’s (MLB) 100-year-old judicially-created antitrust exemption, which would place baseball on the same footing as all other professional sports. U.S. Senator Mike Lee (R-UT) is a cosponsor of the legislation.

“I have said for years that it is time to reconsider MLB’s special antitrust exemption, which allows them to act as a lawful monopoly. It is important to note that MLB is the only professional sport to benefit from a broad exemption from the antitrust laws—one that is based on a Supreme Court decision that the Court itself has said is wrong. My bill would repeal professional baseball’s judicially-created antitrust exemption and finally place baseball on the same footing as all other professional sports,” said Durbin.

As Chair of the Judiciary Committee during the Biden Administration, Durbin led efforts to improve working conditions for minor league baseball players by investigating how MLB’s antitrust exemption impacted those working conditions. In June 2022, Durbin led a letter to Advocates for Minor Leaguers asking about the impact of MLB’s antitrust exemption on competition in the labor market for Minor League players. In July 2022, Durbin sent a similar letter to Commissioner Manfred.

These letters played a role in pushing MLB to recognize the unionization of Minor League Baseball players under the umbrella of the Major League Baseball Players Association (MLBPA) in September 2022.

In November 2023, Durbin and a group of Senators pressed Rob Manfred, the Commissioner of the MLB, on its lobbying for a broad exemption from wage and hour laws at the same time it was negotiating its Minor League CBA with MLBPA. Following this, Durbin introduced the Fair Ball Act, which would have contingently repealed an exemption from federal wage and hour laws for Minor League players if they were not being compensated pursuant to the terms of a CBA.

title: Durbin Leads Illinois, Iowa Bipartisan Lawmakers In Calling On Army, EPA To Consider Delaying Planned Detonation Of Lead Azide, Request Detailed Plans
text:
In their letter, lawmakers express concern about public health and lack of adequate communication from the Army and EPA with local officials and communities

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL); U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL); U.S. Representatives Darin LaHood (R-IL-16), Mary Miller (R-IL-15), and Eric Sorensen (D-IL-17); Illinois Governor JB Pritzker; and Senators-elect Julianna Stratton (D-IL) and Josh Turek (D-IA) today sent a letter to Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin expressing the lawmakers’ grave concerns with Friday’s planned detonation of 9,700 pounds of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa, and called on the Army and EPA to consider delaying this detonation until there is an opportunity to explore safer alternatives. Lead dust is particularly harmful to children and pregnant women, and it can contaminate soil and critical farmland indefinitely. Further, communities across both Iowa and Illinois were informed of the planned detonation only this week.

“While we understand the urgent need to address these volatile materials, their detonation has the potential to spread lead contamination in and around the region. We call on you to consider delaying this detonation until there is an opportunity to explore safer alternatives,” the lawmakers wrote.

At a minimum, the lawmakers—recognizing the risks associated with transporting lead azide—requested an immediate update before the Army proceeds on the detailed detonation plans; mitigation efforts; likely range and location of the possible toxic plume, including as modeled for weather conditions; pre- and post-detonation monitoring and sampling; possibilities of alternative disposal procedures; and plan to remain in timely communication with state and local officials and communities both before and after the detonation.

“We encourage you to remain in timely communication with state and local officials and communities across both Iowa and Illinois, which were informed of the planned detonation only this week,” the lawmakers wrote. “Our offices have received reports of poor communication from the Army and EPA about the detonation plans and anticipated monitoring after the detonation. In addition, there are significant concerns about appropriate Army and EPA oversight of this contractor-operated facility, the site of which remains on the Superfund list. We urge you to examine the contractor’s handling of this and other hazardous material to prevent any future issues.”

The lawmakers’ letter concludes, “Given the urgency of this scheduled detonation, we request an immediate reply to this letter before any planned detonation and look forward to working with you to ensure that the health and safety of families across Iowa and Illinois remains the highest priority.”

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

November 19, 2026

Dear Acting Secretary Telle and Administrator Zeldin:

We write to express our grave concerns with this Friday’s planned detonation of 9,700 pounds of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP) in Middletown, Iowa. While we understand the urgent need to address these volatile materials, their detonation has the potential to spread lead contamination in and around the region. We call on you to consider delaying this detonation until there is an opportunity to explore safer alternatives. At a minimum, we request an immediate update before the Army proceeds on the detailed detonation plans; mitigation efforts; likely range and location of the possible toxic plume, including as modeled for weather conditions; pre- and post-detonation monitoring and sampling; possibilities of alternative disposal procedures; and plan to remain in timely communication with state and local officials and communities both before and after the detonation.

We appreciate that the Army and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) have studied the need to address the degraded lead azide at the IAAAP, including the risks associated with transporting the material. However, Iowa and Illinois residents understandably are concerned about the potential health impacts of the scheduled detonation. Lead dust is particularly harmful to children and pregnant women. It can contaminate soil and critical farmland indefinitely.

We encourage you to remain in timely communication with state and local officials and communities across both Iowa and Illinois, which were informed of the planned detonation only this week. Our offices have received reports of poor communication from the Army and EPA about the detonation plans and anticipated monitoring after the detonation. In addition, there are significant concerns about appropriate Army and EPA oversight of this contractor-operated facility, the site of which remains on the Superfund list. We urge you to examine the contractor’s handling of this and other hazardous material to prevent any future issues.

Given the urgency of this scheduled detonation, we request an immediate reply to this letter before any planned detonation and look forward to working with you to ensure that the health and safety of families across Iowa and Illinois remains the highest priority.

Sincerely,

-30-

title: Durbin Praises Retiring Illinois Congressional Delegation Members In Senate Floor Speech
text:
Durbin acknowledged the accomplishments and public service of five retiring members of the Illinois congressional delegation, who, collectively, have represented Illinois in Congress for almost a century

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) today delivered a speech on the Senate floor honoring the retiring members of the Illinois congressional delegation—Congressman Jesús “Chuy” García (D-IL-04), Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL-08), Congresswoman Robin Kelly (D-IL-02), Congresswoman Jan Schakowsky (D-IL-09), and Congressman Danny K. Davis (D-IL-07). During his remarks, Durbin spoke about each member, highlighting their legislative accomplishments, from expanding access to health care to addressing the gun violence epidemic. Put together, these public servants have represented Illinois in Congress for almost one century.

Durbin began by praising García, thanking him for being an ally in the fight to pass the Dream Act. Born in Los Pinos, Mexico, García came to the U.S. at nine years old. Entering politics in 1984, he has served as Committeeman of the Cook County Democratic Party, became an alderman, and served as a State Senator and Cook County commissioner before coming to Congress.

“He has also been one of my strongest friends and allies in the fight to pass the Dream Act, a measure which I introduced 25 years ago that said if you were brought to the United States as a child, and you grew up here, didn’t get in trouble, did what you were supposed to do, you ought to have a path to citizenship. Chuy agrees with that, and he has been a great champion of that cause. I have been honored to stand by him in that effort,” Durbin said.

Durbin honored Krishnamoorthi, highlighting their partnership in cracking down on illicit e-cigarettes. Krishnamoorthi immigrated from New Delhi, India, to Peoria, Illinois, as a young child. He went on to serve in several statewide offices in Illinois prior to serving in Congress.

“Congressman Krishnamoorthi, shortly after being sworn in, joined protests at O’Hare when President Trump, in his first term, implemented his Muslim travel ban…Closest to my heart were his efforts to fight the vaping epidemic,” Durbin said.

“I want to thank Raja Krishnamoorthi because he’s taken on this cause with the new insidious effort by the tobacco companies to addict our children with vaping…He launched the first ever congressional investigation on the matter in 2019, and he pushed for bans on flavored vaping products. I commend him for that. It took courage and a lot of determination. His work to protect our kids and grandkids from this poison will continue to benefit Americans for generations to come,” Durbin said.

Durbin spoke highly of Kelly, who has served Illinois’ Second Congressional District for almost 14 years. Durbin commended Kelly’s commitment to connecting with every corner of Illinois, not just the Chicago area, when she served as the Chair of the Illinois Democratic Party.

“Congresswoman Kelly is a personal friend. She’s smart. She’s talented. She’s hardworking. She’s also someone who lifts up forgotten voices in the state. In 2021, after she became Chair of the Illinois Democratic Party, she immediately started driving south for a listening tour across Illinois. For these downstate counties, Congresswoman Kelly was the first person from our party many of them had ever seen. In Congress, she fought passionately for reasonable gun control laws, authorizing the first-ever congressional analysis of the American gun violence epidemic. She’s pushed to expand health care, particularly to expectant mothers, economic development, and civil rights across America,” Durbin said. “Congresswoman Kelly has made America proud.”

Durbin then lauded Schakowsky’s accomplishments in Congress and thanked her for her contributions to the Illinois Women’s Institute for Leadership Training Academy, which helps train the next generation of women in Illinois politics.

“She is one of my dearest friends in the delegation,” Durbin said. “She’s been a leader on countless issues from the Affordable Care Act to human rights overseas. How did she get started? She got started as a mom who had a simple idea—she thought dairy products sold in grocery stores ought to have an expiration date, so you know that the milk you’re buying today does not expire tomorrow. It was a simple request, and it took a big battle. But Jan Schakowsky never says quit.”

“I also must note her contributions when it came to an organization near and dear to my family. Twenty-five years ago, my wife, Loretta, and a number of people came together, Bonnie Ettinger, Linda Hawker, to establish the Illinois Women’s Institute for Leadership Training Academy. What they did was recruit 12 women each year to be trained to run for office…If you do the math, you realize that 300 women across our state have gone through this training. Jan Schakowsky was one of the big champions of this program, and I thank her because she’s made a real difference,” Durbin continued.

“Do these women go on to do great things? Let me give you one example. When I retire January 3, the person who will take over my seat as the new Senator from Illinois is Juliana Stratton. Juliana Stratton was a member of this program that I just described that Jan Schakowsky supported. She went through the training early on. She was elected to the statehouse, then elected Lieutenant Governor of Illinois, and now she’s going to succeed me in the Senate,” Durbin said.

Durbin then highlighted Davis’ contributions, applauding him for being a champion for expanding health care access through the Affordable Care Act.

“Congressman Davis joined the House of Representatives the same year I was elected to the Senate, so we’ve been together for 30 years,” Durbin said. “Perhaps his largest legacy can be found in his dedication to health care, where he played a pivotal role expanding treatment for people suffering from sickle cell. He helped push for the passage of the Affordable Care Act and key provisions for Federally Qualified Community Health Centers…In championing the Maternal Infant and Early Childhood Home Visiting program, he brought $119 million to Illinois to improve maternal and children’s health.”

Durbin also commended each member’s partner for supporting their service in the House of Representatives.

“A person’s decision to serve in government comes at a great sacrifice to their families. I’ve been lucky to have the support and strength of my family and my wife, Loretta, throughout this career. To Evelyn García, Priya Krishnamoorthi, Bob Creamer, Vera Davis, and the late Dr. Nathaniel Horn, I want to publicly thank them for their service,” Durbin said.

Durbin concluded his remarks by again thanking the members for working alongside him to serve Illinoisans.

“These Representatives are some of the best Illinois has ever had. Their leadership and service will not soon be forgotten. I want to say to them: it’s been an honor to serve the state of Illinois with you, to work with you for the good of our nation and for the good of the world,” Durbin said.

title: Durbin Receives Highest Distinction From Congress Of Bosniaks Of North America
text:
Durbin was presented with the Order of Lilium Bosniacum in recognition of his decades of support for Bosnia and Herzegovina

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL) today was awarded with the Order of Lilium Bosniacum, the highest distinction awarded by the Congress of Bosniaks of North America. The organization’s executive director, Selma Porca, presented Durbin with the award in recognition of his decades of support for Bosnia and Herzegovina, including his 1995 vote in favor of lifting the arms embargo that consequently led to the Dayton Accords.

“Bosnia has a difficult past, a history marred by devastating conflict and massacres. In my visits to the Balkan region over my decades in Congress, I’ve seen the many challenges that remain decades after the signing of the Dayton Accords,” Durbin said. “It’s my belief that we must continue to support efforts to draw nations, like Bosnia, into the European Union and NATO in hopes of preserving peace, prosperity, and democracy in the region.”

A photo of Durbin receiving the award can be found here.

Last month, Durbin joined his final congressional delegation trip as a U.S. Senator, visiting Bosnia and Herzegovina, Albania, Montenegro, Croatia, and Kosovo. During the trip, the congressional delegation met with government officials, U.S. diplomatic personnel, civil society representatives, and young leaders to discuss regional security, democratic institutions, economic opportunity, and relations with the United States. Meetings addressed the European Union accession processes, NATO cooperation, energy diversification, and implementation of the Western Balkans Democracy and Prosperity Act, enacted as part of the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act. The delegation visited the Srebrenica Memorial Center and Cemetery at Potocari and attended a performance by the House of Good Tones.

Durbin previously traveled to the Balkans in 1999 and 2009.

title: Durbin Releases GAO Report On The Wasteful Immigration Detention Spending Under The Trump Administration
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, today led the release of the Government Accountability Office’s (GAO) newly-completed report examining the cost of immigration detention under the Trump Administration’s U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) entitled, “ICE Should Determine Cost Effectiveness of New Initiatives Before Continuing”.

ICE received $45 billion in immigration detention funding in July 2025 through Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill Act. According to GAO’s report: “In addition to maintaining existing facilities with these funds, ICE began implementing an initiative to buy and renovate a collection of warehouses to use as new detention facilities. However, after acquiring 11 warehouses for about $1.07 billion, ICE scaled down the initiative significantly and plans to sell seven of them. In July and August 2026, ICE also bought four existing detention facilities for about $2.2 billion total. However, the scope, time frames, and estimated costs for further acquisitions remain undetermined. In addition, ICE did not update its spending plan for detention funding to reflect the shifting status of the warehouse initiative or other planned acquisitions, as required by its internal guidance. As a result, the spending plan includes an inflated estimate of planned obligations, which affects oversight efforts and ICE’s ability to assess long-term budget needs.”

“This report has uncovered more of what we’ve come to expect from the Trump Administration—rushed and wasteful spending of taxpayer dollars without any benefit to the American people. Remember when Donald Trump promised to get rid of ‘waste, fraud, and abuse’? Well, GAO continues to expose a shocking pattern of waste within the Administration’s unconscionable mass deportation campaign,” said Durbin. “The midterm elections showed that the American people are sick and tired of the Trump Administration’s cruel immigration tactics. It is time to hold DHS and ICE responsible.”

GAO’s key findings include:

Warehouses bought, then abandoned. From January to March 2026, ICE bought 11 warehouses for about $1.07 billion. It paid at least 50 percent above assessed tax value for nine of them and at least double for seven. After DHS paused the initiative, the DHS Secretary testified that the department “had not conducted appropriate due diligence and planning.” ICE now plans to sell seven of the properties, and GAO warns the sales could lose the government money.

$2.2 billion more in facility purchases, with no expected savings. In July and August 2026, ICE bought four existing detention facilities for about $2.2 billion. ICE officials told GAO they do not expect these purchases to save money because the goal is to keep operating where ICE faces pushback from state governments. ICE is considering buying up to seven more but gave GAO no timeline or cost estimates.

Paying for empty beds. ICE has committed to pay for 46,688 beds at 64 facilities whether or not they are used. From October 2025 to April 2026, an average of 9,733 of those beds sat empty each day. At just four facilities, GAO estimates ICE paid about $13 million a month for empty beds.

Guantánamo Bay at more than $110 million. ICE and the Department of Defense obligated about $111 million for immigration detention at Guantánamo Bay, where the average daily population was fewer than 30. ICE officials told GAO that cost did not factor into the decision and that conserving costs is not a goal there.

An outdated, inflated spending plan. As of June 2026, ICE’s spending plan still projected about $38 billion in fiscal year 2026 obligations. Through July, ICE had obligated $9.1 billion. GAO called it unrealistic that ICE would obligate another $29 billion in two months.

Overstretched oversight staff. The staff who validate facility invoices are short-handed, with 55 of 87 positions vacant while the number of detention facilities roughly doubled.

title: Ernst Applauds Senate for Putting Parents First
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the bipartisan FAIR Leave Act (S. 3321), introduced by Senator Joni Ernst (R-Iowa), passed the Senate. Ernst is now urging the House to pass the bill and send it to the president's desk.

“We talk a lot about putting families first. This is a small, commonsense step that does exactly that,” said Ernst. “The Senate did its part, now it's time for our colleagues in the House to do the same so parents across the country, especially our military families, never miss those precious first weeks with a new baby.”

Background:

Under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) of 1993, married parents who work for the same employer are limited to a combined 12 weeks of leave following the birth or adoption of a child. However, if those same parents work for different employers, each parent is eligible for up to 12 weeks of leave.

This issue particularly impacts military families, where both parents often work for the same employer and face limits on the amount of time they can take off to care for their children.

The bipartisan FAIR Leave Act eliminates this restriction, allowing eligible married parents who work for the same employer to each take up to 12 weeks of FMLA leave. This would help ensure families have the time they deserve to care for and bond with their newborn and newly-adopted children.

title: Fetterman, Colleagues Celebrate Senate Passage of Washington’s Trail Bill
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Following the U.S. Senate’s passage of his bipartisan, bicameral Washington’s Trail — 1753 National Historic Trail Feasibility Study Act by unanimous consent, U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) today released the following statement:

“We are one step closer to preserving Washington’s Trail and protecting this crucial piece of American history as a lasting educational tool for generations to come.

“I’m grateful the Senate passed my bill unanimously today and urge my House colleagues to finish the job.”

Washington’s Trail follows George Washington’s path in 1753 on his way to Fort LeBoeuf in what is now known as Waterford, PA in Erie County. The trail starts in Virginia and includes portions of Maryland, West Virginia, and crosses several Western Pennsylvania counties. In Pennsylvania, the trail features scenic markers and landmarks highlighting major tourist and historical destinations such as the Fort Pitt Museum in Pittsburgh, the Old Economy Village in Ambridge, DeBence Antique Music World Museum in Franklin, Fort LeBoeuf Museum in Erie, and many more iconic places.

The bill was introduced in May by Senator Fetterman and Congressman Mike Kelly (R-PA-16), and was cosponsored by U.S. Senators Dave McCormick (R-PA), Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV), Jim Justice (R-WV), Tim Kaine (D-VA), and Mark Warner (D-VA).

“By designating Washington’s Trail as a national historic trail, we create an opportunity to preserve this history, to build community pride, to connect communities, promote economic revitalization, and create jobs while telling this story of George Washington and the birth of our nation,” said Rep. Kelly. “I commend the work of local volunteers who have brought George Washington’s journey to life. Today’s vote moves us one step closer toward sharing this legacy with current and future generations.”

“Washington’s Trail tells an important story about our nation’s founding, and I’m proud to see this bipartisan legislation pass the Senate,” said Senator McCormick. “I’m grateful to Senator Fetterman and our colleagues for working together to help preserve this critical piece of Pennsylvania’s history, promote tourism, and make it a National Historic Trail.”

“Washington’s Trail represents an amazing chapter in our nation’s founding, and West Virginia is proud to be a part of that story,” said Senator Capito. “I am grateful to see the Senate pass this bill to study the feasibility of designating Washington’s Trail as a National Historic Trail. This effort will help preserve this important legacy and ensure future generations understand West Virginia’s unique role in America’s early history.”

“Some of the earliest chapters of our nation’s story unfolded in West Virginia. Recognizing Washington’s Trail is an incredible opportunity to showcase West Virginia’s role in shaping American history and preserve it for generations to come. I’m thrilled the Senate unanimously passed this legislation today, and I hope the House will quickly get it across the finish line,” said Senator Justice.

“Washington’s Trail follows George Washington’s first military and diplomatic mission and highlights Virginia’s role in our nation’s early history,” said Senator Kaine. “As we celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, I’m glad the Senate has taken a bipartisan step toward preserving this historic route for future generations to learn from and enjoy.”

“Beginning in Williamsburg, Virginia, Washington’s Trail offers a unique glimpse into the military and diplomatic ventures that shaped our nation’s first president,” said Senator Warner. “I’m proud that the Senate has passed this bipartisan legislation to recognize the trail’s historical significance and help preserve it for future generations. This designation would not only honor an important part of our nation’s story, but also bring new opportunities for tourism, education, and economic development to communities along the trail.”

The bill now heads to the U.S. House of Representatives.

title: Gillibrand, Colleagues Urge Amtrak To Reconsider Allowing Firearms In Carry-On Baggage
text:
Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), ranking member of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and Related Agencies (THUD), led a group of 20 senators in a letter to Interim Amtrak President Byl Herrmann urging Amtrak to reconsider its new firearm policies that – for the first time – will allow passengers to carry on firearms on routes that do not have checked baggage cars.

In their letter, the senators called on Amtrak to reconsider its plan to allow unloaded firearms and ammunition in personal lock boxes as carry-on baggage in passenger cars and posed questions about the decision-making and safety concerns.

“We are alarmed by these changes in policies, which seem to be made because of pressure and new arbitrary federal grant conditions, and the increased risks these new policies pose to the safety of passengers aboard Amtrak trains and at stations as well as front-line workers, including onboard service workers, conductors, station personnel, and law enforcement,” wrote the senators. “Further, introducing firearms, even if unloaded, within passenger cars — without separating passengers from the firearms — would not meet the standards established by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) for air travel, which unlike Amtrak, includes strict passenger security screening to board planes.”

The first set of changed policies, effective September 1, 2026, included allowing the transport of unloaded firearms and ammunition on the Auto Train. More drastically, effective January 2027, Amtrak plans to expand firearms allowances to its entire passenger rail network. For routes with no checked baggage cars, which is the majority of Amtrak trains, firearms will be allowed within passenger cars, simply placed at a person’s feet or in the overhead rack.

These changes follow the Trump administration’s Department of Transportation adding new grant conditions to Amtrak’s Fiscal Year 2026 federal grant. Amtrak’s annual federal funding grant is made possible by the THUD appropriations bill.

Prior to September 1, 2026, Amtrak only permitted passengers to transport unloaded, locked firearms and ammunition on Long Distance and select State Supported routes that are equipped with separate checked baggage cars.

“This unprecedented change will result in Amtrak permitting unloaded firearms and ammunition to be present in passenger cars in carry-on baggage on Amtrak trains that carry millions of passengers a year, such as the Northeast Regional, Keystone Service, and Capitol Corridor,” the senators wrote. “Overall, in fiscal year 2025, Amtrak provided 34.5 million customer trips, of which 15.2 million were on the Northeast Regional and Acela trains and 14.8 million were on State Supported Services trains.”

The senators pressed Amtrak on what prompted the policy changes; whether it conducted safety, security, or business case analyses; and whether it explored alternatives to keep firearms separated from passengers. They also asked how Amtrak will handle unstaffed stations; navigate varying state and local gun laws; verify case and lock standards; notify crews and passengers when a firearm is onboard; and consult, train, and staff front-line workers and Amtrak Police, along with what Amtrak expects the total cost and funding sources to be to implement the new rules. They gave Amtrak until December 9, 2026 to respond.

The letter follows labor union calls for concern, including objections raised by the Transport Workers Union. It was also signed by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Chris Coons (D-DE), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Dick Durbin (D-IL), John Fetterman (D-PA), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Angus King (I-ME), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Jack Reed (D-RI), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Mark Warner (D-VA), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI).

The full text of the letter can be found here or below:

Dear Mr. Herrmann:

We are writing regarding Amtrak’s recent and upcoming changes to its firearm transport policies across its Long-Distance, State Supported, and Northeast Corridor Service Lines. We strongly support Amtrak as America’s Railroad and the valuable passenger rail services it provides to millions of customers across the country every year. However, we are concerned by these changing policies and that they could undermine safety.

Since 2009, Amtrak has permitted passengers to transport unloaded firearms and ammunition solely in checked baggage on Long Distance and select State Supported routes that are equipped with checked baggage cars and between Amtrak stations with a ticket office. Passengers choosing to transport these items on those routes have had to follow certain notification and handling requirements, including notifying Amtrak via a phone call at least 24 hours prior to departure that they will be checking firearms and ammunition, completing a two-part Declaration Form at check-in, and locking the unloaded firearm in an approved, hard-sided container which the passenger has the sole possession of the key or the combination to. Before departure, the locked container is then placed in the baggage car by an Amtrak crew member, which is off-limits to passengers.

It is our understanding that pursuant to new grant conditions placed on Amtrak by the United States Department of Transportation in its annual federal grant, made possible by the fiscal year 2026 funding appropriated by Congress, Amtrak is changing its firearm and ammunition handling and notifications requirements to be more lenient and expanding the policies across its service network. First, effective September 1, 2026, Amtrak began to allow the transport of unloaded firearms and ammunition on the Auto Train. Importantly, the unloaded firearms and ammunition must remain locked in the customer’s vehicle or motorcycle onboard the train, which is inaccessible to passengers. This means the firearms still cannot be transported as carry-on baggage in the passenger compartments of the train, such as the Coach car or sleeper accommodations. In addition, effective September 1, 2026, Amtrak reduced the pre-departure notification requirement for passengers checking firearms in checked baggage on eligible routes from 24 hours to six hours.

While these recent changes in policies have only impacted routes that offer a separate space for firearms and ammunition to be stored, previous reporting shed light on Amtrak beginning considerations earlier this year to significantly expand these policies to the rest of its trains. Now, based on information provided to Congress and additional recent reporting, we understand that in January 2027, Amtrak plans to expand its policies for unloaded firearms and ammunition to be transported by passengers for the very first time to the Northeast Corridor and State Supported Service Lines where there are no checked baggage cars. This unprecedented change will result in Amtrak permitting unloaded firearms and ammunition to be present in passenger cars in carry-on baggage on Amtrak trains that carry millions of passengers a year, such as the Northeast Regional, Keystone Service, and Capitol Corridor. Overall, in fiscal year 2025, Amtrak provided 34.5 million customer trips, of which 15.2 million were on the Northeast Regional and Acela trains, and 14.8 million were on State Supported Services trains. Passengers on these routes who wish to transport an unloaded firearm and ammunition will be required to provide a six-hour pre-departure notification to Amtrak and must present a lockable firearm case that can accommodate two locking mechanisms — one lock supplied by the passenger, and one provided by Amtrak — at a staffed station. The Amtrak lock will be a combination lock set by the station agent, and upon arrival at their final destination, passengers must locate appropriate Amtrak personnel to unlock the Amtrak-provided lock.

We are alarmed by these changes in policies, which seem to be made because of pressure and new arbitrary federal grant conditions, and the increased risks these new policies pose to the safety of passengers aboard Amtrak trains and at stations, as well as front-line workers, including onboard service workers, conductors, station personnel, and law enforcement. Further, introducing firearms, even if unloaded, within passenger cars — without separating passengers from the firearms — would not meet the standards established by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) for air travel, which, unlike Amtrak, includes strict passenger security screening to board planes. We urge Amtrak to reconsider its plan to allow the transport of unloaded firearms and ammunition as carry-on baggage in passenger cars and request responses to the following questions no later than December 9, 2026.

What prompted Amtrak to make these firearm transportation policy changes on each of the service lines (Long-Distance, including the Airo Train, State Supported, and Northeast Corridor Service Lines)?

What, if any, issues were the pre-September 1, 2026, policies causing on the Long-Distance and relevant State Supported routes that warranted Amtrak revising its firearm policies for those trains?

What, if any, safety and security analysis did Amtrak conduct for the changes that are to take effect in January 2027, for the Northeast Corridor and State Supported Service Lines where there are no checked baggage cars?

Has Amtrak conducted a business case analysis regarding customer demand and customer concerns with the changes in policies on each of the service lines? What kind of demand and usage of this policy on the newly eligible routes does Amtrak expect?

Did Amtrak consider options for separating passengers and the firearms and ammunition on train routes with no checked baggage service? If so, what were each of the options, and why were they not selected?

How would a passenger who wishes to transport a firearm do so if their departure or arrival location is at an unstaffed station?

How will Amtrak inform its workers, customers, State Supported route partners, and other transit agencies that operate on Amtrak’s network or in its stations about these policy changes?

How will Amtrak notify its workers and passengers when a customer is carrying a firearm onboard a passenger car?

How will Amtrak ensure that firearm cases used in this process meet TSA standards and that there is not a faulty case or unsecure lock that could make the firearm easily accessible in a passenger car?

What considerations has Amtrak made regarding varying state and local firearm laws?

In considering all firearm policy changes, what engagement and feedback solicitation did Amtrak conduct with law enforcement and the unions representing onboard service workers, conductors, station personnel, and law enforcement?

What training and tools will Amtrak provide to frontline workers and law enforcement to oversee and enforce the new policies on all routes?

How many Amtrak Police officers currently ride on Amtrak trains?

Will Amtrak need to increase staff, including Amtrak Police, to support the oversight and enforcement of the new policies on all routes?

What is the total cost to implement the new policies and what are the funding sources?

title: Gillibrand, Duckworth Demand Passage Of Their Government Funding Bill Amendment To Defund And End Trump’s Costly Iran War
text:
Gillibrand: “It Is Time For Democrats And Republicans To Put American Families First, Fund The Government, And End This Conflict.”

**Watch Senator Gillibrand’s Remarks Here**

Today, U.S. Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) held a press conference to demand that their amendment to defund President Trump’s costly, reckless, and illegal Iran war be included in any government funding deal that is struck.

As Senator Gillibrand underscored in her remarks, “The American people have made clear at the grocery store, the gas station, and recently at the ballot box that they want change. They want leaders who will stop President Trump’s chaos. They want lower prices. And they want an end to the war that they never asked for. This legislation proves we are listening. It would stop every new dollar for offensive operations in Iran, while ensuring our troops have the resources to defend themselves.”

President Trump’s illegal war with Iran has driven up prices in New York and across the country.

Today, gas prices in New York are nearly 40 percent higher than they were at the start of the war more than eight months ago.

The average American household has been forced to shell out over 1,200 dollars extra on gas and diesel since this war began.

At the same time, heating oil—which many New Yorkers use to stay warm in the winter—is over 50 percent more expensive today than a year ago.

In addition to blocking any funding toward offensive operations in Iran, the senators’ amendment, which is also backed by Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), would also withhold travel funding for the Secretary of Defense until the Department of Defense produces a report on the impact this illegal war has had on military readiness and our nation’s service members.

The full text of the amendment can be found here.

Senator Gillibrand’s remarks as prepared for delivery are below:

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us to discuss our new effort to lower costs at home and end President Trump’s costly, illegal, and reckless war with Iran.

Ahead of the government funding deadline in December, we are offering a clear, targeted amendment to any proposed budget bill: not one more dime of taxpayer money for offensive military operations in Iran.

Right now, President Trump is bankrolling this war on the backs of the American people.

This administration has already spent nearly 50 billion taxpayer dollars on this war while cutting billions for healthcare and food assistance here at home.

Today, gas prices in New York are nearly 40 percent higher than they were at the start of the war more than eight months ago. The average American household has been forced to shell out over 1,200 dollars extra on gas and diesel since this war began.

To a middle-class family in Upstate New York, or a working mom in New York City – or anywhere else across the country – that’s a lot of money. It’s more than most families spend on a month’s worth of groceries. But now, instead of going to savings or a college fund, it’s simply gone, consumed by rising prices from this unnecessary war.

In total, Americans have spent an extra 160 billion dollars at the pump since the beginning of the war. Let me repeat that: An extra 160 billion dollars now gone from family budgets and local economies.

At the same time, heating oil—which many New Yorkers use to stay warm in the winter—is over 50 percent more expensive today than a year ago. As temperatures continue to drop, that means that more and more New Yorkers are being forced to ration the fuel they use to keep warm or to turn off the heat entirely.

Every day, I hear from New Yorkers about their concerns. The cost of health care. The cost of gas. The cost to keep the lights on, heat their homes, and put food on the table.

Those are the conversations happening at kitchen tables across America. That is what we should be focused on here in Washington—not dropping bombs across the world.

The American people have made clear at the grocery store, the gas station, and recently at the ballot box that they want change. They want leaders who will stop President Trump’s chaos. They want lower prices. And they want an end to the war that they never asked for.

This legislation proves we are listening.

It would stop every new dollar for offensive operations in Iran, while ensuring our troops have the resources to defend themselves.

That means the U.S. would not be able to drop bombs, launch attacks, or spend money to escalate hostilities unless it is in direct defense of American troops or to protect our allies.

It is time for Democrats and Republicans to put American families first, fund the government, and end this conflict.

If Republicans refuse to join us, they are making a clear choice: to prioritize wasting billions of taxpayer dollars on a war abroad over lowering costs for working families and small businesses here at home.

Let’s work together to keep the government open, bring down prices, and invest in American families.

Thank you.
