title: Sens. Markey, Blumenthal: Stop Punishing Asylum Seekers for U.S. Immigration Agency Scheduling Errors
text:
Letter Text (PDF)

Washington (November 19, 2026) - Senators Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.) and Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) today sent a letter to Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) Director Joseph Edlow demanding that USCIS suspend and withdraw a new asylum interview requirement that would unfairly hold immigrants at fault for the agency’s own scheduling errors. Under the new requirement, asylum seekers that request to reschedule their interviews for “exceptional circumstances” and are either denied or ignored by the agency would face punishment, including potential removal proceedings.

In the letter, Senators Markey and Blumenthal condemned the cruel change that unfairly punishes asylum seekers for USCIS convenience and question the legality of the change under the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA).

“U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services’ (USCIS) new asylum-interview policy turns a scheduling problem into an immigration trap: an applicant who cannot prove abuse, serious illness, the death of an immediate family member, or similarly extraordinary harm may be denied a new interview date and then punished for not appearing, even when the applicant asked to reschedule in advance and USCIS failed to respond. A missed appointment should not become a backdoor route into removal proceedings…We urge USCIS to immediately suspend this policy, restore a fair rescheduling process, and bar adverse action while a timely request remains pending.”

The lawmakers request answers by December 9, 2026, to questions including:

What statutory, regulatory, or other legal authority does USCIS rely on for this policy?

How did USCIS develop and adopt the policy?

What factual record supports the policy change?

How does USCIS handle a timely rescheduling request that remains undecided on the interview date?

What safeguards are in place to ensure that applicants receive fair notice and a meaningful opportunity to comply?

In August, Senator Markey released a report titled “Under the Radar II: The Second Trump Administration’s Stealth Attack on the U.S. Immigration System,” to shed light on the Trump administration’s lesser-known but equally harmful efforts to dismantle the U.S. immigration system.

title: MCCORMICK APPLAUDS U.S. SENATE DELIVERING ON LANDMARK PERMITTING REFORM LEGISLATION
text:
Permitting reform legislation builds on Senator McCormick’s longstanding efforts to cut red tape, lower energy costs, unlock American economic growth

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Dave McCormick (R-PA) today applauded the U.S. Senate passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA), landmark legislation to modernize federal permitting processes, accelerate critical infrastructure projects, lower energy costs, and create good-paying American jobs. Senator McCormick thanked U.S. Senators Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Mike Lee (R-UT), and Martin Heinrich (D-NM) for their leadership in delivering this win. This fulfills one of Senator McCormick’s key campaign promises to overhaul our permitting process to lower costs and make Pennsylvania a better place to invest.

In April, Senator McCormick introduced the Unlock American Energy and Jobs Act of 2026, legislation targeting four major federal permitting chokepoints that have delayed energy infrastructure projects: the abuse of onerous water permitting rules, baseless lawsuits brought by environmental groups, outdated nuclear licensing, and federal barriers to LNG exports. BAAJA addresses two of them, streamlining water permitting and shutting down frivolous lawsuits aimed at delaying projects.

“Pennsylvania has the energy resources, skilled workforce, and innovative companies to power America’s future, but burdensome regulations and permitting delays have held us back,” said Senator McCormick. “This was a day one promise of mine when I entered the Senate, and today’s bipartisan passage is a major step toward delivering American energy dominance. I’ll keep pushing next Congress to cut red tape in areas this bill doesn’t address.”

BAAJA reforms the federal environmental review and permitting process, providing greater regulatory certainty for approved projects. It also requires data centers to cover their own transmission costs instead of shifting those expenses onto American ratepayers.

As Pennsylvania continues to attract growing investment in energy, manufacturing, and emerging technologies, modernizing the nation’s permitting system is essential to turning those commitments into real projects, economic growth, and good-paying jobs across the Commonwealth.

The bipartisan legislation now heads to the U.S. House of Representatives for consideration.

title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Passes Bipartisan Measure Protecting People with Disabilities from Discrimination
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.—Senator Ashley Moody today passed her bipartisan Charlotte Woodward Organ Transplant Discrimination Prevention Act through unanimous consent on the Senate Floor. The legislation prohibits discrimination against people with disabilities from receiving lifesaving organ transplants.

“It’s hard to believe that in America, in 2026, a person could be denied consideration for a lifesaving organ transplant simply because they have a disability. That’s why it was so important to me to take to the Senate Floor and urge my colleagues to pass our Charlotte Woodward Organ Transplant Discrimination Prevention Act and eliminate barriers for people with disabilities who need life-saving organ transplants,” said Senator Ashley Moody. “As we prepare to gather with our loved ones this Thanksgiving, I can think of very few things more meaningful than giving families across America something more to be thankful for: the hope of more time with the people they love.”

“NDSS applauds the Senate’s passage of the Charlotte Woodward Organ Transplant Discrimination Prevention Act, named after NDSS staff member and self-advocate Charlotte Woodward. This marks a historic step toward ending discrimination against people with Down syndrome and other disabilities in the organ transplant system. We are grateful to Senators Ashley Moody and Maggie Hassan and Representatives Kat Cammack and Debbie Dingell for their leadership on this critical legislation,” said Kandi Pickard, CEO of the National Down Syndrome Society.

“I am proud to lend my name to the Charlotte Woodward Organ Transplant Discrimination Prevention Act, and I am beyond excited that the Senate has passed this important legislation. Receiving a heart transplant 14 years ago saved my life and allowed me to pursue my dreams. Unfortunately, other individuals with Down syndrome have been denied organ transplants because of discrimination solely on the basis of disability. This bill will ensure that people with disabilities have the same access to life-saving care as everyone else,” said Charlotte Woodward, namesake of the legislation.

BACKGROUND:

The bill is named for Charlotte Woodward, an individual with Down syndrome who received a lifesaving heart transplant over a decade ago.

Senator Moody is joined by Senator Maggie Hassan as an original cosponsor of the legislation.

The National Down Syndrome Society reports that only 52% of people with disabilities who asked for a referral to an organ transplant specialist actually received a referral.

Almost half (43%) of pediatric transplant centers see intellectual disabilities as a factor against transplant due to assumptions about quality of life. Close to two thirds of transplant centers have serious reservations with providing a kidney to those with even mild intellectual disabilities.

Senator Moody’s Charlotte Woodward Organ Transplant Discrimination Prevention Act previously passed out of the House via voice vote.

title: Sen. Moran Announces K-State Salina Selected as an Inaugural NOAA Cooperative Aviation Center
text:
Moran’s legislation established this program to partner with universities & create a pipeline of NOAA Corps pilots

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Jerry Moran (R-Kan.) – chairman of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, and Science – today announced that Kansas State University Salina (K-State Salina) has been selected as one of three universities to participate in the inaugural National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Cooperative Aviation Centers (NCAC). Sen. Moran’s legislation, which was signed into law in 2020, created the initial NOAA Aviation Accession Training Program, which later became NCAC. This program aims to establish partnerships with universities to create a pipeline of qualified pilots for the NOAA Corps.

“K-State Salina’s selection as one of the first NOAA Cooperative Aviation Centers demonstrates the university’s strong legacy of training the next generation of pilots,” said Sen. Moran. “I worked to establish this program to help address the shortage of qualified NOAA pilots while providing a direct pipeline from our local universities to the NOAA Corps. Pilots studying at K-State Salina will now have the opportunity to receive the training they need for a career with the NOAA Corps, conducting research, weather forecasting and collecting critical data for communities across our state and nation.”

“This partnership opens a door for our students to careers they may never have imagined: flying into hurricanes, supporting weather research and gathering data that communities depend on,” said Alysia Starkey, CEO and dean of Kansas State University Salina. "We are grateful to Sen. Moran for his vision in creating this program and for his steadfast support, which has given our students access to the advanced equipment and simulation technology that made this selection possible."

Items to note:

In his role as the lead Republican of the subcommittee that funds NOAA, Sen. Moran has consistently secured federal investments for NOAA aviation training, including $5.5 million for K-State Salina to purchase advanced aviation training equipment and a custom full-motion flight simulator. These investments were critical in helping position K-State Salina to be selected as one of NOAA's first three Cooperative Aviation Centers and will continue to support the university's training partnership with NOAA.

Student applications will open for the two-year program in August 2027. Selected students are expected to enter the program in fall of 2028, intern at NOAA's Aircraft Operations Center (AOC) during summer break of their junior year and graduate in the summer of 2030.

NOAA plans to select up to two students from each university in the program’s first year, with the ability to scale in the future dependent on demand. Students enrolled at or accepted by K-State Salina, Florida Institute of Technology and University of North Dakota are eligible to apply.

title: On Senate Floor, Murray Makes Clear: Democrats Are Going to Invest in Families—Not War
text:
Murray: “We are going to invest in families—not wars, not ICE, not billionaires, but working families, who are the backbone of this country.”

***WATCH: Senator Murray’s full speech***

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, spoke on the Senate floor about how the incoming Democratic Congress will reject President Trump and Republicans’ backward priorities and instead invest in working families.

Senator Murray’s remarks, as delivered, are below:

“Republicans seem to have taken the wrong lesson from the election because the American people just delivered Republicans the largest electoral loss we have seen in decades, and instead of looking inward at the unpopular Republican policies that voters rejected—like making groceries and health care more expensive, or shoveling money at billionaires, and ICE, and wars that no one wanted Trump to start in the first place—Speaker Johnson is blaming voters for making the ‘wrong choice,’ Trump is posting election conspiracies, and Republicans are plotting how to use their last few days in power to double down on the very same ideas that voters just rejected.

“It is incredibly disrespectful to the American people. But at the end of the day, even as Republicans desperately try to cling to power before the clock strikes midnight, the fact of the matter is: the voters have spoken, a Democratic majority is coming, and we are going to waste no time working to undo damage Republicans caused, lowering costs, investigating the corruption they ignored, fighting to end the wars they started, and supporting the communities they left behind.

“Congress is going to look very different, very soon. So today, I wanted to come and talk about the values that have always guided me, and just some of the priorities I am going to be focused on next year. Because my vision—and the priorities of the American people—could not be more different from what we have seen from President Trump.

“You can bet, we are going to make sure we are investing in workers and families, while continuing to reject Trump’s war budget.

“Trump and Republicans have been pushing to leave families in the dust while doubling down on Trump and Hegseth’s wish list.

“We’re going to fight to lower costs and stop corruption, instead of blowing money on foreign wars that we should never have gotten into in the first place, and which Trump has no plan for getting out of.

“There is no way we are going to go along with Trump’s hack-and-slash agenda that would take a chainsaw to things like lifesaving medical research, or housing, or public schools, and so much more.

“We are going to invest in families—not wars, not ICE, not billionaires, but working families, who are the backbone of this country.

“I didn’t run for Congress to shovel money at billionaires and defense contractors. I didn’t run for Congress to let Trump ignore our laws and let his cronies rake in millions through insider trading, no bid contracts, crypto scams, or tax breaks.

“I got into politics to save a preschool program. I got into politics as a mom in tennis shoes—and I am still lacing up those shoes every day so I can pound the pavement and fight to help our families get by.

“The only difference now? I’m not just a mom in tennis shoes—I will be an Appropriations Chair in tennis shoes. And I will never forget where I came from, and the people who sent me here to be their voice.

“I remember what it was like when my dad was too sick to work, and we had to rely on food stamps to get by. I remember how a federal workforce program helped my mom get a better job, and how federal grants allowed my siblings to pursue a higher education, and have fulfilling careers like firefighters, teachers, and more.

“I remember being a new mom, and really understanding how families were struggling to find child care and stressing about taking time off when a kid was sick. I think it makes a big difference for America when you let a mom who’s balanced the checkbook write the bills that fund the government—because my top priority is listening to families, not billionaires.

“To the moms who are clipping coupons and pinching every penny to put food on the table—you have a voice in Congress. I am going to fight tooth and nail to fully fund SNAP and school lunch programs to keep your family fed.

“To the dad who feels his heart drop every time he has to fill the car with gas, or who sees dollar signs every time he adjusts the heat—you have a voice in Congress. I am going to fight to lower your energy bill.

“To the student afraid that dreams like pursuing a higher education, or ever owning a home are just not in the cards—you have a voice in Congress. I will keep fighting for higher education opportunities, and big investments to address the affordable housing crisis.

“We’ve all been fighting for these things nonstop—and even now we are pushing every day. But soon, Democrats will be pushing with the power of a majority behind us, and I am going to make sure we use it to make people’s lives better.

“I want to see America invest in child care. I want to make sure we advance lifesaving medical research. I want the federal government to invest in tribes, and keep our commitments to them.

“We are going to rebuild our public health system and help local experts respond to disease outbreaks, the mental health crisis, and the firehose of disinformation coming from RFK Jr.

“Instead of spending your hard-earned taxpayer dollars fighting Trump’s wars and funding his vanity projects, I want to send those dollars back to our communities where they belong.

“Your tax dollars should be making your community stronger, your life better, your world safer. Not enriching billionaires. Not dropping bombs. But building roads, hiring teachers, opening health centers, finding cures. In short: helping people and solving problems.

“In their blind allegiance to Trump, Republicans lost sight of that. But the American people just sent them a reminder that they cannot be ignored.

“So, I hope they will now join us in fighting for workers and families—because there is a lot we can get done together when we put our families first.”

title: Senators Murray, Moran Introduce Legislation to Improve Support & VA Response Times for Veterans in Crisis
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senators Patty Murray (D-WA), senior member and former Chair of the Veterans’ Affairs Committee, and Jerry Moran (R-KS), Chair of the Veterans’ Affairs Committee, introduced legislation to improve the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veteran Crisis Line (VCL). This legislation was released in response to committee oversight and reports published by the VA Office of Inspector General and the Government Accountability Office (GAO) that showed several areas of needed improvement.

The Veterans Crisis Line Improvement Act would decrease VA’s emergency response time when veterans present an imminent risk of harm to themselves or others, require VA’s local suicide prevention coordinators to connect with veterans the same day they contact the VCL when appropriate, track the scheduling and provision of follow-up care, close after-hours safety gaps and increase transparency and oversight through evaluations of outreach methods.

“When I chaired the Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee, thousands of servicemembers were coming home from Iraq and Afghanistan, and I saw firsthand the toll their service took on their mental health,” said Senator Murray. “For a veteran struggling with PTSD or their mental health, picking up the phone to ask for help can be the hardest step there is. When they finally call the Veterans Crisis Line, we owe them more than a voice on the other end. We owe our veterans real follow-through and a direct path to care. Our legislation strengthens the Crisis Line so that every veteran who reaches out gets the support they need, not only during the call, but also long after it ends. We made a promise to take care of our servicemembers when they come home, and I will always fight to keep it.”

“Veterans who are contacting the VCL for support deserve the best available tools and resources as quickly as possible,” said Senator Moran. “This legislation would help close the gaps that are delaying care to veterans when they are reaching out for help and make certain they receive the care they need when they need it. I appreciate GAO’s investigation and will work to see this legislation pass in the Senate.”

“For warriors experiencing a mental health crisis, reaching out for help is a critical first step,” said Jose Ramos, Senior Vice President of Government & Community Relations at Wounded Warrior Project. “Wounded Warrior Project supports the Veterans Crisis Line Improvement Act because it would help strengthen efforts to connect veterans in crisis with the care and support they need. Ensuring veterans who seek help are effectively connected to services is an important part of broader efforts to prevent suicide and save lives, and we thank Chairman Jerry Moran and Senator Patty Murray for their bipartisan leadership on this important issue.”

In February 2025, GAO examined VCL’s post-contact interactions with veterans after an earlier GAO investigation found a lack of oversight and significant risks with complex callers, chat and text operations as well as critical-incident disclosures at the VCL. The second GAO report found that the VCL received over a million interactions via phone call and text in FY25. Throughout those interactions, VCL employees requested emergency dispatches 60,261 times but local authorities did not dispatch responders in 2,494 cases. The report also found that, while VA closed more than 98% of their over 195,000 referrals to suicide prevention coordinators within three days, VA did not track whether those veterans were contacted or received care after their initial contact with the crisis line.

This legislation is also supported by The American Legion.

title: Padilla, Schiff, Cassidy, Young Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Increase Access to Community-Based Mental Health Facilities
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla, Adam Schiff, (both D-Calif.), Bill Cassidy (R-La.), and Todd Young (R-Ind.) introduced the bipartisan Medicaid Inclusion and Non-Discrimination (MIND) Act, a targeted, protections-first bill to help adults in a mental health crisis more easily get care in small, community-based facilities. The bill would allow Medicaid to cover inpatient psychiatric care at certain facilities with 17 to 32 beds that must also meet strong new federal patient protection standards.

Since Medicaid’s enactment in 1965, the Institution for Mental Diseases (IMD) exclusion has barred federal Medicaid payment for care provided to adults in mental health facilities with more than 16 beds. It is the only provision in federal Medicaid law that denies payment for medically necessary care solely because of the illness being treated. A Medicaid enrollee hospitalized for cancer, heart disease, or diabetes is covered. The same enrollee hospitalized for schizophrenia in a 17-bed facility is not.

Fewer than 8% of psychiatric hospitals fall at or under the 16-bed limit, leaving the vast majority of inpatient mental health settings off limits to Medicaid patients. This bill would extend coverage only to small, community-scale facilities, preserving the strong federal preference for community-based treatment while ending the payment rule that punishes patients for their diagnosis. The MIND Act does not repeal the IMD exclusion but instead updates it to better reflect current needs in our communities.

“Americans in a mental health crisis deserve the same access to care as patients facing other serious illness,” said Senator Padilla. “Right now, an outdated payment rule keeps Medicaid from covering care at many small, community-based mental health facilities, leaving patients to wait in emergency rooms or go without treatment. Our bipartisan bill is a targeted fix with strong patient protections to help close that gap and get people the care they need closer to home.”

“Affordable access to inpatient psychiatric care is already limited, and the current IMD exclusion has caused shortages of psychiatric beds and treatment services across our communities,” said Senator Schiff. “I’m proud to partner with Senators Padilla, Young, and Cassidy to increase the IMD exclusion from 16 to 32 beds — overcoming a key barrier to increasing access to inpatient psychiatric care and easing the financial strain on California’s counties who have been left bearing the costs.”

“Communities need more tools to effectively treat severe mental illness. This legislation will empower states and community providers to give patients the care they need and deserve,” said Dr. Cassidy. “I am pleased to have worked on this legislation to make treatment of severe mental illness more accessible and affordable for the patient.”

“Many Hoosiers struggling with serious mental illness face unnecessary barriers to receiving the care they need,” said Senator Young. “Our bill would remove outdated federal restrictions that limit access to mental health treatment—particularly for our homeless population—and allow community-based facilities greater flexibility to serve patients. This commonsense reform will help expand treatment options and strengthen mental health care services in communities across Indiana.”

Covered facilities must meet requirements on patient rights, restraint and seclusion limits, utilization review, and discharge planning. Specifically, the MIND Act would ensure community-scale medical facilities guarantee:

Informed consent and patient rights: Patients (and their guardians or conservators) may refuse any treatment or experimental procedure absent a court order, and receive an individualized written treatment plan with clear discharge criteria, updated at least every six months;

Strict limits on restraint and seclusion: Never for coercion, discipline, convenience, or retaliation; no standing or as needed orders; full documentation of every order, every shift;

Independent accountability: Utilization review of every continued stay at least every 90 days, unannounced state oversight visits; and

A path back to the community: Confidential access to patient advocates and attorneys, retaliation free grievance rights, and dedicated discharge case management to return each patient safely and quickly to the community of their choice, with annual state reporting to HHS on lengths of stay, restraint and seclusion, and discharge delays.

“Counties finance and operate much of the nation’s local behavioral health and crisis infrastructure. The outdated 16-bed Medicaid Institutions for Mental Disease (IMD) cap limits our ability to deliver timely inpatient care and leaves local jails and emergency rooms to fill the gap,” said National Association of Counties Executive Director Matthew Chase. “Sen. Alex Padilla’s MIND Act is a meaningful step forward, and we strongly support its effort to expand Medicaid coverage to facilities with up to 32 beds while protecting patients and strengthening discharge transitions back into our communities.”

Padilla has championed legislation to guarantee healthcare regardless of income. In July, Padilla joined Senator Andy Kim (D-N.J.) in introducing the MediKids Act, monumental legislation guaranteeing healthcare to all children in America from birth to age 26. Padilla also reintroduced the Health Equity and Accountability Act (HEAA) of 2026, bicameral legislation that would address health disparities among racial and ethnic minorities as well as women, the LGBTQ+ community, rural populations, and socioeconomically disadvantaged communities across the United States. Last year, Padilla joined Senator Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) and over 100 lawmakers in reintroducing the Medicare for All Act, legislation that would guarantee healthcare as a fundamental human right to all people in the United States regardless of income or background.

title: Padilla Statement on Vote Against Permitting Bill
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), a member of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources and Environment and Public Works Committees, issued the following statement after voting against the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026:

“I have long supported commonsense permitting reform and this bill includes many provisions that I support and even authored, particularly to streamline the permitting of transmission infrastructure. Unfortunately, it also contains provisions that would irreparably harm California and the 109 federally recognized Tribes who call California home.

“The bill threatens Tribal sovereignty, and I am deeply concerned that it could allow the destruction of ancestral lands, sacred places, and cultural resources without adequate legal recourse for the communities that have relied on them for generations. It also asks us to rely on assurances from President Trump, who just weeks ago said he would not approve any wind projects – and lacks the enforceable safeguards to ensure renewable energy projects will be judged and approved fairly by the Trump Administration and that oil and gas drilling will not resume off the coast of California.

“While the bill facilitates significant improvements to our electrical grid and I’m proud to have contributed to the language of the bill that will bring more energy supply online to meet growing demand, I cannot sacrifice the rights of Tribal governments or California’s environment. Though I must oppose this bill in its current form, I will continue the work to responsibly cut red tape on renewable energy, transmission, and critical infrastructure projects.”

Senators Padilla and John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.) led Energy and Natural Resources Committee Democrats in drafting the transmission and grid reform section of the bill. This section will give the federal government the authority to approve more transmission lines faster, including by allowing transmission applications to be processed simultaneously with state reviews, so projects clear permitting sooner.

Padilla co-led an amendment with Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) to strike the changes in this bill to the National Historic Preservation Act, based on significant concerns from Tribal governments. California has the largest number of Tribes in the lower 48 states, with 109 distinct federally recognized Tribal governments.

Padilla also submitted five amendments in an effort to improve the legislation, including:

Amendment 6942: Ensures Tribes continue to have meaningful access to the courts through the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA).

Amendment 6943: Ensures federal immigration detention facilities cannot proceed without judicial review.

Amendment 6936 and 6944: Requires existing facilities and operations to comply with new environmental protection and public health standards.

Amendment 6945: Prohibits lease buyouts, including wind leases off of California’s coast.

Amendment 6946: Prohibits offshore oil and gas leasing off the West Coast.

title: WATCH: Padilla Highlights Historic 2026 Midterm Elections, Demands Stronger Voter Safeguards to Protect Democracy
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Two weeks after Election Day, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, delivered remarks on the Senate floor highlighting the historic results of the 2026 midterms and Senate Democrats’ successful Election Protection Task Force, while demanding accountability from President Trump for his baseless attacks on elections and outlining the reforms Congress needs to prioritize to ensure every eligible American’s access to the ballot box. He was joined on the Senate floor by Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) and Senator Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) in celebrating a free and fair election, despite President Trump’s attempts to interfere, and vowing that Democrats will always fight for Americans to have their voices heard.

In his remarks, Padilla celebrated the significant voter turnout for a midterm election, the Senate’s successful Election Observer Program, and underscored the importance of recognizing their demands to hold the Trump Administration accountable for its corruption and harmful executive actions.

“An estimated 124 million Americans voted in this year’s midterm elections, the second highest turnout rate for a midterm in more than a century,” said Senator Padilla. “For months, I predicted that voters would hold this Administration accountable. This historic turnout rate was certainly inspired by the conditions that the American people are living in. Voters sought to hold this Administration accountable for economic policies that are making life increasingly unaffordable. For the corruption, the self-dealing, and the relentless attacks on our institutions. For a reckless and unauthorized and costly war with Iran. And for a cruel mass deportation campaign that has terrorized communities and taken the lives of both immigrants and United States citizens alike.”

Padilla condemned the Trump Administration’s illegal threats to take over elections, and applauded voters for making their voices heard.

“They spread baseless lies about election integrity. They threatened to deploy federal law enforcement and troops to polling locations. They attacked mail-in voting and pressured states to turn over confidential voter rolls. They gutted the Voting Rights Act and pushed aggressive racial and partisan gerrymandering in an attempt to hold on to power,” continued Senator Padilla. “And when states like California stood up to Trump, Trump’s Justice Department filed lawsuits seeking to throw out ballots from eligible voters based on unreliable data, but Americans saw right through it, and they refused to be deterred by this Administration’s attacks. Eligible Americans registered to vote. And then they voted. They voted early. They voted by mail. They returned their ballots to drop boxes, and they made voices heard in record numbers.”

Padilla also emphasized the need to protect elections, highlighting the success of the first-ever Senate Election Observer Program as part of the Senate Democrats’ Election Protection Task Force. Padilla and Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) launched the program earlier this year to protect the 2026 midterms amid Trump’s ongoing threats to meddle in elections and undermine confidence in free and fair elections.

“We trained more than 100 Senate staff in election law and procedure, and deployed more than 60 staff members to more than a dozen states to monitor polling places, the vote counting, canvassing process,” said Senator Padilla. “Your efforts made a difference. Voter suppression executive orders were stopped. Courts rejected the Justice Department’s attempts to obtain state voter roll data 28 times. And in the states of California and Washington, courts blocked the Administration’s efforts to interfere with the counting of eligible, lawful ballots.”

Padilla called for improvements to election administration through national standards around voter registration and vote by mail, redistricting reform, eliminating dark money, and greater resources to increase access to the ballot box amid a rise in voter suppression efforts across the country. He specifically highlighted failures in election administration, including the backlog of 600,000 voter registration applications in Texas that were failed to be processed on time, closures of early-voting polling places at historically Black colleges in North Carolina, and voter purges in Mississippi.

“One election may be behind us, but the next election is less than two years away, and there’s still too many barriers keeping too many eligible Americans from being able to vote,” concluded Senator Padilla. “We need to shore up our elections by giving state and local officials the resources they need to run secure, and accessible, and efficient elections. And we need to ensure that every eligible American’s access to the ballot box by expanding automatic voter registration and vote by mail and preventing eligible voters from being wrongly purged from the voter rolls.”

In the weeks leading up to Election Day, Ranking Member Padilla fought relentlessly to protect our elections and strengthen voting rights.

Padilla, Schumer, and the Senate Democrats’ Election Protection Task Force released a report encouraging voters to cast their ballot early and outlining for the American people what to expect on Election Day, Election Night, and beyond in terms of timelines for counting and announcing election results in several states with 2026 Senate elections.

Padilla led his colleagues in demanding Attorney General Todd Blanche confirm that the Department of Justice (DOJ) will not seize ballots, voting machines, or other election materials in connection with the 2026 midterm elections.

In September, Padilla introduced the Freedom from Intimidation in Elections Act, legislation to protect voters and election workers from intimidation and threats of violence at polling places.

Padilla also led the congressional response to the bombshell whistleblower report that DHS agents violated state laws as part of the “Unlawful Voter Initiative” and called for an immediate investigation into the agency’s misconduct. He also urged California’s Attorney General to investigate the effects these actions could have on Californians.

In August, he led 27 of his Senate colleagues in demanding the Trump Administration stop its illegal voter roll purges before Election Day.

Video of Padilla’s remarks is available here.

Full transcript is available below:

Mr. President, two weeks ago, the American people made history. An estimated 124 million Americans voted in this year’s midterm elections, the second highest turnout rate for a midterm in more than a century. Now, a new generation of leaders, who better reflect the diversity and promise of our nation, is headed to Washington, D.C., into State Capitols across the country.

California, my home state, elected its first Latino governor. The state of Georgia elected the first Black woman as governor, the state of Texas will have its first Latina governor. The state of New Mexico will have its first Native American woman governor, and here in this chamber, we are about to welcome the first Muslim United States senator, the first Black senator from the state of Mississippi since 1881, and the first Native American woman to serve in the United States Senate. All historic victories made possible by the American people who showed up and exercised their right to vote.

Now, for months, I predicted that voters would hold this Administration accountable. This historic turnout rate was certainly inspired by the conditions that the American people are living in. Voters sought to hold this Administration accountable for economic policies that are making life increasingly unaffordable. For the corruption, the self-dealing, and the relentless attacks on our institutions. For a reckless and unauthorized and costly war with Iran. And for a cruel mass deportation campaign that has terrorized communities and taken the lives of both immigrants and United States citizens alike. And two weeks ago, it’s exactly what voters did, and the message they sent could not be any louder and could not be any clearer.

The people want an end to the chaos, an end to the corruption, and an end to the cruelty. They want affordability. They want accountability. And above all, they want a government that works for them, not against them. Now I know Democrats have heard this message loud and clear, and we intend to deliver. But before looking too far ahead, before we start debating about what the next Congress will prioritize and take action on, it’s important that we acknowledge and reflect on what it took for Americans to make their voices heard this year, because if there’s a fundamental lesson to take from these midterm elections, it’s that our democracy is not self-executing. It depends on Americans showing up to defend it, on elections officials ensuring that every eligible vote is counted, and on people wanting to stand up when the right to vote is threatened.

So let’s be clear: these midterms were under threat from the very beginning of this Trump Administration. Donald Trump and his MAGA allies spent nearly two years using the power of the presidency to undermine confidence in our elections and seeking to make it harder for the American people to vote. They spread baseless lies about election integrity. They threatened to deploy federal law enforcement and troops to polling locations. They attacked mail-in voting and pressured states to turn over confidential voter rolls. They gutted the Voting Rights Act and pushed aggressive racial and partisan gerrymandering in an attempt to hold on to power. And when states like California stood up to Trump, Trump’s Justice Department filed lawsuits seeking to throw out ballots from eligible voters based on unreliable data, but Americans saw right through it, and they refused to be deterred by this Administration’s attacks. Eligible Americans registered to vote. And then they voted. They voted early. They voted by mail. They returned their ballots to drop boxes, and they made voices heard in record numbers. As one of President Trump’s own advisers told CNN, the election was, quote, “essentially too big to rig.”

Think about that. Too many Americans showed up. Too many people made their voices heard. The margins of victory was so big – any attempt to slow down the count, throw out ballots, try to, you know, twist the rules to try to eke out some victories when they were losing, wasn’t going to happen. And the record number of people who turned out weren’t alone. An unprecedented coalition of civil society organizations, voting rights groups, and state and local elections officials pushed back on the Administration’s attempts to interfere. And Democrats on the Rules Committee, together with Leader Schumer’s Election Protection Task Force – and I want to give Leader Schumer the credit he deserves for convening this task force and investing in it.

We also worked together to help create the Senate’s first Election Observer program. We trained more than 100 Senate staff in election law and procedure, and deployed more than 60 staff members to more than a dozen states to monitor polling places, the vote counting, canvassing process. It was important to oversee to ensure accountability. And for the staff that served, and for the staff of the Rules Committee who developed and successfully implemented this program: thank you, thank you, thank you for your service, and thank you to all the members of the broad coalition that came together to defend our democracy and our access to the ballot. Your efforts made a difference. Voter suppression executive orders were stopped. Courts rejected the Justice Department’s attempts to obtain state voter roll data 28 times. And in the states of California and Washington, courts blocked the Administration’s efforts to interfere with the counting of eligible, lawful ballots.

Now, these victories sound like common sense, but these victories matter. They show what is possible when people stand together to defend our democracy. But the fight is far from over. One election may be behind us, but the next election is less than two years away, and there’s still too many barriers keeping too many eligible Americans from being able to vote, like the backlog of 600,000 voter registration applications that the state of Texas failed to process on a timely basis. The voters in Tarrant County, Texas, for example, who waited in line for hours after officials slashed a third of the polling places in that county. That’s unacceptable. The young voters in North Carolina who marched for miles along highways to cast ballots because early voting locations at historically Black colleges were closed. Thousands of voters were purged in Mississippi based on unreliable credit agency address data, leading to a surge in affidavits, otherwise known as provisional ballots, two thirds of which were rejected, just in Hinds County alone.

We need to shore up our elections by giving state and local officials the resources they need to run secure, and accessible, and efficient elections. And we need to ensure that every eligible American’s access to the ballot box by expanding automatic voter registration and vote by mail, and preventing eligible voters from being wrongly purged from the voter rolls. There’s plenty of states across the country, not just California, where I believe we have the gold standard, that have implemented these policies, these new laws, the best practices, if you will, to maintain safe and secure elections, but making sure they are free and fair by modernizing elections and giving voters more opportunity to be able to participate in our democracy. It’s so fundamental. We also need fair redistricting, and we need to get big money out of politics and permanently put our elections back in the hands of the people by overturning the Citizens United decision. That is the unfinished work of this democracy that still remains ahead of us. And, Mr. President, if I have the privilege of serving as chair of the Rules Committee in the next Congress, that’s the kind of work that I look forward to taking on.

Mr. President, the American people delivered resounding results and historic firsts of this year’s election because they were sending a message. With the sanctity of our elections threatened, and so much on the line for working families, the American people showed up in record numbers to demand change. They demanded accountability from an Administration that tried to undermine the right to vote, tried to keep the American people from having their voices heard. The same Administration that has put its own interest ahead of theirs.

The people demanded an end to the chaos and the corruption that have gripped our country these last two years, and they demanded a government make life more affordable and gives working families a fair shot at a better future. So, with the election now behind us, we can say the American people have done their part, and now it’s time for us to do ours. Thank you, Mr. President. I yield the floor.

###

title: ON THE JOB FOR MICHIGAN: Michigan Veteran Highlights Peters’ Work to Help Veterans Access Apprenticeships and Job Training Opportunities
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – In a new “On the Job” video from U.S. Senator Gary Peters’ (MI) office, Gulf War veteran Rick Donovan highlights Peters’ efforts to author and pass the Support for Veterans in Effective Apprenticeships Act into law. Peters’ bipartisan legislation allows more veterans to use their GI bill benefits toward securing a registered apprenticeship and job training opportunities. Before this bill was enacted, there were over 1,000 active registered Department of Labor (DOL) apprenticeships in Michigan, but only a couple hundred programs had been approved by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). Peters partnered with Rick Donovan, a Michigan veteran in Oakland County and State Legislative Officer for the Polish Legion of American Veterans Department of Michigan, to introduce the legislation after Donovan reached out to Peters to discuss the lack of apprenticeships that qualify under GI bill benefits. This video is part of the On the Job for Michigan series, which highlights Peters’ leadership and advocacy on behalf of Michigan constituents and communities.

“The bottom line is we had a disconnect. We had DOL apprenticeships that, yes, could be GI bill approved, but whoever was starting the apprenticeship literally had to reach out to the VA as well to start that process,” said Rick Donovan, Gulf War Veteran and former Local Employment Representative for the State of Michigan. “When I reached out to Senator Peters’ office, we found out that we can do a bill where we can ensure that the GI bill approval process was a part of the DOL process.”

“These apprenticeship programs allow for veterans to learn new skills and find good-paying jobs, which makes a real difference in their lives and in their families’ lives,” said Peters. “We need to listen to and partner with veterans like Rick who are tirelessly advocating to open doors to fellow veterans, Michiganders, and Americans so they can achieve economic success in the 21st century.”

Watch the “On The Job” video here.

During his service in the U.S. Navy Reserve, Peters earned a Seabee Combat Warfare Specialist designation and rose to the rank of Lieutenant Commander. After the September 11th terrorist attacks on our country, Peters volunteered again for drilling status and served overseas as part of his Reserve duty. He later earned a diploma from the College of Naval Command and Staff, U.S. Naval War College.

Peters has been a strong advocate in the Senate for Michigan’s servicemembers and their families. In 2021, Peters was inducted into the Michigan Military and Veterans Hall of Honor for his efforts to support our nation’s veterans and military. In 2017, Peters was recognized as Legislator of the Year by the Vietnam Veterans of America for authoring the bipartisan Fairness for Veterans Act, which was signed into law as part of the national defense bill. The legislation requires veteran discharge review boards to give liberal consideration to petitions for honorable discharge status if the servicemember has been diagnosed with PTSD, TBI, or other related conditions connected to their military service. In 2022, Peters helped enact the Sergeant First Class Heath Robinson Honoring our Promise to Address Comprehensive Toxics (PACT) Act – which delivered VA health care and benefits to all generations of toxic-exposed veterans and their survivors for the first time in our nation’s history.

title: ‘Get the Swamp Out of the Way’: Sen. Rick Scott Leads Bipartisan Fight to Ban Lobbying by Former Members of Congress
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, U.S. Senator Rick Scott spoke on the Senate floor to request the immediate passage of his bipartisan bill, the Banning Lobbying and Safeguarding Trust (BLAST) Act, which is co-sponsored by Senator Elizabeth Warren from Massachusetts. The passage of this bill, which establishes a lifelong lobbying ban for former members of Congress, was blocked by Senator Thom Tillis from North Carolina.

Senator Rick Scott said, “Florida families elected me to make Washington work for them by fighting to boost job creation, root out corruption and cut red tape, and lower the cost of living. When members of Congress go from elected office to lobbying, our jobs stop looking like public service and feel more like self-service. That’s why I am proud to lead the bipartisan BLAST Act to ban former members of Congress from lobbying after they leave office. While I am incredibly disappointed that my colleague blocked the passage of my bill, I won’t stop fighting to pass commonsense legislation that restores the American people’s trust in Washington.”

Watch Senator Scott’s remarks by clicking HEREor on the image above

BACKGROUND:

The BLAST Act is a bipartisan bill led by Senators Rick Scott and Elizabeth Warren and was introduced in May 2026.

The bill prohibits two types of activity — lobbyist registration and conduct.

First, it bars former members and elected officers from working as registered lobbyists, as defined by the Lobbying Disclosure Act.

Second, it prohibits them from making lobbying contacts, regardless of their registration status.

This includes making communications or appearances before members of Congress, congressional staff, or legislative offices with the intent to influence official action on behalf of private parties.

Finally, the bill would also address “shadow lobbying” by expanding existing lobbying restrictions to cover former lawmakers who are compensated for lobbying activities, even if they do not formally register as lobbyists or make direct lobbying contacts themselves.

Violation of this law could result in up to five years in prison as well as civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation.

This legislation is part of Senator Rick Scott’s longstanding fight to make Washington work for American families, which has also included ending taxpayer-funded Congressional Pensions, imposing term limits on Congress, and No Budget, No Pay legislation to ensure that politicians do not receive government paychecks during government shutdowns.

title: Risch Celebrates Passage of Bipartisan Permitting Reform
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Jim Risch (R-Idaho) today celebrated Senate passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA). BAAJA is comprehensive permitting reform legislation that will streamline bureaucratic processes, expedite critical infrastructure projects, increase domestic energy production, and lower costs.

“Unnecessary and outdated regulations have created significant barriers to modernizing Idaho’s infrastructure, resulting in fewer jobs and higher prices for Idahoans,” said Risch. “I’m proud to support this much-needed permitting reform package to increase our supply of affordable and reliable energy, promote economic growth, and advance the responsible use of Idaho’s important resources.”

BAAJA would establish more predictable permitting timelines, protect ratepayers, support our essential infrastructure, and provide certainty for U.S. nuclear, geothermal, and critical minerals projects.

The Senate-passed permitting reform bill includes Senator Risch’s:

Mining Regulatory Clarity Act to allow critical mineral production to continue in the West; and

Committing Leases for Energy Access Now (CLEAN) Act to require annual geothermal lease sales and set timelines for processing geothermal permit applications.

The bill now awaits action in the House of Representatives.

title: Rosen, Cruz’s Bipartisan Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act Passes Senate
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, U.S. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and Ted Cruz (R-TX) applauded the Senate passage of their Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act. This bipartisan bill – the first major update to federal boxing laws in over a quarter century – would help revitalize American boxing by allowing league-style Unified Boxing Organizations (UBOs) to compete alongside traditional promoters. It would also strengthen fighter protections and improve health and safety standards, while creating new opportunities for organizations and giving boxers more choices and fans better matchups. The bill was endorsed by Nico Ali Walsh, professional boxer and grandson of Muhammad Ali.

“Las Vegas is the center of the boxing universe, and when boxing thrives, more visitors come to Nevada and help boost our economy,” said Senator Rosen. “I’ve proudly worked on this bill with Chairman Cruz and numerous stakeholders – including Muhammad Ali’s grandson Nico Ali Walsh – in order to revitalize this great sport and make important reforms to protect boxers. I’m thrilled to see our bipartisan legislation pass the Senate today, and I’m hopeful that the House will quickly pass it as well.”

“We’re going to make boxing great again with the bipartisan Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act,” said Senator Cruz. “The bill expands opportunities for fighters, strengthens safety protections, and brings back the marquee matchups fans love. I hope the House quickly sends this bill to the President’s desk and delivers a knockout win for fighters and fans.”

Senator Rosen has been a champion for American sports and has been an advocate for increased sports tourism in Nevada. In September, she joined Senate colleagues in passing the bipartisan Protect College Sports Act to establish clear requirements for name, image, and likeness (NIL) agreements for college student-athletes and protect the integrity of college sports. Senator Rosen also introduced the American Decade of Sports Act, which would promote American sports diplomacy and leverage large sporting events hosted in the U.S. to boost tourism. Additionally, Senator Rosen and UNLV hosted a discussion on sports tourism with representatives from the UFC, the Las Vegas Raiders, the Las Vegas Athletics, and organizers of the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix.

title: Rosen Statement After Voting Again to End Iran War
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) released the following statement after voting once again to end the war with Iran:

“Earlier this month, the American people resoundingly rejected Donald Trump’s unconstitutional war with Iran that has made everything more expensive,” said Senator Rosen. “Hardworking families are tired of having to pay for Trump’s reckless actions, and it’s time that we put a stop to this conflict. That is why I voted to pass this War Powers Resolution, and why I will continue pushing to end this war in Iran.”

Senator Rosen has been a vocal opponent of Trump’s war in Iran. She has voted for every previous War Powers Resolution to remove U.S. troops from hostilities with Iran since the beginning of the war earlier this year. In September, she joined colleagues in demanding a hearing on the administration’s failures to support servicemembers on indefinite deployments. In August, Senator Rosen helped introduce a bill that would restore full and accurate casualty records of fallen and wounded servicemembers during Operation Epic Fury. Senator Rosen also joined her Senate colleagues in demanding answers from the Department of Defense over the tragic U.S. bombing of an Iranian elementary school in February.

title: NEWS: After One Law Firm Reveals Being Coerced into Providing $11.8 Million in Free Legal Work to Trump Administration, Sen. Schiff, Ranking Members Raskin and Blumenthal Slam Nine Other Law Firms For Stonewalling Congressional Inquiry
text:
Lawmakers Want to Know How the Trump Administration Extorted and Used Other Law Firms and Whether They Took on Work Advising on Trump’s Vanity Projects Like Kennedy Center Renaming, Triumphal Arch

Washington, D.C. — Sen. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Md.-08), Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, and Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations Ranking Member Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) demanded records from nine law firms after their investigation uncovered that the law firm Kirkland & Ellis LLP (Kirkland) provided at least $11.8 million in free legal services to federal agencies and federal entities after being threatened with an Equal Employment Opportunity Commission investigation and retributive Executive Orders that the Trump Administration had leveled against other firms. The probe also uncovered that Kirkland balked at helping the Trump Administration rename the Kennedy Center and build the President’s triumphal arch, raising questions about whether other firms that struck deals with the Administration took on those projects.

The lawmakers sent follow-up letters to Latham & Watkins LLP (Latham); Simpson Thacher & Bartlett LLP (Simpson Thacher); Willkie Farr & Gallagher LLP (Willkie); Sullivan & Cromwell LLP (S&C); Hogan Lovells Cadwalader LLP (Cadwalader); Allen Overy Shearman Sterling US LLP (A&O Shearman); Milbank LLP (Milbank); Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP (Paul, Weiss); and Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP (Skadden Arps).

“We have recently received substantial and profoundly troubling information that this corrupt bargain went much further than originally understood. Kirkland & Ellis LLP provided at least $11.8 million in free legal services to numerous federal agencies and entities engaged in questionable activities, including approximately $4 million to the U.S. Department of Commerce, $2.2 million to the U.S. Department of Defense, $1.6 million to the U.S. Postal Service, $2 million to the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation, and $1.8 million to represent an investment entity negotiated between the Trump Administration and Japan to create a $550 billion slush fund. The Trump Administration also unsuccessfully tried to involve Kirkland & Ellis in work supporting the President’s political vanity projects, such as the renaming of the Kennedy Center or supporting the illegal construction of his triumphal arch in Washington, D.C.— raising serious questions of whether other firms acceded to these demands,” the lawmakers wrote.

The lawmakers received this information from Kirkland just two days after the November midterm elections. Since April 2025, the lawmakers have repeatedly demanded answers about the ten firms’ dubious multimillion-dollar deals with President Trump. However, to date, the vast majority of the firms still have yet to provide any substantive answers or turn over a single responsive document.

The lawmakers renewed their demands for all outstanding records about the Executive Order and directed the firms to prioritize records of requests for free or discounted legal services from the White House, any executive branch agency, or any public or private associate of the President. They are seeking the nature of each request, who made it, what services each firm agreed to provide, and the hours and billable value of any work performed.

Today’s letters are the latest salvo in an investigation Ranking Members Raskin and Blumenthal launched in April 2025 into Trump’s unprecedented official coercion of major law firms and the deals firms struck to avoid retaliation. Joined by Sen. Schiff, they subsequently scrutinized firms’ free legal work for the Commerce Department, sought records of Epshteyn’s role in Kirkland’s deal and pressed Skadden over potential conflicts involving its work for Intel and the Commerce Department. In October, the lawmakers rejected Kirkland’s claims of privilege and renewed their demands for records on its $125 million deal after the firm failed to produce a single responsive document and refused to meet with congressional staff.

The lawmakers warned that they will use every tool at their disposal to pursue the investigation in this Congress and the next. As the initial phases of this investigation make clear, the President of the United States abused the power of the federal government to extract nearly $1 billion in free legal services from some of the nation’s largest law firms. Worse, the agreements announced on Truth Social effectively made the President the sole judge of whether those firms were complying with their obligations—putting these firms at the political mercy of the Administration and the personal mercy of the President, driving major firms away from both existing and potential clients and causes that could put them at odds with the mercurial shakedown artist in the White House. For people and communities who rely on pro bono lawyers to defend their rights, that could mean facing the full power and intensifying fury of the federal government alone.

title: NEWS: Sen. Schiff Introduces Legislation to Enhance Transparency Behind Campaign Ads Funded by SuperPACs
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) introduced the Sunlight on SuperPACs Act of 2026, legislation to require federal election campaign ads paid for by Super PACs to disclose the name and dollar amount contributed to that SuperPAC by its top three major donors of $5,000 or more. By providing voters with more information on the funders of election ads, they will be able to make more informed decisions about the content of those ads.

“As each election cycle in recent history has shown us, Super PAC spending on campaign advertisements can have enormous influence, so it’s crucial that Americans know when special interests or corporations are funding these ads. Anonymous and unrestricted spending by Super PACs is dangerous and weakens our democracy, and it’s time for Congress to rein in the lack of transparency that exists in our campaign finance system. This bill is a step in the right direction so that voters can make more informed decisions at the polls,” said Senator Schiff.

Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (D-Ohio-09) and Congressman Kevin Mullin (D-Calif.-15) introduced this legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives.

In the Senate, this bill is cosponsored by Senators Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) and Mazie Hirono (D- Hawaii.).

The legislation is endorsed by Citizens for Responsible Ethics in Washington (CREW), Democracy Defenders Action (DDA), End Citizens United (ECU), Issue One, and Public Citizen.

“At a time when so many Super PACs use fake names and paperwork games to disguise who’s paying for their ads, voters need real information so they can make informed decisions. The Sunlight on SuperPACs Act will give voters the tools they need to evaluate the credibility of campaign ads by seeing who’s really behind them. We applaud Senator Schiff for championing this innovative way to cut through campaign funding schemes and empower voters,” said Jon Golinger, Democracy Advocate, Public Citizen.

“Voters have a right to know who’s trying to sway their vote, but too often, our political system lets special interests hide behind misleadingly named organizations. The Sunlight on SuperPACs Act gives voters the information they need to understand who funds the political ads they see, building on measures that have passed with cross-partisan support in places such as Alaska, Arizona, and California. This bill would increase trust and accountability in our elections, and lawmakers on both sides of the aisle should support it,” said Issue One Founder and CEO Nick Penniman.

“Current loopholes in super PAC disclosure laws have led to anonymous donors making record breaking donations with little to no transparency provided to voters on the source of the funding. Loopholes like this have allowed dark money to influence US elections and allow elected officials to escape accountability for who they are accepting money from. Meaningful campaign finance reform is long overdue. CREW is proud to endorse theSunlight on Super PACs Act sponsored by Senator Adam Schiff and Representatives Marcy Kaptur and Kevin Mullin, and we urge Congress to pass this important legislation,” said Debra Perlin, Vice President for Policy at CREW.

“All Americans deserve to know who is trying to influence their voices and their votes. However, when billionaires and corporate special interests spend millions of dollars in secret political money, voters are too often left in the dark. We commend Senator Schiff for introducing the Sunlight on SuperPACs Act to ensure Americans get the transparency they deserve, and we urge Congress to quickly consider this bill,” said Virginia Canter, Ethics and Anticorruption Chief Counsel and Director with Democracy Defenders Action.

In today’s electoral system, Super PACs can spend an unlimited amount of money to support or oppose political candidates, and they are not limited in how much money they can accept from donors. While they cannot give money directly to candidates or their campaigns, these organizations can have tremendous amounts of influence on elections through spending money on advertising and organizing.

The Sunlight on SuperPACs will give voters information about the source of campaign ad funding in real-time, following the example of successful state and local disclosure initiatives, including an initiative enacted by voters in California.

title: NEWS: Sen. Schiff Unveils Legislation to Unlock New Opportunities for Women-Owned Small Businesses
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) introduced The Women Economic Fairness and Small Business Contracting Act, legislation to increase opportunities for women-owned small businesses by tripling the federal contracting goal and offering different pathways for women entrepreneurs to grow their business.

“Small businesses are vital to our communities and economy, and women-owned small businesses, in particular, make up over 40% of all U.S. businesses. They would grow even faster if they had good and fair opportunities to compete for federal contracts. My legislation will open more doors for women entrepreneurs and level the playing field,” said Senator Schiff.

The Women Economic Fairness and Small Business Contracting Act will:

Increase the Women Owned Small Business (WOSB) Federal Prime subcontracting goal from 5 percent to 15 percent;

Raise the government-wide small business contracting set-aside goal from 23 percent to 33 percent; and

Require the Small Business Administrations (SBA) to meet or exceed its annual prime contracting goals.

U.S. Senator Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.) is a cosponsor.

The bill is endorsed by the American Small Business League.

“Working with Senator Schiff to raise the federal contracting goal for women-owned small businesses from 5% to 15% is an important step toward opening doors to the nation’s largest marketplace and giving women entrepreneurs the opportunities they deserve,” said Lloyd Chapman, President of the American Small Business League. “I applaud Senator Schiff for standing up for women-owned businesses and for America’s small businesses. Every small business owner in this country should know that Senator Schiff is fighting for them and working to ensure they have a meaningful opportunity to compete, grow and succeed.”

title: NEWS: Senate Unanimously Passes Sens. Schiff, Curtis’ Legislation to Explicitly Ban Death and War Prediction Contracts
text:
The DEATH BETS Act is the first bill regulating prediction markets to pass in the Senate in the 119th Congress

Washington, D.C. — Today, the U.S. Senate unanimously passed U.S. Senator Adam Schiff’s (D-Calif.) and John Curtis’ (R-Utah), DEATH BETS Act, legislation to explicitly prohibit any Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)-registered entity from listing any contract that references terrorism, assassination, war, United States Armed Forces military operations, or an individual’s death.

Schiff, a member of the Senate Agriculture Committee, first introduced this bill in March 2026. Representative Mike Levin (D-Calif-49) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives.

Senator Schiff delivered remarks on the Senate floor moments before the bill passed and was joined by Senator Curtis.

Watch his full speech HERE.

“Betting on war and death jeopardizes our national security by creating a perverse environment in which violence is incentivized and insiders are allowed to profit off privileged or classified information. There is no justification for gambling on lives, or public benefit to be derived by such a market. With my bill, Congress is making it clear today that these death bets should be unlawful,” said Senator Schiff.

“No one should be able to wager on terrorism, war, or the death of another human being,” said Senator Curtis. “There is a fundamental difference between legitimate financial markets and gambling on human suffering. The DEATH BETS Act draws a clear moral line by prohibiting these types of wagers on federally regulated exchanges.”

Under the Commodity Exchange Act, the CFTC currently has the authority to prohibit war, terrorism, and assassination contracts from being listed if they are determined by the Commission to be contrary to the public interest. Whether or not these contracts are in the public interest is at the discretion of the CFTC. At a time when CFTC Chair Selig has indicated that he will rewrite the rules on prediction markets, the CFTC can no longer be granted this discretion. This bill will unequivocally ban these contracts.

According to public reporting, there have been numerous cases this year in which individuals were suspected to have traded on prediction markets to profit from inside information related to war and U.S. Armed Services actions. Lawmakers have previously raised the alarm to the CFTC on these “death contracts” being offered on offshore exchanges, such as on whether or not Artemis II would explode, Maduro would be removed from power, or the Ukrainian town of Myrnohad would be captured by Russian forces.

The DEATH BETS Act specifically would:

Codify a prohibition on war, assassination, and terrorism contracts.

Explicitly prohibit contracts that involve an individual’s death, which is not currently referenced in the Commodity Exchange Act.

The full text of the bill is available here.

Read the full transcript of his remarks as delivered below:

Senator Adam Schiff: Mr. President, I’m here today to urge the Senate to pass legislation that I’m proud to lead along with Senator John Curtis, the DEATH BETS Act.

Over the last two years, the rapid growth prediction markets has allowed users to gamble on just about anything. Just this year, we’ve seen these markets offer wagers on whether the Artemis II mission and its four astronauts would explode. It created a market on whether Nicolas Maduro would be removed from power in Venezuela. It even offered a potential profit for those who could correctly predict whether a Ukrainian town of Myrnohrad would be captured by Russia.

In many cases, these contracts offered were offered in contravention of state and Tribal law. They create rampant opportunities for insider trading, and perhaps worst of all, they are offered with no regard for national security and, in far too many cases, even basic morality.

These markets are operating in a wild west, desperately in need of regulation and guardrails.

Today, we have the opportunity to put into place a very simple rule: the first building block to create one of those guardrails. Our bill prohibits prediction markets from offering contracts on war, military operations, and death,

Betting and profiting off of death, both in tragedy and in war, is immoral and ought to be unlawful. Indeed, many of us believe it already is.

But the regulators at CFTC, or in this case, regulator, is not only hands off. He’s acting as the legal infantry for the industry, attempting to preempt state laws and challenging them whenever his agency is unsuccessful.

As a result, the CFTC has created a system with the most perverse incentives that would reward betting on a mass casualty event. A market that one could easily imagine would actually encourage lethal events and jeopardize our national security for the right amount of money. It’s a whole new version of the very idea of a contract kill.

Take the real-life example we’ve seen on these platforms: people placing bets on wildfires, wagering on how devastating they could be; people placing bets on every twist and turn in the war with Iran, sometimes with inside information, motivated by the same underlying principle of financial markets and gaming conventions, the possibility of profit.

But these are not regulated financial markets; they’re not seen by the administration as sports betting or gambling, even though such illegal practices are widespread and the subject of yet another bill that Senator Curtis and I are leading.

There’s no justification for gambling on lives or public benefit to be derived by such a market. It’s dangerous and it’s wrong.

In the absence of real leadership and enforcement at the CFTC, it’s time for Congress to step in and fix this problem.

With our bill, Congress is making clear that these bets should be illegal once and for all.

Simply put, the legislation we are enacting today is a targeted fix of a single pressing problem. The sole purpose of theDEATH BETS Act is to make clear that betting on war, death, military operations, and similar circumstances is unlawful.

But we also want to make clear that the legislation has no effect whatsoever on pending litigation regarding whether sports contracts offered by prediction markets qualify as swaps or other derivatives under federal law, or on whether federal derivatives laws preempt state gaming and consumer protection laws regarding such sports contracts.

We’ve included a rule of construction in the DEATH BETS Act designed to make this crystal clear. Per that rule, no part of this bill will affect the permissibility of any sports contracts or similar agreements. If sports contracts are impermissible under federal or state law today, as I, and many others believe they are, it will remain impermissible after this legislation is enacted.

We are aware that there is active litigation across the country on swaps and preemption issues.

Nothing in the DEATH BETS Act should have any effect on those lawsuits, and it would be improper to draw any inference from this bill that other federal statutes or regulations should be interpreted in a particular way, or that Congress has expressed any intent on how the issues in litigation should be decided.

Nor should the DEATH BETS Act be construed as providing the CFTC with authority to authorize or regulate sports contracts on prediction markets.

The CFTC has no expertise with respect to gaming.

The states and Tribes have long served as the nation’s gaming regulators, and nothing Congress is doing today displaces that traditional state and Tribal authority. Indeed, the CFTC’s recent actions to attempt to assist prediction markets in litigation confirm that the CFTC has strayed far outside its authority.

Sports contracts are sports bets in disguise. The CFTC’s job is to promote fair competition and market efficiency, not to serve as a nationwide sports betting regulator.

This bill is a commonsense step, and merely the first to rein in a runaway prediction market regulation that violates state law and Tribal sovereignty, common sense, and our values.

I want to again thank my colleague Senator Curtis for his advocacy and leadership, not just on this bill but on a broader issue, and I would be proud to yield to Senator Curtis.
