title: READ: “We Won’t Bail Them Out” – Sen. Schiff Says American Taxpayers Must Not Act as Backstop for AI Industry in New Wall Street Journal Op-Ed
text:
Schiff: “Policymakers should make clear that Congress and American taxpayers won’t act as its fail-safe should this industry falter under its own immense weight.”

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) penned an op-ed in the Wall Street Journal highlighting concerns that if an AI industry bubble bursts it has the potential to destabilize the economy. The Senator says that Congress must make clear that American taxpayers will not act as a fail-safe to bail out the industry or its investors.

Schiff notes: “This may be the biggest economic gamble in American history, and policymakers should make clear that Congress and American taxpayers won’t act as its fail-safe should this industry falter under its own immense weight… If these enormous bets fail, Big Tech and Wall Street billionaires will no doubt turn to Washington for emergency rescue, a path unfortunately well-trodden by corporate giants before them. But the risk should be borne by these companies and their investors, not working families.”

In the op-ed, Schiff points to AI’s explosive buildout being financed by opaque debt structures and special-purpose vehicles, as companies are borrowing capital from an increasingly consolidated group of investors and lenders while free cash flow is declining.

Schiff says: “The billionaire investors may be taking this gamble with the assumption that as in 2008, they will be bailed out for failed investments and corporate risk-taking. Congressional majorities should be clear: We won’t bail them out.”

Read the full op-ed below:

Wall Street Journal Op-Ed: No AI Company Is Too Big to Fail

By Adam B. Schiff

Our nation is in the midst of what will be one of the largest economic transformations in human history, driven by rapid advances in artificial intelligence and the corporations fueling their growth.

This technology has boundless potential to enhance our lives and expand our individual and collective capacity. But as the turmoil around Nvidia reminds us, this swift and massive investment also carries significant risk that an industry downturn or a bubble could destabilize the American economy. In the first six days of the scandal involving Nvidia and its former CEO, the sector lost $500 billion in value.

Given the risks to our economy and investors, Congress must make sure that industry understands this: No company is too big to fail, and in the event of a financial collapse of the tech sector, there will be no taxpayer-funded bailout.

The AI industry, after less than five years of market power, is already estimated to represent 3.6% of our nation’s economy. But much of its explosive build-out is financed by an opaque debt structure and expectations of increasing profitability. This may be the biggest economic gamble in American history, and policymakers should make clear that Congress and American taxpayers won’t act as its fail-safe should this industry falter under its own immense weight.

This year alone, AI will see nearly $1 trillion invested in its continued expansion. If these enormous bets fail, Big Tech and Wall Street billionaires will no doubt turn to Washington for emergency rescue, a path unfortunately well-trodden by corporate giants before them. But the risk should be borne by these companies and their investors, not working families.

We have seen this movie before. In the early 2000s, there were warning signs that the housing market had taken on immense systemic risk, which had the potential to drag down our entire economy. The American people and Congress were told by top bank and mortgage lending executives, as well as the Treasury secretary and Federal Reserve chairman, that the subprime mortgage market was contained from the rest of the financial system and that the economy was healthy.

That was catastrophically wrong. In 2008 those same officials begged Congress to forgive their error and pass an industry-wide bailout, while our nation was on the brink of a financial calamity.

The result, reluctantly approved by Democrats and Republicans in Congress amid the crisis, gave executives who gambled with America’s economy billions of dollars to forgive their gambling debt while the American people were plunged into the worst economic recession since the Great Depression. No executives were charged with criminal wrongdoing.

The average American family saw its wealth decline by a third from 2007 to 2010, with 1 in 4 households losing 75 cents of every dollar in its savings, home equity and net worth. Even as the economy began to stabilize, middle-class wealth remained stagnant and wages flat while the wealthiest Americans quickly made up what they had lost in the worst years.

This must not happen again. As venture-capital firms and trillion-dollar companies are increasingly taking on more debt to build out AI without the financial certainty that it will pay off—and with the added danger that AI companies will be held liable for the damage their agents do in the wild—they should do so understanding that this risk won’t be borne by others.

Now is the time to right-size the risk and debt, before a crisis. This is true not only of the big banks and investment houses, but also of the regional banks and pension funds. The collapse of Silicon Valley Bank demonstrated the fragility of the system when the financial liquidity of even midsize firms is threatened. Regulators should take precautions now, not after the fact.

Big Tech hyperscaling companies used to be able to finance their data-center infrastructure build-outs from the profits of their existing businesses. But as they race to invest massive sums they don’t have on hand to project confidence in their businesses, these companies are borrowing capital from an increasingly consolidated group of investors and lenders while their free cash flow is declining.

Smaller infrastructure companies are even more leveraged, borrowing billions against GPUs, data centers and anticipated future lease payments. Banks, private credit funds, insurers and pension funds are also financing this expansion, often through complicated corporate structures and special-purpose vehicles that obscure who ultimately holds the risk.

The billionaire investors may be taking this gamble with the assumption that as in 2008, they will be bailed out for failed investments and corporate risk-taking. Congressional majorities should be clear: We won’t bail them out.

On Election Day the American people rejected the corruption and special treatment that exists in our current politics across party lines, under which billionaires and industry giants get sweetheart deals at the expense of everyone else. We should listen to the message voters sent us.

Mr. Schiff, a Democrat, is a U.S. senator from California.

###

title: STATEMENT: Sen. Schiff Statement After Senate Vote to Advance Permitting Reform Legislation
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), member of the Senate Committee on Environment and Public Works and Ranking Member of the Fisheries, Water, and Wildlife Subcommittee, issued the following statement after voting against the permitting reform legislation on the Senate floor:

“We desperately need permitting reform to build out new infrastructure, bring costs down, and bring new, renewable sources of energy online. But it needs to be the right kind of regulatory reform, not oil and gas development masquerading as reform. And throughout the negotiation process, I have made my priorities clear: to bring down energy costs through new clean energy development, to lower emission rates, to support and protect tribal sovereignty, to stop the administration from attacking American clean energy projects, and to ensure that any permitting reform legislation cannot be weaponized by this or any future administration to single out states for adverse treatment and provide giveaways to the oil and gas industries. This is why I submitted more than a dozen amendments for consideration in both the managers’ package and on the Senate floor that would have made the bill better.

“As it stands, this bill achieves some critically important priorities, but falls short on others. I appreciate the bipartisan work on this bill and the support of the 36 Senators who joined me in pushing for an amendment that would have struck the legislation’s changes to the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA). In the new Congress, there will be a lot of opportunity to improve protections for tribal sovereignty, and I will continue consulting with California’s tribal leaders to ensure their voices are heard in the halls of Congress.

“I strongly believe we need permitting reform and to build new infrastructure quickly and efficiently. But I also believe that this can be done in a way that does not needlessly degrade clean water, endanger wildlife, or disrespect tribal nations. And for those fundamental reasons, I opposed the bill. It is my hope that when this bill is again considered in the new Congress, that a Democrat majority can pass a more balanced work product that accomplishes all of these objectives.”

title: Schmitt Praises Senate Passage of Bipartisan Bill to Boost American Energy Dominance
text:
Legislation Lowers Energy Costs for Missouri Families, Holds Data Centers Accountable for Costs They Create

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) celebrated Senate passage of the “Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA),” landmark legislation to boost American energy production and drive down energy costs for Missouri families. The bill also requires data centers to shoulder the costs they inflict upon the grid, ensuring Missourians do not foot the bill for their increased energy demand.

“Tonight, I voted for landmark legislation on permitting reform that, for the first time forces data centers to pay their own way. No more fleecing ratepayers. It also unleashes American energy production by cutting leftist red tape and lowering costs, and it makes it easier to build in America again. More jobs! The reindustrialization of America is on. It’s past time we protect our communities and rebuild this country,” said Senator Schmitt.

BAAJA protects Missouri consumers from paying for data center development costs:

Requires new data centers to pay the costs they create by requiring utilities to recover the costs of serving data centers—including their electricity usage, power supply impact, and the grid upgrades necessary to meet them—from those companies.

Mandates that a customer’s share of new federally approved transmission costs must be in line with the benefits they receive by preventing customers from being forced to pay when those projects provide them with no meaningful benefit.

Ends a federal restriction on charging data centers for both the existing transmission grid and the additional upgrades needed to serve them by requiring utilities’ transmission rates to collect both charges from data centers.

Creates new reporting requirements for data centers’ electricity use to provide a clearer picture of their contribution to increasing energy demand.

Helps local government officials understand a proposed data center’s impacts before making decisions by creating a program that provides fact-based information and technical assistance upon request about its energy, water, economic, and community impacts.

Explicitly recognizes a state’s ability to charge data centers more than their costs and uses the extra revenue from data centers to lower electricity rates for homes and small businesses.

title: Sen. Tim Scott votes to bolster American energy and infrastructure
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Tim Scott (R-S.C.) voted today to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, legislation to clarify and improve environmental review and permitting processes. By providing greater certainty for permitted energy and infrastructure projects and streamlining permitting procedures, the legislation will help lower costs for hardworking Americans, create jobs, and advance American energy dominance. The Senate passed the bill by a vote of 62-33. The legislation now heads to the U.S. House of Representatives and must pass the House and be signed by the president before becoming law.

“After years of congressional efforts to reform our nation’s permitting process, this bipartisan package marks a significant step toward providing greater certainty for American energy and infrastructure projects,” said Sen. Scott. “By streamlining environmental reviews and permitting procedures, this legislation will help lower energy costs, create jobs, and unlock economic growth in South Carolina and across the country. This is how we get America building again, strengthen our nation’s infrastructure, and advance American energy dominance, and I’m pleased to see the Senate come together to pass this bill.”

The legislation also includes Sen. Scott’s bill, the Efficient Nuclear Licensing Hearings Act, to eliminate unnecessary and outdated nuclear licensing procedures. The amendment removes the Nuclear Regulatory Commission’s (NRC) hearing requirement for uncontested licensing proceedings, reducing time spent on noncontroversial hearings. The amendment preserves the public’s opportunity to comment while ensuring the NRC uses its time and resources more efficiently and saves taxpayer money.

Background

The legislation prevents administrations from arbitrarily revoking or suspending construction and operations for projects that have already obtained the necessary permits. It ensures permits cannot be revoked without proper justification based on violations of federal law.

To protect applicants and industries denied permits based on political bias, the legislation establishes a legal right to challenge those decisions.

Democrats have previously sought to block permits for certain sectors, including fossil fuels, mining, forestry, and manufacturing. During the Biden administration, Democrats used the permitting process to block the Keystone XL pipeline.

In South Carolina:

$22.6 billion worth of projects are currently stalled in the federal permitting process.

Federal permitting delays have cost South Carolina manufacturers $310 million annually.

$45.3 billion in total economic impact, including jobs, in-state spending, tax revenue, and more, is on hold due to the current federal permitting backlog in South Carolina.

Across the country:

Between $240 billion and $280 billion in new investments enter the federal permitting process each year.

Between $1.1 trillion and $1.5 trillion in investments are currently on hold awaiting permitting decisions.

$1.7-2.4 trillion in potential economic benefits are left untapped annually.

title: Shaheen, Collins Lead 243 Lawmakers in Pushing for Reauthorization of Special Diabetes Program
text:
(Washington, DC) – U.S. Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) and Susan Collins (R-ME), co-chairs of the U.S. Senate Diabetes Caucus and leaders of the bipartisan INSULIN Act to cap monthly out-of-pocket insulin costs at $35, are leading 56 of their Senate colleagues and 185 U.S. Representatives in a bipartisan letter to Senate and House leadership emphasizing the importance of the Special Diabetes Program (SDP) and the Special Diabetes Program for Indians (SDPI). They were joined in this effort by House Diabetes Caucus Co-chairs Diana DeGette (D-CO-1) and Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-12). Earlier this year, Shaheen and Collins secured a short-term reauthorization of SDP funding at a rate of approximately $200 million per year as part of the Fiscal Year 2026 funding packages—the highest level in the program’s nearly 30-year history. Without further action in Congress, however, authorization for the SDP will expire on December 31, 2026.

The lawmakers wrote, in part: “Diabetes is one of our country’s most expensive diseases in both human and economic terms, affecting people of all ages and races, and in every region of our country [...] Although the costs and prevalence of diabetes continue to increase, the SDP is making meaningful progress. The SDP comprises two partner components: the Special Statutory Funding Program for Type 1 Diabetes Research (SDP) and the Special Diabetes Program for Indians (SDPI). Since the program’s inception, both components have delivered critical resources and research breakthroughs for the more than 40 million Americans with diabetes and 115.2 million with prediabetes, as well as their loved ones.”

They continued: “Research funded by the program is leading to new insights and treatment options that improve the lives of diabetes patients and accelerate progress toward curing and preventing the disease [...] According to a 2025 study, advances supported by SDP-funded research have generated an estimated $50 billion in federal healthcare cost savings through improved diabetes management. Long-term, sustained investment in this program would provide the stability researchers need to continue large-scale trials, conduct outreach and education, and determine where best to allocate resources – all of which play an important role in helping to better treat, prevent, and ultimately cure diabetes.”

They concluded: “Congress has reauthorized these programs with bipartisan support on a regular basis since the programs’ inception in 1997. The researchers and clinicians who deliver the programs’ benefits require stable, predictable funding to maximize their contributions to the diabetes community [...] A multi-year extension of SDP beyond December 2026 will continue the program’s momentum and provide renewed hope for the diabetes community. We urge you to support a multi-year extension of SDP and SDPI.”

The full letter can be read HERE.

In addition to Senators Collins and Shaheen, the letter was signed by Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Maria Cantwell (D-WA), Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV), Chris Coons (D-DE), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Kevin Cramer (R-ND), Mike Crapo (R-ID), Steve Daines (R-MT), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Joni Ernst (R-IA), Deb Fischer (R-NE), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Chuck Grassley (R-IA), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), John Hoeven (R-ND), Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-MS), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Angus King (I-ME), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), Cynthia Lummis (R-WY), Ed Markey (D-MA), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Jerry Moran (R-KS), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), Patty Murray (D-WA), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Gary Peters (D-MI), Jack Reed (D-RI), Jim Risch (R-ID), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Mike Rounds (R-SD), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), Tina Smith (D-MN), Dan Sullivan (R-AK), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Mark Warner (D-VA), Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Roger Wicker (R-MS), Peter Welch (D-VT), Ron Wyden (D-OR) and Todd Young (R-IN).

As co-chairs of the U.S. Senate Diabetes Caucus, Shaheen and Collins have championed bipartisan efforts to lower insulin costs, expand access to treatment and advance critical diabetes research. The Senators have consistently worked to hold insulin manufacturers, insurers and pharmacy benefit managers accountable for the high costs of life-saving insulin, including through their landmark, bipartisan Improving Needed Safeguards for Users of Lifesaving Insulin Now (INSULIN) Act. The INSULIN Act, which would cap monthly out-of-pocket insulin costs at $35, is closer than ever before to passing out of the U.S. Senate after advancing out of the U.S. Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee earlier this year.

The Senators also lead the bicameral, bipartisan Strengthening Collective Resources for Encouraging Education Needed (SCREEN) for Type 1 Diabetes Act to improve early detection and screening for Type 1 diabetes and the bipartisan Diabetes Interventions Addressing Barriers to Enrollment, Technology and Education Services (DIABETES) Act to ensure care for diabetic patients is not interrupted when they enroll in Medicare.

title: U.S. Senator Tina Smith’s Statement in Opposition to Permitting Reform Legislation
text:
The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) would endanger sacred Tribal sites, pave the way for copper-sulfide mining near the Boundary Waters

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Tina Smith (D-MN) released the following statement after voting against the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), which seeks to update the nation’s permitting laws. The legislation passed the Senate (62 – 33).

“I have always said, and I still believe, that we need permitting reform. We need to update our outdated permitting process so we can lower energy costs by getting cleaner, cheaper power connected to the grid, but this bill is a bad deal that Democrats should not take,” said Sen. Tina Smith. “Language in this bill would not only make it much easier for Antofagasta to build its copper-sulfide mine in the watershed of our precious Boundary Waters, but also put sacred historical sites of Tribal Nations at risk and violate their sovereignty. We can reform permitting without violating Tribal sovereignty or sacrificing our water quality and precious public lands, in Minnesota and around the country.”

title: Thune: Historic Permitting Bill Will Cut Costs, Spur Economic Growth
text:
Click here to watch the video.

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) today delivered the following remarks on the Senate floor:

Thune’s remarks below (as delivered):

“Mr. President, later today, the Good Lord willing, the Senate will pass a historic permitting reform bill.

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act cuts through decades of red tape that has made it unnecessarily difficult and costly to build things in America.

“The status quo contributes to higher costs and headaches for consumers, businessowners, and builders.

“And in too many cases, permitting delays have caused projects to be abandoned altogether.

“Mr. President, this bill makes significant reforms to restore balance to the federal permitting process.

“It ensures that local stakeholders are adequately consulted on projects in their communities.

“And it prevents federal agencies in Washington from holding up projects through unnecessary bureaucratic delays.

“Mr. President, the slow pace of our current permitting process has had an impact on everything from drinking water to broadband to bridge and road repairs.

“And those delays have consequences for the American people, not least in the higher costs that they pay for energy and other essential goods.

“It’s estimated that this bill will save the average household hundreds of dollars each year, which is to say nothing of the benefits Americans will see in better roads, more American manufacturing, and better-paying jobs.

“Mr. President, this bill is years in the making and is the result of a lot of hard work from a number of people.

“I’m grateful to Chairmen Shelley Moore Capito and Mike Lee, and their staffs, for getting to a bipartisan agreement on this important issue.

“And I want to thank, also, our colleague … Alan Armstrong, whose expertise on this issue was invaluable.

“Mr. President, Alan Armstrong arrived in the Senate earlier this year with a mission: permitting reform.

“With nearly forty years of experience in energy development – starting as an engineer and working his way up to CEO – few know as much as Alan about energy production in this country and the realities of our permitting process.

“I’m grateful to him for lending his expertise to this important issue.

“His time with us has been short, but he can be assured that the impact of this one bill will echo for many years to come.

“Mr. President, as I understand it, Alan has another mission in mind after he leaves the Senate: sailing across the Atlantic with his wife, Shelly.

“I wish my friend fair winds and following seas, and I thank him for his contributions here in the Senate.”

title: Thune Underscores Importance of Strengthening Rural Health Care
text:
Click here to watch the video.

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) today delivered the following remarks on the Senate floor:

Thune’s remarks below (as delivered):

“Mr. President, before I conclude my remarks this morning, I’d like to say a few words about National Rural Health Day today.

“I represent a rural state.

“Half of my constituents in South Dakota live in rural areas.

“Life in a rural area comes with many charms but also a number of challenges.

“Mr. President, accessing health care is often one of those challenges.

“So is providing health care.

“Mr. President, health care professionals who serve rural communities often work in small teams.

“They may not have access to the latest technology that their peers in a big metro area may have.

“And sending a patient to a specialist can be a longer trip than a walk down the hall.

“So I want to express my gratitude to health care workers in rural America – especially in South Dakota – for the work they do every day to provide quality care in faraway places.

“Mr. President, those who work in health care have a passion for helping people – I think that’s especially true of health care professionals in rural areas.

“And the Rural Health Transformation Program that Republicans created in the Working Families Tax Cuts is designed to help them provide quality care in these communities.

“It’s a multi-year initiative that allows states to use funds to address their unique needs and to help rural providers get on a more sustainable footing.

“And as we begin the second year of this initiative, we’re seeing that play out across the country.

“Mr. President, the future of rural health care depends on health care professionals choosing to serve rural communities.

“I’m glad to see states using this funding to retain and recruit medical professionals to their rural communities: strengthening the pipeline for medical students to do their residencies in rural areas, targeting educational assistance, and helping to build a strong rural health care workforce from physicians to nurses to lab technicians and other professions.

“I read a story about one rural hospital that has just two physicians who deliver babies.

“One of them is always on call.

“And thanks to the Rural Health Transformation Program, that hospital will receive funding dedicated to maternal and neonatal care.

“It will be able to provide advanced family medicine training for physicians and increased obstetric and newborn care training for its nurses.

“Mr. President, I’m proud to see funding from the Rural Health Transformation Program going toward improving pipelines and training for doctors, for nurses, and other health care professionals to serve rural areas – among other critical areas of investment.

“And I’m grateful to everyone working today to provide quality care across rural America.”

title: Van Hollen Calls on Senate to Act on AI
text:
Last night, U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) released the following video on the latest developments on Artificial Intelligence, calling for the Senate to immediately address the urgent threats posed to working Americans by AI. To watch the video, click here. A transcript of the video is provided below:

The last 24 hours and the next 24 hours show us how urgent it is to address the risks posed by AI.

We just had OpenAI release their latest model, which creates more risks. We have Anthropic going public tomorrow, which will be great for the billionaires, but we need to act urgently to address the threats to the rest of us.

We need to protect our workforce and our workers. We need to make sure that all of you aren't paying higher electric bills for data centers built by the biggest and richest corporations on the planet. We need to deal with issues of privacy.

There's one issue that is immediately pressing, and that is the issue of AI safety. And Congress and the Senate better have a day-one plan for how we're going to deal with this.

So, we need mandatory and independent third-party evaluation of these companies.

Number two, we need to make sure that companies are held accountable, liable, and responsible for any harm they do, like if these agents escape containment and get onto the internet. And there should be penalties also for putting people at risk.

We also need to deal with the very urgent matter of bioweapons and cyberattacks.

And finally, given how rapidly this is evolving, we need to consider banning recursive self-improvement. In other words, the fact that AI begins to train AI and get beyond human capacity to intervene.

That could put us all at risk, and we need to move quickly to address that big threat to all of us.

title: Warner, Kennedy, Alsobrooks, Rounds Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Increase Transparency and Oversight of AI Investments
text:
WASHINGTON— U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner (D-VA), a senior member of the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs and one of Congress’s leading voices on artificial intelligence policy, Sen. John Kennedy (R-LA), Sen. Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), and Sen. Mike Rounds (R-SD) introduced the Advancing Uniform Disclosure of Investments and Transparency of Artificial Intelligence (AUDIT AI) Act, legislation to increase transparency around how publicly traded companies are investing in, deploying, and managing AI.

The legislation comes amid growing concerns about the unprecedented scale of AI investment and the increasingly complex financing arrangements underpinning the industry’s rapid expansion. As companies pour trillions of dollars into AI infrastructure, investors and regulators often lack a clear picture of the financing exposure, governance practices, and potential risks associated with these investments.

“AI has enormous potential to transform our economy, but the trillions of dollars pouring into this technology come with real financial risks,” said Sen. Warner. “Investors and policymakers deserve to know where that money is going, how these deals are being financed, and what risks are involved. We can’t afford to have massive financial exposure building up behind the scenes, only to discover it when something goes wrong. This bipartisan legislation would bring much-needed transparency and accountability to AI investments and help ensure we’re not setting ourselves up for the next financial crisis.”

“AI is the future, but investing in it shouldn’t be a guessing game. Companies are spending trillions of dollars on this technology, and investors deserve to know where that money is going and what risks they’re taking. Our bill will help make sure these companies put all their cards on the table,” said Sen. Kennedy.

“AI is no longer a far-off technology; it is already shaping how people work, learn, and receive health care. It is also reshaping our financial system, requiring clear guardrails from Congress to protect investors and consumers. Our bipartisan bill takes responsible steps to increase transparency around AI funding and protect our financial system. I will keep fighting to ensure AI expands opportunity, protects workers and consumers, strengthens American competitiveness, and builds public trust,” said Sen. Alsobrooks.

“Economic growth in the United States has been driven in large part by investment in the development of artificial intelligence capabilities,” said Sen. Rounds. “As AI continues to advance, it’s important that public companies disclose material information about how they oversee AI capabilities internally and where they invest their resources in outside AI capabilities. Our legislation would create transparent disclosure guidelines for public companies regarding their implementation of AI capabilities.”

The rapid expansion of AI is fueling an unprecedented wave of investment in data centers, semiconductors, energy infrastructure, and other critical resources. A recent report published by the Brookings Institution estimates that building out AI infrastructure could require $10.3 trillion in investment from 2025 to 2032, equivalent to approximately 3.6 percent of U.S. GDP each year. The scale of this investment could surpass historic American infrastructure booms, including the expansion of railroads, highways, electrification, canals, and telecommunications.

Slowdown in the buildout could ignite shockwaves throughout the U.S. economy and have far-reaching consequences for the financial sector. These risks are compounded by complex financing arrangements, including joint ventures, special purpose vehicles, and other debt structures, that can make it difficult for investors and policymakers to fully assess companies’ financial exposure. The AUDIT AI Act would help close these transparency gaps by strengthening corporate disclosures, improving oversight, and giving investors a clearer picture of the risks associated with these investments. Greater transparency will help policymakers and regulators better understand how these investments are connected to the broader financial system and where vulnerabilities could emerge.

Specifically, the AUDIT AI Act would:

Strengthen AI governance by requiring public companies to disclose whether they have an AI governance policy and a dedicated board committee focused on AI, and explain why if they do not. Companies with an AI governance policy would be required to make it publicly available.

Shed light on AI infrastructure financing by requiring non-financial public companies to disclose AI-related joint ventures, special purpose vehicles, variable interest entities, and other major debt arrangements in SEC filings and at the SEC’s discretion.

Standardize AI risk disclosure by requiring companies with significant AI exposure to provide standardized disclosure of material risks, including dependence on third-party models, compute concentration, costs, and data liabilities.

Examine whether financial reporting is keeping pace with AI by directing the SEC to study how companies account for AI research and development, revenues, and capital expenditures and make recommendations for future policymaking or standard setting.

Monitor AI’s impact on financial markets by requiring the SEC to report annually on how automated investment strategies are affecting price discovery, market efficiency, and potential herding behavior.

“Both the enormous potential and unprecedented risks of AI are top of mind in most American boardrooms. This bill will give investors critical insight on whether, and how, corporate leaders are overseeing the technology that will define our future. And it will shine crucial light on how enormous and opaque AI investments are actually being funded. Ordinary investors deserve to know who is behind the systemic shifts that AI will soon bring—and how they’re paying for it,” said Robert J. Jackson, Jr., Former Commissioner of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

“I strongly support greater transparency in the financing of the AI buildout. Investors and policymakers need a clear picture of the debt, lease commitments, and guarantees supporting this investment–and who ultimately bears the risks. As financing spreads across joint ventures, private credit, and off-balance-sheet vehicles, conventional corporate accounts reveal only part of the story. Better disclosure is essential to support informed investment, strengthen accountability, and identify financial vulnerabilities while this rapidly growing industry is still taking shape,” said Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh, the Earl Kazis and Benjamin Schore Professor of Real Estate at Columbia Business School.

“Governance and effective control over AI development and applications are critical aspects of a company’s effective and appropriate use of AI tools. Investors need greater transparency and visibility into companies’ governance and oversight process over development and use of AI applications that are important to a company’s ongoing operations,” said Paul Munter, Former Chief Accountant of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Read the full bill here and a section-by-section explainer of the bill here.

title: Welch Statement on Senate’s Permitting Reform Bill
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.) today voted against the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), the Senate’s permitting reform legislative package, after the Senate failed to adopt amendments that would have improved the bill while preserving its historic gains in transmission and clean energy development—including ensuring states can enforce their own drinking water laws, and preventing developers from abusing the courtsand securing excessive damages at taxpayers’ expense, among others.

“We need to build things faster and more efficiently in Vermont and across the country. Permitting reform is especially important as we work to transition to the affordable, clean energy infrastructure we need to address climate change and lower utility bills for families. I am all for getting to yes or no faster. Unfortunately, the Senate failed to address several outstanding issues in the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, including provisions that could open the government up to unprecedented financial liability and changes that undercut states’ ability to protect their clean water resources,” said Senator Welch. “I offered fixes and amendments to this bill and am disappointed the Senate failed to consider these important changes to protect our communities.”

Senator Welch’s amendments to BAAJA included provisions to:

Prevent Project Developers from Abusing the Courts

Welch filed an amendment to eliminate the excessive damages in the permitting certainty sections of BAAJA, preventing project developers from receiving between 25-100% of project costs as settlements in certain cases where a permit is revoked or denied.

Mitigate Harms from BAAJA’s Changes to the Clean Water Act

Welch filed amendments to protect states’ authority to consider a range of project impacts that may harm clean water resources. The amendments would also prevent states from having to meet an unreachable burden of proof to protect clean water resources in court.

Protect Judicial Remedies Under the National Environment Policy Act (NEPA)

This amendment would maintain the courts’ authority to stop projects from moving forward with construction if they find a major NEPA violation.

Exclude Data Centers from Benefitting from the Bill

Welch filed an amendment to exclude data centers from BAAJA’s permitting certainty provisions, preventing data center approvals from being locked in by the current administration and protecting taxpayer dollars from potentially being awarded in settlements to Big Tech companies.

Better Support Local Communities That Host Transmission Projects

Welch filed an amendment to add his Energizing Our Communities Act to the bill. This legislation aims to support national transmission build-out by ensuring communities see the benefits of transmission at the ground level by investing revenue from certain Department of Energy loan programs back into communities, including tribal governments, that host transmission infrastructure.

Harness Energy Efficiency to Reduce Electricity Bills

Welch filed an amendment to ensure that energy efficiency and demand response resources are eligible tocompete in wholesale markets as distributed energy resources under the bill. It would add key components of Senator Welch’s E-Access Act to guarantee ratepayers have access to their energy consumption data in order toparticipate in these programs.

title: Welch: “The Congress should impeach, and the Senate should convict, Secretary Hegseth.”
text:
Welch demands impeachment of Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth if the Trump Administration refuses to fire him

Welch’s remarks come ahead of Senate’s vote to end the war in Iran

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.) today called for the impeachment of Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, citing Hegseth’s reckless handling of the war in Iran and mismanagement of the Department of Defense. Senator Welch’s call for Hegseth’s impeachment came as he spoke in support of a War Powers Resolution to end President Trump’s unauthorized and unconstitutional war with Iran.

“We have the authority, under the War Powers Act, to approve or disapprove a conflict after 60 days that has been initiated by the president. And we are here again today, but this time we’re here after the American people in this election made it very clear that they have no support for this war without end. My hope is that all of us here will accept our responsibility to make a decision as to whether we authorize the commander-in-chief to be in this reckless war. My hope is each and every one of us will vote no,” said Senator Welch. “I believe Secretary Hegseth should be fired. And I believe if the president chooses to retain but not fire Secretary Hegseth, the Congress should impeach and the Senate should convict Secretary Hegseth, so that we can stand for the honor and integrity of the men and women of the military.”

Senator Welch has voted 15 times to end the president’s illegal war with Iran.

Read the Senator’s full remarks as deliveredand watch his full speech below and on YouTube:

Read key excerpts from the Senator’s remarks on the Senate Floor:

“The illegal war in Iran must end. This has been a catastrophic, unilateral decision by the President of the United States to plunge us into a war. What he’s done has broken a promise he made to the American people when he ran for president: to make certain it was ‘America First,’ not ‘America in forever wars in the Middle East.’ That’s what this war is. The decision he made—without consultation or approval from Congress, without consultation or attention to advice even from within his own administration—about the folly of a bombing campaign without any awareness or appreciation that this would directly cause the closing of the Strait of Hormuz, would directly lead to astronomical diesel prices, fertilizer prices that are hitting every American—particularly our farmers—is a catastrophic decision by the president.”

•••

“Every single day, the president and all of us, should be asking ourselves what justifies the sacrifice that’s being expected of men and women in the military. To deny that we’ve lost any lives in the past five months—when that is totally false—is a terrible indictment of the casual attitude the president has about the consequences of this war on the men and women in the military.

“I want to honor those brave men and women. We’ve lost 23 brave men and women during this war, including nine in the past five months that President Trump wouldn’t even acknowledge…I know every member of the United States Senate wants never to forget, and always acknowledge the sacrifice that those men and women made—their answer to the call of duty.”

title: Chairman Wicker Leads SASC Hearing to Consider Four Senior Pentagon Nominees
text:
Watch Video Here

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Roger Wicker, R-Miss., Chairman of the Senate Armed Services Committee, today led a hearing to consider the nominations for senior defense management, coordination, acquisition, and financial leadership positions.

Mr. William Toti, nominated to be Under Secretary of the Navy, Mr. Daniel Zimmerman, nominated to be Assistant Secretary of Defense for International Armaments Cooperation, Mr. Richard Breckenridge, nominated to be Assistant Secretary of the Navy for Research, Development, and Acquisition, and Mr. Arthur Miller, nominated to be Assistant Secretary of the Navy for Financial Management and Comptroller, appeared before the committee.

In his opening remarks, Chairman Wicker stressed the importance of strong leadership to address the Navy’s challenges and improve its overall readiness. He outlined the nominees’ responsibilities in strengthening shipbuilding and maintenance, speeding up the development and delivery of new military technology, and ensuring the Navy’s budget is managed effectively. Wicker emphasized that each nominee will play an important role in making America’s Armed Forces more capable, accountable, and prepared to meet future threats.

Read Chairman Wicker’s hearing opening statement as delivered.

I welcome our nominees and their families, and I am grateful for their willingness to serve our nation. The United States faces an increasingly dangerous threat environment, and we need experienced leaders willing to step up and tackle the challenges facing our nation.

First, Mr. William Toti has been nominated to serve as Under Secretary of the Navy. He brings decades of Navy experience, along with an understanding of the challenges facing the Department in the maritime industrial base. If confirmed, he will play a critical role in the daily management of the Department of the Navy and in translating the Secretary’s priorities into results. There is no shortage of work ahead: revitalizing our shipbuilding enterprise, improving maintenance and fleet readiness, strengthening our industrial base, and ensuring our Sailors and Marines have the resources they need to accomplish their missions. His leadership and willingness to work with Congress will be essential in building a more capable and ready naval force.

Daniel Zimmerman is welcomed back to the committee. He is the only nominee in recent history who enjoyed the confirmation process so much that he decided to do it twice in two years. He is currently an acting Deputy Under Secretary, working for Mike Duffey in Acquisition, but he has now been nominated to be the Assistant Secretary of Defense for International Armaments Cooperation, a position created only last year. In this role, he would serve as the principal advisor to Mr. Duffey for defense industrial base cooperation with our allies and partners. Since Congress created this office, it has been capably led by Katherine Katina, and it has seen impressive successes. The team executed $500 million of Defense Exportability Features program funding from last year’s reconciliation law, along with a $500 million match from industry, all to adjust our weapons for export. Senator Shaheen has been advocating for that for years. It is going to make a big difference. Now more than ever, we must work with our allies to strengthen our shared industrial base and weapons stockpiles. I look forward to hearing Daniel’s vision for this office, as well as his plans to synchronize U.S. government actions across these critical lines of international cooperation.

Mr. Richard Breckenridge has been nominated to serve as Assistant Secretary of the Navy for Research, Development, and Acquisition. He brings decades of Navy experience. His background in engineering and undersea warfare gives him a valuable perspective on the technological demands facing our Navy. If confirmed, he will be responsible for overseeing the development and acquisition of the capabilities our Sailors and Marines need to maintain our military advantage. We must accelerate the delivery of new technologies, improve acquisition performance, and address the cost and schedule challenges that have plagued major programs. Surely everyone within the sound of my voice agrees with that. I look forward to hearing how Mr. Breckenridge plans to translate his operational experience into better acquisition outcomes and ensure our Navy can meet the demands of a potential conflict in an appropriate amount of time.

And finally, Mr. Arthur Miller has been nominated to serve as Assistant Secretary of the Navy for Financial Management and Comptroller. He currently serves as the Department of Defense’s Deputy Comptroller for Budget and Appropriations Affairs, where he advises senior Department leadership and serves as a principal liaison with the congressional appropriations committees. If confirmed, he will be responsible for ensuring the Navy’s resources are effectively managed and aligned with its operational priorities. I look forward to hearing how he plans to improve budget execution to strengthen financial accountability by achieving a clean audit opinion and to ensure the Navy gets the greatest possible return on its investments.

We have four talented nominees here, and we need to move with dispatch in this hearing and get them reported. With that, I turn to my friend and colleague, Ranking Member Reed.

###

title: Wicker’s Maritime Research & Development Bills Advance from Commerce Committee
text:
WASHINGTON – The U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation this week advanced two bills authored by U.S. Senator Roger Wicker, R-Miss.: the Cooperative Institute Act of 2026 (S. 5332) and the Marine Aquaculture Research for America (MARA) Act (S. 2586).

Earlier this year, Senators Wicker, Hyde-Smith, R-Miss., Cantwell, D-Wash., and Hickenlooper, D-Colo., introduced the Cooperative Institute Act of 2026. The senators’ bill would codify and modernize the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s (NOAA) research partnerships at colleges and universities across the country. Mississippi State University, the University of Southern Mississippi, and Jackson State University have all partnered with NOAA in this area of study.

“Mississippi universities are working on the cutting edge of many exciting scientific breakthroughs, made possible through cooperation with NOAA. The Cooperative Institute Act of 2026 will bring stability to several research projects that have been indispensable to storm tracking efforts and our coastal industries,” said Senator Wicker.

Senator Wicker introduced the MARA Act along with Senator Brian Schatz, D-Hawaii, to expand aquaculture along the Mississippi coast and beyond, to support workforce development in this field, and to reduce the U.S. seafood trade deficit. Currently, a complex web of regulatory barriers prevents offshore aquaculture projects from operating in federal waters. Senator Wicker’s bill seeks to remedy this issue by streamlining the permitting process and establishing an assessment program through NOAA to authorize offshore demonstration projects.

“The Mississippi coast is blessed with an abundance of marine life, yet burdensome regulations keep us from tapping into its full potential,” said Senator Wicker. “The MARA Act will open up more aquaculture opportunities in our waters, as my colleagues recognized when the Commerce Committee advanced this important legislation.”

The Marine Aquaculture Research for America (MARA) Act would:

Establish an Office of Aquaculture within the National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) to coordinate implementation, outreach, research, best management practices, regional aquaculture activities, and regulatory and scientific issues

Establish a NOAA assessment program and authorize commercial-scale offshore aquaculture demonstration projects to evaluate environmental, technological, operational, and commercial viability

Authorize 10-year demonstration permits, renewable for an additional decade, subject to eligibility criteria, public notice and comment, reporting, environmental safeguards, and NOAA authority to modify or terminate projects

Require coastal state review under the Coastal Zone Management Act, establish a process for governors to object to offshore aquaculture operations in adjacent federal waters, and minimize interference with existing fishing access and recreational activities

Designate NOAA as the lead federal agency for permitting coordination, establish a unified interagency permitting and review process, consolidate National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) review where permissible, and establish timelines for permit coordination and decisions, including congressional reporting requirements for delays

Support aquaculture marketing, workforce development, regional technical assistance, information sharing, and access to capital through existing programs, while promoting sustainable aquaculture feed sourcing, including alternatives to wild fish

Require a National Academies study and a Government Accountability Office report on the environmental, economic, regulatory, and operational viability of offshore aquaculture and potential future regulatory approaches

Preserve existing federal and state permitting authorities and clarify that demonstration permits issued under the Act do not replace other authorizations

title: Young, Banks Introduce Bill to Rename Muncie Post Office in Honor of Corporal Blake Reynolds
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators Todd Young (R-Ind.) and Jim Banks (R-Ind.) introduced legislation to rename the United States Post Office located at 501 West Memorial Drive in Muncie, Indiana, in honor of Delaware County Sheriff’s Corporal Blake A. Reynolds, who died in the line of duty in November 2025.

The legislation would designate the facility as the “Officer Blake A. Reynolds Post Office Building.” Representative Victoria Spartz (R-IN-05) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives in September, with support from the Indiana congressional delegation.

“Corporal Blake Reynolds dedicated his life to serving his community and protecting his fellow Hoosiers,” said Senator Young. “His tragic death was a tremendous loss for Delaware County and the entire law enforcement community. Renaming this post office in his honor is a fitting tribute to his service and sacrifice, and a meaningful way for the community he served to honor his memory.”

“Corporal Blake Reynolds gave his life serving the people of Delaware County,” said Senator Banks. “He was a dedicated deputy, a member of the Indiana Army National Guard, and a proud son of the Muncie Community. Naming this post office in his honor would recognize his sacrifice and ensure his service is remembered for generations.”

Background:

Born in Muncie, Reynolds graduated from Delta High School in 2013 and earned a bachelor’s degree in criminal justice from Ball State University. He served in the Indiana Army National Guard before joining the Delaware County Sheriff’s Office in 2022, where he rose to the rank of Corporal.

On November 12, 2025, Reynolds was killed in the line of duty while assisting the driver of a disabled semitrailer on Interstate 69.

Reynolds was the first officer in the history of the Delaware County Sheriff’s Department to die in the line of duty.

The legislation is supported by the Reynolds family and Muncie Mayor Dan Ridenour.

title: Reps. Houlahan, Fry, Carter Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Strengthen Early Outbreak Detection
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representatives Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Russell Fry (SC-07), and Troy Carter (LA-02) introduced the bipartisan Public health Response and Emergency Detection through Integrated wastewater Community Testing (PREDICT) Act. The PREDICT Act would strengthen the nation’s wastewater monitoring capabilities, better positioning the United States to improve early detection of infectious diseases.

U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Tim Scott (R-SC) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. Senate.

Viral, bacterial, and fungal pathogens such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), measles, West Nile virus, and influenza A and B can shed viral or bacterial material even in the absence of visible symptoms. Wastewater surveillance allows public health officials to analyze sewage to detect viruses and bacteria circulating in a community, identify potential outbreaks more proactively, and hasten responses to better protect communities. As the United States lost its Measles Elimination Status earlier this week, early detection systems will be a crucial tool for public health officials to identify and track infectious diseases as the nation works to stop the measles outbreak, protect American families, and regain the United States’ measles elimination status.

“Wastewater monitoring can help health officials detect infectious diseases earlier, giving them valuable time to respond and protect their communities,” said Rep. Houlahan. “As pandemic-era funding runs out, we cannot afford to lose that capability. The PREDICT Act would strengthen the CDC’s wastewater surveillance program and help local health departments use this tool to keep Pennsylvanians and all Americans safer.”

“Wastewater surveillance gives health officials a critical head start, allowing them to detect and contain infectious diseases before they become full-blown outbreaks,” said Rep. Fry. “Early detection tools like proactive wastewater monitoring protects American families and equips communities to stop emerging threats in their tracks. This legislation has the potential to save lives, especially in light of measles continuing to spread across the U.S. I’m hopeful the House will move swiftly in considering our bill.”

“During the COVID-19 crisis, the CDC began incorporating wastewater surveillance as an early warning sign of the spread of the virus, and the public health lessons from that technological innovation should continue to inform and shape legislation and public policy responses to infectious diseases,” said Congressman Carter. “I’m joining Rep. Fry to introduce a bipartisan, bicameral PREDICT Act to fund and broaden the use of wastewater surveillance to additional diseases and regions of the country as well as track the data, promote innovation, and require a national strategic plan for its use from the CDC. With the expansion of this cost-effective technology, Congress and CDC can protect Americans’ health and stop the spread of deadly diseases like COVID-19, measles, and more.”

The PREDICT ACT is endorsed by the Wastewater Action Alliance, AdvaMedDx, Big Cities Health Coalition, National Network of Public Health Institutes, Clear Labs, the Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America, the National Association of Clean Water Agencies, and the American Society for Microbiology.

"Representatives Fry, Carter, and Houlahan have shown exactly the kind of bipartisan leadership we need to protect our communities from the next outbreak, and we are calling on Congress to pass the PREDICT Act now during the lame-duck session," said Kate Hull, Executive Director of the Wastewater Action Alliance. "Communities across America depend on Wastewater monitoring to detect measles, RSV, influenza, and other infectious diseases days or even weeks before people show up sick at hospitals. Americans cannot afford to lose wastewater monitoring, and they are counting on Congress to act."

The PREDICT Act would:

Direct the CDC to award grants to state, tribal, and local health departments, educational institutions, nonprofits, and public-private partnerships to establish, maintain, or improve wastewater surveillance activities

Support advanced testing capabilities so laboratories can detect new pathogens quickly and simultaneously track multiple infectious diseases using consistent testing methods

Improve data transparency and sharing by establishing a timely and accessible dashboard for state and local public health officials

Promote innovation and flexibility by directing the CDC to issue guidance supporting new technologies and adaptable surveillance systems

Require a national strategic plan outlining how the CDC will strengthen wastewater monitoring nationwide and maintain an early-warning system capable of detecting emerging health threats

The full text of the bill is available here.

title: Congressman Al Green Calls for Greater Transparency and Congressional Oversight Following Widespread Technology Outages
text:
(Washington, D.C.) — On Friday, November 20, 2026, Congressman Al Green expressed serious concern over recent widespread technology outages that have disrupted essential services across the United States, calling for greater transparency regarding their causes and stronger congressional oversight to prevent similar incidents in the future.

Congressman Al Green stated, “These widespread technology outages are a matter of serious concern. Americans have been locked out of their bank accounts, stranded at airports for hours or even days, and left unable to access essential services. These disruptions have raised understandable concerns among Houstonians and Americans nationwide about the reliability and security of the technological systems upon which we depend, as well as the competency with which new technologies are integrated into existing systems.

The Director of National Intelligence and the Deputy Director of the FBI indicated during a November 18, 2026, Committee on Homeland Security ‘Worldwide Threats’ hearing, which I attended in my capacity as a member of the Committee, that these outages were unrelated and expressed confidence that they were not the result of attacks by foreign adversaries. While these assessments may provide some reassurance, the American people deserve to know what caused these disruptions and what steps are being taken to prevent them. President Trump was quick to attribute malfunctions under the Biden administration to incompetence and diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) policies. Yet, as multiple widespread outages occur under his own administration, we are now being asked to accept that these incidents are merely unrelated coincidences, not incompetence. The American people deserve a more thorough explanation.

Regardless of the cause, Congress has a responsibility to seek answers from federal agencies and technology companies, determine whether existing safeguards are sufficient, and take appropriate action to prevent similar disruptions in the future. The American people deserve reliable access to the essential services upon which their daily lives depend, and we must ensure that our nation’s technological infrastructure is secure, resilient, and worthy of their trust. The American people deserve answers, not double standards that characterize malfunctions as incompetence under one administration but dismiss them as coincidence under another.”

title: Rep. Balint Calls for Rejection of BAAJA Ahead of House Vote
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Ahead of an upcoming House vote on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), Representative Becca Balint (VT-AL) is urging her colleagues to reject the legislation. Balint released the following statement:

“Permitting reform should help us build the infrastructure our communities need, create good-paying jobs, and accelerate the transition to a clean energy future. BAAJA would roll back critical environmental protections, weaken historic preservation, undermine Tribal sovereignty, and put communities at risk. This bill sacrifices environmental protections in the name of accelerating energy deployment and advancing infrastructure projects. What’s more, there are too many giveaways to oil and gas development, undermining our efforts to transition to clean domestic energy deployment. As we prepare to take back the House majority in January, we have both the opportunity and the obligation to lead on meaningful reform that accomplishes our goals while also respecting Tribal Nations and protecting our environment for future generations. We have the chance to get this right, and we should take it. We can do better.”

title: Rep. Bera Statement on President Trump's Trilateral Summit with Putin and Xi
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representative Ami Bera, M.D. (CA-06), Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on East Asia and the Pacific, issued a statement following President Donald Trump's trilateral summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and People’s Republic of China (PRC) President Xi Jinping:

“Diplomacy with our adversaries is important. But when the President of the United States sits down with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, the American people should expect meaningful results. Unfortunately, the Administration has offered little detail about what was discussed, what was accomplished, or what concrete steps were agreed upon. Congress and the American people deserve a full accounting of the summit's outcomes.

“President Trump should have confronted Putin over his illegal war in Ukraine and demanded the withdrawal of Russian troops. He should have pressed Xi on China's increasing military aggression toward Taiwan and its support for Russia's war effort. He should have held both leaders accountable for providing Iran technical and intelligence support that has contributed to the deaths of American troops. This summit should also have delivered concrete progress toward ending the war in Iran, establishing guardrails on artificial intelligence, and resolving ongoing trade and tariff disputes.

“Standing alongside Putin and Xi without delivering meaningful results does little to inspire confidence among our allies in Europe and Asia. The American people have made clear they do not trust President Trump's judgment or that of the people advising him. This summit gives them little reason to think otherwise.”

title: Rep. Calvert Raises Alarm Over Biased Ads Placed by the Riverside County Registrar of Voters
text:
Congressman Ken Calvert (CA-41) sent a letter to the Riverside County Board of Supervisors raising concerns about inherently biased ads placed by the Riverside County Registrar of Voters that encouraged voting among very select populations prior to the November general election. Recent reporting discovered the Riverside County Registrar of Voters placed ads on Meta platforms using targeting keywords that included “Gangsta rap,” “Wiz Khalifa,” “Rick Ross,” “Kanye West,” and “2 Chainz” among others. A portion of the ads were also targeted to one specific zip code, located in downtown Riverside.

“Americans expect those who conduct our elections to do so in a manner that is fair and without any political bias,” said Rep. Calvert. “The decision by the Riverside County Registrar of Voters office to spend tax dollars to encourage select populations of voters to cast a ballot in the November election is deeply troubling. Riverside County voters deserve to know why the Registrar of Voters wants fans of ‘gangsta rap’ to vote more than fans of other genres, like country music. Riverside County voters also deserve to know why the Registrar of Voters wants residents of a single downtown Riverside zip code to vote more than residents in other zip codes.”

According to the Meta Ad Library database, the Riverside County Registrar of Voters targeted ads using the following keywords:

Erykah Badu, Freestyle rap, Future (rapper), Gangsta rap, Gucci Mane, Janelle Monáe, Jay-Z, Jhené Aiko, Jill Scott, Kanye West, Kehlani, Meek Mill, Metro Boomin, Migos, Rae Sremmurd, Rapping, Rick Ross, Solange Knowles, Soul music, Southern hip hop, SZA (singer), T.I., Teyana Taylor, Tinashe, Tory Lanez, Underground hip hop, Wiz Khalifa.

Meta’s disclosure database also indicates that more than 10 percent of social media ads placed by the Riverside County ROV were geographically targeted to a single zip code, 92501, located in downtown Riverside.

In 2024, a Cornell University study found that hip-hop and rap music streaming online occurs more heavily in Democratic-leaning communities than in Republican-leaning region. Furthermore, according to a YouGov poll conducted in 2024, Democrats are twice as likely as Republicans to name hip-hop as their favorite genre.

title: Casten and Lieu Introduce Bill to Combat Insider Trading on Prediction Markets
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Representatives Sean Casten (IL-06) and Ted Lieu (CA-36) introduced the Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act of 2026, legislation to incentivize whistleblowers to report information to federal law enforcement agencies about potential insider trading that occurs on prediction market platforms.

“It is reprehensible that government insiders are profiting off advanced knowledge of when and where the United States will conduct military strikes,” said Rep. Sean Casten. “Prediction markets have a serious insider trading problem, and the current Administration is engaged in corruption of epic proportions. By encouraging whistleblowers to come forward and report wrongdoing, we can take an important step in cracking down on insider trading to restore accountability and public confidence in the U.S. rule of law.”

“Government insiders should not be able to profit from betting on U.S. military operations or the contents of a President’s speech. They should not be able to use their positions of public trust to manipulate prediction markets,” said Congressman Lieu. “The Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act of 2026 will encourage whistleblowers to report insider trading on prediction market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket. This blatant corruption needs to end.”

Specifically, the Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act would establish a new program at the Department of Justice (DOJ) where eligible whistleblowers can anonymously report original, credible, and crucial information about suspected fraudulent activity involving prediction markets. Whistleblowers would potentially receive financial compensation if such information leads to a successful enforcement action.

In recent months, several high-profile examples have emphasized the need for legislation like the Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act. For example, one anonymous trader has made nearly $1 million from dozens of suspiciously timed and accurate bets on military actions that the United States has taken against Iran. Another trader made more than $550,000 from bets that Iran’s Supreme Leader would be removed, just before his assassination. President Trump’s teleprompter operator earned more than $100,000 by betting on which words the President would use in his speeches. Lastly, the Nobel Institute is investigating a bet placed by a newly created account on Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado winning the Nobel Peace Prize hours before the announcement, resulting in a profit of more than $50,000.

Text of the legislation can be found here.

The legislation is endorsed by Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW), Project on Government Oversight (POGO), Transparency International U.S., the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA), Americans for Financial Reform, and Public Citizen.

Earlier this year, Reps. Casten and Lieu led 54 House Democrats in urging the DOJ to more aggressively pursue insider trading violations that occur on prediction markets. Following their letter, the DOJ has increased enforcement against suspected government and corporate insiders who have misused confidential information for personal financial gain, and is reportedly investigating offshore and unregulated prediction market platforms that have created new avenues for insider trading and may be illegally serving U.S. customers.

title: Smith: “Grynspan could jeopardize support in Congress for funding of the UN regular budget”Smith leads letter to Sec. Rubio opposing nomination of Rebeca Grynspan to be the next UN Secretary General
text:
Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ), Co-Chair of the Congressional Pro-Life Caucus, today led 8 Members of Congress in sending a letter to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, urging the United States—in its capacity as a permanent member of the United Nations (UN) Security Council—to veto the selection of Rebeca Grynspan as the next UN Secretary General (UNSG).

“We urge the United States, as a permanent member of the Security Council, to veto Ms. Grynspan’s selection in favor of a candidate who has a demonstrated respect for the right of sovereign nations to legislate to protect and defend the weakest and most vulnerable—unborn children,” the Republican lawmakers write.

In their letter, the lawmakers highlight Ms. Grynspan’s well-established history of promoting abortion-on-demand—including her contributions to reports from UN Women and the Ibero-American General Secretariat, which advocated for abortion extremism—and argue that her record is incompatible with the Trump Administration’s vision for the next UNSG. This vision includes stopping the “propagation of divisive ideologies that undermine national sovereignty and stir controversy,” and instead promotes “bring[ing] member states together to address issues of common concern.”

The 2017 UN Women report, for which Ms. Grynspan served as an expert advisor, urged the elimination of the “legal, economic, and social barriers that prevent access to… abortion—primarily for adolescents.” And while under her leadership in 2016, the Ibero-American General Secretariat published a report that strongly recommended “[e]nsur[ing] universal access to sexual and reproductive health and reproductive rights”—i.e., unfettered access to abortion-on-demand.

Smith, the most senior member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and a four-time congressional delegate to the UN, further noted that “Ms. Grynspan may not be suited to drive the deep reforms that are necessary to restore the United Nations to its original purpose and could jeopardize support in Congress for funding of the UN regular budget.”

“If past is prologue, Ms. Grynspan’s record absolutely suggests that she would use the UNSG position to promote the killing of unborn children by abortion everywhere and continue to undermine the pro-life laws and policies of sovereign nations,” the Members of Congress write.

“The United States should use its voice and vote—and, if necessary, veto—to prevent Ms. Grynspan from being selected as UNSG and instead promote a candidate who is more clearly committed to the defense of innocent human life and to bringing the UN ‘back to basics.’”
