title: Save Jersey article on Smith's Christian persecution hearing'Chris Smith presses Washington to confront persecution facing 1 in 7 Christians worldwide'
text:
By The Staff

Published November 20, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C. — In Nigeria, Christians face deadly attacks for their faith. In Turkey, a church can lose its pastor to deportation. This week, Rep. Chris Smith (R-NJ) chaired a congressional hearing at which witnesses described how both kinds of pressure can threaten a Christian community’s survival and urged Washington to do more to protect religious freedom abroad.

Smith, who serves as co-chairman of the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission, cited Open Doors’ 2026 World Watch List, which estimates that more than 388 million Christians worldwide face persecution and discrimination solely because of their faith.

“That’s more than one in seven of the world’s Christians,” Smith said. “And this horrific problem is not confined to a handful of countries or a single region.”

David K. Trimble, the president of the Religious Freedom Institute, delivered some of the hearing’s sharpest criticism. He accused Nigerian authorities of ignoring attacks on Christians and, in some cases, complicity in the violence. In Syria, he testified, Christians continue to face violence and intimidation despite the transitional government’s promises to protect religious minorities.

“They have failed to hold violent perpetrators systematically accountable,” Trimble said of Nigerian authorities.

John Eibner, international president of Christian Solidarity International, urged Washington to reassess its alliance with Turkey. Under President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Eibner testified, Turkish authorities have interfered with church leadership and deported foreign church workers, while pro-government media portray Christians as outsiders in their own country.

The debate also reached Western Europe. Jeremy Tedesco, senior counsel at Alliance Defending Freedom, argued that the European Union’s Digital Services Act and the United Kingdom’s Online Safety Act put pressure on online platforms to restrict religious speech. He urged members of Congress to raise the issue directly with European officials, warning that American churches and ministries can feel the effects of those restrictions when they publish online.

University of Dallas scholar Timothy Shah cited Pew Research Center findings that Christians faced harassment from government officials or private actors in 165 countries in 2023. For some families, those pressures ultimately force a decision about whether they can stay. World Relief’s Matthew Soerens told Smith’s panel that, according to Open Doors, more than 224,000 Christians fled their homes to escape persecution in a single reporting year.

title: Rep. Cisneros Leads Bipartisan Letter Urging President Trump to Rescind Vladimir Putin’s G20 Invitation
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31), alongside Congressman Pat Ryan (NY-18) and Congressman Don Bacon (NE-08), led seventeen Members of Congress in a bipartisan letter urging President Trump to rescind his invitation to Vladimir Putin to attend the G20 Summit in Miami this December.

The members’ letter follows troubling reports that Russia is sharing intelligence with Iran that supported Iranian strikes on U.S. forces abroad. As of November 2026, at least 23 U.S. servicemembers have lost their lives in the war with Iran.

“We write to express serious concern regarding your invitation to Vladimir Putin to attend the G20 summit in Miami this December and urge you to immediately rescind this invitation. Not only did Russia launch an unprovoked and unjustified invasion of Ukraine over four years ago, but we are now seeing troubling reports that Russia has provided Iran with satellite imagery and related intelligence that may have assisted Iranian strikes on U.S. forces, including the late-March attack on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia. That attack reportedly wounded twelve American servicemembers and destroyed a U.S. Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) aircraft,” wrote the members in the letter.

“By inviting Putin to attend the G20 summit, President Trump has endorsed Russia’s deadly aggression, sided with a dictator, and undermined our national security,” said Rep. Gil Cisneros. “A fair and just leader would punish Russia for providing Iran with imagery reportedly linked to an attack that wounded twelve of our troops and destroyed a military aircraft. Instead, the president’s actions betray our men and women in uniform and leave the Ukrainian people behind. The U.S. should be standing with our allies, not empowering their adversary. The president must rescind this invitation and hold the authoritarian Russian regime accountable for their destructive actions that harm our American servicemembers.”

“There’s nothing President Trump loves more than cozying up to his dictator buddies. It’s insane and infuriating that a U.S. president spent this week shaking hands with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin and is preparing to roll out the red carpet for Putin at the upcoming G20 Summit in Miami,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “23 brave Americans have lost their lives in this war in Iran, and it is well-documented that Russia has been providing the Iranians with intelligence, satellite imagery, and weapons used against U.S. forces. Trump’s invitation to Putin is not only a betrayal of our troops, but only further emboldens Russia in its support of our enemies and pursuit of their unjust war in Ukraine."

Read the full text of the letter here.

Rep. Cisneros is a Navy Veteran and the former Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness. He currently serves on the House Armed Services Committee, Subcommittee on Military Personnel, and Subcommittee on Intelligence and Special Operations. Rep. Cisneros is a member of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and serves on its leadership team as the Freshman Representative.

title: Cleaver, Booker, Kamlager-Dove Reintroduce Bill Package to End the Exploitation of Incarcerated Workers in Correctional Facilities
text:
(Washington, D.C.) – Today, U.S. Representatives Emanuel Cleaver, II (D-MO) and Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA), along with U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ), a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, reintroduced three bills in a legislative package to end exploitative labor practices in the nation's correctional facilities, where incarcerated individuals often work for pennies an hour without basic workplace protections. The package includes the Ensuring Work Opportunities in Correctional Facilities Act, the Combating Workplace Discrimination in Correctional Facilities Act, and the Correctional Facilities Occupational Safety and Health Act. Congressman Cleaver, Senator Booker, and Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove reintroduced the Fair Wages for Incarcerated Workers Act, legislation that would ensure incarcerated workers are paid at least the federal minimum wage, in March.

“One of the top priorities of America’s correctional system should be ensuring that incarcerated individuals are rehabilitated in such a way that they can successfully reintegrate into society upon their release,” said Congressman Cleaver. “Part of that conversation must focus on ensuring that inmates are afforded the dignities that all Americans deserve, including the protection of basic civil rights, accessibility measures for those with disabilities, and workplace safety standards. I’m proud to stand with Senator Booker and Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove as we introduce this package that will make historic strides on each of these fronts.”

“Corrupt and exploitative practices against incarcerated workers in correctional facilities have turned ‘prison labor’ into a modern-day form of slavery, forcing people to work in dangerous conditions for little to no pay,” said Senator Booker. “There is nothing just about a system that profits from people’s labor while denying them the basic rights, protections, and dignity every worker deserves. I have spent my career fighting for the dignity and humanity of every person, and these bills are part of that fight. Exploiting incarcerated workers also hurts workers outside prison—employers who can pay pennies an hour have no reason to pay fair wages. These bills would end the exploitation of incarcerated workers, guarantee fair wages and safe working conditions, and hold correctional facilities accountable for discriminatory practices. Being behind bars should never mean being stripped of your humanity.”

"The prison labor system in America is a moral stain on this country. Incarcerated workers, like all workers, deserve fair labor standards, fair wages, and dignity," said Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove. "Incarcerated workers, who are disproportionately Black and people of color, shouldn't be paid pennies on the dollar for prison labor that often lacks protections. I’m proud to join Senator Booker and Rep. Cleaver in introducing these crucial pieces of legislation to dramatically reform prison labor. We must end the exploitation."

"When families across the country are struggling to afford the basics, the federal government should not be contributing to depressed wages by operating prisons where people can be required to work for pennies on the dollar and without federal safety protections that are provided to other workers. Senator Booker’s and Representative Cleaver’s legislative package takes an important step to end some of the federal prison system's most exploitative labor practices by protecting people from harassment and retaliation, extending workplace safety protections to prevent physical injuries, and expanding meaningful opportunities to build skills and prepare for reentry. The federal government should be setting the standard for fair and safe work, not exploiting a prison workforce with very little power to demand better," said Nina Patel, ACLU Senior Policy Counsel, Justice Division.

“Tzedek Association is proud to endorse these bills. We believe the best way to reduce the risk of reoffending is to give people the opportunity to work and learn job skills while they’re incarcerated, so they can earn a living when they come home. These bills also help spouses and children who often bear the heaviest burden of incarceration. When a parent goes to prison, the bills still come due and the children still need to eat. Helping families put food on the table is both a humane response and a way to reduce the risk that financial desperation will lead to crime,” said Rabbi Moshe Margaretten, President of Tzedek Association.

Approximately 80 percent of incarcerated individuals work jobs ranging from facility maintenance to fighting wildfires with an average pay of $0.12 to $0.40 per hour. Many also face dangerous working conditions, limited medical care, and few workplace protections. The legislative package would:

Expand pathways to employment: The Ensuring Work Opportunities in Correctional Facilities Act would authorize $210 million for federal prison job training and education programs, increase the number of authorized private-sector work programs from 50 to 100, and expand funding for state and local education and reentry programs.

Protect incarcerated workers from discrimination: The Combating Workplace Discrimination in Correctional Facilities Act would strengthen protections for incarcerated workers who face discrimination in work assignments or who face retaliation, discipline, or sanctions for declining to work.

Hold correctional facilities accountable for unsafe working conditions: The Correctional Facilities Occupational Safety and Health Act would extend federal and state workplace safety protections to incarcerated workers, require regular reporting on labor conditions and potential violations, and provide grants to help state and local governments enforce workplace safety standards.

Earlier this year, Congressman Cleaver, Senator Booker, and Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove reintroduced the Fair Wages for Incarcerated Workers Act, which would ensure incarcerated workers are paid at least the federal minimum wage and would eliminate excessive wage deductions. Kim Kardashian endorsed the bill, saying “No matter where you stand politically, we can all agree: when someone works, they should be paid fairly. And if we want people to return home ready to contribute to society, we need to give them a fair shot.”

All three bills are endorsed by the ACLU, Illinois Alliance for Reentry and Justice, JustLeadership USA, Multifaith Initiative to End Mass Incarceration, National Council of Churches, Reentry Working Group, Safer Foundation, stopthedrugwar.org, and Tzedek Association.

All three bills are cosponsored by Reps. Delia Ramirez (D-IL) , Rashida Tlaib (D-MI), Bonnie Watson Coleman (D-NJ), and Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC).

Official text of the Ensuring Work Opportunities in Correctional Facilities Act is available here.

Official text of the Combating Workplace Discrimination in Correctional Facilities Act is available here.

Official text of the Correctional Facilities Occupational Safety and Health Act is available here.

Emanuel Cleaver, II is the U.S. Representative for Missouri's Fifth Congressional District, which includes Kansas City, Independence, Lee's Summit, Raytown, Grandview, Sugar Creek, Greenwood, Blue Springs, North Kansas City, Gladstone, and Claycomo. He is a member of the exclusive House Financial Services Committee and Ranking Member of the House Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance.

title: DeLauro Demands Israel, Hamas Stop Failing Gaza’s Families as Winter Sets In
text:
WASHINGTON – Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Committee Rosa DeLauro (CT-03) released a statement demanding Israel and Hamas allow humanitarian aid to flow into Gaza as winter storms and flooding make the ongoing humanitarian crisis worse:

“Families in Gaza are heading into another winter in tents that cannot keep out the rain or cold. This suffering is the result of choices being made by those with the power to end it. The current Israeli government and Hamas both made commitments under the ceasefire and they are both failing them – and this failure pulls us further from lasting peace.

“The season’s first winter storm flooded the tents and shelters of about 26,000 households and killed at least five people. Aid groups have only been able to deliver roughly 2,800 tents inside Gaza against a need of about 121,000.

“The Israeli government must stop standing in the way of life-saving aid. Their severe border restrictions are keeping adequate shelter materials out of Gaza. That is unacceptable. They must allow humanitarian aid to surge into the region without delay. Keeping blankets out of Gaza will not make Israel safer. The survival of Palestinian families and Israel’s security are not competing goals and must not be treated as such.

“I have been clear about Hamas from the start, and I will be just as clear about the Israeli government. Neither get a pass when children are freezing in flooded tents. Peace will not come from each side waiting for the other to fold first. Hamas, the Israeli government, and all parties involved must honor their word.”

title: Ranking Member DeSaulnier Statement on Committee on Ethics Reforms Aimed at Improving Investigations of Sexual Misconduct
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), the Ranking Member on the House Committee on Ethics, issued the following statement upon the Committee’s adoption of changes to the Rules of the Committee aimed at improving the speed and transparency of investigations, particularly with respect to allegations of sexual misconduct.

“The House of Representatives must have a zero-tolerance policy for sexual harassment and misconduct and the Committee on Ethics is committed to ensuring that its practices and processes sufficiently hold perpetrators accountable and deliver justice for survivors. title: Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. Confronts Oracle CEO on Harm to Veterans and Urges Congress to Block More VA Contract Funding
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03), confronted Oracle CEO Mike Sicilia at a House Veterans’ Affairs Committee (HVAC) hearing Thursday over direct harm to veterans attributed to failures in Oracle’s electronic health record system and concerns that founder Larry Ellison’s relationship with President Trump has influenced the terms of Oracle’s contract with the VA. The Congresswoman is urging Congress to halt further funding for Oracle’s VA contract after its spending cap rose from $10 billion to more than $27 billion.

“VA’s own doctors have raised red flags about the safety and effectiveness of Oracle’s electronic health record deployment,” Congresswoman Dexter said. “As a former VA physician, my heart breaks for the veterans, their families, and my dedicated colleagues who are clinicians having to micromanage and monitor this disastrous system. As a representative of this government, I’m struggling to understand why we continue to fund a contract that we KNOW is killing our veterans.”

According to VA patient-safety data reported by The Spokesman-Review and The Washington Post, the system played a role in 4,601 reported cases of patient harm, including:

46 major cases, involving permanent lessening of bodily function.

10 catastrophic cases, a category encompassing death or major permanent loss of function.

The VA raised Oracle’s contract ceiling by over $17 billion through a no-bid extension in August. In September, the HVAC voted unanimously, 19-0, to approve Rep. Dexter’s motion to subpoena Oracle’s top executives after the company declined to participate in an earlier hearing. Ellison is scheduled to testify before the committee on Dec. 10.

title: Reps. Fry, Carter, Houlahan Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Strengthen Early Outbreak Detection
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representatives Russell Fry (SC-07), Troy Carter (LA-02), and Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06) introduced the bipartisan Public health Response and Emergency Detection through Integrated wastewater Community Testing (PREDICT) Act. The PREDICT Act would strengthen the nation’s wastewater monitoring capabilities, better positioning the United States to improve early detection of infectious diseases.

U.S. Senators Tim Scott (R-SC) and Cory Booker (D-NJ) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. Senate.

Viral, bacterial, and fungal pathogens such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), measles, West Nile virus, and influenza A and B can shed viral or bacterial material even in the absence of visible symptoms. Wastewater surveillance allows public health officials to analyze sewage to detect viruses and bacteria circulating in a community, identify potential outbreaks more proactively, and hasten responses to better protect communities. As the United States lost its Measles Elimination Status earlier this week, early detection systems will be a crucial tool for public health officials to identify and track infectious diseases as the nation works to stop the measles outbreak, protect American families, and regain the United States’ measles elimination status.

“Wastewater surveillance gives health officials a critical head start, allowing them to detect and contain infectious diseases before they become full-blown outbreaks,” said Rep. Fry. “Early detection tools like proactive wastewater monitoring protects American families and equips communities to stop emerging threats in their tracks. This legislation has the potential to save lives, especially in light of measles continuing to spread across the U.S. I’m hopeful the House will move swiftly in considering our bill.”

“During the COVID-19 crisis, the CDC began incorporating wastewater surveillance as an early warning sign of the spread of the virus, and the public health lessons from that technological innovation should continue to inform and shape legislation and public policy responses to infectious diseases,” said Congressman Carter. “I’m joining Rep. Fry to introduce a bipartisan, bicameral PREDICT Act to fund and broaden the use of wastewater surveillance to additional diseases and regions of the country as well as track the data, promote innovation, and require a national strategic plan for its use from the CDC. With the expansion of this cost-effective technology, Congress and CDC can protect Americans’ health and stop the spread of deadly diseases like COVID-19, measles, and more.”

“Wastewater monitoring can help health officials detect infectious diseases earlier, giving them valuable time to respond and protect their communities,” said Rep. Houlahan. “As pandemic-era funding runs out, we cannot afford to lose that capability. The PREDICT Act would strengthen the CDC’s wastewater surveillance program and help local health departments use this tool to keep Pennsylvanians and all Americans safer.”

“I’m glad to see Representatives Fry and Carter taking the lead on the House companion bill to the PREDICT Act,” said Senator Tim Scott. “Wastewater surveillance is a proven method for identifying signs of infectious diseases earlier, giving public health officials the information they need to respond faster, protect our communities, and prevent outbreaks. This bill would maintain and strengthen this innovative tool, and I look forward to working with my colleagues to get it across the finish line!”

The PREDICT ACT is endorsed by the Wastewater Action Alliance, AdvaMedDx, Big Cities Health Coalition, the National Network of Public Health Institutes, Clear Labs, the Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America, the National Association of Clean Water Agencies, and the American Society for Microbiology.

"Representatives Fry, Carter, and Houlahan have shown exactly the kind of bipartisan leadership we need to protect our communities from the next outbreak, and we are calling on Congress to pass the PREDICT Act now during the lame-duck session," said Kate Hull, Executive Director of the Wastewater Action Alliance. "Communities across America depend on Wastewater monitoring to detect measles, RSV, influenza, and other infectious diseases days or even weeks before people show up sick at hospitals. Americans cannot afford to lose wastewater monitoring, and they are counting on Congress to act."

The PREDICT Act would:

Direct the CDC to award grants to state, tribal, and local health departments, educational institutions, nonprofits, and public-private partnerships to establish, maintain, or improve wastewater surveillance activities

Support advanced testing capabilities so laboratories can detect new pathogens quickly and simultaneously track multiple infectious diseases using consistent testing methods

Improve data transparency and sharing by establishing a timely and accessible dashboard for state and local public health officials

Promote innovation and flexibility by directing the CDC to issue guidance supporting new technologies and adaptable surveillance systems

Require a national strategic plan outlining how the CDC will strengthen wastewater monitoring nationwide and maintain an early-warning system capable of detecting emerging health threats

title: Congressman Hamadeh Reprimands Oracle Executives Over $27B Failure to Deliver Working VA Health Record System
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, Congressman Abe Hamadeh (AZ-08) called for accountability from executives with the software giant, Oracle, during the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs oversight hearing titled “Beyond Go-Live: VA Electronic Health Record Modernization Status Update.”

The hearing examined Oracle’s performance as the prime contractor for the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Electronic Health Record Modernization (EHRM) program. The Committee heard testimony from Oracle Chief Executive Officer Mike Sicilia, who appeared only after being subpoenaed.

In August 2026, the VA increased the ceiling on its EHRM contract with Oracle from approximately $10 billion to an

astonishing $27 billion. Even more troubling, Congress learned of this massive increase through public reporting rather than directly from the VA or Oracle.

Building on the Committee’s September 2, 2026, hearing, Congressman Hamadeh sought answers about the justification for this $17 billion increase, Oracle’s previous commitments to Congress regarding program costs, the quality of training provided to VA personnel, and the accountability necessary to deliver a functioning electronic health record system for our veterans at a reasonable cost to American taxpayers.

After nearly a decade, billions of dollars in expenditures, and a system deployed at only a fraction of VA facilities, Oracle’s performance has been abysmal. The Congressman believes the American people deserve answers, and our veterans deserve far better.

Congressman Hamadeh made his frustration and outrage unmistakably clear, letting Oracle’s leadership know that the company’s performance has fallen far short of what veterans and taxpayers deserve.

Congressman Hamadeh’s comments:

“When we ask you to testify, we are asking to testify in front of the American people. We are representatives. It's embarrassing that it required a subpoena to get you to testify here today. And I look forward to working with my colleagues on the other side of the aisle to ensure that we get justice because from what I see, Google, when you Google Oracle, you are a software company, the biggest software company in the world. Perhaps you were selected to get a job done. It's been 10 years. This isn't we're talking about software. We're not talking about things that are tangible.

I am just shocked because over the past year, we've seen in Minnesota all this fraud, the Somali fraud. This is equivalent to this. This is corporate corruption. I usually don't get animated in meetings like this. I'm deeply offended. I'm a veteran myself.

$17 billion in addition to $10 billion. $27 billion for software that has only been implemented at 19 centers over 10 years. What the hell are we doing? It cost a billion dollars to build the Empire State Building. And it took one year.

What you could do with $27 billion is permanently house every single homeless veteran. $27 billion. You can build a 100,000 Americans homes. You could erase over 3 million American student loan debt for $27 billion.

I haven't seen an apology. I haven't seen any justification really on why you have why you need this extra $17 billion. You know, back when America had honorable people, honorable men and women like capitalists, industrialists, like Carnegie, like Vanderbilt, like Rockefeller, they provided value to society. They understood there's a social contract between the American people and them and their wealth. They built libraries. They invested in the arts and culture and universities.

What the hell has happened? Software for $27 billion.

You all should be ashamed. I'm truly appalled.

It's unacceptable and I refuse to be complicit in that. You know, there's an old saying, there's an old adage that pigs get fat and hogs get slaughtered. I have no idea why the VA continues to invest in this program or to continue to waste money this program because there's nothing to show for it. And I was elected to defend the American public and that's exactly what I intend to do because our veterans, they deserve the best care. They don't deserve this. They're sitting at home looking, seeing this corporation, $27 billion with nothing to show for it. It's unacceptable.

I have no questions for you because you've answered them all over 10 years. Over 10 years. It's embarrassing. No further money should move until Oracle and the VA produce a GAO accepted cost estimate, a fixed deployment schedule, and a clear accounting of what has already been wasted.

What I managed to gather is that you still have $800 million left to draw on your budget. Now, that should be sufficient to fulfill my request. Oracle must justify every single dollar it is charging. The VA must justify every single dollar it's approving. There are no more free passes.

My duty as a congressman and as a member of this committee is to protect our veterans and also punish the corrupt. And I assure you this is just the beginning.”

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Introduces Bill to Keep Chinese Companies Out of American Data Centers
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) introduced the Digital Infrastructure Security Act of 2026 to stop Chinese telecommunications companies from maintaining access to American data centers after losing their licenses over national security concerns. The bill would help protect the systems Americans rely on for banking, healthcare, business, and national defense.

“China has spent years stealing American technology and targeting our communications networks, and we know they're not going to stop,” said Congressman Harrigan. “What concerns me is that we've already identified these companies as national security threats, revoked their licenses, and somehow still allowed them to keep a foothold in our data centers. My bill would prohibit them from operating data centers here or doing business with Americans through cloud services. And they wouldn't be able to get around those restrictions by using a subsidiary or another company to do it for them. When we're talking about the systems that handle Americans' financial information, medical records, and sensitive military data, I think that's a pretty reasonable safeguard.”

“I’m proud to sponsor this legislation that will shore up the safety and national security of our telecommunications systems,” said Congressman Dave Min. “By banning companies that we know are national security threats from owning or operating data centers or cloud services in the United States, we are shoring up the security of this increasingly important critical infrastructure and protecting ourselves from bad actors and foreign adversaries.”

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) previously revoked or denied licenses for China Telecom Americas, China Unicom Americas, and China Mobile USA over national security concerns. But those actions didn't automatically remove their equipment and connections from American data centers. Investigations identified more than 108,000 incidents involving Chinese-linked networks redirecting internet traffic between 2018 and 2025, raising concerns about the potential for foreign interference and the exposure of sensitive information.

The legislation would extend existing telecommunications restrictions to data centers and cloud services, including certain affiliated companies and business partners. The FCC would enforce the law, with fines of up to $1 million per violation or per day for ongoing violations. Existing operations and contracts would have 180 days to comply after enactment, and the bill will now be referred to the appropriate House committee for consideration.

title: Jayapal, Jacobs, Takano, Hirono Commemorate Transgender Day of Remembrance
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) and Sara Jacobs (CA-51), the Co-Chairs of the Congressional Equality Caucus’ Transgender Equality Task Force, Representative Mark Takano (CA-39), Chair of the Congressional Equality Caucus, and Senator Mazie Hirono (D-HI) announced the introduction of a resolution commemorating November 20, 2026, as Transgender Day of Remembrance (TDOR).

“Trans people across this country are facing growing violence, as politicians continue to use their lives and identities as a talking point, diminishing their value and promoting violence against them,” said Jayapal. “On Transgender Day of Remembrance, this resolution honors the lives of those we have tragically lost and reaffirms the remarkable strength and resilience of the trans community. Every person, regardless of their identity, deserves to live free from prejudice, discrimination, and violence. Today, we recommit ourselves to standing against transphobia and violence and building a future where trans people have the safety and security they deserve.”

“I am holding grief and hope, side by side, in my heart today for our trans community,” said Rep. Sara Jacobs. “I am grieving for all of the transgender people who have lost their lives simply for being who they are. But I remain hopeful for the future, that we can and will create a world where everyone, including trans and gender non-conforming folks, can express their identity without fear of discrimination or violence. This resolution serves as our guiding light in the fight for equality, and now it is up to us in Congress to fulfill that promise.”

“Transgender Day of Remembrance is a promise to never forget our transgender siblings taken from us by acts of hate and violence. No one deserves to live in fear because of who they are or how they present themselves to the world—that is why we must all keep fighting to end hate-fueled violence and build a safer future for all,” said Rep. Mark Takano, Chair of the Congressional Equality Caucus. “I’m proud to co-lead this resolution and make this promise alongside Congresswomen Pramila Jayapal and Sara Jacobs, the leaders of our Transgender Equality Task Force, and Senator Mazie Hirono. Together, we will continue fighting for the rights, dignity, and safety of the transgender community.”

“As anti-transgender hate continues to rise nationwide, bolstered by the Trump regime’s harmful rhetoric, supporting and protecting transgender and gender-nonconforming individuals is critical. This resolution honors the lives of those who were lost to violence and educates communities about the dangers and discrimination transgender people face,” said Senator Hirono. “Transgender rights are human rights, and I remain committed to defending everyone’s right to live openly, safely, and without fear.”

Following the still-unsolved murder of Rita Hester, a transgender woman of color, Gwendolyn Ann Smith founded TDOR in 1999 to honor Hester and other transgender people whose lives were lost to violence. In 2026, violent crime against transgender people is still widely prevalent, with 64 percent of transgender and gender-diverse people worldwide having experienced physical or sexual violence during their lifetimes.

The TDOR resolution memorializes the lives of transgender people lost due to violence in the United States and around the world. The text of the full resolution can be found here.

The resolution is also sponsored by Representatives Gabe Amo (RI-01), Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Becca Balint (VT-AL), Wesley Bell (MO-01), Everton Blair (GA-13), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Shontel Brown (OH-11), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Troy Carter (LA-02), Greg Casar (TX-35), Judy Chu (CA-28), Angie Craig (MN-02), Danny David (IL-07), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Diana DeGette (CO-01), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Suzan DelBene (WA-01), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Mark DeSaulnier (CA-10), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Dwight Evans (PA-03), Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Julie Johnson (TX-32), Robin Kelly (IL-02), Timothy Kennedy (NY-26), Ro Khanna (CA-17), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Zoe Lofgren (CA-18), Stephen Lynch (MA-08), Sarah McBride (DE-AL), April McClain Delaney (MD-06), Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), Betty McCollum (MN-04), Jim McGovern (MA-02), LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Christian Menefee (TX-18), Robert Menendez (NJ-08), Grace Meng (NY-06), Gwen Moore (WI-04), Kevin Mullin (CA-15), Jerry Nadler (NY-12), Eleanor Norton (DC-00), Scott Peters (CA-50), Brittany Pettersen (CO-07), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Mark Pocan (WI-02), Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Emily Randall (WA-06), Luz Rivas (CA-29), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Jan Schakowsky (IL-09), Bradley Schneider (IL-10), Brad Sherman (CA-32), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Eric Sorensen (IL-17), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Shri Thanedar (MI-12), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Paul Tonko (NY-20), Ritchie Torres (NY-15), Juan Vargas (CA-52), Aisha Wahab (CA-14), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), Nikema Williams (GA-05), and Frederica Wilson (FL-24).

title: Kaptur & Murray Call for Independent Review of DOE’s Sweeping Rewrite of Safety and Accountability Rules
text:
ICYMI: Kaptur, Murray Demand Energy Department Restore Eliminated Safety Rules, Justify Rewrite of Dozens of Critical Safety and Accountability Measures

Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, and Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, sent a series of letters to the Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Inspector General (OIG), the Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board (DNFSB), and the Government Accountability Office (GAO) asking for each to investigate the sweeping changes that DOE is making to its operating directives. The cumulative impact of these changes risks the safety of work being done at DOE labs, plants, and sites, and they reduce transparency and oversight and risk wasting taxpayer dollars.

In September, Kaptur and Murray called on DOE to restore critical safety rules it scrapped and to justify its revisions to dozens more of the operating directives. But DOE has failed to respond—prompting the lawmakers to call for independent investigation.

In a letter to DOE’s Inspector General, Kaptur and Murray requested the OIG evaluate DOE’s decision to revise forty-six operating directives and cancel four orders, which required DOE to track safety incidents and worker injuries across its labs and sites, and let workers formally challenge technical decisions they believed put safety at risk. The lawmakers wrote: “While the Department claims Project Velocity modernizes operations by shifting from procedural compliance to performance-based accountability, we are concerned that these sweeping rollbacks weaken critical safety protections, eliminate standardized occurrence and injury reporting, and eliminate formal dispute-resolution mechanisms. Further, we are troubled by the lack of transparency around the process of determining which DOE orders were modified or cancelled, who was involved in that process, and what criteria were used to make final determinations under Project Velocity.”

In a letter to DNFSB, the primary independent Federal agency charged by Congress with providing recommendations and oversight regarding defense nuclear facilities, Kaptur and Murray also asked to investigate the changes to the critical safety and accountability measures: “We are deeply concerned over the scale and speed of these regulatory changes, particularly because the changes touch upon nuclear facility safety, quality assurance, conduct of operations, worker training, and incident reporting. We remain very concerned about these simultaneous changes weakening critical safety controls and diminishing independent Federal oversight.”

In a letter to GAO, Kaptur and Murray ask the agency to conduct a comprehensive review of the operating directives. “GAO has raised concerns over the Department’s contract management and project oversight for decades, making this recent wholesale rewrite by the Department of dozens of operating directives highly concerning,” the lawmakers wrote to GAO. “Project Velocity represents a massive expansion of regulatory rollback across dozens of orders and directives. While DOE characterizes these changes as a transition from ‘procedural compliance’ to ‘performance-based accountability,’ we are deeply concerned that the scale and speed of these alterations weaken critical safety protections, undermine independent Federal oversight, shift core responsibilities to Management and Operating (M&O) contractors without adequate safeguards, and potentially increase taxpayer liabilities and costs.”

The lawmakers requested detailed answers and in-depth reviews from all three entities within 30 days to guarantee independent safety oversight is maintained to ensure public health and worker safety are preserved across all nuclear labs, facilities, and sites.

title: Kelly calls on colleagues to fulfill oath of office: "There’s no excuse for any of us to not show up to work"

title: Kelly, Fetterman celebrate Senate passage of Washington's Trail legislation
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Today, U.S. Rep. Mike Kelly (R-PA), U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA), and colleagues celebrated the U.S. Senate's passage of the bipartisan, bicameral Washington’s Trail — 1753 National Historic Trail Feasibility Study Act, which passed by unanimous consent on Thursday.

In July 2025, Kelly introduced the bill in the U.S. House of Representatives and Fetterman introduced the bill in the U.S. Senate in May 2026. The Senate bill is co-sponsored by U.S. Senators Dave McCormick (R-PA), Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV), Jim Justice (R-WV), Tim Kaine (D-VA), and Mark Warner (D-VA). The House legislation is co-sponsored by Representatives Chris Deluzio (D-PA) and Glenn "GT" Thompson (R-PA).

“By designating Washington’s Trail as a national historic trail, we create an opportunity to preserve this history, to build community pride, to connect communities, promote economic revitalization, and create jobs while telling this story of George Washington and the birth of our nation,” said Rep. Kelly. “I commend the work of local volunteers who have brought George Washington’s journey to life. Today’s vote moves us one step closer toward sharing this legacy with current and future generations.”

“We are one step closer to preserving Washington’s Trail and protecting this crucial piece of American history as a lasting educational tool for generations to come. I’m grateful the Senate passed my bill unanimously today and urge my House colleagues to finish the job," said Sen. Fetterman.

“Washington’s Trail tells an important story about our nation’s founding, and I’m proud to see this bipartisan legislation pass the Senate,” said Senator McCormick. “I’m grateful to Senator Fetterman and our colleagues for working together to help preserve this critical piece of Pennsylvania’s history, promote tourism, and make it a National Historic Trail.”

The bill now heads to the U.S. House of Representatives for consideration.

BACKGROUND

Washington’s Trail follows George Washington’s path in 1753 on his way to Fort LeBoeuf in what is now known as Waterford, PA in Erie County. The trail starts in Virginia and includes portions of Maryland, West Virginia, and crosses several Western Pennsylvania counties.

In Pennsylvania, the trail features scenic markers and landmarks highlighting major tourist and historical destinations such as the Fort Pitt Museum in Pittsburgh, the Old Economy Village in Ambridge, DeBence Antique Music World Museum in Franklin, Fort LeBoeuf Museum in Erie, and many more iconic places.

title: Congressman David Kustoff Applauds FCC Action to Combat Contraband Cellphones in Prisons
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman David Kustoff (R-TN-08) today applauded Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr and the Commission for approving final rules that allow state and local correctional facilities to use cellphone jamming technology to combat contraband devices.

“In correctional facilities across our country, inmates are using contraband cellphones to run drug operations, order violent attacks, and organize escapes,” said Congressman Kustoff. “I applaud Chairman Carr and the FCC for giving correctional officials another tool to stop inmates from directing crime from behind bars. Today’s vote is an important step toward protecting correctional officers and our communities, and I will keep working to make this authority permanent in federal law.”

Background:

Congressman Kustoff introduced H.R. 2350, the Cellphone Jamming Reform Act of 2025, on March 26, 2025. Senator Tom Cotton (R-AR) introduced the Senate companion, S. 1137. The bill would prevent the FCC from stopping state and federal correctional facilities from operating jamming systems in inmate housing areas. Congressman Kustoff has led this effort in the House since 2019.

The FCC’s action establishes a framework for eligible state and local correctional facilities to use radio frequency jamming technology against contraband cellphones. Facilities may use the technology, but are not required to. The rules include safeguards to protect 911 calls and wireless service outside prison walls. Today’s decision builds on the work of Congressman Kustoff, whose Cellphone Jamming Reform Act would give state and federal prisons the authority to use cellphone jamming technology without interference from the FCC.

title: REPS LIEU AND CASTEN INTRODUCE BILL TO COMBAT INSIDER TRADING ON PREDICTION MARKETS
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - U.S. Representatives Ted Lieu (D-Los Angeles County) and Sean Casten (D-IL) introduced the Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act of 2026, legislation to incentivize whistleblowers to report information to federal law enforcement agencies about potential insider trading that occurs on prediction market platforms.

“Government insiders should not be able to profit from betting on U.S. military operations or the contents of a President’s speech. They should not be able to use their positions of public trust to manipulate prediction markets,” said Congressman Lieu. “The Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act of 2026 will encourage whistleblowers to report insider trading on prediction market platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket. This blatant corruption needs to end.”

“It is reprehensible that government insiders are profiting off advanced knowledge of when and where the United States will conduct military strikes,” said Rep. Sean Casten. “Prediction markets have a serious insider trading problem, and the current Administration is engaged in corruption of epic proportions. By encouraging whistleblowers to come forward and report wrongdoing, we can take an important step in cracking down on insider trading to restore accountability and public confidence in the U.S. rule of law.”

Specifically, the Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act would establish a new program at the Department of Justice (DOJ) where eligible whistleblowers can anonymously report original, credible, and crucial information about suspected fraudulent activity involving prediction markets. Whistleblowers would potentially receive financial compensation if such information leads to a successful enforcement action.

In recent months, several high-profile examples have emphasized the need for legislation like the Policing Insider Trading in Prediction Markets Act. For example, one anonymous trader has made nearly $1 million from dozens of suspiciously timed and accurate bets on military actions that the United States has taken against Iran. Another trader made more than $550,000 from bets that Iran’s Supreme Leader would be removed, just before his assassination. President Trump’s teleprompter operator earned more than $100,000 by betting on which words the President would use in his speeches. Lastly, the Nobel Institute is investigating a bet placed by a newly created account on Venezuelan opposition leader María Machado winning the Nobel Peace Prize hours before the announcement, resulting in a profit of more than $50,000.

Text of the legislation can be found here.

The legislation is endorsed by Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW), Project on Government Oversight (POGO), Transparency International U.S., the Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA), Americans for Financial Reform, and Public Citizen.

Earlier this year, Reps. Casten and Lieu led 54 House Democrats in urging the DOJ to more aggressively pursue insider trading violations that occur on prediction markets. Following their letter, the DOJ has increased enforcement against suspected government and corporate insiders who have misused confidential information for personal financial gain, and is reportedly investigating offshore and unregulated prediction market platforms that have created new avenues for insider trading and may be illegally serving U.S. customers.

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces Bill to Crack Down on SNAP Abuse, Ban Taxpayer-Funded Food Deliveries
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (Nov. 20, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace introduced the No Online Delivery Allowed for SNAP Households Act, or the NO DASH Act, legislation to crack down on SNAP abuse and put an end to taxpayer-funded food delivery orders through the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program.

Under current law, SNAP benefits may be used for qualifying online food purchases, including orders for delivery. The NO DASH Act would close this loophole by requiring online SNAP food orders to be picked up at the retail food store or another designated location by a member of the recipient’s household or a caregiver.

“SNAP was created to temporarily supplement nutrition needs, helping families put food on the table, not turn hardworking taxpayers into a permanent personal food delivery service,” said Congresswoman Mace. “Government assistance should serve those who genuinely need it, not pay for the convenience of those perfectly capable of picking up their own groceries. Every SNAP dollar comes from the American taxpayer, and taxpayers deserve accountability for how their money is spent. It is time to restore common sense and put guardrails back on a program taxpayers fund.”

According to the U.S. Department of Agriculture, online SNAP and P-EBT purchases have grown rapidly in just a few years. In 2020, just $234 million in benefits were used for online purchases. By 2023, online redemptions had skyrocketed to $2.3 billion in a single quarter, accounting for 8.8% of all benefit usage. Online purchasing has also expanded from just seven participating retailers in 45 states to 341 retailers nationwide. As online SNAP spending continues to grow, we need stronger guardrails to ensure taxpayer dollars are used responsibly.

The NO DASH Act would:

Prohibit SNAP-funded delivery orders: Prevent the USDA from approving retailers to accept SNAP benefits for online food delivery orders.

Require in-person pickup: Require online food orders purchased with SNAP benefits to be picked up by a household member or caregiver.

Preserve caregiver access: Allow caregivers assisting the elderly or chronically ill to pick up food orders on their behalf.

The legislation directs the Secretary of Agriculture to issue implementing regulations within 180 days of enactment. The changes would take effect 180 days after enactment.

title: Congresswoman McCollum Statement on the Passage of the Senate Permitting Package (S. 5653)
text:
Congresswoman Betty McCollum (D), Dean of the Minnesota Congressional Delegation, issued the following statement on the Senate’s passage of S. 5653, the Senate permitting package:

“I strongly oppose the Senate permitting bill in its current form because it makes sweeping changes to the permitting process that radically undercuts Tribal sovereignty and protections of our most treasured land and water that belong to all Americans in order to speed up the agenda of private industries.

“Building out transmission lines is essential to the clean energy transition, but it should not come at the cost of permanently destroying our nation’s most treasured public lands or undermining Tribal sovereignty.

“The bill threatens our nation’s most treasured public lands like the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness. A provision in the bill would permanently lock in any leases that the Trump administration might issue to build a toxic sulfide ore copper mine in the headwaters of the Boundary Waters. No future administration would be able to undo the leases—even if they were issued illegally. And it’s not just the Boundary Waters that are under threat. This same provision could allow the Trump administration to permanently pollute the Arctic National Refuge, Chaco Canyon, and Bear’s Ears National Monument with oil, gas, and mining development.

“The bill would also substantively change the National Historic Preservation Act Section 106 process that helps Tribal Nations protect and preserve cultural heritage sites. Yet, when the bill was negotiated between the Senate and the White House there was no consultation with Tribal Nations. We must respect the sovereignty of tribal nations and protect their right to preserve cultural heritage sites. At a time when the Federal government is turning away from meaningful consultation with Tribal Nations, Congress should be strengthening—not weakening—the process to ensure that when we build vital infrastructure in this country, it does not come at the cost of desecrating sacred places, harming ancestral lands, and ignoring the cultural heritage of Tribal Nations.”

title: Reps. Analilia Mejia and Everton Blair Introduce the POSSIBLE Act to Shield Seniors’ Social Security from Student Loan Garnishment
text:
For Immediate Release: November 20, 2026

Contact: Beth Wiesinger | NJ11AMPress@Mail.House.Gov

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Representatives Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) and Everton Blair Jr. (GA-13) have introduced the Protect Our Seniors’ Security and Income by Balancing Loan Exemptions (POSSIBLE) Act, proposed legislation to protect low-income older Americans from having their Social Security benefits garnished over defaulted federal student loans.

Across the United States, 3.5 million Americans aged 60 and older carry more than $125 billion in student loan debt. The number of people 60 years of age or older who have student loan debt has increased sixfold over the last 20 years, and their debt load has increased nearly 2000%. More than one-third of Social Security beneficiaries with student loans rely on those monthly Social Security checks just to make ends meet.

Under current federal law, the government may garnish up to 15% of a senior's Social Security check if they are late on their federal student loan payments, provided that they are left with at least 750 a month (9,000 a year). Congress set the $750 threshold in 1996 and has never updated it for inflation, despite prices rising by 115% over the past three decades, meaning a dollar in 1996 holds the purchasing power of roughly $2.15 today.

“As the cost of education climbs, more than 450,000 seniors who rely on Social Security face having their benefits seized over defaulted student loans. Many of these seniors already live on limited incomes and are forced to choose between prescriptions and groceries. Taking their benefits only deepens that strain. After a lifetime of work, our seniors have a right to the security they were promised. I’m proud to co-lead the POSSIBLE Act to ease this burden, because seniors deserve a government that works for them, not against them. We must protect their benefits and keep that money in their pockets.” said Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11).

With nearly half of American seniors living on less than $30,000 annually and roughly 40% of older workers holding no retirement savings, garnishing Social Security benefits forces tens of millions of older people to choose between housing, groceries, familial support and medical care.

“I’m proud to co-lead the POSSIBLE Act. No senior should ever have to worry about making ends meet because they chose to pursue an education and the government took their one financial lifeline," said Congressman Everton Blair Jr. (GA-13). “Our job is to put money back into people's pockets and help them live with dignity, not add to their financial hardships. This is especially true for seniors who have worked a lifetime with the promise of Social Security. This bill eases the pressure of rising costs by protecting the benefits that our seniors have rightfully earned.”

The POSSIBLE Act modernizes federal debt collection rules by:

Raising the protected benefit floor: Seniors will keep at least 1,183 a month(14,196 a year) before the federal government can garnish a single penny

Keeping up with inflation: The protected income threshold will automatically adjust every year based on the Consumer Price Index to match with the rising cost of living, and

Delivering immediate relief: Protections apply retroactively to protect seniors who are already dealing with old student loan debt, in addition to it applying to new borrowers.

Reps. Mejia and Blair remain committed to fighting for the economic security of older Americans and call on their House colleagues to join them in advancing commonsense solutions to this growing crisis.

title: Meuser Moves to Impose Heightened Penalties and Mandatory Minimums for Fraudsters
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.— Today, Congressman Dan Meuser (PA-09) introduced the Federal Accountability for Fraud Offenders (FAFO) Act, legislation that would deter fraud in taxpayer-funded programs and hold fraudsters accountable by establishing mandatory minimum prison sentences.

Currently, federal law establishes maximum penalties for those who defraud federal programs and steal taxpayer money. However, these penalties are rarely enforced, with most convicted criminals who stole millions of taxpayer dollars being sentenced to a year in prison or even probation. The FAFO Act would ensure that criminals are held accountable for defrauding government programs and effectively deter future fraud schemes.

The FAFO Act also makes state and local government officials responsible if they knowingly or recklessly ignore fraud. This provision ensures that officials entrusted with administering taxpayer-funded programs cannot disregard fraudulent activity without facing significant consequences.

“Billions of dollars in taxpayer funds are lost to fraud, yet individuals who commit these crimes too often receive little more than probation,” said Congressman Meuser. “Identifying fraud is an important first step, but those who defraud taxpayer-funded programs must face penalties that reflect the severity of their crimes. The FAFO Act establishes mandatory minimum sentences to strengthen enforcement, deter future fraud, and ensure that stealing from American taxpayers carries meaningful consequences.”

Background:

Congressman Meuser is a member of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, which has identified $260.7 billion in potential fraud across federal agencies and stopped approximately $72 billion in fraudulent payments. This summer, the Congressman participated in a Task Force roundtable, where members discussed the need for stronger criminal penalties to deter bad actors and ensure individuals who defraud federal programs face meaningful consequences.

Individuals convicted of defrauding taxpayer-funded programs are not always held fully accountable for their crimes. In Minneapolis, an individual who defrauded the state's Medicaid program of $2.2 million received no jail time and just five years' probation. Under the FAFO Act, this individual would have faced a mandatory minimum of 10 years in prison, helping ensure that penalties reflect the seriousness of the offense and deter future fraud.

The FAFO Act would establish mandatory minimum prison sentences for individuals convicted of defrauding taxpayer-funded programs. Instead of allowing criminals to walk away with just a slap on the wrist, this legislation would require fraudsters to serve at least one year in prison, with sentences increasing based on the total amount of money stolen from the government. All violations would carry a maximum penalty of life imprisonment. The legislation would also prohibit courts from granting probation or suspending sentences for individuals convicted of benefit fraud.

title: Rep. Rogers Honored with W. Stuart Symington Award for Contributions to National Defense
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Rep. Mike Rogers (AL-03), Chairman of the House Armed Services Committee, was presented with the W. Stuart Symington Award by the Air and Space Force Association for his contributions to national defense, particularly his leadership in the establishment of the United States Space Force. The Symington Award, named for the first Secretary of the Air Force, is the AFA’s highest civilian honor. Previous honorees include President Ronald Reagan, President George H.W. Bush, Senator John McCain, among others.

“I am honored to be the 2026 recipient of the W. Stuart Symington Award,” said Rep. Rogers. “Now more than ever, air and space dominance are critical to our national defense. The Air and Space Force Association has been a long-time ally of this mission, and I am thankful for their leadership in this subject. Many of my personal heroes have received the Symington Award, and I truly count this as a career highlight.”

“Few in Congress have done as much for our nation’s defense as Representative Rogers. His more than two decades on the House Armed Services Committee have helped ensure our Airmen, Guardians, and warfighters across the Joint Force have the capabilities and capacity they need for a strong national defense. AFA sincerely thanks him for his dedication to our military, especially his early support of the Space Force,” said AFA Chair of the Board, Kathleen Ferguson.

Background:

title: Moran Introduces Legislation to Give Access to Health Savings Accounts for Small Business Employees
text:
U.S. Representative Nathaniel Moran (TX-01) introduced the Main Street Health Savings Act to give small business owners greater flexibility to pair affordable bronze health plans with employee health savings accounts (HSAs).

“Small businesses drive the East Texas economy, and their employees deserve the same tools to save for health care as anyone else,” said Rep. Moran. “This legislation would allow employers to offer lower-premium health plans while contributing to their employees’ health savings accounts (HSAs), reducing health care costs for workers. This legislation gives Main Street workers more control over their health care dollars.”

This legislation:

Gives small business workers that enroll in a bronze plan offered by their employer the same HSA opportunity as Americans who buy their own coverage. Bronze plans purchased as individual coverage already qualify for an HSA. This bill extends HSA qualifications to bronze plans offered by small employers.

Gives small businesses another way to offer valuable benefits. Small employers can pair an affordable bronze plan with an HSA, which helps them compete with larger companies for workers.

Background:

An HSA lets people set aside money tax-free to pay for medical expenses. Contributions are tax-deductible, the balance grows tax-free, and withdrawals for qualified medical costs are not taxed. To contribute, a person must be covered by a qualifying health plan. The Working Families Tax Cuts law made all bronze plans a qualifying health plan for HSAs when purchased through the individual market but it left out bronze plans that small employers offer to their workers. This legislation would create parity for bronze plans offered by employers with those purchased through the individual market.

title: Congresswoman Nikema Williams Leads Push to Restore CDC’s Drowning Prevention Program
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Nikema Williams (GA-05) led 14 congressional colleagues in a letter to Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., demanding the department restore the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s (CDC) Drowning Prevention Program after the Trump Administration effectively eliminated the program and terminated the federal employees responsible for drowning surveillance, research, and prevention.

Congress established dedicated funding for drowning prevention at CDC in Fiscal Year 2022 and subsequently provided $2 million annually for this work. The funding supported proven drowning-prevention programs with national organizations serving underserved and diverse youth, state drowning-surveillance efforts, and the development of a national water-safety plan.

Between 2020 and 2022, more than 4,500 people died from drowning each year. And this burden is disproportionate: American Indian and Alaska Native people experienced the highest drowning rates from 2019 through 2022, followed by Black Americans, whose drowning death rate increased 28 percent in 2021 compared with 2019. Drowning remains the leading cause of death for children ages one through four and the second-leading cause of unintentional injury death among children ages five through fourteen.

The Members wrote:

“Eliminating the federal personnel responsible for this work raises serious questions about who is now responsible for carrying out CDC’s drowning-prevention functions, whether congressionally directed activities are continuing, and whether the agency retains sufficient capacity to provide timely and comprehensive drowning surveillance data. These concerns are especially troubling given the disproportionate impact of drowning on children and historically underserved communities, whose safety depends on sustained investment in accessible water-safety education and evidence-based prevention efforts”

“Given these concerns, we request that HHS restore CDC’s Drowning Prevention Program and the federal expertise necessary to carry out its surveillance, research, and prevention responsibilities.”

In the letter, the Members requested answers to the following questions:

How many CDC employees working primarily or substantially on drowning prevention were terminated, placed on administrative leave, reassigned, or otherwise affected by reductions in force since January 20, 2025?

Which office and personnel are currently responsible for CDC’s drowning surveillance, research, prevention, and public-education activities, and how many full-time equivalent employees are assigned to this work?

How has HHS obligated or expended funds appropriated by Congress for CDC drowning prevention since Fiscal Year 2025, and have any such funds been withheld, redirected, or left unobligated?

What is the status of drowning-prevention research, state surveillance support, community partnerships, and other projects that were underway before the April 2025 reductions in force, including work intended to identify populations at greatest risk and evaluate effective prevention strategies?

What steps will HHS and CDC take to ensure the federal government maintains the personnel, expertise, and resources necessary to conduct drowning surveillance and prevention, regularly analyze and publish national drowning data, support state and local surveillance efforts, evaluate evidence-based interventions, and provide timely water-safety guidance to the public?

This letter was co-signed by Rep. Gabe Amo (RI-01), Rep. Shontel Brown (OH-11), Rep. Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Rep. Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Rep. Val Hoyle (OR-04), Rep. William Keating (MA-09), Rep. Timothy Kennedy (NY-26), Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Rep. LaMonica McIver (NJ-10), Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Rep. Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25).

This letter was endorsed by The YMCA of Metro Atlanta.

title: Reps. Onder and Vindman Reintroduce the Student Loan Disclosure Transparency Act of 2026
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

November 20, 2026

Contact: Brooke Morgan

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Representative Bob Onder (R-MO), alongside Representative Eugene Vindman (D-VA), reintroduced the bipartisan Student Loan Disclosure Transparency Act of 2026 to improve transparency in federal student loan disclosures.

The legislation would require disclosures before loan disbursement, provide projected monthly payment amounts, establish required monthly disclosures, and direct a report to Congress on consumer testing. The bill would take effect beginning with the first award year that starts at least 12 months after enactment.

“Students and families deserve clear, straightforward information about the costs of attending college and the financial commitments that come with borrowing for their education. As a member of the House Education and Workforce Committee, I am committed to ensuring borrowers understand exactly what they are paying for. The bipartisan Student Loan Disclosure Transparency Act would require loan holders to provide regular monthly disclosures detailing key fees and interest rates, giving students and families the information they need to make informed decisions about their education and financial future,” said Congressman Bob Onder.

“Students and families deserve to know exactly what they are signing up for before taking on tens of thousands of dollars in student loan debt,” said Congressman Vindman. “Borrowers should not have to navigate confusing fine print or guess what their monthly payments will look like. This commonsense legislation will give students clear, straightforward information about the true cost of their loans so they can make informed decisions about their education and their financial future. Providing that level of transparency is the least the federal government can do.”

“The American Council on Education is proud to endorse the Student Loan Disclosure Transparency Act. This bipartisan bill will ensure that federal student loan borrowers truly understand the terms and conditions of their loans by requiring the lender to provide a separate disclosure in a format that is simple and easy to understand. Any choice to borrow should be an informed choice, but too often students and families take on debt not fully aware of their obligations. The Student Loan Disclosure Transparency Act would be an important step in supporting students and families to afford higher education. We urge Congress to put students first by passing this bill before the end of the 119th Congress.” - Ted Mitchell, President, American Council on Education

“NASFAA is pleased to endorse the Student Loan Disclosure Transparency Act, which gives students clear, timely information about what their loans will cost, from the first disbursement through the last payment,” says Karen McCarthy, Vice President of Public Policy and Federal Relations at NASFAA. “Importantly, its consumer testing requirements will help ensure that disclosures are clear, meaningful, and effective. Good information leads to better decisions, and this bill puts that information in students’ hands when it can make the most difference.”

“American families deserve to know what they are getting into when they take on student loan debt. Clear, regular disclosures help borrowers understand what they owe, how interest grows, and what they will ultimately repay, promoting transparency and responsible borrowing. Informed borrowers make smarter financial decisions, and that is good for students, families, and taxpayers alike.” - Christopher Schorr, Director of Higher Education Policy at America First Policy Institute

Click HERE to read the full bill.

Background Information

The federal student loan portfolio now stands at roughly $1.7 trillion, with nearly 43 million Americans carrying federal student loan debt. Washington has spent years debating proposals to refinance loans or cancel debt. But there is a simpler principle on which we should all agree: before the federal government lends a student tens of thousands of dollars, that student should know exactly what the loan will cost.

For many young Americans, choosing a college and deciding how much to borrow are among the first major financial decisions they will ever make. Yet students are too often asked to accept substantial debt based on disclosures filled with technical language, incomplete information, and repayment estimates that are difficult to understand.

The bipartisan Student Loan Disclosure Transparency Act of 2026 is a common-sense reform that would give borrowers clear, accessible information about their federal student loans.

Before a loan is disbursed, borrowers would receive a straightforward disclosure showing the principal amount, interest rate, Annual Percentage Rate (APR) calculated under Truth in Lending Act (TILA) standards, projected monthly payment, and total amount expected to be repaid over the life of the loan.

The bill would also require borrowers to receive monthly statements throughout the life of the loan, including while they are attending school or in deferment or forbearance. These statements would clearly show the outstanding balance and the interest that continues to accrue.

Finally, borrowers would receive plain-language explanations of their repayment options, including notice that an income-driven repayment plan may increase the total amount repaid and that certain forgiven balances may be treated as taxable income.

These are the kinds of basic disclosures Americans expect when taking out other significant loans. Federal student loans should not be held to a lower standard. Transparency alone will not solve every challenge in higher education, but students cannot make responsible decisions without accurate information. This legislation will empower borrowers to understand the commitment they are making and choose the path that is best for both their educational and financial futures.

title: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN BLASTS VERIZON PROPOSAL TO END LANDLINE SERVICE AND DISCONNECT THE HUDSON VALLEY
text:
Verizon is seeking FCC approval to remove copper landlines across New York State – including in the Hudson Valley

Ryan is urging the FCC to reject Verizon’s proposal, flagging concerns about the impact on Hudson Valley seniors and rural communities who rely on landline service for ease and dependable connection

WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Pat Ryan is raising the alarm on a Verizon proposal to end copper landline service in the Hudson Valley. In a letter to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), Ryan urged Chairman Brendan Carr to reject the proposal that would eliminate dependable phone service for thousands of his constituents.

“In many parts of the Hudson Valley, landlines are often the only reliable way for folks to stay connected – but now Verizon is trying to rip that critical service away without a thought of how it will impact us,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “That’s unacceptable – especially for seniors who rely on landlines for their safety and medical needs, and for rural families that can’t count on reliable cell service. No one in the Hudson Valley should have to worry about losing their ability to dial 911 during an emergency or call a loved one when the power goes out just because Verizon wants to cut costs. I’m urging the FCC to tell Verizon to pump the breaks and present an actual, viable alternative instead of just ripping the rug out from under us.”

Ryan’s September letter to Chairman Carr is included below.

Dear Chairman Carr,

I write on behalf of my constituents in New York’s 18th Congressional District to express concern regarding Verizon's proposal before the FCC to phase out traditional copper landline telephone service. While I support continued investment in modern infrastructure, many of my constituents — particularly seniors who depend on landlines for ease, safety, and even medical devices, and rural residents who lack access to reliable cellular coverage — could be left without dependable phone and emergency service if this transition is not handled with care. I respectfully urge the FCC to reject Verizon’s proposal so that no customer is moved off copper service until a genuinely reliable, verified alternative is available at their location, and to guarantee strong consumer protections throughout.

I appreciate the Commission's attention to this important matter and welcome the opportunity to discuss it further with your office.

Sincerely,

Patrick Ryan

Member of Congress

title: On Anniversary of H.R. 40 Introduction, Pressley Continues Push for Reparations and Reparative Justice Agenda
text:
Transcript: On Anniversary of H.R. 40 Introduction, Pressley Continues Push for Reparations and Reparative Justice Agenda

November 17, 2026

U.S. House of Representatives

Mr. Speaker,

This week, we honor a bridge between generations and recommit ourselves to the work of repair.

That history runs through Massachusetts. State Senator Bill Owens drafted reparations legislation that helped provide a model for Congressman John Conyers’ federal effort.

On November 20, 1989, Congressman Conyers introduced the federal reparations commission bill that would evolve into H.R. 40.

Today, I am honored to carry H.R. 40 and clear-eyed about our responsibility to advance reparations.

This movement did not begin in Washington. It was carried here by organizers, advocates, and lawmakers who refused to accept that justice for Black people must always wait.

Same fight. New generation. An obligation still unmet.

This is about confronting the injustices of our past and repairing the harm that endures in Black folks’ housing, school funding, health care and the ability to build and pass on wealth.

Justice delayed is justice denied, and we will not back down in our pursuit of healing and reparative justice.

Same fight. New generation.

I yield.
