title: Pressley, Warren, Scanlon, 46 Lawmakers Renew Push To Reduce Violence Against Individuals with Mental Health Conditions and Disabilities
text:
Bill Text (PDF) | One-Pager (PDF)

WASHINGTON – Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) and Representative Mary Gay Scanlon (D-Penn.), along with 46 of their Democratic colleagues, reintroduced the Mental Health Justice Act to reduce violence against individuals with mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and intellectual and/or developmental disabilities. The bill would fund grants for state and local governments to send trained mental health professionals instead of police when 911 or 988 is called because an individual is experiencing a mental health or substance use crisis.

“Community members experiencing a mental health crisis should be met with compassion, resources, and care—NOT criminalization,” said Representative Pressley. “Criminalizing mental health crises only makes our communities less safe. That’s why I’m proud to reintroduce the Mental Health Justice Act alongside Senator Warren and Congresswoman Scanlon to ensure mental health professionals—instead of police—can support people in moments of crisis.”

“Part of keeping our communities safe is keeping people suffering from a mental health or substance use crisis safe,” said Senator Warren. “Rather than criminalizing mental health, this legislation would make it easier for trained mental health professionals to respond when someone needs help or support—not jail time.”

“Individuals experiencing a mental health crisis should be connected with mental health professionals, not put on a one-way track to jail,” said Representative Scanlon. “Too often we see the tragic consequences of encounters between people in crisis and law enforcement officers who lack the appropriate support or training to handle mental health issues. I’m proud to introduce this bill with Senator Warren to keep both citizens and law enforcement professionals safe.”

The Mental Health Justice Act would:

Create a federal grant program for state, local, and Tribal governments to hire, train, and dispatch mental health professionals as first responders in place of police during mental health and substance use emergencies;

Prioritize funding for communities with high rates of arrest and incarceration of people with behavioral health needs, and reward jurisdictions that successfully reduce incarceration rates and death rates for people with mental health conditions and intellectual and/or developmental disabilities;

Fund the training of mental health first responders and dispatch centers in de-escalation techniques and developmentally appropriate interventions;

Require grant recipients to report to HHS on key program outcomes, and direct HHS and DOJ to study the long-term impact of these programs on diversion from arrest and incarceration;

Direct HHS and DOJ to assist jurisdictions with implementation of alternative crisis response programs and to publish best practices to assist local leaders with implementation.

This bill is joined by Senators Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), and Representatives Jim McGovern (D-Mass.), Mark Pocan (D-Wis.), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-Ill.), Stephen Lynch (D-Mass.), Bonnie Watson Coleman (D-N.J.), Kevin Mullin (D-Calif.), Jill Tokuda (D-Hawaii), Betty McCollum (D-Minn.), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), Deborah Ross (D-N.C.), Judy Chu (D-Calif.), Jonathan L. Jackson (D-Ill.), Hank Johnson (D-Ga.), Lois Frankel (D-Fla.), Greg Casar (D-Texas), Becca Balint (D-Vt.), Troy Carter (D-La.), Nikema Williams (D-Ga.), Ritchie Torres (D-N.Y.), Norma J. Torres (D-Calif.), Scott Peters (D-Calif.), Lauren Underwood (D-Ill.), Nydia Velázquez (D-N.Y.), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-D.C.), Juan Vargas (D-Calif.), Sharice Davids (D-Kan.), Mike Quigley (D-Ill.), Josh Gottheimer (D-N.J.), Madeleine Dean (D-Pa.), Adam Smith (D-Wash.), Delia Catalina Ramirez (D-Ill.), Ed Case (D-Hawaii), J. Luis Correa (D-Calif.), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-Fla.), Nanette Barragán (D-Calif.), André Carson (D-Ind.), Debbie Dingell (D-Mich.), Yvette Clarke (D-N.Y.), and Lizzie Fletcher (D-Texas).

The Mental Health Justice Act is endorsed by 31 advocacy organizations: American Civil Liberties Union, Center for Policing Equity, the Orange County Sheriff’s Office, National Alliance on Mental Illness, The Kennedy Forum, CommunicationFIRST, Access Ready Inc., Autistic Women & Nonbinary Network, Bend the Arc: Jewish Action, National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, Autism Society of America, American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, American Association on Health and Disability, Lakeshore Foundation, Association of University Centers on Disabilities, Postpartum Support International, Union for Reform Judaism, National Association of Councils on Developmental Disabilities, Alternative Mobile Services Association, Justice in Aging, American Society of Addiction Medicine, National Health Care for the Homeless Council, Clinical Social Work Association, National Association of County Behavioral Health and Developmental Disability Directors, American Association of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, Association for Behavioral Health and Wellness, National Action Network, American Association of Suicidology, Bazelon Center for Mental Health Law, American Psychological Association, and the Disability Rights Education & Defense Fund.

Bill text can be accessed here, and a one-pager on the bill can be accessed here.

Throughout her career, Congresswoman Pressley has been a tireless advocate for trauma-conscious policymaking.

She leads the Ending PUSHOUT Act and Counseling Not Criminalization in Schools Actto collectively end the discriminatory treatment of Black and brown students, LGBTQIA+ students, and students with disabilities in schools, and invest in safe, nurturing learning environments for all students. She also leads the STRONG Support for Children Act to support communities in addressing childhood trauma through healing-centered, neighborhood-based, gender-responsive, culturally specific, and trauma-informed approaches that acknowledge the impact of systemic racism and inequities over generations.

In November 2026, Rep. Pressley reintroduced the Support Through Loss Act to support those navigating pregnancy loss by establishing new paid leave benefits for workers across the nation who are experiencing painful, traumatic challenges while seeking to start or grow their family.

In February 2026, Rep. Pressley boycotted Donald Trump’s State of the Union address and instead uplifted children who have been detained and traumatized by ICE as honorary guests.

In February 2024, Rep. Pressley sent a letter to the Department of Health and Human Services to address the growing crisis of childhood trauma that was exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic.

In March 2023, Rep. Pressley celebrated $250,000 in Community Project Funding she secured for Big Sister Association of Greater Boston (Big Sister) to support its one-to-one mentoring and enrichment programs for girls.

In March 2021, Rep. Pressley sent a letter to President Biden calling on him to address the nation’s growing trauma crisis and laying out a series of steps the administration should take to confront the far-reaching hurt plaguing our communities and our nation. In April 2021, she published an op-ed where she reflected on the collective pain experienced by communities in her district over the past year.

In July 2019, she worked with Chairman Cummings to convene the first-ever Congressional hearings on childhood trauma. Watch Congresswoman Pressley’s full question line and follow-up questions here and here.

As a Boston City Councilor, she convened the Council’s first-ever listening-only session to hear directly from those impacted by the trauma of community gun violence.

title: U.S. Senate Unanimously Passes Rep. Ritchie Torres’ Bipartisan Lithium-Ion Battery Safety Bill
text:
Yesterday, the Senate unanimously passed H.R. 973 the Setting Consumer Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries Act, bipartisan legislation led in the House by Congressman Ritchie Torres (NY-15). The bill passed the House by a 365-42 vote in April 2025 and passed the Senate by unanimous consent on November 19, 2026.

The bill would require the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) to adopt safety standards for rechargeable lithium-ion batteries and electrical systems used in e-bikes, e-scooters and other micromobility devices. It also provides for future updates to the standards and requires the CPSC to report to Congress on related fires, explosions and other hazards.

The urgency of these protections was underscored by a devastating fire at NYCHA Patterson Houses in the Bronx on October 28th, when a lithium-ion battery-powered e-bike sparked an apartment fire that claimed the lives of four members of one family and critically injured another. This tragedy is a heartbreaking reminder of the deadly consequences of battery fires and the need for stronger federal safety standards.

On the Senate’s passage of the bill, Rep. Torres said:

“Unanimous Senate passage sends a clear message: keeping families, workers, and first responders safe from preventable lithium-ion battery fires is a bipartisan priority. This bill establishes clear, lifesaving federal safety standards for batteries used in e-bikes, e-scooters, and other micromobility devices. I thank Senator Gillibrand and our colleagues in both chambers for helping move this legislation forward.”

Rep. Nick Langworthy said:

“With Senate passage of the Setting Consumer Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries Act, this bipartisan legislation is now on its way to becoming law and delivering important protections for New Yorkers and consumers across the country. I applaud Senator Gillibrand for her leadership in getting this bill passed in the Senate, and I am proud to have co-led this effort alongside Rep. Torres. This commonsense legislation will establish clear safety standards and ensure that only safe, tested products reach American consumers. I urge President Trump to sign it into law so we can put these protections in place and help prevent dangerous battery fires.”

Rep. Yvette D. Clarke said:

“The Senate’s unanimous passage of this legislation brings us one step closer to establishing the critical safeguards needed to prevent deadly lithium-ion battery fires. The recent tragedy at Patterson Houses in the Bronx, which claimed four lives, is a painful reminder of the devastating risks these devices can pose to our communities. As an original cosponsor, I am proud to have worked alongside Congressman Ritchie Torres and our bipartisan colleagues to move these protections forward. Now, we must ensure this legislation becomes law and that families, workers, and first responders have the protections they deserve.”

Rep. Andrew R. Garbarino said:

“I am proud to see the Setting Consumer Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries Act pass the Senate after receiving overwhelming bipartisan support in the House. We have seen the dangers of lithium-ion battery fires firsthand in New York, and it is clear that stronger safety standards are needed to protect our communities. I want to thank Congressman Ritchie Torres for his partnership on this legislation, and I look forward to seeing the President sign it into law.”

Rep. Torres introduced the House bill with original cosponsors Reps. Andrew Garbarino, Yvette D. Clarke and Nick Langworthy. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand led the Senate companion with original cosponsors Senators Marsha Blackburn, Deb Fischer and Chuck Schumer.

Senator Gillibrand cited recent data underscoring the need for these standards. A 2026 CPSC report identified 367 micromobility battery-related fires and 45 deaths nationwide between 2017 and 2024. Gillibrand also cited FDNY figures showing 362 fires and five deaths in New York City in 2026 involving e-bikes, e-scooters and similar devices.

The legislation also received support from fire service organizations, standards-setting experts, building owners, and industry stakeholders.

FDNY Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore said:

“Since 2021, the FDNY has been sounding the alarm about the dangers of uncertified lithium-ion batteries. We have done tremendous work to stop the injuries, deaths, and intensely dangerous fires that are all too common with these devices.

We applaud our partners in the U.S. House of Representatives and U.S. Senate, including Congressman Torres and Senator Gillibrand, for their strong leadership in passing this critical legislation. We know once it’s signed into law, it will save lives. This is a major step in the fight to keep people safe.”

International Association of Fire Fighters (IAFF) General President Edward A. Kelly said:

“Fire fighters see the dangers of lithium-ion battery fires firsthand. We know – and, tragically, so do New Yorkers – that stronger safety standards are needed to protect the public from this deadly threat. The IAFF thanks Rep. Torres and Sen. Gillibrand for their leadership on the Setting Consumer Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries Act. Its bipartisan passage is a reminder that the safety of our communities and our nation’s fire fighters must be everyone’s priority.”

Chief Steven A. Locke, President and Board Chair of the International Association of Fire Chiefs (IAFC), said:

“I want to thank the hard work and dedication of Representative Ritchie Torres, from New York, who led the charge in getting this passed in the United States House of Representatives. Fire Chiefs across America can thank Congress for taking action to make micromobility devices fire safe.”

Steven W. Hirsch, Chair of the National Volunteer Fire Council, said:

“Lithium-ion batteries, especially those of inferior quality, can be prone to explosion, thermal runaway, and other hazards. As devices powered by these batteries have become more common, so have the risks associated with them. I applaud Senator Gillibrand and Rep. Torres for their leadership in passing this important legislation, which will require lithium-ion batteries powering certain mobility devices to meet quality and safety standards, thereby reducing the fire risk these devices pose.”

Building Owners and Managers Association (BOMA) International said:

“The perseverance of Congressman Ritchie Torres and Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, and the hard work of their staffs, were critical to getting this important legislation across the finish line.

Since our BOMA New York members first raised the issue with us in 2023, BOMA International has worked with stakeholders to advocate for a solution that protects our members and their buildings while giving the public greater confidence in the safety of lithium-ion battery-powered micromobility devices.”

Jeff Marootian, President and CEO of UL Standards & Engagement, said:

“E-mobility battery fires put homes, buildings, and communities at risk. We are grateful for Representative Torres’ strong support in championing this bill, building bipartisan support, and helping to protect Americans nationwide from unsafe e-mobility devices.”

Gabe Knight, Senior Safety Policy Analyst for Consumer Reports, said:

“The enactment of this life-saving bill cannot come soon enough. Far too many Americans have been seriously injured or killed by preventable micromobility battery fires. While this legislation cannot undo the destruction communities have endured, it will ensure that going forward, consumers can trust that their e-bike or scooter battery is designed to be safe. Consumer Reports thanks Congressman Ritchie Torres for his leadership on this critical bipartisan safety bill, and urges the President to swiftly sign it into law.”

John Horton, Vice President, Head of North America Policy at DoorDash, said:

“The passage of this bill represents a major milestone for battery safety. By establishing a new federal standard for lithium-ion batteries coming into the country, this legislation will prevent unsafe products from ever reaching the market and protect people who use e-bikes and devices like them, as well as the communities where they live and work. We thank the bipartisan leaders in Congress, led by sponsors like Senators Kirsten Gillibrand, Chuck Schumer, and Congressman Ritchie Torres, who championed this issue and helped usher in a safer future for micromobility nationwide.”

Uber said:

“The Setting Consumer Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries Act will help prevent dangerous battery failures and make e-bikes and other e-mobility devices safer. Uber applauds the bipartisan leadership behind this bill and looks forward to working together to make e-devices safer for everyone who rides or delivers.”

Dominic Sanchez, Grubhub’s Associate Director of Government Affairs, said:

“Dangerous, uncertified lithium-ion batteries are a national problem that require comprehensive, national solutions. With the passage of the Setting Consumer Standards for Lithium-Ion Batteries Act by the United States Senate, this important legislation will improve safety for the many Americans who rely on lithium ion-powered micro mobility devices. Grubhub thanks Senator Gillibrand and Representative Torres and the many cosponsors of this legislation for their leadership on this critical public safety issue.”

On the need to make these protections law, Rep. Torres said:

“Families and first responders should not have to bear the consequences of preventable lithium-ion battery fires. I urge the President to sign this bipartisan bill into law so the CPSC can put these vital safety standards in place.”

title: Congresswoman Luz Rivas Urges L.A. Metro to Reconsider Options for the Sepulveda Transit Corridor Project’s Maintenance and Storage Site
text:
LOS ANGELES – Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29) submitted a public comment letter urging Los Angeles Country Metropolitan Transportation Authority’s (Metro) Board of Directors to reconsider the Westfield Fashion Square mall in Sherman Oaks and The Plant Shopping Center (The Plant) in Panorama City as potential sites for a new Maintenance Storage Facility (MSF) for the Sepulveda Transit Corridor Project (Project). Her public comment letter additionally calls on Metro to extend the public comment period from November 23, 2026, to January 2027 to allow sufficient time for community input.

“The proposed sites of the Westfield Fashion Square mall and The Plant are established commercial centers that are economic drivers for the surrounding area,” wrote Congresswoman Rivas. “These locations serve as important gathering places for the community. I do not support either location being considered as a location for Metro’s MSF. Members of the community deserve to be involved through a robust public comment process on where this facility is ultimately located.”

Residents in surrounding areas of the Westfield Fashion Square mall and The Plant have shared concerns about the potential impacts a maintenance and storage facility would have on established commercial centers, local businesses, employees, and communities.

Congresswoman Rivas continued: “The success of the Project is dependent on meaningful community engagement and a transparent planning process. Metro's November 23, 2026, deadline does not provide sufficient time for affected community members to review the proposals and submit informed feedback. An extended public comment period will allow residents, businesses, and community organizations a meaningful opportunity to provide feedback on the proposed MSF locations.”

A full copy of Congresswoman Rivas’ letter to Metro can be found here.

title: Rep. Kelly Reintroduces Bill to Track Whether Federal Dollars Reach Veterans, Women, and Entrepreneurs of Color
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congresswoman Robin Kelly (IL-02) has reintroduced the Increasing Transparency and Accountability in Federal Spending Act to show whether veterans, women, and entrepreneurs of color are getting a fair share of federal grants, loans, and contracts. Federal award tracking does not currently record the race, ethnicity, veteran status, or sex of the people who own or lead the businesses and organizations receiving federal dollars, which leaves Congress unable to see who is being left behind. U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) introduced companion legislation in the United States Senate.

“Taxpayer dollars should lift up every community, yet right now, Congress and federal agencies lack the complete data needed to see if women, veterans, and business owners of color are truly getting a fair shot at federal contracts and grants,” said Congresswoman Robin Kelly. “Accountability starts with transparency. Reintroducing the Increasing Transparency and Accountability in Federal Spending Act is a critical step toward closing our federal data gaps and ensuring public investments reach historically underinvested communities.”

"Federal contracting is a major economic driver for our country, with the power to transform a small business or a startup from a dream into a thriving company," said Senator Booker. "Every entrepreneur should have the same opportunity to compete for and win a federal contract, regardless of their background or ZIP code. Better data will close a critical gap in what Congress knows about where federal money goes, so we can make sure it reaches communities fairly and effectively."

The bill would amend the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act to require the Office of Management and Budget to collect and report the race, ethnicity, veteran status, and sex of the highest-paid executive officers and private business owners of any entity that receives a federal award of more than $30,000, including contracts, subcontracts, grants, subgrants, loans, and other federal financial assistance. The bill would also direct the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to review the accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and accessibility of publicly available federal spending data within three years.

This bill is endorsed by the Small Business Majority and Project On Government Oversight.

title: Reps. Kelly, Watson Coleman, and Simon Press President Trump for Answers on Women’s Health Research Task Force
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswomen Robin Kelly (IL-02), Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), and Lateefah Simon (CA-12) sent a letter to President Donald Trump regarding the execution of Executive Order 14437, which directs the Department of Health and Human Services to create a Women’s Health Division within the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

The letter stresses the importance of women’s health research and asks for increased transparency into the work of the convened task force. Through a list of clarifying questions, the lawmakers ask how research will be funded, how it will build on previous initiatives, and how it will advance efforts focused on known health disparities within minoritized communities. Finally, the lawmakers warn that the executive order must be more than messaging to make a meaningful impact.

The letter also raises concern that the initiative duplicates ongoing work at NIH’s Office of Research on Women’s Health. It notes that the administration has repeatedly canceled and rolled back women’s health research programs, including research on women of color.

“We know that women’s health issues are underfunded and under-researched compared to men’s health—a disparity that disproportionately impacts Black women,” said Congresswoman Robin Kelly. “Too often, research is developed with only white patients in mind, resulting in more Black people dying from preventable causes and treatable diseases. A task force that only makes headlines will not change that. If this Administration is serious about women’s health, it must answer our questions, build on the science that came before, and make sure women of color are in the room and in the trials. Women deserve more than rhetoric.”

“Serious federal investments in women's health have taken a backseat for far too long," said Congresswoman Watson Coleman. "Too often, the policies that have been implemented to support them have had disparate impacts on Black women. The NIH's Women’s Health Division has the opportunity to significantly improve health outcomes for millions of women, but any changes made must be a result of conversations involving a diversity of voices. Considering the Trump administration's track record of empty promises, political theater, and health funding cuts, it is incumbent upon us to ensure the administration has an actual plan to improve lives.”

“Women’s health research has been severely underfunded, creating pervasive gaps in the quality of health care they receive,” said Congresswoman Lateefah Simon. “The Trump Administration has only exacerbated the gap by slashing funding for the National Institutes of Health, canceling reproductive health and family planning programs, and dismantling critical maternal and infant health infrastructure. As the first congenitally blind Member of Congress, I know these cuts only also disproportionately impact disabled communities and women of color. I’m proud to work alongside Reps. Kelly and Watson Coleman to conduct oversight of the Trump Administration and demand answers on their plan for women’s health research.”

In the letter, the lawmakers ask the President to answer:

How the initiatives under Executive Order 14437 will be integrated with ongoing and previous federal women’s health efforts

How the research agenda will include urban, suburban, and rural populations, and women from communities historically underrepresented in clinical trials

How the research will be funded, who will determine which lines of inquiry are worthy of consideration, and what role political appointees will have compared to experts and researchers

Whether research will include quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods studies, and whether it will expand on previous NIH-funded findings

The lawmakers have requested a written response within 30 days.

title: Scanlon, Warren, Pressley Introduce Legislation to Expand Community-Based Programs that Protect and Serve Americans Experiencing Mental Health Crises
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07) today introduced the Mental Health Justice Act, legislation to empower state and local governments to send trained mental health professionals in response to 911 calls when an individual is experiencing a mental health crisis.

According to the Treatment Advocacy Center, 1 in 4 police encounters involves someone with a severe mental illness. Additional research from the American Psychological Association estimates that more than 1 in 5 emergency calls involve someone experiencing a mental health or substance use crisis.

“Individuals experiencing a mental health crisis should be connected with mental health professionals, not put on a one-way track to jail,” said Rep. Scanlon. “Too often we see the tragic consequences of encounters between people in crisis and law enforcement officers who lack the appropriate support or training to handle mental health issues. I’m proud to introduce this bill with Senator Warren to keep both citizens and law enforcement professionals safe.”

“Part of keeping our communities safe is keeping people suffering from a mental health or substance use crisis safe,” said Senator Warren. “Rather than criminalizing mental health, this legislation would make it easier for trained mental health professionals to respond when someone needs help or support—not jail time.”

“Community members experiencing a mental health crisis should be met with compassion, resources, and care—NOT criminalization,” said Rep. Pressley. “Criminalizing mental health crises only makes our communities less safe. That’s why I'm proud to reintroduce the Mental Health Justice Act alongside Senator Warren and Congresswoman Scanlon to ensure mental health professionals instead of police—can support people in moments of crisis.”

The Mental Health Justice Act will establish a grant program to pay for hiring, training, salary, benefits, and additional expenses for mental health provider first responder units. Upon establishment, mental health providers would be the first on the scene to assist an individual experiencing a mental health crisis and help them to access appropriate community resources.

In Fiscal Year 2022, Congresswoman Scanlon secured $650,000 in Community Project Funding for Delaware County’s Crisis Co-Response Program. The program currently operates in Haverford and Upper Darby, but additional funding would be critical in expanding services for extended hours and additional locations.

The bill is endorsed by the ACLU, Center for Policing Equity, National Alliance on Mental Illness, The Kennedy Forum, CommunicationFIRST, Access Ready Inc., Autistic Women & Nonbinary Network, Bend the Arc: Jewish Action, National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, Autism Society of America, American Foundation for Suicide Prevention, American Association on Health and Disability, Lakeshore Foundation, Association of University Centers on Disabilities, Postpartum Support International, Union for Reform Judaism, National Association of Councils on Developmental Disabilities, Alternative Mobile Services Association, Justice in Aging, American Society of Addiction Medicine, National Health Care for the Homeless Council, Clinical Social Work Association, National Association of County Behavioral Health and Developmental Disability Directors, American Association of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, Association for Behavioral Health and Wellness, National Action Network, American Association of Suicidology, Bazelon Center for Mental Health Law, American Psychological Association, the Disability Rights Education & Defense Fund, and Orange County Sheriff’s Department.

title: Schakowsky, Mullin Introduce Legislation to Enhance Consumer Protection, Hold Mega-Corporations Accountable for Consumer Safety Violations
text:
Full Text of Bill (PDF)

WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representative Jan Schakowsky, Ranking Member of the House Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade Subcommittee, and U.S. Representative Kevin Mullin (CA-15) introduced the Consumer Advocacy and Protection (CAP) Act, legislation to strengthen consumer protections and give the Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) greater authority to hold companies accountable for safety violations. The CAP Act aims to deter companies from violating consumer safety laws by increasing CPSC's penalty authority. U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-VT) introduced companion legislation in the Senate.

“The current limits on civil penalties have allowed big corporations to skirt real accountability when their products are found to be harmful, and in some cases, deadly. Companies must pay the price when they violate consumer safety protections,” said Congresswoman Jan Schakowsky. “That is why I am proud to introduce the CAP Act to strengthen penalties for safety violations, better reflect the severity of offenses, and hold violators accountable. We must do everything possible to ensure the products people buy for themselves and their children are safe.”

“Protecting consumers starts with holding corporate actors accountable and making sure they put safety first,” said Congressman Kevin Mullin (CA-15). “Current penalties are not strong enough to discourage businesses from breaking the law and putting consumers at risk. This critical legislation takes an important step toward addressing that gap by increasing the financial consequences for companies that violate consumer protection laws and encouraging greater responsibility, transparency, and safer products.”

“Integrity and transparency are crucial to ensuring consumer protection. But right now, massive companies continue to undermine federal safety standards and evade responsibility. We need to create incentives that put consumer and product safety first,” said Senator Peter Welch. “Our commonsense bill will hold corporations accountable when they knowingly put products on the market that endanger consumers.”

Under current law, manufacturers, importers, and distributors of consumer products are required to report immediately to the CPSC information that reasonably supports the conclusion that a product contains a defect that could create a substantial product hazard or an unreasonable risk of serious injury or death. If violations occur, the applicable civil penalty is a maximum of $100,000 per individual violation and $15,000,000 for a series of related violations. Following an inflation adjustment in 2021, the maximum penalties increased to $120,000 per violation and $17,150,000 for a series of related violations. The CPSC can adjust maximum civil penalty amounts for inflation every five years.

Specifically, the CAP Act would:

Eliminate the maximum civil penalty cap on a series of related violations.

Increase the maximum penalty for an individual violation from $100,000 to $250,000.

Clarify the types of offenses for which the CPSC can impose civil penalties.

Change the inflation review period from every five years to every year.

Establish a new formula and procedures for calculating inflation adjustments.

The CAP Act is also cosponsored by U.S. Representatives Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), and Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05), as well as U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Edward Markey (D-MA), Brian Schatz (D-HI), and Ben Ray Luján (D-NM).

The CAP Act is endorsed by the Consumer Federation of America, Consumer Reports, and National Consumers League.

title: House Unanimously Passes Shreve Bill to Shut Down Foreign Scam Syndicates
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, the House unanimously passed the Dismantle Foreign Scam Syndicates Act (H.R. 5490), introduced by Congressman Jefferson Shreve (IN-06), Chairman of the Stop Scams Caucus. The bill directs the Secretary of State to lead a federal task force to dismantle overseas criminal networks that steal billions of dollars from Americans each year.

“Hoosiers have lost their life savings to criminals operating halfway around the world,” said Rep. Shreve. “These syndicates run scams on an industrial scale. Some have protection from the very governments that should shut them down. My bill puts the Secretary of State in charge of coordinating our response. Congress and the public deserve to know who’s been sanctioned, who’s been arrested and how many victims have been rescued.”

The task force brings together the State Department, the FBI and the Departments of Homeland Security and the Treasury. It would develop a strategy to dismantle the syndicates and report annually to Congress on the results. The bill also supports sanctions against the individuals and companies behind the scams.

Congressman Shreve’s bill drew more than 70 cosponsors from both parties and passed the House Foreign Affairs Committee unanimously, 48–0. Now, after passing the House unanimously, it heads to the Senate.

title: Congresswoman Torres Calls for Investigation Into ICE’s $950 Million Adelanto Purchase
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35), a member of the House Appropriations Committee, requested that Department of Homeland Security Inspector General Joseph Cuffari investigate ICE’s $950 million purchase of the Adelanto ICE Processing Center from GEO Group, including whether taxpayers were left responsible for infrastructure failures identified before the sale.

“Taxpayers should not be on the hook for infrastructure and repair costs that were known before ICE signed this deal,” said Congresswoman Torres. “Before spending nearly a billion dollars, ICE owes the public a full accounting of the repair costs, who would pay them, and whether the purchase served a legitimate public purpose. If an investigation proves illegal or corrupt actions influenced this purchase, then DHS must pursue every available legal remedy to unwind the deal and recover taxpayer dollars, seeking a full refund to the extent permitted by law. Anyone who violates the law must be held accountable.”

The letter cites a September 2026 Government Accountability Office report finding that ICE expanded detention capacity without necessary planning and analysis. Torres asked whether ICE addressed those recommendations to prevent waste of taxpayer dollars before buying the Adelanto facility and whether ICE evaluated its long-term repair, maintenance, and operating costs.

Torres also requested scrutiny of the purchase price, procurement integrity, and whether ICE Acting Director David Venturella, a former GEO Group executive who committed to recusing himself from matters involving the company, participated in the transaction.

Rep. Norma Torres' office has conducted more than 20 oversight visits to Adelanto this Congress. The letter describes persistent failures in medical care and living conditions, questions whether federal ownership was intended to evade oversight, and notes that GEO Group will continue operating the facilities.

“Changing ownership does not erase dangerous conditions or the obligation to comply with court orders,” Torres added. “Congress and the public deserve to know who approved this purchase, who benefits, and what it will ultimately cost taxpayers.”

title: Rep. Vasquez Passes Bipartisan Bill to Boost New Mexico Geothermal Energy Production Through the House
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) passed the bipartisan Earth MRI Reauthorization Act out of the House, boosting New Mexico’s geothermal energy production and supporting an all-of-the-above approach to meeting our country’s growing energy needs. The bill reauthorizes the Earth Mapping Resources Initiative, a U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) program that businesses, state geologists, and communities rely on to understand where the critical minerals needed for clean energy are found, guide their responsible development, and better understand natural hazards. This update will provide much-needed stability for developers seeking to invest in energy projects to bring down utility bills for New Mexicans.

“Earth MRI puts federal dollars to work right here in New Mexico, helping the state find geothermal energy deposits that will power our communities. I’m proud to cosponsor this bipartisan bill and keep working to lower energy costs for New Mexico families,” said Vasquez. “New Mexico is one of the nation’s leading energy-producing states, and we can’t plan for our economic, water, or energy future without knowing what’s going on right under us.”

Lowering energy costs for New Mexicans is a core pillar of Rep. Vasquez’s Affordability Agenda, a concrete plan to address the affordability crisis facing hardworking New Mexicans. Rep. Vasquez has:

Introduced the Energy Bills Relief Act, which takes a multi-pronged approach to bring down prices for hardworking New Mexicans.

Rolled out bipartisan legislation to cut red tape and reduce energy costs for families, such as the Create Expedited Reviews to Transform American Infrastructure Now (CERTAIN) Act.

title: Wasserman Schultz, Moskowitz Join Hollywood Mayor Levy to Assess Flood Damage
text:
Hollywood, FL — Today, U.S. Reps. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25) and Jared Moskowitz (FL-23) joined Hollywood Mayor Josh Levy and other local elected officials to assess the damage from torrential rainfall and flooding that battered South Florida by doing an inspection at Temple Sinai of Hollywood and Park East. The roof of Temple Sinai of Hollywood partially collapsed due to the dangerous storms, and the Park East neighborhood of Hollywood faced some of the worst damage in the city.

The Members saw homes and the synagogue falling apart, homes with knee-high waterlines, scattered furniture and other devastation. They also called on the Federal government to provide supportive resources to rebuild and prevent further damage from natural disasters like this, and the local community to come together to support those who experienced property damage in the short term.

“What we see all around us are neighbors dealing with a clear disaster — the kind of event that has become more frequent and more severe as climate change takes place,” said Wasserman Schultz. “I’m going to work overtime alongside my Congressional colleagues, state authorities, and local leaders to get a disaster declaration formalized and unlock as many resources as possible.”

“Hurricane season was relatively quiet for South Florida, but this is what an El Niño event looks like: severe weather that doesn't get a name or get followed as closely as a hurricane. Losing this sanctuary is a real loss, but this community will rebuild, and at some point there will be High Holiday services on these grounds again. Local and state officials are continuing to assess the damage. Governor DeSantis has expanded his emergency declaration to include Broward and Palm Beach counties and has requested federal disaster assistance,” said Moskowitz. “I recently co-led a bipartisan letter urging President Trump to approve the Governor's request for a major disaster declaration, and I'll continue working with Congresswoman Wasserman Schultz, our colleagues in the Florida congressional delegation, and federal and state officials to ensure affected communities receive the assistance they need.”

Florida has deployed hundreds of Florida National Guard and Florida State Guard members as Broward and surrounding counties remain in a State of Emergency. The state has also submitted a disaster assistance request to the President.

title: Congresswoman Maxine Waters’ Statement Opposing BAAJA
text:
“I am deeply concerned about the so-called Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), and I cannot support this bill if it comes before the House of Representatives without significant improvements.

This bill fast tracks the permitting processes for a wide variety of types of projects, including fossil fuel projects, pipelines, and data centers. Many of these projects could have a devastating impact on local communities and the environment if they are granted permits without careful consideration.

BAAJA adds restrictions to the Clean Water Act and the National Environmental Policy Act that limit opportunities for communities to provide input on projects that directly impact them and makes it more difficult for communities to challenge potentially dangerous projects. BAAJA forces states to rush project reviews and shifts the burden of proof for harmful impacts onto the states, instead of requiring developers to prove that their projects would not cause environmental damage. BAAJA also weakens the protections of the Endangered Species Act and forces states to assume the burden of determining whether a project would jeopardize an endangered species. Furthermore, BAAJA substantially reduces the ability of courts to pause construction or stop projects that violate these landmark environmental laws.

BAAJA reduces the rights of Tribes under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, limiting their ability to protect their lands, reducing opportunities for Tribal consultation, and imposing shorter timelines for project reviews and narrower limits on challenging decisions in court.

Meanwhile, BAAJA does nothing to address the Trump administration’s illegal withholding of $7.5 billion in funding for renewable energy projects from states that voted for Kamala Harris in 2024. If we cannot trust the Trump administration to fund clean energy projects as required by law, we must not make it easier for Trump to fast track fossil fuel and data center projects for wealthy special interests and favored campaign donors.”

title: Sen. Banks, Sen. Young Urge NASA to Consider Indiana for U.S. Space Academy
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Todd Young (R-Ind.) are urging NASA to give Indiana’s proposal for the United States Space Academy full and fair consideration. In a letter to NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, chair of the Presidential Commission on the United States Space Academy, the senators backed the state of Indiana’s response to NASA’s request for information and highlighted the state’s resources to support the Academy.

The senators said Indiana’s universities, defense installations, manufacturers, and technology companies could help the Academy prepare the talent needed to maintain U.S. leadership in space. Indiana University, Purdue, Notre Dame, and Ivy Tech have proposed meeting the Academy’s immediate academic needs and training workers for NASA and the Department of War, while the state has identified potential locations for the Academy.

Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.): “Indiana has the universities, military and research assets, and skilled workforce to help prepare the next generation of Americans for careers serving our country. I am proud to support Indiana’s proposal for the United States Space Academy and will keep working with our state partners to strengthen Indiana’s role in America’s national defense.”

Read the full letter here or below:

Dear Administrator Isaacman:

We write in strong support of the State of Indiana’s response to NASA’s Request for Information regarding the establishment of the United States Space Academy.

American leadership in space is critical to our national security. As our adversaries invest in capabilities intended to challenge the United States, we must ensure our country has the scientists, engineers, and military and civilian leaders necessary to maintain our advantage.

President Trump’s vision for the United States Space Academy recognizes that our future success in space will depend as much on developing talented Americans as it will on advancing new technologies.

Indiana has a long history of contributing to America’s space program, from the earliest days of NASA through today’s missions. Our state is home to leading research universities, major defense installations, advanced manufacturers, and companies developing technologies important to our national security.

We are particularly encouraged by the leadership and collaboration among Indiana University, Purdue University, the University of Notre Dame, and Ivy Tech Community College. These institutions have come together to address the Academy’s immediate academic needs while also developing an additional approach to producing more of the highly skilled Americans NASA and the Department of War will need in the years ahead. This partnership demonstrates Indiana’s ability to bring together its academic resources to address a national challenge. All of these institutions are led by Presidents who support their institutions’ engagement with our national security and defense apparatus through research and workforce development. Particularly noteworthy, Purdue University announced this month that Retired Lt. Gen. Jay B. Silveria will be the next President of the University. His past role as Superintendent of the US Air Force Academy will bring familiarity to the role of the Academy, its operations, and end goals.

Indiana’s response also identifies multiple locations capable of supporting the Academy and its long-term growth. Each offers access to academic, military, research, and industry assets that can contribute to the Academy’s success.

As Indiana’s United States Senators, we have worked closely with Governor Braun, our congressional delegation, and leaders across the state to strengthen Indiana’s role in our national defense. Our work to advance unmanned systems, military testing, microelectronics, and defense manufacturing reflects a shared commitment to ensuring Indiana continues to contribute to America’s military readiness and technological superiority. The United States Space Academy would build on that work while helping prepare the next generation of Americans to serve our country.

We strongly support Indiana’s response and respectfully urge you to give it full and fair consideration. We stand ready to work with NASA, the Administration, and our state partners to support this important national mission.

title: Bennet, Cornyn Introduce Legislation to Lower Prescription Drug Costs and Increase Access to Biosimilars
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet and Senator John Cornyn (R-Texas) introduced the Increasing Access to Biosimilars Act, legislation that would direct the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to Create a Medicare pilot program to expand access to lower-cost alternatives to expensive biologic medicines that are as safe and effective as the original drugs. These medicines treat a range of serious conditions, including rheumatoid arthritis, Crohn’s disease, and certain types of cancer, such as breast cancer.

“Skyrocketing prescription drug prices are causing too many Americans to have to choose between their life-saving medications and putting food on the table, especially seniors, communities of color, and the millions of people living on fixed incomes who need their prescriptions to live,” said Bennet. “This important legislation would increase patient access to lower-cost biosimilars, saving them and our health care system billions of dollars. Every American deserves affordable health care, and I look forward to working with my colleagues to move this legislation forward.”

“Texas seniors should not have to break the bank to pay for their medication that’s essential to their health and well-being, yet millions are being forced to endure this financial burden because of the skyrocketing cost of prescription drugs,” said Cornyn. “I am proud to co-lead this bipartisan legislation to help ensure our seniors can afford the treatments they need by expanding access to biosimilars, which lowers drug costs for patients and alleviates the burden on Medicare beneficiaries.”

Currently, providers in Medicare Part B are reimbursed for administering biologic drugs, including biosimilars, at average sales price plus +6 percent, of which the federal government pays 80 percent, and beneficiaries pay 20 percent coinsurance. This means providers are reimbursed at a higher rate for using higher-cost biologic products rather than lower-cost biosimilars. At the same time, Medicare beneficiaries are forced to pay higher copays on those brand name biologic products.

This legislation would direct HHS to establish a shared savings demonstration project to increase access to biosimilars in the Medicare Part B program. Under the demonstration, Medicare would provide an additional payment to providers for using lower-cost biosimilar products, reflecting savings created in contrast to administering higher-cost reference biologic drugs. Additionally, Medicare can use a portion of those savings to reduce the beneficiary’s coinsurance payment. This would encourage physicians to prescribe less-expensive biosimilars, increasing patient access to more affordable, life-saving drugs and lowering patient out-of-pocket costs.

Under the demonstration, Medicare would provide an additional payment to providers for using lower-cost biosimilar products that reflects the savings created in contrast to administering the higher-cost reference biological product. Additionally, Medicare can use a portion of those savings to reduce the beneficiary’s coinsurance payment.

The Increasing Access to Biosimilar Act is supported by the Biosimilars Forum, Association for Accessible Medicines, Viatris, Biosimilars Council, and American Podiatric Medical Association.

“Biosimilars are the commonsense, proven solution to America’s prescription drug affordability crisis. The Biosimilars Forum thanks Senators Bennet and Cornyn for their bipartisan leadership, and we urge Congress to pass this important bill,” said Juliana M. Reed, executive director of the Biosimilars Forum. “Biosimilars have already saved the U.S. health care system $81.6 billion, including $25.4 billion in 2025 alone. The Increasing Access to Biosimilars Act builds on that record by realigning Medicare Part B incentives so more seniors can access these lower-cost medicines. We are entering the second decade of biosimilars. The first decade proved the science. The second decade is about delivering the full promise of biosimilars. This means new products coming to market and new savings for patients, taxpayers, and the health care system.”

“The Biosimilars Council and the Association for Accessible Medicines thank Senators Bennet and Cornyn for their work and dedication on behalf of American patients with the reintroduction of the Increasing Access to Biosimilars Act,” said Alex Keeton, Executive Director, Biosimilars Council. “This bipartisan bill is based on a simple idea – that Medicare policies should encourage and prioritize the most effective, lowest-cost medicine. Biosimilars consistently deliver significant savings compared to high-priced brand biologics. We encourage Congress and the Administration to quickly implement this policy and deliver savings to America’s patients and taxpayers, and to put generic and biosimilar medicines first.”

Bennet has consistently worked to bring down prescription drug costs for Coloradans. In October, Bennet hosted Colorado parents, seniors, and caregivers as well as pharmacists, senior advocates, and health care leaders for a discussion on high-cost prescriptions and access to affordable medications. In April 2026, Bennet joined Senator Ron Wyden (D-Ore.) and 16 Senate Democrats to introduce legislation to force the Trump Administration to disclose the terms of deals the administration made with more than a dozen of the largest pharmaceutical companies, and conduct an independent analysis to determine whether American families will actually see lower prices from the deals. Additionally, in February 2026, Bennet’s Prescription Drug Supply Chain Pricing Transparency Act was passed into law. This legislation will require the Government Accountability Office to conduct a study and submit a report to Congress about the ways the current pharmaceutical drug supply chain structure encourages drug manufacturers, Pharmacy Benefit Managers, insurance companies, and other actors to hike up drug prices.

In December 2025, Bennet demanded four major pharmaceutical companies provide specific details about agreements they announced with President Donald Trump to lower drug costs as millions of Americans saw the cost of health care skyrocket. In March 2023, he urged the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services Administrator Chiquita Brooks-LaSure to ensure swift implementation of the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) provisions that will lower the cost of Medicare Part B prescription drugs. In August 2022, Bennet helped secure enhanced health insurance premium tax credits and the requirement for Medicare to negotiate drug prices in the IRA, first introduced as part of his Medicare-X public option bill.

title: NEWS: Senators Blunt Rochester, Coons Join Colleagues in Urging Amtrak to Change Firearm Transport Policies
text:
Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), a Member of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation and Senator Chris Coons (D-Del.), joined Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.) and their colleagues in sending a letter to Amtrak expressing concern with upcoming changes to firearm transport policies.

In accordance with President Trump’s Executive Order 14206, “Protecting Second Amendment Rights,” Amtrak announced that in January 2027, it will expand its firearm transport policies to allow passengers traveling on routes with no checked baggage cars, such as the Northeast Regional and Acela, to transport a firearm in their carry-on luggage at their seat.

“We are writing regarding Amtrak’s recent and upcoming changes to its firearm transport policies across its Long-Distance, State Supported, and Northeast Corridor Service Lines. We strongly support Amtrak as America’s Railroad and the valuable passenger rail services it provides to millions of customers across the country every year. However, we are concerned by these changing policies and that they could undermine safety,” the Senators wrote. “It is our understanding that pursuant to new grant conditions placed on Amtrak by the United States Department of Transportation in its annual federal grant, made possible by the fiscal year 2026 funding appropriated by Congress, Amtrak is changing its firearm and ammunition handling and notifications requirements to be more lenient and expanding the policies across its service network.”

“Now, based on information provided to Congress and additional recent reporting, we understand that in January 2027, Amtrak plans to expand its policies for unloaded firearms and ammunition to be transported by passengers for the very first time to the Northeast Corridor and State Supported Service Lines where there are no checked baggage cars. This unprecedented change will result in Amtrak permitting unloaded firearms and ammunition to be present in passenger cars in carry-on baggage on Amtrak trains that carry millions of passengers a year, such as the Northeast Regional, Keystone Service, and Capitol Corridor,” the Senators continued.

“We are alarmed by these changes in policies, which seem to be made because of pressure and new arbitrary federal grant conditions, and the increased risks these new policies pose to the safety of passengers aboard Amtrak trains and at stations, as well as front-line workers, including onboard service workers, conductors, station personnel, and law enforcement,” the Senators concluded. “Further, introducing firearms, even if unloaded, within passenger cars — without separating passengers from the firearms — would not meet the standards established by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) for air travel, which, unlike Amtrak, includes strict passenger security screening to board planes. We urge Amtrak to reconsider its plan to allow the transport of unloaded firearms and ammunition as carry-on baggage in passenger cars…”

In addition to Senators Gillibrand, Coons, and Blunt Rochester, the letter was signed by Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) and Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), John Fetterman (D-Pa.), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Angus King (I-Maine), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Mark Warner (D-Va.), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.).

title: Booker Reintroduces Bill to Track Whether Federal Dollars Reach Veterans, Women, and Entrepreneurs of Color
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) has reintroduced the Increasing Transparency and Accountability in Federal Spending Act to show whether veterans, women, and entrepreneurs of color are getting a fair share of federal grants, loans, and contracts. Federal award tracking does not currently record the race, ethnicity, veteran status, or sex of the people who own or lead the businesses and organizations receiving federal dollars, which leaves Congress unable to see who is being left behind. Congresswoman Robin Kelly (IL-02) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

"Federal contracting is a major economic driver for our country, with the power to transform a small business or a startup from a dream into a thriving company," said Senator Booker. "Every entrepreneur should have the same opportunity to compete for and win a federal contract, regardless of their background or ZIP code. Better data will close a critical gap in what Congress knows about where federal money goes, so we can make sure it reaches communities fairly and effectively."

“Taxpayer dollars should lift up every community, yet right now, Congress and federal agencies lack the complete data needed to see if women, veterans, and business owners of color are truly getting a fair shot at federal contracts and grants,” said Congresswoman Robin Kelly. “Accountability starts with transparency. Reintroducing the Increasing Transparency and Accountability in Federal Spending Act is a critical step toward closing our federal data gaps and ensuring public investments reach historically underinvested communities.”

The bill would amend the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act to require the Office of Management and Budget to collect and report the race, ethnicity, veteran status, and sex of the highest-paid executive officers and private business owners of any entity that receives a federal award of more than $30,000, including contracts, subcontracts, grants, subgrants, loans, and other federal financial assistance. The bill would also direct the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to review the accuracy, completeness, timeliness, and accessibility of publicly available federal spending data within three years.

This bill is endorsed by the Small Business Majority and Project On Government Oversight.

title: Booker, Chu Reintroduce DIPLOMA Act to Strengthen School and Community Partnerships, Support Students
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. – U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) and U.S.Representative Judy Chu (D-CA-28) reintroduced the Developing Innovative Partnerships and Learning Opportunities that Motivate Achievement (DIPLOMA) Act, legislation that would provide federal grants to states to encourage and support community schools, which are collaborations between schools and community partners to address students’ holistic needs through evidence-based practices. The bill would also provide planning grants to help states design their strategies, ensuring thoughtful and effective implementation.

“Serving the people of Newark, I have seen firsthand how strong communities can open doors for young people and how inequities can hold them back,” said Senator Booker. “The DIPLOMA Act will help bring schools, families, and community partners together to ensure every child has access to the resources, support, and opportunities they need to succeed.”

“As a former educator, I know that students are much more likely to struggle in the classroom when their basic needs aren’t being met,” said Representative Chu. “Schools and teachers shouldn’t have to solve these challenges alone. The DIPLOMA Act would bring more comprehensive services like health care, tutoring, and family support into our schools, helping them become full-service community hubs that set students and families up for success in and out of the classroom. I’m proud to reintroduce this bill with Senator Booker so that every child has the resources to succeed.”

“The DIPLOMA Act will equip states with the resources needed to implement and scale the Community Schools we know they want, as well as strengthen school-community partnerships around comprehensive, evidence-based goals for continuous improvement,” said Kwesi Rollins, interim president, Institute for Educational Leadership (the home of the Coalition for Community Schools).“At IEL, we know that in order to build resiliency in our education system, we need innovation and robust public policy that is informed by the needs and interests of those most affected by policy decisions: youth, families, and communities. We believe this bill provides just that and are excited to see the continued expansion of Community Schools through this state-level support.”

The DIPLOMA Act would provide state-led grants to support local partnerships between public schools and at least one community partner such as a local government, institution of higher education, nonprofit, business, or foundation. These partnerships could use funds to:

Integrate services: Build a continuum of academic and social support by coordinating public and private services in a collaborative framework.

Enhance early childhood and family programs: Support early reading initiatives, child care, home visitation, and parental education programs.

Provide academic enrichment and remediation: Offer tutoring, afterschool programs, and summer learning to close achievement gaps and reduce absenteeism.

Expand pathways to graduation: Establish programs such as dual enrollment, early college high schools, and dropout recovery initiatives.

Promote youth development: Facilitate mentoring, leadership training, civic engagement, and career counseling opportunities.

Improve health services: Provide primary care, mental health, dental care, and nutrition services to address students’ physical and emotional well-being.

Strengthen teacher support: Invest in professional development and training for educators and staff to enhance recruitment and retention.

Engage families and communities: Develop programs to educate families, encourage parental involvement, and foster strong community connections.

The DIPLOMA Act is endorsed by the Institute for Educational Leadership (IEL), the Coalition for Community Schools, and the American Federation of Teachers (AFT).

title: Booker, Cleaver Reintroduce Bill Package to End the Exploitation of Incarcerated Workers in Correctional Facilities
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-N.J.), a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, reintroduced three bills in a legislative package to end exploitative labor practices in the nation's correctional facilities, where incarcerated individuals often work for pennies an hour without basic workplace protections. The package includes the Ensuring Work Opportunities in Correctional Facilities Act, the Combating Workplace Discrimination in Correctional Facilities Act, and the Correctional Facilities Occupational Safety and Health Act. Senator Booker reintroduced the Fair Wages for Incarcerated Workers Act, legislation that would ensure incarcerated workers are paid at least the federal minimum wage, in March. U.S. Representative Emanuel Cleaver (MO-05) introduced companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

“Corrupt and exploitative practices against incarcerated workers in correctional facilities have turned ‘prison labor’ into a modern-day form of slavery, forcing people to work in dangerous conditions for little to no pay,” said Senator Booker. “There is nothing just about a system that profits from people’s labor while denying them the basic rights, protections, and dignity every worker deserves. I have spent my career fighting for the dignity and humanity of every person, and these bills are part of that fight. Exploiting incarcerated workers also hurts workers outside prison—employers who can pay pennies an hour have no reason to pay fair wages. These bills would end the exploitation of incarcerated workers, guarantee fair wages and safe working conditions, and hold correctional facilities accountable for discriminatory practices. Being behind bars should never mean being stripped of your humanity.”

“One of the top priorities of America’s correctional system should be ensuring that incarcerated individuals are rehabilitated in such a way that they can successfully reintegrate into society upon their release,” said Congressman Cleaver. “Part of that conversation must focus on ensuring that inmates are afforded the dignities that all Americans deserve, including the protection of basic civil rights, accessibility measures for those with disabilities, and workplace safety standards. I’m proud to stand with Senator Booker and Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove as we introduce this package that will make historic strides on each of these fronts.”

Approximately 80 percent of incarcerated individuals work jobs ranging from facility maintenance to fighting wildfires with an average pay of $0.12 to $0.40 per hour. Many also face dangerous working conditions, limited medical care, and few workplace protections. The legislative package would:

Expand pathways to employment: The Ensuring Work Opportunities in Correctional Facilities Act would authorize $210 million for federal prison job training and education programs, increase the number of authorized private-sector work programs from 50 to 100, and expand funding for state and local education and reentry programs.

Protect incarcerated workers from discrimination: The Combating Workplace Discrimination in Correctional Facilities Act would strengthen protections for incarcerated workers who face discrimination in work assignments or who face retaliation, discipline, or sanctions for declining to work.

Hold correctional facilities accountable for unsafe working conditions: The Correctional Facilities Occupational Safety and Health Act would extend federal and state workplace safety protections to incarcerated workers, require regular reporting on labor conditions and potential violations, and provide grants to help state and local governments enforce workplace safety standards.

"When families across the country are struggling to afford the basics, the federal government should not be contributing to depressed wages by operating prisons where people can be required to work for pennies on the dollar and without federal safety protections that are provided to other workers. Senator Booker’s and Representative Cleaver’s legislative package takes an important step to end some of the federal prison system's most exploitative labor practices by protecting people from harassment and retaliation, extending workplace safety protections to prevent physical injuries, and expanding meaningful opportunities to build skills and prepare for reentry. The federal government should be setting the standard for fair and safe work, not exploiting a prison workforce with very little power to demand better," said Nina Patel, ACLU Senior Policy Counsel, Justice Division.

“Tzedek Association is proud to endorse these bills. We believe the best way to reduce the risk of reoffending is to give people the opportunity to work and learn job skills while they’re incarcerated, so they can earn a living when they come home. These bills also help spouses and children who often bear the heaviest burden of incarceration. When a parent goes to prison, the bills still come due and the children still need to eat. Helping families put food on the table is both a humane response and a way to reduce the risk that financial desperation will lead to crime,” said Rabbi Moshe Margaretten, President of Tzedek Association.

Earlier this year, Senator Booker reintroduced the Fair Wages for Incarcerated Workers Act, which would ensure incarcerated workers are paid at least the federal minimum wage and would eliminate excessive wage deductions. Kim Kardashian endorsed the bill, saying “No matter where you stand politically, we can all agree: when someone works, they should be paid fairly. And if we want people to return home ready to contribute to society, we need to give them a fair shot.”

All three bills are endorsed by the ACLU, Brennan Center, Illinois Alliance for Reentry and Justice, JustLeadership USA, Multifaith Initiative to End Mass Incarceration, National Council of Churches, Reentry Working Group, Safer Foundation, stopthedrugwar.org, and Tzedek Association.

Read the full text of the Combating Workplace Discrimination in Correctional Facilities Act here.

title: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Announces Alabama Power Company Customer Rate Cut
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) announced that Alabama Power Company this morning filed with the Alabama Public Service Commission to reduce customer rates, following a year-long push from her to do so.

“I asked Alabama Power to find a way to lower rates — not just freeze them, but achieve lower power bills for Alabama households. Today, I am excited to say that is happening,” said Senator Britt. “I am proud to have successfully led this charge and that it’s resulted in putting more money back in hardworking Alabamians’ pockets.”

In November 2025, Senator Britt publicly stated that Alabama’s electricity bills were unacceptably high and called for rates to be driven down. Days later, Alabama Power announced a two-year rate freeze.

“I appreciated this step but also knew that more was needed to help Alabama families,” Senator Britt outlined. “That’s why I have been in discussion with Alabama Power over the past 12 months about lowering bills and giving our state’s households even more relief past 2027. Today, the company made good on our conversations, and the result is a win for Alabamians.”

Alabama Power Company this morning filed a rate reduction of $160 million for 2027. Base rates will also stay at or below the newly reduced level throughout 2028, per the filing. The company in a press release said the reduction is driven primarily by increased revenue expected from data centers.

“I’d like to thank Jeff Peoples and his team at Alabama Power for keeping true to their word and working diligently to find a way to make this happen,” Senator Britt added. “As we applaud this rate reduction, it’s not the end of the mission. I want to see more economic growth in Alabama lead to power bills being further driven down for families and small businesses across our great state. Nothing is more important to me as your U.S. Senator than keeping the American Dream alive and well for generations to come. I’m going to continue fighting for hardworking Alabamians every single day.”

The announcement also follows Senator Britt’s vote Thursday to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026. She explained that this permitting reform package is another key prong of her plan to deliver more affordable energy for Alabamians and lower costs across the board.

title: Capito, Colleagues Applaud Senate Passage of Bill to Protect Washington’s Trail
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Recently, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.) joined her colleagues in applauding the U.S. Senate’s passage of the Washington’s Trail — 1753 National Historic Trail Feasibility Study Act by unanimous consent. This legislation would direct the Secretary of the Interior to conduct a feasibility test to designate Washington’s Trail as a national historic trail.

“Washington’s Trail represents an amazing chapter in our nation’s founding, and West Virginia is proud to be a part of that story,” Senator Capito said. “I am grateful to see the Senate pass this bill to study the feasibility of designating Washington’s Trail as a National Historic Trail. This effort will help preserve this important legacy and ensure future generations understand West Virginia’s unique role in America’s early history.”

“We are one step closer to preserving Washington’s Trail and protecting this crucial piece of American history as a lasting educational tool for generations to come,” Senator Fetterman said. “I’m grateful the Senate passed my bill unanimously today and urge my House colleagues to finish the job.”

“Washington’s Trail tells an important story about our nation’s founding, and I’m proud to see this bipartisan legislation pass the Senate,” Senator McCormick said. “I’m grateful to Senator Fetterman and our colleagues for working together to help preserve this critical piece of Pennsylvania’s history, promote tourism, and make it a National Historic Trail.”

“Some of the earliest chapters of our nation’s story unfolded in West Virginia. Recognizing Washington’s Trail is an incredible opportunity to showcase West Virginia’s role in shaping American history and preserve it for generations to come. I’m thrilled the Senate unanimously passed this legislation today, and I hope the House will quickly get it across the finish line,” Senator Justice said.

“Washington’s Trail follows George Washington’s first military and diplomatic mission and highlights Virginia’s role in our nation’s early history,” Senator Kaine said. “As we celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, I’m glad the Senate has taken a bipartisan step toward preserving this historic route for future generations to learn from and enjoy.”

“Beginning in Williamsburg, Virginia, Washington’s Trail offers a unique glimpse into the military and diplomatic ventures that shaped our nation’s first president,” Senator Warner said. “I’m proud that the Senate has passed this bipartisan legislation to recognize the trail’s historical significance and help preserve it for future generations. This designation would not only honor an important part of our nation’s story, but also bring new opportunities for tourism, education, and economic development to communities along the trail.”

The bill now heads to the U.S. House of Representatives, where it was introduced by Representative Mike Kelly (R-Pa.-16).

title: Cramer, Klobuchar Pass Resolution Recognizing National Adoption Month and Day
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – With more than 100,000 children in foster care waiting for adoptive families, co-chairs of the Congressional Coalition on Adoption U.S. Senators Kevin Cramer (R-ND) and Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) brought the issue into national focus with a Senate resolution recognizing November as National Adoption Month and Nov. 21 as National Adoption Day. The Congressional Coalition on Adoption raises awareness and advances policies supporting children and families involved in adoption.

The resolution, unanimously passed by the Senate, recognizes the importance of adoption in providing children with safe, stable, and permanent homes. It also encourages Americans to consider adoption and calls attention to the well-being of children awaiting families.

“As adoptive parents, Kris and I know how life-changing adoption is,” Cramer said. “Every child and family deserves the profound joy and lifelong bond of uniting as a permanent family. National Adoption Month and National Adoption Day are important reminders of the need to strengthen support for children and families throughout the adoption journey. It’s an honor to pass this resolution with Senator Klobuchar, whom I will miss working with in the Senate, especially for a cause that matters so much.”

“We’re grateful for the dedication and commitment of adoptive families who open their homes and hearts to children,” said Klobuchar. “As co-chair of the Congressional Coalition on Adoption, I’m committed to working to ensure every child has a safe, loving, and permanent family.”

The need remains significant. According to the National Council for Adoption, in Fiscal Year 2024, only 46,935 of the 81,752 children in foster care were adopted, leaving nearly 35,000 children seeking their permanent home.

Cramer and Klobuchar have frequently partnered on adoption legislation, like the Supporting Adopted Children and Families Act to expand eligible uses of federal adoption funding and the Safe Home Act to spread awareness of the practice of unregulated custody transfers. They also lead the annual passage of the National Adoption Month and Day Resolution, encouraging Americans to prioritize the welfare of all children.
