title: Sen. Cruz Applauds Senate Passage of Bipartisan Permitting Reform Legislation
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) issued the following statement after the Senate passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026. The bill reforms federal permitting laws to advance critical energy and infrastructure projects.

Sen. Cruz said, “Burdensome regulations and unnecessary permitting delays have made it harder and more expensive to build critical energy infrastructure in America. The Senate’s passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is an important step toward removing these obstacles, expanding domestic energy production and mineral development, lowering costs, and creating American jobs. I urge the House to swiftly advance this legislation to President Trump’s desk.”

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 includes the following permitting reforms:

National Environmental Policy Act: Limits the scope of environmental reviews, expands categorical exclusions for certain projects, establishes a 150-day statute of limitations for legal challenges to environmental documents, and directs courts to remand deficient environmental documents to federal agencies rather than vacating permits or authorizations.

Clean Water Act: Limits certification reviews to compliance with water quality requirements, prohibits states from denying permits for reasons not related to water quality, and establishes a 150-day statute of limitations for challenges to Section 404 permits and permit verifications.

Endangered Species Act: Reduces statutory timelines for Section 7 consultations, establishes a state primacy program under specified conditions, and requires legal challenges to biological opinions to be filed within 150 days of publication.

Data Centers and Large Loads: Requires large data centers to cover specified electricity infrastructure costs rather than shifting those costs to residential and small-business customers.

National Historic Preservation Act: Restricts the range of impacts considered during historic preservation reviews, establishes new consultation deadlines, requires reviews to be completed within applicable NEPA timelines, and sets a 150-day statute of limitations for most challenges. The legislation also generally requires courts to remand deficient reviews rather than vacate approvals, and it restricts judicial review of programmatic agreements and historic preservation determinations.

title: Ernst to Washington: Stop Paying Twice for Broadband
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. –Today Senator Joni Ernst (R-Iowa) introduced the Provide Rigorous Oversight to Optimize Connectivity and Offset Latency (PROTOCOL) Act to improve transparency, prevent duplicative projects, and cut waste, fraud, and abuse in federal broadband spending.

“If we’re going to spend taxpayer dollars on broadband, every dollar should go to unserved communities,” said Ernst. “My PROTOCOL Act will help prevent duplicative projects and make sure rural Iowans, especially our farmers, can count on the same high-speed internet as the rest of the country.”

The PROTOCOL Act would consolidate the Broadband Deployment Locations Map and the National Telecommunications and Information Administration’s (NTIA) Broadband Infrastructure Funding Database into one system. This would ensure taxpayers and government entities have access to a single comprehensive, searchable database of national broadband investments.

Combining these two systems would help federal agencies coordinate projects, Congress and watchdogs track spending, and broadband providers identify communities that still need service.

Representatives August Pfluger (R-Texas) and Debbie Dingell (D-Mich.) are leading companion legislation in the House.

"Billions of taxpayer dollars are flowing into broadband programs, but there is no single avenue to see where those funds are going. The PROTOCOL Act gives Congress, agencies, and the public one searchable database of federal broadband investments, increasing much-needed transparency. Communities across the country are waiting on broadband access, and this legislation brings us one step closer to that reality," said Congressman Pfluger.

“Reliable broadband internet access is critical to every community, and we must ensure no one is left behind,” said Congresswoman Dingell. “The PROTOCOL Act will ensure people across the country, regardless of ZIP code, have access to the opportunities broadband provides by improving the mapping process for broadband funding and better coordinating how funding is awarded.”

"The Broadband Association supports the bipartisan PROTOCOL Act, introduced by Senator Ernst and Reps. Pfluger and Dingell. Using the FCC’s broadband maps to guide federal funding will help agencies better work together, avoid spending taxpayer dollars twice, and get funding to communities that still lack reliable broadband. We urge Congress to pass the PROTOCOL Act,” said Brandon Heiner, Senior Vice President of Government Affairs at USTelecom.

title: WATCH: Gallego Addresses Nationwide Outages, Calls for Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick to Testify
text:
WASHINGTON — This week, Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) joined CNN’s “Erin Burnett OutFront” and MSNOW’s “The Moment with Katy Tur” to discuss the need for Jensen Huang to testify before Congress and answer questions about how advanced AI chips have fallen into Chinese hands and the national security implications, as well as the string of recent outages across government and the private sector that have rightfully concerned Americans. In the wake of this, Senator Gallego re-upped his call to establish his proposed bipartisan Senate select committee on AI to protect against the threats AI poses to our critical infrastructure. He also discussed the Democratic agenda for the upcoming Congress.

Watch: CNN: Erin Burnett OutFront

On Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang:

“I’m not going to jump to the point of saying that he committed a crime. We need to first get to the answers, and we need to get to those questions. That’s why this hearing is going to be important.

“We also need to have Secretary Lutnick under oath for us to understand what was his decision-making process to allow some of these chips to be sold? Was there any outside influence from his sons? Who actually have a lot of interest in data centers in Singapore?

“And so, we want to know exactly what motivated Jensen to actually sell these chips. What was his relationship with this young lady [Alice Huang]? If [it] was one that included potentially selling chips for whatever reason, for whatever cause, then we’ll determine what the next steps are.

“But we need to get to the bottom of this. Our best chips, [Nvidia’s] Blackwell chips, are exactly what puts us ahead of our AI capabilities from China. If we want to continue to win, as Trump claims… we need to have the best infrastructure ahead of them [the Chinese]. And that’s chips.

“And the fact that this administration has been so loose by letting these chips get to China, tell you that there is some type of other pool and motivation that’s going on there.”

On the recent outages across all sectors:

“Not enough information is being shared, especially for people to have oversight. And I think we should be concerned. This is a very high level of encryption. Some of our [highest] levels of communication happen through these channels. So, we should be fairly scared that someone has the capability to do this.

“This is kind of a bigger problem that we’re having right now, You’re seeing the [tech infrastructure] in this country right now — it’s starting to break down. Some of it, supposedly, is mechanical. Some of it can be from malcontents, it can be from other types of potentially bad AI agents.

“And so, what it really calls for is this: this administration, to be on the ball, start actually updating and upgrading all our systems, getting together and getting a good AI policy to really get us ready for a future fight. Because right now it does not look like we are ready for it.”

Watch: MSNOW: The Moment with Katy Tur

On why Congress needs to establish a select committee on AI:

“There’s a lot of things that we have to do, and I think we have to do it very quickly. This is why I think we need to have a select committee of senators that’s going to pass all-encompassing laws that have to deal with AI regulation when it comes to our everyday interactions.

“I have kids. I’m very worried about AI and social media being able to merge and be able to basically mine my kids for information, both for data or for other nefarious things. We should be worried about bad agents that are able to, basically, go rogue and be able to attack and or attack entities that are very important for our national security or even simple things like our bank accounts and things of that nature.

“We need to actually be thinking about what the future looks like when it comes to employment. What’s going to happen when we have a certain percentage of our population that is unemployed. But, at the same time, we have the largest amount of corporate profits that will ever see in the history of this world.

“And yet we’re potentially going to have unemployment that could reach 10 to 15 percent. These are the things that we need to be acting as fast as possible. And I think in a bipartisan manner, what we heard out there was that the concern about AI isn’t just a Democratic thing. It’s not just a Republican thing. It is an American thing.”

On his vision for the 120th Congress:

“There is going to be the opportunity to send standalone bills. Some of that the president may sign, and we should at least give him the opportunity to either veto it [or not]. It could be simple things like minimum wage increases, some of these AI regulation bills, the Medicaid cuts that need to be reversed fairly quickly because they’re about to hit really hard.

“There needs to be all encompassing bills that deal with some of the bigger issues that we are dealing with right now. Childcare, for example. AI, as I was talking about. A bigger conversation on health care. Bigger bills on healthcare. All of these things do need to be going on the same track. And I think that Americans want to see action. They don’t necessarily care about the process. They want to see what the outcome is.”

title: Gillibrand, Colleagues Demand Answers On Dr. Oz’s Actions To Dismantle Medicaid Fraud Prevention
text:
U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) joined five of her Senate colleagues to launch an inquiry into the Trump administration’s politically motivated campaign against state Medicaid programs. This comes after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) withheld billions of dollars from Democratic-led states while dismantling the federal infrastructure designed to detect and prevent fraud.

“The Trump administration’s actions betray the millions of Americans who rely on Medicaid,” said Senator Gillibrand. “This has nothing to do with fraud and everything to do with political retribution against states like New York, and it’s happening while the administration weakens the very oversight that supports Medicaid program integrity. I am demanding answers, and I will do everything in my power to protect New York’s Medicaid funding.”

In their letter to CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz, the senators explained that CMS attacks on state Medicaid programs have undermined fraud-prevention infrastructure within the federal government and targeted Democratic-led states.

“The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services is running the most aggressive public enforcement campaign against state Medicaid programs in the agency’s history, while accelerating the systematic dismantling of the federal infrastructure Congress funded to prevent Medicaid fraud in the first place,” the senators wrote. “That is not program integrity. That is political theater layered over a decade of neglect, with states across the country, and in particular, an overwhelming number of Democratic-led states that have become the Trump administration’s targets, left to answer for both.”

The letter comes as the Trump administration has threatened state health programs with severe funding cuts based on flawed data. CMS recently moved to withhold billions in funding from California and Minnesota without providing any evidence of wrongdoing to the states. In New York, CMS launched a Medicaid fraud investigation after claiming 5 million New Yorkers – nearly 75% of Medicaid enrollees in the state – received personal care services in 2025. Public reporting, including an investigation by the Associated Press, revealed that the actual figure was about 450,000, or 6-7% of enrollees.

Rather than working with states to fix issues, CMS has replaced on-site reviews and dedicated oversight staff with a public relations “War Room” and artificial intelligence pilots. The letter points out that the administration is violating federal law by failing to maintain the minimum required funding and staffing levels for the Medicaid Integrity Program, which was created by Congress to help states fight fraud.

Senator Gillibrand has long fought to protect Medicaid for New Yorkers. In March, she joined Senate colleagues to challenge the Trump administration over its threat to cut New York State’s Medicaid funding. As ranking member of the Senate Aging Committee, she also led colleagues in demanding answers from the administration on how its Medicaid cuts could cause states to scale back services under Medicaid for seniors and people with disabilities.

In addition to Senator Gillibrand, the letter is signed by Senators Adam Schiff (D-CA), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), and Ed Markey (D-MA).

Full text of the letter is availablehere.

title: Grassley Welcomes Over $7.39 Million in Federal Funding for Critical Property Acquisitions to Support Communities Rebuilding after Disaster
text:
WASHINGTON – Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) welcomed news from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) that communities across Iowa will receive over $7.39 million in total federal funding to support key property acquisitions and help Iowans rebuild after disasters. This funding will benefit Iowans in Polk, Dallas, Cherokee, Lyon, Fayette, Buchanan, Sioux and Tama counties.

“This critical funding will help communities across our state repair and rebuild after disaster. I appreciate the Trump administration’s commitment to ensuring Iowans receive this vital funding so critical recovery projects can succeed,” Grassley said. “In the Senate, I’ll keep working to ensure the people of Iowa get the support they need.”

Details on the FEMA awards follow:

City of Clive University Boulevard Property Acquisition: $2,652,127.25 to fund the acquisition and demolition of commercial structures damaged by flooding.

City of Cherokee Property Acquisition: $2,503,800 to fund the acquisition and demolition of 30 residential properties in the city of Cherokee that were damaged as a result of the 2024 flooding and $55,640 to fund the city’s subrecipient management costs.

Lyon County Secondary Roads: $1,498,132.50 to fund permanent repairs as a result of severe storms, flooding, straight-line winds and tornadoes.

Independence - Oelwein Regional Outdoor Warning Siren Project: $456,791.85 to fund the replacement and addition of fifteen outdoor warning sirens as well as the creation of a networked system for regional activation.

Sioux County Conservation Board: $125,502.35 to fund the management of Public Assistance grants as a result of severe storms, flooding, straight-line winds and tornadoes.

City of Toledo Lift Station/Maintenance Building (Generators): $103,936 to fund the installation of two backup generators to the city’s lift station and maintenance building, providing backup power when necessary and with minimal disruption to community services.

title: PHOTOS: Grassley Welcomes Iowa National Guard Members Stationed in D.C. to Capitol for Q&As, Behind-the-Scenes Tours
text:
Click HERE for photos.

WASHINGTON – Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) held three Q&As this week with members of the Iowa National Guard currently deployed to Washington, D.C. and led the service members on three private tours of the U.S. Capitol. Grassley presented each guardsman with a Senate challenge coin.

The service members have been stationed in D.C. since July as part of President Donald Trump’s effort to restore safety to the nation’s capital. In 2024, Washington, D.C., had the fourth-highest homicide rate in the nation and saw an increase of 547% in carjackings between 2018 to 2023. The guardsmen will return to Iowa in mid-December, before Christmas.

Sen. Joni Ernst (R-Iowa) and Reps. Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-Iowa) and Ashley Hinson (R-Iowa) each joined for a Q&A throughout the week.

“For months, these Iowa National Guard members have faithfully served to help make the District of Columbia safe again for residents and visitors alike. I was grateful for the opportunity to thank them personally and express my gratitude by providing them a special tour of the U.S. Capitol. After months away from their friends and family, Iowans can look forward to welcoming them home with open arms just in time for Christmas,” Grassley said.

Grassley speaks with Iowa National Guard members in the U.S. Capitol.

Click HERE for more photos.

Background:

On August 11, 2025, President Trump declared a crime emergency in the nation's capital, mobilizing National Guard troops to support federal and local law enforcement.

In November 2025, two West Virginia National Guard members were shot in a targeted attack just blocks from the White House. Specialist Sarah Beckstrom later died of her wounds, and Staff Sergeant Andrew Wolfe sustained critical injuries. During his 2026 State of the Union address, President Trump awarded Purple Hearts to Wolfe and posthumously to Beckstrom.

Alongside the Make D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force, crime has dropped across the capital, resulting in:

Over 16,000 arrests

35 homicide suspects locked up

More than 100 known gang members removed

Over 3,200 drug-related arrests

Nearly 2,000 illegal firearms seized

25 missing children returned home

title: Q&A: Bipartisan Victory for Affordability
text:
Q: How will the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act help lower energy costs?

A: Families are digging deeper into their wallets to pay their monthly utility bills. This landmark bipartisan legislation cuts government red tape and regulatory uncertainty that drives up energy costs for American families and slows critical infrastructure upgrades. The broken federal permitting system also slows economic growth, delays hiring, chills private sector investment and puts interstate power lines and clean energy projects in the crosshairs of endless litigation. That’s why I supported sensible reforms built by bipartisan consensus to update decades-old environmental permitting rules and fix bureaucratic logjams. Simply put, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act brings sanity to regulatory gridlock. This legislation will pave the way for critical infrastructure projects to strengthen the nation’s energy grid, improve transmission lines and boost pipeline capacity. The Senate-passed legislation helps establish clear timelines from beginning to end, making it harder for previously approved projects from getting kiboshed by frivolous litigation designed to delay and deny. Specifically, the legislation requires most challenges to be filed within 150 days after a project receives government approval. This provision will give the green light to energy and construction companies to hire workers and get shovels in the ground while also providing certainty to lenders and investors that the project won’t get yanked around in the courts. The nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office expects the legislation will boost economic growth and create jobs. Keep in mind, public participation and judicial oversight remain integral to the permitting process.

Q: How have permitting delays impacted Iowa’s economy?

A: During my annual 99 county meetings, I hear directly from Iowa manufacturers and rural electric cooperatives about the impact permitting delays has on their customers and operations. The costs to Iowa manufacturers add up to approximately $280 million every year. At the same time, delayed upgrades to transmission lines and natural gas pipelines contribute to rising utility costs that pinch family budgets. All told, the value of Iowa projects stuck in the federal permitting process comes to $16.8 billion with a total economic impact reaching $29 billion that includes jobs, in-state spending, tax revenue and more. The federal permitting process has become an albatross hanging around the economy’s neck and needlessly delays infrastructure investment in communities across the country. This legislation will help unleash projects to build roads, bridges and energy infrastructure that create jobs, raise wages and foster economic vitality.

Consider the federal permitting process averages four years for a project to advance beyond the regulatory and litigation hurdles. Critical upgrades that impact energy efficiency and public safety are held hostage to arcane procedures, missed deadlines and bureaucratic bottlenecks. This adds up to higher energy costs for American families.

title: VIDEO: Grassley Hears from Mothers Who Lost Children to Deadly Kratom
text:
WASHINGTON – Senate Judiciary Committee Chairman Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) this week met with parents whose children were killed or harmed by botanical kratom and kratom-related substances, including 7-OH. The meeting follows Grassley’s recent letter to the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) urging the agencies to reconsider proposed changes to kratom-related substances’ emergency scheduling order, which would allow deadly kratom products to remain widely sold in gas stations and convenience stores across the country.

“We know that kratom is an opioid that kills people. We have to have strong enforcement of that. I’m sorry for the stories that I’m going to hear, but I’m happy that we have these moms working on this very serious problem that we have with drugs in America. It’s tragic what’s happened to not only these moms, but other families all over the country,” Grassley stated ahead of the meeting.

A fact sheet on kratom and its emergency scheduling order is available HERE.

Wednesday’s meeting attendees included:

Rebecca Strang of Georgia, who lost her son, Robert, at the University of Mississippi in September 2026;

Tia Rustici of Idaho, who lost her daughter, Kielee, in 2025;

Susan Eppard of Michigan, who lost her son, Matthew, in 2021; and

Dean Francis, the founder of End Kratom Addiction, who nearly lost his son, Cameron, to a decade-long battle with kratom addiction.

Following the meeting, Strang, Rustici, Eppard and Francis delivered public remarks. Download video of the mothers’ remarks, filmed by the Foundation for Drug Policy Solutions, HERE. Download video of Grassley’s remarks HERE.

VIDEO

“I'm here today for Robert, because I am determined to find a purpose for my pain, and for Robert's life… My position is very clear: all kratom products should be banned. We have to stop putting profit and industry interests ahead of people's lives. It's time to look beyond who stands to profit and focus on who stands to suffer. Robert's life mattered, and his death matters,” said Rebecca Strang. Full remarks available HERE.

“Something that is sold in the gas station next to the candy bars, something that's marketed as safe, is what destroyed my daughter. Kielee was not using street drugs. She was not drinking alcohol. Most importantly, she was not using 7-OH or synthetics. She was using powder kratom… I cannot bring my daughter back, but if telling her story can help save another parent from being where I am, I will never stop talking,” said Tia Rustici. Full remarks available HERE.

“My 22-year-old son Matthew died from natural botanical kratom leaf powder. According to his toxicology, he had no street drugs, no prescription drugs and no alcohol in his system. The autopsy showed he was perfectly healthy and should have lived out a full life… Kratom leaf is an opioid, and it should be banned throughout the United States… My son should have lived,” said Susan Eppard. Full remarks available HERE.

“These three moms shouldn't have to be here. They live with a pain that very few people will ever understand. But they're here to do everything they can to prevent other families across this nation from the hell and the torment that they endure on a daily basis. All of this is due to the greed of a nefarious industry that exploits loopholes in our dietary supplement laws to masquerade a highly addictive and deadly drug as a plant-based herbal supplement... I want to thank Senator Grassley today for being the fighter that he is to help stop this national nightmare... But no one deserves more credit for today than these three moms who traveled here and openly are sharing their stories in order to protect mothers,” said Dean Francis. Full remarks available HERE.

Photos from the meeting and media availability are available HERE. Photos of Robert Strang, Kielee Rustici and Matthew Eller are available HERE, courtesy of their mothers.

title: Hawley Releases Statement on Anti-Farmer Transmission Bill
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Senator Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) released the following statement after voting against the Senate’s transmission bill:

“Legislation that threatens to take farmers’ land is legislation I won’t support. I offered common sense amendments to protect farmers but was denied so much as a vote. This bill is stuffed with giveaways to data centers and industry at the expense of farmers. Missouri farmers have had enough of that.”

Senator Hawley offered four amendments to add new rights and protections for farmers, ranchers, and landowners from eminent domain takings of their land for electric transmission projects.

title: Hawley Urges State Department to Advocate for Release of Hong Kong Rights Champion Joshua Wong
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Senator Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) wrote to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, urging him to press President Xi of China to release human rights activist Joshua Wong, who was persecuted after fighting for democracy in Hong Kong.

Senator Hawley wrote, “As you lead U.S. diplomacy with China, I urge you to press Beijing to release Hong Kong rights champion Joshua Wong. Just last week, the Hong Kong High Court sentenced Joshua to ten more years in prison on politically motivated charges of foreign collusion. The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) cynically concocted this prosecution to extend Joshua’s imprisonment past January 2027, when he was due to be released after more than six years behind bars for courageously defending the liberty of Hongkongers.”

He continued, “Sadly, the CCP has long used my friendship with Joshua to accuse him of disloyalty. And it is obvious to anyone looking that Hong Kong’s democratic institutions have since 2020 been transformed into instruments of CCP coercion. “

Senator Hawley concluded, “Joshua’s immediate and unconditional release would be a strong signal of China’s willingness to forge a sustainable and cooperative relationship with the United States. I respectfully encourage you to build on the Administration’s successes securing the release of other political prisoners around the world by insisting that President Xi free Joshua Wong.”

Read the full letter here or below.

November 20, 2026

The Honorable Marco Rubio

Secretary of State

U.S. Department of State

2201 C Street, N.W.

Washington, D.C. 20451

Dear Secretary Rubio,

As you lead U.S. diplomacy with China, I urge you to press Beijing to release Hong Kong rights champion Joshua Wong. Just last week, the Hong Kong High Court sentenced Joshua to ten more years in prison on politically motivated charges of foreign collusion. The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) cynically concocted this prosecution to extend Joshua’s imprisonment past January 2027, when he was due to be released after more than six years behind bars for courageously defending the liberty of Hongkongers.

Joshua is a patriot who is being persecuted by the CCP for standing up to tyranny. Like you, I met Joshua during his years fighting for democracy and the rule of law in Hong Kong. The impression left by his character, poise, and resolve has stayed with me to this day.

Sadly, the CCP has long used my friendship with Joshua to accuse him of disloyalty. And it is obvious to anyone looking that Hong Kong’s democratic institutions have since 2020 been transformed into instruments of CCP coercion.

Joshua’s immediate and unconditional release would be a strong signal of China’s willingness to forge a sustainable and cooperative relationship with the United States. I respectfully encourage you to build on the Administration’s successes securing the release of other political prisoners around the world by insisting that President Xi free Joshua Wong.

Sincerely,

title: Hickenlooper, Bennet, Colleagues Introduce Resolution to Commemorate Transgender Day of Remembrance
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators John Hickenlooper, Michael Bennet, and Mazie Hirono, along with 13 of their Senate colleagues, introduced a resolution commemorating November 20, 2026 as Transgender Day of Remembrance (TDOR).

“We’ve experienced years of rising discrimination and hate, specifically anti-transgender hate, across the country. We will not accept it. Transgender rights are human rights,” said Hickenlooper. “Everyone has the right to be who they are without being targeted.”

“On Transgender Day of Remembrance, we stand united against the discrimination and attacks faced by the transgender community in Colorado and across the nation,” said Bennet. “We honor the memory of those lost and recommit to protecting the rights and safety of the transgender community to ensure that everyone can live with dignity and respect.”

“As anti-transgender hate continues to rise nationwide, bolstered by the Trump regime’s harmful rhetoric, supporting and protecting transgender and gender-nonconforming individuals is critical. This resolution honors the lives of those who were lost to violence and educates communities about the dangers and discrimination transgender people face,” said Hirono. “Transgender rights are human rights, and I remain committed to defending everyone’s right to live openly, safely, and without fear.”

Transgender and gender-nonconforming people continue to face disproportionately high rates of violent crime. Following the still-unsolved murder of Rita Hester, a transgender woman of color, Gwendolyn Ann Smith founded TDOR to honor Hester and other transgender people whose lives were lost to violence. This year’s resolution also commemorates Stonewall veteran and longtime transgender advocate, Victoria Cruz, who passed away in June. Ms. Cruz dedicated her life to helping victims of domestic violence, police violence, and rape in the LGBTQ+ community.

The full text of the resolution is available HERE.

title: Hirono Leads Colleagues in Commemorating Transgender Day of Remembrance
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.–Today, U.S. Senator Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI), led 15 of her colleagues in commemorating November 20th, 2026, as Transgender Day of Remembrance (TDOR). Each year, Senator Hirono introduces the Transgender Day of Remembrance resolution to honor the lives of transgender people lost to violence in the United States in the last year.

“As anti-transgender hate continues to rise nationwide, bolstered by the Trump regime’s harmful rhetoric, supporting and protecting transgender and gender-nonconforming individuals is critical. This resolution honors the lives of those who were lost to violence and educates communities about the dangers and discrimination transgender people face,” said Senator Hirono. “Transgender rights are human rights, and I remain committed to defending everyone’s right to live openly, safely, and without fear."

Transgender and gender-nonconforming people continue to face disproportionately high rates of violent crime. Following the still-unsolved murder of Rita Hester, a transgender woman of color, Gwendolyn Ann Smith founded TDOR to honor Hester and other transgender people whose lives were lost to violence. This year’s resolution also commemorates Stonewall veteran and longtime transgender advocate, Victoria Cruz, who passed away in June. Ms. Cruz dedicated her life to helping victims of domestic violence, police violence, and rape in the LGBTQ+ community.

“On Transgender Day of Remembrance, we stand united against the discrimination and attacks faced by the transgender community in Colorado and across the nation,” said Senator Bennet. “We honor the memory of those lost and recommit to protecting the rights and safety of the transgender community to ensure that everyone can live with dignity and respect.”

“All Americans deserve to live their lives freely and authentically—without fear of discrimination or harm simply because of their gender identity. I’m proud to introduce this resolution amplifying the voices of our nation’s transgender communities and recognizing the dangers they face simply for living their lives. Transgender rights are human rights, and I look forward to continuing the fight to make our country a more inclusive place for all,” said Senator Blumenthal.

“On this Transgender Day of Remembrance, we honor the transgender Americans whose lives have been cut short by hate,” said Senator Duckworth. “As Trump continues his campaign of cruelty against the trans community, I will always fight for the safety, dignity and respect that all human beings deserve.”

“We’ve experienced years of rising discrimination and hate, specifically anti-transgender hate, across the country. We will not accept it. Transgender rights are human rights,” said Senator Hickenlooper. “Everyone has the right to be who they are without being targeted."

“This Transgender Day of Remembrance, we reaffirm our commitment that trans rights are human rights, and we honor the trans people who have lost their lives to violence,” said Senator Markey. “As the trans community continues to face an all-out assault of discrimination and hate from the White House, we must continue to fight back against the vitriolic anti-trans policies of this Administration and stand with trans people everywhere to ensure that all people are afforded the basic rights and dignity they deserve.”

“Let us all recognize the enormous discrimination and violence that our transgender communities face,” said Senator Merkley. “On this day of remembrance, we honor the lives and legacies of all in the transgender community who have been taken by violence, just for being who they are, and commit to working toward a world where everyone can live a full and free life.”

“Everyone deserves the opportunity to live authentically without fear of violence or hate, but members of the transgender community have too often been denied that right,” said Senator Padilla. “On Transgender Day of Remembrance, we honor the members of the transgender community whose lives were tragically cut short by violence. Amid an alarming prevalence of violence against transgender people, we must stand together in our fight to build a better future for American to live freely, safely, and authentically.”

“Trans people deserve to live with equality and dignity – just like everyone else,” said Senator Schatz. “Transgender Day of Remembrance is about highlighting the continued threats that the trans community faces every day and honoring those who were killed solely because of who they were.”

“The transgender community has faced increasing hate and violence as the Trump administration has demonized them. I’m proud to join Senator Hirono and my Senate colleagues in standing up against this ugly sentiment, remembering the lives tragically lost in this epidemic of bigotry, and committing ourselves to building a safer and more inclusive future. All Americans deserve to live as their authentic selves without fear for who they are,” said Senator Schiff.

The resolution is endorsed by the Human Rights Campaign, Advocates for Trans Equality (A4TE), and the National LGBTQ Task Force Action Fund.

In addition to Senator Hirono, the resolution was cosponsored by Senators Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Chris Coons (D-DE), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), John Fetterman (D-PA), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Ed Markey (D-MA), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Adam Schiff (D-CA), MD), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), and Elizabeth Warren (D-MA).

A companion resolution was introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives by Representatives Pramila Jaypal (D-WA), Sara Jacobs (D-CA), and Mark Takano (D-CA).

title: Husted-backed package to advance America’s permitting process, lower energy costs passes Senate
text:
“I’m especially proud this package includes language I secured to protect Ohio families, farmers and small businesses from footing the bill for data center energy costs.”

WASHINGTON – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) voted to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), a bill that would reform the nation’s permitting and environmental review processes, accelerate critical infrastructure projects and help lower energy costs for American families.

The package passed the Senate on November 19, 2026, by a vote of 62-33.

“Permitting reform is affordability. This package will help us build more energy, lower costs, create jobs and strengthen America’s energy supply chain. It cuts unnecessary red tape, establishes reasonable timelines for critical projects and gives businesses the certainty they need to invest and grow. I’m especially proud this package includes language I secured to protect Ohio families, farmers and small businesses from footing the bill for data center energy costs. This has been a priority of mine in the Senate, and I’m glad we were able to work across the aisle to get this done,” said Husted.

As a member of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, Husted has been actively involved in efforts to modernize the nation’s permitting system. The bill would:

Establish a clear, efficient federal environmental review process to give infrastructure and energy projects greater predictability.

Create a defined legal process for developers, the public and other stakeholders to resolve disputes without years of costly delays.

Provide greater certainty for approved projects by limiting the circumstances under which federal agencies can rescind or suspend issued permits.

BAAJA also includes language Husted negotiated, similar to provisions in his Ratepayer Protection Act, to protect consumers from footing the bill for data center energy and infrastructure costs.

Currently $45.1 billion of Ohio projects are stuck in the federal permitting process right now, and federal permitting delays cost Ohio manufacturers $669 billion annually. BAAJA would reform the process to be quicker and lower costs.

Specifically, the legislation would:

Set deadlines for environmental reviews, requiring environmental assessments within one year and full environmental impact statements within two years.

Limit lawsuits by requiring claims under the National Environmental Policy Act to be filed within 150 days.

Protect issued permits by limiting the circumstances under which federal agencies can rescind or suspend valid permits.

Preserve Ohio’s authority over transmission line siting and data center electricity rates.

title: Senators Justice, Kelly Introduce the Safe Water Instruction Matters (SWIM) Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – This week, Senator Jim Justice and Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ) introduced the Safe Water Instruction Matters (SWIM) Act, which would authorize basic swimming lessons as a qualified expense for Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs).

“Learning how to swim isn’t some luxury; whether you’re a young kid just starting out or an adult who never got the chance to learn, it’s a life-saving skill that cuts the risk of drowning by nearly 90 percent. Letting West Virginians and folks all across America use their own hard-earned HSA and FSA dollars to pay for swimming lessons for themselves or their kids is a no-brainer in my book. I’m proud to team up with Senator Kelly on this bipartisan bill because saving lives is something every single one of us can get behind,” said Senator Jim Justice.

“Every parent wants to make sure their kids are safe around water, and learning how to swim can save lives. This is particularly true in Arizona, where drowning is the leading cause of death for young children,” said Senator Mark Kelly. “But for too many families, the cost of swim lessons can be a barrier. Making these lessons more affordable is just common sense.”

BACKGROUND:

Each year in the U.S., around 4,000 people lose their lives to drowning, while 8,000 experience nonfatal drownings.

Research shows that formal swimming lessons can reduce the risk of drowning by as much as 88 percent.

Drowning remains the leading cause of death for children aged one to four.

Basic swimming lessons are not currently listed as an eligible HSA or FSA expense.

This legislation would expand eligible HSA and FSA expenses to include swimming lessons, increasing access to potentially lifesaving instruction for both children and adults while reducing financial barriers for families.

Companion legislation (H.R. 1506) was introduced in the House in 2025 by Representative Greg Steube (R-FL-17).

title: Kaine, Senate Foreign Relations Committee Democrats Issue Statement Ahead of President Trump’s Meetings with Xi and Putin
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, U.S. Senators Tim Kaine (D-VA), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Chris Coons (D-DE), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), and Jacky Rosen (D-NV), members of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee (SFRC), released the following statement ahead of President Trump’s meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit:

“President Trump must use this summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin to defend American interests and values and confront the growing threats posed by Beijing and Moscow—not simply look out for his own bottom line,” said the senators.

“This meeting must not be yet another convergence of would-be-strongmen, carving up the world into spheres of influence, but an American president fighting for American values, including the rule of law. He must stand up to President Xi and make clear that the United States will strictly enforce export controls to prevent Beijing from exploiting American technology to erode our economic and national security advantages. He must confront China’s military intimidation of Taiwan and reaffirm our commitments under the Taiwan Relations Act and the Six Assurances by following the law and sending $14 billion in previously approved arms sales to Taiwan. He must also demand the release of Jimmy Lai, Min Zin and all other Americans wrongfully detained in China,” continued the senators.

“China and Russia are cooperating in unprecedented and dangerous ways to undermine American security and prosperity. Xi and Putin cannot be allowed to use this meeting as a forum to advance their interests at the expense of the United States. The President should not let China’s indispensable support for Russia’s brutal war against Ukraine continue; he must crack down on Chinese suppliers and financial institutions facilitating Putin’s war machine that murders Ukrainian civilians with every passing day. This can only be achieved by standing up to Xi and Putin, rather than accommodating their imperial impulses. President Trump must be prepared to tell Putin unequivocally that European security is non-negotiable and that there will be no talks about Ukraine without Ukraine,” stressed the senators.

“American security cannot be traded away for photo opportunities or personal aggrandizement. President Trump must demonstrate that he is prepared to impose real costs on Putin for his aggression, rather than reward him with concessions that undermine Ukraine, our NATO Allies and U.S. national security. It is clear that the American people want lower prices, not more pageantry. We urge President Trump to use this summit to make Americans safer, strengthen our alliances and counter the destructive actions of our adversaries,” concluded the senators.

title: Kelly, Justice Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Make Swimming Lessons More Affordable for Families
text:
Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and Jim Justice (R-WV) introduced the bipartisan Safet Water Instruction Matters (SWIM) Act to help more families afford swimming lessons. The legislation would allow Americans to use their Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) and Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs) to pay for basic swimming lessons for themselves and their children.

Drowning is the leading cause of death for children ages one to four, and research shows that formal swimming lessons can reduce the risk of drowning by as much as 88 percent. However, the cost of lessons can be a barrier for families. The SWIM Act would make swimming instruction an eligible HSA and FSA expense, giving families another way to pay for lessons.

“Every parent wants to make sure their kids are safe around water, and learning how to swim can save lives. This is particularly true in Arizona, where drowning is the leading cause of death for young children,” said Kelly. “But for too many families, the cost of swim lessons can be a barrier. Making these lessons more affordable is just common sense.”

“Learning how to swim isn’t some luxury; whether you’re a young kid just starting out or an adult who never got the chance to learn, it’s a life-saving skill that cuts the risk of drowning by nearly 90 percent. Letting West Virginians and folks all across America use their own hard-earned HSA and FSA dollars to pay for swimming lessons for themselves or their kids is a no brainer in my book. I’m proud to team up with Senator Kelly on this bipartisan bill because saving lives is something every single one of us can get behind,” said Justice.

Background:

Each year, approximately 4,000 Americans die from drowning, and another 8,000 experience nonfatal drownings. Despite the proven benefits of swimming instruction, basic swimming lessons are not currently an eligible expense under HSAs or FSAs.

title: Kelly Presses Hegseth on Reports of Politically Driven Blocks on Military Promotions
text:
Letter demands answers on reported effort to keep qualified officers from senior leadership based on perceived political or ideological views

Read in MS NOW: Democrats demand Hegseth answer why he blocked top brass promotions

Today, Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ) led his Democratic Senate Armed Services Committee colleagues Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Gary Peters (D-MI), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) in pressing Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth over reports that he and his office directed an effort to block the promotions of highly qualified military officers based on perceived political or ideological views.

“On November 9, MS NOW reported that your office has sought to prevent certain officers from advancing to senior leadership positions based on their past participation in the implementation of Department policies under previous administrations, diversity initiatives, or public statements. According to the reporting, your staff conducted internet searches into the backgrounds of military officers and communicated instructions by telephone to avoid creating a written record of additional criteria,” the senators said.

They expressed particular concern that officers could be penalized for carrying out lawful policies set by previous administrations: “It is particularly troubling that officers may be penalized for faithfully implementing lawful policies and directives issued by previous administrations. This sends a dangerous message that servicemembers’ careers depend on whether their past service aligns with the political preferences of the current administration, rather than their performance, judgment, and leadership.”

The senators warned that the practice could damage military readiness for years: “Removing qualified officers from promotion consideration for political reasons risks depriving the military of that experience and undermining trust and respect between military leadership and servicemembers. It could also deter future generations from considering military service if they see accomplished officers’ careers derailed by the political whims of an administration.”

title: WATCH: In SASC Hearing, Kelly Says Rushed Iran War with No Strategic Plan Left Navy Unprepared
text:
During a Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) confirmation hearing, Arizona Senator and Navy combat veteran Mark Kelly (D-AZ) pressed William Toti, nominee for Under Secretary of the Navy, on why the Navy was not prepared for Iranian missile and drone attacks on its primary logistics hub in Bahrain. Kelly said President Donald Trump and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth took the country into war with Iran without a clear strategy, and that the Navy must learn from it.

Kelly opened by asking why the Navy wasn’t ready after Iranian strikes damaged its base in Bahrain: “This vulnerability was not a surprise. We’ve long known adversaries could target the port’s fuel supplies and repair facilities that the Navy depends on. So, why wasn’t the Navy better prepared to sustain operations after losing access to a critical logistics hub? What contingency plans were in place and why weren’t they sufficient?”

Kelly pointed to the White House’s timeline and the lack of a strategic goal as the reason the Navy was caught unprepared: “It seems that the President wanted this to happen on a timeline that was not conducive to the preparation we would need. […] I did not agree with getting into a war with Iran. I think the President got into this without a strategic goal. He had a plan that was probably developed by the Secretary of Defense, who, in my opinion, that plan was not consistent with anything that made sense to me, having experience doing this.”

Kelly said the Administration’s lack of planning has left it with no path forward, and that the Navy must learn from it: “For that reason, the Administration right now is stuck, does not know what to do. We need to be better at planning scenarios, and we need to be thinking ahead. And that did not happen in this case.”

Sen. Kelly questions William Toti during a SASC hearing.

Click here to download a video of Kelly’s remarks. See the transcript below:

Senator Kelly:

Thank you, Mr. Chairman. Mr. Toti, one of the clearest lessons from the war with Iran is how vulnerable our forward deployed logistics infrastructure is to missile and drone attacks. Iran strikes on the Navy base in Bahrain severely damaged the primary logistics hub in the region, forcing the Navy to shift sustainment operations to more distant locations, including Diego Garcia. That is significantly complicated our ability to resupply ships operating in the region.

I talked about this with Hung Cao a little bit yesterday, the impacts of that. But this vulnerability was not a surprise. We’ve long known adversaries could target the port’s fuel supplies and repair facilities that the Navy depends on. So, why wasn’t the Navy better prepared to sustain operations after losing access to a critical logistics hub? What contingency plans were in place and why weren’t they sufficient?

Mr. William J. Toti:

Senator, first, thank you for your leadership in logistics in general and the merchant fleet in particular. As a World War Two guy, historian guy, I understand the lessons learned, the lessons well. We are learning a lot of lessons from the war with Iran. The vulnerability that you speak of shore-based infrastructures is equally true in the Pacific, as you well know, Senator. And so, it’s something we need to understand and learn from. We certainly have thought these things through, as it pertains to the Pacific. And so, we will continue to learn these lessons and continue to develop—

Kelly:

What is the lesson?

Toti:

Lesson is we need multiple ways of achieving the same outcomes, Senator.

Kelly:

So, in the case of— why don’t you talk for a second, what’s the status of the naval support activity in Bahrain?

Toti:

I think it’s already been reported that it is it has been damaged. I do not—

Kelly:

Do we have personnel there?

Toti:

We had personnel there.

Kelly:

Do we have any operations there at all?

Toti:

Senator, I stood down as the Under Secretary on September 14th. I’m not currently apprised of the status. And so, I don’t know the truth on that issue, but I will find out and I’ll bring you the answer.

Kelly:

So, it certainly was in range of Iranian weapon systems. I think it’s fair to say we were not prepared for attacks from the Iranian missiles and drones that hit the base there. Why wasn’t the Navy more prepared? Was it that the white House didn’t give the Navy enough time? Did this? Did this operation start too quickly? It seems that the President wanted this to happen on a timeline that was not conducive to the preparation we would need. Would you agree with that?

Toti:

Senator, I’ve been nominated for the position of Under Secretary of the Navy. As you know, the operational planning is not part of the portfolio of the Under Secretary of the Navy. So, truthfully, I was not involved in the process and couldn’t answer with any real integrity.

Kelly:

But would you agree that we were not prepared at the Navy base in Bahrain?

Toti:

I will certainly agree that we can learn from these lessons and do better the next time.

Kelly:

So, as we think of the Western Pacific, what do you think we should take from what happened in CENTCOM with the base in Bahrain and our logistic challenges, and how do we apply to that them to a conflict if we were to get in a conflict with the Chinese?

Toti:

Senator, we have place already plans to improve our logistic support with ships like landing ship medium. We do need more auxiliary ships, as you well know, sir, you’ve been leading on that issue. And by having mobile logistic forces as opposed to fixed logistic forces, we very much complicate the calculus of any adversary that we might face.

Kelly:

Well, getting logistics across a 5500-mile ocean is going to be a challenge. I’ve talked about that a lot with our sealift capacity. We’re down to U.S.-flagged oceangoing merchant ships with U.S. crews; we’re down to 80. The Chinese have over 5,000. It is a national security imperative to rebuild that fleet. We have the Military Sealift Command, but I think, as folks understand what we have in the inventory on day one of a war is not the same if you’re three or six months in. So, I appreciate you working with us to try to improve the situation here but I also think we need to do a better job of preparing our bases, our forces, when we know there is an imminent conflict, and I did not agree with getting into a war with Iran.

I think the President got into this without a strategic goal. He had a plan that was probably developed by the Secretary of Defense, who, in my opinion, that plan was not consistent with anything that made sense to me, having experience doing this. And for that reason, the Administration right now is stuck, does not know what to do. We need to be better at planning scenarios, and we need to be thinking ahead. And that did not happen in this case. Thank you, Mr. Chairman.

title: WATCH: Kelly, Slotkin, Crow, Goodlander, Houlahan Speak on One-Year Anniversary of “Illegal Orders” Video
text:
“None of us are backing down”

This week, U.S. Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), alongside U.S. Representatives Jason Crow (D-CO-06), Maggie Goodlander (D-NH-02), and Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA-06), spoke about the anniversary of their video citing the Uniform Code of Military Justice stating that members of the military must refuse illegal orders.

Kelly illustrated how Trump’s campaign of threats and intimidation in response to the video demonstrates how the president will use his power to try to silence anyone who tries to hold him accountable.

“Last year, I said we were the first ones through the breach, and we’re seeing that now. Trump is threatening more members of Congress with prosecution for doing their jobs and for asking questions that he just doesn’t want to answer,” Kelly said. “He doesn’t want anyone asking about his tens of thousands of stock trades. He doesn’t want anyone looking into his family’s crypto scams, and he certainly doesn’t want anyone looking into who’s writing the big checks for his new ballroom. So, he’s using the same tired tactics that he tried against us, hoping that those members of Congress will back down. But it’s not going to work. The American people made clear they are sick and tired of Trump’s corruption and chaos.”

Sens. Kelly and Slotkin and Reps. Crow, Goodlander, and Houlahan speak at the Capitol.

Watch Kelly’s full remarks here. See more excerpts below.

Kelly spoke to how a simple reminder of the law showed how far Trump will go to silence his critics:

“As Senator Slotkin pointed out, the five of us, along with Congressman Deluzio, released this video. It was a simple reminder servicemembers must refuse illegal orders. Nothing was controversial about that. It’s the law. But what happened next showed how far Donald Trump will go to silence people. People who question him. Remember, this is a guy who sent a mob to Capitol Hill to attack the other branch of government when he didn’t like the outcome of an election that he lost.”

title: Klobuchar, Cramer Pass Resolution Recognizing National Adoption Month and Day
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Kevin Cramer (R-ND), co-chairs of the Congressional Coalition on Adoption, introduced a Senate resolution recognizing November as National Adoption Month and Nov. 21 as National Adoption Day. The resolution, unanimously passed by the Senate, recognizes the importance of adoption in providing children with safe, stable, and permanent homes. It also encourages Americans to consider adoption and calls attention to the well-being of children awaiting families.

“We’re grateful for the dedication and commitment of adoptive families who open their homes and hearts to children,” said Klobuchar. “As co-chair of the Congressional Coalition on Adoption, I’m committed to working to ensure every child has a safe, loving, and permanent family.”

“As adoptive parents, Kris and I know how life-changing adoption is,” said Cramer. “Every child and family deserves the profound joy and lifelong bond of uniting as a permanent family. National Adoption Month and National Adoption Day are important reminders of the need to strengthen support for children and families throughout the adoption journey. It’s an honor to pass this resolution with Senator Klobuchar, whom I will miss working with in the Senate, especially for a cause that matters so much.”

The Congressional Coalition on Adoption raises awareness and advances policies supporting children and families involved in adoption. The need remains significant. According to the National Council for Adoption, in Fiscal Year 2024, only 46,935 of the 81,752 children in foster care were adopted, leaving nearly 35,000 children seeking their permanent home.

This week, Klobuchar received Voice for Adoption’s Legislative Champion Award, which honors members of Congress for working in a bipartisan manner on behalf of children in foster care and families that help them find a safe, loving, and permanent home.

Klobuchar and Cramer have frequently partnered on adoption legislation, such as the Supporting Adopted Children and Families Act, which expands eligible uses of federal adoption funding, and the Safe Home Act, which raises awareness of unregulated custody transfers.

title: ICYMI: Lankford Applauds Passage of Permitting Reform Bill to Jumpstart Building in America Again
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — US Senator James Lankford (R-OK), Senate Republican Conference Vice Chair, last night applauded Senate passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, bipartisan legislation to cut federal red tape, speed up the permitting process, and make it easier to build major projects across America.

“Gas, electricity, and construction cost too much in America,” said Lankford. “The wasted time and money of federal permitting absolutely drives up the cost of everything. This bill updates the permitting process so government can get out of the way and let Americans build again at a lower cost. This is a great step toward creating more jobs, higher wages, and bringing more economic growth to every zip code in the country.”

The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act changes how federal agencies review and approve major projects.

The cost of permitting delays in Oklahoma:

$161 million: Annual cost of federal permitting delays to Oklahoma manufacturers.

$55 billion: Total economic impact, including jobs, in-state spending, and tax revenue, tied to Oklahoma projects held up in the federal permitting queue.

The cost of permitting delays nationwide:

$240–$280 billion: Value of new investments entering the federal permitting process each year.

$12.1 billion: Annual cost of federal permitting delays to American manufacturers.

title: Lankford Urges Colleagues to Hold the Line on Intoxicating Hemp Ban
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — US Senator James Lankford (R-OK) last week sent a letter urging his colleagues to ensure the ban on intoxicating hemp products takes effect on December 11th and protect children from products disguised as harmless hemp. The ban was delayed in the most recent Continuing Resolution passed on September 2nd.

You can read the letter HERE or below:

Dear Colleague,

Today marks the day when intoxicating hemp products were supposed to be banned from the market. The most recent Continuing Resolution delayed the implementation date to December 11th. It is critical that this ban goes into effect on December 11th. It is also critical that we remember how we got here and what is at stake for American communities, especially children.

One year ago, the Senate voted 76-24 to fix the hemp loophole that was created in the 2018 Farm Bill. In 2018, Congress redefined hemp as cannabis with less than .3% Delta-9 THC. The goal of that definition was to remove non-intoxicating hemp from Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act. Supporters of that provision claimed the focus was to protect industrial hemp–the plant that is used to make rope, fabric, and other consumer goods. I remember that conversation and was supportive of that Farm Bill because it seemed straightforward that a non-intoxicating plant should not be classified as a Schedule I drug.

In the years that followed, the hemp market got creative and exploited a loophole in the new definition of hemp. Our country has witnessed an explosion of intoxicating hemp products that claim to be legal under the 2018 Farm Bill. These products are chemically similar to marijuana products. They contain semi-synthetic cannabinoids derived from the hemp plant. So, while they contain less than .3% Delta-9 THC, they contain high amounts of either Delta-8 THC, Delta-10 THC, or another synthetic cannabinoid that can get you high. They come packaged in gas stations as candy-flavored gummies, sodas, and vapes. A vote to extend the THC limits is a vote for nationwide legalization of marijuana.

Hemp dispensaries explain on their websites that their products are legal under the 2018 Farm Bill. Many intoxicating products even have a disclaimer on the package that claims it is compliant with the 2018 Farm Bill. The population that suffers the most is children. According to the Journal of Medical Toxicology, half of Delta-8 exposures in 2024 were children. 58% of critical care admissions for THC exposure in 2024 were children under the age of 6.

Congress decided this issue years ago. Our communities deserve for these drugs to be taken off the shelves and out of reach of children. It is time for Congress to close the loophole we created in 2018. Hemp producers can sell CBD oil and hemp fibers, but they should not be allowed to sell intoxicating products disguised as harmless hemp.

(X)

Background

Lankford has consistently opposed efforts to expand the marijuana industry and raised concerns about the public safety implications of expanding the industry. In 2026, Lankford introduced the No Deductions for Marijuana Businesses Act to prevent marijuana businesses from claiming federal tax deductions and credits following rescheduling. He has also pressed the Treasury Department on the potential tax implications of the policy change.

###

title: Luján Continues Push for Accountability, Demands FCC Turn Over Records Detailing Nominee’s False Statements Before Congress
text:
Following Revelations of False Statements Before Congress, Luján Presses FCC for Answers and Accountability

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the Senate Commerce Subcommittee on Telecommunications and Media, sent a letter to Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr demanding that the Commission turn over records related to FCC nominee Danielle Thumann’s involvement in media-related issues following exposure of false statements made in her oral and written testimony before Congress.

“At the hearing, Ms. Thumann testified that she had not worked ‘on any media-related issues.’ This statement and her responses to the Questions for the Record directly contradict documents that have been released by the Commission through various Freedom of Information Act requests,” wrote Senator Luján.

“This raises serious questions about whether Ms. Thumann’s testimony before the Committee was intentionally misleading, and I seek to further understand Ms. Thumann’s involvement in actions and decisions involving media-related issues at the Commission,” continued Senator Luán.

Background:

Senator Luján called on Commerce Committee Chairman Ted Cruz (R-Texas) to remove the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) following revelations that appear to contradict her testimony during her nomination hearing.

During Ms. Thumann’s November 10th confirmation hearing, she testified in response to questioning from Senator Luján that she had not worked with FCC Chairman Brendan Carr on any media-related issues. However, documents obtained by Senator Luján reveal that Ms. Thumann worked on several media-related matters, including helping draft commitments made by Skydance that facilitated the FCC’s approval of its merger with Paramount.

The documents reveal that Ms. Thumann reviewed and edited a draft letter that Skydance later submitted to the FCC outlining its commitments to eliminate diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives at Paramount. The documents also reveal Ms. Thumann’s involvement in media issues related to CBS’ 60 Minutes and Jimmy Kimmel complaints, directly contradicting her testimony before the Commerce Committee.

Coverage of Senator Luján’s push is available here.

The full text of the letter is available HERE and below:

Chairman Carr:

On November 10, 2026, Danielle Thumann Severs, your Senior Counsel for the Wireline, Consumer and Governmental Affairs, Public Safety, and Homeland Security Bureaus appeared before the United States Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation to testify regarding her nomination to be a Commissioner at the Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC). At the hearing, Ms. Thumann testified that she had not worked “on any media-related issues.” This statement and her responses to the Questions for the Record directly contradict documents that have been released by the Commission through various Freedom of Information Act requests.

This raises serious questions about whether Ms. Thumann’s testimony before the Committee was intentionally misleading, and I seek to further understand Ms. Thumann’s involvement in actions and decisions involving media-related issues at the Commission.

Accordingly, I request that the Commission produce the following documents no later than Thursday, December 3, 2026. This request covers Danielle Thumann ‘s FCC emails, attachments, calendar invites, Teams chat, and files shared via a network drive. Every attachment to Boone’s 10:48 AM email, including the draft letter Ms. Thumann was asked to review, even if that file was shared via a network link;

The email from Erin Boone of January 21, 2025, 10:24 AM, “Orders rescinding network complaint investigations,” to Chairman Carr, Greg Watson, Danielle Thumann, Arpan Sura, and Benjamin Arden, with all three attachments: “Draft_WCBS_1.113_Order to BC 1.21.25.docx,” “Draft_WPVI_1.113_Order to BC 1.21.25.docx,” and “Draft WNBC 1.113 Order to BC 1.21.25.docx”

I look forward to your prompt response to this request.

title: Lummis-Led Bill Ending the Penny Becomes Law, Saving Taxpayers $56 Million a Year
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) joined President Trump in the Oval Office today as he signed her bipartisan Common Cents Act into law, permanently ending production of the penny, authorizing a new, lower-cost version of the nickel.

Today’s law finishes a fight Wyoming started nearly a decade ago when the late Senator Mike Enzi (R-WY), then Chairman of the Senate Budget Committee, introduced the COINS Act to suspend penny production. Senator Lummis, who succeeded Senator Enzi in 2021, continued his efforts and partnered with Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Senators James Lankford (R-OK) and Ron Wyden (D-OR) to introduce the Common Cents Act. Representatives Lisa McClain (R-MI) and Robert Garcia (D-CA) introduced the companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

“Nearly a decade ago, Senator Mike Enzi called out one of the most obvious examples of waste in Washington: a penny that costs more to make than it’s worth,” said Lummis. “Today, we have modernized our coinage for the future by eliminating the penny and also authorizing Treasury to produce a lower-cost nickel. This is another example of my hard work over the last six years to modernize how Americans make payments and ensure our financial system is competitive for the next generation.”

“Families in South Carolina, and across the country, know what it means to make every dollar count. They expect Washington to do the same,” said Chairman Scott. “It costs nearly four cents to make one penny. The Common Cents Act eliminates wasteful spending, modernizes our currency system, and most importantly gives families and businesses clear rules for everyday cash transactions.”

“Getting clarity on rounding cash transactions is essential to convenience retailers and the retail industry as a whole,” said Pace McMullan, Vice President of Government Relations at the National Association of Convenience Stores. “Senator Lummis was relentless in helping overcome multiple obstacles in Congress. We are grateful for her support of our industry and ceaseless attention in making sure the Common Cents Act was signed into law.”

“Now that the Common Cents Act has become law, restaurant operators can have the confidence that they are handling cash transactions in a way that works for their business and for their customers,” said Sean Kennedy, Chief Advocacy Officer of the National Restaurant Association. “Nearly one in four purchases in restaurants are still made in cash, and as the penny is phased out of circulation, operators will now have clear principles and certainty for rounding that will help keep transactions simple and straightforward. We appreciate President Trump’s support of this bill, and Sen. Lummis’ continued efforts for Wyoming’s restaurant industry.”

In April 2025, Senator Lummis introduced the Common Cents Act (S.1525) with Senator Gillibrand, two months after President Trump directed the Treasury Department to stop minting the penny. The U.S. Mint struck its final circulating penny on November 12, 2025.

The House passed the Common Cents Act by voice vote on September 14, 2026, and the Senate followed by passing the bill by unanimous consent on September 28, 2026. The legislation passed both chambers without opposition.

title: Lummis Secures Wyoming Wins in Bipartisan Permitting Reform Bill
