title: Senate Western Caucus Applauds Passage of Bipartisan Permitting Bill that Delivers Wins for the West
text:
Washington, D.C.— Senate Western Caucus Chair Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) and her Senate Western Caucus colleagues released the following statements after the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 passed the Senate by a vote of 62-33. The bipartisan legislation led by Senate Environment and Public Works Committee Chairman Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV), Senate Energy and Natural Resources Chairman Mike Lee (R-UT), and Ranking Members Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) and Martin Heinrich (D-NM) modernizes federal permitting and environmental review. The bill includes a slate of Senate Western Caucus priorities that give states a stronger role in endangered species decisions, protects ratepayers and energy projects across the west, and strengthens America’s domestic nuclear fuel supply chain. The bill now heads to the House of Representatives.

“No region feels the weight of Washington’s permitting maze like the west,” said Lummis. “With the federal government controlling vast stretches of western land, critical infrastructure projects face years of red tape and endless permitting delays thanks to Washington’s bloated bureaucracy. The Senate voted to put western states back in the driver’s seat by ensuring state wildlife experts lead on endangered species decisions and speeding up the transmission line and wildfire prevention upgrades our communities depend on. The west cannot afford to wait decades for the power, infrastructure, and jobs it needs. The west has the energy, materials, and workforce to help power America. It’s time to get Washington out of the way and put those resources to work.”

“Tonight, the passage of permitting reform in the Senate finally became a reality and we took a major step toward addressing the affordability concerns of the American people,” said Capito. “I have spent years trying to achieve bipartisan compromise on legislation that gets our nation back to building, and the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is the culmination of those efforts. I’m thankful for the determination of my fellow negotiators, Senators Whitehouse, Lee, and Heinrich, and the support the Trump administration and over one thousand stakeholders. I encourage leaders in the House to take advantage of the significant opportunity before us to grow our economy, create jobs, and make American life more affordable by expeditiously passing BAAJA.”

“We once built projects like the Hoover Dam, the Golden Gate Bridge, and the Empire State Building in years, not decades,” said Lee. “America still has the resources and the talent, but what too often stands in the way is a permitting system that takes too long and costs too much. After years of work in Congress and many months of negotiations, I’m proud the Senate passed this bipartisan bill to fix this broken process and get America back to building.”

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act cuts through decades of red tape that has made it unnecessarily difficult and costly to build things in America,” said Thune. “It restores balance to the federal permitting process by ensuring local stakeholders have a say in projects in their community and providing accountability to ensure that bureaucrats in Washington don’t prevent needed projects from moving forward. I’m grateful to Chairmen Shelley Moore Capito and Mike Lee for their work on this important legislation, and I’m glad we’re one step closer to getting it to the president’s desk.”

“Today marks a truly historic moment for our nation,” said Armstrong. “For years, America has been slowly strangling our own ability to build, allowing a broken permitting process to delay critical infrastructure, drive up utility bills for hardworking families, and threaten our national competitiveness. By passing this landmark bipartisan permitting reform legislation, Congress has proven that we can put our long-term national interest ahead of short-term political posturing and party politics. I am deeply grateful to my colleagues on both sides of the aisle who chose to stay at the negotiating table, focus on the facts, and find common ground. I also want to extend my sincere thanks to the coalition spanning nearly every sector of American industry who stepped up to speak with a unified voice on their shared permitting challenges. By coming together without asking for subsidies or picking winners and losers, this coalition gave Congress the leverage and clarity needed to overcome decades of inertia. America was built by generations before us who had the courage to tackle hard problems and build for the future. This bill retains full environmental protections while creating a common-sense, durable process that restores certainty to American investment and delivers real, long-term affordability to consumers. Now, the House must act quickly on this bipartisan agreement and turn it into law.”

“Today, the Senate passed bipartisan permitting reform legislation that will unleash Wyoming energy, lower energy costs, and create jobs across our state. It’s a win for Wyoming and for America,” said Barrasso. “Right now, critical infrastructure projects spend years trapped in the regulatory penalty box. Energy projects in Wyoming bear the brunt of this dysfunction. Wyoming is America’s energy breadbasket. We have world-class coal, oil, natural gas, and uranium. Wyoming energy workers are ready to produce the energy America needs. The broken federal permitting process is standing in our way. That’s why I worked with Senator Joe Manchin last Congress to produce the bipartisan Energy Permitting Reform Act. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 builds on our work. This critical legislation cuts Washington red tape, streamlines environmental reviews, and reins in never-ending, abusive legal challenges. It will help us build better, faster, cheaper, and smarter, and lower energy costs for American families. I urge the House to act quickly so we can send this bill to President Trump’s desk and experience the benefit as soon as possible.”

“I am proud to support this bipartisan solution that would replace the outdated, complex federal permitting system with a more clear, accountable framework that creates certainty,” said Boozman. “Cutting red tape and streamlining the permitting process will help lower costs for American families, strengthen our energy grid and spur economic development and job creation. These reforms will benefit communities across Arkansas by making it easier to get critical infrastructure projects off the ground and less susceptible to unreasonable delays or lawsuits, all while still protecting the environment. I appreciate the hard work of Senators Capito, Whitehouse, Lee, Heinrich and Armstrong, as well as my fellow Arkansan, Rep. Bruce Westerman, for his leadership in advancing the House version of this legislation. I strongly encourage the House to pass this bill and send it to the president’s desk.”

“We can attribute high prices to many factors, but our antiquated and burdensome permitting process is undoubtedly one of them,” said Curtis. “Having both parties come together on a solution to an issue that, for years, has been one of the thorniest to address in Washington is a significant moment for bipartisanship and good-faith governing on behalf of the American people. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will help us build faster, strengthen American energy independence, and create new opportunities for communities in Utah and across the country. I’m proud to see it passed by the Senate.”

“The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is a huge win for Montana and the nation,”said Daines. “It will cut red tape, reduce frivolous litigation, and lower costs, delivering real results to get America building again.”

“Permitting reform is one of the best things we can do for our country, and the package passed by the Senate is objectively good for our country,” said Murkowski.

title: Markey, Hirono, Colleagues Introduce Resolution Commemorating Transgender Day of Remembrance
text:
Resolution Text (PDF)

Washington (November 20, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.) today joined Senator Mazie K. Hirono (D-Hawaii) and 14 of their Senate colleagues in introducing a resolution commemorating November 20th, 2026, as Transgender Day of Remembrance (TDOR). The House companion bill was introduced by U.S. Representatives Pramila Jayapal (D-WA), Sara Jacobs (D-CA), and Mark Takano (D-CA).

“This Transgender Day of Remembrance, we reaffirm our commitment that trans rights are human rights, and we honor the trans people who have lost their lives to violence,” said Senator Markey. “As the trans community continues to face an all-out assault of discrimination and hate from the White House, we must continue to fight back against the vitriolic anti-trans policies of this Administration and stand with trans people everywhere to ensure that all people are afforded the basic rights and dignity they deserve.”

“As anti-transgender hate continues to rise nationwide, bolstered by the Trump regime’s harmful rhetoric, supporting and protecting transgender and gender-nonconforming individuals is critical. This resolution honors the lives of those who were lost to violence and educates communities about the dangers and discrimination transgender people face,” said Senator Hirono. “Transgender rights are human rights, and I remain committed to defending everyone’s right to live openly, safely, and without fear."

Transgender and gender-nonconforming people continue to face disproportionately high rates of violent crime. Following the still-unsolved murder of Rita Hester, a transgender woman of color, Gwendolyn Ann Smith founded TDOR to honor Hester and other transgender people whose lives were lost to violence. This year’s resolution also commemorates Stonewall veteran and longtime transgender advocate, Victoria Cruz, who passed away in June. Ms. Cruz dedicated her life to helping victims of domestic violence, police violence, and rape in the LGBTQ+ community.

“On Transgender Day of Remembrance, we stand united against the discrimination and attacks faced by the transgender community in Colorado and across the nation,” said Senator Bennet. “We honor the memory of those lost and recommit to protecting the rights and safety of the transgender community to ensure that everyone can live with dignity and respect.”

“All Americans deserve to live their lives freely and authentically—without fear of discrimination or harm simply because of their gender identity. I’m proud to introduce this resolution amplifying the voices of our nation’s transgender communities and recognizing the dangers they face simply for living their lives. Transgender rights are human rights, and I look forward to continuing the fight to make our country a more inclusive place for all,” said Senator Blumenthal.

“On this Transgender Day of Remembrance, we honor the transgender Americans whose lives have been cut short by hate,” said Senator Duckworth. “As Trump continues his campaign of cruelty against the trans community, I will always fight for the safety, dignity and respect that all human beings deserve.”

“We’ve experienced years of rising discrimination and hate, specifically anti-transgender hate, across the country. We will not accept it. Transgender rights are human rights,” said Senator Hickenlooper. “Everyone has the right to be who they are without being targeted."

“Let us all recognize the enormous discrimination and violence that our transgender communities face,” said Senator Merkley. “On this day of remembrance, we honor the lives and legacies of all in the transgender community who have been taken by violence, just for being who they are, and commit to working toward a world where everyone can live a full and free life.”

“Trans people deserve to live with equality and dignity – just like everyone else,” said Senator Schatz. “Transgender Day of Remembrance is about highlighting the continued threats that the trans community faces every day and honoring those who were killed solely because of who they were.”

“The transgender community has faced increasing hate and violence as the Trump administration has demonized them. I’m proud to join Senator Hirono and my Senate colleagues in standing up against this ugly sentiment, remembering the lives tragically lost in this epidemic of bigotry, and committing ourselves to building a safer and more inclusive future. All Americans deserve to live as their authentic selves without fear for who they are,” said Senator Schiff.

The resolution is endorsed by the Human Rights Campaign, Advocates for Trans Equality (A4TE), and the National LGBTQ Task Force Action Fund.

In addition to Senators Markey and Hirono, the resolution was cosponsored by Senators Tammy Baldwin (D-Wisc.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Chris Coons (D-Del.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), John Fetterman (D-Penn.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.).

title: SENATE PASSES TWO MCCORMICK, FETTERMAN BILLS TO CONSERVE PUBLIC LANDS
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Dave McCormick (R-PA) and John Fetterman (D-PA) applauded the U.S. Senate passage of two bipartisan bills to preserve Pennsylvania’s historic landscapes, promote tourism, and support economic development across the Commonwealth. The Endless Mountains National Heritage Area Act and the Washington’s Trail — 1753 National Historic Trail Feasibility Study Act would recognize important parts of Pennsylvania’s history as the nation celebrates its 250th anniversary.

“Pennsylvania played a central role in our nation’s history, and we have a responsibility to preserve that legacy for future generations,” said Senator McCormick. “These bipartisan bills will help protect our natural and historic treasures while strengthening tourism and creating new opportunities for Pennsylvania businesses and communities. I’m proud to work with Senator Fetterman to move these commonsense conservation efforts forward.”

The Endless Mountains National Heritage Area Act, introduced by Senators McCormick and Fetterman in March, would designate Bradford, Sullivan, Susquehanna, and Wyoming counties as a National Heritage Area, preserving the region’s natural beauty and history while supporting a tourism economy that generates more than $166 million annually and supports nearly 2,000 jobs. U.S. Congressman Dan Meuser (R-PA-09) leads the House companion bill.

The Washington’s Trail — 1753 National Historic Trail Feasibility Study Act, led by Senator Fetterman and cosponsored by Senator McCormick, would authorize a study of George Washington’s historic 1753 route for potential National Historic Trail designation. The route crosses Western Pennsylvania and connects historic landmarks in Pittsburgh and Erie County. U.S. Congressman Mike Kelly (R-PA-16) leads the House companion bill.

Both bills would help preserve Pennsylvania’s heritage while promoting tourism and economic opportunity across the Commonwealth.

title: Murray, Durbin Reintroduce Legislation to Ensure Victims of Discrimination Can Get the Justice They Are Owed
text:
Washington, D.C. —U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, and Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, reintroduced the Clarifying Civil Rights Remedies Act—legislation to clarify that victims of discrimination can seek damages for emotional distress under federal law—after the Supreme Court April 2022 ruling in Cummings v. Premier Rehab Keller. The legislation ensures that people who suffer emotional distress because of discrimination they have experienced are able to seek restitution under federal anti-discrimination statutes—recognizing that discrimination can and often does cause lasting emotional distress.

“While reversing this decision was always important, it’s become even more urgent. The Trump Administration has abandoned civil rights enforcement even as we continue to hear about egregious violations—just look at the allegations of sexual assault on college campuses,” said Senator Murray. “The reporting out of Cornell, Louisiana State University, and Texas Christian University has been horrific. Victims of discrimination should be able to get damages for the full scope of harm that they suffer.”

“Discrimination can leave a lasting mental impact on those who experience it. That’s why the Supreme Court’s decision in Cummings v. Premier Rehab Keller is so harmful. It prevents those who have suffered emotional distress due to discrimination from seeking damages,” said Senator Durbin. “I’m joining Senator Murray in introducing the Clarifying Civil Rights Remedies Act to clarify that damages for emotional harm are available to victims of discrimination. No one who faces discrimination should be denied justice in court.”

In April 2022, the Supreme Court ruled in a 6-3 decision authored by Chief Justice Roberts that victims of discrimination cannot sue under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 or the Affordable Care Act to recover damages for emotional distress caused by illegal discrimination. The decision denies many victims of discrimination an appropriate remedy for the harms they have suffered.

The Clarifying Civil Rights Remedies Act of 2026 makes explicit that remedies available for violations of Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, the Age Discrimination Act of 1975, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act include compensatory damages, including for emotional harm. The legislation ensures that victims have recourse and that recipients of federal funds comply with federal civil rights laws.

In addition to Senators Murray and Durbin, the legislation is cosponsored by Senators Baldwin, Blumenthal, Booker, Cantwell, Duckworth, Hirono, Kaine, Sanders, Schiff, Van Hollen, Welch, and Whitehouse.

The legislation is endorsed by Bazelon, Public Justice, NWLC, AAJ, ASAN, National Alliance to End Sexual Violence, National Alliance for Partnerships in Equity, Just Solutions, The Trevor Project, and Know Your IX.

title: Murray & Kaptur Call for Independent Review of DOE’s Sweeping Rewrite of Safety and Accountability Rules
text:
ICYMI: Murray, Kaptur Demand Energy Department Restore Eliminated Safety Rules, Justify Rewrite of Dozens of Critical Safety and Accountability Measures

Washington, D.C. — Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, and Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (D-OH-09), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water Development, sent a series of letters to the Department of Energy’s (DOE) Office of Inspector General (OIG), the Defense Nuclear Facilities Safety Board (DNFSB), and the Government Accountability Office (GAO) asking for each to investigate the sweeping changes that DOE is making to its operating directives. The cumulative impact of these changes risks the safety of work being done at DOE labs, plants, and sites, and they reduce transparency and oversight and risk wasting taxpayer dollars.

In September, Murray and Kaptur called on DOE to restore critical safety rules it scrapped and to justify its revisions to dozens more of the operating directives. But DOE has failed to respond—prompting the lawmakers to call for independent investigation.

In a letter to DOE’s Inspector General, Murray and Kaptur requested the OIG evaluate DOE’s decision to revise forty-six operating directives and cancel four orders, which required DOE to track safety incidents and worker injuries across its labs and sites, and let workers formally challenge technical decisions they believed put safety at risk. The lawmakers wrote: “While the Department claims Project Velocity modernizes operations by shifting from procedural compliance to performance-based accountability, we are concerned that these sweeping rollbacks weaken critical safety protections, eliminate standardized occurrence and injury reporting, and eliminate formal dispute-resolution mechanisms. Further, we are troubled by the lack of transparency around the process of determining which DOE orders were modified or cancelled, who was involved in that process, and what criteria were used to make final determinations under Project Velocity.”

In a letter to DNFSB, the primary independent Federal agency charged by Congress with providing recommendations and oversight regarding defense nuclear facilities, Murray and Kaptur also asked to investigate the changes to the critical safety and accountability measures: “We are deeply concerned over the scale and speed of these regulatory changes, particularly because the changes touch upon nuclear facility safety, quality assurance, conduct of operations, worker training, and incident reporting. We remain very concerned about these simultaneous changes weakening critical safety controls and diminishing independent Federal oversight.”

In a letter to GAO, Murray and Kaptur ask the agency to conduct a comprehensive review of the operating directives. “GAO has raised concerns over the Department’s contract management and project oversight for decades, making this recent wholesale rewrite by the Department of dozens of operating directives highly concerning,” the lawmakers wrote to GAO. “Project Velocity represents a massive expansion of regulatory rollback across dozens of orders and directives. While DOE characterizes these changes as a transition from ‘procedural compliance’ to ‘performance-based accountability,’ we are deeply concerned that the scale and speed of these alterations weaken critical safety protections, undermine independent Federal oversight, shift core responsibilities to Management and Operating (M&O) contractors without adequate safeguards, and potentially increase taxpayer liabilities and costs.”

The lawmakers requested detailed answers and in-depth reviews from all three entities within 30 days to guarantee independent safety oversight is maintained to ensure public health and worker safety are preserved across all nuclear labs, facilities, and sites.

title: Senator Murray Presses Secretary Collins on Rising Wait Times and Inadequate Outreach in Caregiver Support Program’s Mental Health Services
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee and senior member and former chair of the Veterans Affairs Committee, sent a letter to Secretary of Veterans Affairs Doug Collins demanding answers on how the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) measures effectiveness and quality of the mental health services it provides to caregivers through the Caregiver Support Program (CSP).

“I am writing to express concern regarding the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Caregiver Support Program (CSP) and its ability to connect eligible caregivers with life-saving mental health resources,” Senator Murray wrote. “As you know, there are over 14 million military and veteran caregivers in the United States. These caregivers perform essential duties every day for their loved ones, but unfortunately, these tasks can be burdensome over time. Multiple studies have shown that caregivers, especially those of post-9/11 veterans, experience tolls on their own well-being while providing for a loved one. In one study, 84 percent of caregivers of post-9/11 veterans experienced high levels of stress, and one-third met the criteria for clinical depression.”

In the letter, Senator Murray points out that despite a nearly $1 billion increase in funding from FY25 to FY26, wait times for the Caregiver Support Line (CSL) have risen at an alarming rate: “Despite an increase in enrollment and funding requested, CSP is facing challenges in providing mental health resources to caregivers. In FY 2024, VA reduced the number of full-time Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers (PCAFC) employees by 6 percent. That same year, the Caregiver Support Line (CSL), which provides information to caregivers, veterans, and community partners, experienced an increased wait time from 16 seconds in FY24 to 120 seconds in FY25. Furthermore, CSL staff answered 91 percent of the calls in FY 2025, a 6 percent decrease from FY 2024.”

Senator Murray referenced a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report released in April 2026 which found that many caregivers are not aware of VA’s CSP resources: “GAO found that these challenges are, in part, related to VA’s inadequate outreach efforts. Specifically, GAO found that CSP only partially implemented key performance management practices to achieve outreach goals and lacked definitions and clear objectives to increase the utilization of the program. In addition, the goals that VHA did create were based on anecdotal feedback instead of quantitative data.”

Senator Murray concluded by pushing for answers on how VA evaluates caregiver awareness, utilization of mental health services, and the overall effectiveness of the program, writing: “It is imperative that caregivers receive the support they need, and the first step to achieving this is ensuring that VA is implementing the programs with clear, objective goals and is taking steps to educate caregivers on the resources available to them.”

The full letter is available HERE and below:

Dear Secretary Collins:

I am writing to express concern regarding the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Caregiver Support Program (CSP) and its ability to connect eligible caregivers with life-saving mental health resources. As you know, there are over 14 million military and veteran caregivers in the United States. These caregivers perform essential duties every day for their loved ones, but unfortunately, these tasks can be burdensome over time. Multiple studies have shown that caregivers, especially those of post-9/11 veterans, experience tolls on their own well-being while providing for a loved one. In one study, 84 percent of caregivers of post-9/11 veterans experienced high levels of stress, and one-third met the criteria for clinical depression.

In accordance with the Caregivers and Veterans Omnibus Health Services Act of 2010, CSP must provide various types of support to caregivers of veterans, including the toll-free Caregiver Support Line, mental health treatment, and support groups. In Fiscal Year (FY) 2025, CSP served about 98,000 caregivers, and the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) obligated $2.6 billion to implement the program. In FY 2026, I worked to secure $3.5 billion for VA’s Caregiver Program and for FY 2027, the Department is requesting $3.6 billion to support anticipated enrollment growth.

Despite an increase in enrollment and funding requested, CSP is facing challenges in providing mental health resources to caregivers. In FY 2024, VA reduced the number of full-time Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers (PCAFC) employees by 6 percent. That same year, the Caregiver Support Line (CSL), which provides information to caregivers, veterans, and community partners, experienced an increased wait time from 16 seconds in FY24 to 120 seconds in FY25. Furthermore, CSL staff answered 91 percent of the calls in FY 2025, a 6 percent decrease from FY 2024.

Not only are caregivers experiencing challenges accessing mental health services through CSP, but according to a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report released in April 2026, many caregivers are not aware of the mental health support available through the program and reported challenges accessing both virtual and in-person therapy appointments. GAO found that these challenges are, in part, related to VA’s inadequate outreach efforts. Specifically, GAO found that CSP only partially implemented key performance management practices to achieve outreach goals and lacked definitions and clear objectives to increase the utilization of the program. In addition, the goals that VHA did create were based on anecdotal feedback instead of quantitative data.

VA’s own reporting to Congress reinforces these concerns. Although the Department’s annual report on the PFAFC provides detailed information on application volumes, reassessments, and appeals, it offers little insight into whether caregivers are aware of or successfully accessing the mental health resources available through the broader CSP. Instead, the report focuses primarily on administrative outputs rather than performance measures that would help Congress evaluate caregiver awareness, utilization of mental health services, or the overall effectiveness of the program.

It is imperative that caregivers receive the support they need, and the first step to achieving this is ensuring that VA is implementing the programs with clear, objective goals and is taking steps to educate caregivers on the resources available to them. To address these concerns, please answer the following questions by December 18, 2026:

How does VA currently measure caregiver awareness of the CSP and the mental health resources available through the program? Please describe the data collected, performance measures used, and any baseline metrics. In addition, please identify the metrics VA uses to measure progress toward each goal.

How does VA evaluate the effectiveness and quality of the mental health services offered through CSP? Please identify the outcome measures VA uses to assess whether these services are improving caregivers’ mental health and well-being and how VA uses performance data to evaluate the effectiveness of the program’s outreach and service delivery.

VA’s annual report to Congress on the PCAFC primarily reports application, reassessment, and appeals data. Does VA intend to include additional performance measures in future reports related to caregiver awareness, utilization of mental health resources, and program outcomes? If so, please describe those planned metrics and the anticipated implementation timeline.

How does VA distinguish between measures of CSP operational efficiency—such as application processing times, caseloads, and wellness contacts—and measures of program effectiveness, such as caregiver awareness, utilization, access, and outcomes related to mental health services?

As VA continues to expand the CSP, it is critical that caregivers are not only aware of the resources available to them, but also that these resources are effective in addressing their mental health needs. Thank you for your attention to this important matter, and we look forward to your response.

Sincerely,

###

title: Senator Murray Statement on Record-Setting Citations, Criminal Referral, in WA Labor & Industries, Ecology’s Investigation of Nippon Dynawave Implosion
text:
L&I cited Nippon Dynawave with 75 violations related to G-tank’s failure amounting to $9.2 million in fines—the largest penalty issued by Washington state

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA) released the following statement in response to the Washington State Department of Labor & Industries (L&I) and Washington State Department of Ecology’s investigation into the disaster at Nippon Dynawave in Longview which concluded with record-setting citations for health and safety, and environmental violations. L&I cited Nippon with 75 violations related to G-tank’s failure as well as other tank-related violations amounting to $9.2 million—the largest penalty issued by Washington state and one of the top five nationally for occupational safety and health violations. Ecology also issued violations of about $300,000 and ordering cost recovery of $600,000. Together, it’s just over $10 million. L&I also made a criminal referral based on its finding of Nippon’s egregious violations to the Washington State Attorney General’s office and the Cowlitz County prosecutor.

“The implosion in Longview earlier this year devastated the community—leaving eleven dead and twelve injured. These record-setting fines and criminal referrals are an important step toward justice for the families affected by what this investigation shows was a completely avoidable tragedy. The new findings from L&I and Ecology’s investigation are deeply troubling and reveals the company’s unsafe work conditions and failure to plan for emergencies. I am grateful for L&I and Ecology conducting a thorough investigation that is leading to serious accountability. It is appalling to learn about the number of times this company had near misses and should have made corrections much sooner. I am heartbroken for the families and community who are learning that this tragedy could—and should—have been prevented. I will continue to follow this prosecution closely and be there in any way I can to support Longview.”

title: Padilla, Warner, Collins, McConnell Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Strengthen Election Security
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, Mark R. Warner (D-Va.), Vice Chair of the Select Committee on Intelligence, Susan Collins (R-Maine), Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, and Mitch McConnell (R-Ky.), Chair of the Committee on Rules and Administration, introduced the bipartisan Election Infrastructure Security Act (EISA) to provide states and localities with a more reliable source of funding to secure American elections. The legislation would repurpose the largely unused Presidential Election Campaign Fund (PECF) to support critical election security needs, including cybersecurity improvements, voting equipment upgrades, and protections for voter registration systems.

State and local election officials often lack the consistent federal resources needed to maintain secure and reliable election systems. Currently, federal election security funding is limited and unpredictable, forcing election officials to rely on already-strained state and local budgets to address evolving threats, replace aging equipment, and maintain critical infrastructure. This legislation would allow election officials to make long-term security improvements, proactively address vulnerabilities, and avoid costly emergency upgrades.

“American elections are safe and secure, but in a time of rising threats at home and abroad we will ensure they stay that way with the right investments in our election infrastructure,” said Senator Padilla. “Our bill would rededicate an existing, but widely unused, voluntary fund to ensure that localities have the resources to support election needs – like improved cybersecurity and voting equipment upgrades. As Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee and California’s former Secretary of State, I recognize that robust and reliable federal funding for elections is a top priority, and I’m proud to support this is commonsense, bipartisan legislation that will help further build up the strength of our democracy.”

“Free and fair elections are the foundation of our democracy. As Vice Chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, I’ve seen firsthand the threats facing our election systems and the critical role that state and local officials play in defending against them,” said Senator Warner. “Keeping our elections secure requires more than sporadic funding; it requires sustained investment. This bipartisan legislation would put an outdated, largely unused federal program to work strengthening election security by providing election officials with reliable funding to modernize voting infrastructure, address evolving threats, and ensure every eligible American can cast their ballot with confidence.”

“Protecting the integrity of our elections is essential to maintaining public confidence in our democratic process,” said Senator Collins. “This bipartisan legislation would support that goal by providing a reliable source of funding to strengthen election security, modernize outdated equipment, and help ensure that our elections remain safe and secure.”

“Election security is a fundamental responsibility of government, and states and local election officials need the resources to carry it out,” said Senator McConnell. “This bipartisan legislation would put an outdated federal fund to better use by providing a dedicated source of funding to strengthen election infrastructure, improve cybersecurity, and modernize voting equipment. It is a practical approach that supports state and local election administration without creating a new federal spending program.”

The PECF was established to provide public financing to eligible presidential candidates through voluntary taxpayer contributions made on federal income tax returns. However, participation has declined significantly as candidates have increasingly relied on private fundraising. No major-party presidential candidate has used the program since 2008, leaving the fund largely obsolete. The Election Infrastructure Security Act would permanently convert the PECF into a dedicated Election Security Fund, providing states with a more predictable source of support to protect and modernize their election systems.

Specifically, the Election Infrastructure Security Act would:

Establish a dedicated Election Security Fund by converting the existing PECF into a program supporting state and local election security. States would receive a guaranteed minimum of $3 million annually, while territories would receive at least $600,000. At least 67 percent of the fund would be directed to local election jurisdictions, except in states that centrally administer federal elections;

Support critical election security improvements by allowing funds to be used for broad purposes, including modernizing election technology, strengthening cybersecurity, upgrading voting equipment, protecting election infrastructure, reimbursing prior security investments, improving election administration, and shortening wait times. Funds cannot be used for litigation;

Require transparent spending plans and accountability by directing states to develop plans outlining how funds would be used, tracked, and monitored, subject to a public notice and comment process;

Modernize the voluntary taxpayer contribution system by increasing the federal income tax checkoff with adjustments for inflation from $3 to $5 for individuals and from $6 to $10 for married couples filing jointly;

Place administration of the fund under the Election Assistance Commission (EAC), which already oversees federal election assistance grants under the Help America Vote Act; and

Strengthen oversight by requiring annual state reports on expenditures, equipment purchases, and program outcomes, as well as periodic EAC audits to ensure funds are used appropriately.

The bill is endorsed by the Bipartisan Policy Center, Responsive Gov Action, Project for Election Infrastructure, and 23 state and local election associations, including the Arizona Recorder Association, California Association of Clerks and Election Officials, Colorado County Clerks Association, Connecticut Town Clerks Association, Florida Supervisors of Elections, Georgia Association of Voter Registration and Election Officials, Kentucky County Clerks Association, Louisiana Registrar of Voters Association Inc., Maine Town & City Clerks Association, and more.

“The Election Infrastructure Security Act is a critical first step in ensuring that state and local officials across the country have the funding and resources they need to keep our elections secure and accurate. It turns a defunct box on a form into an opportunity for Americans to direct sustainable support to the dedicated people who keep elections running. This bipartisan legislation helps fund our elections like the essential infrastructure they are, and I commend the leaders of this bill for putting forward this innovative solution,” said Sam Oliker-Friedland, Chief Executive Officer of Responsive Gov Action.

“Secure elections require modern infrastructure. This legislation provides a fiscally responsible way to ensure election officials have the tools, technology, and cybersecurity protections necessary to administrations elections safely and efficiently. Thank you, Senators, for your steadfast work in a solution that does not increase the deficit or impose new federal mandates, but ensures our elections are safe and secure,” said Sarah Hague, Executive Director of the Project for Election Infrastructure.

“Bipartisan action to better fund elections is one of the most meaningful steps federal lawmakers can take to protect the security, accessibility, and accuracy of our elections. We’re asking election officials to run elections in increasingly complex threat environments, with fewer resources than ever before. Defending against these evolving threats requires continuous vigilance and sustained investment. This legislation would provide the stable, long-term funding election officials need to continuously strengthen the security and resilience of our elections,” said Kathy Boockvar, former Pennsylvania Secretary of State.

“Confidence that election results reflect the will of the voters is the thread that holds our democracy together. This initiative would improve elections across America with no additional net federal spending, helping the tens of thousands of dedicated workers who run our elections to update outdated voting equipment, invest in cyber and physical security, and improve the accuracy of voter rolls,” said Former U.S. Senator and Missouri Secretary of State Roy Blunt.

“The threats facing our elections are increasingly complex and constantly evolving – and election officials are on the front lines of confronting those challenges. They need reliable funding to stay ahead of the latest threats, strengthen election infrastructure, and communicate effectively with voters. The Election Infrastructure Security Act is a timely and, importantly, bipartisan investment in our election infrastructure. This is a consequential way we can support the dedicated public servants in Virginia and across the country who work year-round to administer secure, transparent, and accessible elections,” said Chris Piper, former Virginia Chief Election Official and Commissioner of the Virginia Department of Elections.

As Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee with oversight over federal elections and California’s former Secretary of State, Padilla has been a vocal leader in protecting our elections. In September, Padilla released a statement after the Department of Homeland Security’s Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) released its 2026 Election Infrastructure Security Plan, ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Padilla and Congressman Joe Morelle (D-N.Y.-25), Ranking Member of the House Administration Committee, also demanded the Trump Administration immediately restore funding to the Election Infrastructure Information Sharing and Analysis Center (EI-ISAC), which helps state and local election officials protect federal elections from cybersecurity threats and election mis- and disinformation campaigns. In June, Padilla and Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) announced the State and Local Election Security Act of 2026, legislation to provide up to $10 billion for state and local election administration to support election security and improve efficiency.

Full text of the bill is available here.

title: WATCH: Padilla Honors Life and Legacy of Dolores Huerta
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) took to the Senate floor to honor the life of labor, civil rights, and feminist leader Dolores Huerta. Padilla celebrated Huerta’s legacy and underscored the lasting impact of her lifelong fight for workers’ rights and the empowerment of countless communities nationwide.

“She was an icon and a true trailblazer, a pioneering labor leader, feminist, and advocate who dedicated her life to making the world a better place: fighting for workers’ rights, for voting rights, for health justice, for health care access, for environmental protections, and justice just fundamentally,” said Senator Padilla. “But what made Dolores extraordinary wasn’t just the causes that she championed or the victories that she helped secure. It was the countless barriers that she broke down and the doors she flung open for all those who would follow.”

As a proud son of immigrants, Padilla highlighted Huerta’s impact on his own life and reflected on her labor advocacy helping working families, like his own parents, build better lives with fair wages.

“As many of you know, I’m the proud son of immigrants from Mexico. My father is a proud UNITE HERE Local 11 retiree,” continued Senator Padilla. “So I grew up experiencing firsthand the impact of the fights that Dolores Huerta and generations of labor leaders have advocated for. Those fights helped make it possible for my parents to raise three children in a working-class community.”

Padilla emphasized Huerta’s efforts to ensure future leaders, especially women of color, have opportunities to continue breaking barriers in leadership and advocacy. He recognized her lifelong commitment to advocacy, noting that she inspired future generations by protesting and organizing up until the end of her life.

Padilla underscored the importance of carrying on Huerta’s legacy by continuing to fight for justice, organize, and live by her call, “Si, se puede!”

“The truest measure of Dolores Huerta’s legacy isn’t found in the awards that she’s received. It’s found in the people that she inspired, the communities that she empowered, and the generations of leaders that she helped bring forward,” concluded Senator Padilla. “And the greatest tribute that we can pay to Dolores is to carry her work forward for future generations, to keep organizing, to keep fighting, to keep helping those who are facing injustice, to find their voice, and to keep opening the doors for those who come after us.”

Full video of Padilla’s remarks is available here.

Full transcript available below:

Mr. President, the poet Bessie Anderson Stanley once wrote, “To know even one life has breathed easier because you have lived. This is to have succeeded.” And by that measure, Dolores Huerta’s life was an extraordinary success.

Few people have made more lives breathe easier or opened more doors to a better, brighter future for more people than Dolores Huerta, whom we sadly lost last month at the age of 96.

She was an icon and a true trailblazer, a pioneering labor leader, feminist, and advocate who dedicated her life to making the world a better place. fighting for workers’ rights, for voting rights, for health justice, for health care access, for environmental protections and justice just fundamentally.

Dolores once said, quote, “We must use our lives to make the world a better place. That is what we were put on this earth for.” And I believe that’s exactly how Dolores used her life.

But what made Dolores extraordinary wasn’t just the causes that she championed or the victories that she helped secure. It was the countless barriers that she broke down and the doors she flung open for all those who would follow.

Dolores came of age at a time when women, especially Mexican-American women, were rarely expected to lead political movements or to negotiate with powerful business leaders or to challenge elected officials, both sides of the aisle, I might add. but inspired by her mother who was a business owner who exemplified women’s power by her example and she encouraged Dolores to get involved in her community.

Dolores didn’t wait for permission to start making a difference. She simply rolled up her sleeves and got to work.

As many of you know, I’m the proud son of immigrants from Mexico. My father is a proud UNITE HERE Local 11 retiree.

So I grew up experiencing firsthand the impact of the fights that Dolores Huerta and generations of labor leaders have advocated for. Those fights helped make it possible for my parents to raise three children in a working-class community.

There’s a reason why my siblings and I could see a doctor when we were sick, why my parents could afford to buy a home, and my dad could take time off of work each year for vacation. All because of a good union contract.

Things that might seem ordinary to most, but for working-class families like mine, they represent the difference that a union makes. The difference that fair wages can make, and the difference that the ability to bargain collectively can make, and they’re part of the very future that Dolores spent her life fighting to build.

She understood that the fight for a more just society went beyond the workplace. That fair wages means being able to put food on the table for your family and to keep a roof over their head. That worker protections mean being able to care for a loved one without losing a paycheck and being able to work and live free of harassment and discrimination.

Dolores also understood that building a movement meant ensuring everyone had the opportunity to lead, especially those who has, who have historically been shut out of positions of power.

It’s why she traveled across the country encouraging women, especially Latinas and other women of color, to run for office. She would recruit candidates, help them secure endorsements.

She would knock on doors and campaigned alongside them, helping pave the way for new generations of women in public life.

And no matter how many wins she achieved, Dolores never treated her work as finished. At the age of 89, she was arrested protesting for a raise for home care workers.

And Dolores was still showing up at rallies, still walking precincts, and still talking with young organizers and encouraging people to vote well into her 90s.

And I know she would have been so proud to see so many Americans turning out to exercise their fundamental right to vote in this year’s midterm election.

Dolores continued doing all of this for as long as she was able to because she understood that building a movement isn’t something that you do once. It’s something that you have to keep doing over and over again, generation after generation.

Time and again, Mr. President, Dolores Huerta has been recognized for her contributions to shaping a better, fairer, and more just nation. And as a result, her portrait hangs in U.S. embassies around the world. Schools in several states have been named in her honor. President Obama awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom to her in the year 2012.

But the truest measure of Dolores Huerta’s legacy isn’t found in the awards that she’s received. It’s found in the people that she inspired, the communities that she empowered, and the generations of leaders that she helped bring forward.

And the greatest tribute that we can pay to Dolores, is to carry her work forward for future generations. To keep organizing, to keep fighting, to keep helping those who are facing injustice, to find their voice, and to keep opening the doors for those who come after us.

Yeah, Dolores may have been ahead of her time, but more importantly, she helped change the times. And her legacy will live on in every person who answers her call, “Si, se puede.” And her legacy will live on and on and on.

Thank you, Mr. President. I yield the floor.

###

title: Rosen Introduces Bill to Ban Trump Admin Members from Profiting off Federal Stakes in Private Companies
text:
Bill Builds On Senator Rosen’s Resolution Opposing Senior Administration Officials, Members Of Congress, And Their Families Profiting Off Of Federal Government Sales

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) introduced a bill to combat corruption in federal government purchases and sales of stakes in private companies. The Taxpayer Shares Protection Act would ban Trump Administration officials, members of Congress, and their immediate families from holding a significant interest in companies in which the government takes a stake. It would also increase transparency of these deals, requiring regular public reporting on all federal shareholdings and creating a Special Inspector General to monitor the management and sales of these stakes and investigate fraud and insider dealing. Since January 2025, federal agencies have announced dozens of transactions to acquire equity in private companies, valued at more than $28 billion. Congress never authorized most of these actions, so there are no rules governing how the stakes are managed or sold, and no ethics rules specific to them, opening up the potential for government officials and their families to profit from nonpublic information about government decisions. Officials could even be given or sold lucrative shares of such companies for little to no money.

“While hardworking Americans are struggling with rising prices and losing their health care, Trump administration officials should not be using our government to enrich themselves and those in their inner circle. The American people need to know their hard-earned money is being used responsibly,” said Senator Rosen. “I’m introducing this bill to hold the administration accountable for its financial involvement in private companies, and ensure that no government official profits off of it.”

Senator Rosen has continued to fight against the misuse of taxpayer dollars. This year, she introduced a bill to ban Trump and his Cabinet members from using federal funds for self-promoting ads. Senator Rosen’s bipartisan No CORRUPTION Act, which was signed into law, closed a loophole that allowed former members of Congress to continue receiving taxpayer-funded pensions after being convicted of felonies. Last Congress, she also supported the Government Spending Oversight Act to help reduce fraud, waste, and abuse in federal spending. Senator Rosen has supported legislation to ban Members of Congress and their families from owning or trading individual stocks.

title: Rosen Votes in Senate to Pass Bipartisan Bill to Reform Permitting Processes, Lower Energy Costs
text:
Landmark Bipartisan Permitting Reform Bill Will Make It Easier To Build More Solar, Wind, Geothermal Projects In Nevada, Lowering Energy Costs & Creating Good-Paying Jobs

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) released the following statement after voting in the Senate to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), landmark legislation that will make it easier to build more clean energy projects while keeping strong environmental regulations in place. This will help create more good-paying jobs, lower energy costs, and strengthen American energy independence, all while lowering net carbon emissions. Unfortunately, current government red tape has made it nearly impossible to bring these clean energy projects online, which is why sensible reform like this bipartisan bill is needed,” said Senator Rosen. “While we fought to strengthen this bill, Senate Republicans refused to accept any changes and I believed we couldn’t squander this opportunity to lower energy costs for hardworking Nevada families. I’ve always been clear that making things more affordable for Nevada families and creating good-paying jobs are priorities for me, and this historic bipartisan bill will allow us to achieve both.”

title: ICYMI: Senate Unanimously Passes Sens. Schiff, Curtis’ Legislation to Explicitly Ban Death and War Prediction Contracts
text:
The DEATH BETS Act is the first bill regulating prediction markets to pass in the Senate in the 119th Congress

Washington, D.C. — Last night, the U.S. Senate unanimously passed U.S. Senator Adam Schiff’s (D-Calif.) and John Curtis’ (R-Utah), DEATH BETS Act, legislation to explicitly prohibit any Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)-registered entity from listing any contract that references terrorism, assassination, war, United States Armed Forces military operations, or an individual’s death.

Schiff, a member of the Senate Agriculture Committee, first introduced this bill in March 2026. Representative Mike Levin (D-Calif.-49) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives.

Senator Schiff delivered remarks on the Senate floor moments before the bill passed and was joined by Senator Curtis.

Watch his full speech HERE.

“Betting on war and death jeopardizes our national security by creating a perverse environment in which violence is incentivized and insiders are allowed to profit off privileged or classified information. There is no justification for gambling on lives, or public benefit to be derived by such a market. With my bill, Congress is making it clear today that these death bets should be unlawful,” said Senator Schiff.

“No one should be able to wager on terrorism, war, or the death of another human being,” said Senator Curtis. “There is a fundamental difference between legitimate financial markets and gambling on human suffering. The DEATH BETS Act draws a clear moral line by prohibiting these types of wagers on federally regulated exchanges.”

Under the Commodity Exchange Act, the CFTC currently has the authority to prohibit war, terrorism, and assassination contracts from being listed if they are determined by the Commission to be contrary to the public interest. Whether or not these contracts are in the public interest is at the discretion of the CFTC. At a time when CFTC Chair Selig has indicated that he will rewrite the rules on prediction markets, the CFTC can no longer be granted this discretion. This bill will unequivocally ban these contracts.

According to public reporting, there have been numerous cases this year in which individuals were suspected to have traded on prediction markets to profit from inside information related to war and U.S. Armed Services actions. Lawmakers have previously raised the alarm to the CFTC on these “death contracts” being offered on offshore exchanges, such as on whether or not Artemis II would explode, Maduro would be removed from power, or the Ukrainian town of Myrnohad would be captured by Russian forces.

The DEATH BETS Act specifically would:

Codify a prohibition on war, assassination, and terrorism contracts.

Explicitly prohibit contracts that involve an individual’s death, which is not currently referenced in the Commodity Exchange Act.

The full text of the bill is available here.

Read the full transcript of his remarks as delivered below:

Senator Adam Schiff: Mr. President, I’m here today to urge the Senate to pass legislation that I’m proud to lead along with Senator John Curtis, the DEATH BETS Act.

Over the last two years, the rapid growth prediction markets has allowed users to gamble on just about anything. Just this year, we’ve seen these markets offer wagers on whether the Artemis II mission and its four astronauts would explode. It created a market on whether Nicolas Maduro would be removed from power in Venezuela. It even offered a potential profit for those who could correctly predict whether a Ukrainian town of Myrnohrad would be captured by Russia.

In many cases, these contracts offered were offered in contravention of state and Tribal law. They create rampant opportunities for insider trading, and perhaps worst of all, they are offered with no regard for national security and, in far too many cases, even basic morality.

These markets are operating in a wild west, desperately in need of regulation and guardrails.

Today, we have the opportunity to put into place a very simple rule: the first building block to create one of those guardrails. Our bill prohibits prediction markets from offering contracts on war, military operations, and death,

Betting and profiting off of death, both in tragedy and in war, is immoral and ought to be unlawful. Indeed, many of us believe it already is.

But the regulators at CFTC, or in this case, regulator, is not only hands off. He’s acting as the legal infantry for the industry, attempting to preempt state laws and challenging them whenever his agency is unsuccessful.

As a result, the CFTC has created a system with the most perverse incentives that would reward betting on a mass casualty event. A market that one could easily imagine would actually encourage lethal events and jeopardize our national security for the right amount of money. It’s a whole new version of the very idea of a contract kill.

Take the real-life example we’ve seen on these platforms: people placing bets on wildfires, wagering on how devastating they could be; people placing bets on every twist and turn in the war with Iran, sometimes with inside information, motivated by the same underlying principle of financial markets and gaming conventions, the possibility of profit.

But these are not regulated financial markets; they’re not seen by the administration as sports betting or gambling, even though such illegal practices are widespread and the subject of yet another bill that Senator Curtis and I are leading.

There’s no justification for gambling on lives or public benefit to be derived by such a market. It’s dangerous and it’s wrong.

In the absence of real leadership and enforcement at the CFTC, it’s time for Congress to step in and fix this problem.

With our bill, Congress is making clear that these bets should be illegal once and for all.

Simply put, the legislation we are enacting today is a targeted fix of a single pressing problem. The sole purpose of theDEATH BETS Act is to make clear that betting on war, death, military operations, and similar circumstances is unlawful.

But we also want to make clear that the legislation has no effect whatsoever on pending litigation regarding whether sports contracts offered by prediction markets qualify as swaps or other derivatives under federal law, or on whether federal derivatives laws preempt state gaming and consumer protection laws regarding such sports contracts.

We’ve included a rule of construction in the DEATH BETS Act designed to make this crystal clear. Per that rule, no part of this bill will affect the permissibility of any sports contracts or similar agreements. If sports contracts are impermissible under federal or state law today, as I, and many others believe they are, it will remain impermissible after this legislation is enacted.

We are aware that there is active litigation across the country on swaps and preemption issues.

Nothing in the DEATH BETS Act should have any effect on those lawsuits, and it would be improper to draw any inference from this bill that other federal statutes or regulations should be interpreted in a particular way, or that Congress has expressed any intent on how the issues in litigation should be decided.

Nor should the DEATH BETS Act be construed as providing the CFTC with authority to authorize or regulate sports contracts on prediction markets.

The CFTC has no expertise with respect to gaming.

The states and Tribes have long served as the nation’s gaming regulators, and nothing Congress is doing today displaces that traditional state and Tribal authority. Indeed, the CFTC’s recent actions to attempt to assist prediction markets in litigation confirm that the CFTC has strayed far outside its authority.

Sports contracts are sports bets in disguise. The CFTC’s job is to promote fair competition and market efficiency, not to serve as a nationwide sports betting regulator.

This bill is a commonsense step, and merely the first to rein in a runaway prediction market regulation that violates state law and Tribal sovereignty, common sense, and our values.

I want to again thank my colleague Senator Curtis for his advocacy and leadership, not just on this bill but on a broader issue, and I would be proud to yield to Senator Curtis.

###

title: NEWS: Momentum Continues Growing to Enact Federal Film Tax Credit with New Support Amongst Senate, House, and Key Stakeholders
text:
Washington, D.C. – Momentum continues to grow for the bipartisan and bicameral Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act, legislation to create a federal film tax incentive with the addition of new bipartisan Senate support, key stakeholders, and 60+ new cosponsors in the House of Representatives.

The legislation was introduced in September in the Senate by U.S. Senators Tim Scott (R-S.C.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), and by Representatives Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas-1), Linda Sánchez (D-Calif- 38), Brian Jack (R-Ga-3), and Laura Friedman (D-Calif-30) in the U.S. House of Representatives.

The new Senate cosponsors include: Senators Chris Coons (D-Del.), Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), Katie Britt (R-Ala.) and Dick Durbin (D-Ill.). The legislation is also cosponsored by Senators John Cornyn (R-Texas.), Steve Daines (R-Mont.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Tim Sheehy (R-Montana), Mark Warner (D-Va.), and Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.).

The introduction of the bill follows years of advocacy to create a nationwide tax credit for film and television production, a push recently echoed by President Donald Trump.

“The bipartisan coalition for our bill continues to grow, and I’m proud of the support we have gained from members of Congress representing different states across the country. This bill will create new jobs, boost our local economies, and stop the offshoring of film and TV production from leaving the United States, and it’s time we make this much-needed incentive a reality. Given the support from Republicans and Democrats in both chambers and the president, we can get this legislation across the finish line,” said Senator Schiff.

“Film and television production supports good-paying jobs and drives investment in communities far beyond Hollywood, including in states like Alabama,” said Senator Britt. “But for too long, countries have used aggressive incentives to lure American production companies, and the jobs that come with them, overseas. This bipartisan legislation would level the playing field and reward companies for bringing production back home. I’m proud to join my colleagues in this effort.”

“American film and television are some of our most successful cultural exports and engines of our economy,” said Senator Coons. “It’s worth investing in that power and creativity. I’m glad so many others from Democrats to Republicans to stakeholders agree, and we should keep working to move this bill forward.”

“American film and television productions support good-paying jobs, creative talent, and economic growth in communities across the country. We should be doing everything we can to ensure that these productions stay in the United States rather than move overseas to take advantage of more competitive incentives,” said Senator Durbin. “This legislation will help support American workers, strengthen our economy, and keep these jobs here at home.”

“North Carolina has a rich history in film and television production, and we should be doing everything we can to ensure that legacy continues,” said Senator Tillis. “This bipartisan legislation will help incentivize production companies to bring their projects and investments back to the United States, while supporting hardworking industry professionals and creating economic opportunities for North Carolina workers and businesses.”

“The bipartisan support behind this bill is there for a reason. The need is real. Members of both parties have watched jobs in their districts move overseas. Momentum is on our side, and we need to strike while the iron is hot by passing this bill before the end of the year,”said Congresswoman Linda Sánchez.

“Republicans and Democrats from every corner of the country keep signing on, because this is a national jobs issue with a commonsense fix. Crews in California, Georgia, Texas, New York, New Jersey, and beyond all want the same thing: to keep this industry in America instead of watching the work move overseas. I’m grateful to every partner who has joined this fight, and I’m ready to get a national film tax credit across the finish line,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman.

title: Senator Schmitt Celebrates Senate Passage of Bipartisan Route 66 National Historic Trail Designation Act
text:
Schmitt Helped Lead Effort to Preserve Iconic Highway as National Historic Trail for Its 100th Anniversary

U.S. SENATE – Today, U.S. Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) celebrated the Senate passage of his bipartisan “Route 66 National Historic Trail Designation Act” to designate the historic highway as a National Historic Trail. The bill now heads to the House of Representatives for consideration.

“Route 66 is part of America’s story, and Missouri is at the heart of that story. It was right here in Springfield that the name ‘Route 66’ was first sent by telegram 100 years ago. I’m proud to have helped lead this bipartisan effort alongside Senator Cruz to preserve the Mother Road and recognize the communities, small businesses, and history that make it an American icon. I look forward to getting this across the finish line for Route 66’s 100thanniversary,” said Senator Schmitt.

Route 66 stretches approximately 2,400 miles from Chicago, Illinois, to Santa Monica, California, connecting communities across eight states. The designation would formally recognize the historic highway as a National Historic Trail inside the National Trail System and help preserve its history and legacy for future generations.

Missouri holds a special place in Route 66 history. On April 30, 1926, highway officials sent a telegram from Springfield proposing the name “Route 66” for the new highway. The route was officially established later that year, and 2026 marks its 100th anniversary. Springfield is recognized as the Birthplace of Route 66.

title: Senator Schmitt’s Bipartisan RISE Act to Eliminate Barriers for College Students with Disabilities Passes Senate
text:
Legislation Would Ensure Students with Documented Disabilities Can Access College Accommodations

U.S. SENATE – U.S. Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) praised Senate passage of the bipartisan “Respond, Innovate, Succeed, and Empower (RISE) Act,” legislation that would eliminate unnecessary barriers for college students with documented disabilities seeking accommodations. Senator Schmitt joined Senators Jim Banks (R-Ind.), Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.), and Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA) in introducing the legislation.

“Students with documented disabilities should not have to face unnecessary barriers or pay for duplicative testing to receive the accommodations they need to succeed in college. This issue is personal to me, and I’m proud to work with my colleagues to make disability services more transparent and helps ensure students have the support they need to pursue their education,” said Senator Schmitt.

Approximately 15 percent of public-school students receive services under the Individuals with “Disabilities Education Act.” However, students entering college are often required to undergo and pay for new diagnostic testing before receiving accommodations, even when their disability has already been documented.

Key Provisions of the “RISE Act”:

Closes a loophole that often requires students with documented disabilities to undergo new, costly diagnostic testing to qualify for accommodations.

Makes school policies regarding disability services more transparent for students and families so they can make an informed decision on the college that best fits their needs.

Requires universities to collect and report key data related to undergraduate students who are registered as students with disabilities to the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS).

Provides additional support and authorizes funds for technical assistance to help colleges and universities better serve students with disabilities.

The legislation is endorsed by the National Center for Learning Disabilities, Association of Public and Land-grant Universities, American Council on Education, Association on Higher Education and Disability, American Psychological Association, Autism Society of America, National Disability Rights Network, National Down Syndrome Society, Autism Speaks, The Arc of the United States, and numerous other education and disability advocacy organizations.

title: SCHUMER, GILLIBRAND, MORELLE ANNOUNCE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS BACKED OFF PLANS TO BUILD BORDER PATROL DETENTION CENTER IN DOWNTOWN ROCHESTER FOLLOWING OPPOSITION FROM LAWMAKERS & COMMUNITY MEMBERS
text:
Earlier This Year, Lawmakers Urged U.S. Customs And Border Protection And The U.S. General Services Administration To Halt Plans To Build A Detention Center In Federal Building, Citing Disruptions To Federal Court, A Childcare Facility, & Other Critical Services

Lawmakers Warn Trump Admin Against Moving To Another Facility In Rochester Area & Say Agency Must Be Transparent With Local Officials And Community Members About Any Future Plans In The Region

Schumer, Gillibrand, Morelle: No Detention Facilities In Rochester

Following their opposition to the Trump administration’s plan to build a Border Patrol detention center in downtown Rochester, U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, and U.S. Congressman Joseph Morelle today announced that U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), which oversees U.S. Border Patrol, has backed off its ill-conceived plan to build a detention center in the Kenneth B. Keating Federal Building. The General Services Administration (GSA), which runs the Keating Federal Building, has notified the Western District Federal Court that CBP has withdrawn its request for new space in the Keating Federal Building to assess other options. The lawmakers reiterated their staunch opposition to plans to expand existing or construct new U.S. Border Patrol detention facilities in the region and warned the Trump administration against trying to do so without the input of local leaders and community members.

“I’m proud to announce that there will be no immigration detention center in downtown Rochester at the Keating Federal Building. Earlier this year, after the Trump administration’s Customs and Border Protection announced this absurd plan, with no communication with local officials, no public comment period, and no transparency. We demanded CBP stop the secrecy and back off this ill-conceived plan,” said Senator Schumer. “I applaud Rochester’s local leaders and the community members who joined our call, rallying at the federal building on a nearly weekly basis to push back against CBP’s unwelcome plans. I will always stand with Upstate New Yorkers to protect local communities from the Trump administration’s extreme plans to build or expand detention facilities, including expanding the detention center in Batavia. Border Patrol needs to be reined in and reformed from top to bottom – not expanded.”

“Placing a 24/7 Customs and Border Protection detention center inside the Keating federal building – alongside a childcare facility and critical public services – was the wrong decision from day one. I am proud to have stood with Senator Schumer, Congressman Morelle, and local advocates to stop this plan in its tracks. While I am relieved CBP has withdrawn its request, the Trump administration must not attempt to quietly relocate this facility elsewhere in the Rochester area without full transparency and input from local officials and residents,” said Senator Kirsten Gillibrand.

“This is a major victory for the people of Rochester who made their voices heard and refused to accept the Trump Administration’s reckless plan to bring immigration detention cells into the heart of our downtown,” said Congressman Joe Morelle. “I’m grateful to Senator Schumer and Senator Gillibrand for their partnership in fighting this proposal, and I will continue fighting to protect our community from Donald Trump’s cruel immigration agenda.”

In March, the lawmakers in a letter to the CBP Commissioner and the Acting Administrator of the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) explained that building a detention center would disrupt the day-to-day operations of other federal offices in the building and the Western District of New York Federal Courts. The lawmakers emphasized opposition to this plan from local residents and officials, the legal community, and more, and demanded clarity and transparency from the Trump administration.

title: Sens. Scott, Warnock introduce bill to restore “I Have a Dream” plaque at Lincoln Memorial
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senators Tim Scott (R-S.C.) and Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.) introduced the Renewing the Dream Act to restore the plaque commemorating Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s “I Have a Dream” speech at the Lincoln Memorial. After years of wear and tear, the plaque marking the exact spot where Dr. King delivered his iconic speech during the 1963 March on Washington faded and became increasingly difficult to read. Private funds were raised to replace the plaque, but the King family was informed by the U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) that a replacement would require an act of Congress.

“America was founded on the ideals of life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. To become a more perfect union, leaders like Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. had to speak the truth and challenge our nation to live up to our founding ideals,” said Sen. Scott. “His ‘I Have a Dream’ speech brought the promise of America closer to reality, and by continuing to honor his legacy on this plaque, we can remind future generations of the power of speaking the truth and standing up for justice for all.”

“Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s words from his ‘I Have a Dream’ speech resonate as powerfully today as they did then,” said Sen. Reverend Warnock. “The spot where Georgia’s greatest son spoke those historic words deserves to be properly restored to honor his legacy, vision, and fight for justice.”

title: Shaheen Statement on Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
text:
(Washington, DC) – Today, U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) released the following statement on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act:

“While I am supportive of efforts to improve the way we permit energy and infrastructure projects to help bring down energy costs for Americans, I also have a responsibility to listen to the concerns brought forward by my constituents. I share their fears that this federal legislation would limit Granite Staters’ say in protecting places they care about and weaken New Hampshire’s longstanding role in safeguarding our rivers, lakes, streams and wetlands.

“As major infrastructure and energy projects move forward, as data centers put pressure on local water supplies and as contaminants like PFAS impact more and more communities, we should not be weakening the ability of states and tribes to protect water quality.

“It was my hope that this legislation could be improved, which is why I offered an amendment to preserve the longstanding partnership that allows states and tribes to have a meaningful say in protecting the water that their communities rely on. Absent changes to ensure that states and tribes will be able to maintain their authority, I am unable to support this legislation.”
